A rare white moose filmed in Sweden drew global attention. The BBC says about 100 exist in Sweden; they are not albino but have a genetic mutation for white fur. Twitter users compared it to mythical creatures.

The team calls tomorrow’s game important but notes the long series and says it is regrouping today. It says its powerplay must score more and it cannot let up, after controlling two periods and allowing a third-period comeback.

The passage documents the ADS868xW 16-bit SAR ADC’s integrated high-bandwidth, low-noise, stable ADC driver buffer; internal or external 4.096V reference selection via INTREF_DIS; internal-reference decoupling, accuracy, thermal/solder-reflow shift, and external-reference buffer considerations; single-ended/differential bipolar and unipolar input ranges with straight-binary output; input and AVDD alarm functions with programmable input thresholds/hysteresis and active/tripped flags; multiSPI interface, SPI-compatible and source-synchronous protocols, daisy-chain topology, RESET/ACQ/CONV states, data transfer frames, command/register operations; an eight-channel PLC/DCS/DAS application example using the ADS8681W and MUX36D08; and AVDD/DVDD decoupling, NAP/power-down modes, and PCB layout recommendations.

Princeton scientists and international collaborators developed Diag2Diag, an AI system that uses sensor data to generate synthetic, detailed data for other diagnostics, including plasma-edge measurements that sensors cannot easily capture. Using data from DIII-D experiments, it could reduce reliance on bulky diagnostics and support more compact, affordable, reliable fusion systems. The generated data also supported the magnetic-island theory of ELM suppression, and researchers see potential applications in other fields with missing or limited sensor data.

The passage lists and describes AI content generator and writer tools for 2022, including Jasper, Copy.ai, Frase, Article Forge, Rytr, CopySmith, Hypotenuse, Kafkai, and Peppertype. It covers their features, content types, SEO and plagiarism capabilities, pricing, free trials or plans, and pros and cons. It also notes that the article contains affiliate links and states the author’s opinion that Jasper is one of the best tools for high-quality content.

Origin PC announced the Eon15-S gaming laptop starting at $999 in the US, using Nvidia's GeForce 1050Ti. The base model has an Intel Core i3 and 120GB SSD; $100 more adds a Core i5 and double storage. It costs $100–$200 more than Dell's Inspiron 15 7000 but offers an IPS display and 24/7 US-based lifetime support with a one-year warranty. CNET plans to test it soon.

The Supreme Court declined to hear Ghislaine Maxwell’s appeal of a 2nd Circuit decision on a 2007 Epstein non-prosecution agreement. Maxwell, serving a 20-year sentence, argued the agreement’s co-conspirators clause bound all U.S. attorney’s offices, but the 2nd Circuit held such agreements bind only the region unless they affirmatively show multi-district intent. The Solicitor General opposed review.

The 5-Day Low of the Range Strategy uses two criteria: IBS below 0.25 and the close below the previous 5-day lowest low. From January 1993 to today, it had 517 trades, 309 winners, a 60% win ratio, and an average 0.46% return per trade, above the 0.11% average for any 5-day period. Profitability peaks at 3–7 days; a 5-day exit produced a 10.76% annualized return versus buy and hold. It can be adapted for short selling using criteria such as 0.75 or 0.9, yielding almost 10%, though short strategies are harder and less profitable. Recent performance has not worked well.

The passage describes the need for point-of-care (POC) COVID-19 testing and evaluates the Sal6830™ SARS-CoV-2 Saliva Test. RT-PCR is highly accurate but initially required central laboratories and NPS samples, causing delays, exposure, discomfort, and inconsistent results. Some POC RT-PCR platforms existed but involved extra sample handling and possible contamination. Saliva is non-invasive, lower cost, and SARS-CoV-2 can be detected reliably in it; self-collection is less dependent on collector skill. The Sal6830™ is described as the first saliva-based RT-PCR POC test with emergency use authorization; patients self-deposit saliva into an all-in-one cartridge, reducing biohazard handling and sample mix-up. A study at two clinics evaluated blinded samples and prospective clinical performance by non-laboratory trained healthcare workers, comparing Sal6830™ with the Cepheid Xpert Xpress CoV-2/Flu/RSV. Blinded negative and positive samples were concordant, with one invalid positive result. Clinical positive percent agreement was 87.2%, negative percent agreement 97.2%, and overall percent agreement 93.3%. Usability questionnaire responses indicated the test was easy to use, well integrated, and users were confident and did not require technical support. The conclusion states Sal6830™ can be used accurately and easily by non-laboratory trained healthcare workers in POC settings.

Neural Radiance Cache uses a neural shader to cache and approximate radiance by training tiny neural networks on live game data. It sends path-traced rays after one bounce into the cache, inferring final lighting for many bounces to improve performance and indirect lighting quality in real-time rendering.
State v. Nelson reversed and remanded by unpublished opinion.

A voice-directed inspection system supports multiple inspectors in inspecting business assets. It includes a host computer, site computers, and inspection assistance devices, each with a portable computer device and headset. The host computer sends an inspection plan for an asset to a site computer. The site computer receives assignment requests from multiple inspection assistance devices, determines whether multiple unfinished sections of the inspection plan exist, and if so sends different sections to different devices. The devices provide audible commands for their sections, receive audible updates on completion, and send updates to the site computer, which sends them to the host computer. Sections may be non-overlapping or prioritized, and inspectors may request a specific or any unfinished section. The site computer may indicate no inspection plan if no unfinished sections exist. Methods and non-transient computer-readable media perform similar steps. An inspection plan editor allows operators to create, edit, and modify plans, parameters, prompts, speech recognition, transcription, and review inspection results.

The passage suggests that asking whether judges are good historians is the wrong question because judges are lawyers who decide cases, not historians. It discusses Bruen’s two-step Second Amendment test, criticism that historical inquiry burdens courts, and originalist responses that historical evidence is often manageable and legal tools help judges decide amid uncertainty.

The speaker is thrilled the series is over and credits Buffalo as a good young team. After missing the playoffs last year, the speaker was excited and wanted to give everything. Ten years after winning the Stanley Cup, the speaker reflects on adversity and injuries, noting many players played hurt. Hull and veteran teammates were important, and the team knows how to win.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture presents poker analysis through a decision mentality focused on expected results rather than actual outcomes. It uses credit card roulette and the law of large numbers to argue decisions should be judged without bias from results. The lecture describes three levels of reasoning: level one, specific hand versus specific hand; level two, hand versus opponent’s range using exploitative play; and level three, range versus range using optimal play or Nash equilibrium. It uses rock-paper-scissors to contrast exploitative and optimal play, and the Who’s Taller game to explain why blinds are needed. It covers stack size, effective stack size, position, antes, equity, pot odds, and all-in decisions. It gives tournament advice on raising versus calling, raise sizing, and recommended opening ranges by position, with examples and PokerStove calculations. It concludes with in-class poker hand demonstrations.

In the UK, many women with ovarian cancer are diagnosed only after emergency care, and just one in three cases is identified at the earliest stages. Ovarian Cancer Action says late diagnosis occurs due to difficulties getting timely appointments and being dismissed by healthcare providers. Public awareness is low: 90% of women are unaware of the four main symptoms, and one in four mistakenly believe a test detects ovarian cancer, though there is no screening test. The four main symptoms are persistent bloating, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, urinary urgency or frequency, and persistent abdominal or pelvic pain. Other possible signs include lower back aches, digestive discomfort, nausea, bleeding after menopause, and unusual tiredness. Ovarian Cancer Action offers a free online symptom checker and a downloadable symptoms diary. Early detection gives a 95% chance of survival, while stage four has a 16% survival rate; less than a third of cases are diagnosed at stage 1 or 2. The passage says ovarian cancer is called the “silent killer,” which Stanford considers misleading, and stresses symptom awareness and seeking medical advice early.

DryShips Inc issued a 6-K after the April 17 market close detailing common stock issuance through a continuous offering under a Prospectus Supplement. It raised $14.5 million through 7,912,449 shares at an average price of $1.79, failing to raise the $30 million requested through Kalani Investors. There were 54.92 million shares outstanding at April 17, and shares issued from April 10 through April 17 resulted in 16.8% dilution. Kalani failed three consecutive Fixed Amount Requests and issued only 48% of requested amounts. Equity issuance was 8.86% of volume traded. At about $3.2 million/day, the remaining $173.4 million would take 54 trading days and 105.7 million additional shares at a 15% discount.

Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico on September 20, 2017, with sustained winds of 155 mph, gusts up to 190 mph, rains up to 40 inches, and floods; it destroyed the electricity grid, left 3.4 million without electricity, affected infrastructure, caused over US$82 billion in damages, and destroyed about 80% of crop value, a $780 million loss. The passage discusses indirect deaths from emergencies, limitations in mortality counts and prior Maria excess-death studies, and proposes a semiparametric Poisson regression model to estimate deaths caused by a state of emergency by incorporating intra-annual variability, population displacement, and causes of death including non-communicable and other indirect causes, while capturing the duration of mortality effects by cause.

At the final round of the 2017 Molecule ProKart Series at KartSport Hamilton’s Agrisea Raceway, Dylan Drysdale won the Wifiplus KZ2 title by four points over Aaron Wilson. Tim Loughran took the Aarque Group KZ2 Masters round and series title, with Brett Hollander second overall and Enrico van der Griend third. Garry Cullum won the KZ2 Restricted round and series title for a record fourth time, with Regan Hall second and Aaron Wooley third. The weekend featured wet and dry conditions and time penalties for kerb hopping.

NASA’s HAMMER spacecraft could use an impactor on smaller asteroids, but for large asteroids like Bennu it would deploy a nuclear device. Bennu is a potentially hazardous near-Earth object with a 1-in-2,700 chance of hitting Earth in 2135.

Hendrik Bessembinder’s 2017 study asks whether stocks outperform Treasury Bills and concludes no. From 1926 to 2015, only 43% of equities returned more than Treasury Bills, and only 86 of 26,000 stocks made half the return. The average stock market has performed well, but the median stock has performed poorly, making randomly selected stocks likely losers. Bessembinder identifies 30 stocks that made 30% of all returns. A similar Norwegian study of the Oslo Stock Exchange from 1985 to 2017 found that only 18 large companies explained all value creation, while most shares did worse than risk-free rates. The passage says the easiest solution is a passive fund; individual-stock investors need diversification.

At higher levels, if a soccer player appears injured and the referee allows play to continue, players may show sportsmanship by kicking the ball over the sideline to stop play. After treatment, the referee restarts with a throw-in by the team that did not kick the ball out; that team should return the ball backward to the opponent. Neither team should take advantage. When the referee stops play for injury, a similar dropped-ball courtesy applies.

Predictive maintenance/e-Maintenance is presented as a critical component of e-Manufacturing, using real-time and smart monitoring, performance assessment, globally networked monitoring, prognostics, and web-enabled monitoring, analysis, comparison, reconfiguration, and sustainment to support near-zero downtime. Intelligent decisions can connect to e-business tools such as CRM, ERP, and e-commerce systems. E-Maintenance supports integration of e-Manufacturing and e-business, increasing equipment and process reliability, asset performance, and supplier/customer integration. Research needs include predictive intelligence, quality-degradation mapping, data conversion tools, reliable informatics platforms, security, distributed web-based computing, training, and a new enterprise culture. The text also describes reconfigurable maintenance in business, where customer requirements, product configuration, tolerance, and maintenance policy affect quality and costs, and where systems support intercompany cooperation and shared diagnostics. Modular reconfigurable maintenance uses control-center communication for remote maintenance, monitoring sensors, and an expert/knowledge base to detect abnormalities and identify faults. The conclusion states that mass customization pressures require companies to integrate reconfigurable maintenance to respond cost-effectively and ensure production reliability.

The author says they gave up on the market prematurely and asks if equities might melt up instead. They note low VIX draws attention as complacency, with caution prescribed, and cite 21 charts for doom predictors to reconsider; market breadth that made them bearish now shows strength.

The Teachers’ Union of Ireland warned teachers that becoming Facebook friends with students is ill advised and can narrow professional distance, with virtual friendships and photos potentially compromising them. It warned that social media comments can endanger employment or create legal trouble, advising caution before posting and avoiding online feuds. It criticized employers’ 24/7 social-media expectations and advised members not to respond to unreasonable contact.

This May 17, 2001 VentureWire newsletter includes top stories, new money, bad news, new products, M&A, new directors, new people, VC fund news, VC personnel, and corrections. Top stories cover Tahoe Networks’ $38M first round, Startups.com’s model/name change and layoffs, Hermes/BTPS’s $965M allocation, and OffRoad Capital’s split and 50% staff cut. It also reports various funding rounds, Eazel’s closure, RoundArch’s staff cut, product launches, acquisitions, executive appointments, a $50M Israeli VC fund, VC personnel additions, and a MolecularWare correction.

The speaker, about to assume appointed duties, expresses gratitude and accountability. He outlines his intentions: execute U.S. laws within Executive limits; manage foreign and confederate relations, revenue, forces, and legislative communications; preserve peace and friendship abroad; respect the separate States’ powers; promote strict economy to reduce the national debt; favor agriculture, commerce, and manufactures equally; support internal improvement and knowledge; avoid enlarging standing armies in peace; maintain the Navy, forts, arsenals, and dockyards; rely on the militia for defense; observe a just and liberal policy toward Indian tribes; pursue reform of abuses in patronage and appointments; select diligent and faithful officers; seek guidance and support; and rely on Providence.

This study examines how TRNC Presidents’ discourses on history, identity, and education have influenced education policies and compares different Presidents’ statements and policies. It outlines the education system’s historical phases from the Ottoman and British periods through 1960 and post-1974 restructuring, and notes the role of Education Council decisions, reforms, teacher training, curricula, textbooks, and infrastructure. It discusses education’s role in modernization and Turkish Cypriot identity, history textbooks’ polarizing and reconciliatory potential, and varying emphases under Denktaş, Talat, Eroğlu, Akıncı, and Tatar. It concludes that presidential discourse and Council decisions shape reforms and recommends long-term, scientifically neutral, multi-perspective education policies.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said India's SCO accession increased the grouping's political profile and potential and its capacity to stabilize Central and South Asia and help resolve the Afghanistan crisis. He called India's foreign policy a factor for security and stability, said bilateral trade was unsatisfactory with a $30 billion target by 2025, and said deeper defense cooperation would bring technology transfers. He doubted the new US Afghanistan strategy would work, cited NATO's failure to curb extremism, terrorism, and drug trade, and denied Russian support for the Taliban. He said the US declined the Moscow Process for Six Plus One, and Afghanistan requires all relevant parties; the Kabul Process was too large.

A letter taped to the door of fired assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben’Ary said a false social media post apparently led to his termination while he was in the middle of a terrorism prosecution. The letter warned that DOJ political leadership was making America less safe by removing career officials and was more concerned with punishing perceived Trump enemies than protecting national security. Ben’Ary was fired after pro-Trump commentator Julie Kelly suggested he was an ally of Lisa Monaco.

The speaker says the team must be prepared for an opponent playing for its life and a chance to get a game back in the speaker's building, focus on a strong start, and try to end the series despite the opponent's home playoff success.

New England wide receiver Malcolm Mitchell caught six passes for 70 yards in the Patriots’ 34-28 comeback win over the Atlanta Falcons in Super Bowl XVI. After struggling with reading in college, he taught himself to read better by starting with children’s books. He launched Read with Malcolm, a youth literacy initiative promoting books to students in underserved communities; its goals include introducing book ownership and improving literacy in schools with below-average grade-level reading. Mitchell will receive the Promise Hero Award from America’s Promise Alliance at its 20th Anniversary Summit and Gala in New York. He graduated from the University of Georgia in December 2015 with a communications degree, was drafted by the Patriots last May, and wrote The Magician’s Hat. In an interview, he discussed starting from scratch, reading Colin Powell and The 33 Strategies of War, being inspired by his mother, Pratina Woods, and advising children never to give up.

Yandex announced it will report second-quarter 2018 financial results on July 26, 2018, and hold a conference call and webcast at 8:00 a.m. U.S. Eastern Time; replay is available until August 2, 2018.

The passage discusses digital accessibility, WCAG, legal mandates, low global compliance, and economic and skills gaps tied to limited accessibility education, especially in India. It reports on an informal one-day workshop designed for software professionals and CS educators in India to build capacity in digital accessibility. The workshop used a three-phase model and included five instructional modules—Accessibility Basics, Accessibility Design, Accessible Software Engineering, Accessibility Testing and Reporting, and Teaching Accessibility—plus hands-on activities and thematic booths. Pre- and post-workshop surveys assessed knowledge, attitudes, confidence, and perceptions. The workshop had 73 participants: 33 software engineers, 28 educators, and 12 UX designers. Feedback was positive across engagement, confidence, effectiveness, and likelihood of applying learning; all participants said they would recommend the workshop. Open-ended responses identified interest in advanced inclusive design, AI and emerging technologies, inclusive design for diverse users, organizational strategies and policy, and practice-based learning. The discussion notes what worked well, challenges such as difficulty with technical content and reliance on simulations, and recommendations for future efforts including pre-workshop materials, role-based customization, case studies, peer learning, and continued engagement.

The passage analyzes whether Humphrey’s Executor is headed for Slaughter, focusing on Trump’s firing of FTC commissioner Rebecca Kelly Slaughter and whether presidents may remove FTC heads without cause. It recounts Humphrey’s Executor, which upheld FTC independence based on the FTC’s predominantly legislative and judicial, non-executive duties. It notes that recent decisions, especially Seila Law, require courts to examine an agency’s actual powers; unlike the New Deal-era FTC, the CFPB’s single director, lack of bipartisan multi-member structure, and executive powers defeated independence. It says the modern FTC has more rulemaking and enforcement authority, acts primarily as an executive law enforcement agency, and is increasingly partisan, though it retains a bipartisan multi-member structure. The court seems likely to uphold Slaughter’s firing, partly based on its stay order concerning the NLRB and MSPB, but may avoid overruling Humphrey’s Executor—possibly preserving Federal Reserve independence—and may separate Slaughter’s firing from Humphrey’s future, suggesting a “mend it, don’t end it” approach.

In a SONA debate speech, DA Leader Mmusi Maimane criticized the ANC government and President Jacob Zuma, saying Zuma’s talk of radical economic transformation was a cover for elite self-enrichment. He cited the deaths of mentally ill patients sent to unlicensed NGOs, Marikana, and security around SONA, and said the ANC had become the enemy of the people. He accused Zuma of corruption and of laughing at violence against MPs. He described a “lost generation” of unemployed, out-of-school, and NEET young South Africans. He said land reform, BEE, the Black Industrialists Programme, a nuclear build, the MPRDA Bill, and a state mining company would enrich ANC cronies. Maimane outlined a DA “Rescue Plan”: a lean state; education reforms including teacher training, school vouchers, a National Education Inspectorate, expanded student funding, and vocational training; apprenticeships and internships; private-sector-led job creation; SMME support; infrastructure investment; stopping the nuclear deal; opening electricity to independent producers; partial privatization of SOEs; mining policy changes; mass-inclusion BEE; land title deeds and farm equity schemes; more police; a health plan; and anti-corruption measures including fewer ministries and reduced perks. He said the DA would work with the people and bring hope to the lost generation.

Alexa can help make cleaning and organizing easier. Users can use Cleaning Buddy to create a cleaning schedule, set up voice purchasing to order supplies from Amazon, control connected robot vacuums like Neato or Roomba with voice commands, and use Laundrapp for laundry pickup and delivery or skills like Good Housekeeping or Stains Be Gone for stain-removal advice.

Using WLI and AFM, this work examined defects introduced by electropolishing on mechanically polished bulk Nb. It characterized intergranular sloped steps and calculated magnetic field enhancement and superheating field suppression factors within London theory. Grain boundaries hosted substantial slope angles and step heights that compromise high-field stability of the Meissner state; these defects significantly limit electropolished bulk Nb from achieving peak fields near the superheating field and can cause larger degradation than previously expected. Random and sequential EP measurements showed no obvious dependence of slope angle or step height on EP removal, with steps primarily controlled by relative grain orientation; electrolyte exposure caused small changes, while electropolishing was the primary cause. Impurity diffusion simulations indicated reduced impurity concentration at the bottom of sloped steps and enhanced concentration at the top, affecting uniformity of shallow impurity profiles such as low-temperature baking or nitrogen infusion. The work concludes that smoother surfaces are needed for high-field performance and that by-eye “mirror-smooth” evaluation is inadequate.

MIT researchers developed an improved prime editing system by modifying Cas9 proteins and adding an RNA binding protein to stabilize the RNA template, creating an editor called vPE. The method reduced errors, lowering the rate for the most common editing type from about one in seven to one in 101 and in a more precise mode from one in 122 to one in 543, or 1/60th of the original rate. Tests were performed in mouse and human cells. The team says the approach could make gene therapy safer and more effective for genetic diseases and is working on improving efficiency and delivery.

Police declared a major incident after a man and woman in their 40s were found unconscious in Amesbury and hospitalized in critical condition from an unknown substance. Counterterrorism officers are working with Wiltshire Police. The town is eight miles from Salisbury, where Sergei and Yulia Skripal were poisoned in March. Testing is ongoing, and it is unclear whether a crime occurred.

The bankruptcy court considered D.A.N. Joint Venture III, L.P.’s complaint to deny Ambrozy Jerry Fasolak’s Chapter 7 discharge under § 727(a)(2), (a)(3), (a)(4), and (a)(5). The plaintiff alleged fraudulent transfer or concealment, failure to keep records, false oaths, and failure to explain loss of assets. The court found that the debtor transferred certain funds and a vehicle title to his wife and made inaccurate or incomplete statements and schedules, later amended to disclose prior bankruptcies, A & F stock, and consulting income. The court nonetheless found no fraudulent intent, no identified specific missing records, no knowing and fraudulent false oaths, and no established identifiable asset loss requiring explanation. It therefore ruled for the debtor on all counts, ordered final judgment against the plaintiff, and directed entry of the debtor’s discharge.

Polo originated in Persia (modern-day Iran) more than 20 centuries ago and later spread through the Middle East, Central Asia and the Far East. The modern game stems most directly from India, where it was called sagol kangjei, kanjai-bazee or pulu, after the wooden ball; British travelers brought it to England and then the U.S. There are about 250 U.S. polo clubs in 43 states. The Milwaukee Polo Club is in Hartland, about 26 miles west of Milwaukee, and is described as this generation’s extension of the original Milwaukee-area polo formation in 1923; it has been at its current location for more than 20 years. Thomas Esser says the club aims to make polo approachable, calling it “blue collar” polo, with members including nurses, students, bartenders, retirees, teenagers, adults and seniors; tickets are $5 and children are free. Games usually consist of six seven-minute chukkers, a halftime divot stomp, and last about two hours. Outdoor polo is fair-weather driven by safety, and if the surface cannot hold a horse’s footing, play will not proceed; if it is not raining, the club will be at the fields. Esser says horses are treated as teammates, with limits on work and attention to physical and mental balance. The club is located at N75 W30311 County Highway VV in Hartland, had its summer season opener June 18, and offers phone numbers and milwaukeepoloclub.com for information.

The speaker says success comes from preparation, focus, and execution rather than momentum or carryover. Losing is devastating, especially in a cap world where opportunities are rare and injuries can affect chances. The speaker stresses depth, drafting, development, and contributions from all players, plus favorable matchups and controlling games. Team building is described as winning together and sacrificing for one another. Other points include puck handling and forecheck execution, goaltending being better at home than on the road, a player feeling good, and enjoying current opportunities because they may not come again.

After ICE detained at least 51 people in the Austin and San Antonio area, Austin ISD lawyers told principals and staff not to share student resources or fliers not vetted by the superintendent’s office or general counsel. A memo barred employees from speaking on political affiliation, views, protests, advocacy, or controversial topics on district property and warned of scrutiny or repercussions. Board Vice President Paul Saldana criticized the memo, saying the board was not briefed. Superintendent Paul Cruz posted immigrant and refugee resources; Education Austin distributed rights information and planned events.

A 13-year-old girl was shot in the thigh while sitting with others in an open garage in Guildford, Sydney, on Tuesday night. She was hospitalized in serious but stable condition, and police believe the shooting was not random.

The passage argues that penny stocks are often bad investments because many companies have unproven or failing business models, lack financial disclosure, are illiquid, volatile, and traded largely on unregulated OTC and Pink Sheets markets. They are exposed to scams such as pump-and-dump, dump-and-dilute, and “know-it-all” schemes. Most penny stocks fail or become worthless, and the passage recommends avoiding them.

Sen. Mark Warner said Republicans are engaged in an unprecedented attempt to undermine special counsel Robert Mueller’s investigation and FBI integrity. He criticized the Nunes memo’s release, said he and Sen. Richard Burr were denied pre-release access, and called it partisan. House Speaker Paul Ryan supported transparency and Democrats releasing their memo. Warner said the Senate Russia investigation continues and the cyber threat has not been acknowledged as a national threat.

The passage studies two-sided many-to-one matching and fairness for both participants and teams. It notes that participant-justified envy-freeness can be unfair to teams and that team-EF1 and participant-justified EF may not coexist in many-to-one settings. It introduces team-justified EF1, including stochastic-dominance versions under ordinal preferences with ties, to account for participants’ preferences when assessing team envy. Two warm-up approaches satisfy only some desired properties. The main polynomial-time algorithm creates team-slots, maintains eligibility sets for participants, and computes lexicographically optimized eligible matchings. It returns allocations satisfying team-justified SD-EF1, participant-justified EF, balancedness, Pareto optimality, and therefore swap stability. The algorithm reduces to the round-robin algorithm when participants are indifferent among teams and to the Gale–Shapley algorithm under strict preferences. With augmented tie-breaking, it is group-strategyproof for participants. The passage also extends the approach to teams with quotas and to participants or teams that may prefer being unassigned, yielding an allocation satisfying stability, extended team-justified SD-EF1, Pareto optimality, and group-strategyproofness for participants.

The passage contrasts digital leaders and laggards in building data cultures. Digital laggards prioritize short-term imperatives and existing initiatives, offer narrow on-the-job training, discourage risk, and often lack trust. They tightly control data access, store data in silos, require burdensome requests, favor “need-to-know” sharing, data hoarding, business judgment, and a “culture of genius” over data-driven decisions. They set aspirational goals insufficiently grounded in data, focus on process over objective measurement, and fail to connect goals with strategy.

Digital leaders emphasize a learning mindset, transparent data access, appropriate governance controls, measurement, structured yet flexible goals, and alignment through shared objectives. They use data-driven objectives to coordinate across the organization, often through top-down and bottom-up processes. Even leaders face challenges balancing risk-taking, deadlines, inconsistent data attitudes, and over-analysis. Regulated industries may discourage risk-taking, but localized experimentation can foster innovation, as shown by a pharmaceutical company automating compliance checks and a retail company implementing real-time sales reporting.

The passage also notes that organizations may fit patterns such as data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant. Changing entrenched mindsets and behaviors is described as a difficult part of digital transformation, but laggards are not necessarily doomed to stall.

At the centennial of the first written U.S. constitution, the speaker reviews the nation’s dangers, the adoption of the Constitution, and its effects: enlarged freedom, strengthened order and peace, twenty-five added states, and expanded jurisdiction. He recalls the Civil War as the Constitution’s supreme trial, after which the Union emerged purified and stronger. He states the people have registered their will and that the Executive must interpret and execute it under the Constitution. He calls the elevation of the negro race from slavery to citizenship the most important political change since 1787, discusses disturbances in Southern communities, equal suffrage, and dangers of ignorance and illiteracy, urging universal education. He addresses currency and coinage, paper money, debt refunding, agriculture, manufacturers, transportation, an interoceanic canal, religious freedom and Mormon polygamy, and civil service regulation. He says his Administration will maintain national authority, enforce laws, demand economy, and require faithful service, and he invokes support and blessings of Almighty God.

The passage describes the ATR trailing stop as a technical indicator introduced by J. Welles Wilder that uses average true range to help traders set dynamic stop-loss levels based on price volatility. It can help protect profits, minimize losses, determine exit points, and may also provide entry signals. Calculation involves multiplying ATR by a multiplier, typically 3.5, then subtracting from or adding to the previous close for long or short positions. ATR bands are derived from ATR values, and cross points or consistent breaches of trailing stop levels can indicate market changes or potential trend reversals. Risks include not accounting for past performance or price movements and inherent trading uncertainties.

Drew Faust, Harvard’s first female president, announced she will step down on June 30, 2018, after 11 years, as the university’s fundraising campaign concludes. A historian, she plans a sabbatical and return to scholarship. She was credited with restoring trust, fostering collaboration, expanding financial aid, and supporting arts and sciences; the campaign raised $8 billion. She also faced controversies over all-male clubs, diversity, a soccer team suspension, and an endowment loss. A search committee will seek her replacement.

Texas A&M has had at least one first-round NFL draft pick every year since 2011. Receiver Christian Kirk, who bypassed his senior season, is A&M’s best hope to keep the streak alive; he projects as a fringe first-round pick. Safety Armani Watts forecasts as a mid-round choice, and receiver Damion Ratley might be selected in the late rounds. Defensive tackle Zaycoven Henderson was arrested in December and may not be drafted. The 2018 draft starts Thursday at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, and Kirk plans to be at home in Arizona.

Michigan State Superintendent Michael Rice is retiring Friday after leading since 2019; Sue Carnell will serve as interim until Glenn Maleyko starts. Rice led during the pandemic, which was followed by worse exam performance, increased chronic absenteeism, and mental health concerns, with slow academic recovery and record-low third-grade reading scores on M-STEP. In an interview, Rice said lawmakers must stop schools from counting up to seven professional development days as instructional days and raised concerns about online instruction and lost instructional time. He cited progress in equitable funding, preschool enrollment, and a record 82% graduation rate, but said no state education goals are fully met. He pointed to Mississippi’s reading gains and wants mandatory science-of-reading training for K-5 teachers. Teacher shortages are improving after state investments, he said, but are not over.

Alphabet, which owns YouTube, will pay $24.5 million to settle a case brought by Donald Trump after YouTube suspended him following January 6, 2021. Of that, $22 million will go to Trump, and $2.5 million will go to co-plaintiffs. Trump directed his $22 million to the Trust for the National Mall and construction of a White House ballroom. The settlement includes no admission of liability. YouTube’s restrictions on Trump were lifted in March 2023. Trump previously settled with X and Meta, with more than $57 million total in settlement money related to his post-January 6 bans.

Peter Lynch is a retired money manager who managed Fidelity’s Magellan Fund from 1977 to 1990, achieving annual returns of 29.2% and retiring at his peak in 1990. He was a value investing proponent known for “invest in what you know” and “ten baggers,” and he recommended his 1989 book One Up On Wall Street. Born January 19, 1944, he spent his childhood in Boston and Massachusetts. His father died when he was 11, and Lynch worked as a caddy at Brae Burn golf club, where he met corporate executives. He first bought Flying Tiger Airlines stock at $7; it rose to $32 within two years. After an internship at Fidelity in 1966, he returned in 1969, was promoted in 1974, and took over Magellan in May 1977. The fund then had $20 million and 40 companies; under Lynch, its portfolio value increased more than 20 times, average annual return reached 29%, and it grew to $14 billion and 1,200 companies by his May 1990 retirement at age 43. His strategy focused on understandable, undervalued companies and fundamentals rather than market prediction or short-term fluctuations. He categorized companies as slow-growing, moderately growing, fast-growing, cyclical, crisis recovery, and undervalued assets. He preferred simple, clear businesses, analyzed market share and fundamental indicators, and allocated the portfolio mainly to growth stocks, with portions in moderate, cyclical, turnaround, and minor companies. He reviewed holdings every three months, rebalanced, held no cash, and sold or reduced based on price and fundamentals.

Ghana Football Association Vice President George Afriyie was relieved of his duties after an Executive Committee meeting on Tuesday. The decision came weeks after Afriyie announced at his 50th birthday party that he intended to contest the 2019 GFA polls. The media waited for Kwesi Nyantakyi’s blessing, but it never came, highlighting a rumoured rift. The rift began months earlier when Afriyie described Nyantakyi as greedy after financial disagreements; Nyantakyi had also said he wanted his deputy out because he suspected Afriyie of conniving with Nii Lante Vanderpuije. Afriyie’s sacking validated the rumour and will now embolden his quest to wrestle power from Nyantakyi. Previous Vice Presidents Fred Pappoe and Fred Crentsil were sidelined in 2011 and 2015. Afriyie had already been removed as head of the Black Stars Management Committee. The ExCo was divided, and colleagues Kojo Yankah and Winfred Osei publicly shamed him; Osei took his place. It is unclear whether Nyantakyi will seek re-election; he has led since late 2005. The sacking emboldened opinions that Nyantakyi must seek re-election to save his legacy. The passage says Nyantakyi will not be easy to uproot, and “we wait and see.”

The email is an Enron India Newsdesk compilation dated June 8, 2001, with headlines and articles on the Dabhol Power Company/Enron dispute. Articles report that lenders appointed Stone & Webster to evaluate suspension costs for DPC’s 2,184-MW project; Enron India MD K. Wade Cline suggested temporary suspension; Phase II was postponed pending settlement over rescinding the PPA. Private power producers expected an early end after PM Vajpayee’s optimistic comments. Reports said states could not afford DPC power above about Rs 3 per unit. Lenders unanimously suggested a one-year closure and asked Stone & Webster for a feasibility report. DPC was willing to cut its rate of return from 16% to 11%, while the Godbole panel said RoE should not exceed 16%. DPC appealed to the Bombay High Court against MERC’s order, challenged MERC jurisdiction, and objected to public hearings. Lenders formed a committee to negotiate with MSEB. Enron sought assurance on Phase I drawal. The Godbole panel charged DPC with doublespeak, and Medha Patkar demanded a judicial inquiry.
Scientists urge listing cheetahs as Endangered on the IUCN, citing low southern Africa population estimates; research reported cheetahs disappeared from 91 percent of their historic range.

Vector-borne diseases transmitted by mosquitoes are a global concern, with dengue cases in the Americas surpassing 7 million by May 2024. Climate change, global warming, and human mobility are facilitating mosquito spread and imported cases in temperate regions, including Europe and the Basque Country. In the Basque Country, no autochthonous Aedes mosquito-borne disease cases have been recorded, but imported dengue, chikungunya, and Zika cases increased, and Aedes albopictus eggs and Aedes japonicus populations have increased. This study estimates Aedes invasive mosquito abundance in the Basque Country using ovitrap egg counts and environmental factors—temperature, humidity, and precipitation—focusing on Gipuzkoa and Bizkaia because Araba had insufficient data. It applies GLM, SARIMAX, Random Forest, and Conditional Inference Trees, including lagged variables. Lagged independent and dependent variables generally improved model performance. Temperature was the most important climate feature, precipitation had less influence, and egg abundance was a key predictor. Random Forest performed best in training, while GLM performed best in testing, followed by SARIMAX; Conditional Inference Trees performed worst. Bizkaia’s test performance was affected by unusually high egg counts in 2023 compared with training data. Models predicted lower mosquito abundance in 2024 than the previous year. The study emphasizes ongoing localized surveillance for forecasting and control.

The speaker says four games were anybody’s game and two were controlled by one team, with momentum shifting and teams tilting the rink. Both teams now have an opportunity, and the speaker has been impressed by how hard the teams played; their own playoff run has been a major battle because of injuries and the players’ will and attitude. Winning changes the speaker’s feeling compared with last year, and the Stanley Cup is called hockey’s greatest prize. The speaker notes being more comfortable, quicker, and more assertive at home than on the road in the playoffs, and recalls a previous game where the team became paralyzed after giving up a goal and worried instead of playing. The speaker values Red Wings history, learning from great players, sharing the run with Detroit and Michigan fans amid economic hardship, and says Hossa needs only to do what he does because it does not matter who scores.

Eight years after graduating, the author reflects on college, saying they loved it but would do things differently, including not taking advantage of opportunities and not realizing how much time they had for adventure. They note everyone does college differently and that they can only speak to their own experience, then move on to things they did wrong.

Seven more candidates qualified Feb. 14 for the 6th Congressional District race to replace U.S. Rep. Tom Price, making 15 candidates with one qualifying day left. A special election is April 18, with a runoff June 20.
Liverpool’s 2017/18 Premier League fixtures include opening at Watford Aug 12, Everton Dec 9 and Apr 7, Manchester United Oct 14 and Mar 10, Swansea home Boxing Day, and Brighton May 13.

Smoking can exacerbate diabetes, is responsible for nearly half of all liver cancers, and quitting reduces cardiovascular disease risk by 50 percent after one year. A Thorax study led by UK researchers found CT lung cancer screening may push smokers to quit. Researchers sent information to a random sample of nearly 2.5 million British residents aged 50–75; 8,729 high-risk patients were identified. Eligible smokers were invited or not to CT screening, while all received standard cessation information. After two weeks, 10 percent of screened participants had quit versus 5 percent; after two years, 15 percent versus 5 percent. Authors noted self-selection and that concern about lung cancer may motivate cessation. They concluded CT screening offers a teachable moment and could be integrated with anti-smoking interventions.

The Geminid meteor shower will peak Wednesday night, with best viewing between midnight and 4 a.m. Thursday. Up to 50 meteors may be visible, especially in rural areas; no telescope is needed, and viewing should be better this year due to a smaller crescent moon.

Caltech and six other institutions received $4.9 million from the U.S. Geological Survey to develop a West Coast earthquake-warning system. The agency also announced about $1 million in sensor equipment for ShakeAlert, designed to give several seconds of advance warning.

Northwestern's first NCAA bid is within reach after a 66-59 upset of Wisconsin, but increased media attention may be a hurdle. Coach Chris Collins and players Bryant McIntosh and Vic Law said the team must avoid distraction and keep performing in remaining Big Ten games. Northwestern next hosts Maryland, with Scottie Lindsey set to miss a fourth game due to mono.

Valmet Oyj’s Board decided a new long-term share-based incentive plan for key employees, aiming to align shareholder and employee objectives, increase long-term Company value, commit employees and offer competitive share-based rewards. It covers discretionary periods 2018–2020; the Board sets criteria and targets. The 2018 reward is based on Comparable EBITA margin and stable-business orders received growth, paid partly in shares and cash in 2019. About 120 participants are included, and total rewards are capped at approximately 586,000 shares.

A U.S. study of 202 staff at Head Start and other Illinois daycare centers found nutrition, exercise and tooth brushing were ranked as top health priorities more often than sun protection. Less than one in five listed sun protection as a top priority. About half provided sunscreen, but 77 percent of those did not allow children to apply it themselves. Some used spray sunscreen, though many sprayed children’s faces incorrectly. Most reported no sunburns and followed heat-index guidelines. The study was limited to Illinois. Experts said teachers and parents need education about sun protection.

A Denver federal jury found radio host David Mueller assaulted and battered Taylor Swift during a 2013 preconcert photo session. Mueller had sued in 2015, saying Swift’s accusation was false and led to his firing by KYGO; Swift countersued. The jury awarded Swift the $1 she sought. It also decided Swift’s mother and manager had not interfered with Mueller’s contract. Swift said she would donate an unspecified amount to organizations helping sexual assault victims. The judge had dropped Swift from Mueller’s suit, finding insufficient evidence she made up the encounter. Closing arguments disputed credibility and an image; Mueller denied inappropriate contact but acknowledged spilling coffee on a computer containing a secret recording.

Angela B. Ryan recounts working as a pregnant lawyer for 27 months, during which judges, colleagues, and opposing counsel commented on or touched her belly without consent, including in court. She describes such touching as assault, notes that pregnancy discrimination law and EEOC guidance address unwelcome physical conduct, and argues that consent does not end with conception. She calls for explicit workplace and court policies, training, and education prohibiting touching pregnant people without consent.

The speaker says the team has not scored many goals but has played better, managed the puck better, put it in better spots, and tried to keep it away from Brodeur while getting it into the offensive zone. They expect a good game, see no home-road issue, feel confident after two wins, and call Thursday the most important game. They feel good about overtime and matchups, and say both teams are strong defensively and have shown they can come back.
