Pre-erase ACMD23 defines the number of write blocks to be pre-erased before a Multiple Block Write, can make the operation faster, resets to default 1 after the operation, and is recommended before CMD25; ACMD22 reports the number of well-written blocks after an error. Erase uses CMD32/CMD33 for start/end addresses and CMD38 for ERASE; out-of-sequence commands set ERASE_SEQ_ERROR or ERASE_RESET, write-protected sectors are left intact with WP_ERASE_SKIP, and post-erase data is '0' or '1' as defined by SCR DATA_STAT_AFTER_ERASE. DISCARD may deallocate blocks, treats discarded content as 'don't care', is for SDHC/SDXC only and not SPI, has 250 ms busy per command, and pending Discard is forgotten on power cycle. FULE logically erases the entire user area, uses CMD38 argument 00000002h, is SDHC/SDXC only and not SPI, and has 1 s busy per command. Write protection includes mechanical switch, internal write protection (blank), and password lock. Password and FEP registers are non-volatile; locked cards accept basic commands, ACMD41, CMD16, and lock commands. Lock/unlock uses transfer state and single-block write structure. COP prevents reuse without PWD; FEP disables Force Erase and Clear PWD, and COP Unlock is required after power-up if FEP is set. Force Erase erases all content including PWD, fails on unlocked card or if FEP=set; FEP Force Erase requires matching FEP and leaves FEP unchanged. ACMD6 is rejected when locked. CMD55 precedes ACMD; undefined ACMDs are handled as regular commands unless illegal. CMD6 switches functions via six groups, with mode 0 query and mode 1 set, returning 512-bit status on DAT lines and using access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit groups; default power limit is 0.72 W. High-Speed mode reaches 25 MB/s at 50 MHz via CMD6. CMD8 checks interface voltage in Idle before ACMD41. CCS distinguishes SDSC from SDHC/SDXC; high-capacity cards use block addressing and fixed 512-byte blocks. Bus clock can be lowered or stopped with specified clock cycles after transactions. CRC7 protects commands/responses/CSD/CID; CRC16 protects data. Read timeout is 100 ms; write busy is generally 250 ms with SDXC exceptions up to 500 ms; erase timeout is estimated by card parameters or block write delay. Commands are 48 bits, divided into classes, and responses include R1, R1b, R2, R3, and R6.

On Christmas Eve 2012, Chris Hadfield played Santa aboard the International Space Station, hiding family-written cards for five sleeping astronauts. He noted complications of marking holidays while orbiting Earth every 92 minutes and seeing 16 sunrises daily. His crew celebrated with fruitcake, ready-to-eat turkey, potatoes, vegetables, a velcroed artificial Christmas tree, and personalized stockings. The American and Russian crew chose holidays from their cultures. Hadfield treated holidays seriously because psychological health is fundamental to mission success. He now shares this cross-cultural perspective through a forthcoming science-based variety show. The authors say customs ground people, even in space.
A100 provides 1.5x L1/shared capacity per SM vs V100, 40 GB HBM2 at 1555 GB/s, a 40 MB L2 cache, L2 residency controls, and Compute Data Compression.

Polling began in 69 of Uttarakhand's 70 seats amid tight security; Karnaprayag was postponed to March 9 after a BSP candidate died. Over 74 lakh voters and 628 candidates are voting at 10,685 booths, 30,000 security and 60,000 officials.

In McGillivray v. Eramian, the plaintiff was injured when a splinter from the defendant’s bowling alley “sliding floor” entered his finger as he delivered a bowl with his hand close to the floor. Evidence showed the floor behind the foul line was uneven, wavy, old, dirty, and had missing slivers; the plaintiff did not touch the floor. The defendant moved for a directed verdict and requested instructions that the approach was for walking and sliding, not for hands, and that striking it with his hand was negligence. The court held denial of the directed verdict and refusal of the instructions were proper: the evidence warranted a finding of the proprietor’s negligence regarding the floor’s condition, and contributory negligence was a jury question. Judgment was to be entered for the plaintiff according to the verdict.

Samsung announced three cheaper, water- and dust-resistant Galaxy A smartphones—A3, A5 and A7—differentiated by screen size. They will launch in Russia later this month and expand afterward. Pricing was not announced. The unveiling follows the Galaxy Note 7 recall.

Only the Secretary of State may grant and issue U.S. passports. Eligible applicants in the United States must submit a written affidavit to the Secretary of State with required personal details, an oath of allegiance, a physical description, and a witness certificate; applicants abroad apply through diplomatic or consular officers, and applicants in insular possessions apply to the chief executive. Passports are forbidden to persons not owing allegiance to the United States and to persons who have only declared an intention to become citizens. Additional requirements apply to native citizens, foreign-born persons whose fathers were native citizens, naturalized citizens, women, children claiming citizenship through a parent’s naturalization, and insular-possession residents owing allegiance to the United States.

Camp Mystic parents whose children died in the July 4 Kerr County floods advocated for tighter summer camp safety regulations. Matthew and Wendie Childress, whose 18-year-old daughter Chloe was a counselor who died, joined other families in Austin on Sept. 4 before Gov. Greg Abbott was expected to sign the bills. The reforms would require overnight cabins to move out of floodplains, camps to use radios and alert systems for weather warnings, and staff to train on emergency plans including moving children to higher ground. The flood killed 25 Camp Mystic campers, two counselors and the camp director, with one camper missing. Parents, including Blake Bonner, whose 9-year-old daughter Lila died, worked with lobbyists, met officials and testified. Abbott signed the bills on Sept. 5. Parents said they honored their daughters but their grief remains because their daughters are not coming back.

The passage references system MMU details and L4 Fast/Slow Peripheral memory maps. It describes TILER extended addressing: an additional 4-GBytes via a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame buffer views, accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS; other masters can access one view through the 512-MB TILER region. It also lists package pin assignments and terminal functions, including boot configuration pins multiplexed with GPMC functions and BTMODE sampling at reset.

China launched a new visa program to attract young professionals and science and technology graduates from top universities for study and business, as the US imposed a $100,000 H-1B fee. The move provoked xenophobic backlash.

Social scientists seek predictive patterns in individual and collective behavior. Interpretivist critics argue researchers simplify human behavior and social interaction and face objectivity challenges. Computational social science uses large-scale behavioral data, reducing researcher presence and improving granularity and scale, but AI adoption faces limited high-quality datasets and high training/deployment costs. LLMs pre-trained on web-scale text may improve data access and automate analysis. Three methodological problems are identified: synthesizing research data via LLM role-playing, with concerns about accuracy, biases, stereotypes, personalization, and data quality/cost; using LLMs for tasks like stance detection, sentiment analysis, free-text coding, and in-context learning, with ethical challenges such as misinformation and needs for alignment, watermarking, and multidisciplinary societal engagement; and exploring novel social theories, where LLMs may propose hypotheses but face concerns about originality and validity, requiring human-AI collaboration.

Generative AI brings legal and ethical challenges, including misinformation, deepfakes, and bias/discrimination. Governments and companies have introduced laws, principles, and responsible AI policies. Challenges remain: gaps between industry and government, lack of international consensus, inconsistent regulations, and micro-level risks like jailbreaking. The passage calls for human-centered, safe, secure, and trustworthy AI; top-down partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers; forward-looking regulation; and top-down plus bottom-up governance involving developers, users, and communities, with transparent issue reporting and social computing to monitor regulatory needs.

The passage reports a cross-sectional analysis of COVID-PCD data from 747 people with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) across 49 countries. Most participants (92%) reported diagnostic testing; 49% of those aged ≥5 reported nasal nitric oxide measurement, 75% reported biopsy, and 58% reported genetic testing. Among biopsy reports, 58% cited high-speed video microscopy and 50% electron microscopy. Test use varied by country, with biopsy most common except in North America and France, where genetic testing dominated. Recall varied by test and country, and was poorest in Switzerland. One-third of participants aged ≥5 with diagnostic tests reported all three tests. More recent diagnosis was associated with more reported tests, while situs abnormalities were associated with fewer. The study notes limitations including self-reported data and possible selection bias. It concludes that PCD diagnostics differ markedly worldwide, many people have incomplete diagnostic work-up, and supplementary testing may be needed for diagnostic characterization and personalized medicine.

A federal judge rejected a challenge to the Biden-era gainful-employment rule and sided with the Education Department. The rule requires for-profit and nondegree programs to show graduates can afford loans and earn more than high school graduates; failing twice could end federal aid. Trump officials defended the rule in court, and a rulemaking process is expected later this year.

The Third Circuit reviewed Prava Chatterjee’s appeal from the denial of her petition to vacate a settlement and release of her deceased son’s admiralty claim arising from the 1975 S.S. EDGAR M. QUEENY collision. Chatterjee alleged that her son-in-law lacked authority, forged her signature on a special power of attorney, and that she received no settlement proceeds. The district court denied relief, excluded prior Calcutta Commission testimony, denied a new commission, and found the shipowners proved the release valid. The Third Circuit held Indian law governs the power of attorney and federal maritime law governs the release; Garrett’s scrutiny applies to relatives, with shipowners bearing the burden. It found no abuse in excluding the prior transcript, but the denial of a new commission and related rulings deprived Chatterjee of a fair trial. It vacated and remanded to invoke a commission in India under Rule 28(b).
Halliburton reported first-quarter net income of $46 million, or 5 cents per share; adjusted earnings of 41 cents met expectations, while revenue of $5.74 billion missed forecasts.

The National Travel and Tourism Office reported 19 percent fewer international students arrived in the U.S. in August than in August 2024. Experts say the figure aligns with enrollment predictions but does not fully represent declines; DHS/SEVIS data showed a 0.8 percent increase from September 2024 to September 2025, which NAFSA criticized as likely inaccurate. The arrivals drop follows visa interview freezes and social media reviews. Declines were especially stark for Africa (32 percent), Asia (24 percent), the Middle East (17 percent), and Iran, Syria, Haiti, Ghana, Nigeria, and India; Europe and Oceania stayed relatively flat. Over 33,000 fewer Indian students arrived. Experts expect total declines may exceed 19 or 20 percent and could be larger in 2026, affecting universities, college towns, and the economy. IIE’s mid-November Fall Snapshot may provide firmer data.

Canada has benefited from NAFTA, which supported economic growth and transformed manufacturing. As Canada pursues more FTAs, the passage says NAFTA renegotiations show Canada does not export enough outside North America and needs a stronger, globally competitive manufacturing sector. Signing new trade deals alone will not ensure prosperity; Canada has 14 FTAs, but exports to most of those markets have not expanded. The passage calls for a plan with five elements: improve domestic business competitiveness through tax and regulatory reform; ensure FTAs address tariffs and non-tariff barriers; focus on countries with natural business ties rather than political expedience; leverage existing integrated supply chains; and support small and medium enterprises’ global growth. It argues Canada needs comprehensive structural changes and should not wait for renegotiation outcomes.

A Delhi court deferred to July 6 the hearing on the ED chargesheet against Karti Chidambaram and two companies in the Aircel-Maxis money laundering case. The ED chargesheeted them under the PMLA on June 13. The CBI and ED are investigating Karti’s alleged role in FIPB clearance for the 2006 deal; the chargesheet made claims about FDI and payments. Karti is also an accused in the INX Media case.

The speaker apologizes for sitting because of steel on his legs and a fourteen-thousand-mile trip. He reports on the Crimea Conference/Yalta and asks Congress and the American people to support its conclusions. The conference sought to defeat Germany quickly with minimal Allied losses and to build an international foundation for postwar order and peace. Agreements included occupation and control of Germany, destruction of German militarism, punishment of Nazi war criminals, disarmament, reparations in kind, and coordinated control by Britain, Russia, France, and the United States in separate zones under a Berlin Control Council. It also addressed Security Council voting, liberated areas, Yugoslavia, and Poland, including a reorganized provisional government and free elections. A United Nations conference was set for San Francisco on April 25, 1945. The speaker says the Pacific war continues and Japan’s unconditional surrender is essential. He met leaders in Egypt, Ethiopia, and Saudi Arabia and urges world collaboration to prevent another war.

A player probably won't play; the speaker won't disclose his status for tomorrow and doesn't know if he will play. He cites no fatigue factor, an inconclusive replay, no huge location impact, possible home distractions affecting top players early, and two overtime games.

Pokémon GO’s fire- and ice-themed Solstice Event has been live for over a day, with spawn changes and reward tweaks before the anniversary. For a week, catching Pokémon and nice, great, excellent, curveball, and first throws give 3x XP; with a discounted Lucky Egg, catch-related actions give 6x XP. Evolving gets no special bonus XP, reducing the incentive to grind Pokédex XP. The bonuses may help casual and midcore players level before planned gym updates.

Theresa May has been warned that failing to deliver Brexit would be “catastrophic” for the Conservatives ahead of a Chequers meeting of ministers. Conservative MP Andrea Jenkyns said a “half in and half out” Brexit would damage trust, after Jacob Rees-Mogg warned Leave-supporting Tories could revolt if May failed to stand firm. May has promised to leave the single market and customs union, but MPs fear she may compromise on “soft Brexit.” Remain-supporting MPs argue a pragmatic course is needed. Michael Gove said he is sure May will not smudge her red lines and downplayed suggestions pro-Brexit ministers could resign.

The passage states that the U.S. stock market has nearly quadrupled from post-crisis lows to recent all-time highs, but market conditions have been changing and may be entering a more challenging climate. It notes the S&P 500 had gone more than 60 trading days without a new all-time high since January 26, the longest such streak since 2015–2016. It says the Federal Reserve has raised rates once in 2018, is expected to raise more, and is shrinking its balance sheet, so it is no longer supporting stock investors as in past volatility episodes; other global central banks are increasingly disconnected. Corporate earnings growth is projected to rise due to tax cuts, but much may go to buybacks and dividends. Volatility has increased: after low 2017, the VIX spiked in February and remained elevated, and 2018 has had far more 1% and 2% moves than 2017, ranking among volatile years since WWII. The passage compares low-volatility periods to 1944 and 1963–64 and current volatility to 2006–07, suggesting a possible bull market top. It concludes markets are distorted by policy, price discovery may reassert itself, volatility may continue or increase through 2018 and into 2019, and investors should look for dangers the mainstream market is not yet seeing.

The passage describes the Bogleheads 3 Fund Portfolio as a low-cost strategy using U.S. Total Stock Market, International Stock Market, and U.S. Total Bond Market index funds, while the Bogleheads 4 Fund Portfolio adds a Total International Bond Market Index Fund. It states both aim for diversification, low costs, and long-term growth. The article allocates the 3-fund portfolio as 50% U.S. stocks, 30% international stocks, and 20% U.S. bonds, with a backtest annual return of 7.6% and max drawdown of 28%. It allocates the 4-fund portfolio as 50% U.S. stocks, 30% international stocks, 10% U.S. bonds, and 10% international bonds, with a backtest annual return of 7.8% and max drawdown of 31%. Market conditions can affect stock and bond components, including interest-rate effects on bonds.

Cabinet approved hosting the CWWA’s 26th Annual Conference and Exhibition from October 16–20 at the Guyana Marriott Hotel, themed “Promoting Innovation and Creativity in Water, Wastewater and Waste.” It will include technical papers, water-governance documents for the 2018 World Water Forum, and a review of a regional waste management action plan.

The speaker announces a nationwide mobilization to provide relief for unemployed citizens and families during the coming winter. A national organization under Walter Gifford will cooperate with governors, state and local agencies, business, labor, welfare, churches, and fraternal and patriotic societies. Over a thousand towns and cities have relief committees or community chests; the movement seeks funds for work, direct relief, and health and character building. The Federal Government is expanding public works, providing livelihoods for nearly 700,000 families, stopping immigration, adopting credit measures, and encouraging employers to spread work; states, counties, and municipalities are also acting. Voluntary action is still needed. Similar efforts under Colonel Woods succeeded last winter, but needs are greater now. The speaker appeals for community-by-community giving and designates November 26 as a Thanksgiving occasion to demonstrate relief for those in distress.

LG introduced the LG V35 ThinQ, a premium smartphone succeeding the V30S ThinQ. It features a Snapdragon 845, 6GB RAM, 6-inch 2880x1440 OLED display, no notch, headphone jack, dual 16MP rear cameras, 8MP front camera, AI camera features, Google Lens, far-field voice recognition, 3,300mAh battery, 64/128GB storage, microSD, face/fingerprint recognition, and Quick Charge 3.0. It joins the G7 ThinQ; the V-series secondary display is eliminated. Pricing and release date are unannounced.

Drug repurposing identifies new therapeutic uses for existing drugs and can reduce the time and cost of drug development; it accounts for about one-third of drug approvals and nearly 25% of pharmaceutical sector revenue. It is especially relevant for rare diseases, which have limited treatments and small patient populations. Knowledge graphs represent biomedical entities and relationships and, with machine learning, are used to predict new drug-disease connections. The Elsevier Biology Knowledge Graph (EBKG) extracts relationships from open access (OA) and controlled access (CA) literature and databases. For drug repurposing, EBKG includes rare disease relations and drug-target relations. Analysis found OA and CA contributions roughly equal at the knowledge graph relation level, while Elsevier NLP asserted 1.5 times more statements in CA than OA. OA contribution grew after 2006, and more than 50% of relations needed for rare disease drug repurposing are now in OA. Rare diseases with more than 100 relations tend to have more than 50% OA relations, but drug-target relations showed no such bias. Most relations are supported by a single reference; 40% of single-reference relations are OA, and essentially all relations with four or more references are OA. CA-only facts increase yearly but slower than OA. No difference was found in citation rate or average time to first citation between OA and CA. Single-reference relations accumulate exponentially in both OA and CA, mostly from original research articles not followed up; 85% of uncited relations came from peer-reviewed literature. Among retracted articles, 31.7% were OA, and the passage reports a higher retraction rate in CA journals. The conclusion states that additional confidence scores are necessary for knowledge graph relations.

The lecture previews an upcoming closed-book quiz with one page of notes, a calculator, and provided statistics tables. It reviews control charting as a running hypothesis test: alpha sets control limits and false alarm rate; beta is missed-alarm probability; increasing sample size tightens distributions and lowers beta while maintaining alpha; average run length is defined for false alarms and shift detection. It distinguishes control limits from specification limits and introduces CP, CPK, tolerances, and quality loss functions to relate process mean and variance to requirements. It advises investigating alarms by checking measurement, historical data, trends, operators, and equipment, and notes rules like WECO. It discusses alternative charts for detecting small shifts, including moving average, EWMA, and CUSUM, and issues with n=1, autocorrelation, multiple process steps or parameters, and aggregate false alarm rates.

Managed by Q, founded by Dan Teran and Saman Rahmanian, launched in April 2014 in New York as an on-demand office cleaning and maintenance company. It offered cleaning, maintenance, and office and cleaning supplies through a customized iPad dashboard and operator app. After initially subcontracting cleaners, Q switched to hiring employees, paying and training them above industry standards and offering stable schedules, benefits, and promotion opportunities. By July 2015, Q had raised $15 million in a Series A round, expanded to Chicago and San Francisco, and reported high customer satisfaction. About 70% of a typical customer’s monthly spending came from cleaning, with the rest from maintenance and supplies. CEO Teran considered whether to grow by entering new markets or by acquiring more customers in existing markets and offering more services.

President Donald Trump will deliver his first State of the Union address Tuesday night as lawmakers use the speech to make points. Female Democratic lawmakers plan to wear black to support the #MeToo movement, and some invited guests tied to sexual harassment issues. Democratic lawmakers invited young DACA recipients to highlight immigration, while Republican Rep. Kevin Cramer invited a border-wall contractor. At least eight Democratic lawmakers are boycotting. Bill Nye is attending as a guest of Republican Rep. Jim Bridenstine, Trump’s NASA nominee. Rep. Joe Kennedy will deliver the Democratic response.

Iraq began an aerial bombardment of Islamic State-controlled Tal Afar, west of Mosul, an Iraqi Defence Ministry spokesman said. The ground attack should start after the air campaign; Iraqi authorities said Tal Afar would be the next target.

Sarahah is a popular anonymous-messaging app, already a hit in Egypt and Saudi Arabia. Users create profiles anyone can visit and leave anonymous messages; logged-in users may tag their identity. Messages appear in an inbox where users can flag, delete, reply to, or favorite them. It is polarizing, with near 50-50 Google Play ratings. Creators say it aids self-development through constructive anonymous feedback, but anonymity can enable hurtful behavior, and reviews warn of hateful comments. Privacy features allow removing profiles from search, limiting audiences, disabling unauthorized users, and blocking senders. It is barebones and focuses on messaging rather than social media. Fully anonymous comments and inability to respond to messages make bullying possible. It is trendy, but too soon to know if it will last; free on Android and iOS.

The passage is a chronological list of telegram entries and reference numbers dated from January 8, 1942, to September 3, 1942, sent from or received in Washington, Helsinki, Kuibyshev (Moscow), Stockholm, London, and Ankara, with dates, times, and receipt times.

The PGA848 is a monolithic, high-voltage, high-bandwidth, precision programmable gain instrumentation amplifier with a single-ended output, combining a high-speed current-feedback input stage, an internally matched gain resistor network, and a four-resistor differential amplifier output stage. It has eight binary gain settings from 0.5V/V to 100V/V selected by A0, A1, and A2. Applications include factory automation and control, analog input modules, data acquisition, test and measurement, and semiconductor test. Its linear operating input range extends within 3V (maximum) of either power supply. A typical application drives a 16-bit, 1MSPS SAR ADC, the ADS8860, using ±15V input-stage supplies and a 5.3V output-stage supply, a REF6250 5V reference, an OPA192 REF buffer, and three filters. Nominal f–3dB bandwidth is 318kHz, changing to 277kHz at high feedback resistor tolerance, with –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz. Power supply recommendations specify ±15V input and output supplies, with output-stage supplies clamped within input-stage levels; voltages above 40V (±20V) permanently damage the device. Layout guidelines address symmetry, bypass capacitors, trace separation, leakage, parasitic capacitance, thermal junctions, and thermal sources. The document also lists simulation software, related documentation, update notifications, support resources, trademarks, ESD caution, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

This study analyzes tungsten oxidation at 400–1050°C and WO3 sublimation in synthetic air, motivated by fusion reactor maintenance, accident, waste-handling, and detritiation scenarios. Pure W and W oxide powders were characterized using STA/TGA/DSC, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, SEM, and EBSD. Oxidation shows a transition from parabolic to linear kinetics, with activation energies of 180.4 ± 3.8 kJ/mol and 117.5 ± 3.3 kJ/mol, respectively. Preferential oxidation occurs at specimen edges, and oxidation rate increases with perimeter-to-area ratio; edge effects are negligible in the parabolic regime but significant in the linear regime. Oxide scale spalling and brittleness were observed. WO3 sublimation rate increases with temperature, with an activation energy of 335.8 ± 17 kJ/mol. The oxide scale consists of an inner WO2 layer (~30–50 nm), a middle WO2.72 layer (10–20 µm), and an outer WO2.9/WO3 layer. Above 600°C, voids, cracks, and spalling occur. The WO2 layer is suggested as a possible explanation for low detritiation efficiency in JET W tiles.

A Washington, Missouri, detective inhaled heroin mixed with fentanyl while aiding an overdose victim; both were hospitalized and are okay. Police say the combination is increasingly dangerous to first responders.

In a Barrie court, parents Liz Hoage and Bill Tanner learned Joseph Nicholson, convicted in the 2007 Father’s Day stabbing death of their 16-year-old son Joey Tanner and the attempted murder of Jeremy Rodgers, will become eligible for parole earlier. The Ontario Court of Appeal overturned the first-degree murder verdict and ordered sentencing for second-degree murder, citing inadequate jury instructions. Second-degree murder carries life with parole ineligibility of 10 to 25 years. The Crown seeks 16 years. Nicholson apologized, and Justice Guy Di Tomaso will sentence him Aug. 11.

Katie Albert, a Waterloo resident and Southern Illinois University Edwardsville student, describes the second half of her study-abroad semester in Florence. She discusses her Italian, painting, and drawing classes; university cultural activities such as a cooking class; and school trips to Siena, Pisa, and Lucca. During a 10-day spring break she visited seven countries, including a meaningful trip to Becherbach, Germany, where her fourth-great-grandfather was born. After returning to Florence, she noticed tourist season had begun and later traveled to Split, Croatia, for rafting, cliff diving, and beach time. She reached 20 countries by age 20 and, with three weeks left, describes her departure as bittersweet.

Australia’s Turnbull Government is combining existing childcare subsidies into a single means- and activity-tested payment from July 2. About 1.2 million families are eligible for childcare subsidies, but 489,000 may miss out unless they update Centrelink details through myGov. Required information includes estimated 2018/19 income and work hours for both parents. Both parents must work, study, volunteer or search for work at least eight hours a fortnight. Households earning under $186,958 will no longer face an annual rebate cap; higher earners’ cap rises from $7,500 to just over $10,000 per child. Education Minister Simon Birmingham said the switch is not automatic. Labor says one in four families will be worse off and most missing out are in the lowest two income brackets.

Jeffing, created in the 1970s by Olympian Jeff Galloway, is a run-walk-run fitness method that alternates running with planned walking breaks. It aims to make exercise easier and more manageable, and it can fit into a busy lifestyle. Benefits include improved aerobic endurance with reduced fatigue, built-in muscle recovery, less intimidation, better pacing, and reduced injury risk when implemented properly. Beginners can start with 1–2 minutes running and walking, then adjust gradually. Experienced runners can use it on long runs or recovery weeks. It may especially help long-distance runners prevent injuries, but may be less suitable for athletes needing sustained high-intensity effort. Poor progression or mechanics can still cause injury.

The passage is a survey on resonance and Lie algebras of matroids and arrangements. It introduces matroids, their lattices of flats, multinets, reduced multinets, nets, Latin squares, and realizations by 3-nets. It defines the Orlik–Solomon algebra, holonomy Lie algebra, holonomy Chen Lie algebra, resonance varieties, and Koszul modules, discussing their connections to matroid dependencies, Chen ranks, and hyperplane arrangements. It addresses realizable versus non-realizable matroids and open questions, including torsion, linearity of higher-degree resonance varieties, and the Chen ranks conjecture. The survey is organized into sections on matroids and multinets, algebras associated to matroids, resonance varieties, and hyperplane arrangements.

The last trading day of the month is described as a weak day and negative seasonality, distinct from the last calendar day. In SPY from 1993, investing from the close of the second-last trading day to the close of the last trading day produced an average loss of 0.06% per trade and negative 0.8% CAGR. Exiting at the open gave a 0.04% average gain, while open-to-close on the last trading day averaged -0.11% with a 42% win ratio. The passage states there is no end-of-month effect on the last trading day; it performs worse than an average day. Profit-taking is speculated as an obvious reason, and a strategy has been made.

Sharon Haliwell, 48, wife of a Wigan millionaire businessman, died by suicide last April; a coroner cited sleeping-pill addiction and abuse by her husband. The coroner raised concerns about poor communication between North West Boroughs NHS Foundation Trust teams. Its chief executive described training, information-system flagging and amended procedures by March 2018. Inquest evidence said two assessments showed suicide risk, but a referral error occurred; a prevention of death notice was issued, with communication concerns remaining. Addaction’s involvement ended when she denied pill abuse.

The speaker says the Stanley Cup final is a race to four where fatigue is overcome by adrenaline. Though the team has not won a game, it has rebounded strongly. Experienced players and line chemistry help, and Joe is playing well despite not scoring, with his line creating offensive-zone matchups.

Anna Ryder Richardson is leaving Manor House Wildlife Park in Pembrokeshire for France and divorcing Colin MacDougall, father of her daughters Bibi and Dixie. She says the stresses and expense of running the wildlife park destroyed their 16-year relationship. They bought the rundown zoo for £1 million in 2008, spent seven months renovating it and a further £1 million, and lived in a cabin while the animals had warmer homes. The family appeared in Channel 4’s Chaos At The Zoo and Anna’s Welsh Zoo, which she says made their lives public and contributed to marital problems. In August 2010 a tree fell and seriously injured a three-year-old visitor and his mother; the couple faced more than £100,000 in fines and costs, and the case against Anna was thrown out after Colin took the blame and pleaded guilty. They later realised their marriage was over, though they remain friends. Anna has bought a ruin near Bordeaux, is learning French, and plans to live there with her daughters; Colin will continue to manage the zoo. She is returning to television to co-present 60 Minute Makeover with Peter Andre.

The American Heart Association's Go Red For Women campaign encourages women to take heart health seriously. Tiffany Gholston, born with a heart murmur, received her first pacemaker at 20; she now stays active, eats well, meditates, and supports the AHA's Circle of Red and research fundraising.

Hackers released more unaired HBO episodes, without anything on “Game of Thrones,” including “Curb Your Enthusiasm,” “Insecure,” “Ballers” and “The Deuce.” HBO said it would not communicate with or comment on the hacker’s leaks. The hack came as Time Warner awaited approval to sell to AT&T.

The all-girls camp where 27 children and counselors died in July’s devastating floods in west Texas plans to reopen next summer. The passage otherwise consists of numerous headlines and requests to support and donate to The 74.

The passage promotes several credit card offers and includes advertising disclosures. It highlights the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card with unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 bonus after spending $500 in the first 3 months, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, a $0 annual fee, and cell phone protection. It also describes the Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card with 1.5% cash back, 5% on Capital One Travel, up to $300 in welcome bonuses, 0% intro APR for 15 months, and no annual fee. Another offer provides 2% cash back, a $200 cash back bonus after $1,500 spent in 6 months, and 0% intro APR on balance transfers for 18 months. Research from Albert Einstein College of Medicine, published in PLOS Biology, reports that intense exercise curbs appetite via proopiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons in the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus (ARC). In mice, capsaicin and heat activated ARC POMC neurons, about two-thirds of which had TRPV1-like receptors; capsaicin infusion reduced food intake, while blocking or silencing these receptors prevented appetite suppression. Treadmill exercise raised body and ARC temperatures and reduced food intake by about 50%, but not in mice whose ARC POMC neurons lacked TRPV1 receptors. The study suggests body temperature can act as a biological signal regulating feeding behavior and may lead to appetite or weight-loss approaches.

The Texas Supreme Court denied Anna Black’s application for writ of error against the Texas Department of Labor and Standards. It stated that denial did not approve the court of appeals’ witness-document distinction or relieve a party of the duty to show good cause under Rule 215.5.

Researchers propose using a global network of citizen scientists with mobile phones and low-cost radio receivers to detect fast radio bursts (FRBs). Phones would monitor candidate signals, upload data to a central site for correlation, and use GPS-based arrival times and dispersion measures to locate a Galactic FRB. FRBs are brief radio signals from unknown deep-space sources; most were identified after the event, though FRB 121102 has repeated. Researchers estimate a Milky Way FRB might occur every 30 to 1,500 years, or weekly if repeating.

McLaren says its pre-season reliability issues have been sorted as it heads to the F1 season opener confident of a step forward. After problems in Barcelona, Eric Boullier says the issues were addressed at the factory, while Fernando Alonso says the Renault-powered MCL33 showed promise; Boullier says the tight midfield makes McLaren's position hard to judge.

Disclosed are systems and methods for adapting and/or updating radiotherapy treatment plans and/or radiation delivery during a treatment session based on biological and/or physiological data and/or anatomical data extracted from real-time imaging data, and methods for evaluating treatment plans based on such imaging data. Systems may include an imaging system, a radiation treatment system, a controller, and a communication interface. Methods may include measuring biological activity data such as PET tracer uptake or kinetics, comparing measured data with initial or pre-determined ranges, calculating plan quality index values or dose-volume histograms, and updating treatment plans if values are outside ranges. Updates may change dosimetric objectives, target geometry, fractionation, number or duration of treatment sessions, or dose distribution. Methods also include generating acceptable PQI or biological activity ranges and bounded DVHs, and displaying notifications such as PASS/GO or FAIL/NO GO.

The speaker says he waited eight years for this moment, through difficult times and many hockey games and minutes. He praises his teammates, Larry Murphy, and dressing-room leaders, saying everyone did a good job. He came into the league eight years ago, had to start over, faced ups and downs, and says not many believed he could win the cup. He thanks Scotty for the chance, his teammates, family, and his daughter Dasha. He feels good, healthy, and motivated, though possibly slower, and may play another series. He discusses bringing the Stanley Cup to Moscow and asking Commissioner Gary Bettman, saying it could help Russian hockey and attract investors.

Early forecasts make viewing the partial solar eclipse in Philadelphia uncertain. A meteorologist cites unsettled southern weather that may move north; Friday forecasts should be more reliable. Philadelphia is not in totality; South Carolina is nearest. The last U.S. total eclipse was 1979.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated October 26, 2017, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2017, furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod.

Huddersfield Giants aim to build on early-season momentum after a 12-0 pre-season win at Warrington and a 28-16 Super League opening win at Widnes. Coach Rick Stone wants more from his players ahead of their opening home 2017 clash with Salford Red Devils.

Reports from participating governments include English versions from the United States, Britain, the USSR, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. This compilation bridges the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals and the UN Charter, concentrating on the United States’ role in establishing the UN legal framework. It presents the American Delegation’s position on issues, discussions, and decisions at informal and formal levels, emphasizing how agreements were reached among major Powers. It traces US policy preparation to May 1945 and Conference work through the Charter’s signing, using delegation, Big Four, Big Five, and other records, with selected unpublished and published documentation.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting that on March 22, 2016, it entered an accelerated share repurchase agreement with Barclays Bank PLC. NVIDIA will pay $500 million and receive 12,108,715 shares, as part of its previously announced intention to return $1 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Settlement may involve additional shares or cash based on the daily volume-weighted average price of NVIDIA common stock.

The speaker says the team’s philosophy is to shorten shifts in the third period so players do not come to the bench tired and can perform on the next shift. The team is weighing lineup options involving Hrkac, Plante, Hogue, Sydor, and Keane, with Sydor possibly providing a bigger physical impact. The speaker is doubtful about an injured player’s readiness, citing soreness and the risk of further damage, and says the team is preparing as if Brett Hull will not play and is also without Marshall. He says the team does not disclose exact injury locations to protect the player and team, but tries to be upfront about whether someone will play. Keane and Carbonneau have played many minutes; Keane chose to skate tomorrow rather than today. On Hull, the speaker describes a compromise: Hull can do what he wants with the puck, but without it he must play the team’s physical, aggressive style. He says Nieuwendyk is calm in intense situations and able to exploit goaltender weaknesses, and notes Hogue may return after progressing in a short timeframe. He also says the team discussed not making enough physical and mental sacrifices in the previous Colorado overtime loss and wants a stronger performance. The team wants to keep creative players like Hull and Modano from losing creativity, but requires team play when possession is not controlled, and wants to prevent Peca from controlling the game and keep him away from its net.

Intel is in early talks with AMD to manufacture chips for it in its foundry business, according to Semafor. Intel shares rose 7% and AMD shares over 1%. Such a move would be a significant win for Intel’s foundry, which is seeking big customers, and would signal AMD’s confidence in manufacturing with its biggest competitor. It is unclear how much manufacturing AMD would do with Intel. Intel declined to comment; AMD said it does not comment on rumor or speculation.

An email from Ann Schmidt dated May 18, 2001, lists Enron Mentions news articles. An options report says investors were selling options as a flat market loomed. Other articles report that Saudi Arabia selected international oil companies for three major natural gas projects requiring about $25 billion in investment. Exxon Mobil and Royal Dutch/Shell were major winners. Exxon Mobil was awarded leadership of Core Venture 2, the Red Sea project, with Occidental and Enron receiving stakes. Core Venture 1, the South Ghawar project, was awarded to ExxonMobil, Shell, BP, and Phillips, with no leader announced. Core Venture 3, Shaybah, was awarded to Shell, TotalFinaElf, and Conoco, also with no leader announced. Leaders for Core Ventures 1 and 3 were to be announced by June 5, and memoranda of understanding were expected by then. The U.S. Energy Department welcomed the awards to American firms, and Shell said it was pleased to participate.

The included articles report that Boeing, Caterpillar, Enron, Halliburton, and others are lobbying to protect the Export-Import Bank from proposed budget cuts, which the White House labels corporate welfare; they also cover Houston office projects, Dutch gas competition, California power deals and lawsuits, Sierra Pacific’s doubts about SEC approval of its purchase of Enron’s Portland General Electric, and falling U.S. natural gas prices.

The Stack Offense compacts players into two stack alignments just outside the free throw line, letting three ballhandlers maneuver sideline to sideline while two post players act as stationary screeners unless help is needed. It includes continuity options such as penetrate and pop, basket rolls when defenders overplay, dribble penetration if the basket is unprotected, and back cuts when passing lanes are denied. After back cuts, O2 and O4 reset their stack alignment, and O1 may dribble penetrate to either wing.

This study examined accessibility of electronically prescribed nameless expedited partner therapy (EPT) at retail pharmacies in New York City using a secret shopper methodology, and whether acceptance varied by neighborhood socioeconomic vulnerability measured by the Social Vulnerability Index. Among 335 pharmacies surveyed, 40% of pharmacists were aware of EPT. Awareness was associated with willingness to dispense nameless EPT (48% vs. 18%; p<0.001), but socioeconomic vulnerability was not associated with willingness. Pharmacist approaches varied: 28% used the term “Expedited Partner,” 34% used double prescriptions or refills under the index patient’s name, 6% required the partner’s name, and 31% were unwilling to fill or terminated the call. Common refusal reasons were unfamiliarity with EPT (62%) and belief that a patient name was legally required (28%). Of fillable prescriptions, 46% adhered to New York State EPT guidelines, and insurance was usable in 86%. Chlamydia rates and borough were not significantly associated with awareness or willingness. Logistic regression found national chain pharmacies were more likely to report EPT awareness than non-chain pharmacies, and higher SVI economic quartiles were positively associated with awareness, but no significant associations were found for willingness to fill. The authors conclude that barriers include limited awareness, low willingness to dispense nameless prescriptions, and poor guideline adherence, requiring targeted education, policy interventions, and electronic prescribing improvements.

First Lady Melania Trump said at the UN General Assembly last month that combating bullying among children was a top priority. After a video of Horace Maynard Middle School sixth-grader Keaton Jones describing being bullied went viral, Principal Greg Clay said the incident had been resolved and action was taken with other children; he said he was unaware of repeated bullying. The video, posted by Kimberly Jones, showed Jones saying milk was poured on him and ham put down his clothes. The school planned an assembly on bullying and a January anti-bullying talk. Other parents said bullying occurs from time to time but is not more of an issue in Union County than elsewhere.

Embodiments relate to AI, ML, and Neural Architecture Search for hardware-aware model searching. ML models depend on parameters and hyperparameters, while conventional ML design and NAS can be time-consuming and resource-intensive and may not be optimized for different hardware platforms. The disclosure provides an ML architecture search framework and an ML model scaling (MLMS) system that selects and interchanges ML models/subnets in an energy- and communication-efficient way while adapting to real-time system and hardware constraints. The MLMS system includes an MLMS engine, MLMS interface, subnet selector, and performance auditor, and it monitors performance metrics and context information such as operation mode, system state, physical environment, and networking environment. When changes trigger a search, the subnet selector searches a supernet/subnet pool using NAS or other search algorithms and chooses a replacement subnet with maximum overlap in pre-trained parameters to minimize memory write and data-transfer overhead. It evaluates candidate subnets using performance margins and constraints and selects the one with minimal transfer cost. The system is agnostic to the search and weight-sharing approach and supports AI/ML applications across edge, IoT, and other resource-constrained platforms. The passage also describes performance metrics and example hardware and software configurations.

The passage examines globalization and its relationship to education, especially English curricula. It cites scholars and organizations on globalization, policy change, power transitions, textbooks, university global education, and global issues as teaching materials. It argues that English is a tool for international communication and suggests that English curricula include global issues such as HIV/AIDS, global warming, and war. It describes an 18-week study at three Taiwanese universities with 372 non-English majors; participants discussed global topics in groups or pairs and through Facebook, used online materials and films, and completed surveys. Results report high agreement on the importance of globalization education (95%), interesting globalization topics (87%), inclusion in formal curricula (79%), online discussions or YouTube investigations (89%), and stimulation of English learning motivation (96%); 57% reported increased confidence to participate in global events. Students identified global warming, global energy, and environmental protection as important topics. Pedagogical suggestions included travel, disaster films, historical and current events, music, international speakers, English-language news, exchange students, and debates. The passage concludes that globalization education can help students become global citizens and that English teachers should incorporate global issues into EFL curricula.

Skinimalism is a streamlined skincare routine focused on essentials, using a few high-quality, well-chosen, targeted, multitasking products instead of layering many steps. Dr Hazel Parkinson says it protects the skin barrier, reduces irritation and sensitivity, and may improve wellbeing by reducing overwhelm. It can also mean less waste, packaging, and cost. Most people can benefit from a balanced, barrier-friendly routine, but skinimalism is not necessarily for everyone. People with acne, pigmentation, rosacea, sensitive skin, or menopause may still need specific ingredients or richer moisturisers, but Parkinson advises treating concerns intelligently with fewer products and gradual introduction. For healthy skin, a basic routine plus an optional retinoid or exfoliant used 1–2 times weekly may be enough, adjusted for age, lifestyle, and skin needs. When transitioning, remove one or two products at a time and allow 2–4 weeks for skin to adapt.

This case study examined smartphone touchscreen interactions in a man in his late twenties with refractory right temporal lobe epilepsy during anti-seizure medication changes and seizures. Over six months, 718,357 touchscreen interactions were recorded using the TapCounter app, alongside a seizure diary. During a five-day epilepsy monitoring unit admission, anti-seizure medication was reduced and withdrawn, and video-EEG documented seizures, including one focal to bilateral tonic-clonic convulsion. Cluster-based permutation tests showed significant differences in interaction probability distributions with medication load: fast next-interval dynamics increased after tapering and reversed after medication restart. On the convulsion day, slow next-interval dynamics increased compared with the three preceding days. The study suggests smartphones may help track medication- and seizure-related behavioural changes, but cohort studies are needed to establish generalisability.

Market Basket, a New England supermarket chain, was controlled by the Demoulas family. In June 2014, Arthur T. Demoulas was fired as CEO by a board controlled by his cousin Arthur S. Demoulas. Employees, vendors, and customers protested for six weeks, demanding his reinstatement; headquarters, warehouse, and trucking employees walked out, store employees picketed and encouraged boycotts, sales fell, and competitors and local businesses were affected. On August 27, 2014, the board and shareholders agreed for Arthur T. and his family to purchase 50.5% of the company for $1.6 billion, and Arthur T. was reinstated with full operational authority along with his management team. The deal involved debt, and employees later received $49 million in bonuses. The passage also describes Market Basket’s low-price, high-volume business model; its employee practices, including profit-sharing, promotions from within, and low turnover; its customer service and supplier relations; and the family litigation and governance disputes preceding the firing.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2018. For the three months then ended, revenue was $29,084 million, gross margin $19,179 million, operating income $9,955 million, net income $8,824 million, basic earnings per share $1.15, and diluted earnings per share $1.14. Revenue increased 19%, operating income 29%, and net income 34% compared with the prior-year period. Segment revenue was $9,771 million for Productivity and Business Processes, $8,567 million for Intelligent Cloud, and $10,746 million for More Personal Computing; segment operating income was $3,881 million, $2,931 million, and $3,143 million, respectively. Commercial cloud revenue increased 47% to $8.5 billion. The effective tax rate was 14%. A definitive agreement to acquire GitHub, Inc. for $7.5 billion in a stock transaction was expected to close by the end of October 2018. The filing also includes financial statements, notes, MD&A, market risk disclosures, controls and procedures, legal proceedings, risk factors, and exhibits.

The passage states that the 2022 NFL draft had a record six wide receivers taken in the first 20 picks, as offenses shift toward passing. It describes wide receivers as key to the passing game alongside offensive line and quarterback play, using route-running, availability, catching, and 1-on-1 matchups. Their secondary responsibility is run blocking. The name comes from splitting wide and receiving passes; other names include WR, wideout, split-end, and flanker. Skills include route-running, run-blocking, body control, speed, strong hands, coordination, and agility, with a general body type of 5’10–6’4 and 180–220 pounds. It names Jerry Rice, Randy Moss, and Steve Largent as among the best ever. It says elite receivers disrupt defenses and force alignment decisions for offensive coordinators.

Perovskite solar cells have progressed from 3.9% efficiency in 2009 to PCE exceeding 27%. The microscopic morphology of perovskite thin films, including crystallinity, grain size, boundaries, defects, and residual lead iodide, affects charge transport, recombination, performance, and stability. SEM is used for high-resolution morphological analysis, but manual interpretation is labor-intensive, subjective, and unsuitable for high-throughput analysis. Traditional machine learning and DL segmentation methods have limitations involving blurry boundaries, low contrast, scalability, manual parameter adjustment, computational inefficiency, and dependence on large annotated datasets. The authors propose PerovSegNet, a lightweight high-precision segmentation framework tailored for SEM images of perovskite and lead iodide. Built on YOLOv8-seg, it incorporates ASDCB for multi-scale feature fusion and channel recalibration, and SAD for capturing fine-scale textures and large-scale structures. They construct PerovData, comprising 10,994 annotated SEM images expanded from 40 manually labeled samples via augmentation; UMAP analysis shows separability of perovskite, lead iodide, and defects. Training used PyTorch, CUDA, and an NVIDIA A100. Experiments compare PerovSegNet with Mask R-CNN, Cascade Mask R-CNN, and Cascade InternImage-XL. PerovSegNet achieved improved segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency; ablation shows SAD and ASDCB improve mAP@0.5, with the combined model reaching the highest mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 while reducing parameters and GFLOPs versus baseline. Qualitative evaluation shows cleaner boundaries and fewer missed lead iodide clusters and defects. PerovSegNet also provides quantitative descriptors such as area and count of perovskite, lead iodide, and defects. Correlation analysis over approximately 25 papers reports perovskite area positively correlated with PCE, lead iodide area mildly positively correlated, and defect area/count negatively correlated. The authors note limitations: correlations are observational, segmentation errors and class imbalance can affect metrics, imaging conditions impact outputs, and larger datasets, uncertainty quantification, cross-magnification validation, and further acceleration are needed. The conclusion states PerovSegNet establishes a foundation for data-informed process optimization and potential high-throughput screening and real-time quality control in perovskite manufacturing.

A University of Connecticut study found that vaping nicotine-based e-cigarette liquid caused DNA damage approximately equivalent to smoking unfiltered tobacco cigarettes, using a 3D-printed screening device. DNA damage increased with more puffs and depended on inhaled vapor and additives. Cellular mutations from DNA damage can lead to cancer. Researchers are planning further study.

The article explains backtesting a momentum strategy in Python: downloading sector SPDR ETF adjusted close data with yfinance, resampling monthly, calculating 9-month momentum, and buying the top 3 ETFs monthly in an equally weighted portfolio. It compares returns with SPY, reporting a 9.89% CAGR versus SPY’s 9.46%, concluding performance was nearly identical with not much alpha.

The passage describes the Evening Star as a bearish three-candle reversal pattern: a tall bullish candle, a small candle gapping above it, and a bearish candle closing below the first candle’s midpoint. It outlines a trading strategy for identifying potential bearish reversals, confirming with technical tools, managing exits and risk, and backtesting patterns. It also lists FAQ topics including benefits, pros and cons, rules, guidelines, tips, strategies, examples, risks, timeframes, market-condition adjustments, and indicators.

Authorities said a 92-year-old Arizona woman, Anna Mae Blessing, was charged with first-degree murder, aggravated assault and kidnapping after allegedly shooting her 72-year-old son, who had wanted to put her in an assisted living facility. She hid two pistols, shot him, was disarmed by his girlfriend, and arrested.

Modern U.S. education has adopted business-developed practices, with Horace Mann framing public education as improving economic opportunity and schools importing bureaucratic structures and categorizing students by age, sex, race, grade, subject, and IQ. A Nation at Risk concluded teachers were underqualified and underpaid and schools had poor conditions; A Nation Prepared proposed professionalism and standards, leading to the National Board for Professional Teaching Standards. Teacher professionalization did not increase pay or security, and student test scores showed little impact. NCLB (2001) introduced competition, incentives, accountability, standardized testing, AYP, and sanctions including closure or charter conversion. Charter schools showed mixed or isolated success, segregation, financial inefficiencies, and no wide test-score gains. The medical model attributes learning success to inborn biological features, tracing to eugenics and slavery; diagnosis can foster fixed mindset, stigma, stereotype threat, and disengagement. The passage proposes reframing education as problem solving, using mindfulness, role models, self-discovery, project-based learning, and Dewey/Montessori. It describes problem solving as agent-environment interaction, cross-disciplinary, scale-free cognition, explanation and error correction, and child scientist theory. It links perception, heuristics, metacognition, teacher/mentor/peer review, and argues for a recursive problem-solving structure from student to teacher to administration, emphasizing self-directed learning and assessment against oneself rather than norms. It concludes that American education needs radical restructuring away from business-modeled commodification toward problem-solving and self-regulated learning.

Autism Units are expected to be built in Leitrim during the 2018/19 school term. Minister Bruton said 12 Autism Units will be built in Sligo/Leitrim and Donegal. Leitrim’s ASD special classes rose from two to five since 2011, with five new primary and seven new post-primary ASD classes. Bruton discussed selection processes, and the NCSE advises early written applications.

The writer answers Hartman, who traces INF deployment's impetus to Europeans, especially Schmidt, to correct regional imbalance and decoupling; Hartman now calls deployment divisive and would trade it for arms control. Dobrynin and the Secretary agreed to meet regularly on US-Soviet issues and likely hold a Foreign Ministers' meeting before the next UNGA, though no date was set. Dobrynin said arms control progress was limited; the Shultz-Gromyko channel could resolve problems, Geneva negotiators lacked flexibility, and major problems required Foreign Ministers.

Barrett, Gazelle, and Alabama Claims whaling ships.

Chemical polishing/etching of Cd1-xZnxTe1-ySey (CZTS) crystals with 5% bromine in methanol was studied for X-ray and gamma-ray detector processing. Cutting and polishing produce a damaged layer that must be removed for detector properties. Samples with similar zinc content and selenium concentrations y = 0, 0.02, 0.06, and 0.1 were etched in stages up to 8 min at +19°C, and etching trajectories and average rates were determined. Average rates were 24 μm/min for CZT (y = 0), 18 μm/min for y = 0.02, 15 μm/min for y = 0.06, and 13 μm/min for y = 0.1. A sharp decrease of about 20% at y ~ 0.02 versus CZT is reported as first direct evidence of CZTS crystal matrix hardening. A thermodynamic model relates the rate decrease to excess Gibbs energy, giving a calculated 22% versus experimental 24% change. Etching depends on surface roughness, damaged layer, temperature, and stirring; stirring increases the rate. At higher selenium concentrations, etching-rate differences converge. Zinc addition is expected to increase the etching rate. The results may aid processing of CZTS detector elements.

Vanuatu’s Reserve Bank may look into questions about the AFIC savings and loan scheme. Ambae volcano’s rating was lowered from level 4 to 3; eruptions remain stable and essentials are being collected for evacuees. New teacher salary scales begin in 2018, and 21 retired teachers received medals.

Crystal Palace host Newcastle United at Selhurst Park on Sunday (2.15pm, Sky Sports PL), with Andre Marriner refereeing. Neither Benítez nor Hodgson is satisfied with transfer business; Slimani may play for Newcastle, while Hodgson has lost Sako to a broken ankle, a sixth long-term absentee, and may use young signings. Newcastle hope to repeat Sunderland’s 4-0 win there last year.

The second edition of The New Zealand Land and Food Annual was launched at National Field Days in Mystery Creek. Published by Massey University Press, it gathers 31 contributors on how New Zealand can address food and land issues. Editor Professor Claire Massey says sustainable food production is a constant goal, while contributor Ralph Sims says current practices are not sustainable.

The passage reviews small-body reservoirs in planetary systems and their role as sources of exocomets. It describes Solar System populations, including near-Earth asteroids, the main belt, Hildas, Trojans, trans-Neptunian objects, Centaurs, Jupiter-family comets, and the Oort cloud. It discusses star formation environments, protoplanetary discs, dust growth, planetesimal formation through gravitational collapse and the streaming instability, and the transition to debris discs. Thermal conditions and snowlines influence planetesimal composition, while host star mass affects snowline locations. Debris discs are likely exocomet reservoirs, though exocomets are often detected around A-type stars even though planet formation occurs around stars of varied masses. The passage also covers observational evidence from Solar System bodies and missions, Oort cloud formation, and open questions. It concludes that small-body reservoirs are probable at young stars, shaped by stellar environment, planetary architecture, disc processes, and collisional depletion over time.

The document also lists changes to protocol-specified analyses and appendices on data presentation, SAS QC, and planned tables, figures, and listings.

The State Department instructed diplomatic and consular officers that passports need not be refused solely because applicants could not or would not state an intent to return within two years; passports should be refused only if applicants did not intend to return or circumstances negated that intent, with no fixed period, and passports are valid for two years with possible renewal upon a new satisfactory application. It construed article 19 to provide that the first secretary ordinarily acts as chargé d’affaires ad interim when the mission head is absent, with emergency arrangements requiring prior consultation and the chargé exercising discretion regarding other secretaries. An Executive order prohibited diplomatic and consular officers from attacking, preferring charges against, or publicly criticizing other officers in either service except in communications to the Department of State.

Seminary graduation for 16 Miami Valley seniors was held May 20 at The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Huber Heights. Graduates received certificates for studying the Book of Mormon. Speakers included Mark Skouson and three students. Eleven volunteers taught; seminary is open to high school students.

Design details for the TPS7H500x-SP push-pull converter include a leading-edge blank time initially about 50 ns with RLEB 49.9 kΩ, which may need optimization for parasitics, gate-driver propagation delay, and minimum on-time. Soft-start uses a 33-nF capacitor, giving about 7.5 ms. The transformer design targets a 35% maximum duty cycle, selects a 2.5 turns ratio, and uses a 40-μH primary inductance versus 33 μH calculated, with magnetizing current targeted at 6% of output current. Primary GaN FETs are rated 170 V; synchronous rectifier GaN FETs are rated 80 V, with an optional parallel Schottky diode. The RCD clamp requires testing optimization. The output inductor is 0.47 μH with 40% ripple. Output capacitance requires at least 1.3 mF; about 2.3 mF was used, via seven 330-μF polymer tantalum capacitors, to address ripple, load transients, and SET mitigation, with an optional output filter. Overcurrent limiting begins near 35 A, using a 1:100 current sense transformer and a 7.5-Ω RCS. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation targets 10 kHz crossover, with RCOMP 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP 15 nF, and CHF 47 pF. The slope compensation resistor is 102 kΩ. The controller operates from 4 V to 14 V input with at least a 0.1-µF VIN bypass. Layout guidance emphasizes minimizing noise, separating AVSS from power ground at one point, placing bypass and compensation components close, routing sensitive signals away from high dv/dt nodes, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS. Revision history and mechanical/orderable information are also included.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2019 describes its business, risk factors, properties, legal proceedings, market information, selected consolidated financial data, and management’s discussion and analysis. It reports 2019 net sales of $280,522 million, operating income of $14,541 million, net income of $11,588 million, total assets of $225,248 million, and approximately 798,000 employees.

Anthology Inc. lost nearly $80 million over the past two years and has more than $1 billion in debt after years of mergers and acquisitions. As part of a restructuring plan to emerge debt-free by early next year, Oaktree Capital Management and Nexus Capital Management are giving Anthology $50 million to focus on Blackboard, while it sells its enterprise operations, life-cycle engagement, and student success businesses. Encoura has agreed to be the stalking horse bidder for the life-cycle engagement and student success businesses, while Ellucian will do the same for enterprise operations. The breakup is not expected to affect institutions that contract with Anthology because products are being spun off. Analysts say Anthology incorrectly assumed colleges would buy its entire suite and cross-sell LMS, SIS, and CRM products, but academics choose the LMS separately. Formed in 2020 by combining Campus Management, Campus Labs, and iModules, Anthology later acquired Blackboard. M&A integration burdens, competition, revenue decline, rising interest rates, and conservative buyers made its debt unmanageable. Its bankruptcy is part of a higher education technology market reset, and colleges may benefit as companies focus on their expertise.

Janet Yellen questioned Trump's economic policies and refused to back rolling back Dodd-Frank. She told lawmakers the Fed saw healthy lending growth, well-capitalized banks, and a more resilient financial system, and questioned claims that Dodd-Frank hurt lending or competitiveness. Yellen acknowledged community banks' regulatory burden and suggested exempting them from the Volcker Rule, declined direct comment on Trump's spending and tax plans while favoring productivity and sustainable fiscal accounts, and said rates should rise sooner than expected.

The DAWN-plasma study is a randomized, open-label, phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter trial evaluating convalescent plasma safety and efficacy in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. It compares standard of care versus standard of care plus convalescent plasma, with outcomes partly based on WHO's draft master protocol.

Germany is an industrialized Western European country whose education system, including special education, has been shaped by its history. After unification in 1871, Bismarck introduced universal mandatory education based on the Prussian system. The Nazis standardized higher secondary education in 1938. After World War II, West Germany adopted a three-tier secondary system—Hauptschule, Realschule, and Gymnasium—while Gesamtschule was introduced in the 1960s. East Germany established a free education system from primary through higher grades. After reunification, public education became free, though private schools play a minor role. Education is primarily under the federal states, with the KMK coordinating policies.

Special education schools, or Hilfsschulen, began in the 1920s. In 1960, the KMK established special schools for various disabilities. Inclusion efforts since the 1990s have grown, but only 33.6% of children with disabilities are included in elementary schools and 14.9% in secondary schools. About 577,000 students with disabilities attend seven special school categories; in 2019–2020 there were about 2,800 special education schools and 68,500 educators. In 2021–2022, 92,911 students with special needs were in elementary general schools and 24,933 in secondary.

Teacher training includes university study and a two-year Referendariat; special educators receive more pedagogy and behavior management training and often work in elementary or vocational secondary schools. Laws and policies include the 1990 free public education, the 2006 General Equal Treatment Act, the 2008 UN CRPD, a 2013 North Rhine-Westphalia inclusive education policy, and 2015 KMK recommendations. Current issues include inclusion practices, funding, teacher perceptions, MTSS/RTI implementation, and the high proportion of included secondary students attending Hauptschule; the system is shifting toward more inclusion.

This application is a continuation of several U.S. applications and claims benefit of U.S. Provisional Application No. 62/491,823, all titled “Metal Gates of Transistors Having Reduced Resistivity.” The passage discusses MOS devices with polysilicon gates suffering poly depletion and metal gate electrodes as a solution. The Mailbox module facilitates communication among the ARM Cortex-A8, C674x DSP, and Media Controller; senders write messages to mailbox registers, interrupts notify queuing or overflow, and it supports flexible mailbox-to-processor assignment, four-message FIFO depth per queue, and interrupts. When choosing one child to receive a $25 Treasury bond or a raffle entry, mothers favored daughters and fathers favored sons. Results were similar across cultures and appeared driven by parents identifying with same-sex children. Over 90% of participants said they did not prefer one child.

The Boston Zone Offense was developed and refined by Tom Davis and received national exposure when he coached Boston College. Its Iowa version has players play only one position and flip sides rather than interchange. It emphasizes a strong low post attack and uses dribble entry rather than pass entry, is keyed off dribble penetration, suits early offense for up-tempo teams, and combines overloading and spreading principles. Hawaiʻi is involving more charter schools in its goal to provide all 3- and 4-year-olds access to preschool by 2032. Waikīkī Community Preschool became the state’s first private preschool to transition to a charter, making it tuition-free and state-funded under the Public Charter School Commission. Charter schools currently operate 33 preschool classrooms, including six at Waikīkī. The state opened 26 preschool classrooms on DOE campuses this fall and plans about 25 more next year, but about 6,700 children lack access and roughly 330 classrooms are needed over seven years.

Supporters say charter preschools can address teacher shortages by providing state funding, higher wages, and K-12 benefits, though licensing requirements and funding shortfalls remain challenges. Charter preschools receive $171,000 per classroom, which advocates say is insufficient. Waikīkī expects a $150,000 to $200,000 shortfall and relies on its nonprofit partner for fundraising; Parkway Village Preschool also faces shortfalls. Converting private programs may not add new seats but can stabilize existing programs if funding increases. The state has set aside $20 million for preschool construction on certain DOE and charter campuses.

FPIs showed huge interest in corporate bond investment limits. On Monday, 58 bidders bid Rs 5,898 crore against Rs 3,360 crore notified; corporate cut-off was 15.25 bps versus 1.20 bps for G-secs.

The Turnaround Tuesday effect occurs from Monday’s close until at least Tuesday’s close. Backtests indicate that buying on weakness on Mondays and selling at Tuesday’s close has been profitable over about 30 years, with returns higher than other weekdays, and the strategy works best on weak Mondays. Buying on strength on a Monday is not a good idea. An example given is Black Monday, October 19, 1987, after which the market rebounded 5.3% on Tuesday and 9.1% on Wednesday.

King appointed Allen and Carter to negotiate a reciprocity agreement, signed at Washington January 30, 1875, effective September 9, 1876. Great Britain and initially Germany objected under the 1852 parity/favored-nation clause; Carter contested the German claim. A proposed 10 percent duty compromise on British imports of free-schedule articles was not accepted and withdrawn. Controversy led to a change of ministry and eventually admission by the King’s minister of U.S. exclusive privileges and pledge to hold the treaty inviolate. An “annexation scare” prompted Evarts to instruct Comly on August 6, 1878, to disabuse minds of further U.S. projects beyond the treaty. Later interpretation, customs, and fraud questions involving British claims were settled diplomatically by notes. A domestic scandal caused ministerial changes and a briefly requested recall of foreign representatives, including Comly, which was promptly recalled. The U.S. also aided liquor-traffic suppression in the Ralik Islands, sought a consular agent there, and assisted a Hawaii-Japan treaty. In June 1881 Comly reported continued British efforts under the parity clause.

FemNoC is used to study ultrafast magnetization fluctuations in the canted antiferromagnet Sm0.7Er0.3FeO3 across its spin reorientation transition and under external magnetic fields. The reported results show that picosecond spin fluctuation magnitude is governed by the free energy potential, increasing where the potential softens. An external magnetic field suppresses fluctuations and increases the quasi-ferromagnetic magnon frequency by stiffening the potential. Atomistic spin-noise and Monte Carlo simulations support these experimental trends. The findings indicate external-field tunability of ultrafast spin fluctuations and demonstrate FemNoC as a tool for characterizing magnetization potentials in complex magnetic systems.

The passage describes a camera module, molded circuit board assembly, molded photosensitive assembly, molding mould, and manufacturing methods. It explains that conventional molded packaging for camera modules has mass-production problems, including deformation or flashing during demoulding, friction damage from a square through-hole forming block, stray light reflected by inner walls, and the need to balance light flux, structural strength, reflectivity, demoulding, and damage prevention. The described assemblies include a circuit board, a photosensitive element, and a molded base integrally formed by a molding process. The molded base forms a light window that is not a prismatic column; portions of its inner and outer side surfaces are inclined at acute angles, including first, second, and third inclination angles within specified ranges, to facilitate demoulding, reduce friction and damage, reduce stray light, increase light flux, and provide mounting areas. The molding mould includes a light window forming block and a base forming guide groove, with the light window forming block having a trapezoidal or multi-step trapezoidal cross-section. Manufacturing methods place the circuit board in a mould, fill liquid molding material around the light window forming block, solidify the material, and demould to form the molded base. The passage also describes molded circuit board and photosensitive assembly arrays, cutting separated assemblies, and application to electronic devices. The application claims priority through a chain of continuation and divisional applications to four China applications filed Aug. 1, 2016.

This lecture by David Hardt discusses manufacturing process control from a mechanical engineering perspective. It defines processes as geometry change through removal, addition, formation, or deformation, caused by directed energy exchange—mechanical, electrical, thermal, or chemical. Processes are classified as serial when the interaction area is small compared with the total area changed, or parallel when interaction occurs over the whole area.
