Serial processes tend to favor flexibility; parallel processes favor speed. Examples include machining, turning, injection molding, rolling, CVD, stereolithography, and 3D printing. The lecture separates process parameters into equipment and material properties and states. Equipment states are generally controllable, while material properties and states tend to be variable and hard to know. Material uncertainty and uncertain energy coupling are major sources of variation.

The speaker is happy to be part of a special group, with many returning, that tried to go back-to-back despite difficulty and overcame challenges. He values sharing success with teammates, family, and friends during a short career, praises the group’s competitiveness and willingness to do whatever it takes, and says passing the Cup to a long-time player without a playoff game was special.

The lecture discusses interactions between neutral atoms. Classically, two neutral atoms have no attraction because creating a dipole or fluctuating dipole costs more energy than the dipole interaction returns. Quantum mechanically, the square of the dipole operator has a nonzero expectation value due to zero-point fluctuations, leading to the van der Waals interaction. Perturbation theory gives a first-order 1/R³ potential for ground and excited atoms, and a second-order 1/R⁶ van der Waals potential for two ground-state atoms. The lecture offers three interpretations: perturbation theory, coupled LC circuits/capacitors, and zero-point atomic dipole fluctuations producing aligned induced dipoles. Vacuum fluctuations of the electromagnetic field can induce correlated dipole moments, yielding a 1/R⁷ Casimir-Polder potential at long range, while 1/R⁶ applies at short range; the transition depends on the resonant wavelength. Diagrammatically, QED interactions arise through virtual photon exchange in fourth-order perturbation, with energy denominators distinguishing short- and long-range cases.

The study assessed the potentiality and apprehensions of AI in education from the perspectives of education staff at Kuwait University. It used a cross-sectional online survey with random sampling of 63 academic staff and administrators in the Faculty of Education. The questionnaire included the Attitudes for Artificial Intelligence scale, the Teachers’ Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence Questionnaire, and the Scenarios of AI Education and AI-related Applications Questionnaire. Results showed medium acceptance of AI in education (mean 3.37), with high agreement that AI will benefit humanity (4.03) and confidence in AI (3.78). Most participants (58.7%) had no prior teaching experience with AI. Linking education to AI was moderate (4.21), with highest scores for data analysis, machine learning, and natural language processing. Student empowerment requirements in using AI were moderate (4.36), including identifying AI use cases, assessing AI intelligence, and identifying technical limitations. Challenges and difficulties in using AI were high (4.83), including lack of suitable teaching materials, lack of required experience, and subject complexity. Scenarios for education using AI were high (4.82), especially personalized intelligent teaching, smart schools, and online and mobile remote education. Inferential tests showed no statistically significant differences attributed to gender, academic degree, and academic department, except for reported challenges and difficulties of using AI between males and females. The study concluded that both apprehensions and potentiality concerning AI integration in education are high, and reforms are needed. Limitations included not considering students’ perspectives, and future studies were suggested with larger samples.

The lecture discusses risk preferences, mainly from the expected utility perspective. It notes that many economic choices involve risk, such as education, buying a house, insurance, farming, investment portfolios, health, dating, and friendship choices, and that people use risk-mitigating strategies.

Three stylized facts are presented: people are risk averse in many contexts; risk reduction has a price, and people will take on risk if the return is high enough; and people sometimes take on risk for its own sake, as with casinos, lotteries, and sports betting.

The expected utility model assumes utility over final outcomes, weights utilities by probabilities, and evaluates lotteries by expected utility. It assumes only final outcomes matter and that probabilities enter linearly. Risk neutrality means a person is indifferent between a lottery and its expected monetary value; risk aversion means preferring the expected monetary value for sure; risk loving means preferring the lottery. Risk aversion comes from concavity of the utility function, and a risk-averse person with a concave utility function rejects all fair gambles.

Risk aversion is measured through the concavity of the utility function, using coefficients of absolute and relative risk aversion. Constant relative risk aversion functions are emphasized. Measurement methods include choices between gambles, certainty equivalents, and insurance choices. A certainty-equivalent example with wealth of $50,000 or $100,000 at 50% each yields implied gamma values depending on the guaranteed amount chosen. Large-scale choices suggest gamma is not too large, often assumed between 0 and 2, while rejecting a small 50-50 gamble to lose $10 and win $11 implies gamma greater than 18.

The lecture discusses Matthew Rabin’s paper, which shows that under weak concavity, rejecting small gambles implies implausibly rapid declines in marginal utility and absurd conclusions for large-scale gambles. Thus expected utility has trouble reconciling small-scale and large-scale risk choices. The lecture says an alternative model, reference dependence or loss aversion, will be considered later.

The lecture also introduces Justin Sydnor’s paper using real home insurance choices. The data include about 50,000 standard policies, menus of four deductibles, premiums, claims, and new customers. Deductibles are amounts paid out of pocket before insurance pays. Claim rates are low. Using deductible choices and premiums relative to a $1,000 policy, Sydnor estimates bounds on gamma. The lecture announces that problem set two will be posted later, late submissions will not be accepted except for medical or excuse notice, and previous problem sets, midterms, and finals will be posted for practice.
Sears is borrowing $100 million from CEO Eddie Lampert's hedge fund affiliates, which agreed to lend up to $100 million more by Dec. 1, amid store closures and sales declines.

CSUSB veteran students discuss military tuition benefits. Active duty members receive tuition assistance up to $4,500 yearly, but training can disrupt school. The Post-9/11 GI Bill offers up to four years of benefits, covering tuition at public schools, while the Montgomery GI Bill has different payment rates and requires students to pay certain expenses. Veterans have 10–15 years to use benefits.

Preparation of numerous memoranda for President Roosevelt and the American delegation for the Malta and Yalta Conferences was completed on January 16, 1945, and the “Yalta Briefing Book” was presented to the President. A memorandum of conversation by Leo Pasvolsky describes a second meeting with the Soviet Ambassador about the Dumbarton Oaks Documents. At the Ambassador’s request, they continued their January 11 conversation for over two and one-half hours. The Ambassador had reread the President’s proposal and was puzzled by a reference to Chapter VIII, Section C, paragraph 1; Pasvolsky explained it concerned whether the Council should encourage a regional group or agency to settle local or regional disputes. They discussed the voting formula without new points and other open items, including the Court, which the Ambassador considered settled in substance, and dependent areas. Pasvolsky outlined approaches to dependent-area problems and said only international trusteeship belonged on the United Nations Conference agenda. The Ambassador asked whether colonial problems would involve only colonial powers or all important powers, possibly through the future international organization, and Pasvolsky said any procedure was possible.

R. L. Wells was convicted of embezzlement and sentenced to two years. His appeal was dismissed because his appeal bond, though approved by the sheriff, was approved by another judge instead of the judge who tried the case, as required by law.

The court affirmed Shircliff’s conviction on an indictment charging him and O’Connor with conspiracy to bribe township and school trustee Valentine Strange to employ O’Connor as a public school teacher, with Strange to retain $50 from O’Connor’s wages. The indictment was sufficient under R. S. 1881 sections 2139 and 2009 without averring that any school was vacant. Affidavits for a continuance and a bill of exceptions filed after term without time granted were not part of the record. An objection to discharging O’Connor to testify, first raised in the Supreme Court, came too late. The second special judge’s appointment was presumed proper because the first appointee was absent or unable to preside. Judgment affirmed.

Congressional Democrats are holding the line on health care demands as shutdown talks near the funding deadline. House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries reiterated opposition to the GOP-backed spending proposal, saying Democrats will not support a partisan Republican spending bill. Democrats insist any deal to avert a shutdown at 12:01 a.m. ET Wednesday must extend enhanced Obamacare tax credits due to expire at the end of 2025. Republicans say negotiations on continuing those credits should happen after a funding resolution is approved by the Senate. Trump is set to meet at 3 p.m. ET with Jeffries, Chuck Schumer, Mike Johnson, and John Thune. At least seven Senate Democrats would need to vote with Republicans to pass legislation averting a shutdown.

H&M said March local-currency sales rose 6%, below a preliminary estimate, in another sign it may struggle to reach its full-year target. It missed sales forecasts last year and saw profits fall amid competition. February sales shrank for the first time in four years. The CEO said weak first-quarter sales made a 10-15% annual growth target harder. Analysts cited a tough market and questioned continued store expansion. H&M had 4,426 stores at end-March, up 11%. April sales may be supported by Easter but limited by cold weather.

The passage includes XBRL metadata and Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022. The Form 10-K reports SEC filing details, Nasdaq-listed securities, shares outstanding, market value, and describes Microsoft’s business, products, three operating segments, approximately 221,000 full-time employees, corporate social responsibility efforts, human capital, operations, R&D, distribution, licensing, customers, executive officers, and risk factors including competition.

The court accepted the parties’ stipulation that glassware, furniture, and smoker’s articles exported from France were appraised on foreign value, with invoice unit values plus 12.44% plus packing, and 40 excess boxes of item 21008 at 337 francs each plus 12.44% plus packing, with no higher export value. Judgment was rendered accordingly.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2016. Q1 2016 net sales were $29.128 billion, operating income was $1.071 billion, net income was $513 million, and diluted earnings per share were $1.07, compared with Q1 2015 net sales of $22.717 billion, operating income of $255 million, net loss of $57 million, and diluted loss per share of $(0.12). Q1 2016 operating cash flow was $(2.160) billion, investing cash flow was $(693) million, and financing cash flow was $(789) million. The company organized operations into North America, International, and AWS segments. The report includes financial statements, accounting policies, commitments and contingencies, legal proceedings, income taxes, long-term debt, stockholders’ equity, segment information, MD&A, and risk factors. In February 2016, the Board authorized repurchasing up to $5 billion of common stock; no repurchases occurred in Q1 2016 or Q1 2015.

The U.S. provided over $55,000 to Cambodia to preserve 3,000–5,000 items belonging to prisoners at the Khmer Rouge’s Tuol Sleng/S-21 prison. The agreement was signed Monday; U.S. and Cambodian officials said the deteriorating items will be conserved, with some displayed at the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum.

Connor McDavid signed a two-year, $25 million extension with the Oilers, with a $12.5 million AAV. Less than two hours later, Edmonton signed defenseman Jake Walman to a seven-year, $49 million extension. The report notes McDavid’s career points and awards, his past contract and pending UFA status, and Edmonton’s two straight Stanley Cup Final losses; it also cites Walman’s stats and Edmonton’s defensemen contracts. Other headlines cover Bruins retiring Chara’s No. 33, Lightning-Panthers penalties, signings involving Grzelcyk, Ellis, and Gustavsson, and fantasy/season preview content.

NVIDIA Corporation filed Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended April 29, 2018. It reported revenue of $3.207 billion, net income of $1.244 billion, diluted net income per share of $1.98, gross margin of 64.5%, and income from operations of $1.295 billion. GPU business revenue was $2.765 billion and Tegra Processor business revenue was $442 million. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $7.30 billion. During the quarter, NVIDIA repurchased 3 million shares for $655 million and paid $91 million in dividends. The filing also discusses legal proceedings, including Polaris and ZiiLabs patent matters, and states no material changes to risk factors or internal controls.

The passage outlines U.S. objectives for dependent areas, including international collaboration to advance dependent peoples, self-government, higher economic and social standards, security, and non-discriminatory treatment. A March 9, 1943 draft declaration distinguished mandated or detached territories from colonial territories, proposed international trusteeship for the former, regional commissions for colonial areas, and progressive self-government leading to full independence on a fixed schedule. British objections were noted at Quebec, Moscow, and London talks. The trusteeship chapter was deleted from the American Tentative Proposals at the Joint Chiefs of Staff’s request, and dependent territories were not discussed at Dumbarton Oaks, though later consideration was expected. The documents were being revised and submitted to the President. Leo Pasvolsky acknowledged British acceptance of the President’s proposal on Security Council voting. Secretary of War Stimson argued against raising territorial or trusteeship questions during the war before Russian commitment to Pacific participation.

NVIDIA Turing GPUs use RT Cores to accelerate real-time ray tracing by handling BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection tests, offloading SMs. Combined with denoising, hybrid rendering, and RTX APIs, Turing enables ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, and is significantly faster than Pascal. The passage also covers NVIDIA NGX, a deep-learning stack using Tensor Cores with features including DLSS, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS uses DNNs trained on 64x supersampled images to improve image quality and performance; DLSS 2X targets quality near 64xSS. NGX does not work on pre-Turing architectures. Mesh Shading introduces Task and Mesh shaders to reduce CPU draw call bottlenecks and support LOD and geometry manipulation. Variable Rate Shading allows per-16x16-region shading rates for Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling by shading in texture space. Multi-View Rendering supports multiple views in a single pass. The passage also describes resource binding, VR support, TU104, TU106, and Tesla T4 specifications, the RTX-OPS workload metric, and ray tracing fundamentals including BVH and denoising. It concludes that hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH, and RT Cores enable real-time ray tracing.

The President submits to Congress a letter from the U.S. agent to the Creek Indians seeking protection of rights and territory secured by the April 22 treaty. Surveyors from Georgia are reported to be surveying lands within the Indian Territory, and some may have been arrested by Indians. The 1802 act regulating trade and intercourse with Indian tribes provides penalties for surveying such lands and two enforcement processes, military and civil. The President chose the civil process first, directing prosecution of the surveyors in Georgia and assuring the Indians of protection while urging their forbearance. He abstained from military force because the surveys were under color of Georgia authority and could lead to conflict with the state. He states Georgia’s actions violate the treaty and supreme law, and that if Georgia persists, the Executive may be compelled to enforce the laws by all force, with military force only after other expedients fail. Congress is asked to determine whether further legislation is necessary.

The passage surveys container and distributed-system design patterns. It introduces the ambassador pattern for brokering interactions between application containers and external services, with examples involving sharded Redis, service brokering, and request splitting. It then covers the adapter pattern for adapting heterogeneous application interfaces for monitoring, logging, and health checks, with Prometheus, fluentd, and MySQL examples. It discusses microservices and multi-node patterns including replicated load-balanced stateless services, session-tracked services, caching, rate limiting, SSL termination, sharded services and caches, sharding functions and consistent hashing, scatter/gather, and function-as-a-service/event-driven processing, including their benefits and challenges.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended December 26, 2015 reports net sales of $75,872 million, net income of $18,361 million, basic earnings per share of $3.30 and diluted earnings per share of $3.28, compared with net sales of $74,599 million, net income of $18,024 million, basic earnings per share of $3.08 and diluted earnings per share of $3.06 for the prior-year period. Total assets were $293,284 million as of December 26, 2015. Cash generated by operating activities was $27,463 million; cash used in investing activities was $20,450 million and cash used in financing activities was $11,444 million. The company declared cash dividends of $0.52 per share and repurchased common stock. Segment net sales were Americas $29,325 million, Europe $17,932 million, Greater China $18,373 million, Japan $4,794 million, and Rest of Asia Pacific $5,448 million. Product net sales included iPhone $51,635 million, iPad $7,084 million, Mac $6,746 million, Services $6,056 million, and Other Products $4,351 million. Gross margin was 40.1%, operating expenses were $6,252 million, and the effective tax rate was 25.3%. The filing also discusses debt, derivatives, commitments, contingencies, and legal proceedings, including Samsung’s $548 million payment.

AT&T announced it will turn on LTE-M nationwide by the end of June for Internet of Things devices. LTE-M is a version of cellular technology tuned for everyday objects; it uses less energy, can last up to 10 years on a charge, penetrates walls up to 8 inches thicker than standard signals, and allows about 386 kilobits per second. Companies demonstrated uses including Pepsi soda fountains, RM2 pallets with built-in radios, and Capstone smart water meters. Such devices use little data and are mostly off the network. AT&T has not announced prices but may charge per bit or device.

Detroit Red Wings is described as a club with weaknesses and maybe not doing well in the playoffs, but expected to prepare and play better next game. The few penalties taken make every chance important, and the power play is called important. A great player brings offense and works hard on defense. His confidence is higher in his third NHL year and second finals. The speaker recounts injury recovery, bad feelings while unable to help a losing team, changes after returning, and a competitive series against the same team that beat them last year.

Stock futures were little changed after the S&P 500 snapped a 7-day win streak. Tesla debuted more affordable standard versions of its Model Y SUV, priced just below $40,000, and Model 3 sedan, starting around $37,000. The Model Y standard lacks a panoramic glass roof, leather seats and light bars, costs about $5,000 less than the previous entry-level Model Y, and has an estimated 321-mile range versus 357 miles for a Long Range rear-wheel-drive version. Lower prices may help Tesla after the loss of $7,500 federal EV tax credits. Tesla shares rose 5% Monday and dipped about 3% Tuesday.

The Rock Springs City Council will hold a May 1 public hearing on amendments allowing downtown restaurants to offer outdoor dining decks. The Planning & Zoning Commission approved the petition April 11. If approved, dining decks would be seasonal and subject to approval, sidewalk clearance, parking, alcohol, maintenance, and inspection requirements.

Tigers face ALDS Game 4 elimination against the Mariners, and manager A.J. Hinch said Tarik Skubal is not available. Skubal pitched seven innings, allowed two runs and struck out nine in Game 2, setting him up for a potential Game 5 on normal rest. Detroit will have its high-leverage relievers available for Game 4.

Lego DC Super Villains was announced with a full trailer. Players create a super villain and work with DC classic bad guys to save a city in a parallel universe without superheroes. It releases October 16, 2018, for PC, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Nintendo Switch, with special editions and bonus characters.

The speaker says one player has been among the league’s best for two or three years and is hard to replace as a right winger, though his first-period minutes were too high and were reduced. Jordan and Rhett played less together after the first period, and Jordan and Andrew can play both sides. Another player is a quality veteran like Andreychuk who leads by example and suits a high-energy, short-focus format. The first period was not their best, but they improved in the second. An older defenseman is underrated, disciplined, plays against top players, and is still viewed as young with room to grow; the team changed by not having older defensemen protect others and brought Rhett in as an experienced young defenseman. Jarome is a slow starter who became team leader and captain. Bad ice, extra playoff games, and travel are not treated as excuses, and one official is respected for communicating with players.

Pakistan stopped work on three CPEC road projects after China stopped funding; work will resume once Chinese money arrives. Pakistan’s planning minister confirmed this, while a parliamentary committee said the projects were not shelved and China was reviewing their financial mechanism.

The speaker urges national legislators to enact a graduated inheritance tax, with rates increasing according to the amount inherited and the beneficiary’s remoteness of kin, small on moderate amounts and heavier on swollen fortunes. Such a tax should be introduced gradually; national inheritance taxes were imposed in 1797, 1862, and 1898, and the Supreme Court upheld the Civil War succession tax and the 1898 inheritance-tax feature. The passage also discusses the desirability and constitutional difficulty of a national income tax, noting that the 1894 law was held unconstitutional by one majority; if legislation fails, a constitutional amendment may ultimately be necessary.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed 290 patients aged 41–80 years (244 male, 46 female) who underwent CABG for coronary artery disease at Mordovian Republic Hospital from 2017 to 2021. The study sought to clarify the role of the number of used shunts and internal thoracic arteries in post-CABG complications. Of the patients, 278 underwent on-pump CABG and 12 off-pump CABG. Reported postoperative complications included arrhythmia, psychosis, stroke, myocardial infarction, hydrothorax, re-sternotomy, dyspnea, and sternal wound infection; the most frequently reported was hydrothorax. Five patients died. Elderly patients had higher risks of arrhythmia, psychosis, and stroke and longer ICU and total hospitalization. Diabetes mellitus was associated with higher BMI and longer ICU and total hospitalization, and diabetes complications were associated with obesity and longer hospitalization. Post-myocardial infarction myocardial sclerosis was associated with reduced ejection fraction and longer ICU stay. Hydrothorax was associated with low BMI, longer CPB time, and longer aortic cross-clamp time. Progressive angina and PMIMS increased the number of complications. The number of complications was not statistically associated with the number of shunts or internal thoracic arteries, nor with living/deceased status. The study concludes that elderly CABG patients are at higher risk of psychosis, arrhythmia, stroke, and longer hospitalization; hydrothorax is seen with low BMI and long aortic cross-clamp time leading to longer CPB; progressive angina and PMIMS increase postoperative complication risk, particularly hydrothorax.

The comments discuss matching up four centermen, Tanner and Tyler playing together, and a top-end two-way player nominated for the Selke. They note Kopy’s playoff playmaking and heavy minutes, competitive and tenacious players, Justin’s puck strength, and Mike as a reliable role model for Toffoli and Pearson. The team is described as prepared, matured, young, playoff-proven but still learning, led by leadership, and focused on the whole rather than individuals. Slava, first Stanley Cup final games, speed, elimination games, a top goalie, and a probable game tomorrow are also mentioned.

The speaker says the team had experience, felt it beat itself, and gained confidence from playing better at home. Pat stressed early that the team be tough to play at home, which paid off. John was key all year after Holik left, became the defensive go-to player, and stepped up when Joe was injured. The speaker notes playoff injuries, travel, and many games took a toll, and calls the outcome the greatest day. The team faced adversity, trades, and lost leaders but grew together. The Conn Smythe winner deserves it and was the big reason the Mighty Ducks went far. Winning is nice, but a missed opportunity remains; the team wants to build on this and be considered a dynasty in the future, though not now.

In this appeal from a false imprisonment judgment for the plaintiff, the court considered whether an action against assignees for the benefit of creditors was an action for money received in a fiduciary capacity under the Code, allowing arrest. The court held it was not. The action sought an accounting and distribution of funds, requiring determination of the net amount chargeable to the assignees, the creditors entitled, and pro rata payment, rather than merely recovery of money received. The Code provision did not extend beyond cases where a person who received money in a fiduciary capacity could be sued for money had and received. The execution against the plaintiff’s person was therefore unauthorized, and the judgment was affirmed with costs.

Only two in five U.S. households report good or excellent savings progress. America Saves Week, annual since 2007, promotes savings behavior; 2017 runs Feb. 27–Mar. 4 with resources and Military Saves Week registration.

Erik Brust and his cousin Jonathan Jeffrey brainstormed a fruity, creamy frozen treat made from natural, simple ingredients; after Jeffrey died of a drug overdose, Brust named the company JonnyPops in his honor and recruited classmates including Connor Wray to develop and sample it. JonnyPops launched around the Twin Cities in 2012, expanded distribution, and became a full-time business after Brust and Wray graduated. The company now has 10,000 distribution points, a new Delights line, and a social mission involving messages on pop sticks and fundraising for addiction treatment organizations.

After reelection, the author expresses gratitude, sees the election’s accord as evidence of the Union’s strength, and promises to conduct the Administration on stated principles. The prior term included a war with a powerful nation that ended on equal and honorable terms, with commerce driven from the sea, frontiers invaded, life lost, and $120,000,000 added to the public debt. After the war, land forces were reduced, and provisions were made for coastal fortifications and an augmented navy, described as economical defense and a means to prevent war. Foreign relations include neutrality between Spain and the South American colonies, suppression of piracy and the slave trade, treaties with Spain and Britain, acquisition of Florida, and negotiations with France and the Barbary Powers. Financially, nearly $67,000,000 of public debt was paid, internal taxes were repealed, revenue diminished, and loans were authorized. The author discusses future revenue policy and proposes securing land rights and funds for Indian tribes. Europe is unsettled, but the United States remains in amity and neutral while maintaining its rights. Internally, the government is elective and has avoided defects of ancient republics; territory, new states, and population have expanded. The address closes with confidence and reliance on Almighty God.

Jensen Huang reportedly said in an internal memo that Nvidia will continue sponsoring H-1B visa employees, stating “Legal immigration remains essential.” Nvidia would owe an estimated $147.3 million if President Donald Trump’s new $100,000 fee applied to the H-1B visa-holders it had approved in 2025, though the fee applies only to new applicants, not renewals or current holders. Huang previously praised the visa changes but later said the $100,000 fee “probably sets the bar a little too high.”

Investment analysts issued multiple price target changes on Friday, October 6th. New price targets were assigned to Covestro, Costco, Basf, Evonik, Inovio, Linde, Eli Lilly and, Lanxess, Mallinckrodt, and Wacker Chemie. Price targets were raised for AdvanSix, Deckers Outdoor, New Oriental Education & Technology Group, Netflix, Plug Power, Constellation Brands, 2U, and Yum China. Price targets were lowered for Ascena Retail Group and Rite Aid Corporation. Ratings mentioned included sell, buy, neutral, outperform, sector perform, and hold.

This paper describes a planned review, part of a series, to collate and evaluate published data on infectivity assessment in immunosuppressed patients with SARS-CoV-2, limited to studies using viral cell culture, and to estimate the relationship between viral culture and repeat rt-PCR Ct values or other measures of viral burden. It focuses on solid organ or hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. The research questions concern the relationship between serial PCR Ct/viral burden and the likelihood and duration of infectious virus from culture, and the influence of age, sex, underlying pathologies, immunosuppression degree, vaccination status, and COVID-19 symptoms and course. Databases to be searched are LitCovid, medRxiv, Google Scholar, and the WHO Covid-19 database from November 2019 to December 31, 2021, with no language restrictions. Screening and extraction procedures are described. Inclusion requires serial Ct or other viral burden measures from respiratory samples with viral culture on the same samples in pre- or post-transplant SARS-CoV-2 patients. Exclusions include post-mortem-only or non-respiratory-only samples and studies without viral cultures. Quality assessment uses five criteria. The review anticipates mostly case studies or case series, will report according to PRISMA, will not pool data due to laboratory differences, and may examine age or sex if data allow.

A Chief Magistrate has died for the fourth time, and the constitutional successor assumes the Executive chair. The passage mourns the murdered President, states that the government remains stable through constitutional succession, promises to profit from his example, notes prosperity, settled fiscal policy, peaceful foreign relations, and no need for an unusual session of Congress, and accepts the duties relying on divine guidance and the American people.

Lincolnshire County Council approved a new care leavers strategy. Support includes council tax discounts, advice and guidance up to age 25, university costs, driving licence funding, and contact for care leavers in custody. The leaving care services budget is about £1.2 million, with over 600 people in care and 300 in leaving care services, a number expected to rise. Support can be accessed through the council or Barnardos.

A fossil found in southwestern China shows Dinocephalosaurus, a fish-eating, long-necked marine reptile from about 245 million years ago, was pregnant with an embryo, indicating live birth rather than egg-laying. It is the first known archosauromorph to give birth this way. Estimated at 13 feet with a 5.5-foot neck, paddle-like flippers, small head, and teeth, it was fully marine. The curled embryo faced forward, not like swallowed prey; sex was genetically determined.

The Farmers State Bank of Craig sued Samuel J. Lydick on a $3,000 promissory note. Lydick alleged fraud and lack of consideration related to an earlier $5,000 note and the purchase of Missouri Valley Cattle Loan Company stock, involving Everett J. Martin, the bank’s officer. The jury found the bank was a purchaser for value without notice before maturity and found for Martin; the court withdrew a second cross-petition count. The appellate court upheld the instructions and verdict, applying the rule that a payee who receives a negotiable instrument in good faith, for value, before maturity, and without notice of infirmity, from a holder not maker or drawer, is a holder in due course. Judgment affirmed.

James Schenck, PenFed Credit Union president and CEO, accepted the Large Business Philanthropist of the Year award from Volunteer Alexandria at the 20th annual Business Philanthropy Summit, speaking on behalf of PenFed’s 2,500 employees and the philosophy “People Helping People.” The passage lists recent PenFed and PenFed Foundation donations for veterans and community causes, including gifts to Serve our Willing Warriors, the Kennedy Center, DC Habitat for Humanity, MOAA, Bunker Labs, and the Gary Sinise Foundation, and the launch of VEIP. It also describes Schenck’s volunteer roles, board service, and recognitions, and provides background on PenFed Credit Union and the PenFed Foundation.

Amazon Prime Day 2 is scheduled for October 7 and 8, with early deals already available. WIRED says it covers only actual deals on gear it has hand-tested and plans additional coverage and a liveblog when the event begins. An update on September 30, 2025 added 10 new deals on Amazon devices, a cheap laptop, a fitness tracker, a smart bird feeder, and other gadgets; the article lists discounts on products including an iPad, MacBook Air, Kindle Scribe, security camera, power bank, and smart ring.

For about 20 years, China has sought to modernise and upgrade its armed forces to gain military strength matching its soft power, defend regional interests and territorial claims, protect sea lanes, support initiatives like AIIB and OBOR, and counter US presence. The PLA has become a modern fighting force and China more assertive; the outcome remains open.

North Korea’s rarely traded defaulted debt may move further into the twilight zone after new sanctions. The debt includes syndicated loans with about $1 billion face value, in default since the 1980s, repackaged in 1997 into NK Debt Corporation by BNP. Total debt, including principal and interest, was estimated at about $3 billion in 2013. The securities traded regularly from around 2000, and prices rose after Kim Jong-il’s 2011 death, but hopes faded. Exotix says the market froze in early 2013 after UN sanctions, with no trading seen in three to four years. New UN sanctions and U.S.-North Korea tensions further discourage holders. Franklin Emerging Markets Debt Opportunities Fund held NK Debt zero-coupon bonds with $15.5 million principal maturing in 2020. Cuba and Iran investments also face obstacles.

Latin American stocks rebounded Monday from last week's selloff as U.S.-North Korea tensions abated and officials downplayed imminent war. Mexico's IPC rose 1.1%; Brazil's Bovespa touched its highest since May, led by Cia Paranaense. Currency moves were subdued: Mexico's peso firmed 0.3% before NAFTA negotiations, while Brazil's real fluctuated ahead of a fiscal goal revision. Scotiabank said geopolitical risks fell but some remained.

The passage presents a modular framework for AI-driven, multi-modal, multi-beamline synchrotron experiments at NSLS-II. It integrates existing Bluesky infrastructure for data acquisition, queue-server measurement management, Tiled data storage and access, and JupyterHub with AI agents for data processing, analysis, and decision-making. Agents are plug-and-play, configurable, and queryable through Tiled; passive agents analyze and report, while active agents suggest measurements. Autonomous operation uses Bayesian optimization with K-means dimensionality reduction, Gaussian process models, a scientific value function, and acquisition functions. Adjudicators and queue servers mediate measurement requests, preserving human control and safety.

The framework was tested through synchronous XRD and XAFS mapping of identical Al-Ni-Pt thin-film combinatorial libraries on the PDF and BMM beamlines. XRD-based measurement suggestions from PDF were sent to both beamlines, with adjudicators eliminating redundancies. The experiment achieved inter-beamline measurement requests, inter-agent communication, on-the-fly processing, analysis, interpretation, and autonomous and grid-based acquisition. Data analysis found composition gradients, FCC and FCT phases, overlapping peaks, texturing, and other complexities. Agents sometimes over-prioritized exploitation, showing the need for configurable operating modes.

A digital twin simulated an Al-Li-Fe oxide combinatorial library for benchmarking. In silico campaigns showed AI-driven mapping surpassed geometric series and random sampling in model accuracy and in resolving phase boundaries and localized minor phases after fewer measurements.

The passage discusses infrastructure needs, including the High Throughput Science Network, Bluesky, Tiled, Bluesky Adaptive, FAIR data, and simulation and replay capabilities. It defines beamline operating modes from fully autonomous to manual with AI assist and collaborative, and automation levels 0–3. It concludes that the framework enables collaborative human-AI autonomous synchrotron experiments, with open-source extensibility and potential for increased facility throughput.

Let’s Grow Kids, a Vermont statewide child care advocacy organization founded by Rick Davis in 2015, was designed to sunset after ten years. Aly Richards led it after Davis recruited her. It aimed to create permanent child care infrastructure and provide quality child care for every Vermont child. Over the decade, it raised over $70 million in private philanthropy and grew to 40 staff. Its efforts supported Act 76, signed in 2023, creating Vermont’s near-universal child care program. More than 100 new child care programs opened, creating over 1,000 spaces for children and 230 early childhood educator jobs, and an additional 4,000 children now qualify for tuition assistance. The organization officially sunset on Oct. 3. Leaders said the time-limited structure aided focus, fundraising, hiring and transition planning. It built partnerships and phase-out plans; staff moved to other organizations, and remaining staff transitioned to the Let’s Grow Kids Action Network. Act 76 did not make child care fully universal; 80% to 90% of Vermont families with children in child care programs are eligible for subsidies, according to an internal analysis.

Court documents say a Facebook argument led four people to Jennifer Bartell’s Portsmouth home, where Joshua Bowen allegedly shot her on March 14. Bowen is Albany Pierce’s boyfriend; Pierce, Shaunicka Cooley, and Shyrayno Jackson were charged as accessories after the fact. Neighbors were shocked but relieved the shooting was not random.

A federal judge ruled that the 1991 Nirvana album cover showing a naked baby underwater toward a dollar bill is not child pornography and dismissed Spencer Elden’s 2021 lawsuit. The judge found that only Elden’s nudity came close to the child pornography statute and compared the image to a family photo of a nude child bathing.

A Florida Museum study examined blood-sucking lice and their symbiotic bacteria, which supply vitamins missing from blood and are passed from female lice to offspring. Researchers found that lice parasitizing primates and humans hosted these endosymbionts continuously for at least 20 to 25 million years, evolving in step with primates. Sequencing endosymbiont genomes from human, chimpanzee, gorilla, and red colobus monkey lice showed tiny genomes, extensive remodeling, and genes for vitamin synthesis. This system may inform bacterial genome evolution and primate/human evolutionary history.

A study using deep learning on over 50,000 satellite images from European Mars orbiters found that Martian dust devils and surrounding winds can reach about 44 m/s, or 160 km/h, faster than previously assumed. These strong winds may lift much more dust into the atmosphere, influencing Mars’ weather and climate. The findings may help improve atmospheric models and planning for future Mars missions.

This study investigated whether resting-state functional connectivity (FC) of the nucleus accumbens (NAc) could predict the course of ADHD symptoms in newly diagnosed adult patients. Fifty-four participants underwent baseline fMRI and Wender-Reimherr-Interview (WRI) assessment at diagnosis (t1) and clinical follow-up about three years later (t2). WRI scores decreased from t1 to t2. Higher baseline symptom load correlated with lower NAc-right paracingulate gyrus FC. Greater symptom improvement over time correlated with lower NAc-right anterior insular cortex FC. Among patients still taking stimulants at t2, higher NAc-right posterior insular cortex FC predicted better outcome; among those not taking medication, higher FC predicted worse outcome. Treated and non-responder groups did not differ significantly in motion. The authors conclude that FC between the reward system and the default mode and salience networks correlates with ADHD clinical course and medication response, with potential as a biological marker, while noting limitations including small sample size.

A Utah audit found the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control overcharged businesses $1,161 and lost $186 after seven items were incorrectly marked up. The department plans refunds and has added a computer program to flag incorrect markups. Auditors also found it failed to transfer $4.6 million in required revenue in November 2017, which it later corrected.

The Aedes aegypti mosquito, recently associated with Zika, also spread yellow fever in 1793 Philadelphia after a hot, dry summer and Caribbean refugees arrived. Symptoms included fever, bleeding, vomiting, and yellow skin; about 5,000 people died, and many including Washington fled. Doctors led by Benjamin Rush tried bloodletting, smoke, and quarantine without success. More than a century later, mosquitoes were identified as the vector, leading to sanitation, drainage, and public education efforts. The last North American outbreak was in New Orleans in 1905. Since December 2016, Brazil has had its worst human yellow fever outbreak in decades, with 326 confirmed cases and 220 deaths, near Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo. An effective yellow fever vaccine exists and is recommended by WHO; Brazil requested doses. Penn researchers are developing Zika vaccines, using the yellow fever vaccine as a foundation.

Rachael Caplan has Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS), which causes constant severe pain and has left her bedridden and confined to the top floor of her parents’ home; she has not been outside since August 2016. CRPS is described as a relatively rare disease that begins like an autoimmune condition and progresses into a neurological disease with intense pain and other symptoms. Caplan first had symptoms in law school, faced delays in diagnosis, and has tried many treatments without success. Her friends and family are raising awareness through a Facebook page and an ice-water challenge with #AceThisFire, while green light therapy has improved her sleep. Caplan hopes sharing her story will lead to quicker diagnoses, more treatment options, or a cure.

Gulf Island Fabrication trades at a significant discount to book value, though its offshore markets are weak and its near-term outlook is challenging. Q4 was hurt by technical problems on two Hornbeck MPSVs, delaying delivery to 2019 and causing a $23.9 million loss; the company reported a $24.3 million quarterly loss on $37.3 million revenue. It has essentially no debt after drawing $10 million under a $40 million credit facility. Most backlog is in shipyards, including two MPSVs, eight brown water tugs, a research vessel, and an icebreaker-class vessel. SeaOne selected it as prime contractor for the CGL Caribbean Fuels Supply Project, expected to start mid-2018, and it received an EEW memorandum for an East Coast offshore wind project. It is selling Texas facilities: a $55 million option for South Yard and North Yard for sale; facilities and equipment are booked at about $100 million. With market capitalization around $120 million, the rest of the company implies about $30 million. The stated thesis is valuation, with potential contracts as a bonus; shares fell 40%, and $7 is cited as strong technical support.

QoCGM is presented as an open-source MATLAB tool for comprehensive continuous glucose monitoring data analysis. It processes preprocessed CSV CGM data through preprocessing and metric derivation stages, including duplicate removal, missing-period identification, PCHIP interpolation or removal of missing periods, and generation of a CSV of derived metrics. QoCGM requires inputs such as sampling frequency, sampling tolerance, end-of-night hour, unit conversion flag, plotting flag, and missing-data handling choice. Its metrics cover basic descriptive statistics, time-in-range, glycemic risk, glycemic variability, glycemic control, and entropy/complexity, including daytime/nighttime and day-to-day measures. In an example using DiaMonT trial data from 324 participants with insulin-treated T2DM over the first week, median glucose was 162 mg/dL, TIR was 65%, and CV was 24%; R² analysis showed overlap among many metrics, while some metrics had low R² values, and diurnal and nocturnal TIR metrics differed. Further research is required to explore clinical implications.

A decision on a new line will probably not be pressed to conclusion; negotiations will begin with the Allies controlling the outer world and materials essential to German reconstruction. European statesmen will seek recuperation. Demobilization risks insurrection or economic crisis unless raw materials, transportation, markets, and credit work; allocating these will be the strongest negotiating instrument. Access to sea-borne materials is more immediately important than the Baltic-Balkans-Persian Gulf belt. Germany’s Near East supremacy is seen as her victory, but the blockade is an overpowering difficulty; Mittel-Europa cannot be closed and needs outer-world supplies and regained markets. Two German imperialist schools agree on dominating eastern Europe and needing outer-world access but disagree on method: Kühlmann favors accommodation with western nations; the Fatherland Party favors military/naval power and retaining Belgium. Belgium is the pivot; control would prevent England landing in France and leave France at Germany’s mercy. Bethmann considered an administrative division of Belgium.

Dunkin' Donuts will launch fall-inspired foods and beverages on Aug. 28, returning pumpkin spice and adding maple, pecan, and bacon items, including pumpkin cream cheese and a limited-time maple sugar bacon breakfast sandwich. McDonald's and Starbucks have not announced this year's plans. Dunkin' has reported better-than-expected earnings for seven straight quarters, with new and limited-time products providing a boost.

Sarasota County petitioned the Department of Administration for a declaratory statement under Section 120.565, seeking to apply Chapter 380, the Florida Environmental Land and Water Management Act of 1972, to a proposed crude oil splitter in Manatee County. The Department issued a declaratory statement that the definition of a development of regional impact in Section 380.06(1) is limited by Fla.Admin.Code Rule 22F-2 under Section 380.06(2). No hearing was requested or held. The County sought review under Section 120.68. The court denied the petition for writ of certiorari, finding the County lacked standing because it was not a developer, regional planning agency, appropriate local government, or state planning agency authorized to initiate the DRI process. Boardman concurred specially, noting possible alternatives under Section 380.06(3) or Section 403.412. Scheb dissented, stating the declaratory statement was final agency action, that the Department incorrectly limited the DRI definition to presumed DRIs in Rule 22F-2, and that he would grant review and remand.

A player is fine and received a day off, usually day-to-day. In two Boston games, second periods were a problem; the team must improve and make every shift and period count. Two self-demanding players are playing better than their point total indicates but have been shut down; the speaker expects the tide to turn. Roberto and the group focus on one game at a time, will execute tomorrow’s plan, and call the hardest trophy physically taxing and demanding.

ICICI Bank said its mortgage loan portfolio crossed Rs 1.5 trillion, making it the largest private player, and it targets Rs 2 trillion by FY20 with 15% annual growth. The mortgage book is half of its Rs 3 trillion retail loan portfolio. It plans to expand digitisation and add 50% more loan processing centres. ICICI Bank has been under probe since March over a loan to Videocon; Chanda Kochhar was asked to go on leave.

SARS-CoV-2 vaccines reduced COVID-19 cases, hospitalisations, and deaths, but variant emergence, especially Omicron, reduced effectiveness against infection and transmission, while protection against severe outcomes was more durable. The passage describes a model inferring immune waning and boosting from clinical endpoints, fitted to national-level vaccine effectiveness estimates from England for AZD1222, BNT162b2, and mRNA-1273 against mild disease, hospitalisation, and death for Delta and Omicron BA.1/BA.2. The model estimates a 6.5-fold reduction in immunity against Omicron relative to Delta and predicts declining effectiveness over time, with mRNA-1273 generating the highest immune level, followed by BNT162b2 and AZD1222. It estimates Omicron hospitalisation effectiveness 180 days after boosting as 49.5% for AZD1222, 69.8% for mRNA-1273, and 63.7% for BNT162b2, with further declines after one year. Using immunogenicity data, it estimates the mRNA-1273.214 bivalent vaccine has a 1.61-fold increase in neutralizing antibody titres against BA.1 versus mRNA-1273; compared with original booster, it predicts little short-term difference in severe-outcome protection but less rapid decline over one year, with 77.9% hospitalisation effectiveness at 365 days versus 60.0% for the original vaccine. Limitations include inability to distinguish infection- and vaccine-induced immunity, lack of immunological measurements, difficulty classifying COVID-19 hospitalisations/deaths, and sensitivity to model assumptions.

New research surveying 2,000 British adults found the average Brit wakes three times nightly, with one in 10 waking 7–10 times. Cited reasons include toilet needs (47%), snoring (41%), partner space-taking (25%), discomfort (19%), bad dreams (11%), tossing/turning (10.5%), sleep talk/noises (10%), partner phone use (10%), anxiety (6%), and partner reading/TV (4.6%). Psychologist Robert Stewart attributes sleep quality to sleep hygiene and cycles, noting environment affects returning to sleep.

Larry Connors’ R3 strategy, from Chapter 4 of High Probability ETF Trading, is a mean-reversion strategy. Its rules require the close above the 200-day moving average, the 2-day RSI to drop three consecutive days with the first day’s drop from below 60, entry when the 2-day RSI is below 10, and exit when it is above 70. The aggressive version was not tested. Testing could not replicate Connors’ results 100%, with fewer fills. About 50% of strategies performed worse in the last 12 years. SPY had a 90% win ratio and 79 trades since 1993. The 25-ETF portfolio from 2000 to December 2020 had 992 trades, 75% win ratio, 0.68% average gain per trade, 2.08 profit factor, -16% maximum drawdown in August 2011, and 6.47% CAGR. QQQ/SPY with 50% allocation had a 3.37 profit factor, 2.69% CAGR, and 4.5% time in market. The passage concludes R3 still works after 12 years, is mean reversion, works best on equity markets, and may be improved.

Treasury bills of 91 and 182 days worth N62.4 billion are expected this week, offset by a same-amount rollover, while N168.1 billion OMO maturity is also expected. Afrinvest said CBN liquidity mop-up would affect liquidity and keep OBB and overnight rates in check. Financial system liquidity stayed negative last week; CBN mopped up N28.6 billion in OMO sales. OBB and overnight rates rose to 105.0% and 107.8% Wednesday, fell to 46.7% and 52.2% Thursday after N113.05 billion OMO maturity, and closed Friday at 55.8% and 59.3%. The FEC approved dollar-backed treasury instruments to reduce debt and extended tenors to two and three years, and approved the 2018-2020 MTEF with a $45 oil benchmark and N305/$ rate. The T-bills market closed bearish with average yield 18.5%. In forex, CBN auctioned $100 million SMIS; official rate was N305.55/$, NAFEX N365.91/$, NIFEX N365.20/$, and parallel N367/$. The bond market was bearish with average yield 16.8%. The I&E window attracted $4 billion from April, and the Bankers’ Committee said the economy was recovering.

Six Texas public university systems are reviewing curricula, syllabi and course descriptions as conservative Texas politicians target faculty who teach gender identity. After criticism of a children’s literature lesson on gender identity, Texas A&M demoted two administrators, pushed out its president, and ordered an audit of all courses, later extended systemwide. The University of North Texas, University of Texas, University of Houston and Texas Woman’s University systems also conducted or ordered reviews, some citing compliance with laws or executive orders stating there are only two sexes; the passage says no current federal or state laws prohibit public university professors from teaching about transgender identity. It is unclear whether courses will be censored or removed. Conservative politicians have found professors through online syllabi and course information; some Texas institutions’ Simple Syllabus pages are public under HB 2504. A University of Houston lecturer was targeted by a conservative news site after it used Simple Syllabus, and faculty are discussing syllabus privacy and detail.
In Earl Ringo v. Donald Roper, the Eighth Circuit denied rehearing en banc and panel rehearing; Judge Bye would grant en banc rehearing, and Judge Benton did not participate.

Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by high blood glucose due to insufficient insulin production or insulin resistance. COVID-19 vaccination reduces symptomatic infection, hospitalization, and mortality. In a longitudinal clinical trial, mRNA COVID-19 booster shots increased immune responses similarly in healthy, pre-diabetic, and diabetic subjects, but elevated HbA1c, HOMA-IR, triglyceride, and TyG in pre-diabetic and diabetic subjects, indicating aggravated insulin resistance. In mice, repeated COVID-19 vaccination impaired glucose tolerance and insulin signaling; metformin alleviated vaccine-induced insulin resistance and rescued impaired insulin signaling without affecting SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, spike IgG, or sVNT levels. The study suggests boosters may weaken insulin sensitivity in pre-diabetic and diabetic patients and that metformin may be an adjunctive treatment for maintaining glucose control after COVID-19 vaccination.

Love in the Time of Chasmosaurs is an offbeat, educational dinosaur website. It contains factual reports from scientists and paleontologists, paleoart of prehistoric life, and reviews of books, toys, films and TV shows. It also covers museum visits with observations and photos. Active since 2009, it posts nearly weekly plus monthly dinosaur news round-ups. Its name appears to be a play on a novel title, and it has a mascot. The writer urges interested readers to visit.

Olivia Munn had a clear mammogram and no breast cancer symptoms, but a two-minute online lifetime risk assessment showed a 37% risk and led to her stage 1 breast cancer diagnosis at 43. Her mother, Kim Munn, also took the assessment and was diagnosed with stage 1 breast cancer in July 2025. Munn said the assessment should be standard care.

Hugh Jackman revealed he is being treated again for basal cell carcinoma, posting a bandaged-nose photo on social media. The common, rarely fatal skin cancer has been treated at least four times previously, first in 2013. His upcoming films Logan and The Greatest Showman remain scheduled.

Newly minted Progressive Conservative leader Doug Ford began his election campaign at the Toronto Congress Centre, where the event felt more like a rock concert. He entered to Survivor’s “Eye of the Tiger” as the crowd chanted “Doug, Doug, Doug,” after holding hands with wife Karla. Ford sought to unify a split party; defeated leadership candidate Christine Elliott embraced him, and rivals Caroline Mulroney and Tanya Granic Allen attended. Kory Teneycke was reported as campaign manager and Jeff Silverstein as communications manager. Ford said the opponent is Premier Kathleen Wynne and the Liberals, promised to end spending taxpayers’ money, and promised “a day of prosperity” for all Ontario. Attendees expressed confidence and noted difficulty ahead. The event resembled a FordFest.

Comic book creator Stan Lee was hospitalized after experiencing shortness of breath and an irregular heartbeat, but his representative said he was released, doing well, and feeling good. His latest public appearance was at the “Black Panther” premiere on Jan. 30.

Valeant, J. Michael Pearson, Pershing Square Capital Management and William Ackman entered a litigation management agreement covering a California class action and Allergan litigation. It splits the first $10 million in fees/expenses 50/50, includes Pershing forbearance and mutual release, and terminates Nov. 1, 2017 without a California settlement stipulation.

The speaker says big games require drawing on experience and preparation, with good habits and work ethic paying off; the stakes differ but the approach stays the same. Most teammates take optionals and like skating on game days except back-to-backs, though Billy Guerin might not like it. The speaker is excited but focused on routine and team play, not personal pressure, and says the group may be having its last morning skate together. He recalls minor hockey and the Joe Lamontagne tournament, calls reaching and winning the final a dream come true, and credits sacrifices by parents, coaches, teammates, and others. An injury—a knee jammed between Franzen’s hip and the dasher—left him unable to walk or skate much; he took one shift and pain pills but couldn’t risk playing against Datsyuk and Zetterberg. He notes Gonch’s third final, fans’ support, winning a fourth series on the road, and Pittsburgh fans’ loyalty after last year’s loss, finishing it off.

Severe storms spawned tornadoes across the Southeast on Monday night, damaging homes and downing trees. Forecasters warned the storms could threaten more than 29 million people with powerful tornadoes, damaging winds and large hail. Northern Alabama had power outages and at least three confirmed tornadoes; Limestone County reported roof damage, and Jacksonville State University reported major roof damage. Tornado warnings and a watch remained as the line moved east. Officials raised Alabama’s threat level, schools let out early, universities suspended operations, and the governor urged safety preparations.

This prospective study examined 101 patients with cardiomyopathy (43 dilated cardiomyopathy and 58 other cardiomyopathies) and 101 healthy controls. Inflammatory and oxidative stress markers measured included CRP, TNF-α, IL-6, NT-proBNP, MDA, and GPX. Cardiomyopathy patients had significantly higher CRP, TNF-α, MDA, GPX, and NT-proBNP than controls. In cardiomyopathy patients, TNF-α positively correlated with GPX and MDA, and NT-proBNP correlated with MDA and GPX. The passage concludes that inflammatory and oxidative stress indicators correlate in cardiomyopathy patients but not in normal cases, suggesting cross-talk between these processes in late-stage cardiomyopathy.

Premier Li Keqiang said China will further open its economy, increase access to services and manufacturing, lower import tariffs, and let foreign and domestic firms compete equally. He also said there will be no forced technology transfers and intellectual property rights will be better protected, amid concerns over a potential global trade war.

The passage is a correction of a 10 February 2017 Amadeus FiRe AG voting rights announcement. It states that BNP Paribas Investment Partners S.A. crossed or reached a threshold on 9 February 2017, with resulting total positions of 4.99% voting rights and 0% through instruments, totaling 5,198,237 voting rights; the previous notification was 5.003%. BNP Paribas Investment Partners Belgium S.A. is named as directly holding 3% or more voting rights.

Huntington University Hospital cardiac surgery patients often required blood transfusions, and a 2006 study cited lower six-month and 10-year survival after transfusion for AVR or CABG. The U.S. average transfusion rate was 48.9%, while HUH’s rate from 2011 to 2013 was around 71%. Dr. Frank Young led a blood conservation project at HUH’s Center for Cardiac Medicine to reduce blood product utilization by two-thirds by the end of 2014, bring rates to the national average, save $2.5 million annually, and save an additional 125 lives per year over 10 years. He faced challenges including surgeon autonomy, complex teaching-hospital structure, 20-person surgical teams, no formal authority over many team members, and practices in which surgeons were not always notified before transfusions. The Center had seven surgeons and over 900 heart surgeries annually. A Committee for Operational Excellence found that 51% of Center patients had bleeding-related complications and that 2013 AVR/CABG transfusions averaged 65%; direct costs from bleeding-related complications were nearly $8 million in 2013. Young identified autologous blood harvest and retrograde autologous priming as conservation techniques. Supporters included Anil Gupta, administrators, nurses, perfusion staff, cardiologists, and some surgeons; skeptics included veteran heart surgeons. Young had to decide where to start, whom to involve, how to persuade skeptics, and how to make changes stick.
Ajman's ruler reduced the tourism fee for hotels and tourism companies from 10% to 7%, effective immediately until December 31, to promote tourism and improve the investment environment.

This statistical analysis plan describes a multicenter study comparing dasiglucagon, placebo, and GlucaGen. Sample size is based on detecting a difference between dasiglucagon 0.6 mg and placebo using median time to plasma glucose recovery of 10 vs 50 minutes, with 90% power, 45-minute follow-up, and a 2-sided log-rank test at 5% significance; 20 patients are randomized to dasiglucagon, 10 to placebo, and 10 to GlucaGen. Analyses use summary tables, listings, and figures, generally two-sided at 0.05. Analysis sets include safety analysis set, full analysis set (FAS), and per protocol set (PPS). The primary efficacy endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as first increase of ≥20 mg/dL from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose, analyzed in FAS using Kaplan-Meier and stratified log-rank methods with sensitivity and supportive analyses. Secondary endpoints include recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes and plasma glucose changes from baseline. PK and PD analyses include plasma dasiglucagon/GlucaGen concentrations, PK metrics, plasma glucose, and AUE0-30min. Safety analyses cover exposure, local tolerability, adverse events/TEAEs, laboratory parameters, vital signs, ECG, and immunogenicity ADA.

Meb Faber’s Three-Way Momentum/Trend-Following Model Strategy invests equally in stocks, bonds, and gold when the monthly 3-bar moving average is above the 10-bar moving average. It returned 13% annually from 1971 to 2015. An updated backtest using GLD, SPY, and TLT from 2006 had an 8.9% CAGR, 57% win rate, 1.6 profit factor, and 18% maximum drawdown; since 2015, annual performance was 5.3%. With 1.5 leverage, returns were 13.1% and maximum drawdown was 26%. Nearby optimized settings produced similar results, suggesting the strategy is not curve fitted. The passage also describes momentum investing and states the strategy is still working and has been defensive during major downturns.

This passage defines soccer passing-direction terminology for the path a pass is expected to take from the passer to a potential receiver, usually when facing the attacking goal but applying in any direction. It lists clockwise general directions: forward angled right, right, back and right, back, back and left, left, and angled left. It also defines related terms such as forward/ahead, deep, downfield/down, down the line, forward/front, long, parallel, short, straight/straight ahead, upfield, angled, corner, diagonal, line, post, centering, flat, lateral, square, wide, back, behind, straight back, reverse, and left/right variants. Additional terms include angle of a pass, back heel, center, far post, horizontal axis, interface, near post, outlet, passing angle, possession, reverse field, straight lines, switch fields, and vertical axis.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 31, 2017, reporting that it issued a press release and data sheet regarding financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2016, attached as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. The filing was signed by CFO Luca Maestri.

Mark E. Haedicke requests removal from the State Bar of Michigan e-Journal email list. The included State Bar of Michigan e-Journal for Wednesday, October 25, 2000 contains case summaries for constitutional, criminal, family, litigation, malpractice, and worker’s compensation law; classified, fields of practice, and editorial sections; news and moves; bar events; and subscription, unsubscription, and contact information.

Samsung Galaxy J5 Prime launched in India at Rs 14,900 with a 5-inch HD TFT display, 13MP rear and 5MP front cameras, 1.4GHz quad-core processor, 3GB RAM, 32GB storage, dual-SIM 4G, 2400mAh battery, and metal unibody. It originally ran Android 6.0 Marshmallow and has begun receiving Android 7.0 Nougat OTA in UAE; imported Indian models might get it. The update adds features and bug fixes.

GA10x Ampere GPUs move ROPs into the GPC, increasing ROP count; GA102 has 112 ROPs versus TU102’s 96. The GA10x SM has four partitions, a 128 KB L1/shared subsystem, one third-generation Tensor Core per partition, and FP32 on both datapaths, allowing each partition to execute 32 FP32 or 16 FP32 and 16 INT32 operations per clock. Combined L1/shared memory is 33% larger, shared memory bandwidth is doubled, and Ampere is up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection testing over Turing, add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit for motion blur, and support concurrent RT with graphics or compute. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32, BF16, and structured sparsity, with up to 2x matrix throughput. DLSS is enhanced with a 9x Super Resolution scaling factor for 8K60 gaming. GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/s, plus EDR. RTX IO works with DirectStorage for GPU-based lossless decompression, up to 100x I/O performance. The A40 data center GPU offers up to 2X FP32, 2X ray tracing, 5X (10X with sparsity) AI, 48GB memory and NVLink scaling; A6000 has 10,752 CUDA cores and 48GB. Display supports 4K120/8K60, HDMI 2.1, DSC; NVDEC adds AV1 decode, and NVENC supports 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

U.S. stocks fell sharply Friday, with the Dow dropping more than 650 points, or 2.5 percent, below 26,000. The S&P 500 fell 2.2 percent and the Nasdaq Composite declined 2 percent, capping the Dow’s worst week in two years. Investors sold off on fears that a stronger-than-expected jobs report would prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates more than expected. January added 200,000 jobs versus 190,000 expected, with wage growth of 2.9 percent. Trump’s Twitter feed was silent Friday on the downturn and instead highlighted the jobs report.

Peloton launched AI-powered fitness equipment, including refreshed bikes and treadmills plus a new rowing machine, with an AI coaching system called Peloton IQ. It also raised product prices and increased monthly membership fees to $49.99. The company has faced post-pandemic challenges, leadership changes, layoffs, a recall fine, and a stock decline; its shares fell 3.67% on launch day.

RaySearch and Eckert & Ziegler BEBIG signed a partnership to integrate RayStation and RayCare with BEBIG brachytherapy systems, enabling a complete brachytherapy solution. Brachytherapy uses radioactive implants to deliver higher radiation doses to smaller areas, commonly treating prostate and other cancers.

The 48-inch LG C4 OLED is at its lowest seen price on Amazon, $800, for Prime Day; the 65-inch model is $1,300. The C4 offers OLED picture performance, HDR brightness, up to 144-Hz VRR gaming features, webOS, a magic remote, and a slim design.

Phlogopite is described as a layered dark mica used in industrial and research applications and studied for its response to ionizing radiation. The passage reports simulations with XTANT-3, combining tight-binding molecular dynamics, transport Monte Carlo, and Boltzmann collision integrals to model electronic and atomic dynamics under a 92 eV, 10 fs pulse at various doses. Calculated DOS and a bandgap of 7.5 eV, shrinking to ~6.5 eV at room temperature, validate the tight-binding parameterization. At ~0.17 eV/atom (Te~11,000 K), hydrogen first detaches and migrates; this is close to an experimental dose converted to ~0.2 eV/atom. Electron-phonon coupling cools electrons and increases the damage threshold relative to Born-Oppenheimer simulations. At ~0.4 eV/atom, Mg becomes liquid-like while other sublattices remain stable, forming a superionic state. At ~0.5 eV/atom the lattice disorders at different rates; at ~0.9 eV/atom the bandgap collapses and a liquid metallic state forms. At ~2 eV/atom, nonthermal acceleration heats atoms on femtosecond timescales, especially K and O, leading to complete disorder. The passage also estimates damage threshold fluences for future X-ray experiments and suggests various transient states can be tuned by irradiation dose.

The lecture discusses real estate decision-making in Winthrop Center, Cornell Tech, and 425 Park Avenue. For Winthrop Center, market signals showed Boston CBD buyers did not price a green premium; State Street chose 1 Congress over Winthrop due to floor plate, condo-focused design, and rent premium. Winthrop had 0% pre-leasing before construction, lost State Street, and faced HSBC pulling debt during COVID, pausing construction about three months before a Kuwait-based fund financed a $700 million loan. Cornell Tech was cited as a 250,000-square-foot Passive House project that de-risked Winthrop. A study found Passive House cost premiums of 1%–8%, with Winthrop at 1%. Boston/Massachusetts and tenants were described as beneficiaries, with BERDO 2.0, building codes, and MEPA mentioned.

For 425 Park Avenue, L&L considered a 670,000-square-foot office plus 18,000-square-foot retail project in 2012, with a ground lease, cash drain, requirement to retain 25% of the existing structure, and an 8% cost premium. It targeted health and wellness, comparing ventilation/filtration, WELL, Fitwell, and LEED. Costs included $12.3 million initial and $3.9 million operating increases; case projections reached 2%–6% premium and a 5% rent premium. Diffusion of innovation, Crossing the Chasm, leasing strategy, and tenant/LP-GP incentives were discussed. Citadel signed 200,000 square feet and later extended to 300,000; the building set a record NYC office lease price but later faced distress, delayed over a year, $100 million cost, and wiped-out equity before Blackstone salvaged it. The lecture ends with flight-to-quality demand trends.

Lecture 16 covers utility from beliefs, anticipatory utility, information acquisition, and learning. It explains that anticipatory utility can affect when people consume or act and whether they seek information, with negative information such as Huntington’s disease sometimes avoided to feel better. A model imposes correct beliefs conditional on available information; concave utility from beliefs implies information aversion, while convex implies information-loving. If beliefs can be manipulated, people may prefer overly positive beliefs unless outcomes depend on beliefs, incorrect beliefs distort decisions, or disappointment and reference points matter. Evidence includes Weinstein’s measures of overoptimism, rosy beliefs about marriage, business success, smoking risks, and abilities, and MIT survey findings on under-confidence, especially among women. Ego utility, positive illusions, mental health, and depressive realism are discussed. Biases increase for personally important, ambiguous, or controllable prospects, and decrease with imminent objective feedback. Experiments by Eil and Rao, Mobius et al., and Zimmermann address asymmetric updating and motivated memory; real-world evidence includes overconfident investors and managerial hubris. Bayesian learning is difficult, so people use heuristics and show gambler’s fallacy, hot-hand fallacy, base-rate neglect, belief in the law of small numbers, representativeness, and availability biases. These can affect judges, umpires, loan officers, and tests, with different policy implications depending on whether people miss information, hold wrong theories, dislike learning, or learn poorly.

The speaker says the team was a step behind and lacked offense, physicality, speed, defense, and special-teams play, citing two playoff games as unsatisfactory. He expresses confidence in goaltender Michael, notes better home play and some road letdowns, and declines to comment on lineups or Chicago’s goalie. He discusses Chicago’s early pressure and late-period goals, past painful playoff losses, coaching motivation, player professionalism, Mike Richards, Jeff’s injuries and expected contribution, and the need to play a good game tomorrow.

The speaker says Oskar and Barbie are underrated, hardworking, and have good timing, and that his line has good chemistry and communication. He says the team has improved each series, wants to keep improving, and views the next game as a best-of-three opportunity. After the prior game, he says they returned to structure, were more composed, and got big stops from Binner, but still need to improve in every facet.

Lasers are sensitive to defects, mirror alignment, and other details that reduce efficiency. Increasing power can introduce new colors, destabilize output, and distort the beam profile. Topological insulators have an insulating bulk but conducting surface states in which electrons moving in one direction have a fixed spin orientation; reversing direction requires a spin flip, which is difficult, so surface electrons flow with minimal resistance despite defects. The passage proposes using analogous protected states for light in a laser. Researchers used rings of optical waveguides that can emit or absorb light. Depending on how the rings are excited and interconnected, light can be confined to the edge and scattered only if it changes color; protected light is then amplified by laser gain. Experiments compared protected and unprotected edge states. The protected-state laser could lose rings and keep operating, was more efficient, and did not show new colors as power increased, unlike the unprotected laser. Such specific-color lasers are described as critical for 5G networks and space-based interferometers.

Security for Super Bowl LII in Minneapolis involves two years of planning and coordination among federal, state, and local agencies, led by the Minneapolis Police Department. US Bank Stadium’s downtown location and nearby events complicate security. Measures include increased police presence, tactical gear, bomb-sniffing dogs, choppers, fencing, indoor prescreening, and stadium screening starting over four hours before the game. The FBI leads counterterrorism, threat assessments, and credential checks for possibly more than 30,000 people.
