President Andrew Johnson appointed William W. Holden provisional governor of North Carolina. The proclamation cites the Constitution’s guarantee of a republican form of government, the President’s duties as Commander in Chief and chief civil executive, and the rebellion having deprived North Carolina of civil government. Holden is to prescribe rules for convening a convention of loyal delegates to alter or amend the state constitution, restore North Carolina’s constitutional relations to the federal government, and present a republican state government. Delegates and electors must have taken the amnesty oath from the May 29, 1865 proclamation and been qualified voters under North Carolina law before May 20, 1861. The proclamation directs military and naval officers to assist Holden and directs various federal departments and officials to enforce applicable laws and appointments within the state. It is dated May 29, 1865.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed the district court’s dismissal of plaintiffs’ 42 U.S.C. § 1983 civil rights complaint. Defendants were involved in a child abuse investigation by New Mexico Human Services that transferred custody of Charles Meeker’s four minor daughters. The district court dismissed: service was invalid for four defendants; res judicata barred claims against all defendants except Grout because of prior federal and state suits; and Grout, the guardian ad litem, was dismissed for failure to state a claim and because Grout did not act under color of state law. The court addressed only Charles Meeker’s appeal, holding he could not represent his daughters, and affirmed, adopting the district court’s reasoning and holding a guardian ad litem is not a state actor under § 1983.

The Missouri Court of Appeals affirmed the circuit court’s summary judgment for defendants Bank of St. Louis, Joseph A. Trotcha, and Harold Rathman in Harvey F. Euge’s malicious prosecution action. Euge sought damages, alleging defendants caused his indictment and conviction for obtaining money by a bogus check; that conviction was later reversed by the Missouri Supreme Court. The appellate court held that the conviction created a presumption of probable cause, which Euge did not overcome, and that the undisputed facts established probable cause as a matter of law. It also stated that the reversal based on a narrow statutory construction did not eliminate probable cause.

The passage introduces video object segmentation-aware audio generation, a task for generating audio focused on a specified region in a video. It proposes SAGANet, built on MMAudio, which extends a pretrained multimodal audio model with a segmentation-aware control module using text, video, and video object segmentation masks. The module combines global video and focal crop streams with mask embeddings and gated cross-attention; optional LoRA fine-tuning is also explored. The authors introduce Segmented Music Solos, a dataset of 5-second solo instrument clips with sounding-object masks derived from MUSIC21, AVSBench, and Solos, and use URMP for testing. They report that SAGANet, trained on single-source samples, generalizes to multi-source scenes and improves all evaluated metrics over the base model, with the greatest improvement in temporal synchronization. Ablation results indicate both global and local visual information are important. The passage concludes that the approach improves semantic relevance and temporal alignment and supports more controllable Foley models.

Britain's FTSE 100 closed up 0.6 percent at 7,353.89, recovering from a three-month low, while mid caps rose 0.8 percent. Banks rose 0.8 percent and miners 1.7 percent. TUI gained 4.8 percent to an all-time high after a Credit Suisse upgrade. Experian and G4S fell after Morgan Stanley downgrades. Shell ended flat and BP fell 0.4 percent as oil retreated.

A senior Iranian Revolutionary Guards commander said the Guards were ready to implement a policy preventing regional oil exports if the US banned Iranian oil sales, after President Hassan Rouhani appeared to threaten disrupting neighboring countries’ oil shipments. The US withdrew from a multinational nuclear deal in May and told countries to halt Iranian oil imports by Nov. 4 or face financial measures. An Iranian oil official said the pressure would raise prices and hurt the US economy. Rouhani said Iran would remain in the nuclear deal without the US if remaining signatories guaranteed Iran’s benefits; foreign ministers were to meet Friday in Vienna.

Tom Petty, 66, died last week after a cardiac arrest; his cause of death was deferred pending further tests after autopsy. His family agreed to switch off life support after learning he had no brain activity. Tributes followed, and he had hits with the Heartbreakers and Traveling Wilburys.

The Gretna Trust & Savings Bank, as dative testamentary executor of Priscilla Lewis’s succession, sued David Lewis to recover $505.58 allegedly withdrawn from the deceased’s bank account after her death, and also claimed rent. David Lewis admitted the withdrawal but claimed he was a creditor of the estate and denied owing rent. The trial court dismissed the suit. The Court of Appeal found the account was in the mother’s name and the money was withdrawn after her death, held the withdrawal illegal because a creditor cannot take succession assets to satisfy a claim, and found the rent claim not proved. The judgment was reversed, with $505.58 plus legal interest and costs awarded to the executor.

The passage presents a method for robots to model, reason about, and explain differences between competing plans. It addresses two research questions: how robots can model and reason about what differentiates plans, and how they can use an ontological model to explain those differences. The work conducts an ontological analysis and extends the OCRA ontology, inheriting DUL, to formalize plan qualities such as cost, makespan, and number of tasks, as well as relations for comparing qualities and plans, including better, worse, and equivalent. Plans are instantiated using ROSPlan knowledge and compared through logical rules implemented in Knowrob/Prolog. It also introduces ACXON, extending XONCRA/AXON, to retrieve divergent knowledge and construct textual contrastive explanatory narratives at different specificity levels. Evaluation uses IPC planning domains and compares ACXON with AXON using metrics for number of attributes, communication time, and readability. ACXON reduces knowledge tuples and interaction times, especially at specificity levels 2 and 3, while readability is similar or more complex. A modification is proposed to restrict knowledge retrieval to selected aspects, shortening narratives and allowing more personalized explanations. The conclusion states the approach is general and outperforms the baseline, with future work on language accessibility and user studies.

The RSPCA investigated 2,902 animal cruelty complaints in Nottinghamshire in 2017, about eight daily and down about 8% from 3,157 in 2016. Examples included two four-month-old kittens beaten to death, leading to a 20-week jail sentence, and 40 animals kept in stacked cages; five dogs were put down and a puppy died. Most complaints concerned dogs (1,702), then cats (737) and horses (281). Nationally, 141,760 animal welfare complaints were investigated in 2017. An RSPCA chief inspector said the complaints show animals need daily help and urged the public to report concerns.

The article examines the relationship between Treasury liquidity and the stock market and the saying “Sell in May and come back in November.” A chart shows US Treasury cash balances from 2006–2017 with recurring peaks around January D23, May D89, and November D198. May involves tax refunds, often received by wealthy people and saved in stocks, bonds, and real estate, potentially causing a stock market pop; November involves Fed Treasury buybacks, giving ex-bondholders money to invest, causing another pop. February and November open market operations are less consistent. The article concludes liquidity spikes largely explain the saying, May is the most consistent spike due to tax refunds, and Feb/Nov spikes relate to Fed open market operations maintaining the veil over government money creation. Tax law changes could make May 2018 and 2019 strong.

A Karolinska Institutet study of 27,500 middle-aged and older UK Biobank participants used MRI and machine learning to estimate brain age. Sleep quality was scored from self-reported chronotype, sleep duration, insomnia, snoring, and daytime sleepiness. The gap between brain age and chronological age widened by about six months per 1-point decrease in healthy sleep score; poor sleepers’ brains appeared about one year older on average. Low-grade inflammation explained just over 10% of the association. Researchers say poor sleep may contribute to accelerated brain aging, and because sleep is modifiable it might help prevent cognitive decline, though dementia causality is unclear. Limitations include a healthier-than-general UK sample and self-reported sleep.

The Directorate General of Goods and Services Tax Intelligence has sent notices to many banks demanding taxes on free or bundled services to account-holders meeting minimum balance norms; the demand could exceed Rs 6,000 crore. Banks are likely to challenge it. If upheld, customers may suffer as banks pass on charges, and the demand is retrospective for over five years. The passage calls the demand ham-fisted and says it perpetuates tax terror.

The passage reviews cosmic shear measurements from KiDS, DES, and HSC, which have established weak lensing as a competitive cosmological probe and achieved percent-level measurements of S8. It notes that Ωm and σ8 are degenerate in lensing alone and require additional data, and that cosmic shear precision is mainly limited by intrinsic alignment (IA) and baryonic feedback; the paper focuses on IA. Unaccounted-for IA can bias cosmological parameters by 4–5σ, and inaccurate IA models can impair inference. IA models discussed include NLA, density-weighted NLA, tidal torque, TATT, halo model, and effective field theory. Observations suggest red bright galaxies are strongly aligned, blue galaxies are consistent with no alignment, and survey selection complicates generalization. The paper presents a pipeline infusing NLA, extended-NLA, and TT models on the same large N-body simulation, introduces extended-TT, couples cosmic tidal fields with HOD galaxies, and uses SkySim5000 to study IA, source clustering, and non-Gaussian lensing statistics. It also describes cosmic shear statistics: γ-2PCF via the Limber approximation and CosmoSIS with LSST Year-1 redshift distributions, and non-Gaussian statistics measured on convergence or aperture mass maps using Kaiser-Squires inversion and Healpix.

Tesla, Inc. filed Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2019. As of September 30, 2019, Tesla reported total assets of $32,795 million, total liabilities of $25,313 million, total stockholders’ equity of $6,040 million, and cash and cash equivalents of $5,338 million. For the three months ended September 30, 2019, total revenues were $6,303 million and net income was $150 million, with net income attributable to common stockholders of $143 million. For the nine months ended September 30, 2019, total revenues were $17,194 million and net loss was $907 million, with net loss attributable to common stockholders of $967 million. The filing covers two reportable segments, automotive and energy generation and storage, and includes notes on revenue recognition, leases, business combinations, debt, inventory, property, and related financial matters. As of October 21, 2019, 180,244,858 shares of common stock were outstanding.

The passage welcomes Israeli and Palestinian leaders on behalf of the United States and Russia, cosponsors of the Middle East peace process. It recalls past peace efforts at Camp David and Madrid and thanks Norway for nurturing the agreement. It notes that Israel and the PLO will sign a declaration of principles on interim Palestinian self-government. It pledges U.S. support for the difficult work ahead, acknowledges enemies of peace, and stresses the importance of the region’s next generation.
A 14-year-old girl was arrested after a tantrum over a nonworking phone, charged with mischief, and released to her mother with conditions and a future court date.

Oil fell further below US$56 a barrel after an API report showed U.S. crude inventories rose 9.9 million barrels, signaling ample supply despite OPEC’s record compliance with supply cuts. Brent was down 35 cents at US$55.62; U.S. crude fell 36 cents to US$52.84. Analysts expected the EIA to report a 3.5 million-barrel rise, and a strong dollar also pressured oil.

Restoration Affiliates (RA) was formed in 2011 by Rich Piltch of ARS, Damon Gersh, Ras Fenger, and Andy Goldberg as an equal, collaborative partnership among smaller regional restoration and reconstruction firms. Guided by ARS’s Go-Giver philosophy, RA sought to help members compete with national players such as Belfor by offering national coverage while retaining local expertise. By fall 2013, RA had 21 members with combined $300 million in revenue. It was structured as an LLC with equal shareholders and a nine-person board, and had membership requirements, dues, referral fees, and operating expectations. The passage discusses the restoration industry, RA’s formation and bylaws, its Forest City contract, and unresolved strategic questions including administrator authority, communication and transparency, standards, referral fees, internal competition, software, pricing, and marketing.

The passage introduces a general, uniform method for codensity presentations of monads based on the principle “Codensity Monads = Density + Duality.” It reviews monads, algebraic categories, dual adjunctions, dense functors, Kan extensions, and codensity monads. The main technical notion is a codensity setting, consisting of an adjunction L ⊣ R, an equivalence E, a dense functor G, and a commuting-up-to-isomorphism square RGop ≅ FE. Theorem 3.2 states that in every codensity setting, the codensity monad of F exists, is pointwise, and is isomorphic to the monad induced by L ⊣ R, RL ≅ CodyF. The paper applies this theorem to derive known and new codensity presentations for ultrafilter and filter monads, double dualization monads, Isbell duality, Vietoris and lower Vietoris monads, the sobrification monad, and probability monads including the expectation monad, Giry monad, Radon monad, Kantorovich monad, and semiring-valued measures. It argues this approach reduces codensity proofs to choosing a suitable dual adjunction and using known density results. Future work includes formal monad theory, monad extensions, and further Vietoris-related examples.

The passage commemorates Henry Clay, describing his birth on April 12, 1777, in Hanover County, Virginia; his father’s early death; and his limited but continued education. It recounts his legal practice in Lexington, Kentucky, and his offices, including Kentucky legislator, U.S. senator, U.S. representative, Speaker, commissioner to negotiate a peace treaty in 1814, Secretary of State, and U.S. senator until shortly before his death. It states he was a presidential candidate in 1824 and was defeated, and was again defeated in 1832 and 1844. It credits him with leading roles in the War of 1812, the Missouri question, Nullification, and slavery-related compromise measures, and with devotion to the Union and human liberty. It notes his eloquence and influence, that he opposed slavery while owning slaves, supported gradual emancipation, and was president of the American Colonization Society. It includes an adopted journal eulogy after his death in Washington and says the nation mourns him. The passage concludes that his life is closed and expresses hope that Providence will provide future leaders.
The passage is a collection of quotations attributed to various figures on taxation, debt, banking, corporations, patriotism, mistakes, and education.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting that on January 30, 2017, it entered into an Underwriting Agreement with several underwriters for the issuance and sale of notes including 1.850% Notes due 2020, 2.400% Notes due 2022, 2.875% Notes due 2024, 3.300% Notes due 2027, 4.100% Notes due 2037, 4.250% Notes due 2047, and 4.500% Notes due 2057. The notes will be issued under a base indenture and a twelfth supplemental indenture, pay interest semi-annually, and be senior unsecured obligations. The filing includes exhibits and was signed February 3, 2017.

A visiting Harvard Law School professor, Carlos Portugal Gouvêa, was arrested Oct. 1 for firing a pellet gun near a Jewish temple during Yom Kippur and told police he was hunting rats. He was placed on administrative leave, charged, and police and synagogue officials said antisemitism was not believed to be a factor.

Jacob Hackin became the first person in Cambridge prosecuted for dog fouling after failing to pay a fixed penalty notice for not clearing up at Midsummer Common. He pleaded guilty and was fined £75, plus £125 costs and a £30 victim surcharge. The council said owners must clear up after their dogs.

Prosecutors say former CIA case officer Kevin Mallory, 60, betrayed his country by giving a Chinese spy human-asset and other top-secret information for $25,000. Defense lawyers say he was a loyal American who fed the Chinese phony documents to expose their intelligence operation. Opening statements began Wednesday. Prosecutors said an April 2017 O’Hare screening found $16,500 in undeclared cash, and later searches found secret and top-secret documents on discs and a Samsung phone showing texts. Defense said Mallory contacted CIA contacts in February 2017. CIA witnesses testified about that contact. Mallory faces up to life in prison.

Kelly Keefe will become president of ERC on Jan. 1, becoming the first woman to lead the Highland Heights-based HR services provider in its 97-year history. She succeeds Pat Perry, president for nearly 20 years, who will remain as chairman supporting the transition and focusing on NorthCoast 99, ERChealth and client relations. Keefe, currently ERC’s vice president of training, consulting and coaching services and an almost 13-year employee, previously spent eight years at Deloitte.

This application claims priority as a continuation of earlier U.S. patent applications and describes virtual object machine learning. The system uses 3D models with rigging and metadata to programmatically generate labeled synthetic training images by varying poses or gestures, model textures, environmental backgrounds and lighting, and virtual camera positions. A machine learning engine trains a classifier to detect objects, key points, poses, and gestures, and the system may be used in a messaging system to analyze images and apply annotations. The passage further describes messaging system components, message structures, ephemeral access processes, databases, software architecture, and machine components.

Upgrade blends sci-fi, horror, and action in the near future. After Grey Trace is paralyzed in an attack, he receives STEM, a processor that lets him move with mechanical precision, and seeks revenge. The film explores artificial intelligence and unchecked technology’s dangers through violent action and a central mystery, though its reveal is predictable and its 95-minute runtime could have been longer. It is described as a must-see and Whannell’s best since Saw.

The President transmits to Congress correspondence between agents of the Hawaiian or Sandwich Islands and the Secretary of State. The islands are of interest because their inhabitants are progressing in civilization, they are important for refitting and provisioning vessels, and they are a stopping place for ships crossing the Pacific, especially U.S. whaling vessels. Their government is emerging from barbarism, still feeble, but appears just and pacific and seeks improvement. The U.S. seeks no exclusive control and wants their independent existence respected, and the President recommends a moderate allowance for the U.S. consul there.

The President also reports that English military operations against China ended in a treaty opening Amoy, Foo-Choo-Foo, Ningpo, and Chinghai to British merchants; it is unclear whether U.S. commerce will be admitted. U.S. trade with China is large and growing, and China may be ending its nonintercourse policy. The President recommends appropriating compensation for a commissioner to reside in China to protect American citizens and property and conduct intercourse with Chinese authorities.

Sen. John McCain criticized President Trump for approving the release of the GOP-Nunes memo, calling it a partisan attack on the FBI and Justice Department. He urged officials to stop viewing Robert Mueller’s investigation through politics, saying undermining the rule of law does Putin’s job. Democrats decried the memo and sought their own memo.

In Freeman v. Polstein, a broker sued the purchaser for a commission. The plaintiff failed to bring about a sale; another broker procured an accepted offer. With no proof of a special contract making the purchaser liable for commissions, the judgment was reversed and a new trial granted.

Thabane Sigadla, 24, of KwaDabeka, received an effective 38-year sentence for carjacking, unlicensed firearm and ammunition; he was linked to 2016 and 2017 hijackings and convicted by Pinetown Regional Court.

Azerbaijani Health Ministry spokesperson Safaya Ahmadova said the US State Department’s recommendation against surgery in Azerbaijan and to bring prescription medicine is unrelated to the country’s healthcare. She said tuberculosis figures fall yearly, confirmed by the Global Fund, and foreigners receive treatment in Azerbaijan.

The paper proposes AI-Noether, an abductive reasoning system for reconciling derived scientific hypotheses or formulae with background theory when both are expressible as polynomial equations. Given axioms and a hypothesis not implied by them, the system seeks candidate additional axioms, with smallest residual, that would explain the hypothesis. Its method has three steps: Encode the solution set as ideals/varieties; Decompose it via primary decomposition into irreducible components; and Reason by extracting generators and testing whether adding a generator allows derivation of the hypothesis, using Gröbner basis elimination. It returns candidate missing axioms or certifies failure. The paper states this is the first work studying abductive reasoning in scientific discovery with fully general polynomial axioms. Tests include systems from AI Hilbert and a recent paper. It recovers missing axioms in single-axiom tests across several physical theories, and in multiple-axiom tests success rates range from 25–60%, with most failures when three axioms are missing in larger systems. A theorem gives a sufficient criterion for recovering missing axioms. The conclusion states AI-Noether bridges AI-driven scientific discoveries and existing knowledge for real polynomials, demonstrates effectiveness on laws including Kepler’s Third Law and the Carrier-Resolved Photo-Hall effect, and suggests future work on non-polynomial laws such as ODEs or PDEs and new data-driven discoveries.

Nanyang Polytechnic scientists, including Dr Henry Leung, have found a more sustainable way to turn coffee waste into biodegradable plastic. Water and bacteria are added to coffee waste; after seven to 10 days, the bacteria produce PHA, which is extracted and used to make biodegradable plastic. The team uses Cupriavidus necator, modified bacteria, and eco-friendly solvents, achieving over 50% purity and about 1g to 3g of PHA per 100g of coffee waste. Lab experiments begun in 2013 are complete; the team seeks industrial partners and aims to commercialise in three to five years. PHA decomposes faster and releases fewer toxic compounds than PVC.

The passage is a STAT biotech news roundup. It asks which biotechs are affected by the government shutdown, notes a fourth-quarter events guide, and reports that patient advocacy groups asked the U.K. antitrust regulator to investigate drugmakers’ investment halts. It is partly exclusive to STAT+ subscribers and lists headlines on shutdown furloughs, pharma tariffs, Pfizer pricing, women’s health, Leucovorin, Tylenol, FDA criticism, MoonLake, Lilly, Amgen, and biotech stock-moving events.

Gary G. Kehde was discharged by Dubuque Packing Company after a supervisor found him holding a lit marijuana cigarette on company premises. He filed for unemployment benefits; Dubuque Pack protested, and the Department denied benefits for misconduct. After the appeal board affirmed, Dubuque Pack withdrew its protest, but the appeal board refused to give effect to the withdrawal. On judicial review, the district court reversed and ordered benefits. The Iowa Supreme Court reversed. It held the district court had jurisdiction because an application for rehearing under section 96.6(8) is not a prerequisite to judicial review. It also held the Department’s refusal to permit withdrawal of the protest was harmless because eligibility is determined from the facts, and withdrawal did not alter them. Finally, substantial evidence supported disqualification for misconduct based on Kehde’s deliberate possession of a lit marijuana cigarette on company premises, a serious misdemeanor that created safety concerns and violated employer expectations. The case was reversed and remanded.

A regulation American football field measures 120 yards long and 53.3 yards wide, or 360 by 160 feet, covering about 1.32 acres. The playing field between the end zones is 100 yards long; each end zone is 10 yards deep. Goal lines are 100 yards apart, yard lines are marked every yard, and numbers generally appear every 10 yards. Hash marks help spot the ball and differ by level: NFL 18 feet 6 inches apart, college 40 feet, high school 53 feet 4 inches. Numbers are placed 12 yards from the sideline in the NFL, 9 in college, and 6 in high school. Sidelines are 6 feet wide, and coaches are commonly restricted between the 25-yard lines.

Industry-sponsored clinical trials are excessively complex, increasing duration and burden on participants, staff, and sites. ICH E19 encourages reducing data collection, but little progress has been made. Copy-and-paste in schedule of assessments (SoA) design contributes to complexity. The Faro Smart Design Tool quantifies hours, burden, resources, costs, and complexity. Merck’s Lean Design rebuilds SoAs from Ground Zero using simplification principles. Workshops on six protocols from cardiovascular, other medical, psychiatry, and cancer areas recommended changes; most teams adopted some but not all, often due to late-stage development. Recommendations reduced participant hours by 4 to 47 per participant per trial and produced substantial cost and complexity savings, such as in a cardiovascular trial. Teams sometimes retained assessments due to FDA/regulatory concerns or asserted PRO/PK-PD changes could not be made. The passage concludes that rebuilding protocols from Ground Zero with quantitative feedback may substantially reduce inessential SoA elements, burdens, and costs; earlier use and leadership support are important, and generalizability should be tested.

The IMF described Ghana’s “Ghana beyond Aid” vision and the economy’s first year under President Akufo-Addo as an inspiration to Africa at the IMF/World Bank Spring Meetings. Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta outlined plans to fund the agenda through domestic resource mobilization, real-sector investment, jobs, and incomes, and said recent growth would be maintained.

From 2015, WebRTC VPN bugs leaked real IPs even when using VPN services, and providers sought solutions. On March 27, 2018, Stagno tested 124 VPNs and proxy providers; 20 leaked users’ IPs via WebRTC (16.13%), while 101 hid them. The passage lists leaking providers, links to a Google Docs complete list with logging policy information, notes the list is incomplete, provides IP leak test pages, advises disabling WebRTC or installing an add-on if leaks occur, and lists and ranks VPN services that can protect privacy.

MoviePass, despite customer service and other issues, offers value to movie lovers. It announced data showing its ticket purchases accounted for 13.21% of Roman J. Israel, Esq.’s domestic opening weekend box office and 10.00% of Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri’s, with percentages increasing in later weeks for Justice League, Coco, and The Snowman. MoviePass signed a marketing and performance-based revenue agreement with an undisclosed independent movie distribution company to provide active marketing for a title and earn revenue based on incremental ticket price increases. It will show ads, aiming to collect viewing data and target subscribers, as its CEO compared to Facebook or Google.

An improved non-occluding intravascular blood pump is described for reduced or minimal hemolysis. It includes a shroud with an inlet and outlet, an impeller sharing a central axis, a motor coupled to the impeller, and pillars coupling the motor to the shroud. Design features for reducing hemolysis include a trumpeted shroud with a larger inlet than outlet, elongated inlet, raked-back impeller leading edges, large bare hub length, matching pillar angle to outlet blade angle, matching impeller and stator flare angles, desired shroud-impeller clearance, and wrap angle. Testing and iterative CFD analysis identified shear-stress hotspots in the impeller, inflow shroud, and pillars. Prototype P_31, with extended shroud, 30° pillars, and modified impeller, showed reduced maximum and mean shear stress, lower predicted and experimental hemolysis potential, improved efficiency, and maintained hydraulic output compared with P_ref.

MRC Vaudreuil-Soulanges council sought to reassure residents that recyclables are valued despite reports of a global recycling crisis. China’s stricter rules have reduced acceptance of contaminated plastics and paper, concerning Canadian municipalities. The MRC is a Tricentris member; officials visited the Lachute sorting centre, and Hans Gruenwald said Tricentris is doing well and citizens should continue recycling and improving material quality.

In Mason Brothers & Tarlin v. United States, a reappraisement appeal concerned Christmas tree ornaments exported from Germany and imported at Boston. The parties stipulated similarity to the Woolworth Co. case and incorporated that record. The court found the ornaments freely offered in the Sonneberg-Lauscha district and held dutiable values were invoice unit prices plus 3% social assessments and specified packing-related costs when not included, as invoiced and reported dutiable. The appeal was dismissed as to other merchandise.

Asteroid 2025 TF, about 1 to 3 meters wide, passed over Antarctica on October 1 at 00:47:26 UTC, coming within 428 km of Earth. It was detected by the Catalina Sky Survey hours after the flyby and posed no danger. ESA’s Planetary Defence Office later observed it with the Las Cumbres Observatory, confirming its distance and timing with precision. Small asteroids are generally harmless, while larger ones can cause local to global effects. Worldwide surveys and planetary defense efforts monitor near-Earth objects.

This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to examine radiation damage in pure niobium at 300 K for PKA energies from 1 to 75 keV, comparing EAM, FS-1, FS-2, and SNAP interatomic potentials. It analyzes cascade evolution, subcascade formation, Frenkel pair production, defect clustering, maximum cluster sizes, and defect cluster morphology. All potentials show rapid defect production followed by recombination and stabilization, with surviving defects increasing with PKA energy and following a two-regime power law; subcascades begin around 20 keV. Vacancy clustering is high and robust across potentials, while interstitial clustering is lower and more sensitive to energy and potential. EAM produces a balanced mix of 1/2⟨111⟩ and 1/2⟨110⟩ loops, C15 rings, and hybrid structures, and has the highest vacancy clustering and largest vacancy clusters. FS-2 favors extended 1/2⟨111⟩ dumbbells, crowdions, and dislocation loops, with the largest interstitial clusters. FS-1 and SNAP generate more compact or disordered clusters; FS-1 produces ⟨110⟩ dumbbells/crowdions and small C15 rings, while SNAP produces a high fraction of C15-like rings up to nine atoms that may evolve into 1/2⟨111⟩ and ⟨100⟩ dislocation loops. The study concludes that interatomic potential choice significantly affects defect formation, clustering, and morphology, and that high-energy cascade behavior cannot be explained by |S/R|, TDE, or formation energies alone once subcascades form.

Big win gives confidence and advantage by forcing adjustments. Four or five days off is enough; extra time after San Jose win was good. Day-to-day player is key on faceoffs and penalty kills. Opponent is big, strong, makes plays, sees ice well, tough; reaching potential is key.

Live Nation is offering $20 all-in tickets to over 2,000 summer concerts during National Concert Week, April 30 through May 8, on its website. The promotion includes over 1.5 million tickets for genres such as comedy, country, hip-hop, Latin, metal, rock, and pop, featuring artists including Alan Jackson, Bon Jovi, Kevin Hart, Keith Urban, and Shakira.

Horsell Lodge near Woking offers residential and dementia care, from respite to long-term, with bespoke care and personal possessions encouraged. It advises checking suitability; page information is provided by the care home.

The passage compares the Google Pixel Watch 4 with the Apple Watch Ultra 3 as outdoor smartwatches. The Pixel Watch 4 costs $399 for the 45-mm version and $349 for the 41-mm case, while the Watch Ultra 3 costs about twice as much. Both have battery life lasting a full weekend and satellite communications requiring an active carrier plan and a clear sky. The Pixel Watch 4 offers satellite emergency services only in the contiguous US; the Watch Ultra 3 supports regular satellite texts and international satellite messaging. The Pixel Watch 4 is 5ATM, while the Watch Ultra 3 is 10ATM and can be used as a dive computer. The Pixel Watch 4 has a domed display, integrated bike computer, dual-band GPS, Google Maps offline maps, and Fitbit-based sleep and health tracking. Both have check-in, fall detection, and crash detection, though the Pixel Watch 4 did not detect a fall during testing. The passage states the Watch Ultra 3 is obviously the better adventure watch in most ways, but the Pixel Watch 4 has better and more useful health features and is much cheaper. It notes few outdoor watches under $500 offer satellite communications, and Garmin does not.

ML-assisted GWAS uses machine learning to impute missing phenotypes from observed variables and then performs GWAS on imputed phenotypes. The passage reports that current ML-assisted GWAS approaches treat imputed phenotypes as observed and can produce pervasive false-positive associations. In a UK Biobank T2D benchmark, GWAS on imputed T2D had replication failure rates of 81%, 69%, and 17% at thresholds 5e-8, 5e-6, and 0.05 versus ground truth; replication in DIAMENTE showed 48%, 39%, and 16%. High imputation quality and near-perfect genetic correlation did not guarantee validity. Existing methods are non-negative weighted sums of GWAS on observed and imputed phenotypes and require strong conditions for validity. The authors introduce POP-GWAS, a weighted sum of three estimators using imputed phenotype in unlabeled samples, observed phenotype in labeled samples, and imputed phenotype in labeled samples. POP-GWAS is reported to provide unbiased estimates, valid p-values, controlled type-I error, greater power than GWAS on observed phenotypes, minimal assumptions about imputation, and only GWAS summary statistics as input. It is described as the best linear unbiased estimator and is computationally efficient. Simulations and T2D benchmarking supported its validity and power. In DXA-BMD across 14 skeletal sites, POP-GWAS identified 188 independent loci versus 135 by conventional GWAS, including 89 novel loci, and revealed site-specific genetic architecture such as a head-specific LGR5 signal. The DXA-BMD GWAS was mainly restricted to European ancestry.

A Katsina Federal High Court ordered former Governor Ibrahim Shema remanded in EFCC custody until April 27 over alleged misappropriation of N5.7 billion SURE-P funds. He pleaded not guilty; his bail application will be heard April 27.

The passage discusses algebraic generalizations in computer science using semirings, including applications in decision, counting, and geometric problems. It defines semiring semantics for propositional, first-order, and existential second-order logic (PL=K, FO=K, ESO=K), along with satisfiability SAT=K. It presents BSSK machines over semirings and defines the complexity class NPK, polynomial-time reductions, and NPK-completeness. The main contributions extend prior work to existential second-order logic, proving analogues of Fagin’s and Cook’s theorems. It shows ESO=K ⊆ NPK and ESO=K = NPK, and generalizes the connection between the Boolean part of NPR and ETR from real numbers to positive and commutative semirings. It also states that the true existential theory of K is complete for the Boolean part of NPK, using a novel non-arithmetic reduction. The passage includes examples such as 4-FEAS≥0 and discusses semiring provenance for database queries.

This work addresses the difficulty of predicting mechanical and rheological properties of polymeric materials, since design parameters such as polymer concentration or molecular weight affect shear modulus G0, relaxation time τ, solution viscosity, and normal stress effects. It reports a method to design dilute viscoelastic Boger fluids with desired properties, using polyisobutylene (PIB) as polymer and polybutene/light mineral oil as solvent. Fabrication, gel permeation chromatography, and rheological measurements are described. The study characterizes the dilute-to-semi-dilute transition, finds solvent viscosity depends exponentially on polybutene weight fraction, and applies the Zimm model to identify G0, τ, and polymer-solvent interaction parameter χ; χ is treated as roughly constant. It measures scaling relationships between G0, τ, first normal stress difference coefficient ψ1, and δχ with concentration, molecular weight, and solvent viscosity, comparing theoretical and observed power laws. Because the experimental design matrix is invertible, the work introduces a framework to calculate fluid compositions for target G0, τ, and ψ1. Demonstrations fabricate fluids with independently varied G0 or τ and fluids with nearly constant ψ1 despite varied viscosity. The work concludes that this framework can design controlled Boger fluids, help decouple viscous and elastic effects, estimate molecular weight changes, and be extended to other flexible polymer systems.

Jason Day will face Louis Oosthuizen in a rematch of his 2016 final in the WGC-Match Play group stage in Texas, and will also play Jason Dufner and James Hahn. Marc Leishman was drawn with Branden Grace, Bubba Watson and Julian Suri. Cameron Smith faces Hideki Matsuyama, Patrick Cantlay and Yusaku Miyazato, needing a strong finish for a Masters invitation. An all-Australian final is possible.

Week 6 Idaho high school football left the top 15 largely intact, with top-ranked Bishop Kelly and No. 4 Eagle surviving scares to remain undefeated while other top teams won. The biggest change came at the bottom of the rankings: Minico (4-1) and Ririe (6-0) entered, while Middleton and Capital fell out. The passage also details results and top performers for many ranked teams, along with related links and a contributor biography.

The Supreme Court returns for its annual long conference after a three-month summer break; the 2025-26 term begins Oct. 6. Justice Clarence Thomas discussed stare decisis, saying it should not be a talismanic phrase, as the court is set to revisit prior rulings. Former Justice Anthony Kennedy, promoting an Oct. 14 book, expressed concern about partisanship and antagonistic discourse. Louisiana Solicitor General J. Benjamin Aguiñaga, a former Samuel Alito clerk, is involved in Voting Rights Act and Ten Commandments disputes; Callais v. Louisiana could affect minority voter protections. Joel Klein wrote about clerking for Lewis Powell, and George Will wrote about Amy Coney Barrett and originalism. The court issued an emergency order allowing the Trump administration to withhold billions in foreign-aid funding. The administration asked the court to review birthright citizenship, and a response brief is due on Venezuelan protected status. The long conference is expected to grant five to 15 cases. Order-list procedures and emergency docket timing, including 2024 ideological differences, were also discussed.

The article describes Enron’s transformation from a pipeline company into a trading colossus under Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling. Skilling’s Gas Bank and trading operations made Enron dominant in natural gas and electricity, supported by a culture that prized smart, aggressive employees, merit-based bonuses, long hours, and a forced-ranking Performance Review Committee. Enron expanded into coal, paper, steel, weather, broadband, and water through Azurix, while using mark-to-market accounting and short-term profit goals. By 2001 its stock had fallen from $80 to around $35; it faced criticism over California’s energy crisis, the Dabhol, India, power plant, telecommunications losses, and accounting questions. Skilling became CEO in February 2001 but resigned after six months; Lay returned and promised a kinder, gentler Enron closer to its core. The article also describes Rebecca Mark’s exit, Azurix’s decline, internal paranoia and lack of loyalty, and Skilling’s statement that most of his net worth remained in Enron and his interest in future commodity trading.

Euro zone stocks opened 2017 at their highest in over a year after the bloc’s factory PMI hit 54.9, showing the fastest activity in more than five years. Trading was thin due to holidays. The euro slipped 0.4 percent below US$1.05, while the dollar index climbed 0.5 percent. Italy’s FTSE MIB rose 1.5 percent, Germany’s DAX 0.9 percent, and France’s CAC 0.5 percent; Italian, Spanish, and Portuguese 10-year bond yields fell about 8 basis points. An Istanbul gun attack killed 39 and was claimed by Islamic State, with little market impact; the yen fell 0.3 percent and the lira slipped 0.5 percent. A Baghdad Islamic State attack killed 24. China’s manufacturing expanded for a fifth month, though growth slowed; the yuan had its biggest annual loss in over 20 years in 2016, and bitcoin rose above US$1,000.

The NBA unveiled its full 2017-18 schedule on Monday, four days after releasing the Christmas Day and first-week national TV schedules, and provided the national TV schedule for the entire season, listing dates, Eastern times, matchups, and networks from Oct. 17 through April 11.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 26, 2015, describes its business, products, services, segments, markets and distribution, competition, supply of components, R&D, patents, employees, risk factors, properties, legal proceedings, stock price ranges, dividends, and share repurchases. It states Apple designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers, and portable digital music players, and sells related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications. Products include iPhone, iPad, Mac, iPod, Apple Watch, and Apple TV; operating systems include iOS, OS X, watchOS, and tvOS; services include Internet Services, iCloud, AppleCare, and Apple Pay. Reportable segments are the Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific. Net sales were 26% direct and 74% indirect, and 35% domestic and 65% international. R&D expense was $8.1 billion in 2015, and the Company had approximately 110,000 full-time equivalent employees as of September 26, 2015.

The passage gives Bengali digit/symbol mappings, states that “~” after a symbol removes the previously typed Bengali character before typing the symbol, lists special sequences for symbols with special meaning, and describes ZWJ/ZWNJ for alternate ligature renderings and separating vowels.

The passage cites an aphorism attributed to Baron Rothschild about buying when there is blood in the streets. It says the retail apparel industry is bleeding, with the sector down about 20% in 52 weeks due to e-commerce threats, overexpansion, and supply-chain/trade-policy uncertainty from TPP withdrawal, NAFTA renegotiation, and Brexit. The author believes Francesca's Holdings Corp. (FRAN) can survive and emerge stronger. FRAN has $488 million in sales, a $320 million market cap, $48 million cash, no debt, about $57.6 million free cash flow, and 670+ stores in 48 states; it sells apparel, jewelry, and accessories to women ages 18-35 and plans 900 stores. In 1Q17, sales rose 1% to $107.7 million, comparable sales fell 5%, and diluted EPS were $0.12. FY18 guidance expects net sales of $518-$537 million, EPS of $1.07-$1.17, and 60-65 boutique openings. The author discloses no positions.

Oil prices fell after Israel and Hamas struck a rare truce. U.S. stocks paused near records: the S&P 500 rose 0.1%, the Dow added 26 points, and the Nasdaq was little changed. Gold was at $4,054.50 per ounce, and Treasury yields rose slightly. PepsiCo shares edged up less than 1% after quarterly results; net income fell 11% to $2.6 billion, while adjusted EPS of $2.29 beat forecasts. Delta topped profit expectations and forecast $6 full-year EPS, lifting airline shares. The maker of weight-loss drug Wegovy agreed to buy Akero Therapeutics for $4.7 billion cash, sending Akero up 18%. U.S. crude fell 21 cents to $62.34; Brent fell 18 cents to $66.07. European shares were mixed, while most Asian stocks rose.

Callinex Mines Inc. announced it filed an independent technical report for a Preliminary Economic Assessment on SEDAR for its wholly owned Nash Creek and Superjack Projects in New Brunswick. The PEA outlines a 10-year, 3,900 tpd open-pit operation with Dense Media Separation and a 1,950 tpd flotation facility at Nash Creek. It reports pre-tax IRR of 34.1%, post-tax 25.2%, pre-tax NPV8% of C$230 million, post-tax C$128 million, pre-production capital costs of C$168 million, and zinc price of US$1.25/lb. Callinex plans to start drilling within 10 days. The PEA is preliminary and includes Inferred Mineral Resources; no certainty it will be realized.

Adult-onset dementia includes Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and vascular dementia (VaD). This study used METRO, a multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association study, with GENOA genotype and gene expression data from 1,032 African ancestry and 801 European ancestry participants and GWAS summary statistics for general cognitive function, white matter hyperintensity (WMH), AD in European ancestry, and AD in African ancestry. METRO identified 602 genes for general cognitive function, 45 for WMH, 231 for AD (EA GWAS), and 9 for AD (AA GWAS). After FOCUS fine-mapping, 266, 23, 69, and 2 genes remained in 90% credible sets, respectively. ICA1L overlapped between WMH and AD, TOMM40 overlapped between AD EA and AA, and ICA1L was the only gene overlapping all four AD and WMH TWAS results. Identified genes were enriched in pathways involving protein binding, neurodevelopment, zinc finger motifs, amyloid formation and clearance, microglial activation, hematopoietic cell lineage, and neuroinflammation. The study reports limitations including use of EBV-transformed B-lymphocytes, single-gene TWAS analysis, and primarily EA GWAS with an underpowered AA AD GWAS, while noting strengths in multi-ancestry expression mapping and fine-mapping. It concludes that immune, vascular dysfunction, and neuroinflammatory mechanisms may contribute to AD, VaD, and cognitive function, and that downregulation of ICA1L may contribute to overlapping AD and VaD neuropathology.

According to The Chronicle of Higher Education survey reported by The New York Times, private college president pay continued rising: 58 presidents earned over $1 million in 2015, up from 39 in 2014, and average compensation rose 9% to $570,000, while average American worker pay rose 3% to 4% annually.

The African Union Commission’s Department of Trade and Industry organized the First African Union Start Up Fest under the theme “How to Unleash their Potential through Start-Ups Development?” It exchanged ideas on Youth Entrepreneurship and public-private responses. Objectives included assessing Start-up and Tech-Hub capacity needs, policy-private interaction, laying foundations for an African Association of Start-ups, and political support. Participants included Tech-Hubs, Youth Entrepreneurs, officials, RECs, business leaders, development partners, academia, and civil society. Speakers addressed SMEs and competitiveness, unemployment, youth entrepreneurship, digital economy, inclusion, education, skills, employment, technology, economic opportunities, and Agenda 2063. Outcomes included a follow-up side event at the 2018 Transform Africa Summit in Kigali, Rwanda, on setting up an African Association of Community Innovation Hub; the AUC, i4Policy, and participants would draft its agenda.

Not all offsites need to produce world-changing innovations; some focus on aligning, communicating, coordinating, or celebrating. Tesla, Inc. filed Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2022. As of April 19, 2022, 1,036,009,925 common shares were outstanding. For the three months ended March 31, 2022, total revenues were $18,756 million, net income was $3,280 million, net income attributable to common stockholders was $3,318 million, basic EPS was $3.20, and diluted EPS was $2.86. The filing covers automotive and energy generation and storage segments; COVID-19, supply chain, and inflation impacts; revenue recognition; digital assets; debt; equity incentive plans; commitments and contingencies; and legal proceedings, including SolarCity acquisition, 2018 CEO Performance Award, going-private, race discrimination, and government investigation matters. An email from Ann M. Schmidt dated June 7, 2001 lists Enron-related articles. They report that Enron and Exelon’s Commonwealth Edison signed an agreement to supply power to Chicago and 47 suburbs, with Enron providing 60% of 400 megawatts annually; Enron Broadband Services joined a $30 million investment in AP Engines; and Enron Power Operations pre-let additional office space at 21 Grosvenor Place. Several articles concern Enron’s Dabhol Power project in India: lenders met in Singapore over the $3 billion project; talks ended “positively” but issues remained; Indian Prime Minister Vajpayee expressed confidence in resolving the dispute; DPC said its PPA remained in force and it might bill MSEB for second-phase power; and Enron’s Indian unit planned to challenge a Maharashtra regulator order barring international arbitration. This study reports two cohorts examining SARS-CoV-2 immunity from vaccination and natural infection. It found that hybrid immunity from combined vaccination and natural infection produced higher variant-neutralizing serum antibody titers than vaccination alone. Longer intervals between vaccination and infection, up to at least 400 days, correlated with greater neutralizing antibody titers and improved cross-neutralization of variants, with the largest increases against Omicron BA.1, even though samples were collected before BA.1 emerged. The results suggest the immune response to vaccination or infection continues developing for over a year without additional exposures. The authors conclude that longer infection-vaccination intervals improve antibody responses and support increased vaccine access, while intentional infection is not a reasonable public health approach.

Chris Jones said he did not pursue Trevor Lawrence on Jacksonville’s game-winning touchdown because he thought the play was over and Lawrence was down, calling it a teaching point and learning lesson and saying it won’t happen again. He said he deactivated his X and Instagram accounts before Monday’s game, not to avoid criticism, and that he has focused on the Lions. The passage also presents numerous NFL headlines on teams, players, injuries, betting, fantasy football, playoff projections, and draft order.

DPI (UK), a Castle Donington-based maker of aluminium frames and lightboxes, received more than £12,200 from Collaborate, a scheme funded by ERDF and partners and overseen by Leicester City Council. The grant will buy an automated saw so larger aluminium panels and structures can be made in the UK instead of imported, cutting contract times and eventually creating jobs. DPI has grown since launching three years ago, adding staff and moving to bigger premises.

Andrew W. Lo’s introductory lecture for MIT 15.401 Finance Theory is aimed primarily at first-year MBA students over 13 weeks. Lo defines finance as mathematics plus money, or the systematic study of financial transactions. He cites James Simons, Warren Buffett, and Jack Welch as successful individuals with different backgrounds who understand finance. The financial system components covered are households, financial intermediaries, non-financial corporations, and capital markets. Lo says financial analysis has two fundamental challenges: valuation and management of assets. He stresses time and risk as what make finance challenging, and lists six basic principles of finance, discussing the first three. He demonstrates price discovery through an auction of an unknown item, sold for $45 and later revealed as an iPod Nano valued at $149. The course covers valuation, risk, and corporate finance. Requirements include readings, attendance/participation (10%), a case study (10%), midterm (25%), and final (55%); there are no problem sets, but a problem package will supply most exam points. Lo advises reviewing lecture notes, taking notes, working problems in groups and alone, asking questions, and mentions the Practice of Finance pro-seminar.

President Trump’s labeling of a House-passed health care bill as “mean” is aggravating conservatives he pressed to back it, while Senate attempts to reshape the measure may extend into July. Senate Republicans remain divided over Medicaid, coverage requirements and subsidies; John Cornyn called July 4 a goal but suggested end of July.

ARDD issued a report on Jordan's legal response to the Syrian refugee crisis, commending governmental agencies and UNHCR for rapid support. Legal sections in refugee camps were internationally recognised for specialised services like juvenile courts and family protection. Coordination mechanisms provide free protection services and documentation. Challenges remain, including access to the formal labour market outside camps, pressure on resources, and limited evaluation of legal aid. A registration campaign has newly registered 25,000 refugees.

This passage describes a database privacy system that responds to queries by executing differentially private versions on a private database. A hardware database privacy device is coupled to a private database system; it receives a client query, identifies a differential privacy level including a privacy parameter indicating information released, identifies corresponding data and operations, accesses the data, modifies operations based on the privacy level, performs the modified operations to produce a differentially private result set, and provides the result to the client for display. The system includes a differentially private security system with user interface, library, account management, query handling, data integration, and privacy system. The privacy system contains engines for count, median, mean, variance, IQR, batch gradient, stochastic gradient, random forest, histogram, model testing, synthetic database, and validation. It defines differential privacy for neighboring data objects, privacy parameters ε and δ, sensitivity, random variables, and noise-perturbed query outputs. It supports DP visualizations, synthetic databases, perturbed confusion matrices, and validation of whether queries satisfy differential privacy. A process and machine execute these methodologies.

Despite risks to India’s 3.3% fiscal deficit target for the year ending March 2019, Moody’s said the government may still meet it, likely by cutting planned capital spending. Polls in Singapore and Mumbai saw rising crude oil prices as a major risk, most respondents expected fiscal slippage, and PSB recapitalisation was deemed insufficient.
High-tech sensors reveal bats snatch birds.

TyreWatch predictive tyre management launched on 16 May at the Harwell Innovation and Science Campus. It monitors tyre pressure and temperature via wheel-rim sensors, sends data to a central server using cellular and satellite communications, and uses artificial intelligence to issue maintenance or critical alerts. It is designed to improve fleet productivity and efficiency, reduce fuel consumption, tyre wear, breakdowns, downtime and carbon footprint, and support road safety. TyreWatch uses open system architecture and is offered as software as a service; testing reportedly prevented 95% of tyre-related breakdowns. It is a product of the Pathway to Autonomous Commercial Vehicles consortium, funded with £1.2 million through Innovate UK.

Against a Box & One when the star player is a ballhandler, the “horns” or double mid screen alignment can isolate and free the star, who can go right or left and drive past the mid screen to create an outnumbered situation. If unable to drive, options include feeding the rolling screener or kicking out to corner shooters. Help reads can include a drop pass to a cutting ballside shooter, and screen-and-pop and single/double continuity are variations. Success depends on execution, coordination, communication, timing, experience, scouting, and varying alignments.

Japanese government bonds firmed after a strong two-year auction, with the 10-year yield steady, futures up, and shorter and superlong yields falling. Investors awaited the Bank of Japan’s May bond-purchasing details. The BOJ kept monetary policy unchanged and gave a more optimistic economic assessment; Governor Kuroda said interest rates, not the pace of bond buying, were the main target. Japan’s core consumer prices rose slower than expected in March but increased for a third straight month.

The address expresses gratitude for healthful seasons, abundant harvests, peace abroad, tranquillity at home, and civil and religious liberty. It reports generally peaceful foreign relations, including the war between Russia and the Ottoman Porte, with hope for moderation and aid to the Greeks; relations with France and unresolved indemnity claims; a boundary controversy with Great Britain submitted to the King of the Netherlands as umpire; commercial relations affected by duties and colonial exclusion; a prepared treaty with Austria; and progress on Danish indemnity claims. It describes disturbances among Latin American nations, treaties with Mexico not concluded, peace between Buenos Aires and Brazil, and indemnity obtained from Brazil. Revenue is favorable, with receipts, expenditures, and public debt reduction detailed. The tariff is discussed as affecting revenue and different sections, with possible revisal. The address discusses federal and state sovereignty and potential conflict. It reviews War Department reports, Indian tribes, fortifications, surveys, public improvements, West Point, Navy matters including piracy and a Pacific expedition, Post Office growth, public buildings, Ghent claims, public lands, and the fifth census. It closes with a desire for measures tending to the general welfare.

Deputy Chief Minister Nirmal Singh interacted with students of two women’s colleges and said the government is considering skill development courses and an optional skill development paper. He praised their vocational projects and urged upgraded skills and product quality to foster entrepreneurship.

A fired Washington Walmart employee who allegedly tried to steal a safe returned to retrieve drugs left inside. Employees found heroin and Xanax, called 911; the 24-year-old said the narcotics were his and was booked into Pierce County Jail for unlawful possession.

This study reviewed adrenalectomy specimens from 2018 to September 2022 to examine adrenal vascular morphology. Normal adult adrenal veins showed asymmetrical longitudinal smooth muscle bundles, gapping muscular media, nodular smooth muscle hyperplasia, diminished or absent elastic layers, and uneven SMYOHC expression. These features resembled fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD). In adrenal cortical adenomas, arteries showed hyalinized media with CD68-positive macrophages, intimal fibroplasia, and myxoid/fibrinoid medial degeneration or necrosis, consistent with segmental arterial mediolysis (SAM) and similar to acute atherosis. Pheochromocytoma arteries were mostly thin-walled with reduced muscular thickness, blood lakes, myxoid/fibrinoid degeneration, and intimal fibroplasia. Among 30 cases, asymmetrical bundles were seen in normal adrenal tissues, SAM was common in cortical adenomas and pheochromocytomas, and no FMD or FMD-like lesions were found outside the adrenal gland. Fetal adrenal vessels were normal. The findings suggest FMD and SAM may represent a single spectrum, with adrenal hormone actions or hormone receptor abnormalities possibly contributing to pathogenesis.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years for the 2014 murder of Dan Markel, a Florida State University law professor and her former son-in-law, and for conspiracy and solicitation. She said she was innocent and would have stopped the plot; the judge warned he could consider her “utter lack of remorse.”

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated October 26, 2021. It issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2021, furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing also includes Exhibit 104 and states the information is not deemed “filed” under Section 18.

IDC states that HPC has advanced with hardware and cloud architecture, broadening options to include custom, prebuilt, and cloud products. Among manufacturing enterprises already using or planning HPC, the public cloud is expected to become by far the most important HPC architecture, followed by hybrid cloud and prebuilt systems. IDC recommends deciding whether to make or buy, noting public cloud OPEX advantages over in-house CAPEX and limitations of in-house HPC in performance, expansion, maintenance, operating costs, peak underuse, and agility. Security and resilience are important; hybrid HPC can analyze sensitive data in-house while handling peaks or noncritical workloads in the public cloud. HPCaaS advantages include flexible maximum performance, cost optimization, OPEX/pay-as-you-go, and suitability for occasional or beginning users. It can support global cooperation, hybrid work, common databases, engineering workstations as a Service, and scalable HPC-based business models; 81% of respondents already using HPC intend to implement HPC-based business models. HPCaaS may outsource infrastructure operation completely or let users avoid setting up their own infrastructure, but trained IT and analysis/HPC personnel are required. Cloud providers offer modern technologies and cutting-edge methods/hardware. The conclusion says HPC technologies are becoming a prerequisite for simulations, modeling, and analytics, with public cloud and HPCaaS unlocking potential; data integration and a single source of truth are key. Recommendations cover virtual product and manufacturing development, a holistic data strategy, evaluating HPC operating models, considering scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise. The findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and other departmental decision makers in industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.
Two pieces of ammunition were found in a Litchfield High School bathroom Wednesday, prompting a lockdown; high and middle school students were dismissed to parents around 10:00.

The Yankees align with baseball’s decreased emphasis on starting pitching and increased emphasis on relievers/closers, exemplified by Aroldis Chapman’s contract. The Yankees have been a forerunner in bullpen buildup since Joe Torre’s era with Wettland, Nelson, and Rivera, continuing in 2017 with Betances and Chapman. The passage questions whether $20–25 million starters earn their keep when managers like Girardi, Bochy, and Maddon pull starters after five innings. It cites 2015 starters averaging 87 pitches and 2016 Quality Starts rankings, with Tanaka No. 24 and Sabathia No. 42. John Smoltz advocates more pitching. Bullpen overuse contributes to game length, and the Commissioner has considered limiting relievers, requiring Player’s Association input.

A new Boeing-funded study on airplane germ risks concluded that the safest advice is to take a window seat and not move. Researchers tested surfaces and air on 10 flights and observed contacts, but found none of 18 cold and flu viruses and only one coughing person. Modeling estimated about one infection among 150 passengers near a hypothetical infectious aisle passenger. Outside researchers said the small study cannot support broad conclusions.

SuperTrend is a trend-following indicator created by Oliver Seban that signals trend direction, continuation, or changes. It appears as a line on the price chart, green when price is above it and red when below; it reverses when a bar closes across the previous period’s value. Its formula uses median price and ATR bands, with Seban’s default 10-period ATR and multiplier 3. A weekly S&P 500 long-only backtest showed about a 67% win rate, a 24.6% max drawdown versus 56.24% for buy-and-hold, and acceptable risk-adjusted returns. The indicator is lagging and may produce false signals; backtesting is recommended. The best timeframe is weekly, though it can be applied intraday or daily.

Nathan Calvin, general counsel of the three-person AI policy nonprofit Encode, publicly accused OpenAI of using intimidation tactics to undermine California’s AI safety law, SB 53. He alleged OpenAI used its lawsuit against Elon Musk as a pretext to target critics, including Encode, and subpoenaed his private communications on SB 53. OpenAI’s Jason Kwon said Encode’s support for Musk’s lawsuit and undisclosed funding raised legitimate questions, and that subpoenas are standard in litigation. Calvin also alleged OpenAI sought to weaken SB 53 by urging California to treat companies as compliant if they had signed federal safety agreements or joined international frameworks. Encode refused to turn over documents, saying it is not funded by Musk. Former OpenAI employees, researchers, and another nonprofit founder also expressed concern.

The President transmits information on the state of the Union and recommendations. He reports peace, effective national defense, devoted executive departments, less industrial conflict, advances in education and science, high public health, and peaceful acceptance of election results. Relief efforts involve private agencies, local and State authorities, and Reconstruction Finance Corporation loans to States. A worldwide economic depression continued, with acute crises from European collapse; emergency measures prevented economic disaster and a turn toward recovery appeared. He recommends continuing recovery measures, then liquidating emergency agencies; balancing the Federal Budget through expenditure reductions; reorganizing the banking system; and cooperating with other nations on disarmament, economic recovery, currency stability, and war-debt payments. He also proposes Government reorganization, tax changes, veterans’ allowance reductions, salary cuts, and other legislation, while emphasizing individualism, State and local responsibility, and government as regulator rather than participant except in emergencies.

New research by Case Western Reserve University social scientists estimates the federal government spends $55 billion annually on effects of childhood exposure to domestic violence, with higher health-care costs, crime rates, and lower productivity. The study calculates a lifetime economic cost of nearly $50,000 per exposed child by age 64 and calls the issue a significant public-health problem.

Plaintiffs, targets or subjects of a grand jury investigation, sued NASD Regulation to bar it from compelling individual plaintiffs to testify in its Pallet investigation, punishing them for invoking self-incrimination, and misusing grand jury materials. After an evidentiary hearing, the court found no governmental coercion or suggestion behind the Rule 8210 demands and no credible proof that Rule 6(e) grand jury materials were disclosed to or used by unauthorized Regulation personnel. The court found no basis to enjoin the interviews and no Rule 6(e) violation, while noting that Regulation’s CPAG/DOE arrangements left doubt sufficient to require a trial and might warrant more careful controls.

The Shepherd Express has criticized We Energies’ management, high rates and high executive pay. As a regulated monopoly, We Energies lacks significant competitors, and the PSC sets rates for an allowable return over 10%. The article says municipal power companies are usually lower-cost and accountable to customers. It says Milwaukee-area electric rates were among the lowest until CEO Charlie McNeer retired; after Gov. Tommy Thompson’s PSC appointments, rates rose to the Midwest’s highest, driven by rate hikes for overbuilding and shareholder returns. The PSC comprises governor-appointed six-year commissioners. CUB and large businesses have pushed back; a new group, ICE, has formed. We Energies proposes a rate freeze through 2019, which MMAC supports, while ICE and CUB say a rollback is needed. The article says scrutiny is overdue.

Canadian Blood Services is opening the largest blood donation clinic in the country, a 20-bed Eau Claire Market clinic, on July 10. It replaces an 18-bed clinic closing July 7. Amid a blood shortage, O negative supply is under three days, and the goal of 150,000 donations by July 1 needs 50,000 more. Calgary’s supply is strong; a new operations facility is set to open in 2020.

F2 Logistics aims to extend its winning streak to four and secure the No. 2 seed against Generika-Ayala in the 2018 Chooks to Go-Philippine Superliga Grand Prix at The Arena in San Juan City. Generika-Ayala, after its first win over Smart, seeks added confidence. Sta. Lucia faces winless Smart in the opener, while several teams compete for positions.

The passage presents the SD Card Association’s Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 and related release/licensing conditions. It states that if a proposed specification implements, incorporates by reference, or refers to versions 1.0 or 1.01 of the SD Specifications, Members using the adopted specification must obtain appropriate licenses from SD-3C, LLC; examples include an SD Host Ancillary License Agreement for host devices and an SD Memory Card License Agreement for SD Cards with memory storage. In Hogg’s Estate, the majority, per Bok, J., affirmed the auditing judge and dismissed exceptions. The exceptants argued that only grandchildren whose parents were named in the will should inherit. The majority held that the word “grandchildren” obviously means all grandchildren, is unambiguous, and would include children of afterborn children. It stated that an heir cannot be disinherited except by express words or necessary implication, cited Robison’s Estate, Luce v. Harris, and Ludwick’s Estate, and concluded that “per stirpes” determines shares, not discrimination among ancestors; Miller’s Estate did not alter the situation. The account was confirmed absolutely.

Steakne, J., dissenting, joined by Sinkler, J., would sustain the exceptions. The dissent argued that the court must seek the testator’s intent and that the will showed the sole objects of bounty were the four named children and their issue. The testator contemplated only grandchildren from those named children, while afterborn children caused a pro tanto revocation and received full shares by law. The dissent deemed it error to award the afterborn child’s two children half the trust while the three grandchildren of named children received thirds, and found this contrary to the testator’s plain intent.

The Dogs of the Dow is a stock-picking strategy that selects the 10 highest dividend-yielding stocks among the 30 components of the Dow Jones Industrial Average, invests equal amounts, and rebalances annually. FULE logically erases the entire user area using CMD32 (0), CMD33 (end of user area), and CMD38 (00000002h). Hosts check FULE_SUPPORT (b312); unsupported cards execute ERASE. Out-of-sequence commands set ERASE_SEQ_ERROR or ERASE_RESET and reset the sequence. FULE is SDHC/SDXC only, not SPI.

The passage describes COVIDFast, a laboratory-developed assay with SwabFAST and SalivaFAST for rapid, high-throughput, RNA extraction-free RT-qPCR detection of SARS-CoV-2. It notes that conventional PCR relies on nucleic acid extraction, which is laborious, expensive, and prone to contamination and supply shortages. COVIDFast uses a proprietary buffer, collection devices, and compatible lab equipment to enable automated processing. Buffer optimization identified TBE-based viral transport buffer for swab samples and TCEP buffer for saliva; VTB remained stable across tested temperatures and durations. Analytical comparisons showed extraction-free results were qualitatively and quantitatively similar to RNA extraction methods, and the limit of detection was 4 copies/µL with 20/20 positive replicates for both specimen types. Clinical validation against extraction showed 100% PPV and NPV for swab samples and 98.8% PPV and 99.4% NPV for saliva. Against SalivaDirect, SwabFAST had 83.3% PPV and 99.4% NPV, and SalivaFAST had 95% PPV and 100% NPV. As of December 23, 2021, 409,883 tests had been performed, with 83.62% SwabFAST, 16.38% SalivaFAST, and an 8.10% total positive rate.

The S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price NSA Index reported a 6.3% annual gain in February, up from 6.1% the previous month. Blitzer said home prices continue to rise, with the National Index up 6.3% in the 12 months through February 2018 and continuous year-over-year increases for 70 months since May 2012, averaging 6% annually. In Betteys v. Ætna Life Insurance Co., the beneficiary sued on an accident policy for death benefits and weekly indemnity. The trial court entered judgment for plaintiff. The appellate court held that letters from defendant and its agents were admissible on waiver of proof of death and cause, and that defendant’s denial of liability excused such proof. However, defendant was not estopped from invoking the policy’s time limit for suit on death benefits; waiver of proof time did not waive the suit-time limitation. Because suit was not brought within the contractual period, the death-benefit claim was barred. The judgment was reversed and a new trial granted as to weekly indemnity.

SD Memory Card physical-layer procedures are described: a Tuning block tunes sampling points, with CMD19 used for tuning and subject to sequence/time limits; data transfer modes include CMD7 selection/deselection, CMD12 aborting reads/writes, block read/write, erase, DISCARD, FULE, pre-erase, and write-protection handling; lock/unlock, password, COP, and FEP operations are defined; ACMD55, CMD56, CMD6 switch functions, high-speed and command-system modes, CMD8, SDSC versus SDHC/SDXC addressing, clock control, CRC7/CRC16, and read/write/erase timeout conditions are covered.

The paper proposes a hybrid DNN-Transformer-AE deep learning framework for corporate tax risk supervision and risk-level assessment. It combines a DNN for static enterprise features, a Transformer for temporal financial data, and an Autoencoder for anomaly detection, then fuses outputs to predict risk scores and classify firms as high, medium, or low risk. The model is evaluated on real corporate tax data with about 12,000 enterprises across multiple industries, using static features, time-series features, and expert-assigned risk labels. Compared with Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and DNN-LSTM, the proposed model achieves 0.91 accuracy, 0.86 recall, and 0.88 F1-score. Training and validation loss converge around 40 epochs at about 0.05. The study concludes that the framework improves risk identification and supports regulatory resource allocation, while noting limitations: it excludes macroeconomic conditions and inter-firm relationships, and its computational complexity may hinder deployment in resource-constrained tax offices. Future work could integrate macroeconomic and policy data and develop interpretable, lightweight models.

The passage presents a theoretical study of orbital degrees of freedom (ODF) in hybrid magnon–phonon systems, unifying magnons and phonons through orbital angular momentum (OAM). It states that the ODF of bosonic quasiparticles such as magnons and phonons originates from global rotation and from the quantum geometry of magnon-polaron wavefunctions. Magnon–phonon coupling breaks P⊕T symmetry and enables intra-band and inter-band OAM transfer between magnon and phonon components. In a 2D honeycomb antiferromagnet with Néel order, out-of-plane phonon modes can acquire finite out-of-plane OAM and a spin moment via hybridization with magnons. The resulting finite OAM, together with the magnon magnetic moment, is predicted to yield a measurable transverse voltage under a temperature or strain gradient, with the orbital contribution dominating at low magnetic fields and enhanced by magnon–phonon coupling. The work concludes that the quantum-geometric origin of ODF is universal for bosonic and fermionic quasiparticles, supports phonon orbitronics, and connects phonon and magnon orbitronics.
