The passage states that as storage sizes have grown, storage performance has also grown, with gamers using SSDs to reduce game load times; hard drives are limited to 50-100 MB/sec throughput, while the latest M.2 PCIe Gen4 SSDs deliver up to 7 GB/sec. In the traditional storage model, game data is read from the hard disk, passed from system memory and CPU, then passed to the GPU. Games historically read files from the hard disk and used the CPU to decompress the game image, with lossless compression reducing install sizes and improving I/O performance. As storage performance increased, traditional file systems and storage APIs became a bottleneck. Decompressing data from a 100 MB/sec hard drive takes only a few CPU cores, but decompressing data from a 7 GB/sec PCIe Gen4 SSD can consume more than twenty AMD Ryzen Threadripper 3960X CPU cores. Using the traditional model, game decompression can consume all 24 cores on a Threadripper CPU, and modern game engines have exceeded traditional storage APIs.

NVIDIA RTX IO is described as a suite of technologies enabling rapid GPU-based loading and decompression of game and creative assets, accelerating I/O performance up to 100x compared to hard drives and traditional storage APIs. With Microsoft’s DirectStorage for Windows API, RTX IO offloads dozens of CPU cores’ worth of work to an RTX GPU. It improves frame rates, enables near-instantaneous game loading, reduces object pop-in and stutter, streams high-quality textures, and with lossless compression can reduce download and install sizes. It benefits artists and designers working with large datasets such as CAD models and 3D scientific visualizations, and enables high-resolution, high-framerate virtual reality imagery. RTX IO plugs into DirectStorage, brings GPU-based lossless decompression, keeps reads compressed and delivered to the GPU for decompression, removes CPU load, and improves I/O performance by a factor of two. GeForce RTX GPUs deliver decompression performance beyond Gen4 SSDs using high-performance compute kernels, DMA and copy engines of Turing and Ampere, and advanced SM architecture. Microsoft is targeting a DirectStorage for Windows developer preview for game developers next year, and Turing and Ampere gamers will be able to use RTX IO-enhanced games when available.

The NVIDIA A40, based on GA10x Ampere, is called the world’s most powerful data center GPU for visual computing. Compared to the Quadro RTX 6000, it delivers up to 2X FP32 throughput, up to 2X ray-tracing throughput, and up to 5X (10X with Sparsity) throughput for AI training and data science. Its PCIe Gen4 interface delivers up to 2X higher bandwidth compared to Turing-based GPUs. It has 48GB of GPU memory, scalable to 96GB by connecting two A40s via third-generation NVLink, and includes three DisplayPort 1.4 outputs. The A40 supports NVIDIA vGPU software, is configured for virtualization by default with display outputs disabled, supports Quadro Sync, and is compatible with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere architecture GPUs support 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz. The display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a, and Ampere is the first discrete GPU to support HDMI 2.1, with 48 Gbps maximum bandwidth. Ampere supports HDCP 2.3 and HDCP 1.x. The fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware-accelerated decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1. NVIDIA is the first GPU vendor to support AV1 decode in hardware; GA10x GPUs can play AV1 up to 8K60 HDR with low CPU usage. The seventh-generation NVENC offloads video encoding, allowing high-quality, ultra-low-latency encoding without utilizing CPU, with quality exceeding x264 Fast and on par with x264 Medium, and enabling up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC encoding. GA10x provides up to 2x performance improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI; the second-generation RT Core doubles ray/triangle intersection performance and supports ray-traced motion blur; the third-generation Tensor Core implements structural sparsity. GA10x is the first GPU to support GDDR6X, achieving up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak memory bandwidth in the GeForce RTX 3090. The RTX 3090 uses GA102, has 24GB GDDR6X, 82 SMs, 10496 CUDA Cores, and is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX. The RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6, and is faster than the RTX 2080 Ti. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) on GDDR6X detects data transmission errors and replays transactions; plateauing performance indicates the memory overclock limit. The RTX A6000 includes a GA102 GPU with 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, 336 next generation RT Cores, and 48GB GDDR6 memory, with 96GB combined memory via third-generation NVLink. The passage also includes a legal disclaimer stating that information is believed accurate but provided without warranties, NVIDIA reserves the right to make changes, products are not designed for medical, military, aircraft, space, or life support use, and materials are provided “AS IS.”

Alexis Perez pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit mail fraud and was sentenced to 51 months. He appealed, arguing the sentence was unreasonable because the district court did not reduce his base offense level by three levels under U.S.S.G. § 2X1.1(b)(2) for an incomplete conspiracy and did not grant a minor-role reduction under U.S.S.G. § 3B1.2. The appellate court affirmed. It found Perez and co-conspirators had taken crucial steps toward completing the offense and were on the verge of executing it, so the three-level reduction did not apply. It also found the record supported that Perez played an important role—he was involved in planning, knew how the scheme would be implemented, and was paid—and he did not show he was less culpable than most others. The sentence appeal waiver was not enforced, and Perez could not adopt codefendants’ arguments.

A day trading price action strategy uses patterns of price movement to determine trade entries and exits. Price action analysis is a form of technical analysis that focuses on price movements, swing highs and lows, chart patterns, and candlestick patterns, with little or no indicator input, and can be discretionary or quantitative. Day traders may use pure price action or combine it with indicators. Strategies include trend following, breakouts, reversal trades, and scalping. Backtesting is advised to assess performance, though price action strategies can be difficult to code and manual backtesting may be affected by biases. Trading rules depend on the strategy and market. An example WTI crude oil futures backtest showed poor historical performance, while a later out-of-sample test had a positive average over 21 trades.

In 2016, credit card debt and auto loans increased household bills. Paying off debt requires dedication and persistence. Suggested methods include reducing credit card use, setting a spending plan, building an emergency fund, paying as much as possible monthly, cutting spending, prioritizing high-interest debts, doubling payments after paying one, and making gradual lifestyle changes.

Spanish police dismantled a prostitution network that recruited Venezuelan transsexuals through fake "Miss Trans" competitions, freed over 20 victims, and arrested 14 suspects; it earned up to 1 million euros over five years.

Google Doodle honored Max Born’s 135th birthday. Born contributed to quantum mechanics, which led to computers, lasers, and medical imaging. Born was born Dec. 11, 1882, in Breslau, Germany, now Wrocław, Poland. He was a theoretical physics professor at the University of Göttingen for 12 years. His colleagues included Werner Heisenberg, Enrico Fermi, J. Robert Oppenheimer, and Maria Goeppert-Mayer. He was friends with Albert Einstein for more than 40 years. He worked with Otto Stern after World War I. Born emigrated to England when Hitler rose to power, and a 1935 letter from Hitler expelled him from Göttingen University. He won the 1954 Nobel Prize for the Born Rule. He died Jan. 5, 1970, at age 87.

The Regulatory Sandbox in Education bill permits district or charter schools to create innovation plans and seek state board rule waivers, and permits LEAs to use certain restricted funding and accept private grants. It requires charter amendments, plan submissions, possible termination, and state board reporting, including annual reports by November 30. Because no applications or approved plans are known, recommendations urge the State Board to create awareness through website information, optional application forms, and existing communication channels.

UK employment rose in the three months to April, with the employment rate at 74.8%, but regular earnings grew only 1.7% while inflation reached 2.9%, meaning real pay is falling. This squeezes households and adds to concerns about the economic outlook, with consumer spending under strain and growth dependent on exports, corporate services and business investment. Post-election and Brexit uncertainty may undermine business confidence. Input cost inflation moderated, suggesting consumer inflation may cool later, but weak wage growth may persist and the labour market may weaken, so Bank of England policymakers are likely to keep interest rates on hold.

The passage describes the AGESA™ software interface to a host BIOS, including bridge code in the host BIOS, the AGESA dispatcher in the binary image, and a call-out router for AGESA-to-host calls. It covers host environment responsibilities such as establishing a stack, using module dispatchers, creating standard headers, and implementing required call-outs like AgesaAllocateBuffer. It also outlines UEFI SEC, PEI, DXE, and RTP stages; libraries and build targets; tools; configuration options; PEIM and DXE driver duties; PPIs and HOBs; binary-module and source-integration build methods; stack procedures; and time-ordered entry procedures including AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitLate, AmdInitRtb, and resume-related functions.

Schoenfeld called on Foreign Minister Witting and left a personal note containing the Secretary’s three points but omitting Procopé personally. Witting said Procopé had qualified his report, not changing his unoptimistic long-range view. Witting cited Finnish strategic aims including control of Karelian and Onega Isthmuses because of Murmansk railroad development; Schoenfeld questioned extending defense eastward, and Witting said Finland could not. Witting compared German and British statements on small nations and said Germans merely got there first; he described Finnish realism as based on experience with Russians. He also reported Procopé’s account of private State Department views on postwar control of small nations and purging German industry. Schoenfeld said Witting realized Finland was increasingly a toy of uncontrollable forces. Separately, the Secretary of State told Procopé that the January 3 inquiries applied to American-citizen Finnish Legation and Consulate personnel under Finnish jurisdiction; the Minister could require compliance or sever official connections, and Finnish consular personnel in the U.S. must make such inquiries before leaving their consular city limits.

Apple Inc. filed an 8-K dated December 21, 2015. On that date, Apple’s Board adopted amendments to its Amended and Restated Bylaws to implement proxy access. New Section 5.15 permits a shareholder, or a group of up to twenty shareholders, owning at least three percent of Apple’s common stock continuously for at least three years to nominate and include director nominees constituting up to twenty percent of the Board in proxy materials, subject to Bylaws requirements. Section 5.14 was changed, and Sections 2.4, 5.4 and 10.6 received ministerial, clarifying and conforming changes. Exhibit 3.2 contains the Bylaws.

NEMA South East zonal coordinator Walson Ibarakumo warned of impending flood in Enugu, Anambra and Ebonyi States, citing NIHSA and NiMET forecasts and climate change. He advised residents to change their attitude, especially energy use, and prepare for possible devastation. He listed Enugu South/East; Aguata, Idemili North and Ogbaru; and Afikpo South, Abakaliki, Ebonyi, Ezza South, Ikwo, Ohaukwu and Afikpo as highly probable or prone areas.

DBS says Indian bond outlook is challenging but some value is emerging after the sharp sell-off. It expects continued yield pressure from FY2019 supply and developed-market monetary normalisation, though most selling may be over and rises modest. CPI easing favours shorter-term bonds, while DBS is neutral-to-negative on longer-term bonds. The rupee and Sensex were Asia ex-Japan’s second-worst performers, and DBS expects the rupee to depreciate toward 67 this year amid capital-inflow needs and the current-account deficit.

Al-Qaida-linked militants in Syria downed a Russian Su-25 on Saturday and killed its pilot after he ejected in Idlib; the pilot resisted capture and fired at the militants, who killed him, while Russia confirmed the downing and said he died fighting “terrorists.” A report said preliminary information indicated a portable ground-to-air missile hit the plane in an area controlled by al-Qaida’s Syrian branch. Intense airstrikes hit Idlib, including more than 35 on Saraqeb since late Friday, and Syrian troops captured Maasaran and Tel Tokan hill. The U.N. says more than 270,000 people have been displaced in Idlib since Dec. 15. In Afrin, fighting continued between Turkish troops and allied Syrian opposition fighters and a Syrian Kurdish militia; Turkey said two soldiers were killed in Syria and one on the Turkish border in its Olive Branch operation against the U.S.-backed YPG.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-K for fiscal year ended January 25, 2015 covers its visual computing business, GPU and Tegra Processor segments, and four markets: Gaming, Enterprise, HPC & Cloud, and Automotive. It describes strategies, sales and marketing, fabless manufacturing, R&D, competition, patents, employees, environmental compliance, executive officers, and available information. The filing also includes risk factors, properties, legal proceedings, market and dividend information, share repurchases, selected financial data, and MD&A. For fiscal 2015, NVIDIA reported revenue of $4,681.5 million, income from operations of $759.0 million, net income of $630.6 million, and cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $4,623.3 million; it paid dividends of $186.5 million and repurchased 44.4 million shares for $813.6 million.

Strong, caring relationships with adult and peer mentors can help young people thrive academically and overcome educational challenges. Mentoring can occur through school-based volunteer programs, afterschool programs, community organizations, or naturally through extended kin, family friends, community leaders, and educators; teachers and school personnel are commonly cited mentors. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted students’ educational engagement and progress, especially for low-income students, students of color, students with learning disabilities, and marginalized youth, and many students report disconnection from caring adults and school community.

The passage cites meta-analyses and research syntheses finding that mentoring programs generally have positive impacts on academic achievement and educational success, including attendance, grades, test scores, classroom behavior, truancy, absenteeism, scholastic efficacy, misconduct, peer support, school connectedness, engagement, self-confidence, and attitudes toward school. Cross-age peer mentoring improves school connectedness and belonging and can benefit both younger students and older mentors. Specific studies of school-based, after-school, and natural mentoring programs show improvements in academic performance, attendance, graduation, college enrollment, discipline, and related outcomes. Natural mentoring from teachers and school personnel is associated with stronger school attachment, motivation, GPA, educational expectations, and attainment, and may be particularly impactful for students of color.

The passage concludes that mentoring can positively affect students’ educational success, but access is inequitable, with youth of color, low-income youth, and youth whose parents have limited education reporting fewer mentoring relationships. It calls for private and public investment at local, state, and federal levels and policies to expand the quantity and quality of mentoring.

Xiaomi’s Redmi 5 will go on sale in India today at 12 pm on Amazon India, Mi.com, and Mi Home stores, starting at Rs 7,999. It comes in 2GB RAM+16GB storage at Rs 7,999, 3GB RAM+32GB at Rs 8,999, and 4GB RAM+64GB at Rs 10,999, with a 5.7-inch HD+ 18:9 display, Snapdragon 450 processor, 3300 mAh battery, 12MP rear and 5MP front cameras, Android Nougat 7.1.2 with MIUI 9, and four color options.

The President transmitted the Secretary of State’s report and related documents to the Senate and explained why he did not send the proposed 1853 U.S.–Mexico Tehuantepec transit convention for ratification. He cited numerous conclusive objections, especially that it would bind the U.S. to guarantee a private company’s contract, protect persons and property, and guarantee invested capital over a long term, with withdrawal requiring one year’s notice. He also said it would conflict with the 1850 U.S.–Great Britain convention covering Tehuantepec communications.

This longitudinal evaluation characterized SARS-CoV-2–specific immune responses in residents of a 149-bed nursing home during an outbreak from October 2020 to April 2021. Among 127 residents in at least one CDC point prevalence survey, 47 were antigen-positive, 31 were eligible, 12 enrolled, and 11 were analyzed. Median age was 74 years; most were male, White, and had underlying conditions; four had severe COVID-19 and one died. Ten received two doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine; one refused. Post-infection, 9/10 had detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA antibodies, 8/10 had IgM, and one had no binding antibodies. Median time to detection was 13 days for Pan-Ig and IgG, 16 days for IgA, and 15 days for IgM. At first antibody detection, two-thirds were still RT-PCR-positive but none were viral culture-positive. Pan-Ig and IgG remained elevated post-infection, while IgM and IgA declined during 31–60 days, with seroreversion in some participants. Post-vaccination, all 10 had detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA, and six had IgM; Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA decreased during 61–90 days post-vaccination. Post-vaccination Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA titers were higher than post-infection titers. The evaluation concluded that nursing home residents mounted robust humoral immune responses post-infection and post-vaccination. Limitations included small sample size, receipt of only the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine, possible missed exact timing of seroconversion, peak titers, and seroreversion, and occurrence before the Delta and Omicron variants.

The Colts have blown six leads, including four double-digit second-half leads. In their latest loss, a negated conversion and a 43-yard extra point in blizzard conditions tied the score before a 13-7 overtime defeat. Coach Chuck Pagano said weather left players with dead legs before a Thursday game against Denver. The four-game skid is Pagano's longest with Indianapolis; the team is eliminated, and his future is again in question.

The passage says Oclaro achieved 47% revenue growth, with margins expanding 11 points to 39% and EPS of $0.79, up 460%, while trading at about 11 times fiscal 2017 earnings. Analysts expect $0.74 EPS in fiscal 2018 and $0.82 in 2019. Demand is booming in 100G, which is 81% of revenue, and QSFP28 sales doubled sequentially; legacy CFP and 40G-and-below products declined. China revenue fell 11% sequentially and is expected to decline about 15% in Q1 and be flat to down in Q2, though management believes Chinese demand drivers remain intact and QSFP28 demand may change in 2018. It has no debt, $258M cash and short-term investments, $46M operating cash flow, and $11.5M free cash flow. Q1 2018 guidance is $151–159M revenue, 38–41% gross margins, and $30–34M operating income. The author sees reasons for optimism and does not expect a cyclical downturn soon.

The court affirmed the Commissioner’s dismissal of Lever Brothers’ opposition to Thrift-D-Lux Cleaners’ application to register “Thrift-D-Lux Cleaners” for dry cleaning and pressing services. The opposition was based on prior use and registration of “Lux” for soaps and detergents. The court found the marks not confusingly similar because “Thrift-D-Lux” suggests thrift and de luxe, while “Lux” is generally understood as the Latin word for light; “de luxe” is suggestive and commonly used. It also found no evidence of confusion with “Lux Laundries,” and distinguished appellant’s cited cases.

An outside day is a two-bar price pattern where the current bar has a higher high and lower low than the previous bar, with its open and close outside the first bar’s open and/or close. It indicates rising volatility and can act as a continuation or reversal pattern depending on context, configuration, and price swing. Outside bar strategies are popular but subjective and require backtesting. Backtests of SPY and other ETFs found performance after outside days to be random or not tradable, though other opportunities may exist.

The speaker thanks President Reagan, notes he repeated George Washington’s oath on Washington’s Bible at the bicentennial inauguration, and prays that power be used to help people. He assumes the presidency at a promising, peaceful, prosperous time, saying freedom, free markets, free speech, free elections, and free will work and are right. He says America is proud and free but not measured by possessions, and needs moral purpose to help the homeless, children, addicts, and those facing crime and unplanned motherhood. Public money alone cannot solve these problems amid deficits, so he calls for American goodness, courage, community organizations, and a Thousand Points of Light. He urges new engagement with Congress, compromise, and bipartisanship after Vietnam, and a strong foreign policy that keeps agreements, protects Americans abroad, maintains alliances, and improves Soviet relations. He calls for intolerance of drugs and for unity, diversity, and generosity, with work beginning tomorrow.

Noble et al. v. The Thompson Oil Co. involved an action on a recognisance after a Pennsylvania judgment was assigned to Brown and others. The assignees were Pennsylvania citizens, and the judgment, assignor, and assignees were in Pennsylvania at assignment. Defendants in the judgment were later served in New York as garnishees in a foreign attachment after the assignment but before notice. The New York court entered judgment against them, and they paid it. The Pennsylvania court held that oyer of the record had been waived; the assignment was valid and left the assignor with no attachable interest; the attaching creditor stood no better than its debtor; and the New York judgment did not bar the assignees because the New York court lacked jurisdiction over the assignees or property, the assignees were not parties or privies, and notice did not change the result. Judgment on the demurrer for plaintiffs was affirmed.

Aziz Ansari says he still uses a flip phone and has not had email for about 10 years, relying on an assistant. He is skeptical of ChatGPT, saying it outsources critical thinking, makes opinions similar, is prone to mistakes, and reinforces existing views; he prefers human conversation. He says low-tech living gives him space to think and helps him write, though he acknowledges privilege. Other celebrities, including Christopher Nolan, Dolly Parton, and Christopher Walken, have also described low-tech habits, and some non-celebrities have switched to dumb phones or makeshift landlines to reduce screen time.

The appellate court affirmed summary judgment dismissing the plastic surgeon’s human rights action. It found that the essence of the action challenged the Administrative Review Board’s revocation of his medical license, so review had to be sought through a CPLR article 78 proceeding, which was time-barred. The court rejected the argument that an independent action was permitted.

Northern Ireland's health service is the UK's only region not led by a minister. It faces UK-wide pressures, long waiting lists, and a £30m allocation. Figures show 83,392 waited over a year. Crises included neurology recalls and Dunmurry Manor. Bengoa's 2016 ten-year reform recommendations won cross-party support, but Stormont's collapse left no minister to lead reforms.

Nassau County Court jurors acquitted 18-year-old Jasmine Copeland of all charges in the Nov. 1, 2014 killing of 17-year-old Abbigale Thomas during a brawl. After about three hours, jurors found her not guilty of manslaughter and other charges. Prosecutors said Copeland stabbed Thomas; her attorney said she was innocent and had no contact with Thomas.

This lecture wraps up stochastic methods. It reviews evaluating multidimensional integrals with probability densities and weighting factors, including Bayesian analysis. Metropolis Monte Carlo is discussed, covering step-size and acceptance issues, adaptive step sizing, initial-state sensitivity, and accuracy scaling as 1/√N. Kinetic Monte Carlo is presented for time-dependent probabilities and very large state spaces, using Gillespie trajectories, random numbers, Poisson initial conditions, and approximations for fast or slow processes. Molecular dynamics is described as solving Newton’s equations with force fields, Verlet integration, and thermostats; it is useful for time-dependent properties but limited by small timesteps and nanosecond timescales. The lecture stresses choosing tools suited to the problem and knowing expected answers for verification, then gives course announcements.

Players discussed recent two-goal deficits and the need for better starts and the first goal. Marian Gaborik said three overtime games in a row is tough, that returning to the Garden after being traded and seeing renovations will be special, and that it is his first final. Dwight King discussed rest days, battling McDonagh in front of the net, screen traffic on goaltenders within the rules, home ice, playoff momentum, and the team’s calm belief and vocal leaders.

Zeta Global is acquiring Marigold's enterprise software business for $325 million in its largest-ever acquisition, its 17th. The assets include Marigold's Loyalty brand, Cheetah Digital, Sailthru, and Selligent; Marigold will keep Campaign Monitor, Emma, and Vuture. Zeta says the deal expands its Fortune 500 customer base and EMEA footprint, adding more than 100 large brands. Zeta will pay $100 million cash and $100 million in shares upfront, with $125 million in cash and stock via a seller note within three months of closing.

Provided is technology for detecting neoplasia, particularly gastric cancer, by assessing DNA methylation states of markers in samples such as gastric tissue, plasma, or stool. The passage reports identification of 123 novel DNA methylation markers and optimal marker sets, including 10 markers for stomach cancer, 30 markers for stomach cancer, and 12 markers for gastric cancer in plasma. Methods include assaying differentially methylated regions (DMRs, e.g., DMR 1-274 from Tables 1, 2, 4, and 7), comparing methylation states with controls, and using related compositions, kits, reagents, and systems.

Old rocket parts and decommissioned satellites in low Earth orbit risk colliding with modern satellites. A paper by Darren McKnight identifies the 50 most concerning debris objects; 76% were deposited last century, 88% are rocket bodies, and Russia/Soviet Union leads with 34, followed by China with 10. Removing all 50 would reduce debris-generating potential by 50%, and removing the top 10 by 30%. Since January 1, 2024, 26 rocket bodies have been abandoned in orbit for more than 25 years, 21 from China. China frequently abandons upper stages, and its Guowang and Thousand Sails megaconstellations could add many more, though some rockets such as Long March 5 with YZ-2 can deorbit. Reasons include lack of restartable engines and fuel/payload tradeoffs. Active debris removal is technically feasible but funding and market questions remain; ESA and Japan have funded low levels, and Astroscale demonstrated a mission.

The petitioner sought a writ of error, claiming his conviction and death sentence violated the Constitution because a juror was mentally and physically incapacitated and the jury separated. The state Court of Appeals affirmed, finding the juror’s competency and alleged separation were factual and discretionary matters and no new trial was warranted. The Supreme Court denied the application, holding that a juror’s physical and mental condition and competency to return a verdict is a question of fact not reviewable on writ of error to a state court in an action at law.

Industrial relations between East Dunbartonshire Council and unions show no sign of improving. Three unions advised that refuse collections will be affected by strikes on July 12–15: GMB waste operatives at Hilton Depot and Mavis Valley Recycling Centre, Unison waste operatives, and Unite members at Hilton Depot. Action short of strike continues. Council leaders expressed disappointment and concern, while discussions are set to continue; last month’s four-day action caused widespread disruption.

Cerebras Systems said Friday it is withdrawing its IPO plans, a little over a year after filing its prospectus and days after raising $1.1 billion at an $8.1 billion valuation. In an SEC filing, it said it does not intend to conduct the offering “at this time” but gave no reason; a spokesperson said it still hopes to go public as soon as possible. The spokesperson said the government shutdown did not factor into the decision, and CEO Andrew Feldman said the original prospectus was out of date.

The UN World Water Development Report 2018 praised community-led water efforts in India, particularly Tarun Bharat Sangh in Rajasthan, where local communities restored water cycles and built water harvesting structures, increasing forest cover, groundwater levels and cropland productivity. It also lauded women’s leadership and cited nature-based solutions such as China’s rainwater recycling and Sponge City, India’s forest regeneration and Ukraine’s artificial wetlands. The report warned that population growth and climate change could leave five billion people with poor water access by 2050.

This WIRED guide reviews Google’s Pixel 10, Pixel 9a, Pixel 10 Pro/Pro XL, Pixel 10 Pro Fold, and older Pixel 9 models, along with case, accessory, and software-feature recommendations. The Pixel 9a is described as all the phone most people need, with a 6.3-inch OLED, Tensor G4, 8 GB RAM, 48-MP main/13-MP ultrawide/13-MP selfie cameras, a 5,100-mAh battery, and seven years of software support, but it lacks Pixel Screenshots and Call Notes. The Pixel 10 adds a 5X optical zoom, Tensor G5, brighter screen, louder speakers, Qi2/Pixelsnap charging, and better selfie autofocus, though US models are eSIM-only. The Pixel 10 Pro and Pro XL are the best Google offers, with 16 GB RAM, vapor chamber cooling, LTPO displays, larger camera sensors, Pro Res Zoom, Video Boost, and, on the XL, Qi2 25W charging and louder speakers. The Pixel 10 Pro Fold is a heavy folding phone with Pixelsnap and durability claims but lacks some Pro features. Older Pixel 9 phones can save money but lack Qi2 and, on the base model, 5X zoom. The guide notes battery issues in some older A-series Pixels, Google’s response about the Pixel 9a, and Pixel Care+ insurance options. It also lists Pixel software features such as Call Screen, Direct My Call, Hold for Me, Call Notes, Live Translate, Recorder, Gemini, Magic Cue, Pixel Screenshots, Camera Coach, Pro Res Zoom, Help Me Edit, Best Take, Magic Editor, Reimagine, Audio Magic Eraser, Video Boost, and theft/safety tools. Accessory recommendations include Google, Mous, Dbrand, Bellroy, and Peak Design cases, Qi2 chargers, screen protectors, Pixel Buds Pro 2, and Pixel Watch 4.

The passage profiles Ryan, a six-year-old YouTube star whose parents have posted videos of him opening, playing with, and reviewing toys on “Ryan ToysReview” since he was three. Forbes ranked him eighth among highest-paid YouTube entrepreneurs, with $11 million in revenue from June 2016 to June 2017 before fees and taxes, tying Smosh. The channel began in March 2015 with a Lego Duplo train set video and grew after a viral video reviewing over 100 toy cars in a giant egg surprise. It reached more than 10 million subscribers and over 16 million views. The passage says his last name and residence are secret, his videos include ads and product links, and he has influenced children and parents, some of whom describe daily viewing and toy purchases. His family donates most reviewed toys to charity, and his parents said 99 percent of the channel’s videos are not branded.

This passage specifies AGESA™ software interface requirements for host BIOS/UEFI environments. It prohibits calling unpublished functions and enabling code execution caching before main memory initialization except through provided AGESA™ functions. It describes reported errors and returned status codes, event logging, binary module and call-out mechanisms, UEFI execution phases, PEIM/DXE drivers, PPIs/HOBs, build tools and configuration options, stack procedures, helper procedures, initialization entry points, and platform configuration structures for processor, memory, graphics, PCIe®, FCH, suspend/resume, and late ACPI/DMI table generation.

Michael Cohen removed “personal attorney to President Donald J. Trump” from his Twitter biography, while his LinkedIn page still described him that way. His relationship with Trump gained importance after an FBI raid and disclosure of a criminal investigation. Cohen admitted facilitating a hush payment to Stormy Daniels; Rudy Giuliani said Trump reimbursed Cohen. In an ABC interview, Cohen said he puts family and country before loyalty to Trump and respects the FBI.

On November 18, 2004, the court in Lewis v. Bayer AG ruled on plaintiffs’ motion for class certification in litigation over Baycol (Cerivastatin). The court found numerosity satisfied. It certified only Class I, a Pennsylvania medical monitoring class of persons prescribed and ingesting Baycol who have not been diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis or congestive heart failure. The class seeks testing for CoQ10 depletion, elevated CK levels, chest x-rays, a court-supervised monitoring program, epidemiological research, and other equitable relief. Arthur Conner, Milton Angert, and Lisa Frost were named Class I representatives, and plaintiffs’ counsel was appointed class counsel. Certification was denied for all other classes. The court found commonality for Class I medical monitoring, but not for Class I UTPCPL or general unjust enrichment claims because of individualized reliance, causation, and factual issues. It found individual issues of law and fact predominated for Classes II, III, and IV due to individualized causation and varying state laws. The court concluded class treatment was fair and efficient for the limited Class I medical monitoring claim and ordered notice proposals within 30 days.

The speaker says Peter’s aggressive system took about one to two months to master, is effective, pressures all over the ice, and requires great fitness; since Peter took over, the team is in better shape and has success. He calls Peter competitive, tenacious, hard-working, and versatile. With a quick schedule and little time off, he sees no letdowns in the finals. The team must play consistent hockey, possibly seven games, defend well, avoid a track meet, and score gritty goals by putting pucks to the net and bodies in front. He respects him as a leader, tenacious, nonstop, and one of the best players in the world.

Methods and apparatuses for downlink assignments for downlink control channels are disclosed. A UE monitors a first PDCCH candidate scheduling a first downlink data channel in a first control resource set and a second PDCCH candidate scheduling a second downlink data channel in a second control resource set. Upon receiving a downlink assignment, the UE determines a downlink data channel allocation and a demodulation reference signal symbol location based on the assignment and the OFDM symbol sets of the control resource sets, and decodes the downlink data channel. In another method, a UE receives search space identities for associated search spaces, determines monitoring occasions for the search spaces, determines a third set of monitoring occasions as a subset, and monitors PDCCH candidates in at least one slot if they carry the same downlink control information. The associated search spaces correspond to two different control resource sets whose demodulation reference signal ports are quasi-collocated with different reference signal sets.

The team isn’t frustrated because the series isn’t over; it is playing better, creating chances, and expected a tough series against a great team. The speaker believes in Marc, who has proved himself, and says both are dedicated; home matchups and lineup changes may build momentum.

In soccer, a defensive switch may be required when the first defender is beaten after the second/support defender is positioned behind, inside, goalside, and at the proper distance and stance. The second defender calls for the switch, takes the ball carrier, and the first defender covers the opponent originally marked by the second defender, exchanging positions. The support defender communicates arrival and may call for the first defender to jockey/contain or tackle. Most switches are crossing-pattern runs initiated by the support defender. After the immediate play, defenders return to original assignments, with a “switch back” or “return” call usually made by the player who called the initial switch. The passage also provides instruction and scenarios for practicing basic, alternative, and switch-back defensive switches.

The passage reports that Adm. This lecture discusses model-free optimal control, comparing policy gradient and value-function methods. Policy gradients can scale to high dimensions, are local search, may have high variance and require many trials, require smoothness, but convergence is virtually guaranteed. Value methods are efficient and reuse data, but with function approximation and changing policies convergence is not guaranteed; they can oscillate or diverge, and small value-estimate changes can cause large policy changes. Actor-critic combines a policy (actor) and value estimate (critic) in a two-time-scale algorithm, using the value function to reduce update variance while retaining policy-gradient convergence. The lecture cites Konda and Tsitsiklis, Sutton, and Peters. A case study describes the Toddler walking robot: an underactuated passive walker with ankle actuators, online actor-critic learning, per-footstep updates, and a cost based on a desired return map. It learned to walk in minutes, was robust to disturbances and terrain, and learned faster when a value function was retained. The lecture also announces project write-ups and oral presentations.

Kathrine Clark, pro se, appealed the Chatham County Superior Court’s order granting Ricky G. Rau’s petition to modify custody and child support. The parties have three minor children. After an earlier order granting joint legal custody with split physical custody, Rau sought modification, alleging changed circumstances; after a bench trial, the court awarded Rau sole legal and physical custody. No transcript was included, and Clark’s appellate brief did not comply with Court of Appeals Rules 22 and 25, lacking a statement of facts, record citations, and distinct enumerations of error with argument. The majority presumed regularity, found any discernible arguments could not be addressed without a transcript, and affirmed, also finding no specific findings were requested and that the trial court essentially addressed the children’s welfare. The dissent, joined by several judges, argued the custody order was facially deficient because it failed to reflect a finding that modification was in the children’s best interest, and would vacate and remand for application of the proper legal standard. Clark had argued, among other things, that the trial court failed to allow her evidence and did not consider statutory best-interest factors.

SOS switching is an integral part of the SOS Pressure Defense. Automatic switching eliminates hesitation and reduces fouls. “Screen-Over-Switch” describes switching action. Off-ball screens are disrupted by attacking passing lanes; a Hi-Lo switching technique defends baseline screens. On-ball screens above the free throw line extended are switched aggressively, and below it are trapped aggressively. Contact Switching denies passing lanes, prevents quick catches and open jump shots, disrupts screening offense, commits fewer fouls, forces turnovers or bad shots, and creates transition points. Mismatches are addressed with immediate automatic traps using Near Player rotations. Techniques include calling Screen, hedging Over, and switching. Off-ball down and back screens use contact switches and snuggle pass denial. Base screens switch when the cutter goes low but not high. On-ball screens above the free throw line use contact switch, snuggle, and smother; below the line use baseline trap, Triangle I, and close out.

The study develops TOPIC, a crystal structure prediction algorithm constrained by corner-sharing (CS) bond topology, to discover oxide solid-state electrolytes (SSEs). This prospective study enrolled 157 patients hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure and performed bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS) at admission and discharge to measure overhydration (OH) and the OH-to-extracellular water (OH/ECW) ratio. Among patients, 72 had chronic kidney disease (CKD) and 111 had heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). CKD patients had higher OH and OH/ECW ratios at admission but no association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) or heart failure hospitalization (HHF). HFrEF patients showed greater reductions in OH/ECW than non-HFrEF patients, but these changes did not improve clinical outcomes. Across subgroups, OH, OH/ECW, and their changes were not significant predictors of MACE or HHF during follow-up. BIS effectively monitored fluid status, particularly in HFrEF, but its prognostic utility in CKD and HFpEF was limited, warranting further investigation.

This lecture discusses wireless communication fading. It starts with free-space propagation, where the received field falls as 1/r, has an antenna pattern and propagation delay, and behaves like a linear time-invariant channel with white Gaussian noise. Moving receivers introduce Doppler shift, but a single Doppler shift can be tracked. Multipath from reflectors causes multiple Doppler shifts and fast/multipath fading through beat cancellation. Reflecting walls and ground reflections can make received power fall as 1/r⁴ or 1/r⁶. Ray tracing models the channel as multiple paths with time-varying attenuations and delays. The channel is linear but time-varying, represented by time-varying convolution and a baseband equivalent. Doppler spread between paths determines how long the channel looks time invariant and how often measurements must be updated.

The lecture covers folding polygons into convex polyhedra by gluing polygon boundaries, represented with gluing trees. It presents combinatorial bounds and algorithms for decision, enumeration, and counting of gluings. General gluings have exponentially many combinatorial types, with exponential upper and lower bounds; edge-to-edge gluings have a polynomial decision algorithm but exponential enumeration; bounded-sharpness polygons have polynomial bounds and algorithms. For general arbitrary gluings, deciding existence remains open, with the best known algorithm exponential. The lecture defines combinatorial gluing types using abstract gluing trees and vertex/edge assignments at junctions, proves exponential upper and lower bounds, and describes dynamic-programming algorithms for edge-to-edge enumeration and decision, generalized enumeration for arbitrary gluings, and polynomial behavior under bounded sharpness. It also shows examples including a cube/cross, spiky-star polygons, perimeter halving, the Latin cross with 85 gluings and 23 polyhedra, and triangle/square rolling belts.

Because #HV is delivered without regard to interrupt shadows, guests cannot control HLT/interrupt interaction as with typical delivery. A guest ready to halt should not examine pending interrupts or enable interrupts; it should execute HLT with interrupts disabled. If the host receives an HLT intercept while interrupts or non-maskable events are pending, it should immediately re-enter the guest. When a guest resumes after HLT, it should examine interrupt state as if it has just received #HV. Doorbell page configuration uses VMGEXIT SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0014 with functions for a hypervisor-preferred address, SET, and QUERY; the host may use RMPUPDATE, the guest should PVALIDATE, and the page must be accessed with C=0. The host emulates APIC interrupt presentation by writing a vector to PendingEvent, setting NoFurtherSignal and NoEoiRequired, delivering #HV, tracking in-service interrupts, and performing EOI cycles. The guest, upon #HV, may acknowledge by atomically exchanging PendingEvent to zero, process or defer interrupts, perform EOI via NoEoiRequired or an APIC register write, and handle non-maskable events. Non-cooperative host or guest behavior may cause denial of service or lost #HV, but not affect host integrity.

The passage introduces ASTROCO, a conformer-style encoder for astronomical light curves that combines global self-attention with local depthwise convolutions and gating. It aims to address limitations of transformer encoders that treat every time step equally and lack explicit mechanisms to regulate noisy or distant measurements. ASTROCO uses multi-head self-attention, a depthwise convolutional sublayer with Gated Linear Units, and a gated feed-forward network, connected with residual connections and layer normalization. Magnitudes and uncertainties are concatenated with time embeddings and fused through a learned projection. Pretraining uses masked reconstruction. On the MACHO R-band dataset, ASTROCO-S and ASTROCO-L achieve lower reconstruction error and higher macro-F1 classification scores than Astromer v1/v2, with the smaller model surpassing Astromer using fewer resources. The passage states that locality-aware convolutions and gating improve representation quality, soft feature mixing across layers yields better embeddings than fixed pooling, and the approach is resource-efficient.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture. A100 Tensor Cores accelerate HPC with IEEE-compliant FP64, delivering up to 2.5x V100 FP64 performance; 108 SMs give 19.5 TFLOPS peak FP64. Mixed-precision Tensor Cores support HPC iterative refinement, and cuSOLVER’s TCAIRS automates mixed precision; TF32 was fastest and most robust among tested modes, with 2.0x geomean speedup over FP64 and up to 4x for large complex matrices. A100 introduces fine-grained structured 2:4 sparsity, sparse MMA skipping zeros for 2x throughput, and a prune/fine-tune recipe. It has combined 192 KB L1/shared memory per SM, simultaneous FP32/INT32 execution, 40 GB HBM2 at 1555 GB/s, SECDED ECC, 40 MB L2 cache, L2 residency controls, and compute data compression. MIG partitions A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances; Compute Instances enable simultaneous contexts. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/s total bandwidth, and PCIe Gen4 with SR-IOV is supported. Error/fault detection, isolation, and containment are included. Additional features include NVJPG decode, an optical flow accelerator, improved atomics, and five NVDECs. CUDA 11 supports task graphs, async copy, async barriers, L2 residency control, and cooperative groups. DGX A100 uses eight A100 GPUs, NVSwitch, 5 PFLOPS, and NGC software. An appendix covers sparse neural networks and 2:4 sparsity accuracy.

This study reviews literature indicating that Asian HEIs are less competitive than American counterparts in global rankings and that research has focused on ranking indexes, policies, and selected Asian cases, with a gap in longitudinal understanding of Asian HEIs’ overall ranking positions. The study examines the global rankings of five HEIs in ten Asian countries—Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Pakistan, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, and the Russian Federation—from 2015 to 2025 using THE World University Rankings. It uses a qualitative multiple case study design and document analysis, selecting top HEIs based on 2024 THE Asia University Rankings and, for Russia, 2025 THE WUR. Findings show that Chinese and Japanese HEIs generally ranked highest and improved, Russian HEIs were stable and positive, and Indian HEIs advanced. HEIs in the Philippines, Indonesia, Thailand, and Pakistan had neutral or decreasing trends; Bangladeshi HEIs were newer with neutral trends; Vietnamese HEIs showed a marked downward trend. The study concludes that most Asian HEIs lag behind international competitors and lack stable ranking profiles, except in China, Japan, and Russia. It recommends higher education policies to diversify globalization networks, improve global marketing, expand funding, and open overseas offices, while noting limitations that only top five HEIs in selected countries and only THE WUR were examined.

The lecture reviews renormalization and logarithm summation in the effective theory, using b to s gamma and a heavy-to-light current as an example. It explains the counterterms for ultraviolet divergences, the running of the Wilson coefficient, and an anomalous dimension containing a regular term and a cusp term; taking the cusp term leads to Sudakov double logarithms. It discusses leading-log, next-to-leading-log, and higher-order counting and the loop orders needed for matching and anomalous dimensions. It explains the cusp as arising from Wilson lines with a sharp angle and discusses when labels are fixed by external kinematics versus when renormalization involves integrals, citing DGLAP, Brodsky-Lepage, and deeply virtual Compton scattering. The lecture then turns to deep inelastic scattering, Breit-frame kinematics, hard-collinear factorization, and operators related to quark and gluon parton distribution functions.

The passage discusses the rise of open source software and the value of patterns for distributed systems. It describes patterns as general blueprints that help developers learn from others, share vocabulary, and build reusable components. It presents single-node container patterns—sidecar, ambassador, and adapter—for modular, reusable containers coscheduled on one machine. Sidecars augment application containers, with examples such as adding HTTPS, configuration synchronization, topz monitoring, and a simple PaaS. Ambassadors broker interactions between an application and external services, including sharded Redis, service brokering, and request splitting. Adapters modify an application’s interface to match a predefined interface, such as for Prometheus monitoring, Fluentd logging, and MySQL health checks. The passage also introduces multi-node patterns for microservices, including replicated load-balanced stateless services, session-tracked services, caching layers, rate limiting, SSL termination, and sharded services, including sharded and replicated sharded caches.

This study examined whether increasing physical education hours with cognitively engaging activities improved attention among middle school students. Seventy-five participants from two classes (Class 6 and Class 7) were divided into experimental (n=41) and control (n=34) groups. Class 6 had four PE hours per week; Class 7 had two. From October to December, students followed PE curricula including agility drills, coordination circuits, and strategic team games. Attention was assessed with the Bells Test, measuring processing speed in 30 seconds and total detection over 120 seconds. Results showed significant improvement in attention speed for the experimental groups in both Class 6 and Class 7 (p<0.001); control groups showed no significant changes. Sustained attention over 120 seconds improved significantly only in the experimental Class 6 group (p=0.012), with no notable change in Class 7. The study concludes that increasing PE hours, especially with designed activities, can improve short-term attention, but further research is needed on long-term effects and content-specific impacts.

A method configures hardware for implementing a Deep Neural Network by using a programmable lookup table in an activation module to approximate an activation function. Calibration data is provided to a representation of the hardware, inputs to the activation module are monitored to determine an input range, lookup data representing the activation function over that range is generated, and the lookup data is loaded into the hardware lookup table. The process may be repeated for multiple activation functions and activation modules. The passage also describes interpolation using most significant bits as lookup addresses and remaining bits for interpolation, simultaneous lookup from two data stores, clamping or extrapolating inputs outside the determined range, applying an offset, determining ranges by maximum/minimum values or histograms, switching lookup data sets, using a ReLU path and turning off the lookup table when appropriate, and manufacturing hardware using an integrated circuit definition dataset.

The passage addresses the limitations of traditional relational databases for spatiotemporal data and the adoption of spatial extensions such as PostGIS. It explains that GeoSQL requires spatial data types, functions, indexes, and operators, posing usability challenges for users with different backgrounds. While LLMs can generate SQL from natural language, extending this to PostGIS introduces errors including function hallucination, parameter misuse, invalid geometry construction, syntax misuse, SRID/projection errors, and environment-dependent behavior. Existing benchmarks such as Spider, WikiSQL, BIRD, GeoCode-Eval, AutoGEEval, SPOK, GeoGPT, GeoQueryJP, and SpatialSQL do not fully evaluate PostGIS GeoSQL generation.

The study introduces GeoSQL-Eval, described as the first end-to-end automated evaluation framework for systematically assessing LLMs in PostGIS query generation, and GeoSQL-Bench, a benchmark spanning language understanding to query execution. The framework uses four cognitive dimensions, five capability levels, and twenty task types. GeoSQL-Bench contains 14,178 tasks: 2,380 multiple-choice and true/false questions, 3,744 syntax-level SQL generation questions with distractor formulations, and 2,155 table schema retrieval questions with distractor counterparts. It evaluates conceptual understanding, structured SQL generation, semantic alignment and invocation, execution and result accuracy, and robust generalization and reasoning.

The study evaluates 24 models across six categories: general non-reasoning, general reasoning-enhanced, general code generation, geospatial code generation, general SQL generation, and GeoSQL generation strategy models. Results show general non-reasoning and reasoning-enhanced models generally perform well, while table schema retrieval remains a major bottleneck. Errors are mainly PostGIS function errors and SQL syntax errors, together accounting for about 70%. General non-reasoning models perform best in efficiency, and o4-mini balances accuracy and computational overhead. The study also releases a GeoSQL-Eval leaderboard platform. Limitations include incomplete coverage of PostGIS functions, focus on vector processing functions and the PostGIS plugin, and limited model coverage.

The passage discusses the cup and handle pattern, also called cup with handle. It is a bullish continuation chart formation resembling a cup with a handle, consisting of a rounded cup after a price rally and a handle trading range on the right side. The pattern completes when price breaks out from the handle, signaling continuation of the prior rally. An inverted version forms in a downtrend and signals downtrend continuation. The passage covers identifying the pattern in different markets, the role of volume and price action, setting stop-loss orders, common mistakes, fitting it into broader strategies, long-term trends, volatility’s effect, and psychological aspects. It notes William O’Neil described the pattern and traders may place a stop buy order above the handle’s upper trendline. It mentions examples, double cup and handle, target measurement, and backtests by Ali Akhtari and Thomas Bulkowski. Bulkowski found a 26% failure rate, dropping to 10% after an upside breakout, with a 38% average gain; Akhtari’s 2016–2018 test underperformed the S&P 500 but showed good metrics with low market exposure. The passage says a 100% quantified cup and handle strategy was not developed.

The lecture revisits the graph removal lemma and discusses the induced graph removal lemma, where induced copies of H are considered and graphs may be edited by adding or deleting fewer than εN² edges. Irregular pairs are identified as an obstacle, motivating the strong regularity lemma. That lemma gives a pair of partitions P and Q, with Q refining P, P ε₀-regular, Q extremely regular, and bounded energy difference; it is proved by repeatedly applying Szemerédi’s regularity lemma. A corollary yields an equitable partition with subsets W_i such that W_i,W_j pairs are regular, including self-regularity, and edge densities between V_i,V_j and W_i,W_j are mostly similar. This corollary is used to prove the induced removal lemma by partition, cleaning, and counting. The lecture also states a colorful removal lemma, an infinite removal lemma for possibly infinite families of induced patterns, and connects removal lemmas to property testing, stating that hereditary properties are testable by oblivious testers with one-sided error.

Higher-order Feynman diagrams, especially a self-energy correction to a propagator, produce a loop integral that diverges at infinity. Introducing a cutoff leaves an infinite contribution. Renormalization can redefine physical masses and couplings as bare values plus corrections. Since experiments occur at a specific scale, high-scale infinities are not a practical problem for comparing theory and experiment. Couplings run with energy; electromagnetic, weak, and strong couplings do not all converge at high mass scales unless new particles are introduced, which can change running behavior and possibly allow unification. Observed masses and couplings are evaluated at a specific scale.

Boston has been the world’s leading life sciences hub, with the most lab space and large venture capital and federal research funding, but federal funding cuts and threats to higher education are challenging its competitive edge.

The passage compares dollar-cost averaging, which invests fixed amounts at regular intervals, with lump sum investing, which invests a large amount all at once. It concludes that historically lump sum investing provides a higher probability of success, favors being invested over long-term horizons of preferably at least ten years, and says financial crises become insignificant over the long run.

NeoWorld is a framework for constructing an infinitely expandable, interactive virtual world from a single image, initially representing the environment in 2D and progressively unfolding detailed 3D models as users interact. It uses a hybrid object-centric scene structure with lightweight 2D/2.5D Gaussian backgrounds and full 3D foreground objects, guided by camera trajectory, object proximity, or user prompts. The system integrates inverse rendering, panoptic segmentation, codebook-based object-centric attributes, image-to-3D reconstruction and alignment, and LLM-based interpretation of natural language for object manipulation and physics-based animation. Experiments compare NeoWorld with world generation, object-centric learning, and video/interactive baselines, reporting advantages in interactive world generation, object-centric IoU, and text-guided dynamics. Limitations include reliance on cascaded pre-trained modules, where upstream errors can propagate and affect final world simulation.

Senator Gatchalian urged DepEd to address delays in public school teachers’ performance-based bonuses, calling delays since SY 2012–2013 unacceptable and seeking streamlined clearances. Teachers have not received SY 2016–2017 bonuses; DepEd cited failed biddings and delayed clearances.

Former president Robert Mugabe returned home amid allegations after the June 24 Bulawayo bomb explosion, which killed two and injured over 40, including officials. Government claims it was an attempt on President Emmerson Mnangagwa’s life. Mnangagwa said in a BBC interview he suspected Mugabe’s G40 allies and could not trust Grace Mugabe. Jonathan Moyo said the administration was seeing ghosts everywhere.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with a built-in analog front end. Each analog input has an internal clamp protection circuit allowing swings up to ±18V; beyond that the clamp turns on, input current must not exceed ±10mA, and a series resistor can limit current and form an antialiasing low-pass filter. Each channel has a PGA supporting single-ended and differential bipolar inputs, programmable input ranges, and programmable LPF options. A common-mode rejection circuit supports common-mode voltages up to ±12V. The device outputs 20 bits in straight-binary or two’s-complement format. It uses a differential or single-ended free-running sampling clock, SMPL_SYNC for multi-device synchronization, internal or external reference, and a 2-lane or 4-lane SDR/DDR data interface with DCLKOUT and FCLKOUT; the 20-bit result is output MSB first in a 24-bit packet with six zero bits. Features include data output randomizer, simple and moving averaging, test patterns, reset and power-down, initialization sequence, speed-boost mode up to 8MSPS for a selected channel pair, SPI register access, and SPI daisy-chain configuration. Application information covers ATE use, TUE, power supplies, layout, and development tools.

On February 2, 2015, Apple Inc. entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. and Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. for the issuance of $500,000,000 floating rate notes due 2020 and fixed rate notes totaling $6,000,000,000 across 2020, 2022, 2025, and 2045 maturities. The notes will be issued under an indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A. as trustee, pay interest quarterly or semi-annually, and are Apple’s senior unsecured obligations. The passage describes tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and spread by inhaled aerosol droplets. WHO estimated about 10 million people fell ill and 1.4 million died from TB in 2019, with 1.6 million deaths in 2021; TB is a major cause of adult mortality from a single infectious agent, surpassed by COVID-19. COVID-19 affected TB diagnosis, treatment, and burden, and corticosteroid use was linked to reactivation of latent TB. Pulmonary TB is most common. Standard drug-sensitive treatment uses rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for a two-month intensive phase, followed by isoniazid and rifampicin for at least four months; resistance can emerge. Extrapulmonary TB (EPTB) accounted for about 16% of reported cases in 2019, with lymph node TB most frequent, followed by pleural TB. EPTB is overlooked and less studied. The study develops a whole-body human physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model to simulate distribution of all four first-line anti-TB drugs at extrapulmonary sites, adding pleura and lymph node compartments and considering slow and rapid isoniazid acetylation. The model is calibrated and validated using reported plasma and lung concentration data. Simulations compare drug concentrations with WHO critical concentrations. Results suggest rifampicin and isoniazid often exceed critical concentrations, ethambutol and pyrazinamide often do not, and rifampicin pleural concentrations are over-predicted. Limitations include assumptions of drug-susceptible TB, no drug-drug interactions, no rifampicin autoinduction, and a single lymph node compartment. The authors state the model can help evaluate and optimize EPTB treatment.

Microsoft Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2017 includes unaudited consolidated financial statements, notes, an independent registered public accounting firm review report, management's discussion and analysis, market risk disclosures, controls and procedures, and other information. For the three months ended September 30, 2017, revenue was $24,538 million, net income was $6,576 million, basic earnings per share were $0.85, and diluted earnings per share were $0.84, compared with revenue of $21,928 million, net income of $5,667 million, basic earnings per share of $0.73, and diluted earnings per share of $0.72 for the same period in 2016. The notes cover accounting policies, the early adoption of new revenue recognition and leases standards effective July 1, 2017 with restated prior periods, investments, derivatives, fair value measurements, debt, income taxes, unearned revenue, leases, contingencies, stockholders' equity, accumulated other comprehensive income, and segment information. The Federal Reserve raised the federal funds rate by 0.25 points to a 1–1.25 percent target after a two-day FOMC meeting, its second hike in six months and third since Janet Yellen ended the post-crisis flatline policy.

The K-T collaborative EVT registry harmonized CRCS-K in South Korea and TREAT-AIS in Taiwan, comprising 9,941 EVT-treated patients and about 200 common data fields. It aimed to describe registry structure and patient characteristics and examine age’s impact on EVT outcomes. Taiwanese patients were older, had more vascular risk factors, more severe strokes, lower pre-stroke independence, lower IV thrombolysis rates, and longer treatment times. Successful recanalization and symptomatic hemorrhage rates were similar; 90-day functional independence was less common in Taiwan, while 90-day mortality was higher in Korea. Older age was associated with worse functional recovery, higher mortality, and lower successful recanalization, but SICH was comparable across age groups; age’s relationship with recovery and mortality was nonlinear, most pronounced at 75–85 years. Pre-stroke independence and bridging thrombolysis predicted better outcomes in the elderly. Limitations included registry data differences, varying inclusion periods, unavailable imaging/post-discharge data, and retrospective analyses. The study concludes that harmonizing stroke registries can advance care and that selected elderly patients can benefit from EVT.

Dr. Maria Pane became a neonatologist after medical school. At GBMC, she treats very sick, tiny patients, includes parents in rounds, empathizes with them, supports a NICU fundraiser, and values team collaboration.

For Q2 2022, total net sales were $121,234 million, operating income was $3,317 million, and net loss was $2,028 million, compared with net sales of $113,080 million, operating income of $7,702 million, and net income of $7,778 million in Q2 2021. The lecture introduces probabilistically checkable proofs (PCPs), defining them by completeness, soundness, randomness, and query parameters, with a verifier that has oracle access to bits of the proof and often uses nonadaptive queries. It states that for all NP languages one can construct PCPs with completeness 1, soundness 1/2, and polylog n randomness and query complexity, while known PCPs can use O(log n) randomness and 3 queries. The construction for 3SAT uses the GKR protocol: it computes low-degree extensions of layers and includes all possible sumcheck transcripts, and the verifier simulates GKR while checking low-degree extensions and the input. Soundness follows from the 2d sumchecks via a union bound, with field size chosen to keep the PCP polynomial. The lecture also says the second part moves to cryptography by relaxing soundness to computational soundness or arguments.

This study investigated the impact of mydriasis on retinal image gradability and AI-based diabetic retinopathy screening. Patients underwent imaging before and after mydriasis with Tropicamide 0.5%, with two images per eye captured using a portable Phelcom Eyer camera. A CNN pre-trained on ImageNet, trained on mBRSET and validated on the study dataset, classified images as normal or diabetic retinopathy. The study included 327 patients. In the mydriasis group, 1056 images (82.1%) were gradable versus 699 (55.6%) in the non-mydriasis group (P < 0.001). In non-mydriasis, systemic hypertension, age, diabetes duration, male gender, and Indigenous race were associated with lower image quality. AI performance was better with mydriasis: accuracy 82.91%, F1 0.83, AUC 0.94, compared with non-mydriasis accuracy 79.23%, F1 0.79, AUC 0.93. The mydriatic group had fewer false positives (83, 13.9%) than the non-mydriatic group (106, 17.8%), but slightly more false negatives (19, 3.2% vs. 18, 3.0%). A Chi-square test showed no statistically significant difference between groups (P = 0.3279). The discussion notes that mydriasis may improve image quality and model performance, but non-mydriatic imaging may be the only option in some LMICs. Limitations include learning curve, selection bias, single dataset/camera, and combined referral groups.

Robert Pearl Bryson was convicted by a Stephens County jury of aggravated sodomy, aggravated child molestation, child molestation, and failure to register as a sex offender. On appeal, he challenged the sufficiency of the evidence, the denial of motions to quash the indictment and Count 8, the denial of trial counsel’s motion to withdraw, the denial of severance, the admission of a no contest plea, and ineffective assistance of trial counsel. The court found no error, holding the evidence sufficient, the trial court’s rulings proper, and Bryson’s ineffective assistance claim waived. The judgment was affirmed.

Image registration is described as a non-linear inverse problem that seeks a coordinate transform deforming a moving image to resemble a fixed image by minimizing a cost and regularization. The passage identifies memory bottlenecks in deformable interpolation and warp composition, cross-correlation loss, and mutual information loss. It proposes a composite implicit grid sampler, implicit Parzen windowing for Mattes mutual information, and a fused local normalized cross-correlation kernel to reduce HBM usage. It introduces Flash Fused Distributed Primitives (FFDP), including Grid Parallel for boundary-synchronized image sharding and a distributed ring sampler, to shard images, warp fields, and optimizer state across GPUs and scale to arbitrarily large problems. FFDP accelerates traditional registration pipelines by up to 7.48× with up to 59% less memory and deep learning pipelines by up to 6.14× with up to 24% less memory. It registers a 250µm in-vivo MRI to a 100µm ex-vivo FLASH human brain volume with over 11.8B transform parameters in one minute using 8 A6000 GPUs. On faux-OASIS at 250µm, it improves Dice by 18.1 points, InvDice by 31.6 points, and reduces AvgHD90 by 62.1%.

The paper addresses digital transformation and AI innovation, focusing on relationships among Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data (BD), and Advanced Analytics (AA). It aims to develop a multidimensional, data-driven AI innovation taxonomy framework and related AI/BD/AA value chains and maturity levels. The research uses a conceptual, multilayered framework approach, literature review, and semi-structured expert interviews with members of the Russian National Technology Initiative, one interview per NTI market, averaging 50 minutes, recorded, transcribed, and thematically analyzed. The paper discusses definitions and backgrounds of AI, BD, and AA; analytics categories; digital business platforms; seven overlapping technology platform areas; an AI/BD/AA micro-level value chain; and a five-level data-driven AI maturity framework. It concludes that organizations must evaluate vision and transform people, processes, technology, and data readiness to use AI, and presents an AI/BD/AA micro-level value chain, a multidimensional BD-driven AI enterprise maturity framework, and corresponding value-chain levels to help with strategic innovation planning, investment decisions, and automation use cases.

This AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 Specification Update (31534D, March 2006) lists issues and resolutions for the CS5535. It covers SSMI event reliability; PIO/UDMA IDE access to CD-ROM; ACPI S3 wake events; RTC CMOS RAM accesses; legacy DMA to LPC devices; USB clock gating; ATAPI packet commands after bus master enable; KEL AuxOutputFull; UDMA tACK timing; ATAC PRD alignment; LPC aborts on Long_Sync/Ready_Sync; SMB NEGACK; GLPCI retry counting; GPIO High Bank writes after suspend; SMBus hold time; LOWBAT_FLAG after standby; and Sleep_X deassertion. Ulysses S. Gandy appealed his second manslaughter conviction and ten-year sentence. He assigned as error the sufficiency of the evidence, refusal of Instruction D-13, admission of State’s Exhibits 1, 5, and 7, and the failure to give the jury a food or refreshment recess. The Mississippi Supreme Court found sufficient evidence supported the verdict, no reversible error in refusing the instruction, no abuse of discretion in admitting the exhibits, and no merit in the recess claim. This paper develops a meta-population extended SIR model to relate Google Community Mobility Reports (GCMR) to SARS-CoV-2 transmission. It models four GCMR settings—grocery and pharmacy, retail and recreation, transit stations, and workplaces—as additive contributors to transmissibility, with temperature/seasonality and Alpha and Delta variants as multiplicative factors, plus region- and week-specific effects and vaccination. It was applied to Norwegian and Swedish regions from February 2020 to July 2021 and to Bavaria and Berlin. The model attributed 60.0% of Swedish and 38.7% of Norwegian infections to GCMR settings, and about 65% in the German regions. Transit stations and workplaces were most important in Norway and Sweden, while retail and recreation was most important in Germany. A 20°C temperature increase reduced transmissibility by about 40%; Delta roughly doubled it, and Alpha showed an estimated 20% increase in Norway. Limitations include linearity assumptions, measurement error, and simplified vaccination. The authors conclude GCMRs are associated with infection dynamics and useful but require strong assumptions and complex modeling.

Grief is an emotional reaction to losing someone or something cared about, and it can also follow significant life changes. It is highly personal, crosses generations, and may occur before a loss as anticipatory grief. Grief can also occur when moving from a long-held home, and major moving decisions after bereavement should be deferred if possible. Grief is complex and variable rather than sequential. Reactions may include numbness, denial, acceptance and relief, yearning and searching, repeating the event, restlessness and disturbed sleep, loss of confidence, guilt, anger, and profound sadness or depression. There is no simple answer for how long grief lasts; time alone does not heal, but most people eventually find good days outnumber bad days. Support and professional help are mentioned.

The ADS9803 features simple and moving data averaging to improve SNR; simple averaging reduces output data rate by a factor of 2, while moving averaging does not affect output data rate. It supports test patterns that replace ADC output data with predefined digital data for debugging and verifying the data interface, configured via registers 0x13 through 0x1B in bank 1 for channel groups CH[4:1] and CH[8:5]. Supported test patterns include fixed pattern, digital ramp, and alternating test pattern. The device can be reset via the RESET pin or register write, powered down via the PWDN pin or register write, and initialized with a sequence of register writes after power-up or reset. Speed-boost mode allows up to 8 MSPS for a user-selected analog input channel pair while remaining channels are idle. SPI register access uses three register banks, bank selection, read-enable bits, and daisy-chain topology. The passage also provides register descriptions, application information for ATE, power supply and layout recommendations, development tools, support resources, revision history, and packaging/orderable information.

The New England Patriots had a poor offensive performance against the Miami Dolphins on Monday night, including two first-quarter yards and 0-for-11 on third downs. After a late field goal, they trailed by seven, but Stephen Gostkowski’s bizarre onside kick was recovered by Miami, which won.

Gray Davis; Duke Energy was accused by Sen.
