Researchers led by Joshua Caldwell reported in Nature Materials a fundamental advance in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) for hyperlensing. Using isotopically purified boron to make hBN crystals, they reduced optical losses in the infrared, increased polariton lifetime three-fold, and tripled travel distance, improving imaging resolution by about a factor of ten over previous hBN. The purified crystal can in principle capture objects as small as 30 nanometers. Hyperlenses may image living cells in natural environments using low-energy infrared light and provide spectroscopic “fingerprint” information, unlike electron-based or atomic-force microscopes. Potential applications include biological and medical science, communications, and nanoscale optical components. Researchers suggest further improvement is possible.

Beating the offside trap is part of defeating offside. Defenders usually delay and retreat, but in the trap they move up, changing the space behind them and placing strikers offside. To beat it, attackers must recognize the trap, adjust to avoid being called offside, and use the space behind defenders, in both run-of-play and free kicks. Patience is required: not run into offside positions, not interfere if offside, and execute tactics. Tactics include dribbling through, through pass, horizontal or lateral run, checking run, pass short, deep-lying run, bending run, back-pass, delay for time, delayed run, and use of a designated “non-runner.” Fakes may reveal the trap before free kicks. A defender may fail to move up, leaving attackers onside, and attackers should take advantage. If successful, the striker with the ball is one-on-one with the goalkeeper and must be prepared to score; after being beaten once, the opposing team is often less likely to use the trap again.

Researchers found that periwinkle sea snails exposed to predicted 2100 ocean acidification declined in metabolism but sped shell-making with less-dense inner shells and developed less-soluble shells, suggesting they and potentially other calcifying organisms may adapt.

This appeal from the District Court of Humacao is almost identical to case No. 2037, differing only in the loan amount; the issue, evidence, and fundamental errors are the same. For the reasons in No. 2037, the judgment is reversed and the defendant is acquitted.

China has blacklisted Canadian research firm TechInsights and nine subsidiaries on its unreliable entity list, accusing it of endangering national security after publishing analysis of Huawei’s advanced AI chips. Barron's Jack Hough suggests Netflix could lose more than half its value, citing Disney's 2019 content pull, Facebook's video service, Amazon Prime, cash burn, and accounting tactics. The passage argues competition fears are overblown because Netflix grew despite Amazon and YouTube; Netflix has raised prices in the U.S., Australia, and Canada without losing subscribers; and its 104 million streaming accounts provide scale, pricing power, and advantages with content creators. It says valuation and debt/accounting critiques ignore Netflix's moat and growth, and that betting against Netflix is dangerous.

A Pediatrics study found that from 1990 to 2015, nearly 17,000 children under 6 were treated in emergency rooms for window-blind injuries; nearly one child died per month and about two were injured daily. Most injuries were minor, often from being struck, but entanglement—11.9% of cases—was linked to nearly 80% of 726 hospitalizations and over 94% of 271 deaths, almost all involving cords, mostly at home and often unwitnessed. Dr. Gary Smith advocates mandatory unexposed or inaccessible cords. A voluntary standard has existed since 1996; in 2014 the CPSC approved a petition for a mandatory standard, and a 2017 proposal would require stock products to be cordless or have inaccessible cords, awaiting final approval. The CPSC recommends cordless or inaccessible-cord coverings, and the manufacturers association suggests a “Best for Kids” label. Linda Kaiser favors a mandatory rule.

Ryan Kerr, 26, of Maesdown Road, Evercreech, admitted attacks including punching a woman and leaving a man unconscious in a pub. The court heard he showed no remorse. He was remanded in custody until October 13 while sentencing is considered, after his lawyer sought psychiatric reports.

Cllr John Holdich reports that 179 of 574 privately-owned homes empty for over six months were brought back into use last year under the Empty Homes strategy; 663 were brought back over five years, generating over £3 million in New Homes Bonus. Phase Two budget proposals and a consultation were published. He cites LGA Chairman Lord Porter’s warning of further core funding cuts and says Peterborough’s grants fell 80% from £55 million to £10 million over eight years, with funding based on outdated population figures; a Stand Up For Peterborough campaign is promoted. Shannon Bard announced that Zapoteca, the Portland restaurant she and her husband Tom owned, is permanently closed. She cited changing priorities as their children enter late high school and college and a desire to spend more time with them. The Bards still have Toroso and Salud, a cooking school and catering company.

The passage describes a study evaluating best supportive care plus convalescent plasma versus best supportive care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. The primary objective was clinical efficacy and safety; the secondary objective was clinical efficacy versus Standard of Care as assessed by clinical severity, oxygenation, ventilation, and hospitalization. It also states that ethics approval was obtained, informed consent was required, serious/unexpected adverse events were reported to ethics committees, and the study followed Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines. It notes the COVID-19 burden, limited therapeutic options, convalescent plasma rationale, and a hypothesis that high-volume, high-titer plasma early in hospitalization reduces the need for mechanical ventilation.

The NAAIM Exposure Index, compiled by the National Association of Active Investment Managers, measures the average US equity market exposure reported by its members and is a two-week moving average of weekly survey responses. It is used to gauge investor sentiment and may act as a contrarian indicator, but backtests found better contrarian indicators and poor performance for NAAIM trading strategies. The index is not predictive and is of little value in determining future stock market behavior.

Lubrizol Corp. will spend US$80 million to expand production capacity and technology for its engineered polymers TPU business in North America, Europe, and Asia, citing increased demand. It is adding North American production, storage, and logistics capabilities; compounding and extrusion lines in Songjiang, China; and European production capabilities, with further investment planned in Asia and Europe in 2019.

Jeff Horn will defend his WBO welterweight title against Gary Corcoran in Brisbane on Wednesday. Promoter Bob Arum said a win could lead to major fights in 2018, with Terence Crawford as mandatory and a potential Pacquiao return. Horn aims to dispel doubts about his contentious win over Manny Pacquiao. Corcoran, 17-1 and WBO-ranked 10th, is the underdog fighting outside Britain and Ireland for the first time for a world title. Sanofi confirmed it is being investigated by the European Commission for potentially anticompetitive activity. President Trump announced Pfizer agreed to lower prices on its drugs for Medicaid and directly to patients, launch new medicines at parity with other countries, and, if it continues investing in U.S. manufacturing, avoid certain tariffs on imported drugs. Manchester City hosts Burnley on Jan. 2 at Etihad Stadium. City need wins, Chelsea chase the title, and Burnley need points to avoid relegation. This study used EEG to investigate increased neural noise in Tourette syndrome (TS), operationalized as trial-by-trial variability in magnitude and/or timing of responses to median nerve electrical stimulation. Participants were 20 adults with TS, one of whom did not complete EEG, and 19 matched healthy controls. The passage reports that early and mid-latency SEP amplitude, timing, and topography were mostly similar between groups, except for a 1 ms P1 delay and increased P2 (P100) amplitude in TS; P100 magnitude was associated with tic impairment. Contrary to predictions, timing variability was not increased in TS, and N2 timing variability was reduced. Trial-by-trial SEP amplitude variability was increased in TS throughout the epoch, but standardized variability and coefficient of variation decreased after stimulation similarly in both groups. Power spectral density was increased in TS at high-beta and gamma frequencies, and 1/f slopes were flatter in TS. Inter-trial phase coherence increased after stimulation in both groups, with some between-group differences in alpha, beta, and gamma coherence. The passage concludes that trial-by-trial recruitment of sensorimotor populations may be less stable at rest in TS but may normalize in response to stimulation, and that increased P100 may relate to altered central processing of somatosensory stimuli.

The paper surveys and evaluates ontologies and ontology design patterns (ODPs) for process modeling in Materials Science and Engineering. It defines three domain requirements—process structure, data and resources, and project goals and participant roles—and uses them to assess relevant ontologies, including P-PLAN, Metadata4Ing, OPMW, WILD, GPO, and PMDcore. ODPs were manually derived and reviewed by domain experts in the Linked Open Data Working Group, then a baseline method for automated extraction was evaluated using semantic similarity and ROBOT-based modular extraction against ground truth with precision, recall, and F1-score. P-PLAN achieved the top F1 scores for Process and Resource ODPs, while PMDcore supported all three ODP categories. The paper reports limitations related to annotation quality, requirement formulation, and independent ontology processing, and proposes future work on additional MSE subdomains, ontology mappings, improved evaluation, and a platform for publishing extracted patterns.

In July 2021, Public Health Wales investigated an outbreak of salmonella gastroenteritis linked to an Eid al-Adha celebration barbecue in a Cardiff public park. Cases were defined as diarrhoea and/or vomiting with onset on the barbecue day and an epidemiological link to the celebration meal. A cohort study of 36 attendees and a nested case-control study using Firth logistic regression were conducted, along with culturally sensitive communications developed with the community. In total, 22 symptomatic cases were identified. Consumption of the traditional raw liver dish “marrara” at the barbecue was the most likely vehicle for infection (aOR 49.99, 95% CI 1.71–1461.54, p=0.02). Meat came from two local butchers with the same supplier, and food samples yielded whole genome sequences identical to those from cases. Five cultured human isolates were Salmonella Typhimurium and were genetically indistinguishable. Many cases were severely unwell, with 12 cases seeking emergency hospital care, six admitted overnight, and one requiring intensive care. The authors concluded that this outbreak identified a new vehicle of interest, a traditional raw offal dish, and that future outbreak investigations, particularly those associated with cultural events, should consider dishes beyond routine questionnaires that may be relevant to the community. They also highlighted the need for appropriate food hygiene advice and culturally sensitive public health messaging.

An appeals court ruled the federal government cannot legally stop trade of Burmese pythons and other giant exotic snakes within the continental U.S. The ruling does not change the ban on importing these snakes or state laws. The case followed 2012 and 2015 bans intended to protect native wildlife. A reptile keepers association said the ban was unnecessary, and an attorney said the ruling has implications for invasive species.

The passage discusses the Coppock Curve strategy, devised by economist E.S.C. Coppock under an Episcopal Church mandate to find long-term investment opportunities. Also called the Coppock Guide, it was introduced in 1965. It is a smoothed momentum indicator used mainly for long-term significant market swings, primarily in stocks. Its formula is a 10-month weighted moving average of the sum of the 11-month and 14-month rate of change; these values were originally proposed by Coppock after estimating 11 to 14 months for recovery from mourning. Signals are a long entry when the curve crosses above zero and an exit when it crosses below zero. The strategy uses a monthly timeframe and has few trades. A backtest on the S&P 500 since 1960 lists 12 trades over 63 years, reduced drawdown, about a quarter less time in the market, and risk-adjusted return exceeding buy-and-hold.

Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, flood insurance, appraisals, and social equity concerns are discussed. Green mortgages and energy-efficient mortgages may offer lower rates or larger loans due to higher property value, lower energy bills, and lower default risk. A blitz is a defensive play where five or more defenders rush into the offensive backfield to attack the ball carrier and disrupt the offense, compared with the usual four rushers. A blitz can use five to eight players. It carries risk because fewer defenders remain to cover receivers, and mobile quarterbacks can evade it, but a well-timed blitz can be catastrophic. Defensive coordinators call defensive plays and may use blitzes to outsmart the offense. Types include conventional blitzes, zone blitzes, safety blitzes, cornerback blitzes, zero blitzes, and run blitzes. Offenses can beat blitzes with quick passes, often to running backs; mobile quarterback play; and max protection schemes that keep extra players back to block. Blitzes often leave a weak point for the offense to exploit.

The passage discusses LIS initial education and lifelong learning in Romania. The passage presents a framework for information design with LLMs that combines Bayesian persuasion with framing. It models a sender and receiver, where the sender observes the state and may choose a recommendation scheme, a framing, or both; framing maps to receiver beliefs via a belief oracle, while recommendation-induced belief updates are Bayesian. It analyzes recommendation-only, framing-only, and joint optimization. Framing-only is shown to be discontinuous and NP-hard even to approximate, whereas joint optimization is continuous and admits a QPTAS. Empirically, a hill-climbing method using LLMs for joint optimization is tested in realtor and clothing-brand case studies; LLM reactions are highly responsive, while human subjects show less pronounced but directionally correct and magnitude-approximate effects. Related work and formal model definitions are also reviewed.

The passage describes the adapter pattern as the final single-node container pattern, where an adapter container modifies an application container’s interface to conform to a consistent predefined interface. It then introduces multi-node distributed patterns, including microservices, replicated load-balanced services, stateless services with readiness probes, session-tracked services, application-layer replicated services with caching, rate limiting, and SSL termination, as well as sharded services, sharded caches, sharding functions, consistent hashing, replicated sharded serving, and hot sharding. It also presents the scatter/gather pattern, including leaf sharding and trade-offs such as overhead, stragglers, and reliability, and discusses FaaS and event-driven processing, covering benefits, challenges, background processing, memory needs, cost considerations, and patterns such as decorators, event handling, two-factor authentication, and event-based pipelines.

The study investigates high-energy (1 MeV) electron beam irradiation as a controlled method for defect engineering in monolayer MoS2. CVD-grown MoS2 on SiO2/Si was irradiated at a flux of 3×10^6 electrons/s for 30, 60, and 120 s. Raman spectra showed shifts in E1 2g and A1g modes, increased A1g/E1 2g ratio, and enhanced LO(M) and LA(M) modes with exposure, consistent with chalcogen vacancies and disorder. PL showed excitonic blueshift and quenching, with defect-related emission 200–300 meV below the A exciton that broadened and intensified with irradiation. XPS indicated Mo5+ and Mo6+ states and Mo-O bonding, while KPFM showed decreased surface potential and increased work function (4.8 to 5.24 eV), indicating p-type doping. Temperature- and power-dependent PL showed strong electron-phonon coupling for defect-bound excitons and saturation of defect states. Circular polarization-resolved PL showed reduced valley polarization from 62% to 38% with irradiation. First-principles calculations for sulfur vacancies and oxygen interactions showed donor states from vacancies and acceptor states near the valence band from oxygen interactions, supporting p-type doping and the defect PL peak. The work concludes that high-energy electron beams can controllably introduce defects in MoS2.

The Wing-T offense uses misdirection, unusual formations, and a diverse run game to exploit overly aggressive and undisciplined defenders. It was developed by Harold “Tubby” Raymond at the University of Delaware. It requires at least two solid running backs, an athletic quarterback, and can use smaller, quicker offensive linemen. Its strengths include slowing aggressive defenses, experienced adjustments, and being unusual; its main weakness is the lack of a traditional dropback pass game. Common formations include Wing, Wing-Slot, and Unbalanced; common runs include Buck Sweep, Down, and Trap; common passes include Waggle, Single Receiver Option Route, and Play Action Vertical. The traditional offense is largely extinct in major college football but remains common in high school, and its principles have influenced spread offenses, including Gus Malzahn’s.

The document covers the ADS868xW device’s ACQ and CONV states, NAP mode, programming, data transfer frames, commands, output data word, protocols, register maps, application information, power supply recommendations, layout, support resources, and revision history. In ACQ state the device acquires analog input; it enters ACQ on power-up, reset, or conversion end, and transitions to RESET on the RST falling edge or to CONV on the CONVST/CS rising edge. CONV uses an internal clock and ignores CONVST/CS transitions until conversion completes. Programming supports nine configuration registers and read/write operations; frames begin on the CONVST/CS falling edge and end on the rising edge, with SCLK counter values of 32, less than 32, or greater than 32 determining optimal, short, or long frames. Commands are 32 bits; HWORD commands ignore the LSB of the 9-bit address. Output data depends on frame commands and DATA_VAL bits, with optional flags appended in a specified sequence. Protocols include legacy SPI single/dual SDO-x and source-synchronous modes. The register map lists DEVICE_ID, RST_PWRCTL, SDI_CTL, SDO_CTL, DATAOUT_CTL, RANGE_SEL, ALARM, ALARM_H_TH, and ALARM_L_TH registers. Application information includes a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated AFE and reference, an eight-channel industrial input example using MUX36D08, alarm hysteresis for an NTC thermistor, power-supply decoupling, NAP and power-down modes, and PCB layout guidance.

Corning’s Growth and Strategy Council (GSC) centrally managed innovation. Led by CEO Wendell Weeks, COO Peter Volanakis, and CTO Joe Miller, it met once or twice a month to advise Corning’s four business segments and make strategic decisions, including resource allocation. Charlie Devins, a visiting CTO, questioned whether the GSC created political tensions, slowed innovation, could scale, or be replicated.

Corning had a history of innovation since 1851, including light bulbs, Pyrex, fiberglass, fiber optics, CorningWare, and catalytic converter substrates. After the telecom crash cut revenues from $6.3 billion in 2001 to $3.1 billion, stock fell from $100 to $1.50, with a $5.4 billion loss and over 12,000 layoffs. By 2008 Corning had 24,800 employees, stock at $23, LCD glass leadership, recovered telecom sales, and about 70% of the people who left during the downturn back.

In 2008 Corning had four segments: Display Technologies, Telecommunications, Environmental Technologies, and Life Sciences. Business units were run by GMs reporting to the COO, while longer-term research was centralized at Sullivan Park under the CTO. The GSC, begun in 2001 and later used by Weeks to centralize research spending decisions, focused on high-potential Stage 2 and Stages 3–4 innovation projects; the Technology Council handled early Stage 1–2 projects. The GSC’s role included pacing and investment decisions, resource allocation, portfolio balance, and advice. It met several times a month with core members, used agendas and presenters, and held a September portfolio review with zero-based budgeting at the project level.

Innovation followed a stage-gate process, keystone components, and “patient money,” with long-term investments. RD&E was 10% of revenue. The GSC supported decisions such as diesel filters for Volkswagen in 2005 and fiber-to-the-home for Verizon in 2003. Challenges included scaling, larger meetings, maintaining frank dialogue, prioritizing strategic questions, and addressing new businesses and business models.

The article uses optimization to find profitable robotics and AI trading strategies, focusing on BOTZ, the Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF. The article recommends out-of-sample backtesting and an incubation period before live trading. A 2-hour timeframe also showed a smooth equity curve and nearly as good results, but caution is advised.

The passage describes a simple, scalable fabrication method for visible Fabry–Perot microcavities using buckled dielectric membrane mirrors. The process starts with a double-sided polished Si wafer, applies wet thermal smoothing, deposits an ion-beam-sputtered SiO2/Ta2O5 coating, uses photolithography, and etches from the backside with a Bosch process to create freestanding mirrors that buckle due to compressive strain. Mirrors with varied diameters achieve ROCs from 0.9 mm to 21 mm. At 780.24 nm, the highest measured finesse is 0.89×10^6 and the highest Q is 2.3×10^9; finesse decreases with cavity length due to diffractive loss. Compact cavity assemblies of 45 µm and 1 mm lengths are also demonstrated, with corresponding F and Q values. The method yields state-of-the-art surface roughness and enables single mirrors, arrays, and cavity assemblies, with potential uses in quantum networking, visible lasers, sensing, filters, and external or transfer cavities.

The present disclosure relates to digital twins and digital twin simulations. A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical object, system, or asset that tracks changes across its lifespan; sensors and IoT devices collect real-time data mapped to the virtual model. Embodiments provide computer-implemented methods, systems, and computer program products for executing a digital twin simulation that bypasses one or more input parameters. A real-time data feed from a data collection device creates a digital twin model representing a physical asset’s components and performance. Separate versions of the model reflect changes over time. Input to a simulation is configured by selecting a version or a hybrid of components from multiple versions, selecting at least one component to bypass, optionally substituting components or providing overriding values for non-simulated components, and outputting simulation results. The disclosure also describes computing environments, cloud and container implementations, version management, simulation and reporting engines, and algorithms for creating and simulating digital twins.

The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on Oct. 7 in a challenge to Colorado’s 2019 ban on conversion therapy for minors, which prohibits licensed mental health professionals from providing such treatment to clients under 18 but not to those engaged in religious ministry. Kaley Chiles, a licensed counselor, argues the ban violates free speech by gagging counselors who use only talk therapy, discriminates based on content or viewpoint, and fails strict scrutiny. Colorado argues the law regulates healthcare treatment, not speech, because conversion therapy is unsafe and ineffective, and that it is narrow and survives even strict scrutiny. The district court and a divided 10th Circuit rejected Chiles, applying rational basis review; a dissent said the majority treated speech as conduct. The federal government supports Chiles, saying the law regulates speech as speech and should be remanded for strict scrutiny.

A 167-million-year-old Jurassic lizard discovered on Scotland’s Isle of Skye, named Breugnathair elgolensis, combined snake-like jaws and hook-like teeth similar to pythons with a short body and fully formed limbs. Researchers studied the fossil for nearly a decade and placed it in a new extinct predatory squamate group, Parviraptoridae. The specimen shows both snake-like and gecko-like features in one animal, rejecting earlier suggestions that such bones came from two animals. It was one of the largest lizards in its ecosystem and likely preyed on smaller vertebrates. The authors could not conclusively determine whether it was a lizard-like ancestor of snakes or a stem-squamate that independently evolved snake-like teeth and jaws.

Genel Altimeaux challenged the Unemployment Appeals Commission’s order denying him unemployment compensation benefits. After an initial hearing without Altimeaux, the appeals referee found that he had voluntarily quit; the UAC accepted that finding. On appeal, this court reversed and remanded because Altimeaux had not received notice. On remand, the referee found that Altimeaux lacked notice, and a second hearing was held. Based on testimony from both hearings, the referee again found that Altimeaux voluntarily quit, relying on Bruce Milliken’s earlier testimony. The court held that the referee’s determination was not based on competent, substantial evidence because Milliken’s earlier testimony was not subject to cross-examination. The remaining testimony did not support a finding that Altimeaux voluntarily quit: William Tranowski admitted he did not personally hear Altimeaux quit, and Altimeaux testified that he did not quit. The court reversed with directions to reinstate Altimeaux’s unemployment award.

The Pin and Pull run play creates favorable down-block angles and gets lead blockers into space on the perimeter. Its strengths include adding extra blockers to the point of attack, versatility, allowing offensive linemen to down block or pull based on alignment, and letting the tailback take the ball from the C-gap to the sideline. Its weaknesses are that it requires specific personnel, including at least two guards who can pull and run, and it works best with a speed back; power backs can have relative success. Unlike the original Buck Sweep, which requires a simultaneous inside run threat, Pin and Pull is a true perimeter run. The passage also details assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts and describes two variations: Pin and Pull Toss and TE-Wing Pin and Pull Toss.

Researchers used biologgers with accelerometers, magnetometers, altimeters, and microphones to track greater noctule bats. The study reports that these bats fly above migrating songbirds, dive vertically, and capture, dismember, and consume passerines in flight. Recordings captured feeding buzzes, chewing sounds, and one bird’s distress calls during a 23-minute in-flight meal; one bird escaped near the ground. No video was recorded. DNA from wing wounds and netted bats with feathers and red-stained lips supported the findings. Researchers say this is the first tracking of such a hunt and advances understanding of the greater noctule as a top predator, though little is known about the species.

Jane Goodall died on October 1 at 91. The author recalls a 1990 call with Goodall, who had studied Gombe chimpanzees for nearly 30 years and assembled a unique collection of chimp skeletons. Her team retrieved bodies, let insects clean them in a tin drum, and cleaned the bones. Each skeleton came from an individual with known sex, age, body weight, and life experiences, allowing research on how development influenced skeletal features; ancient hominid fossil researchers lack such information. Goodall said implications for hominids and skeletal variations were unknown. She collected skeletons from the beginning because field workers shouldn’t waste anything. The skeleton of matriarch Flo was larger than most but weighed less than a smaller, stockier male, showing difficulty estimating body weight from bones, and showed bone loss unlike human osteoporosis; Flo gave birth within a few years of dying near age 50. Goodall’s preservation efforts continued to yield scientific dividends.

The passage describes multi-camera imaging systems for imaging faint objects using arrays of cameras that individually may be incapable or low-performance. A common field array includes multiple cameras with a common field-of-view region; a computing system co-registers and combines their images to generate a combined image with greater signal-to-noise ratio, at least √N times an individual image for N images. A hybrid field array uses multiple camera arrays, each with a common field-of-view region; combined images from the arrays are stitched based on partial overlap of their common regions to produce a composite wider-field-of-view image. An adaptive field array detects a target in one camera and automatically reconfigures cameras to a common field-of-view region containing the target, then co-registers and combines images. The systems may increase bit depth, reduce cosmic-ray artifacts, lower costs, scale by adding or removing cameras, and support applications such as astrophotography, satellite detection and tracking, tactical sensing, and night vision. The passage also describes calibration, data collection, and data reduction processes for detecting uncorrelated targets.

The paper reports shock-loading experiments on a natural zircon single crystal from Mud Tank, Australia, cut as (100)-oriented plates and compressed to 13.6 and 51.3 GPa. Samples were investigated by X-ray diffraction, Raman, IR, photoluminescence, cathodoluminescence, and electron microscopy. At 13.6 GPa, zircon was retained; fractures formed, but no evidence of polymorphic transformation was observed, although reidite microdomains could not be completely excluded. CL was generally similar to starting zircon, with reddish patches near fractures. At 51.3 GPa, the material transformed to textured, mosaic reidite with weak relict zircon. It was strongly fractured, showed lower and blue-shifted CL (~430 nm), changed REE3+ luminescence, and contained bright yellow 2–10 μm speckles with enhanced REE3+ emission, apparently confined to planar defects. The discussion attributes reduced CL and REE line changes to defects and multiple REE sites; the bright speckles are interpreted as rapid segregation of REE on dislocations/planar defects during zircon–reidite transformation, on a time scale of tens of seconds. The conclusions state that shock-induced zircon-to-reidite transformation can cause segregation of trace cations such as REE on planar defects, possibly due to the reconstructive mechanism, charge imbalance, and expulsion of admixture atoms. Isotopic characteristics and trace element ratios in zircon and reidite lattices may remain approximately the same as in starting zircon.

During the 2014-2016 West African Ebola epidemic, a new analysis found that 3 percent of patients caused more than 60 percent of infections in others. The epidemic spread across Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia, infecting over 28,000 and killing at least 11,000. Ebola spreads through infected bodily fluids, and dying people and dead bodies can be most dangerous. Traditional funeral practices helped drive spread. Computer models found each patient infected 2.39 others on average, but many infected no one. There was little transmission after people reached hospitals and care centers; those who stayed home drove spread. Superspreaders accounted for about 61 percent of infections, with age as a predictor. Similar superspreading occurred in SARS and MERS. Ebola was stopped by public health efforts including safe burial and quick hospitalization, not vaccines or drugs.

Robert Eugene Poindexter petitioned the Tax Court to review an Appeals officer’s determination that the Commissioner could collect by levy unpaid 1994 and 1996 income taxes. Poindexter had reported the taxes on returns but did not pay. He requested a collection due process hearing, claiming the returns were incorrect because of a dispute with record companies over royalties and asking the IRS to subpoena information from them. At the hearing, he said he did not believe the amounts were correct but did not state whether his correct income was higher or lower and declined to file amended returns. The Appeals officer did not consider the underlying liabilities, verified applicable requirements, and determined the levy balanced efficient collection with intrusiveness. The Court rejected the Commissioner’s first summary-judgment ground under Montgomery, but granted summary judgment on the second and third grounds because Poindexter failed to aver facts sufficient to show error in the assessments or any other error in the determination. Decision for respondent.

Acting CDC Director Jim O’Neill approved recommendations allowing anyone over 6 months to receive an updated Covid-19 shot after discussing risks and benefits with a provider. The recommendation maintains insurance coverage but does not specify whether some individuals will need a prescription, as approved by the FDA. O’Neill also approved giving children under 4 the MMR and chickenpox vaccines separately rather than as a combined shot. The approvals allow states to order updated Covid vaccines for low-income children through the Vaccines for Children program; a delay had left about 50% of U.S. children relying on VFC unable to access them. A new routine childhood vaccine schedule is expected Tuesday.

Agents Mutual, owner of OnTheMarket, is preparing to float on London's AIM to raise £50million and challenge rivals. OnTheMarket is Britain's third biggest online property site behind Rightmove and Zoopla. It plans to use funds to boost marketing, sales, customer relations and technology, including a heavyweight media campaign. It has abandoned mutual status and signed long-term listing agreements. An analyst said toppling Rightmove remains a significant challenge.

While with his children, he was spat at, punched to the floor and kicked after confronting a group with a motorbike. Police described the attackers, a woman with them, and appealed for witnesses.

The case concerns burglary insurance policies that excluded coverage unless the insured kept records enabling the insurer to accurately determine the loss. The plaintiff kept a check-cashing fund and totaled cash and checks nightly on a scratch-pad, without separately listing the checks or recording data needed to claim against drawers. The court held that the plaintiff failed to comply with the record-keeping clause as a matter of law, reversed the judgment, and remanded with directions to dismiss the complaint.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed the Tax Court’s judgment that Pacific Basin Manufacturing & Trade Co. was liable for income tax deficiencies for tax years ending June 30, 1975 and 1976. The taxpayer, a Delaware corporation operating in American Samoa, had excluded revenue from sales to its Hawaii parent under § 931(a). The court held that under § 931(b), the amounts were taxable because they were physically received in the United States when the parent deposited checks in the taxpayer’s Honolulu bank account. It rejected the taxpayer’s argument that receipt depended on the corporation’s primary physical presence.

This work examines variance reduction techniques (VRTs) and population control techniques (PCTs) for time-dependent Monte Carlo neutron transport. Monte Carlo is accurate but converges slowly; VRTs improve efficiency, but many were designed for steady-state calculations and modify particle weights, potentially conflicting with PCTs needed for time-dependent simulations. VRTs discussed include implicit capture (IC), weight windows, CADIS, FW-CADIS, and Cooper-Larsen (CL). PCTs discussed are uniform combing (UC) and weight-based combing (WC). The study uses Shift and MC/DC on a pulsed slab, AZURV1, and a 1D SCRAM problem, with performance measured by runtime and figure of merit.

Results show that weight-based combing with CL weight windows failed due to excessive splitting and memory exhaustion, while IC paired with UC underperformed. CL weight windows with UC performed best in several tests, and time-dependent weight windows improved efficiency over static ones. FW-CADIS performed best among VRTs in the pulsed slab, but efficiency gains were modest. PCTs were valuable for managing particle populations and memory. The work concludes that unsuitable VRT/PCT combinations can harm efficiency, while appropriate combinations can significantly improve time-dependent simulations. Steady-state VRTs can be adapted for time dependence, and further optimization may benefit complex time-dependent problems.

The passage states that languages are vital, but U.S. K–12 and postsecondary language enrollment is low, with some programs threatened or cut and a focus on Spanish or Spanish and another popular language. Its purpose is to reconnect the “why” of language learning and put it into classroom practice, using ACTFL’s “language connects” as a key. It discusses connection as essential and languages as connecting people to languages, cultures, and speakers. It proposes fostering imagined communities—connections formed through imagination—and reports a yearlong study in two suburban eighth-grade German classrooms in the Northeastern U.S. aimed at increasing interest and retention and keeping the German program viable. The approach requires intentional planning but no extra funding and is best done through task-based instruction with authentic tasks. Examples include planning a move abroad, finding an apartment, shopping, using transit, writing emails, résumés, and cover letters. Implementation guidelines include plausible authentic scenarios, activities, assignments, and assessments around them, student autonomy, just-in-time instruction, and authentic assessments. Reported outcomes include students going more in-depth, examining cultures in new ways, increased connection or ability to relate, and increased membership; anecdotally, more students continued language study. It recommends cataloging and collaborating for sustainability and says the approach can be used at all K–16 levels, contexts, and languages. The conclusion says imagined communities provide the why and connection key to language education success.

About 150 Native languages are spoken in the U.S., including 20 in Alaska. He felt fine and energized late in the third period despite many power plays and penalty kills. He says the team’s strength is having four scoring lines. A New York Times survey found dozens of federal judges expressing concern about the Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions in Trump-related cases since his second term. Of 65 responding judges, 12 said the Court used the docket appropriately, 12 said lower courts had sufficient guidance, and 2 of 54 said it improved public perception; 42 said it harmed perception. Some judges anonymously criticized the orders as “mystical,” “overly blunt,” “incredibly demoralizing” and “a slap in the face to the district courts,” while one Trump appointee said they were “flushing out anti-democratic rulings.” The Times acknowledged possible nonrepresentativeness, and the Volokh Conspiracy critiqued possible response bias and district selection.

President Trump was angered by FBI raids on his personal attorney Michael Cohen, calling them an attack on the country. Days later, he pardoned former Bush aide Scooter Libby, convicted in 2007 of perjury and obstruction in a classified leak case. The White House called it clemency to correct an injustice; critics said it sent a message to targets of the Russia investigation. The Constitution gives presidents broad pardon power, but its limits are debated, including whether a corrupt-purpose pardon or self-pardon would be valid. Historical examples include George H.W. Bush’s Iran-Contra pardons, Nixon’s reported consideration of a self-pardon before resigning and being pardoned by Ford, and Clinton’s pardon of Marc Rich. The White House refused to rule out a future pardon for Cohen. Reports said Trump’s lawyer discussed pardons with lawyers for Michael Flynn and Paul Manafort; the lawyer denied it. Rep. Adam Schiff introduced a bill requiring disclosure of connections between pardons and the president’s interests. New York’s attorney general sought to close a double-jeopardy loophole for state prosecutions. Legal experts said a pardon could advance an investigation because recipients lose Fifth Amendment protection and must testify truthfully.

JPMorgan downgraded Valero Energy from Overweight to Neutral and raised its price target from $75 to $78. Analysts said Valero has benefited from more stable returns and improved capital discipline under CEO Joe Gorder, but further multiple uplift may take time due to refining cyclicality. This study uses a Schelling-variant urban migration model with over 200 LLM-driven agents to examine egoism and altruism in group decision-making. Agents choose migration and message-board actions while weighing individual and system utility. Quantitative metrics include Price of Anarchy, Residential Gini Index, and a behavioral archetype matrix; qualitative analysis uses an LLM-as-judge inspired by Grounded Theory. Results identify two LLM archetypes: “Adaptive Egoists” (e.g., o1-mini, o3-mini, Qwen2.5-7B), which default to self-interest but show increased altruism with a message board, and “Altruistic Optimizers” (e.g., Gemini-2.5-pro, Deepseek series), which consistently pursue collective welfare even at personal cost. The authors argue that choosing an LLM for social simulation is a theoretical choice: Adaptive Egoists may better model bounded-rational human dynamics, while Altruistic Optimizers suit idealized pro-social actors. Limitations include simplified migration and homogeneous agents; future work includes human-in-the-loop validation and large-scale simulations with real-world profiles.

This retrospective study used MIMIC-IV data from 1,918 adult ICU patients with intracerebral hemorrhage to examine the association between resting heart rate (RHR) and all-cause mortality (ACM) at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year. Higher RHR was associated with increased ACM, with a nonlinear relationship and a cutoff of 90.3 bpm. RHR below 90.3 bpm appeared independently protective, while RHR above 90.3 bpm was independently associated with higher ACM risk. Subgroup analyses showed interactions with age and intraventricular hemorrhage, and mediation analysis indicated age mediated the relationship. The study concluded that RHR stratification may help guide heart rate control and management, while noting limitations and the need for further trials.

The lecture explains using hedonic pricing to quantify benefits and premiums of green buildings and cities by decomposing housing transaction prices or rents into attributes, such as rooms, subway access, parks, and LEED/green certification, plus a residual, estimated through regression. It contrasts stated-preference surveys with revealed-preference housing-market data and reports green rent and price premiums from literature, including about 6% rent, 7.6% price, and about 6% for LEED and Energy Star. It discusses causal inference issues—counterfactuals, omitted variables, reverse causality, selection bias, and endogeneity—and the need for apples-to-apples comparisons. Techniques mentioned include controls/fixed effects, matching and geographic matching, propensity score matching, RCTs, instrumental variables, regression discontinuity, and difference-in-differences. Examples include Winthrop Center, Bryant Park, High Line Park and gentrification, subway/TOD valuation, and using housing data to value schools, parks, pollution, and accessibility.

Turtle Trading is a trend-following strategy developed by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt in the 1980s. The 1983 experiment tested whether trading could be learned; Dennis trained 14 novices called Turtles, funded their accounts, and many succeeded. Original rules included volatility-based position sizing using ATR, pyramiding winners, and stop-loss exits. Trades used breakouts, such as 20-day highs/lows, with 55-day breakouts for adding positions. The strategy still works today in markets with clear trends; original breakout rules work reasonably well, but traders modify them with technical indicators. It may not be as profitable as in the 1980s, but the Barclay CTA index and successful hedge funds like Swedish Lynx indicate good returns. Backtests from 2007 showed lower performance than earlier periods. Lessons include that trading can be learned, but trend-following has many whipsaws, a low win rate, long drawdowns, and returns concentrated in short periods.

The ADS868xW device includes a second-order antialiasing low-pass filter at the PGA output with a typical –3 dB cutoff of 500 kHz, an integrated high-bandwidth, low-noise ADC driver buffer, and internal or external 4.096 V reference selection via the INTREF_DIS bit. The internal reference is factory-trimmed, temperature compensated from –40°C to +125°C, and can shift due to thermal or reflow stress; external reference mode applies 4.096 V at REFIO and uses REFCAP decoupling. The ADC supports single-ended and differential bipolar or unipolar inputs with straight-binary output and LSB = FSR / 2^16. Alarm features include input and AVDD alarms, programmable input thresholds and hysteresis, fixed AVDD thresholds of 4.7 V and 5.3 V, and active/tripped flags readable through the alarm pin, registers, or appended output data. The multiSPI interface uses shift and configuration registers and supports single-device, standard SPI, and daisy-chain topologies. Device states are RESET, ACQ, and CONV. Programming uses nine configuration registers, 32-bit data transfer frames, input commands, output data words, and SPI or source-synchronous protocols. Register maps and application information cover an industrial analog input module example, thermistor alarm use, AVDD/DVDD decoupling, NAP and power-down modes, PCB layout, and related documentation, revision, and package information.

Preliminary BC Coroners Service data indicated 1,422 suspected illicit drug overdose deaths in British Columbia in 2017, a 43% increase from 993 in 2016. Monthly deaths averaged 129.5 in the first eight months and 96.5 from September to December. Fentanyl was detected in about 81% of deaths, often with cocaine, heroin or methamphetamines; carfentanil was detected in 64 deaths from June to December. Most deaths occurred indoors, over half in private residences; about four in five were male, and more than half were ages 30–49. Officials described a continuing public-health crisis and supported intensified prevention strategies. No deaths occurred at supervised consumption or overdose prevention sites.
A Harvard Business School study shows several AI companions use tricks to keep conversations from ending.

This study investigated DSSCs using natural dyes from mangosteen peel (MP) and grass jelly leaves (GJL) mixed at various MP:GJL volume ratios. DSSCs were fabricated with TiO2 films on ITO glass, dye extracts, iodide/ethylene glycol electrolyte, and graphite counter electrodes. Absorption spectra showed complementary anthocyanin/α-mangostin and chlorophyll-related peaks; blending broadened visible light absorption. Morphological analysis found MP-rich films had cracking, while mixed ratios, especially 1:1, were more uniform; FESEM showed a homogeneous nanoporous mixed-dye photoanode with consistent 15–20 μm thickness. Photovoltaic efficiencies ranged from 2.12% to 3.50%, with the highest PCE at 1:3 MP:GJL (3.50 ± 0.19%), compared with MP alone 2.75 ± 0.31% and GJL alone 2.12 ± 0.46%. Stability tests over ten cycles showed GJL-rich 1:3 and 1:2 retained higher initial efficiencies, 1:1 collapsed rapidly, and MP-dominant samples had intermediate behavior. The study concludes that blending MP and GJL dyes improves DSSC performance via synergistic absorption and offers low-cost, eco-friendly sensitizers, with future work needed on long-term stability.

18-year-old Luca Speight received the Outstanding Achievement Award and Isle of Wight College Student of the Year 2018. He was praised for catching up after a three-month illness, volunteering, and excelling at his work placement; he thanked tutors, course mates, family, and friends.

Depoe Bay, Oregon, home to 1,500 residents and one traffic light, is preparing for the Aug. 21 total eclipse, which will first appear near the town before crossing 14 states. Fearing thousands to hundreds of thousands of visitors, the city has rented portable restrooms, added garbage cans, ordered protective glasses, distributed preparedness leaflets, and planned emergency staffing. It worries about gridlock on the only access road, Highway 101, and about boaters using its lone boat launch; the Coast Guard will monitor harbor traffic. The Feather River basin is expected to receive 7.5 inches of rain over 10 days, less than the 13.6 inches from Feb. 5–11, with rain more spread out and mostly colder, producing snow at lower elevations and less runoff. Meteorologist Jan Null said inflows could be about a quarter of the previous storm’s. Upstream dams are holding water, and Oroville reservoir drainage has averaged about 4 inches per hour, leaving the level at 885.57 feet Tuesday, about 15 feet below the emergency spillway. Officials may gain a nearly 40-foot buffer by Friday. Null noted the record snowpack could cause serious inflow if warm spring weather arrives suddenly.

The lecture reviews the LSZ theorem relating scattering amplitudes to momentum-space time-ordered correlation functions by taking external momenta on shell and stripping external propagators; initial momenta use the negative energy root and final momenta the positive root. It states that only truncated connected diagrams are needed, while external-leg corrections are absorbed into a constant Z. The lecture then turns to fermions, discussing the Klein-Gordon equation’s difficulties, Dirac’s first-order equation, Hermitian matrices alpha and beta, four-component spinors, and the requirement that squaring the equation reduce to Klein-Gordon, yielding anticommutation conditions. Rewriting with gamma matrices gives the Dirac equation and the Clifford algebra. It notes that similarity transformations give equivalent representations, that the massless case can use two-component spinors, and that a conserved current exists classically. Lorentz covariance is to be shown next time.

Phuket Governor Norraphat Plodthong ordered lifeguards back on Phuket beaches by April 1, per NNT. Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt will fund a project using four uncrewed surface vessels to collect data in the rough waters around Antarctica. It is part of Schmidt Sciences’ $45 million, five-year suite of carbon-cycle research funding. Scientists lack data on the Southern Ocean, a major carbon sink, because of extreme conditions and limited ship routes. The drone boats are to operate remotely and continuously, including in winter, take CO2 measurements, use machine learning to plan routes, and make data public. Funding is structured as a public-private partnership in which Schmidt Sciences buys data from USV companies contracted through NOAA. The article also notes proposed federal research funding cuts and says outside funding is becoming more crucial.

The passage documents AGESA host-environment procedures. It covers native assembler, stackless register-passing routines to enable and disable a pre-memory stack, including core-specific stack allocation, MTRR mapping, CAR-mode disable, and cache flushing. It also describes AmdCreateStruct for allocating and pre-initializing structures; procedures to obtain data eye results, APIC address, execution cache size, base PCI address, current processor core identity, and the DIMM/FRU location corresponding to a memory address.
