Lab experiments suggest jostling microbubbles of air and methane can create tiny electrical sparks, or microlightning, possibly igniting swamp gas and forming will-o’-the-wisps. Researchers 3-D printed a nozzle to mimic gas seeping from a swamp, bubbled air and methane through water, and used a photon counter and high-speed camera. When bubbles were made smaller and closer together, the camera captured microlightning. Some scientists are not convinced this solves will-o’-the-wisps, noting swamps differ from lab setups and the lights hover in air, not underwater; lantern flames may also ignite swamp gas. The work may aid triboelectricity, chemical reactions, and environmental chemistry, including pollutant behavior and breakdown.

In daisy-chain topology, all devices’ CONVST/CS and SCLK inputs connect to the host; device 1’s SDI connects to host SDO-x, each SDO-0 connects to the next SDI, and the last SDO-0 connects to host SDI. The host programs identical configuration registers and sets SDO_CTL_REG bits 7–0 to 00h. Devices sample on CONVST/CS rising, shift MSB-first, and host receives device N through device 1. Optimal frames have 32×N SCLK capture edges; shorter frames cause erroneous configuration.

Solawave’s 4-in-1 Renewal Wand is on sale during Prime Day for a little over $100, offering targeted red-light therapy with vibration and warmth. It requires manual three-minute use and has a single 630-nm wavelength; some WIRED staffers reported skin tightening around the eyes. Solawave’s Red Light Therapy Face Mask is also on sale for $227.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated February 10, 2016. The Board elected Wendell P. Weeks as a director and Audit Committee member, granting him 1,365 restricted stock units vesting in three annual installments and entering an indemnification agreement. The Board approved a two-year leave of absence for Diego Piacentini beginning August 2016 and suspended forfeiture of his restricted stock units; Russ Grandinetti will assume responsibility for the international consumer business, reporting to Jeffrey A. Wilke. The Board authorized repurchases of up to $5 billion of common stock, replacing the previous $2 billion authorization, with no fixed expiration.

EUR/USD has a bearish channel; price should reach wave 3's 161.8% Fibonacci before breaking resistance, while 1-hour may retrace to wave 4 Fibonacci resistance. GBP/USD tests contracting-triangle resistance; breakout could support waves 3, but support break invalidates. USD/JPY has a bull flag; 1-hour support break may signal wave 2 retracement.

The message urges legislation to conserve national resources, including improving waterways; reclaiming and irrigating arid, semiarid, and swamp lands; preserving forests and reforesting suitable areas; and reclassifying the public domain to separate mineral, coal, phosphate, and water-power sites from agricultural settlement. It reports a reduced public domain, describes past disposal and fraud under old laws, and calls for classifying lands by principal value, validating and authorizing withdrawals, separating surface rights from mining rights, leasing minerals on royalty terms with anti-monopoly provisions, and retaining government control over water-power sites. It stresses soil conservation, notes dry-farming and reclamation projects, recommends bonds to complete reclamation projects, repeal of timber-land acts and public sale of timber, reforestation, and improvement of inland waterways such as Ohio River dams and Mississippi/Missouri projects. It also urges prompt action on these recommendations without awaiting the ordered investigation.

The passage describes NVIDIA RTX IO, which benefits artists and designers using large datasets such as CAD models and 3D scientific visualizations, and can enable high-resolution, high-framerate VR imagery. It addresses storage-to-GPU data bottlenecks, plugs into Microsoft’s DirectStorage API, and brings GPU-based lossless decompression so reads remain compressed until delivered to the GPU, reducing CPU load and improving I/O performance by a factor of two. A figure claims 100X throughput and 20X lower CPU utilization. RTX IO uses compute kernels, DMA and copy engines, and Turing/Ampere SMs; DirectStorage is targeted for a developer preview for Windows next year, and RTX IO-enhanced games will be available for Turing and Ampere gamers.

The passage also covers NVIDIA A40 for data centers: GA10x Ampere architecture, second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, up to 2X FP32 throughput, up to 2X ray-tracing throughput, and up to 5X or 10X with Sparsity AI throughput compared with Quadro RTX 6000. It has PCIe Gen4, 48GB GPU memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, three DP1.4 outputs, vGPU support, and EGX Platform compatibility.

Ampere display support includes 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz, DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a, two 8K60 displays, HDMI 2.1 with 48Gbps, and HDCP 2.3/1.x. Fifth-generation NVDEC supports hardware decoding for MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1; AV1 offers bitrate savings and low CPU usage up to 8K60 HDR. Seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding, offloading CPU work for streaming and recording; GA10x encodes up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

GA10x Ampere provides up to 2x improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. The second-generation RT Core doubles ray/triangle intersection performance and supports ray-traced motion blur; the third-generation Tensor Core implements structural sparsity. GA10x is the first GPU to support GDDR6X memory. RTX A6000 has a GA102 GPU, 10,752 CUDA cores, 48GB GDDR6, and 96GB combined memory via NVLink. GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 24GB GDDR6X, 82 SMs, and 10,496 CUDA cores; RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6. Appendix B describes Error Detection and Replay on GDDR6X, which detects transmission errors and replays transactions, causing performance to plateau during overclocking.

The document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests so a guest OS can interoperate with hypervisors. It defines protocol versions and revisions, hypervisor feature advertisement via a FEATURES bitmap, GHCB MSR protocol requests/responses, GHCB GPA registration/unregistration, and negotiation examples. It lists Non-Automatic Exits and describes handling for IOIO, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO, Page State Change, SNP Guest/Extended/TIO Requests, AP Creation, #HV Doorbell Page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, Secure AVIC, and Termination Request. It also covers guest identification of SEV-ES, SMP booting, AP Jump Table, NMI, debug registers, #HV doorbell data and host behavior, and states SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

The passage discusses consumer confidence and its relationship to stock market returns, focusing on the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index and related backtests. Consumer confidence is defined as consumers’ optimism or pessimism about the economy. The Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index surveys 5,000 U.S. households monthly using five questions answered positive, negative, or neutral; changes under 5% are usually deemed insignificant, while changes over 5% indicate a shift in economic momentum. The University of Michigan index is a monthly telephone survey dating to the 1940s, covering personal finances and short- and long-term economic expectations, with preliminary and final reports. The backtests use OECD U.S. consumer confidence data from 1993. A strategy investing in the S&P 500 only when confidence is above its 12-month moving average turns $10,000 into $99,000, with an 8.4% CAGR, 23% max drawdown, and 55% time invested; buy-and-hold turns $10,000 into $159,000, with a 10.4% CAGR and 55% max drawdown. The opposite strategy, invested only when confidence is below its 12-month average, turns $10,000 into $15,000, or 1.58% annually. The passage concludes that stocks tend to perform better when consumer confidence is bullish and worse when bearish, and that confidence is an important economic indicator affecting spending and market sentiment.

Natalie Grabow, 80, set the world record as the oldest female to finish the Kona Ironman World Championship, completing the course in 16 hours, 45 minutes, and 26 seconds. She was the only woman in the 80–84 age category. Grabow learned to swim at 59 and began triathlons at 60. She had earlier run 5Ks and 10Ks, and at 61 qualified for Kona, where she did her first ocean swim and marathon. She prepares for months, working out about two hours daily, eats a varied healthy diet without restriction, and takes multivitamins. In the 2025 race, she fell near the finish line and was greeted by previous record holder Cherie Gruenfeld. She received a winner’s bowl and plans to recover before training and competing again.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A40 as a data center GPU optimized for visual computing, based on the GA10x Ampere architecture, with performance gains over the Turing-based Quadro RTX 6000, PCIe Gen4, 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, vGPU and EGX compatibility, and display outputs. It also covers Ampere display technologies, NVDEC/NVENC video decoding and encoding including AV1, GeForce RTX 30-series gaming features, RTX A6000 workstation specifications, GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay, and legal notices.

Lenovo officially unveiled the ThinkPad 25, a limited-edition retro laptop based on the T470 but inspired by the 700C. It has a 14-inch Full HD touchscreen, Intel Core i7-7500U, GeForce 940MX, 16GB DDR4, 512GB SSD, multiple ports, Windows Hello fingerprint scanner, and 18-hour battery life. It is available in limited quantities in select countries starting at $1,899.

The passage discusses molecular dynamics methods for calculating thermal properties, particularly the Green-Kubo and non-equilibrium MD methods, and the central role of heat flux in determining thermal conductivity and interfacial thermal conductance. It notes that spectral decomposition of heat current requires defining mechanical power from interatomic forces and is difficult for many-body interactions. LAMMPS originally used a heat-flux formula valid only for pair potentials, which can yield incorrect thermal conductivity. Correct formulations exist, but implementations have limited applicability. The work extends and implements Torii et al. formulas in LAMMPS for heat flux in a control volume and control surface, and for spectral decomposition, for arbitrary many-body potentials. The article presents theoretical background, comparative tests, and findings.

COPD is a leading U.S. cause of death, caused almost exclusively by smoking. Symptoms include chronic coughing and shortness of breath. Diagnosis involves smoking history and pulmonary function tests; treatments include inhalers, oxygen, and pulmonary rehabilitation. There is no cure; stopping smoking is most important to prevent or reduce severity.

This text discusses distance education’s growth and history, especially during COVID-19, and reports a qualitative study on distance education in sports higher education in Turkey. The study used semi-structured interviews with 14 lecturers and descriptive analysis. Findings were grouped into positive aspects, negative aspects, challenges, and management. Positive aspects included time and space flexibility, access to resources, technology use, socioeconomic benefits, and reduced pandemic spread. Negative aspects included socialization and psychological issues, communication and participation problems, motivation issues, inequality, technology/access problems, and ineffectiveness for applied sports lessons. Challenges included infrastructure and connection issues, assessment difficulties, ineffective communication, and lesson-related difficulties. Participants saw distance education as useful in mandatory situations but felt the process was not well managed. The study concludes that distance education is an alternative model, but problems affect teaching and participation; sports education needs field-specific design, data security measures, and further research.

This paper studies the tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) effect in Mn3Sn(01¯10)/MgO(110)/Mn3Sn magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) using first-principles calculations. Mn3Sn is a kagome noncollinear antiferromagnet with an inverse 120° antiferromagnetic structure at room temperature that macroscopically breaks time-reversal symmetry. The authors calculate the tunneling conductance with a scattering-theory/Landauer–Büttiker approach and obtain a finite TMR effect, with the TMR ratio reaching ≳1000% at 12 MgO layers. The analysis of bulk Mn3Sn spin polarization, momentum-resolved transmission, and the complex band structure of MgO indicates that the TMR effect arises from momentum-dependent spin splitting in Mn3Sn and screening/filtering of tunneling electrons by MgO, with the x-component of spin polarization identified as dominant.

Jeff Bezos suggested orbital data centres could address Earth’s digital infrastructure constraints by easing land, energy, and cooling limits and providing resilience. However, radiation shielding, power storage, vacuum cooling, low-latency communication, and launch/maintenance costs remain hurdles. Aerospace and technology firms are exploring orbital and lunar infrastructure amid falling launch costs and rising cloud and AI demand.

Owl eyes are immobile and tubular, giving binocular vision. A Journal of Neuroscience study tested barn owls’ ability to find a moving target among shifting backgrounds, a task previously tested only in primates. The research suggests barn owls, with simpler brains, also group elements moving in the same direction. The owls spotted the target and were better when the contrasting dot direction was uniform. Ocular tectum activity varied with dot movement, suggesting it performs this task.

Strong U.S. job creation and wage gains raised expectations of Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes, sending the dollar and Treasury yields higher while stocks slumped; 10-year Treasury yields hit a four-year high.

Gold edged lower Friday as the dollar rose ahead of U.S. nonfarm payrolls, expected to show 180,000 January jobs. Strong data could support Fed rate hikes, pressuring gold. The Fed held rates but raised its inflation outlook and flagged gradual increases. Gold was little changed for the week after recent gains and a 17-month high. Global stocks headed for their biggest weekly drop since late 2016; silver and platinum fell, while palladium rose but was set for its biggest weekly drop since September.

Pat Skorkowsky retired as Clark County Schools superintendent on the last day of school after five years as superintendent and 30 years in the district. He announced retirement last fall; the school board named Dr. Jesus Jara as his replacement. Skorkowsky cited graduation-rate growth from 60% to 83% and expanded magnet schools, while noting a $60 million budget shortfall. He said the 2019 legislative session would be pivotal, wanted marijuana revenue for the county where generated, and addressed school safety, funding, teacher pay, and mental health. He advised Jara to know the community and listen.

Lifeline Fiji's Merekula said suicide remains a taboo subject in Fiji. NSAAC statistics recorded 124 suicides and 107 attempts in 2015, and 102 suicides and 104 attempts in 2016. From 2011 to March this year, 627 suicides and 694 attempts were recorded, including 56 child suicides and 97 child attempts. He cited lack of help-seeking, community support, and awareness; Lifeline Fiji runs a 24/7 helpline.

At RSA Conference 2017, Intel Security’s Chris Young warned that attackers can corrupt data used for decisions—“data landmines”—causing bad choices, missed opportunities, and losses; he cited the 2016 election and risks from altered small data in big-data analysis. He also called home networks and IoT devices an attack surface, noting Mirai, and urged cooperation. Microsoft President Brad Smith asked the tech community to act as a “digital Switzerland,” defending civilian cyber assets through principles such as defense only, collaboration, and refusing attacks on civilians. He proposed a digital Geneva Conventions, no attacks on private sector or civil infrastructure, no government stockpiling of vulnerabilities, an international cyber agency, and government agreements.

This disclosure describes a location sharing system and map GUI for a social media application. The system receives location information from a first user’s client device, determines a current trajectory, accesses historical location information, and correlates them to determine a presumed destination. It displays an icon for the presumed destination on a map on a second user’s client device, and may display an estimated time of arrival. Historical location information can be used to extract trajectory patterns, and when new location information is unavailable, the system may predict an updated location along an identified trajectory pattern. User authorization may be required before using or sharing location information.

The passage covers MSPM0G microcontroller features and documentation, including the ARM Cortex-M0+ CPU subsystem, operating modes and power domains, PMU, clock module, DMA, event manager, memory organization, flash, SRAM, GPIO, IOMUX, ADC, temperature sensor, VREF, comparator, DAC, security functions, TRNG, AESADV, keystore, CRC, MATHACL, UART, I2C, SPI, CAN-FD, LFSS, RTC_B, IWDT_B, WWDT, timers, device analog connections, I/O diagrams, SWD, BSL, factory constants, application/layout guidance, development tools and documentation support, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

Radyr, a Cardiff suburb, has lacked a pub since the Radyr Arms closed in 2003. Vale of Glamorgan Brewery has applied to open the Radyr Tap micropub in an empty Station Road unit, formerly a dry cleaners, following a Twitter campaign. A consultation runs until June 19 before Cardiff council decides. Plans include local cask ales, craft beers, wines, spirits, takeaway drinks, and bar snacks, but no cooked food.

MIT rejected the Trump administration’s “Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education,” which would mandate campus changes in exchange for preferential federal funding. MIT is the first of nine invited universities to publicly reject it. President Sally Kornbluth said MIT meets many outlined standards but opposes demands that would restrict free expression and institutional independence, and holds that funding should be based on merit. Most other invited universities are reviewing the compact; Texas officials expressed enthusiasm, Dartmouth said deliberations continue, and a UVA working group is studying it. California, Virginia, and Pennsylvania officials have threatened funding consequences for signatories. Academic and political reactions followed, including praise for MIT and hints of possible retaliation.

Komar Uddin, a 68-year-old priest and spiritual healer, denies sexual assault, assault by penetration, causing a female to engage in sexual activity, and two counts of rape on February 25, 2015. A jury heard he allegedly twice raped a 19-year-old in her Leicester bedroom during a candlelit ritual to drive out an evil spirit while her family was downstairs. The prosecution said he rubbed holy oil on her, touched her, and raped her; an internal swab contained his DNA. The woman said she was too scared to object. Uddin was invited by her father. He was arrested, bailed, left the country, and was extradited from Germany. Defence counsel suggested she lied and instigated contact. The trial continues.

The passage is Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2020. It describes Amazon’s business, organized into North America, International, and Amazon Web Services segments; customers including consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators; competition; intellectual property; seasonality; human capital; executive officers and directors; risk factors; properties; selected consolidated financial data; management’s discussion and analysis; COVID-19 effects; critical accounting judgments; liquidity and capital resources; and referenced financial statements. As of December 31, 2020, Amazon employed approximately 1,298,000 full-time and part-time employees. For 2020, net sales were $386,064 million, operating income was $22,899 million, net income was $21,331 million, and net cash provided by operating activities was $66,064 million; total assets as of December 31, 2020 were $321,195 million.

Prosecutors released cellphone videos in which Nikolas Cruz, suspect in the Feb. 14 shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School that killed 17 and injured 17, says he will be the next school shooter, plans to use an AR-15 to kill at least 20, and describes his loneliness, anger, and hatred. Cruz is charged with 17 counts of murder and 17 counts of attempted murder. His lawyers say he would plead guilty for life without parole; prosecutors refuse to waive the death penalty. The videos were released under Florida public-record law.

The passage calls for a thousand additional officers, larger Annapolis classes, retirement of impaired officers, and fostered promotion. It notes officers, especially lieutenants and junior grades, face unusual labor and fatigue; with no immediate foreign trouble, it argues an efficient navy prevents trouble and disaster. It reports Post-Office receipts of $121,848,047.26 for the last fiscal year, an increase of $10,216,853.87, and says rural free delivery is a fixed policy with benefits and need for expansion. It also discusses nationally aided irrigation, forest protection, and ending the slaughter of game such as elk.

Michael T. Klare argues that Donald Trump is not only disrupting the existing international order but also trying to build a new one divided between fossil-fuel powers and post-carbon, green-energy states. Domestically, Trump seeks to weaken alternative energy and prolong a carbon-dominated economy; abroad, he seeks an alliance of fossil-fuel states led by the U.S., Russia, and Saudi Arabia while trying to isolate renewable-energy powers such as Germany and China. This vision differs from Wilsonian and Huntingtonian models. Klare cites Trump’s Middle East and Europe trip: in Saudi Arabia he revitalized the U.S.-Saudi alliance, signed a $110 billion arms deal, and discussed energy cooperation; in Europe he dismissed NATO and the EU and downplayed Russian cyber threats; and he withdrew the U.S. from the Paris climate accord to support coal and fossil fuels. Klare says Trump aims at a trilateral U.S.-Russia-Saudi energy alliance. The three are leading oil and gas producers, and with linked producers they would control about 57% of world oil output and 59% of natural gas production. The U.S.-Saudi arm is active; efforts toward Russia have been impeded by investigations into Russian election meddling and Michael Flynn’s contacts, though Trump favors improved ties. Putin met Saudi Deputy Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman after Trump’s Riyadh visit, with energy cooperation emphasized. Klare notes obstacles: Russia and Saudi Arabia differ over Syria and Iran, but the meeting suggests they might be overcome.

Blocking the protein Ant2 reprograms T cell energy metabolism, making T cells more active, resilient, and better at attacking tumors. The study focuses on mitochondria and shows altered T cells have greater stamina, faster replication, and sharper targeting of cancer. This metabolic rewiring can be triggered by genetic modifications or drugs, suggesting potential clinical applications. The research may lead to new cancer immunotherapies that strengthen the body’s immune response, though more studies and clinical trials are needed.

Facebook took over two hours to remove live videos of Robert Godwin’s shooting death. Hugo Castro, a U.S. Border Angels activist, went missing in Mexico after a Facebook Live plea. Jon Ossoff raised a record-setting $8.3 million in Georgia’s 6th District.

This study investigated the knowledge, attitudes, and exposure of Belgian medical students toward global surgery and approaches to curriculum development. An anonymous online survey was distributed to first- to final-year medical students at seven Belgian universities; 304 responses from four universities were included. Knowledge of global surgery was poor, with only 23.9% correctly identifying that five billion people lack access and 21.7% knowing that approximately 150 million additional surgical procedures are needed annually. A minority reported exposure to global surgery (24.7%), most often through social media, and 28.6% had heard of InciSioN. Most students (75.3%) wanted more exposure, and many agreed global surgery is relevant and should be compulsory. Master’s students were less likely than bachelor’s students to agree global surgery is relevant, want compulsory teaching, or be interested in more exposure. Reported obstacles included personal or family responsibilities, language barriers, lack of established career paths, financial constraints, and lack of role models or mentorship. The study advocates preclinical global surgery seminars and equitable, bilateral international clinical internships in undergraduate medical education. Limitations included non-random sampling, inclusion of four universities, possible selection bias, lack of a validated questionnaire, and limited generalizability.

Fifty years after Paul Ehrlich’s The Population Bomb, the passage revisits fears about overpopulation and megacities. Ehrlich described Delhi’s crowded slum as overpopulation, but Jack Caldwell said similar crowds existed in London, Paris, or New York, and that Ehrlich saw poor non-Europeans. The passage asks whether environmental concerns about developing-world megacities sometimes involve racism. It says cities matter: half the world lives in urban areas, predicted to reach 66 percent by 2050, with growth in developing countries. Cities are not the cause of rising numbers but the solution, as urban fertility is lower than rural fertility. Urban migration raises city numbers, and migrants adopt smaller families. However, cities also create consumption, consuming three-quarters of materials while housing half the population; London’s resource use and waste are cited.

Since 2015, WebRTC VPN bugs have leaked real IPs despite VPN use, and providers have sought solutions; most can now hide IPs. A March 27, 2018 test of 124 VPN and proxy providers found 20 leaked users’ IPs via WebRTC (16.13%) and 101 kept them hidden. The passage lists leaking providers, links to a complete Google Docs list and IP leak testing pages, advises disabling WebRTC or using an add-on because most browsers enable it by default except Tor Browser, Edge, and Internet Explorer, and lists ranked VPN services that can protect privacy.

This section contains mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for designated devices, current at publication and subject to change. Footnotes explain status, preproduction material type, RoHS values, lead finish/ball material, MSL/peak reflow, and part marking. TI’s disclaimer states information is as of its date, based on third-party information, without warranty; destructive testing or chemical analysis may not have been conducted, and proprietary CAS numbers may not be released. TI’s liability shall not exceed the total annual purchase price. Tape dimensions and pin 1 quadrant assignments are shown; package family image may vary. TI resources are provided “as is,” for skilled developers, subject to change, with limited permission and disclaimers.

A gauge of global equity markets fell Monday as U.S. bond yields approached 3 percent and commodity declines pressured materials stocks. The 10-year yield hit 2.998 percent, its highest in over four years, amid worries over government debt supply and inflation. Commodities sold off after the U.S. hinted it might ease sanctions on Rusal; aluminum and Alcoa fell, while gold dropped. The dollar rose to a seven-week high, pressuring the euro and yen. Oil was volatile but settled higher. U.S. stocks were little changed ahead of earnings, with the Dow and Nasdaq lower and the S&P 500 slightly higher.

Caterpillar’s board voted to keep the quarterly dividend flat at $0.77 per share, payable May 20 to stockholders of record April 24. This is the seventh straight flat quarter; the yield is 3.25%, above the S&P 500 average of 2.2% and 10-year Treasury yield of 2.26%, with 23 consecutive years of higher dividends. Goldman Sachs added Caterpillar to its “conviction buy” list, citing higher mining capital spending, potential $8 per share earnings, and a $120 price target. Shares have gained almost 20% in nine months, outperforming the Dow and S&P 500, aided by Trump policies, infrastructure plans, US economic improvement, oil prices, and easing China concerns. Shares trade around $95, near a 52-week high of $99.45, at 29-times this year’s and 21-times next year’s estimates, amid a federal tax investigation. Risks include uncertainty over Trump’s infrastructure bill. In 2016, revenue and EBITDA fell 18% and 39%, and excess cash fell to $881 million from $4.6 billion in 2013. Caterpillar expects 2017 revenue to fall 2.6% and adjusted EPS to fall 15.2%; the author suggests investor caution.

Electrocardiograms (ECGs) are widely used for cardiac assessment, and research aims to estimate echocardiogram (ECHO) variables from ECGs. Challenges include ECG signal complexity and scarce ECG data labeled with ECHO outcomes. The passage proposes EchoingECG, a probabilistic student-teacher framework integrating PCME++ and ECHO-CLIP. It uses probabilistic cross-modal embeddings for many-to-many mappings and uncertainty modeling, and leverages ECHO-CLIP as a teacher to guide ECG representation learning on ECHO-ECG pairs. Contributions include a probabilistic multimodal ECG model, knowledge distillation reducing reliance on large annotated datasets, and uncertainty-aware downstream evaluation.

Stimson concluded that territorial adjustments, including trusteeships, should not be brought up for discussion until the war was much further along and Russian participation in the Pacific war was accomplished; they should be avoided if possible, and trusteeships could wait because no satisfactory discussion was possible without full knowledge of the territories. The passage also references the Japanese mandated islands and the Cairo Declaration. At a January 26, 1945 meeting, Grew discussed plans for a Mexico City conference, study of international organization and the inter-American system, the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals, and the need for a peace and security organization prepared to use all means, including force, though hoping force would not be necessary.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on April 20, 2022, reporting that it released its financial results for the quarter ended March 31, 2022 by posting its First Quarter 2022 Update on its website, attached as Exhibit 99.1.

Chris King, 57, visited Headingley Carnegie Stadium in Leeds to watch the Rhinos play Widnes, after having both hands replaced in a pioneering operation at Leeds General Infirmary last July following a work accident. He was applauded at half-time after drawing the golden gamble winning ticket and enjoyed the Rhinos' 42-22 victory.

After a five-year legal battle, the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office rejected Crocs’ design patent, finding another company filed for a similar patent earlier. Crocs plans to appeal; the ruling is a major blow as Crocs closes 160 stores and revenue dropped 3.3 percent.

This bibliometric analysis examines Digital Accessibility in Education using Web of Science, Scopus, and ERIC from 2013–2024, with searches for “Digital Accessibility” and “Digital Accessibility” AND Education. Publications increased significantly over time, especially after 2020, reaching 502 publications on digital accessibility and 339 on Digital Accessibility in Education in 2024. Scopus contained the most publications. Journal articles were the most common publication type, followed by conference papers and book chapters. Research areas included Digital Accessibility and Inclusion, Education/Higher Education/Social Sciences, and Computer Science/Engineering Sciences. English was the dominant language, and higher education had the most publications. The USA, UK, and Spain contributed the most publications. Citation analyses identified influential documents, authors, and countries, while showing uneven citation distribution and limited collaboration. The study concludes that digital accessibility in education is increasingly important and calls for broader cooperation and further research.

A study extended the International Consortium framework for clinical implementation of OGM with a VIA-based analysis and reporting workflow for hematologic malignancies, focused on myeloid neoplasms. Ten retrospective cases (nine AML, one MDS) were analyzed in 5–6 replicates by independent technologist-director teams. OGM via VIA identified all SOC-reported variants and additional reportable findings in five of six positive cases, including Tier 1A fusions and complex variants. Technologist review averaged 25.2 minutes for negative, 28.5 minutes for simple, and 47.3 minutes for complex cases, with VIA reported to reduce time by about 50% versus Bionano Access 1.7 alone. The workflow used custom views, panels, filters, and classifications, with technologist pre-classification and director final review. The conclusion states OGM with VIA offers a streamlined, efficient, digital, objective approach to interpreting and reporting cytogenomic variants and may help standardize analysis and clinical interpretation.

A community backed St. Patrick’s Catholic Primary School headteacher Mark Ryan after an inaccurate report claimed he took a two-week term-time holiday abroad for a wedding. The report also wrongly alleged he told a parent she would face a fine. He had instead taken sanctioned three-day term-time leave, June 7-9, for a close family friend’s wedding. Ryan cited his 22-year record and thanked supporters, while governors and a priest defended him.

The Shippers Group held a DC Chamber ribbon-cutting on September 15 for its new 540,000-square-foot distribution facility in Austell, providing warehousing, transportation, packaging and e-commerce fulfillment. Founded in 1901, it has eleven nationwide locations and 1.5 million square feet of Georgia warehouses.

After missing the playoffs despite the most expensive opening-day roster in baseball, the Mets are overhauling their staff. Manager Carlos Mendoza will return, but pitching coach Jeremy Hefner, hitting coaches Jeremy Barnes and Eric Chavez, and third base coach Mike Sarbaugh won’t return. Bench coach John Gibbons resigned, and catching coach Glenn Sherlock is retiring. Assistant pitching coach Desi Druschel and bullpen coach José Rosado can speak with other teams, while several other coaches were invited back. Pitching and defense were major problems, and president of baseball operations David Stearns said the staff would be evaluated.
Apple, long the world’s most valuable public company, has approached a $1 trillion market cap, but Amazon is closing the gap rapidly with large 2018 stock gains.

World stocks dipped as the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield crossed 3 percent for the first time in four years and the two-year yield touched 2.5 percent. European and U.S. equities fell, with Alphabet and AMS declining. Brent crude rose above $75 a barrel and U.S. crude reached $68.75. Despite strong earnings, higher yields dampened stock appetite, and MSCI’s global index fell for a third session.

The Best 6 Months Timing Model by Yale Hirsch is an active, simple market-timing strategy that uses entry and exit signals and can be implemented with any asset class and portfolio. The passage covers Yale Hirsch’s background, portfolio components including stocks, bonds, REITs, and commodities, trading rules, and a 16-year backtest. The timing model’s drawdown was -27.27%, compared with -47.77% for buy and hold.

The speaker rebuts Secretary Muskie’s criticism of his military-strength position, saying he seeks superiority only to keep the nation secure and deter violations of peace. He claims the Soviets are outspending the U.S. and advancing through proxies and allies, including in Africa, Ethiopia, South Yemen, Afghanistan, and Central America, while the Carter Administration seems oblivious. He says peace is the top priority but must not be peace at any price, humiliation, or surrender. He defends the U.S. cause in Vietnam as noble, criticizes the “Vietnam Syndrome” and shabby treatment of veterans, and says if forced to fight the U.S. must have means and determination to prevail. He cites post-WWII military superiority and Korea as examples.

Home Capital is in talks with banks including RBC, BMO and TD to secure about $2 billion to replace its April emergency credit line. It has also held talks with international banks. Depositors withdrew 95% of high-interest savings funds since March 27, though withdrawals slowed since mid-May.

This paper examines the normative assumption in studies of educational disparities. It states that educational disparities are gaps in educational opportunities, resources, and attainments caused by social background factors such as socioeconomic status, gender, region of origin, ethnicity, or disability, and that studies assume these disparities are unjust and should be corrected. The value of fairness behind this assumption can be clarified or justified by luck egalitarianism, which holds that inequalities caused by brute luck—factors beyond individual control—are unfair and should be eliminated, while inequalities due to option luck fall within individual responsibility. The paper considers Elizabeth Anderson’s critiques of luck egalitarianism: the harshness objection, illustrated by cases such as an uninsured driver and a musician who dropped out, and the humiliation objection, illustrated by “letters to the disabled” and classroom stigma. It discusses responses to these objections through three values to be added to fairness: fresh start, sufficiency, and respect. Fresh start and dynamic luck egalitarianism justify giving people opportunities to reconsider past choices; sufficientarianism guarantees an absolute threshold but is indifferent above it; respect addresses humiliation and shameful revelations. The paper concludes that empirical research on educational disparities should not only examine fairness but also fresh start, sufficiency, and respect, using longitudinal data, threshold analysis, and questions about humiliation in classrooms.

In Hardin v. White et al., an action sought to enjoin an execution sale of real estate; the circuit court ruled for the plaintiff, and White appealed. The court held that an injunction bond need not be double the judgment where the action seeks only to restrain the sale of specific property under a general execution, not to stay collection of the judgment. It also held that a judgment creditor who sold real estate under an execution for part of a judgment cannot later sell the debtor’s statutory right of redemption under another execution for the remaining debt, even if the second execution was issued under a decree in another action, because the debt is the same and the creditor is entitled to only one satisfaction. Barnes v. Cavanagh was distinguished. On rehearing, the court found its original theory substantially correct and affirmed.

Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a group of genetic red blood cell disorders that causes abnormal sickle-shaped hemoglobin cells. These cells carry oxygen, do not last as long as normal cells, and can stick in blood vessels and block blood flow. SCD can cause problems in nearly any body area. Symptoms include sickle cell crisis, acute chest syndrome, swollen hands and feet, anemia, jaundice, kidney, spleen, gallbladder, bone and joint problems, infections, leg sores, lung high blood pressure, heart failure, eye disease, and strokes. Smoking may increase pain episodes and acute chest syndrome. Diagnosis uses a blood test, with newborn screening in the U.S. and prenatal tests available. Treatment includes education, screenings and checkups, vaccinations, antibiotics for children until age 5, pain relief, medications to increase fetal hemoglobin, blood transfusions, and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, the only permanent treatment. Lifestyle choices include quitting smoking, limiting tobacco smoke and alcohol, eating a balanced diet, resting, and exercising. SCD is lifelong, and reducing complications can improve quality of life.

Heikin Ashi is a Japanese candlestick representation imported to the West in the second half of the 1990s, largely described by Dan Valcu in 2004. It means “average bar” and is another version of Japanese candlesticks, designed to highlight trends or consolidation by smoothing price movements and reducing noise. Heikin Ashi does not show real prices; its open, high, low, and close are calculated values, so it cannot be traded directly. It is a lagging technical indicator, often used as a supplement to other indicators. Calculations include haClose as the average of the four prices, haOpen as an exponential moving average of the total price, and haHigh/haLow acting as resistance and support. The passage tests a simple trend-following strategy: buy when haClose crosses above haOpen, sell when haClose crosses below haOpen, backtested on the S&P 500 from 1960 monthly. It reports a 49.4% win ratio and favorable asymmetric profit/loss distribution. ADX-filtered rules were also tested. Heikin Ashi works mostly on long time frames, and its Open parameter can be customized.

This applies when legally married, not to singles or engaged couples. If a spouse’s credit hurts the profile, a conventional loan may be considered; it requires 1.5 percent more down payment than FHA and lacks this requirement. Side Screen is a motion offense using continuous on-ball side screens that burdens defenses with quick options, ball reversal, and player movement. Plasma microbial cell-free DNA (mcfDNA) sequencing integrates genomic sequencing, computation, and cell-free DNA as a blood analyte. PCR-based tests have limitations, and a meta-analysis found next-generation sequencing had satisfactory diagnostic performance. The Karius Test is an analytically and clinically validated mcfDNA sequencing test available in the US since 2017; it identifies and quantitates MPM from >1,500 bacteria, DNA viruses, fungi, and parasites. This study reviewed a large commercial laboratory cohort: 19,739 samples from 16,172 patients in 39 states and the District of Columbia; median receipt-to-result time was 26 hours and 96% had valid results. Of valid results, 42% were negative and 58% positive, with 701 unique taxa and 22,792 detections; the top 50 taxa represented 69% of detections. Detections included difficult-to-diagnose Legionella, Nocardia, Mycobacterium, fungi, and parasites. Test performance metrics were not significantly different from the initial validation study. The 58% positivity was lower than the 70–85% reported for defined clinical uses, supporting diagnostic stewardship. Limitations included lack of orthogonal testing, therapy, and clinical context data, which were available for only 29% of patients. The study concludes unbiased plasma mcfDNA sequencing may enhance patient outcomes and public health with careful clinical application and stewardship.

The passage discusses thyroid nodules, their benign or malignant classification, and risks such as thyroid cancer. It describes diagnosis through physical exams, Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA), and ultrasound, noting FNA is invasive, painful, and time-consuming, while ultrasound requires expert interpretation. The study aims to determine if a CNN can classify thyroid ultrasound images as benign or malignant. It uses the public TDID dataset, sorted by TI-RADS, with preprocessing, image augmentation excluding noising/blurring, early stopping, and class weights for imbalanced data. A hybrid pre-trained VGG16 and InceptionV3 model is implemented in Python/TensorFlow and trained for 10 epochs with batch size 8. Results show 87.5% accuracy and an AUROC of 0.929. The passage states the small, skewed dataset limits performance and that larger clinical datasets would improve the model. It concludes CNNs can accurately identify benign/malignant thyroid nodules from ultrasound to assist or replace radiologists.

The passage defines open education as an educational trend including open educational resources, MOOCs, open textbooks, and open-access journals, aimed at democratizing education through inclusivity, affordability, and collaboration. It notes rapid global expansion but identifies fragmented research focused mainly on isolated elements. The study asks what key trends and emerging areas exist in open education and how findings can inform equitable access policy and practice. Using bibliometric analysis of 402 Web of Science articles, it applies co-citation and co-word analyses. Co-citation found five clusters: evolving open education, OER’s role, adoption of open education, educational paradigms of MOOCs, and implementation of open educational practices. Co-word analysis found five clusters: blended learning, openness during COVID-19, challenges of OER adoption, inclusive digital pedagogy, and collaborative online academia. The study discusses OER benefits such as cost savings, accessibility, and flexibility, while noting barriers like faculty reluctance and limited institutional support. Limitations include using only Web of Science, subjective interpretation and thresholds, and limited regional or institutional variation; future research should combine methods and examine contextual factors.

The OHL trading strategy is an intraday stock strategy that uses the open, high, and low price configuration in the first few minutes of the session to determine entries. A buy signal occurs when the open equals the day’s low, and a sell signal when the open equals the day’s high. It is best suited to lower timeframes, such as 1-, 5-, or at most 15-minute charts, and can be combined with CPR levels for long/short filters. Backtests on S&P 500/ES and WTI crude oil from 0930 to 1600 NY time showed small average gains, with results improving when the open was above yesterday’s close and weakening or turning negative when below. The article states the first minutes can set the tone for the rest of the day in those markets.

This work discusses physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) as mesh-free alternatives for PDEs and their limitations for complex, multi-patch CAD geometries: enforcing solution continuity across patches, imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions, and normalizing data with varying geometry. It introduces a neural solver combining PINNs with isogeometric analysis (IGA), based on FETI and mortaring methods. The solver uses NN-based ansatz functions on IGA reference domains, maps solutions to physical domains via NURBS parametrization, strongly imposes Dirichlet BCs, ensures differentiability within patches, and enforces C0 continuity across patch interfaces with interface-specific NNs. Training uses a variational PINN framework that minimizes a discretized energy functional. The contributions are control over patch-interface continuity, strong Dirichlet BC imposition, and natural input normalization by operating on the reference domain. It is demonstrated on a 2D magnetostatics quadrupole magnet and a 3D nonlinear solid mechanics mechanical holder with hyperelasticity, contact BCs, and parametric dependencies. Related work has combined NNs/PINNs with IGA, but most concern single-patch geometries.

First-principles computations are powerful but costly; machine learning force fields offer a computationally efficient alternative, often with runtimes orders of magnitude lower than DFT. State-of-the-art MLFFs are often graph-based equivariant neural networks, which excel when training data is scarce but face challenges for point defects, including large supercells and local-interaction limitations, while non-local interactions matter for defect structure. Inspired by Transformers, the passage introduces ADAPT, a coordinate-based Transformer with attention over all possible atom interactions, trained to predict per-atom forces from raw Cartesian coordinates and atomic features using a DFT database of defects in silicon. ADAPT reportedly achieves state-of-the-art energy and force performance, outperforming MACE, MatterSim, and retrained MACE, with training cost two orders of magnitude lower than message-passing architectures. It uses distinct networks for forces and energies, avoids graphs and inductive biases, and tokenizes each atom as a 12-dimensional vector embedded into a higher-dimensional space.

The research article examines K12 parents’ experiences, opinions, criticisms, and suggestions regarding emergency compulsory distance education in Turkey during COVID-19. After face-to-face education was suspended on 14 March 2020, Turkey used EBA, TV broadcasting, ADES, technical support, and psychological support. The study used a descriptive survey model and quota sampling across Turkey’s NUTS first level; 2,371 parents participated. Data were collected through a 16-question questionnaire distributed via teachers through social network groups and analyzed with descriptive statistics, frequency analysis, and content analysis using SPSS 24 and NVIVO 10. Findings show 57.7% positive and 42.3% negative views of distance education; most parents did not arrange private lessons. WhatsApp was the most used parent-teacher communication channel. Parents most agreed that internet connection fees should not be charged for EBA, that students had difficulty adapting, that distance education exams did not measure real success, and that students could not gain work discipline. They most disagreed that distance education should completely replace face-to-face education. Criticisms included inadequacy, difficulty, time problems, dissimilarity to face-to-face education, and technical problems. Positive views concerned process management, opportunity to repeat, and health. Suggestions included testing, continuing distance education as support, content/material support, and increased time. The study concludes parents viewed distance education as positive but not a replacement for face-to-face education, and it identifies infrastructure, inequality, digital divide, content, and communication issues.

Renewable energy generation fluctuates with natural resource variability, and because the grid lacks storage, production must be consumed immediately or risk outages; traditional plants are kept running as backup. Prof. Mahesh Bandi of OIST used turbulence theory and wind plant data in a Physical Review Letters paper to explain the statistical nature of wind power fluctuations. Prior assumptions that wind power and wind speed spectra were identical because power equals wind speed cubed were misleading. Bandi showed the spectra match for a different reason, accounting for fixed-location time measurements versus distributed spatial measurements. Turbulence eddies cause turbines within the same short- and long-timescale eddies to fluctuate together. Geographic smoothing works only to a limited extent: high-frequency fluctuations average out, but low-frequency fluctuations remain correlated. Data from Texas and Ireland confirmed this limit. This can improve estimates of reserve energy and inform environmental policy and energy-source combinations.

Merger arbitrage seeks to profit from the spread between a target company’s market price and an acquisition offer price. It requires assessing deal completion, regulatory hurdles, deal terms, risk management, market conditions, and liquidity. Backtests show the IQ Merger Arbitrage ETF had a 2.73% CAGR versus the S&P 500’s 18.52%, and The Merger Fund had a 4.46% CAGR versus SPY’s 17.37%, both with lower volatility. A Verdad study of 835 deals from 2000–2020 found an 89% closure rate, about 2.0% average return on successful deals, 2.8% loss on canceled deals, and a 1.5% blended average return; shorting acquirers reduced returns but mitigated volatility. The passage concludes merger arbitrage may offer uncorrelated returns with disciplined research but is difficult qualitatively.

Oxygen-containing rare-earth hydrides (REHO) are color-neutral photochromic materials that are transparent in the visible and near-IR and lose transmittance under ambient conditions, making them candidates for smart windows. REHO films are typically made by magnetron sputtering or e-beam evaporation; deposition conditions, thickness, environment, and illumination wavelength affect photochromism, with thicker films showing stronger response. Their phase composition and photochromic mechanism remain debated, with single-phase oxyhydride models contrasted with evidence of O-rich and H-rich regions and H migration. This work studies YHO transmittance under blue light and bleaching, finding fast initial darkening (≈30% in 2–3 min) followed by slower darkening, and slower bleaching. Zero-, first-, and second-order kinetics do not fit. EELS shows a plasmon peak at 14.4 eV for photochromic YHO versus 15.9 eV for opaque YHO, suggesting more free or mobile H. A modified first-order model with H diffusion yields two-phase exponential decay plus a nonphotoactive constant, with fast (k1=0.016 s−1) and slow (k2=0.001 s−1) processes. The fast process is linked to local light-driven changes and possible loosely bound H loss; the slow process to H migration/diffusion and lattice contraction. YHO films were deposited by reactive magnetron sputtering and measured by transmittance under a 405 nm LED. The model fits well and may aid comparison of photochromic films for energy-efficient devices.

Congress failed to avert a government shutdown, and the federal government ceased operating at midnight Wednesday. For most schools, short-term disruptions would be minimal: the U.S. Department of Education said Title I funds for low-income schools and special education funding would be available as expected. Districts near military installations or national parks could face cash-flow problems; nearly 1,100 districts serving about eight million students are eligible for those funds. A shutdown lasting a few weeks or more could cause additional funding problems for Head Start and school nutrition programs. Most federal employees stop working; civil rights investigations would be on hold, regulations and guidance work would halt, and states and districts could not reach anyone about grants or programs. The Office of Management and Budget told agencies to consider additional mass layoffs, and Trump said good can come from shutdowns. The Department of Agriculture said it has enough funds for September and October school meals, and SNAP benefits should not be affected if the shutdown lasts no more than a week.

This study investigated commercial NMC/graphite coin cells cycled at 1C–3C between 2.7 and 4.3 V at 25 °C. Capacity declined progressively, especially at 3C, while internal resistance increased; coulombic efficiency remained relatively stable but slightly decreased at higher C-rates. XRD, SEM, EDS, and Li-NRA were used to examine structural, morphological, compositional, and lithium-depth changes. XRD showed cathode c-lattice contraction and anode c-lattice expansion after extended cycling. SEM indicated cathode surface decomposition/micro-cavities and graphite cracking, exfoliation, and SEI formation. EDS showed decreased cathode density and increased anode density. Li-NRA revealed bulk lithium loss in the dead NMC cathode and corresponding lithium gain in the dead graphite anode, indicating irreversible lithium consumption, lithium trapping, and plating. The conclusions state that high C-rate cycling accelerates Ni-rich NMC degradation, increases internal resistance, and causes capacity fade, with lithium plating on graphite as a main aging mechanism. Li-NRA is described as a mostly non-destructive method for quantitative lithium depth profiling.

The passage describes methods and systems using a cache coherent switch on chip with Compute Express Link (CXL) to provide cache coherency and resource sharing among accelerators, memory, storage, ASICs, NICs, and other components. It describes virtual hierarchies, fabric management, port assignment, hot plug, memory pooling and expansion across servers and racks, and bridging CXL traffic over Ethernet or other networks. It also discusses using cache buffers, prefetchers, compression and security functions, erasure coding, legacy bridges, software stacks, and frame formats, including a configurable L2 interframe gap. The passage states that these techniques can bypass CPU bottlenecks, improve resource utilization, enable composable or disaggregated servers, and reduce memory stranding.

Extracted from sugarcane and sugar beet, sugar is a sweet carbohydrate used to sweeten food. Sugar futures are derivative contracts traded on ICE and CME, representing a legally binding agreement to receive or deliver a specified quantity of sugar on a future date at a pre-agreed price. CME Globex (YO) is financially settled, while ICE (SB) is settled by physical delivery. Both use 112,000-pound contracts, 0.0001 per pound minimum fluctuation, $11.20 tick size, and March, May, July, and October cycles. Strategies use technical and fundamental analysis, entry/exit signals, position sizing, and risk management for speculation, diversification, or hedging. Factors affecting sugar include subsidies, tariffs, ethanol and oil demand, Brazil’s currency, and weather. Seasonality is noted in February, June, July, November, and December. The all-time high is 66.00 US cents in November 1974; the all-time low is 2.63 US cents in June 1985. Risks include leverage and adverse price movement. ETFs exist. Sugar is described as hard to trade, and the author does not trade a sugar strategy.

The Supreme Court heard arguments in William Case’s challenge to a 2021 warrantless police entry that left him shot in the abdomen. The justices appeared likely to give police more leeway than the probable cause standard Case proposed. Case’s former girlfriend told police he threatened suicide and to harm officers. Officers knew Case, knocked and yelled without answer, and saw a notepad believed to be a suicide note and an empty holster. About 40 minutes later they entered; an officer saw an object at Case’s waist believed to be a gun and shot him. Prosecutors charged Case with assault; he sought to exclude evidence, but state courts held that in noncriminal investigations police need only a reasonable warrantless entry. Justices questioned the probable cause standard and discussed an “objectively reasonable” emergency-help standard. Some favored remand; others favored applying the standard. A decision is expected by late June or early July.

Thomas Jefferson issued a proclamation on November 27, 1806, stating that U.S. citizens or residents were conspiring to prepare a military expedition against Spain by fitting out vessels, collecting arms, provisions, and military stores, and seducing citizens. He ordered participants to withdraw and cease, required civil and military officers to search out, punish, seize means, and prevent the enterprise, and asked citizens to assist and give information.

The passage describes market structure trading strategy as analyzing swing highs and lows, support and resistance, and trendlines to interpret price movements. It identifies three primary market structures: trending, ranging, and consolidating. Key components include swing highs/lows, support/resistance, and trendlines/channels. It discusses candlestick patterns, volume analysis, Fibonacci retracements, breakout trading, pullback trading, risk management through stop-loss orders and position sizing, multiple time frame analysis, and harmonic patterns. The passage notes that Fibonacci, multiple time frame strategies, and harmonic patterns are difficult to backtest, and it recommends backtesting. It states position size may be adjusted based on market structure strength.

The message transmits dispatches from Mr. Wise, U.S. minister at Brazil, on the slave trade and methods used to evade laws. It regrets that some U.S. citizens cooperate with foreign subjects, though the trade occurs in foreign parts. American vessels, believed to be with owners’ and masters’ knowledge, are nominally chartered but actually sold to Brazilian slave dealers aided by English brokers; new crews carry slaves back to Brazil. Rio examinations implicate British and U.S. citizens; British factors and agents supply goods and abuse the American flag. Wise’s suggestions to the British envoy deserve consideration. U.S. laws provide for restoring captured slaves to Africa and supporting them; the message regrets Britain’s policy of transferring captured Africans to the West Indies as apprentices and paying bounties, which may perpetuate the trade, and hopes Britain adopts more effective measures.

The message reports a favorable state of the Union: domestic tranquility, contentment, harmonious management-labor relations, freedom from industrial strife, and prosperity, along with foreign peace, goodwill, and friendship. It attributes these blessings to the American people’s integrity and faith and to Federal cooperation. It describes conservation of national resources, constructive economy, a shift from force to reason, reduced expenditures and tax rates, increased profits, four internal revenue revisions, one-third of the national debt paid, refunding at lower rates, and national income increased nearly 50 percent to over $90 billion. It warns that no surplus exists for further tax revision, that a threatened deficit became an indicated surplus of about $37 million, and that new immediate appropriations should be avoided or offset by new revenue to prevent an unbalanced budget. It notes the national debt was reduced about $906 million last year and that savings did not reduce legitimate public needs.

Foreign relations show peace and progress, including the Sixth International Conference of American States at Habana, a conference on conciliation and arbitration, new arbitration treaties, Nicaragua intervention and a free election, resumed Chile-Peru relations, improved Mexico relations, recognition of China’s Nationalist Government and tariff autonomy, pending Greek and Austrian debt settlements, and a Paris treaty renouncing war while not superseding national defense. The message also addresses national defense, veterans’ relief, agriculture and a farm board, commerce and aviation, railroads, merchant marine, waterways, conservation, immigration, labor wages, civil service, education, public buildings, Indian and Negro advancement, the Philippines, Porto Rico, Department of Justice consolidation, oil cases, and prohibition enforcement. It concludes that prosperity and peace can be lost and require effort, generosity, moderation, patience, and humility.

The passage states that most aborigines, Creoles, and naturalized foreigners favor annexation of Hawaii to the United States. It says the king’s death without an heir would create a crisis and an occasion to effect annexation as the majority’s will, peacefully and honorably, with U.S. approval. A mother warned parents to keep sick children home after her 3-year-old daughter, who has asthma, was hospitalized with RSV after playing with a sick cousin at Christmas dinner; the cousin’s family said the lung infection was not contagious. The child received antibiotics and a breathing machine.

The Foreign Office offered to keep Matthews informed about talks with the Belgians; no usual negotiations were underway, only occasional calls by a Belgian official with Makins. Matthews saw no present advantage in participating and would telegraph a memorandum summary. This study examines the (re)construction of professional identities of teachers in initial formation, focusing on negotiation between personal and professional selves and Alsup’s borderland discourse. It arises from concerns about being a teacher in public schools without omitting the personal self. The article discusses identity as multiple, transitory, transformational, contextual, and negotiated through claimed and assigned identities, discourse, and social practices. It analyzes internship reports and Moodle interactions of two participants, Laura and Richard, over four semesters. Both show dissatisfaction with academic formation and tension between theory and practice. Laura develops a flexible, critical, responsible foreign-language-teacher identity, adapting to classroom contexts and students’ diversity. Richard engages in borderland discourse, critiques trainer-teachers and traditional university formation, worries about being evaluated, and ultimately refuses to be an English teacher while identifying as a mother-language teacher. The final considerations state that participants confronted long change, that professional identities are transient and not chronological, that Supervised Internship is important for reconstructing professional identity, and that Moodle was a space for sharing experiences and served as emotional scaffolds; narratives in virtual and presence contexts help understand the role of language in identity construction.

New CFPB rules would require payday and auto title lenders to assess borrowers’ ability to repay within 30 days and limit account debits. The CFPB estimates the rules could halve loan volume and force many of 16,000 stores to close; industry says they would devastate lenders serving 30–40 million customers and drive borrowers to unregulated lenders. A Pew poll found 70% of surveyed adults want more payday lender regulation.

The lecture covers quantum states of light, focusing on coherent states as eigenstates of the annihilation operator with complex eigenvalue alpha, their connection to the classical electric field, time evolution, Poissonian statistics, and role in quasi-probability distributions Q, P, and W. Q is a positive diagonal matrix element; P can be positive or negative and gives a delta function for coherent states; W can be negative and its projections give position and momentum distributions. Coherent states are minimum uncertainty states. The lecture introduces intensity fluctuations through the second-order coherence function g2 and the Fano factor. For single-mode light, g2 relates to photon-number fluctuations: coherent states have Fano factor 0 and g2=1; thermal states have Fano factor n-bar and g2=2; number/Fock states have Fano factor -1 and g2=(n-1)/n, below the classical limit. Single-photon states are non-classical; attenuated coherent states are not single-photon Fock states. Single photons can be produced using single atoms or ions in cavities, or heralded photons from many atoms. The Hanbury Brown Twiss experiment measures g2 using a beam splitter and coincidence detectors; thermal light has g2=2, coherent light g2=1, and single-photon light has g2=0. Single-mode treatment makes results independent of tau, while multi-mode effects relate to coherence time.

Research combining robotic float data and ship-based plankton surveys in the Gulf of Alaska found that marine heatwaves altered plankton communities and food webs, disrupting the ocean’s biological carbon pump. During the 2013–2015 and 2019–2020 heatwaves, carbon accumulated near the surface or in the upper twilight zone instead of sinking to the deep sea, though the effects differed between events. The study calls for sustained, coordinated ocean observation to understand future impacts on ecosystems, fisheries, and climate.

Yen Bai province aims to develop comprehensive raw-material and hi-tech processing facilities to boost its agro-forestry-fishery sector. The Austro-Hungarian Government received the enemy states’ reply to its December 12 peace-negotiation note. After examining it with its allies, it said the enemies declined the proposal, calling it insincere and unimportant, and made a direct answer impossible. It therefore addressed its views to neutral powers. It said the reply avoided means to end the war and reverted to prewar facts, military strength, and motives; Austria-Hungary would not renew discussion of war antecedents, citing Serbia and Sarajevo. It left military advantage to public opinion. It said Austria-Hungary and its allies sought defensive ends, while enemies sought its annihilation, Alsace-Lorraine, partition of Turkey, and curtailment of Bulgaria. It rejected the “stratagem” charge, asserted sincerity, said adversaries declined without counterproposal, cited Irish, Finnish, Boer, North African, and Greek cases, disclaimed responsibility for continuing war, and pledged to continue until a secure peace.

Starbucks stock has been flat since late 2015, disappointing investors. This study developed the Grocery Basket Score (GBS), a model to rate shopping baskets for health properties using dietary data from NHANES 2001–2018 linked with 2019 mortality data. The data were self-reported dietary recalls. After exclusions, 35,462 individuals were included, with 25% randomly assigned to a test set. The model used density and deficiency dietary signals and Cox proportional hazard models adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and poverty-income ratio. The final GBS used separate food and beverage models combined as a calorie-weighted average. Food signals included saturated fats, protein deficiency, sugar, fiber, sodium, vitamin C deficiency, and iron deficiency; the beverage signal was calories from beverages divided by beverage weight. Fiber had a protective coefficient; the other signals were associated with increased risk. Validation against Nutri-Score on Open Food Facts items yielded an overall correlation of 0.60, with cluster correlations from 0.25 to 0.75. Validation against AHEI in 4,382 NHANES 2017–2018 participants yielded correlations of -0.62 without the protective effect of moderate alcohol consumption and -0.60 with it; calorie-weighted Nutri-Score correlations with AHEI were -0.48 and -0.47. Limitations included U.S.-based development, self-reported dietary data, missing nutritional information during validation, use of Nutri-Score 2017 for AHEI validation, and not modeling alcohol effects beyond calorie density. Strengths included no required manual annotation and suitability for automated deployment on retail loyalty or digital basket programs. The GBS was concluded to align with nutritional guidelines and can be used in combination with product-level systems such as Nutri-Score.

Cam Newton apologized in an October 5 video for sexist comments at a press conference, where he told Carolina beat writer Jourdan Rodrigue it was funny a female asked about routes. The Tates filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy with above-median income. The bankruptcy court dismissed their case for abuse, and the district court affirmed, holding that the Tates could not claim a vehicle ownership deduction because they had no loan or lease payments on their cars. The Fifth Circuit reversed. The sole issue was whether a debtor may claim a vehicle ownership expense under 11 U.S.C. § 707(b)(2) for a vehicle not encumbered by debt or lease. Reviewing de novo, the court noted a split between the “plain language” approach, which allows the deduction based on geographic region and number of vehicles, and the “IRM” approach, which disallows it without a debt or lease payment. The Fifth Circuit adopted the Seventh Circuit’s plain language approach, concluding that “applicable monthly expense amounts” cannot mean “actual monthly expenses,” that the statute’s statement that monthly expenses shall not include debt payments conflicts with requiring a car payment, and that other provisions expressly require actual expenses while this one does not. The court also found the IRM was not incorporated and that policy considerations supported allowing the deduction. It reversed and remanded.

This Tiered Memory Page Migration Operations Guide describes optional extensions to SEV and SNP for page migration. TMPM is an engine that aids page migration, requires IOMMU enablement, and uses the ENGINE_READY bit in PM_Status. It migrates pages between physical memory tiers while maintaining the guest physical address. It supports PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO for pages concurrently targeted by DMA and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST for SNP guest pages. Multi-page commands can migrate up to 128 pages using Page Migration Lists. The document also covers TMPM commands, statuses, parameter blocks, error handling, restrictions, and performance guidelines. TMPM firmware can be reloaded only when operations are paused and the ring buffer is torn down, using the BIOS to PSP mailbox protocol. PM_GET_CAPABILITIES returns FW_VER_Major to distinguish EPYC families; Family 19h is represented by 71 decimal.

Liberty Island was evacuated after a climber climbed the Statue of Liberty’s base on the Fourth of July, following arrests over an “Abolish I.C.E.” banner; organizers said the climber was unconnected.

FoodSEM is a fine-tuned open-source LLM for food named-entity linking (NEL) that links food-related entity mentions to URIs from FoodOn, SNOMED-CT, and the Hansard taxonomy. It uses instruction-response datasets created from CafeteriaFCD and CafeteriaSA corpora, with artificial IR instances added to balance entity distribution. The model is fine-tuned from Meta Llama 3 8B using LoRA and evaluated in five-fold cross-validation. FoodSEM achieves high macro-weighted precision, recall, and F1, up to 98% F1 on some ontologies, and outperforms non-fine-tuned 0-shot, 1-shot, and 5-shot baselines. Performance is lower on CafeteriaSA, attributed to NER errors propagating to NEL. The paper contributes food-annotated corpora in IR format, a robust model, and a benchmark for food NEL; future work will extend to scientific datasets and retrieval-augmented generation.

Checkr, founded in 2014 by Daniel Yanisse and Jonathan Perichon, is a background check technology company. Fair chance hiring refers to offering fair and equal job opportunities to individuals with records without lowering hiring standards. The passage discusses barriers faced by justice-impacted people, labor shortages, and claimed benefits of fair chance hiring, including larger talent pools, retention, performance, diversity, reduced recidivism, and economic gains. It also employs fair chance talent, runs an apprenticeship, provides volunteer time, and uses an onboarding simulation. Yanisse seeks to expand the movement while emphasizing alignment between mission and business. The passage raises questions about a possible IPO and making the business case to new stakeholders.

No statistically significant differences between randomized treatment groups were found for any secondary endpoints; estimated treatment effects were close to identity, and results were similar for the Per Protocol Set. TEAEs, laboratory parameters (D-Dimer, CRP, Ferritin), and vital signs (body temperature) were similar between groups. A total of 139 (28.78%) patients experienced any AE: 90 (28.13%) in plasma+SOC and 49 (30.06%) in SOC. Fatal AEs occurred in 49 (10.14%) patients: 33 (10.31%) plasma+SOC and 16 (9.82%) SOC. SAEs were reported in 66 (20.63%) and 34 (20.86%) patients. No differences were observed. Five AEs led to discontinuation of study treatment, all in plasma+SOC; two led to discontinuation from study, one in each group. Fourteen AEs in 12 patients (3.75% plasma+SOC) were treatment-related; seven treatment-related SAEs in 7 patients (2.19% plasma+SOC). CRP, ferritin, and D-dimer data showed no clinically meaningful changes. Transfusion-related side effects were reported in 19/320 intervention patients (6.0%); no TRALI. Neutralizing antibody titres increased from baseline to day 6 but were not influenced by the intervention; better outcome correlated with higher titres at day 0 and day 6, but not with the magnitude of increase. The DAWN-plasma trial was prospective, multicenter, randomized, open label; 320 patients received convalescent plasma plus SOC and 163 received control in a 2:1 allocation. The intervention had no impact on the primary endpoint, mortality, day 30 outcomes, or other secondary endpoints; serious or severe adverse events were similar.

The passage covers ESD protection, Power-on Reset, comparator operation, and hysteresis for TLV321x devices. Inputs and outputs have internal ESD protection to (V+) and (V-), with input voltages limited to 0.2V beyond the rails and a recommended 10mA or less current limit when using low-impedance sources. The POR circuit activates for up to 32µs after VPOR of 1.65V is crossed, holding the output low. Comparator operation compares VIN to VREF, with propagation delay affected by overdrive voltage. External hysteresis can prevent chatter. Typical applications include low-side current sensing, with design and layout guidance. The passage also includes support resources, trademarks, ESD handling cautions, revision history, package/orderable information, and TI legal notices.

TMPM is an optional extension to SEV and SNP that facilitates page migration by copying page content and updating virtual-to-physical mappings. It lets software move frequently accessed data to faster memory tiers, can pause DMA traffic to a page during migration, and can migrate SNP-protected guest pages. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement. Commands are sent through a page migration ring buffer separate from the SEV/SNP ring buffer, with multi-page commands moving up to 128 pages. Commands include PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, and PM_NOOP. The passage also covers command formats, statuses and sub-statuses, parameter blocks, IOMMU host page table handling, driver initialization/shutdown/pause/resume, interrupts, SPA encoding, error handling and mitigation, firmware reloading for EPYC family differences, performance guidelines, and restrictions such as 4K alignment for migratable SPAs. Non-migratable data structures include IOMMU memory structures, vIOMMU page tables and pinned buffers, and the ring buffer and argument pages.

Penfield forwarded Count Tisza's January 25 letter: enemy peace conditions involved Germany's mutilation and humiliation and Austria-Hungary's and Turkey's dismemberment, contradicted President Wilson's views, and compelled a fight for existence. NVIDIA’s Ampere GA10x architecture includes GDDR6X/GDDR6 memory, third-generation NVLink, PCIe Gen 4, GA102 GPU organization, ROP optimizations, GA10x SM design, second-generation ray tracing, third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, DLSS, RTX IO, A40 and RTX A6000, display support, NVDEC/NVENC, and EDR.
