The passage discusses Robert Oscar Lopez, a former tenured professor at California State University, Northridge, who resigned after opposing same-sex adoption and alleged a coached Title IX complaint against him. Lopez now argues academic freedom is not a virtue or reality, linking it to a corrupted tenure system that leaves adjuncts unprotected and rewards favorable views. The author calls academic freedom impossible because lines would be drawn on pedophilia, genocide, slavery, or Nazi beliefs, and calls it a “lie” and “con.” The passage claims conservatives face ideological persecution while leftist professors receive defenses. It cites Lopez’s view that higher education is a “diabolical machine,” proposes cutting college funding and encouraging trade schools and apprenticeships, and argues teaching should be governed by whether something is Truth or a lie rather than academic freedom. The passage discusses the first trading day of the month effect, defined as the first trading day, not the first calendar day. It reports that the S&P 500 (SPY) performs better on the first trading day, with an average gain of 0.24% from the last trading day’s close to the first day’s close, compared with 0.04% for an average day. Simply trading the effect is described as unstable and unreliable, with most gains before 2008/09. Adding a filter or criterion improves average gains and strategy metrics, and these strategies are presented to paying members. The passage says the likely cause is capital inflows.

The passage addresses profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade, where a broker seeks payment from the buyer minus payment to the seller while satisfying dominant-strategy incentive compatibility and individual rationality. It studies online learning regret relative to the best mechanism in hindsight, in adversarial and stochastic i.i.d. models. In the stochastic i.i.d. setting with possibly correlated valuations, it reports a polynomial-time algorithm with ˜O(√T) regret, matched by an Ω(√T) lower bound, implying roughly 1/ε² samples suffice and are necessary for an expected ε-optimal mechanism. In the adversarial setting, it states that no algorithm can achieve sublinear regret with respect to a 2/3 + ε fraction of optimal profit. It also notes a separation between adversarial and stochastic models, discusses intermediate models as open, and reports reducing a joint ads problem regret bound from O(T^{3/4}) to ˜O(√T). The challenges include a non-parametric action space, non-regular profit function, and insufficiency of fixed discretization.
The passage lists multiple views of a cooling fan design and states that broken lines indicate unclaimed portions.

Mediation analysis examines mediator variables in the causal pathway from intervention to outcome. Valid mediators can explain mechanisms, guide intervention refinement, and serve as early indicators. Mediator candidates must be tested empirically using robust methods. SEM is standard for latent mediators but relies on sequential ignorability, which is rarely achievable; omitted confounders can bias estimates. RPMs based on g-estimation are robust to omitted variable bias under a no-effect-modifier/no-essential-heterogeneity assumption, but have not been extended to latent variable models. The passage introduces RAPSEM, a rank-preserving structural equation model that integrates RPM with factor score regression and interaction corrections, allowing latent constructs while maintaining the relaxed no-effect-modifier assumption. RAPSEM aims to enable robust mediation analysis with measurement error and omitted confounders between mediator and outcome. It defines controlled direct and controlled mediation effects, describes model formulation, estimation, assumptions, inference, simulation studies, and strengths and limitations.

The speaker says the team felt comfortable and played well, capitalized on chances, and is happy for a goalie after a trying year for both goalies; the goalie is mature, experienced, and must stay hot for three games. This study examined visceral leishmaniasis (VL) in Denan district, Shebelle zone, Somali Regional State, southeastern Ethiopia. A cross-sectional study was conducted from April to August 2021 among 187 participants. The overall DAT sero-prevalence of VL was 9.63%. Factors significantly associated with VL included age group 19–36, damp floor, outdoor sleeping, and sleeping near animal shelter. Among participants, 53.48% had heard of VL, 42% identified sand fly bite as transmission, 89% knew at least one clinical sign/symptom, 78% considered VL treatable, 36% believed it preventable, and 42% used bed nets. Entomological collection yielded 823 sand flies and 12 species, including Phlebotomus and Sergentomyia. Sergentomyia clydie was predominant overall, while P. orientalis was the dominant Phlebotomus species and was collected mainly from termite mounds and forest, with no specimens caught indoors. The study concluded that VL sero-prevalence was relatively high in this new focus, risk factors included damp floors and outdoor sleeping near animal shelters, knowledge and attitudes/practices were poor, and P. orientalis apparently contributes to transmission; further studies were recommended.

The passage investigates whether transformers can learn transitive relations, equivalently graph connectivity, from connectivity information provided as individual training examples rather than in-context examples. It compares k-dimensional grid graphs, where connectivity can be inferred from low-dimensional node embeddings, with disconnected chain graphs. Experiments indicate transformers more easily learn connectivity on grid graphs, especially low-dimensional ones, while they struggle on disconnected chain graphs, higher-dimensional grids, and graphs with many chains. Scaling model size helps grid graphs more than disconnected chain graphs; scaling graph size keeps grid-graph performance consistent and improves disconnected chain graphs. Data/graph scaling benefits performance more than model scaling for higher-dimensional grids and many-chain disconnected graphs. Future work includes assessing real-world graphs such as knowledge and causal graphs.

The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on Oct. 7 in Barrett’s case, which asks whether Section 924(j) creates a separate crime and punishment from Section 924(c). Barrett was convicted under both provisions for armed robberies and a shooting death. Section 924(c) prohibits using a firearm in a federal crime of violence or drug-trafficking offense; Section 924(j) applies when that violation causes death. Under double jeopardy principles, courts compare elements: if each offense requires proof the other does not, separate punishments are presumed; if one is a subset of the other, multiple convictions are barred unless Congress clearly intended otherwise. Section 924(c) requires consecutive sentences. Barrett and the government agree separate sentences for the same conduct are not permitted. The Supreme Court appointed an amicus to defend the 2nd Circuit’s judgment allowing separate convictions and sentences; McCloud argues Section 924(c)(1)(D)(ii) suffices. The court had previously left the double jeopardy question unaddressed.

The passage discusses assessment in vocational education and training (VET). Formative assessment is described as a complicated, socially oriented process requiring active participation from teachers and students, immediate feedback, allotted lesson time, professional judgment, and student self-assessment. Complications include spontaneous teachable moments, student reluctance to debrief, and added teacher workload. Formative assessment identifies learning difficulties, misunderstandings, or missed opportunities and includes communicating expectations, descriptive and prescriptive feedback, multiple task attempts, peer reviews, self-assessments, and socially oriented methods. It can increase motivation and deeper learning.

VET teachers must assess using both vocation-based formative and academic-based summative methods. Academic assessment practices and written tests may not suit VET and may document objective assessment rather than measure learning. Competence-based education (CBE) connects classroom theory to workplace skills, defines competence as industry-standard performance in context, and requires specified essential tasks, clear standards, and workplace evaluations. Authenticity in assessment is emphasized over reliability to prepare students for work. Authentic competence-based assessment develops deeper understanding and relevant technical skills, uses rubrics and professional development, and includes workplace feedback. Balancing authenticity and reliability is essential.

A comprehensive assessment program should include traditional written testing, technical skills assessments, workplace or practicum evaluations, assessment of processes and products, and both summative and formative methods. It should evaluate students across the range of vocational knowledge. Assessment in VET must account for both theoretical knowledge and technical skills.

This study used PREVEND longitudinal cohort data to model transitions between consecutive KDIGO risk stages before new-onset heart failure (HF) and to estimate age- and sex-specific associations of KDIGO risk stages with new-onset HF, accounting for dynamic change and potential misclassification in kidney measures. Among 8,569 participants, 6,838 were low risk, 1,279 intermediate, and 303 high or very high risk at baseline. During median follow-up of 12.6 years, 373 participants developed new-onset HF and 710 died before HF. Forward transition rates increased with age; the intermediate-to-high/very-high transition increased exponentially and was lower in women, while low-to-intermediate transitions did not differ significantly by sex. Backward transition from intermediate to low risk was higher in younger subjects and women. Progression to intermediate risk mostly occurred between ages 60 and 70, and progression to high/very high risk after age 70. Intermediate and high/very high risk stages were associated with increased risk of new-onset HF compared with low risk; relative risk attenuated with age, while absolute rate differences strengthened with age. Misclassification probabilities were estimated, and sensitivity analysis using cystatin C-based eGFR showed mostly consistent results. The authors conclude that kidney disease progresses fast in middle-aged populations, more advanced KDIGO status is associated with increased new-onset HF risk, and slowing KDIGO risk stage progression may reduce new-onset HF incidence.

The passage discusses Australian trading markets and strategies. The study examines values education through distance education and aims to develop a valid and reliable scale for prospective teachers’ attitudes toward values education through distance education. The descriptive survey included 341 prospective teachers at Gazi University. Following scale-development steps, a 43-item pool was created, reviewed by experts, piloted, and analyzed. After exploratory factor analysis, a two-factor, 36-item scale was obtained: “Necessity and Usefulness” with 21 items and “Feasibility” with 15 items. The scale explained 63.286% of total variance. Cronbach Alpha reliability was .969 for the first factor and .961 for the second; Spearman-Brown split-half reliability was .934 and .930. Item analysis indicated the items were distinctive. The scale lacked additivity, so the factors should be evaluated separately. Limitations included a majority of female participants, participants from only Gazi University, and no comparable external scale. The study recommends confirmatory factor analysis with prospective teachers from different universities and further validity and reliability studies.

Children of obese women are twice as likely to be obese by age two as children of women with recommended BMI; childhood obesity is also linked with paternal obesity. Egg and sperm carry DNA plus molecules responding to parents’ nutrition that can shape child characteristics, including obesity risk. Maternal BMI at conception is most associated with early childhood obesity; paternal BMI is linked with boys’ birthweight and daughters’ body fat, and two obese parents further increase risk. Sperm non-coding RNAs differ in obese male mice and men, and injecting obese-mouse sperm RNA into eggs makes offspring fatter. Eggs are influenced by maternal nutrition; IVF embryos from obese women have different metabolism, and defective egg mitochondria are maternally inherited and increase offspring obesity/diabetes susceptibility. Embryos respond to signals; in mice, anti-diabetes drugs and exercise improve egg/sperm quality, and diet/exercise stop obesity transmission from obese males. Human data are limited; gastric banding studies show children conceived after surgery were less obese than prior siblings. The passage supports pre-conception interventions for both parents and preventing obesity in adolescents and young adults.

Football has become offense-first, making cornerbacks valuable for shutting down the pass. A cornerback primarily covers opposing wide receivers in man or zone coverage. In man coverage, he mirrors the receiver one-on-one and must stay with him, often at a disadvantage because the receiver knows the route. The position is named for protecting the outside thirds near the boundary and is part of the defensive backs with safeties. Teams usually use two cornerbacks, sometimes a third in a nickel package for a slot receiver. Cornerbacks may be called DBs, and great ones are called “lockdown corners.” They need speed, agility, backpedaling, sharp turns, sprinting, and run defense outside. Deion Sanders is considered the best cornerback all time; others named include Charles Woodson, Mel Blount, Champ Bailey, Ty Law, and Darrell Revis, with 18 cornerbacks in the Hall of Fame. Great cornerbacks are important because otherwise receivers would dismantle a defense, quarterbacks target weaknesses, and trusted corners can cover “on an island,” as with “Revis Island.”

Defending goal kicks uses positioning and pressing to win possession, aiming either to gain the ball immediately in a dangerous area or deny an easy build-up or successful long kick. A goal kick occurs when the ball crosses the defenders’ end line after last touching an attacker, and is taken from the Goal Area with the ball stationary. The ball becomes live once kicked and visibly moves; opponents may then enter the Penalty Area. If an opponent inside the Penalty Area touches, is struck by, or challenges for the ball before it is in play, the goal kick is retaken. Tactics include covering potential receivers with man-to-man and zone defending, moving aggressively to the ball first, transitioning to attack if won, and pressing if not won. Positioning is described for strikers, midfielders, and backs. For youth, smaller fields and build-out/retreat lines are used to let defenders retreat and encourage building from the back; at older youth levels, target options expand, and adults may use all options, with the goalkeeper usually taking the kick. Coaches should drill defending goal kicks, scout tendencies, and ensure players know where the ball is.

The paper analyzes data from 147 student surveys to understand how students evaluate university education within Education 4.0 and their acquired skills for the changing job market. It reviews Industry 4.0, Education 4.0, required competences, and top job skills. Participants were second-year undergraduate students at a Hungarian university from engineering and business/management faculties. The study tested three hypotheses about differences between engineering and technical management students in soft-skill priorities, career-important skills, and expectations from higher education. Results showed both groups ranked problem solving highest; engineering students favored knowledge related to specialization and technical/mathematical knowledge, while technical management students favored learning decision-making techniques and analytical thinking. Significant differences were found for these specific skills. For future career success, students ranked individual talents and skills, professional devotion, and excellent network highest; no significant differences were detected between faculties. For higher education’s contribution, more than half agreed on knowledge related to future work and digital literacy skills. Significant differences between faculties were found for analyzing quantitative problems, working effectively in teams, better understanding oneself, and knowledge related to future workplace. The first hypothesis was accepted, the second was not accepted, and the third was partly accepted. The study concludes that Education 4.0 requires curriculum changes integrating hard and soft skills. Limitations include non-probabilistic sampling, low sample size, and no general conclusions; future research is recommended.

The passage argues that slavery is seldom recognized as a starting point in discussions of pedagogy, though scholars across disciplines suggest it may be integral to understanding teaching and learning, especially as digital surveillance becomes ubiquitous. The author uses Foucault’s theory of panopticism to examine how slavery and pedagogy are entwined through surveillance as extraction, a capitalist imperative, and a technology of power. Foucault links surveillance to teaching and education; Browne says surveillance’s historical formation is not outside slavery. Bernasconi contends Foucault ignored race-based slavery, while others call for recalibrating his work. The panopticon, borrowed from Bentham, describes power exercised through monitoring and observation, often secretly, to induce docility and utility. Schools employ panoptic practices such as examination and record-keeping, enabling surveillance textualization—inscribing human experience into texts for labeling, categorizing, and normalizing. Digitalization and computerization intensify this through learning management systems and platforms that extract, mine, and code data to control behavior. The author reviews pedagogy literature, noting that Ancient Greek pedagogues were typically enslaved but this is often omitted. The passage discusses Givens’s fugitive pedagogy and advances surveillance pedagogy to link slavery, pedagogy, and surveillance capitalism. It examines data-driven pedagogy, scientific management, and Zuboff’s surveillance capitalism, where learning becomes labor and data is monetized. It also covers racial chattel slavery, the pushing system, plantation record-keeping, and the school-to-prison pipeline. Surveillance pedagogy is defined as observation or monitoring by authority, constituted by extraction, textualization, and differentiation of personal and private data. The conclusion says surveillance pedagogy provides a framework, showing extractive and textualizing continuities from slavery to digital surveillance and arguing that pedagogy and slavery are inseparable.

This cross-sectional study assessed lung function decline and associated factors among heroin users on methadone at the MAT clinic at Muhimbili National Hospital in Dar-es-salaam, Tanzania. Of 310 enrolled, 302 completed spirometry. Participants had a mean age of 42.78±7.56 years, and 95.7% were male. Lung function decline was found in 28.5%, with a mean age at onset of 44±8 years. Patterns included obstructive (11%), restrictive (13.2%), and mixed abnormality (4.3%). Underweight, HIV infection, and history of pulmonary TB were independently associated with lung function decline (aOR 4.73, 2.61, and 2.48, respectively). The study concluded that over a quarter of clients had lung function decline and recommended routine lung function screening for this population. A limitation was the inability to perform bronchodilator reversibility testing.

The paper analyzes intimate performances in “personal attention” ASMR YouTube videos, using affect and performance studies and examples from Olivia Kissper. It explores how media infrastructures produce sexuality through mediated intimacy, redefining sexuality around affect and framing ASMR consumption as sexual practice and its configuration as sexual relation.

The Superior Court denied Clay Williams’s petition for remand, affirmed his judgment of sentence of life in prison for first-degree murder, robbery, and firearms convictions, and dismissed his ineffective assistance of counsel claims without prejudice to collateral review. It found several issues waived because his Pa.R.A.P. 1925(b) statement was defective or because the claim was not properly developed, and it declined to address ineffective assistance claims on direct appeal because no evidentiary record had been developed.

The passage discusses placing free-floating drifters as Lagrangian observers to measure ocean currents, noting existing campaigns use space-filling, ad-hoc, or hand-crafted criteria, and that active learning has not yet been presented for placement. It proposes BALLAST, a Bayesian active learning method with lookahead amendment for sea-drifter trajectories, which simulates hypothetical trajectories using vector fields. BALLAST uses a spatio-temporal vector-output Gaussian process surrogate, an information-theoretic utility function, and an SPDE approach for efficient utility computation. The contributions are introducing active learning to Lagrangian observer placement, proposing BALLAST, and developing a new GP posterior sampling method. Numerical results suggest benefits on synthetic and high-fidelity ocean current models.

A report commissioned by the Elementary Teachers’ Federation of Ontario says the learning opportunities grant distributes about $179 per student to needy areas, while school fundraising brings in $548 million to boards, or an average of $280 per student. It says school-based fundraising reverses the grant’s impact, with boards receiving less grant money raising more than average and those receiving the most raising less. The report, by economist Hugh Mackenzie, notes special education, English-as-a-Second-Language and maintenance have been underfunded for two decades. Ontario spends $23 billion, or $12,107 per student, but much added money went to class size reductions and full-day kindergarten. In June, the government announced an extra $219 million for 875 teachers and 1,600 education workers. ETFO is seeking regular funding reviews and more funding for special education, mental health, counselors, psychologists, social workers and speech therapists.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated May 25, 2022. Shareholders approved an amendment to the Restated Certificate of Incorporation to effect a 20-for-1 common stock split and a proportionate increase in authorized common shares. The amendment became effective May 27, 2022; holders of record on May 27 will receive 19 additional shares per share, reflected on or about June 3, with split-adjusted trading expected June 6. At the annual meeting, shareholders elected listed directors, ratified Ernst & Young LLP as independent auditors, approved named executive officer compensation in an advisory vote, and approved the stock split amendment. Various shareholder proposals were not approved. The Form 8-K includes Exhibit 3.1 and was signed by David A. Zapolsky on May 27, 2022.

The Citi Simplicity® Card offers a 0% intro APR for 21 months on balance transfers and 12 months on purchases from account opening. After that, the variable APR is 17.99%–28.74%, based on creditworthiness. Balance transfers must be completed within 4 months; the intro transfer fee is 3% (minimum $5), then 5% (minimum $5). The card has no annual fee, no late fees, and no penalty rate, and cardholders can choose a payment date. Recommended credit is Good/Excellent (670–850). Motley Fool Money receives compensation from partners, including for offers on the page, and Citi is an advertising partner, but product ratings are not influenced by compensation.

The Fifth Circuit affirmed Joe Ezeokeke’s 138-month sentence for possession of cocaine with intent to distribute. The court upheld the obstruction-of-justice adjustment under U.S.S.G. § 3C1.1 because Ezeokeke testified falsely about material matters that would have negated elements of the offense. It also found his within-range sentence substantively reasonable, as he did not rebut the presumption of correctness or show mitigating factors.

This cross-sectional study of 1,284 Kailuan cohort participants examined long-term visit-to-visit blood pressure variability and cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD). High systolic blood pressure variability was associated with moderate cSVD burden and visible perivascular spaces (PVS); high diastolic blood pressure variability with lacunae (LA); and high pulse pressure variability with moderate/severe cSVD burden, LA, and PVS. Associations were modified by age and hypertension status; in participants under 60, high pulse pressure variability was associated with severe cSVD burden, LA, and PVS, and systolic and pulse pressure variability effects on cSVD burden were significant only in participants with hypertension. The authors conclude that high long-term blood pressure variability, especially with hypertension, is a risk factor for total cSVD burden, LA, and PVS, and that pulse pressure variability is important in young adults.

This lecture on payments, part two discusses Bitcoin’s 10th anniversary and related statistics, then examines payment system pain points such as intermediaries, high costs, settlement speed, financial inclusion, chargebacks, fraud, privacy, cybersecurity, and cross-border FX. It debates whether blockchain can address these through lower verification and networking costs while noting challenges including scalability, transaction costs, slowness, interoperability, error resolution, governance, regulation, liquidity, and volatility. The class discusses delayed versus final settlement, smart contracts, and whether blockchain is necessary or mainly a catalyst for incumbent systems. It reviews crypto payment companies and services, including BitPay, exchanges, Ripple/xRapid, MasterCard/Visa patents, and a media lab Bitcoin vending machine. It also covers cross-border payments using crypto as a bridge currency, correspondent banking, liquidity and risk issues, and remittance costs, concluding with a preview of central bank digital currencies.

The host can lock a card using a password stored in non-volatile PWD/PWD_LEN registers, with optional FEP/FEP_LEN registers if COP is supported. Locked cards permit only limited commands and lock automatically after power-on if PWD_LEN is nonzero. Lock/unlock is a transfer-state command resembling a single block write.

The passage contains an ESD caution stating that integrated circuits can be damaged by ESD and should be handled with appropriate precautions, with damage ranging from performance degradation to complete device failure. Sheree Coffman, Northmont High School Student Assistance Counselor, spoke to the Northmont Rotary about the Student Assistance Program, which identifies and helps students facing family crises, depression, substance abuse, and relationship issues. The program provides early identification and intervention through universal, targeted, and indicated prevention. It includes the Alternative to Expulsion Program, Peer Facilitation, SADD, grief and coping groups, and U.N.I.T.Y. Day, which has involved over 400 students, 60 small group leaders, and 60 mentors over four days for the past three years.

The article explains Bollinger Bands, a technical indicator developed by John Bollinger in the early 1980s with a middle simple moving average and upper/lower bands based on standard deviations. It describes asking ChatGPT to create Bollinger Band trading strategies and backtest one in Python. ChatGPT proposed mean reversion and squeeze strategies; the squeeze is identified when Bollinger Bands move inside Keltner Channels using ATR. Trading rules buy and hold when the lower Bollinger Band is above the Keltner lower band and the upper Bollinger Band is under the Keltner upper band, selling otherwise. Backtesting SPY from 1993, unadjusted for dividends and splits, showed low, erratic returns and high drawdown. The strategy performed poorly, though ChatGPT completed the backtest perfectly.

The passage ranks Taylor Swift’s 20 best breakup songs in ascending order, noting she is known for breakup songs and that the best examples include “Dear John,” “Champagne Problems,” and “All Too Well,” with three songs from “The Tortured Poets Department” newly joining the top 20. It then describes each ranked song.

Ocwen reached a Connecticut servicing settlement, bringing total settlements to 28 of 31 jurisdictions that took regulatory action. Like earlier settlements, it bars new residential mortgage servicing rights until April 30, 2018 and requires moving from REALServicing to Black Knight, but adds borrower communications, review/reporting obligations, and a $500,000 noncompliance fine. Ocwen is still seeking resolutions with remaining regulators.

Geologists found evidence of platinum, gold and rare earth elements in western Queensland, in rare geological pipe structures south-west of Mount Isa near the Northern Territory border. The discovery, loosely called the Diamantina Minerals Province, covers an area from Fifield in New South Wales through north-west Queensland to the Merlin diamond mine in the Northern Territory. The pipes could be up to six kilometres in diameter and may contain many listed minerals. Officials said the discovery could open a new frontier for Queensland and support technologies worth trillions.

Hubble images show NGC 4536, in Virgo 50 million light-years away, rapidly turning gas into stars. It has intense star formation and abundant gas, possibly from a galactic collision; starburst stars burn fast, emitting ultraviolet light that colors gas clouds.

At NATO Parliamentary Assembly spring session in Tbilisi, President Paolo Alli said territorial integrity and inviolable borders are fundamental to NATO cooperation. He noted Georgia’s armed forces reforms aid NATO integration, discussed NATO spending and other issues. Georgian officials spoke. A declaration supporting Georgia’s Euro-Atlantic integration will be adopted.

Sarah Illig was bitten by a nurse shark during a Caribbean honeymoon resort attraction while swimming with sharks. Her husband, Evan Carroll, filmed the incident and shared the aftermath. Illig said she had flesh wounds, did not get stitches, and was healing well. Nurse shark bites are rare unless provoked, though the sharks are popular at some Caribbean resorts.

Kent McFarland of the Vermont Center for Ecostudies will speak on mercury along elevational gradients as part of Lyndon State College’s Natural Science Weekly Seminar series on February 15 at 4 p.m. in Room S-102 of the Thaddeus Fairbanks Science Wing. Webber, Deputy Collector, certifies on December 7, 1891, that the within document is a true copy of the crew list of the bark Cape Horn Pigeon, New Bedford, mastered by Thomas Scullan, taken from the original on file. At the French Open, Novak Djokovic beat Spanish qualifier Jaume Munar 7-6(1), 6-4, 6-4 but was unsatisfied with his performance and serve. Since elbow surgery, he has changed his service motion and racket, and in 2018 he has yet to reach a final. He will next face Roberto Bautista Agut.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K reporting that on January 23, 2018 it issued a press release announcing a January 21, 2018 grant of a 100% performance-based stock option award to CEO and Chairman Elon Musk, subject to stockholder approval by a majority of votes cast excluding shares owned by Elon Musk or Kimbal Musk. Tesla plans to file a proxy statement for a special meeting.

The Czech crown firmed, reversing an early slide to 18-month lows against the euro, as the central bank’s commitment to capping its value ended Friday. The CNB confirmed its commitment to keep the crown weaker than 27 per euro would expire at the end of the first quarter, and it omitted a line saying it would end its 3-1/2-year-old weak crown regime around mid-year, meaning it could remove the cap any time after Friday. The crown rebounded from 27.252 to 27.024, and forward implied rates also rebounded. The CNB spent tens of billions of euros defending the cap. Czech bonds were mixed, while Polish yields were near their lowest this year, Hungarian yields near multi-week lows, the forint firmed 0.1 percent and the zloty eased 0.4 percent. A dealer said some investors closing Czech crown positions may reinvest elsewhere in Central Europe, including the forint.

In Meola v. Ziman, the plaintiff sought lost wages after an automobile accident. The defendant argued that the plaintiff’s sick pay and wages for personal and family illness days were collateral sources under N.J.S.A. 2A:15-97 and should reduce any lost-wage award. The court held that these benefits were earned compensation that the plaintiff surrendered and could no longer use for future illness, injury, or retirement cash-out. Therefore, they were not collateral-source benefits under the statute and could not be set off against the plaintiff’s lost-wage claim.

The paper argues that Ontario’s K-12 education system excludes disabled and marginalized students despite claims of inclusion. It uses Carella’s statement that inclusion means believing someone belongs and Slee’s phrase that inclusive education “isn’t dead, it just smells funny” to critique special education. It outlines terminology, UNESCO’s inclusion definition, and exclusive education. It traces special education history in Ontario from 1860s residential institutions and 1880s special classes through segregation, 1960s civil rights changes, and later multicultural and anti-racist education, noting racialized students’ overrepresentation in special education. It discusses the “empty vessel” view, IEP implementation, school-based disability identification, placement categories, and the Policy on Accessible Education for Students with Disabilities (2018), including undue hardship. Barriers include inadequate funding, teacher training, resources, and policy implementation. Recommendations include improved policies, teacher education, involvement of students and disabled educators, and addressing systemic barriers.

The FDA approved another generic version of the mifepristone abortion pill, triggering pushback from anti-abortion groups and Trump-aligned politicians. Three U.S. companies can now produce mifepristone, though the approval is unlikely to affect access; the drug is typically taken with misoprostol, and the combination accounts for roughly two-thirds of U.S. abortions. Amgen said its cholesterol-lowering shot Repatha prevented a composite of heart disease death, heart attack, and the most common stroke in a 12,000-patient trial, but did not provide full results, saying only that the study met two primary goals. The Trump administration delayed closing a loophole that exempts some drugs from Medicare price negotiation.

A Stanley Cup Final broadcast welcomes viewers and describes Nashville’s playoff atmosphere, intensified by CMA Fest. The worldwide telecast will open with a special rooftop performance from Tootsie’s Orchid Lounge. Pittsburgh’s PPG Arena is sold out, Nashville screens will show the performance and game, and Luke Bryan will perform.

The passage discusses risks from Large Language Models (LLMs), including jailbreak attacks that bypass safety mechanisms. It notes that existing defenses often analyze only input prompts and are limited against complex attacks, while analyzing outputs can add latency. Inspired by human multistage reasoning, the authors propose SafeBehavior, a hierarchical jailbreak defense mechanism with three stages: intention inference, self-introspection, and self-revision. Intention inference quickly identifies obvious input risks; self-introspection evaluates the model’s generated response and produces a confidence score; self-revision rewrites uncertain responses to preserve user intent while reducing risk. The passage reviews jailbreak attacks as white-box or black-box and defenses as prompt-level or model-level. It describes a threat model with an adversary crafting arbitrary prompts and goals of robust output integrity, effective threat mitigation, and efficient execution. It states SafeBehavior is evaluated on five jailbreak attack types and compared with seven defenses, and lists contributions including the novel hierarchical mechanism, incorporation of human-like multistage reasoning into LLM inference, and comprehensive evaluation.

This qualitative study aimed to develop and validate a short learning module introducing pre-service English language teachers to critical multicultural education (CME) and critical language teaching. The two-week, six-hour module was developed in four stages: researcher brainstorming, critical friend feedback, implementation with a small group, and implementation with a larger group. Findings showed personal benefits, such as positive attitudes toward diversity and perspectives on social issues, and professional benefits, such as pedagogical insights on CME, lesson planning, critical awareness of teaching’s political position, material development, and implementing CME. Reported challenges included limited time, dense content, teacher-centeredness, and insufficient information on critical action. The study concluded that the module met its aims of raising awareness, increasing curiosity, and initiating attitude and emotion change, and suggested extending the module, increasing interactivity and research opportunities, and integrating CME into teacher education.

Higher education in Pakistan was largely neglected after 1947; at the start of the new millennium only two percent of university-age students were enrolled. In 2002 the government established the HEC and initiated reforms including new campuses, tuition waivers, scholarships, applied research, and technology. Enrollment reportedly rose from 2% to 12.6% from 2003 to 2021, and by about 500% from 2001–02 to 2020–21, though total participation remained 12%. The passage states that access and equity challenges persist, with disparities by rural-urban, gender, and socioeconomic factors. Universities and colleges are concentrated in big cities; more than half of Pakistan’s 120 districts lack college campuses. Private universities, including for-profit institutions, charge higher fees and are mainly in big cities; philanthropic universities also have high entrance standards. Post-COVID conditions worsened challenges due to the digital divide, lack of institutional support, and online learning systems.

The passage outlines national commitments to equitable access in the Constitution, National Education Policies 2009 and 2017, Pakistan Vision 2025, and SDG 4.3. It frames the study through distributive social justice, examining participatory parity and macro-level patterns by region, urban/rural context, sex, and public/private sector. Using secondary data from HEC, AEPAM, PBS/PSLM, and PPAF, it provides descriptive analyses.

Findings show substantial enrollment growth but not inclusive access. Enrollment increases as poverty decreases; extreme poverty zones have one public university, no private university, and less than half a percent enrollment, while low-poverty zones have 40% of the population and more than 70% of universities. Private universities are largely urban and in low-poverty zones. Rural areas, high-poverty zones, Baluchistan, and rural Sindh have low enrollment; Islamabad and other developed/urban regions have higher shares. Female enrollment rose overall, from 36% in 2001 to 47% in 2014, but gender disparity remains tied to poverty and region; in extreme poverty female enrollment is 0.02% versus 0.18% male, while in low-poverty zones it is 32% female versus 46% male. The passage concludes that HE reforms have not sufficiently addressed structural inequalities, that private universities can increase disparities, and recommends targeted public universities in rural/high-poverty areas, regulation, scholarships, financial support, inclusive environments, community colleges, and further research on HE and vocational equity.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated May 4, 2020. LLC as representatives. Interest is payable semi-annually on May 11 and November 11, beginning November 11, 2020. The passage contrasts digital leaders with digital laggards in building a data culture. Digital leaders adopt a growth mindset, use data for shared context, encourage teams to examine data, align through common targets, and promote risk-taking, experimentation, continuous learning, training, transparent data access with governance, measurement, and data-driven goals with flexibility. Digital laggards prioritize short-term efforts, optimize existing initiatives, discourage risk, offer narrow transactional training, tightly control data, favor business judgment or a “culture of genius,” and set aspirational goals not grounded in data, leading to process focus and misalignment. Even leaders face challenges balancing risk and failure, short-term pressures, inconsistent data attitudes, and over-analysis; regulated industries may create localized experimentation. Case studies describe a pharmaceutical company using a controlled experimentation team and a retail company implementing real-time sales reporting. The passage also identifies four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—and states organizations can build on strengths to develop a strong data culture.

University of Wisconsin’s Blake Geoffrion, the 2010 Hobey Baker winner, is called the new Crown Prince of NCAA Hockey; his hockey bloodlines trace back four generations, including great-grandfather Howie Morenz, grandfather Bernie “Boom-Boom” Geoffrion, and father Dan. The article recounts Howie Morenz’s life: born in Mitchell, Ontario, raised in Stratford, he starred for the Stratford Midgets, signed with the Montreal Canadiens in 1923, and became a record-setting scorer and Stanley Cup winner. After being traded to Chicago and the New York Rangers, he was reacquired by Montreal. In a game against the Black Hawks, he broke his leg, later suffered a nervous breakdown and heart attack, and died on March 8. Thousands attended his funeral at the Montreal Forum.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 31, 2022 reports Q1 2022 net sales of $116,444 million, operating income of $3,669 million, and net loss of $3,844 million, compared with Q1 2021 net sales of $108,518 million, operating income of $8,865 million, and net income of $8,107 million. This lecture continues from the Einstein field equations and introduces linearized general relativity as the first of three solution routes: weak gravity, symmetric solutions, and numerical solution. In linearized gravity, spacetime is nearly flat, with metric η_{αβ}+h_{αβ}, where h is small in nearly Lorentz coordinates and terms beyond linear order are neglected. The inverse metric is η−h at linear order. Infinitesimal coordinate transformations act as gauge transformations and leave the Riemann tensor unchanged. The trace-reversed perturbation h̄ is defined, and choosing Lorentz gauge simplifies the linearized Einstein tensor. The linearized field equations become a flat-spacetime wave equation for h̄. For a static, non-relativistic perfect fluid, the solution reduces to the Newtonian limit, yielding spacetime components related to the Newtonian gravitational potential. The lecture says the next lecture will solve the linearized equations generally and lead to gravitational radiation.

This qualitative study uses semi-structured interviews with 32 leaders, academic staff, and undergraduate and graduate students at six Mexican universities to examine stakeholder perspectives on online learning’s relationship to access and quality in Mexican higher education. Findings indicate online learning has widened reach, especially for non-traditional students with work or family commitments, but access is limited by economic barriers, infrastructure and internet deficiencies, resource divides between institutions, and rural/urban inequality; neurodivergent students and others needing support face challenges. Regarding quality, stakeholders report varied faculty proficiency with digital platforms, a need for ongoing teacher training, lower student engagement, collaboration and communication difficulties, differing subject-matter suitability, and perceived academic dishonesty. Stakeholders generally view online learning as valuable and flexible, useful for international collaboration, but as a complement to, not a replacement for, in-person education. They recommend improved internet infrastructure, increased resources for universities and non-traditional students, pedagogical support for teachers, and learning and mental health support for students. The study concludes that online learning can potentially democratize higher education in Mexico, but existing digital divides and lack of interventions may make it an equalizer or a divider depending on how disparities are addressed.

The passage describes a face mask from esthetician Renée Rouleau that the author says helped with premenstrual skin issues. Rouleau previously identified the author’s melasma, which she linked to birth control, and later diagnosed acne cosmetica after a Coachella Valley trip, recommending powder foundation. The author trusts Rouleau and tested her Rapid Response Detox Masque ($61), an anti-breakout solution for hormonal acne that is not drying. It addresses clogged pores from travel, hormones, and sleeping with makeup on; Rouleau suggests it for premenstrual acne to help “disrupt the acne cycle.” The mask is a lightweight golden, shimmery gel. Ingredients include tea tree leaf oil, lichocalchone or Chinese licorice, manuka branch/leaf oil, and a salicylic acid complex. It excludes parabens, synthetic fragrances, synthetic dyes, SD alcohol, and gluten. The author uses it once a week, leaves it on about 15 minutes, and says it removes easily and leaves a glow.

The passage is an AMD Geode™ CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update. It lists numbered hardware/software issues and errata for the CS5535, covering areas such as PIT, debug port, PIC, DMA, ATAC/IDE, USB, ACPI/PMC, GLIU, LPC, SMBus, GPIO, RTC, UART, and clock gating. The TPS7H500x-SP family consists of radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. The passage describes soft-start control via the SS pin, three oscillator modes configured through RT and SYNC pins, primary outputs OUTA/OUTB, synchronous rectifier outputs SRA/SRB, programmable dead time and leading-edge blank time, duty-cycle limits via DCL, current sensing and current limit through CS_ILIM, hiccup-mode operation, external FAULT protection, slope compensation, frequency compensation, and thermal shutdown. It also provides a design example for a synchronous push-pull converter using the TPS7H5001-SP at 500 kHz, covering component selection, power supply recommendations, and layout guidelines.

The passage describes a force transmission mechanism for teleoperated surgical instruments. The mechanism includes a drive pulley, a drive cable operably coupled with the drive pulley, a driven pulley operably coupled with the drive cable, and an actuation member coupled to the driven pulley. The actuation member transmits force to actuate an end effector, and rotational motion of the driven pulley causes translational movement of the actuation element. A surgical instrument includes a shaft, an end effector at a distal portion of the shaft, and the force transmission mechanism at a proximal portion of the shaft. A method includes winding a drive cable over a drive pulley by rotating the drive pulley, rotating a driven pulley by unwinding another portion of the drive cable, translating an actuation element, and operating an end effector. Detailed embodiments include pulley axes that may be parallel or perpendicular, a capstan drive pulley, one or two drive cables, idler pulleys, cable guides, grooves, a ball joint connecting the driven pulley to a drive rod, and pre-tensioning using upper and lower sheaves and a clamp screw. The mechanism may provide mechanical advantage based on pulley diameters and ball-joint distance from the driven pulley rotational axis, and the actuation rod may comprise a resilient material. Compared to toothed gear arrangements, disclosed embodiments may have lower friction, higher force transmission efficiency, greater range of motion, and reduced tooth skipping under high torque.

This passage discusses evolving theories and definitions of teams, teamwork, interdisciplinary studies, and interprofessional education (IPE). It distinguishes interdisciplinary studies, which draw on two or more disciplines, from IPE, defined by the World Health Organization as students from two or more professions learning about, from, and with each other. Both approaches share themes such as multiple perspectives, shared knowledge, conflict management, and knowledge integration.

Clarkson College formed an IPE committee in 2016 to develop an IPE curriculum. Its framework draws on the IPEC Core Competencies—values/ethics, roles/responsibilities, interprofessional communication, and teams/teamwork—as well as the Quadruple Aim, NCICLE guidance, and consultation with CIPER. The college added community involvement, service, and online learning as attributes of its model. The online IPE 301 course has five modules: the first four cover didactic IPE topics and must be completed in the first semester; module five requires real-time IPE events in knowledge, community, and service categories, with at least one event per category.

Since Fall 2018, all incoming students are enrolled in IPE 301 during their first semester; associate through doctoral degree-seeking students must complete it to graduate, and completion is documented though zero credit. Faculty and staff also complete a similar five-module course. The Interprofessional Collaborative Competencies Attainment Survey is used as pre-, mid-, and post-test, and reflection journals are analyzed. Data from Fall 2018 to Summer 2021 for 428 students who completed the course and all surveys showed perceived improvements in interprofessional collaboration; qualitative analysis found students enjoyed IPE events and reported learning in teamwork, collaboration, communication, and career awareness. The passage attributes success to curriculum planning, leadership buy-in, faculty engagement, and continuous monitoring, and describes committee transition to sustainability tasks.

On Nov. 8, 2001, Enron Corp. was reported to be in talks with Dynegy Inc. over a possible business combination, with Dynegy potentially acquiring Enron for about $8 billion in stock and ChevronTexaco, which owned about 27% of Dynegy, possibly providing $1.5 billion and an additional $1 billion at closing. Enron confirmed it restated earnings from 1997 through 2000 and the first two quarters of 2001, provided information to the SEC about partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, and believed Fastow received more than $30 million from those partnerships. Other articles covered U.S. stocks, European rate cuts, retail sales, jobless claims, NewPower’s narrower third-quarter loss, and Fitch’s comments on Wessex Water ratings.

This lecture recaps the Schwarzschild solution as a vacuum spacetime with mass m, a tidal singularity at r=0, and a coordinate singularity at r=2GM. An infalling body reaches r=2GM and r=0 in finite proper time, but in Schwarzschild coordinate time it only asymptotically approaches r=2GM. Light emitted near r=2GM is infinitely redshifted for distant observers, and pulse intervals stretch without bound, breaking Einstein synchronization. To address this, tortoise coordinates, null coordinates v=t+r* and u=t-r*, and Kruskal-Szekeres coordinates are introduced. In Kruskal-Szekeres coordinates, radial null geodesics move at 45 degrees, the metric is well-behaved except at r=0, and r=2GM is an event horizon: trajectories crossing it move toward r=0, and no event inside can causally influence outside. This spacetime is called a black hole. The lecture also describes Reissner-Nordstrom, Kerr, and Kerr-Newman black holes. It states the No-Hair theorem: the only stationary 3+1 dimensional spacetimes with event horizons are Kerr-Newman black holes, parameterized by mass, spin, and charge. It notes Kerr has survived tests and that Price’s theorem says non-Kerr-Newman structure radiates away, leaving Kerr-Newman. The final lecture will study orbits around black holes.

The passage describes features, architecture, peripherals, memory maps, pin/terminal functions, boot configurations, and revision history for the TMS320DM8127 DaVinci Digital Media processors. The state Department of Workforce Development awarded nearly $480,000 to seven projects to train almost 600 Milwaukee residents for jobs at area companies. The awards are part of $4.5 million in state funding Gov. Scott Walker announced in August after unrest in Sherman Park. Projects include training for community health workers, childcare and adult day caregivers, construction, permeable pavement installation, CNC and industrial sewing machine operators, and call center/customer service work.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture and GA100 GPU. It covers A100 features including third-generation Tensor Cores supporting FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary data types; fine-grained structured sparsity; simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution; HBM2 memory; and a 40 MB L2 cache. It discusses performance improvements over Tesla V100, Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitioning into up to seven GPU Instances with isolation and QoS, third-generation NVLink, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, and improved error and fault detection, isolation, and containment. It further presents NVIDIA DGX A100 as a system using eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch, MIG, and an optimized software stack for AI infrastructure.

Reports from Page, Droppers, and Sharp describe Allied and Greek responses. Page says the Allies’ joint reply was decided in conference, will be sent by Briand after Russia approves, and will be friendly though likely without details of war aims; Italy denied delaying its answer. Droppers reports Greece’s preliminary reply as conciliatory but indefinite, insisting on assurances, mixed commissions, and reparations; Italian conditions required Greek acceptance in principle within 48 hours and execution in 15 days, with the blockade lifted only after fulfillment. Sharp reports Briand delivered the Allied reply and a separate Belgian note, with publication planned for Friday the 12th. The French note praises the American note, supports a league of nations and international agreements with sanctions, but says peace requires settlement of the current conflict, reparation, restitution, and guaranties, and denies selfish Allied aims.

Solanko discussed Mikkola and Wrede, Finnish Legation personnel in New York; Mikkola was due Monday and Wrede was ordered back immediately. The U.S. said earlier return was unnecessary and its note applied to future visits outside Washington. The U.S. was unfamiliar with details of Finnish restrictions but thought them similar; delays in communications were discussed and the Department promised to expedite inquiries. Solanko was factual but surprised and once mentioned “prison regulations,” which was corrected. The Finnish Minister said Helsinki restrictions applied universally to all diplomats in a “war area”; the U.S. replied that all Finland was a war area and diplomats could move around the city, promising later communication. Schoenfeld reported Finnish opinion for December 21–January 4 was shaped by U.S. Far Eastern reverses and closer U.S.-British-Soviet cooperation, with satisfaction at Japan’s blows to the U.S. mixed with alarm at U.S. cooperation with the U.S.S.R.

The passage lists nine podcasts aimed at boosting financial knowledge. They cover side hustles and passive income, personal and business finances, audience money questions, building wealth with minimal resources, adolescent and young-adult finances, personal finance, real estate, investing, financial goals and plans, financial freedom, and how money, the economy, and financial markets work. Hosts named include Nick Loper, Farnoosh Torabi, Pat Flynn, Shannah Compton Game, Joshua Sheats, and David Stein.

VentureWire, published by Technologic Partners on Thursday, October 5, 2000, reports private company business news. Its top stories say Broadcom will acquire Element 14 for about $640 million in an all-stock transaction; Sony Broadband Entertainment formed 550 Digital Media Ventures; AC Ventures and Softbank Venture Capital launched GameChange with investments totaling up to $100 million; Enterprise Investors raised $200 million in a first close for its fourth Polish fund, PEF IV, targeting $300 million; Productopia closed; and CyOptics secured $57 million in venture funding. The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system. The passage describes its source-synchronous data interface, DCLKOUT capture clock, data clock and frame clock equations, data-output randomizer using XOR with the LSB or XOR_PRBS, simple and moving data averaging, and fixed, digital ramp, and alternating test patterns for channel groups CH[4:1] and CH[8:5]. Stafford Global, in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE, invites working professionals to online open days/webinars on distance learning. It advertises a University of Northampton MBA webinar on 01 May 2018, requires prior registration, offers free CV review/eligibility assessment with CV and certificates, and lists partner universities.

It also reports new funding rounds, Babygear.com’s Chapter 7 shutdown, product launches, name changes, new deals, M&A, board and executive appointments, VC fund news, and VC personnel news. Initial U.S. jobless claims fell 12,000 to a seasonally adjusted 260,000 for the week ended Sept. 30, more than expected, though Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, and Maria affected the data. The August trade deficit narrowed 2.7% to $42.4 billion, the smallest since September 2016, as exports rose 0.4% to $195.3 billion and imports dipped 0.1%. The real trade deficit was little changed at $61.8 billion. Hurricanes were expected to cut September job growth and third-quarter GDP, but trade could soften the economic blow.

NVIDIA Corporation's Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended October 31, 2021, contains unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and related notes, management's discussion and analysis, and other disclosures. For the three months ended October 31, 2021, revenue was $7,103 million, net income was $2,464 million, and diluted net income per share was $0.97; for the nine months ended October 31, 2021, revenue was $19,271 million, net income was $6,749 million, and diluted net income per share was $2.67. California lawmakers revived a proposal to set a goal of 100 percent carbon-free energy. A committee sent the bill to the full Assembly for a vote later this year. The bill, by Sen. Kevin de Leon, would raise the renewable portfolio standard from 50 percent to 60 percent by 2030 using specified renewable resources and set a 2045 goal for all remaining energy to come from sources that don't produce climate-changing gases, with details later. Critics, including business interests and utilities, warn of higher prices and stranded fossil fuel assets. Lawmakers are also considering regionalizing the grid operator and changing wildfire liability rules.

Two memoranda. The first says Moscow favors multi-level U.S.-Soviet dialogues to exploit divisions in democratic societies; the U.S. limited contacts to ministerial/ambassadorial levels, rejected separate White House links, and should await concessions through Gromyko or Dobrynin before lower-level talks or a summit. It calls a proposed summit and expanded specialist dialogues premature, citing no Soviet readiness to concede. It recommends another meeting with Gromyko and possibly Andropov; if no progress, maintain firm policy and portray the USSR as an obstacle to peace, since false expectations could pressure concessions. The second disputes Ambassador Hartman’s argument that the zero-zero option should be abandoned. It argues deterrence requires redressing strategic-nuclear asymmetries favoring the USSR and restoring parity at intercontinental and theater levels; non-zero solutions would perpetuate Soviet superiority in long-range Euro-based nuclear systems.

After 70 years, the University of Ghana appointed Mary Chinery Hesse as its first woman chancellor, effective August 2018, succeeding Kofi Annan. She is the first woman to hold such a position in Ghana’s public universities. She previously served as ILO deputy director-general from 1989–1999, held UN roles, and serves on several Ghanaian and AU boards. As chancellor, she will oversee university operations and preside over graduation ceremonies.

The passage discusses nominal techniques and formalization frameworks. It notes that Isabelle’s nominal package provides infrastructure and automation, while Rocq lacks such a framework; a Rocq proof of concept exists, and Pitts mentions limited nominal support in dependent-type systems such as Rocq and Agda. The authors propose a Rocq formalization of constructive nominal sets as a foundation toward a nominal framework, closely following an Agda development. The passage presents constructive nominal sets, including names, finite permutations as swaps, Perm-sets, support, nominal sets, freshness, α-equivalence, name abstraction, finitely supported functions, the Freshness Theorem, and the Freshness Condition for Binders. Constructively, least support cannot be proved, so some support is used, with some/any principles for freshness and α-equivalence. The Rocq development defines an abstract atom type with infinitude and decidable equality, permutations as lists of swaps modulo equivalence, typeclasses for PermT and Nominal, freshness with a some/any lemma, NameAbstraction with α-equivalence, supported functions as records, the Freshness Theorem, and FCB. It uses Rocq typeclasses and generalized rewriting to reduce setoid burden. Related work compares with Agda and discusses α-structural principles; currently only an α-recursion principle for the λ-calculus is derived, with α-induction left as ongoing work.

Authorities fatally shot a 28-year-old parolee suspected of shooting two teenagers at a Pasadena birthday party. He and a 36-year-old woman were found in a vehicle Friday in Duarte; officers from three agencies opened fire after contact. The man died at a hospital. The woman was shot, expected to survive, and arrested on suspicion of possessing narcotics. One officer had minor injuries. The 19-year-old male victim was critical, and the 16-year-old girl was treated and discharged. A task force including U.S. Marshals, Pasadena, Glendale, and state corrections had tracked the suspect.

Netflix began in 1997 as a DVD rental company and became a leading streaming video on demand provider, with 167 million paid subscribers and operations in 190 countries by 2019. It shifted from licensing content to investing heavily in original programming, including House of Cards, and executives attributed growth to a corporate culture emphasizing agility, innovation, independent decision making, transparency, candor, retaining high performers, and avoiding rules. Competitors consolidated and launched streaming services, including Disney+. Netflix viewed India as the source of its next 100 million subscribers, entered in 2016, and introduced a mobile-only plan, but faced a price-sensitive market, local-language preferences, and rivals such as Hotstar and Amazon Prime Video. The case asks whether Netflix should change premium pricing, its ad-free pledge, content types, partnership or acquisition strategy, or local decision making to grow in India.

Accern Sentiment Analysis reported that Senseonics Holdings news coverage trended somewhat positive, earning a media sentiment score of 0.19 and an impact score of 43.9168410140594, indicating recent press was somewhat unlikely to affect its share price immediately. On Friday midday, SENS traded up 5.03% to $3.34 on 1,001,915 shares; market capitalization was $411.49 million.

Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez Bezos have been a public couple since 2019 and often wear complementary looks on red carpets. The passage recounts their best style moments together, including coordinated outfits at events such as Amazon Prime Video, the Baby2Baby gala, “The Lord of the Rings” premieres, Versace and Staud fashion shows, Vanity Fair Oscar parties, a White House state dinner, the Met Gala, the Breakthrough Prize ceremony, their June 2025 wedding celebrations, and Paris Fashion Week.

The speaker, elected President and having taken the constitutional oath, pledges to execute all laws faithfully, express views to Congress, and use the veto when advisable. He will recommend policies but not enforce them against the people’s will. Noting the country has emerged from a great rebellion, he calls for calm settlement of questions without prejudice, hate, or sectional pride, and for security of person, property, and free religious and political opinion. He addresses payment of the public debt, specie resumption, gold payment unless contracts stipulate otherwise, revenue collection, accountability, and retrenchment. He discusses foreign policy, treatment of Indians toward civilization, Christianization, and citizenship, and suffrage, hoping for ratification of the Fifteenth Amendment. He asks mutual forbearance and prayers for union.

DISCARD, similar to ERASE, de-allocates discarded blocks partially or completely; contents become don't care and may remain partially or fully readable. It uses ERASE_WR_BLK_START/END and DISCARD (CMD38, argument 00000001h) for multiple blocks. Host must check DISCARD_SUPPORT; unsupported cards erase instead. Out-of-sequence/out-of-range commands cause errors and sequence reset. DISCARD is SDHC/SDXC-only, not SPI, with DAT0-low busy timeout 250ms.

The passage describes native assembler, stackless procedures using register passing. One procedure initializes the processor and cache to create a pre-memory stack region, divides it among cores, maps it to global address space, sets x86-64 MTRRs, runs on all cores, checks protected mode, handles SS/ESP or SS:ESP, creates UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF, and returns AGESA_SUCCESS, AGESA_WARNING, or AGESA_FATAL codes. AARCH64 APUs with PSP do not use the stack or very early macros; PSP initializes DRAM. The host must use this procedure; destroyed registers include EAX, ECX, EDX, EDI, ESI, and DS, ES in 16-bit. Another procedure removes the pre-memory stack, preserves EBX, returns processor and cache to a non-stack-enabled state, disables CAR mode without modifying MCRR settings, flushes cache lines, runs once on all cores, and is BSP-only; 16-bit code requires Big Real mode 32-bit data addressing. AmdCreateStruct creates and pre-initializes structure storage using PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, or ByHost methods, requires a stack, and returns status codes. Obtain data eye results returns a 31-element by 32-bit bitmap for a specified DIMM/channel/read-write, normalized to 1D trained Center[+16, -15], requiring coherent HyperTransport links and a stack.

The speaker marks the beginning of a new presidential term and announces the leading principles he wishes to follow, repeating views stated before the election. He calls permanent pacification and protection of all citizens’ constitutional rights supremely important. Southern States remain impoverished and need honest, peaceful local self-government that recognizes the rights of all and guards both races equally, with loyalty to the Constitution and laws. He discusses emancipation of 4,000,000 people, a moral obligation to protect their rights, and says the South’s evils require united efforts of both races, local self-government, material development, and improved education through free schools. He urges thorough civil-service reform, appointments not based on partisan service, and recommends a constitutional amendment for a six-year presidential term without reelection. He notes commercial depression since September 1873 and favors a coin-based, convertible paper currency and early resumption of specie payments. Abroad, he supports noninterference and arbitration. The close election and electoral-vote dispute were referred to a tribunal, whose decisions were accepted; he calls for peaceful adjustment, unity, justice, and peace.

Linda Farr, 68, received a 20-month jail sentence suspended for two years after admitting gross negligence manslaughter of her 86-year-old mother, Doreen Shufflebotham, who died on September 6, 2016. Medical experts estimated Shufflebotham had not moved from her chair for 8 to 12 months; she had multiple injuries and conditions. Neighbors reported flies, and local residents criticized the sentence online.

In Chicago, Barack Obama says it is good to be home, thanks Americans, and reflects on conversations with them. He recalls beginning community work in Chicago and says change happens when ordinary people engage. He cites progress including recession reversal, auto industry reboot, job creation, Cuba, Iran’s nuclear program, bin Laden, marriage equality, and health insurance for 20 million. He identifies threats to democracy: economic inequality and automation, racial division, and partisanship/media bubbles undermining shared facts. He discusses climate change, terrorism, and upholding constitutional principles without fear. He says in 10 days there will be a peaceful transfer of power to President-elect Trump and that his administration will ensure a smooth transition. He calls for citizenship, participation, voting, ethics, and compromise. He thanks Michelle, Malia, Sasha, Joe Biden, staff, and supporters, expresses optimism, and asks Americans to believe in their own ability to bring change.

A New Zealand man, Nigel Rothsay, learned in December that a property transfer mix-up meant he owned his neighbour's house, not the one he purchased in 2012, after police restrained the neighbour's property during a methamphetamine investigation and sought to confiscate it. Police were trying to remedy the situation.

The passage discusses reasoning language models (RLMs) trained with reinforcement learning to reason via chain-of-thought, and the challenge of selecting an RLM and reasoning budget that balances performance and cost. It notes that over 50% of MATH-500 queries can be solved by Qwen3-0.6B with minimal reasoning, while difficult queries may require stronger RLMs or higher effort, and strong RLMs can over-think. To address this, the passage proposes RADAR (Reasoning—Ability and Difficulty-Aware Routing), which selects among discretized {RLM, reasoning budget} configurations. RADAR uses a custom item response theory model to estimate query difficulties and configuration abilities, formulates routing as multi-objective optimization using linear or Chebyshev scalarization, and is black-box, plug-and-play, low-latency, and able to add new RLM configurations via adaptive testing. Experiments on reasoning benchmarks and out-of-distribution long-context QA report superior performance-cost tradeoffs, including matching 90% of OpenAI o4-mini high reasoning effort at 1.31% cost on MATH-500 and at 10% cost on FRAMES. Contributions include Pareto-optimal routing, IRT-based calibration, adaptive integration, and strong OOD generalization.

A Campaign for Black Male Achievement “Promise of Place” report says Milwaukee is progressing in improving life outlook for African-American boys and young men, scoring 71, up from 63, and ranking 13th among 50 cities on engagement indicators. It cites the MPS Department of Black and Latino Male Achievement, MyBlackStory.us, and support for the Black Male Achievement Advisory Council. Officials say increased engagement has not yet translated into lower crime or higher graduation rates. The council is in limbo after Mike Williams’ firing; some efforts stagnated, though some initiatives succeeded. The department identified strategies including school design, media narratives, manhood academies, and hiring more male teachers of color.

The slowed outflow boundary is moving slowly southeastward. Storms are developing over southeastern Missouri from Gulf moisture, and an MCV may trigger an organized severe bow potentially affecting part of the Tri-State.

Reckitt Benckiser’s shares are trading below their 52-week highs across RBGLY, RBGPF, and London RB, and its P/E is 22.79 versus the Household Products industry average of 24.62 and S&P 500 average of 25.03. The passage attributes the fall partly to legal fears over a South Korean dehumidifier incident involving at least 92 deaths and 530 injured, and partly to the $17.9 billion Mead Johnson acquisition. It argues these are short-term events, citing Reckitt’s brand-building record and five-year revenue/net income. Debt to total capital is 67.57%, with £2.39 billion debt, £18.02 billion assets, £765 million cash, and a $4.2 billion food-business sale to McCormick. Health and hygiene are 83% of the portfolio, with China important to the Mead Johnson deal. It notes a 2.37% dividend yield, 53% payout ratio, and a 15% discount to the 52-week high, concluding now is a good time to start a position.

A Hands Across the Sand gathering at Laguna’s Main Beach on Feb. 3 protested a Trump administration proposal to expand U.S. offshore drilling. The plan would lease 47 offshore areas from 2019 to 2024, including seven in the Pacific; California has more than 30 Southern California offshore platforms dating to the 1950s.

Baylor NAACP’s #myblackhistory hashtag features videos of African-American Baylor students sharing diverse perspectives on their experiences and what being African-American means to them. The group also celebrated the NAACP’s 108th founders day with a viewing of “A Raisin in the Sun” and will support upcoming multicultural events. Baylor NAACP president Reginald Singletary commented on the organization’s history and future work.

One in two Americans have a chronic disease. The Area Agency on Aging and Preble County Council on Aging urge attending Healthy U, six weekly workshops on Tuesdays, March 6–April 10, 9:30 a.m.–noon in Eaton, to learn symptom-management skills. Advance registration is required.

Constable Godknows Dube (36), stationed at Guyu Police Station and deployed at Gungwe Police Base, was facing rape charges and due in court on October 26. After leaving his girlfriend’s place for work, he was found hanging from a tree at the police base around 6AM. A source said no suicide note was left and suspected pressure from the rape allegations. A police spokesperson had not received a report. The passage also mentions two past police suicides.

In this insurance coverage dispute, Jill Kearns sued after an August 1998 fall, and the case settled for $100,000. Essex and Anton paid portions, and Vigilant and Travelers split Essex’s $87,500 payment while reserving contribution rights. The District Court ruled Vigilant’s coverage had priority, making Vigilant primarily liable for the entire $87,500. Vigilant appealed, arguing Travelers’ policy was ambiguous about priority. The Court of Appeals agreed with Essex that Travelers’ policy was unambiguous: Endorsement # 0192 specifically addresses additional insureds and subordinates Travelers’ coverage to other valid, collectible insurance available to Essex as an additional insured under Vigilant’s policy. No other provision contradicted it, so the District Court’s judgment was affirmed.

Biologists from the University of Bonn studied African cichlid Pelvicachromis taeniatus over two years, adding alarm substances to one group’s water. Males in the supposed predator group grew faster and developed larger eyes and longer dorsal-fin spines, and at the beginning of sexual maturity were more discreetly colored than males without alarm signals. These differences occurred only in males, possibly because males stay outside breeding caves and are more exposed. By about one year, both groups had the same conspicuous color, which serves as social signaling.

UBS’s Sergio Ermotti is seen as stronger than Barclays’ Jes Staley, reflected in UBS’s higher valuation. First-quarter results support this only partly: both lagged major U.S. peers in investment banking. UBS relies less on fixed income and gained in wealth management, while Barclays was hurt by U.S. macro trading and flat UK operations. Excluding a writedown, Barclays’ returns were close to UBS’s, and UBS faces expected outflows and possible margin pressure. Barclays’ discount appears too large.

Write blocks can be erased simultaneously using ERASE_WR_BLK_START, ERASE_WR_BLK_END, and ERASE commands in sequence. Out-of-sequence address or erase commands set ERASE_SEQ_ERROR; other out-of-sequence commands set ERASE_RESET. Write-protected sectors remain intact and WP_ERASE_SKIP is set. Addresses use byte-unit write block addresses; DAT0 low indicates erase in progress; post-erase data is 0 or 1 by vendor.

A cousin’s planned move from New York City to Nevada because winter cold makes her depressed introduces seasonal affective disorder (SAD), recurring depression tied to seasonal change. Winter SAD is most common; reverse summer SAD is rare. SAD affects an estimated 1–10% globally, more women, often starting in young adulthood, and roughly 10 million Americans. Its clinical definition appeared in the 1980s, though seasonal illness has been described since ancient times. Causes remain unclear; many scientists link reduced sunlight to hormone imbalance involving serotonin and melatonin, but some question whether SAD exists. Symptoms differ for winter and summer SAD. Untreated SAD can worsen. Treatment includes light therapy, medication, psychotherapy, and mind-body techniques, with preventive measures and physician consultation advised.

The Arms Index, or TRIN, is a market sentiment indicator created by Richard W. Arms in 1967. It compares the AD Ratio of increasing and decreasing stocks to AD Volume, helping gauge a market’s internal strength or weakness and spot short-term extremes. A reading of 1.0 indicates balance; below 1.0 is generally seen as bullish, above 1.0 as bearish. Readings above 3.0 may indicate an oversold market and possible bullish reversal, while below 0.50 may indicate overbought conditions. The AD Volume Line measures market breadth through net volume and can show buying or selling pressure and divergences. Backtests of a simple TRIN strategy showed 522 trades and 0.39% average gain per trade, which was not tradable. Adding a second indicator almost doubled average gain to 0.66%, with a 77% win rate and 2.4 profit factor. The passage states TRIN may be useful but likely not on its own, and should be backtested with other confirmations.
