The paper presents PAST, a Pilot-and-Adaptive Stable Trading framework for market-oriented edge-assisted UAV networks with spatio-temporal dynamism (STD-EUNs). It addresses reducing overhead and failure risk from online/spot trading, using pre-signed futures agreements and overbooking to improve market efficiency, and adaptively updating agreements and overbooking rates under uncertainty. PAST has two stages: PilotAO, which establishes pilot trading agreements with overbooking via stable many-to-many matching between UAVs as service buyers and edge servers as service sellers, specifying task assignments, service prices, and default clauses while balancing expected utilities and risks; and AdaptAO, which uses deep reinforcement learning, specifically a double deep Q-network, to dynamically update agreements and overbooking rates based on real-time demand, UAV mobility, resource availability, utilities, interactions, and reputation. The passage models UAVs and ESs, broader trading units and small trading units, Markov UAV mobility, Poisson inherent ES demands, utilities, risks, and matching problems. PilotAO is stated to satisfy individual rationality, fairness, non-wastefulness, strong stability, competitive equilibrium, and weak Pareto optimality. Experiments on real-world datasets compare PAST with ConSM, ConFM_NoA, ConFM_NoO, GrdM, and RandM, evaluating runtime, number of interactions, practical task completion time, social welfare, ES and UAV utilities, resource utilization, task completion rate under PT agreements, and individual rationality. PAST is reported to improve service success, resource utilization, decision efficiency, and social welfare, reduce overhead and latency relative to ConSM, and outperform static futures trading methods while ensuring individual rationality. Future work includes privacy-preserving mechanisms, machine learning for task specification such as target detection, and extension to heterogeneous multi-UAV, multi-ES networks.

While 2017 saw growth in plant-based eating, 2018 began with USDA predictions of record U.S. meat consumption. Although total per capita meat consumption has risen over five decades, the mix has shifted: beef peaked in the 1970s and has declined by about one-third; pork stayed relatively constant; chicken more than doubled, and 2018 could be another record year for chicken. Beef has not been “king” since around 1990. Replacing beef with chicken can raise animal welfare concerns but reduces environmental pressure: beef uses about seven times more land and emits seven times more greenhouse gases than chicken per gram of protein; plant-based foods are better still. U.S. diet-related greenhouse gas emissions fell about 10 percent from 2005 to 2014, mostly due to a 17 percent decline in beef consumption. Causes of the beef-to-chicken shift include health concerns, more women in the workforce, ready-to-cook chicken, production efficiency, and lower chicken prices. Beef remains the most environmentally consequential U.S. food, nearly half of Americans’ dietary footprint, and U.S. per capita beef consumption is four times the world average. Limiting global warming to 2°C will be difficult without further beef reductions in high-consuming countries. More shifts toward plant-based foods are needed.

This lecture reviews empirical work on price discrimination. Early studies examined whether observed price differences reflect discrimination rather than costs. Borenstein argued the leaded/unleaded gasoline price gap was too large to be cost-based, and Shepard studied self-service versus full-service gasoline as evidence of second-degree price discrimination. In racial and gender retail pricing, Ayres and Siegelman’s audit study found substantial discrimination against women and minorities in car bargaining; Goldberg found no racial price differences using Consumer Expenditure Survey data; Graddy found Asians paid 7% less than whites at the Fulton Street Fish Market.

Scott Morton, Zettelmeyer, and Silva-Risso used Autobytel and JD Power data. They found small price differences: Black areas paid about 1.5% more, Hispanic areas 1.1% more, Asian areas 0.4% less, and women 0.2% more. Autobytel buyers paid less, and race and gender effects were largely eliminated. The authors argued the results were consistent with profit-maximizing discrimination against less sophisticated or higher-search-cost buyers.

Shiller used ComScore web-browsing data for Netflix. He estimated demand elasticities without price variation by assuming known costs and profit maximization. Demographic targeting raised profits by 0.3%, while web-browsing targeting raised profits by 13%. Demographic targeting slightly increased consumer surplus; web-browsing targeting slightly decreased it. Second-degree discrimination was argued to be more powerful.

Dubé and Misra studied ZipRecruiter using a randomized pricing experiment with 7,867 firms and 133 features. ZipRecruiter was found not to be short-run profit maximizing at $99 per month; the estimated optimal uniform price was $327. Personalized prices ranged from $126 to $6,292, with a capped counterfactual at $499. Discrimination raised profits by 8.2%, while optimal personalized pricing reduced consumer surplus by about 25% and reduced social welfare relative to uniform pricing. A follow-up experiment supported the model’s predictions. ZipRecruiter later charged $249 but did not adopt personalized pricing. The lecture also notes limitations involving assumptions, short-run effects, two-sided markets, and possible reputational concerns.

The passage presents the work of the Policies in Research Organisations for Research Software (PRO4RS) Working Group, a joint ReSA–RDA initiative from 2023 to 2025. It states that research software is central to modern science and that research-performing organisations need robust policies to support sustainable, maintainable software, recognition of research software personnel, and reproducibility. Institutional policies on research software remain underdeveloped, though many institutions include software in infrastructure, licensing, or open science policies. PRO4RS produced outputs including a list of institutional policies, reports on policy change and gaps, and case studies, using the FAIR for Research Software definition. The passage also discusses broader research assessment reform initiatives, such as DORA, CoARA, Science Europe, and the Amsterdam Declaration, that support recognition of software and code. It proposes a layered framework: an optional central research software policy, middle-layer alignment across related policies, and outer-layer alignment with guidelines and frameworks. It recommends actions for institutional leadership and grassroots communities: highlighting institutional research software volume, advocating for recognition, and engaging stakeholders. It concludes that few institutions have formal research software policies and that institutions, as employers of software personnel, play a critical role in promoting good practices, collaboration, reproducibility, and research impact.

Following President Tyler’s December 30, 1842 recommendation, Congress appropriated compensation for a diplomatic officer to the Sandwich Islands. George Brown was appointed March 3, 1843, arrived at Honolulu in October, and asked the King for favorable treatment of U.S. citizens while disclaiming exclusive privileges; the King promised equal privileges with the most favored nation. A serious dispute arose over John Wiley, an American denied jury trial, amid French and British agreements containing jury clauses and a British convention objected to as discriminatory. With no U.S. treaty, the King’s promise was ignored on the advice of attorney-general John Ricord. The King requested Brown’s recall, though Brown was approved; Ten Eyck was appointed. Calhoun later confirmed U.S. recognition of Hawaiian independence. French and British conventions modified jury and liquor clauses but did not recognize complete independence. A Denmark treaty contained a favored-nation clause and first conveyed unrestricted acknowledgment of Hawaiian independence. Ten Eyck’s negotiations failed; he resigned in September 1848, and Charles Fames was appointed January 12, 1849.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture GA100 GPU, is an 8th-generation data center GPU for AI, HPC, and data analytics. It is fabricated on TSMC 7nm N7, has 54.2 billion transistors, 826 mm² die size, and includes up to 108 SMs, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 40 GB HBM2 memory, 1555 GB/sec memory bandwidth, and 40 MB L2 cache. It adds third-generation Tensor Cores supporting FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary, plus fine-grained structured sparsity. Stated speedups over V100 include TF32 10x, or 20x with sparsity; FP16/FP32 mixed precision 2.5x, or 5x with sparsity; FP64 2.5x; and sparse INT8 up to 20x. A100 introduces MIG, which can partition one GPU into as many as seven GPU Instances with isolated compute and memory resources, QoS, and fault isolation. It has third-generation NVLink with 600 GB/s total bandwidth, NVSwitch support, PCIe Gen 4, and SR-IOV. It also adds error/fault detection, isolation, and containment; asynchronous copy and barriers; task graph acceleration; L2 cache residency controls; compute data compression; NVJPG decode; optical flow accelerator; improved atomics; and five NVDEC units. CUDA 11 supports these features. The A100 powers scalable systems including DGX A100, which contains eight A100 GPUs, delivers up to 5 PFLOPS, and can provide up to 56 isolated accelerators via MIG. The passage also describes sparse neural network concepts and MIG architecture, GPU/Compute Instances, and the DGX A100 software stack.

This passage examines citizenship education in U.S. social studies and an inquiry-based community oral history project involving elementary preservice teachers (PSTs). It discusses concerns that PSTs often misunderstand citizenship and that social studies and citizenship instruction have been marginalized. The qualitative case study involved 38 elementary PSTs in four undergraduate K–6 social studies methods courses at a South Florida university. PSTs chose citizenship topics, interviewed anonymous community members, researched their topics, prepared 10 open-ended questions, used technology, and transcribed interviews. Data came from post-survey follow-up questions and were analyzed thematically. Findings indicate PSTs gained content knowledge through personal experiences and differing perspectives, were personally affected, and planned to use oral histories, community speakers, and difficult topics in future citizenship teaching. Limitations included no pre-survey and only four course sections. The study concludes that the oral history project helped PSTs better understand citizenship and increased their desire to teach it.

President Ford delivered his final State of the Union address to the 95th Congress, reporting that the state of the Union is good but can improve and is more perfect than when his stewardship began. He congratulated the new President and Congress and described the transition as proceeding well.

He recalled that when he became President in August 1974, the nation was divided, the Vice President and President had resigned, the Vietnam War’s effects continued, the economy was unstable, jobs and living costs were worsening, Congress and the executive were in conflict, and confidence in institutions was questioned. He reported progress in rebuilding confidence, maintaining peace, strengthening defenses and alliances, and conducting foreign policy. He cited relations with Western Europe, Japan, Canada, the Soviet Union, the Middle East, China, Asia, Latin America, and Africa, as well as efforts on trade, nuclear proliferation, and oceans.

Domestically, he cited economic recovery, lower inflation, more jobs, revenue sharing, community and manpower programs, and reduced crime growth, while noting unemployment remained a regret. He proposed tax reduction and investment measures. He said energy independence had not been satisfactorily achieved and dependence on foreign oil had increased, and he urged action on energy proposals. He discussed government reform, federal courts, legislative costs, and defense. He reported reversing a decline in defense resources and advocated strategic programs including Trident, the B-1 bomber, and a more advanced ICBM, along with NATO and naval forces.

He emphasized the Constitution, checks and balances, separation of powers, and his gratitude for public service.
Judgment modified by deducting $914.36 with interest; affirmed without costs.

The passage presents a study on whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) possess the specialized knowledge needed for marine ecology conservation. It notes that aquatic biodiversity monitoring is labor-intensive, remote, and expert-dependent. The study evaluates zero-shot marine species recognition and finds poor performance, with Qwen2.5-VL achieving 6.2% accuracy on frequent species and 0.2% on rare species. It designs tasks to diagnose domain knowledge, visual domain knowledge, and perception capabilities. It introduces FishNet++, a large-scale multimodal benchmark with 99,556 images, 17,393 fish species, 35,133 textual descriptions, 119,399 bounding boxes, and 706,426 key-point annotations. The benchmark includes taxonomic corrections, expert-validated descriptions, and additional images. Experiments show models improve at genus and family levels but struggle with fine-grained distinctions. Name translation and fine-grained verification reveal domain-knowledge and visual-perception deficits. Fine-tuning on FishNet++ raises Qwen2.5-VL frequent-species accuracy from 6.2% to 37.0%, and explainable fine-tuning adds interpretability. The study concludes that domain-specific benchmarks and fine-tuning are important for marine MLLMs.

LeBron James announced via X a “Second Decision” for October 7 at 12pm EST, shifting attention from the Lakers’ title hopes as Luka Dončić waits. Speculation says retirement is unlikely; many expect a partnership or business move. James is the first active NBA player to reach billionaire status. Dončić may have been notified before social media.

Bougainville, Papua New Guinea, has lifted a 40-year ban on new mining and exploration, allowing applications in iron ore-rich Tore, Isina and Jaba but excluding Panguna. President John Momis said this aims to ensure economic development. The ban, since 1971 except Panguna, was due to concerns over revenue-sharing and environmental impact.

Aaron Rodgers threw for 300 yards and four touchdowns as Green Bay beat Detroit 31-24 on Sunday night to win the NFC North by one game. The Packers finished the regular season on a six-game winning streak; Rodgers threw 18 touchdowns with no interceptions in the final seven games. Green Bay (10-6) will host the New York Giants, while Detroit (9-7) plays at Seattle as a wild card. The Lions, seeking their first division title since 1993, lost their final three games. Rodgers finished with 4,428 passing yards, 40 touchdowns and seven interceptions despite a sore right calf. Green Bay scored at least 30 points in four straight games and had 448 yards against Detroit.

President returns Senate bill No. 71, “An act to execute certain treaty stipulations relating to Chinese,” with objections to its passage. He states that treaty obligations may be repudiated only when in conflict with paramount interests and after reasonable means of modification are exhausted. The Burlingame treaty gave Chinese subjects reciprocal rights of voluntary emigration. A later treaty with China modified it, allowing the U.S. to regulate, limit, or suspend—but not absolutely prohibit—the coming or residence of Chinese laborers, reasonably and only as to laborers, not other classes. The President says the act’s 20-year suspension is broader than the treaty’s recital, affects residence and immigration nationwide, and amounts to a prohibition; he regards it as a breach of national faith. He also questions personal registration and passports as undemocratic, notes no provision for transit of Chinese subjects residing in foreign countries, and recommends a shorter experimental suspension. He concurs with many congressional objectives but warns the policy may repel Oriental trade.

A group including former NHLer Willie Mitchell was fishing for tuna about 120 kilometres off Tofino when a large shark fin appeared. They initially thought it was a great white, but a GoPro showed an eight-to-nine-foot salmon shark. Experts say salmon sharks resemble great whites, mainly eat Pacific salmon, are generally timid and rarely seen, though common in B.C. waters. The sighting was called a good ecosystem sign. Mitchell noted respect for sharks after swimming there. Warming waters could push southern sharks, including great whites, north; 13 other shark species have been documented in B.C. waters.

Sean Combs was sentenced to 50 months in prison on Friday, ending his criminal case but not his legal and reputational troubles. He still faces dozens of civil suits, and attorney Tony Buzbee said more will be filed. Combs has denied all accusations of sexual assault. His ex-girlfriend Ventura’s civil suit helped spotlight his behavior, and trial evidence may support civil cases. His business empire declined: Diageo cut ties, Sean John was pulled from Macy’s, he left Revolt and sold his stake, and music licensing and touring prospects suffered. Combs wrote that he lost his business, career, and reputation. Experts say his reputation is shattered and he is unlikely to regain his former status.

Single-crystalline graphene was grown on single-crystal Cu(111)/sapphire by ambient-pressure CVD. Although aligned graphene flakes are generally expected to stitch seamlessly, SEM and AFM revealed merging lines at some coalescence regions; STM showed some are overlapped junctions where one flake edge lies atop another. Wet oxidation in hot water oxidized the Cu underneath defective merging regions, detected by Cu2O Raman signal, indicating water-permeable structural defects. Among 122 merging regions, about 45% were defective and 55% likely seamless. The work classifies merging as Type A seamless stitching, Type B defective stitching, and Type C overlapped junction. These defects may enable molecular transport and applications such as nanofiltration, water desalination, and molecular sieving.

Meghan Linsey, 31, a 2015 runner-up on *The Voice*, woke on February 12 with a stinging face and a dead spider in her right hand. She went to urgent care and was diagnosed with a poisonous brown recluse spider bite. Brown recluse spiders are typically found in southern and central U.S. states; bites are rare and rarely deadly, and only about 10 percent require medical attention. Symptoms can include stinging pain, chills, itching, fever, nausea, sweating, and a sore. There is no antidote, only treatment for symptoms and wounds, which can take weeks or months to heal. Linsey experienced nerve pain, muscle spasms, rash, swelling, and a necrotic wound under her eye. After hyperbaric oxygen therapy and more than two months, her wound is healing well, her scar is almost unnoticeable with makeup, and she is back to performing. She shared her story to raise awareness.

The passage describes Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and Vision–Language Action frameworks, noting that tokenizing high-resolution images or video creates long visual sequences, memory and latency bottlenecks, making efficient pruning important for real-time use. It states that existing training-free token pruning methods often use fixed schedules or layer-specific heuristics that lack adaptability and do not explicitly adhere to a global computational budget. To address this, the passage proposes Complexity-Adaptive Pruning (AutoPrune), a training-free framework that estimates sample complexity via mutual information between early-layer visual and textual tokens and maps this estimate onto logistic retention curves. These curves are modulated by the mutual information score and rescaled so the area under the curve matches a user-specified token or FLOPs budget. AutoPrune is described as plug-and-play for VLM and VLA models, including LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, and Senna. The passage reports experiments on vision–language benchmarks, autonomous driving scene understanding, and planning, stating that AutoPrune outperforms existing training-free methods across pruning ratios. For LLaVA-1.5-7B, it reports pruning 89% of visual tokens, reducing inference FLOPs by 76.8%, and retaining 96.7% of original accuracy averaged over all tasks, a 9.1% improvement over PDrop.

The passage examines the paradox of moral education in philosophy of education and its reliance on a tacit libertarian concept of free will. It describes the dilemma of determinism: if determinism is true, alternative possibilities and moral responsibility are undermined; if indeterminism is true, actions lack adequate control. It presents Frankfurt’s thought experiment and hierarchical theory of the will, based on first-order desires, second-order desires/aspirations, identification, and volitional control. On this view, moral responsibility and autonomy/authenticity do not require alternative possibilities or self-determination and can be assessed in the actual scenario. The passage concludes that this hierarchical interpretation resolves the paradox of moral education and implies that moral education should focus on the quality of the will, identification, and responsibility even when individuals cannot act differently.

The plaintiff sought specific performance of a written agreement to sell land to the defendant. The plaintiff’s 1898 deed conveyed lots subject to restrictions to remain in force for twenty years from August 20, 1896, and included a provision that the grantee could redivide the land but no lot should have a frontage of less than fifty feet. The defendant refused title because of doubt whether that frontage restriction expired with the twenty-year period. The Superior Court dismissed the bill, finding reasonable doubt. The Supreme Judicial Court held that nothing in the deed or circumstances showed the frontage provision was part of a scheme for the benefit of other lots; it was a personal agreement between grantor and grantee, was omitted from later deeds, and did not create an equitable easement appurtenant to remaining lots. The possibility of later claimants was not a sufficient defect or doubt to deny specific performance, since the issue was construction of a written instrument with no reasonable doubt. Marine heatwaves are defined as prolonged periods of unusually warm water at a particular location for that time of year and can occur in any season. Analysis of more than 100 years of sea surface temperature data found that marine heatwaves have become longer and more frequent globally. The number of marine heatwave days increased 54% from 1925 to 2016, with an accelerating trend since 1982; comparing 1925–1954 and 1987–2016, frequency increased 34% and duration 17%. These trends are explained by ongoing ocean warming, and continued warming is expected to bring more marine heatwaves. Examples cited include a 2011 western Australia heatwave that killed a kelp forest and caused a persistent ecosystem shift, a 2012 Gulf of Maine heatwave that disrupted the lobster fishery, and “The Blob” in the North Pacific from 2014–2016, which caused fishery closures, marine mammal strandings, harmful algal blooms, and changed weather patterns. Anthropogenic climate change is linked to some recent events. Scientists next aim to quantify future changes and develop forecasts; urgent action to curb greenhouse gas emissions is still needed.

The lecture discusses Kerberos, a cryptographically secure protocol for authenticating computers and applications over a network. It was designed for distributed systems with client workstations and servers such as file, mail, and printer servers, to authenticate users to servers without trusting the network, unlike R login’s use of IP addresses. Kerberos introduces a Kerberos server, or KDC, which stores a shared key for every entity in a realm and maps names to keys. All parties must trust the KDC, and users must trust their workstations; additional trust relationships between servers can introduce risks.

The KDC has two interfaces: Kerberos and the Ticket Granting Service (TGS). Initially a client sends its name and requested service principal; the KDC returns a ticket encrypted with the service key and a shared key encrypted with the client key KC, derived from the user’s password. The client decrypts this, then discards KC. Later, the client uses a TGS ticket and an authenticator to request tickets for other services. A ticket contains server and client names, client IP, timestamp, expiration, and a shared key KCS; an authenticator contains client name, IP, timestamp, and is encrypted with the client-server key. Kerberos provides authentication, while services perform authorization using ACLs. Principal names must be handled carefully because reuse can grant access through stale ACLs.

The lecture describes problems in Kerberos 4: it assumed encryption also provided integrity/authentication, allowed offline password guessing, used the same key in both directions leading to reflection attacks, used fixed DES, and in password changing, disclosure of an old password could allow decryption of later password changes. Kerberos 5 addresses these with explicit authentication, multiple encryption schemes, separate directional keys, and Diffie-Hellman. It also notes KDC compromise is severe, KDC replicas are read-only, service key compromise requires changing the service key, remote dial-up login uses an extra step to authenticate the KDC, and the password-changing service only accepts tickets obtained directly from Kerberos with KC, not through TGS.

One year after Loper Bright overruled Chevron and ended a 40-year deference regime, questions remain about judicial review of agency interpretations. The passage highlights three shifts to watch. First, courts are directed to use independent judgment and find the single best statutory meaning, making agency-action justifications more textualist. Second, Skidmore deference, cited in Loper Bright, has appeared in lower courts as “shadow Skidmore,” sometimes as support or legitimation, though its future is unclear. Third, Loper Bright did not alter or mention the major questions doctrine; in the FCC universal-service case, Kavanaugh’s concurrence suggested the doctrine should not apply to national security and foreign policy because of Article II powers, a point noted in litigation over IEEPA tariffs. The passage concludes Chevron is dead, but the administrative state continues under a new framework of text, an unclear major questions doctrine, and Skidmore’s shadow.

Scaling in means gradually building a position as more entry opportunities appear, as part of a trading plan rather than a reaction to a losing trade. For stock investors, it involves buying additional shares as price drops to lower the average purchase price, often through dollar-cost averaging. Day traders may test the market with a small size and add to winning positions. Institutional traders use it to enter large orders gradually and avoid front-running and price impact. The passage distinguishes scale-in from double-down and Martingale strategies, which add to losing positions to try to reach breakeven. Scale-out is the gradual exit from a position, taking partial profits while leaving part open. Benefits include lower average entry price, less slippage and front-running, and adding to winners; risks include not filling the intended position before a reversal and losses after adding to winners. A backtest showed lower CAGR but improved risk-adjusted return/efficiency. Swing traders’ use depends on mean-reversion or trend-following approaches.

This retrospective single-center cohort study included 226 adult patients admitted to Rennes University Hospital between January 2020 and December 2022 for aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. Rebleeding occurred in 33 patients (15%). No statistically significant differences were observed between patients with and without rebleeding for the main risk factors from the literature. In univariate analysis, only time-to-event since first symptoms was associated with rebleeding, with odds increasing by 0.7% per additional hour; this remained significant in multivariate analysis, as did WFNS score. Mean time to event was shorter in patients without rebleeding; two-thirds of rebleeding events occurred more than 24 hours after symptom onset, and rebleeding before securing was 9% among patients treated within 24 hours versus 21% after 24 hours. Prognosis at 1 and 6 months did not differ statistically, though a trend at 6 months and higher GOS 5 incidence in non-rebleeding patients were observed. The study concludes that time elapsed since headache onset is a significant risk factor for rebleeding, highlighting the importance of promptly addressing delay when planning aneurysm securing.

This study examined whether the German 17-item Speech, Spatial and Qualities of Hearing Scale (SSQ17) is suitable for assessing hearing loss-related quality of life in patients with Menière’s disease (MD). Patients were part of a multicenter prospective MD registry; 97 consecutive patients were included, most with definite MD. Hearing loss was assessed by pure-tone and speech audiometry, and the SSQ17 measured patient-reported hearing ability across speech hearing, spatial hearing, qualities of hearing, and two additional questions. Audiometry showed asymmetric hearing loss, worse in affected ears, with impaired speech recognition. The SSQ17 total mean score was 6.0 ± 2.1; subscale means were 5.3 ± 2.5 for speech hearing, 5.1 ± 2.7 for spatial hearing, and 7.2 ± 2.1 for qualities of hearing. No statistically significant differences in SSQ17 results were found between diagnostic categories. Cronbach’s alpha was 0.960 for the total score and 0.904–0.956 for subscales. SSQ17 scores showed negative correlations with pure-tone thresholds of the affected ear and positive correlations with speech recognition scores for some scales. The study concludes that the SSQ is a viable tool for assessing hearing loss burden in advanced listening conditions in MD patients, though it is limited to hearing-related disability and does not capture vertigo spells.

This scoping review examines inflammation in depression and anti-inflammatory treatment strategies. It reports that inflammatory processes are associated with depression, and that anti-inflammatory drugs such as NSAIDs, Omega-3 fatty acids, and steroids have shown antidepressant effects. The literature review covers 31 animal studies on neuroinflammatory targets, including NLRP3, NF-κB, and P2X7R, and on pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions. The scoping review screened 1,057 articles and analyzed 11 randomized controlled trials involving 907 patients with depression. The included studies used varied anti-inflammatory drugs, treatment durations, and inflammatory markers; many markers were undetectable, while detectable markers included CRP, hs-CRP, sTNFR1, sTNFR2, IL-2, IL-6, and TNF-α. Anti-inflammatory strategies may improve depressive symptoms, but the passage identifies challenges including individual variability, drug safety, cost, ambiguous definitions of inflammation, and limited long-term and translational evidence. The discussion states that immune inflammation mechanisms do not fully explain depression and that clinical translation of anti-inflammatory strategies is inadequate. The authors propose systematic selection of inflammatory indicators and possible use of artificial intelligence and micro-robots to support monitoring and treatment. The conclusion states that anti-inflammatory pharmacological treatment for depression currently has limited research value and poor feasibility, and suggests shifting future focus toward non-pharmacological anti-inflammatory strategies and low-cost, generalizable public-interest studies.

Digital laggards often fail to connect goals with strategy: priorities reflect high-level outcomes, teams poorly understand objectives, and company-wide misalignment results; a “culture of genius” exacerbates this. A data-driven culture can align organizations vertically through metrics and objectives and horizontally through common data models and transparent access. Digital leaders emphasize data culture as central, aligning beliefs, values, and actions; laggards show gaps between espoused values and behavior due to entrenched habits, lack of skills, and insufficient top-down focus. Changing mindsets is challenging but laggards are not doomed, and mature organizations must continue growing culturally. Technologically mature firms differ in data culture. Organizations fit four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—and can build on strengths with targeted actions.

A Seattle Public Utilities study found that while Seattle’s short showers and drizzle persist, extreme rainstorms have become more common and more extreme over the last 15 years. Based on about four decades of data from 17 rain gauges, the study confirms anecdotal reports and is described as a climate-change preview. A 24-hour storm once considered a once-in-a-century event at 4 inches can now be expected every 25 years, and the new once-in-a-century standard is more than 5 inches; a 6-hour, 1.86-inch storm has similarly shifted. Storms lasting six hours and three days are also becoming more extreme. SPU uses the data for drainage and sewage planning, including flood-prevention projects and a storage tunnel under the Lake Washington Ship Canal. Officials say Seattle’s infrastructure was built for a different climate, and the National Weather Service says the study underscores the need to prepare for flooding.

Delvin Payton and five other former arrestees released on bail from Illinois county jails filed a putative class action challenging the counties’ practice, authorized by Illinois law, of imposing a bail fee above the set bail amount as a condition of release. The district court dismissed the action, finding the named plaintiffs lacked standing, and denied class certification as moot. The Seventh Circuit reversed and remanded. It concluded the named plaintiffs stated individual claims against Kane and DuPage Counties and reversed dismissal of those individual actions and the putative class actions against those counties. As to the other 17 counties, the court discussed the juridical link doctrine and held that, once a class is properly certified, standing may be assessed as to the class as a whole; plaintiffs may represent a class suing all 19 counties if they satisfy Rule 23. This work demonstrates solid-state NIR-to-visible photon upconversion using a DIB-SQ:PCBM bulk-heterojunction sensitizer with a rubrene or DBP-doped rubrene annihilator/photoemitter. The 1:3 DIB-SQ:PCBM blend was optimal, enabling UC emission under 690 nm excitation. The mechanism uses 3CT states formed in the fullerene-based BHJ to populate rubrene triplet states, followed by TTA. Neat DIB-SQ or PCBM sensitizer devices showed reduced or no UC emission. Rubrene:DBP devices showed a 605 nm UC emission peak, a saturated UC quantum yield of 1.36%, and a threshold intensity of 60.5 mW/cm². Time-resolved and steady-state spectroscopy identified CS, 3CT, and molecular triplet intermediates, and magnetic-field measurements supported a TTA-defined mechanism. The approach repurposes back electron transfer/3CT states, typically a loss channel, for NIR-to-visible upconversion.

In Bracero v. S. Ramírez & Co., an action for damages after bags of rice fell on Bracero in a shop, the defendant argued it lacked ownership or control of the shop and that Bracero was a workman under the Workmen’s Compensation Act. The court found Bracero was an independent contractor and found evidence sufficient to justify that the defendant had a branch in Ponce. The majority reversed the judgment, finding no negligence attributable to the defendant at the time of the accident. It criticized the briefs, especially the appellant’s non-concise statement and late assignment of errors, and discussed res ipsa loquitur, noting the doctrine was not applied below and that plaintiff and other workmen had intervened with the pile; it found no reason to apply the doctrine. Chief Justice Del Toro dissented, joined by Justice Hutchison, believing the evidence supported the trial court. The trial court found Bracero contracted with defendant’s branch to transport rice; while waiting, a pile twenty bags high fell and injured him. It found the pile was defectively erected by defendant’s employees, without warning, and the accident was due solely to defendant’s fault and negligence. Witness Mayol testified he warned defendant’s employees the pile was badly formed and might fall; they said it was all right and later built another pile in front, propping up the leaning pile. The dissent would affirm.

The passage introduces an evolutionary hypergame dynamics framework in which players have heterogeneous strategy sets rather than full access to all strategies. It studies a three-strategy prisoner’s dilemma with Cooperation (C), Defection (D), and Loner (L). On a fast timescale, players update strategies through introspection dynamics; on a slow timescale, the composition of strategy sets evolves under replicator or payoff-monotone dynamics. The framework is analyzed in pairwise tournaments, well-mixed populations, and spatially structured populations.

Results depend on the benefit-to-cost ratio and introspection strength w, a proxy for rationality. Under weak introspection, defection-containing strategy sets generally outperform cooperation-containing sets, and {C,D} often dominates self-play except at high benefit. As w increases, {C,L} gains advantage through self-reciprocity and resistance to exploitation, eventually becoming dominant for sufficiently high w and benefit-to-cost ratios. Theoretical analysis shows higher w increases mutual cooperation payoffs within {C,L} and reduces defectors’ gains, with {C,L} surpassing {D} and {D,L} beyond critical thresholds.

In evolutionary dynamics, weak introspection favors {D,L} or {L}, while higher introspection favors {C,L} in both well-mixed and structured populations. With seven strategy sets, structured populations show transitions from {L} dominance at low w, to coexistence and increasing {C} at intermediate w, to {C,L} dominance at high w. The passage concludes that heterogeneity in strategy sets and their co-evolution reshape evolutionary outcomes, with greater introspection promoting cooperation.

The passage summarizes a study that searched PubMed for papers on antimalarial resistance in Africa and found few studies combining ex vivo drug susceptibility with genotyping. The study assessed ex vivo susceptibility of Ugandan Plasmodium falciparum parasites to nine antimalarial drugs from July, 2019, to June, 2024, using more than 1100 isolates from eastern and northern Uganda, and characterized genotype-phenotype associations by sequencing 80 potential resistance genes. Parasites were mostly sensitive to commonly used antimalarial drugs, but genotypes and phenotypes changed over time. Susceptibility to chloroquine increased, while susceptibilities to dihydroartemisinin and lumefantrine decreased over time, although the decreases were modest and clinical implications are uncertain. Many isolates had ring-stage survival above previously established artemisinin resistance cut-offs. PfCRT K76T and PfMDR1 N86Y mutations were very low or decreasing; PfK13 C469Y and A675V were associated with decreased dihydroartemisinin and lumefantrine activity but not with ring-stage survival assay results. Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance mutations were highly prevalent, and pyrimethamine susceptibility was poor. The passage states that continued parasitological and genomic surveillance and policy changes to limit resistance selection and treatment failure should be high priorities.

The passage introduces InVirtuoGen, a continuous-time discrete flow model for fragment-based drug discovery that operates directly on fragmented SMILES. It states that FBDD uses fragment-constrained design but is often guided by expert heuristics, while existing in silico models use graph or SMILES linearizations that disrupt substructures and limit scaffold control. InVirtuoGen instead refines all sequence positions simultaneously, using fragmented SMILES with explicit attachment points and revised BRICS decomposition. It is evaluated on de novo generation, fragment-constrained generation, PMO target property optimization, and lead optimization, after pretraining on ZINC and UniChem. The passage reports competitive or improved results, including superior quality-diversity trade-offs in de novo generation, competitive fragment-constrained results, state-of-the-art PMO results, and a hybrid genetic algorithm with PPO framework.

The lecture reviews Wald’s equality for stopping trials, defining a stopping trial J as a random variable where the indicator of J=n depends on X1 through Xn, and a possibly defective stopping trial as one that may be defective. Wald’s equality requires the Xn to be IID with mean Xbar and gives E[S_J] = Xbar E[J] when E[J] is finite. The lecture applies this to the elementary renewal theorem, showing that E[N(t)]/t approaches 1/Xbar. N(t) is not itself a stopping trial because the last arrival before t can only be identified after seeing a later arrival, so J = N(t)+1 is used. Wald’s equality gives a lower bound on E[N(t)], while the upper bound and proof use truncation of X at a large value B, proof for the truncated variable, and then letting B approach infinity; details are in the notes.

A generalized stopping trial is then defined for pairs of random variables (X1,V1), (X2,V2), etc., where the stopping indicator depends on those pairs up to n. Wald’s equality still holds by the same proof. This is applied to the G/G/1 queue with IID interarrival times X and IID service times V. The first arrival to an empty system is a generalized stopping trial, and after it the future arrivals and service times are independent of the past. Intervals between new busy periods form a renewal process, and the same analysis applies to G/G/m and broader systems, provided the queue sometimes empties; if service times exceed interarrival times, renewals may not occur.

Little’s theorem is presented for queues where the system empties and restarts. L(t)=A(t)-D(t) is the number in the system. Over an inter-renewal period, the integral of L(t) equals the sum of waiting times W_i. Taking limits gives that the time average number in the system equals lambda times the expected delay, L = lambda W. This is described as an accounting identity, with renewal theory used to justify the limits.

The Pollaczek-Khinchin formula for M/G/1 queues is given: with Poisson arrivals at rate lambda and IID service times having mean Vbar and second moment V^2bar, the expected waiting time in queue is W_q = lambda V^2bar / [2(1-rho)], where rho = lambda Vbar. If rho exceeds 1, the system is in trouble; if the second moment is infinite, the expected wait can be infinite. Examples include M/D/1 and exponential service, and a heavy-tailed binary service distribution giving W_q = rho/[epsilon(1-rho)]. The derivation uses residual life, queue length, and Little’s theorem.

The passage discusses magnetic monopoles, Dirac’s proposal, artificial quasiparticles with monopole properties, and the lack of direct observation of a fundamental magnetic monopole. It describes the topological magnetoelectric effect in topological insulators, where magnetic field induces electric polarization and vice versa, making it possible to induce a magnetic monopole by applying an electric field on a 3D TI. The work presents an STM/STS method to investigate image potential states (IPS) on 3-Bi, Bi(110), and Bi(111). A vertical electric field produces Rydberg IPS, while a radially distributed electric field on a vacuum-TI-substrate structure creates a circulating Hall current and inverse magnetic monopoles only in 3D TIs beyond the 2D limit. IPS on 3D TI are considered induced by positive charges and magnetic monopoles, forming dyons and electron-dyon quasiparticles; introducing a magnetic monopole reduces degeneracy and splits energy levels. Bi was grown on Si(111), producing 3-Bi, Bi(110), and Bi(111). IPS on 3-Bi and Bi(110) fit Gaussian distributions, with FWHM decreasing with principal quantum number n. On Bi(111), IPS peaks for n>1 deviate from Gaussian; n=2 splits into n=2 and 2′, while splitting for n=3,4 overlaps. Alternative explanations—symmetric/antisymmetric IPS, quantum well states, and quantum confinement—were considered and ruled out. The splitting is attributed to the Zeeman effect of orbital magnetic moments interacting with the magnetic field from magnetic monopoles. The n=2 splitting energy is about 400 meV, compared with a theoretical estimate of 204 meV. Varying tunneling current changes the tip electric field and splitting, and at zero electric field the subpeaks recombine. The conclusion states this demonstrates generation and detection of magnetic monopoles on 3D TI surfaces, supports magnetic monopole detection, and offers a platform for exploring their properties and applications.

Blackwell adds hardware encode and decode support for 4:2:2 chroma in H.264 and H.265. The passage states that the double decision was perceived mainly as strengthening U.S. credibility in Europe and the Atlantic alliance, so any INF solution should strengthen or at least not weaken the alliance. Heating oil is a low-viscosity liquid refined from crude oil, used almost exclusively for heating residential and commercial buildings; demand rises as temperatures drop in winter. Heating oil futures are derivatives for buying or selling a specified quantity on a future date at a pre-agreed price, traded on ICE Futures Europe and CME. ICE uses symbol UHO and is cash-settled; CME uses HO and is physically delivered. Both contracts are 42,000 gallons or 1,000 barrels, with a minimum fluctuation of $0.0001 per gallon, or $4.20 per contract. Trading hours and settlement methods vary by exchange. A heating oil futures strategy uses technical and fundamental analysis and risk management. A backtest of 168 trades returned an average of USD 370 per trade, a profit factor of 2.02, and a 59% win rate. Heating oil tends to perform better between February and August. The all-time high is $5.2215 in April 2022; the all-time low is $0.2920 in February 1999. Factors affecting prices include weather, crude oil prices, refinery capacity, and alternative heating fuel costs. Risks include adverse price movement and leverage. A HEAT ETF tracks the market, and CFDs are offered by some brokers.

An inside day occurs when today’s price action is completely within yesterday’s high and low. Inside days happen frequently, especially on daily bars, and are the opposite of outside days. According to the passage’s research and backtests, inside days alone are a poor trading signal, do not strongly indicate future movement, and require additional variables to develop a potentially workable strategy.

Strength training builds muscle mass, strength and endurance but requires correct technique and proper warm-up and cool-down to avoid injuries. Common injuries include rotator cuff injuries from repetitive overhead motions; hamstring strains or tears from sudden powerful movements; herniated discs from sudden extreme or repetitive poor movement during weightlifting; tendonitis from repetitive motions or sudden impact; and tennis or golfer's elbow from repetitive wrist and arm movements. Prevention includes good shoulder posture, stretching, gradual increases in intensity, rest and recovery, hydration, a good diet, and ice, compression and elevation. Seek medical help for persistent pain, and consult a qualified fitness instructor or doctor when needed.

The passage introduces spin diffusion length (ls) as key for spintronic devices and notes the need for accurate simulations. It describes a previously developed ab initio approach for ls and spin lifetime, successful for various materials, but challenged by electric fields along periodic directions. The work extends this approach using a covariant derivative formalism to include the spin-drift effect from a longitudinal electric field. It derives a linearized steady-state quantum master equation under finite E, describes solving ls(E) via eigenvalue problems, proposes a Rayleigh-Ritz-based model formula, and compares ab initio ls(E) results with model estimates for monolayer WSe2, bulk GaAs, bulk GaN, and graphene-h-BN.

After protesters disrupted Charles Murray’s planned lecture at Middlebury last March, administrators acted on a Public Safety officer’s accusation that Addis Fouche-Channer ’17 was at the protest, though she says she was never there. The officer identified her by name as the person pulled off Bill Burger’s car but gave no other evidence, transcripts show. Middlebury police requested an interview; she declined. Private investigators asked for a statement; she declined three times. A judicial dean charged her May 9 with violating the Demonstrations and Protests policy. She contested and provided evidence, including IT Wi-Fi logs, five statements, blog posts, emails and a phone step counter. On May 13, the dean said there was no good reason to proceed with a hearing. Fouche-Channer later sought an apology from Public Safety, prompting an internal investigation into whether the officer racially profiled her. The investigation was complete by Sept. 14, but no decision had been made as of press time; it was delayed until the following week. Officials and the officer did not comment.

This paper examines the feasibility of vehicular cloud computing in 5G-enabled urban environments, focusing on performance, sustainability, and incentives. It proposes a centralized 5G architecture involving end-users, gNodeB, a controller, vehicles, and cloud resources, and models offloading time, energy consumption, costs, and task allocation under deadlines and capacity constraints. The stated contributions include an integrated delay- and energy-aware task allocation framework, a stochastic coalitional game for revenue sharing with a non-empty robust core, and assessment of CO2 savings and long-term vehicle participation incentives. The passage also reviews related work on task allocation, cooperative and intelligent offloading, and game-theoretic cooperation, then presents the system architecture, system model, task allocation optimization problem, and revenue-sharing mechanisms.

Chamomile is a group of plants used since ancient times as an herbal remedy. Matricaria recutita and Chamaemelum nobile are widely grown. Matricaria recutita has been used in teas for fevers, flu, digestive disorders, and skin ailments. Its flower extract, chamomile or blue oil, contains coumarins, sesquiterpenes, polyacetylenes, flavonoids, chamazulene, farnesene, bisabolol, and terpene alcohol. Extracted mainly by steam distillation with yields of 0.2–0.4%, it is used for relaxation, insomnia, mood, anxiety, aching joints and muscles, skin lotions, digestive problems, conjunctivitis, and commercial products.

The passage presents a protocol for the Canadian Social Determinants Urban Laboratory (CSDUL), a multilevel, longitudinal virtual environment combining surveys and administrative databases to study how social determinants affect income-related health inequalities in urban Canada. Guided by the WHO Social Determinants of Health framework, CSDUL will use Statistics Canada’s Canadian Population Health Survey, area-level indicators, and a hub-and-node structure with five nodes: political and economic context, environmental context, socioeconomic context, material circumstances, and health systems. It aims to replicate WHO/Europe’s decomposition analysis of income-related inequalities in self-reported health and report the relative impact of social determinants at micro, meso, and macro levels. The project will analyze database strengths and limitations, develop variables, examine interaction effects by gender and non-white identity, and support multisectoral interventions. The preprint is noted as not certified by peer review.

A meta-analysis of 333,247 adults found moderate alcohol consumption was linked to lower all-cause mortality than abstention or heavy drinking, especially in older people, women, and non-Latino whites. Moderate drinkers were about 25% less likely to die of heart disease or stroke than never-drinkers but no less likely to die of cancer. Heavy drinkers had slightly worse all-cause mortality than moderate and never-drinkers and about 45% higher cancer-death odds than moderate drinkers. Moderate means ≤14 servings/week for men and ≤7 for women; weekly binge drinking raised death odds about 16%, largely through cancer. New research found heavy drinking raised all-cause and cancer mortality in men but not women; non-Latino whites, not non-Latino blacks, appeared to benefit from moderation; protective effects were greater at 60+ and absent at 18–39.
