Zhengzhong Jin’s lecture presents batch arguments (BARGs, also called SNARGs for Batch NP). A BARG is defined by a generator, prover, and verifier sharing a CRS; the prover gives a single proof that all instances x1,...,xk belong to an NP language L, using witnesses w1,...,wk. Succinctness means the proof is smaller than the total witness length, and completeness and soundness are required. The lecture discusses applications, statistical-soundness questions, and the Gentry-Wichs impossibility result for general SNARGs, then states a BARG construction from learning with errors with proof size dominated by the relation circuit size and verification time with an online phase independent of k. The construction starts from a Kilian-style PCP protocol: PCPs for k statements are arranged in a matrix, columns are hashed, a PCP query is made, and queried columns are opened and checked. To make it non-interactive, the lecture recalls correlation-intractable hashing for three-round public-coin protocols and notes the need for a sparse relation. It introduces an SSB hash built from FHE, with key indistinguishability, statistical binding, and extraction, and uses it to bind a selected row. The soundness proof fixes an index i* whose statement is not in L, switches the CRS to the SSB key for i*, extracts the PCP for i*, defines a relation, and invokes CI-hash correlation intractability.

Carbon-related spin defects in hBN were created by 13C ion implantation followed by high-temperature annealing. A single defect complex showed a PL peak near 600 nm and g(2)(0) = 0.21. It is described as a spin pair of two electron spins; one electron spin strongly hyperfine-couples to a 13C nuclear spin, forming a four-level, two-qubit electron-nuclear system controllable with MW and RF pulses. ODMR revealed two resonances split by ~290 MHz and a central resonance; ODNMR showed peaks at 141 and 145 MHz. CPMG dynamical decoupling extended electron spin coherence from T2,echo = 148 ± 8 ns to T2,e = 38 ± 10 µs with CPMG-1024, scaling as N^0.77±0.09. Using selective gates, the electron-nuclear system was initialized, all four Bell states were generated, and density matrices were reconstructed by quantum state tomography.

Apple Inc. (AAPL) is a multinational technology company headquartered in Cupertino, California, founded in 1976. It designs, develops, and sells consumer electronics, software, and online services, including iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, Apple Watch, AirPods, and HomePod. AAPL is the Nasdaq ticker and began trading December 12, 1980. It is a Dow Jones component, one of the world’s largest and most valuable publicly traded companies, and Berkshire Hathaway has a major position.

AAPL trades during regular hours, usually 9:30 am to 4:00 pm ET, and not 24 hours. It pays an annual dividend of $0.82 per share and has options. It does not expire and can be held long-term. Its average return over the past five years is about 16.1%; its all-time high is $233.47, reached October 3, 2018. It can be bought through a broker. Swing trading, scalping, and day trading are possible, though scalping is not recommended. VXAPL is a VIX for AAPL. AAPL is subject to capital gains taxes when sold; short-term gains are taxed at regular income rates and long-term at lower rates in the US. Dividends may be withheld 15–35% for foreigners, subject to tax agreements. Popularity is attributed to strong fundamentals, known products, size, dividends, share appreciation, and a long upward trend. Trading success is difficult; becoming a millionaire is possible but unlikely, and most fail. Best strategy, indicator, and time frame depend on the individual and backtesting. Selling depends on factors including financial goals, valuation, diversification, fundamentals, market conditions, taxes, personal circumstances, psychology, performance, and risk tolerance.

The passage states that Communist regimes create millions of refugees by claiming jurisdiction over all of society and demanding changes that violate internalized values and habits. It cites Hoang Van Hoan on Vietnam’s treatment of Chinese inhabitants: expulsion, dispossession, relocation to new economic zones without aid, and death from disease, hardship, and humiliation. It says over six million refugees had fled Marxist governments by the end of 1978, and contrasts refugees from Marxist regimes with those from other autocracies, including Cuba versus Argentina, Brazil, and Chile, and Guinea/Guinea Bissau versus Zimbabwe Rhodesia. It argues radical totalitarian regimes are unlikely to transform themselves, while liberalization is more likely in several listed non-Marxist governments. It recommends U.S. policy encourage gradual liberalization/democratization, warns victorious Marxist insurgency is unlikely to produce anything but totalitarian tyranny, distinguishes authentic democratic revolutionaries from Marxist revolutionaries and Nicaragua’s current leaders, and says groups defining themselves as enemies should be treated as enemies.

The lecture reviews covariant derivatives, Lie derivatives, Killing vectors, and Killing’s equation. It discusses tensor densities, the Levi-Civita symbol, the determinant of the metric as a tensor density of weight minus 2, converting tensor densities into tensors, and constructing volume elements. It derives an identity for contracted Christoffel symbols using the determinant of the metric, applies it to vector divergence and Gauss’s theorem, and notes that tensor divergence generally cannot be similarly simplified except for antisymmetric tensors; local conservation of stress-energy does not generally become global conservation. The lecture then formulates test-body motion in curved spacetime through parallel transport, derives the geodesic equation, discusses affine parameterization, and outlines an action principle for extremal proper time. It ends by noting future treatment of null trajectories and conserved quantities from Killing vectors.

The Double Seven strategy, by Larry Connors and Cesar Alvarez from Short Term Trading Strategies That Work, is a simple mean-reversion system that buys when the close is above the 200-day moving average and at a seven-day low, and sells when the close is at a seven-day high, with no stop loss. Backtests over twenty-one years on liquid ETFs found it still works, but Connors has other strategies that work better. On SPY since 1993, it had 154 trades, 1.18% average gain, 82.5% win ratio, 2.58 profit factor, 1.4 Sharpe ratio, 33% maximum drawdown, 26% exposure, and 6.3% CAGR versus 10.1% buy-and-hold. An ETF portfolio had 1,189 trades, 0.63% average gain, and 6.3% CAGR, mostly before 2010. A SPY/QQQ portfolio did not work because of overlapping trades. The strategy performed reasonably well on 2–15 days on the S&P 500, while the short version performed badly.

During Card Identification Mode the host remains at fOD; in Data Transfer Mode it may operate at fPP. CMD9 obtains CSD, CMD4 configures DSR, and CMD7 selects one card into Transfer State; RCA 0x0000 returns all cards to Stand-by. Only one card can be in Transfer State, and CMD7 with un-matched RCA de-selects. Data Transfer Mode communication is point-to-point. Read commands can be aborted by CMD12; write commands must be stopped before CMD7 de-selection. Successful write completion moves the card to Programming State, otherwise Transfer State. Block write may be buffered; CSD write, write protection, and erase are not buffered. Parameter set and read commands are not allowed while programming. Reset can terminate programming and may destroy data. Wide bus operation is selected/deselected by ACMD6; default is 1-bit. For 2 GByte cards, maximum block length is 1024 bytes but CMD16 block length is up to 512 bytes. Read/write are block-oriented with CRC; block length can be up to 512 bytes. CMD17/CMD18 read, CMD24/CMD25 write, and CMD12 stops transfers. Erase uses CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38; DISCARD and FULE are similar, supported for SDHC/SDXC and not SPI, with specified busy timeouts. Write protection includes mechanical switch, card internal, and password protection. CMD42 supports lock/unlock, passwords, Force Erase, FEP Force Erase, and COP functions. APP_CMD (CMD55) introduces ACMDs; GEN_CMD (CMD56) section is blank. CMD6 switches functions such as access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. High-Speed Mode uses 50 MHz for 25 MB/sec and requires one card. CMD34-37, CMD50, CMD57 are reserved for command system expansion. CMD8 initializes version 2.00+ cards in Idle state. CCS in ACMD41 distinguishes SDSC from SDHC/SDXC; SDHC/SDXC use block addressing with fixed 512-byte block length and disable partial/misalign access. Clock can be lowered/stopped with restrictions, including ACMD41 polling and clock cycles after transactions. CRC7 protects commands/responses/CSD/CID; CRC16 protects data blocks. Illegal commands set error bits and do not change state. Read/write/erase timeout conditions are specified, including read/write busy limits and UHS-II Data Burst busy.

The partnership will use a system-agnostic, evidence-based approach to evaluate and combine plant medicines from every culture, with Research Needs validating protocols. In 2018, it plans clinical trials and observational studies for HPV, Herpes, Trigeminal Neuralgia, Vertigo, Tinnitus, and Cataract. Biogetica combines nutraceuticals, herbs, and resonance homeopathies.

The Biorepository and Integrative Genomics (BIG) Initiative analyzed 13,152 genomes from a diverse Mid-South population, including underrepresented groups. It found significant genetic diversity, with 50% of participants inferred to have non-European or admixed ancestry; ancestry is geographically stratified, with African ancestry more common in urban areas and European ancestry in suburban regions. Novel variants are ancestry-specific and enriched for functional or clinical relevance. Disease prevalence linked ancestry and environmental factors, showing higher odds ratios for asthma and obesity in minority groups, particularly in urban areas. Discrepancies were observed between self-reported race and genetic ancestry, including related individuals self-identifying in different racial categories, underscoring limitations of race as a biomedical variable. BIG integrates genomics education and community engagement, and future goals include cohort expansion and enhanced genomic analysis for equitable healthcare outcomes.

SpaceX’s Falcon Heavy rocket has a target launch date of Feb. 6 at 1:30 p.m. EST, with Feb. 7 as a backup; longer delays could mean indefinite postponement because federal funding expires Feb. 8 and SpaceX cannot launch during a government shutdown on government property. SpaceX plans to land all three first stages. The launch follows a successful hold-down engine test and has an FAA license. Musk is managing expectations, saying the rocket might not reach orbit and he would consider it a win if the launch pad is not destroyed.

The passage presents a PRISMA-guided systematic review of empirical literature on large language models in education, focusing on documented applications and risks. It addresses four research questions about frequently examined educational applications, assessment methods, risks, and mitigation strategies. The review screened 3,453 records and included 70 papers from 2023–2025. It organizes applications into operational effectiveness, personalized applications, and interactive learning tools. Risks are grouped as inherent technical, pedagogical, and societal, including toxic content, misinformation, bias amplification, hallucinations, privacy violations, cognitive risks, memory erosion, academic integrity, AI divide, data colonialism, environmental harm, and policy/regulatory gaps. The review reports risk frequencies by application and proposes mitigation strategies for educators, developers, students, and governments. It introduces an LLM-Risk Adapted Learning Model, adapted from Self-Regulated Learning, with Interaction, Monitoring, and Outcome stages, to map how risks emerge and compound during LLM-mediated learning. It concludes that LLMs offer educational applications but raise technical, pedagogical, and societal risks, requiring interdisciplinary, human-centred, context-sensitive implementation. Limitations include possible exclusion of recent developments, English-language focus, and mostly short-term evidence.

A commodity trading advisor (CTA) is an individual or organization that advises on or manages trades in futures contracts, commodity options, retail off-exchange forex contracts, or swaps, or a fund using a managed futures strategy. CTAs can manage client accounts or CTA funds, invest across global sectors, and charge management and incentive fees, with registration required with the CFTC and NFA. Many CTAs use systematic models, and trend following is predominant. CTAs manage about $350bn. CTA funds differ from hedge funds because CTAs are limited to futures, options, and swaps. Strategies may include momentum and multi-asset trading. An example is a 200-day moving average strategy on the S&P 500. The passage emphasizes many uncorrelated CTA strategies and correlation as much as performance. Risks include losses, volatility, and unreliable data; limitations include capital, market knowledge, and complexity.

The passage argues that internal incentives—military support, economic demands, and Andropov’s political competition with Chernenko and Soviet intellectuals—may make an arms-control agreement in his interest. It advises focusing on arms control, especially the INF talks, with START later. It recommends a private channel because Andropov prefers secrecy and because U.S. bureaucratic and ideological opposition could leak or undermine negotiations. The first overture should be a short letter recognizing possible renewed confrontation, common interest in peace, and serious interest in reducing nuclear arms, inviting a reply through the same channel.

Partial differential equation models often rely on unknown or approximate initial conditions, causing error; data assimilation estimates the initial state from sparse observations. The variational method 4D-Var minimizes discrepancy between model simulations and observations. Its gradient-based optimization can use Hessian information, but direct Hessian computation is expensive. This study leverages Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs) to improve 4D-Var efficiency and accuracy, reinterpreting FNO through meta-learning and training it to model the inverse Hessian operator across 4D-Var problems. The FNO serves as a surrogate inverse Hessian to solve the optimal initial-state equation in one step, mapping f, computed from observations via the adjoint, to u0. The 4D-Var loss, gradient, Hessian, and incremental 4D-Var extension are presented, and the FNO is trained on 5,400 points. Experiments use a linear advection equation on a periodic domain with specified parameters, observation configurations, and SOAR background error covariance. Results show standalone FNO is generally less accurate than CG, but FNO-CG improves accuracy and efficiency, reducing average relative error by 62% and iteration count by 17%, especially for ill-conditioned problems. The conclusion states FNOs can approximate operators beyond PDE solvers, and future work will extend the approach to nonlinear PDEs, including chaotic systems such as the Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation.

The passage states that soccer coaches should use contingency planning to avoid reacting when something goes wrong. It recommends answering “what if” questions, and for applicable items, developing answers collegially among coaches, players, and/or parents, documenting them, and communicating them as a contingency plan. The questions cover communications, players/practices, pre-game, within-game, post-practice/post-game, and extended or total absence. Topics include communication processes, backups, cancellations, field locations, player absences, injuries, allergies, eligibility, fees, disruptive players, problem parents, cuts, field conditions, equipment, uniforms, medical forms, referees, weather, ejections, transportation, and succession planning. The passage also advises creating checklists, delegating, recognizing that some things cannot be controlled or anticipated, instilling contingency planning in assistants, players, and parents, and teaching players to be prepared for contingencies.

A compilation of Oct. 25, 2001 news items reports on Enron’s financial and credit troubles. BusinessWeek said Enron’s failure to extend its energy-trading model to other commodities was costly; it recorded a $1.01 billion charge covering broadband and water trading and the unraveling of limited partnerships overseen by CFO Andrew Fastow, resulting in a $618 million third-quarter loss versus a $292 million year-earlier profit; without the charge, profit would have been $393 million. S&P affirmed Enron’s ratings but changed its long-term outlook to negative because the drop in market capitalization hurt financial flexibility; it saw no liquidity threat, steady core trading, no risk-management lapses, and potential credit benefits from management changes. Dow Jones, Reuters, and Bloomberg reported that trading partners were concerned but mostly made no credit-policy changes, Enron handled about 25% of U.S. power and gas trading, and EnronOnline remained active. Enron’s shares fell, credit was on watch by Moody’s and Fitch, and some debt traded like junk. Enron replaced Fastow with Jeff McMahon; Kenneth Lay resigned from i2’s board after reassuming Enron’s CEO role. Enron cited $3.35–$3.4 billion credit lines, sought a $750 million loan, had $1.85 billion in commercial paper, and faced $3.3 billion in potential affiliate liabilities. Other items discussed SEC inquiries, shareholder lawsuits, analyst ratings, acquisition speculation, bond-information access for average investors, and broader market activity.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS DAQ system with 2-lane/4-lane SDR and DDR data interfaces. Its 20-bit conversion result is output MSB first in a 24-bit packet with the last six bits zero. It includes source-synchronous DCLKOUT/FCLKOUT, a data randomizer, simple and moving averaging, test patterns, reset/power-down/initialization, speed-boost mode, SPI register access with bank selection and daisy-chain, and ATE application information.

Low volatility stock strategy involves investing in stocks with lower volatility or price fluctuation than the overall market. These stocks are often considered less risky, may offer more consistent returns, and may have lower returns than higher-volatility stocks depending on the time horizon. Low volatility stocks generally have a beta below 1 and can come from sectors such as consumer staples, utilities, and healthcare. Implementation can include low volatility ETFs or mutual funds, selecting stocks using historical data and analysis, diversifying across sectors, and reviewing or rebalancing the portfolio. Backtesting evaluates past performance but only roughly estimates future results. The passage also discusses benefits, risks, return-enhancement strategies, and limitations, noting that low volatility strategies can have long periods of underperformance and may not suit all investors. Cited research includes Kenneth French’s findings on volatile stocks and low-volatility deciles, Baker, Bradley, and Taliaferro on the low beta anomaly, Nardin Baker and Robert Haugen on international markets, and Buffett/Berkshire research on leverage and cheap, safe, quality stocks. It states past performance does not guarantee future results.

The passage features comments on a retiring Swedish hockey player praised as a role model, professional, and possibly Sweden’s best, though underappreciated. His four Stanley Cups, seven Norris trophies, and two decades of consistent, durable play are cited. Another speaker says he feels physically fine and hopes for a chance to play.

A TeamLease survey on job loss risk across nine cities found Delhi has the highest risk, followed by Bengaluru and Hyderabad, while Pune has the lowest. Industrial manufacturing and allied sectors have the highest industry risk; healthcare and telecom rank lowest.

David Wybron, headteacher at Lord Williams’s School in Thame, is appealing to the Government to change the exam system. He says state school students face greater examination pressures than independent school peers under the new GCSEs and questions league table penalties, declining further study in some subjects, and exam content. He also cites teacher recruitment difficulties, immigration controls hindering overseas appointments, and funding challenges, including students receiving over £1,000 less per head than those in well-funded authorities before deprivation funding. He calls for fairness, a rethink of exam content and structures, an option to pursue IGCSEs without league table penalties, expanded shortage occupation status for teachers, and honesty on recruitment and funding.

The Triple RSI trading strategy is a modified RSI strategy using four key variables, three based on RSI. It focuses on mean reversion, with rules involving RSI readings, the 200-day moving average, and buy/sell signals. Backtesting on SPY since 1993 produced 83 trades, an average 1.4% gain per trade, a 90% win rate, and a profit factor of 5. It can complement a long-term buy-and-hold portfolio and potentially use small leverage in a margin account.
Naughty Dog spotlighted Uncharted: The Lost Legacy over The Last of Us Part 2 at E3 2017. It features Chloe Frazer and Nadine Ross; development began weeks after Uncharted 4.

This document is an AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update. It states that issue numbers may not be sequential because omitted issues were resolved. Covered areas include PIT operation, GLIU/debug port, PIC/XPIC interrupts, DMA rotation and software DMA, thermal alarm and standby recovery, PMC sleep clock controls, GLIU error detection, UART access during DMA, LPC transactions, 8237 DMA, PCI I/O addressing, USB over-voltage protection, LBAR settings, automatic clock gating, ATAC/IDE UDMA operations, ACPI PM registers, KEL emulation, PCI back-to-back reads, PIC polling mode, UART clock gating, PCI timing, SSMI generation, CD-ROM UDMA/PIO behavior, S3 wake events, RTC CMOS RAM accesses, LPC DMA blocking, USB clock gating, KEL AuxOutputFull behavior, UDMA timing, PRD alignment, LPC aborts, SMB NEGACK status, GLPCI retry counter, GPIO suspend writes, SMBus hold time, LOWBAT_FLAG, and Sleep_X/Sleep_Y deassertion. Defensive tackles play a critical role in stopping the run and pressuring quarterbacks. They often face double teams, free up second- and third-level defenders, and are less likely to have one-on-one pass-rush matchups; their sacks are well earned. They need strength, agility, recognition, and toughness, with a thick build around 6’2–6’4 and 300–335 pounds. The position has also been called nose tackle or nose guard. Aaron Donald and Joe Greene are cited as among the best. Their upfront work helps defenses succeed in run and pass coverage.

Material properties are determined by quantum mechanical equations, often approximated by DFT, whose high cost limits large atomic systems. ML force fields trained on DFT data serve as scalable surrogates, and their performance depends on atomic representations. Early hand-engineered descriptors were interpretable but biased and poorly transferable. Graph Neural Networks became mainstream for crystals, evolving from pairwise local interactions to angular embeddings and equivariant/invariant GNNs. However, crystals are infinite 3D systems, and current real-space encoders often fail to capture long-term interactions, mapping distinct structures to the same representation. Diffraction-space encoding is presented as a unique alternative, but traditional diffraction relies on fixed atomic form factors and cannot distinguish same-element atoms in different local environments. The work introduces PRDNet, a learned pseudo-particle representation and multimodal graph-and-diffraction framework invariant to rotations, reflections, and translations. Evaluations on Materials Project, JARVIS-DFT, and MatBench demonstrate state-of-the-art crystal property prediction. Related work discusses limitations of multi-edge graphs, angular embeddings, and periodic vector-based systems. Preliminaries define crystal structures, diffraction, pseudo-particles, and the prediction problem; the method motivates learned pseudo-particles over fixed X-ray form factors.

Real-time ray tracing is computationally expensive; NVIDIA created DLSS, powered by Tensor Cores, to use a deep neural network and multiple frames to construct a high-quality image comparable to native resolution with higher performance. Ampere enhances DLSS with third-generation Tensor Cores and a 9x Super Resolution scaling factor, making 8K gaming at 60 fps feasible for ray-traced games; the RTX 3090 can deliver 60 fps at 8K with DLSS.

GA10x uses GDDR6X, developed with Micron, featuring PAM4 signaling, MTA encoding, up to 19.5 Gbps, up to 936 GB/sec, over 52% improvement over TU102, and up to 64% more bandwidth than previous GPU generations; it includes pseudo-independent memory channels and aids BVH ray traversal. RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and decompression with Microsoft DirectStorage, accelerating I/O up to 100x versus hard drives and traditional APIs, offloading CPU work, improving frame rates and near-instant loading, and benefiting games and professional workloads.

The A40 data center GPU is based on GA10x Ampere with second-generation RT Cores and third-generation Tensor Cores, up to 2X FP32, 2X ray-tracing, and 5X (10X with Sparsity) AI throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000, PCIe Gen4, 48GB scalable to 96GB via NVLink, display outputs, vGPU, Quadro Sync, and EGX compatibility.

Ampere GPUs support 4K 120Hz and 8K 60Hz displays, DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a, HDMI 2.1, and HDCP 2.3/1.x. Fifth-generation NVDEC supports hardware decoding of MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1; GA10x is first to provide AV1 hardware decode. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding. Ampere offers up to 2x performance improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI; second-generation RT Core doubles ray/triangle intersection and supports motion blur and concurrent operations; third-generation Tensor Core implements structural sparsity. RTX A6000 includes GA102, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 48GB GDDR6, NVLink scaling to 96GB, and professional certifications. EDR on GDDR6X detects and replays memory transmission errors, with plateauing performance indicating overclock limits. GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102, 24GB GDDR6X, 82 SMs, and 10,496 CUDA Cores; RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6.

China's official manufacturing PMI rose to 51.9 in May from 51.4 in April, the fastest in eight months and above 50 for the 22nd straight month, beating a Reuters forecast of 51.3. Production expanded at a six-month high, while new orders reached an eight-month high and export orders improved. Some economists doubted the strength would last, citing temporary pollution-control easing, deleveraging, and trade tensions. Small firms contracted, and 40.1% of manufacturers raised funding concerns. The non-manufacturing PMI rose to 54.9, construction fell to 60.1, and the composite PMI rose to 54.6. Economists expect growth to slow to 6.5% this year from 6.9% in 2017.

Intel shares rose 3% Thursday, with monthly gains over 50%. The surge pushed the stock past $37 and the U.S. government’s stake to roughly $16 billion; the Trump administration negotiated an $8.9 billion August investment.

In a farewell address, Truman says Eisenhower will be inaugurated and he will return to Independence, Missouri, as a private citizen, praising the peaceful transfer of power. He recounts his presidency, including his 1945 succession after Roosevelt’s death, decisions on the United Nations, Germany’s surrender, the atomic bomb, postwar reconversion, and the cold war. He cites actions regarding Iran, Greece and Turkey, the Marshall Plan, Berlin airlift, NATO, and Korea. He urges support for the new President regardless of politics, calls atomic war unthinkable, and predicts eventual change in the Soviet world. He notes U.S. prosperity and civil rights progress, says he leaves without regret, and thanks the people for their support.

Large language model-driven summarization can reshape source incentives, and LLMs are susceptible to hallucinations, adversarial manipulation, and conflicting claims. The passage proposes Truthful Text Summarization (TTS), an incentive-aligned pipeline that decomposes documents into atomic claims, uses leave-one-out claim generation so sources cannot influence their evaluation, applies multi-task peer-prediction scoring that rewards informative corroboration, and filters low-scoring sources before re-summarization. It provides theoretical guarantees that truthful reporting maximizes expected score, including informed and strong truthfulness with finite-sample bounds. Experiments on NQ and ClashEval show TTS improves factuality and robustness against adversarial and coordinated uninformative content compared with baselines, while truthful reporting maximizes source score.

Lilly Nguyen and Phil De Carlos married in the chapel at Texas Children’s Hospital. Their son Lucas was born at 24 weeks in late October, weighing 1 lb. 12 oz.; he now weighs 4 lbs. 4 oz. De Carlos proposed in Lucas’s NICU room on December 15, and the couple married New Year’s Day to involve their son.

William Eckels became involved with The Opportunity Project (TOP) after stopping for pizza and hearing about a Parent Cafe. TOP is a nonprofit early education program for children ages 1 to 5 in high-poverty areas of Wichita and Derby. A study published in the Journal of Research in Childhood Education found TOP graduates outperformed comparable students who had not attended TOP in academics, social skills, and attendance through eighth grade, and were more likely to read at grade level. TOP uses a Reggio Emilia-inspired philosophy and offers scholarships funded by grants, donors, subsidies, and other sources. Parents sign an attendance contract, and TOP connects families to resources and college partnerships. Executive director Cornelia Stevens says early education is key to addressing poverty. Eckels says TOP taught him as well as his son, and he is considering returning to school for an education degree.

MIT and the Carnegie Institution for Science released a public dataset of nearly 61,000 measurements of more than 1,600 nearby stars, gathered over 20 years by the W.M. Keck Observatory, plus open-source software and an online tutorial. Researchers hope the public will help hunt exoplanets; over 100 potential exoplanets have already been detected.

Turing GPUs add enhanced NVENC with H.265/HEVC 8K at 30 fps, up to 25% bitrate savings for HEVC and 15% for H.264, and NVDEC support for HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing encoding improves quality over Pascal and software encoders, with lower CPU utilization and 4K streaming capability. Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink, delivering power, display, and data over one USB-C connector for VR headsets. Turing TU102/TU104 use NVLink for SLI; TU102 has two x8 second-generation NVLink links, TU104 has one, each 25 GB/s per direction, and only two-way SLI is supported. Turing introduces RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 for real-time ray tracing with NVIDIA RTX, enabling physically correct reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. Hybrid rendering combines ray tracing and rasterization. NGX uses Tensor Cores for AI graphics only on Turing and includes DLSS, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. TU104 has six GPCs, 48 SMs, 256-bit memory, 13.6 billion transistors, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one x8 NVLink. TU106 has three GPCs, 36 SMs, 256-bit memory, 10.8 billion transistors, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, and no NVLink or SLI. Tesla T4 uses TU104 with five GPCs, 40 SMs, 2560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, 256-bit interface, and 320 GB/s. RTX-OPS derates Tensor operations 20%, CUDA cores 80%, RT cores 40%, and INT32 pipes 28%. Ray tracing casts rays from the camera through pixels, uses BVH traversal and denoising, and RT Cores accelerate BVH and ray/triangle intersection. Ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections address limitations of shadow maps, SSAO, and screen-space reflections.

The Trump administration began laying off federal workers on Friday, the 10th day of the government shutdown. OMB Director Russell Vought said “RIFs have begun,” and Trump said the number would be “a lot” and “Democrat-oriented.” The permanent cuts differ from furloughs. Smith Tower, a 103-year-old Seattle landmark, is automating its manually operated elevators. Unico Properties, which purchased the building in 2015, began modernization in June; Seattle’s Landmarks Preservation Board approved alterations on Aug. 16 to improve safety, reliability, and accessibility while respecting the building’s history. Operators will no longer be required as of mid-2018, though at least one will remain. Hamilton Beale, an operator for 18 years, plans to return to Virginia next May. The building opened in 1914 with eight Otis elevators and was once the tallest west of the Mississippi River.

The appellate court affirmed a judgment for Catharine Heilmann against Diedrick Grafing’s executrices. Grafing had deposited $2,000 in the East River Savings Institution in his name in trust for Heilmann, and $3,000 similarly in the Metropolitan Savings Bank. He retained the bank books and drew interest during his life. The court held the deposits created a valid trust, not a gift or testamentary disposition; retaining the books and drawing interest was not inconsistent with intent to create a trust. Payment of part of the principal to Heilmann was not evidence of a loan. If Heilmann promised to pay others, those parties had to seek their own remedies. Judgment affirmed with costs.

A fake Michael Flynn Twitter account fooled House Democrats Nancy Pelosi and Elijah Cummings, who cited its tweets about Flynn being a scapegoat while criticizing Republican investigations. Both later acknowledged the mistake, and The New York Times also corrected a story that cited the unverified account.

The passage explains the 123 pattern reversal strategy, a three-swing price formation with three swing points that indicates a potential trend reversal. A bearish 123 pattern occurs in an uptrend when price fails to make a higher high and then breaks below the previous low; a bullish 123 pattern occurs in a downtrend when price fails to make a lower low and then breaks above the previous high. A 123 bottom is the bullish pattern. Trading rules include entry after the breakout of point 2, stop loss below point 3 for bullish setups or above point 3 for bearish setups, and a profit target measured from the pattern. It can be used in stocks, forex, commodities, and Bitcoin. Backtests on GLD showed a profit factor of 2.22 for a 20-day bullish exit, while bearish reversal performance was weaker. The strategy is subjective and may be improved.

The passage describes techniques for cooperative monitoring networks that detect events at monitoring systems, evaluate them against rules, and form networks among nearby monitoring systems to share alerts and data and coordinate monitoring. It details system components such as monitoring control units, sensors, cameras, user devices, monitoring application servers, and central alarm station servers. Cooperative networks may be activated or modified based on proximity, vacancy, user preferences, and event type, and can support tracking intruders, medical emergencies, personal security, and neighborhood-wide malfunctions using cascading notifications, rule sets, and user interfaces. Security researchers report that Hajime, a rival IoT malware to Mirai, is spreading and has created a botnet estimated at about 100,000 devices. Like Mirai, it scans for poorly secured IoT devices and compromises them using username/password attempts and a malicious program. Unlike Mirai, Hajime uses a peer-to-peer network based on BitTorrent protocols instead of a command-and-control server, making it more decentralized and harder to block. It has not been observed launching DDoS attacks, and its purpose is unknown; possibilities include cybercrime, research, or disrupting Mirai. Hajime appears more widespread than Mirai but infects a smaller pool of ARM-based devices, while Mirai strains target more platforms. Researchers say patching vulnerable devices is needed, but many remain unpatched, so both malware likely persist.

OpenAI reached a $500 billion valuation after a secondary share sale in which current and former employees sold about $6.6 billion in stock. The sale, authorized for up to $10 billion, drew investors including SoftBank, Thrive Capital, Dragoneer Investment Group, MGX, and T. Rowe Price. The valuation rose from around $300 billion earlier in the year, supported by $4.3 billion in first-half 2025 revenue, already more than 15% above full-year 2024 revenue. The milestone strengthens OpenAI’s position among private technology firms and pressures AI rivals, while providing employee liquidity. Questions remain about sustaining growth, profitability, regulation, governance, and market concentration.

The UCLA High Post Rub offense was instrumental to UCLA NCAA championship teams under John Wooden and is used at all levels, including the NBA. It is based on sound principles and court spacing, uses inside and outside attack, and can suit teams without a bona fide low post player by using a post player with passing and shooting skills and a point guard able to post up. It features quick reversal and simultaneous down screens. The 1-4 set is favored against pressure defenses; positions can interchange, especially 4 and 5 and 2 and 3, and it can be initiated on either side. The basic option has O1 pass to O3 and rub off O5’s high post screen; O3 looks to feed O1 for a layup or post-up, or reverses to O5. The passage also covers reads and counters against trailing, denying, going behind, show-and-recover, and switching defenders, plus back screen options, post isolation, low post reads, ball reversal down screens, weakside low post split, automatic counters against overplay, teaching and implementation, game strategy, and defending the offense.

The lecture continues NPV applications to capital budgeting and project financing. It notes adjusted present value (APV) as a later refinement that adjusts for taxes, project interactions, strategic alternatives, and optionality, while NPV remains the current criterion. It discusses three alternatives to NPV: payback period, discounted payback, internal rate of return (IRR), and profitability index. NPV is always recommended for capital budgeting.

Payback period is the minimum time for future cash flows to exceed the initial investment. It is short-sighted, ignores scale, risk, and cash flows after payback, though it can reflect uncertainty, liquidity, or career risk. Discounted payback uses discounted cash flows but still ignores post-payback cash flows. Profitability index is gross present value divided by initial investment; above 1 accept, below 1 reject, but it ignores scale. IRR is the break-even rate or bond yield to maturity; it may not exist, may have multiple real solutions, gives incorrect rankings for loans, and ignores scale. It is used in bonds and private equity. A survey shows payback is popular, IRR is used, and NPV has gained ground. Advanced topics include APV, competitive response, and capital rationing.

The lecture concludes that capital budgeting should use NPV or APV, take positive NPV projects, choose the highest NPV among mutually exclusive projects, use after-tax cash flows, use CAPM for discount rates, consider changing risk, and be aware of other alternatives. It then begins efficient markets, arguing market prices aggregate information, illustrated by the Challenger crash: Morton Thiokol’s stock fell within minutes, while a commission took about six months to identify the O-ring. The next lecture will discuss when markets fail.

The speaker hopes the heat in Dallas won’t be a factor if the team has depth. A loss at this point is a lost opportunity, but the team must not get too high or low, correct mistakes, and improve. This study used multi-omics data from 116 mother-child pairs in the VDAART cohort to assess associations between maternal and child gut microbiomes and children’s neurodevelopment measured by ASQ at years one, two, and three. The maternal gut microbiome was more relevant to first-year neurodevelopment than the infant (months 3–6) or year-one child microbiome. The predictive power of maternal and infant gut microbiomes diminished for year-two neurodevelopment, and neither maternal nor child microbiome had predictive power for year-three neurodevelopment. Shared taxa were found, but the same taxa in maternal and infant gut microbiota did not necessarily play the same role; Fusobacteriia and Fusobacteriota showed divergent associations. The study notes limitations including limited sample size and low Fusobacteriia abundance.

Observations show 14 of 16 satellite galaxies orbiting Centaurus A move in a common plane, unlike the random directions predicted by the lambda cold dark matter model. Such preferentially oriented orbits have been seen around the Milky Way and Andromeda but are the first found outside the Local Group. Study author Marcel Pawlowski says this raises questions about the validity of certain cosmological models and may require alternative explanations, while other astrophysicists argue there is not enough evidence to abandon the standard model, calling the finding a possible statistical fluke or explainable by other factors. Scientists say more research, including observations of more distant galaxies, is needed.

The passage describes offensive corner kick options in soccer. It states all offensive corner kicks are planned restarts containing a designed set play, a designated target area, target player, or target receiver, and a proper service kick by a designated corner taker; other players may create misdirection or influence defenders away from the target. Corner kicks are characterized by target area. Common types listed are Far Post, Near Post, Medium, Top-of-the-Arc, Short, Skip Header, and Direct Score, also called Olympico. The passage also discusses a Floated-ball Corner as a tactical option. Coaches may select plays based on player abilities, choose takers and receivers based on required service and heading ability, teach all types and positions, and practice progressively with attackers and defenders. Coaching tips include addressing wind, goalkeeper ability, referee readiness, signals, offside, timing runs, rebounds, clearances, and counterattacks.

Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease in which protective cartilage wears down and underlying bone changes due to an imbalance in cartilage catabolism. It affects joints such as hands, knees, hips, and/or spine. According to WHO, 9.6% of men and 18% of women aged 60+ are estimated to have symptomatic OA worldwide. OA development is believed to begin with pericellular matrix alteration, extracellular matrix softening, increased chondrocyte mechanical stress, and increased secretion of proteolytic enzymes degrading type II collagen and proteoglycans, eventually causing macroscopic cartilage degradation. OA also involves low-grade joint inflammation. Diagnosis is limited to radiographic evaluation, clinical examination, and signs/symptoms; there are no approved molecular diagnostics. The study investigates lubricin glycoforms in synovial fluid (SF) and plasma in relation to OA and develops and validates a Fluorescent Immuno-Lectin Assay (FILA). Five lectins—MGL, SNA, MAA, PNA, and Gal-3—were attached to fluorescent nanoparticles to measure glycoepitopes on captured lubricin. FILA was validated using spike-and-recovery, dilution-recovery, and inter-/intra-plate variation and benchmarked against LC-SRM for lubricin glycans from OA SF. FILA showed SF lubricin glycoform levels 1–3 orders of magnitude higher than plasma, and plasma lubricin glycosylation differed from SF, with higher ratios of MAA, PNA, SNA, and Gal-3 to MGL in plasma. In plasma from OA patients and controls, MAA, Gal-3, PNA, and MGL glycoforms were not significantly different; SNA glycoform levels and the SNA/MGL ratio were decreased in OA. BMI positively correlated with Gal-3, MAA, and SNA, while age negatively correlated with MAA and SNA and positively with MGL. The study concludes that plasma and SF lubricin differ in glycosylation, OA-related SF glycosylation changes have limited impact on plasma lubricin, only SNA-detected glycoforms were altered in OA plasma, and plasma lubricin glycosylation is altered by age and increased BMI/metabolic syndrome.

This longitudinal household study enrolled adults aged 60 or older, without younger household residents, over two autumn/winter seasons to evaluate within-household pneumococcal transmission and acquisition risks among community-dwelling older adults. Saliva samples were collected every 2 weeks for six visits and tested for pneumococcus primarily by piaB qPCR, with serotyping, respiratory virus testing, and urine antigen detection. Overall, 52/1088 samples (4.8%) were piaB-positive, and 27/121 individuals (22.3%) were colonized at least once. Carriage prevalence was higher among those reporting contact with children, especially younger children, and higher with daily or frequent contact. Mean colonization duration was 17.7 days, and average time to acquisition was 358 days. Recent contact with children aged under 10 was associated with increased acquisition. No clear evidence of adult-adult transmission was found; both household members were rarely carriers. Serotyping was limited by incomplete coverage and non-pneumococcal Streptococci confounding. Urine antigen tests were negative. The study concludes that adult PCV immunization may directly protect adults exposed to children but may not greatly affect onward transmission to other adults; adult-to-child transmission was not evaluated.

The facility terminates on June 10, 2020, with no amounts outstanding on the Closing Date. Availability is based on borrowing base certifications.
