The Stack Zone Offense is a prolific zone offense based on the overload principle. It is simple to teach and master, uses precise spacing and movement, creates matchup and adjustment problems, assigns specific player roles, and can flop sides to attack the weakside. It has multiple entries and Crunch Time specials, and offensive rebounding is a major strength, with missed shots often becoming put-back opportunities. Mike Frink was instrumental in introducing this continuity. Roles include point guard as quarterback/leader, shooting guard as best three-point shooter, small forward as active front-line/corner shooter, power forward and post operating in low/high post and rebounding. The offense includes basic overload reads, pass-and-cut action, high post roll, side post feed and weakside post attack reads, automatic skip pass reads, ball reversal, and continuity left repeat. Optional entries include Flop, Exchange, Triple Stack, Dribble Entry, Weakside Flop Attack, and Post Roll; Triple Stack is a contribution by Tom Newell. Crunch Time specials include Vegas, Back, and Cat, along with pass-out-of-trap, post-roll, and back-cut rules.

Set pieces in soccer restart play after a foul or infraction. Free kicks must follow Law 13 and account for distance and angle to goal. The referee places the ball where the infraction occurred; the non-offending team restarts, defenders must stand at least 10 yards away, and the ball is in play once touched by an offensive player and visibly moves. The original kicker may not touch it again immediately. Free kicks are direct, allowing a goal without another touch, or indirect, requiring a touch by another player before scoring. Defensive-half free kicks are usually short passes; offensive-third free kicks become set pieces. Defenses typically build a wall, so offensive designs aim to defeat the wall with minimal complexity and produce an effective shot. Designs depend on proximity, direct/indirect status, and player skill. The passage lists five near locations and three far locations, plus features such as direct shots, simple touches, crosses, stepovers, misdirection, screening, committee setups, single or two passes, chips, decoys, ghosting, crashing, and rebounds. Players must understand roles, direct/indirect status, and referee readiness; a dead-ball specialist may be used, and a team may ask for 10 yards. Free kicks may be ceremonial or quick. Rare indirect free kicks inside 10 yards are also discussed. Practice includes running plays without defenders, then with mannequins, stationary defenders, and live defenders. Coaching tips include contingencies, scouting, incorporating the indirect touch, and simplicity.

In Hunter and Others v. Bales, Bales, as assignee of Thompson, sought specific performance of a land sale contract. In a specific performance suit, the plaintiff may offer in the complaint to bring purchase money into court when liquidated. After tender and refusal, the vendee is not chargeable with interest unless the vendor proves the money was used. The judgment was affirmed.

This study compared nasopharyngeal samples (n = 29) from individuals with suspected acute upper respiratory infection using a Fast Track Diagnostic Respiratory Pathogens 33 PCR panel and a hybridization capture-based mNGS workflow, then phenotypically classified detected microorganisms. PCR detected 28/29 samples positive and identified 15 etiological agents; mNGS identified 44 microorganisms, including 29 additional microorganisms beyond the PCR panel, and detected co-infections in 26/29 samples. Concordance for shared targets was 98.33% PPA and 100% NPA. The authors conclude the targeted hybridization-capture-based mNGS workflow may supplement current syndromic tests and aid phenotypic characterization of respiratory (co)infections and trafficking potential, though further investigations are needed.

This paper introduces an architecture for digitally structured information exchange between industrial enterprises, focusing on the lifecycle domain and especially technical information. It states that current communication is largely manual, standards do not cover all information types, no digital medium scales well for an arbitrarily large ecosystem, and spreadsheets and manual input are used instead. The proposed architecture uses an open consortium to agree on common business practices and information structures, with communication via mediators that act as multi-sided platforms. Each business party integrates through an adapter, enabling scalability via a single integration. The paper presents a prototype that delivers equipment information from suppliers to plant operators for maintenance and renewal cases using import/export applications, spreadsheets, XML mappings, and a web application platform. Experiments successfully delivered equipment information. Limitations include the absence of an open consortium, open API specifications, actual adapters, and a mediator network; the prototype has a single mediator and limited support for information types and business processes. The paper concludes that the architecture can improve information management efficiency and calls for future work to form the consortium, extend the prototype, and broaden scope to financing, logistics, manufacturing, and marine industry.

In Asa B. Meech and others v. City of Buffalo, plaintiffs sought to restrain collection of a second sewer assessment. The common council first assessed $1,058.63 and contracted with Randolph to construct the sewer for that amount. After Randolph encountered unexpected quicksand and stopped work, the council increased the contract price by $588.13 and directed an additional assessment on benefited real estate. The special term held the second assessment illegal, but the general term reversed. The Court held the supplementary assessment was authorized by the city charter as a “further assessment” where the first assessment proved insufficient, and that the council could increase the contract price absent charter prohibition. Judgment affirmed.

This case study examined first-year physical education and sports teaching program students’ experiences in a 14-week movement education course supported by peer mentoring. Participants were three peer mentors, 25 first-year peer learners, and the course lecturer. Peer mentors created storytelling content by combining known series, cartoons, or digital game narratives with fundamental movement skills. Pre-lesson information and reminders were shared through Instagram and Discord; during lessons, task cards with story fiction were used and monitored by peer mentors; after lessons, reels and reflections were shared, and peer mentors and the lecturer held weekly meetings. In the final four weeks, peer learner groups taught their own storytelling designs with peer mentor feedback. Data included field notes, reflection notes, weekly meetings, audio recordings, social media messages, weekly short films, peer feedback, and online reflections, analyzed by inductive continuous comparison. Three themes emerged: peer learners allowed group members who made an effort to continue and excluded those who did not, while peer mentors divided responsibilities to complete tasks; peer mentors and peer learners produced storytelling content, making learning more permanent and increasing teacher awareness; and real-life narrative content helped connect learning to daily life. The study reports that peer mentors developed accountability and responsibility, while peer learners observed teaching and later taught, using collaboration, teamwork, and technology. Storytelling and gamification increased interest, permanence, self-evaluation, and awareness of innovative teaching. The passage concludes that peer mentoring provided real field experience and a bridge between students and teaching staff, and recommends integrating and sustaining peer mentoring and storytelling in undergraduate teacher education and conducting long-term studies.

Version 2 introduces advertisement of hypervisor-supported features through a FEATURES bitmap, limited to 52 bits so it can be returned via the GHCB MSR protocol before a GHCB is established. Supported features include base SEV-SNP, SEV-SNP guest AP VMSA creation, Restricted Injection, Restricted Injection Timer, APIC ID list, running a vCPU at different VMPL levels, SNP Run VMPL MSR protocol, Page State Change for SEV-ES, trusted IO devices (TDISP), and unregistering the registered GHCB GPA. The GHCB location is guest-specified, mapped decrypted/shared, saved and restored by hardware in VMCB offset 0xa0, readable and writable through MSR 0xc001_0130, must be 4K aligned, and the hypervisor must not intercept MSR 0xc001_0130. The GHCB MSR protocol uses lower 12 bits for requests/responses; 0x080/0x081 support the feature bitmap, while SEV Information provides protocol version range and SEV page table encryption bit number. CPUID request protocol can obtain CPUID register values before GHCB establishment, but does not support non-zero sub-leafs or function 0x0000_000d. AP reset hold, preferred/register/unregister GHCB GPA, page state change, Run VMPL, and termination requests are described. GHCB GPA registration is required for SEV-SNP; registering automatically unregisters the current GPA, and Multi-VMPL allows per-VMPL registration. Negotiation examples cover SEV-ES and SEV-SNP setup with VMCB, encryption bit, CPUID, SEV Information, GHCB page setup, and registration.

NAE events are non-AE exits handled through #VC and VMGEXIT. The guest inspects the #VC error code, copies required state to the GHCB, sets VALID_BITMAP, and invokes VMGEXIT; the hypervisor returns status/errors in SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2. NAE events include MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV Doorbell Page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, Run VMPL, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, Termination Request, and Unsupported NAE. SNP Guest Request uses shared request/response pages and SNP_GUEST_REQUEST; Extended returns certificates; TIO handles trusted devices and TDISP data. AP Creation supports VMSA-based AP creation/destruction and vCPU hotplug. NMI injection uses NMI Complete; debug registers use DebugVirtualization or DR7 intercept caching. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported. The #HV doorbell page defines PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields, with host APIC emulation and guest atomic acknowledgement/EOI behavior.

The passage presents a PRISMA-compliant systematic review and computational taxonomy of social science research on large language models (LLMs), arguing that LLMs should be studied as social artifacts at the intersection of engineering design and social embedding. From 64,717 records, screening yielded 270 studies, mostly journal articles, preprints, and conference papers concentrated in 2023–2025. Study 1 used Sentence-BERT embeddings, K-means clustering, UMAP visualization, and LDA topic modeling. Internal indices and stability analyses supported a three-cluster taxonomy: LLM as Social Minds, LLM Societies, and LLM–Human Interactions. Study 2 compared this machine-derived structure with an expert taxonomy and reported strong alignment (Macro-F1 = 0.954 ± 0.018; NMI = 0.811; ARI = 0.867). The discussion treats the three blocs as levels of analysis and a measurement model, notes limitations including English-language coverage, a September 2025 cut-off, and narrative rather than pooled synthesis, and proposes an agenda focused on robust measurement, institutional design, trust calibration, and auditing socio-technical institutions rather than asking whether LLMs resemble persons.

TMPM is an optional extension to System Encryption, SEV, and SNP for page migration. It copies page content and updates virtual-to-physical mappings, requires IOMMU enablement, and supports tiered memory optimization by moving frequently accessed data to faster memory. TMPM can pause DMA to a page during migration and act as a trusted agent for SNP/SEV guest pages. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO supports concurrent DMA targets and SNP hypervisor pages; PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST supports SNP guest pages and uses a Pre-Migration state. Commands can move up to 128 pages via a Page Migration List with per-page statuses and no order dependence. Performance improves with 16 or more pages and is maximum at 128. Unsupported structures include IOMMU SPA-accessed data, vIOMMU private address space/page tables, pinned buffers, ring buffer, and argument pages. Firmware reload requires no in-flight operations; errors include invalid reload request and version issues. SPAs must be 4K aligned.

Student teachers used “actualising” to integrate LGBTQ+ identities, but found trans identities often excluded due to fear of media debates and proposed guidance. The passage also covers storytelling and counter-stories, LGBTQ+ role models, equality and human rights legislation, international principles, whole-school visibility, behavior management, anti-bullying policies, bystander/upstander training and Pride groups. The message calls attention to a prior December message and asks Congress to provide a substantial reduction in tariff duties on Cuban imports to the United States. It cites Cuba’s Constitution affirming closer international relations with the U.S., President McKinley’s earlier statements on friendly and reciprocal commercial relations, and President Palms’s cable appeal for legislative relief before Cuba is financially ruined. It says reciprocity with Cuba is unique, consistent with the protective system, and could be arranged to prevent benefits from going mainly to American sugar refiners; other tariff schedules are not at issue. Opponents’ fears are compared to earlier opposition to Hawaiian admission, which proved baseless. It argues no American industry will be hurt and many will benefit, and that the growing Cuban market should be controlled by American producers. It cites post-Spanish War events and the prospective Isthmian Canal as increasing U.S. interest in the West Indies and Central America. Noting Cuba is an independent republic with special obligations, it asks special economic concessions for Cuba, arguing help is warranted because Cuba is weak and has received U.S. aid, and that completing this policy is important for the U.S. as a world power.

Magda Enriquez secretly worked for the Sandinistas in Somoza’s Nicaragua. When her husband asked her to choose between him and the Revolution, she said the choice had already been made. Six years later she was a Council of State member representing AMNLAE, divorced, and proud of the new life patterns and her six children. Though she appeared a bourgeois executive, she was a trained soldier, peasant organizer, Sandinista exponent, and mother, including an adopted child. After studying in the U.S., she returned to Nicaragua in 1970 and founded the first school for mentally retarded children; discovering malnutrition caused many cases led her into Managua’s slums. As a Roman Catholic believing in liberation theology, she secretly joined the Sandinistas in 1976 and became a founding member of the women’s association in 1977. After a 1978 land sit-in where poison and delayed treatment killed ten children, she requested military training. Her oldest son later joined the militia under age. She described solidarity and party/neighborhood support during long absences. She said women’s problems remained and the Revolution gave opportunities to solve them, and she helped prepare election procedures.

The passage discusses how likely retirees and FIRE individuals are to go broke, citing low interest rates, sequence of returns, withdrawal rates, and lack of diversification as key risks. It says being dependent on capital for income involves many “ifs” and that without a huge margin of safety, retirees are very likely to go broke. An example describes a couple retiring in January 2000 with $1 million, withdrawing $50,000 yearly adjusted for inflation from a US large-cap fund, who were forced to return to work and ended penniless in 2017 without additional income. The passage discusses the 4% rule by William Bengen, notes FIREs have longer time frames and more risk, and says conservative withdrawal rates, diversification, and moderate spending can help mitigate sequence risk. It concludes that how likely one is to go broke depends on planning, margin of safety, and frugality.

This study examined whether sex and trauma type affect the relationship between self-reported PCL-5 and clinician-administered CAPS-5 PTSD symptom severity scores. One hundred adult participants completed both assessments. CAPS-5 scores did not differ significantly between males and females or between military and civilian trauma. PCL-5 and CAPS-5 scores were significantly correlated overall, but females showed a stronger correlation than males. The odds ratio for PCL-5 predicting CAPS-5 was higher for females than males. Males showed significant deviation from the ideal regression line and a higher proportion of misclassified PTSD cases based on PCL-5 alone compared with females. Civilian trauma was associated with a stronger PCL-5/CAPS-5 correlation than military trauma across all participants and within each sex. The study concluded that sex and trauma type should be considered when assessing PTSD, particularly when using PCL-5 in males and military populations. Limitations included sample size and regional sampling.

This lecture continues continuity: intuitively, if x is sufficiently close to c, f(x) is close to f(c). It proves a theorem relating continuity at c to limits and sequences: if c is not a cluster point of the domain, every function is continuous at c; if c is a cluster point, f is continuous at c iff lim x→c f(x)=f(c), iff for every sequence xₙ in the domain converging to c, f(xₙ) converges to f(c). It proves these parts, including the sequence-contrapositive argument. It then shows sine and cosine are continuous: sine directly by epsilon-delta using trigonometric identities and bounds; cosine via the sequence characterization and cos x = sin(x+π/2). It gives an example of a function defined by rational/irrational values that is discontinuous at every real number, using density of rationals and irrationals and the sequence characterization. It states that if f and g are continuous at c, then f+g, fg, and f/g (where g(x)≠0) are continuous at c, and that composition of continuous functions is continuous. Consequences include continuity of xⁿ, polynomials, and functions such as 1/(3+sin⁴x). It announces next topics: min/max theorems for continuous functions on closed bounded intervals and the intermediate value theorem.

Cover 3 is a 4-under, 3-deep zone defense common at all levels, used by coaches such as Nick Saban and Pete Carroll. Three deep defenders cover deep thirds: cornerbacks take outside thirds and the free safety covers the deep middle. Four underneath defenders cover Hook, Curl, and Flat zones on the strong and weak sides. It adds a deep defensive back and can place an extra safety near the line to help stop the run. Strengths include balanced coverage against deep and intermediate routes and against both run and pass. Weaknesses include the flats, short passes, four verticals/seam routes, and perimeter runs. Variations include flipping safeties, Cover 3 Fire Zone, Cover 3 Buzz, and pattern-reading coverages such as Rip/Liz.

The President replies to House resolutions by transmitting a report from the Secretary of State and documents and correspondence relating to the Treaty of Peace with Mexico concluded at Guadalupe Hidalgo on February 2, 1848, and to the Senate amendments. The documents include instructions to U.S. commissioners. The President had previously declined to furnish these instructions, citing public interest, but now transmits them because the House again requested them and they are indispensable to understanding other documents. He still holds that publishing instructions to ministers during important negotiations would generally harm public interests.

The instructions of March 18, 1848, directed commissioners to obtain Mexican ratification of the treaty as amended by the Senate, without negotiating a new treaty or changing the ratified treaty. The Secretary of State’s letter of March 18, 1848, explaining the amendments to Mexico, was communicated to Congress and published. The Mexican Congress approved the amended treaty on May 25, 1848, without modification, before U.S. commissioners were officially received or held conferences, except to transmit the Secretary of State’s letter. Ratifications were exchanged on May 26, 1848. The ratified treaty was received at Washington on July 4, 1848, proclaimed, and communicated to Congress on July 6.

Additional papers are now transmitted: the commissioners’ address, the Mexican President’s reply, the protocol, and correspondence. The President states that the protocol did not modify the treaty, occurred after Mexican congressional ratification, and was not treated as a new negotiation. He examines its explanations concerning the ninth, tenth, and twelfth articles and concludes they were in accordance with the amended treaty, so no action was necessary.

A study in the Journal of Hematology & Thromboembolic Diseases reports that Bt toxins engineered into most GMO food crops may have leukemogenic properties. Brazilian researchers found that Bt spore-crystals expressing Cry1Aa, Cry1Ab, Cry1Ac, or Cry2A caused hematotoxicity, particularly to erythroid cells, red blood cell changes such as anemia, suppressed bone marrow proliferation, and abnormal lymphocyte patterns consistent with some leukemias. A dose of Cry1Ab as low as 27 mg/kg induced hypochromic anemia in mice, effects were stronger after 72 hours, and high doses caused bone marrow damage. The authors concluded further studies are needed before these toxins are considered safe for mammals. The passage also cites a French GM corn/Roundup rat study, questions combined Cry toxin/glyphosate toxicity, and discusses calls to ban GMOs and the March Against Monsanto.

H H Martyn & Co closed in 1971. Founded in Cheltenham in 1888 by Herbert Henry Martyn, it became a large art crafts and engineering company. It moved to Sunningend and employed over 1,000 people by 1910. Its work included the Marble Arch iron gates, Royal Warrant work at Buckingham Palace and Windsor Castle, commissions worldwide, Selfridges’ frontage, the Cenotaph, and the Speaker’s Chair and Dispatch Boxes. It fitted out over 100 ocean liners, made military aeroplanes in the Great War—leading to the Gloster Aircraft Company—and was involved with the Golden Arrow, Wolseley cars, and the Unibus. It produced many statues and art metal works. Bought by Maples in the mid-1930s, it faced post-1945 recession; Maples sold its assets and closed it in 1971.

Under May 1825 instructions to Commodore Hull, Thomas ap Catesby Jones was sent in 1826 to Honolulu for friendly inspection, to relieve annoyance from American deserters, and to adjust American claims. He accomplished these objects and negotiated a treaty of friendship, commerce, and navigation signed December 23, 1826—the first Hawaiian treaty with any foreign power; it was never ratified by the United States, though some stipulations were considered morally binding. Later U.S. naval vessels intervened friendly. The Potomac, with Commodore Downs, interceded for persecuted Catholic converts. Persecutions were not finally arrested until 1839, when the French frigate L'Artémise, under Laplace, demanded Catholic protection and a treaty, threatening hostilities; the treaty was signed and violence averted. British consul Charlton's representations led to Lord Edward Russell's 1836 treaty. In 1843 Lord George Paulet seized the islands and forced cession; Commodore Kearney protested, and the Hawaiian flag was restored July 31, 1843, with Paulet's seizure disavowed.

The passage discusses community detection in network data, defining communities as groups with denser internal connections. It reviews stochastic block models, including degree-corrected and mixed-membership extensions, as well as edge exchangeable and latent space models. The passage presents consistency results for recursive bipartitioning under the stochastic block model using Erdős-Rényi modularity, and outlines simulation, real stroke transfer data, and discussion sections.
I am unable to summarize this passage.

The finding is described as the strongest evidence to date for an exoplanet stratosphere and may help future studies of smaller, cooler planets.

It covers free care at the point of use, with exceptions such as prescriptions in England, dentistry, and eye care; equal access regardless of personal characteristics; waiting time standards and alternatives if unmet; safe, clean care by qualified staff; access to NICE-recommended medicines and treatments and routine vaccinations; consent, clear information, and privacy; choice of GP, involvement in decisions, and openness when something goes wrong; and complaints, escalation to the Ombudsman, judicial review, and compensation for negligence. The strategy performs better risk-adjusted but has almost the same drawdown as buy and hold; results are not promising, though pairing ATR with other indicators might improve them.

A University of Bristol-led study examined the origin, timing, and habitat of chloroplast evolution. It found the chloroplast lineage split from its closest cyanobacterial ancestor more than 2.1 billion years ago in low-salinity environments, with symbiotic association occurring 200 million years later. Marine algae diversified around 800–750 million years ago, implying algae first evolved in freshwater before colonizing marine environments.

Controversial neo-Nazi website the Daily Stormer had trouble finding a domain registrar. After it published an article mocking Heather Heyer, killed in Charlottesville, and celebrating alleged killer James Fields, GoDaddy gave it 24 hours to move; GoDaddy said the article could incite violence. The site moved to Google Domains, which then cancelled its registration for violating terms. At publication, the site remained active and WHOIS listed Google as registrar. GoDaddy and Google did not host it; Cloudflare obscured its host. The Daily Stormer had attacked Google over James Damore’s firing. An Anonymous post claimed control, but Anglin said he regained it. The SPLC sued Anglin over harassment of Tanya Gersh’s family; he declined to participate, said he left for Lagos, Nigeria, but Reveal found he falsified information. His whereabouts are unknown. If the suit succeeds, his assets could be seized and the website shut down.

NASA announced the next ISS spacewalk is scheduled for August 17, with coverage on NASA Live from 10:00am EDT. Expedition 52 cosmonauts Fyodor Yurchikhin and Sergey Ryazanskiy will exit the Pirs airlock at about 10:45am EDT for a six-hour mission. They will deploy five nanosatellites, including one with a 3D-printed casing and one commemorating Russian space anniversaries, scrape residue samples, and attach handrails and struts. This is Expedition 52’s only planned spacewalk and among 2017’s longest.

Measles is a highly contagious, largely vaccine-preventable viral disease; Uganda continues to experience outbreaks despite free vaccines, and measles contributes to under-5 mortality. This retrospective cohort study reviewed records of children admitted with clinical measles at Mulago National Referral Hospital from January 1 to December 31, 2018, to describe immediate outcomes and estimate direct costs to the health care delivery system. Of 570 admissions, 553 charts were retrieved and 267 were sampled. The median age was 1.0 year, 63% were under 1 year, and median hospital stay was 4.0 days. Thirty patients (11.3%) died, and 185 (69.3%) had multiple complications, including severe pneumonia (39.5%), gastroenteritis (24.0%), and conjunctivitis (18.0%). Among deaths, 57% were male, 70% were aged 0–1 year, 44% were not immunized, and 86% stayed fewer than 7 days.

Average direct health care cost per patient was 33.13 USD: blood tests 11.73 USD, radiology 3.48 USD, and treatment 21.98 USD. Average overhead/direct non-health care cost was 81.37 USD, mostly human resources. Total estimated direct cost was 114.50 USD. Costs were higher for male patients, those with comorbidities, those hospitalized over 15 days, and those who died. The cost of immunizing a child was estimated at 0.86 USD. The study concludes that mortality was high, complications were common, and direct treatment costs were considerable, supporting efforts to promote measles immunization.

Ten people were killed and 15 injured when a van drove through pedestrians on Yonge Street and Finch Avenue in Toronto around 1:30pm ET Monday. Victim Anne-Marie D'Amico, an Invesco employee, was identified and her family informed. Alex Minassian, 25, was arrested and due in court; police said the attack appeared deliberate and appealed for witnesses as the motive remained unknown.

The present disclosure relates to big data and provides a recommendation model training method and related apparatus. The method includes selecting a positive sample from a sample set and adding it to a training set; calculating sampling probabilities of negative samples using a preset algorithm obtained based on one or more rules: the sampling probability is negatively correlated with a score difference between estimated scores of a positive sample and a current negative sample, negatively correlated with a vector distance between their eigenvectors, and/or positively correlated with a variation of a ranking indicator after exchanging rankings of the positive sample and the current negative sample; selecting a negative sample based on the sampling probability and adding it to the training set; and training using the training set to obtain a recommendation model. The recommendation model may be used to score and rank to-be-recommended objects and recommend top M objects to a target user. The disclosure also describes apparatuses, processors and memories, computer-readable storage media, and computer program products for implementing these methods.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture and built on TSMC 7nm N7 FinFET, is designed for AI and HPC. It introduces Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), which can partition an A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances for isolation and QoS. The A100 implementation has 108 SMs, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, and 40 GB HBM2 with 1555 GB/sec memory bandwidth. It supports PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, third-generation NVLink with twelve links and 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, and improved error/fault detection, isolation, and containment. A100 adds asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, task graph acceleration, fine-grained structured sparsity, TF32/BF16/FP64 Tensor Core formats, combined L1/shared memory, simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, L2 cache residency controls, compute data compression, NVJPG, optical flow accelerator, NVDEC, and atomics improvements. CUDA 11 supports these features. DGX A100 uses eight A100 GPUs and MIG to provide up to 56 isolated accelerators, 5 PFLOPS, and NVSwitch/InfiniBand scaling. The appendix discusses sparse neural networks and 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity.

This document specifies GHCB and VMGEXIT communication for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors. It defines MSR-protocol requests such as CPUID, AP reset hold, preferred/register/unregister GHCB GPA, page state change, hypervisor feature support, and termination, including GHCBData field usage and error reporting. It describes GHCB negotiation examples, NAE events, #VC exception handling, VALID_BITMAP rules, and SW_EXITCODE/SW_EXITINFO1/SW_EXITINFO2 error handling. It covers event-specific handling for MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV doorbell page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and Termination Request. It also addresses SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guest identification, SMP booting and AP jump tables, NMI handling, debug registers, unsupported SMM and nested virtualization, and #HV doorbell pending-event, EOI, interrupt-shadow, host, and guest behaviors.

On February 8, 2022, NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting that NVIDIA, SoftBank Group Capital Limited and SVF Holdco (UK) Limited mutually terminated the September 13, 2020 Share Purchase Agreement involving Arm Limited due to regulatory challenges. The Sellers will retain the $1.25 billion prepayment, and NVIDIA will retain its 20-year Arm license. NVIDIA intends to record a $1.36 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2023.

The passage describes the High/Low zone offense, saying it can be used at all levels and complements the Big 10 three-player High/Low passing game. It combines an outside three-player passing attack with an inside high/low rotation, can be initiated from almost any alignment or entry, and relies on continuity, interior movement, ball movement, sharp passing, and weakside attack. It covers fundamentals, continuity, post roll and flash options, entries such as Dribble Clear, 1-4 Slice, Mid Screen, and Horns, and specials including Pin Down, Weakside Double, and Vegas for clock situations or after timeouts.

Charlie Tillett presents on creating business plan financials, using an Excel template that can be downloaded and modified. He says financial projections help entrepreneurs understand key assumptions, business drivers, and cash needs. He discusses venture capital expectations, including 3x to 5x returns over five to seven years, significant investment and ownership, and an equity formula based on investment divided by pre-money value plus investment. He gives Series A and B dilution examples and notes investors receive preferred shares, board representation, and anti-dilution provisions. He explains income statement components: revenue, cost of goods sold, sales and marketing, R&D, G&A, and operating profit or EBITDA. He compares business models in retail, restaurants, technology hardware, software, and internet companies, showing gross margins, R&D spending, and revenue per employee. He advises building sales projections bottom-up, using staffing plans as a major expense driver, and using formulas for non-salary expenses. He says cash flow is difficult to model and suggests cumulative operating losses plus capital expenses as a proxy. He discusses founder pay, equity distribution among founders, employees, angels, and VCs, and recommends vesting over three or four years. He also answers questions about board control, overfunded small opportunities, and founder vesting.

The paper presents a knowledge-graph-based solution for analyzing instant messaging app data in criminal investigations. Chat dumps are processed into a Neo4j property graph containing chats, participants, messages, and metadata. Multimedia enrichment currently transcribes audio messages using Whisper, with future plans for images and videos. A NEEL pipeline extracts entities through NER, NEL, NIL prediction, and entity clustering, annotating chats and updating the knowledge graph. Two main interfaces are described: Neo4j for graph queries and visual exploration, and DAVE for faceted search and document exploration with editable annotations. The work was tested in two real investigations on fraud and corruption, with statistics reported for chats, messages, attachments, persons, and extracted entities. NER evaluation results were not satisfactory, and limitations include the need for in-domain fine-tuning and expertise in Neo4j querying. Investigators found graph visualizations, combined text and relational search, speech-to-text, and NLP useful. Future work includes improving NEEL, developing interfaces, and extending enrichment to images and videos. Ethical considerations include consultant contracts, local servers, restricted access, avoiding external APIs, and verification against original data.

Aqua Terra announced it filed a preliminary long form prospectus with securities commissions in Canadian provinces except Québec for an initial public offering of common shares through underwriters co-led by TD Securities, Canaccord Genuity and RBC Capital Markets. The number and price of shares are undetermined, depend on market conditions, and completion is not assured. Aqua Terra provides oilfield water disposal services to Canadian and U.S. onshore oil and natural gas producers, with infrastructure in specified regions.

The lecture begins with final-exam logistics and then discusses coding for bandwidth-limited additive white Gaussian noise channels. It covers lattice constellations, union-bound estimates, coding gain, shaping gain, and SNR norm. Optimum n-sphere shaping gives at most 1.53 dB, and shaping methods such as shell mapping and trellis shaping are described, including use in V.34. It surveys lattices including hexagonal, D4, E8, Barnes-Wall, and Leech, noting their coding gains and large numbers of near neighbors, which limit effective coding gain. Trellis-coded modulation uses set partitioning and Viterbi decoding, with coding gains up to about 6 dB; Wei’s four-dimensional codes were adopted in V.34 and ADSL. Higher-performance schemes such as turbo codes, sequential decoding, multi-level coding, and BICM can approach the Shannon limit. The professor concludes that coding for AWGN channels is mature, though questions about iterative decoding remain.

The newsletter reports that top drugmakers will meet in early December with Donald Trump Jr. and senior Trump administration officials at a summit hosted by BlinkRx, which has Trump Jr. on its board; some drug-company representatives were uneasy about the meeting because of BlinkRx’s ties to the president’s family. BlinkRx could benefit from President Trump’s push for direct-to-consumer drug sales, including the planned TrumpRx website. Separately, Pfizer’s price-lowering agreement with the administration has led other drugmakers to seek deals; some hope to announce agreements soon, though whether they will lower prices remains unknown. The passage also notes a Sarepta setback after a New York panel recommended pausing state Medicaid coverage of its Duchenne drug.

The lecture discusses thesis research on using hot embossing of thermoplastic polymers to manufacture microfluidic devices, motivated by polymer cost, transparency, and mechanical toughness. It covers process parameters such as temperature, load, and hold time; approaches for modeling and simulating embossed topography; experiments on pattern-dependent filling and material characterization; and challenges involving de-molding, thermal contraction, and dimensional stability.

The passage discusses the gold/silver chart ratio strategy, which trades gold and silver based on their price relationship. The ratio equals the number of silver ounces needed to match one ounce of gold, calculated by dividing gold’s price by silver’s price using the same currency and weight. A high ratio means gold is expensive relative to silver; a low ratio means the opposite. Traders generally use the ratio on a contrarian or mean-reversion basis, buying silver and shorting gold when the ratio is high, and reversing when it is low, through futures, options, or ETFs. Historically, the ratio was fixed by governments—12:1 in Rome, 15:1 in the U.S. in 1792, and 15.5:1 in France in 1803—before floating after the gold standard ended in the 1970s. The 20th-century average was 47:1; in the 21st century it mainly ranged from 50:1 to 70:1, peaked at 114.77 in 2020, and hit a low of 35:1 in 2011. Backtests found a simple GLD strategy performed poorly, the SLV equity curve was poor, and a GLD/SLV pair trade was flat. The passage states risk-on/off backtests failed to find meaningful profitable strategies and no robust gold/silver ratio strategies were found.

Hetzner now peers directly at NAP Africa in Isando via a 10Gbps circuit, joining Africa’s largest active peering community. It hosts over 330,000 websites and, with NAP Africa and JINX, routes over 65% of local traffic through exchange points and contributes over 4Gbps. It advocates settlement-free peering and peers with many South African network operators. Its carrier-neutral Samrand data centre and redundant 10Gbps links support connectivity. NAP Africa is a neutral layer 2 IXP in Teraco data centres. Hetzner invites network operators to peer.

The letter opposes the development permit for 7592 119A St. and 7551–7597 120 St., saying it conflicts with the North Delta Area Plan and Cougar Creek ISMP. It notes the Area Plan calls for six storeys, while 35 are proposed, and for tree preservation, canopy cover, stormwater management, rainwater infiltration, and pocket parks, which the proposal does not meet. The letter says the parking garage would leave no room for infiltration and that the project would not qualify for Scott Road Revitalization Bylaw benefits due to high environmental impact. It argues approval would encourage upzoning, speculation, and higher prices, and says highrise condos have not solved housing supply. It suggests only considering the proposal with major mitigation, including at least 15% permeable open space, and calls for all multi-family developments to set aside 15% permeable land.

SFS attestation requires OS/platform software to request attestation data via side-band/SPDM or in-band/DPE, with SFS providing measurements; some attestation schemes prevent updating certain AMD firmware. Update packages must ensure correct firmware versions before applying and avoid partial updates/resets. SFS updates are non-persistent across reboots and can be applied at OS boot, after boot, or during operation. SFS commands require memory alignment and a customer SFS Deployment Agent that creates a TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER, appends co-signing data/package/signature, and communicates via mailbox. ASP protects memory, verifies customer and AMD signatures, loads/runs patches, updates patch level, and returns status. GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO returns firmware/version data. Packages are binary, aligned to AGESA releases, named fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg. Updates run alongside x86/DMA traffic with minimal impact; some SEV or SEV/ES VMs must restart for SEV firmware updates.

Apple Inc.'s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2018 includes condensed consolidated financial statements and notes. For the three months ended June 30, 2018, net sales were $53,265 million, net income was $11,519 million, and diluted earnings per share were $2.34; for the nine months, net sales were $202,695 million, net income was $45,406 million, and diluted earnings per share were $8.99. Net sales increased 17% in the third quarter and 15% in the first nine months, driven by iPhone, Services, and Other Products, with favorable foreign currency effects. The report discusses the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, European Commission State Aid Decision, debt, derivatives, share repurchases, benefit plans, commitments, contingencies including VirnetX and Qualcomm, and segment results. In the third quarter, Apple repurchased $20.0 billion of common stock and paid $3.7 billion in dividends; a new $100 billion repurchase program was authorized. Gross margin was 38.3% for the quarter and 38.4% for nine months, and the effective tax rate was 13.3% and 19.6%, respectively.

This work addresses CBCT-to-CT image synthesis for image-guided radiotherapy, noting CBCT limitations such as scatter, artifacts, and inconsistent HU values, and CT’s better soft-tissue contrast and HU calibration. It reviews registration-based methods, GANs, CNN/transformer/hybrid models, and diffusion models. The proposed EqDiff-CT is a conditional DDPM framework using a time-conditioned, group-equivariant, attention-enhanced U-Net denoiser via e2cnn, with C4 rotational equivariance and self-attention, trained on 2D axial slices using MSE and SSIM on predicted noise and variance-correct reverse diffusion. Evaluated on SynthRAD2025 Head & Neck with an 80/20 patient split, it reports slice- and volume-wise metrics and outperforms a baseline diffusion model and CycleGAN in SSIM, PSNR, MSE, and MAE while preserving the mandible, airway, and cervical spine. It also uses an HU-preserving preprocessing/post-processing pipeline and outlines notation and paper organization.

The speaker says the team made mistakes but believes its opponent can play better and has a strong record after a first-game loss, so they are preparing for the opponent’s best. They say they are not dwelling on the past and are focusing on preparation and on what Dallas might do differently, noting Dallas’s slower first game against Colorado followed by more aggressive forechecking and physical play. They stress taking away time from Dallas’s skilled players, with defense and forwards working together. They call the next game important because a 2–0 lead would pressure the opponent and the team cannot be a flash in the pan. They mention health is generally fine apart from Madden’s injury, discuss rivalries and the long playoffs, praise Brian when he is on his game, and say poor puck decisions and Dallas’s forechecking made it their worst recent game. An offside miss preceded Hull’s goal but was not the reason for the loss. They say the series is 1–1, there is no panic, and the team must play better in Dallas.

A CDC report states that U.S. illnesses from mosquito, tick, and flea bites have tripled since 2004. In Venice, still waters in the canals and Ballona Wetlands can breed mosquitoes, and West Nile Virus has been present in the area. About 80 percent of infected people show no symptoms; others may experience nausea, vomiting, rash, diarrhea, swollen lymph glands, and, in less than one percent of cases, neuroinvasive disease. Los Angeles County West Vector Control manages standing water and recommends repellent and eliminating yard water.

The Weston Public Library plans eclipse events: free solar viewers from Aug. 14, a pinhole projector event Aug. 15, and NASA livestream Aug. 21. Weston expects about 70% coverage; the next eclipse is April 2024.

The study developed a model to understand potential sources of influenza A H5 RNA in wastewater and to interpret H5 RNA wastewater detections. It considered human, cow milk, poultry feces, and wildfowl feces as likely sources. The passage describes H5N1 outbreaks in birds and cattle, human cases, and H5 RNA detections in wastewater. It retrospectively analyzed wastewater solids from September 2023 to May 2024 at a California publicly owned treatment work for total IAV and H1, H3, and H5 RNA, and developed a mass balance model of theoretical inputs. Objectives were to identify the timing of first H5 detection and contextualize findings using the model.

The SteelSeries Arctis GameBuds, rated 9/10 and WIRED Recommends, are discounted at Amazon to $128. They offer portability, Xbox or PlayStation compatibility, work with Switch, PC, and smartphones, and include a USB-C dongle with low-latency 2.4GHz and Bluetooth. Battery life is about 10 hours in the buds and 40 total with the case. The mobile app offers ANC and game equalizer settings, and the earbuds are comfortable with physical controls.

Two hydrogen-bonded MIOC crystals, ZnCl2HIm2 (MIOC-4) and ZnCl2HbIm2 (MIOC-7), were synthesized by slow evaporation using chloride introduced into ZIF-4 and ZIF-7. Their supramolecular structures are assembled by hydrogen bonding, with MIOC-7 also showing π-π interactions. MIOC-4 is monoclinic with Tm 440 K and Tg 282 K; MIOC-7 is triclinic with Tm 508 K and Tg 359 K. Mixed-ligand synthesis produced binary MIOC mixed crystals with reduced melting points and tunable glass-transition temperatures. In situ XRD showed melting begins with slippage and distortion of hydrogen-bonded structures, followed by disordering upon hydrogen-bond breaking. FT-IR, Raman, solid-state NMR, and high-energy XRD indicated that vitrification weakens C-H···Cl and strengthens N-H···Cl hydrogen bonds, while short-range Zn-N, Zn-Cl, and Zn-C correlations are preserved and medium- and long-range intermolecular correlations vanish. The ligand-tuning approach was extended to Cu/Co metal nodes and SCN- anions. MIOC-7 glass exhibited enhanced photoluminescence, with PLQY 3.4% versus 1.2% for the crystal, excitation-dependent emission, and potential anti-counterfeiting applications.

James Harden became the first NBA player to score 60 points in a triple-double as the Houston Rockets beat the Orlando Magic 114-107. Harden scored 18 in the fourth quarter, breaking Calvin Murphy’s Houston record of 57 points from 1978. He had 10 rebounds, 11 assists, four steals and a block while playing a season-high 46:26. The Rockets were without Chris Paul, Trevor Ariza and Eric Gordon. It was Harden’s fourth 50-point game this season, surpassing his previous career-high of 56.

The passage describes a networked exercise system and methods for providing live and on-demand exercise classes. It includes exercise machines such as treadmills with displays, digital hardware, sensors, motors, and controls. Example treadmills have a deck with a continuous track and slats, posts, arms, crossbars, and first and second rotary controls configured to control different functions. The system supports interactivity among instructors and users, performance metrics, competition, gamification, audio/video chat, and user interfaces for featured, archived, and live classes, leaderboards, and performance data. It also describes a method of manufacturing a treadmill with an upper assembly and rotary controls.

Socket 940’s allowable outline is shown in Figure 3, with dimensions in millimeters. Its cover accommodates the package pin shoulder and braze/solder fillet, supports the package substrate, and has a seating-plane flatness better than 0.25 mm unmated and mated; after PCB mounting, the seating plane is 4.00 ± 0.20 mm from the mounting. Base and cover are LCP with UL 94 V-0 rating; base is black, cover natural or ivory. Cover thickness including the 0.30 mm pocket recess must not exceed 1.17 mm, and flatness must remain <0.25 mm before/after SMT reflow and after testing. A removable tape or plastic overlay covers pin holes for vacuum pick-and-place and must not outgas or leave residue. Molded markings include “SOCKET 940,” locked/unlocked designator near the lever, triangular A01 orientation symbol, supplier UL symbol, and lot traceability number visible after PCB mounting. Contacts are high-strength copper alloy, plated with minimum 1.27 µm nickel and minimum 0.76 µm gold on mating areas. SMT solder balls are 63/37 ±5% tin-lead, 0.76 mm diameter, with 0.64 mm PCB pads; a solder barrier prevents wicking, and solder ball co-planarity is 0.20 mm. A stainless steel lever on the right side of the cam box actuates contacts. Open-position insertion/extraction forces are conceptually zero and must not exceed 2 kgf actual; closed extraction is at least 0.013 kgf per pin. A latch locks the closed lever; actuation/de-actuation force <3.6 kgf and pin displacement <1.0 mm. The socket must maintain integrity after 50 cycles. Electrical requirements include 1.5 A per contact with <30°C rise, initial/final LLCR ≤25 mΩ with Kovar pins, inductance <4 nH single pin and 3 nH ±10% for two/three pins, capacitance <1 pF, differential impedance 100 Ω ±10%, propagation delay skew <10 ps plus measurement error, dielectric withstanding voltage ≥650 Vac, and insulation resistance ≥1000 MΩ. No lubricants are allowed on contact mating areas of shipped assembled sockets.

The passage states that early offense and press break success depends on precise execution, coordination, and coaching before games. It recommends teaching with the Whole-Part-Whole method: demonstrating roles, walking through options, using progressive breakdown drills, and then practicing live at game speed against tough defense. Objectives include attacking presses, making outlet/inbound passes, advancing with short passes, handling double teams, flowing into early offense, and going to offensive boards. Press break should be part of every practice. Game strategies include disruptive defense, breaking every possession, scouting opponents, and anticipating defensive changes; defensive pressure can disrupt fast breaks and early offense.

The speaker highlights a goalie’s response to his first adversity: after a loss, he played outstanding in the next game and remained calm, even-keeled, and mentally in a good spot. He compares Bergeron and O’Reilly as hardworking players who are strong in the faceoff circle and on both sides of the puck. He also sees team similarities in defensive play, top-line scoring, forechecking, physicality, and discipline between and after whistles, while stressing a team-first identity and the need for two goalies given schedule and travel.

A Kentucky valedictorian, Christian Bales, used a bullhorn to give his graduation speech outside after the Diocese of Covington said he could not speak at Holy Cross High School’s commencement. Student council president Katherine Frantz also gave her speech by bullhorn after the diocese nixed it. The diocese said the speeches were not submitted on time and were political and inconsistent with Catholic Church teaching. Bales’s speech praised student gun-law advocates at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School and said young people must speak candidly; he made no mention of his sexual orientation. The speeches drew widespread media attention.

The Trump administration wants to hire hundreds of new government lawyers, including more than 400 additional assistant US attorneys, but hiring is off to a slow start. LinkedIn data show about 42 people updated their profiles from January through August to say they joined the Justice Department as assistant US attorneys, down by more than half from the same period in each of the prior four years. Current and former prosecutors attribute the slowdown to budget and political pressures, hiring freezes, pay raises, DOJ turmoil, sagging morale, and potential recruits’ concerns about ethically murky casework. Other cited factors include public skepticism of law enforcement and rising wages. The data are not comprehensive. The hiring freeze initially affected some lawyer hiring, though prosecutors were later exempted, while a workforce-reduction initiative spurred firings and retirements. Some offices are understaffed and some are hiring. New hires often come from prominent law firms, state and local prosecutors’ offices, or Top 14 law schools. Some former prosecutors encourage young lawyers to seek AUSA jobs; others advise caution.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture adds concurrent RT Core/graphics, RT Core/compute, and compute-compute processing in each SM, with workload priority controls. The second-generation RT Core doubles ray/triangle intersection testing over Turing and adds an Interpolate Triangle Position unit for ray-traced motion blur, stated as up to 8x faster than Turing and measured up to 5x faster on RTX 3080 versus RTX 2080 Super in a Blender Cycles 2.90 OptiX 7.0 demo. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BFloat16, support sparsity with up to 2x throughput, and enhance DLSS, including 9x Super Resolution scaling for 8K 60 fps gaming; RTX 3080 is stated to deliver 2.7x higher peak FP16 Tensor Core throughput with sparsity than RTX 2080 Super. GA10x uses GDDR6X with PAM4 signaling, up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth, and adds Error Detection and Replay for memory overclocking. RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage for GPU-based lossless decompression and faster loading while offloading CPU work. The A40 data center GPU offers up to 2X FP32, 2X ray-tracing, and up to 5X (10X with sparsity) AI throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000, 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, and virtualization support. Display support includes DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 for 8K60/4K120, plus HDCP 2.3. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC supports high-quality encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. The RTX A6000 includes GA102, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, 336 next-generation cores, and 48GB GDDR6 scalable to 96GB via NVLink. Appendix specs cover RTX 3090, RTX 3070, and EDR on GDDR6X.

The article examines the ADX (Average Directional Movement Index), developed by Welles Wilder in his 1978 book New Concepts In Technical Trading Systems, along with RSI, ATR, and parabolic SAR. It states ADX measures trend strength, not direction, ranges from 0 to 100, is lagging, and has components including DI+ and DI-. Wilder classified readings under 15 as non-trending and above 20 as trending. Backtests of a DI+/- crossover on the S&P 500 showed an average trade of 0.42%, CAGR of 5.4%, 55% time invested, and profit factor of 1.71; 10 days was among the best time frames. An ADX breakout strategy optimized at 35 days for DMs and 15 days for ADX produced 13.76% drawdown versus 55% buy-and-hold, but CAGR of 3.03% versus 9.9%. Standalone ADX was not sufficient, though as a filter it improved a mean-reverting strategy: on SPY CAGR was 9% with 24% exposure and profit factor 2.15, and with an ADX filter CAGR was 7.3%, exposure 7%, and profit factor 2.6; on QQQ CAGR was 12.5% with 8% exposure. The article concludes ADX performs reasonably alone but better with another indicator and recommends backtesting.

The speaker discusses power-play and penalty-kill play, saying overtime momentum came from a delay penalty and a clean chance decided the game. He says the puck came to him and he found a teammate in a great spot for a good shot. He notes penalties hurt momentum, the team must stay out of the box, and opponents have elite personnel and many threats. He praises the hockey town, fans, and team personnel, saying many guys can step in and make an impact despite losing key players.

A study by researchers at Stanford, Harvard and the Census Bureau found that in 99 percent of U.S. neighborhoods, black boys earn less in adulthood than white boys from similar socioeconomic backgrounds, undermining the belief that class is the most fundamental predictor of economic outcomes. Using data on 20 million U.S. children and parents, it found black and Native American children had the lowest upward mobility, while whites and Asians were at the top. The black-white income gap persisted even among the wealthiest families and was almost entirely driven by differences between men; black women earned slightly more than white women when parental income was controlled. Neighborhoods still affect adult earnings, some areas showed parity, and Hendren speculated history may play a role in persistent disparities.

On October 7, 2016, NVIDIA Corporation entered into a Credit Agreement with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as administrative agent, and other lenders. The agreement permits borrowing, repayment, and re-borrowing up to $575 million for working capital and general corporate purposes, available for five years ending October 7, 2021. It also permits additional revolving loan and letter of credit commitments up to $425 million. Loans bear interest at the Adjusted LIBO Rate or Alternate Base Rate plus the Applicable Rate. The agreement includes customary representations, covenants, and default provisions. The obligations are unsecured senior obligations. Item 2.03 incorporates Item 1.01, and Exhibit 1.1 is the Credit Agreement.

Future Electronics and NXP are hosting a free seminar on the i.MX RT Series Crossover Processor in San Sebastian, Spain, on July 4, 2018. The workshop introduces the i.MX RT Series, described as the industry’s first crossover processor, with a high-performance Arm Cortex-M core, real-time functionality, and MCU usability at an affordable price. It includes hands-on exercises. The i.MX RT 105x processors use the Cortex M7 core and lack flash memory, allowing implementation flexibility at an interesting cost.

The speaker thanks Berliners and celebrates German unity where the city was divided. He recalls Berliners’ courage and says the Wall is gone. This paper studies satisficing paths from a topological perspective, introducing the grouped satisficing path as an extension of the satisficing path under the “win-stay, lose-shift” principle. It formalizes pure strategy games, best responses, equilibria, best response group count, and local minima/maxima. Theorem 1 gives conditions under which the original game can be reduced to a sub-game. Theorem 2 establishes sufficient conditions for existence: if strategy sets are convex and compact, payoff functions are continuous and partially analytic, and any sub-game has an equilibrium, then for any initial joint strategy there exists a finite-length grouped satisficing path to an equilibrium. Corollaries apply this to continuous games, N-player games, and finite-state Markov games, including stationary and k-step settings. The paper also discusses open problems and concludes that such finite-length satisficing paths exist for N-player and finite-state Markov games from any initial joint mixed strategy to a mixed equilibrium.

The lecture continues protein folding and introduces interlocked chains. For protein folding, it discusses theoretical work on forces and algorithms, focusing on the HP model, which represents hydrophobic and hydrophilic/polar nodes and models only hydrophobicity. Chains fold on a lattice, and the score is the number of adjacent H-H nodes, which is maximized. Optimal folding in the HP model is NP-hard in 3D and 2D lattices. A known 1/3 approximation algorithm is described. The lecture also discusses unique optimal foldings, proved to exist for closed chains of all even lengths and open chains of doubly even lengths, with open problems for other lengths and grids. Protein design is presented as an open problem.

For interlocked chains, it discusses Lubiw’s problem: the minimum number of cuts needed to unlock a 3D chain, known to be between about n/4 and n/2. It presents separability and interlocking results for chains of lengths 2 through 5, including hairpins and open/closed chains, and describes geometric and topological arguments for several interlocking examples. It notes that PSPACE-completeness for motion between configurations of 3D chains uses interlocked chains to build rigid infrastructure, while the problem of unfolding a straight chain remains open.

An e-mini trading strategy trades one of the e-mini contracts. E-minis are electronically traded futures contracts that are a fraction of the value of corresponding standard futures contracts; they were first created by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and are predominantly traded on its Globex platform. They are available on indexes, commodities, and currencies, and the first E-mini futures contract was launched in 1997 for the S&P 500 index. E-minis allow investors to hedge or speculate and are smaller and more accessible to retail traders, but they can be highly volatile and involve leverage risk. How much is needed to trade depends on contract value and minimum margin; for example, an S&P 500 E-mini at 4,000 points has a $200,000 contract value, with CME specifying $10,000 and brokers possibly requiring about $13,000 to $15,000. The passage also presents a backtested @ES strategy with 163 trades, 0.89% average gain per trade, 79% win ratio, and a profit factor of 2; in 2022 it had 13 trades averaging 0.18%, compared with an S&P 500 loss of 15%. It notes risks, costs, settlement on expiration, resources for learning, and the importance of a written, backtested plan.

This article examines Songshan Culture, Songyang Academy, and general education. It used documentary and field study methods, interviews, observations, literature websites, local chronicles, books, promotional films, documentaries, and recording equipment. Findings describe Songyang Academy as one of China’s four major academies, with over 1,500 years of history through the Tang, Song, Ming, Yuan, and Qing dynasties and the transition to modern China. It began as Songyang Temple in 484 AD, later became Taiyi School and Songyang School, flourished in the Northern Song, declined under later dynasties, and lost its glory after the imperial examination system was abolished. Its educational philosophy emphasized moral education, character cultivation, learning for practical use, unity of knowledge and action, autonomous learning, mutual questioning, and equal access. The article relates this philosophy to general education’s emphasis on all-round development. It concludes that Songyang Academy’s educational philosophy is closely related to modern general education and offers experience for modern educational reform, talent cultivation, inheritance, and protection.

Kobe University researchers found that orchids rely on wood-decaying fungi to germinate, obtaining carbon from decaying logs. Seeds of four orchid species germinated only near decaying logs, and seedlings associated almost exclusively with wood-decaying fungi. These fungal partnerships matched those of adult orchids with coral-shaped rhizomes of the same species; orchids without such rhizomes may shift to other fungi as nutritional needs change and log carbon diminishes. The finding links deadwood fungi to orchid ecology and evolution, including full mycoheterotrophy, and suggests conservation requires protecting deadwood and its fungi.

Since the mid-1940s, NIH funding to university researchers has led to many lifesaving treatments. Advocates and researchers warn a 40 percent NIH budget cut could threaten U.S. medical innovation. A paper, “What if NIH had been 40% smaller?,” examined NIH grants in the bottom 40 percent of funding priority from 1980–2007 and FDA-approved drugs with new active ingredients from 2000–2023. It found more than half of 21st-century approved drugs were linked to research at risk under a smaller budget. Forty of 557 drugs had patents acknowledging NIH extramural funding; 14 cited an at-risk grant, including Cerdelga. Fifty-nine percent cited NIH-supported research, and 65 of 557 were highly linked. Drugs linked to at-risk research had higher FDA priority review rates and average market value. Authors called the estimates conservative.

The court unanimously affirmed dismissal of plaintiff’s defamation action for failure to state a cause of action. The dispute arose from a letter by PBA president Caruso in New York’s Finest magazine. They were not actionable as defamation, false statements, or mixed opinion. Affirmed without costs.

North America held the largest share; Asia-Pacific is expected to grow fast during 2016–2022. The market is expected to reach about USD 6 billion by 2022 at 21% CAGR.

Escalating global population increases pressure for cereal production and pesticide use. The grain and cereal crop protection market includes advancements, crop rotation, and protection chemicals, though these chemicals can harm the environment, health, and soil. By type, it comprises insecticides, herbicides, and fungicides; herbicides dominate and are expected to continue due to low cost and R&D. North America is prominent, followed by Asia Pacific and Europe, with Asia Pacific expected to expand rapidly. Demand is boosted by population, food consumption, and health awareness in India, China, and Japan. Local, regional, and international vendors operate, with global vendors leading in differentiation, quality, price, innovation, and distribution.

The TPS7H500x-SP family consists of radiation-hardness-assured current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They can be paired with external gate drivers, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and be used for topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. The devices use fixed-frequency peak current mode control; the oscillator initiates turn-on, sensed current is compared through an internal comparator to a stepped-down COMP voltage, and the switch is turned off when the sensed current reaches that voltage.

Hiccup mode: when CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V, cycle-by-cycle current limiting occurs; CHICC is charged by an 80-µA hiccup delay current, and when CHICC reaches 0.6 V, SS is discharged and switching stops. HICC is pulled to 1 V, then a 1-µA hiccup restart current discharges CHICC; switching resumes when HICC falls to 0.3 V, initiating soft-start. CHICC controls delay and hiccup times, with a recommended minimum of 3.3 nF.

FAULT pin: if voltage exceeds 0.6 V for the FAULT minimum pulse width (0.4 µs to 1.4 µs), fault shutdown occurs; SS is discharged and outputs stop. After FAULT falls below 0.5 V, a delay approximately equal to 15 switching cycles plus internal logic delay occurs before soft-start; if FAULT is exceeded during the delay, the sequence restarts.

Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation when duty cycle exceeds 50% in peak current mode. The minimum slope compensation is 0.5 × m, and 1 × m is recommended. A resistor from RSC to AVSS sets slope compensation. The devices use an OTA, allowing Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation; Type 2A adds CHF for high-frequency noise attenuation. Thermal shutdown stops switching if junction temperature exceeds 175°C typical and reinitiates power-up below 160°C typical.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V with at least 0.1 µF input bypass. Layout guidelines address noise, grounding, high-current traces, bypass capacitors, compensation components, and CFP backside metallization. The passage also includes revision history, documentation, support, trademark, ESD, and mechanical/packaging information.

This withdrawn medRxiv preprint evaluates six machine-learning models—Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, Neural Network, Decision Tree, and SuperLearner—for pancreatic cancer diagnosis using a synthetic dataset. All models had similar accuracy (76.05%–76.35%) but very low sensitivity. Random Forest and Decision Tree identified no true positives, SVM had the highest sensitivity at 1.90%, and SuperLearner had the highest precision at 66.67%. The study attributes poor true-positive detection to class imbalance and recommends resampling, cost-sensitive learning, threshold tuning, feature engineering, interpretability tools, real-world data, and clinician–data scientist collaboration to improve clinical utility.

Research by the Cinnamon Network found faith-based organisations are supporting the NHS, with more than 3,500 churches and 200,000 volunteers involved in health and social care initiatives that plug gaps left by funding cuts and limited resources. Its report, The Church’s Impact on Health and Care, was cited by Bishop of London Sarah Mullally as showing the church’s contribution. The network studied 32 church-led projects addressing mental health, obesity and social isolation. David Simmons said the projects are cost-effective; 2016 research estimated UK church and faith groups’ community time at £3bn a year. The report highlighted parish nursing, in which churches recruit nurses to support patients. There are over 100 parish nurses across 85 UK churches, with 100 more expected in 18 months; supporters say they provide preventative care and support but do not replace NHS nurses.

The IDC White Paper examines goals and challenges of industrial simulation, modeling, data analysis, and HPC infrastructures, and describes usage scenarios and success factors. In December 2021, IDC surveyed 200 IT and departmental decision makers from discrete and process manufacturing enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Manufacturers face geopolitical uncertainties, rising energy prices, raw material shortages, supply chain disruptions, skilled labor shortfalls, sustainability concerns, and digitalization. Simulation, modeling, and analysis support innovation, quality, product development speed, time to market, cost reduction, and decision-making, with expanding deployment in product development, production and process planning, and quality management. Challenges include data silos and the absence of a holistic data strategy. HPC is described as a game changer for product and process innovation because it enables complex calculations, higher quality and intensity of use, new usage scenarios, and greater innovation and agility. More than a quarter of surveyed enterprises already use HPC, 39% plan or pilot it, and 15% are not engaging with it.

Columbiana defeated Lisbon 49-47 in a girls basketball game. With 36 seconds left, Lisbon’s Izzy Perez made a free throw for a 47-45 lead. Columbiana’s Alexis Cross scored with 23 seconds remaining to tie the game at 47, and Kayla Muslovski’s steal and layup ten seconds later provided the winning points. Columbiana improved to 5-0 overall and 3-0 in the league; Lisbon fell to 3-2 and 2-1 in league play. Muslovski and Cross each scored 14 for Columbiana. Perez scored a game-high 17 for Lisbon, and Maddie Liberati added 12.

Alexa ranks Reddit third most visited US platform, ahead of Facebook, behind Google and YouTube. Reddit users average 15:10 daily versus Facebook’s 10:50; Facebook faces the Cambridge Analytica scandal and GDPR-related changes.

At ICC Board meetings in Kolkata on Wednesday and Thursday, the BCCI would resist any ICC attempt to scrap the 2021 Champions Trophy in India and replace it with a World T20. BCCI treasurer Anirudh Chaudhry said this would cause an approximately $30 million loss to the BCCI and criticized ICC chairman Shashank Manohar. Suspected jihadists killed at least 18 people and wounded several in a raid on a restaurant in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. Security forces shot dead both attackers and freed trapped people. The communications minister called it a terrorist attack and said the toll was provisional. Burkina Faso has faced sporadic jihadist attacks, mostly along its northern border with Mali.

The Southeast faced a severe storm threat Monday, with 29 million people at risk of damaging hail, high wind, and tornadoes. Hail fell in northern Mississippi near Ripley and along a path from Holly Springs to Booneville. Forecasters expressed increasing confidence in strong tornadoes, especially in northern Alabama, with several tornadic supercells possible. The passage presents iMOOE, a physics-guided invariant learning method for zero-shot out-of-distribution PDE dynamics forecasting. It states that zero-shot OOD generalization in PDE dynamics learning remains underexplored, while existing methods such as domain-aware meta-learning, parameter conditioning, and pretraining lack sufficient zero-shot OOD capability because they do not explicitly illuminate PDE invariance. The work formulates OOD forecasting as a min-max risk optimization problem and defines a two-fold PDE invariance: operator invariance, where elementary spatial operators remain invariant across domains, and compositionality invariance, where the fixed composition of operators, parameters, and forcing terms governs a PDE system. iMOOE uses a mixture of operator experts with derivative masks and a fusion network, plus a frequency-enriched invariant learning objective combining maximal prediction loss, risk equality loss, frequency enrichment loss, and mask diversity loss. Experiments on Diffusion-Reaction, Navier-Stokes, Burgers, Shallow-Water, Heat-Conduction, and real-world Sea Surface Temperature report state-of-the-art zero-shot ID/OOD and time extrapolation results, compatibility with diverse neural operators, and sensitivity to the number of operator experts. The conclusion notes validation is limited to a limited diversity of dynamical systems and future work will extend iMOOE to other PDE dynamics.
