The lecture covers ultra-cold quantum gases, ideal and interacting Bose and Fermi gases, and superfluidity determined by interactions. It reviews the Bogoliubov approximation for a homogeneous interacting Bose gas, which replaces the zero-momentum condensate operator by a number and diagonalizes the Hamiltonian into noninteracting quasiparticles. It discusses observing sound and quasiparticles through laser-induced density perturbations, light scattering, the dynamic structure factor, and stimulated Raman spectroscopy. For trapped inhomogeneous condensates, it introduces field operators, the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, the Thomas-Fermi approximation, the healing length, and vortices. It then treats optical lattices and the Bose-Hubbard model with tunneling \(j\) and on-site interaction \(U\), deriving superfluid and Mott-insulator limits and using mean-field decoupling to obtain the phase transition and phase diagram. Observation methods include time-of-flight interference and quantum gas microscopy.

Crude sulfate turpentine is a flammable turpentine derivative obtained by distilling resin from live trees, especially pines, and as a byproduct of the Kraft process. It contains terpene hydrocarbons and sulfur compounds, mainly alpha-pinene and beta-pinene, with smaller amounts of limonene, camphene, carene, and terpinene. It is used in fragrances, flavors, cosmetics, food and beverages, paints, varnishes, and organic synthesis. Market growth may be restrained by high distillation investments and limited black liquor retrieval. Alpha-pinene is used as an anti-inflammatory and antibiotic constituent; beta-pinene in perfumery; carene has pine-like, sweet, woodsy, cedar, and pungent fragrances.

The passage presents a pragmatic randomized controlled trial protocol within a Learning Health System to evaluate Ambient AI for clinical documentation. It uses a Pragmatic Trial Operations playbook with governance, user experience, technical, documentation sustainment, and analytics components. Ambient AI was integrated into the EHR at UW Health. Alpha-phase testing assessed safety, usability, and workflow; the beta phase was a 24-week multisite, closed-cohort stepped-wedge PRCT of 66 providers in three waves, using the Professional Fulfillment Index as an outcome. Alpha-phase results from 20 providers and 8,527 encounters showed weighted median utilization of 65.4%; interviews identified organizational, readiness, and service/task barriers. Documentation accuracy decreased from 79% to 35% after implementation and returned to pre-intervention levels with a new note template. An LLM-based ICD-10 review and real-time dashboard were developed. Recruitment was completed, and the trial began on schedule. The discussion states that aligning research and operations within an LHS framework can accelerate evaluation and support scalable GenAI adoption.
The speaker stresses focusing on winning each shift and period, not the outcome, and seizing a shared, possibly final chance to win the Cup.

The Utah Court of Appeals affirmed the district court’s summary judgment against Kari L. Baumann. Baumann sued The Kroger Company and Dr. Gregory P. Tayler in 2013 under Utah’s savings statute, alleging malpractice and related claims. She stipulated to disclose expert witnesses by June 6, 2014, and complete expert discovery by September 5, 2014, but failed to disclose expert witnesses or reports. Defendants moved for summary judgment. Baumann later filed a Kroger-specific expert report on the day of the November 17, 2014 hearing and no report for Dr. Tayler. The district court found no good cause for her failure to disclose, determined expert testimony was required, and precluded use of undisclosed witnesses or materials under rule 26(d)(4). On appeal, the court declined to review the Dr. Tayler report issue as unpreserved. For the Kroger report, the court held rule 26(d)(4), not rule 16(d), applied and that the district court did not abuse its discretion in excluding the report and affirming summary judgment.

This paper investigates LLM effectiveness in detecting and fixing API misuses in data science libraries. It proposes DSCHECKER, which combines API directives and dynamic variable information in prompts. Evaluations use DSMISUSES, containing 76 code snippets from 38 misuses across NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, scikit-learn, and seaborn, plus a reproduced sample of deep learning misuses. Adding API directives and data information generally improves performance; llama with the full prompt achieved the best zero-shot detection F1-score of 61.18% and fix rate of 51.28%. Few-shot prompting produced varied model-specific results. DSCHECKER detected about 35% more misuses than LLMAPIDET on DSMISUSES, while LLMAPIDET fixed none of its detected DSMISUSES misuses. On the DL sample, DSCHECKER achieved 48% detection F1-score and 26.67% fix rate. DSCHECKERagent achieved 48.65% detection F1-score and 39.47% fix rate with 4o, lower than DSCHECKER but promising for practical settings without prior misuse information.

Island flying foxes, large bats, are important pollinators of durian, a valuable Southeast Asian fruit. A study in Ecology and Evolution used camera traps in a Malaysian durian orchard on Tioman Island and found that the bats feed on nectar without damaging flowers, positively affecting durian reproductive success. Although flying foxes are often blamed for crop damage, the footage shows they help durian. Island flying fox populations are decreasing and the species is endangered in Malaysia, threatened by hunting and habitat loss. Bats are major pollinators of economically important tropical crops, and the study’s author says more research on bat ecosystem services is needed to support conservation.

New European research at the University of Eastern Finland studying 2,480 men aged 42–60 for an average of 22 years found that the highest blood linoleic acid levels were associated with a 43 percent lower risk of premature death from all causes compared with the lowest levels. Higher linoleic acid was also linked to lower cardiovascular death risk, but not cancer death; arachidonic acid showed a similar, weaker association.

The lecture is the last videotaped lecture before student presentations. It covers inverse and ill-posed problems, starting with a least-squares duality example and an optimality condition connecting x and w, and presents a geometry identity as an open proof problem. Examples of inverse problems include finding velocities from positions, seismology and oil exploration, CT/MRI/PET scans, finding Earth’s density from gravity, scattering, finding coefficients in Laplace/Poisson equations, and reconstructing matrices. The lecture also discusses integral equations of the first kind, Volterra and Fredholm equations, and regularization by adding a multiple of the identity. GPS is described as using satellites and least squares to find position and time, with Doppler/frequency-domain options for velocity. Tikhonov regularization minimizes A x minus b squared plus alpha x squared, leading to the normal equation A transpose A plus alpha I times u alpha equals b; with noise delta, the error is of size delta over square root of alpha, and alpha equal to delta to the 2/3 is given as a good choice. Genomics is mentioned as estimating gene importance from few samples in high dimension.

Opioid misuse is a worldwide epidemic involving high overdose and mortality rates. The mu-opioid receptor (MOR) is targeted by opioid drugs of abuse and OUD medications, with respiratory depression as a major risk. Naloxone reverses opioid effects. MORs are widely expressed, and [11C]CFN-PET has advanced MOR study, mostly in brain. Long axial field-of-view PET, including PennPET Explorer, enables whole-body C-11 radiotracer imaging. This study presents first human whole-body neuroreceptor [11C]CFN-PET imaging, investigating extra-CNS reference regions. Methods included healthy participants aged 18–45, exclusions, MRI, [11C]CFN preparation and PET acquisition on PennPET Explorer, and image analysis using PMOD, AAL VOIs, Logan DVR, and naloxone percent receptor occupancy.

Mitch Larkin is considering adding the individual medley to his Commonwealth Games trials program to maintain hunger for Olympic redemption. He won the 400m IM at the Queensland titles. A dual backstroke world champion, Larkin is unsure whether he will swim the medley at trials or the Commonwealth Games and wants to refocus on backstroke. After Rio disappointment, coaching changes and a difficult year, he says he has no regrets and is hungrier to return to the top.
Ventura's police chief says his department will review procedures after a restaurant patron was fatally stabbed by a homeless man. The suspect is charged with murder.

The U.S. will experience a total solar eclipse on Aug. 21, when the sun, moon and Earth align and the moon’s shadow crosses from Oregon to South Carolina, the first coast-to-coast total eclipse in 99 years. NASA and others will observe with balloons, satellites, telescopes, ships, planes and the International Space Station. Festivals and events are planned along the path, and researchers will study how animals and plants react as darkness falls. The total eclipse will last about 1 1/2 hours as the shadow crosses at more than 1,500 mph; totality will range from under two minutes in Oregon to 2 minutes 44 seconds in Illinois and 2 1/2 minutes in South Carolina. Eye protection is needed except during totality. Large crowds are expected, and a partial eclipse will be visible elsewhere. Another eclipse is due in 2024.

Canon’s EOS M6, replacing the M3, targets entry-level mirrorless buyers wanting DSLR-like photo quality. It uses a 24.2MP Dual Pixel sensor and Digic 7 but differs from the M5 with an optional viewfinder, popup flash, repositioned non-locking mode dial and power lever, and lower-resolution 3.2-inch touchscreen. The lecture defines additive energy \(E(A,B)\) as the number of quadruples \(a_1,a_2\in A\), \(b_1,b_2\in B\) with \(a_1+b_1=a_2+b_2\). For one set, \(E(A)=E(A,A)\), analogous to 4-cycles. Writing \(r_{A,B}(x)\) as the number of ways \(x=a+b\), additive energy is the sum of squares of these representation counts. Trivial bounds are \(|A|^2 \le E(A) \le |A|^3\). Small doubling implies large additive energy: if \(|A+A|\le k|A|\), then \(E(A)\ge |A|^3/k\). The converse fails: a set can have large energy and large doubling if it contains a structured piece plus unstructured elements.

The Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers theorem states that large additive energy implies there is a large subset \(A'\subseteq A\) with small doubling, losing only polynomial factors in the error parameters. A two-set version says that if \(A,B\) have large energy, then large \(A'\subseteq A\), \(B'\subseteq B\) exist such that \(A'+B'\) is not too large; this implies the one-set version via the Ruzsa triangle inequality.

The proof goes through a graphical version: a dense bipartite graph \(G\) between \(A\) and \(B\) with small restricted sumset yields large \(A',B'\) whose unrestricted sumset is not too large. The lecture reduces the theorem to this graphical result, then proves it using a path-of-length-2 lemma and a path-of-length-3 lemma. The path-of-length-2 lemma uses dependent random choice; the path-of-length-3 lemma uses trimming and the length-2 lemma to find large subsets such that every pair has many length-3 paths. These paths give many representations \(a+b=x-y+z\) in the restricted sumset, proving the graphical version and hence Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers. The next lecture will discuss the sum-product problem.

Douglas Haig, an Arizona man, was charged with conspiracy to manufacture and sell armor-piercing ammunition without a license to Las Vegas gunman Stephen Paddock, who killed 58 people and wounded hundreds in an October 1 mass shooting before killing himself. Deion Sanders was to undergo a medical procedure Tuesday after saying he thought he was dealing with blood clots again. Scientists at The Rockefeller University kept a tiny sliver of gerbil cochlea alive and functional outside the body, directly observing how hair cells amplify sound. A custom chamber reproduced the tissue’s living environment with endolymph, perilymph, temperature, and voltage. Researchers witnessed ion-channel activity in hair bundles adding energy to vibrations and outer hair cells elongating and contracting through electromotility. They found that a Hopf bifurcation—a tipping point between stillness and oscillation—is key to the active process in the mammalian cochlea, supporting a principle seen across animals. The advance may improve understanding of hearing and lead to targeted experiments and future therapies for hearing loss.

NVIDIA Ampere adds BF16, TF32, and FP64 to Tensor Cores. FP16/BF16 train neural networks in mixed precision, matching FP32, and provide 16x FP32 throughput in A100. TF32 enables default Tensor Core AI training. AMP supports FP16 mixed precision.

The passage describes memory arrays and related structures. Memory arrays comprise vertically alternating tiers of insulative material and memory cells. Individual memory cells include a transistor with first and second source/drain regions, a channel region between them, and a gate operatively proximate the channel region; at least a portion of the channel region is horizontally oriented for horizontal current flow. The memory cells also include a capacitor with first and second electrodes and a capacitor insulator; the first electrode is electrically coupled to the first source/drain region. In various embodiments, second capacitor electrodes of multiple capacitors are electrically coupled together; a sense-line structure extends elevationally through the tiers and is electrically coupled to second source/drain regions of transistors in different memory cell tiers; and/or a capacitor-electrode structure extends elevationally through the tiers and is electrically coupled to second electrodes of capacitors in different memory cell tiers. Some tiers include two memory cells one directly above the other, or a gate and another gate one directly above the other. The passage also describes example manufacturing methods, staircase regions, conductive vias, and background on memory, capacitors, ferroelectric materials, and field effect transistors.

The President, speaking in Pittsburgh, says he returned as President to lay out a vision to rebuild the backbone of America through the eyes of hardworking people, union workers, and ordinary Americans. He cites 547,296 U.S. deaths from the virus and economic anxiety, and says the American Rescue Plan was passed to save jobs, businesses, and lives. He notes a goal of 200 million vaccination shots in the first 100 days, predicted 6 percent economic growth this year, and the possibility of cutting child poverty in half. He proposes the American Jobs Plan and American Families Plan, calling the Jobs Plan a once-in-a-generation investment and the largest American jobs investment since World War II. It would modernize transportation infrastructure, rail, transit, ports, water systems, broadband, power grids, housing, caregiving, and research and development; promote clean energy, electric vehicles, and Buy American; and create millions of jobs, estimated by some Wall Street outfits at over 18 million over four years. He describes a roughly $2 trillion investment over largely eight years. To pay for it, he says no one making under $400,000 will see federal taxes rise, and proposes raising the corporate tax to 28 percent, a 21 percent global minimum tax, eliminating deductions for offshoring, and increasing IRS enforcement. He calls for bipartisan cooperation and frames the effort as competition with China and a test for democracies.

Bear markets are described as longer and steeper than corrections, with high volatility and sharp rallies. They are shorter than bull markets; depending on criteria, the market spends about 80% in bull markets and 20% in bear markets. The S&P 500 spent 70% of the time above its 200-day moving average since 1960 and 85% since 2010. Bear markets lead to sudden drops but take longer to recover. The Louisiana Supreme Court declined to consider relator’s untimely writ. It held relator exhausted state post-conviction relief unless a narrow exception for successive applications applies, and ordered a minute entry.

β-Ga2O3 has promising electronic and mechanical properties but low thermal conductivity and is subject to strains from fabrication and operation. This work investigates thermal transport in β-Ga2O3 under uniaxial and biaxial uniform strain and strain gradients for 10-nm and 100-nm films, using first-principles-based neuroevolution potentials combined with phonon Boltzmann transport equation and a strain gradient model. The NEP reproduces DFT energies, forces, virial, phonon dispersions, and thermal conductivity. Uniform strain modulates thermal conductivity primarily through intrinsic phonon lifetime and three-phonon scattering, with b-axis strains producing the largest changes. Strain gradients suppress thermal conductivity more strongly than corresponding uniform tensile strain at 300 K. For 10-nm films, uniaxial ηzb 0.6%/nm reduces ka, kb, and kc by 31.8%, 35.3%, and 36.6%, respectively; biaxial ηzab 0.6%/nm reduces them by 42.4%, 43.3%, and 41.6%, about 1.5 times the equivalent uniform biaxial strain. Nanowire reductions reach 30.5%. The suppression is attributed to phonon spectral broadening, activation of forbidden scattering channels, localized vibrational modes, altered inter-mode frequency gaps, and expanded scattering phase space, with strain-gradient scattering dominating heat-carrying phonons below 10 THz. Unlike uniform strain, strain gradients reduce thermal conductivity without substantially changing thermal anisotropy. The findings identify strain gradients as essential for accurate thermal modeling in β-Ga2O3 and UWBGS device design and as potentially useful for thermal isolation in flexible electronics.

Initial fundraising can be stressful for startup owners. Understanding investor expectations can help create an attractive offering. Key areas to focus on include return on investment, equity terms, flexibility, and possible investor mentorship. The owner and team should present themselves confidently and persuasively, accept advice, and show experience, support, and market traction. Investors may consider industry experience, emerging markets, market gaps, or disruptive ideas. A detailed, coherent business plan with accurate facts and figures, supported projections, and analysis of competition, challenges, opportunities, and threats is crucial. Securing startup funding can be difficult, but mental preparation helps, and a confident, articulate, business-savvy owner inspires confidence.

UCLA researchers led by Heather Christofk and William Lowry found that hair follicle stem cell metabolism differs from other skin cells and that lactate production helps activate quiescent hair follicle stem cells. In mice, blocking lactate prevented activation, while increasing lactate accelerated activation and the hair cycle. Two drugs, RCGD423 and UK5099, promoted lactate production and hair growth in mice by activating JAK-Stat or blocking pyruvate entry into mitochondria. The findings may lead to new drugs for baldness or alopecia. The drugs were tested only preclinically and are not approved for humans. Patents were filed.

The lecture reviews digital communication as communication with a binary interface between source and destination, discussing standardization, layering, and no performance loss. It focuses on source coding, dividing it into sampling/expansion, quantization, and discrete coding, while assuming an error-free binary channel. It explains fixed-length codes and generalized fixed-length codes over blocks, noting fixed-length coding can approach log base 2 of m bits per source symbol as block length grows. It introduces variable-length codes, unique decodability, prefix-free codes, and binary trees, stating prefix-free codes are uniquely decodable and explaining the Kraft inequality as a condition on code word lengths. Finally, it defines discrete memoryless sources as independent, identically distributed sequences of letters from a finite alphabet.

The passage explains the shallow cross concept, which combines a basic route and a shallow drag route from opposite directions to conflict defenders and work against man and zone coverage. It stresses linebacker-level players and can provide a triangle read or a secondary QB progression. It is effective against man, Tampa 2, and Cover 4, but not traditional Cover 3. The passage lists route assignments: TB flare, TE basic at 10–12 yards, slot shallow drag at 3–4 yards, Z go, and X post, with adjustments to settle in zone voids. The QB reads downfield routes before progressing to post, drag, basic, and RB checkdown, and can go quickly to drag/basic versus blitz. Variations include Bunch X Shallow Cross and Empty Shallow Cross Post-Wheel. A video by Coach Shawn Liotta is also mentioned.

This MIT OCW lecture on the economics of green buildings recaps the triple bottom line—planet, people, and profit—and notes that over 80% of urban building stock is supplied by the private sector, so private incentives matter. Using Millennium Partners as an example, it shows changing developer priorities: San Francisco’s Millennium Tower had structural/foundation problems and lawsuits; Boston’s Millennium Place was pitched around job creation and downtown revitalization; Boston’s Millennium Tower around health and wellness; and Winthrop Center around sustainability and certifications including Passive House and LEED. The lecture models an office building’s cash flow and pro forma for three stakeholders—tenant, owner/investor, and developer—as a chain. Tenant willingness to pay can raise rent and lower vacancy; for owners, this can lower operating costs, risk, and cost of capital, raising NOI, market value, and NPV, which increases owner willingness to pay and developer sale price. Potential benefits include lower operating/maintenance costs, lower financing costs, easier permits, health/productivity, talent retention, ESG/reputation, and lower depreciation. Empirical ranges are given, including a rent premium mean around 6% and a price premium around 7.6%, with operational costs inconclusive. The lecture discusses construction cost premiums, passive versus active design, and dynamic cost premiums affected by skills, technology, and supply chains. It then introduces market failures: information asymmetry, split incentives, and externalities. Information asymmetry includes experience and credence goods, greenwashing, and adverse selection; certification such as LEED is described as helping solve information problems.

The passage states that higher education has emphasized program- and institution-level learning assessment since the mid-1980s, largely due to accreditation. While assessment literature and processes exist for credit-bearing courses and programs, less has been written about noncredit continuing education. Noncredit continuing education is defined as organized, systematic educational activities that do not lead to a degree or credential, including professional competency/licensure education, skill and knowledge building for career advancement or change, and personal enrichment.

The passage notes that lack of attention to assessment in noncredit continuing education has continued. A national survey of community college noncredit courses included no questions about student learning and outcomes. Satisfaction surveys remain prevalent, while direct learning assessments are less common. Credential-ending noncredit courses are plentiful, but the literature shows little evidence that other noncredit courses evaluate learning outcomes. The authors believe assessment is sparse because noncredit courses are often shorter, taught by field experts, and enroll learners with varying motivations, leading institutions not to invest limited resources in learning outcome assessment. Because noncredit education is common, in demand, and often fee-based, the authors suggest using assessment to guide curriculum and pedagogy and improve outcomes.

The paper discusses learning outcome statements, learning outcome-focused surveys, and direct assessment in noncredit continuing professional education. It recommends clear, measurable learning outcomes and lists considerations such as course duration, learners’ prior knowledge, use of frameworks, SMART outcomes, instructor collaboration, and learner feedback. It provides examples from University of Hawai‘i programs.

For surveys, the passage states that end-of-course surveys commonly measure satisfaction, instructor quality, or marketing effectiveness but typically do not evaluate learning outcomes. Learning outcome-focused survey questions can ask learners to self-rate their learning achievement; these are subjective, not direct assessments. Steps include selecting outcomes, adding self-rating questions, analyzing results, reviewing low results, and re-administering surveys. Retrospective pre-post surveys are suggested for short courses.

Direct assessment involves an expert evaluating a learner’s product or performance. In short and medium programs, the passage suggests adding quiz-type questions to course surveys, using simple 2-point scoring, and having learners complete activities or products that demonstrate learning. It recommends expert help for validity and reliability, fairness through transparency and reflection, and products that benefit learners.

The conclusion states that learning outcomes assessment provides information for decisions and that its scarcity in noncredit continuing education is a missed opportunity. It recommends well-crafted outcomes, learning outcome-focused survey questions, and direct assessment, and suggests micro-credentials or digital credentials to motivate learners. The authors report using assessment results for improvement plans, evidence of quality, and resource arguments.

The lecture finishes Markov chains and introduces dynamic programming. It reviews eigenvalues and eigenvectors, including a block upper-diagonal transition matrix whose determinant factors into transient and recurrent parts, so its eigenvalues are those of the transient matrix plus the recurrent matrix. It then discusses rewards or costs associated with states, expected rewards, expected aggregate reward over n steps, steady-state gain per step, and expected first passage time to a chosen state using a trapping state and linear equations. The passage explains the power play: a gap run with a backside guard pulling, a kick-out block, and back blocks to create angles at the point of attack. It can be run from many personnel groups and formations. Its strengths are creating angles and double teams at the point of attack, outnumbering the defense, and allowing less physically imposing offensive lines to run it if leverage and angles are mastered; double teams can be vertical or horizontal. Its weaknesses are backside pursuit and penetration, especially through the pulling guard’s gap. Against even fronts, the backside edge defender can turn the corner; against odd fronts, the Center’s point call is critical to avoid a free backside rusher. The passage also details blocking versus 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts and variations: Diamond Fullhouse and Gun Same-Side Power RPO.

In Bill Purswell v. State, the appellant was convicted of unlawfully transporting intoxicating liquor and sentenced to one year in the penitentiary. Officers hidden in a field at McElvain’s home saw appellant carrying a jug, arrested him, and found whiskey. The court held the search-and-seizure objection was unavailable because appellant did not own or possess the premises; the arrest was lawful for a felony committed in the officers’ presence, and the evidence was admissible. A general objection to the jury charge was insufficient. On rehearing, an unsupported affidavit alleging jury misconduct for appellant’s failure to testify did not show misconduct, and the judgment overruling the new trial was presumed supported by evidence. The judgment was affirmed and rehearing overruled.

In Dairylea Cooperative v. Lefkowitz, reviewing an order denying a petition to quash an Attorney-General subpoena duces tecum returnable before a grand jury, the court rejected the State’s cited authorities and addressed the merits. Petitioner claimed the Attorney-General lacked authority; the court agreed that the Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets had made a request, and affirmed without costs.

The present disclosure relates to improved transmitting devices and methods for radio resource selection and sensing, particularly for sidelink/V2X communication. It provides background on LTE, LTE-Advanced carrier aggregation, MAC/RRC/PHY layers, semi-persistent scheduling, D2D/ProSe, V2X services, and ProSe resource allocation. ProSe Mode 1 uses eNB-scheduled resources; Mode 2 uses UE-autonomous selection. For V2X sidelink, sensing and resource reservation support semi-persistent transmission. Sensing monitors scheduling assignments and may measure signal energy; reserved resources are excluded. Because half-duplex operation prevents sensing during transmissions, missed sensing opportunities are addressed by distinguishing primary subframes, where sensing was fully performed in corresponding sensing-window subframes, from secondary subframes, where sensing was not fully performed due to UE transmission. An autonomous resource allocation selects resources in primary subframes preferably over secondary subframes. Candidate ranking is performed separately for primary and secondary subframes and may consider time delay and energy prediction. The same approach can be applied to scheduling assignment transmissions, which may reserve resources for future scheduling assignments and/or data, either separately or commonly, and may indicate the reservation in the scheduling assignment.

The Arctic is described as a dynamic, interconnected system in which environmental, geopolitical, economic, and sociocultural factors interact and produce cascading effects. Systems thinking is presented as an educational framework for Arctic security that identifies components, interactions, and effects over time, contrasting with linear and reductionist approaches. Its principles include seeing the whole, recognizing patterns and connections, and identifying leverage points. The passage proposes a Systems Thinking Education Model with core principles, leverage points, and structured learning and assessment strategies. It recommends interdisciplinary curricula, scenario-based learning, concept mapping, simulations and wargaming, role-playing, interactive case studies, and assessment through scenario-based problem-solving, reflective analysis, and competency-based metrics. The framework is said to suit online graduate education and to help professionals anticipate unintended consequences, adapt strategies, and develop sustainable security approaches. The conclusion states that Arctic security challenges cannot be addressed in isolation and that systems thinking is necessary for holistic, forward-looking security education.

The DAWN-plasma study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter trial evaluating best supportive care plus convalescent plasma versus best supportive care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19, with a 2:1 randomization ratio. Convalescent plasma was given as 800–1000 mL in four doses, with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization and the second between 24 and 36 hours after the first two units. The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints assessed clinical status, time to sustained clinical improvement or discharge, mechanical ventilation or death, safety, quality of life, laboratory data, and vital signs. The study was conducted according to the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH Good Clinical Practice, with informed consent required before enrollment.

Digital technologies have transformed conventional business, and e-commerce can be grouped into B2B, B2C, C2C, C2B, E2E, G2C, G2B, C2G, B2G, and G2G. The online marketplace has its own ecosystem, and successful e-business requires strategy, digital business infrastructure management, digital marketing, e-supply chain management, e-procurement, and e-customer relationship management practices. Usability is defined as ease of using software to achieve its intended objective with effectiveness, efficiency, and user satisfaction; unusable e-business websites may fail to convert or retain customers. This study explores usability implications for e-business applications in Saudi Arabia, an emerging market ranked 46th on the UNCTAD B2C e-business index, where 58% of residents have shopped online and online shopping is estimated to reach $13.9 billion by 2021. The cross-sectional evaluation used two groups of 26 and 39 trained participants, eight popular retail and booking websites, 30-minute interactions, and a Likert questionnaire covering navigation, design, and content. Findings showed generally positive ratings but weaknesses in internal navigation, sitemap links, disappearing menus, orphan pages, language inconsistency, font size, layout simplicity, icon labeling, ordering, contact information, sitemap inclusion, and last-update dates. Cronbach Alpha was 0.66 for Group 1 and 0.79 for Group 2. The paper concludes Saudi e-business portals need improved usability, user-centered design, and content, and notes limitations of small sample size and limited generalizability.

The passage examines coherent control of 15N nuclear spins adjacent to the V−B center in isotopically enriched hBN. It reports pulsed electron-nuclear double resonance measurements on h10B15N that selectively address four nuclear spin states of the three identical spin-1/2 nitrogen nuclei. Hyperfine coupling induces state-dependent electron-nuclear mixing, lifts degeneracy, produces α, β, and γ transition shifts, and enhances the nuclear g-factor, increasing the nuclear Rabi frequency by about 116 compared with pure nuclear spin states. Rabi oscillations have coherence times exceeding 10 µs, and ENDOR linewidths are as narrow as 1.2 MHz. Optical pumping causes loss of nuclear polarization, thermalizing the nuclear spin within 1 µs, tentatively assigned to the 3E′′ excited state. Magnetic-field-dependent measurements and simulations support fitted hyperfine tensors. The authors conclude that nearest-neighbor 15N nuclear spins of V−B centers are a controllable resource for quantum sensing and hBN-based quantum devices.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court affirmed the Commonwealth Court, holding that the Nonpublic Elementary and Secondary Education Act (“Act 109”) is constitutional and enforceable as applied to nonsectarian nonpublic schools. The Department of Education argued that Act 109 was held unconstitutional in its entirety in Lemon v. Kurtzman, that it was not severable, that it had been impliedly repealed, and that it could not be constitutionally administered. The court rejected these contentions. It concluded that Lemon I and Lemon II held Act 109 unconstitutional only as applied to sectarian nonpublic schools, not nonsectarian schools. It held Act 109 was severable under statutory construction principles, the Act’s severability clause, and its legislative purpose. It also held Act 109 was not impliedly repealed by subsequent legislation and that determining whether a school is sectarian or nonsectarian does not cause excessive entanglement with religion. EAGEN, J., dissented.

The device offers NAP and PD low-power modes. To unlock RST_PWRCTL_REG, write 69h to address 05h; NAP is enabled with NAP_EN and CONVST/CS high, exits on a falling edge after tNAP_WKUP, and PD is enabled with PWRDN, powers down analog blocks while retaining interface and registers, and requires clearing PWRDN and waiting tPWRUP. Layout guidance covers analog/digital partitioning, bypassing AVDD/DVDD, and decoupling REFCAP and REFIO. The passage also includes related documentation, support resources, trademarks, ESD caution, revision history, and mechanical/packaging/orderable information.

Bill Belichick took responsibility for penalties and defensive lapses in North Carolina’s 38–10 loss to Clemson. He cited early big plays, 399 Clemson passing yards, and three illegal formations as costly. UNC’s offense struggled, with Max Johnson throwing for 213 yards and no touchdowns while converting 2-of-11 third downs. Belichick declined to evaluate the rebuild, praised the team’s effort, and said they must keep grinding and improve.

Moscow denies involvement in the poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal, while UK officials say Russia violated the Chemical Weapons Convention and have evidence it continued producing and stockpiling Novichok. The passage calls for stronger Western sanctions and action against Russian assets hidden in the West.

The article studies braiding of topological edge states in coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains protected by inversion symmetry and time-dependent interchain symmetry. In a double-coupled chain, two pairs of edge states exhibit a twisted spectrum and symmetry-protected adiabatic evolution, enabling ratio-tunable topological transport from one chain end to two ends of another chain. Extending to triple-coupled chains yields non-Abelian braiding of three edge-state pairs, operation-sequence-dependent topological transport, and non-Abelian Hong-Ou-Mandel interference that generates spatially entangled two-particle NOON states. The results are discussed as extendable to bulk states and experimentally feasible in adiabatically modulated photonic waveguide arrays.

Speedy floated on the stock market in March 1999, and Russell Down became chief executive in summer 2015 after joining as group finance director and becoming CEO three months later following a profit warning. Down found financial and operational challenges, including unreliable asset hire information after an IT upgrade, lost focus on smaller customers, and a cost strategy that moved equipment testing and repair to regional superstores, creating backlogs and leaving more than 50% of products unavailable in September 2015. Under Down, the company focused on customers, costs, product availability, and asset utilisation. Results for the six months to end-September showed profits up 58.8% to £10.8m, reduced net debt, and improved ROCE. It reintroduced staff surveys, used customer surveys, and made two powered access acquisitions, Prolift Access Limited and Platform Sales & Hire Limited. Down says banking partners support its strategy and it is in a financially strong position for sustainable profitable growth.

Clark County schools are individually deciding how to use their share of new state spending targeting English language learners who also live in poverty. The Nevada Legislature approved a weighted funding formula allocating $1,200 per eligible student based on bottom-quartile test scores, English learner status or poverty, and not attending a school already receiving Zoom or Victory funding. Clark County received more than $34 million of the $36 million total; Garside Junior High is receiving more than $450,000 and is finalizing spending plans, with teacher suggestions including more after-school tutoring and technology. Spending will be tracked separately and analyzed for student achievement.

Bovine mastitis is the dairy industry's most expensive disease; antibiotics kill bacteria but cannot restore damaged mammary tissue. Cornell researchers are investigating secretions from bovine mammary stem cells as an alternative therapy. Their report found these secreted factors promote new blood vessel formation and cell migration, protect epithelial cells from bacterial toxins, and include antimicrobial peptides. They were more effective against toxins from gram-negative bacteria, potentially complementing antibiotics effective against gram-positive bacteria. The researchers plan to test whether the secretome works in cows with mastitis.

Hyundai and Kia set up a V2X vehicle-road communication system on a 14-kilometer road with seven intersections in Hwaseong to advance autonomous driving. They plan to research its validity and gather data by year-end, aiming to operate it in a government infrastructure project by 2020.

The message transmits for Senate ratification a treaty of annexation concluded Feb. 14, 1893, between Secretary of State John W. Foster and Hawaiian commissioners. The provisional treaty leaves related questions to future adjustment. It says the monarchy’s overthrow was not promoted by the U.S., attributes it to Queen Liliuokalani’s policy, calls the monarchy effete and restoration undesirable if not impossible. It favors annexation over a protectorate to secure U.S. interests and prevent other powers from securing the islands, urges prompt action, and notes accompanying correspondence.

Caitlin Bassett says the build-up to Saturday’s Super Netball grand final, where Sunshine Coast Lightning face Greater Western Sydney at Brisbane Entertainment Centre, is unlike anything in her career. The 29-year-old has waited a fortnight and had sleepless nights. Geva Mentor and Laura Langman advised her to soak it up. Mentor may face Kristina Brice and has trained against 215cm Junior Levi.

RSI, developed by Welles Wilder and introduced in Commodities in June 1978, is an oscillator measuring gains and losses over n days on a 0–100 scale; low readings are considered more bullish than high readings, and it is mainly used as an overbought/oversold indicator. The article says RSI works best on stocks and mean-reverting assets and should be combined with a second indicator, variable, or filter. It reports that backtests over 20 years show RSI works reasonably well on stocks and stock indices, with shorter time frames generally best and settings between 2–6; examples include buying below 15 and selling above 85, or buying below 30 and selling above 70 for a 10-day RSI. Daily bars are described as best overall, though one section says hourly bars are better for day trading while another says intraday data is not particularly useful. RSI divergences are said to be visible only in hindsight and hard to quantify. Variants include Connors RSI and Cutler’s RSI. RSI 14 reacts more quickly than RSI 21. A QQQ backtest showed about 300 trades, 0.82% average gain, 71% win rate, and 23% worst drawdown.

The passage explains how to introduce corner kick offense in soccer. A corner kick occurs when the defending team touches the ball over its own end line, and the attacking team restarts play. Coaches are advised to teach Law 17, demonstrate fundamental corner kick skills, introduce a play with three designated positions—corner taker, receiver, and cover man—and rotate players through all positions. It also covers right-footed and left-footed kicks from right and left corner arcs, assigning specific players, and adding passive then active defenders. Coaching tips include having the referee point to the correct arc, waiting for referee acknowledgment, and encouraging longer, directed, lofted balls as players improve.

The passage discusses Landor v. Louisiana Department of Corrections and Public Safety, in which Damon Landor, a Rastafarian inmate, had his dreadlocks shaved by prison officials despite prior accommodation. Landor sued under RLUIPA, but a lower court held that the statute does not authorize money damages as “appropriate relief.” The Supreme Court agreed to hear the case, and the passage argues Landor should win because the lower court’s reading would gut RLUIPA. It also criticizes common narratives that religious-freedom cases are always partisan and divisive, benefit only a majority, or involve conservative culture-war foot-soldiers. It notes many important religious-liberty decisions have been unanimous and says religious freedom is a foundational right for all.
San Diego police pursued a wanted shooting suspect in City Heights; the suspect crashed into Central Elementary School and fire station fences and was arrested nearby.

This retrospective analytical study included 671 patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI) from 07/01/2017–17/12/2018: 212 females (31.59%) and 459 males (68.40%). The mean age was 46.016 years, and mean hospitalization was 12.75 days. Statistical analysis used the t test, one- and two-way ANOVA, and Pearson correlation. The most frequently reported TBI cause in both women and men was domestic accident. Men were affected by TBI at an earlier age than women, and men were hospitalized longer than women. Patients living in the village were at increased risk of TBI, and total hospitalization days were associated with age. Alcohol-related brain injury occurred in 139 patients. Of 671 patients, 198 required surgical treatment, 668 required conservative therapy, and 3 required blood transfusion. The study concluded that domestic accidents were the most frequent cause of TBI in men and women, men were affected earlier, village residence increased TBI risk, and gender plays a crucial role in TBI severity and incidence/post-TBI outcomes and complications. A limitation was the absence of a control group.

The passage lists 1945 U.S. foreign-policy documents and developments. It cites Truman statements on China, a Department of National Defense, and immigration of certain displaced persons and refugees. It details State Department organization and personnel changes, including resignations and appointments involving Stettinius, Byrnes, Grew, Acheson, Hurley, Marshall, and Hull. It also describes Executive Order 9608 terminating the Office of War Information and transferring international information functions to the State Department, and Executive Order 9621 transferring OSS Research and Analysis and Presentation Branches to State while abolishing OSS and transferring remaining activities to the War Department. It references related statements and proposals on international and overseas information services.

Blackwell introduces advanced power gating, separate voltage rails, new clock gating, accelerated frequency switching, and low-latency sleep; it is 10x faster to enter the deepest sleep state than Ada, with up to 50% power savings observed in an SLM inference example. DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame using a new AI model that is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame, alongside enhanced Flip Metering. DLSS 4 also moves to transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, lighting detail, and motion detail. Blackwell supports neural shaders, the Cooperative Vectors API, and RTX neural technologies including Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. The GB202, GB203, and GB205 GPUs target multiple graphics segments, with RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070 specifications compared to prior generations.

Sodium cumenesulfonate is a water-soluble hydrotrope with hydrophilic and hydrophobic parts, available in powder and liquid forms. It increases solubility, lowers cloud point, promotes ingredient compatibility, and moderates viscosity. It is used as a solubilizer and cloud point depressor in cleaners, drilling, laundry, detergents, and in metal processing, oilfield, and hydrogen sulfide scavenging. Raw material price volatility, declining R&D, and health hazards such as eye and respiratory irritation may hamper the market. Industrialization and household detergent use in emerging economies drive demand. Liquid form and household application held major market shares in 2015 and are expected to dominate.

U.S. stocks sank about 2% on Monday, with the Dow shedding nearly 400 points, as Facebook led a technology selloff on reports that a political consultancy gained inappropriate access to data on more than 50 million users. Facebook fell 7.1%, while Nasdaq, S&P tech, and FAANG stocks declined. All 11 major S&P sectors were lower amid trade-war worries and a Federal Reserve meeting.

Frost Brown Todd and Gibbons plan to merge in January, forming FBT Gibbons, a firm with 800 lawyers in 25 offices. Frost Brown Todd currently has more than 650 lawyers in 18 offices; the merger adds Northeast offices including New York and New Jersey. Robert Sartin will be chairman, while Adam Hall and Peter Torcicollo will be co-managing partners. Leaders said the focus is integration and possible further growth. Merger discussions followed a retreat hosted by the Zeughauser Group.

Stephen Hawking, a theoretical physicist, died, a family spokesman said. His children said his work and legacy will live on. Hawking wrote the best-selling “A Brief History of Time,” lived with ALS for more than 50 years, communicated through an electronic voice synthesizer, continued scientific work, appeared on television, and married a second time. He sought a unified theory of physics, later suggested one might not exist, and was portrayed in the film “The Theory of Everything.”

Stipulated annuities and admission of the Kingdom as a State of the Union were objected to; before conclusion, Kamehameha III died in February 1855 and was succeeded by a prince unfavorable to the project, so the treaty failed. A July 20, 1855 reciprocity treaty concluded at Washington by Marcy and Lee failed Senate ratification despite apparent committee favor. Later correspondence chiefly concerned claims and routine matters; in 1863 the diplomatic rank was raised to minister resident and James McBride was appointed. Civil War attention deferred reciprocity. In 1866 Queen Emma visited the United States. In 1867 McCook was instructed to revive the 1855 treaty on terms more liberal to the United States; a May 21, 1867 San Francisco treaty was approved by the President but failed Senate ratification. McCook raised annexation; Seward authorized confidential soundings, said annexation was preferred over reciprocity if they conflicted, and warned that annexation supporters would oppose reciprocity. The Lackawanna’s presence delayed ratification; the treaty was ratified July 30, 1867, but the U.S. Senate rejected it June 1, 1870.

The speaker takes the presidential oath, asks God for wisdom, and seeks support to restore harmony and preserve free institutions, stating he will not seek reelection. He says the recent presidential contest ended with submission to the majority’s constitutional will. Congress left slavery in the Territories to the people under the Constitution, with Kansas admitted with or without slavery as its constitution provides; a timing dispute is before the Supreme Court and he will submit to its decision. He favors popular sovereignty, hopes agitation ends, warns disunion would harm all sections, and stresses preserving the Constitution and Union free from corruption. He addresses the Treasury surplus, tariff adjustment, public lands for actual settlers, strict construction of federal powers, a military road for Pacific defense, and foreign policy of peace, justice, noninterference, and no entangling alliances. He then takes the oath.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated February 16, 2016. On that date, Apple entered into an underwriting agreement with representatives of several underwriters for the issuance and sale of Floating Rate Notes due 2019 and 2021 and Fixed Rate Notes due 2018, 2019, 2021, 2023, 2026, 2036, and 2046. The notes have specified aggregate principal amounts, interest rates, interest payment dates, and maturity dates. They are issued under an indenture dated April 29, 2013, and an officer’s certificate dated February 23, 2016, and are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. Apple furnished related agreements and forms as exhibits, along with other exhibits. The report is dated February 23, 2016, and signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President, Chief Financial Officer.

Synaptics announced plans to mass produce an optical in-display fingerprint sensor, called Clear ID, embedded under a phone screen to ease unlocking bezel-less smartphones. The company claims it is twice as fast as 3D facial recognition, requires one touch, and allows unlocking from any angle. It says consumers prefer front fingerprint authentication, though the timing of its smartphone appearance remains uncertain.

Bemidji (14-6) beat the Prowlers 77-45, leading 45-25 at halftime. Caden Rolfes scored 18, Linaes Whiting 17, Caleb Carlson 14, and Jeremy Beberg 10. Coach Travis Peterson called it a big step forward. BHS plays at Fergus Falls on Feb. 18.

The passage defines container APIs as including the function executed when a container runs, calls to other services, and provided HTTP or other APIs. It argues sidecars should be modular and reusable, with stable APIs; changing parameter names or units can break users. It advises documenting container images using Dockerfiles, EXPOSE, ENV defaults, and LABEL metadata from the Label Schema project. It summarizes the sidecar pattern, then introduces the ambassador pattern, where an ambassador brokers interactions between an application container and the outside world. Ambassador uses include sharded services with twemproxy and Redis, service brokering, and request splitting or experimentation with nginx. It then describes the adapter pattern, where an adapter container modifies an application interface to a common one, with monitoring examples using Prometheus for Redis, logging normalization with Fluentd, and MySQL health checks. It introduces multi-node patterns and microservices, contrasting them with monoliths, citing reliability, agility, API contracts, independent scaling, and debugging or design challenges. It describes replicated load-balanced stateless services, readiness probes, session-tracked services, application-layer replicated services, caching layers with Varnish, rate limiting, and SSL termination with nginx. It covers sharded services and caches, sharding functions, determinism and uniformity, selecting keys, consistent hashing, and hot sharding. It describes scatter/gather for parallel request servicing, including document search, leaf sharding, overhead and straggler problems, and replicated sharded scatter/gather for reliability and scale. Finally, it discusses event-driven request handling and function-as-a-service or serverless computing.

Florida State University President John Thrasher named a 15-member committee, chaired by Renisha Gibbs, to review FSU policy on campus names and markers, including statues. The President’s Advisory Panel on University Namings and Recognitions will seek input from the Florida State community and determine criteria for naming policies. The campus chapter of Students for a Democratic Society has sought removal of the Francis Eppes statue. The committee meets next week; meetings will be public, and a website will launch soon.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU is NVIDIA’s 8th-generation data center GPU, based on the Ampere architecture GA100, designed for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads in cloud data centers, servers, clusters, edge systems, workstations, and supercomputers. It builds on Tesla V100 and adds third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary support; Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitioning into as many as seven GPU Instances; 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth; 40 MB L2 cache; third-generation NVLink with 600 GB/sec total bandwidth; PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV; asynchronous copy and barriers; task graph acceleration; L2 cache residency controls; and improved error/fault detection, isolation, and containment. A100 supports CUDA 11, CUDA-X libraries, NGC containers, Kubernetes, and Magnum IO/Mellanox InfiniBand and Ethernet. The passage reports performance improvements over V100 for AI training/inference and HPC applications, including TF32, FP16/FP32, BF16, FP64, and sparse Tensor Core operations. MIG provides QoS and fault isolation for CSPs and multi-tenant use and supports vGPU migration. A100 is used in NVIDIA DGX A100, HGX A100, and EGX systems. The passage also describes A100 architecture in depth, including GA100 GPU composition, SM features, Tensor Core data types, sparsity, memory hierarchy, NVLink, PCIe Gen 4, MIG architecture, CUDA advances, NVJPG, optical flow accelerator, atomics, NVDEC, and the DGX A100 software stack. An appendix provides a sparse neural network primer.

Federal aviation safety workers, including air traffic controllers and TSA agents, are working without pay during a government shutdown, though employees say flying remains safe. Workers report strain, missed paychecks, furloughed colleagues, less efficient work, possible slower repairs, and fears of more airport delays and cancellations. FAA and TSA officials say safety remains protected, while workers worry about firings, union rights, and unpaid commuting. A union leader says his group will not organize sick-outs.

The 23rd BMO Okanagan Marathon is expected to draw close to 3,000 participants to Kelowna this weekend. Events include the marathon, half marathon, 10 km, timed 5 km, ABC Kids activities and a 1 km kids run. The Boston Marathon-qualifying course runs along Okanagan Lake. New features are a timed 5 km and beverage garden. Events start Saturday and continue Sunday from City Park, with race package pickup available. The event supports The Sunshine Foundation of Canada.

The passage describes a robotic and/or navigation-assisted surgical system and tool assembly for spinal procedures, including preparation of a vertebra and placement of implants such as tap markers or pedicle screws. The system includes a manipulator, navigation system with localizer and trackers, controllers, drive couplers, interchangeable working tools, and an elongate sleeve. Drive couplers removably couple working tools to an input device and can transfer rotational and/or translational movement. Working tools include scalpels, dilators, burs, drills, tap inserters, and tap markers. The elongate sleeve can be placed in soft tissue to provide a working channel, retract tissue, and prevent tissue ingress; it may include a movable distal feature that opens when a working tool advances and may include bone-engaging spikes. Methods include positioning and advancing a screw and sleeve along an insertion trajectory, advancing the screw relative to the sleeve, and disengaging the screw from the sleeve. Tracking devices may be removably coupled to working tools, including by magnetic coupling or a ratcheting mechanism, to track or relocalize bony anatomy and account for movement during procedures such as discectomy and cage placement.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 27, 2022, reporting first fiscal quarter results for the period ended December 25, 2021. The filing states that Apple issued a related press release, attached as Exhibit 99.1, and is signed by CFO Luca Maestri.

Anjuna police registered two unnatural death cases involving tourists from Tamil Nadu and Kerala. Pravin Sundaram, 28, from Tamil Nadu, collapsed in Vagator’s parking area and was declared dead; police have not ruled out drug overdose. Abdul, a Kerala native, was brought to a private hospital by an unknown person and died. Autopsies were sent to GMC, and viscera preserved. Police are investigating and tracing the person in the second case. A minister called the deaths unfortunate and sought stopping outdoor music parties.

A New York panel unanimously recommended that the state Medicaid program pause coverage of Sarepta’s Duchenne muscular dystrophy treatment Elevidys, following a safety controversy. The board said the state should wait for the FDA to add safety and clinical trial data to the drug’s labeling and first evaluate a forthcoming regimen to mitigate liver failure risk. New York will still cover some patients under 21 case-by-case through Medicaid’s EPSDT benefit if medically necessary. Adoption of the recommendation is uncertain, and other states will likely watch the outcome.

The St. John’s Edge defeated the London Lightning 123-110 in Game 4, tying the best-of-seven NBL Canada Central Division final 2-2. Game 5 is Thursday in St. John’s, and Game 6 will be Sunday in London. London led early but played poorly, was outscored in the paint 50-38, and missed 13 free throws. Royce White and Ryan Anderson tugged at each other at the end of the third quarter. Edge coach Jeff Dunlap adjusted by starting Alex Johnson; Charles Hinkle and Coron Williams scored 28 each, and Ryan Reid had 22. White led London with 32 points and Anderson added 21. Coach Keith Vassell took responsibility and said he would revisit his adjustments and short bench. Before Game 4, a complaint and NBL investigation concerned an allegation that a Lightning player used a homophobic slur in Game 3.

The speaker recalls playing on pavement, outdoor ice rinks, and with buddies. They say being in the game is a good opportunity, note yesterday would have been nice, and focus on finishing Wednesday. They stress putting past games behind them and confidence as a good road team. Keys include forechecking, getting pucks deep, making it hard on defensemen, closing gaps in the D zone, and being tough on forwards. They thought the team played well overall, though the opponent scored quick third-period goals, and praise both goalies. They mention travel, rest, work, getting on the ice, and looking forward to an important player returning. They plan a simple, consistent road game, getting pucks in deep to give themselves a chance to win, call the home crowd unreal, and say it is business as usual on the road.

Mums and children with Down’s syndrome made an emotional Carpool Karaoke-style video, seen over 600,000 times, praised by Christina Perri and James Corden. Inspired by a Makaton SingingHands video for World Down’s Syndrome Day, it features A Thousand Years and was organized by the DesignerGenes Facebook group, originating with Coventry mum Becky Carless.

This qualitative case study examined Turkish teachers’ opinions about the Turkish course and technological tools used during pandemic distance education. It was conducted with 20 Turkish teachers in Hazro district of Diyarbakır using semi-structured interviews, with data analyzed descriptively. Findings showed that 45% of participants thought education progressed, 20% thought it did not, 25% thought it progressed but was insufficient, and 10% were neutral. Regarding EBA/EBA TV, 10 participants saw them as advantageous, 3 considered them insufficient due to infrastructure problems, and 7 did not comment. No participant found distance education fully efficient: 30% found it not efficient and 70% not efficient enough. Target behaviors and achievements were viewed as partially achieved; lack of internet and materials was a major factor. Problems included students’ lack of equipment, parents with multiple school-age children, infrastructure problems, and teachers’ attendance/time issues. For Turkish lessons, needs identified were technological materials, books/dictionaries, both, and practice/activity. Communication was mostly by phone, especially WhatsApp, followed by Zoom and EBA. Teacher qualifications included subject knowledge, planning, self-expression, empathy, activity orientation, attention to individual differences, computer skills, technological currency, and agenda following. Suggestions included reducing textbook volume, establishing drama classes/libraries, compensation programs, hybrid education, improving rural infrastructure, developing EBA, technology seminars, and cooperation among teacher, student, and parent. The study concluded teachers were not fully ready for distance education but managed within available means; attendance and material problems reduced efficiency and achievement. Recommendations included resolving infrastructure and material inequalities, updating EBA, using distance education to support face-to-face education, professional development, reading activities, considering student characteristics, and rearranging post-pandemic targets.

Topshop recalled all display stands at tills nationwide after a 10-year-old boy, Kaden Reddick, died from serious head injuries in an incident involving a store display barrier in its Reading store. Police are investigating the circumstances, with the council working closely with them.

The speaker calls for sharing the majesty of the orderly transfer of power and says this can be a moment of beginning. Forces are converging to make possible the hope that man’s deepest aspirations can be realized, and the times are on the side of peace. America will soon mark its 200th anniversary, and mankind will begin the third millennium. The speaker cites achievements in science, industry, agriculture, broader wealth, economic management, and freedom for black and white, and praises America’s youth. Yet the crisis is spiritual: rich in goods but ragged in spirit, caught in war wanting peace, torn by division wanting unity. The answer is spiritual, found in simple things such as goodness, decency, love, and kindness. Government will listen and work with the people on employment, housing, education, cities, rural areas, environment, and quality of life. The speaker says freedom requires shared destiny and going forward together, black and white together, and with all mankind. Goals include peace, negotiation, open communication, cooperation, and strength as needed. The Apollo view of Earth showed that man’s destiny is not divisible and lies on Earth.

The U.S. FDA announced a crackdown on illegal sales of Juul e-cigarettes to teens, including nationwide undercover enforcement at stores and online. Juul products resemble computer flash drives, contain high nicotine, and hold more than half the e-cigarette market. Since March, FDA checks found 40 violations and issued 40 warning letters. The FDA contacted eBay, which removed Juul listings, and asked Juul’s maker for documents explaining youth appeal; it plans similar requests and further enforcement against misleading marketing to minors. The FDA also cited education and efforts to make tobacco products less toxic, addictive, and appealing.

Diana Beresford-Kroeger lives with her husband Christian on a 160-acre property near Merrickville, where they built a house and planted rare plants and trees. Born in Ireland, she lost her family at 11 and was taught old Irish teachings about nature. She earned science degrees from University College Cork and studied at the University of Connecticut before pursuing a doctorate at Carleton and a diploma in experimental surgery while doing cardiovascular research at the University of Ottawa. After moving to Merrickville, a wedding gift of trees helped start her arboretum and organic garden, Carrigliath. She and Christian classified local species and saved what they could. She has written books and spoken worldwide. Her latest project, the Canadian-made film Call of the Forest, addresses deforestation and climate change, and her Bioplan proposes planting one tree per person yearly for six years. The film is based on The Global Forest and has drawn large audiences and award nominations. She hopes to help future generations.

Ravita Meghwar, a Hindu girl in Pakistan, is now Gulnaz Shah, married and Muslim. Her family says she was drugged, abducted, and forcibly converted; she says she eloped by choice. Recent years have seen many cases in Sindh of Hindu girls converting to Islam, which Hindus say are forcible, follow similar patterns, and target minors. Hindus are about 2 percent of Pakistan’s population; in Sindh, over 6 percent. Some Hindus are reassessing their place in Pakistan as hardline religious groups gain influence and minorities have little voice. Forced-conversion cases are mostly reported in Sindh, where lower-caste, low-income Hindus face discrimination and economic servitude. Muslim religious activists defend conversions as blessings; shrines, seminaries, clerics, and politicians back couples, and girls’ testimony often settles cases. In 2012, cases including Rinkle Kumari reached the Supreme Court, which allowed the women to live with Muslim husbands. Sindh’s 2016 bill banning forcible conversions and conversions under 18 was not signed after religious opposition. Activists use underage-marriage law. Mass conversions and migration of Hindus, including to India, are reported.

The speaker says he knew the coach could be a head coach, calling him tough, honest, hardworking, and funny. He notes the opponent has good defense and depth, making it a challenging but familiar task requiring hard work. He feels old, waited years for this chance, and wants to enjoy it with a good team sharing the same dream. He praises Canadian hockey fans and expects Ottawa’s crowd to be loud like Edmonton’s. He says goalies are big, athletic, and hard to beat, needing perfect shots. He likes his team’s forward depth, younger lines, and Pahlsson’s line scoring key goals. He says age is just numbers and he feels like the younger players. He repeats Pronger’s view that the small market keeps Giggy from more attention, and jokes about insurance.

A high school senior describes being disengaged and disconnected during his first two years, considering dropping out. After getting a job, he maintained a 4.0 GPA, connected schoolwork to the real world, learned durable skills, and gained confidence. He says research links youth employment, internships, and apprenticeships to better outcomes. The passage notes many youth aged 16–24 are not in education, employment, or training, with higher rates among young men and African American youth. It says apprenticeships and internships are rare and youth unemployment is high. It mentions state tax credits and transportation or scheduling barriers, and a Nevada bill supporting NEETs that did not get a hearing. The author argues governments and leaders should incentivize businesses to provide youth jobs, internships, and apprenticeships, benefiting the whole community.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated August 1, 2017, reporting that it issued a press release on its financial results for the third fiscal quarter ended July 1, 2017, and a related data sheet. The filing includes Exhibit 99.1 (press release) and Exhibit 99.2 (data sheet), and is signed by CFO Luca Maestri.

The speaker says the team played two periods of perfect Dallas Stars hockey but made critical puck-support mistakes in the third period that created problems and gave the opponent odd-man rushes. He says the team hurt itself and that these are correctable mistakes, and he expects the team to return and play hard on Thursday. He says the focus is bringing the game back to their building, not winning three games. He notes past junior comebacks but says this situation is different because the opposing goaltender has been good. He praises the opponent’s speed, size, commitment to defend, and several players, saying their ability to get to loose pucks beat the team. He discusses the mental and emotional challenge of facing elimination, saying the dressing room and leadership must supply passion, and the team must stay with the program, avoid trying to hit home runs, and raise its level when the game goes up. He also comments on coaching, player roles, and past series.

Saturday nights have been the ratings battleground between BBC1 and ITV for over 50 years. Winning the competitive early-evening slot, especially for the BBC, demonstrates its entertainment remit and still offers family viewing. New shows usually fail, so schedules rely on old favourites. Getting ratings is not easy, and only a few entertainment shows have lasted. Few shows created in the last decade have succeeded, apart from The Voice UK. After Blind Date ended, Strictly and The X Factor revived Saturday entertainment; X Factor attracts younger viewers, Strictly the rest. When such shows end, formats and hosts become boring. Controllers seek new formats and talent, but nothing similar has emerged. New shows often fail; controllers rely on instinct, producers’ records, and hope.

Based on 5 analyst opinions, the mean 52-week target is $8.8, with a high of $10 and low of $6; the latest close was $5.94. The average brokerage recommendation is 1, with 3 recommendations, and its industry rank by ABR is 202 out of 265. Combination defenses can devastate unprepared teams. They primarily deny or limit touches of outstanding offensive players and serve as surprise tactics; timing and surprise are critical to success. Common types include Box & One, Diamond & One, and Triangle & Two.

Pre-existing depression/anxiety and psychoactive drug use may raise long-term opioid use risk, especially with prior substance use disorders; harmful opioid outcomes also predicted it. Nearly 1.7% of opioid-prescription patients became long-term users, with higher risks from ADHD medications, prior substance use, and prior opioid use disorders. Researchers suggest mental health assessment/intervention with long-term opioid therapy.

The far-right AfD is gaining support in Bavaria, presumably prompting Interior Minister Horst Seehofer to revolt against Chancellor Angela Merkel. Merkel agreed to a deal making it harder for migrants to enter Germany, involving asylum transit camps along three Austrian borders. Asylum seekers who already applied in other EU countries will be held at transit centers; rejected asylum seekers will be sent back to their countries after negotiations, or to Austria if no deal is reached. The deal, meant to save Merkel’s coalition and appease Bavarian allies, has raised doubts in the SPD. Austria and Italy have refused migrants, and other EU states also refuse immigrants, signaling a European rift. Germany once took in over 1.4 million refugees in 2015 but now takes about 10,000 monthly.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU is based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture GA100 GPU, fabricated on TSMC’s 7nm N7 process, with 54.2 billion transistors and an 826 mm² die. The A100 includes 108 SMs, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 40 GB HBM2 memory, 1555 GB/s memory bandwidth, and 40 MB L2 cache. Its third-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary data types, and a fine-grained structured sparsity feature can double Tensor Core throughput. The passage reports speedups over Tesla V100, including 10x faster TF32 than V100 FP32 FMA, 2.5x FP16/FP32 mixed precision, 2.5x FP64, and up to 20x sparse INT8. A100 adds Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), which can partition one GPU into as many as seven GPU Instances with isolated compute and memory resources. It also adds third-generation NVLink with twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, improved error and fault detection, isolation, and containment, asynchronous copy and barriers, CUDA Task Graph acceleration, L2 cache residency controls, Compute Data Compression, NVJPG decode, an optical flow accelerator, improved atomics, and five NVDEC units. The passage also describes DGX A100, an eight-A100-GPU system delivering 5 PFLOPS with NVSwitch, Mellanox ConnectX-6 HDR InfiniBand, and an optimized software stack, and notes support for NVIDIA Magnum IO and Mellanox Interconnect Solutions.

This MIT OCW lecture reviews binary detection. It considers a one-bit transmission through channel encoding, modulation, noise, demodulation, and sampling, producing an observation v from which the detector guesses hypothesis H (0 or 1). Hypothesis testing, decision making, and decoding are described as the same thing. The detector assumes a known probability model and uses MAP to minimize error probability; MAP rules compare a posteriori probabilities and become likelihood-ratio threshold tests with threshold p1/p0. For 2PAM/antipodal signaling, v is plus or minus a plus Gaussian noise of variance n0/2; the log-likelihood ratio is 4av/n0, and the decision compares v with a threshold. Error probability uses the Q function; for equal priors it is q(sqrt(2Eb/n0)). Non-antipodal signals have error determined by distance between points, while shifting away from the midpoint wastes energy, e.g., 3 dB if c equals a. For real antipodal vectors in white Gaussian noise, the inner product with a is sufficient and corresponds to a matched filter; error reduces to the one-dimensional case.

The NPD Group identified five trends shaping Britain’s £57 billion foodservice industry in 2018: smartphone click & collect, which may reduce order and wait times and require efficiency and express-lane changes; investment in and training of staff to improve customer satisfaction, loyalty and profits; tiered and personalized loyalty schemes with premium or VIP offers; avoiding broken brand promises by aligning quality, service, support and marketing with consumer expectations; and recommendations from sources including staff, technology and customer data. Cyril Lavenant said the trends depend on innovation, seeing opportunities and responding well, with potential in click & collect, staff, loyalty and recommendations, while brand promises must be delivered because disappointed consumers can spread the word quickly on social media.

Three chemists, including one from UC Berkeley, Susumu Kitagawa, and Richard Robson, won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry Wednesday for developing metal-organic frameworks since the 1990s. These combine metal ions and carbon-based molecules; over 100,000 exist and can harvest water or store toxic gases.

Defendant appealed, disputing a trial agreement, raising the statute of frauds, and claiming warranty breach. The court found delivery and acceptance, found no sustained warranty defense, and affirmed with costs.
