Systems and methods are provided for creating arbitrarily-shaped ion energy distribution functions (IEDFs) using shaped-pulse bias. A method applies a shaped pulse bias to an electrode of a process chamber and modulates the amplitude of the negative voltage jump (V_OUT), and hence the sheath voltage (V_SH), so the relative number of pulses at a specific amplitude determines the relative ion fraction at the corresponding ion energy. Bursts of pulses with given amplitudes can be repeated; relative burst number determines relative ion portions, and V_OUT determines ion energy. Examples include trains for a two-peak IEDF with 25% low-energy and 75% high-energy ions, or HML for three equal peaks. Other methods overcompensate or undercompensate for ion current during the ion compensation phase by making the voltage ramp more or less negative, producing ion energy spread and a non-monoenergetic IEDF whose width is controlled by the ramp slope. The systems can include a substrate support assembly, power electrode, ceramic layer, bias supply, and/or controller.

In United States v. Nagy, Paul Nagy appeals the denial of his Fed.R.Civ.P. 60(b) motion. The Fourth Circuit finds no reversible error, affirms on the district court’s reasoning, and dispenses with oral argument. AFFIRMED.

A Kazakh man died and another was hospitalized after falling debris from a Russian space launch caused a steppe fire. The fire, in a Soyuz rocket’s planned fallout zone from Baikonur, was extinguished; Roscosmos confirmed the death and said the men were clearing debris.

GA102, fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm 8N NVIDIA Custom Process, has 28.3 billion transistors and a 628.4 mm2 die. It contains CUDA Cores, second-generation RT Cores, and third-generation Tensor Cores; a full GA102 has 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores. GA10x SMs double FP32 processing, RT Cores double ray/triangle testing and support motion blur, and Tensor Cores support sparsity, TF32, BF16, and AI features. GA10x uses GDDR6X/GDDR6 memory, third-generation NVLink, PCIe Gen 4, 112 ROPs, 128 KB L1 per SM, and 6144 KB L2 on full GA102. It supports RTX IO, DLSS up to 8K, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a, fifth-generation NVDEC including AV1 decode, and seventh-generation NVENC. NVIDIA A40 and RTX A6000 are GA10x-based professional GPUs with 48 GB memory scalable to 96 GB via NVLink.

The Princeton offense is described as an unstructured style similar to the Passing Game, relying on constant motion and counter actions based on defensive reads, with the back door cut as its signature. Developed and popularized by Pete Carril, it involves all five players and requires outside shooting, passing and driving with either hand, court savvy, unselfishness, patience, and conditioning. Coaches must be fully committed under the “All or None Principle.” The offense emphasizes adaptability, spacing of 12–15 feet, continuity, entries, exchanges, post action, ball control, and 15 to 20 passes per possession. Entries are automatic from passes or dribbles; exchanges and ball movement set up back cuts and give-and-go cuts. Post play often collapses the defense for kick-out passes. Dribbling is used sparingly for spacing, exchanges, counters, and drive-and-kick. It includes quick-hitting specials and press-break preparation. Psychologically, it is described as a “giant slayer” that pressures opponents in low-possession games, exposes weak defenders, causes fatigue and errors, and uses the threat of holding the ball while attacking on cuts.

It feels great, but there is a long road ahead and more wins are needed. A shorthanded goal was a big boost, and the team hopes to steal a game, return to Edmonton, and play a similar style to force a game. They played four lines, skated well, clogged the neutral zone, and got a strong first period; the third period was also viewed as good despite limited shots.

The speaker says the team lacked work boots in the second period, got out-muscled, then adjusted and played well late in the second and in the third. An important player plays five-on-five, power play, and penalty kill and came up big. Their third-period scoring success continued in the playoffs; the twins’ line helped tie the game, Boston gave up a lead, and they won in overtime. Manny played well on faceoffs and created chances. The speaker declines to disclose a player’s game-time status to protect him. It took three years to tell the twins apart; Danny is quieter and Henrik more outspoken. If a player returns, they will ease him in, use his faceoffs and defensive smarts, and not break up the Torres-Lapierre-Hansen line; they want fewer offensive-zone penalties and a better power play.

Bertie Secor, Administrator, et al., appellants, appealed from a district court decree dismissing their action against James E. Siver et al. The action sought recovery on a foreign judgment and an injunction against conveyances alleged to be fraudulent. The Sivers filed a counterclaim alleging Secor fraudulently represented land exchanged for their New York property; after an earlier reversal, trial dismissed the petition. The appellate court affirmed. It held objections to witness competency must specifically state facts, and a general assertion that a witness is “incompetent and unqualified” is insufficient. It also held interested witnesses may testify in a damages action for fraudulent representations against a deceased’s administrator as to property description, quality, value, reliance on representations, and condition of property received, and an objection to personal transactions with a deceased does not necessarily raise personal communications. Costs taxed to a defeated administrator in official capacity were not relaxed on appeal. Stevens, J., dissenting, with Ladd and Salinger, JJ., disagreed on the competency objections and admissibility of the Sivers’ testimony.

Volunteers in southern NSW and the ACT are surveying platypuses in late winter, including a fourth annual survey on a stretch of the Upper Murrumbidgee River. Organizers say the shy, cryptic species is hard to spot, and four years of surveys suggest numbers there are stable. The citizen-science data are described as valuable baseline information for the near-threatened species, whose numbers have declined across eastern Australia and Tasmania.

The lecture reviews Wald’s identity for random walks with two thresholds and a stopping time, then applies it to sequential hypothesis testing using likelihood ratios and log-likelihood ratios. It discusses fixed-sample and sequential tests, error probabilities, threshold choices, r* equal to 1, and expected numbers of tests. Taking derivatives of Wald’s identity at r = 0 yields Wald’s equality and a second-order relation involving S_J and J. The lecture then introduces martingales as sequences satisfying E[Z_n | Z_{n-1}, ..., Z_1] = Z_{n-1}, with examples including zero-mean random walks, sums of dependent zero-mean variables, product-form martingales, and double-or-nothing. It notes a case where limit and expectation cannot be interchanged. It defines submartingales and supermartingales and states Jensen’s inequality for convex functions.

It states these tools can help creators save time and produce high-quality content, that AI amplifies rather than replaces creativity, and that features and pricing may change and the article contains affiliate links.

Socket markings include molded “SOCKET 940,” locked/unlocked directional designators, a triangular A01 orientation symbol, supplier UL symbol, and lot traceability number on the socket cover, visible as specified after mounting. Brands are moving toward thin bezels, but selfie cameras and sensors complicate full-screen displays. Xiaomi moved them to the bottom on the Mi Mix 2s; Apple used a notch on iPhone X, which the industry followed. Vivo's Apex concept uses an under-screen fingerprint sensor and pop-up selfie camera, but its complex mechanism adds cost and bulk. The author suggests transparent OLED panels as a permanent solution, outlining protective glass, a transparent OLED, and a hidden selfie camera, with per-pixel opacity control. Such setups may first appear on high-end phones; companies have showcased transparent OLED for TVs and smart windows.

A new study shows that adding four live ants to warmed cow’s milk and burying the jar in an ant mound overnight can acidify and thicken the milk into early yogurt. Bacteria on ants, plus formic acid and enzymes from ants and bacteria, aid fermentation. Live ants work better than frozen or dehydrated ants, but live ants can carry a parasite, so making it at home is not recommended.

The speaker says he was caught up in everything and credits coach Burns for putting him in the situation and showing belief in him. He felt calm, helped by the team’s veterans and leadership. In his third season in the organization, after playing in Albany, he was called up in January and never expected to be in the Stanley Cup finals. He trained for possible injuries and wanted to contribute in any way, not necessarily on the scoresheet. He praises teammates for stepping up, says Jeff’s first goal was huge, Marty came through, and a leader not in the lineup inspired him. The final minutes felt long, with a chaotic bench.

The Clark County School District announced Dr. Jesus Jara as its new superintendent after the Board of Trustees voted for him on May 2, 2018. Jara had been deputy superintendent for Orange County Public Schools in Orlando since 2012 and previously superintendent at Monroe County Public Schools. The board was split; Dr. Mike Barton was defeated 4-3, and some trustees and speakers supported Barton. After further debate, Jara won. Six finalists were considered from 77 applications, all interviewed April 27. The board hoped Jara could begin in June before current superintendent Pat Skorkowsky retires, with negotiations expected.

This command moves SNP guest page contents within system physical address space as a faster replacement for SNP PAGE_MOVE. A 2M page must consist of physically contiguous 4K pages and be 2M aligned; non-physically contiguous 2M pages cannot migrate directly. DMA to migrating pages is not supported, and concurrent DMA may abort. CPU access must be prevented. Source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid; destination pages must be Pre-Migration. After migration, destination pages take the source page’s state, and source pages return to Pre-Migration. Firmware performs per-entry actions and checks, including RMP_ENFORCE, page/state/GCTX/RMP exclusivity/page-size checks, TLB invalidate/sync, copying, and RMP updates, returning status codes. It marks the end of page migration command strings and can interrupt on completion. Input fields except PM_SUB_COMMAND and interrupt fields are ignored. Errors are reported in commands/list entries, PM_STATUS, command status, or MCA. A command can operate on up to 128 pages; hardware errors may make pages unrecoverable, and the system may eventually cease functioning.

The passage discusses gamification in academic education. It states that higher education should provide knowledge, skills, and social competences defined in curricula, and that challenges from the knowledge society and broad access to databases make innovative education techniques important. Gamification is defined as the conscious and purposeful use of game mechanisms and techniques to increase dedication and loyalty and modify behaviors and habits. It is presented as transferring game mechanisms to education and achieving concentrated motivation through clear aims, instructions, confidence that tasks can be completed, and immediate feedback. The passage mentions fun, positive emotions, memory, competition, ludology, and game elements such as gameplay, game structure, game world, and players, and lists winning condition, aim, action, obstacles, and rules as features of game structure.

The passage then discusses four projects at the Institute of Pedagogy at the University of Wrocław. The Kulturalny Wrocław project used location-based games in two courses for Master’s students. Participants located cultural places, sent photographs, solved riddles, completed a crossword, used poses for letters, and reached a final point. Evaluations were highly positive for the method, socializing, outdoor lessons, independence, internet use, changed relations, and memory hooks, though some questioned lesson effectiveness. It was low-cost, logistically simple, weather-dependent, clear, and adaptable.

The five-day career management seminar aimed to increase graduates’ labor-market competitiveness. It included expert meetings and a gamified science-fiction mission plot with levels, missions, points, badges, bonuses, and a final game exam. It was reported as effective, with broad subjects covered in five days, high exam results, fast integration, dedication, positive reception, self-diagnosis, and transfer to practice. Instructors reported high preparation effort and said gamified programs are effective only when repeated.

The Entrepreneurship in Lower Silesian educational practice project used a location-based game. Teams named after entrepreneurs had maps, money, props, quests, and a final income-tax task. Evaluations noted socializing, movement plus intellectual tasks, fun and education, dynamics, attractiveness, and soft-skills potential. Competition and internet access were ambivalent; weak points included weather, organizational problems, unfamiliar location, and terrain.

The Learning through games project used a LARP, Spell of the Black Magic Master. Students drew character roles and worked in a fantasy plot to neutralize a spell within 120 minutes through stages, props, and a final play. Students with RPG/LARP experience were more confident; those without had difficulties, lower satisfaction, and integration problems. Soft skills developed indirectly, and educational goals were achieved, but complexity, lack of preparation, time-consuming organization, and need for pilot and repeated sessions were noted.

The passage concludes that location-based games have potential in academic education, that students’ game experience is mostly with computer games, and that educational games must consider previous experience, topic, time, and expenses. Simple games with clear rules and strategy are well received. Longer complex games suit subsidized projects for those seeking competences and competitiveness and should be preceded by socializing activities and tutorials.

The passage says progress in reducing tobacco deaths is celebrated, but the acceptable number of preventable deaths is zero. It argues smokers are victims and the tobacco industry bears responsibility, citing the Danish Institute for Human Rights and the Cape Town Declaration, endorsed by over 150 organizations. ASH aims for a tobacco-free world with zero tobacco deaths.

Eddie Woo, a Sydney maths teacher, gained widespread attention through his YouTube channel “Wootube,” which he started in 2012 by filming lessons for a seriously ill student. The channel has more than 200,000 subscribers and over 12 million views. He was named Australia’s Local Hero for 2018 and became one of 10 finalists for the 2018 Global Teacher Prize, though he did not win. He also became a NSW Department of Education “master teacher,” mentoring students and teachers across the state while retaining his job at Cherrybrook Technology High School. The passage also describes his popular school visits in the NSW Riverina and notes that his busier schedule has downsides for his family.
Appeal dismissed: an order sustaining a demurrer to an amended petition, without further disposition, is not final, so no appeal lies.

The passage consists largely of repeated financial and business headlines and information about Pan Finance’s global media network and readership. The court addressed consolidated appeals from Chancery Division denials of costs and counsel fees under N.J.S. 2A:15-53. In the arbitration case, the union and Borkowski sought fees after the Appellate Division reversed a restraint and held Borkowski’s discharge arbitrable. The court affirmed denial, finding the action was not within the Anti-Injunction Act but was essentially a declaratory judgment on arbitrability with an ancillary stay; no rule authorized fees. In the strike case, the union sought fees after an interlocutory injunction against mass picketing was reversed by the Appellate Division on procedural grounds. The court affirmed denial, because the Appellate Division found a substantive basis for injunctive relief and the reversal was not on the merits; the fee provision was not intended to impose fees where the suit was not wrongfully brought or for procedural default not attributable to plaintiff. Judgments affirmed, with costs to respondent in the arbitration case only.

It describes a portable digital audio/video player with a 1.9” color screen, FM tuner if applicable, built-in microphone, microSDHC slot, supported audio/video/photo formats, voice recording, and a non-replaceable rechargeable battery. It explains charging, powering on/off, resetting, using the Hold switch and thumbwheel, connecting to a computer, updating firmware, formatting, and transferring music, photos, and videos using drag-and-drop, Windows Media Player, or Sansa Media Converter. Central Huron Council heard a presentation from Huron County’s Acting CAO, Director of Cultural Services and County Librarian Meighan Wark, who proposed working with the municipality on a renovation project to bring Clinton Library up to accreditation status and improve community services. In 2015, the Huron County Library received five-year accreditation, and 11 branches were approved, but Clinton did not meet minimum standards due to accessibility and square footage issues. Wark said renovations would help Clinton earn accreditation, improve accessibility and inclusivity, and benefit the public. The county is responsible for staff, materials, furniture, equipment and library services; the municipality is responsible for the building, maintenance and utilities. Standards are based on Ontario Public Library Guidelines, with space needs determined by population served. Next steps include agreeing on required components, then preparing architect drawings for council and community. Wark said provincial funding is possible with a shovel-ready project, and the county could invest in the interior if the municipality commits to changes. Council will continue discussions.

Turing features a new SM design with two SMs per TPC; each SM has 64 FP32 and 64 INT32 cores, supports concurrent FP32/INT32 execution and independent thread scheduling, and includes eight Tensor Cores and one RT Core. Each SM is partitioned into four processing blocks with 16 FP32 cores, 16 INT32 cores, two Tensor Cores, a warp scheduler, a dispatch unit, a new L0 instruction cache, and a 64 KB register file; the blocks share 96 KB L1/shared memory that can be partitioned for graphics or compute. Turing Tensor Cores add INT8 and INT4 modes and support FP16, accelerating matrix operations and NGX AI features such as DLSS, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing for real-time ray tracing with hybrid rendering. The architecture also includes GDDR6 memory, larger L2 cache, memory compression, an enhanced video/display engine, NVLink for SLI, mesh shading, variable rate shading, texture space shading, multi-view rendering, and USB-C/VirtualLink support. The passage also lists TU102, TU104, TU106, and Tesla T4 configurations.

Charlie Alliston, then 18, is on trial at the Old Bailey over the death of Kim Briggs, 44, a mother of two. The court heard that on February 12 last year he hit Briggs at about 20mph on Old Street, east London, while riding a black Planet X fixed-wheel track bike with no front brake, which the prosecution said could not lawfully be ridden on a public road without modification. Briggs, who was crossing during her lunch break, suffered two skull fractures and brain bleeding and died a week later. Prosecutors allege manslaughter and causing bodily harm by wanton or furious driving, saying reconstructions showed a front brake would have allowed him to stop in time and that his riding was unlawful and dangerous. The court heard Alliston posted comments blaming Briggs and denying fault. He denies the charges.

Elijah Brown scored 27 points, including 17 of New Mexico’s final 19, as New Mexico beat Boise State 78-73. New Mexico used an 11-0 first-half run, and Boise State never led. Chandler Hutchison had a career-high 31 points for Boise State, with James Reid adding 18. Obij Ajet and Damien Jefferson each scored 14 for New Mexico, and Jordan Hunter had nine points and five assists. New Mexico made 22 free throws to Boise State’s 13 and had nine blocks. Tim Williams missed his fourth straight game with a foot injury. New Mexico plays at Fresno State; Boise State hosts Wyoming.

A Dec. 5 Harvard Institute of Politics poll found 65% of 18-29 year-olds favor Democrats and 33% Republicans. It found 14% believe the U.S. is headed in the right direction, Trump’s approval among millennials is 25%, 67% see threats coming from inside the country, and 61% support stricter gun laws.

This retrospective cohort study used HCUP-NIS data from 2017–2019 to examine whether perinatal mood disorders are associated with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) and other cardiac events. Among over 2.2 million hospitalizations, 168,729 (7.4%) had a mood disorder diagnosis. PPCM incidence was higher in patients with mood disorders (0.12% vs 0.05%), as was the composite of adverse cardiac events (0.36% vs 0.14%). After adjustment, PPCM remained associated with mood disorders (aOR 1.36, 95% CI 1.03–1.80), as did composite adverse cardiac events (aOR 1.57, 95% CI 1.37–1.81) and pulmonary edema (aOR 1.62, 95% CI 1.39–1.89). Maternal death was not significantly associated. The study concludes that perinatal mood disorders were associated with increased rates of PPCM and other cardiac events.

Preempt announced new data and enforcement integrations for its Preempt Behavioral Firewall. Data integrations include Okta, Azure Active Directory, and VPN gateways; enforcement integrations include SecureAuth, RSA SecurID, Duo, Google Authenticator, and HP Aruba ClearPass. The firewall combines UEBA with automated adaptive response, using contextual data and policies based on user or entity role, behavior, and targeted assets, and can redirect, confirm, or block verified threats.

In card identification mode, the host resets cards, validates voltage, identifies them, and asks them to publish an RCA, separately on the CMD line. CMD0 resets cards to Idle State, except Inactive cards. After power-on or CMD0, CMD lines wait for a start bit; default RCA is 0x0000, with default driver strength and 400 KHz clock. In UHS-II, CMD0 does not clear RCA. CMD8 verifies operating condition using VHS, CRC, and check pattern; unsupported voltage gets no response and idle state. CMD8 is mandatory before first ACMD41 for SDHC/SDXC.

The speaker would give up one award to get another and credits his teammates. He calls the loss tough, says the opposing team deserved to win, and notes home-ice advantage and loud fans in both buildings. He says the playoffs taught him about aggression, energy, and preparation. He was not surprised by booing in New Jersey and found cheers and Devils players’ support nice. He calls another player probably the best since Patrick retired and congratulates him. He plans to approach next season one game at a time. He is sad because he wanted the Stanley Cup for his mother, who is not doing well, but says he will move on.

Washington police will announce charges against 12 Turkish security agents over violence during Turkey’s president’s visit; seven face felonies and five misdemeanors. Two men, Sinan Narin and Eyup Yildirim, were arrested in Virginia and New Jersey. U.S. officials criticized Turkish forces for breaking up a May 16 protest.

In Mary Meeker’s Internet Trends report, slide 246 shows a sharp rise in Chinese time spent on short-form videos (under five minutes), apparently at the expense of long-form and ahead of live/game streaming. Short-video time rose 360% in 2017; 76% of consumers use a single app. Douyin and Kuaishou report about 100 million daily active users and 52 minutes per viewer daily.

Apple's iOS 11.4 update adds AirPlay 2, enabling multi-room streaming, stereo HomePod pairing, larger network buffer, uninterrupted playback during calls or other media, and moving music by Siri. It also adds HomePod Siri calendar support, though no individual voice recognition. Third parties announced AirPlay 2 support, but iOS devices act as streaming hub. The update also introduces Messages in iCloud, syncing messages and attachments while using iCloud storage. Siri otherwise remains unchanged, and the update is available now.

U.S. stocks rose Wednesday, recovering most of the prior day’s losses, as investors hoped Italy could avoid new elections. Banks and energy companies gained, and smaller companies rose more, with the Russell 2000 closing at a record high. The S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq all advanced. Italy’s FTSE MIB rebounded, the euro and Treasury yields rose, and U.S. crude and Brent oil climbed. Trade tensions between the U.S. and China and U.S.-EU tariff talks continued. Gold, silver, and copper rose.

At NVIDIA Corporation’s 2018 Annual Meeting on May 16, 2018, stockholders elected eleven directors, approved on an advisory basis the compensation of named executive officers, ratified PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent registered accounting firm, approved the amended and restated 2007 Equity Incentive Plan to increase its share reserve by 23,000,000 shares, and approved the amended and restated 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan to increase its share reserve by 13,500,000 shares. NVIDIA filed the Form 8-K on May 21, 2018.

Court modified the order and affirmed as modified with costs to plaintiff. Supreme Court erred in dismissing plaintiff’s bad-faith settlement negotiation causes; evidence supported a jury finding that defendant primary insurer negotiated in bad faith by not timely offering policy limits, depriving plaintiff of a better settlement, and sufficient evidence supported damages. Credibility and probative value are for the jury. The dismissal of plaintiff’s fourth cause under Insurance Law § 2601 was affirmed.

A study found low doses of alcohol may benefit brain health by improving the glymphatic system, the brain’s cleaning process that flushes waste, including proteins associated with Alzheimer’s disease and dementia. Conducted in mice at the University of Rochester Medical Centre, the study examined acute and chronic alcohol exposure. Low alcohol (0.5 g/kg, about 2.5 drinks/day) significantly improved glymphatic activity, reduced brain inflammation, and matched teetotal mice in cognitive and motor tests. Intermediate (1.5 g/kg) and high (4 g/kg) doses reduced glymphatic function; high long-term exposure increased an inflammation marker, especially in astrocytes, and impaired cognition and motor skills. Suppression after moderate chronic exposure was restored 24 hours after termination. The findings were said to match a J-shaped model and were published in Scientific Reports.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers can operate in external synchronization mode by leaving RT floating and applying a 200-kHz to 4-MHz clock to SYNC at twice the desired switching frequency, with a 40%–60% duty cycle, preferably 50%; the clock is internally inverted. Two controllers can be used in primary-secondary mode through SYNC, with the primary RT populated and the secondary RT floating, for independent converters or interleaved parallel converters. The devices provide OUTA or OUTA/OUTB primary outputs and SRA or SRA/SRB synchronous rectifier outputs, with roughly 150-mA peak capability and recommended external gate drive. Dead times, leading edge blank time, pulse skipping, duty cycle limits, current sensing and overcurrent protection, hiccup mode, external fault protection, slope compensation, and thermal shutdown are described. The series uses fixed-frequency peak current mode control, and the passage also includes a synchronous push-pull converter design example, power supply recommendations, layout guidelines, packaging, and orderable information.

Modern RPO and Air Raid concepts have led many defenses to use match coverage and middle-of-the-field-open coverages, but run fits are often overlooked. Coaches use “coach speak” to communicate run-fit approaches, but must translate terms like front spacing and gapped-out fits into executable scheme for players; run fits vary by talent and philosophy. Defensive spacing refers to run fits, and every fit stems from front spacing and the coverage behind it. Even spacing has the open gap in the B gap; odd spacing moves open gaps to the C gaps, often distinguished by a head-up or shaded nose. Spacing is also described as 7-, 8-, or 9-man based on box defenders versus 12/21 personnel and coverage. In 7-man spacing the defense is a defender short in the box, often in MOFO coverage, with tools such as two-gapping a lineman, tite front, stunts, stack-track-fallback versus zone, and spill-overlap versus gap. In 8-man spacing the defense is gapped out with equal box numbers, often MOFC coverage, uses one-gap fits, indicator fitting, and lever-spill-lever versus gap. In 9-man spacing the defense is maxed out with an extra box defender, often cover 0 or blitz fits, and can play aggressively with an extra hat. The passage also gives 3-4 defense examples for 7-, 8-, and 9-man spacing versus zone and power, including tite/mint fronts and overhangs filling or freezing based on the back.

The lecture then covers forwards and futures. A forward is a customized, nonstandard, over-the-counter agreement to buy or sell an asset in the future at a price agreed today; it typically involves physical delivery and has illiquidity and counterparty risk. Futures are standardized exchange-traded contracts with fixed amounts, qualities, settlement dates, and prices, marked to market daily, with margins and a clearing corporation as intermediary. Examples include soybeans and NYMEX crude oil futures. Hedging motives, views on derivatives, and corporate hedging policies are also discussed.

The lecture focuses on understanding light forces, particularly the stimulated force, using the dressed atom picture. In this picture, the atom-laser interaction is solved exactly by diagonalizing a two-by-two matrix, and then spontaneous emission is allowed. The dressed states are superpositions of bare ground and excited states with N or N+1 laser photons. In the strong-Rabi-frequency limit, the density-matrix equations decouple into rate equations for populations and equations for coherences; steady-state populations are given by angle theta, and relaxation times for populations and coherences determine features of the Mollow triplet, including different widths. Spontaneous emission can be described in the bare basis as antibunching, or in the dressed basis as a radiative cascade producing sidebands and alternating blue- and red-detuned photons; these descriptions are complementary and depend on temporal versus spectral resolution.

Applying the dressed atom picture to the dipole force: dressed levels are split by the generalized Rabi frequency, and atoms in the two dressed levels experience opposite forces. The net dipole force depends on population imbalance. Red detuning gives an attractive force; blue detuning gives a repulsive force; on resonance populations are equal and the average force is zero. For slow motion, non-adiabatic time lag in adjusting dressed-state populations produces a friction force; blue-detuned light cools in this case (blue molasses). The friction coefficient is calculated for a blue-detuned standing wave. Heating is described by the momentum diffusion coefficient from force fluctuations; radiative cascades between dressed levels reverse the force and cause heating, which can dominate photon recoil in strong fields.

The lecture also presents Sisyphus cooling for a two-level atom in a blue-detuned standing wave: the atom climbs potential hills and spontaneously emits mainly at the top, then falls to the bottom, so on average it climbs more than it descends, producing cooling. The cooling rate is the switching rate between dressed levels times the lattice depth. In a perturbative large-detuning limit, dressed states, transition rates, potentials, friction, and diffusion are derived. The ultimate temperature is comparable to the standing-wave amplitude, implying laser cooling cannot localize two-level atoms in an optical lattice; lower temperatures require physics beyond the discussed two-level model. Additional discussion covers dipole potential derivations, optical trapping of mesoscopic objects and optical tweezers, and the dependence on whether the index of refraction is greater or less than one. The lecture also outlines upcoming topics on magnetic trapping, evaporative cooling, Bose and Fermi gases, and quantum logic with ions.

The lecture discusses trajectory optimization. It reviews policy search, where a control policy is parameterized and optimized over parameters, including open-loop policies represented as zero-order-hold control tapes. For open-loop trajectory optimization, it presents shooting methods, which simulate forward, adjust parameters, and compute gradients using either the adjoint/backprop-through-time method or real-time recurrent learning. SNOPT/SQP is presented as preferable to gradient descent because it avoids learning-rate tuning, converges faster, and handles constraints. Direct collocation is then presented: it augments the parameter vector with states, evaluates cost and gradients without simulation, and adds dynamics consistency as explicit constraints. Examples include pendulum swing-up, acrobot, and path planning with local minima. Direct collocation methods are widely used, fast, and good at constraints, though less accurate than shooting due to fixed-step integration. Local minima exist but are often acceptable. Stabilizing trajectories with LQR and iterative LQR is planned for later.

The article descriptively analyzes 377 percutaneous tracheostomies performed in intubated, mechanically ventilated COVID-19 ICU patients at Jaber Al Ahmad Al Sabah Hospital between March 2020 and March 2022. It reports a mean intubation-to-tracheostomy duration of 17.4 days; 59% of patients were male, diabetes and hypertension were common comorbidities, and 29% were on ECMO and 23% on dialysis. Complications occurred in 85 cases (23%), most commonly minor bleeding; 203 patients (54%) were weaned from sedation and 156 (41%) from mechanical ventilation, while 236 (63%) died from COVID-19 complications, with no deaths attributed to the procedure. The authors conclude percutaneous tracheostomy can be safely performed and suggest performing it as soon as possible after day 7, while noting limitations including no open-tracheostomy comparison, lack of long-term outcomes, and no PCR testing of staff.

Yale-New Haven Hospital sued Clifford Mitchell and Laureen and Vincent Wilczynski for unpaid medical services. The hospital moved for summary judgment, arguing no genuine issues of material fact and that the defenses and counterclaims lacked legal merit. The court denied summary judgment. It found the defendants could assert violations of the Hill-Burton Act and hospital bed funds statute as defenses, that private causes of action exist under both statutes, that alleged violations could support CUTPA claims, and that the CUTPA counterclaims raised factual issues for trial. The passage explains NHS cancer screening, which detects early signs of cancer in people without symptoms. Cancer Research UK says screening has saved around 90,000 lives in five years. Dr Alexandra Moorhouse advises eligible people to attend even if they feel healthy. The NHS offers three main programmes. Cervical screening is every five years for women and people with a cervix aged 25–64, checking for high-risk HPV; results may lead to further cell analysis or colposcopy. Breast screening is every three years for women aged 50–71 using mammograms; over-71s can arrange it, and under-50s concerned should speak to their doctor. Bowel screening is every two years for people aged 50–74 using an at-home FIT kit to detect tiny amounts of blood; positive results lead to urgent colonoscopy, and over-75s can contact the helpline. Screening is free, invitation-based, and can detect pre-cancerous changes and improve outcomes. Some screenings, such as prostate, are not national and may be discussed case by case. Private screening and earlier mammograms for women with NF1 are also mentioned.

This lecture discusses computation of the discrete Fourier transform. A direct DFT requires on the order of N squared complex multiplies and adds. The fast Fourier transform, a class of algorithms disclosed by Cooley and Tukey in 1965 and reinvented in various forms, is more efficient, especially for highly composite N. For N a power of 2, complexity is proportional to N log base 2 N rather than N squared. The derivation uses decimation-in-time: split the sequence into even and odd points, compute N/2-point DFTs G[k] and H[k], and combine them as X[k] = G[k] + W_N^k H[k], using periodicity. This is repeated down to two-point DFTs. The flow graph uses butterfly computations, with multiplications by powers of W on the bottom branch; because W_N^{N/2} = -1, this can be simplified, reducing multiplications and using addition and subtraction. Input values appear in bit-reversed order, while outputs are sequential. Applications include spectral analysis, FIR filters, and convolution.

Yufei Zhao’s lecture presents Szemerédi’s graph regularity lemma. It defines edge density, epsilon-regular pairs, and epsilon-regular partitions. Informally, any large dense graph can be partitioned into a bounded number of parts so that between most pairs of parts the graph looks random-like. The lemma states that for every epsilon there is M depending only on epsilon such that every graph has an epsilon-regular partition into at most M parts; an equitable version guarantees an epsilon-regular equitable partition into k parts between a minimum m0 and a bounded maximum. The proof uses an energy increment argument: energy is a weighted mean squared edge density between partition parts, lies between 0 and 1, does not decrease under refinement, and increases by at least epsilon^5 when refining a non-epsilon-regular partition using witnessing sets. Iterating stops after a bounded number of steps, yielding an epsilon-regular partition. The produced bound is huge and independent of graph size; Gowers showed it cannot be substantially improved. The lecture also discusses modifying the proof to obtain equitable partitions.

The article analyzes digital piracy and how firms can design business models to minimize its negative impact. It focuses on content distribution and monetization, using qualitative case studies of Netflix and Spotify based on archival sources and interviews. The findings describe digital piracy’s appeal—free access, large catalogs, bypassing release windows and geographical restrictions, and lack of DRM restrictions—alongside its downsides. Netflix and Spotify respond with subscription and free-tier models, streaming convenience, broad device access, catalog licensing, consistent quality, social and community features, personalization, and improved geographical access. The article argues their competitive advantage comes from enriching the consumption experience rather than competing only on price or content. It also discusses limitations and challenges, including licensing agreements, advertising, subscriber conversion, price discrimination, Internet quality, unauthorized sharing, and value captured by social media providers. Implications are presented for technological innovation, firm diversification, and network competition.

This paper used a relative risk statistic with French ICU admission data to examine the roles of age groups during four Omicron waves in France from March 1 to December 29, 2022. The highest relative risk was in ages 10-19 in the Spring and Autumn waves, ages 0-9 in the Summer wave, and ages 30-39 in the Autumn-Winter wave, followed by ages 40-49 and over 80. The leading relative roles shifted from children and younger adults to persons aged 30-49 and over 80. The authors suggest increasing booster vaccination coverage for all adults and possibly children, and further efforts to prevent spread in elderly persons, including in long-term care facilities.

Larry Connors’ MDU/MDD strategy is described in Chapter 6 of *High Probability Trading*. It uses mean reversion in ETFs, buying when an ETF is above its 200-day moving average, below its 5-day moving average, and has dropped at least 4 of the last 5 trading days; it sells when the ETF closes above its 5-day moving average, with no stop-loss. Tests cover the original 20 ETFs plus five added ETFs, from inception until December 2020. A five-position portfolio (20% each each) is simulated from 2000 to December 2020, compounded without commissions or slippage. The strategy has the lowest profit factor among four Connors mean-reversion strategies; some ETFs may not suit mean reversion. SPY/QQQ-only results show 287 trades, profit factor 1.82, 12% max drawdown, 2.4% CAGR, and 7.7% time in market. Short-side results are difficult; a SPY/QQQ short version has a 65% win ratio and 0.68% average gain. The strategy can likely be improved.
Around 400 Brentwood students were sent home after a 9-foot boa escaped; it was found beneath ripped-up flooring, wrapped around pipes.

Freeport High School recognized students in grades 9–12 on the second quarter honor roll in High Honors and Honors categories. North Yarmouth Academy recognized students in The Forecaster’s coverage area in grades 5–12 on the first semester honor roll in Highest Honors, High Honors, and Honors categories.

Virginia Chestnuts is a family-owned orchard in Nelson County, in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains. David and Kim Bryant purchased land in 2003 and planted 200 test trees, then more than 1,600 Dunstan American-Chinese hybrid trees. The trees are blight resistant but not weather resistant; the orchard faced a harsh winter and cicadas between 2009 and 2014, then a bumper crop in 2015. The 2017 harvest was robust, and this year’s harvest yielded at least 3,000 pounds. Chestnuts are harvested from mid-September to late October, processed, graded, washed, sanitized, dried, and stored on-site. They are sold raw whole or peeled and roasted at events, including Dickie Brothers Orchard and Fire, Flour & Fork. They are used in breads, stuffing, beer, restaurant dishes, and desserts. Virginia Chestnuts is part of a five-orchard growers group in Nelson County and uses the motto “taste of history.”

A skull found in eastern Utah belongs to a new species, Cifelliodon wahkarmoosuch, a 2.5-pound, 6-inch-tall animal with buck teeth and plant-crushing molars. A Nature study says the find suggests Pangea split about 15 million years later than previously thought and that reptile-like mammals diversified across continents. The fossil was found under a Hippodraco dinosaur’s foot and is displayed at the Natural History Museum of Utah.

A Michigan State University study evaluated adaptive multi-paddock (AMP) grass-fed and grain-fed feedlot beef production. It found AMP grazing can potentially offset greenhouse gas emissions, and the finishing phase could be a net carbon sink, while feedlot emissions were mainly in the red due to feed-based nitrogen emissions from fertilizer. Feedlots were more productive, producing the same beef on half the land. AMP grazing produced more beef on a land basis than continuous grazing, though carbon sequestration may lessen over time. Researchers suggested lower per capita beef consumption with greater environmental benefits, and said feedlots could improve with less fertilizer and cover crops. Rowntree said the study did not advocate one approach over another but identified best practices supporting environmental stewardship in both systems.

Both SFS and co-signing options are off by default; customers must opt in and configure BIOS, optionally co-signing update packages. In early boot, customer BIOS can pass a public signing key to the ASP; if enabled, SFS packages authenticate first against the customer key, then the AMD SFS key, and the signature cannot be updated after setup. Co-signing uses RSA 2048- or 4096-bit keys with specified RSA-PSS schemes. SFS checks patch/firmware versions, can patch registers or values, replace firmware images, or update firmware portions. SEV updates auto-commit and prevent rollback; SNP requires HV-FIXED pages. Update packages are non-persistent across reboots and may be applied during OS boot, after boot, or during operation. Commands require 2MB-aligned buffers and a customer SFS deployment agent. ASP verifies signatures, loads/runs the patch, updates patch level, and returns status. Packages are named by family, AGESA release, and count, and must match the system’s firmware/patch combination. Updates run in parallel with x86 and DMA traffic with minimal impact.

The Second Circuit affirmed the district court’s denial of Nicholson’s habeas corpus petition. Nicholson claimed the state courts violated due process by ruling Darnell Phelps’s hearsay confession inadmissible under Chambers. Assuming Chambers applied, the court found no mechanistic rejection of reliable hearsay: Phelps’s confession was inconsistent, could not be cross-examined at retrial, and did not necessarily exonerate Nicholson, while an eyewitness testified she saw Nicholson shooting the victim and was deemed credible. Thus, no due process violation was shown.

Ready to Learn (RTL), a program at Helping Hands Hawaii, hosts its annual school supply drive from June 1 to July 31, 2017, providing free basic educational tools to low-income and homeless students. American Savings Bank branches serve as collection sites from June 14 to July 14, with donations remaining on each island. RTL prepares basic school supply kits valued at approximately $10 each. As of April 2017, the program raised more than $12,000 and collected enough supplies for 3,115 kits, valued at about $31,000, benefiting more than 6,000 students. Donations, fundraising drives, and volunteers are sought. Students in grades K to 12 must be recommended by a case manager from a participating referral organization; the application deadline is June 23, 2017.

During a government shutdown, federal workers may miss paychecks, but members of Congress still get paid because their salaries are mandatory spending and Constitution-protected. The UC1825B-SP oscillator is a sawtooth controlled by the RT pin and CT capacitance, with RT recommended from 1 kΩ to 100 kΩ and DMAX below 70% not recommended. The device is a dual-output controller with integrated drivers for push-pull topology and can be used for half-bridge and full-bridge applications with external high-side drivers; it supports voltage mode and, with minimal external components, current mode. A design chose 215 kHz, RT = 10 kΩ, CT = 680 pF, a targeted duty cycle of 30%, transformer turns ratio 2.2, auxiliary winding turns ratio 1.5, primary inductance 120 µH, output inductor 2.2 µH, output capacitance about 1145 µF, and output filter inductance 500 nH. The input supply range is 10 V to 30 V and should be well regulated; additional bulk capacitance may be required if the supply is more than a few inches away, with a 100 µF tantalum capacitor as a typical choice. Layout guidance includes keeping feedback traces away from inductors and noisy power traces, placing input/output capacitors and compensation components close to the IC, using short, direct, thick power traces, and connecting grounds close together to a ground plane. The integrated circuit can be damaged by ESD and should be handled with appropriate precautions.

The passage discusses the Bollinger Band Squeeze strategy, which uses Bollinger Bands to measure volatility and trades in the breakout direction after low volatility. It explains Bollinger Bands, including a center average and bands based on standard deviations, and notes contractions/expansions. Backtests did not perform particularly well for most assets, perhaps except consumer staples; on Pepsi it did not beat buy and hold (12.5% vs. 14.8%) and was invested 61% of the time. Many versions and assets failed. It briefly profiles John A. Bollinger’s development of Bollinger Bands. FAQs state the squeeze is a breakout strategy with lower win rate and whipsaws, requiring positive expectancy and backtesting; common mistakes are lacking positive expectancy and not following the strategy; assets differ, so a strategy may not work on all. Mechanical trading is favored.

Cory Booker campaigned in Alabama for Democratic Senate nominee Doug Jones on the final weekend before the election, with the subtext being the 2020 presidential race. In Pfeiffer v. Commissioner, the Second Circuit reviewed a Board of Tax Appeals decision partially affirming a $89,841.75 deficiency for 1931. The Commissioner included the value of preferred stock distributed as a dividend on common stock in 1931 and $200,000 from redemption of 2,000 preferred shares received in 1928. The Board upheld taxation of the 1931 stock dividend under section 115(f), but held the redeemed shares had a $100 basis and produced no taxable income. The court reversed, finding section 115(f)’s unqualified exemption for stock dividends covered the preferred stock dividend on common stock; it also rejected taxing the redemption because that issue was not properly before it and section 115(g) had not been found applicable. L. Hand dissented, arguing Congress exempted stock dividends only because of Eisner v. Macomber, that preferred stock issued on common was income, and that the Board was right.

Edwin P. Whitmore et al., executors of Horace M. Whitmore’s will, sued the San Francisco Savings Union and De Fremery et al. The complaint alleged Horace gave the Savings Union a $1,500 promissory note in 1869, secured by a deed of trust on Alameda County land with power to sell on default. After Horace died in 1870, his will was probated, notice to creditors required claims within ten months, and the Savings Union did not present its claim. Trustees later advertised the land for sale. The trial court enjoined the sale and decreed defendants had no title. The Court reversed, holding that failure to present the claim did not extinguish the debt but only took away a remedy. Because the debt remained subsisting and unpaid, equity would not compel the creditor to surrender the security or enjoin a sale under the deed of trust; requiring surrender without payment would violate the maxim that he who seeks equity must do equity. The cause was remanded with directions to sustain the demurrer. Crockett, J., dissented, joined by McKinstry, J., arguing that failure to present the claim abrogated the lien and the legal title should be released for administration of the estate.

Google canceled Daily Stormer’s website-hosting registration after GoDaddy gave the neo-Nazi site 24 hours to find a new host. Google said the site violated policies against inciting violence; it declined to specify the content. GoDaddy cited Charlottesville events and terms against promoting violence. Daily Stormer had posted hateful content and ridiculed Heather Heyer, killed while protesting a white nationalist rally. YouTube terminated its channel for hate-speech violations; Facebook removes links unless clearly condemning content and pulled an event listing. Daily Stormer registered with Google before Google canceled it. The site’s host was unclear; Tucows denied hosting but said it ended contact-privacy service, and Cloudflare said it wasn’t the host. The Southern Poverty Law Center called on GoDaddy to pull support from two other sites. Activist Amy Siskind helped spur the campaign.

Matthew James Phelps, 29, called 911 on September 1 saying he took Coricidin cough medicine, had a dream, and woke to find his wife Lauren, 29, dead; he said he believed the medicine made him kill her. Police found Lauren mortally wounded, and she died at the hospital. Phelps faces first-degree murder charges and is held without bail. A search found red-stained bedding and an empty Coricidin box, among other items.

The passage describes bonded optical devices for wearable electronics and displays, including microLED-based devices. It claims priority to U.S. Provisional Patent Application No. 62/949,312 and U.S. patent application Ser. No. 17/124,408. Embodiments bond optical elements having arrays of monochromatic light emitters, such as red, green, and blue LEDs, to at least one carrier or processor element, optionally by direct or hybrid bonding without an adhesive. The processor element can include active circuitry to control the optical elements. Multiple optical elements can be coupled to an optical pathway or waveguide so that superimposed light from different colors is transmitted to an optical output for viewing by a user. Bonding can be performed in die-to-wafer, die-to-die, or wafer-to-wafer processes. The passage also describes contact pads, bonding pitches, optical isolation structures to limit crosstalk, independent control of emitters, and optical systems incorporating such assemblies.

Transport Cabinet Secretary James Macharia attributed the motorbike menace to poor enforcement of existing regulations, saying NTSA has failed to implement them. He told the National Assembly Transport Committee the ministry is working with county transport committees and the traffic department. Ruiru MP Simon King’ara called for a separate motorbike safety authority, criticized NTSA, urged enforcement, and suggested benchmarking with Rwanda. The IRS is furloughing about 34,000 workers, nearly half its workforce, amid the government shutdown; 39,870 employees (53.6%) remain. Due to lapsed appropriations, most operations are closed and an IRS-wide furlough began Oct. 8, 2025.

The GA10x SM is partitioned into four processing blocks, each with a 64 KB register file, L0 instruction cache, warp scheduler, dispatch unit, and math units, sharing a 128 KB L1 data cache/shared memory subsystem. It includes one third-generation Tensor Core per partition, four total, each twice as powerful as a Turing Tensor Core. Compared with Turing, combined L1/shared memory capacity is 33% larger, and graphics workload cache partition capacity is doubled. GA10x includes FP32 processing on both datapaths, doubling peak FP32 operations; each partition can execute 32 FP32 operations per clock or 16 FP32 and 16 INT32 operations per clock. It supports double-speed FP16, with standard FP16 handled by Tensor Cores. The unified shared memory, L1 data cache, and texture caching design is reconfigurable; L1 data cache capacity is 128 KB per SM. GA102 has 10752 KB of L1 cache, and shared memory bandwidth doubles to 128 bytes/clock per SM versus Turing. Ampere GPUs are up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing at the same performance level.

GA10x GPUs feature second-generation RT Cores with dedicated hardware for BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, doubling ray/triangle intersection testing rate over Turing. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit accelerates ray-traced motion blur, enabling accurate motion blur rendering up to eight times faster than Turing. GA10x supports concurrent RT Core and graphics, RT Core and compute, and compute-compute workloads. Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32 and BFloat16, include a Sparsity feature, and deliver up to 2x speedup for matrix multiplication compared to Turing Tensor Cores. RTX 3080 delivers 119 peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS with FP16 accumulate, 238 with Sparsity, 238 peak INT8 Tensor TOPS, and 476 peak INT4 Tensor TOPS, doubled with Sparsity.

GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling and MTA encoding, supports up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak memory bandwidth, and includes Error Detection and Replay. RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and decompression with Microsoft DirectStorage, accelerating I/O up to 100x compared to hard drives and traditional storage APIs. Ampere supports 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz, DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, DSC 1.2a, and HDCP 2.3/1.x. Fifth-generation NVDEC supports MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1 decode. Seventh-generation NVENC is included.

NVIDIA A40 is a GA10x data center GPU for visual computing, with up to 2X FP32, 2X ray-tracing, and 5X (10X with Sparsity) AI throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000, PCIe Gen4, 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, DP1.4 outputs, vGPU support, and EGX compatibility. RTX A6000 includes GA102, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, 336 next generation RT Cores, and 48GB GDDR6, scalable to 96GB via NVLink. GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 82 SMs, 10496 CUDA Cores, and 24GB GDDR6X. GeForce RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6, delivering performance faster than RTX 2080 Ti. The passage also presents performance, power efficiency, rendering, HPC, and deep learning comparisons.

This study provides an analytical overview of public financing instruments for innovative cleantech start-ups and SMEs in Europe. Common funding types are loan-based and equity-based, with some grants and guarantees, in fields including energy efficiency, smart cities, ICT, renewable energy, and healthcare. The EIB and EIF are prominent managing bodies. Instruments are benchmarked on metrics such as portfolio size, investment size, success rate, technology readiness levels, consortium requirements, project finance percentage, and monitoring frequency. William Brock was convicted of molestation of a juvenile and sentenced to ten years at hard labor. On appeal, he argued insufficient evidence and an excessive sentence. The court found the evidence sufficient, citing the victim’s statement that Brock touched her private area, medical testimony that vaginal trauma resulted from manual digital manipulation and was not self-inflicted, and evidence that Brock had control or supervision over the child. The court also found the sentence not excessive because the trial court complied with sentencing requirements and considered aggravating and mitigating factors. This study examined education faculty students’ attitudes toward the Research Methods in Education (RME) course and their views on it using quantitative and qualitative methods. The quantitative sample consisted of 190 students from three departments at Bayburt University Faculty of Education; the qualitative sample consisted of 10 prospective teachers. An attitude scale and focus group interview form were used. Attitudes did not differ significantly by department but differed significantly by class, between first and fourth class. Most participants found the course necessary, reported scientific, personal, and profession-oriented gains, and cited insufficient course duration, lecturer-related factors, and material/use issues. Recommendations included providing foundational courses before RME, offering it to third- or fourth-year students, and making or extending it.

This cross-sectional survey study explored mentorship needs and experiences of entry-level occupational therapy students, collecting responses from 133 students, 59 of whom identified as from a historically underrepresented group. Results indicated current mentorship programming was insufficient for these students. Participants wanted mentors who understood the transition from academia to clinical practice and demonstrated cultural humility, empathy, anti-racism allyship, and support for handling workplace discrimination. BIPOC students were more likely to rate mentors’ consideration of their own biases and prejudices as important. Hispanic/Latinx students were significantly more likely to report lower effectiveness in mentors working across cultural differences and integrating life outside school with school responsibilities. Students valued professional connections, networking, exam and job preparation, work/life balance, emotional support, and regular communication. The study concluded that occupational therapy programs should implement culturally sensitive mentorship programs integrating career support with emotional and social validation, using formal and informal elements, training, and institutional support. Limitations included a single urban institution, cross-sectional design, and focus on race and ethnicity.

In this original prohibition proceeding, the Colorado Supreme Court reviewed whether the Denver district court had personal jurisdiction over defendants served in California under Rule 4(f)(1), which allows out-of-state personal service on Colorado residents. Defendants, formerly of Denver, moved to Ventura, California, and specially appeared to quash service, asserting they were no longer Colorado residents. The trial court denied the motion and ordered them to answer. The Supreme Court held the California service invalid and the trial court without jurisdiction over defendants’ persons. The uncontroverted facts showed defendants left Colorado in September 1951, had no Colorado residence or abode, intended not to return, settled in Ventura, obtained employment and California licenses, registered to vote in California, and purchased lots there. Plaintiffs failed to prove defendants were Colorado residents. The Court also rejected jurisdictional objections, stating that proceeding without jurisdiction of the person is of great public importance. The rule to show cause was made absolute.

The passage presents a hybrid Constraint Acquisition framework, HCAR, designed to address over-fitting in learned global constraints. It has three phases: passive learning generates candidate global constraints (AllDifferent, Sum, Count) and a refined fixed-arity bias from few positive examples; a Query-Driven Interactive Refinement phase evaluates global candidates using machine-learning priors, Bayesian confidence updates, oracle queries, acceptance/rejection thresholds, structured pruning, subset exploration for rejected constraints, and adaptive query budget allocation; final active learning uses MQuAcq-2 to learn remaining fixed-arity constraints. Contributions include the three-phase architecture, a subset exploration mechanism that modifies scopes while preserving parameters, and ML-based prior probability estimation with Bayesian confidence updates. Empirical validation on benchmarks is reported to achieve high accuracy and target model coverage from limited examples with manageable query complexity, highlighting the interactive refinement phase’s role in overcoming over-fitting.

The study examined typical research expectations for US mathematics education faculty and whether they differ by institution type, department type, and research commitment. Based on a literature review, it surveyed US mathematics education faculty with research expectations; 404 target respondents completed the survey. Overall, faculty were expected to publish about 1.64 papers per year, and research journal articles were most valued. R1 faculty were more likely to be in education departments, expected to devote 40% of time to research, and expected about 2.25 papers per year; they were less likely than R2 faculty to have expected numbers in written documents, valued other publications less, and were more likely to require presentations, external funding pursuit or obtaining, and sole authorship. R2 faculty were fairly evenly split between education and mathematics departments; about 65% were expected to devote at least 40% of time to research, with about 1.5 papers per year, and were more likely to have written expectations documents. Other institutions had more mathematics departments, about 20% research time, about 1 paper per year, and were more likely than R2 faculty to value presentations and professional development and less likely to expect external funding. A 10% increase in research commitment was associated with 0.184 more expected papers. Higher research commitment was associated with less likelihood of explicit written paper expectations, less value for books or book chapters and practitioner articles, more requirement to pursue or obtain funding, less value for professional development, and more value for sole and lead authorship. Department differences were few; mathematics departments reported 0.309 fewer expected papers than education departments, valued conference proceedings and funding more, and were less likely to require professional development or presentations or value first authorship. The study concludes that expectations vary by institution type, department type, and research commitment, and recommends clearer written expectations.

This paper studies the orbital Edelstein effect (OEE) and spin Edelstein effect (SEE) in doped monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) in the 2H structure under a perpendicular gate field. The field breaks the σh mirror symmetry, changing the point group to C3v and producing chiral in-plane spin/orbital textures and Edelstein effects due to non-equilibrium Fermi surface shifts. A minimal 5×5 Hamiltonian in the metal d orbital subspace, derived from a tight-binding model including chalcogen orbitals and fitted to DFT bands, is used with electric-field and spin-orbit coupling terms. For hole doping, the Γ valley dominates the response because γ1 is much larger than γ2; the OEE from the two valence subbands adds, while the SEE nearly cancels. Populating the Γ pocket requires a critical hole concentration, but small compressive strain can reduce the Γ-K separation and strongly enhance both OEE and SEE. For electron doping at K/K′, the OEE is several times stronger than the SEE; Korb increases linearly with electron concentration, while Kspin remains smaller due to cancellation between bands. The computed Edelstein susceptibilities are large, with Korb typically around 10−8–10−7 μB V−1m, larger than reported for other systems. The results suggest doped TMDs are promising platforms for studying the OEE and SEE and for spintronics applications.

Keltner Channels, also called Keltner Bands, are technical analysis tools created by Chester W. Keltner in the 1960s. They are used to assess volatility and price trends, overbought or oversold conditions, support and resistance, and entry or exit signals. They consist of three lines: a middle moving average, often a 20-period EMA or SMA/typical price, and upper and lower bands set by an ATR multiplier, commonly 2. Bands expand and contract with volatility. They do not repaint. Compared with Bollinger Bands, Keltner Bands use ATR rather than standard deviation and are less responsive. They can be used for mean reversion, momentum, scalping, and swing trading, and can be customized. Common settings vary; a 20-period EMA with a 2 ATR multiplier is common. In a backtest, a Keltner strategy on SPY had 288 trades, a 77% win rate, 6.3% CAGR, 15% time in market, and a 2 profit factor. Momentum with long periods around 30 days and ATR 1–1.3 produced 143 SPY trades and 3.6% CAGR. Profitability depends on market conditions, discipline, risk management, and skill. Pitfalls include over-reliance and ignoring broader market context.

The Fabian Market Timing Model is a long-term trend-following strategy developed by Richard Fabian in the 1960s. Buy and sell rules are simple and executed weekly, though specific rules require Bronze membership. Backtests show low volatility and maximum drawdown, with returns historically closer to buy-and-hold; high CAGR reflects starting after the dot.com peak. The passage emphasizes mechanical rules and discipline.

The lecture discusses trabecular bone and models osteoporosis using Voronoi honeycombs. It describes obtaining a whale vertebra for testing, then finite element analyses comparing random Voronoi honeycombs with periodic hexagonal honeycombs. The modulus results were close to analytical models, while compressive strength was lower and affected by broader strain/stress distributions. It also models bone loss by thinning versus removing struts; removing struts reduces modulus and strength more strongly and reaches a percolation threshold. Models are adapted toward vertebral bone and extended to 3D. The lecture reviews metal foams for bone substitutes or implant coatings, including manufacturing methods and foam-like stress-strain behavior. Finally, it discusses evolutionary studies comparing trabecular architecture in hominid fossils with humans and other primates to infer bipedalism, and previews tissue engineering scaffolds.

This article by Rinholm, Solem, and Ulleberg explores dialogic classroom practices in music and mathematics education using concepts including epistemological and ontological dialogue, Bildung, musicking, and mathematizing. It is an interdisciplinary qualitative study based on two cases: a pre-service music teacher choir project involving the song “Seasons of Love” and a teacher’s personal AIDS-related story, and an upper-primary mathematics classroom talk about fractions and patterns. Using narrative and hermeneutic analysis, the study finds that both teachers established didactic contracts, listened to students, allowed student input to shape activities, and combined epistemological dialogue about subject knowledge with ontological dialogue engaging students as persons. The music case is analyzed through musicking and existential Bildung; the mathematics case through mathematizing and Bildung. The discussion identifies common dialogic features such as uptake, risk-taking, teacher vulnerability, and subject–subject relations, and raises paradoxes about teacher influence and the limits of controlling Bildung or democratic outcomes. The conclusion states that the chosen concepts helped make sense of dialogic classroom practices and that the teachers promoted participation through both ontological and epistemological dialogic aspects.

This lecture examines gravitational radiation in linearized gravity. It reviews decomposing a flat-space perturbation into six gauge-invariant and four gauge degrees of freedom, governed by four Poisson-type equations; the transverse, traceless part hijTT is the radiative degree of freedom with two polarizations. For a wave propagating in z, hijTT depends on t−z, with components constrained by symmetry, trace-freedom, and orthogonality to propagation. Free-falling bodies follow geodesics, so wave effects are studied through geodesic deviation or light-travel-time changes between separated bodies. The two polarizations are plus and cross, producing tidal stretch and squeeze; LIGO measures these via laser timing and interference. To compute hijTT from a source, the lecture uses linearized Einstein equations in Lorentz gauge with a retarded-time solution. Assuming the far-field limit r much larger than the source, using spatial components and the tensor virial theorem leads to the quadrupole moment Iij and hijTT proportional to 2G/r times two time derivatives of Iij, projected transverse and traceless. This is the quadrupole formula for gravitational waves. The next lecture will discuss a version describing gravitational-wave energy content.

The study validated the longitudinal Grade of Membership (L-GoM) model, developed using Predictors 2 and previously validated in Predictors 1, in the Predictors 3 cohort. Predictors 3 consisted of community-dwelling, multiethnic older adults from Washington Heights/Inwood, Manhattan, recruited through WHICAP, including AD dementia and MCI cases. Initial-visit data were used to predict individual survival and need for full-time care (FTC) over up to 7.5 years, compared with observed group/subgroup proportions.

Of 292 participants, 273 were analyzed: 123 had MCI (83 nonconverters, 40 converters) and 150 had AD dementia (118 nonreverters, 32 reverters). Survival and FTC predictions fit AD nonreverters and MCI cases, and overall fit improved after excluding AD reverters. The model did not fit AD reverters, who survived longer and had lower FTC than predicted and likely were misdiagnosed. L-GoM scores differed by diagnosis, sex, ethnicity, and ApoE. The study concludes the model can predict outcomes in community-dwelling older adults of different ethnic, linguistic, and SES backgrounds and extends to MCI, though further validation for other minority groups is needed.

Fibonacci trading uses Fibonacci tools—such as retracement, expansion, fan, and channel—to identify potential support and resistance and help plan entries, exits, stops, and limits. These tools may lead price, unlike lagging indicators. There is no best timeframe; it depends on trading style, though higher timeframes are often better. Common ratios include 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, and 78.6%; many traders prefer 50%–61.8%. The passage states success is disputed: claims are anecdotal, with no scientific evidence, and a cited backtest by Clarissa Gunawan on Vanguard ETFs found passive trading outperformed an active Fibonacci retracement strategy. The author says they have not seen successful Fibonacci traders or meaningful backtests, recommends caution and combining Fibonacci with other indicators, and suggests other strategies may be better. It also states Fibonacci is probably not good for day trading or crypto.

The passage presents a day trading strategy glossary and FAQ. It defines day trading as buying and selling financial instruments within the same trading day to capitalize on short-term price movements. It lists strategies including momentum, range, scalping, breakout, pullback, reversal, gap, news, pattern, seasonal, dark pool, statistical arbitrage, pairs, order flow, market making, short squeeze, statistical volatility, market profile, regime switching, volatility targeting, and phase analysis. It discusses risks such as market volatility, leverage, and financial loss; the importance of discipline, psychology, technical analysis, and backtesting; capital needs, including FINRA’s $25,000 minimum for pattern day traders; and how time of day, holidays, and seasons affect trading. It states strategies can apply to stocks, forex, futures, and cryptocurrencies with adaptation, and that day trading differs from swing trading by time horizon. FAQ points include that most day traders do not make money, as little as 10% make any money; a $10,000 account might earn $200–$300 daily at a 2%–3% return; consistent 1% daily is unrealistic; and the 11am rule suggests a trending security reaching a new high between 11:15 and 11:30 am EST may end near its high of day.

Yale and Brookings researchers say AI’s effect on the labor market is a “lightning strike,” not a “house fire.” Their study, using BLS data on job losses, unemployment, and occupational composition, finds movement but nothing outside historical norms. Current labor-market shifts appear driven more by a slowing economy, an aging population, and reduced immigration than by AI. The market is described as “low hire, low fire,” with recent graduates struggling and youth unemployment at 10.5%, but no broad AI-driven disruption. The authors argue exposure to AI is often confused with displacement; AI may change work rather than eliminate jobs. Generative AI may affect knowledge and tech cities more than the industrial heartland. Early impacts in software, customer service, and creative work are real but not economy-wide. Real displacement will likely come from redesigned enterprise workflows, not individual chatbot use, and systemic effects could take years.

The passage identifies 1993 and 2023 as major turning points in school choice. After Minnesota authorized charter schools in 1991 and California followed in 1992, the “class of 1993”—Colorado, Georgia, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Mexico, and Wisconsin—helped pave the way for charter authorization in nearly every state. In 2023, a wave of universal multifaceted vouchers appeared as Education Savings Accounts (ESAs). Arizona introduced ESAs in 2011 for specific students, especially those with disabilities; Florida, Mississippi, North Carolina, and Tennessee replicated this. In 2022, Arizona and West Virginia redefined ESAs as vouchers for all students for private school tuition, pods, or homeschooling costs. The “class of 2023” comprised Arkansas, Florida, Iowa, and Utah. The political alignments differ: the class of 1993 and its antecedents were mostly blue, while the class of 2023 and its antecedents, later 2024 states Alabama, Georgia, and Louisiana, and 2025 states Tennessee and Wyoming are red; Texas may join if Governor Greg Abbott succeeds.

Universal ESAs have few strings attached. They derive from Milton Friedman’s 1955 and 1973 essays advocating vouchers for basic education, with parents able to top up, to reduce government’s role and save taxpayers money. ESA amounts generally fall below per-pupil public school spending. EdChoice documents savings and provides a calculator. Chester Finn warns of windfalls, wealth-area entrepreneurship, and dubious purchases; Henry Levin warns of transparency and segregation problems.

Recent issues include spending accountability problems in Arizona and Florida; lack of pedagogical accountability, teacher certification, testing, and curriculum alignment; rising private school tuition after Iowa’s ESAs; ballooning state costs; likely impacts on public school budgets, rural schools, and civic life; and discrimination against students and faculty/staff. ESAs may spread through lobbying and the federal ECCA, though lower private teacher pay and limits on homeschooling/pods provide brakes. The passage recommends resisting expansion, stricter oversight, audits, certified teachers, assessments, civil rights compliance, public hearings or referenda, and local documentation and awareness efforts.

The Side Screen Offense is a two-player screen and roll isolation, described as the most used play in the NBA and found in every team’s playbook. It can be triggered by a point guard dribble-clearing the wing or by passing to the wing and cutting. The basic option is for the guard or wing to drive over the “ON” ball screen, with options such as turning the corner, pulling up, passing to the post, or kicking out. Success depends on execution, coordination, footwork, timing, communication, and experience. The passage outlines defensive reads and counters, including chase over, baseline help, weakside sag, go under, cheat over, fight through, show and recover, switch, mismatches, anticipated switch, denied screen, and traps. Entries include High Post Rub, Power/Motion, and Horns. Continuity options include Flex, Triangle Game, Single/Double Motion, Double Screen, and Baseline Screen. Teaching and implementation use drills, scrimmaging, individual skill work, scouting, and game adjustments. Even if not using it, teams should know how to defend against it.
