The passage examines COVID-19’s impact on education and the introduction of distance education, especially in Greek preschool education. It notes that the Greek Ministry of Education issued guidance for distance education in primary and pre-school education to maintain students’ contact and interest, while kindergarten teachers needed digital skills despite scarce use due to lack of internet and technological access, inadequate school digital infrastructure, family financial inequalities, and lack of teacher training. It reviews preschool education, the Greek curriculum, social and motor skills, communication, definitions and forms of distance education, and the role of parents as facilitators.

The study investigated kindergarten teachers’ views on distance education after its COVID-19 application in the Epirus region of Greece during 2020–2021. It used a quantitative approach, a probability sample of 82 kindergarten teachers, a web questionnaire, and SPSS. Most participants were women, many had 15–25 years of service, and most held bachelor’s degrees. About half had basic ICT certification and 35.4% had enhanced ICT certification. More than three-fourths were little or not at all familiar with distance education before the pandemic, and over 90% had not integrated it before the pandemic. Synchronous distance education was preferred by about 65%, and Webex was used by almost 89%; email and eclass were also used.

Participants’ views were mostly negative: about 90% said distance education reduces psychomotor activities and requires an adult supervisor; 86% said it is less effective than conventional education for developing social skills; 78% said preschool students have difficulty using technology independently; 73% reported limited internet and technological access; and over 65% reported severe school digital infrastructure problems. Some positive views concerned digital skills and flexible learning. A statistically significant difference was found in pre-pandemic familiarity with distance education by ICT certificate, with Level B holders more familiar than those with no certificate. No statistically significant relationship was found between years of service and ICT familiarity. The discussion concludes that teachers lacked readiness and familiarity, that distance education as applied did not meet Greek preschool curriculum principles, and that training, infrastructure, interactive resources, and parent support are needed. The study was limited to Epirus and cannot be safely generalized to the whole country.

A Take a Knee Chart is a downloadable PDF and Google Sheets resource for football coaches to determine when the offense can take a knee. The play, run from the victory formation, is nearly risk-free and runs time off the clock when the offense is ahead; the quarterback kneels, counting as a run, and the chart usually shows player positions and movement order. The passage also stresses clock management, practice, 40-second play clocks, and avoiding incomplete passes.

ML²B is introduced as the first benchmark for evaluating LLMs on generating complete ML pipelines from multilingual natural language descriptions. It extends real Kaggle competition tasks into 13 languages, containing 30 competitions (24 public, 6 private) and 390 evaluation instances, covering tabular, text, and image modalities across 12 domains. It includes human-reviewed task descriptions, structured metadata, standardized data cards, and leakage controls. The benchmark comprises BenchPipeline, Docker runtime, and a code grader, supporting MONO_PREDICT and MODULAR_PREDICT submission formats. Translation used GPT-4o with native-speaker validation. Evaluation uses percentile ranks on the Kaggle leaderboard. Five LLMs across AIDE and ML Master frameworks showed 15–45% performance degradation on non-English tasks. Results indicate English generally yields lower percentiles, low-resource languages have higher/worse percentiles and more non-functional code, and hybrid models partially mitigate gaps. Static leakage analysis found potential leakage in 61 of 554 modular submissions, leaving 33 (5.9%) after further analysis. The conclusion states ML²B surfaces systematic weaknesses in non-English ML code generation and calls for expanded private tasks, domain balance, and multilingual alignment strategies.

The 9 EMA trading strategy uses the 9-period exponential moving average to identify short-term market trends and generate buy and sell signals. A buy signal occurs when price moves above the 9 EMA, and a sell signal occurs when price moves below it. It can be applied to stocks, forex, commodities, options, and crypto. Backtesting showed it worked well in trending assets like Bitcoin but failed in mean-reverting markets like stocks. On Bitcoin, a crossover system had 284 trades with an average gain of 2.65%; adding a 200-day moving average filter reduced trades to 153 with an average gain of 4%. On the S&P 500/SPY, it was described as not tradable, even with the filter. The strategy can be combined with indicators such as RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and candlestick patterns, and with risk management techniques.

Mark Palmer forwarded to Enron recipients a class-action complaint filed in San Diego Superior Court by Pamela R. Gordon against several electricity generators and traders. The complaint alleges violations of California antitrust and unfair business practices laws, the Consumers Legal Remedies Act, and unconscionability, claiming defendants manipulated California’s wholesale electricity market in 2000 by using confidential real-time data, withholding capacity, exporting or parking power, and scheduling outages to inflate prices. It seeks class certification, damages, restitution, disgorgement, and injunctive relief for electricity customers, including SDG&E retail customers, who purchased electricity through the California Power Exchange from May 22, 2000 onward. The passage argues that law’s real efficiency often depends less on publicly exciting acts than on less noticed acts that interested parties seek to defeat. It notes the Government has begun using criminal law in trust and interstate commerce cases where success seems reasonable, after initially relying on civil proceedings; criminal actions have produced successes and deterrent penalties. Judge Holt’s opinion describes a flagrant rebate case with clear evidence, large amounts, deliberate conduct by educated businessmen and a railroad corporation, difficult proof, and few prosecutions since the 1887 Interstate Commerce Act. He says the penalty should match the offense, with the principal penalty on the corporation; the traffic manager acted without personal advantage, under authority or the employer’s policy or wishes.

On August 24, 2025, the Konektadong Pinoy Bill became law to remove roadblocks to Philippine telco competition. It may let Virtual Network Operators compete with PLDT. The passage sets forth regulations for issuing U.S. passports. A passport expires two years after issuance; a new application is required, and naturalized citizens may submit the old passport in lieu of a naturalization certificate under specified conditions. One passport may cover a wife, minor children, or a servant if the application states this and gives the children’s ages and the servant’s allegiance; others require separate passports. Professional titles are excluded. The fee is one dollar, payable by currency or postal money order to the disbursing clerk, not by draft or check. The Department of State does not procure visés. Application forms are furnished, and communications go to the Passport Bureau with a post-office address. The Secretary of State may reject applications for unlawful or improper purposes or noncompliance. Additional rules cover applications in insular possessions, allegiance requirements, and affidavit contents.

The International Nurses Association welcomes Louisiana Registered Nurse Joy Williams, BSN, RN, to its organization and upcoming publication. With over seven years’ nursing experience, she earned a 2009 practical nursing diploma and a 2016 BSN.

Small group differentiation is presented as a pedagogical strategy for enhancing learning outcomes and inclusivity in elementary and higher education, especially for diverse students with varying learning skills and linguistic barriers. The passage cites increasing U.S. demographic and language diversity, notes that differentiation benefits all students, and defines it as tailoring teaching to student needs rather than using one-size-fits-all instruction. The review used literature from 2000–2023 and is guided by Constructivism and Sociocultural Theory. It identifies content, process, products, and learning environment as classroom elements teachers can differentiate; discusses small groups based on student profiles, scaffolding, ongoing assessment, student autonomy, and culturally responsive and inclusive practices; and notes benefits such as engagement, dialogue, relationships, and support for struggling students. It also describes challenges including planning time, inadequate administrative support, large class sizes, and complexity in higher education, where one-size-fits-all instruction persists. Differences between elementary and higher education include student independence, content complexity, assessment, class size, teacher philosophy, resources, and training. Limitations include lack of data for comparative analysis and limited empirical evidence linking small group instruction to outcomes and test scores. The conclusion emphasizes flexible, ongoing assessment and inclusive environments; recommendations include longitudinal studies and research on differentiation by learning styles.

The passage presents the Atlas of Human-AI Interaction, an LLM-based framework for mapping empirical findings from human-AI interaction research. It describes collecting 1,888 abstracts, extracting 2,037 findings from 1,124 papers as [cause, relationship, effect] triplets, processing terms through embeddings, clustering, and graph construction, resulting in 1,310 nodes and 3,908 edges. The Atlas provides 3D Graph, Cause-Effect, and Paper views. Analysis identifies 24 topic clusters, frequent relationships involving students, explanation/trust, design, decision support, and self-referential research; network analysis identifies structural holes around LLMs, generative AI, trust, chatbots, and agents. A user study with 20 experts found the Atlas supported landscape visualization, relationship discovery, and gap identification, while limitations included insufficient detail, concerns about comprehensiveness and temporal analysis, and weaker suitability for technical or formula-based domains. Future work includes continuous updates, more relationship types, improved extraction, and connectivity analysis.

The 4-3 defense uses four defensive linemen, three linebackers, and four defensive backs. It was brought to the NFL by Tom Landry, modernized by Jimmy Johnson, and later associated with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ “Tampa 2.” The defense uses smaller, athletic front-seven players, with the 3-technique tackle and Mike linebacker often considered key. Its strengths include run defense, gap soundness, and multiple coverages; weaknesses include struggles against modern spread offenses and personnel specificity. Offenses attack it by spreading the field and running to the edge. The article also describes common blitzes, Tampa 2 and Cover 3, and teams/coaches such as the 2000s Buccaneers, Chicago Bears, and Montini Catholic HS.

Google has launched Gemini Enterprise, a business-focused AI platform offering advanced Gemini Ultra models and enterprise-grade data governance, security, compliance, explainability, and access controls. It enables firms to deploy and customise AI applications on Google Cloud using proprietary data, competing with Microsoft, Amazon, and OpenAI. Targeted at financial, healthcare, and manufacturing clients, it integrates with Google Workspace and third-party software. Google aims to monetise enterprise AI deployment but must prove reliability and measurable returns.

Ray Dalio’s All Weather Portfolio is a diversified strategy of stocks, bonds, and commodities designed to perform in inflation, deflation, or stagflation. It uses diversification and risk parity to smooth returns and lower drawdowns. Backtests show lower annual returns than stocks but substantially smaller drawdowns, with better performance than stocks during 2008/09, Covid-19 in 2020, and the 2022 bear market. It can be built with ETFs and rebalanced at least yearly, preferably in a tax-deferred account. Leverage or changed allocations can raise CAGR but also increase drawdowns. It is defensive, may underperform in bull markets, and may suit risk-averse investors, retirees, or FIREs, though future performance is not guaranteed.

Mother appealed a dissolution judgment awarding $31 per month per child, arguing it was too low and that abating support during father’s visitation was error. The court agreed father’s visitation expenses should be considered but found $31 insufficient. Because father’s future income was difficult to estimate, the Smith and Belt formulas did not readily apply. The judgment was modified to require $65 per month per child effective on the decision date, affirmed as modified, with no costs.

Please, Continue (Hamlet), by Yan Duyvendak and Roger Bernat, stages a trial of Hamlet for Polonius’s murder in a real courtroom using real judges, barristers and legal teams, with 12 audience members selected as the jury. It has been performed in 12 countries since its 2011 Swiss premiere and differs according to local law; it is staged only in countries with jury systems. The work developed from the creators’ interest in participatory theatre and the Guantánamo trials, and it integrates a real 2010 case in which a young man was accused of killing his girlfriend’s father. After final arguments, the jury decides whether to acquit, aiming to show the complexity of the justice system.

This study used a systematic review and descriptive bibliometric analysis of Scopus data, following PRISMA, to examine metaverse research in education over the last ten years. It analyzed 270 English-language journal articles published between January 2015 and July 2024 using VOSviewer. Research questions addressed annual trends and productive countries, influential journals and articles, and prominent topics and future areas. Findings show no publications before 2020, four articles each in 2020 and 2021, 36 in 2022, a peak of 131 in 2023, and 91 by July 2024. South Korea, China, and the United States were most productive; South Korea led citations, followed by the United Kingdom and China. IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies had the most articles, while Sustainability (Switzerland) was most cited. The most cited article was Dwivedi et al. (2022), followed by Hwang and Chien (2022) and Akour et al. (2022). Frequent keywords included metaverse, virtual reality, education, augmented reality, and artificial intelligence. Prominent topics were the metaverse as a technology for virtual educational environments and perceptions and attitudes toward metaverse adoption. Future research needs longitudinal studies and cross-cultural comparisons. Overall, publications increased from 2020, surged in 2022, peaked in 2023, and metaverse technology was described as bringing revolutionary changes to education.
Order affirmed with $10 costs and disbursements; Thomas, J., dissented; Carr, J., did not vote.

During Severe Weather Awareness Week, Michigan officials are encouraging residents and organizations to take part in a voluntary statewide tornado drill at 1 p.m. Wednesday; nearly all state facilities will participate. Officials urge tornado preparedness, including identifying shelter, conducting drills, monitoring weather, knowing watch versus warning, recognizing tornado indicators, and preparing 72-hour emergency kits. If severe weather occurs April 19, the drill will move to 1 p.m. Thursday.

Transition defense is described as beginning with good offense: taking care of the ball, good shot selection, accurate passing, eliminating unforced turnovers, offensive rebounding, and maintaining defensive balance. Defenders should sprint back, get ahead of the ball, keep vision on the ball, never run with their backs to the ball, and force at least two passes before a shot. Outnumbered situations require pressuring the ball, delaying advancement, forcing extra passes, preventing easy shots, boxing out, and rebounding. The passage covers missed field goals, missed free throws, turnovers, steals, and blocked shots, including jamming the rebounder, denying or disrupting outlet passes, slowing penetration, matching up, and trapping variations. Game strategies include scouting opponents, denying outlet passes to the primary ballhandler, and substituting players who do not sprint back. Implementation includes objectives, Whole-Part-Whole teaching, drills, and including transition defense in full-court scrimmages.

The passage specifies GHCB state and VALID_BITMAP handling for NAE events, including resetting the bitmap before each event, setting required bits for SW_EXITCODE and SW_EXITINFO1/2, and calculating VALID_BITMAP bit positions from field offsets. VMGEXIT should be protected by disabling interrupts and preemption. A non-zero SW_EXITINFO1[31:0] indicates a hypervisor-returned error. The passage describes standard NAE handling and exceptions for MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV Doorbell Page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SEV-TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC, Termination Request, and unsupported NAE handling. It also covers SEV-ES CPUID identification, SMP boot challenges and AP reset hold/jump table mechanisms, NMI completion using #DB intercept, debug register virtualization or DR7 intercept/caching, non-support for SMM and nested virtualization, and #HV doorbell PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields with interrupt-shadow, APIC emulation, EOI, host behavior, and guest behavior requirements.

During Alcohol Awareness Month, the Navy’s free Pier Pressure app helps Sailors make responsible drinking choices. Part of the Keep What You’ve Earned campaign, it includes a calorie counter, Uber and Lyft integration, and has been played over 30,000 times.

On Tuesday, the Dow fell 424.56 points, or 1.74 percent, to 24,024.13 amid fears of rising interest rates and Caterpillar's growth-halt hint. The S&P 500 fell 1.3 percent, Nasdaq 1.7 percent; Caterpillar, 3M and Alphabet shares dropped. The 10-year Treasury yield rose above 3 percent.

In this wrongful death suit, the Court of Civil Appeals of Texas, Amarillo, reviewed a judgment awarding appellees $30,890 against appellants. Appellants appealed, assigning errors in the jury charge. The court found reversible error in charges accompanying several special issues: assuming the deceased husband’s 34½-year life expectancy and support, assuming the surviving mother’s approximately 20-year life expectancy, allowing recovery for loss of love and fatherly advice, and allowing consideration of college education expenses without sufficient basis. It also found error in failing to exclude sorrow and grief and in improper argument by appellees’ counsel. The court held that requested issues on sole proximate cause and new independent cause were properly refused. The judgment was reversed and remanded.

A security researcher found a keylogger in hundreds of HP notebooks, tablets, and other devices, linked to Synaptics touchpad drivers. It is disabled by default, and HP released patches for more than 450 products after confirming the issue. A registry change could let a malicious actor monitor keyboard activity. HP said neither it nor Synaptics has access to customer data from the issue. A similar keylogger issue affecting HP devices was reported in May in Conexant audio drivers.

Police in China shot dead three knife-wielding assailants who killed five and injured 10 in southern Xinjiang’s Pishan County on Tuesday evening, authorities announced Wednesday. Authorities called them “thugs,” said social order was restored and an investigation launched, and did not elaborate on ethnic backgrounds.

The passage reviews MLS midweek matches, noting Philadelphia’s playoff contention and Borek Dockal’s strong performance. It highlights Ilsinho’s goal against Bastian Schweinsteiger, questions Antonio Delamea Milnar’s defending on Josef Martinez, and mentions New England’s late Teal Bunbury penalty in a 1-1 draw.

Johnny Juzang, on a non-guaranteed contract, is making a case for a Timberwolves roster spot as a possible replacement for Nickeil Alexander-Walker. He scored 20 points in 14 preseason minutes and has made 9-of-15 preseason three-pointers, after shooting over 38% from three over the last two seasons.

Researchers at Johns Hopkins and Mayo Clinic compiled a guideline to help stop CK-MB blood testing for suspected heart attack. Published in JAMA Internal Medicine, it cites an American College of Cardiology statement and five studies concluding CK-MB is not effective for detecting damaged heart muscle and can be eliminated. The report is the first HVPAA implementation guide. Despite guidelines favoring troponin, a 2013 survey found 77% of U.S. labs still used CK-MB. The report offers a four-step phase-out blueprint: education, stakeholder partnership, electronic alerts, and measuring outcomes. Additional HVPAA guides target other unnecessary practices.

The paper combines SPH simulations, time-dependent chemistry, and radiative transfer to study observational infall diagnostics in prestellar cores. A critical Bonnor-Ebert sphere (5 M⊙, 0.221 pc, 0.2 km s−1 sound speed) embedded in a lower-density background is given a 10% mass increase to induce collapse and evolved for 0.87 Myr. Molecular abundances are computed with uclchem, and line emission is modelled with radmc3d for C18O, N2H+, HCO+, H13CO+, CS, and C34S. Infall velocities are derived from line profiles using the Myers et al. (1996) method for apertures of 0.2 and 0.05 pc at 0.81 and 0.87 Myr. The line profiles are similar across timesteps but differ with aperture size. Calculated infall velocities fall significantly below the true mass-weighted values; CS gives results closest, about half the true value, while HCO+ often gives values an order of magnitude smaller. The paper attributes this to constant-velocity, two-slab model assumptions and self-absorption originating in outer, lower-velocity regions. It concludes that such techniques underestimate true infall velocities and prestellar mass accretion rates, potentially by an order of magnitude, and notes that optically thin non-thermal velocity dispersions are typically within a factor of two of the mass-weighted infall velocity.

An Indian-origin surgeon, Dr Sachiendra Amaragiri, was struck off the UK medical register after a tribunal found he abused his professional position by writing a love letter to a female patient; he apologised and intends to appeal.

Tesla’s March 11, 2021 Form 8-K states that Jerome Guillen transitioned from President, Automotive, to President, Tesla Heavy Trucking, effective that date; he will lead all aspects of the Tesla Semi program, including related charging and servicing networks.

Sony launched a U.S. instant rebate and trade-in program through September 30, 2017, offering up to $500 for trading in an interchangeable-lens camera plus instant savings on select full-frame cameras, including the A9. It also offers up to $300 off select cameras, up to $200 off A7 cameras, up to $100 off select full-frame lenses and accessories, and free U.S. shipping; eligible discounted models and prices are listed.

Compass Minerals International remains rated “Buy,” with shares attractively valued and recent operational improvement. Revenue and volumes, especially in salt and plant nutrition, are rising, while cost-cutting improves cash flow and EBITDA. Despite higher net debt and leverage than peers, CMP trades at lower multiples with upside potential. Management projects 2025 top-line growth, though leverage risk prevents a “Strong Buy” rating.

CANSLIM is a seven-variable stock-selection method developed by William O’Neill and described in How To Make Money In Stocks. IBD provides the IBD 50 list of stocks fitting the criteria. Backtests indicate the method beat the S&P 500 since 2003 but with higher volatility and larger drawdowns, possibly due to small-cap exposure; recent performance has underperformed the S&P 500. It is intended mainly for long-term investing, is difficult to implement and backtest, and carries risks including market volatility, capital loss, and companies not performing as expected.

He feels great and has not thought much about it. The team needed a win; Rucchin scored two goals, Jiggy played well, and the team played well. He was not at his best in the finals but was glad to contribute offensively. He says they controlled the game, must keep preparing with Mike, and he leads by example. He calls the first two New Jersey games an aberration and says both teams held serve. He discusses a hit, being checked, and returning. Long series create animosity. He recalls Rucchin’s goal as a fond memory.

Following the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge’s hospital appearance with their newborn, Peter Crouch tweeted a quip that drew many retweets and likes; Abbey Clancy replied and commenters reacted. After Kate Middleton gave birth to a boy, Crystal Palace tweeted “Great name!” in response to an AFP tweet saying she gave birth to a son: palace.

A talented basketball team’s tendency to rely on comebacks is a concern, according to Mark Jackson and Jeff Van Gundy, who say persistent slow starts will eventually hurt. The passage cites Golden State’s strong third-quarter scoring and comeback wins over Houston in Games 6 and 7, but also failures in Games 2, 4, and 5, along with historical comeback examples and the warning that endings cannot always be scripted.

Savvy investors are buying closed-end equity mutual fund schemes on stock exchanges at discounts to NAV because these schemes have lock-ins and poor liquidity, so existing investors may sell below NAV. Buyers may profit if they hold until maturity, when redemption occurs at NAV. Examples include Reliance Close Ended Mutual Fund Series A at a 10% discount and HDFC Equity Opportunities Fund at 6%. Discounts depend on time to maturity and tax considerations; spotting opportunities is difficult, and schemes with larger assets under management may be more likely to trade.

Airbus plans to test Project Vahana, an autonomous helicopter-style flying car capable of shuttling several riders, avoiding congested roads through booked airborne taxis, using clean technology, and reducing infrastructure costs. Airbus hopes for short-haul trips by 2021 and a fully functional prototype by 2017. Other efforts include Uber’s proposed VTOL network, Urban Aeronautics’ Cormorant passenger drone for possible military use, AeroMobil’s land-and-air vehicle, and investments from tech figures. The passage says 2017 may be the year flying cars come to fruition.

A letter from fired assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben’Ary said a false social media post apparently led to his termination during a terrorism prosecution. It warned DOJ leadership was removing career officials and was more concerned with punishing the president’s perceived enemies than protecting national security.

A light emitting diode device includes a thin film transistor substrate having light emitting areas; first and second diode electrodes; a first passivation pattern between the electrodes; micro light emitting diodes on the first passivation pattern; a first bridge pattern electrically connecting the first diode electrode to the micro light emitting diodes; and a second bridge pattern electrically connecting the second diode electrode to the micro light emitting diodes. Each sidewall of each micro light emitting diode and each sidewall of the first passivation pattern form a same plane. A method of manufacturing the device forms the first passivation pattern, micro light emitting diode, and second passivation pattern by a single mask process including two etching processes, and then forms the first and second bridge patterns.

The passage covers MLB wild-card action, including three win-or-go-home Game 3s, the second time in baseball history three winner-takes-all playoff games are held in one day. It notes Detroit’s struggles converting scoring chances, a Padres-Cubs bullpen battle with Yu Darvish and Jameson Taillon on quick hooks, and Boston’s bullpen concerns after Alex Cora pulled Brayan Bello early in Game 2. Aspen is replacing its annual Fourth of July fireworks with a 15-minute, 50-drone patriotic light show at Wagner Park due to wildfire risk amid drought and Colorado fire restrictions. Organizers cite increased fire dangers and possible influence from a pre-recorded 2018 Winter Olympics drone display.

The passage reports that U.S. national debt surpassed $21 trillion, growing by $73 billion in one day, $215 billion in February, and more than $1 trillion in six months. It says debt growth has outpaced GDP growth: debt rose 6% last year versus 4.4% economic growth including inflation, and over a decade debt grew 123% while the economy grew 36%. It also describes three public attitudes toward the debt and argues the debt matters.

Jio announced Jio Galaxy Club offers for Samsung Galaxy J2 2018 and Galaxy J7 Duo, both launched in India in April at Rs 8,190 and Rs 16,990. Buyers get Rs 2,750 cashback via 55 vouchers of Rs 50, plus extra or double data on select plans, valid until September 30, online and offline. Specs include qHD/HD displays, Snapdragon/Exynos processors, 2GB/4GB RAM, 8MP/13MP rear cameras, 5MP front cameras, and 2600/3000mAh batteries.

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau finalized rules that could force many payday lenders out of business, but Congress may roll them back. The rules would require payday and auto title lenders to assess borrowers’ ability to repay within 30 days and limit repeated account debits. Supporters say this prevents debt traps; opponents say it would devastate a $39 billion industry serving 30 million to 40 million customers and push borrowers to unregulated lenders. The CFPB estimates loan volume could be cut in half and many stores could close. The rule would take effect in 2019; Republicans and the Trump administration have criticized the CFPB, while a Pew poll found 70 percent want more regulation.

Sarcomas are diverse mesenchymal-derived tumors. Metastatic sarcoma management is generally palliative and relies on systemic therapies, with first-line chemotherapy ORR around 20%, indicating need for new treatments and patient selection. ICI has shown activity in sarcomas. MSI and high TMB predict response in carcinomas but are rare/low in sarcomas; tertiary lymphoid structures and B-cell/CD8+ T-cell infiltrates correlate with ICI response in some soft tissue sarcomas. Epigenetic states regulate transcription and immune signaling, and TE de-repression can stimulate antiviral immune signaling. The study hypothesized that baseline immune infiltrates and immunotherapy outcomes are influenced by TE and epigenetic regulator expression. It analyzed pre-treatment transcriptomic profiles from 67 patients in 3 ICI trials and a validation cohort, identifying immune-cold and immune-hot clusters. Immune-hot tumors had higher ORR (30% vs 8.1%) and longer PFS (3.65 vs 1.7 months; HR=0.43). Immune types were analogous to previously described sarcoma immune classes. Lasso models found TEs and epigenetic regulators predicted immune type, with signature TEs and IKZF1 associated with immune-hot. TE score and IKZF1 expression were significantly associated with immune type, correlated with immune/inflammatory pathways including cGAS-STING, type I/II interferon, antigen processing, CD8+ T-cell effector, and CD274, and correlated with prolonged PFS and higher ORR. In a TCGA validation cohort of 190 sarcoma samples, immune-hot was associated with improved OS; TE and IKZF1 correlated with immune pathways, and high TE score or IKZF1 was associated with greater OS. The authors conclude pretreatment immune status can predict ICI outcomes, propose IKZF1 expression and TE score as potential predictive biomarkers requiring validation, and suggest pharmacologic TE de-repression could be explored. Limitations included small sample size, subtype heterogeneity, three different ICI regimens, polyA selection, and treating epigenetic genes as independent.

Meagan Holt writes about her 3-year-old daughter Madeline, who has Zellweger Syndrome. Seattle Children’s Pediatric Advanced Care Team offers a journaling program to help parents express emotions; consultant Julie Arguez says it empowers them and can bring calm, relief, and acceptance. Holt says writing helps her cope, and the program relies on donations.

The filing includes Exhibit 99.1, the press release announcing those results, and Exhibit 99.2 regarding non-GAAP financial measures. Happy Home Furnishers is closing its Neath store after 33 years. Its managing director cited lack of free parking, increased business rates, and anti-social behaviour, including disruption from pavement works, a bench placed nearby, and problems staff faced. Other retailers described anti-social behaviour, especially in summer, though one stallholder said it did not directly affect him. Neath Council said the street works were completed years ago, benches were removed after anti-social use, and it supports police efforts; it noted a multi-storey car park and free parking on level three after 3pm. The Welsh Government sets business rates and provides relief schemes. The company will continue at other locations and may seek another Neath site, thanking customers.

The passage presents a study exploring physics teachers’ attitudes toward science education research and potential science scepticism toward physics education research (SSSE). It reviews the theory-practice gap and scepticism toward educational research, then reports a two-step mixed-methods design: interviews with 13 in-service German physics teachers and a survey of 174 physics teachers from Germany and Austria. Interview analysis yielded seven main attitudes, both positive and sceptical, and survey items were developed from them. Exploratory factor analysis identified four factors: relevance for individual teachers, feasibility of findings, general relevance for teaching practice, and cooperation between research and school practice. Latent profile analysis identified four teacher profiles: Sceptical Ones (14%), Uncertain Ones (27%), Undersupplied Ones (41%), and Research Advocates (18%). Multinomial logistic regression found only frequency of reading instructional journals significantly predicted profile membership. The discussion states that physics teachers are not generally sceptical but that notable scepticism exists, especially regarding cooperation between research and practice, and considers implications for teacher education and researcher-practitioner cooperation. Limitations include small interview and convenience samples, possible Hawthorne effect, profile classification error, and caution about the instructional-journal measure.

The Ravens are trading pass rusher Odafe Oweh and a 2026 fifth-round pick to the Chargers for safety Alohi Gilman, sources said. Oweh, 26, had no sacks in five games after a career-high 10 last season and saw his playing time fall to a career-low 45% of defensive snaps. Baltimore frees about $8 million in cap space. The Ravens, 1-4 and allowing 35.4 points per game, also added safety Gardner-Johnson. Gilman, 28, was a key deep safety for the Chargers, who needed an edge rusher.

At the 18th VAT Administrators in Africa forum in Lilongwe, Malawi’s Treasury Secretary Ben Botolo urged African countries to use modern technology, including electronic fiscal devices, to address tax noncompliance and improve revenue collection. VADA chair Henry Saka called for formalized regulatory strategies and African solutions to tax evasion.

The lecture reviews propagators in free scalar field theory, interpreted heuristically as transition amplitudes and as correlation functions. It discusses Feynman/time-ordered, retarded, and advanced Green’s functions, their contour singularities, and an epsilon prescription to handle them. Vacuum n-point functions factorize into two-point functions. Composite operators can have singular behavior and require renormalization. The lecture then introduces interactions by adding a φ⁴ term to the Lagrangian, noting the nonlinear equation of motion cannot be solved exactly and is treated perturbatively for small coupling. It defines scattering as the main experimental probe of interactions and introduces the S-matrix, its unitarity and momentum conservation, and the scattering amplitude M. The LSZ theorem is stated as relating M to time-ordered correlation functions in the full interacting vacuum. The path integral will be introduced next.

The speaker discusses the team’s need to stay focused despite the home environment and potential distractions, noting that several players have prior experience in such situations. He also discusses a player’s skating and scoring, trades and player movement, the ice and the team’s routine of staying away the night before games, defensive pairings involving Fetisov, Konstantinov, Murphy and Lidstrom, forward coverage, a previous series against New Jersey, and Kirk Maltby being tried on left wing because the organization had many right wingers.

This application provides a sidelink positioning method and apparatus. Existing positioning determines a terminal device’s position based on reference signal measurement between a network device and the terminal device, is controlled by a core network, and has increased error as distance increases. The proposed method uses sidelink signals between a first terminal device and a second terminal device. A network device sends sidelink positioning configurations to the terminal devices. The first terminal device sends a first sidelink positioning reference signal to the second terminal device, which measures it to obtain a first measurement value. The second terminal device may also send a second sidelink positioning reference signal to the first terminal device, which measures it to obtain a second measurement value. The position of the first terminal device is determined by the first terminal device or the network device based on the first measurement value and/or the second measurement value and the position of the second terminal device. The configurations include reference signal time-frequency resources, sequence information, information about the second terminal device, and reporting configurations; reporting may use Uu or PC5 interfaces. The method is described as reducing positioning latency, improving positioning accuracy, and being applicable when the first terminal device does not support sidelink reference signal measurement.
The passage describes perspective, front, back, side, top, and bottom views of first and second embodiments of an analytical instrument design, noting that broken-line features are not claimed.

A retired lawyer decluttered his house and discarded his McGill University law schoolbooks, bought over 50 years earlier. He considered each book, recalling cases about a smoke-ball reward, damages, an unenforceable carriage and prostitute contract, property concepts like fee simple and fee tail, and a ship explosion. He threw them in the blue recycle bin, later noting a used hardcover listed on Amazon for over $1,000 Canadian. He kept one thick book as a reading stand.

In June 2014, a Wall Street Journal article reported that Hertz Global Holdings would have to restate and correct results from the past three years due to more widespread accounting problems, and its stock had closed down about 9%. Analyst Abby Devins wondered whether Hertz’s accounting issues related to its large rental fleet and what impact this might have on future vehicle acquisition plans. The passage describes the U.S. car rental industry, Hertz’s history and operations, and its 2013 financial performance. In 2013, the industry totaled about $36 billion in revenue and was dominated by Enterprise Holdings, Avis Budget Group, and Hertz. Hertz had about 30,000 employees, almost 12,000 locations in 145 countries, and a rental fleet over 700,000 cars. It reported 2013 revenues of $10,771.9 million and net income attributable to Hertz of $346.2 million. The passage also explains depreciation, Hertz’s rental fleet depreciation accounting, useful life estimates, program versus non-program cars, and comparative data for Hertz and Avis Budget Group.

The passage examines how AI may reshape human cognition, learning, creativity, social organization, social science research, and governance. It states AI may augment cognitive abilities, boost learning, expand imagination, and create new skills and professions, but risks include over-reliance and limited internalization of learned capabilities. Mitigations include avoiding passive learning, selectively delegating non-essential tasks, encouraging critical thinking, and using AI for personalized education and human augmentation. LLMs may disrupt knowledge-scarcity-based social structures and the middle class, prompting changes such as the gig economy and networked global collaboration, with needs for regulations, welfare, and equitable access. In social science, LLMs may synthesize data, automate analysis, and help explore novel theories, but raise concerns about accuracy, bias, misinformation, ethics, and cost. For AI governance, the passage notes challenges such as misinformation, deepfakes, bias, industry-government gaps, and lack of international consensus. It calls for forward-looking, human-centered regulation and cooperation among industry, academia, policymakers, developers, and users through top-down and bottom-up approaches.

The passage gives application and operation guidance for the TLV321x/TLV322x comparators. Unused inputs should not be tied together; they must be tied within the specified input voltage range with at least 50 mV differential voltage. The devices have 1.8 mV of internal hysteresis. Push-pull outputs sink and source current, must not be connected to another output, and unused push-pull outputs must be left floating. Open-drain outputs sink current, can be pulled up to an external voltage from 0 V to 5.5 V independent of V+, and unused open-drain outputs can be left floating or tied to V−. Output shorting can cause thermal runaway and device destruction, so series current-limiting resistors are recommended if shorts are possible. ESD protection circuits connect to V+ and V−, input voltages are limited to 0.2 V beyond the rails, and low-impedance input sources should use series current-limiting resistors to limit transient current to 10 mA or less. POR holds the output low during the POR period after VPOR of 1.65 V is crossed, for up to 32 µs. The passage also covers comparator propagation delay, overdrive effects, external hysteresis using positive feedback, high-speed PCB layout and bypassing recommendations, and a low-side current-sensing application.

Governor Nyesom Wike called for a US Visa Office in Port Harcourt for the South-South and South-East. He described the NDDC as a fund-raising commission for politicians and a corruption cesspit, alleging misuse of funds and failure to act on Rivers projects; he cited the Mother and Child Hospital counterpart funding dispute and said the state took over. He called for Ogoni cleanup and expressed interest in US partnerships in agriculture, oil and gas, and industrialization. US Ambassador William Symington said he wanted to interact with and learn about the state.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated March 19, 2020. Under Item 7.01, Tesla published a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1 and incorporated by reference; it was furnished, not deemed filed, under the Exchange Act except as expressly referenced. Coach Vigneault said he has not personally talked to Dan, though assistants have and he is sure Dan’s teammates have; a bounce did not work out, so the team must move on. He has watched parts of the game and said the team must bring its A game against a very strong opponent; its B game will not win, and there are no obvious areas to exploit. He thought the first period was good but the third was not good enough. He praised Johnny’s skating and consistency and said Rafa has done well. He said the opponent is experienced, structured, skilled, physical, and follows its plan exactly. He said the team must compete, execute, stick to the plan, play to its strengths, especially speed, and turn the page. He praised Rick’s play, size, defense, and scoring chances, and said one player’s stamina and all-around play have been excellent.

The passage is a lecture on possible pathways to nuclear war. The speaker contrasts climate change, described as nearly certain and slow, with nuclear war, described as low-probability on any given day but catastrophic and potentially causing nuclear winter. He discusses debates over nuclear weapons’ utility, Hiroshima and Nagasaki, deterrence, nuclear taboo, and whether possession makes countries more secure, including Ukraine and Kazakhstan after the Soviet breakup. He says early post-1945 arms control failed, citing the Franck Report and scientists’ fears of a Cold War and arms race. The buildup led to MAD, driven by fear and distrust. He identifies accidental US-Russia launch, including early-warning malfunction or cyber attack, and escalation from conventional war between India and Pakistan as main pathways; North Korea is less likely and seeks deterrence and regime survival. Pakistan’s aggressive posture and delegated control raise rogue-commander risks; India has civilian control and no-first-use but has not pursued a political solution with Pakistan. On the NPT, he notes nonproliferation obligations, Article VI disarmament, review conferences, states outside the treaty, and fewer nuclear-armed states than earlier predictions. On Iran, he describes negotiations, an interim agreement, inspections, centrifuges, and sanctions debates. He addresses abolition as possibly desirable but unlikely, and argues deterrence does not reliably coerce and can introduce instability. He assesses Obama’s record as mixed, citing the Prague speech, New START, nuclear security, continued hair-trigger alert, modernization, strategic patience toward North Korea, and test-monitoring efforts. He concludes the present situation is stable “with luck” and that public opinion and arms control organizations matter.

The passage expresses hope for a secretary of commerce with a Cabinet seat, citing labor and capital questions, corporate growth, and commercial support, and urges Congress to create the department with large powers over interstate corporations. It hopes to submit a reciprocity treaty with Cuba and notes a concluded convention with Great Britain for reciprocal trade with Newfoundland. It discusses arbitration and The Hague tribunal, citing U.S.-Mexico use, and commends Hawaiian fire claims. It notes Congress provided for an isthmian canal, preferably at Panama, with negotiations pending with Colombia, and says the work should continue across administrations.

An environment watchdog criticized a council’s claim that Central Bedfordshire needs up to 55,000 new homes over 20 years. CPRE Bedfordshire said a Freedom of Information request showed 60% would be for people moving into the area. An assessment identified an objectively assessed need of 32,000 homes for 2015–2035, with 41% meeting current residents’ needs. The council added 7,400 homes for Luton residents and up to 20% contingency. CPRE called this unsustainable, citing infrastructure. CBC said government requires it to plan for migration trends and population needs.

President Andrew Johnson transmitted to the House of Representatives correspondence with General U. S. Grant concerning Grant’s vacation of the War Office, including Johnson’s letter of February 10, 1868, and accompanying papers. In that letter Johnson disputes Grant’s account of their January 14 Cabinet conversation, submits statements from five Cabinet members who were present, asserts that Grant accepted the office of Secretary of War ad interim to defeat Johnson’s purpose regarding Stanton, and charges Grant with insubordination for refusing to obey Johnson’s order concerning orders from the War Department. The Cabinet replies by Gideon Welles, Hugh McCulloch, Alex W. Randall, O. H. Browning, and William H. Seward give their recollections of the January 14 conversation, with several stating that Johnson’s account was substantially correct. Johnson also forwarded Grant’s February 11 letter to the House. Grant acknowledged receipt, did not admit any differences from his prior statements, denied intending to disobey any legal order distinctly given by the President, explained his interpretation of the order, and enclosed War Department correspondence involving Secretary Stanton, the Treasury Department, and the Post Office Department.

Grieving people may find holidays difficult. Grief specialists Vicki Travnicek and Nicole Bruder advise making a plan, limiting events, having an exit plan, being honest with hosts, feeling emotions, sharing memories, being patient, self-care, and creating new traditions while keeping some old ones. The Surviving Suicide Grief Support Group meets first and third Tuesdays at Smith-Leroy; other grief programs are also listed.

Under Item 2.02, Microsoft issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2016, furnished as Exhibit 99.1. This study explored medical students’ perceptions of resilience and a curriculum-based resilience skills building course at Mohammed Bin Rashid University of Medicine and Health Sciences, Dubai, UAE. The six-hour course was delivered during Year 4 of the MBBS to raise awareness of stress and burnout and provide tools for understanding, developing, and deploying resilience. It was assessed through attendance, an OSCE, and reflective essays. Using a qualitative phenomenological design, the study analyzed reflective essays from 37 of 38 enrolled Year 4 students. Thematic analysis generated three interlinked themes: Awareness, Application, and Appraisal, termed the 3As of Building Resilience. Awareness included personal interpretations, associations, relevance, and conscious practice. Application included concept, exercises, and faced challenges. Appraisal included building resilience, the course, and exercises. Students described resilience as an ongoing, learnable process and associated it with mindfulness, meditation, social support, and emotional intelligence. They reported relevance to personal, academic, professional, and clinical contexts, and cited exercises such as mindfulness, breathing, yoga, reflection, gratitude, prayer, physical activity, and cognitive reframing. Challenges included scepticism, lack of time, effort, and difficulty prioritizing practice. Students positively appraised the course, reporting perceived benefits for wellbeing, relationships, academic performance, self-awareness, emotional regulation, coping, and clinical training. The discussion states the course was anchored in constructivism and experiential learning and fostered self-directed learning. Limitations include a single-cohort context, transferability, social desirability bias, and the need for mixed methods and validated pre/post measures. The study concluded that integrating such a course into medical curricula is likely to be positively appraised and raises awareness and proactive application of resilience skills.

North Carolina lost 38-10 to Clemson, falling to 2-3 and 0-3 against Power 4 teams with a combined 120-33 scoring deficit in those games. Coach Bill Belichick said the team must keep doing what it is doing but better, citing self-inflicted wounds, execution, concentration, and coaching, and taking responsibility. After a GM letter described a rebuilding season, Belichick said UNC is building for recruits, but receiver Shipp said he is there to win, not rebuild. Belichick said he won’t make personnel changes based on a long-term vision; the best players will play.

The passage describes an undergraduate special education course, “All Means All: Inclusive Teaching for Students with Disabilities,” created by Dr. Harper and taken by first-year student Madison. The article argues that advocacy is a professional responsibility for special education teachers and should be integrated into teacher preparation coursework as a recurring theme rather than a standalone lesson. The five-credit, 10-week course uses learning goals, weekly TED Talk analyses, low-stakes reflections, a jigsaw activity on special education law and policy, an in-class debate on inclusion, Week Nine instruction on disability advocacy and policy, and a final TED Talk and paper to build advocacy and argumentation skills. The passage states such coursework prepares pre-service teachers to advocate for students, navigate systemic barriers, and use evidence-based practices. It concludes that advocacy should be incorporated into every pre-service special educator course and notes Madison later seeks Dr. Harper’s advice on advocating at her school, with recommendations to connect with other special educators and CEC chapters.

Community-based organizations and out-of-school-time programs should be part of youth mental health support because families and schools cannot do it all. These spaces build trusted relationships and can offer basic mental health support—recognizing, responding to, and referring youth to professionals—if staff receive tools, training, and resources. The passage cites urgent youth mental health needs, young people’s openness to support, and recommendations to invest in partnerships, staff training, mental health infrastructure, and frontline worker well-being to complement school-based efforts.

MITOCW 14.271 F22 Lecture 11 is a lecture by a professor substituting for Glenn; he will teach two classes, one on the morality of markets and one on regulating tech giants. The lecture focuses on platforms as two-sided markets and issues of too little cooperation, including concerns about behavioral manipulation, self-preferencing, contestability, and access/fair compensation for merchants and apps. It reviews the Chicago School argument that platforms benefit from rich ecosystems and need not discriminate, then lists rebuttals: regulated consumer prices, zero lower bounds from negative opportunity costs and arbitrage, protection of the core segment, and a second zero lower bound for apps/merchants that can yield supranormal profits. It notes limits to regulating platforms like public utilities because firms are global and fast-changing. It discusses the EU Digital Markets Act and similar US moves, contestability, multihoming, interoperability, portability, entry/acquisition issues, and access pricing. In a two-sided platform model with in-house and third-party apps, access charges affect foreclosure, price squeezes, and profits; too-low access can lead to foreclosure, too-high to squeeze. The optimal access charge is b under added considerations, but eliciting b is difficult; simple regulatory rules are needed. The next class will cover the morality of markets.

Avoyelles Parish is projected to spend about $8,123 per student in state and local revenues for 2017-18, second-lowest among 69 districts; its local share is $2,102, 68th of 69. The state average is $9,015, while Bogalusa will spend the most at $11,546. Louisiana reduced education spending by 5.1 percent from 2008 to 2017. The MFP formula gives more state funds to poorer systems and includes adjustments; Avoyelles receives about 74.15 percent state and 25.85 percent local revenues. A Senate resolution requests a BESE task force report on actual education costs by Feb. 1, 2018.

EO 11905, issued by President Ford in 1976 after congressional investigations, replaced the 40 Committee with the Operations Advisory Group, specified its membership, required meetings and periodic reviews, and banned U.S. Government employees from political assassinations and domestic intelligence activities. Hughes-Ryan continued to govern covert action approval and oversight. President Carter replaced the OAG with the NSC’s Special Coordination Committee, later SCC–Intelligence, which continued OAG procedures and membership; EO 11985 formalized the replacement, and EO 12036 reaffirmed it, making the Attorney General and OMB Director full members. The SCC–I created the SAWG, active through at least 1978, later falling out of use; by late 1979 an Aaron-chaired interagency group handled certain covert actions. Carter used worldwide/general covert-action findings; Perspectives, drafted by CIA and cleared by State, provided tasking, initially without further OAG/SCC/President coordination, with field reports and, from 1978, line-item additions to a worldwide finding.

The passage welcomes Super Bowl LII weekend, notes the Patriots will play the Eagles in Minneapolis, and suggests Steelers fans pull for the Eagles. It mentions a game thread, a contest, five Friday night questions, and two bonus questions about playoffs, Kirk Cousins, Nick Foles, the coin flip, Rob Gronkowski, combined scoring/explosive plays/turnovers, and Alan Faneca. The passage is a lecture for 18.100A Real Analysis. The instructor states the course goals are to gain experience reading and writing proofs and to prove statements about real numbers, functions, and limits. This daily news roundup covers continued Russia investigations after Flynn’s exit, Netanyahu’s White House visit and a suggested policy shift, Kim Jong Nam’s killing and an arrest, NATO defense talks, cracks at California’s Oroville Dam, a study on risky driving, a Boeing union vote, high-tech Swedish produce, Kate Upton’s Sports Illustrated cover, and Rumor’s Westminster win.

New computer modeling and reanalysis of decades of data indicate Uranus releases about 15% more energy than it receives from the Sun, suggesting it has internal heat. This contrasts with the long-held view after Voyager 2’s 1986 flyby that Uranus had no internal heat. Researchers combined observations from ground- and space-based telescopes, including Hubble and NASA’s Infrared Telescope Facility, with data on Uranus’ hazes, clouds, and seasonal changes to estimate its energy budget. Uranus still emits far less heat than Neptune, which emits more than twice the energy it receives. The findings may help explain Uranus’ past and inform understanding of similarly sized exoplanets.

Oclaro Inc shares recently traded down 0.99%. Analysts project a 52-week consensus target of $9.27 from 13 opinions, with a high of $11.25 and low of $6.5, versus a latest close of $9.04. Its ABR is 2.38, with 2 Buy, 3 Outperform, 9 Hold, 0 Underperform, and 0 Sell ratings. The passage reports a study assessing machine learning (ML) models to predict restriction from spirometry. ERS/ATS guidelines define restriction as TLC below the lower limit of normal and allow absence of restriction to be predicted from a normal FVC, citing a 1999 study. A recent diverse multicenter reassessment using race-neutral equations estimated the FVC LLN negative predictive value (NPV) at 80.5%, lower among non-Hispanic Black patients. The study developed and externally validated logistic regression, random forest, and boosted tree models using demographic, anthropometric, and spirometric data. Development and validation datasets included 42,462 and 24,524 PFTs. The random forest model had the highest overall performance; in validation, its NPV was 88.3% versus 72.7% for FVC LLN, sensitivity 83.3% versus 46.0%, specificity 82.9% versus 94.4%, and AUC-ROC 0.91, though calibration was poor. It excluded static lung volume measurement in 56.7% of tests versus 78.4% for FVC LLN. NPV among non-Hispanic Black patients was 74.6% for random forest versus 49.5% for FVC LLN, and 90.9% versus 79.6% among non-Hispanic White patients. Decision curve analysis favored the random forest model for most thresholds, while FVC LLN was preferred for thresholds 0.59 to 0.76. The study concludes ML improved accuracy and equity in excluding restriction from spirometry, with limitations including academic-center data, ascertainment bias, limited racial/ethnic diversity, and no patient/provider feedback.

In a certiorari proceeding, G. M. Cox challenged Judge George W. Burnham’s jurisdiction after a pharmacist’s application for a liquor permit was continued beyond the term to which it was brought and later granted. Cox argued the application could be heard only at the first term. The court held that the relevant liquor-permit statutes are not mandatory and do not deprive the court of jurisdiction. An adjournment does not ipso facto dismiss the application, and absent contrary proof, cause for continuance is presumed. The proceedings were dismissed.

Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2018 describes it as designing, developing, manufacturing, and selling fully electric vehicles and energy generation and storage systems, installing and maintaining energy systems, and selling solar electricity. It produces Model S, Model X, and Model 3, with future planned vehicles including Model Y, Tesla Semi, pickup truck, and a new Tesla Roadster. Energy products include Powerwall 2, Powerpack 2, solar energy systems, and Solar Roof. It operates two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. Manufacturing occurs in Fremont and Lathrop, California; Tilburg, Netherlands; Gigafactory 1 near Reno, Nevada; and Gigafactory 2 in Buffalo, New York, and it began constructing Gigafactory Shanghai in January 2019. As of December 31, 2018, it had 48,817 full-time employees. The filing also discusses risks including delays in product design, manufacture, launch, production, delivery, and servicing; Model 3 ramp and cost/volume targets; supplier and single-source dependence; Gigafactory expansion; product defects; growth management; manufacturing costs; and material and lithium-ion cell supply/costs.

Asian stocks were mixed as investors worried about a Sino-U.S. trade war before the July 6 deadline for U.S. tariffs on $34 billion in Chinese imports. MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index outside Japan rose 0.1% after a nine-month low, while Japan’s Nikkei fell 0.5%. Wall Street fell, with technology shares under pressure. Facebook, Tesla, Micron and Japanese chip-related shares declined. The yuan remained near 11-month lows, though China’s central bank pledged stability. The Mexican peso surged 2.6%. Oil rose on U.S. stockpile data, while copper hit nine-month lows.

To identify monthly “best all-around” CCC stocks, the passage first uses the Dugan Stock Scoring System, then applies filters. These include being in the top Dugan-scoring half of non-REIT and non-MLP companies on David Fish’s January 2017 “All CCC” list of 684 companies; minimum 2.25% yield; minimum $5B market cap; maximum relative Graham number of 70; maximum payout ratio of 70; minimum most-recent dividend increase of 5%; minimum estimated EPS growth of 5% next year and 5%/year over five years; maximum debt/equity of 1; and minimum Dugan Score of 50. The first filter is most important. The Dugan system evaluates quality across Risk, Value, Past Performance, and Future Performance Expectations, with a broker sector-weighting bonus or penalty. The 2017 system and filters yielded 21 companies.

East of England Ambulance Service NHS Trust was rated Requires Improvement overall by the CQC, with Outstanding for caring and Requires Improvement for safety, effectiveness, leadership and responsiveness. Inspectors found progress in safeguarding, Mental Capacity Act understanding and incident reporting, but the trust still did not meet national ambulance response standards, winter delays led to serious incidents, and staff morale was low. The trust acknowledged room for improvement, welcomed recognition in some areas, and cited challenges including staff engagement across a large area and additional funding.

Coach DeBoer said the team has been in similar situations before against the Rangers and Philly and believes it can win several in a row, starting with one win. He said lineup changes are considered after watching tape and assessing available depth, but he does not favor changes just because of a loss or panicking. He credited LA’s goaltender and team, noted missed quality chances by Zajac, Kovalchuk and Elias, and said the team must score more than one goal and convert power plays. He cited past frustration by Lundqvist and Florida’s power play, said officiating has been good and both teams are trying to stay disciplined, discussed travel and start-time adjustments, questioned a lost-sight puck call, and said he was not disappointed because the team played to the final buzzer.

Temple Grandin, professor and author known for animal behavior and livestock handling research, will present "Livestock Handling and Animal Behavior" at a Feb. 23 breakfast event at the Tehama District Fairground in Red Bluff, sponsored by Shasta College and UC Cooperative Extension.

Apple Inc. filed Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended March 30, 2019. For the three months ended March 30, 2019, net sales were $58,015 million, net income was $11,561 million, basic EPS was $2.47, and diluted EPS was $2.46. For the six months ended March 30, 2019, net sales were $142,325 million and net income was $31,526 million. On April 30, 2019, Apple announced an increase in its share repurchase authorization from $100 billion to $175 billion. The filing also covers accounting pronouncements, financial instruments, income taxes, debt, shareholders’ equity, benefit plans, commitments and contingencies, legal proceedings, segment information, and management’s discussion and analysis.

Israel and Canada signed a modernized Canada-Israel Free Trade Agreement in Montreal, replacing their 1997 agreement. It eliminates duties on thousands of additional products and adds chapters or provisions on labor, the environment, trade and gender, small and medium-sized enterprises, corporate social responsibility, and dispute settlement. Officials called it historic and said it would bolster economies and open opportunities; it aims to double trade and takes effect after ratification by both parliaments.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture enables real-time ray tracing in single-GPU systems via RT Cores, RTX software, and filtering. It works with Microsoft’s DirectML and DXR APIs, adds advanced shading, and inherits CUDA Volta enhancements. GeForce and Quadro products will use Turing GPUs; the paper focuses on TU102, shipping in GeForce RTX 2080 Ti and Quadro RTX 6000.

This study reports a PRISMA-guided meta-analysis of 13 studies from 2015 to July 2024 examining AI-related technologies in education across eight countries. It found an overall positive effect size of 0.86 (95% CI [0.45, 1.27], p < 0.0001), with substantial heterogeneity and publication bias. Chatbots and generative AI had an effect size of 1.02 (95% CI [0.45, 1.59], p < 0.0001); online learning and virtual reality had 0.79 (95% CI [-0.04, 1.62], p < 0.07); learning management systems and AI platforms had 0.62 (95% CI [0.03, 1.21], p < 0.05). Novel Naive Bayes, TF-IDF/BM25, and BERT-based algorithms were applied in meta-analysis experiments, and a weighted hybrid random- and fixed-effects model yielded 0.88 (95% CI [0.48, 1.29], p < 0.0001). The study concludes that AI technologies generally show positive effects in education, but effectiveness varies by context and implementation, and further research is needed.

The passage states that during colder months, when colds and flu spread, food can provide some protection. Rest and hydration aid recovery, while good nutrition supplies nutrients and energy for immune function; poor nutritional choices can slow recovery and worsen symptoms. Fruit and vegetables, especially varied and different coloured ones, provide vitamins, minerals, fibre/prebiotics, vitamin A and C, magnesium and zinc. Protein supports growth, repair, digestion, hormones and immune defences. Herbs, spices, probiotics, and nuts and seeds can also support immunity, gut health, nutrient absorption, and cell repair after infection. These food groups can be included in daily diets.

A Danish study of 4,741 mothers found children of older mothers had fewer behavioural, social and emotional difficulties at ages seven and 11, but no difference by 15. Older mothers were described as worrying less during pregnancy, more positive about parenting, often in stable, educated, better-off circumstances, and psychologically mature, scolding/disciplining less. Researchers noted later motherhood also carries health risks and psychosocial pros and cons.

Fredrik went for X-rays, with a report expected by the end of the day; he returned and finished the game after missing a few shifts. A line that has played together since early in the Colorado series or before has been productive, including McCarty’s hat trick and a goal last night; Darren hit the post, and the speaker does not see the line as a problem. On the power play, Colorado blocked shots and pressured quickly, so better shots are needed. The next game is different, the second game is crucial, and the focus is evening the series. One player had a poor game, but others had chances; possible line adjustments, faceoffs, and referee penalty calls are noted. Penalty time caused ice-time imbalance for Yzerman, Fedorov, and Shanahan, reducing minutes for others, so adjustments and more balance are needed. Carolina moves the puck out quickly, and Detroit must correct entries, get the puck deep, and change its forecheck.
Scientists made functional human egg cells from skin cells; these could form early embryos.

Niu Technologies’ stock has posted big gains in 2025, helped by strong growth in recent quarters. This growth needs to continue, but that is not assured. Factors could disrupt expected growth and make it insufficient to justify the rally and valuations. The author is neutral on NIU stock with a hold rating.

The passage describes CAR T cell therapies with enhanced efficacy. It provides engineered immune effector cells, such as T or NK cells, expressing a CAR, in which Tet1, Tet2, and/or Tet3 expression or function is reduced or eliminated, particularly Tet2. It also provides Tet inhibitors, including gene editing systems (e.g., CRISPR/Cas9, zinc finger nucleases, TALENs, meganucleases), siRNA/shRNA, dominant-negative proteins, small molecules, and nucleic acids encoding them, as well as vectors comprising CAR and Tet inhibitor sequences. Methods include increasing CAR-expressing cell therapeutic efficacy by decreasing 5-hydroxymethylcytosine levels, contacting cells with a Tet inhibitor ex vivo or in vivo, manufacturing CAR-expressing cells, and treating subjects with cancer or other diseases associated with tumor antigen expression. The passage further presents figures and data on CAR19 insertion into Tet2, Tet2 disruption, 5-hydroxymethylcytosine changes, Tscm expansion, and Tet2 knockdown/editing.

"Russian math" after-school programs are growing in the U.S., led by the Russian School of Mathematics, with 22,000 students and 40 branches. They draw on Russian teaching traditions emphasizing reasoning, deep understanding, and early algebra and geometry rather than memorization. Parents cite dissatisfaction with American math, children’s interest, and future opportunities. Classes usually meet weekly and cost about $2,000 a year. The trend traces to Soviet math education and Russian emigration, especially to the Boston area. It poses challenges for American schools, including students already covering topics, possible overconfidence, and performance gaps between families who can and cannot afford it. Some report growth in honors classes, but researchers say effects are not extensively studied and data are lacking.

This Mendelian randomization study assessed genetically determined pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) and multiple cardiovascular disease (CVD) risks and the mediating role of hypertension. Using 11 SNPs as instrumental variables from GWAS data and IVW with sensitivity analyses, it found genetically determined PAT was significantly correlated with higher risks of CVD, heart failure, hypertension, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and venous thromboembolism. No obvious relevance was found for cardiac arrhythmias, atrial fibrillation, aortic aneurysm, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, myocardial infarction, cardioembolic stroke, small vessel stroke, large artery stroke, or subarachnoid hemorrhage. A 2-step mediation MR indicated hypertension mediated associations of PAT with CVD, HF, CHD, IHD, and IS, with mediated proportions for HF 13.23%, CHD 13.51%, IHD 19.18%, and IS 14.51%. The study concluded PAT may be a potential therapeutic target and antihypertensive drugs could be used conjunctly, especially for people with obesity and greater PAT accumulation, while limitations included European participants, lack of multivariable MR, sample overlap, and small cases for some outcomes.

Enron disclosed that the SEC requested information about related-party transactions involving partnerships run by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron called it an informal inquiry and said it would cooperate. The disclosure followed a $1.01 billion third-quarter write-off, a $618 million loss, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity from unwinding the LJM partnerships. Enron shares fell more than 20% to $20.65. Analysts and investors criticized unclear disclosure and raised concerns about other off-balance-sheet trusts, possible dilution, and additional losses. Shareholder and class-action lawsuits were filed, and Enron scheduled a conference call.

Indian troops killed three youths during a siege and search operation in Awneera, Shopian district; a mosque and four houses were blasted, and protests led to pellet-fire injuries. Earlier, two Indian soldiers were killed and several injured in Awneera, and three troops were injured in Bandipora. Train services were suspended. Resistance leaders opposed undermining Jammu and Kashmir’s disputed status or demographic change, and a Dalgate blast victim died.
