This passage presents a metagenomic next-generation sequencing workflow combining HostEL, a magnetic bead-immobilized nuclease strategy for human background depletion and pathogen DNA/RNA enrichment after selective lysis, and AmpRE, a single-tube additive DNA/RNA library preparation. Analytical validation used human plasma spiked with ZymoBIOMICS Microbial Community Standard at dilutions down to 70,000 cells/mL, equivalent to 70 copies/µL, and sequencing on iSeq 100 and MiniSeq with different turnaround times. HostEL preserved species distribution and increased non-human reads; with HostEL, sensitivity and specificity were 96% each, versus 82% and 97% for controls. Clinical validation used 42 plasma samples, with 93% agreement with qPCR results. Both DNA and RNA viruses were detected when Ct was less than 33. The workflow detected bacteria, fungi, DNA viruses, and RNA viruses, showed 100% agreement with negative clinical molecular diagnosis samples, and achieved concordance with positive clinical molecular diagnosis samples. It can deliver results in 27 hours on iSeq 100 or 13 hours on MiniSeq, with shorter protocols showing comparable sensitivity. Limitations noted include inapplicability to parasite infections and limited pathogen and biofluid diversity.

Cruzin’ for Life, a Santa Maria nonprofit, raised funds to retrofit a transport van for Mission Hope Cancer Center. In its first year, the van transported more than 2,600 cancer patients and logged over 34,000 miles across several area communities. The group continues fundraising through events including a Valentine’s Day crab feed and an annual car show and cruise, and may consider a second van if need and funding exist.

A woman in South Africa was declared dead by paramedics after a car crash and later found alive in a mortuary refrigerator; two other occupants died. Ambulance service Distress Alert said procedures were followed and launched an investigation.

Jim Montgomery enters his first full season as Blues coach in 2025–26 after a midseason takeover led to the playoffs’ first round. The Blues open Oct. 9 at Enterprise Center, with seven of their first 11 games at home. Early rivalry games include an Oct. 18 meeting, the first since last year’s postseason clash. Other key dates include Oct. 15, Dec. 12, Jan. 7 at Chicago, April Central Division games against Colorado, Winnipeg, Chicago, and Minnesota, and an April 16 finale in Utah. The NHL pauses Feb. 5–25 for the Olympics. Montgomery inherits veterans and young talent, with questions about defense, young forwards, and adapting to Central Division play across 26 division games.

San Juan Mayor Carmen Yulin Cruz called new Hurricane Maria death toll estimates “a day of collective mourning.” A Harvard study estimated 4,645 “excess deaths” from Sept. 20 to Dec. 31, more than 70 times Puerto Rico’s official toll of 64, with a margin of error of plus or minus 3,852 and a likely figure of about 5,000. Yulin Cruz criticized the government and Trump and said Puerto Rico is not prepared for the hurricane season.

The passage reports a backtest of a NIFTY 50 end-of-month effect using Yahoo Finance data starting in 2007. It says the optimal exit was the close of the second trading day of the new month, and the best entry by profit factor was the fifth or sixth last trading day. A strategy going long at the close of the fifth last trading day and selling at the close of the second trading day of the new month showed a 10.5% CAGR, 30% market exposure, and a 26% maximum drawdown, outperforming buy and hold. It notes some curve fitting but reasonable robustness and comparability to the US turn-of-month effect.

Celtic’s 2-1 win at Ibrox gives them a 19-point lead over Rangers with a game in hand, set to be the biggest gap between the clubs in 91 years. In 1925-26 Celtic won the title while Rangers finished sixth, 20 equivalent points behind. Rangers were also 15 points behind in 1985-86, converted to 22 today.

This study reviews literature on drama and STEAM education and reports a qualitative pilot case study. It asks how higher education students view dramatic activities in science or history and what students can achieve in a STEAM classroom when engaged in dramatic activities. The literature review discusses arts-based educational approaches, drama-based pedagogy, and drama’s reported benefits for achievement, psychological and social outcomes, skills, imagination, creativity, collaboration, communication, confidence, and problem-solving. It also discusses STEAM education, art-based methods, interdisciplinary teacher collaboration, and challenges of using drama in STEAM, including management, curriculum, time, teacher qualifications, and student participation.

The pilot study used participant observation and detailed field notes with 19 first-year university students, all women, at ELTE University in Budapest during a bachelor art-based methods course. Two drama activities were conducted: “The Life Cycle of a Butterfly” and “Indian Caste System.” In the first, groups of three created and presented movements about the butterfly life cycle. In the second, groups of four or five sketched and presented a scene about a day in the life of an Indian caste group. Students reflected on the activities.

Findings were grouped into four observations: creativity, group collaboration, problem-solving and thinking skills, and motivation and involvement. Students reported interest, creativity, varied interpretations, collaboration, support, and enthusiasm. The conclusion states that drama can be a valuable, enjoyable, motivating tool in STEAM education and can support competence development, confidence, concentration, language skills, and group work, though challenges include nonparticipation, difficulty, and lack of time, experience, and confidence. Limitations include the small sample of 19 students, narrow demographic characteristics, limited experience with STEAM and drama-based pedagogy, and concerns about generalizability.

The passage describes an autonomous vehicle control system with multiple independent control systems for redundancy in safety-critical situations. It includes vehicle interfaces, an autonomous control system with multiple sensors and processing resources that determines vehicle actions or states and signals control parameters to the interfaces, and a bypass control unit that operates independently to detect specific conditions or events and implement a predetermined response through a preselected vehicle interface. Auxiliary control units may act as failsafes or bypasses, perform trajectory verification, or provide avoidance or mitigation responses. They may receive trajectory data, use dedicated sensors, communicate vehicle response outputs to the AV control system or directly to vehicle interfaces, and take priority over AV commands. The units may be optimized for reliability, including hardware or firmware architectures and ASIL metrics. Examples include control systems, an autonomous vehicle, and methods for operating the vehicle.

TrackR unveiled new Bluetooth tracking devices ahead of CES: the TrackR pixel, an updated TrackR wallet 2.0, and the TrackR atlas. The pixel is a cheaper, colorful alternative to the TrackR bravo. The wallet is visually similar to a credit card and called the thinnest item-finder. All offer Bluetooth tracking and crowd-sourced discovery. The atlas is a smart plug that maps a home and supports Amazon Alexa. Batteries last about a year and are replaceable. Prices are $24.99, $29.99, and $39.99; pre-orders were announced for today, with only the atlas available as of writing, and launch is expected in Spring.

The passage lists five lightning myths: lightning is attracted to metal, rubber tires protect car occupants, sunny weather is safe, lightning never strikes twice, and trees are good shelter. It states metal does not attract lightning; height, pointy shape, and isolation matter. A car’s metal roof and sides, not tires, protect occupants. Lightning can strike up to 10 miles from a thunderstorm, repeatedly strike tall isolated objects, and hit trees. Most leisure lightning deaths occur on or near water.

NVIDIA Corporation reported that on May 2, 2016, it announced NVIDIA and Samsung agreed to settle all pending intellectual property litigation. The agreement will immediately dismiss all pending IP litigation between the companies in U.S. district courts, the U.S. International Trade Commission, and the U.S. Patent Office. It includes each company licensing a small number of patents to the other, with no broad cross-licensing or other compensation.

Thinking Machines Lab, led by Mira Murati and other former OpenAI researchers, launched its first product, Tinker, a tool that automates creation of custom frontier AI models. Tinker lets users fine-tune two open source models, Meta’s Llama and Alibaba’s Qwen, through an API using supervised learning or reinforcement learning, then download and run the fine-tuned model. The company says it aims to make frontier capabilities more accessible and demystify model tuning. Access is by application, currently free with eventual charges. Beta testers described Tinker as more powerful, user-friendly, and simpler than some alternatives. The startup raised $2 billion in seed funding at a $12 billion valuation. Thinking Machines vets API access and plans automated safeguards against misuse. The launch reflects a bet that fine-tuning frontier models is the next AI frontier and a commitment to openness amid increasingly closed commercial models.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2021, states that it seeks to be Earth’s most customer-centric company and operates in North America, International, and Amazon Web Services segments, serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, advertisers, and employees. The filing discusses business, competition, intellectual property, seasonality, human capital, executive officers and directors, risk factors, properties, legal proceedings, market and shareholder matters, management’s discussion and analysis, critical accounting judgments, liquidity and capital resources, and financial condition. It reports approximately 1,608,000 employees as of December 31, 2021, cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities of $96.0 billion, operating cash flow of $46.3 billion, investing cash flow of $(58.2) billion, financing cash flow of $6.3 billion, and cash capital expenditures of $55.4 billion for 2021.

This study developed and externally validated deep learning algorithms using axial T2-weighted prostate MRI of the entire prostate gland and seminal vesicles to identify extra-prostatic extension (EPE) and seminal vesicle invasion (SVI) in localized prostate cancer (PCa). The primary cohort included 820 biopsy-proven PCa patients treated at Yale with surgery or radiation; 612 were used for training and 208 for internal testing. External validation used 65 patients from community hospitals and 41 from the Prostate-Dx dataset. Ground-truth EPE and SVI labels came from pathology and radiology reports and were validated by board-certified radiologists and a radiation oncologist. EPE and SVI ground-truth labels were associated with biochemical recurrence (BCR). The EPE model achieved AUCs of 0.719, 0.743, and 0.611 on the Yale, community hospital, and Prostate-Dx test sets; the SVI model achieved AUCs of 0.724, 0.678, and 0.775. Patients classified as bEPE+ or bSVI+ had increased likelihood of BCR and worse 5-year BCR-free survival. Combining EPE and SVI biomarkers improved prognostic value over either biomarker alone. Integrating the combined imaging biomarker into NCCN and UCSF-CAPRA risk groups reclassified 26.4% of patients and improved C-indexes and 5-year AUCs for BCR. Interpretability analyses included Grad-CAM, unsupervised hierarchical clustering, and dimensionality reduction. Limitations included no evaluation of overall survival or PCa-specific mortality, no comparison with tissue-based classifiers, and underrepresentation of African American patients. The study concluded that the deep learning algorithms accurately identify EPE and SVI on prostate MRI and improve risk stratification of localized PCa.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2015 describes the company as a technology company whose mission is to empower every person and organization to achieve more, with a strategy to build platforms and productivity services for a mobile-first, cloud-first world. It develops, licenses, and supports software products, services, and devices; offers cloud-based services; designs, manufactures, and sells devices; and delivers online advertising. It reports six operating segments: D&C Licensing, Computing and Gaming Hardware, Phone Hardware, D&C Other, Commercial Licensing, and Commercial Other. The filing discusses three ambitions—reinvent productivity and business processes, build the intelligent cloud platform, and create more personal computing—and notes the July 2015 launch of Windows 10. Research and development expense was $12.0 billion, $11.4 billion, and $10.4 billion in fiscal 2015, 2014, and 2013, respectively, at 13% of revenue each year. As of June 30, 2015, Microsoft employed approximately 118,000 people, and management approved a restructuring plan eliminating up to 7,800 positions in fiscal 2016, primarily in Phone Hardware. The filing also lists executive officers, sales and licensing channels, and extensive risk factors including competition, cloud services, acquisitions, intellectual property, security and privacy, outages, government regulation, taxes, supply and quality issues, global operations, and catastrophic events.

The passage describes device reset behavior, including Software Global Warm Reset via PRM_RSTCTRL, Test Reset, reset priority, PCIE and EMAC Switch reset isolation, reset during power domain switching, pin behavior at reset, and reset timing. It also covers clock inputs, PLLs, SYSCLKs, module clocks, interrupts for the ARM Cortex-A8 and C674x DSP, and EDMA events. Peripheral sections provide features, registers, timing requirements, and electrical data for DCAN, EMAC switch, MDIO, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, HDMI, HDVPSS, video DAC, I2C, ISS, JTAG, trace, AET, and the DDR2/DDR3 memory controller.

Michael Flynn’s resignation raises questions about President Trump and Russia. The Washington Post first reported Flynn discussed U.S. sanctions with Russia’s ambassador before Trump was inaugurated. Some officials knew of the talks; Sally Yates told White House counsel Donald McGahn that Flynn was vulnerable to Russian blackmail. CNN reported Trump was officially aware weeks before Vice President Pence, who had defended Flynn. Trump did not address the situation, instead condemning illegal leaks and blaming Clinton supporters and media. Pundits say he is deflecting; a Politico source said Flynn lacked diplomacy experience, was loyal, and likely had high governmental backing. John McCain and others seek an investigation into Russian interference, and more Republicans are open to it. If hearings yield incriminating evidence, Flynn could testify; because the talks preceded Trump’s inauguration, he is exempt from executive privilege and, having resigned, has only the Fifth Amendment. If Flynn implicates Trump, Trump could be complicit. McGahn may also be relevant.

The "Power" set offense is used by almost every NBA team to free outstanding shooters through baseline and down screens. Its initial attack goes down the middle and attacks both sides, making defensive help difficult. It begins with shooters crossing under the basket and then curling off down screens, with reads and counters for defensive actions such as chasing, cheating over, switching, and showing and recovering. The offense also covers offensive rebounding, automatic counters, and continuities including Motion, Side Screen, Drive & Kick, and Triangle Post, plus a Single/Double variation. It stresses execution, coordination, teaching drills, individual skill development, scouting, game strategies, and knowing how to defend against it.

The president's message to Congress concerns the boundary controversy between Great Britain and Venezuela. It recalls that the U.S. had proposed arbitration and that the British reply, appended, addresses the Monroe Doctrine, claiming the U.S. seeks a new extension of it and that it is inapplicable to the boundary dispute. The president defends the Monroe Doctrine as strong, sound, and vital to U.S. peace, safety, and institutions, and argues it applies to the present controversy. The British reply argues the doctrine is not established international law; the president responds that U.S. claims under it have a place in international law. The British government declines arbitration on grounds the president finds unsatisfactory, though it expresses sympathy for Monroe's policy and opposition to disturbing territorial distribution. The president says the U.S. must determine the true boundary line and recommends a congressional appropriation for an Executive-appointed commission to investigate and report. If the report is accepted, he says the U.S. should resist by every means Great Britain's appropriation of lands or jurisdiction determined to belong to Venezuela, while acknowledging the responsibility and consequences.

Apple Inc. reported a June 3, 2015 underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs International and Mitsubishi UFJ Securities International plc for the issuance and sale of ¥250,000,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 0.350% Notes due 2020. Interest is payable semiannually on June 10 and December 10, beginning December 10, 2015; the Notes mature June 10, 2020, are senior unsecured obligations, and are issued under an indenture and officer’s certificate. Exhibits are listed.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2015, containing unaudited financial statements and related disclosures. It reports Q2 net sales of $23,185 million and net income of $92 million, and six-month net sales of $45,901 million and net income of $35 million. The filing also covers cash flows, balance sheet items, commitments and contingencies, legal proceedings, acquisitions, long-term debt, stockholders’ equity, income taxes, segment information for North America, International, and AWS, and management’s discussion and analysis.

Ruston (La.) plays at Stephenville (Texas) in a midseason interstate matchup. Ruston is 4-0 and ranked No. 2 in Louisiana and No. 25 in Texas; Stephenville is 5-0. Last year, Ruston beat Stephenville 63-17. In the game, after a Dalen Powell fumble, Stephenville’s Trot Jordan threw a 19-yard touchdown to Jhett Banuelos; both teams opened with three-and-outs.

The article previews the U.S. Supreme Court’s October 2025 term, saying it will include cases with profound effects on law and American society. It notes unprecedented summer activity on the emergency docket, where the court allowed several Trump administration actions, mostly in 6-3 rulings with liberal dissents. The term’s docket includes challenges to presidential power over tariffs, removal of agency heads and whether to overrule a 90-year-old precedent, and birthright citizenship. It also includes a rehearing on Louisiana congressional districts and Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, with possible implications for disparate-impact liability under other civil rights laws. Other cases involve Colorado’s conversion-therapy ban, Idaho and West Virginia laws on transgender athletes, and a Fourth Amendment emergency-aid search issue. The author expects blockbuster rulings.

Karmel Davis was named the Tupelo Public School District’s 2017 Parent of the Year. Corey Crayton received a Habitat for Humanity home funded by HomeStretch Furniture. Noah Barbieri, a Millsaps College junior, was named a Truman Scholar, one of 62 nationally, receiving $30,000 toward graduate school and professional development programming.

DHS proposed ending duration of status for international students, capping stays at four years with possible USCIS extensions and barring major changes or transfers, to reduce F and J visa overstays. Higher education, hospitals, and private-sector commenters opposed it, citing students needing more than four years, Ph.D. and clinical programs, costly and uncertain extensions, processing delays, effects on J-1 physicians in hospitals, and industry research. NAFSA said DHS overestimates overstays and SEVIS already alerts ICE. The comment period closed Sept. 29 with more than 15,700 comments. Some supported the rule; the Council for Christian Colleges and Universities urged limiting it to colleges with admission rates under 30 percent.

The speaker says losing after playing hard in both games was difficult, especially in the finals, close yet far. The team must regroup and try its best tomorrow. They have bounced back before. Both goalies played well, with only one goal in six periods. They need to do things differently to regain success and not dwell on missed opportunities.

This qualitative phenomenological study explored the perspectives of 8 bilingual and 8 monolingual early childhood teachers in Ankara, Türkiye, on bilingualism and bilingual education. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed by content analysis, yielding five themes: benefits of bilingual education, bilingual children attending monolingual schools, bilingual education programs, issues in bilingual education, and the impact of bilingualism on children’s development. Teachers generally viewed bilingual education as advantageous and supported expanding bilingual schools in Türkiye, although their views varied by bilingual/monolingual status and school setting. Reported benefits included career, self-esteem, travel, brain development, communication skills, social awareness, and global citizenship. Some teachers said bilingual children in monolingual schools may lose one language or cultural identity, while some monolingual teachers saw no disadvantage and noted native-language improvement, daily spoken language acquisition, or single-language specialization. Teachers had limited knowledge about bilingual education programs but emphasized that staff should use both languages effectively and that environments should include bilingual stimuli and books. Identified issues included ineffective use of both languages by teachers, financial and human resource shortcomings, personnel quality, children’s language deficiencies, family cultural conflicts or lack of familiarity with the second language, and program implementation problems. Views on bilingual children’s development differed: some cited communication skills, self-confidence, cultural awareness, and cognitive skills, while others cited peer rejection or not knowing the community language. All teachers reportedly agreed that bilingualism is an advantage and that bilingual schools should be more widespread, while noting gaps in training and the need for professional development, resources, parental support, and further research.

The article examines how AI may create new disputes over drug patents, including whether predictive technology changes what inventions are obvious. It notes unresolved intellectual property questions such as whether AI can be an inventor and hold a patent, and what “a person skilled in the art” might reasonably know, which patent lawyer DeAnn Smith expects future litigation to clarify.

This review examines lung cancer screening methods, focusing on biomarkers. Articles were filtered for biomarker methods, U.S. research within the past 10 years, clinical settings, and primary lung cancer. The review reports sensitivities and specificities for volatile organic compounds, circulating tumor DNA, miRNA molecules, methylation of genomic sequences in sputum and serum, Ga-Alfatide II scans, combined score, and WT-IDH. Circulating tumor DNA had 80% sensitivity and 96% specificity; Ga-Alfatide II scans had 86% sensitivity and 85% specificity. The discussion states current low-dose lung CT screening for patients aged 50–80 can be inaccurate due to false positives and overdiagnosis. It identifies ctDNA and Ga-Alfatide II CT/PET as promising, with ctDNA potentially usable throughout the population and Ga-Alfatide II appropriate for high-risk or suspected patients. Limitations included U.S.-only articles from the past 10 years, restricted sample size, and possible false positives/negatives. The conclusion states these biomarkers may increase early detection, decrease mortality, inform treatment, and clarify morbidity; immunotherapy and chemotherapy are described as promising therapeutic options.

This study compared three surveys on primary care physicians’ EHR use and interoperability: the 2021 NEHRS, the 2022 ABFM Continuous Certification Questionnaire (CCQ), and the 2022 UCSF Physician Health IT Survey. The CCQ had the highest response rate at 100% and 3,991 eligible respondents; NEHRS had 1,875 eligible respondents (18.2%), and the UCSF survey had 3,209 respondents (3.6%). Respondent demographics, practice settings, EHR platforms, satisfaction, documentation, and interoperability responses differed across surveys. All surveys showed limited EHR satisfaction and interoperability problems: about one quarter were very satisfied, about three-quarters documented after work, and about 20% often had outside information available. Differences persisted in stratified comparisons. The authors suggest response bias and survey composition affect results, and that certifying-board data may supplement NEHRS, though the CCQ covered only family physicians and question differences limited comparisons.

The PrAISED randomised controlled trial evaluated a 12-month dementia-specific exercise and functional activity rehabilitation programme for people with mild dementia or mild cognitive impairment. The intervention was individually tailored, carer-involved, delivered by therapists, and was well received, but it had no effect on activities of daily living, physical activity, quality of life, falls, cognition, or other health status outcomes. There were small, statistically uncertain signals for reduced falls and some cognitive measures, but these did not translate into functional gains. The trial was disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The authors conclude that exercise or functionally oriented rehabilitation is unlikely to change the rate of loss of ability in dementia, and that different ways of defining wellbeing and supporting people after diagnosis are needed.

On August 17, Expedition 52 Commander Fyodor Yurchikhin and Flight Engineer Sergey Ryazanskiy will conduct a spacewalk from the ISS’s Pirs airlock. Ryazanskiy will deploy five nanosatellites; the cosmonauts will also collect residue samples and install handrails and struts. NASA reported it will be the 202nd station-support spacewalk and seventh this year.

Stenabolic (SR9009), developed by Scripps Research Institute under Thomas Burris, is an oral synthetic Rev-ErbA ligand linked with SARMs. It binds and activates Rev-Erb protein, affecting circadian rhythms, lipid and glucose metabolism, fat-storing cells, and macrophages. It can increase muscle mitochondria and metabolism, improving endurance and muscle strength and burning fat. Studies found it reduces plasma triglycerides by 12%, total cholesterol by 47%, non-esterified fatty acids by 23%, plasma glucose by 19%, insulin by 35%, and IL-6 by 72%.

Steven C. Gittens, Sr., proceeding pro se, sued Garlocks Sealing Technologies/Garlocks, Inc. under the ADA for disability discrimination. Garlocks moved for summary judgment. Gittens failed to respond to the motion or comply with court orders despite warnings that failure could result in dismissal. The court granted summary judgment and dismissed the complaint with prejudice under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 41(b), 16(f), and 56. The court found dismissal warranted for failure to prosecute, failure to obey scheduling orders, and failure to show a genuine issue of material fact. On the ADA claim, the court found Gittens did not establish disability within the ADA because his 25–30 pound lifting restriction and inability to perform a particular punch press job did not substantially limit a major life activity; it also found Garlock articulated legitimate non-discriminatory reasons for reassignment.

The passage argues that justice should be sure, swift, and under the law rather than mob violence or lynching. It states that education, especially public and industrial schooling, is important for all people, including Negroes, and helps prevent brutal crime. It warns that inflammatory speeches and writings can incite mobs, increase lynching, and encourage further crime. It also condemns preachers of discontent and demagogues who promote class hatred against the wealthy, saying they harm genuine reform and society. It calls for resolute, sane, cool-headed reform rather than violence, corruption, or exploitation.

The Pocatello-Chubbuck School District announced plans to finalize high school boundary changes, with three focus groups providing trustee input. Meetings will be public, and a timeline and agendas will be posted online. Trustees previously tabled the decision for more feedback. The district ended a two-decade school-choice policy due to enrollment and socioeconomic disparities.

The bankruptcy court issued a memorandum of decision and judgment in the Chapter 13 case of Jeffery Wayne and Paulette Monee Smith. The court granted in part and denied in part the Standing Chapter 13 Trustee’s objection and confirmed the debtors’ amended Chapter 13 plan as modified. The court addressed the treatment of Chrysler’s and NBD Bank’s claims under 11 U.S.C. § 1322, the good faith requirement of § 1325(a)(3), and the disposable income test of § 1325(b)(1)(B). The court permitted the debtors’ proposed full payment to Chrysler, finding no unfair discrimination or bad faith. It held that deferred ERISA-qualified Profit Sharing Plan benefits were not disposable income unless received in cash. The plan was modified to provide: 3.9% rather than 8% interest on Chrysler’s claim; semiannual paycheck stubs and year-to-date earnings to the Trustee; increased plan payments for overtime income above projections; a $75 monthly payment increase from $1,733.33 to $1,808.33; payment of net proceeds of any cash Profit Sharing distribution to creditors; and cessation of voluntary retirement or 401(k) contributions during the plan.

The passage contains a passport oath and request form with blanks for an applicant’s birthplace, parentage, residence, occupation, travel, passport number, allegiance to the United States, oath to support and defend the Constitution, physical description, and supporting affidavits. It also includes extracts from an Argentine President’s message, transmitted by Mr. Lord to Mr. Hay on May 10, 1902. The message discusses Argentina’s affairs, international relations, and finances, and notes disappointment that negotiations mediated by the British Government for limiting armaments between Argentina and Chile were treated generally. It states both countries increased armaments, incurred debt and deficits, strained credit, and faced economic difficulties, and that they recognize war policy is ruinous and costly expenditures should be stopped.

The passage says the author does not understand Snap’s vision or valuation and sees no value in owning the stock short term. It cites competition, noting Snapchat lacks barriers to entry, downloads fell 22% year-over-year and 40% on Apple, and Facebook’s Instagram has over 200 million users versus Snap’s 166 million DAUs; Microsoft built something similar on Skype. It also says 7% of marketers used Snapchat in 1Q17 versus 94% for Facebook, and mentions a McDonald’s video-ad collaboration. The upcoming lock-up expiration could release an additional 1.2 billion shares by the end of July, an estimated 84% dilution, with possible insider selling. For the March quarter, Snap reported $150 million revenue versus $158 million consensus, a loss of $2.31 per share versus $0.20 expected, and 166 million DAUs versus 167.3 million expected. With 28% of the float short, shorting is risky and puts are expensive. It concludes Snap’s business model is suspect, the stock may be volatile until after the lock-up, and no trade recommendation is made.

Linux Foundation news included Jim Zemlin's keynote on Linux use and $14.5B project value; Hart's Gold Membership and HartOS, a HIPAA-compliant health-data API platform; a free open source basics publication; and CNCF's 11 new members.

Overall safety endpoints at 24 and 48 weeks were similar between study groups. Reported adverse events, related adverse events, serious adverse events, discontinuations, bleeding events, and major bleeding events were comparable, with some fatal bleeding events. Twenty-four deaths were reported, and no pregnancies or clinically concerning laboratory signals were noted. The AEGEAN study showed high adherence and persistence through 24 and 48 weeks in subjects initiating apixaban for atrial fibrillation; a proactive educational program did not provide additional adherence or persistence benefits.

The passage describes attacking the Triangle & Two defense with a “Single/Double” offense, which uses screens to free shooters from pass-denying chasers. It outlines left and right entries, double and single screen options, base and side screen actions, reads and counters, and implementation needs such as execution, coordination, communication, timing, and experience. It also advises scouting opponents, recognizing defensive changes, using various alignments and entries, and attacking weaker defenders.

The passage examines Greek primary teachers’ views on STEM education and the conditions for its implementation. It reviews inquiry and scientific practices, STEM education literature, and Greece’s 2021-2022 introduction of STEM through “skills workshops,” which was accompanied by voluntary online training but not by educational material or increased school funding. The study used a questionnaire with 26 Likert-scale and 4 open-ended questions plus 27 structured interviews with 114 primary teachers (23 male, 91 female) in Attica, mostly experienced and about half with master’s degrees. Teachers considered scientific thinking very important (63%) or extremely important (20%), mainly for everyday problem solving, inquiry and critical thinking, social skills, experiential/interdisciplinary learning, and knowledge acquisition. Most rated STEM practices such as problem solving, small-group work, predictions, observations and measurements, use of instruments, explanations, and presentations as important (58-75%), but only 7-19% reported students often developing them. Only 20-30% reported teaching science effectively and 30-40% mathematics effectively. Teachers identified STEM advantages including attractive experiential/interdisciplinary learning, connection to everyday life, scientific methodology, cooperation, inquiry/creativity, and increased participation/critical thinking. Weaknesses included lack of teacher training and materials (58%), lack of infrastructure/equipment and high costs (42%), and lack of time/unclear curriculum place (31%). Requested support included more training (71%), infrastructure/equipment (31%), training materials (21%), ongoing support/guidance (16%), sample teachings (13%), and more timetable time/curriculum reduction (11%). The study concludes that teachers are positive about STEM but describe its introduction as hesitant, stressful, rough, and disorganized; successful implementation requires teacher training, infrastructure/equipment, and more time. Some teachers viewed STEM as reducing inequalities and supporting social skills and participation. Limitations include convenient, limited sampling.
Newfound microstructures help dandelion seeds catch upward gusts, lift off, or grip to wait for better breeze.

A report said South Korea's birthrate fell in the mid-1980s as more married women received higher education. The fertility rate dropped to 1.6 in 1987 from 2.1 in 1984. Married women's education and labor-force participation rose over time. South Korea's fertility rate was 1.24 in 2015, below the replacement level of 2.1.

The document specifies WHODrug/ATC coding and listing/summarization of concomitant medications and current diabetes treatment, including prior-versus-concomitant classification. Efficacy analyses use the FAS, with the primary endpoint being time to plasma glucose recovery (≥20 mg/dL increase within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose), analyzed via Kaplan-Meier, stratified log-rank, and supportive/sensitivity methods; secondary endpoints include recovery and glucose changes at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes. Safety analyses cover exposure, local tolerability, TEAEs, laboratory parameters, vital signs, ECG, immunogenicity, and PK/PD summaries, with specified data-handling, missing-data, SAS QC, and table/figure/listing requirements.

During excavation of two Amstel riverbed sites for a new Amsterdam subway line, archaeologists found 700,000 everyday discarded objects dating from Neolithic stone axes to cellphones. The finds are part of the “Below the Surface” project within a 15-year subway construction. The objects provide a source of urban history. When Rokin station opens, 10,000 excavated objects will be displayed; the North/South line and eight stations open July 22. An interactive website offers about 30,000 object photos and data, attracting 40,000–60,000 daily visitors and 13 million social media reach. A book-catalog, “Stuff,” with 13,000 photos, was distributed to schools. The project cost 6 million Euros.

The speaker recounts a breakaway save, including an initial save and a soccer-goalie-style save. He says playoffs and finals have ups and downs, confidence is important for a goalie, the first two games had good things though he wasn't happy personally, and the last two were huge. He compares two plays and made the second after wishing he could change the first. He calls Nashville home and praises the city, hockey growth, fans, crowd, and timely saves as confidence boosts.

The lecture reviews tools for proving Freiman’s theorem. It recalls Ruzsa’s modeling lemma and Freiman isomorphism, then presents Bogolyubov’s lemma in F₂ⁿ and Z mod n: a large subset’s iterated sumset 2A − 2A contains a bounded-codimensional subspace or Bohr set. It introduces Bohr sets, the geometry of numbers, lattices, successive minima, and Minkowski’s second theorem. Using these, it shows that a Bohr set contains a proper generalized arithmetic progression, setting up the conclusion of Freiman’s theorem in the next lecture and mentioning the polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture.

The ScottishPower Foundation donated £95,220 to the Sussex Wildlife Trust for its 50-year celebrations at Woods Mill, Henfield. The funding will allow 1,300 more participants, ten wildlife identification courses, training for 250 wildlife champions, and a young naturalists club. It will also support habitat improvements, including reed bed restoration and path access, and has installed a kestrel nesting box camera. Trustees visited the site, which opened on 8 June 1968.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture adds third-generation Tensor Cores that share data across all 32 threads in a warp, reduce register file bandwidth and storage, increase the k dimension up to 4x versus V100, and issue 8x fewer instructions and perform 2.9x fewer register file accesses for matrix multiply. It includes asynchronous copy from global memory to shared memory bypassing L1 and the register file, asynchronous barriers, and 1.7x larger SMEM allocation. A100 uses 5-site HBM2 with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, 2.3x the L2 read bandwidth of V100, a 40 MB L2 cache, L2 cache management controls, and Compute Data Compression saving up to 4x DRAM read/write and L2 read bandwidth/capacity.

MIG can partition each A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances with isolated memory paths, QoS, fault isolation, and support for VMs, containers, processes, and Linux; it uses GPU slices, Sys Pipes, and Compute Instances, and supports vGPU migration. Third-generation NVLink provides 50 Gbit/sec per signal pair, twelve links, and 600 GB/sec total bandwidth for A100, with NVSwitch and DGX A100 systems. A100 supports PCIe Gen 4 and SR-IOV, and includes error/fault detection, isolation, and containment technologies.

Additional features include NVJPG decode, an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomics (11x FP16 and 2.7x FP32 over V100), five NVDEC units, and CUDA 11 advances: Task Graphs, async copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency control, Cooperative Groups, and warp reduce. DGX A100 is described as a 5-PFLOPS AI system powered by A100 and MIG, with up to 56 discrete accelerators and an NGC software stack. A sparse neural network primer discusses pruning, fine-grained and coarse-grained sparsity, fine-grained structured sparsity on A100, and 2:4 sparsity accuracy.

Before COVID-19, Japanese universities lagged in ICT use for education due to beliefs about university education and structural factors. The pandemic forced a shift from face-to-face to online classes. The study examines MEXT, academic staff, students, and lifelong learning, and digitalization through LMS/MOOCs. Japan has 788 national, municipal, and private universities, nearly three-quarters private. Enrollment was 83.8% postsecondary and 54.9% in universities/colleges in 2021. Undergraduates are younger than the OECD average; faculty education time increased.

MEXT planned digitalization before the pandemic, with a 1999 60-credit remote-learning limit and a 2018 report linking digitalization to Society 5.0. After COVID-19, a June 2020 survey showed about 90% of universities offered remote classes and about 60% offered no face-to-face classes. MEXT allowed more than 60 remote credits in July 2020. Student complaints about interaction and quality led MEXT to promote face-to-face classes with infection control. April 2021 policy considered courses not more than half remote as face-to-face and allowed >60 remote credits only as an emergency exception. Face-to-face classes increased; by fall 2022, 99.8% of universities offered more than half face-to-face. Calls to eliminate credit limits were not adopted in March 2022, though quality-assured universities could receive exceptions; standards were revised in October 2022. Scheem-D and Plus-DX supported digitalization. Cabinet policies promoted digitalization and “My Number,” but data-sharing raised personal information risks.

Faculty ICT use was low pre-pandemic; AXIES surveys showed limited LMS/file-sharing due to paper preference, mismatch, and technological anxiety. Pandemic distance learning increased but posed challenges in communication, practical skills, assessing understanding, student support, group work, and computer literacy. Good practices were shared online, and MEXT in March 2022 promoted face-to-face learning and communication alongside distance education. Iiyoshi’s cultural aspect remained a concern; the face-to-face myth was altered, but cultural transformation was uncertain.

For students, the credit system’s “substantiation” was problematic: 124 credits, 45 hours per credit, but only five weekly study hours outside class on average. Causes included many courses, job hunting, graduation research, and Japanese views of education. Online classes increased assignments and out-of-class study; ICT may help substantiate credits, but 49.7% cited heavy reports/assignments as a bad point.

Lifelong learning has low institutionalization. Degree programs relied on university distance learning, with the 2001 revision allowing all 124 credits online. During the pandemic, distance education was not fully used due to separation from commuter programs. Non-degree Kokaikoza was offered by 95.7% of universities but only 7.6% via ICT distance; new vocational programs were more digitalized, with about three-quarters of universities implementing new online programs. The pandemic expedited digitalization and offered adult learner opportunities, but challenges remained in university culture, credit substantiation, lifelong learning, and protection of student data.

The SUSHI study developed an online version of the SInQUE social inclusion assessment tool for mental health supported accommodation and examined its acceptability, utility, and uptake. The study included lab-testing with six supported accommodation staff using think-aloud interviews and field-testing over five months in one inner London borough, with semi-structured interviews with 12 staff and 12 service users. Field-testing included a local implementation strategy and monitoring of use in two other areas without such support. The online SInQUE assessed social inclusion across nine areas, identified priority areas, and generated summary reports.

Results indicated that the online SInQUE was generally perceived as acceptable, user-friendly, relevant, and potentially useful, with relatively few and minor changes made after testing. Implementation support was considered essential, as no assessments were completed in areas without it. In the London borough, 27 staff registered, 17 staff from six providers used the tool, and 30 assessments were completed with 28 service users, about 10% of estimated service users; uptake was highest in supported housing. Findings were less conclusive for residential care and floating outreach. Limitations included low uptake, limited generalisability, no female service user participants, and inability to assess outcomes. The study concluded that the SInQUE may be useful in supported accommodation, especially supported housing, with active leadership endorsement, and recommended further research.

Steven J. Kean forwarded an “Enron Mentions” email from Ann M. Schmidt to Jeffrey McMahon, noting the last story and congratulating him. The forwarded articles cover Wisconsin Gas’s agreement to buy Northern Natural Gas’s Eagle pipeline for $5 million; LME copper falling as stocks rose, with unconfirmed talk that Enron was behind the stock increase; a FTSE 100 rally led by telecoms and drug stocks; the New York Mercantile Exchange’s debut of a low-sulfur coal futures contract; and a Modern Metals article on Enron’s push into steel hedging and varied industry reactions.

The speaker addresses Cabinet members, White House staff, and friends at a farewell, calling the event spontaneous. The speaker asks them to serve the next President with devotion and dedication, as they served him and previous Presidents. The White House is called the best house because of the great heart of those who serve, not its size or art. The speaker praises the Cabinet, sub-Cabinet, and White House staff, says the Administration made mistakes but that no one profited at public expense or left with more worldly goods. Government service is described as offering a cause bigger than oneself: making the nation the world’s leader, bringing peace and plenty rather than war and starvation. The speaker mentions his father’s jobs and his mother’s saintliness, recalls a T.R. quote about loss, and says defeat or death is only a beginning; greatness comes through tests and valleys. The speaker urges pride, continued service, best effort, no discouragement or pettiness, and warns against hate. He leaves with hope, humility, gratitude, and prayers for the staff.

A Dalhousie researcher says P.E.I. blueberry fields have enough native bees, which are more efficient, buzz pollinate, and suit the climate, so farmers need not bring honey bees. She says convincing farmers is challenging, and honey bees are expensive and risky due to hive shortages and parasites.

Michael Dell says the AI-driven data-center boom is still strong, with customers deploying infrastructure immediately and facing power-grid limits. Dell Technologies’ stock rose, its server-networking business grew 58%, and it raised revenue and EPS growth forecasts. While analysts and the Bank of England warned about stretched valuations, Dell said he sees no signs yet that too many data centers are being built.

The document standardizes the GHCB memory area so a guest OS can interoperate with hypervisors supporting SEV-ES or SEV-SNP, including required Non-Automatic Exits, minimum guest state exposed, and actions such as NMI handling and SMP booting. It defines the 4,096-byte GHCB format, protocol versions, hypervisor feature advertisement, GHCB MSR protocol requests and responses, GHCB GPA registration, page state change, SNP guest and extended guest requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID list, Run VMPL, Secure AVIC, SEV-TIO, termination, NMI, and debug handling. Revisions 2.01–2.04 add sequence-number, error-code, VLEK, APIC ID, VMPL, page-state-change, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and related protocol updates. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

The Dark Cloud Cover is a bearish reversal candlestick pattern that occurs after an uptrend. It forms when a bearish candlestick follows a bullish candlestick, opening above the previous close but closing below its midpoint. It signals a potential shift from bullish to bearish sentiment and can be used for short selling or closing long positions, especially in down-trending markets or rallies. Confirmation may come from price action or indicators such as Moving Averages, MACD, or RSI. The pattern is not a guarantee of reversal and should be combined with other analysis and risk management. The passage also covers benefits, trading steps, tips, backtesting, example trades, pros and cons, comparisons, timeframes, market suitability, and common mistakes.

This paper studies variability in Fairall 9 using roughly 1000 days of monitoring. It reviews that standard AGN disc models fail to reproduce observed UV/X-ray variability, SED shape, soft excess, and X-ray corona properties. The SED analysis divides the light curves into segments and fits an agnsed model plus reflection and absorption. Between segment 1a and segments 2/3, the optical/UV disc power increases, corresponding to a roughly 40–50% increase in mass-accretion rate, while integrated X-ray power remains roughly constant and the hot and warm photon indices soften. The Fourier analysis uses Gaussian Process regression to estimate power spectra, phase lags, and coherence. UVW2 power drops rapidly at high frequency; HX power is flatter. Segments 1a and 2 show a low-frequency semi-coherent X-ray-leading UV lag, while segment 3 lacks this signal. Including the rising phase gives a coherent UV-leading X-ray lag. An analytic model describes observed UV and X-ray emission as linear combinations of intrinsic disc and coronal emission with seed-photon, reverberation, and wind components. Segments 2 and 3 can be consistent with the same underlying model; the rising phase requires an additional slow inward component. The paper concludes that Fairall 9’s inner structure evolves on observable time-scales and that current AGN variability models do not adequately explain the observed phenomenology.

The paper interrogates the policy assumptions behind South Australia’s “World Class” public education initiative, initiated in 2018, using Bacchi’s WPR framework on publicly available and FOI-accessed documents. It situates the policy within the Global Education Reform Movement, PISA, and McKinsey’s Universal Scale. The authors argue the Department represented the problem as competing educator voices and principal leadership hindering central change, and the solution as centralising information, adopting McKinsey’s roadmap, using NAPLAN as a proxy, ranking and differentiating schools, using a “single source of truth” dashboard, increasing Education Directors, and providing scripted curriculum materials. The paper identifies assumptions that excellence could be bought, that the McKinsey scale measured system quality, and that central control and “complexity reduction” were necessary. It states these approaches eroded trust in educators, narrowed schooling purposes, disadvantaged schools serving disadvantaged communities, and produced effects including declining PIRLS results, a widening PISA equity gap, absenteeism, disengagement, lower retention, and reduced completion. The authors propose a “Beyond World Class” framework emphasizing equity, inclusion, democratic partnerships, professional trust, and the Alice Springs (Mparntwe) Education Declaration.

Non-centrosymmetric crystals exhibit properties such as piezoelectricity, ferroelectricity, and pyroelectricity, with 10 of 21 non-centrosymmetric crystal classes being polar. Ferroelectrics are insulators with switchable spontaneous polarization below their Curie temperature. Polar metals combine a polar crystal structure with mobile carriers and conductivity; electric fields are screened, so polarity cannot be reversed by an applied electric field. The polar metal field followed Anderson and Blount’s 1965 discussion and expanded after LiOsO3 in 2013. Distortive polar metals (DPMs) are defined by a centrosymmetry-lifting transformation, often described by the weak coupling principle or decoupled space mechanism. This study analyzes domain boundaries in metallic DPM Mn5Al8. In off-stoichiometric Mn51Al49, a first-order cubic γ-brass to rhombohedral γ2 transition occurs at ∼880°C, producing a polar R3m structure and metallic behavior by resistivity and DFT. The transformation is martensitic and forms rank-2 laminate twins with herringbone morphology and four polar variants. EBSD, HAADF-STEM, and 4D-STEM DPC reveal head-to-head and tail-to-tail charged domain boundaries and an interlocking Y pattern. Low-voltage SEM, EFM, copper deposition, and oxidation show variable surface reactivity, with copper and oxide accumulation at H-H boundaries, suggesting carrier surplus/depletion and local DOS/work function variation. Chemical sorting of the ICSD identified at least 134 metallic polar metals, about 20% DPMs. The study concludes that bound charge influences carrier concentration at Mn5Al8 domain boundaries, though the mechanism remains unclear, and metallic DPMs may challenge the weak-coupling principle and offer metallurgical processing opportunities.

Jane Goodall, a pioneering primatologist and conservationist, died at 91 while on tour in California; the Jane Goodall Institute said she died in her sleep of natural causes. She first visited Kenya in 1957, met Louis Leakey, and began observing wild chimpanzees at Gombe in 1960. Her research found that chimpanzees make and use tools, engage in war, and have personalities. She later earned a PhD from Cambridge, founded the Jane Goodall Institute in 1977, created the Roots & Shoots program, advocated for wildlife conservation, and was named a UN Messenger of Peace and a Dame of the British Empire.

This randomized controlled trial examined the safety and preliminary efficacy of group MBSR plus psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy (MBSR+PAP) versus MBSR alone for frontline physicians and nurses with depression and burnout related to COVID-19. Among 25 enrolled participants, MBSR+PAP was associated with significantly greater reduction in depressive symptoms at 2 weeks, greater reductions in some burnout, demoralization, and connectedness measures, and no serious treatment-emergent adverse events. Limitations included a small, homogeneous sample and lack of blinding; the authors concluded that combining MBSR with psilocybin appears safe, feasible, and potentially efficacious, and that larger, more diverse, placebo-controlled studies are needed.

The passage explains stock trading strategies as defined rules and methods for buying and selling stocks and ETFs, meant to guide traders. The 3-2 zone is a variation of the 1-2-2 zone. The point defender drops to the free throw line, letting wing defenders play wider and deny wing passing lanes, disrupting zone offenses and protecting against high-post passes. It allows point-guard open shots; if the point guard is an excellent outside shooter, it can be adjusted to a 1-2-2 or 1-3-1 zone. The point and an active, taller wing can be interchanged, making high-post passes more difficult and helping weakside rebounding. Like the 1-2-2, it is good for fast breaks. Basic shifts are described for ball in the middle, on either wing, and in either corner, along with a point/wing interchange variant.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system. Each analog input channel can be single-ended or differential and includes input clamp protection, a PGA with selectable bandwidth, and a 20-bit SAR ADC. The device has eight simultaneous-sampling ADCs, a 4.096V internal reference, programmable averaging, test patterns, SPI configuration, daisy-chain support, and 2-lane or 4-lane SDR/DDR data interfaces. It operates from 5V and 1.8V analog supplies, supports true bipolar inputs, tolerates ±18V at the inputs, provides 1MΩ input impedance, and includes common-mode rejection up to ±12V. A speed-boost mode allows up to 8MSPS for a selected channel pair. The passage also describes output formats, clock/sync requirements, reference options, data randomizer, power-down/reset/initialization, register access, and ATE application information.

The article tests the options expiration (OPEX) week effect. US-listed stock options generally expire on the Friday before the third Saturday each month, shifting to Thursday if Friday is a holiday. Quadruple witching occurs in March, June, September, and December. The S&P 500 shows above-average returns during OPEX week, with monthly variation. A backtest buying at the OPEX week open and exiting at OPEX day close shows a 2% CAGR and 0.2% average weekly gain, but the effect has been weak recently. OPEX day itself shows negative average returns in backtests. The week after OPEX is lower than a random week on average, with September worst and August best. The article concludes there is an OPEX week effect but it is not tradeable alone and needs parameters; international backtests did not find a consistent edge.

This lecture covers corporate carbon footprints through a WidgetCo case. WidgetCo is an office chair manufacturer with a fully owned Michigan plant, a 50-50 Shanghai joint venture, two U.S. distribution centers, retailer showcase space, 3PL ocean/rail/truck transport, a private truck fleet, and industrial customers who mostly pick up. Corporate carbon footprints are calculated mainly by multiplying activity data by emission factors, such as electricity consumption times an emissions factor; transportation can use fuel consumption or ton-miles, though aggregating ton-miles and weight can cause errors. Emissions factors cover Kyoto gases and are reported in CO2 equivalence. Emissions are classified as scope 1 direct, scope 2 electricity indirect, and scope 3 other indirect. Organizational boundaries—equity share or control—determine whether activities like the China joint venture are included; scope 3 is mostly optional, creating discretion. Student estimates for WidgetCo ranged mostly from 300,000 to 400,000 tons; including everything was about 580,000 tons, while a corporate-only boundary was just over 200,000 tons. The lecture discusses disclosure, noting CDP reporting growth, investor and supplier pressure, and difficulty comparing companies because boundaries differ. FerretCo disclosed 55,000 tons and 1.1 kg per product, but uses contract manufacturers and different boundaries, so comparisons are problematic. Carbon footprints are used for external reporting and internal goals, require manual data gathering, and face issues such as missing values, aggregation, units, and emission factors. Next class covers life cycle assessment and product-level standards.

This retrospective study analyzed 1,383 noma patients managed at Noma Children’s Hospital, Sokoto, Nigeria, from September 1999 to October 2024. Patients ranged from 8 months to 80 years old, with a median age of 6 years; 54.2% were male. Acute noma was more common than arrested noma, and gangrene was the most frequent active stage. Most cases were from Sokoto, Zamfara, Kebbi, and Kano. The estimated overall incidence of noma in northern Nigeria was 114.5 cases per 100,000, with annual average and median incidences of 4.4 and 2.2 cases per 100,000. Incidence was higher among males and among those under 10 years old. Sokoto had the highest state incidence and Adamawa the lowest. The study concludes that noma has a high incidence in northern Nigeria and underscores the need for awareness and screening programs for early detection.

This study used Q methodology with 13 Turkish university mathematics education faculty members to examine barriers to distance education after online teaching was adopted due to the COVID-19 pandemic and the February 2023 earthquake. Data were collected through 50 Q statements and interviews. Analysis yielded three factors: student-related barriers, technology-related barriers, and pedagogical barriers; a teacher-related barrier factor did not emerge. Overall, curriculum/pedagogical barriers had the highest mean score, followed by teacher, technology, and student barriers. Participants generally viewed distance education alone as unsuitable for mathematics education and favored blended or hybrid models.

The patent application relates to secure and zero-knowledge data sharing for cloud applications. It describes problems in sharing encrypted data, especially protected health information, including EMR enrollment burdens and cloud providers controlling encryption keys. Embodiments use layered encryption and a key hierarchy structure (KHS) with data encryption keys (DEKs), master encryption keys (MEKs), password-based derived keys (PDK), and questions-based derived keys (QDK). Public key encryption may encrypt messages for a recipient, and dual keys may secure patient data. A client derives keys from credentials, decrypts an encrypted MEK, then an encrypted DEK, then encrypted user data, while keys are not stored in plaintext and the server or cloud provider may not access the data. For sharing, a shared data KHS (SD-KHS) stores encrypted shared data encryption keys (ESDEKs) for recipients; a recipient decrypts an ESDEK with a private key and decrypts shared data with the SDEK, with edits requiring owner acceptance. Public keys may be retrieved from a global lookup directory. The passage also describes client devices, registration and login, key generation, asymmetric sharing between client devices, printer-driver sharing, and claims for methods, media, and systems implementing these techniques.

Natural bacteria from grape plants may help neutralize wine’s ashy aftertaste by breaking down guaiacol, a main smoke-taint compound. Interdisciplinary research (IDR) is generally viewed as important for creativity and innovation, but its relationship to impact is debated. This paper compares IDR in highly impactful medical journals (top 10% SJR) and less/not impactful journals by constructing correlation networks of second-level MeSH terms in the Disease branch from PubMed articles for 1999, 2010, and 2022, using an NI-June sample to address sample-size effects. Results indicate that NI-June networks have higher average node strength and density, suggesting less impactful research is more interdisciplinary, while impactful networks have higher modularity; GCC and assortativity are similar. Core analysis identifies stable inner cores, and cancer-related research is seen as the main driver of IDR. Difference networks show weak co-location of stronger links and clustering around topics that change over time, while absolute prominence remains stable. The paper concludes that highly impactful medical journals tend to publish relatively more disciplinary-based articles, with possible explanations involving peer review, clinical guideline evidence standards, and reporting-compliance infrastructures.

Bodycam footage shows Emily Weinman, 20, refusing to give her last name after Wildwood, New Jersey police stopped her over suspected underage drinking during Memorial Day weekend. The lecture reviews plasma diagnostics via spectroscopy and simplified equilibria. Thermodynamic equilibrium features Boltzmann occupation, one shared temperature for electrons, ions, and radiation, balanced opposing processes, and optical thickness; it is rare. Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) assumes an optically thin plasma where radiative processes are ignored for level balance, collisional processes dominate, and Saha equilibrium gives ionization populations using temperature, ionization potential, degeneracy, and related factors. Coronal or collisional-radiative equilibrium applies to low-density, optically thin plasmas: collisional excitation is balanced by radiative de-excitation, and upper-state populations depend on excitation and downward rates. Non-local thermodynamic equilibrium requires considering all relevant processes for a specific plasma, such as photoionization in an X-ray-driven gas. The spectroscopy workflow includes choosing an equilibrium, calculating ionization and excited states, calculating line strengths, predicting spectra, accounting for radiation transport, reflections, detector response, and comparing or iterating with experimental data. Line-ratio techniques use isolated, identified, strong lines to infer ionization-state ratios and temperature. X-ray spectroscopy discusses characteristic K- and L-shell lines, with K alpha strongest, and X-ray filters with element-dependent absorption edges. Pinhole imaging is limited by geometric blur and diffraction. Bent crystals provide monochromatic imaging. Detectors include film, image plates, time-gated cameras, and streak cameras, with trade-offs in time resolution, spatial resolution, cost, and linearity.

Reverse osmosis is widely used at dairies to remove water from milk, but moving concentration on-farm could reduce water transport. Researchers at Aarhus University, with Arla, examined how on-farm concentration affects milk quality. They found reverse osmosis did not negatively affect total bacterial count, free fatty acid levels, or protein breakdown; concentrated milk could be used for cheese and milk powder. Milk powder quality and durability were the same as powder from ordinary milk, while cheese showed a minor enzyme difference and concentrated milk coagulated about ten minutes later. On-farm concentration occurs elsewhere, with different ownership and service models. Herd size and distance matter for resources and profitability, as small installations use more power. Farmers showed interest, dairies were skeptical, and Arla is assessing profitability.

Play action is a pass play designed to look like a run. The quarterback fakes a handoff, holds the ball, bootlegs, and looks downfield. It works when the offense sells the run and the defense reacts, pulling linebackers and safeties toward the line and creating space for receivers on routes such as crossing and drag routes. The offensive line blocks as if for a run before switching to pass protection. It is most effective when a team has established the run or when the defense expects a run, including short-yardage, goal-line, and red-zone situations. Common concepts include the double post and bubble Y over. A play action pass is always a pass, unlike an RPO, which can become a run or pass based on the defense’s reaction.

Resolute Marine Energy (RME), founded in 2007 by CEO Bill Staby, with Olivier Ceberio as COO, sought to commercialize a wave-driven desalination system called the Wave O™. It targeted Ugu, South Africa, where 700,000 residents faced expensive water ($1.00/m3 after a government subsidy) due in part to a weak electric grid and reliance on diesel. RME signed an MOU and NDA with Ugu and an NDA with CSIR; the Development Bank of South Africa expressed interest in funding the South African side, and Ugu applied for a $1.2 million DBSA grant. RME needed $6 million for a second ocean trial and an integrated South African pilot. Financing had come mostly from public sources, plus $400,000 private investment and $50,000 from MassChallenge; RME believed impact investors were the best fit. The Wave O™ was still in prototype stages and awaiting its second ocean trial. It consisted of an offshore wave energy converter, a flow smoother/pressure intensifier, and a reverse osmosis desalination plant. RME estimated water costs of $1.00–$2.00/m3, compared with $3.00–$8.00/m3 for diesel-powered desalination.

RME debated three approaches for South Africa. Approach #1 was a WEC producing electricity for an off-the-shelf desalination system; it was easier, eligible for U.S. grants, and used known technology, but would price output as electricity rather than water, reduce margins, require brine disposal, lose conversion efficiencies, risk “plug and play,” face large competitors, and sell to a single customer, Eskom. Approach #2, in RME’s business plan, used hydraulic power to operate desalination; it was cleaner, more efficient, had lower production costs, could charge water prices, faced fewer direct competitors, and offered IP potential, but required private funding, was untested, and required a desalination partner. Approach #3 was a “black box” all-in-one system owned by RME; it would allow hybrid water and electricity production, system optimization, and no desalination partner, but required more capital and time, desalination expertise, pricing decisions, and carried investor-confusion and no-local-partner risks.

RME also pursued an Alaska opportunity to provide electricity to off-grid communities dependent on diesel, where electricity could cost $0.60/kWh and diesel $8.00/gallon. Staby saw it as a learning platform and not a distraction; Ceberio questioned how a dual work stream would appear to investors. RME had filed 10 provisional patents and three PCTs, had no national patents, and was considering one in South Africa. The passage concludes that RME faced a critical decision about which entry approach to take, how to position itself as an energy, water, or more complex company, and how to serve stakeholders and attract investors.

The Federal Circuit affirmed the Court of Federal Claims in White v. United States. Sheriff Harold Ray Presley died in 2001; his mother, Christine H. Roberts, filed a PSOBA death-benefit claim and later died. The Bureau denied her estate’s claim, but the trial court reversed and awarded $250,000. The majority held that a beneficiary who survives the public safety officer’s death is entitled to benefits, and the beneficiary’s later death before payment does not terminate eligibility; the statute unambiguously sets eligibility at the officer’s death, so the agency’s contrary interpretation and living-payee regulation were not entitled to deference. Judge Prost dissented, arguing the statute is silent or ambiguous on whether estates are eligible recipients, and would defer to the agency’s permissible interpretation requiring a living payee and reverse.

Apixaban compliance was >95% at Weeks 4, 12, and 24 in the Primary SOC and Additional Educational Program groups; at Week 48, mean compliance was >94% in all 3 study groups. In the Primary Efficacy Set, mean adherence at 24 weeks was 91.64% in the Primary SOC group and 91.88% in the Additional Educational Program group, with no significant difference. This paper develops an Alzheimer’s disease (AD) diagnostic tool using a causal Bayesian Network (BN) that combines knowledge and data. The BN distinguishes suspected AD from diagnosed AD, follows medical idioms, and includes variables from validated AD diagnostic criteria. Parameters are specified using the NACC UDS dataset, literature, and knowledge-based judgment. The model estimates probabilities of suspected AD, formal diagnosis, treatment, and complications, and updates predictions as evidence is observed. It reviews related AI approaches, noting limitations of black-box models and prior BN models. Validation includes internal consistency with AD prevalence and external clinical scenarios involving symptoms, biomarker tests, age, genetic mutation, other dementia, and level of independence. The authors conclude it can serve as a complementary, interpretable clinical decision support tool. Limitations include aggregation of non-AD conditions, reliance on data from diagnosed AD individuals, incomplete accounting for misdiagnosis/undiagnosed cases, manual parameter setting, and uneven NPT sample distribution. Future work includes modeling individual causes of cognitive impairment, early-onset AD details, AD management, and a research-purpose BN including preclinical AD.

The passage reports an investigation of the intermetallic CoSn2, a structurally simple 3D compound primarily applicable for battery storage. It finds a resistivity slope change below 25 K, no specific-heat anomaly, and paramagnetic susceptibility from 2–300 K, indicating no magnetic transition. Single-crystal x-ray diffraction at 22 K reveals weak commensurate satellite reflections at q1=(1/2,0,1/2) and q2=(0,1/2,1/2), I-centering-violating reflections, and symmetry lowering from tetragonal I4/mcm to acentric monoclinic X2/C2 with doubling of a and c and loss of fourfold symmetry. Angle-dependent magnetoresistance changes from fourfold above 40 K to twofold below 20 K. Phonons are dynamically stable; electronic calculations show van Hove singularities and flat bands far from the Fermi level, parallel Fermi-surface contours, and susceptibility maxima at N and X, suggesting possible electronic instability. ARPES shows a diamond-shaped pocket with lobes, matching DFT except for an unobserved inner pocket. Polarization-dependent ARPES shows fourfold symmetry under LH polarization and strong asymmetry under LV polarization, possibly from Co-dxy orbital contribution. Band dispersion shows type-I and type-II crossings at NP1, another Dirac-type crossing NP2, and a nodal loop in the kx–kz plane with a small SOC gap. The passage concludes that CoSn2 exhibits a symmetry-broken state below 25 K associated with electronic instability and orbital-selective anisotropy, despite a stable lattice and no magnetic order, positioning it as a platform for symmetry breaking in an itinerant, nonmagnetic nodal line semimetal.

The court affirmed the circuit court’s judgment in a malicious prosecution action brought by Susan Ann Vansickle after her arrest for obstructing a public highway. Evidence of the arresting officer’s uncivil conduct was inadmissible absent evidence that the defendant instigated it. The trespass judgment involving William Vansickle was inadmissible because it did not show the road issue was involved and was begun after the arrest. The 1871 county court proceedings were irrelevant because they did not vacate an established road. Evidence of the county court’s verbal instructions was admissible to show the defendant’s good faith, not the road’s legality. The defendant could testify that he acted in good faith. Probable cause required belief in guilt based on reasonable grounds. Voluntary waiver of preliminary examination and entry into a recognizance was prima facie evidence of probable cause. Malicious prosecution required malice; want of probable cause alone was insufficient and did not create a legal inference of malice.

The document describes AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine and optional extensions to SEV and SNP for page migration. TMPM copies page content and updates virtual-to-physical mappings, can pause DMA traffic, and can migrate SNP-protected guest pages. It requires IOMMU enablement, and support is checked through the ENGINE_READY bit. Commands are sent through a page migration ring buffer and parameter pages containing up to 128 migration entries. Key commands include PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, and PM_NOOP. The document covers pre-migration RMP state, multi-page commands, performance guidance, non-migratable IOMMU data structures, IOMMU mapping requirements, TMPM firmware reload procedures for EPYC Family 19h, debugging, restrictions, command formats, statuses, parameter blocks, and error handling and mitigation. It also specifies 4k alignment restrictions, SPA encoding, ring buffer initialization, shutdown, pause/resume, interrupts, and that certain errors may be reported in command status or via MCA.

The article investigates pedagogical approaches to education for sustainable development (ESD) in South African school curricula, focusing on the Technology curriculum. It notes global acceptance of sustainable development, the UN SDGs, and ESD’s environmental, social, and economic dimensions, while stating that ESD integration remains under-addressed in schools and particularly in the Technology curriculum. The study asks what knowledge Technology Education teachers have about ESD, how Technology content informs ESD teaching, and what pedagogical approaches can be used. It uses experiential learning theory and a qualitative descriptive case study with eight Senior Phase Technology teachers in Mpumalanga’s Ehlanzeni District, using semi-structured interviews and classroom observations analyzed through content analysis. Findings show teachers understood ESD as resource preservation, minimizing technology’s environmental impact, renewable energy, societal standards, and indigenous knowledge. Teachers identified opportunities in technology-driven solutions, processing, recycling, the design process, and investigative teaching, but actual teaching lacked ESD emphasis. They highlighted collaborative learning, group work, cross-cultural collaboration, environmental stewardship, and creativity/practical solutions, although classroom practice mainly used demonstrations. The study discusses limited implementation despite opportunities and recommends holistic integration, resource use, design and manufacturing, recycling, collaborative learning, critical thinking, and further qualitative and quantitative research.
