Breast cancer patients reported lower quality of life, and chemotherapy worsened it. Cannabinoids from Cannabis sativa have been studied for chemotherapy- and tumor-associated symptoms. A pilot study of CBD and THC in advanced cancer palliative patients found tolerated average daily amounts and symptom benefit. Mouse models showed cannabinoids possess anti-tumor activities, with CBD as the most potent inhibitor of cancer cell proliferation. Human microbiota, dysbiosis, fungal signatures, skin microbiota, and oral microbiome have also been associated with breast cancer. Thai DTAM manufactures Metta Osot and Ganja Oil under license, both added to the National List of Essential Medicines. The current randomized placebo-controlled study aims to explore Thai cannabis oil’s efficacy on quality of life in advanced breast cancer patients treated with chemotherapy, its adverse effects, and microbial alteration and diversity. It will recruit 90 adult women with metastatic breast cancer receiving chemotherapy at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital, with ESAS score ≥3, excluding specified conditions. Participants will be allocated 1:1:1 to Ganja Oil, Metta Osot, or placebo oil once daily before bedtime for 90 days. Four visits occur during the trial, with blood, saliva, stool, and skin samples collected at baseline and post-treatment, followed by one month of withdrawal monitoring. Outcomes include ESAS symptom intensity, microbiome profile, cytokines, bacterial metabolites, pharmacokinetic parameters, and pharmacogenetics. Analysis will be intention-to-treat using Stata, with diversity and statistical tests. The trial is expected to provide efficacy data for Thai cannabis oil in metastatic breast cancer patients, including chemotherapy-related side effects, quality of life, adverse effects, microbiome, metabolites, cytokines, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacogenetics.

Soccer position numbers began in England in the 1920s, assigned from back to front and right to left in a 2-3-5 formation. The W-M formation in the 1950s kept the numbering and names but moved inside forwards back, making the center forward prominent and leading to “Number 9” and “Number 10” references, and moved the center halfback into defense. From the 1960s, experimentation, merging roles, and “Total Football” ended the tie between numbers and positions; halfbacks became midfielders. In 2012, U.S. Soccer standardized position names and numbers based on a 4-3-3 and described TTPM profiles. It also notes terms such as “False 9” and “Double-9s.”

Jonathan Huberdeau scored with 7.7 seconds left to give the Florida Panthers a 3-2 win over the Detroit Red Wings. Aleksander Barkov and Aaron Ekblad also scored, and Harri Sateri made 26 saves. Danny DeKeyser scored both Detroit goals, and Petr Mrazek stopped 30 shots.

Punters enter when an offense fails to convert, and their job is to flip field position by punting after the snap. They need hang-time, accuracy, touch, leg strength, and the ability to execute different trajectories. They may also run or throw on fake punts and serve as holders. The position is called punter because the punter punts after the snap, unlike kicks on extra points, field goals, and kickoffs. Skills include accuracy, leg strength, coordination, flexibility, and creativity; typical body type is 5’10–6’2, 180–210 pounds, slim. Shane Lechler holds the NFL record for highest average yards per punt at 47.6, and Ray Guy was a first-round pick who helped the Raiders win three Super Bowls. Punting is important because field position correlates with scoring chances, and a punter helps pin opponents deep and affect games statistically or in momentum.

Avoiding stocks may risk retirement security, since the S&P 500 averaged a 7.92% return from 2007-2017 while money market returns were low. Experts say risk should be put in perspective and some stock-market risk is necessary; simple portfolios and robo-advisors can help beginners.

The passage discusses the MOVE Index and a TLT trading strategy. The MOVE Index measures U.S. interest rate volatility through implied volatility from 1-month OTC options; it is called the “VIX of the bond market,” was created by Merrill Lynch in 1998, and acquired by ICE in 2019. It recently rose due to Fed rate hikes and banking crisis, from 120 to 199 in March, compared with an all-time high of 264 in October 2008, current 118, and average around 85 since 2000. High MOVE levels generally do not signal a good time to buy bonds and generate few signals. A strategy holding TLT when MOVE is below its historical mean and selling when above was backtested from 2002. It was not super profitable, hurt returns in 2008 but helped in 2022, and had about half the maximum drawdown of buy-and-hold. The passage concludes MOVE is a great indicator of bond market volatility but not a good indicator for trading bonds, and avoiding high volatility does not seem like a good idea.

Vision on the soccer field is the ability to see, comprehend, and respond to play, enabling pinpoint passing, defending, and goalkeeping. Pelé reportedly had 30 percent greater peripheral vision than the average athlete and studied geometry and chess. Educational research indicates at least 75 percent of learning is visual. Coaches stress fundamentals: be aware of everyone’s positioning, constantly scan, get the head up quickly after controlling the ball, keep eyes and body moving, analyze and anticipate, move to better positions, and practice peripheral recognition. On offense, scanning helps identify passing options; on defense, it helps identify threats and runs. Goalkeepers have the best view, followed by center backs, central midfielders, and trailing center striker, and should communicate. Tips include playing first touch away from the body, receiving left passes with the right foot and right passes with the left foot, and using drills that require scanning. Visualization can be used to improve vision, though it is not the same as vision.

The DAWN-plasma study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter trial comparing standard of care plus convalescent plasma with standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15; secondary and exploratory endpoints included clinical status, time to sustained improvement or discharge, mechanical ventilation or death, safety, quality of life, laboratory data, vital signs, PCR, and neutralizing antibody titers. Eligible patients had confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, illness of any duration, and specified respiratory or radiographic criteria; exclusions included prior or current mechanical ventilation, certain safety hazards, severe plasma allergy, treatment restrictions excluding ventilation, and recent anti-CD20 antibody therapy. Participants were randomized 2:1. Convalescent plasma was given as 800–1000 mL in 4 doses, with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization and units requiring neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/160. The study was approved by IECs/IRB and conducted per Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP; informed consent was required. Between May 2, 2020, and January 26, 2021, 499 patients were assessed and 489 randomized to plasma (n=326) or control (n=163). Day 15 visits occurred in 434 patients and Day 30 visits in 423. The FAS excluded specified randomized patients; the PPS excluded protocol violations such as receiving fewer than 4 plasma units or SOC patients receiving plasma before Day 30. In the plasma group, median time to first transfusion was 5 hours, median volume was 884 mL, 80.7% of units had titers ≥1/320, and 91.9% received all 4 units.

The passage discusses the Covid-19 pandemic’s effects on higher education and the shift to online learning, along with problems such as adaptation, practical courses, exam safety, negative perceptions, motivation, digital competence, and cheating. The disclosure provides apparatus and methods for measuring the type and degree of tissue damage around a burn or other wound. It describes capacitive, bioimpedance, or SEM sensors using electrodes, including virtual sensors formed from electrode arrays, to measure tissue capacitance and convert it to sub-epidermal moisture (SEM) values. Burn wounds may have zones of necrosis, stasis, and hyperaemia with differing SEM levels. The apparatus can compare measured capacitance or SEM values to thresholds or data arrays to determine burn depth and boundaries between viable and non-viable tissue. Mapping apparatuses may use visual indicators, perforations for marking, or a projector to indicate boundaries. Methods include obtaining capacitance measurements over tissue including a wound, converting them to SEM values, and marking boundaries encompassing regions with SEM values below a threshold. Systems may also store or print images and measurements.

Sungi Cho earned a B.S. in Mechanical Engineering from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 2013. While serving as a Black Hawk helicopter pilot, he encountered deficiencies in standard-issue gear. Using 3D printing, he developed a plastic hook that let soldiers hang warbelts and loadouts. After field testing and positive feedback, he founded a company to sell the Warbelt Hanger at $10.99; customers later expanded to law enforcement. He then developed the MOLLE Backer, a universal base mount for hard and soft MOLLE systems, launched at $10.99 for a two-pack. He later left the Army to pursue an MBA at MIT Sloan, moved from Seattle to Cambridge with fifteen printers, rented space near campus, and hired two undergraduate engineering majors at $20 per hour. Backer monthly sales stabilized at about 1,800 units. Cho considered transitioning from 3D printing to injection molding and gathered production and cost data. Ten printers dedicated to Backers each produce 180 salable units per month and need replacement after five years. A third-party manufacturer could produce 200 salable units per hour, with an eight-hour minimum run. The mold cost $11,487 versus $1,716 per printer. Cho was unsure how to structure the data and had not yet considered non-financial factors.

This study investigated preoperative prediction of pTERT mutation in glioblastoma using MRI and ResNet. Among 266 GBM patients, DWI data were available for 147. ResNet models using DWI and ADC maps (DWI*) achieved 85.20% slice accuracy (AUC 0.934) and 86.6% patient accuracy, outperforming conventional structural MRI (best 51.53%, AUC 0.571). The entire tumor ROI performed best (85.20%, AUC 0.934) versus tumor core (78.06%, AUC 0.856) and enhanced tumor (81.70%, AUC 0.869). Clinical characteristics alone had 70.91% accuracy (AUC 0.735), and adding them to DWI* did not improve performance. The study concluded DWI plus ADC has value for pTERT prediction in GBM, with limitations including small sample and retrospective design.

Antipsychotics are the primary treatment for severe mental health conditions and improve psychiatric outcomes, but approximately 40%-80% of people prescribed them experience metabolic syndrome (MS), characterized by weight gain, glucose dysregulation, and dyslipidaemia. Antipsychotic-induced MS is associated with hypertension, increased cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes risk, and premature mortality. Reported non-modifiable determinants include gender, ethnic background, age, and family history; modifiable behavioural determinants include calorie intake and sedentary behaviour. Non-pharmacological interventions target behavioural determinants, but few studies report clinically significant attenuation of MS, and the preferred healthcare setting is unclear. This scoping review will follow Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and PRISMA-ScR, search electronic databases and grey literature, include qualitative, quantitative, mixed-method studies and evidence syntheses, and screen, extract, and synthesise data. It aims to describe determinants of antipsychotic-induced MS in community-dwelling adults, non-pharmacological interventions to prevent or treat it, and preferred delivery contexts, while highlighting knowledge gaps and informing future research.

The passage describes cervical cancer as preventable but the second most common cancer among women worldwide, with most cases and deaths in low- and middle-income countries, especially sub-Saharan Africa. Current precancer treatment methods require trained professionals and access is limited. The study explored women’s experiences with and acceptability of self-administered intravaginal 5-fluorouracil (5FU) following a Phase I pilot trial in Kisumu, Kenya. Twelve women living with HIV, aged 18–49, with a history of CIN2/3 and prior ablation or excision, self-administered 2 g of 5FU intravaginally at home every other week for eight applications. Acceptability was assessed at week 16 using a questionnaire and in-depth interviews. All 12 completed the questionnaire; some initially reported worry, anxiety, or fear, but all later strongly agreed the cream was safe and that they used it correctly. All preferred the cream over ablation or excision. Challenges included measuring the dose, tampon use, side effects, condom use, abstinence, partner support, and privacy. Qualitative findings highlighted reduced pain, ease, privacy, home delivery, education, and clinic support as factors increasing acceptability. The trial previously found 5FU safe with primarily grade I adverse events, all 12 tolerated all eight doses, and adherence was supported for 96% of doses. The study concludes high acceptability of self-administered intravaginal 5FU as an adjuvant treatment for CIN2/3 among women living with HIV and supports ongoing research into topical self-administered therapies in low- and middle-income countries, while noting limitations of a small, single-site pilot study.

The Trump administration gave the Labor Department more control over career and technical education, moving responsibilities that had been under the Education Department to Labor. Officials say the goal is to boost labor-force participation, reduce state administrative burdens, and centralize workforce development. Supporters say the change could improve alignment and accountability and help more young people get jobs; the U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation’s Jason Tyszko says the Labor Department has apprenticeship experience and could better assess workforce outcomes. Critics, including many CTE advocates and congressional Democrats, say the transfer may dismantle the Education Department, should have gone through Congress, and could steer students toward short-term training with fewer advancement paths. They also fear insufficient federal staff, less guidance, especially for students with disabilities, and an overemphasis on short-term credentials. Alabama’s Anna Chappelle hopes federal changes mirror state efforts to align education and workforce programs.

Posted January 3, 2025, this withdrawn medRxiv preprint evaluates Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, Neural Network, Decision Tree, and SuperLearner for pancreatic cancer diagnosis using a synthetic dataset with demographic, clinical, and symptom predictors and a binary diagnosis. In Horejs v. Milford, Laura Shaner died after complications from surgery and dialysis. Her husband David Shaner sued Dr. Milford, St. Margaret Mercy Healthcare Centers, and TRC-Indiana for wrongful death, seeking final-expense damages and survivor damages including loss of consortium. While the suit was pending, David died intestate with no known heirs, and his estate escheated to Indiana. The trial court granted partial summary judgment for defendants on the survivor damages claim, and the Court of Appeals affirmed. The Indiana Supreme Court granted transfer and reversed, holding that the wrongful death and survival statutes allow David’s survivor damages claim to survive his death regardless of whether an heir exists, and that Bemenderfer did not require an heir. However, the Court was not convinced the proper party was maintaining the claim, noting the trial court had found Laura’s estate co-administrators lacked standing to continue a claim on behalf of David’s estate. It remanded for the trial court to determine whether a proper party exists to continue the action.

The device’s active-high alarm output on ALARM/SDO-1/GPO is enabled by setting SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] to 01b. Active and tripped flags are in ALARM_REG; flags can be read via the ALARM pin, registers, or appended data output.

The signal may be less reliable for the S&P 500 than for the Russell 2000, as small-cap stocks are more volatile. Backtests used cash indexes, not ETFs.

The Ichimoku trading strategy is a technical analysis system that identifies support and resistance levels, trend direction, and momentum by plotting multiple averages that form a “cloud.” Its components are the Tenkan-Sen, Kijun-Sen, Senkou Span A, Senkou Span B, and Chikou Span. Price above the cloud indicates an uptrend, price below indicates a downtrend, and cloud thickness is used to gauge volatility. Crossovers, the Chikou Span, and Senkou spans can provide signals or confirmations. Traders can create quantified strategies from its components and should backtest and forward-test them. Risks include signals that may not be accurate or reliable. Backtests across assets suggested the strategy spends less time in the market and avoids drawdowns but often underperforms risk-adjusted buy-and-hold returns, so it is not among the best. Different timeframes are used, and the only way to find the best is to backtest, though daily bars are believed best.

This paper examines whether group-based versus individualized brain parcellations affect estimates of functional connectivity (FC) differences in psychosis using Human Connectome Project–Early Psychosis data. Group-based parcellations map a standard atlas to individuals, while individualized parcellations adjust parcel borders using individual FC data while preserving region labels. Individualized parcellations reassigned over 40% of vertices, increased within-parcel functional homogeneity, and yielded more conservative case-control FC differences than group-based parcellations. Group-based parcellations detected larger and more widespread differences, including a Network Based Statistic component about 9% larger, and led to different conclusions about specific affected edges and regions, although network-level findings were largely consistent. The authors conclude that group-based parcellations may inflate case-control FC differences in psychosis, whereas individualized parcellations can provide more refined estimates. Limitations include low mesh resolution and medication/clinical heterogeneity.

The lecture postpones DAEs and reviews prior topics. It recalls solving linear systems with Matlab backslash, unique solutions, n cubed operations, machine accuracy, and ill conditioning, which can allow multiple x values or cause small changes in b to produce large changes in x. For nonlinear systems, Newton-Raphson repeatedly uses j\f and costs iterations times n cubed; dogleg/trust-region methods may be used, and fsolve converts root finding into minimizing the norm of f. fmincon involves saddle points and gradients. Practical cost often scales as n squared because of Jacobian construction, and initial guesses affect iteration counts. Implicit ODE methods require solving a nonlinear equation for y_new at each time step, costing time steps times nonlinear iterations times n squared. Functionals take function names as inputs, including fsolve, derivatives, gradients, Jacobian, and density functional theory energy functionals. Numerical integration interpolates functions using basis functions: k<n approximates, k=n interpolates, and orthogonal basis functions avoid singular matrices. Polynomials are common, but high-order polynomials can oscillate, and monomials can have exponentially growing condition numbers. Lagrange polynomials make coefficients equal f values; Newton polynomials allow adding points without changing previous coefficients. Gauss quadrature chooses weights and points to integrate polynomials up to order 2n-1 exactly, with a related 15-point method for error estimation. Multidimensional integration nests quadrature, increasing cost exponentially, called the curse of dimensionality.

The lecture includes a Q&A on the Hawking-Page transition, thermal AdS, sphere setups, and a first-order transition at a critical temperature between thermal AdS and black-hole phases dominated by different energy scales. It then introduces entanglement entropy: for a system split into A and B, tracing out B gives the reduced density matrix, whose von Neumann entropy defines EE. For pure states SA=SB; for mixed states they generally differ and include classical correlations. A two-spin example illustrates entanglement, followed by subadditivity and strong subadditivity. In local many-body systems and QFTs, ground states obey an area law, with EE’s leading term proportional to boundary area over a short-distance cutoff; subleading terms encode long-range and topological information. In 1+1D CFT, EE is (c/3) log(L/epsilon), linking central charge to degrees of freedom. The Ryu-Takayanagi proposal relates boundary EE to the area of a minimal bulk surface ending on the boundary divided by 4G_N. Checks include strong subadditivity. For AdS3/CFT2, the minimal curve is a half-circle and reproduces the CFT formula. At finite temperature, large regions hug the black-hole horizon, recovering black-hole entropy. The lecture concludes that holographic entanglement connects geometry to quantum information and unifies quantum many-body, gravity, and black-hole physics.

The passage presents a study on integrating transformer-based large language models (LLMs) into domain-specific financial report analysis workflows. It notes that LLMs have transformed NLP, but domain-specific use requires understanding unique circumstances. Financial report analysis remains largely manual, time-intensive, and inconsistent, with challenges including data sensitivity, domain terminology, interpretability, and accuracy. The study collaborates with Getinge AB, uses an exploratory case study, and is guided by two research questions: RQ1, the primary software engineering challenges in integrating LLMs into domain-specific report analysis workflows; and RQ2, how open-source and commercial LLMs compare in software engineering complexity, performance, and maintainability. It reviews NLP and LLM background, prompting and agent-based approaches, implementation challenges such as computational demands, security and privacy, and hallucinations, as well as financial statement analysis and related work on software engineering for LLM systems and LLMs in finance.

The method is a field study using Design Science Research, a literature review, and collaboration with Getinge’s finance department. Cycle 0 used focus groups and task analysis with business controllers to identify use cases: UC1 generating income statement comments, UC2 summarizing order intake changes, and UC3 summarizing net sales changes. Data came in varied formats requiring preprocessing; sensitive-data restrictions meant UC1 was not pursued, while UC2 and UC3 used structured, anonymized, or synthetic data. Cycle 1 tested locally hosted LLMs via Ollama, including Qwen, LLaMA, and DeepSeek models. Single prompting was ineffective, so a four-agent prompt-chained workflow was implemented with a Financial Data Analyst, Business Analyst, Report Writer, and Financial Validator. Small models struggled with instruction-following, hallucinated, and sometimes returned code; errors propagated downstream. Larger 8B models still showed hallucination and instability, and compute constraints impeded further local experimentation. Cycle 2 used OpenAI’s GPT-4o via API with Python, similar preprocessing, system role definition, user instructions, few-shot examples, and post-processing. GPT-4o captured trends with less task decomposition but sometimes missed insights; examples caused rigid copying, while no examples improved trend capture but not format. High compute made on-premise deployment infeasible, raising privacy, compliance, and vendor-dependence concerns.

Evaluation had two professionals assess 20 summaries per model across usefulness, accuracy, clarity, trust, and workflow integration. Both models produced professional language; GPT-4o was preferred for reporting conciseness, while the local LLM was more descriptive and potentially suitable for internal use. Both showed redundancy, unclear main drivers or detractors, omissions, misprioritization, incorrect regional attributions, lack of numerical values, and limited transparency; manual review remained necessary. A refinement of Cycle 2 used a two-agent prompt-chained analyst and report writer, improving analysis alignment but still producing formatting and logical issues, repeated product lines, and contradictions.

The discussion identifies RQ1 challenges as task specificity in prompt and system design, data preparation variability, and data sensitivity constraints. For RQ2, local open-source models offer data control, privacy, and reduced dependency but require engineering effort and infrastructure and have reliability issues; GPT-4o offers ease, stronger out-of-box performance and tone, but limited control, compliance and vendor lock-in risks, and residual logic and reliability issues. Both need verification and post-processing, lack interpretability, and produce draft-quality rather than report-ready summaries. Implications include underdeveloped software engineering guidance, the need for structured methods, evaluation, and architectural support, and trade-offs among control, cost, and ease. Limitations include a small expert sample, qualitative assessment, transformed or old data, a single company context, and non-determinism. The conclusion states that LLMs have potential for partial automation but face significant engineering challenges, and full end-to-end automation of formal financial reporting remains challenging. Future work includes modular and rule-aware prompts, conditional logic, prompt versioning and documentation, coordination protocols and fault isolation in multi-agent setups, and hybrid deployment strategies.

The DAWN-plasma study was a randomized, open-label, multicenter phase 2 proof-of-concept trial evaluating best supportive care plus convalescent plasma versus best supportive care alone in hospitalized adult patients with COVID-19. Patients were randomized 2:1 and received 800–1000 mL convalescent plasma in 4 doses, with the first dose within 12 hours. The primary endpoint was the proportion alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Among 499 patients assessed, 489 were randomized (326 plasma, 163 control). The primary endpoint did not differ between groups (plasma 83.7% vs control 84.1%; OR 0.99; p=0.976). No statistically significant differences were found for secondary endpoints, mortality, mechanical ventilation at Day 30, or other outcomes. Adverse events, fatal AEs, and SAEs were similar between groups; treatment-related AEs occurred in 12 plasma+SOC patients (3.75%) and treatment-related SAEs in 7 (2.19%); transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19/320 (6.0%). The study was conducted per Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP, with IEC approval and informed consent.

Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) arises in the mucosal linings of the upper aerodigestive tract, and oral carcinomas can evolve from oral potentially malignant lesions (OPMLs). Fanconi anemia (FA) patients have a high incidence of HNSCC and frequently develop OPMLs. This proof-of-principle study used next-generation sequencing to detect cancer DNA mutations in saliva and plasma from 16 FA patients in a prospective longitudinal study. Liquid biopsies were collected repeatedly, and DNA was sequenced with the Oncomine Pan-Cancer Cell-Free Assay. Mutations were found in 15 samples from 9 patients, mostly in TP53. Among 14 patients with follow-up, 6/7 who developed lesions or carcinomas had at least one liquid biopsy mutation, detected before clinical diagnosis with lead times of 23–630 days (median 205 days). No mutations were found in five patients free of lesions/tumors. The test’s accuracy was 92%, with 86% sensitivity and 100% specificity. The authors conclude that deep-sequencing of saliva and plasma can detect cancer gene mutations that stratify FA patients into risk groups, such that closer surveillance should be recommended for patients with such mutations.

The passage explains that football terminology, especially offensive line play and block types, can confuse people, and it aims to explain these blocks and linemen’s responsibilities. It defines Trap block as leaving a defensive lineman unblocked and kicking him out; Base block as any one-on-one block in run or pass protection requiring inside leverage; Reach block as establishing and maintaining outside leverage on the front side of a run; Down block as an angle block on an inside defender on the front side of a run; Log block as a pulling blocker sealing a defender inside on the front side; Pull as a blocker moving around another offensive player to another position; Veer block as a drop-step and rip through the defensive front to block second-level linebackers, mostly in under-center triple option offenses; Combo block as two offensive players blocking a first-level defender to a second-level defender; Drive block as a one-on-one run block driving a defender off the line while maintaining inside leverage; Double Team Block as the first part of a Combo block, using post and trail players; Scoop block as a backside combo block seeking leverage on the far point of first- and second-level defenders; Cut block as diving at a defender’s legs in run or pass; Crack block as a perimeter player coming back inside to block an interior defender; and Kick Out block as similar to Trap but one gap wider outside the tackle, creating a C-gap running lane and becoming a Log if the defender wrong-arms. The passage also describes examples, footwork, and uses for many of these blocks.

In Phase 2/3, researchers compared COVID-19 from 7 days after Dose 2 of BNT162b2 or placebo to 03 December 2020. BNT162b2 was 95% effective versus placebo, with similar results for participants with or without prior COVID-19; researchers decided results were not likely due to chance. First 2 doses of 30 µg BNT162b2 gave protection against COVID-19 in participants aged 16 years and older regardless of past COVID-19.

Immune responses were measured 1 month after BNT162b2 or BNT162b2SA. In participants who had BNT162b2 before and no past COVID-19 up to 1 month after booster, responses against the original strain after BNT162b2 booster were as good as after Dose 2, and responses against Beta after BNT162b2SA booster were as good as responses against original after Dose 2. In those who had not received BNT162b2 before and no past COVID-19 up to 1 month after Dose 2, responses against Beta after BNT162b2SA were as good as responses against original after BNT162b2. Researchers decided these results were not likely due to chance.

Medical problems were recorded. In Phase 1, a few participants had temporary lymphocyte drops 1–3 days after Dose 1 of BNT162b1 or BNT162b2; counts returned to normal by 6–8 days, and none had low lymphocytes 6–8 days after Dose 2. Injection site reactions and systemic events within 7 days were well tolerated and mostly mild or moderate; pain was the most common injection site reaction, and tiredness and headache were the most common systemic events. Phase 1 doses were well tolerated except BNT162b1 100 µg, which was stopped after Dose 1; BNT162b2 30 µg was selected for Phase 2/3. Most Phase 2/3 medical problems were mild or moderate, and few participants left due to medical problems (32/21,926 BNT162b2; 36/21,921 placebo). Serious medical problems were few; some in Phase 2/3 were considered possibly related, while others were not believed related. No participant died in Phase 1; Phase 2/3 deaths occurred among BNT162b2 and placebo recipients, from different causes, and researchers did not believe they were caused by BNT162b2. No participant died in Phase 3 among those without prior BNT162b2 who received BNT162b2SA. More details are available from study staff or the full scientific report.

GA10x features 2x FP32 processing, second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with TF32, BF16, and Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, plus concurrent RT Core and graphics/compute operation. It adds ray-traced motion blur acceleration, GDDR6X/GDDR6 memory, third-generation NVLink, PCIe Gen 4, ROP optimizations, and EDR for GDDR6X memory errors. It supports DLSS up to 8K, RTX IO with DirectStorage, DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 decode, and seventh-generation NVENC. RTX A6000 and A40 use 48 GB GDDR6 scalable to 96 GB via NVLink; A40 is for data center visual computing, and A6000 is for desktop workstations. GeForce RTX 3090 is built for 8K HDR gaming, and RTX 3070 uses GA104 with GDDR6. The passage also lists specifications, comparisons, and performance data for these GPUs.

In this action, Manuel and Esther Kitrosser sued The CIT Group/Factoring, Inc. over guarantees and pledge agreements securing factoring and lending services CIT provided to Top Form Mills, Inc. and Top Blush Corporation. The court could not determine the exact account balance but resolved three issues. It held that postpetition interest continued to accrue on Top Form’s factoring debit balance and term loan; because the bankruptcy petitions were dismissed without discharge, CIT could collect that interest from Top Form and, consequently, from the Kays under their guarantees. CIT’s settlement with the EDA for less than the full guaranteed amount did not reduce Mr. Kay’s liability, because the guarantee permitted release and CIT reserved its rights. The Kays’ new amended claims based on CIT’s reduction of Top Blush’s advance rate did not relate back to the original complaint and were time-barred. The paper presents a DFT+DMFT study of strongly correlated itinerant magnets using a multi-orbital Hubbard model with local and non-local self-energy corrections from charge and spin fluctuations. Numerical calculations are performed for α-iron, CrO2, CrTe2, and altermagnet CrSb using Quantum Espresso, Wannier90, CT-QMC iQIST, and analytic continuation. For iron and CrO2, non-local magnetic correlations near the Curie temperature produce band splitting near van Hove singularities and make the paramagnetic spectrum resemble the ferromagnetic DFT band structure. For CrTe2 and CrSb, where d filling is closer to half filling, strong local spin correlations already cause splitting, expected over a broader temperature range. The split bands are dispersive, carry partial spectral weight, lack definite spin polarization, and are expected to be sensitive to magnetic field. The density-density approximation overestimates magnetic transition temperatures; future extension to an SU(2) symmetric Hund interaction is suggested.

GEM is a cryo-EM reconstruction framework that uses 3D Gaussian Splatting as an explicit protein-density representation. It places 3D Gaussians only in nonzero-density regions, enables parallel rasterization, and restricts gradient computation to Gaussians contributing to each pixel, avoiding the cubic memory and computation overhead of NeRF-based real-space methods and the information loss of Fourier-based methods. On four widely used cryo-EM datasets, GEM achieves lower memory usage and faster training than CryoNeRF, surpasses CryoDRGN and CryoNeRF in reconstruction quality, attains GSFSC resolutions better than 3 Å, and provides up to 48× faster training.

AMD testing indicates TMPM performance improves with commands of 16 or more pages and is maximum at 128 pages, and the command input ring buffer works best when commands arrive quickly enough to keep the ring buffer ahead of the engine. Interrupts should not be requested on every command but at the end of a sequence, such as with a NOP command or Interrupt on Complete; a low-water interrupt can help refill the queue. Several data structures do not support migration: IOMMU memory structures accessed via SPA, including host page tables, command buffer, and event log; IOMMU page tables mapping vIOMMU Private Address Space; vIOMMU pinned backing storage buffers; the Ring Buffer; and argument pages. For PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, source pages must be DMA-mapped using IOMMU host page tables, and only one IOMMU host page table may DMA-map any migrated system physical page. An IOMMU host page table must map the memory containing IOMMU host page tables; this virtual address space is HPTVA. TMPM may modify referenced IOMMU host page table entries non-atomically, so host software must avoid concurrent modifications and account for TMPM setting Access and Dirty bits, such as by pausing ring buffer processing or careful command creation.

TMPM firmware can be reloaded only when no operations are in flight. HV/OS should pause operations, tear down the ring buffer, disable PAGEMIGRATION_EN bits in IOMMUs, and issue the reload command using the BIOS to PSP mailbox protocol. If the ring buffer is initialized, reload returns PM_MX_INVALID_RELOAD_REQUEST; version and other reload issues also return errors. Drivers should check ENGINE_READY before communicating with firmware. Reload methodology varies by EPYC family; the driver uses PM_GET_CAPABILITIES and its FW_VER_Major field, with EPYC Family 19h represented by 71 decimal, to choose the reload path. For Family 19h, software places the updated firmware image and a reload firmware header in system memory and follows a specified register-based algorithm.

The TMPM driver initializes by checking PM_Status, setting the ring buffer SPA, queue configuration, write pointer, interrupt hook, and DRIVER_INITIALIZED, then waiting for DRIVER_INIT_COMPLETE; PAUSE can pause or resume ring buffer processing. The ring buffer is separate from the SEV/SNP ring buffer, and commands may execute asynchronously, so execution order is not guaranteed and completion is known when the Read Pointer passes a command. Each TMPM command contains a parameter page in PM_LIST_PADDR with 1–128 Migration Entries. TMPM moves data only between 4k-aligned pages, so all SPAs must be 4k aligned, except host page table entry physical addresses are 8-byte aligned; 2M pages require the bottom 21 bits to be zero. Interrupt sources include RBWritePtr_Err, RBMem_Err, QfreeIntStat, QthreshIntStat, IntOnError, and IntOnComplt. SPA encoding supports 46- or 52-bit addresses and encryption information for SMEE/SME-MK. Commands include PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, and a command to mark the end of a sequence. Errors are reported in command status, migration list entries, PM_STATUS, and/or MCA, and may affect memory state or require ring buffer termination or reinitialization.

The passage reports a DFT study of the reaction 2CH2 → H2C=CH2 on a gold monolayer and on three layers of gold using a 2D periodic gold (111) surface. Layer thickness strongly affects adsorption energies, reaction path, and energetics. On the monolayer, reactants and products are more strongly bound, the reaction energy is −432.06 kJ mol−1, and the activation energy is 4.78 kJ mol−1. On three layers, binding is weaker, the reaction energy is −335.50 kJ mol−1, and the activation energy is 52.10 kJ mol−1. The monolayer reaction proceeds more straightforwardly, while the three-layer reaction includes more pronounced rotational motion and less stable intermediate association. The study concludes that surface morphology and layer properties affect carbon upconversion and suggests further studies on other surface characteristics.

The On-Balance Volume (OBV) is a volume-based technical indicator that estimates buying and selling pressure by adding volume when price closes higher and subtracting volume when it closes lower. It usually follows price in uptrends and downtrends, but can show non-confirmation or advanced breakout/breakdown scenarios. Its formula depends on whether today’s close is higher, lower, or equal to the previous close. Joseph Granville first published OBV in 1963 in New Key to Stock Market Profits, linking it to smart money and institutional investors. A backtest on SPY using RSI on OBV found one 5-day RSI with a buy threshold of 30 produced 337 trades, 0.55% average gain per trade, 73% win rate, 24% max drawdown, and 2.09 profit factor. The passage concludes volume is of limited value overall and not optimal alone.

The passage transitions from linear algebra to solving nonlinear equations and optimization. It reviews singular value decomposition and condition numbers, then discusses iterative solutions and convergence criteria: step norm, function norm/residual, and absolute versus relative tolerance. It emphasizes validating numerical results through multiple methods, experiments, or analytical limits. Nonlinear systems are defined as finding roots of f(x)=0, with locally unique solutions linked to the Jacobian and inverse function theorem. Linearization and Taylor expansion are used near roots, and convergence can be linear, superlinear, or quadratic. The Newton-Raphson method is presented for nonlinear systems, using the Jacobian to determine steps, with local convergence near locally unique solutions and possible failure from poor initial guesses or singular/ill-conditioned Jacobians. Examples include the Van der Waals equation for vapor-liquid coexistence and intersecting circles.

In Bost v. Illinois State Board of Elections, to be argued Oct. 8, the Supreme Court will consider whether a congressional candidate has standing to challenge an Illinois rule counting mail-in votes up to 14 days after polls close if postmarked by election day. Republican Rep. Michael Bost sued, arguing federal law supersedes the rule; the district court dismissed for lack of standing, and a divided 7th Circuit affirmed. The lower courts rejected his vote-dilution claim as a generalized grievance and his observer-cost and electoral-prospects claims as self-imposed or speculative. Before the Supreme Court, Bost argues he suffered pocketbook injury from keeping observers during extra counting and that the rule harms his electoral chances, including by reducing his margin of victory. He also urges a broad rule that candidates have standing to challenge rules governing their elections. The United States supports his narrow standing argument but opposes that blanket rule.

The study evaluated the Happy Ring, a finger-worn device with electrodermal activity, accelerometry, photoplethysmography-derived heart rate, and skin temperature sensors, for sleep-wake detection and sleep stage classification. Data were collected from 40 participants over 122 nights, with 36 adults across 77 nights ultimately analyzed. Participants underwent one laboratory night with polysomnography and two at-home nights using the Dreem headband, and also wore Actiwatch, Fitbit, Whoop, and Oura devices when available. The Happy Ring used 30-second epochs and two scoring approaches: Happy Generalized, using leave-one-out cross-validation at the night level, and Happy Personalized, using training and testing on non-overlapping time windows. Results showed sleep-wake detection accuracy of 0.92 for Happy Personalized and 0.91 for Happy Generalized in the laboratory, with other devices ranging from 0.84 to 0.88. At home, Happy Personalized and Happy Generalized each had accuracy of 0.92 and 0.91, respectively, while other devices ranged from 0.89 to 0.92. Happy Personalized demonstrated significantly higher accuracy and specificity for sleep-wake detection than all other devices studied in the laboratory. For light, deep, and REM sleep, Happy Personalized showed the highest sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy compared with other devices. The study concluded that the Happy Ring performed well relative to laboratory and at-home polysomnography, with the personalized approach consistently outperforming the generalized approach. Limitations included a relatively small, generally healthy sample, use of Dreem for home polysomnography, and undisclosed algorithm factors.

iCVS is a dynamical mechanistic model of the cardiovascular system intended to infer hidden cardiovascular states in real time from routinely available bedside measurements. It includes autonomic and non-autonomic regulation, has fifteen hidden parameters, and uses five observables extracted from arterial and venous blood pressure waveforms: mean arterial pressure, mean venous pressure, heart rate, peripheral resistance, and pulse pressure. Estimation uses age, weight, and constrained nonlinear optimization. The model was tested on data from 10 pediatric intensive care unit patients and used to identify hypovolemic, distributive, and cardiogenic shock states through parameters such as Iex, MSVR, and maximal relative contractility. Results are compared with clinical documentation and expert labels. The passage notes the need for larger prospective validation and limitations involving noisy recordings and model assumptions.

This pragmatic, two-stage adaptive open-label randomized clinical trial examined emergency department (ED) acupuncture for acute musculoskeletal pain. The study aimed to identify which acupuncture style—auricular acupuncture (AA) based on Battlefield Acupuncture or peripheral acupuncture (PA)—was more feasible, acceptable, and efficacious, then compare the selected style with usual care only (UC) for pain reduction. It took place in a U.S. academic tertiary-care ED. English-speaking adult patients with acute (≤7 days) new-onset or exacerbated chronic neck, back, arm, and/or leg musculoskeletal pain were enrolled. Participants were randomized to AA+UC, PA+UC, or UC. In Stage 1, allocation was 1:1:1; in Stage 2, it was 2:2:1. Of 911 screened, 236 were randomized. Feasibility goals were met, with >95% of the intention-to-treat population completing the one-hour outcome. At one hour, estimated pain reductions were 2.1 for AA+UC, 1.6 for PA+UC, and 0.5 for UC. AA+UC and PA+UC did not differ significantly. Satisfaction with acupuncture was high, and adverse events were few with no serious adverse events. The authors conclude that both auricular and peripheral acupuncture are feasible, acceptable, and effective for acute musculoskeletal pain in the ED and should be further explored for wider implementation. Limitations included a single urban ED, English-speaking enrollment, treatment by licensed acupuncturists, and unblinded patients.

This lecture discusses thermal properties of foams. Closed-cell foams are widely used for thermal insulation because their low thermal conductivity mainly comes from a high gas volume fraction and low solid volume fraction. Small cells reduce convection and radiation. Only aerogels have lower thermal conductivity, but they are very weak and brittle. Foam thermal conductivity includes contributions from solid conduction, gas conduction, convection within cells, and radiation. Most conductivity comes from the gas. Low-conductivity gases are used for insulation, but aging allows gas diffusion and increases conductivity over time. Convection is negligible in most foams because cells are smaller than about 20 mm. Radiation decreases with higher relative density, creating a tradeoff with solid conduction and sometimes a minimum in overall conductivity. Conductivity increases with cell size. Aerogels have very small pores, below the mean free path of air, reducing conductivity. Foam specific heat and thermal expansion coefficient equal those of the solid. Foams have good thermal shock resistance, with a critical temperature change for cracking larger than that of the solid by a factor of 0.2 divided by the square root of relative density. Applications include building insulation, refrigerated vehicles, and LNG tankers.

El artículo estudia la expresión lingüística de las emociones en cuentas corporativas de Twitter de Acciona e Iberdrola, mediante un corpus de 798 tuits publicados entre abril y junio de 2016. Analiza tipos de emociones, unidades verbales, metáforas y su relación con la misión, visión y valores empresariales. Los resultados muestran predominio de emociones positivas —orgullo, alegría-felicidad-optimismo, interés y confianza— y escasa presencia de negativas. Las metáforas se vinculan a la identidad corporativa: Iberdrola, luz/verde; Acciona, sostenibilidad. Concluye que el microblog corporativo es un corpus válido, que refuerza la identidad organizacional y sugiere aplicaciones para la enseñanza del español de negocios.

The study presents a fully automatic machine learning-based tool that uses multisequence MRI to segment diffuse midline glioma (DMG) subregions and predict overall survival. It was trained and evaluated on internal and external two-center MRI data acquired at diagnosis and post-radiation therapy, achieving 77–85% accuracy for DMG survival prediction. Data-driven analysis identified homogeneous whole tumor intensity in baseline T2 FLAIR and a larger post-therapy tumor core/whole tumor volume ratio as indicators of worse prognosis. The tool may help predict clinical outcome, stratify patients into risk groups, monitor therapeutic response, adapt treatment, and support consistent evaluation in multi-institutional clinical trials. Limitations include small cohorts and scanner/protocol variability.

The Associated Press interviewed 29 Rohingya women and girls in refugee camps in Bangladesh who fled Myanmar and described rapes by Myanmar’s security forces between October 2016 and mid-September. Their accounts bolster a U.N. contention that Myanmar’s armed forces systematically use rape as a calculated tool of terror aimed at exterminating the Rohingya. Myanmar’s armed forces did not respond to AP requests; an internal military investigation concluded no assaults occurred. Officials dismissed rape allegations, while doctors and aid workers reported treating many sexual violence survivors, including children. One woman, F, said soldiers raped her in Myanmar, killed her husband, and burned her house; later she was raped again, then fled to Bangladesh, where she was pregnant and living in a bamboo shelter.

The "Pound Cake" offense attacks a Box & One defense by isolating the star player 1-on-1 in the post/middle. If no good shot is available, the star can roll to the basket using base screens or pop out for a 1-on-1 isolation. The offense includes base-screen reads and counters, ball reversal and post flash options, screener pop, guard basket cut, and a double mid-screen ("Horns") variation. Success requires coordinated execution of mid screens, base screens, and post ups, plus defensive recognition, communication, timing, experience, scouting, and in-game adjustments.

The Supreme Court will consider whether a trial court may prevent a criminal defense lawyer from talking to his client about the client’s ongoing testimony during an overnight recess. In David Villarreal’s murder trial, after he testified on direct examination, the judge instructed him and his attorneys to act as if he were on the stand and barred conferring about his testimony overnight. Villarreal was convicted and argues the order violated his Sixth Amendment right to effective assistance of counsel. Texas courts upheld the order. Precedents set limits: a 1976 ruling barred an overnight “about anything” no-confer order, while a 1989 ruling allowed a 15-minute midday no-contact order. State supreme courts and federal appeals courts have split. Texas and the United States defend limited conferral orders; Villarreal argues the rule is unworkable, chills advice, and threatens attorney-client privilege. The parties also dispute historical practice.

The bark Cape Horn Pigeon was released too late to continue its whaling voyage that season. It had been seized by the Imperial Russian Government, taken from its fishing grounds, and detained at Vladivostok, causing damages to its owners, officers, and crew. The captain estimated damages at $49,500 and presented a claim in September 1892. U.S. diplomatic notes in 1893 and 1894 sought investigation and presented indemnity claims. A Russian commission found the vessel had navigated within Russian territorial waters but found no reason for confiscation, attributed the arrest to a misunderstanding, and ordered release. Russia suggested $2,500 as sufficient indemnity and later requested vouchers for $3,400 in expenses.

The court affirmed the order granting defendants summary judgment and dismissing the complaint. Plaintiff appealed dismissal of claims including conversion, fraud, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and invasion of privacy, arising from defendants’ use of a signed medical expense reimbursement form to obtain decedent’s medical records to defend a workers’ compensation claim. The conversion claim failed because plaintiff lacked a possessory interest in the records, which belong to the doctor. The fraud claim failed because Tryon’s statements were not material misrepresentations and alleged misrepresentations were made to hospitals, not plaintiff. The emotional distress claim failed because defendants’ conduct was not sufficiently outrageous. Offensive linemen sustain successful offenses but receive blame when offenses struggle and little praise from outsiders, especially offensive tackles. Positioned at the end of the offensive line, tackles often block an opponent’s best pass rusher with little help. They run block defensive linemen and linebackers and pass block one-on-one to give the quarterback a sound pocket. They have run or pass blocking assignments and must handle pre-snap looks, blitzes, and movement with athleticism, agility, coordination, footwork, hand placement, and football IQ. The name “offensive tackle” originated from outside running plays in early football, when edge defenders tackled ball carriers. Tackles are two of five offensive linemen, line up as the outermost linemen, and are abbreviated OT or T. Common nicknames include Hogs, Bruisers, Bulldozers, and Big Uglies. NFL body types are generally 6’3–6’8 and 300–340 pounds with a thick build. Notable tackles include Jonathan Ogden, Anthony Munoz, and Joe Thomas. Left tackles protect the quarterback’s blind side and are often considered a team’s most talented offensive lineman. Offensive tackles help provide pocket comfort and running lanes.

The lecture gives assignment advice to focus on numerical methods rather than chemical engineering definitions. It reviews unconstrained optimization via steepest descent, using a Taylor expansion to choose an optimal step size, and notes convergence problems for steep functions. Linear equations Ax = b can be cast as minimizing a quadratic functional when A is symmetric positive definite. Steepest descent is difficult for such problems; conjugate gradient chooses conjugate directions, preserves previous minimization, solves n-equation systems in at most n iterations, and requires only matrix-vector products. Newton-Raphson for grad f = 0 uses the Hessian in place of the Jacobian, converges quadratically and exactly for quadratic functions, but can go uphill if Hessian eigenvalues are not positive. Trust-region methods combine Newton-Raphson and steepest descent based on a trust-region radius, growing or shrinking it as needed; Matlab’s fsolve and minimizers use such heuristics, including dogleg trust-region methods.

Backtests on SPY found best results with short lookback periods, especially two days, with strong performance during 2008–09 and Covid-19, though it did not work for shorts. Compared with RSI, Williams %R showed higher CAGR in the tests; another strategy on QQQ also produced solid results. The passage concludes Williams %R seems to work well and is underappreciated.

This study investigated the relation between hypertension, blood pressure, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) leakage in human subjects using a sparsely sampled dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI protocol at 7 Tesla. Twenty-three patients with essential hypertension and 20 normotensive controls were included, matched on age and sex; after outlier exclusion, 22 hypertensive patients and 19 controls were analyzed. No significant difference in BBB leakage rate (Ki) was found between hypertensive patients and controls after adjusting for age and sex. However, plasma volume fraction (vp) was significantly higher in hypertensive patients in grey matter regions of interest and showed a comparable trend in white matter. Higher systolic and diastolic blood pressure and mean arterial pressure were positively associated with Ki in cortical grey matter, and diastolic blood pressure and mean arterial pressure with Ki in total grey matter. No significant relations were found for white matter or deep grey matter. Associations generally remained after adjusting for cardiovascular risk factors, medication intake, and cerebral small vessel disease score. Post-hoc analyses showed that well-treated hypertensive patients had lower leakage rates than patients with current hypertension in total and cortical grey matter. The authors conclude that current blood pressure, rather than dichotomous hypertension status, relates to BBB leakage in grey matter, and that effective antihypertensive medication may have a protective effect, though larger or longitudinal studies are needed.

The lecture reviews mean-variance portfolio theory. Combining imperfectly correlated securities creates a bullet-shaped risk/return curve, with rational investors preferring the upper efficient frontier. Using GM, IBM, and Motorola, portfolios are weighted combinations based on means, standard deviations, and covariances; adding more stocks shifts the frontier northwest and cannot make investors worse off. Mixing a riskless asset with risky portfolios creates straight lines, and the tangency portfolio has the highest Sharpe ratio. With mean-variance preferences, all investors want the tangency line; in equilibrium, the tangency portfolio is market portfolio M, held in proportion to market capitalization because supply equals demand. The lecture gives the efficient-portfolio relationship using portfolio/market standard-deviation ratio and market excess return, then Sharpe’s general relationship using beta, defined as covariance with the market divided by market variance, to determine appropriate discount rates. Assumptions include static analysis, stable parameters, equal borrowing and lending rates, and mean-variance preferences.

Belarus is a landlocked Eastern European country, formerly a USSR republic, independent in 1991. Its education system was influenced by the USSR and later absorbed ideas from EU countries, combining both systems. Out-of-school education is a significant component. Its development has three stages: early 20th-century literacy programs for poor and uneducated people; Soviet-era construction of an out-of-school system in labor education, outdoor practice, occupation choice, and youth talent identification/selection; and post-Soviet integration of Soviet-style out-of-school education with EU ideas and laws, focusing on individual development and lifelong learning. In 2011, amendments to The Code defined out-of-school education as part of lifelong learning, with chapters 46–49 covering institutions, training, methodology, and access. Subsequent decrees addressed areas including civic, patriotic, moral, aesthetic, health, labor, ecological, safety, and psychological education. By end-2021, Belarus had 318 out-of-school institutions: 3 national, 315 regional; 185 comprehensive and 133 specialized. Specialized institutions included regional study tours (62), ecosystem protection (30), physical training (15), science/technology training (13), professional training (9), and art training (4). About one-third of Belarusian children and adolescents are trained in out-of-school institutions; state-run institutions are popular due to lower fees and competitions aiding university admission. Main characteristics include clear orientation and legislative guarantees, diverse options, personality development, patriotism/national identity, physical fitness, ecological awareness, and scientific literacy. Public out-of-school education is often first choice; paid training accounts for 10%–30%, with some areas free, while private capital is entering. Cultivation objectives are four key abilities: mastering IT knowledge, developing social personality, surviving in a multicultural world, and sustaining lifelong study. Representative institutions include Minsk State Children’s Palace, Belarusian Youth League, and Firefighters Association. Shortcomings include funding shortages, outdated equipment, unequal access, neglect of small-scale interpersonal skills, and short-term cultural activities. The passage concludes that Belarus combined Soviet and EU approaches with legislative guarantees and four key abilities, and its experience may be useful for China.

The President transmits to the Senate for ratification a convention between the United States and Great Britain, concluded at Washington by John M. Clayton and Sir Henry Lytton Bulwer. The article presents four overnight S&P 500 strategies that buy at the close and sell the next open, using short holding periods to limit drawdowns. Strategy 1 buys on a new n-day low with two variables and requires the close above the 200-day moving average; it returns 8.43% with a 29% win rate, and the equity curve worsens without that condition. Strategy 2 also uses a new n-day low plus criteria, returning 12.69% with a 14% win rate and a 2.6 profit factor. Strategy 3 uses three variables and has a profit factor of about 3.8. Strategy 4, a variation of Strategy 3, benefits from short-term oversold bounces; holding to the close raises total P/L to 80% but is more erratic. A twist holds if SPY opens below -0.1%.

This study examined dropout tendencies among undergraduate and preparatory students at Turkish public universities during the 2023–2024 academic year. Using Tinto’s Theoretical Dropout Model and the School Dropout Scale in Higher Education, data were collected from 1,061 students. Results showed a moderate overall dropout tendency (mean 2.67). Dropout tendencies did not differ significantly by gender, but were higher among students in their third year or above, those studying outside metropolitan cities, those working while studying, and those with close friends who had dropped out. Dropout tendency was negatively correlated with school attendance frequency, mother’s and father’s education, GPA, and family income, and positively correlated with number of siblings. The scale’s subdimensions were positively correlated with overall dropout tendency. The study recommended retention strategies, especially in non-metropolitan regions, including academic mentoring, financial support, mental health services, attendance monitoring, and early identification of at-risk students. Limitations included reliance on self-reported data, and future research was suggested to use longitudinal and mixed-method approaches and compare public and private universities.

The work reports synthesis and characterization of ZnSe-WSe2 and ZnSe-MoSe2 core-shell nanowires. ZnSe nanowires were grown by CVD; MoO3 or WO3 precursor layers were deposited by DC magnetron sputtering and converted to MoSe2 or WSe2 shells by selenization in a three-zone furnace. Selenization temperatures were 600 and 650 °C for ZnSe-MoSe2 and 700 and 750 °C for ZnSe-WSe2. TEM showed conformal, layered TMD shells at 600 °C for MoSe2 and 700 °C for WSe2, while higher temperatures produced discontinuous shells with protruding TMD crystals. XRD, XPS, and Raman confirmed wurtzite ZnSe, MoSe2, and WSe2 phases and complete conversion from oxide precursors. PL was used to study optical properties. The results indicate a temperature-dependent transition from solid-state reaction and smoother shell growth to oxide evaporation, gas-phase reaction, and crystalline island growth. The observed trends are proposed as extendable to other semiconductor nanowire/TMD core-shell heterostructures for nanoscale applications.

A Princeton-led study published Aug. 2 in Nature found that ATP-dependent ISWI chromatin remodelers use the nucleosome’s “acidic patch,” a negatively charged surface formed by H2A and H2B, to remodel chromatin. High-throughput screening showed this recognition had not previously been implicated in remodeling. Other remodeling enzymes also used the feature, suggesting a general requirement. Chemical modifications near the acidic patch enhanced or inhibited ISWI activity, and tested proteins had distinct responses. The study generated data for future research and may inform cancer therapeutic targets.

The passage presents EduVidQA, a pedagogically designed QA dataset for educational lecture videos. It reports a preliminary survey of 52 STEM students showing many used online lecture videos at least weekly and felt the need to ask questions, while few asked questions in comments. The dataset contains 5,252 QA pairs: 270 expert-verified real-world pairs from YouTube videos and 4,982 synthetic pairs from 197 NPTEL videos. A qualitative preference study identifies Clarity, Encouraging Critical Thinking, and Uses Pedagogical Techniques as important metrics; Depth and Conciseness were excluded from later work due to dependence on student expertise. The paper benchmarks MLLMs on real-world and synthetic test sets using text-based and qualitative metrics. Results show supervised finetuning on synthetic data improves open-source models, with finetuned mPLUG-Owl 3 8B and Llava-13B performing best qualitatively, and smaller open-source models comparable to or better than larger closed models on some metrics. Limitations include restricted demographics, dataset size and domain coverage, LLM-dependent metrics, and compute constraints.

This paper addresses memory management for long-running Low-Code/No-Code (LCNC) LLM agents, identifying memory inflation and contextual degradation as problems caused by finite context windows. It proposes a hybrid memory system with working memory, episodic memory, and semantic memory. An Intelligent Decay mechanism scores memories by recency, relevance, and user utility, then prunes or consolidates low-utility entries into semantic memory. A user-centric visual interface lets non-technical users retain, forget, or consolidate memories as Human-in-the-Loop actions. Experiments on a 500-turn project-planning task compare sliding window, basic RAG, and the hybrid system. The hybrid system reports 92.5% task completion, 890 average token cost per turn, 0.94 semantic consistency, and 1.2% contradiction rate. It maintains or improves performance over time, while an All-Add strategy degrades. Limitations include tuning decay hyperparameters and reliance on user feedback. Future work includes autonomous parameter calibration, structured pruning, multimodal and procedural memory, and integration with stateful agent frameworks.

The passage describes SEV-ES/SEV-SNP guest-hypervisor communication mechanisms. The AP Creation NAE event lets an SEV-SNP guest create, destroy, or change an AP’s register state at a VMPL, using RMPADJUST to mark a VMSA page. Create/Add can defer VMSA use until INIT-SIPI or install it immediately; Destroy/Remove updates or destroys a vCPU at a VMPL/APIC ID. Hypervisor validates VMPL/APIC ID, uses VMSA page SPA, and VMPL is valid only if Multi-VMPL is advertised. The guest tracks VMSA pages. The #HV Doorbell Page NAE event registers a doorbell page for #HV when Restricted Injection is enabled, with GET_PREFERRED, SET, QUERY, and CLEAR actions. The #HV Send IPI NAE event sends IPIs using SW_EXITINFO1 in x2APIC ICR format. The #HV Timer NAE event provides emulated APIC timer support with SET and GET actions. The APIC ID List NAE event returns guest APIC IDs using shared contiguous pages, returning required page count in RAX if insufficient. The SNP Run VMPL NAE event runs the current vCPU at a different VMPL, associating a unique VMSA per VMPL and updating VMSA/GHCB SPAs. SEV-TIO binds guests to trusted devices, discovered via TEE-IO PCIe capabilities, with SNP TIO Guest Request using Guest PCI ID, MMIO range, TDISP status, and optional shared data pages; returned data uses GUID table entries. Secure AVIC manages guest-owned APIC state with a private backing page per vCPU via REGISTER_BACKING_PAGE and UNREGISTER_BACKING_PAGE. The Termination Request NAE event lets a guest request termination, with reason codes in SW_EXITINFO1 and 64-bit info in SW_EXITINFO2. Unsupported NAEs use the “Unsupported Event” VMGEXIT. For SEV-ES identification, hypervisor CPUID properties indicate hypervisor, SEV support, encryption bit, and physical address reduction. SMP booting under SEV-ES/SNP cannot update measured/encrypted registers; methods include reset vector memory locations and predetermined CS/IP. Subsequent AP resets use AP Reset Hold NAE/MSR, SIPI, and AP jump table via SET/GET NAE and Secrets Page. NMI handling uses #DB intercept and “NMI Complete.” Debug registers are virtualized if DebugVirtualization is set, otherwise DR7 is intercepted and cached. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported. The #HV doorbell page contains PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields, with host APIC emulation and guest atomic exchange behavior.

At the time of seizure, Joseph Wing and William R. Wing of New Bedford, Massachusetts, were agents and managing owners of the Cape Horn Pigeon. NVIDIA’s Turing GPUs improve encoding quality over Pascal and software x264 encoders with lower CPU utilization, enabling 4K streaming. Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink, a USB-C alternate mode that delivers power, display, and data for VR headsets through one connector, supporting HBR3 DisplayPort and SuperSpeed USB 3. Turing uses NVLink instead of MIO and PCIe for SLI GPU-to-GPU transfers; TU102 has two x8 second-generation NVLink links and TU104 has one, with two-way SLI supported but not 3-way or 4-way. Turing adds RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 SMs with RTX software for real-time ray tracing, using hybrid rendering, rasterization, denoising, and BVH acceleration; RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection, and Turing ray tracing is faster than Pascal. NGX uses Tensor Cores for AI functions including DLSS, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez; DLSS uses DNNs trained against 64xSS and has a DLSS 2X mode. Mesh Shading adds Task and Mesh Shaders; VRS adjusts shading rate per 16x16 region; TSS decouples visibility and appearance sampling; MVR supports multiple views per pass. Turing supports bindless CBVs/UAVs and resource heap Tier 2. For VR, Turing offers VirtualLink, MVR, VRS foveated rendering, and RT Core-accelerated VRWorks Audio. TU104 contains six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6 billion transistors, and second-generation NVLink; Tesla T4 uses TU104 with 40 SMs, 2560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, and a 256-bit interface. TU106 has three GPCs, 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, and no NVLink or SLI. RTX-OPS is a workload-based metric derating Tensor 20%, CUDA 80%, RT 40%, and INT32 28%. The appendix describes ray tracing, BVH building and refitting, denoising, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections.

This paper examines structural and policy-related obstacles Peru faced in ensuring access to medical oxygen, using a problem-based political economy analysis with key informant interviews and reviews of academic literature, grey literature, and policies. Medical oxygen is essential for treating respiratory and critical conditions and was included in the WHO essential medicine list in 2002 for anesthetic use, with hypoxemia added in 2017. COVID-19 increased demand and exposed global supply gaps. Peru, a middle-income country of about 34 million, had economic growth and expanded healthcare access but persistent disparities. Its health system is fragmented among public, EsSalud, and private subsystems, with decentralized regional governance and political instability. Before the pandemic, oxygen supply was generally sufficient but distribution varied. A >99% purity requirement created a “policy trap,” limiting competition to a few suppliers despite the WHO’s recommendation of 93% or higher. During COVID-19, demand overwhelmed suppliers, especially in Andean and jungle regions. Peru declared quarantine in March 2020, but infections, hospitalizations, and deaths rose; at least 20% of hospitalized and ICU patients required oxygen. Government response was slow; lowering purity to 93% required two laws, three ministerial resolutions, and seven months. Lack of data, no national oxygen system, and fragmented procurement worsened the crisis. The RENOXI registry launched late, had reliability concerns, and suffered a cyberattack. Civil society and the private sector donated oxygen plants, but many lacked maintenance plans; nearly 200 plants are now unused, broken, or abandoned. The paper concludes Peru needs a National Oxygen System with supply tracking, forecasting, maintenance, quality control, training, and equitable distribution to prepare for future pandemics.

This scoping review examined approaches to measuring socioeconomic status in sub-Saharan African health research. It included 65 articles and identified 41 SES measures grouped into 11 categories. The asset-based Wealth Index was the most used measure (61.9%), with the Wealth Index representing 28.6%; Principal Component Analysis was the predominant calculation method. South Africa, Kenya, and Ghana were most frequently represented. Cross-sectional studies (52%) and cohort studies (23%) were most common; SES assessment/wealth/poverty and maternal, child, youth, family health and wellbeing were the most frequent themes. The review recommends standardization of SES measurement methods in Africa while allowing adjustments for local contexts.

Researchers confirmed through 3D modeling and field experiments that Rapa Nui’s moai statues could be “walked” upright using a rocking, zig-zag motion with rope and few people. Distinctive features such as wide D-shaped bases and a forward lean, along with concave roads, supported this method. A 4.35-ton replica was moved 100 meters in 40 minutes by 18 people. The findings are presented as evidence of the Rapa Nui people’s innovation and engineering intelligence.

Sudan, the last male northern white rhinoceros, died in Kenya on Monday at age 45 after a severe leg infection; his veterinary team euthanized him when he could no longer stand. Captured in 1975 and later moved to Ol Pejeta Conservancy in 2009 with females Najin and Fatu, he never reproduced. War and poaching drove northern white rhinos extinct in the wild. Scientists collected sperm, but the two remaining females cannot gestate. Proposed efforts include collecting eggs for implantation in a southern white rhino, a procedure never done and risky for the females.

This study developed and tested a maternal vulnerability segmentation tool (MVST) to identify pregnant women at higher risk of not using essential maternal services. Data came from the baseline of a community-based quasi-experiment in Oromia, Ethiopia, in early 2024. A total of 1,614 households were visited, 1,189 pregnant women were listed as eligible, and 470 pregnant women were included in the baseline sample. The MVST was a 20-item questionnaire covering economic, social, and information/service access drivers. Factor analyses retained four items for urban-rural settings and six items for rural settings, with acceptable reliability and fit. Women in higher vulnerability groups were less likely to use antenatal care and deliver in health facilities. Cutoff points indicated that scores above 3 for health facility delivery and 1 or more for antenatal care reflected greater vulnerability. Mediation analysis examined effects of vulnerability on health facility delivery through antenatal care. The MVST is intended to help community health workers classify pregnant women by vulnerability for targeted interventions, but it is not itself an intervention strategy. The authors note limitations, including context-specific applicability and changing vulnerability during pregnancy, and call for further validation and research.
