PAM4 signaling on GDDR6X sends two bits each clock edge using four voltage levels in 250 mV steps, instead of two-level NRZ on GDDR6. MTA encoding limits high-speed signal transitions by preventing highest-to-lowest and lowest-to-highest changes, improving interface SNR; new interface training, adaptations, equalization, and package/PCB design were also introduced. GDDR6X supports up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth on GA10x GPUs, over 52% more than TU102 in the GeForce RTX 2080 Ti. Pseudo-independent memory channels help with BVH ray traversal in RT Cores.

NVIDIA RTX IO enables rapid GPU-based loading and decompression, accelerating I/O up to 100x versus hard drives and traditional APIs. With Microsoft DirectStorage, it offloads CPU work to RTX GPUs, improves frame rates and loading, reduces pop-in and stutter, supports lossless compression, and provides GPU-based lossless decompression, improving I/O performance by a factor of two. It uses DMA and copy engines and Turing/Ampere SMs.

The NVIDIA A40, based on GA10x Ampere, is a data center GPU for visual computing. Compared with Quadro RTX 6000, it delivers up to 2X FP32, 2X ray-tracing, and up to 5X (10X with sparsity) AI throughput; PCIe Gen4 provides up to 2X higher bandwidth. It has 48GB memory, scalable to 96GB via NVLink, three DP1.4 outputs, vGPU support, Quadro Sync, and EGX compatibility.

Ampere supports 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz, DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a, HDMI 2.1 at 48 Gbps, and HDCP 2.3/1.x. Fifth-generation NVDEC decodes MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1; GA10x is first with AV1 hardware decode, supporting up to 8K60 HDR at low CPU. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding, with quality exceeding x264 Fast and on par with x264 Medium, up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

GA10x Ampere provides up to 2x improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Second-generation RT Core doubles ray/triangle intersection performance, supports motion blur, and concurrent ray tracing and shading/compute. Third-generation Tensor Core implements structural sparsity. It is first GPU to support GDDR6X. GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102, 24GB GDDR6X, 82 SMs, 10,496 CUDA cores, and is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX. RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6. EDR for GDDR6X detects transmission errors via CRC and replays transactions, causing performance plateau during overclocking. RTX A6000 has GA102, 48GB GDDR6, and NVLink for 96GB combined.

Harvey Weinstein has been indicted on rape and criminal sex act charges. Manhattan DA Cyrus Vance Jr. said this brings him closer to accountability. A grand jury voted to indict him on first- and third-degree rape and first-degree criminal sexual act. Weinstein did not testify before the grand jury on his lawyers’ advice.

This work studies quantum learning of nonlinear functions, particularly estimating tr(ρ^{k+1}O) under k-replica protocols. It proves that k-replica protocols require exponentially many samples for certain observables, while (k+1)-replica protocols can estimate the quantity efficiently, yielding a hierarchy of replica quantum advantage. The paper introduces an indistinguishability principle for Haar-assembled ensembles, showing such ensembles are hard to distinguish from their averages without joint measurements. It applies this principle to lower bounds for nonlinear property estimation, spectrum testing, and rank testing, and gives upper bounds showing ⌈(k+1)/2⌉-replica protocols can match the √d dependence. It also discusses related work, future directions, and concurrent work on replica separations.

The forwarded Texas Monthly November 2001 article, “How Enron Blew It,” describes Enron’s transformation from Houston Natural Gas/InterNorth under Ken Lay into a trading company shaped by Jeff Skilling. It recounts Skilling’s Gas Bank, Enron’s expansion into trading and markets, its use of mark-to-market accounting, and a culture valuing aggressive, smart employees, merit bonuses, and high performance. It describes Enron’s growth, dominance in natural gas and electricity, entry into online trading, broadband, and water, and its troubles: falling stock, California energy crisis criticism, the India/Dabhol plant, Azurix, the telecom downturn, accounting questions, executive stock sales, and a CFO-run fund. It discusses internal practices including the Performance Review Committee, known as “rank and yank,” confidentiality, pressure, paranoia, and turnover. It notes Skilling became CEO in February 2001, resigned after six months, and Ken Lay returned, saying Enron would innovate closer to its core and that the PRC could have been applied better. Skilling says most of his net worth was in Enron and discusses future commodity trading.

Vertex Resource Group Ltd. acquired a private company providing hydro-vac services to the Edmonton, Alberta region for $4.3 million. The acquisition adds 11 hydro-vac units, doubles Vertex’s hydro-vac fleet, expands hydro-vac services into Edmonton, and is expected to add approximately $5 million in annual revenue. The speaker addresses the Foreign Service Institute, praising Americans preparing to serve abroad and stating that their task is peace. The passage contrasts diplomacy’s past with the present goal of building a world order in which conflict yields to human yearnings. It describes Europe’s recovery after 1945 through common action, interdependent institutions, and collective security, and focuses on NATO as part of that design. Flash characteristics are specified over the operating free-air temperature range unless noted. Microsoft describes itself as a technology company whose mission is to empower every person and organization. The passage explains that a penalty-kick tiebreaker, or shoot-out, may decide a tied soccer game when a winner is required, often in single-elimination tournaments, with the procedure described in IFAB Law 10 and penalty-kick technical aspects in Law 14; competition rules determine when it is used. It describes teams alternating five penalty kicks from the 12-yard spot, then proceeding to sudden death if still tied, with the first team to score while the other misses winning. It outlines referee coin tosses, eligible players, kick order, goalkeeper rules, and “reduce to equate,” and notes the shoot-out result is recorded as part of the match result but shoot-out goals do not count toward individual statistics. The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card is a no-annual-fee card designed for paying down debt or financing large purchases. It offers 0% intro APR for 21 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, then a 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74% variable APR. Tesla entered an Indemnification Agreement with CEO Elon Musk on June 24, 2020, for a 90-day Bridge Term. Sony’s Xperia XZ Premium will receive Android Oreo later this year, gaining the XZ1 siblings’ camera improvements and 3D Creator app for scanning faces, heads, food, and random objects. The court affirmed dismissal of petitioner’s CPLR article 78 proceeding challenging the Board of Parole’s denial of parole release. Petitioner claimed the Board relied on erroneous criminal history, specifically that he shot an individual in the arm although charges were dismissed. The record showed the information came from the presentence investigation report, petitioner did not refute it when asked, and he never sought to correct the report. Because he did not timely challenge it, he was precluded from arguing the Board could not rely on it. The Board considered statutory factors, and its decision was not irrational.

AGNC Investment, a mortgage REIT with significant agency MBS holdings, may benefit from Fed rate cuts through lower financing costs and higher MBS valuations. It reported a third consecutive quarter of positive NII in Q2'25 and trades at a premium to book value. The author remains bullish, citing strong NII and an attractive monthly dividend.

The speaker addresses Congress, saying profound events require a break with tradition because America’s programs and institutions need reform. He states that peace is the first priority, including ending the war in Vietnam with a just peace, and describes a foreign policy of reduced U.S. involvement and shared responsibility, moving from confrontation to negotiation with the Soviet Union and resumed talks with Communist China. A new swimming robot will investigate damage at Fukushima Dai-Ichi after the 2011 earthquake and tsunami. Andrea Conti’s agent Mario Giuffredi said Conti only wants Milan, his time at Atalanta is over, and Gasperini should not block the transfer; Conti scored eight goals and added four assists in 33 Serie A appearances this season.

Nassim Nicholas Taleb is described as a statistician, mathematician, philosopher, trader, and investor focused on randomness, uncertainty, and probabilities. The lecture examines initial coin offerings (ICOs), a form of crowdfunding in which a startup sells its own crypto token to raise money, often with an expectation of future value. It credits JR Willett with proposing the idea atop Bitcoin in 2010. It traces ICOs from Ethereum’s $18 million offering and the failed DAO raise to the 2017–18 boom, when EOS raised $4.2 billion and Telegram $1.7 billion; roughly $25 billion was raised from June 2017 to June 2018, about 20–30% of worldwide annual venture capital, before falling below $0.5 billion per month. ICOs typically raise proceeds to build a network before it is functional; most are based on an idea, development is often centralized, and many do not publish source code. Tokens are often fungible and transferable, and promoters retain some. Evaluation criteria include token use-case viability, white paper, team, venture capital involvement, community, monetary policy, and token distribution. Accounting treatment is usually deferred or current revenue rather than equity, and US regulation mainly involves the SEC. Q3 2018 statistics show 84% on Ethereum, 57% raising less than $100,000, 76% only an idea, and 1.7% with code; many ICOs failed or were unsuccessful. The lecture concludes ICOs are a new but diminishing form of crowdfunding, with many failures, though blockchain technology may persist.

Trump said the U.S.-Canada trade relationship would only be “tweaked,” but the passage notes a severe imbalance: 18% of U.S. foreign trade goes to Canada, while 76% of Canada’s goes to the U.S. After Trump and Trudeau met, friendly language concealed issues including U.S. grievances over beef, supply management and softwood lumber, and Ambrose warned Trump’s deregulation and low-tax policy could make Canada uncompetitive. The Santa Cruz County Board of Supervisors selected Carlos Palacios, currently assistant county administrative officer and former Watsonville city manager, to replace retiring County Administrative Officer Susan Mauriello. The paper studies ML-definability and ML-separability of modal μ-calculus (µML) formulae over all models, words, binary trees, and d-ary trees for d ≥ 3, along with separator construction and Craig interpolant existence. It reports completeness results: over all models, ML-definability and ML-separability are ExpTime-complete; over words, both are PSpace-complete; over binary trees, both are ExpTime-complete; over d-ary trees with d ≥ 3, ML-definability is ExpTime-complete while ML-separability is 2-ExpTime-complete. Separator constructions are double exponential over all models, single exponential over words, double exponential over binary trees, and triple exponential over d ≥ 3 trees. Interpolants always exist over all models, words, and binary trees, but interpolant existence over d ≥ 3 trees is coNExpTime-complete; consequently ML lacks the Craig interpolation property over trees of outdegree d ≥ 3, and K⊕alt_d enjoys CIP iff d ≤ 2. The paper also treats graded modalities: grML-definability and grML-separability are ExpTime-complete, while ML-definability of graded µML formulae is ExpTime-complete and ML-separability is 2-ExpTime-complete.

The DAWN-plasma study was a randomized, open-label, multicenter phase 2 proof-of-concept trial comparing best supportive care combined with convalescent plasma versus best supportive care only in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Protocol amendments and informed consent documents were approved by Independent Ethics Committees, and the study was conducted per the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP. The primary objective evaluated clinical efficacy and safety, with the primary endpoint being the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints included clinical status, time to sustained improvement, mechanical ventilation or death, venous thromboembolism, transfusion-related side effects, correlation with neutralizing antibody titers, safety, quality of life, adverse events, laboratory data, and vital signs. Participants were randomized 2:1 to convalescent plasma plus standard of care or standard of care alone. Plasma was administered as 800–1000 mL in four doses, with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization. Analyses used a Full Analysis Set and Per Protocol Set. Results showed no difference in the primary endpoint: 83.7% in the convalescent plasma group versus 84.1% in the control group were alive and free of mechanical ventilation at Day 15 (OR 0.99, p=0.976). No statistically significant differences were found for secondary endpoints. Adverse events, fatal adverse events, and serious adverse events were similar between groups. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19/320 intervention patients (6.0%), with no TRALI cases reported. Neutralizing antibody titers increased from baseline to Day 6 but were not influenced by the intervention; better outcome correlated with higher NT50 at Day 0 and Day 6. The study concluded that high-volume convalescent plasma with high neutralizing antibody titers early in hospitalization did not change the natural course.

Ashley Hollis, an A&O Shearman associate, won the reality TV show “Big Brother.” She attributed her victory to hiding her profession by posing as a social media marketing manager and channeling Elle Woods. Hollis said she used attorney skills in her final speech. She plans to give a good chunk of her $750,000 prize to her parents and is considering buying a home.

This bibliometric study analyzed STEAM education with gamification using Scopus, limited to English documents from 2017 to 2023. The final dataset included 34 articles and 155 citations. Publication output began in 2017, grew from 2020 to 2023, and peaked in 2022. The most cited article was by Wannapiroon and Pimdee (2022), with 30 citations. Ceur Workshop Proceedings had the most publications among sources. Nilsook, Wannapiroon, Kummanee, Lee, and Piriyasurawong each had three publications. Leading countries by publications included Thailand, Bulgaria, Italy, and Malaysia; Thailand had six publications and 68 citations. Computer science accounted for 37.7% of papers and social sciences 20.5%. Frequent author keywords included gamification, STEAM, STEAM education, and computational thinking. Germany, Latvia, Norway, and France were most actively engaged in joint research. Factorial analysis grouped topics into three clusters involving educational methodologies and tools, student-centered learning environments, and educational technologies and engagement strategies.

The Tharisa plc Investor Presentation features CEO Phoevos Pouroulis presenting a phased transition from 15 years of open cast mining to underground mining, starting with the west mine as open pit resources deplete. It describes a vision of a fully integrated complex to unlock multigenerational value beyond the open pit, which has coproduced platinum group metals and chrome concentrate and remained profitable over the last 11 years.

The passage presents Santiago and Mattos’s study of a remote emergency dialogic educational activity during the COVID-19 pandemic in a physics teacher education course. The activity used Discord, was inspired by Freire’s critical pedagogy, and was analyzed through Cultural Historical Activity Theory. It involved 19 students discussing school reopening and scientific dissemination, with stages from thematic survey to critical pedagogy and an infographic shared via social media. The authors describe how Discord supported dialogue, student autonomy, self-organization, and agency through text and voice channels and independent group meetings, while noting the context of Brazilian inequality and emergency remote teaching limitations.
In Benghazi, the LNA lost four men and 10 were wounded in December, five months after Khalifa Haftar declared victory; clashes continue in Khreibish amid a broader post-Gaddafi conflict.

The disclosure relates to electronic gaming systems and methods including a stop-based bonus game, such as a wheel or reel having stop positions. The bonus game is associated with first awards, such as jackpot awards, and second awards, such as credit or non-jackpot awards. A trigger event causes selection of a stop position. If a selected stop position is associated with a second award, the second award may be awarded, and that stop position is instead associated with a first award for future play, increasing opportunities to win a first award. In some implementations, a bonus wheel may trigger a secondary jackpot wheel; selecting a stop position on the secondary jackpot wheel associated with a credit prize may award the credit prize and replace it with a jackpot award. The disclosure also describes electronic gaming systems, methods, and articles of manufacture including displays, player input interfaces, credit input mechanisms, processors, and memory, as well as persistence of associations, resetting or reducing first-award stop positions after a first award is won, and constructs including wheels, reels, dice, or grid-based treasure maps.

Fran Horowitz, CEO of Abercrombie & Fitch Co., says the retailer is not chasing “cool” but aiming to be a long-lasting “lifestyle” brand. After taking over in 2017, she shifted from command-and-control management, sought more employee input, raised clothing quality, and avoided chasing trends. A&F’s sales nearly doubled to $2.6 billion between 2019 and 2024, and combined A&F and Hollister sales will top $5 billion this year. To maintain momentum, the company partnered with Macy’s for Abercrombie Kids and became the NFL’s first fashion partner, seeking customer acquisition, brand awareness, and better serving female NFL fans.

The passage reports a study on using generative AI in an undergraduate physics laboratory. It compared three instructional approaches for teaching electric potential and equipotential lines: a traditional physical-equipment lab, a prebuilt digital simulation designed with AI tools, and an AI-engagement lab in which students prompted, validated, and refined an AI-generated simulation.

The study took place in spring 2025 in an introductory physics for life sciences course at a large R1 public university. Students completed conceptual questions immediately after the lab, attitude questions, and later midterm and final exams. Results showed significant differences in immediate conceptual-question performance across lab types, with both the AI-engagement and prebuilt-simulation groups performing significantly better than the traditional physical lab; there was no significant difference between the two simulation groups. No significant differences were found across lab types on midterm or final exam performance. On attitude questions, students using AI and prebuilt simulations reported more positive attitudes than those using physical equipment, while the prebuilt-simulation group showed a significant advantage over the AI group on one question.

The passage concludes that AI-guided simulation development can support conceptual learning comparably to a prebuilt simulation and better than physical equipment immediately after the lab, without compromising later exam performance. It also discusses potential modeling-skill benefits, student frustrations, limitations such as abstraction differences, technical restrictions, and a single concept/sample/institution, and suggests prebuilt simulations, AI-guided development, and physical equipment as complementary pathways.

The Problem Solvers helped veteran Rodney Orton, whose mobility scooter malfunctioned after 15 years. The VA told him a new evaluation appointment was six weeks away, but Travis Guillory contacted the VA. The VA found a locally inventoried scooter matching his medical needs and delivered it to his hospital room the next morning. Diana Kinion said this was rare and most orders are delivered within a few weeks. Orton and his Chihuahua, Pita, now have a new scooter.

This document is an AMD Geode™ CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update. It lists numbered issues with descriptions, implications, and resolutions, covering DMA, PIT/PIC, PMC sleep clock, GLIU, UART access, LPC, PCI, UDMA/ATAC/IDE, ACPI/PMC register accesses, KEL, SMBus, GPIO, USB clock gating, wake events, RTC CMOS, timing, and standby/power states. Resolutions include avoiding certain modes, registers, or access types; using alternate procedures; or disabling features.
Some dogs can be irresistibly drawn to toys in ways that may parallel human behavioral addictions.

A Stanford University Department of Psychology study examined whether descriptive vegetable labels would encourage college students to eat more vegetables. Same-prepared dishes were labeled as great-tasting, basic, healthy-positive, or healthy-restrictive. Among nearly 28,000 students, the great-tasting label led diners to choose 25 percent more vegetables than the basic label, 35 percent more than the healthy-positive label, and 41 percent more than the healthy-restrictive label; students also piled more produce on their plates. The passage notes that taste drives food choices and suggests using taste-focused labels at home, followed by recipes for vegetable dishes.

NASA shared a Hubble image of the Tarantula Nebula, also called 30 Doradus, named for spindly gas filaments. It also shows the Honeycomb Nebula, whose bubble-like shape may involve supernova interactions and viewing angle, per 2010 research.

The lecture examines electroweak unification by combining weak and electromagnetic interactions. It notes differing interaction strengths, mitigated by heavy gauge bosons, and differing coupling structures: QED vector coupling versus weak vector-axial coupling. The 1−γ5 term is treated as a projection defining left-handed spinors. Using isospin concepts, neutrino and electron are written as a doublet, and charged and neutral weak currents are expressed with τ matrices. The Gell-Mann–Nishijima relation defines hypercharge, yielding a current that also includes right-handed particles. The theory uses an isospin triplet W1, W2, W3 and a singlet B. W+ and W− are combinations of W1 and W2; photon and Z arise from mixing the third triplet component and B via the weak mixing angle. Coupling relations yield a consistent W+, W−, photon, and Z picture.

The President reports to Congress that the nation has continued to grow in strength, comfort, knowledge, education, moral and spiritual forces, and peace. He discusses foreign relations, including the Kellogg-Briand pact, adherence to the International Court of Justice, a London naval conference, mediation in Latin America, and marines in Nicaragua, Haiti, and China. He reports the Army and Navy are efficient but defense expenditures are rising, and recommends economy. He states government finances are sound, the public debt has been reduced, surpluses are expected, and recommends tax reduction; he also discusses foreign debt settlements. This cross-sectional study described plasma AD biomarkers in Amish participants from CAAMP. No significant differences were found in plasma amyloid biomarkers between diagnostic groups, but AD individuals had higher p-tau181 and lower Aβ42/p-tau181 than cognitively unimpaired individuals. p-tau181 was associated with AD among APOE ε4 carriers, and p-tau181 and Aβ42/p-tau181 were associated with cognitive preservation in sensitivity analyses. Clustering using Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau181 identified subgroups with differing AD-risk profiles. Limitations included the small, nonrepresentative Amish sample, lack of imaging/CSF data, and cross-sectional design.

The Triangle Rotation offense attacks the triangle zone of a Triangle & Two defense using three-player clockwise and counterclockwise rotations. Options include point guard dribble penetration to an elbow, O4 popping to the opposite elbow, a baseline cut to O5, a lob to O1, and side screens involving O5, O4, and O1. Two government studies exposing rats and mice to cellphone radiation found a weak link to some heart tumors. The rat study showed a small increase in an unusual heart tumor in male rats, but no significant problems in female rats or in mice, and no hard evidence on brain tumors. Officials and scientists said the findings do not change their view that cellphones are safe, noting the animals received radiation levels much higher than typical use. The FDA said current safety limits are acceptable. Previous human studies found little evidence of cancer risk, though critics remain concerned and IARC listed cellphones as possibly carcinogenic. California issued guidance to reduce exposure if worried.

This study reviews ChatGPT’s development and its use in education, focusing on evaluating the accuracy and validity of its responses. ChatGPT, developed by OpenAI, evolved from GPT-1 in June 2018 to GPT-4 in March 2023. In education, scholars report potential benefits such as personalized learning, feedback, assessment support, collaboration, engagement, and skill development, but also concerns about plagiarism, cheating, bias, accuracy, reliability, and effects on higher-order thinking. Using a PRISMA-guided systematic review, the author searched Web of Science, EBSCOhost, and Google Scholar for peer-reviewed empirical English studies, selecting 18 studies across fields including medicine, writing, business, finance, chemistry, academic advising, physics, social science, and coding. Results indicate ChatGPT can generate coherent, structured, and sometimes creative text and can pass many undergraduate exams, but it struggles with complex scientific and calculation problems, lacks depth, argumentation, judgment, and higher-order thinking, can give false or hallucinated information confidently, and does not guarantee repeated answers. The author recommends validating ChatGPT content, carefully structuring prompts, redesigning assessments, developing guidelines and policies, guiding students, and using an ABCD framework. Limitations include database/search date restrictions and inclusion of only empirical peer-reviewed studies. Future research should examine AI effects on learning and innovative evaluation frameworks.

This study assessed pregnant women’s awareness of and attitudes toward labor epidural analgesia (LEA) and factors influencing their decision to consider it at Hemen Medical Center in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. An institution-based cross-sectional study included 267 third-trimester pregnant women, with 230 analyzed. Among participants, 78% had heard of LEA, most commonly from previous users, family/friends, and the internet; only 6.5% cited healthcare providers, and 34% received explanations from providers during ANC. While 47% believed LEA was effective for labor pain, only 14.3% were willing to consider it; 47.8% had no plan and 37.8% were undecided. Concerns included maternal side effects, baby’s safety, interference with natural labor, and cost. Education level, family income, perceived fetal problems, and perceived pain-relief effectiveness were significantly associated with the decision to receive LEA. The study concludes that awareness is relatively high but hesitancy remains, and antenatal education/counseling is needed.

A King’s College London analysis of 49 studies involving 266,939 people found that higher physical activity was linked to lower odds of future depression in children, adults, and older adults. Researchers hope to study different activity types and dosages and call for policy changes to promote exercise.

Four Down is primarily for taking the last shot in a period but can also be an effective spread offense for a team with a talented ballhandler. It is called by the ballhandler raising his hand and pointing four fingers downward, and is sometimes called “Four Low” or “Four Flat.” The four non-ball handlers align along the baseline, with the best shooters in the corners, creating space for the ballhandler to operate one-on-one. Primary reads include driving or pulling up for a jumper; posts crash the boards, while corners spot up for threes and defensive balance. Help from a baseline defender allows a drop pass to the open post; help from a wing defender allows a kick out for three. If no shot is taken, the ball returns to the ballhandler and the action continues. Pressure release has corners pop out; the corner may return the ball or take over isolation while the original ballhandler moves to the corner. Specials include Mid Screen, Triple Base Screen, and Misdirection Double.

The 2-3 zone is the most commonly used zone defense. It keeps big players inside, protects the basket and against dribble penetration, and is effective against poor outside shooting teams, but vulnerable to good outside shooters. It is often used when teams lack quickness, athleticism, and skill, but with quick, agile players it can be aggressive and trapping. It also defends talented or big low-post players. Defensive guards play side by side above the free throw line, the post stays between the ball and basket, and baseline players are outside the three-second area above the blocks, with active arms and hands. The passage covers basic shifts for ball in the middle, wings, and corners; wing corner shift options; defending ball reversal and skip passes; a 1-1-3 variation with middle shift and tandem options; advanced trap options including corner, point, and automatic wing traps; and defending a “Footer” by adjusting to double and triple team a low-post player.

Community Board 7 sought an article 78 proceeding to compel disclosure under FOIL of documents related to the proposed Trump City project after the Planning Department denied its request. The Court of Appeals held that the community board lacked capacity to maintain the proceeding, reversing the lower courts. Although it found the issue not moot, the Court distinguished standing from capacity and stated that a legislatively created entity has no inherent right to sue; capacity must derive from enabling legislation or necessary implication absent clear legislative intent to the contrary. The Court concluded that the board’s advisory role, the absence of express authorization to sue, the lack of subpoena power or independent counsel, the specific ULURP document provisions, and the Charter’s legislative history indicated no intent to authorize community board suits for document disclosure. FOIL’s standing provisions did not supply capacity, so the petition should have been dismissed.

The passage reports a study of the spatiotemporal evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Alpha and Delta variants in Vietnam in 2021. Vietnam reported 1,465 PCR-confirmed infections and 35 deaths in 2020 after early border/travel restrictions, contact tracing, mass testing, quarantine, and public communication. Importations of Alpha and then Delta led to a nationwide outbreak, with over 1.7 million infections and 32,000 deaths by the end of 2021. Of 1,303 sequenced genomes, 1,222 (93.8%) were Delta, 74 (5.7%) Alpha, 5 A.23.1, and 2 B.1.637; no recombinants were detected, and 99.2% of Delta sequences were AY.57. Alpha sequences clustered into four major groups, suggesting multiple introductions between January and May 2021 without sustained community transmission. AY.57 was first introduced into the Northeast region in early 2021, with estimated tMRCA March 14, 2021; the Northeast and Red River delta seeded other regions, especially the Southeast, which later seeded the north and rest of Vietnam. Viral dispersal between provinces/cities was not frequent. Genetic diversity increased sharply between April and August 2021, then remained relatively stable with a slight decrease in late November. Mean dN/dS for polyprotein coding sequences was 0.86, and the estimated evolutionary rate of AY.57 coding sequences was 5.29×10−4 substitutions per site per year. The authors conclude that rigorous measures contained Alpha, while AY.57 introduction into an immunologically naïve population resulted in an explosive outbreak, and that genomic surveillance is critical for pandemic response.

This systematic review examined marijuana/cannabis and cannabinoid use and alterations in the microbiome. It describes cannabis constituents, cannabinoid effects on immune and gastrointestinal systems, and the gut-brain axis. The review was registered on PROSPERO and searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane up to July 20, 2022, including English-language human studies and excluding animal, in vitro, and non-peer-reviewed studies. Nine studies were included: one case-control, six cohort studies, and two clinical trials, with 2,526 participants from 1983 to 2021 across the USA, Iran, Israel, and the UK. Patients’ mean age was 56.5 years versus 28.4 years for controls; women made up over 85%. Patients most commonly had cognitive impairment (76.6%) or HIV (11.1%). Risk of bias was assessed using NOS and ROBINS-I, with some studies showing high risk due to lack of blinding, follow-up descriptions, or selection/exposure reporting. Qualitative analysis linked marijuana or endocannabinoid supplements to microbiota changes in HIV, inflammation, obesity, cognitive deficits, oral conditions, and pain. Reported adverse events included coughing, wheezing, drowsiness, night sweats, systemic aspergillosis, and coughing bouts. A meta-analysis could not be conducted because of limited data across varied pathological conditions.

Chinese textile firms are increasingly using North Korean factories for cheaper labour, traders in Dandong said. Clothes made in North Korea are labelled "Made in China" and exported globally. UN sanctions do not ban textile exports. Textiles were North Korea's second-biggest export in 2016 at $752 million. Chinese suppliers send fabrics and raw materials to North Korean factories, where garments are assembled and exported. Traders said manufacturers can save up to 75 percent; North Korean factories are state-owned and often fully booked; workers produce 30 percent more clothes daily and are paid less than Chinese workers. Chinese companies also employ North Korean workers in China, with much of their wages remitted to the North Korean state. New UN sanctions ban increasing North Korean labourers abroad and have completely banned coal exports.

The study develops a mathematical model to evaluate a screening-isolation strategy for controlling infectious diseases in a semi-isolated community when medications and vaccinations are unavailable. It uses a simplified compartmental model and computer simulations with Poisson-distributed daily changes. Theoretical analysis indicates disease control depends on screening time lag and transmission parameters, while improved screening efficiency has only a weak contribution to robustness. Simulations show that with R0=3.0 infection is uncontrolled without screening but controlled by daily screening at efficiency 0.9; R0=6.0 remains controlled, while R0=8.0 is not. Screening once per 3 days controls infection, once per week is worse, and once per 2 weeks is out of control. Higher screening efficiency reduces cumulative infections. Increased influx raises infection size, indicating strict border control is necessary. The study concludes regular periodic screening can help control epidemic transmission in semi-isolated communities without vaccines and medications, with screening frequency, efficiency, and migration rate affecting infection size.

The manuscript reports exact-diagonalization evidence for an intervalley superconducting phase proximate to the non-Abelian fractional spin Hall insulator in the half-filled second moiré bands of approximately 2°-twisted bilayer MoTe2. The superconducting state emerges when the short-range intervalley interaction is screened, exhibits time-reversal symmetry and extended nodal s-wave pairing, is continuously connected to the fractional spin Hall insulator, and is described by an effective field theory. Over-the-counter (OTC) trading involves financial instruments traded directly between two parties without a centralized exchange, often electronically through dealer networks. OTC markets are decentralized, less transparent, less regulated, and may use customized contracts. Instruments include stocks, debt securities, derivatives, commodities, ETFs, and ADRs. OTC stocks are often small companies unable to meet exchange listing requirements, though some large foreign ADRs trade OTC. Risks include counterparty risk, manipulation, fraud, limited information, lower liquidity, and slippage. The passage states OTC stocks as a group have negative returns, many penny stocks fail, and studies cited report average and median losses. OTC markets can help companies raise capital and provide liquidity, and OTC derivatives allow customized risk exposure. Crypto mostly trades on exchanges, but OTC desks handle large off-market deals. The passage concludes OTC stocks are generally not recommended for long-term investment, and short-term or day trading them is also risky.

"Brainsaver" classes are part of a 12-week OptumCare course focusing on brain-healthy activities like physical exercise, stress reduction, cognitive exercises, education, socialization, and foods for the brain. Offered at three Valley locations, the classes are believed to help keep Alzheimer's Disease at bay and include students from their mid-50s to late 80s.

A federal shutdown appeared more likely after top Democrats and Republicans met with President Trump at the White House. Vice President JD Vance said, “We’re headed to a shutdown because the Democrats won’t do the right thing,” while Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said there were “very large differences” but that Trump heard Democrats’ objections. Republicans want a stopgap bill to maintain funding at current levels until late November. Democrats demand that it include funding and protection for key measures, especially an extension of enhanced Obamacare tax credits. Both sides blame the other for a possible shutdown, and dueling short-term funding bills failed earlier in the Senate.

Moina Shaiq placed a newspaper ad offering “Questions and answers about being Muslim” and started “Meet a Muslim” after about 100 people attended her first coffee-house event in Fremont, California. She has since spoken about Islam at libraries, pizza parlors, coffee shops, churches, service clubs and private homes, and traveled to Arizona and Atlanta, addressing topics such as hijab, niqab, Sunni-Shia differences, women’s rights and American Muslim life. Similar programs emerged after 9/11 and have resurged amid anti-Muslim incidents. Shaiq has faced threats, including one in Atlanta. Muslim leaders call such initiatives important amid heightened fear and xenophobia, while critics question their effectiveness and favor policy change. Shaiq says her program shares love, compassion and peace and educates Americans that Muslims are human.

The disclosure relates to a wireless communication system and proposes transmitting/receiving a sounding reference signal (SRS), including setting and/or indicating a guard period for SRS transmission/reception, particularly considering SRS and other uplink transmission such as PUCCH or PUSCH. A UE receives SRS configuration information including SRS resources and usage and performs SRS transmission using the resources; a guard period related to the SRS resources is configured, and when the guard period overlaps a specific uplink channel, the priority between the guard period and the specific uplink channel is the same as between the SRS and the specific uplink channel. The guard period may be configured for antenna switching, may be based on configured subcarrier spacing, may have one or two symbols, may be configured per SRS resource set via higher layer signaling, and may include a starting position index, number of symbols, and/or whether it is configured between SRS and adjacent uplink transmission. When no guard period is configured, the UE may use the same transmission beam before and after the guard period, indicated by an SRI and/or TPMI. The disclosure also addresses collision between the guard period and SRS resource sets, including priority, dropping, shifting, and reconfiguration.
Tensor Cores perform deep learning matrix operations. Turing Tensor Cores accelerate neural network training and inferencing, add INT8/INT4 modes, and power DLSS on GeForce and Quadro systems.

After failing to attend court while on bail, he hid in Litherland for eight days before being arrested. He admitted breaching bail and received an additional 10 days. The child, now 22 months old and in foster care, requires lifelong support.

Coach Quenneville describes a consistent coaching approach with accountability, communication, and commitment to daily improvement. He discusses the Blackhawks' goaltending situation, including changes between Corey Crawford and Scott Darling, and says the competition was based on Darling's play and Crawford remaining solid. Cover 0 is a man-to-man defense with zero safeties over the top. Every non-defensive lineman, and sometimes linemen, either covers an offensive player man-to-man or applies pressure by stunting or blitzing. Its purpose is to bring maximum blitz pressure while covering all eligible receivers, often by adding up to six players to the line of scrimmage. Strengths include simple assignments, easy adjustment to motion, effectiveness against the run, RPOs, short and long routes, and screens. It can also be disguised pre-snap. Weaknesses include high risk because coverage players have no help, vulnerability to big plays, draw plays, quarterback scrambles, and pick plays. The middle of the field is open. General rules assign defensive backs and linebackers to specific receivers, with linebackers blitzing. Variations include Cover 0 “Rat,” which rushes five and leaves one free player to cut crossing routes and watch the quarterback, and dropping a hybrid defensive lineman into coverage. Al Davis forbade Raiders defensive coordinators from running Cover 0.

Astronomers report that Oumuamua, the first confirmed interstellar object in our solar system, probably originated in a binary star system, likely ejected as planets formed. Discovered in October by a Hawaiian observatory, the red-tinged asteroid is about 1,300 feet long, moving away at over 16 miles per second, and may be tumbling after a collision. Researchers suggest binary star systems may be the source of most interstellar objects.

The passage discusses holistic education in the Indian higher education context, tracing education’s Latin roots and Indian sages-thinkers’ emphasis on integrated development. It contrasts contemporary materialist education with holistic approaches and examines modern policies including India’s NEP 2020 and UN SDG 4.7. The study used a literature review and a PRISMA-guided systematic review of eight original articles from Scopus and Semantic Scholar, limited to English articles published before 2021. The review found support for the four LIBRE/EMC2 dimensions—empathy, mindfulness, compassion, and critical inquiry—as core holistic education dimensions aligned with Indian philosophical traditions and contemporary policy goals. It concludes that these dimensions can support culturally grounded assessment and curriculum development, while noting limitations such as reliance on two databases and exclusion of the Holistic Education Review journal, and calls for expanded database coverage and culturally sensitive measurement tools.

President Woodrow Wilson proclaims that a state of war exists between the United States and the Imperial German Government, directs civil and military officers to act with vigilance, and appeals to citizens to uphold the laws and support war measures. It applies to all land and water under United States jurisdiction.

The passage covers NVIDIA graphics technologies and Blackwell architecture. Ray Reconstruction uses AI to generate additional pixels in ray-traced scenes, replacing hand-tuned denoisers with a supercomputer-trained AI network; its transformer model improves quality in challenging lighting and reduces common denoiser artifacts. DLAA uses DLSS Super Resolution technology to create a higher-quality native-resolution image with increased temporal stability and detail in motion. It then outlines shader evolution from fixed-function pipelines through vertex, pixel, geometry, tessellation, compute, primitive/mesh, and RTX shaders to Blackwell neural shaders. Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan allows Tensor Cores to be accessed through shaders, enabling neural texture compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Neural shaders approximate complex light interaction, decompress supercompressed textures, predict indirect lighting, and approximate subsurface scattering. Specific technologies include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Stochastic Texture Filtering, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Blackwell GPUs include GB202, GB203, and GB205, with specifications for RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070 compared with prior generations. The passage also includes NVIDIA legal disclaimers and trademark information.

In JUAN ARCHIBEQUE v. JOSE MARIA MIERA, the court held that under the organic act only the supreme court has appellate powers and the legislature cannot confer strictly appellate or revisory jurisdiction on district courts. An appeal from a justice of the peace is tried de novo in district court as an original action; the transcript serves only to show that the case originated, was tried, and was appealed, and errors in it do not require dismissal. The jury weighs testimony and discrepancies. A new trial for a verdict against evidence is discretionary and should be denied unless the verdict is clearly against the weight of evidence. The district court’s judgment for Miera was affirmed because no clear preponderance of testimony appeared against the verdict.

Evidence before this study indicated that sleep disturbance and anxiety are linked to depressive symptoms, but prior studies mainly used conventional group comparisons in single cohorts. This study applied machine learning in the HCP-Young dataset and validated findings in HCP-Aging and eNKI cohorts, including longitudinal eNKI data, using sleep quality, anxiety, depressive symptom severity, and brain measures. Poor sleep quality robustly predicted depressive symptoms across three cohorts; adding anxiety improved prediction and mediated the sleep–depressive symptom link. Brain structure and function did not play an important role. The reverse direction was less robust. Longitudinal data showed future depressive symptom severity was predictable from sleep and anxiety, and neurofeedback influenced prediction. The authors conclude that identifying poor sleep and anxiety is critical to reduce depressive symptom burden and design better individual-level therapeutic approaches.

The passage states the U.S. suffered major strategic blows in Iran and Nicaragua, where the Carter administration failed to prevent and collaborated in replacing friendly moderate autocrats with less friendly extremist ones. It says outcomes remain uncertain but may worsen; both revolutionary leaders show intolerance and arrogance and reject power sharing or constitutional government. It notes no serious attention to the U.S. role in these developments despite warnings of similar situations elsewhere. It calls for a morally and strategically acceptable, politically realistic policy toward non-democratic governments threatened by Soviet-sponsored subversion, warning that otherwise the same reflexes will guide U.S. actions from Korea to Mexico. Kirkpatrick describes Carter officials’ assumptions as favoring the progressive side in rightist-autocracy versus leftist-challenge conflicts, being willing to destabilize friendly or neutral autocracies without assurance about replacements, and failing from lack of realism about traditional versus revolutionary autocracies. She argues traditional authoritarian governments are less repressive, more susceptible to liberalization, and more compatible with U.S. interests than revolutionary autocracies, citing Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, China, Taiwan, North Korea, and South Korea, and says traditional autocrats tolerate existing inequities while revolutionary autocracies create them.

The Base Cross Offense is a basketball offense that uses a small player setting a baseline screen for a big player to create mismatches and post-up opportunities. The point guard O1 initiates with an entry pass to wing O3 and a give-and-go cut; if not open, O1 sets a baseline screen for O5. Variations include Pass Entry, Dribble Clear Entry, UCLA High Post Rub Entry, and Hawk Entry. The offense emphasizes execution of the baseline screen, with reads and counters for defenders trailing, playing low or high, switching, showing and recovering, or fronting the post, including back cuts, go over/under, screen and pop, slips, lobs, and ball reversal. It also covers posting up strong, low post moves, two-person game, post splits, ball reversal options, weakside down screens, mid/side screens, reversal pass denial, teaching and implementation, drills, game strategies, and preparing to defend the offense.

The Patient Charter, also called the NHS Constitution, sets out patients’ legal rights, NHS pledges, and responsibilities. It says healthcare should be available to everyone, free at the point of use, based on need, with exceptions such as prescriptions in England, dentistry, and eye care. Rights include equal access, waiting time standards and alternatives or explanations if standards slip, safe and regulated care, clean settings, food and hydration, continuous improvement, access to NICE-recommended medicines and treatments if a doctor agrees, fair local decisions, vaccinations, consent, clear risk information, privacy, GP choice, involvement in decisions, openness when something goes wrong, complaints, Ombudsman escalation, judicial review, and compensation for negligence. Responsibilities include looking after one’s health, respecting NHS staff and other patients, following or discussing treatment plans, and taking part in vaccination and screening programmes. The Charter is described as empowerment, NHS commitments beyond the legal minimum, and a partnership amid NHS pressures.

A study of the nocebo effect found people reported stronger side effects when a treatment appeared more expensive. Volunteers given fake creams for itchy skin were told the creams could increase pain sensitivity. The expensive-looking cream increased reported pain by nearly 30%, versus about 3% for the generic-looking cream compared with a control. Brain imaging showed activity differences in the prefrontal cortex and periaqueductal gray. The finding may help clinicians discuss medications and minimize the nocebo effect.

In Pacific Gamble Robinson Co. v. Lapp, a creditor sued on a promissory note executed in Colorado by Conrad Lapp and Joslyn Fruit Company; the Lapps later moved to Washington. The Washington Supreme Court applied the most significant relationship test, concluded Colorado law governed, and held that property subject to the debt in Colorado—including Mr. Lapp’s wages and acquisitions, though characterized as community property in Washington—was likewise subject to the debt in Washington. It reversed the Court of Appeals. The dissent argued that while Colorado law governed contract validity, Washington law should determine whether Washington community property could be reached, and under Washington law the community was not liable for Mr. Lapp’s noncommunity debt.

Cryptocurrency trading is the exchange of digital assets such as Bitcoin or Ethereum for profit or speculation. It uses varied strategies, including day trading, whale watching, swing, dark pool, trend following, range, fork, breakout, mean reversion, arbitrage, grid, sentiment and social-media sentiment, Genesis block, technical analysis, zombie coin, Proof of Stake, quantum, Ichimoku cloud, and NFT trading. Cryptocurrencies differ from stocks in being purely digital, decentralized, and identity-concealing. Prices are influenced by demand, investor sentiment, regulatory developments, technological advancements, and macroeconomic trends. Fees vary by platform. Risks include volatility, scams, cybercrime, exchange insolvencies, blockchain complexity, lost private keys, and lack of centralized regulation. Hard forks can cause volatility, uncertainty, and new coins. Halving can reduce new coin creation, increase scarcity, and potentially raise prices. USDT offers a stablecoin for hedging and moving funds but carries peg risk. DeFi can enable peer-to-peer trading and lower transaction costs. The best strategy depends on investment goals and risk tolerance; HODL or dollar-cost averaging may suit long-term value, while day trading can be profitable but high-risk. Backtesting is recommended.

This paper addresses model misspecification in simulation-based inference (SBI), where a simulator’s likelihood differs from the real data likelihood and can cause biased or overconfident posterior estimates. It proposes Flow Matching for Corrected Posterior Estimation (FMCPE), which uses abundant simulations, a pretrained neural posterior estimator, and scarce high-fidelity calibration pairs. FMCPE combines flow matching steps: a transport map TX couples real observations with simulator-domain counterparts, and a transport map TΘ moves samples from a qX|Y-weighted simulation-based posterior toward the corrected posterior. The vector fields are trained jointly, with a simulation-informed source distribution updated during training and gradients stopped through the intermediate sample. FMCPE is described as agnostic to misspecification type, amortized, computationally efficient, and applicable as post-processing to SBI models. Experiments on Gaussian, Pendulum, WindTunnel, and LightTunnel tasks compare FMCPE with NPE and MF-NPE using jC2ST, Wasserstein distance, and MSE; FMCPE consistently outperforms baselines, especially at small calibration sizes.

DS-STAR is introduced as a data science agent that generates solution code through iterative planning and verification. Data science workflows are complex and time-consuming, and existing LLM-based agents mainly focus on well-structured data, neglect heterogeneous formats, and lack robust verification because executable code does not always guarantee correct answers. DS-STAR addresses these limitations by analyzing all files in a directory to produce textual summaries of their structure and content, then entering a loop of planning, implementation, and verification. An LLM-based judge evaluates whether the current plan is sufficient; if not, DS-STAR refines the plan by adding or modifying steps, operating sequentially until a satisfactory plan is verified or a maximum number of iterations is reached. Additional modules include a debugging agent and a retriever. Evaluations on DABStep, KramaBench, and DA-Code show DS-STAR outperforms state-of-the-art methods, improving accuracy from 41.0% to 45.2%, 39.8% to 44.7%, and 37.0% to 38.5%, respectively. Ablation studies indicate the analyzer and router agents are critical. The conclusion states DS-STAR autonomously solves data science problems and suggests extending it to human-in-the-loop settings.

Sell the rip is a strategy of selling an asset when its price is considered overvalued, either closing a long position or opening a short position. It follows “buy low, sell high” and mean reversion, and is used by short-term traders. It can target weak, overpriced stocks but is not considered good for strong fundamentals or long-term investing. It is similar to selling the rally, though “rip” refers to an overpriced or overvalued market. Indicators include oscillating and momentum indicators, moving averages, and Bollinger Bands. A backtest on SPY using RSI produced 391 trades, 0.61% average gain, 75% win rate, and 1.6 profit factor, but large and long drawdowns. Changed sell criteria improved the equity curve and reduced drawdowns, with 0.48% average gain and more trades. The strategy has been profitable in the S&P 500 over three decades, less before the 1990s and less in commodity or trend-following markets. Backtest code is offered.

Sietsema is a Greek Orthodox priest, former linguistics professor, and former Merriam-Webster pronunciation editor. The passage argues that AI and personalized learning require greater student autonomy, but the prescribed curriculum remains central to schooling and limits student control. Although education has changed in curriculum, pedagogy, assessment, technology, and skills, the “grammar of schooling” has not changed; students have little say over what, how, with whom, and where to learn. Curriculum is described as the anchor connecting educational elements and carrying societal needs, and its prescription has been strengthened over 200 years. Using panarchy theory, the passage analyzes education as nested systems with adaptive cycles of growth, conservation, release, and reorganization, along with resilience, adaptability, and transformability. It proposes a balanced curriculum dividing control between prescribed content and student autonomy, with balance determined by age, experience, ability, and support. It categorizes innovations as tiny, small, large, and transformational, and argues transformative change is resisted. It suggests starting new subsystems within schools, as in the ICEE program in Chongqing/Hongfan and Australian examples such as Studio School and ScotsX, to allow personalized, product-oriented, AI-supported learning and eventually influence the larger system. It concludes transformation must start small around an anchor factor and expand through layers.
