He notes constant learning in playoff hockey, that this group earned its way through good and tough times, and that while hockey is a business, they enjoy playing in June. Both teams are hungry, and the next game is big.

The passage details ADS868xW device configuration and read protocols, including legacy SPI-compatible protocols (SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, SPI-11-S), selection through SDI_MODE[1:0] and SDO_MODE[1:0], dual SDO-x operation, and source-synchronous protocols with configurable output clock source and bus width. It maps nine configuration registers: DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG, SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, ALARM_REG, ALARM_H_TH_REG, and ALARM_L_TH_REG. Application information describes the ADS868xW as a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated AFE and precision reference for industrial analog input modules, alarm/thermistor use, power supply decoupling, NAP and power-down modes, PCB layout guidance, related documentation, support resources, trademarks, ESD caution, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

On August 28, 2017, Amazon.com, Inc. completed its acquisition of Whole Foods Market, Inc. through a merger in which Whole Foods Market became a wholly owned subsidiary. Each outstanding Whole Foods Market share was converted into the right to receive $42.00 in cash, without interest, subject to the exceptions described in the passage. Outstanding equity awards were converted or canceled as described. Aggregate consideration was approximately $13.55 billion, financed with net proceeds from previously disclosed debt financing. Amazon.com intends to file required Whole Foods Market financial statements and pro forma financial information as an amendment within 71 days. The Merger Agreement is incorporated by reference as Exhibit 2.1.

The Martingale trading strategy involves adding a larger trade size—typically doubling—after a losing trade, hoping the market reverses so one win recovers losses plus a profit equal to the initial bet. It originated in gambling and is based on 50% probability outcomes. The passage says it is risk-seeking, contrasts with anti-Martingale, double-down, and averaging down, and relies on mean reversion. It requires an infinite supply of money to work, has a high theoretical win rate but can produce large losses or total loss during long losing streaks. It may be dangerous in stocks because stocks can fall to zero; long-only use with broad market index ETFs is suggested as less risky. A simple SPY benchmark backtest had 409 trades, 0.64% average gain, 8.68% annual returns, and 23% maximum drawdown; a modified Martingale version did not look good. The passage does not recommend Martingale for trading.

A New York Times survey found dozens of federal judges expressing concern about the U.S. Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions in cases related to President Donald Trump since his second term. Of 65 judges, 12 said the court used the docket appropriately and 12 said lower-court judges had sufficient guidance, while 47 and 48 disagreed. Of 54, two said the docket improved public perception of the judiciary. Some anonymously described the orders as “mystical,” “overly blunt,” “incredibly demoralizing” and “a slap in the face to the district courts.” One Trump appointee said the orders were “flushing out anti-democratic rulings.” The article says the litigation has created strains in the federal judicial system, that at least seven of about 20 emergency orders lacked reasoning, and that nearly all benefited Trump. It also notes the Times acknowledged respondents may not be representative and that the Volokh Conspiracy published a critique of the survey.

This article examines whether dance education can be integrated with social studies education in US elementary and secondary education. It states that formal educational measurement excludes arts education and focuses on reading, mathematics, and science, while social studies is not tested in PISA and only tangentially in the US. The article reviews literature and reports a Qualtrics survey of 91 US dance education graduates. Survey questions used NCSS social studies concepts. Results show concepts such as people, places, and environments (94% yes) and individual development and identity (97% yes) were most frequently included; culture, time/continuity/change, individuals/groups/institutions, and global connections also appeared. Less attention was paid to power/authority/governance, science/technology/society, and civic ideals/practices. Responses ranged from literal to implied interpretations. Limitations include IRB restrictions, a US-only pool, a small non-generalizable sample, and mostly yes/no questions. The article suggests policy and curriculum changes, professional development, and cites the UNESCO Framework for Culture and Arts Education.

A Colorado panel voted first-in-the-nation to limit what health plans in the state pay for Amgen’s arthritis drug Enbrel. The Colorado Prescription Drug Affordability Board set a payment ceiling for government agencies and commercial plans covering state residents. The limit is $600 per unit—the Medicare maximum fair price effective in January—about $30,350 yearly per person, versus roughly $53,000 paid by the average state insurance plan in 2023.

Turkey will extend state of emergency by three months from April 19, citing terror threats against FETO. It was declared July 20, 2016, after failed July 15 coup blamed on Fethullah Gulen; it has lasted nine months, allowing bypass of parliament and limits on rights.

The passage presents NFL headlines and reports that Miami beat the Jets on Monday Night Football for its first win of the season, but Dolphins receiver Tyreek Hill suffered a feared dislocated left knee, was carted off and hospitalized, and is expected to miss the remainder of the season. Miami got two touchdown catches from Darren Waller, while the Jets committed three turnovers and 12 penalties, and Aaron Glenn started his Jets career 0-4.

A new paper proposes searching for alien artifacts rather than synchronized signals. Hector Socas-Navarro suggests looking for artificial satellites around distant planets, especially geostationary satellites. Advanced alien societies might have billions or trillions of such satellites. When a planet transits its star, the satellites could cause slight dimming before and after the planet’s dimming, especially if seen edge-on. This method avoids synchronicity, may detect artifacts that outlast their makers, requires no new telescopes or experiments, and could use existing exoplanet data. Its chances may be small, but it is easy to try.

China reduced the US dollar’s weight in its trade-weighted foreign-exchange basket from 26.4% to 22.4% and expanded the basket from 13 to 24 currencies starting in 2017, the first weighting adjustment since the basket was published in December 2015. The move aims to redirect market attention from yuan-dollar parity; the yuan lost about 7% against the dollar in 2016, its largest annual loss since 1994. The change comes before Donald Trump takes office, while Chinese officials say the dollar is strong rather than the yuan weak.

IMI plc received a consensus “Hold” rating from eighteen covering research firms, with two sell, twelve hold, and four buy ratings. The average 12-month target price is GBX 1,027.29 ($12.84). Recent reports included BNP Paribas raising its target to GBX 1,400 with an “outperform” rating, while Goldman Sachs, Credit Suisse, and J P Morgan Chase reaffirmed “neutral” ratings and Barclays reaffirmed “overweight.” The stock opened at 1216.00 on Thursday, with a market capitalization of GBX 3.29 billion and a 52-week range of GBX 751.00 to GBX 1,223.00.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated July 28, 2022, reporting that on July 28, 2022 it issued a press release regarding financial results for its third fiscal quarter ended June 25, 2022. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1; the filing lists registered securities and is signed by CFO Luca Maestri.

The lecture concludes the discussion of conjugate gradients and reviews Arnoldi. Arnoldi produces an orthogonal basis for the Krylov subspace and a matrix H; for symmetric A, H is symmetric tridiagonal. This is described as a good way to find low eigenvalues of large matrices by using a submatrix whose eigenvalues are called Ritz values. Conjugate gradients applies to symmetric positive definite A. It uses orthogonal residuals and conjugate directions, where conjugate means orthogonal in the A inner product. The method determines x_k in the Krylov space, uses a short recurrence with alpha and beta, and each cycle requires one multiplication by A, two inner products, and a few vector updates. The lecture gives a convergence estimate involving lambda max, lambda min, and the condition number. It connects conjugate gradients to minimizing the quadratic energy 1/2 x^T A x - b^T x, whose gradient is Ax - b, and contrasts it with steepest descent. For unsymmetric or not positive definite problems, denominators may vanish; min res is suggested as safer but more expensive, using Arnoldi and a least-squares problem. The lecture also notes that choosing between direct elimination and iterative methods such as conjugate gradients depends on experiments.

Police are warning the public about fraud during festive shopping. Crimestoppers is appealing for information on those making, buying, or selling counterfeit banknotes. In the first half of 2017, over 237,000 fake notes worth over £4.88 million were removed from UK streets. Although less than 1% of notes are counterfeit, retailers, businesses, schools, charities, and the elderly have been affected. Christmas increases cash use, especially £20 and £50 notes, and fraudsters target busy shops with temporary staff. Counterfeit notes are linked to organized crime. Crimestoppers and the Bank of England launched the Banknote Checking Scheme, and the public can report information anonymously.

GSK said Luke Miels, its chief commercial officer, will become CEO on Jan. 1, replacing Emma Walmsley, whose tenure included spinning off consumer health into Haleon and focusing on innovative medicines; investors have questioned GSK’s strategy amid patent and vaccine challenges. AstraZeneca plans to list shares on the NYSE while keeping its London listing, giving U.S. investors easier access, amid UK drug-pricing criticism and companies moving listings to New York. AstraZeneca already offers Nasdaq ADRs and is listed in Stockholm and London. AstraZeneca and Novartis are opening U.S. DTC sales channels.

Zimbabwe's Department of Livestock and Veterinary Services faces FMD vaccination challenges due to inconsistent vaccine supplies over two years. The virus has spread unchecked in several provinces, with active infections in Chipinge South, Mwenezi, Chivi and Chiredzi. The department cites weak veterinary staffing, logistics, funding, infrastructure, animal identification, movement controls and stakeholder support; zonal control loss has increased cattle requiring vaccination.

The passage is a VentureWire newsletter dated Tuesday, September 19, 2000, published by Technologic Partners. Its top stories report that Pseudo.com shut down and laid off all 175 employees; Broadbase will acquire Servicesoft in a deal worth about $645 million; Enfrastructure launched with over $100 million from Arthur Andersen, Avaya, Hanny Holdings, IBM, and Microsoft; Mary Coleman became CEO of RightWorks; Interregnum opened a GBP 75 million ($105 million) IT fund; and Q9 Networks raised $26.5 million in Series A funding. The issue also contains New Money items on numerous funding rounds, New Products items on launches, subsidiary formation, and name changes, M&A items on acquisitions, New Directors and New People appointments, VC Fund News and VC Personnel announcements, and VW Corrections. It includes advertisements for Bessemer Venture Partners, a Harvard Business School course, and The Wall Street Journal Technology Summit.

Cheltenham Town face a second successive summer battle to retain Harry Pell, with a rival League Two club keen and a different fourth-tier club approaching. Pell nearly joined Blackpool for £200,000 last August, but personal terms failed. Under contract until the end of next season after a January 2017 extension, he has made over 120 starts and scored three goals in his last five games. He missed Saturday's Cambridge defeat after wisdom teeth removal.

The University of Nebraska-Lincoln is making targeted investments in agricultural and environmental-studies buildings and research under a strategic plan. Its agricultural and natural resources programs account for 48.5 per cent of $295 million in research expenditures, and undergraduate enrolment rose 78 per cent from 2006-16. The passage cites new facilities, relocated Food Science and Technology, Beadle Center work, a $20 million NSF root and soil microbe grant involving multiple institutions, and INFEWS. The Buffalo County Historical Society opened a Family History Center at Trails & Rails Museum for preservation and exhibits; it is phase 1, with $660,000 sought for phase 2. Lincoln Public Schools has the smallest student-teacher ratio among Nebraska’s 10 largest districts, and the piece discusses class size, student achievement, budget concerns, and future costs. Alliance expects eclipse visitors and events; Carhenge, built from junked cars by Jim Reinders, is a major attraction.

Stone tools found in India dated 385,000–172,000 years ago suggest humans may have migrated from Africa earlier than previously thought; researchers had thought such tool-making reached India 140,000–90,000 years ago. The Attirampakkam tools, published in Nature, had no human remains, leaving interpretations and questions about their makers and influences unresolved.

This cross-sectional study from November 2023 to May 2024 at ACS Medical College and Hospital in Chennai analyzed 346 specimens to investigate antimicrobial resistance prevalence and patterns among clinical isolates. It aimed to identify common resistant organisms and propose antimicrobial stewardship strategies. Specimens included urine, blood, sputum, wound/pus, and other swabs; tissue samples and specimens from patients with prior antimicrobial therapy were excluded. Cultures were processed aseptically, identified by staining and biochemical tests, and tested by Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion using CLSI guidelines. Of 346 samples, 264 (76.3%) showed positive growth, with Gram-negative organisms accounting for 75.4%. Urine was the largest sample and positive-culture category. E. coli (28.8%), Klebsiella (26.9%), Staphylococcus (13.2%), and Pseudomonas (9.5%) were common. High resistance was observed for Cefoperazone/sulbactam (97.4%), Cefotaxime (92.1%), Cefuroxime (93.4%), and Polymyxin B (98.7%); Amikacin (71.1%) and Gentamycin (63.2%) had higher sensitivity. The discussion cites Gram-negative dominance, older-adult vulnerability, multidrug resistance, limitations such as short duration and small sample size, and recommendations for stewardship and future research.

The passage describes an industrial data services platform for industrial automation systems, including continuation applications related to an industrial data services platform. It covers industrial controllers, industrial devices, HMIs, gateways, higher-level systems, and basic information data types (state, rate, odometer, and event). Embodiments register an industrial asset’s identity, a hierarchical asset model referencing data tags on industrial devices, and available data service applications on a cloud platform. A client device associated with an end-user owner selects a data service application; a gateway collects industrial data from the referenced data tags; and the data is processed according to the selected application. The passage also describes gateway discovery and asset models, application server aggregation into plant models, graphical presentations, and secure cloud communication via a gateway device registry.

This study used finite element simulations of thoracic aortic aneurysms initiated by combined insults to elastic fiber integrity and mechanosensing to train neural network models. Inputs were dilatation maps alone or dilatation and distensibility maps, in grayscale or heat map formats; outputs were insult profiles. Across CNN-DeepONet, FNN-DeepONet, UNet, and LNO architectures, using both dilatation and distensibility reduced prediction errors roughly twofold compared with dilatation alone. UNet generally achieved the best accuracy, especially with both inputs, while LNO performed worst in dilatation-only cases. Distensibility was important for accurately determining the relative contributions of combined disease drivers. The authors conclude that full-field dilatation and distensibility measurements could improve personalized TAA diagnosis and treatment, though limitations include synthetic data, a single initial geometry, stable TAA simulations, and no consideration of ascending aortic curvature.

Joe Hadzima presents educational background on legal issues for startups, noting it is not legal advice and is fact-specific. He covers intellectual property—trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, patents, filing timing, provisional applications, and MIT licensing—as well as legal entity choice, S corporation taxation, Section 83, founder equity, vesting, and employee equity compensation. He also discusses securities-law compliance, convertible notes, term sheets, and angel/venture financing terms such as preferred returns, liquidation preferences, and anti-dilution protection.

The President communicates his approval of an act to regulate the counting of votes for President and Vice-President and to decide questions arising thereon for the term beginning March 4, 1877. He states that a dispute exists over the election result, and that the act provides a constitutional, orderly means of decision. He notes the bill addresses the recent election, may not be perfect, and may require future general legislation. Believing it will secure peace and acceptance of the result, he signs it.

The passage is a manual for the SanDisk Sansa Fuze portable digital audio/video player. It covers home/personal use, copyright notice, features including a 1.9” color screen, FM tuner, built-in MIC, microSDHC slot, supported media formats, battery charging, controls, Hold Switch, power/reset, computer connection, media transfer, playback, FM radio presets, voice recording, deleting content, system settings, troubleshooting, technical support, warranty, and software license terms.

This paper examines the impact of digitalization on the main sustainability components: economy, society, and environment. Its hypothesis is that digitalization affects sustainable development, and it asks whether and to what extent digital transformation affects sustainable development and its components, and whether digital transformation level is affected by a society’s cultural characteristics. It compares the Digital Economy and Society Index (DESI) with global indices measuring sustainable development aspects and with Hofstede’s cultural dimensions for 28 EU countries, using data from 2014 to 2017.

Results show that DESI significantly correlates with most selected measures, including GCI, GII, GEI, GDP, GoCI, and SDGI. Digitalization is positively related to economic and social aspects, but the environmental dimension is neglected with a medium negative impact. Cultural dimensions show a high negative correlation for Power distance, negative correlation for Uncertainty Avoidance, positive correlation for Individualism and Indulgence, and no relationship for Long term orientation.

The study concludes that digitalization significantly correlates with sustainable development components, confirming the hypothesis, and that cultural differences affect digitalization. It notes limitations: the country set is limited to EU countries, sustainability methodologies are not fully developed, and DESI has a limited scope.

Ari Ne’eman compares the Trump administration’s autism policy to the 1963 President’s Panel on Mental Retardation trip to the USSR. The passage says HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. linked autism to vaccination and acetaminophen. The PPMR trip, requested by President Kennedy, found Soviet research constrained by political ideology: intelligence testing and Mendelian genetics were rejected, socioeconomic causes were politically untenable, and diagnoses often required an organic cause. U.S. and Soviet prevalence differed, which delegates increasingly attributed to diagnostic practices. The passage describes later U.S. declines in intellectual disability diagnoses and shifts toward autism, broadened autism criteria, diagnostic substitution, and improved access. It states a 2006 Pediatrics study faced criticism from autism parent groups claiming a vaccine-caused epidemic. Ne’eman argues the administration ignores evidence for diagnostic substitution, broadened criteria, and improved access, resurrects older bad ideas, and proposes cutting the Developmental Disabilities Act and Medicaid, while comparing officials to Soviet researchers compelled by political doctrine.

The Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the judgment, finding no error in the trial court's jury instruction regarding inconsistency between interrogatory No. 4 and the general verdict and substantial evidence supporting the verdict.

The Houston Astros won their sixth straight game, completing a three-game sweep of the Chicago White Sox with a 7-1 victory Sunday and outscoring Chicago 27-2 in the series. Jose Altuve hit a go-ahead single in a five-run seventh inning; Lance McCullers Jr. allowed one run and eight hits over six innings, and Evan Gattis homered. Chicago has lost seven straight and dropped to 4-14.

The passage specifies SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 details for COP lock/unlock, CMD42 modes, CMD55, CMD6, CMD8, command formats/classes, CRC, timeouts, status registers, and speed classes. It states that accepting COP Unlock moves a COP Card to CMD42 ver.2.0 mode; before that it is CMD42 Ver.1.0 Compatible mode and CMD42 with COP bit=1 is ignored except COP Unlock. FEP=0 allows only set FEP among COP functions. Set PWD requires COP bit=0. Password replacement includes old and new passwords; an incorrect old password sets LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED and leaves the old password unchanged; a correct old password saves the new password in FEP and FEP_LEN. Setting FEP disables “Force Erase” and “Reset PWD,” while clearing FEP enables them and disables “FEP Force Erase” and other COP operations. COP locked state after reset requires COP Unlock; cards not supporting COP reject COP enabling with LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED. Force Erase erases all card content including PWD/PWD_LEN and unlocks, but is prevented if FEP=set; FEP Force Erase requires matching FEP, erases all content, unlocks, and leaves FEP/FEP_LEN unchanged. Locked cards accept listed commands; ACMD6 is rejected when locked. Lock/unlock types 1, 2, and 3 differ by version.

The passage describes CMD55/APP_CMD for ACMDs, including APP_CMD bit response rules and exceptions. CMD56 is blank. CMD6 switches or expands functions across Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, and Power Limit; mode 0 checks functions, mode 1 sets functions, with 512-bit status and busy indications. It covers high-speed mode, command system reservations, CMD8 initialization/voltage check, capacity-type differences for addressing, block length, partial/misalign access, and write-protected groups. It describes clock control, CRC7/CRC16 generation and error handling, read/write/erase timeouts, command types/format, command classes/CCC, responses R1-R3/R6/R7, card/SD/task status, write protection, timings, speed class methods, allocation/recording units, read/write performance, and FAT update during recording.

Sarah Blakely and her husband sold their renovated Toronto home for more than $1 million after buying it for over $300,000 seven years earlier, then bought a larger Ottawa home and expect to be mortgage-free. Her agent, Josie Stern, says the Toronto market is cooling, with buyers delaying purchases before a scheduled meeting among Finance Minister Bill Morneau, Ontario Finance Minister Charles Sousa and Toronto Mayor John Tory on reining in the market, and as Ontario promises affordability measures. The GTA average sale rose 33.2 per cent year-over-year to $916,567, but sellers are rushing to list and many are not getting recent high bids. Some sellers are downsizing or moving to cheaper markets, including Hamilton-Burlington and Nova Scotia, while Vancouver’s foreign buyers’ tax affected luxury homes. Stern seeks a crackdown on speculators and cautions that cashing out carries risk.
A fire at a private Lucknow hospital caused panic; over 50 patients and attendants escaped uninjured, ICU patients were moved, and a probe was ordered.

India will aim to dominate Bangladesh in the second semi-final of the Champions Trophy at Edgbaston on Thursday. Bangladesh beat New Zealand by five wickets in their last Group A match. The match on 15 June will be broadcast on Star Sports and streamed on Hotstar from 3 PM IST.

LeBron James, a four-time NBA champion, four-time MVP, and 19-time All-Star, is the highest-paid NBA player and a billionaire. He has made $479.5 million during his 21-year NBA career, signed a two-year, $97 million Lakers extension, and earns millions from endorsements including Nike, Beats, AT&T, Walmart, Intel, Kia, Pepsi, and others. His investments include Liverpool FC, Fenway Sports Group, Blaze Pizza, Lobos 1707, Uninterrupted, SpringHill, and Canyon Bicycles. He owns homes in Akron, Miami, and Los Angeles and has owned luxury cars. He is described as cheap in some habits but spends heavily on his body, tattoos, and family. He and wife Savannah have three children; he played alongside son Bronny in October 2024. His philanthropy includes the I Promise School, LeBron James Family Foundation, and More Than a Vote. After hinting at retirement and teasing a major announcement, his October 2025 announcement was revealed as a Hennessy ad.

The passage discusses the Baku Declaration of the 18th Mid-Term Ministerial Meeting of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), held in Azerbaijan on 3–6 April 2018, and the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) Communiqué issued in London on 20 April 2018. It notes that NAM represents the Global South and 55 per cent of the world’s population, while the Commonwealth has fifty-three countries and 2.4 billion people, including large, small, rich, and poor states. The Baku Declaration is described as a prelude to the XVIIIth NAM in Azerbaijan in 2019. India was represented at Baku by External Affairs Minister Sushma Swaraj, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended CHOGM in London. Observers questioned India’s priorities, especially since Modi did not attend the XVIIth NAM summit in Venezuela in 2016.

Swaraj said NAM’s values and principles remain relevant and that it epitomises autonomy in policymaking. The Baku Conference expressed concern over the global financial and economic crisis, rising protectionism in developed countries, and effects on developing-country exports. It referred to the Doha Development Round and imbalances in the multilateral trading system. It described South-South cooperation as complementary to, not a substitute for, North-South cooperation. The passage argues the Global South has become a passive stakeholder and that India hardly resists unequal global trade. The Baku Declaration supported ending Israel’s occupation of Palestinian territory, condemned Israeli policies and violence in Gaza, and demanded Israeli withdrawal from the occupied Syrian Golan. It also called for tolerance, respect for diversity, and opposition to racism, racial discrimination, and xenophobia, which the passage connects to criticism of India’s intolerance policies.

The CHOGM Communiqué expressed concern about protectionism, reaffirmed commitment to free trade and the Doha Round, supported the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement, and aimed to boost intra-Commonwealth trade to US$2 trillion by 2030. It recognised vulnerabilities of small states, unsustainable debt, limited development financing, and “de-risking.” It welcomed the New York Declaration for Refugees and Migrants and expressed solidarity with Bangladesh over Rohingya refugees, calling for their sustainable return to Myanmar under UNHCR oversight. The passage notes India’s negative position on Rohingyas and that India is not a signatory to refugee conventions. It concludes that both documents contain welcome statements on migration, refugees, illegal occupation, international crimes, and intolerance, but do not seriously address fundamental existential issues. It says the XVIIIth NAM is scheduled for Baku in 2019 and questions whether underprivileged countries can devise alternative strategies on trade, technology transfer, market access, currency transactions, and autonomy in policymaking.

The Federal Circuit reversed the district court’s denial of Hilite’s motion for judgment as a matter of law. The majority held the asserted patent claims invalid: claim 22 of the ’017 patent was anticipated by Danckert because the disputed “direct transfer in a closed line” was not a claim limitation, and the asserted claims of the ’506 and ’254 patents were obvious over Danckert in view of Shirai. Judge Newman concurred in the judgment of no liability, disagreeing that the claims were invalid for anticipation; she would find infringement unsupported because the parties stipulated no infringement when the pump supplied oil and no evidence showed operation contrary to design during transition.

Despite Norway’s high digital infrastructure, student and teacher use of digital technology in Norwegian schools is limited to basic ICT. Digital competence is a basic competence across subjects, including PE, and the curriculum states digital resources in PE should help students explore, create, and solve practical challenges. Teachers and pre-service teachers often feel unprepared to integrate technology, and research on digital technology in PE is limited, though available literature suggests it may promote learning and motivation. Flipped learning (FL) introduces course concepts before class and uses class time for active, practical application. FL has grown in higher education and teacher education, with positive findings, but research in PE/PETE is scarce. This study investigates students’ perceptions of an FL framework in Norwegian PETE. It uses a qualitative, social constructivist, constructivist grounded theory approach. Participants were 22 PETE students, average age 24.2, equally distributed by gender. FL was applied in two units over two semesters in 2016/2017, covering dance and motor learning, with 11 FL lectures and pre-class videos. Data came from semi-structured interviews in five groups. Analysis produced five themes: expectations, simple input, deep learning, supportive learning environment, and challenges. Students reported overall positive perceptions: videos helped preparation, peer expectations encouraged watching, content was compact and timesaving, repeated viewing aided deeper understanding, and advance preparation created security, especially for practical dance. Challenges included missing immediate questions, technical problems, and time consumption. The discussion and conclusion state FL was perceived as useful and interesting, improving engagement, motivation, understanding, and applicability to diverse PETE modules; students saw it as a tool for future PE teaching. Reported advantages outweighed challenges. Limitations included initial focus on motivation and learning, possible overlooked perceptions, and data from different institutions potentially increasing trustworthiness. Future research should investigate digital technology implementation in PETE and TPACK effects on student motivation and learning in school PE.

St. Jude researchers identified kinases Mst1 and Mst2 as hidden drivers regulating dendritic cell subsets and T cell responses. Using the NetBID algorithm, they found Hippo signaling controls dendritic cell function. CD8α+ dendritic cells were more metabolically active than CD8α- cells, and Mst1/2 used NF-κB signaling to trigger IL-12. The findings suggest new treatment strategies for cancer or immune disorders.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 27, 2021. On that date, Apple issued a press release regarding its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 26, 2020, attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing lists registered securities including common stock and various notes on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC. It is signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President, Chief Financial Officer.

A Roman pottery fragment found by a dog walker on Chapel St Leonards’ beach near Skegness is the third Roman artefact found there in months, following a coin and brooch part. Experts say it may indicate a lost Roman settlement, possibly under the sand. The council urges reporting finds.

The Alabama Supreme Court answered the Eleventh Circuit’s certified question in the negative, holding that a policy provision defining an “insured” as an employee acting “within the scope of duties” while conducting the employer’s business does not conflict with a separate provision covering “violations of constitutional/civil rights” so as to create an ambiguity construed against the insurer. It concluded the Titan cases were not controlling because Titan II rested on law of the case and the policies differed, and that the policy was neither ambiguous nor illusory because conduct can fall within both “color of law” and scope of employment.

COVID-19 is a respiratory infection caused by SARS-CoV-2, with clinical responses from asymptomatic to severe respiratory failure and death; the pandemic caused 645 million confirmed cases and 6.6 million deaths worldwide. Meteorological factors may influence many infectious diseases, and the Omicron variant became dominant in early 2022. COVID-19 seasonality remains poorly understood. The study hypothesizes a “compromised airway epithelium” in infected persons that can be disturbed by external triggers such as outdoor temperature drops, leading to increased symptoms and severity. It examines outdoor temperature and COVID-19 deterioration during the Omicron wave in Tomsk from January 1 to March 31, 2022, using temperature data and daily hospitalizations. The analysis identified 14 temperature drops greater than 3°C associated with hospitalization bursts with a 1–2 day lag; temperature was a primary trigger in 8 and an additional factor in 6. Of 17 hospitalization surges, 3 were not linked to temperature. The study concludes that small or short-term outdoor daily temperature drops on compromised airway epithelium can increase COVID-19 symptoms and severity, and may help predict hospitalization increases and prepare health care systems. It also discusses future study of humidity, supersaturation, and air pollution.

The family of Peter Joseph Saville, a Worthing dentist for over four decades at West Park Lane, paid tribute after his death at home on June 27 aged 90. His granddaughter Anne described him as kind, gentle, and selfless. Born in Ilford in 1928, he studied dentistry at Guys Hospital, served as a dental surgeon in the army, married Josephine in 1954, and moved to Worthing, where he joined a Lancing practice before opening his own. He was a sportsman, Catholic, charity supporter, and committee member. He is survived by his wife, six children, and eight grandchildren. His funeral mass will be at Saint Mary of the Angels on July 12, followed by burial at Durrington Cemetery.

Minor league baseball completed its first full week. Call to the Pen outlined weekly coverage, including Monday news and top performers, Tuesday weekend reviews, Wednesday draft and college news, Thursday weekend previews, Friday video/scouting, and scattered scouting reports. Top performer Mike Soroka, a 19-year-old Braves right-hander at AA, went 2-0 with 11 2/3 innings, 0.77 ERA, no walks, and a 34.15 percent strikeout rate. Big moments included Kyle Tucker’s seven RBI, Jose Medina’s three home runs, Dane Dunning’s 13 strikeouts, Josh Staumont’s 12 strikeouts, Visalia’s nine perfect innings, and Kane County’s combined no-hitter. Leaders were Ian Happ (6 HR), Jorge Mateo (9 SB), and Mike Clevinger (25 strikeouts). Phillip Wellman won his 1,000th game as a manager.

The passage examines war’s effect on stock markets and other assets. It says history suggests stocks show less volatility during wars and geopolitical conflicts, and US stocks have performed reasonably well during wars, though wars on home soil may change this. During WWII, stocks fell almost 20% after Pearl Harbor but bottomed months later; the Dow rose over 60% before German and Japanese surrender. After Iraq invaded Kuwait, markets sold off initially, discounted war by October, and rose when Iraqi forces were expelled. A study of US stocks from 1890–2017 found less volatility during war/conflict, with defense expenditures inversely correlated (-0.26) with volatility. Chiral phonons carrying angular momentum can transport energy in metallic and insulating materials, unlike CISS, which is restricted to conducting materials. In chiral materials, phonon band degeneracy is lifted, while non-chiral materials require optical excitation for transient chiral phonons. Ferromagnets can transfer angular momentum to chiral phonons via spin-phonon coupling, and ultrafast demagnetization can transfer heat and angular momentum, particularly to acoustic chiral phonons. The passage reports chirality-selective heat transfer and a nanoscale chiral thermal switch in ferromagnetic [Co/Pt]/chiral α-SiO2 heterostructures. Time-resolved magneto-optic Kerr effect measurements showed a 7% difference in apparent thermal conductivity of α-SiO2 when reversing magnetization in [Co/Pt]. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that angular momentum conservation in chiral phonons affects heat propagation and produces chirality-dependent spatiotemporal temperature profiles. The thermal on/off ratio was about 1.07 at room temperature and could be enhanced to 1.2 at 50 K due to reduced phonon-phonon scattering. First-principles-based calculations supported a chiral phonon diode effect. The findings suggest that chiral degrees of freedom in phonons influence thermal transport and offer a guideline for chirality-selective nano-thermal switches using ferromagnet/chiral material heterostructures.

Voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC) reduces heterosexual HIV acquisition risk by 50%–60% and was adopted by Uganda’s Ministry of Health in 2007 following WHO and UNICEF recommendations, including 42 days of abstinence after VMMC. VMMC is provided free in Uganda with PEPFAR/CDC support, and men receive pre-VMMC counseling and follow-up at 24 hours and 7 days. The study estimated early sex resumption (ESR) prevalence and associated factors among men undergoing VMMC in Rakai, Uganda, over 2013–2020, using cross-sectional Rakai Community Cohort Study data from four survey rounds. Participants were males aged 15–49 who reported circumcision within 3 years. ESR declined from 45.1% in 2013/2015 to 14.9% in 2018/2020. ESR was higher among married men, men with multiple sexual partners, some older age groups, fishermen in some rounds, and those with primary or no formal education. HIV-positive status was associated with ESR in some rounds. Multivariate analysis found married status and multiple partners associated with ESR; in 2018/2020, primary education was associated, while occupation and HIV status were not associated across all rounds. The discussion states the decline could be due to comprehensive HIV programs and strengthened counseling starting in 2016, though ESR remained above the WHO target. Limitations included self-reported sexual resumption and inability to determine HIV status at VMMC uptake. The conclusions state ESR declined over time, counseling may have affected post-VMMC behavior, and involving female partners and targeted counseling for men with lower education could reduce ESR.

This Phase 1/2 outpatient, crossover, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled human laboratory study translated preclinical mifepristone/yohimbine work in AUD. Non-abstinent, non-treatment-seeking individuals with AUD received 7-day mifepristone (600 mg/day) or placebo, crossed over after a 3-week washout, and underwent laboratory procedures including yohimbine (32.4 mg/1 day), cue reactivity, priming alcohol, and open-bar self-administration. Primary outcome was safety/tolerability; secondary outcomes included craving and consumption, with mediation and moderation analyses. Thirty-two participants were randomized and included in ITT. No serious adverse events occurred with mifepristone, yohimbine, and alcohol co-administration; non-serious AEs did not differ significantly. Mifepristone did not alter alcohol pharmacokinetics or subjective stimulation/sedation. Mifepristone attenuated alcohol craving/urge at the first alcohol trial and cue-elicited salivary output in both trials. Cortisol was higher with mifepristone, but the craving effect was independent of cortisol. Family history density of alcoholism moderated effects, with craving/urge reductions mainly in low FHDA and salivary reductions in both groups. Alcohol consumption did not differ significantly. The authors concluded mifepristone was safe and acceptable for AUD, while noting limitations such as no yohimbine control, no mifepristone blood levels, and few females.

This lecture moves from tree-level QED diagrams to loop diagrams. It gives examples: electron propagation with a virtual photon loop, photon propagation creating and annihilating a virtual electron-positron pair, and vertex correction. Loop diagrams require integrating over internal momentum from minus infinity to plus infinity, which can produce divergences not removable by simple subtraction or division. The lecture says these divergences arise from extrapolating QED to arbitrarily high energy or short distance and led to renormalization, developed by Schwinger, Feynman, and Tomonaga, simplified by Dyson, and later understood physically by Wilson’s renormalization group.

It also describes new features: loops include vacuum quantum fluctuations; physical mass, charge, and fields differ from the bare parameters and fields in the Lagrangian. Electron propagator correction shifts mass and residue; the photon remains massless due to gauge symmetry but its field strength renormalizes; the vertex correction changes charge and generates an anomalous magnetic moment. The lecture explains that the Dirac equation in the nonrelativistic limit predicts g=2, while Schwinger’s calculation of the vertex correction gives a correction alpha/2pi. Higher-order corrections involve more diagrams, such as seven diagrams for the next order and 72 for the following order, and are compared with highly accurate experimental measurements.

This study analyzed gene expression in muscle biopsies from patients with granulomatous myositis (GM) and compared it with other inflammatory myopathies, other myopathies, and healthy controls. GM showed marked upregulation of IFNγ and IFNγ-inducible genes, elevated proinflammatory cytokines including IL1B, TNF, and TGFB1, increased T-cell, B-cell, plasma cell, and macrophage markers, and higher HLA type II expression than other inflammatory myopathies. The study identified 1,293 specifically upregulated and 256 specifically downregulated genes in GM; CHIT1 was the most significantly upregulated. These gene sets correlated with transcriptomic markers of disease activity, and spatial transcriptomics localized key findings to non-caseating granulomas. Machine learning models, especially support vector machines, classified GM with high accuracy. Limitations included lack of infectious or genetic granulomatous muscle disease cases and RNA-level identification for most markers except CHIT1. The authors conclude that the study defines transcriptomic features and a specific gene expression profile of GM, providing potential diagnostic, monitoring, and therapeutic insights.

The lecture recaps linear feedback for the system q double dot equals u, including phase-portrait reshaping and minimum-time optimal control with bounded u, which produced switching surfaces and a nonlinear bang-bang controller. It then presents Pontryagin’s minimum principle as a Lagrange-multiplier method for constrained finite-time optimization. Next, dynamic programming is introduced through recursive discrete-time cost-to-go, the principle of optimality, and the continuous-time Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation and sufficiency theorem. Using HJB, the lecture derives the linear quadratic regulator for x dot equals Ax plus Bu with quadratic cost, obtaining the Riccati equation, the optimal feedback u equals negative R inverse B transpose S(t)x, and the infinite-horizon steady-state solution. Applying LQR to the double integrator gives a specific S matrix and closed-loop dynamics. The lecture notes that HJB requires a smooth value function, while Pontryagin works along trajectories and suits bang-bang problems. It concludes that these analytical optimal control tools provide a foundation for later algorithmic methods.

Hedge funds are investment pools contributed by a limited number of private investors and run by professional managers to maximize returns and minimize risk. They are risky alternative investments, usually requiring high minimum investments or net worth, and are intended for accredited investors and institutions. They trade relatively liquid assets and may use short selling, leverage, derivatives, and complex risk management, distinguishing them from mutual funds and ETFs. They differ from private equity funds because they generally invest in liquid assets and are usually open-ended. They often aim for neutral market direction through hedging. Common strategies include long/short equity, event-driven, global macro, relative value, and fixed income arbitrage. Funds may be systematic or discretionary, diversified or concentrated, and some focus on niches such as real estate, cryptocurrency, or insurance-linked instruments. Examples include long/short equity and merger arbitrage. Strategy correlation and complementarity are emphasized, as is running a “one-man hedge fund” with professionalism, planning, a trade journal, and adequate capital. FAQs state advantages include potential higher returns, diversification, professional managers, and unique investments; minimums typically range from $100,000–$500,000; hedge funds are privately offered to accredited investors, use more aggressive strategies, charge higher fees, and have wider mandates than mutual funds. Risks include liquidity, leverage, counterparty, and strategy failure. Hedge funds typically report quarterly, and tax implications exist, so investors should consult a tax advisor.

Ultraviolet femtosecond pulsed-laser irradiation (λ = 343 nm, τp = 238 fs) was used to form surface nanostructures on Nb thin films, evolving into quasi-1D periodic corrugations (LIPSS) with lateral periodicity Λ ≈ 260 nm. Square films and micro-sized bridges were fabricated with LIPSS parallel or perpendicular to the transport current. Increasing laser pulse energy produced gradual microstructural changes: reduced film thickness, reduced Nb lattice parameter, and increased grain size mainly at LIPSS peaks; higher energies caused holes/perforation. XRD showed a (110) peak shift and lattice shrinkage of ≈1.05% for fully LIPSS-covered films. Intrinsic superconducting properties changed: Tc decreased from 8.93 K in pristine films to 8.53 K at full LIPSS; Hc2(T) shifted down, with ΔTc ≈ 0.3 K and ΔHc2 ≈ 50 mT for fully formed LIPSS, isotropically. Transport, inductive, MOI, and TDGL results showed anisotropic critical current density: Jc was higher along LIPSS than across, and optimized samples had higher Jc than pristine in certain field/temperature ranges (H ≲ 100 mT, 6–8 K), while generally reduced pinning otherwise. The anisotropy ratio Jc∥/Jc⊥ ≡ Γ(H,T) increased with temperature, saturated at low fields, and collapsed toward unity near Hc2. TDGL simulations attributed the anisotropy to thickness undulations, with vortices preferring valleys; predicted Jc∥ grows with undulation depth and shows non-monotonic field dependence. The passage concludes that laser processing controls superconducting properties in Nb films and may be extended to other materials, with further work on surface profiles for filters, diodes, and ratchets.

This study introduces PHIVE, a deep learning framework for high-resolution whole-brain MRSI metabolite quantification with simultaneous CRLB estimation. PHIVE uses a variational autoencoder, a convolutional encoder, a physics-informed decoder, and a conditional baseline approach, and is trained unsupervised by minimizing MSE and a KL term. In vivo 7T MRSI data from 12 healthy subjects were used, with eight subjects for training and four for testing. PHIVE was compared with LCModel. Testing took 6 ms per whole-brain MRSI dataset versus about 2 hours for LCModel. PHIVE produced metabolite maps similar to LCModel and correlations for tNAA/tCr, Glx/tCr, tCho/tCr, mIns/tCr, Tau/tCr, and GSH/tCr, with R² ranging from 0.27 to 0.86. It showed no statistically significant differences for tNAA, Glx, tCho, Tau, and GSH, but significantly higher mIns. PHIVE generally had lower CVs for Glx and mIns. It also generated CRLB, epistemic, and aleatoric uncertainty maps, with higher uncertainty in lower-SNR regions. Limitations included lack of ground truth, small sample size, no separate frequency correction, lower tCho/mIns correlations, interpretability concerns, and need for larger and longitudinal validation.

Knees undergo wear and tear throughout life, and painful or damaged knees can be debilitating. Healthy lifestyle choices—such as maintaining a healthy weight, exercising regularly, strengthening the muscles around the knees and the entire body, working on flexibility, and doing low-impact cardio like cycling and swimming—can reduce the risk of joint, cartilage, or ligament damage. Physiotherapy and tailored exercises can aid recovery, reduce recurrence or worsening, and may help avoid or delay surgery. If knee surgery is needed, it can improve quality of life and range of motion, though it carries risks; modern knee replacements often last for decades, and physiotherapy can help recovery.
