This study examined behavioural changes in frontotemporal dementia (FTD), comparing behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) and semantic dementia (SD) and investigating their cognitive and neuroanatomical bases. Forty-seven FTD patients (26 bvFTD, 21 SD) and 18 controls completed informant questionnaires, neuropsychological testing, and structural MRI. Results showed bvFTD had more severe behavioural changes than SD in several domains, but SD also had higher scores than controls on most domains. No behaviours were significantly more prevalent in SD, indicating quantitative rather than qualitative differences. Principal component analysis of informant questionnaires yielded apathy, challenging behaviours, and activities of daily living components. Apathy was associated with executive dysfunction and anterior cingulate cortex atrophy, while no association was found between behavioural change and semantic knowledge or anterior temporal lobe grey matter volume. Semantic memory and executive function discriminated bvFTD from SD more accurately than behavioural measures. The authors conclude that bvFTD and SD show quantitative rather than qualitative behavioural differences and that neuropsychological measures of semantic memory and executive function should be considered for discrimination.

Two actors, Daisy McCrackin and Joseph Capone, were kidnapped and held for ransom for almost three days by an alleged meth-fuelled gang. Keith Andre Stewart, Johntae Jones and Amber Neal were arrested and charged with 17 counts, including kidnapping, assault and conspiracy. The indictment alleges Capone was pistol-whipped and held in a bathtub for 30 hours, while McCrackin was driven to banks to obtain at least $10,000 before escaping and alerting police.

The passage warns that electing an unworthy, violent, hypocritical agitator would damage popular government and put democracy on trial. It says mob rule and plutocracy are equally evil, and honest rich or poor people have as much to fear from a demagogue as from a corruptionist; such figures often work together. It calls for a bill limiting railroad employees’ hours, aiming toward an eight-hour day, with exceptions, and notes enforcement of the eight-hour law through the Bureau of Labor. It supports half holidays for Government employees, a truant court for the District of Columbia, investigation of child and women’s labor, and immediate child-labor legislation for the District of Columbia and Territories.

This Wall $treet Week With Louis Rukeyser year-end 2000 transcript reviews a mixed market year: the Dow fell just over 6% and had its first losing year since 1990; the S&P 500 lost more than 10%; and the Nasdaq fell nearly 40%, was off more than 51% from its March high, and had its worst year ever. Panelists Elizabeth Dater, Louis Holland, Barbara Marcin, and Brian Rogers discuss the Fed, the slowing economy, oil prices, consumer confidence, and the dollar; their 2000 portfolios gained about 42.5%, more than 40%, more than 28%, and more than 7.5%, respectively. They give 2001 Dow and Nasdaq high, low, and close forecasts and specific stock picks. The transcript also lists predictions from all 22 panelists and ordering information.

Invictus MD Strategies Corp. announced that for the fiscal year beginning February 1, 2018, it received $5,777,267 from exercises of previously issued warrants and options: 4,346,731 warrants for $5,267,467 and 337,500 options for $509,800. It has 96,623,857 common shares outstanding. Proceeds are expected to help fund construction and operations. The Company anticipates 262,000 square feet of cannabis cultivation by the end of 2018 and 846,000 square feet by the end of 2019. About 9.9 million warrants and 9.4 million options remain outstanding; if exercised, they would bring an additional $19.7 million and $14.9 million. It granted 120,000 incentive stock options at $1.50, vesting one-third in 3, 9, and 15 months, exercisable over five years.

4-Vertical is a concept in which all four receivers release vertically to stretch the defense vertically and horizontally, push the ball deep, and seek one-on-one matchups or open zone voids; it is often taught as a full-field read. It can work against man and Cover 3 if the quarterback looks off the free safety, but is less effective against Cover 4 and soft zone coverages, especially third-and-long, where horizontal routes may be better. Route coaching points differ against 1-high and 2-high coverages for the tight end, tailback, slot, X, and Z receivers. The quarterback must look off safeties, identify safeties, matchups, and man/zone, find a favorable matchup or void, then check down to the running back. Variations from 3x1 and empty sets keep receiver landmarks while isolating receivers or adding a shallow cross.

Yunnan Lucky Air, founded in 2004, grew into a low-cost airline based in Kunming, serving domestic routes. By 2007 it carried over 1.2 million passengers and had US$104.3 million in revenue, modeling itself on Southwest Airlines. China’s airline industry was heavily regulated, but low-cost competition was increasing. Lucky Air considered e-commerce as an additional competitive advantage, supported by parent Hainan Airlines. China’s air traffic was growing, while costs such as fuel, landing fees, aircraft leasing, and taxes were government-influenced. Ticket distribution involved airlines, authorized agents, online distributors, and TravelSky’s GDS; offline agents dominated and charged commissions. China’s e-commerce was early, with low Internet penetration, payment security issues, and low online purchase rates. Online travel was small and dominated by Ctrip and eLong. Lucky Air sold about 80% of tickets through agents and the rest through luckyair.net; 95% of website tickets were bought by reseller agents, and only 1% of total tickets were bought directly by consumers online. Luckyair.net offered online booking, refunds, validation, flight information, community features, and lower prices, with no call center. U.S. and European practices included CRM, Web 2.0, product reviews, conversion-rate improvement, customer self-service, PayPal, and targeting corporate travelers, students, and loyalty program members. Lucky Air’s executives had to choose an expansion and e-commerce strategy amid regulation, competition, and the need to invest significantly in technology and staff.
The Education Department restarted IBR loan forgiveness for some borrowers who made 25 years of on-time payments, but shutdown delays and an expiring tax exemption could affect processing and taxes.

Brent Honeywell allowed four hits and struck out seven without a walk over six innings as Triple-A Durham beat Columbus, 11-0. Pitching coach Kyle Snyder said Honeywell showed body control and adjustability, with good fastball command, an excellent changeup and improved two-strike execution. Brad Boxberger, Ryne Stanek and Adam Kolarek completed the shutout. Wilson Ramos went 1-for-3 and caught seven innings, and Shane Peterson was a triple short of the cycle with two RBIs.

The President addresses reports on Southeast Asia and announces an increased rate of American troop withdrawals from May 1 to December 1. He recalls that when he left Washington in January 1961 there were no American combat forces in Vietnam, but when he returned as President eight years later there were 540,000 troops, 31,000 dead, 300 lost weekly, and no comprehensive plan to end involvement. He says he implemented a plan to train and equip South Vietnamese forces, withdraw American forces, and end involvement once South Vietnam could defend itself. Withdrawals included 25,000 in June 1969, 40,000 in September, 50,000 in December, and 150,000 in April 1970; by May 1 more than 265,000 had been brought home. He cites reduced American and South Vietnamese casualties. He says the Cambodia operation removed troops in 60 days, cut American casualties in half, and did not delay withdrawals. He says the Laotian operation showed South Vietnamese could fight effectively without American advisers, inflicted heavier enemy casualties, and disrupted enemy supply lines. He concludes Vietnamization has succeeded and announces 100,000 more withdrawals between May 1 and December 1, for a total of 365,000, over two-thirds of the troops present when he took office. He states the goal is total withdrawal through Vietnamization or negotiations, calls on Hanoi to negotiate and release prisoners, and opposes announcing a fixed withdrawal date. He discusses ending the war in a way that gives South Vietnam a chance, supports American soldiers, and brings peace.

Researchers from the University of Washington, Texas A&M University, and the Western Australian Museum discovered and named a new genus and species of clingfish, the duckbilled clingfish (Nettorhamphos radula), after finding specimens preserved in jars, including one caught in 1977. The fish has a broad, flat snout and an estimated 1,800 to 2,300 tiny conical teeth. With only two known specimens, researchers used noninvasive CT scans to study its skeleton and morphology. The description was published April 14 in Copeia, and the discovery highlights museum collections.

Lattice Semiconductor shows early signs of revenue rebound, driven by data center strength but offset by weak automotive and industrial markets. Management highlights opportunities in high-end data center chips and emerging markets such as robotics, vision systems, and security. Inventories are normalizing, financials remain solid with strong cash generation and no debt, and Q3 guidance implies further growth. The author raises the target price to $70 but maintains a HOLD rating due to expensive valuation and a thin margin of safety.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015, with common stock registered on NASDAQ. It designs, develops, manufactures, and sells high-performance fully electric vehicles and energy storage products. It produced and sold Model S and Model X, had delivered over 107,000 Model S vehicles worldwide as of December 31, 2015, began Model X customer deliveries in the third quarter of 2015, and planned to unveil Model 3 in 2016 and start production and deliveries in late 2017. It sells through company-owned stores, service centers, and Supercharger stations and markets energy storage products under Tesla Energy. Manufacturing occurs in Fremont, Lathrop, Tilburg, and the Gigafactory near Reno. The filing also describes numerous risks, including production delays, supplier dependence, electric vehicle adoption, competition, cost control, product liability, and international expansion.

During finals season from Dec. 12 to Dec. 20, students study across campus, especially in Fairchild-Martindale and Linderman libraries, which fill quickly. Some students say limited study spaces add stress and seek alternatives such as academic buildings, cafes, and nearby libraries. Lehigh extends hours for some buildings and offers reservable study rooms through the Center for Career and Professional Development. Students describe strategies such as arriving early, saving seats, and using private rooms for quiet study.

Section 14.7 describes tabulating 12-lead ECG investigator assessments by counts/percentages and presenting descriptive ECG measures by visit and treatment group; QTcF categorical summaries include >450, >480, >500 ms and postbaseline increases >30 and >60 ms. Section 14.8 describes descriptive ADA analysis by treatment group with no statistical tests, deriving ADA incidence from treatment-induced and treatment-boosted patients divided by evaluable patients. Section 15 lists changes to protocol-specified analyses, including reworded primary efficacy analysis with added sensitivity/supportive analyses and changed secondary variable terminology. Appendices cover data presentation/programming specifications, SAS programming QC requirements, and a list of tables, figures, and listings.

Scientists are increasingly convinced that highly engineered ultraprocessed foods can have addictive properties similar to alcohol, nicotine and opioids. Such foods, often combinations of salts, fats and sugars, can trigger brain reward signals and are linked to cravings, loss of control, withdrawal and tolerance. They account for more than half of average U.S. calories. Researchers use the NOVA system to classify foods by processing level and describe some as hyperpalatable. Experts debate whether these products should be called foods or “foodlike products.” Research points to changes in reward-related brain regions and neurochemicals, while about 14 percent of adults and 12 percent of children meet criteria for food addiction on the Yale Food Addiction Scale. Questions remain about who is most at risk and how to respond. Some federal and state efforts are scrutinizing ultraprocessed foods, and Chile’s regulations on packaged foods high in sugar, saturated fat, salt or calories appear to shift purchases. Researchers and experts call for regulation and public protection.

The Trump administration announced a 2018 Nuclear Posture Review to modernize the U.S. nuclear arsenal by developing smaller atomic bombs and enhancing deterrence. Trump said the tailored, flexible strategy modernizes nuclear command, control, communications, the triad, dual-capable aircraft, and infrastructure, aiming to make nuclear use less likely while reaffirming arms control, non-proliferation, a testing moratorium, and efforts against nuclear terrorism. Mattis said effective deterrence is cheaper than undeterred war and U.S. NPT commitments remain strong. The report cites Russia and China as pursuing new nuclear capabilities and modernizing conventional forces, and Russia as relying on nuclear escalation; North Korea and Iran are also cited, with no mention of Pakistan. It proposes low-yield options, forward-deployed bombers and dual-capable aircraft, modified SLBM warheads, and a nuclear-armed SLCM. Officials said extended deterrence commitments to allies remain unwavering.

Finance Minister Bill Morneau announced a two-year agreement in which the federal government will give provinces and territories a 75 per cent share of tax revenues from legalized marijuana sales, with part going to cities and towns to help defray legalization costs. Ottawa will retain 25 per cent, to a maximum of $100 million annually, with any excess going to provinces and territories. Provinces may add a markup outside the taxation model. Morneau said revenues are expected to be about $400 million over the first two years, and ministers will meet again in December 2018. All 14 jurisdictions agreed to the key principles. Ministers also discussed equalization, the Canada Pension Plan review, the global economy, and sharing corporate ownership information.

The speaker accepts the responsibility of office and states that an inaugural address should outline the new administration’s main policies. He pledges to maintain and enforce his predecessor’s reforms against lawlessness and abuses of power by large railroad and industrial combinations in interstate commerce. He urges further legislation and executive action, including railroad relief from certain antitrust restrictions, federal supervision to prevent excessive bond and stock issues by interstate railroads, and reorganization of the Department of Justice, the Bureau of Corporations, and the Interstate Commerce Commission.

He plans to ask Congress to amend antitrust and interstate commerce laws and to revise the tariff, calling an extra session on March 15 to revise the Dingley Act, secure adequate revenue, adjust protective duties, and include a maximum tariff provision. If import duties cannot provide enough revenue, he recommends a graduated inheritance tax. He supports economy but not cuts that weaken necessary government functions.

He lists continued agricultural science, resource conservation, forest and waterway improvement, and construction of the Panama Canal as a lock canal paid for by bonds. He supports an adequate army, navy, and coast defenses, while favoring peace, Hague Tribunal arbitration, and protection of citizens abroad. He addresses Asiatic immigration, federal jurisdiction over treaty rights of aliens, monetary and banking reform, postal savings banks, foreign trade, and conditions in Porto Rico and the Philippines.

On the South and the negro race, he cites the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth amendments, urges enforcement, education, and careful appointments. On labor, he hopes to promote further protective legislation but defends court injunctions in labor disputes, opposes the secondary boycott, and recommends statutory conditions for temporary restraining orders without notice.

ANU and Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris completed a study on glass that could help develop shatter-proof phone screens. Using experiments and computer modelling, they studied alumino-silicate, finding nanoscale organisation and that sodium, potassium, calcium, and magnesium influence flexibility and resistance and can affect fracture start or stop. ANU says manufacturers could use this for more fracture-proof glass. The passage also notes smartphone durability problems, drop-test damage, and Samsung's ongoing research into foldable/bendable screens.

South Africa will probably avoid a Moody’s downgrade to junk this week, with all 15 respondents in a Bloomberg survey saying the change from Jacob Zuma to Cyril Ramaphosa will help it keep its only major investment-grade rating. The rand has rallied and business confidence rebounded. Risks remain from missed budget targets, weak growth, and the ANC’s pursuit of expropriation without compensation. A junk downgrade would remove South Africa from indices including Citigroup’s World Government Bond Index and risk outflows of up to 100 billion rand. Moody’s, which put the ratings on review in November, is scheduled to announce on Friday; S&P and Fitch cut South Africa to junk last year.

The passage addresses antimicrobial resistance as a global health threat and the limitations of culture-based diagnostics and known-gene approaches. It proposes AMR-EnsembleNet, a soft-voting ensemble combining a lightweight 1D CNN that learns local SNP motifs from ordered genomic data with XGBoost that captures non-local feature interactions. The study uses a public GieSSen dataset of 809 E. coli isolates with SNP matrices and binary resistance phenotypes for ciprofloxacin, cefotaxime, ceftazidime, and gentamicin. Models were evaluated on held-out test sets using accuracy, MCC, precision, recall, F1, and macro F1. The ensemble performed best for CTX and GEN, matched top performance for CIP, and acted as a stabilizer for CTZ. SHAP analysis identified influential SNPs that mapped to known AMR-associated genes. The authors conclude the framework is robust, balanced, and computationally feasible for AMR prediction, with future work on MIC regression, transcriptomics, and explainability.

The dollar rose broadly on Monday as traders unwound bearish bets amid less U.S.-North Korea rhetoric over the weekend and calls for a peaceful resolution. The dollar index gained 0.3%, rose against the yen and Swiss franc, and was helped by U.S. stock gains. Investors awaited Tuesday's U.S. retail sales report.

Saskatoon city hall is proposing a $1.2-million, two-year plan to remove and replant black ash trees affected by cottony ash psyllids. Staff have tracked the European lice for more than two years, and a summer assessment suggests 1,000 damaged trees should be removed. Insecticides have only delayed tree removal, the report says, and first-year funding of $757,000 is identified from reserve funds while second-year funding of $423,000 is not.

This study examines electrospun polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofiber yarns and post-processing routes for capillary-driven densification. Electrospun yarns generally show lower mechanical performance than individual fibers due to low packing density, misalignment, and inefficient interfiber load transfer. The work introduces ethanol- and water-assisted rolling followed by drying, with an additional thermal annealing step, to produce as-spun/dry-rolled, water-rolled, ethanol-rolled, and heat-treated yarns. Tensile testing shows as-spun yarns have lower modulus, yield stress, and peak stress but higher failure strains, while liquid-treated yarns are stronger and less ductile. Water-treated yarns show higher average stresses than ethanol-treated ones; ethanol’s rapid evaporation and nanofiber swelling are reported as limiting factors. Heat-treated yarns show increased tensile strength but reduced failure strain and brittle fracture. Thinner yarns exhibit higher effective modulus and peak stress, with diameters below 10 μm approaching single-nanofiber performance. Peak load is higher for treated yarns across diameter ranges, and single-yarn segment tests show water and water-plus-heat treatments increase peak load relative to as-spun yarns. SEM and image analyses quantify alignment and packing density, which correlate with peak load individually and synergistically in multiple regression. A stochastic mean-field constitutive model reproduces the five-regime stress–strain behavior using distributed recruitment and failure, elastic–perfectly plastic fibers, orientation averaging, and post-failure load retention. Model-inferred microstructure parameters map closely to SEM-derived packing and alignment. The study concludes that capillary densification and thermal annealing provide simple, scalable routes to tune PAN yarn mechanics, with alignment and packing acting as complementary strength descriptors.

The class session covers Gary Gensler’s feedback on student papers, a lecture on finance, and upcoming guest and reading announcements. Gensler says papers should use critical reasoning on the chosen week’s topic rather than only answering study questions or describing earlier readings. He describes finance as intermediating, allocating, pricing, and moving money and risk, with sectors including commercial banks, investment banks and brokerage, insurance, asset management, collective investment vehicles, exchanges, and clearinghouses. He distinguishes primary and secondary markets, defines ledgers as records of transactions, and describes payment and settlement systems as transferring value and amending ledgers. Regulation is presented as longstanding, addressing financial stability, consumer and investor protection, and eventually illicit activity, with an ebb and flow over time. Finance and technology are described as symbiotic, and blockchain is discussed as a possible new tool, especially with ledgers. Fintech examples mentioned include AI, biometrics, open banking, big data, RPA, machine learning, cloud, blockchain, and chat bots. Gensler defines credit as borrowing something of value with an agreement to repay, presents US debt data, and lists risks including market, credit, underwriting, liquidity, funding, settlement, model/correlation, operational/cyber, legal/compliance, and reputational risk. He describes the 2008 crisis as involving weak underwriting, predatory lending, easy credit, derivatives and leverage, poor risk management, and incentive problems. He says the banking sector is stronger with more capital but more concentrated, and notes Sheila Bair’s view that homeowners were not helped enough. He announces a surprise guest and readings including Roubini and Krugman.

Physicists developed a method to generate and self-organize liquids into well-defined patterns, potentially aiding pharmaceuticals and consumer products. Using droplets of oil, water, and alcohol in confined geometry, the immiscible liquids de-mix into layers or stripes. The pattern is independent of droplet size but dependent on de-mixing speed. Tuning speed and segregation time allows design of emulsion inner structure. The theoretical model matches data and predicts layer lifetime and step-wise release.

Jose Verastegui appealed his guilty-plea convictions and sentences for being a felon in possession of a firearm and unlawful reentry. He argued his concurrent 120-month sentences, imposed through an upward departure and variance above the 63–78 month guideline range, were unreasonable. He also raised constitutional challenges to 18 U.S.C. § 922(g) and 8 U.S.C. § 1326(b), conceding they were foreclosed by precedent and raising them to preserve review. The Fifth Circuit affirmed.
OnePlus announced official Android Nougat updates for the OnePlus 3 and 3T, rolling out globally with wider release planned within a day or two; the builds appear identical.

The lecture discusses the nuclear force as the residual interaction between quarks in different hadrons, noting its complexity and the use of a mean field approach. Experimental information comes from nucleon-nucleon scattering, binding energies and mass measurements, and nuclear structure data. The nuclear force depends on distance and on spin and angular momentum, with spin-orbit and tensor components, and appears charge independent. It is short range, vanishing beyond about 2 femtometers and strongly repulsive below about 0.5 femtometers. Binding energies per nucleus are roughly constant, indicating interactions with immediate neighbors. Charge independence allows electromagnetic effects to be removed by comparing proton-proton, proton-neutron, and neutron-neutron scattering; mirror nuclei are used to study this and unstable nuclei.

The Enjifit workout partner app launched for iOS devices on July 3, 2018, connecting users with nearby workout partners or personal trainers with similar goals and interests. Users can filter and message others, create reminders, and post sessions. It is free, with a PRO subscription for trainers and nutritionists. It will soon be available for Android.

Milky Tea announced HyperBrawl Tournament will launch on Steam Early Access in June 2017. It is a combat sports arena game combining no-rules handball with PvP combat, offering warriors, weapons, arenas, mini games, and 1–4 player local or online 1v1/2v2 multiplayer.

Pepsi will send 10 lucky fans on an all-expense-paid, 3-day VVIP trip to the One Africa Music Fest in Dubai this November, where they will hang out with Pepsi stars Wizkid, Tiwa Savage, Davido, and Tekno.

The passage describes training and using a depth estimation model to generate a depth map from a single color image. Training includes acquiring images, extracting depth maps with a depth model and poses with a pose decoder, generating synthetic frames, calculating an input scale occlusion and motion aware loss based on comparisons of synthetic frames and images, and adjusting the depth model parameters. The loss can include photometric reconstruction error, minimum error between temporally adjacent monocular video frames, upsampled depth features, and a mask discounting static features. Training data may include monocular video, stereoscopic image pairs, or both. A trained device receives a scene image and generates a depth map.

Tech megacaps lost $770 billion in market value, with Nvidia, Amazon and Tesla each falling about 5% on Friday. The Nasdaq dropped 3.6% and the S&P 500 fell 2.7%, their worst days since April. The slide followed President Trump’s threats of a massive tariff increase on Chinese imports; he later said the U.S. would impose a 100% tariff on China and Nov. 1 export controls on critical software.

An Accenture study found clients across ages and economic brackets want robots and humans together, not one instead of the other. Following BlackRock layoffs favoring data mining and Betterment adding human advice, respondents ranked hybrid wealth management firms higher.

The 2017 ASUN Championship at The Legends at Chateau Elan in Braselton, Ga., concluded Monday. Kennesaw State won the team title at 1-under 863, repeating as champion with a one-shot win over Lipscomb despite a final-round 7-over 295. Jake Fendt and Pablo Rodriguez-Tabernero tied for second at 2 under. The win guaranteed Kennesaw State an NCAA Regional spot for the seventh straight year. Dawson Armstrong of Lipscomb won individual honors at 6-under 210, Lipscomb’s first ASUN individual men’s conference champion. It was Armstrong’s sixth college win and third of 2016-17.

Episode four of UFC 216 Embedded features Demetrious Johnson shopping, Ray Borg at the UFC Performance Institute, Derrick Lewis’s mock weigh-in with Forrest Griffin, Fabricio Werdum’s arrival, Tony Ferguson’s wardrobe fitting, Kevin Lee’s cancer center visit, and media day interviews and faceoffs before UFC 216.

On April 13, 2022, Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting the closing of its sale of seven series of notes: $1.5 billion 2.730% notes due 2024; $1.5 billion 3.000% notes due 2025; $2.0 billion 3.300% notes due 2027; $1.5 billion 3.450% notes due 2029; $2.5 billion 3.600% notes due 2032; $2.5 billion 3.950% notes due 2052; and $1.25 billion 4.100% notes due 2062. The aggregate public offering price was $12.719 billion, with estimated net proceeds of approximately $12.692 billion. The sale was under an April 11, 2022 Underwriting Agreement with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, and was registered under a June 1, 2020 Form S-3. The notes were issued under a 2012 Indenture, as supplemented on April 13, 2022. Exhibits were filed.

A manhunt is underway after a man attempted to get a woman in her 30s into a car on Sisson Street, Rhyl, at 8.25am; she escaped unharmed. Police later confirmed no child was involved, after initial warnings.

Pupils appealed to President Mnangagwa to suspend the 2018 November public examinations, citing inadequate preparation from election-related disturbances and teachers’ absence on Zimbabwe Electoral Commission duties. Education Permanent Secretary Sylvia Utete-Masango revealed this, saying the President’s response was not disclosed. She said schools should organize holiday lessons, with district and provincial coordination, because schools close July 26 for July 30 elections and the third term opens early September 4.

In July 2015, NASA’s New Horizons became the first spacecraft to fly by Pluto, and its extended mission will explore Kuiper Belt Objects. By Jan. 1, 2019, it will arrive at 2014 MU69, nicknamed “Ultima Thule” through a public campaign. MU69, about 1.6 billion km beyond Pluto, is expected to be the most primitive object observed by a spacecraft and the farthest encounter in space exploration. It was selected as a potential destination for research opportunities and fuel savings. Observations suggest it could be an extreme prolate spheroid or a close/contact binary. The nickname is working; a formal name will be submitted to the IAU after the flyby, depending on whether MU69 is a single body, a binary pair, or multiple objects.

Using exome sequencing data from 454,803 UK Biobank (UKB) and 173,585 Geisinger MyCode (GHS) participants, the study generated large CHIP callsets across 23 recurrently mutated genes, identifying 29,669 variants in 27,331 UKB individuals (6%) and 14,766 variants in 12,877 GHS individuals (7.4%). DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, and TP53 were most commonly mutated; prevalence reached about 15% by age 75. CHIP carriers were older and more likely heavy smokers, and women had higher CHIP odds in UKB but not GHS.

Common-variant GWAS in UKB found 27 loci (24 novel) with 57 independent variants; 53 signals were directionally consistent in GHS. Rare-variant and gene-burden ExWAS identified 20 rare variants at 3 loci and 5 genes: ATM, CHEK2, CTC1, CLPTM1L, and KDELC2. Gene-specific analyses found shared, unique, and opposing effects across CHIP subtypes; TCL1A increased DNMT3A-CHIP but reduced TET2- and ASXL1-CHIP; PARP1 and LY75 variants reduced DNMT3A-CHIP; JAK2 46/1 increased JAK2-CHIP. Rare variants in NEURL4 and PML were associated with TP53-CHIP, and NFE2 variants with JAK2-/DNMT3A-CHIP.

CHIP was distinct from mosaic chromosomal alterations but enriched for mCAs and shared genetic factors with mLOY and mLOX. ExWAS also identified rare variant and gene burden associations for mCAaut, mLOY, mLOX, and telomere length. Phenotypic analyses linked high-VAF CHIP to COVID-19 hospitalization and severe infection. Longitudinal analyses found high-VAF CHIP associated with CVD, blood cancers, myeloid more than lymphoid cancers, lung/prostate/breast cancers, and all-cause mortality. TET2-CHIP had greatest blood cancer risk; DNMT3A-CHIP had modest risk unless additional CHIP mutations were present. DNMT3A-CHIP PRS predicted myeloid, lung, and prostate cancers and other CHIP subtypes. The previously reported IL6R protective effect in the first 50K UKB exomes was not found in the full cohort. The study concludes that CHIP is a composite of somatic mutation-driven subtypes with shared and distinct genetic etiologies and clinical risks, and notes lack of serial sampling as a limitation.

Attacking runs in soccer are off-the-ball movements by offensive players other than the ball carrier into open space among, between, or behind defenders to receive a pass. They are spontaneous actions in normal play, as opposed to designed runs for crosses or planned runs for free kicks or set plays. Open space is area not occupied or effectively covered by defenders; recognizing or creating it is a first key, and the ball carrier must recognize the run and pass properly. Seven components are recognizing open space, choosing an appropriate run, breaking away from a defender, getting open, timing the run, receiving an optimal pass, and communications. Named runs include bending, checking, diagonal, hooking, inside, lateral, onside, outlet, sideline, straight, through, and wide runs. The passage also describes techniques, communication methods, a coaching progression using cones and defenders, and tips such as rewarding good runs with good passes and staying involved.

The passage is a transcript of questions to James vanRiemsdyk, Kyle Turris, Patrick Kane, Sam Gagner, Keaton Ellerby, and Karl Alzner about their hockey backgrounds, college choices, NHL draft possibilities, family, coaches, and experiences. They are congratulated and wished luck in Columbus, with media interviews mentioned.

The passage describes the “Clock” offense as a way to attack a Diamond & One defense by placing the Star player in the middle and using 1-3-1-like actions. It details basic rotations, corner pass-and-cut options, ball reversal, post feeds, dribble clears, high-post inside triangle actions, and offensive rebounding advantages. It also covers implementation, scouting, and defensive reads, and notes that Diamond & One uses four zone defenders and one chaser denying the opponent’s scoring ace.

The passage argues that the education sector spends billions designing programs, products, and policies but almost nothing designing the stories that help people understand them, so good ideas stall when old narratives win. It describes public defaults—reforms as top-down control, data as danger, and technology as replacing people—and proposes treating narrative like R&D: frame, test, iterate, and scale. Examples include reframing standards and testing as signposts for student success and an AI pilot as a teaching assistant. It advises leaders to lead with shared values, give concrete pictures and mechanisms, show teachers and students, address risks, and avoid traps such as “silver bullet” or “us vs. them” framing. It concludes that trust is rebuilt through design choices and that narrative infrastructure must be funded, tested, and shipped alongside innovations.

The Texas Supreme Court issued a tentative opinion that the ABA should no longer have final say over Texas bar exam eligibility and licensure. It sought comments by Dec. 1 on a proposal undermining ABA oversight, with proposed changes to be enacted in January. The ABA says it is reviewing and will comment.

The Las Vegas Aces lead the Phoenix Mercury 3-0 in the WNBA Finals after a 90-88 Game 3 win and can complete a sweep in Game 4 on Friday. Las Vegas stayed ahead through coach Becky Hammon’s defensive schemes, including zone and junk defenses, timely reserve scoring from Evans and Jewell Loyd, and its core of A’ja Wilson, Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray. Phoenix rallied from 17 points down to tie Game 3 at 88-88 with 1:01 left but lost; Wilson had 34 points and 14 rebounds. Mercury’s Sabally is out for Game 4 with a concussion. The Aces, seeking their third WNBA championship, were around .500 for the first 2½ months before a 16-game winning streak.

Akure-based lawyer Morakinyo Ogele gave the EFCC a seven-day ultimatum to publicly apologize to the Sun Newspaper’s management for invading its premises and said it should compensate the media organization; the headline cites a N1b compensation demand.

Police in Guilford and Milford, Conn., warn residents to lock car doors after thieves targeted dozens of vehicles nightly along the shoreline. In Guilford, cars were hit in Mulberry Point and River Street; officials say groups of youths steal property and sometimes cars when keys are left inside. Output capacitance can be determined by two calculations: capacitance for maximum allowable voltage deviation during worst-case load transient and capacitance for output voltage ripple. The larger value should be selected. With target ripple of 2% and maximum deviation of 2.5%, at least 1.3 mF is required, considering capacitor derating for aging, temperature, and DC bias. For space-grade designs, radiation-induced SET may require additional capacitance; the design example used about 2.3 mF total. An optional output filter can reduce noise using an additional inductor and ceramic capacitance placed after the main output inductor, with the filter inductor before bulk output capacitance. If high-frequency peaking occurs, a damping resistor can be used. The converter begins cycle-by-cycle limiting near 35 A, giving about 45% margin over 24.25 A peak inductor current; primary current is sensed at CS_ILIM, accounting for turns ratio, using a 1:100 current sense transformer to calculate RCS.

Quantum-correlated pairs are crucial resources for quantum information science, including distributed computation, communication, and metrology. Entangled photon pairs and photon-matter qubit pairs support quantum protocols and hybrid networks. Phonons, similar to photons, are promising for solid-state quantum devices and communication interfaces due to coherent interactions. Advances include ground-state cooling, Fock-state manipulation, oscillator entanglement, transducers, and nonclassical phonon states. However, generating nonclassical phonon pairs via optical control is challenging due to weak single-photon optomechanical coupling and underdeveloped high-order nonlinearity. A method is presented for generating quantum-correlated phonon pairs from an optomechanical crystal nanobeam cavity using effective high-order optomechanical nonlinearity, with simultaneous Stokes and anti-Stokes interactions in one pulse. Analogous to SPDC, effective optomechanical SFWM creates a degenerate correlated phonon pair, retrieved by a second red-detuned pulse and verified by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, potentially enabling mechanical quantum computing.

This work describes electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and a sub-pixel shift-and-add pattern reconstruction algorithm applied to direct electron detector (DED) patterns. EBSD was performed on silicon with a TruePix Timepix-based detector (256x256 pixels, 55 µm pitch) at 20 keV in electron counting mode. Four experiments compared standard detector distance, increased exposure, frame integration, and camera retraction. Pattern quality was evaluated by signal-to-noise ratio from FFT radial profiles. The super-resolution method improved pattern quality and angular information, increasing SNR from 30 to 70 at ~1 s effective exposure, and was superior to an equivalent-dose single pattern. The up-sampled pattern showed comparable features to camera retraction and BWKD simulation. The method requires no hardware modification and may aid pattern analysis, including HR-EBSD and indexing challenges.

This report provides an overview of newcomer education in California and recommendations to improve student outcomes, informed by a CDE data request, interviews with staff from 12 California school districts, a literature review, and the author’s experience. Reliable national data on language proficiency or socioeconomic status are unavailable. Newcomers are often considered a subgroup of English learners but have different profiles and needs, and they lack safeguards comparable to those for foster youth and special education students. California schools struggle to meet their needs due to lack of expertise, resources, systems, community connections, and dedicated funding, resulting in poor outcomes, especially for high school newcomers.

Backtesting simulates a trading strategy against historical market data to assess its accuracy, profitability, and risk without risking real capital. It relies on accurate, comprehensive, and relevant historical data and can help traders define strategy parameters, evaluate risk, refine risk-adjusted returns, and account for trading costs. The passage states that backtesting results cannot guarantee future success and that limitations include survivorship bias, look-ahead bias, overfitting, transaction costs, and slippage. It recommends including delisted or failed assets, using diverse datasets, out-of-sample testing, realistic cost estimates, and sensitivity analysis. It also mentions forward testing, scenario analysis, paper trading, and metrics such as the Sharpe ratio and maximum drawdown for validation and evaluation.

In Skrainka v. Allen, plaintiffs sought execution against Allen as a stockholder in the Illinois and St. Louis Bridge Company for unpaid stock to satisfy a judgment against the corporation. The court held that creditors must be preferred to stockholders, and that personal profits diminishing the common fund must be held for the corporation until creditors are paid. Stockholders receiving bonus stock or second-mortgage bonds in connection with calls were liable to creditors for unpaid stock to the amount realized by sale of the bonds; a corporation could not increase its liabilities by issuing second-mortgage bonds to stockholders without valuable consideration. In a statutory motion against a stockholder, liability was measured by the shares owned at the date of the motion after notice, not at the date of the return of the execution. The circuit court’s ruling on liability for the second-mortgage bond proceeds was affirmed, but because it used the return date, the judgment was reversed and remanded.

The passage describes the 3-3-5 defense as a high-risk, high-reward scheme derived from pressure and athletic defenders, used as a sub-package or base defense. It uses 3 defensive linemen, 3 inside linebackers, and 5 defensive backs, and is also called a 3-5-3 or 3-3 stack. It relies on faster, athletic players, sometimes by moving bigger linebackers to the line and bigger defensive backs to linebacker. Its strengths include flexibility, versatility, disguising Cover 1 and Cover 3 from the same shell, adding rushers, and adjusting to formations. Its weaknesses include vulnerable edges, such as against Buck Sweep and outside zone. Offenses attack it through seams, the edge, four verts, and trips formations. Common blitzes include the Sam Blitz and SAW Blitz. Common coverages include Cover 1 and Cover 3. Joe Lee Dunn is credited as the inventor, with Matt Campbell and Iowa State, Tony Gibson at North Carolina State, and prep coach Tim Racki among users. Coach John Grayson has a video series and playbook on the defense.

New York’s Early Intervention Program providers have not received a substantive raise in three decades, and some reimbursement rates are lower than when the program began in the 1990s. Mounting evidence suggests not all protein sources are equal, and dietary guidelines that treat whole-food proteins as equivalent may need updating. U.S. adults generally eat enough protein but may not get the right mix. Protein quality depends on essential amino acid composition and bioavailability; animal foods such as meat, dairy and eggs typically contain higher-quality proteins than plant foods such as legumes, nuts and seeds. Studies found greater muscle protein synthesis after animal-product meals than plant meals, and EAA-9 scoring indicates more peanut butter or legumes may be needed to match an egg. Older adults are especially vulnerable to inadequate high-quality protein, which can lead to muscle loss, weakness and sarcopenia. Experts say people do not necessarily need more meat; they can adjust plant-based protein amounts, food combinations and preparation. Guidelines could focus on essential amino acids, and the Netherlands is cited as reorienting guidance around plant-based diets while addressing high-quality protein needs.

The article recounts results on transformer expressivity at the intersection of logic, automata, and circuit complexity. It defines formal transformer models varying attention, positional information, masking, and precision. Key results: UHAT with positional encodings is strictly subsumed in AC0; FO[Mon] is expressible by UHAT with positional encodings and by masked UHATs with finite-image positional encodings; masked NoPE-UHAT coincides with FO and star-free languages; Palindrome is in UHAT with positional encodings; verification of masked UHAT with no positional encodings is decidable and EXPSPACE-complete. AHAT languages are in TC0; Counting LTL with unary numerical predicates is in AHAT with positional encodings; Kt[#] is expressible by masked NoPE-AHAT; NoPE-AHAT recognizes precisely permutation-invariant languages with semi-algebraic Parikh images, and its emptiness problem is undecidable. The article also discusses limitations: unclear relations between hard and soft attention, AHAT[U] as a promising approximation of softmax transformers, and distinctions between expressibility and trainability, including PARITY and the RASP-L conjecture.

The lecture addresses gender, discrimination, and identity. It covers reasons to study gender differences: equality/fairness, efficiency/productivity losses from discrimination, learning about preference and personality formation, and equal reward for equal output. It reviews the gender wage gap, noting women earn less than men for equal work; gaps have fallen but remain about 20–30%. Female labor market gains are attributed to reduced education gaps, technological innovations, labor demand shifts toward services, and lower discrimination. Blind orchestra auditions fostered impartiality and increased women in orchestras. Bertrand and Mullainathan found higher callback rates for white-sounding names. Sarsons found female surgeons were punished more for adverse events, including spillovers to other female surgeons, and rewarded less for good outcomes than male surgeons. Algorithms can be biased if trained on biased human decisions but can be designed to reduce bias. Gender identity norms, such as men earning more than wives, are linked to missing mass just above 50% wife income share, less marriage/stability, divorce, reduced work by wives, and more nonmarket childcare. Childbirth creates long-run child penalties for women in earnings, hours, and wages; gender-neutral tenure clock policies reduced female tenure rates and increased male tenure rates. Bursztyn et al. found unmarried female MBA students reported lower ambition when peers, especially single male peers, could observe. Vesterlund et al. found women were more likely to volunteer for and be asked to do non-promotable tasks, and more likely to comply when asked, amplifying differences. The lecture concludes persistent gender gaps remain, with biased beliefs and identity concerns playing major roles.

The device moves from ACQ to CONV on the rising edge of CONVST/CS; conversion uses an internal clock and ignores CONVST/CS transitions until tconv completes, then enters ACQ. The host monitors RVS for a low-to-high transition or waits tconv_max. Programming uses nine configuration registers and supports data write and data read. A data transfer frame begins on the CONVST/CS falling edge and ends on the subsequent rising edge; the SCLK counter determines short, optimal, or long frames. Input commands are 32 bits, with HWORD commands ignoring the LSB of the 9-bit address. Output data depends on DATA_VAL bits and issued READ or READ_HWORD commands, with optional appended flags. Data transfer protocols include legacy SPI-compatible and source-synchronous (SRC) modes, with single or dual SDO-x options. Register maps cover DEVICE_ID, reset/power control, SDI/SDO control, data output control, range selection, and alarm threshold/status registers. Application information describes the ADS868xW as a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated AFE and reference for industrial analog input modules, including a design with ADS8681W and MUX36D08, alarm threshold and hysteresis functions, power supply decoupling, NAP/power-down modes, and layout recommendations.

This study co-produced a community-based active case-finding approach with people with lived experience of Long Covid to identify probable Long Covid cases without formal clinical diagnosis and to understand barriers and stigma to support and care. It formed part of the NIHR STIMULATE-ICP study. A Community Advisory Board contributed to design, documents, and dissemination. The study took place in Camden, Merton, and Derbyshire; leaflets were disseminated through community organisations, local authorities, and social prescribing teams. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with people with probable Long Covid. Thematic analysis identified four themes: uncertainty and Long Covid awareness; barriers to engagement with healthcare; experiences and perceptions of stigma and discrimination; and sources of support. Findings indicated lack of awareness, self-doubt, hesitancy seeking care, multi-system symptoms, perceived discrimination, and enacted, anticipated, and internalised stigma as barriers. Participants also accessed treatment outside the NHS, valued social and community support, and desired changes to primary care and dedicated Long Covid services. The authors conclude that intersecting barriers and stigma congruent with epistemic injustice can prevent people with Long Covid from obtaining diagnosis, treatment, or care, and call for awareness raising, stigma mitigation, listening to lived experience, and signposting to early help.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture improves memory, display, video, VR, rendering, and AI features. Its memory subsystem uses GDDR6 with a redesigned interface, 14 Gbps signaling, 20% power efficiency improvement over GDDR5X, larger/faster L2 caches, and lossless compression, delivering about 50% higher effective bandwidth than Pascal. The display/video engine supports higher resolutions, refresh rates, HDR, DisplayPort 1.4a, DSC 1.2, 8K at 60 Hz, HEVC 8K encode at 30 fps, and updated NVDEC. VirtualLink/USB-C provides power, display, and data for VR headsets through one connector. NVLink replaces MIO/PCIe for SLI on TU102 and TU104, enabling higher bandwidth and new display topologies, with two-way SLI supported. Turing adds RT Cores for real-time ray tracing, hybrid rendering, BVH traversal, ray/triangle intersection, denoising, and RTX software. NGX uses Tensor Cores for AI features including DLSS, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Mesh Shading adds Task and Mesh Shaders; Variable Rate Shading allows per-16x16 shading rates; Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling; Multi-View Rendering supports multiple views per pass. Resource management includes bindless CBVs/UAVs and Tier 2 resource heaps. VR features include VirtualLink, MVR, foveated rendering, and RT Core-accelerated VRWorks Audio. The passage also details TU104, Tesla T4, TU106 specifications and the RTX-OPS workload-based metric, plus ray tracing mechanics, BVH, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections.

The 3 Days Down Overnight Trading Strategy tracks the S&P 500 for three consecutive down days, entering at the third day’s close and exiting at the next day’s open. Backtesting showed 661 trades, a 0.13% average gain, 65% win rate, and 8% maximum drawdown, excluding slippage and commissions. Exiting at the next close raised average gain to 0.24% but lowered win rate to 61% and increased drawdown to 17%, with 5% CAGR and 8% time in market. A modified March 2022 version had a 0.35% average gain, 60% win rate, and 10% drawdown; in the 2022 bear market, it made 35 trades averaging 0.3%. It also works for QQQ and many stocks, though less well than for the S&P 500.

In 1886, a bill authorized a $2,000,000 loan pledging Kingdom revenues, opposed by the U.S. under reciprocity treaty privileges. In early 1887, a proposed political alliance between the Hawaiian and Samoan Kings was brought to the U.S.; Mr. Bayard withheld approval as inexpedient. On December 23, 1887, Britain gave Mr. Bayard a memorandum binding England and France by the 1843 convention to consider the Sandwich Islands independent, proposing a formal declaration for neutrality and equal harbor access, with the U.S., England, and Germany guaranteeing this. On February 15, 1888, Bayard replied that existing U.S.-Hawaii treaties created reciprocities and inhibited cession of Hawaiian territory, so U.S. participation seemed unnecessary; the Pearl Harbor concession did not impair Hawaiian sovereignty. Britain’s chief motive was not evident but connected to prior events. The British commissioner at Honolulu protested the Pearl River Harbor concession, arguing it conflicted with Britain’s treaty and would lead to loss of Hawaiian independence; U.S.-Hawaiian notes stated Article II did not subtract jurisdiction or confer property/exclusive commercial rights and would terminate with the 1875 treaty.

The article explains the double-down trading strategy: adding another position to a losing trade, usually doubling the position when the stock price falls, to improve the average entry price and recover losses. It gives an Amazon example where buying another 100 shares after a decline allows breakeven on a smaller rebound. It notes the strategy can fail if the price keeps declining and focuses on price rather than odds. It differs from scale-in, Martingale, and repair strategies. Backtests indicate doubling down tends to work in mean-reverting assets like SPY, improving average gain but reducing trades and carrying ruin risk, while it worsens results in trending assets like HYG. The conclusion is that doubling down sometimes works in mean-reverting assets and not in trending assets, but it is rarely part of a rational trading plan and is often a trading bias.

GA102 GPUs use NVIDIA’s third-generation NVLink interface with four x4 links, each providing 14.0625 GB/sec in each direction; four links provide 56.25 GB/sec each direction and 112.5 GB/sec total between two GPUs. Two A40 or RTX A6000 GPUs can connect via NVLink to scale 48GB to 96GB; two RTX 3090 GPUs can connect for SLI, with 3-Way and 4-Way SLI unsupported. GA10x features PCIe Gen 4, up to 16 GT/s, x16 up to 64 GB/sec. The full GA102 has seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, 168 FP64 units, and 112 ROPs; it has twelve 32-bit memory controllers (384-bit total) and 6144 KB L2. GA10x SMs contain 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, 256 KB register file, four Texture Units, and 128 KB L1/shared memory. The SM has four partitions; FP32 is supported on both datapaths, enabling 128 FP32 operations per clock per SM or 64 FP32 and 64 INT32. L1 cache is 128 KB per SM, with double shared memory bandwidth versus Turing. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection testing and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit for motion blur; async compute allows concurrent RT and graphics/compute. Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32, BF16, sparsity, and up to 2x matrix multiplication; DLSS uses a 9x Super Resolution factor. GDDR6X memory uses PAM4, up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec; EDR detects and replays memory errors. RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and decompression with DirectStorage. The A40 is a data center GPU with 48GB, scalable to 96GB via NVLink, PCIe Gen4, vGPU, DP1.4, Quadro Sync, and EGX support. Display support includes 4K120 and 8K60, DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, DSC 1.2a, and HDCP 2.3. Fifth-generation NVDEC supports AV1 decode; seventh-generation NVENC handles H.264 and HEVC. RTX A6000 has GA102, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 48GB GDDR6, and NVLink to 96GB.

A persistent heat wave is affecting parts of the Northern Hemisphere, setting weather records in Canada, the U.S., Europe, and the Middle East. Montreal reached 37 C on July 2, and officials blamed heat and humidity for at least 11 deaths; the U.S. reported at least one heat-related death and investigated another. Ottawa’s Canada Day humidex was 47, Denver tied 40 C, Motherwell in Scotland hit 33.2 C, and Oman’s Quriyat stayed above 42.6 C for 51 hours. A climate scientist linked the duration and extremeness of heat waves to climate change.

The President transmits correspondence between Hawaiian agents and the Secretary of State. He reports that the Sandwich Islands are progressing in civilization and civil government, serve as an important Pacific stopping and provisioning place, and are visited heavily by U.S. vessels, especially whalers. The passage covers low-side current sensing using an amplifier and high-speed comparator to amplify shunt resistor voltage, with comparator state changing at the over-current threshold. Design requirements include a logic-high alert when amplifier output exceeds 1.1V and configuration as in Figure 7-7. It emphasizes low-ESR 0.1µF bypass capacitors near supply pins to prevent ringing, false triggers, and oscillations. Devices can use split or single supplies, with input range limits and split-supply output swinging to V-. Layout guidance includes minimizing output-input coupling, series resistors, and controlled impedance traces. It also lists documentation updates, support resources, trademarks, ESD caution, revision history, packaging/orderable information, and TI legal disclaimers.

The Oppo R15 and Vivo X21 launches suggest what to expect from the OnePlus 6, as OnePlus, Oppo, and Vivo are BBK Electronics companies with often similar designs. The passage reviews the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card, calling it a no-frills option for people seeking relief from interest or financing a large purchase. It offers 0% intro APR for 21 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74% variable APR. Students’ FAFSA information has become harder for scholarship providers to access because of colleges’ data privacy concerns stemming from changes to FAFSA. The Education Department’s transition to the Student Aid Index, which takes some data directly from the IRS, made some FAFSA information subject to IRS privacy rules and created confusion about what aid offices can share. A NASFAA survey found many financial aid offices were unwilling to share federal tax data even with student consent, and some ended or modified data-sharing agreements. Native Forward’s scholarship funds were delayed, and other providers reported difficulty accessing cost of attendance, award details, and unmet need, causing postponements or uncertainty. The Education Department issued guidance stating colleges can share federal income tax and other FAFSA data with scholarship organizations with student consent, and that two designated organizations can receive tax information directly without consent. Questions and pending security standards remain; providers seek streamlined consent and standardized data-sharing.

The passage recommends removing the tariff on anthracite coal and placing it on the free list, saying this would have little effect except in crises. It calls for elasticity in the monetary system so interest rates can be equalized and financial stringencies prevented, with banks furnishing and maintaining adequate circulation. It says reconstructing the financial system is unwise and unnecessary now, but additional legislation is desirable; future legislation should encourage instrumentalities that automatically supply legitimate circulation and make all money interchangeable and convertible into the gold standard. It urges passage of a proper immigration law. On labor and capital, it says corporate and labor federations can do good and evil; opposition should target bad conduct, not organizations as such. Each must obey law, respect individual freedom, justice, and fair dealing, and employers and workers should appreciate each other’s viewpoint. It warns against class animosity and says government should judge individuals on their merits, favoring the upright rich or poor.

Each Christmas season, volunteers count birds and species within a 15-mile diameter circle for one day, contributing to ornithology’s longest-running database. Sheridan’s count is Dec. 14; Story-Big Horn’s is Dec. 23. Counts are open to all skill levels.

This paper discusses the IoT and a possible new productivity paradox, tracing debates from the ICT “productivity paradox” to Internet-initiated paradoxes and the emergence of uncaptured GDP. It identifies sources of uncaptured GDP including online intermediaries, consumer surplus, disruptive new goods and services, and online piracy. It then examines the shift from PoT to IoT and the role of digital business strategies and trust-based ICT-driven disruptive business models. Using an empirical analysis of 500 global ICT firms over 2005–2016, the paper finds that high R&D-intensive firms face declining marginal productivity of ICT and seek to activate a self-propagating function through functionality development and soft innovation resources, corresponding to increasing dependency on uncaptured GDP. It concludes with findings and suggestions for global ICT firms’ transformation toward an IoT-based society, including recognizing uncaptured GDP, pursuing sophisticated self-propagating functions, and utilizing soft innovation resources.

The video discusses nuclear binding energies, starting from solar-system nuclear abundances and questions about nuclear stability. Binding energy is calculated by summing proton, neutron, and electron masses and subtracting the nuclear mass. A plot of average binding energy per nucleon versus mass number is fairly stable at 7.5–9 MeV, with a maximum near iron; moving toward lower-energy states enables fission and fusion. The binding energy curve is parameterized by the semi-empirical Weizsäcker formula, also called the liquid-drop model. Its terms are volume, surface, Coulomb, asymmetry, and pairing. The volume term dominates and implies a short-range nuclear force; surface and Coulomb terms reduce binding energy, while asymmetry and pairing terms involve Pauli exclusion and even/odd proton and neutron numbers.

The passage announces Colonel Alfred McCormack’s appointment as Special Assistant to the Secretary of State in Charge of Research and Intelligence on September 27, 1945. Research indicates Uber's iPhone app had a unique Apple-granted entitlement allowing it to secretly record users' screens, reportedly to improve Apple Watch functionality. Sudo Security Group found no other third-party developer had such access. Uber says Apple gave the permission years earlier because Apple Watch couldn't handle map rendering; newer app versions voluntarily removed it. There is no suggestion Uber used it improperly. People who drink more than one glass of wine nightly may be “chronic alcoholics,” researchers say. In New South Wales, 27% of Australians aged 55 to 64 consume alcohol at risky levels, and medical professionals are concerned about the drinking culture. Daily drinkers face increased risks of pancreatitis, liver disease, obesity, and alcoholic dementia. Drinkers should take at least a few days off weekly and have no more than two drinks most days. Alcohol increases cancer risk from the first sip, older people are less aware of safe units, and cheap supermarket drink has affected baby boomers. The two-standard-drink daily limit is not an average.

U.S. imports from China were large, sometimes $9,000,000, and exports to China were an interesting, growing part of U.S. commerce. In 1841 direct U.S. exports were $715,000 in domestic products and $485,000 in foreign merchandise, with indirect trade not shown. President Tyler recommended Congress fund a commissioner to reside in China to protect American interests. The overlap sends an unmarked player from the back into the attack, usually a wing fullback running along the sideline past the midfielder. If the overlapping player is marked, another attacker may be left free, and teammates should get that player the ball. It is not a vertical offensive switch because the midfielder stays in the attack. Overlaps are usually near the sideline for space, width, and a clear vertical lane, and are initiated by the fullback. The usual result is a cross by the overlapping player or a pass to the midfielder if covered. An underlap has the fullback run inside the midfielder, usually leading to a shot or pass. After the play changes, the back defender returns. The passage also notes central overlaps are infrequent, suggests varying overlap and underlap, and describes communication and possible back-heel use.

In Ross Nelson v. Peter John, the plaintiff sought specific performance of an 1892 contract by John Salerhand and his wife, Puyallup Indians, to convey allotted land patented in 1886 subject to treaty restrictions on alienation. The court affirmed judgment for the defendant. It held the restrictions valid; the Bland Act did not impliedly repeal them; and contracts by Puyallup Indians before removal of the restrictions were void. The Act of Congress of March 3, 1893, consenting to removal, provided removal would not take effect until ten years after passage.

The US government auctioned the seized 106-meter superyacht Amadea, which the Justice Department said was taken from a Russian oligarch in Fiji in 2022. The new owner and price were not disclosed; the sealed bid auction closed September 10. It was valued at least $300 million when seized, later appraised near $230 million. The yacht has six decks and luxury features. US holding costs reached nearly $1 million monthly. Ownership is contested: Khudainatov claimed ownership, a judge ruled him a straw owner, and he appealed; his lawyer called the auction improper and premature. The passage presents an SEIR-like model for SARS-CoV-2 spread with nine compartments: susceptible, exposed, vaccinated, asymptomatic infectious, mildly infectious, severely infectious, critically infectious, recovered, and deceased. It uses a time-dependent transmission parameter, with severe, critical, and asymptomatic transmission rates parameterized from the mildly infectious rate. The article analyzes the direct and inverse problems, including well-posedness, non-negativity, continuity, differentiability, and estimation of the transmission parameter from reported daily infections using Tikhonov-type regularization. It also describes the model, theoretical results, and a numerical example with real data.

Researchers at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis found that peroxisomes in brown fat act as a backup heat source, burning fuel and releasing heat through ACOX2, especially when mitochondria lack uncoupling protein 1. The involved fatty acids are found in dairy, human breast milk, and certain gut microbes, suggesting possible dietary, probiotic, nutraceutical, or drug approaches. The studies were in mice, though prior evidence suggests the pathway may be relevant in people.

Gamma-ray bursts are linked to catastrophic events such as compact-object mergers or massive-star collapse. Core collapse of stars above ≈8 M☉ can form a neutron star or black hole, and accretion may launch a relativistic jet. Stripped progenitors can yield Type Ib/c supernovae and long GRBs, while hydrogen-rich RSG/BSG progenitors may choke the jet. Choked jets are suppressed in gamma rays but may produce shock breakout, X-ray/UV flashes, UV/optical transients, and high-energy neutrinos. This work focuses on RMHD simulations of massive BSG/RSG progenitors with extended envelopes to study jet propagation, shock formation, and cocoon dynamics. It describes stellar density profiles, the PLUTO 2.5D spherical computational setup, Taub-Matthews equation of state, choking-time estimates, 39,000 1D runs, breakout and choking scaling relations, jet injection parameters, and a shock finder. In a preliminary RMHD simulation of a BSG with R*=50 R☉, M*=15 M☉, Ljet=10^51 erg/s, Γ0=7, σ=10^-2, θ0=2°, and te=5 s, the jet head reached ≈0.03 R* by 5 s and the cocoon expanded to ≈0.004 R*. Shocks included the external cocoon shock, termination shock, and collimation shock. After engine shutdown, no choking occurred within the simulated time; the collimation shock faded, the cocoon shock accelerated, and at 30 s the forward shock and residual termination shock remained. The jet chokes about a minute after launch. Strong shocks occur at the jet core and external cocoon, and after shutdown dominant acceleration sites shift outward. Future work will derive spectra and light curves for photons and neutrinos and extend the parameter study.

The lecture continues the massive Sudakov form factor, requiring an additional regulator beyond dimensional regularization for rapidity divergences and producing 1/eta poles and log nu. It gives scale choices for collinear, soft, and hard modes. The factorization theorem includes hard, collinear, and soft functions, with renormalization group evolution in two-dimensional mu-nu space. Anomalous dimensions are derived from counterterms, and path independence relates mu and nu anomalous dimensions. Evolution kernels sum large logarithms and permit scale variation. Examples include gg to Higgs pt distribution, involving rapidity divergences, TMD PDFs, and factorization with hard, gluon PDF, and soft functions. Drell-Yan is discussed kinematically with four cases: q_perp, inclusive, endpoint/threshold, and isolated. Inclusive Drell-Yan matches to four-quark operators and standard PDFs, with a caveat about Glauber gluons. Threshold keeps singular 1-tau terms and uses a soft function and hard function. Isolated Drell-Yan uses hemisphere plus-momentum constraints, SCET I, beam functions, a hemisphere soft function, and matching to PDFs and jet functions. Beam functions are chi-bar chi matrix elements measuring large and small momenta. e+e- dijets/jet broadening is mentioned as another SCET II example.

The lecture reviews encoder/decoder design, error-probability rules, minimum-distance decision regions, and bounds, emphasizing the union bound estimate. It defines effective coding gain as the gap between a signal set and 2-PAM at a fixed bit-error probability in the power-limited regime, with an analogous definition using SNR norm and M-PAM in the bandwidth-limited regime. It relates effective coding gain to nominal coding gain and average nearest neighbors, and gives examples showing 0 dB gain for 2-PAM, 4-QAM, and a two-point subset, and about 1 dB for a four-point three-dimensional signal set. Orthogonal signal sets asymptotically approach the Shannon limit but have spectral efficiency tending to zero and high decoding complexity; simplex and bi-orthogonal sets are also discussed. The lecture previews binary block codes, coding/modulation separation, and a binary-signaling loss of at most 0.2 dB in the power-limited regime.

This study analyzed predictors of intention to comply with COVID-19 preventive measures among 15,131 adult residents in Spain during the first-wave lockdown. Data came from the PSY-COVID online cross-sectional survey, using non-probabilistic snowball sampling. The study examined sociodemographic, personality, prevention behavior/cognition, information, proxy control, vulnerability, and future threat variables. Residents of the Canary Islands had the highest post-confinement prevention behavior intention, while Aragón and the Balearic Islands had the lowest. The final linear mixed model found the most influential predictors were self-efficacy, outcome expectations, general adherence to prevention behaviors, information level, experience with prevention behaviors, perceived vulnerability, proxy control of scientists, and social norm. Perceived severity moderated adherence to prevention behaviors to avoid infection and perceived vulnerability of others. Region had a minor but significant effect. Limitations included online data collection, non-probabilistic sampling, and some low reliability for ad-hoc measures. Implications included promoting self-efficacy, consistent communication, and addressing regional disparities.

The passage discusses Markov cohort-state-transition models (MCSTMs), in which transition probability matrices are key but often limited by data issues such as multiple data sources, unequal observation intervals, and missing transitions. It notes Craig and Sendi’s uniformly weighted EM approach and proposes an optimized weighted EM algorithm. In the proposed method, transition count matrices over s time steps are decomposed into estimated 1-step counts; the M-step recomputes the transition probability matrix from a weighted combination of the observed and estimated 1-step counts, with weights chosen by grid search to minimize the variance of a function of the transition probability matrix, such as the ICER, using bootstrap estimates. A fictitious 3-state Markov model compares SuperDrug with placebo. Based on 5,000 bootstrap samples, the weighted method reduced ICER variance by 15.2% and increased the probability of being cost-effective at £20,000/QALY by 3 percentage points, with similar ICER means. The discussion states the method was feasible without significant estimation bias, may be viable if the C(s) matrices come from the same or similar studies, recommends a stepwise approach when transition probability matrices are not uniquely estimable, and calls for further validation using large clinical trial or real-world data.

Cat tail movements, interpreted with body language, can signal relaxation, dreaming, nervousness, possible aggression, friendliness, or defensiveness. The Tiered Memory Page Migration Operations Guide describes optional extensions to SEV and SNP for Page Migration, which copies page content and updates virtual-to-physical mappings. AMD created the TMPM engine to aid this process. TMPM can pause DMA traffic to a page while content is copied and IOMMU page table entries are updated, and it can migrate SNP-protected guest pages. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement; support is indicated by the ENGINE_READY bit in PM_Status. Commands include PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO for pages that are concurrent DMA targets or SNP hypervisor state pages, and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST for SNP guest pages. Multi-page commands can migrate up to 128 pages using a Page Migration List, with no order-dependence between entries or command lists. A Pre-Migration RMP state uses PS_ASID_VAL. Non-migratable data structures include IOMMU SPA-accessed structures, vIOMMU page tables, pinned buffers, the ring buffer, and argument pages. For PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, source pages must be DMA-mapped using IOMMU host page tables, and only one host page table may map a migrated system physical page. TMPM may modify IOMMU host page table entries non-atomically, so software must avoid concurrent modifications. Performance guidance includes using commands with 16 or more pages and up to 128 pages per command.

The passage addresses EMS response time and the Ambulance Location Problem, an extension of Maximal Covering Location Problems. It notes MCLP can favor densely populated areas, leaving rural areas less covered. The contribution is a real-world ambulance station location case study in a rural area with medium and large cities, conducted for two German city councils reopening obsolete stations, with fairness for equal chance within a guaranteed response time. A multi-criteria integer model maximizes weighted demand covered within r1 and r2 while covering all demand within r3. It was applied to 11 outdated stations in two emergency service areas in Southwest Germany. In one example, 17 potential locations were considered for four stations among 70 municipalities, over 764 km², over 450,000 inhabitants, more than 20,000 roads, and 20,444 road segments, with 30 stations including 13 fixed. Travel times used an OpenStreetMap network and ambulance speed profiles, with radii of 5, 10, and 15 minutes. Gurobi and the ε-constraint method yielded 16 Pareto-optimal solutions. Short response times favored urban locations, while longer times favored even rural distribution. The static model was a first decision stage before simulation. Future work includes investment costs, multiple coverage, and simultaneous provision optimization.

A short squeeze occurs when a heavily shorted stock rises instead of falling, forcing short sellers to buy back borrowed shares at higher prices and pushing the price further up. Such events are rare and random; backtesting a short squeeze strategy is practically impossible, and high short interest stocks underperform. Short selling is difficult because gains are limited to 100% while losses are theoretically unlimited. The opposite is a long or bear squeeze. Short squeezes may be illegal if they involve manipulation of stock price or availability; naked short sales are illegal. They typically last 2–4 weeks, often less than a month, with examples including Volkswagen and GameStop. Exit strategies include monitoring price and short interest and using stop-loss or trailing stops.

This study examined resting-state SEEG data from 43 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients to investigate directional connectivity in epilepsy networks. It estimated within-frequency and cross-frequency information flow using DTF and CFD, estimated 1/f power slope with FOOOF, and used balanced random forest classification. Results showed dominant information flow from non-SOZ to SOZ across multiple frequencies: within-frequency flow from SOZ to non-SOZ was weaker than the reverse, SOZ had higher inward strength, and cross-frequency flow was dominant from non-SOZ high-frequency activity to SOZ low-frequency activity. SOZ electrodes had significantly more negative 1/f power slopes than non-SOZ electrodes, suggesting higher excitability in non-SOZ. Larger within-frequency information-flow asymmetry between SOZ and non-SOZ was associated with favorable seizure outcome. Random forest models using within-frequency connectivity achieved accuracy 0.85 and AUC 0.94 for predicting SOZ, and accuracy 0.77 and AUC 0.78 for predicting seizure outcome when SOZ was clinician-identified; when SOZ was model-estimated, seizure outcome prediction accuracy was 0.72 and AUC 0.75. Limitations included use of clinical SOZ, 10-minute artifact/spike-free interictal epochs, and use of only within-frequency information flow for outcome prediction. The authors concluded that combining resting-state connectivity with a balanced random forest model may help localize SOZ and predict seizure outcome, potentially supplementing traditional SEEG interpretation and reducing prolonged recordings.
