The lecture reviews discrete coding, announces problems 1–7 and 26 due October 14, then contrasts Riemann and Lebesgue integration. Riemann quantizes the time axis; Lebesgue quantizes the value axis and uses measure. It covers measure properties, zero-measure sets, countable and uncountable examples, measurable functions, and the definitions of L1 and L2 functions. It states that non-negative measurable functions always have a Lebesgue integral, finite or infinite, and that finite-duration L2 functions are also L1. The lecture then returns to Fourier series, stating that Fourier coefficients exist for L1/L2 functions over finite intervals and that Fourier series converge in mean (l.i.m.) in an energy sense, not necessarily pointwise. It also discusses segmenting functions into intervals for Fourier-series expansions and introduces the Fourier transform.

The passage proposes a variadic nominal anti-unification technique that handles both binders and variadic expressions. It is presented as useful for program analysis, code clone detection, refactoring, symbolic reasoning, and related areas. The paper defines variadic nominal terms, substitutions, freshness contexts, equivalence, and generalization, then introduces the rule-based VNAU algorithm with proofs of termination, soundness, and completeness. Examples illustrate its use in detecting code clones, including type-2 and type-3 clones, and the passage notes efficiency limitations due to high nondeterminism and limited control over selecting similar parts.

The research examined Hungarian education participants’ knowledge, use, and attitudes toward AI through interviews with high school teachers and university lecturers (N=14) and a questionnaire completed by university students (N=53). Respondents were familiar with many AI tools, used them for tasks such as debugging, explaining steps, searching for information, generating code, creating practice tasks, and summarizing material, and predominantly held a positive attitude (91%) toward AI integration in education.

The study also tested Bard/Gemini, ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot on beginner and complex programming tasks. ChatGPT provided the most correct answers, with 46/50 correct in programming theorem tasks, and solved all complex tasks after additional prompts, while the other tools did not fully solve the C task. The conclusion states that AI can be useful in education when users have sufficient prior knowledge and critical thinking, but without these, unsatisfactory or incorrect responses may mislead learners.

This study examines human–AI interactions in conversational information-seeking (CIS) with ChatGPT. It addresses three levels: users’ prompting strategies, ChatGPT’s communication styles in response to prompts and issue controversy, and how ChatGPT’s communication styles affect users’ AI perceptions and issue-specific attitudes. The authors conducted a 3 (issue: health, science, policy) × 2 (issue controversy: controversial, non-controversial) between-subjects experiment with 937 U.S. adults recruited on Prolific in November 2024. Participants sought issue information from GPT-4o for at least 5 turns. The study analyzed 747 valid conversations, extracting five communication styles (self-revealing, information-seeking, fact-oriented, action-seeking, cognitive complexity), citation count, structure count, and 8 prompting strategies grouped into user-supplied information, style-related requests, and content-related requests. Findings: 19.1% of users used at least one prompting strategy, predicted by education level and party affiliation. Issue controversy drove ChatGPT responses’ communication styles and citation counts, while user prompt communication styles remained consistent across issue controversy. ChatGPT responses’ cognitive complexity influenced AI perceptions and issue-relevant attitude changes; more cognitively complex responses were perceived as less favorable but were associated with more positive issue-relevant attitude changes.

The passage describes features and application guidance for the TPS7H500x-SP controllers. The FAULT pin enables external protections; exceeding 0.6 V typically for a 0.4–1.4 µs pulse causes shutdown, discharging SS and stopping outputs until FAULT falls below 0.5 V, followed by a switching-frequency-dependent delay before soft start. Slope compensation via RSC mitigates subharmonic oscillation, with recommended 1×m. The controllers use fixed-frequency peak current mode control and can apply Type 2A or Type 2B compensation. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C and restarts below 160°C. Application guidance includes a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull GaN converter design with component calculations, plus power-supply and layout recommendations. Revision history and packaging/orderable information are also provided.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture. It explains that GEMM operations compute D = A * B + C and are central to neural network training and inference, with problem size denoted as m-by-n-by-k. A100 Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, INT4, binary, TF32, BF16, and FP64; TF32 is used by default for AI training, while FP16 or BF16 mixed precision offers maximum training speed. Sparse MMA with 2:4 structured sparsity doubles Tensor Core compute throughput. Memory features include 40 GB HBM2, 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, 40 MB L2 cache, ECC, and 192 KB/SM combined L1/shared memory. A100 adds MIG, partitioning one GPU into up to seven isolated GPU Instances. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, and PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV is supported. CUDA 11 includes Task Graphs, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and Cooperative Groups. DGX A100 contains eight A100 GPUs, delivers 5 PFLOPS, uses NVSwitch and Mellanox ConnectX-6 HDR InfiniBand, and runs an NGC software stack. The passage also includes a sparsity primer on fine-grained structured sparsity and accuracy results.

An MIT OpenCourseWare lecture by Hong Liu on holographic duality covers course logistics: no textbook or recitation, Monday office hours, online materials, no exam, grades based 75% on about five PSETs due every two weeks and 25% on an 8–10 page final project on holographic duality. The outline is ambitious and flexible. The lecture introduces the proposal that quantum gravity equals field theories on a fixed spacetime, requiring a dictionary between them, and discusses gravity’s emergence, Sakharov’s idea, and hydrodynamics analogies. It presents the Weinberg-Witten theorem: a Lorentz-covariant conserved current forbids massless charged particles of spin greater than 1/2, and a Lorentz-covariant conserved stress tensor forbids massless particles of spin greater than 1, assuming the particles live in the same spacetime. Holographic duality avoids the theorem because gravity does not live in the same spacetime as the original theory. The lecture sketches the theorem’s proof using massless one-particle states and helicity.

The text presents BioRecall, a protocol for a biobank-recall study that collects lifestyle and environmental exposures and combines them with genotypes, biological samples, and clinical outcomes. It addresses gene-environment interactions and gaps in biobank lifestyle/environmental data. The pilot invites Central Finland Biobank donors with type 2 diabetes, available genome-wide DNA data, and recall consent to complete an electronic questionnaire via MyBiobank; 1,386 candidates are eligible. The questionnaire covers current and past lifestyles, anthropometrics, weight loss history, health, symptoms, work characteristics, emotional state, sleep, and residential environment; postcode data allow spatial environmental linkage. Data will be pseudonymized and returned to the biobank. Ethics and biobank approvals are reported. If successful, the study will expand to other donors and Finnish biobanks. Strengths include electronic scalability and automated feedback; limitations include limited sample size, one biobank, and no wearable data.

DNA origami uses DNA base-pairing to self-assemble nanostructures. A team led by Ralf Jungmann reports a super-resolution microscopy method, DNA-PAINT, that visualizes individual strands in DNA origami. Using a flat rectangular structure, they found assembly is robust under a wide range of conditions, though incorporation efficiency depends on the position of a strand’s target sequence. DNA-PAINT uses dye-linked imager strands that bind transiently and repetitively, producing blinking signals. Variations in physical parameters have little effect on overall quality; additional staple strands can enhance efficiency, but not all sites are occupied. The method may optimize DNA nanostructure construction and aid quantitative structural biology.

The paper studies modal extensions of lattice semantics, where valuations and non-modal connectives are based on lattices rather than the two-valued Boolean algebra. Necessity is generally interpreted as the greatest lower bound of values in accessible worlds. Motivation includes interpreting truth values of one logic within another, counterlogical statements, and computer systems where states use different algebraic properties. The work is limited to structures where every world operates in a single lattice semantics.

After background on lattice semantics, the paper defines modal extensions, regularity, and normal modal valuations. It proves that for a complete lattice and designated values F, the normal modal valuation yields a unique regular modal extension iff inf F ∈ F and F is a filter. For finite lattices, the normal extension is regular iff F is a filter. Infinite cases include fuzzy [0,1] and Boolean algebras with non-principal ultrafilters, where regularity can fail.

The paper then relates modal validities to lattice properties. With a top value and a specified implication, any designated set is implicative. F being implicative is equivalent to every frame satisfying (□φ∨□ψ)→□(φ∨ψ). For strictly deductive implication, a complete lattice is linear outside F iff every frame satisfies axiom K. For implication defined as −x+y in anti-monotone, involutive, down-distributive lattices, F is implicative iff every frame satisfies K. An example uses twist algebras for Nelson logic and paraconsistent systems, showing a filter condition for K. Final remarks note connections between linearity/negation properties and K, shared order for cross-logical communication, and interest in the finite-model property.

Modeling noisy, high-dimensional, nonlinear systems is active research; transfer operator theory and RKHSs are approaches for informative algorithms. DMD discretizes the Koopman operator as a Galerkin method blending PCA and the discrete-time Fourier transform, based on eigenvalue decomposition from linear regression. GP regression is a kernel regression framework providing accurate function estimation from noisy targets, probabilistic predictions, and model selection. The work transfers GP features to DMD, develops a Bayesian interpretation of the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator, and modifies Extended DMD to construct models from noisy measurement data of nonlinear dynamical systems and provide uncertainty estimates for multi-step predictions. It aims to apply variational free energy to kernel Koopman operators to balance generalization error and computational complexity. The algorithm is a special case of EDMD and inherits some EDMD limitations. EDMD lacks hyperparameter/dictionary optimization, uncertainty-aware predictions, and measurement noise handling; the amalgamation addresses hyperparameter optimization and sparse dictionary learning. Section 2 introduces Bayesian DMD, Section 3 explores consequences and performance, and Section 4 concludes. Section 2.1 begins a full Bayesian treatment of the embedded PFO, the adjoint of the kernel Koopman operator, using lifted data and isotropic measurement noise.

This work develops an Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) machine learning potential for YBCO trained on DFT data including defects. The potential captures equilibrium and non-equilibrium properties, equation of state, lattice parameters, and oxygen Frenkel pair energetics with high accuracy relative to DFT and improves upon a Buckingham+Coulomb potential. In NPT simulations, it reproduces the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition at about 800 K, with signs of a disordered orthorhombic phase at 700 K, compared with the experimental transition observed at 1000 K. The transition is an order-disorder process in which O atoms migrate from O1 and O4 sites to O5 sites, making the a and b directions equivalent. It is entropy-driven and facilitated by decreasing O Frenkel pair formation energy at expanded lattices. The potential enables investigation of mass transport and may aid annealing strategies for radiation-damaged HTS tapes.

The lecture discusses ion traps and their differences from neutral atoms. Coulomb forces allow electric fields of 100 volts per millimeter to create confinement forces for 10,000 kelvin, while neutral atom traps typically have depths from microkelvin to kelvin. Doppler and evaporative cooling are used, and sideband cooling is special to ions but is also returning to neutral atoms in tight dipole traps.

Science drivers include clocks, precision measurements, quantum information, qubits, quantum algorithms, and quantum simulation, pursued with both neutral atoms and ions. Ions cannot be trapped in stationary electric traps because the divergence of the electric field is zero; dynamic traps are used, except for recent laser-beam ion trapping. Penning traps use electrostatic axial confinement and cyclotron motion; MIT used them for precise mass measurements. RF or Paul traps alternate radio-frequency confinement and anti-confinement. Averaging at fixed position gives zero, but following the trajectory yields an inward force; micromotion provides net trapping, with the harmonic oscillator potential coming from the kinetic energy of micromotion.

The lecture then explains quantum computation with ions, focusing on single-qubit rotations and two-qubit gates. The Cirac-Zoller gate realizes a controlled phase gate using center-of-mass motion as a data bus. The sequence is: cool center-of-mass motion to the ground state; swap ion two’s qubit information into center-of-mass motion; perform a controlled phase gate on ion one; swap the information back. This enables two-qubit operations in an ion chain. The gate is pedagogical but requires ground-state cooling and is limited by the slow center-of-mass motion; other gates exist. The lecture ends the class.

This study investigated race differences in the relationship between blood pressure (BP) and longitudinal cognitive performance. Data came from MARS, MAP, and Black Clinical Core; 2,284 Black or White participants aged ≥55 with at least two cognitive assessments and two BP readings were grouped by race and BP status (normal, high, variable). Cognitive domains included global, episodic memory, semantic memory, working memory, processing speed, and visuospatial ability. Linear mixed effects models adjusted for age, sex, education, and diagnosis. Results showed no racial differences in cognitive decline among those with normal BP. White participants with high BP had faster decline than Black participants in global cognition, processing speed, semantic memory, and working memory. White participants with variable BP had faster decline than all three Black BP groups across global cognition and all five cognitive domains. Exploratory analyses indicated the reduced association between BP and cognitive change in older Black adults was not associated with lower baseline cognitive scores. Limitations included not considering medication adherence or comprehensive medication history. The authors conclude older White adults showed higher susceptibility to cognitive decline with elevated and fluctuating BP than older Black adults.

This document describes AMD's Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS), a secure method for non-persistent updates to running firmware and settings without a BIOS reflash or system reset. SFS targets selected runtime concerns in AMD-provided binary firmware components included in AGESA releases and does not patch x86 code, SMM, AGESA, UEFI, or run-once code such as ABL. Updates apply at runtime and must be reapplied after reboot. AMD cryptographically signs SFS packages, and customers may optionally co-sign by providing a public key to the ASP during early boot. The ASP verifies signatures, applies patches, updates patch-level information, and returns status. Versioning includes SFSPL, individual firmware SPLs, and SYSPL. SFS commands use TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER and ASP registers; subcommands include GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO and UPDATE_FW. Packages are aligned to AGESA releases and named with family, release, and counting number. The document also covers security/threat model, resiliency, operational considerations, and release mechanisms.

The passage says cleaner air may support cognition and health, reduce sick days, and address inequalities, since low-income schools are more likely near pollution and in older buildings. It calls air purifiers low-burden and recommends schools install or reconnect devices, pilot and expand programs, monitor outcomes, and have philanthropy, advocates, and researchers support air-quality efforts.

Australian ecosystems are experiencing abrupt, potentially irreversible changes from gradual climate change combined with extreme weather. Examples include kelp forests shifting to seaweed turfs, destruction of Gondwanan refugia by wildfire, Murray River floodplain forest dieback, alpine forest conversion to shrubland, arid-zone boom and bust, and mangrove dieback in the Gulf of Carpentaria. Even undisturbed systems are not necessarily more resilient. Climate “presses” and extreme-event “pulses” can push ecosystems to tipping points, and frequent events may prevent recovery. Consequences include loss of fish, forest resources, carbon storage, livestock and pasture quality, tourism, and water quality and supply. Predicting collapses is essentially impossible, while interventions are costly and uncertain. Recent widespread catastrophic biological transformations suggest many seemingly healthy, undisturbed ecosystems are at a tipping point.

This retrospective cohort study used All of Us Research Program registered tier v7 data to predict healthy aging from social determinants of health (SDOH). Participants were aged 50 and older with SDOH survey responses and available EHR data. Healthy aging was defined by a composite score of comorbidities, cognitive conditions, and mobility function. Logistic regression, multi-layer perceptron, and XGBoost models were trained; XGBoost with random oversampling performed best, outperforming the other models, and showed predictive parity across race and sex groups. SHAP analysis ranked health insurance type as the most predictive feature, followed by employment status, substance use, and health insurance coverage. The study concluded that machine learning models can accurately predict healthy aging using SDOH and that health insurance significantly contributes to healthy aging. Limitations included no unanimous healthy aging definition, potential selection bias in the volunteer All of Us cohort, and unmeasured confounders.

Zac Taylor said Joe Flacco will start at quarterback for the Bengals against the Packers. Cincinnati acquired Flacco and a 2026 sixth-round pick from Cleveland for a 2026 fifth-round pick. On Oct. 22, 2001, stocks closed higher as investors cheered earnings news despite anthrax reports. Enron shares plunged after Enron said the SEC requested information about certain related-party transactions, including deals with limited partnerships organized by CFO Andrew Fastow. This study simulates the transition from ICE vehicles to BEVs using one year of telematics data from 10,441 private car users in Asti, Italy, covering 10,141,809 cleaned trips. It replicates recorded trips with four BEV models and four charging policies, updating state of charge per trip. Results show current BEV technology is suited to part, but not all, of the population. Scenario 1 performs worst, with 64%–88% average feasible trips depending on vehicle. Scenario 4 performs best; average feasible trips exceed 98% for all models except the Fiat 500e, and with the Audi A6 e-tron 95% of users are suitable and 72% can satisfy 100% of trips. Scenario 3 yields higher average SoC after trips. Limitations include assumed constant energy consumption and charging power, assumed charging infrastructure availability, and no full cost–benefit analysis.

IES Holdings, a diversified infrastructure services provider, has nearly doubled YTD and outperformed infrastructure and Russell 2000 stocks. Its residential division faces challenges, while data center projects help its next two largest divisions. Backlog exceeds $2B, up 20% YoY, with improved cash flow and record cash balances. Linebackers must have toughness, athleticism, and intelligence. They line up behind the defensive line and before the safeties, often relay calls, and are responsible for run and pass defense. Their name comes from their alignment behind the defensive line, and they are also called LB, backer, Sam, Mike, Will, or Jack. Notable linebackers include Ray Lewis, Chuck Bednarik, and Lawrence Taylor, with listed honors. At a Board of Governors meeting, ASCSU President Josh Silva discussed improving student tailgating, citing limited awareness of the lot and students using it mainly for parking; ASCSU rebranded and plans pre-game programming. This study examined whether role-taking and literacy interventions reduce reliance on demographic and appearance cues in social engineering decisions. It used a 4×2 mixed factorial online experiment with Arab participants, comparing Persuader, Persuadee, Literacy, and Control groups. Participants rated trust and likelihood of accepting a hotspot offer from 16 personas varying by age, gender, ethnicity, and attire before intervention and one week after. Results showed no significant intervention effects on risk-taking or trust across persona factors or roles; Bayes Factors supported the null hypothesis. Covariate analyses found no significant interactions except a small time × self-esteem effect for trust toward casual versus formal attire. Word-of-mouth was not significantly affected. Issue of Involvement significantly decreased after intervention, though post hoc role differences were not significant. The discussion states the interventions did not significantly alter demographic or appearance-based biases, possibly due to deeply ingrained cognitive shortcuts and short duration. Participant feedback described the intervention as engaging and awareness-raising. The conclusion states no significant debiasing effects but suggests role-taking and scenario-based methods may raise awareness, with future research needing longer, immersive approaches.

Texas’ new law replaces STAAR with three shorter exams at the beginning, middle, and end of the year and bans practice tests. The first two exams will be chosen from TEA-approved national assessments, while TEA will create the third. Results must be released about two days after testing. Supporters say the law reduces the number of tests and testing time. Critics worry three exams could increase pressure and testing time, especially if they require STAAR-like lockdown protocols. They note schools’ accountability ratings will still heavily depend on the end-of-year test, since a required TEA study is not due until 2029-30 and implementation is not mandated. Experts say the system, launching in 2027-28, may resemble current testing and codify existing district practices. Some parents and educators want more teacher input and less restrictive testing rules.

The passage discusses portable, performant, and productive programming frameworks for computational science and AI/ML. It states traditional CSE relies on C++ and Fortran with models/frameworks such as MPI, OpenMP, OpenACC, Kokkos, Legion, and RAJA, and libraries/frameworks such as Kokkos Kernels, Ginkgo, Trilinos, and PETSc; Kokkos focuses on performance and portability and less on productivity. AI/ML frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, and TensorFlow focus on productivity and portability, rely on manual interfacing to optimized libraries, and are tedious to extend to new architectures. The authors hypothesize an extensible compiler framework supporting performance, portability, and productivity, developed from lessons learned from Kokkos, and address interfacing CSE C++ codes with Python-based ML codes with performance close to native C++. They develop LAPIS, an MLIR-based compiler framework with a Kokkos-focused dialect, a Kokkos C++ emitter, a portable memory model, lowering/raising passes, Kokkos Kernels linear algebra operations, loop mapping, synchronization, and DualView handling. The passage reviews related compilers, background on Kokkos, Kokkos Kernels, and MLIR, and LAPIS inputs from torch-mlir and MPACT. It demonstrates LAPIS on sparse and dense linear algebra and CSE/AI-ML coupling on AMD MI300A and NVIDIA H100 GPUs and Intel Granite Rapids CPUs.

The passage states that the Berlin-Bagdad problem is whether Germany can organize territory under its influence to later use Middle Europe’s resources and manpower for its foreign policy, with Poles, Czechs, South Slavs, and Bulgaria as critical political problems; if these peoples become willing accomplices or helpless servants, Berlin would master the continent. It says the United States should not oppose economic or cultural interplay or unification, but should disestablish a system in which imperialistic groups in Berlin, Vienna, and Budapest use the area’s resources for a selfish foreign policy; the nature of control is the main concern. Present control rests on an alliance of ruling powers in Vienna, Budapest, Sofia, Constantinople, and Berlin, bound by interests in subjecting Poles, Czechs, and Croats, German-Magyar ascendency, Bulgaria’s Treaty of Bucharest grievance, Turkish integrity, and postwar debts. The work constructs strong pseudorandom unitaries (PRUs) in the quantum Haar random oracle model (QHROM). Its construction \(G^U(1^\lambda,k)=X_{k_3}\cdot U_\lambda\cdot X_{k_2}\cdot U_\lambda\cdot X_{k_1}\) makes two queries to the Haar random oracle and requires \(O(\log^{1+\epsilon}(n))\) bits of randomness for security against all polynomial-query adversaries with access to the PRU, Haar oracle, and their inverses. The passage also reviews prior work on PRUs and idealized models, including the QHROM and inverseless QHROM. It outlines a proof using Ma-Huang’s path-recording framework, an approximate merge isometry \(S\), query-by-query analysis, and a sequence of hybrid experiments from the real PRU/Haar oracles to ideal independent Haar oracles. It further presents preliminaries, definitions of strong PRUs, relation and path-recording operators, and useful lemmas.

CEMEX, a Mexico-based company, won a majority stake in Australia’s Rinker Group on June 7, 2007, for $15.3 billion, following its 2005 acquisition of RMC. This made CEMEX one of the world’s largest suppliers of building materials; its share price fell in 2008 amid the global downturn, credit crisis, and financial leverage. From 1992 to 2007, CEMEX’s expansion as an emerging-economy multinational was notable in an industry where cement’s low value-to-weight ratio means little product moves across national boundaries. Much of its success was attributed to its approach to acquisitions and post-merger integration (PMI), including the CEMEX Way: standardized business processes, technology, and organizational structure, with some operational flexibility, plus innovation and continuous improvement. CEMEX’s internationalization had four stages: Laying the Groundwork, Stepping Out, Growing Up, and Stepping Up. Early steps included Mexican acquisitions, divestitures, CEMEXNET, and an Executive Information System. In 1992 it acquired Spanish companies Valenciana and Sanson; PMI was formalized and best practices were transferred. Later acquisitions included Venezuela, Colombia, the Caribbean, the Philippines, Indonesia, Egypt, Chile, and Costa Rica. A difficult Colombian integration led CEMEX to learn from acquired companies, known as internal benchmarking or the CEMEX Way. PMI teams standardized and cataloged practices, and PMI duration fell from 25 months to less than five months. In 1996, CEMEX applied PMI to Mexico. It acquired Southdown in 2000, RMC in 2005, and Rinker in 2007. The appendix describes the heavy building materials industry, including cement’s local nature, consolidation, producers, consumers, and developed- versus developing-market differences.

In June 1953 East Berlin and June 1956 Poznań riots were suppressed by Soviet troops. The 1956 Hungarian revolt was nationwide and a turning point for the Soviet Union and NATO. Hungary had been overrun by the Soviet army in 1944; Communists under Mátyás Rákosi eliminated opponents, won the 1949 elections without other candidates, and imposed collectivization and rapid industrialization. After Stalin’s death, Imre Nagy became prime minister but was replaced after a heart attack in 1955. Discontent in early 1956 stemmed from uncertain leadership, de-Stalinization, economic failure, and Polish events. In October, a Budapest student rally produced a fourteen-point manifesto; a clash with state security police led to revolutionary councils demanding nationalism, neutrality, and Soviet withdrawal. Soviet troops entered Budapest on 24 October, left on 29 October, but Soviet leaders promised sovereignty while massing forces. After the Suez crisis diverted attention, Soviet forces surrounded Budapest on 1 November and attacked on 3/4 November. Fighting ended by 14 November and resistance crumbled by 30 November; about 25,000 Hungarians and 7,000 Soviet soldiers were killed.

The DAWN-plasma study is a randomized, open-label, phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter trial evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adult patients with COVID-19. Participants were randomized 2:1. The primary objective was to evaluate clinical efficacy and safety, with the primary endpoint being the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints included clinical status, time to sustained clinical improvement or discharge, mechanical ventilation or death, venous thromboembolism, transfusion-related side effects, antibody titer correlation, safety, quality of life, adverse events, laboratory data, and vital signs. Convalescent plasma was administered as 800–1000 mL in 4 doses, with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization and the second dose 24–36 hours after the first infusion. Plasma with less than 1/160 neutralizing antibody titers was not allowed. The protocol and informed consent were approved by Independent Ethics Committees, and the study was conducted per the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP. Five patients withdrew consent and one was a screen failure before intervention; six replacements were randomized. No patients were lost to follow-up after intervention.

Williams & Connolly confirmed hackers accessed a small number of attorney email accounts through a zero-day attack. It believes the hackers are affiliated with a nation-state actor tied to recent attacks on law firms and companies.

The passage covers TPS7H500x-SP current-mode PWM controllers, including enable/UVLO configuration, internal 1.23-V reference and 0.613-V error-amplifier reference, transconductance error amplifier, output-voltage programming, soft start, and three oscillator modes: internal oscillator, external synchronization, and primary-secondary. A change of government has been completed: the House became Democratic by a decisive majority two years ago, the Senate about to assemble will be Democratic, and Democrats hold the presidency and vice presidency. The question is what this change means. It means more than a party victory: the Nation seeks to use the Democratic Party to interpret a change in its plans and point of view. National life is great in material wealth, energy, industry, moral force, sympathy, helpfulness, and government, but evils accompany good: waste, human and spiritual costs of industry, and government used for private and selfish purposes. The duty is restoration: to cleanse, reconsider, restore, and correct evil without impairing good, and to purify and humanize common life. Needed changes include tariff, banking and currency, industrial conditions, agriculture, watercourses, waste places, forests, and mines; government should serve humanity through health, justice, and laws on sanitary conditions, pure food, and labor. It urges restoration rather than destruction, dealing with the economic system as it is and may be modified, with justice as the motto. It describes the task as not mere politics but dedication, summoning honest, patriotic, forward-looking men to support it.

Indianapolis Public Schools is opening discussion to parents and community members about closing three high schools. At a Board meeting Tuesday, the Facilities Utilization Taskforce will present a report recommending closure of three high schools by 2018-2019. The report cites declining enrollment—from 109,000 in 1967 to 30,000—and undercapacity high schools. It says three high schools could serve current high school students, while four would allow flexibility. The passage discusses remote sensing change detection (RSCD), including traditional methods and deep learning approaches such as CNNs, Vision Transformers, BIT, and ChangeFormer. It notes challenges including scarce remote sensing data, high annotation costs, multi-source data fusion, and limitations of visual-only foundation-model methods like FastSAM and MobileSAM. Recent studies integrate natural language and CLIP-based visual-language change detection. The paper proposes a visual-linguistic multimodal method, LG-CD, using a pretrained SAM2 encoder and CLIP text encoder. It designs a text fusion attention module to align text with visual features and a visual-semantic fusion decoder to generate change detection masks. Multi-level adapters fine-tune SAM2. The contributions include language-guided change detection, SAM2 adaptation, and text-visual fusion modules.

The White House said it was not defending Roseanne Barr after her racist tweet led to her ABC sitcom’s cancellation, but President Trump and Sarah Sanders said ABC owed an apology for derogatory comments about the administration. Sanders cited examples and called it media bias and a double standard. She said no one was defending Barr’s inappropriate comments, lamented networks not airing Trump’s “right to try” remarks, and insisted he was focused on other matters.

Professor Cyril Dim discusses cervical cancer as cancer of the cervix, caused in almost all cases by sexually transmitted human papillomavirus, especially types 16 and 18 included in vaccines. It has pre-cancerous, early, and late stages. Pre-cancer often has no symptoms and can be detected by Pap smear and treated. Early cancer may be symptomless, later causing post-coital bleeding, foul vaginal discharge, and abnormal bleeding; late stages can cause weight loss, weakness, anaemia, pelvic pain, incontinence, unconsciousness, and death. Diagnosis uses Pap smear; suspected cases require tissue biopsy and histology. Screening is advised every three years for reproductive-age women and later every five years. Men face no known harm from sex with affected women but can carry and spread HPV. Early cancer can be cured with radical surgery or radiotherapy; late cancer is managed with radiotherapy and chemotherapy to prolong life. Survival varies: early cure, late possibly five years, terminal months. In Nigeria, cervical cancer is high, after breast cancer among women and possibly leading in deaths, with about 15,000 new cases and 10,000 deaths yearly. Myths attribute it to witchcraft.

Contributions totaled about $52 million for Democratic-affiliated groups and about $4 million for Republican-affiliated groups, up from a 6-1 Democratic-to-Republican ratio in 2017 through 2020. The lecture discusses discrete symmetries—parity, time reversal, and charge conjugation—in complex scalar and Dirac theories. It reviews how these symmetries are implemented quantum mechanically, noting that time reversal is anti-unitary and has a modified adjoint definition. For complex scalars, parity and time reversal include phases constrained to ±1 for parity, distinguishing scalar and pseudoscalar cases, while charge conjugation exchanges particle and antiparticle. For Dirac fields, parity requires a spinor matrix D commuting with gamma-zero and anticommuting with gamma-i; charge conjugation requires a matrix C, and time reversal is related to C and gamma-five. The lecture then introduces path integrals for fermions, using Berezin’s anti-commuting Grassmann variables. It defines their functions, derivatives, and integration rules: integration is linear, total derivatives integrate to zero, integration acts like differentiation, and change of variables gives a reciprocal factor.

U.S. stock index futures rose Thursday as earnings season began strongly and oil rebounded, though North Korea-U.S. tensions and French elections kept investors cautious. Of 57 S&P 500 companies reported, 75.4% beat expectations; profits were estimated up 10.8%. Qualcomm rose and eBay fell. Jobless claims were expected to rise.

The application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. Nos. 17/186,121, 16/556,683, and 15/719,366. The passage describes sensors such as LIDAR, RADAR, SONAR, and image sensors, including LIDAR scanning by emitting light pulses, detecting reflections, and generating point clouds, and image sensors capturing images using arrays of sensing elements.

Disclosed examples relate to synchronizing a rotating LIDAR sensor and one or more cameras. A system includes a LIDAR sensor with a transmitter and receiver, one or more cameras that detect external light, and a controller. The cameras provide rows of sensing elements aligned with the LIDAR sensor’s axis of rotation. The controller obtains a sequence of image pixel rows, where a first row indicates measurements during a first exposure time period and a second row indicates measurements during a second exposure time period. In a device, an image sensor array has rows arranged according to LIDAR light beams for a pointing direction, an actuator rotates the LIDAR sensor, and a controller obtains a sequence of image pixels based on the beam arrangement and exposure time periods. A method involves rotating a LIDAR sensor, emitting light pulses, detecting reflections, and obtaining image pixel rows using cameras whose sensing element rows are aligned with the LIDAR axis. Detailed implementations include rolling shutter operation, timing and order based on LIDAR orientation and rotation, associating LIDAR data with image pixels, generating 3D representations, camera ring arrangements, and curved image sensors.

An electronic smoking device includes a housing, a liquid supply, and one or more woven fiber tubes. At least one woven fiber tube has an electrically conductive heating section, end sections in contact with the liquid supply, and first and second leads or electrical contacts connectable to a power source. The woven fiber tube can transport liquid through its hollow interior via capillary action and through its porous wall, serve as both heating element and wick, and be formed in U-shape, C-shape, or L-shape. The court denied Fincke’s motion to reconsider its ruling that he violated § 410(a)(2) by falsely stating in the October 2002 Business Plan that Access had been advised by patent counsel that its product did not infringe known patents. The BIRDS workshop aims to bridge digital library professionals and GLAM representatives with computational researchers. Digital library experts often lack technical resources, while computer science researchers may be unaware of real-world digital library challenges and constraints. The workshop seeks to foster collaboration for innovative practical applications, following the Collab-a-thon concept at ECIR 2024. It does not require paper submissions and focuses on scientific speed-dating, a keynote, a panel, and group discussions. Goals include starting a workshop series, identifying common digital library challenges, discussing rough ideas at TPDL, producing a SIGIR Forum report, and continuing at later Digital Library conferences. The full-day, in-person workshop targets practitioners and researchers, especially new community members, with about 25 participants. Organisers are Christin Katharina Kreutz and Hermann Kroll.

In Coleman v. Coleman (1972), the Ohio Supreme Court reviewed the constitutionality of R.C. 3105.03, which requires a plaintiff in divorce or annulment, except alimony alone, to have been an Ohio resident for at least one year before filing. Appellant did not meet that requirement. Applying the compelling-interest test discussed in Shapiro and Dunn, the court held that the one-year durational residency requirement did not penalize the right to interstate travel and that Ohio had a compelling interest in regulating marriage and divorce. The court found divorce is not a basic need, that the requirement was the least restrictive means of keeping Ohio divorce laws from applying to nonresidents, that it encouraged reconsideration of the marriage, and that alimony-alone actions were exempted. Judgment affirmed. A concurrence agreed based on the particular facts, noting the grounds arose in New York and the record was silent as to any compulsion to settle in Ohio, while not foreclosing re-examination in other circumstances.

The Simons Observatory has deployed over 67,000 superconducting TES detectors to three 0.5 m SATs and a 6 m LAT. Its readout uses microwave frequency multiplexing with SMuRF warm electronics and UFMs, reaching a multiplexing factor of about 1,000 per pair of RF transmission lines. For the LAT, the SMuRF electronics and room-temperature coaxial cables are mounted on the LATR and exposed to diurnal temperature swings, which may introduce systematic phase drift. Using off-resonance tones, the study measured time delays correlated with ambient temperature, with the effect at the level of a few picoseconds over one diurnal cycle. After converting the phase drift to inferred TES noise-equivalent current using measured resonator and SQUID parameters, comparisons with an on-sky 150 GHz detector and an open SQUID channel showed the phase-drift contribution is not a significant driver of on-sky detector noise and is within the readout noise budget, so it is not expected to affect the telescope’s mapping speed.

The passage concerns electron-photon interactions in optical cavities described by the Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian, where molecular electronic structure and reactivity are modified and standard quantum chemistry methods are not directly applicable. The DAWN-plasma study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter trial evaluating best supportive care plus convalescent plasma versus best supportive care alone in adults hospitalized with COVID-19. Participants received 800–1000 mL convalescent plasma in 4 doses; plasma with less than 1/160 neutralizing antibody titers was not allowed. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. In the Full Analysis Set, this was 83.7% (n=266) with convalescent plasma versus 84.1% (n=137) with control (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.59–1.68, p=0.976). No statistically significant differences were found for any secondary endpoints. Treatment-emergent, fatal, and serious adverse events were similar between groups. Treatment-related AEs occurred in 12 patients (3.75% of the plasma+SOC group) and treatment-related SAEs in 7 (2.19%). Transfusion-related side effects were reported in 19/320 intervention patients (6.0%), with no TRALI. NT50 increased from baseline to Day 6 but was not influenced by intervention; higher Day 0 and Day 6 NT50 correlated with better outcome. The trial reported that high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma early in hospitalization did not change the natural course.

This study characterized empirical dietary patterns among US adults using pooled 2009-2020 NHANES data. Among 32,498 adults aged >20 years, four dietary patterns were identified: American, Prudent, Legume, and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy. The American pattern was most common and had the lowest HEI-2020 score; Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy had the highest. In adjusted models, the American pattern was more common among adults with prevalent CVD than without. Higher SDOH score was associated with greater alignment with American and Legume patterns and lower alignment with Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy. SNAP participants and income-eligible non-participants had higher American pattern prevalence than non-eligible adults; SNAP participants had lower Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy prevalence and higher Legume prevalence than non-eligible adults. Associations of SDOH and SNAP status with dietary patterns differed by race and ethnicity, while CVD associations did not. The study concludes that empirical dietary patterns vary by cardiovascular health and especially socioeconomic vulnerability, and that initiatives should consider naturally occurring dietary patterns. Limitations include cross-sectional data and self-report.

The Wham play is an obscure football run concept described as Trap with a Tight End or Fullback pulling to kick out a Defensive Lineman instead of a Guard. Its biggest weakness is being complicated and time-consuming to teach and install, requiring correct front and blocking identification, often predictable fronts, and a powerful blocker. The passage reports a study on household transmission of hepatitis C. It states HCV is a global public health problem, with over 170 million infected globally and about 4% prevalence in Rwanda. The study aimed to evaluate horizontal HCV transmission among household members of HCV-positive patients attending CUSP in Huye. It used a descriptive cross-sectional design, calculated a sample size of 180, and enrolled 148 participants from 30 families. Screening used HCV Ab rapid test, with ELISA confirmation for reactive cases. Results found 16/148 (10.8%) were reactive and confirmed. Significant associations were reported for HBV (p=0.001), HIV (p=0.001), and unprotected sex (p=0.016); blood transfusion was not significant (p=0.058). Awareness was low: 139 (93.9%) gave wrong answers, with p=0.079, not significant. The study concluded there was high HCV prevalence among household members and that unprotected sex was the most reported transmission factor. It recommends follow-up of HCV-positive patients, early screening and education for family members, and further non-cross-sectional, countrywide, and phylogenetic studies. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, which could not determine the origin of infection.

President Donald Trump has nominated Travis Hill, a senior Treasury Department adviser, to chair the U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, according to Bloomberg News. If confirmed, he would oversee deposit insurance, bank assessments, and sector failures, and the nomination may attract congressional scrutiny.

The passage introduces Construction Defining Functionality (CDF), a formal model analyzing computational problems through intensional constructions and extensional behaviors. CDF uses a tripartite architecture: syntactic space Ssyn(f), semantic space Ssem(f), and logical space Slog(f), connected by mappings αf: Ssyn→Ssem, βf: Ssem→Slog, and γf: Ssyn→Slog. It distinguishes intensional/internal generative rules from extensional/observable outcomes, and syntax from semantics. CDF-completeness requires disjunctive definability, structural balance, and stable mappings. Stability means |φ(a)|≤C·|a|^k; explosiveness means unbounded logarithmic growth. Compositional coherence holds when γf=βf∘αf; classifications are ComCDF, ExpCDF, and Semi-ExpCDF. The passage compares 2SAT and 3SAT: 2SAT clauses are binary and convertible to implications, yielding local, compositional, stable, polynomial-time reasoning; 3SAT clauses are ternary and non-local, cannot be converted to binary implications, produce exponential semantic growth O(2^n), unstable γf, and NP-complete status. It concludes that 3SAT’s semantic explosion is a structural consequence of syntactic non-locality; stabilizing αf would require changing 3SAT into a fundamentally different problem.

Patents grant inventors a monopoly until expiration, after which everyone can apply the invention without limitation. FDM desktop 3D printers trace to Scott Crump’s 1992 patent; Stratasys still produces industrial 3D printers based on the concept. Industrial 3D printer ASP is $104,222, metal-part printer ASP is $566,570, and desktop machines under $5,000 have an ASP of $1,094. China has become a global leader in the clean energy transition, with Xi Jinping reaffirming its green commitment. China pledged to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 7–10% by 2035, reach 3,600 GW of installed wind and solar capacity by 2035, have more than 30% renewables in its energy mix, make EVs mainstream, expand its carbon emission trading market, and increase forest extent to 34 billion cubic meters. It invested $625 billion in clean energy last year, nearly a third of the global total, and has reshaped the global market for green technologies.

This open-label randomised controlled trial in Western Cambodia compared primaquine regimens to prevent Plasmodium vivax recurrence. Patients with uncomplicated P. vivax received artesunate 2 mg/kg/day for 7 days. G6PD normal patients were randomised to primaquine 3.5 mg/kg over 14 days, 7.0 mg/kg over 14 days, or no primaquine; G6PD deficient patients received no primaquine. Patients were relocated for 90 days to a malaria transmission-free area. Among 156 allocated patients, recurrence within 90 days occurred in 81.4% of the no-primaquine arm, 24.4% of the low-dose primaquine arm, and 4.7% of the high-dose arm. The hazard ratio for high-dose versus low-dose primaquine was 0.17. Both primaquine arms were well tolerated. The authors conclude that 7.0 mg/kg primaquine had greater efficacy than 3.5 mg/kg, with comparable safety and tolerability in G6PD normal patients, and should be recommended to prevent P. vivax relapses in Cambodia and likely other Southeast Asian countries.
Dybala says he has trained with the team and will probably play 100% against Barcelona; he chose to renew with Juventus until 2022 and is happy there.

Sebi permitted debt issuers to request reviews of their credit ratings to curb rating shopping. Such reviews must be conducted by a CRA rating committee with a majority of independent members. Sebi also required CRAs to disclose non-accepted ratings for 12 months and post half-yearly rating summary sheets within 15 days, with separate disclosures for securities and other financial instruments.

Melinda Rosetti-Spence was sentenced to 10 years in prison for embezzling about $266,600 from Pink Hearts Fund, a cancer charity. She must repay about $181,000, with her family paying the balance. She wrote 132 checks to herself from March to July 2016 and pleaded guilty in April. She said she had a gambling problem.

English local authorities are due millions in refunds after being overcharged for council tax summons court fees. The Ministry of Justice said fees had been too high since 2013-14 due to an administrative error, with councils overpaying about £9m a year. It said urgent action would reduce fees and reimbursement details would follow soon.

The U.S. government has frozen about $18 billion in federal funding for New York City projects, citing concerns that contract awards may have relied on unconstitutional DEI criteria. The Office of Management and Budget confirmed the freeze, affecting initiatives including the Second Avenue Subway extension and the Hudson River Tunnel project. The Department of Transportation suspended a $300 million payment pending review and issued an interim rule limiting race- or gender-based preferences. Officials said audits will determine whether grant agreements violated federal anti-discrimination rules. City officials criticized the move, warning of delays, disrupted construction, and cost overruns. The federal shutdown has already complicated contract management. The impact depends on the review’s outcome, and the episode signals a broader shift in Washington’s stance on DEI-linked programs.

LG will release webOS TVs later this month. Sky's EPG is compatible at launch, enabling Sky content viewing and control via LG remote. WebOS's Today menu aggregates apps and live TV, while the TV uses Sky's online EPG data and sends IR signals to the Sky box.

A STAT personnel roundup notes that enGene hired Hussein Sweiti as chief medical officer; he previously was global medical head, oncology clinical development at Johnson & Johnson. It invites reader submissions for comings and goings and notes Ed Silverman’s STAT role. The full article requires a STAT+ subscription.

A group of college accreditors, the Council of Regional Accrediting Commissions, released a statement backing AI use to reduce credit loss during transfer. CRAC, representing seven agencies overseeing 3,000 degree-granting institutions, says the statement is not a mandate but aims to signal that using AI to expand course equivalencies does not conflict with accreditation standards. The statement encourages institutions to default to applying credits toward program completion unless required learning outcomes are not met, and to consider AI for learning evaluation. It says AI can analyze course equivalencies, identify matches, provide timely degree-applicable credit information, reduce administrative burden, and free faculty time. Experts say AI may streamline evaluations and reduce credit loss, though details and reliability matter. CRAC does not aim to remove humans from evaluation. A pilot with 59 institutions is using an AI platform.

Cryotherapy, a wellness trend, uses a chamber reaching 180 degrees below zero. Enthusiasts claim it speeds muscle recovery, reduces inflammation, fixes joint pain, improves circulation, relieves anxiety and depression, elevates mood, boosts immunity, and burns calories. Invented in the 1970s by Japanese doctor Toshima Yamauchi for arthritis, it is popular in Europe and now the U.S., including Polar Brrr in West Michigan. It is not FDA-approved and warnings include frostbite, burns, and eye injuries. The theory is similar to ice baths. Clients include athletes and people with sleep disorders or desk jobs. A person supervises sessions; medical conditions require doctor consultation. Introductory rates are $25 for first class or $90 for three; normally $55. Little science backs benefits, and a 2015 death occurred in an unsupervised enclosed apparatus.

A 2,100-year-old chalk stone bowl fragment engraved with the name "Hyrcanus" in Hebrew was found in Jerusalem. The Israel Antiquities Authority said it is unclear whether it belonged to royalty or a commoner, because Hyrcanus was a common name and two Hasmonean kings had it. Discovered in 2015 under the Givati parking lot at the City of David, beneath an ancient mikvah complex and near remains of the Akra, the fragment is one of the earliest examples of chalk vessels in Jerusalem. Announcement was delayed for study.

Bollinger Bands use a simple moving average as a middle band and upper/lower bands set by standard deviations, typically a 20-day SMA and 2 standard deviations, to measure volatility and overbought or oversold conditions. The passage outlines strategies including Squeeze, Breakouts, %B, Walks, Bounce, Double Bollinger Band Trend-Following, Band Width, RSI Divergence, Pinch Play, Reversal, Volatility Contraction, and Triple Strategy. It states Bollinger Bands are somewhat profitable in the mean-reverting stock market and worked as a breakout indicator in gold, but no useful strategies were found for stock indices. It also notes adjustable settings, limitations, and the importance of confirmation and risk management.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated March 1, 2019, reporting that its Annual Meeting of Shareholders was held on March 1, 2019. Shareholders elected eight directors; approved ratification of Ernst & Young LLP as independent registered public accounting firm for 2019; approved an advisory resolution on executive compensation; and did not approve shareholder proposals titled “Shareholder Proxy Access Amendments” and “True Diversity Board Policy.” The report was signed March 4, 2019, by Katherine Adams.

The passage examines the stock-market holiday effect, a calendar anomaly involving increased returns around holidays, backtested mainly on the S&P 500 using SPY. It reviews seven holiday effects and says only Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas appear tradeable; Martin Luther King Jr. Day, President’s Day, Memorial Day, and Labor Day effects are small or nonexistent. The holiday effect is described as tiny and not a get-rich-quick scheme. Suggested reasons include lower liquidity, holiday optimism, lack of macro news, and pre-holiday risk reduction. Post-holiday backtests show holding over the holiday produced no gains, while the second day after the holiday produced better returns. A post-holiday strategy using an additional variable had 100 trades, 0.56% average gain, 71% win ratio, profit factor 4, and 3.5% annual return while invested 1% of the time.

Scotland's local authorities are setting budgets and can raise the basic council tax by up to 3%, ending the government's freeze; some councils may seek the maximum rise while others may continue the freeze. The passage collects news briefs about Amazon’s Alexa and related technology: Amazon is designing an AI chip for Alexa; its Super Bowl ad was popular on YouTube; CES featured robot dogs and foldable TVs; Amazon and Google discounted home speakers; Echo Dot helped holiday sales; Apple’s home speaker was delayed; an Alexa went rogue; and Alexa will power Big Mouth Billy Bass.

A report by Lucas Chancel and Thomas Piketty says India’s inequality rose rapidly from the 1980s. Water intake recommendations include 6–8 glasses (1.2 liters) daily, with some obtained from food. Drinking too much can cause water intoxication by diluting blood salt, leading to lethargy, light-headedness, and rarely death, often after dehydration and rapid consumption. A researcher suggests drinking according to thirst. A 12-week study found water drinkers before meals lost 15.5 lbs on average versus 11 lbs; earlier studies found two cups before meals reduced intake by 75–90 calories.

The passage discusses limitations of candidate risk factor epidemiology and machine learning for identifying non-genetic determinants, especially mediation, confounding, multiple testing, and bias. It presents Bayesian model averaging and the Doublethink method, which uses a specified prior and large-sample assumptions to convert model-averaged posterior odds into adjusted p-values, permitting simultaneous control of Bayesian FDR and frequentist FWER. The authors applied Doublethink via MCMC to 1,912 variables in UK Biobank to test direct effects on COVID-19 hospitalization, using 1,917 cases and 200,000 down-sampled controls. At a threshold of τ = 10 and α = 10−3.3, nine individual variables were significant; pre-defined and post-hoc groups recovered additional signals, including age, deprivation, sex, obesity, education, dementia, respiratory infection, fall tendency, carer support, and psychiatric care/hypertension proxies. Literature comparison found support for age, sex, obesity, socioeconomic status, smoking, lung disease, alcohol intake, comorbidity, kidney disease, and education, but no significant direct effects for diabetes, cardiovascular disease, or hypertension; psychiatric disorders, infection, dementia, and aging were significant though rarely included in prior UK Biobank COVID-19 studies. Limitations include assessing only direct effects, not total effects or intervention prediction, inability to infer no effect from no direct effect, computational intensity, and dependence on prior assumptions.

The passage traces the history and value of patterns in software development and presents container-based patterns for distributed systems. It notes Knuth’s algorithms as shared, general-purpose tools; the growth of object-oriented programming and the “gang of four” Design Patterns; and the rise of open source software and community development. Patterns are defined as general blueprints for organizing distributed systems without mandating specific technologies, offering guidance, shared vocabulary, reusable components, and lessons from past mistakes.

The passage describes single-node container patterns. The sidecar pattern adds a container to augment an application container, illustrated by adding HTTPS to a legacy service, synchronizing configuration, adding topz monitoring, building a simple PaaS, and designing reusable sidecars through parameterization, API design, and documentation. The ambassador pattern brokers interactions between an application container and external services, with examples for sharded Redis, service brokering, and request splitting/experiments. The adapter pattern modifies an application container’s interface to conform to common interfaces, with examples for Prometheus monitoring, Fluentd log normalization, and MySQL health checks.

For multi-node systems, the passage introduces microservices and distributed patterns. It describes replicated load-balanced stateless services, including readiness probes, session-tracked services, application-layer replicated services, caching layers, rate limiting, and SSL termination. It then describes sharded services, sharded caches, the role of cache hit rate, and replicated sharded caches for resilience and load.

The passage states teams must prepare for three jump ball situations: defensive, even, and offensive. Defensive jump balls occur when the opponent has an advantage and control is doubtful; players should rotate early, watch the jumper’s eyes and hand, maintain contact with the jumper, and use box, diamond, defensive, or “Y” alignments. Even jump balls are similar to offensive rebounds, requiring boxing out, inside position, anticipation, coordinated clockwise or counterclockwise rotation, and predetermined signals. Offensive jump balls can use set plays when there is a 6-inch or greater height advantage, generally tipping forward to the biggest player while maintaining defensive balance and flowing into offense if no good shot is available. Listed plays include Possession, Double Tap, Split, Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem, and Loop.

Baseline out of bounds defense is often neglected. On these plays, the defense has a numerical advantage (5 on 4), making inbounding difficult; failures to inbound have cost NCAA and NBA championships, and some coaches avoid end-of-game timeouts. Defending the ball out of bounds on the baseline differs from defending it out front. In regular half-court offenses, defenders mostly guard shooters moving off screens away from the basket; on baseline out of bounds, shooters go directly to the basket, so errors result in easy baskets. Zones also must adjust and are susceptible to screen and roll and overloads. Four effective methods are Jam, Jump Switch, Trap, and Combination Defense. Jam uses no switching and hard denial, with sag/protect middle, jam/smother, all-out denial, smothering inbounder, then match up or box pressure. Jump Switch aggressively jump switches and denies passing lanes, then smothers inbounder and uses box pressure. Trap double teams the inbounds pass, then traps the receiver and rotates on pass out. Combination Defense uses Box & One, Diamond & One, or Triangle & Two, with sag/protect middle, denial, match up after inbound, and adjustments for one- or two-guard fronts; Triangle & Two uses two chasers and a triangle zone, and can invert against a two-guard front.

This study used Morton’s neuroma as a model to examine the local molecular signature of neuropathic pain in human nerve tissue. Transcriptomic analyses of Morton’s neuroma versus control nerves found many differentially expressed genes, with over-represented processes related to immune/inflammatory response and nervous system development. Deconvolution showed immune cell population differences, including higher macrophage proportions that correlated with paroxysmal pain. Genes for the M(GC) macrophage subset (MARCO, CD163, STAB1) were upregulated, and MARCO expression correlated with paroxysmal pain. Immunohistochemistry confirmed demyelination and increased intraneural T cells and CD163+MARCO+ macrophages; CD68+ macrophage density correlated with burning pain. The findings implicate neuroinflammation in chronic human neuropathic pain and suggest the M(GC) MARCO+ macrophage subset may be of interest in paroxysmal pain.

The passage introduces diffusion models and flow matching as generative approaches and describes the Schrödinger bridge problem and iterative proportional fitting (IPF). Existing IPF variants require samples from both marginals, so they cannot model bridges when one or both marginals are unnormalised densities given by energy functions. The authors propose data-to-energy and energy-to-energy IPF, described as the first general method for inferring such Schrödinger bridges. They report three contributions: their algorithms learn stochastic bridges with low transport cost, performing on par with data-to-data IPF using ground-truth oracle samples; data-to-data IPF can be improved by learning the diffusion coefficient in addition to the drift; and data-to-energy IPF can translate priors to posteriors in latent spaces, generalizing outsourced diffusion sampling to a scalable data-free image-to-image translation method.

Small sided games (SSGs) involve two teams with fewer than 11 players on a downsized field and are used in practice or competition to give individuals more touches on the ball. Practice SSGs range from 3v3 to 9v9, target tactical situations, and are played in restricted areas with age-based formats. In August 2017, U.S. Soccer issued Player Development Initiatives setting small-sided competitive standards for U6 through U12, using fewer players, smaller fields, goals, and balls, shorter games, and modified rules. These standards are implemented by U.S. Soccer youth member organizations. Starting at U9, build-out lines are used; before U9 there is no offside, and headers, goalkeeper punts, and drop kicks are banned.

The lecture explains how to construct SNARGs from BARGs and somewhere extractable/somewhere statistically binding hash functions. It recalls BARG definitions, completeness, semi-adaptive soundness, and succinctness, and describes hash properties including index hiding and binding. It sketches an SSB hash construction using FHE and notes repetition gives binding on multiple locations. The SNARG construction generates a hash key and BARG CRS; the prover computes circuit wires, hashes them, and gives a BARG proving every gate is satisfied and the output wire is 1, while the verifier checks the BARG. Efficiency relies on the BARG’s index-language property so the verifier need not run proportionally to k.

The passage studies cavity coupling to quantum critical systems. It shows that when a cavity mode bilinearly couples to the critical degree of freedom, superradiant phase transitions can occur at arbitrarily weak light-matter coupling, with the critical coupling vanishing at the transverse-field Ising model quantum critical point. Near this point, the system exhibits enhanced intrinsic squeezing and light-matter entanglement compared with the Dicke model. DMRG calculations for a one-dimensional spin-1/2 chain qualitatively support the large-S phase diagram. Coupling to a non-critical mode instead produces competition, a complex phase diagram, and a tricritical point. The work also considers the XY model, discusses experimental implications, and concludes that quantum criticality can amplify optical responses for enhanced entanglement and metrology.

The Reconfigurable Power Station (RPS) is described as an autonomous system for extending range and capabilities of multiple UAVs and other unmanned systems by exchanging depleted Swap Cartridges (SCs) for energized or appropriate cartridges. Experimental progress in orbitronics includes reports of orbital angular momentum effects, predicted orbital Hall and orbital Rashba-Edelstein effects, and measurements mainly via orbital torque using techniques such as spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance or second harmonic analysis in magnetic heterostructures. Because orbital angular momentum does not directly act on conventional spin-based magnetization, it must be converted to spin angular momentum by spin-orbit coupling, either in the ferromagnet or in a conversion layer such as Pt or 4f transition metals. Other approaches include magnetoresistance, orbital pumping and THz emission, direct imaging by circular dichroism via magneto-optical and electron microscopy/energy-loss methods, and orbital Hanle magnetoresistance. CuOx is identified as a strong orbital angular momentum source, enhancing torques in TmIG/Pt/CuOx and Ni-Fe/CuOx; large orbital Hall effects are predicted for Nb, Ta, and Ru. Thickness and sign analyses help identify orbital transport, with long transport lengths, conversion studies, efficient rare-earth materials, and crystal symmetry tuning. Work extends to antiferromagnets, two-dimensional and perpendicular ferromagnets, and reciprocal orbital pumping, though reciprocity remains unclear. Two-dimensional van der Waals systems are explored, including orbital Hall versus valley Hall effects and possible topological orbital Hall insulators. Theoretically, the orbital Hall effect is described as universal, and the orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect also generates orbital angular momentum currents; orbital torque research is active. Magnitude and relaxation of orbital angular momentum current are not fully understood, with expected non-conservation and conflicting predictions on orbital diffusion length. Applications include MRAM, oscillators, logic devices, and THz emitters. Orbital torque may use light metals such as Ti, V, and Cr, but challenges include increasing torque, compatibility with high tunneling magnetoresistance and CoFeB, and reducing layer thickness/diffusion length. A 50% switching power reduction is reported in one device, and comparisons include W/CoFeB/MgO and Cr/CoFeB/MgO. The outlook notes orbitronics may use light, abundant, cheap materials, is tunable, potentially robust, and may couple with photons and phonons.

Cosmetic tooth bleaching is a growing $3.2 billion global industry, but consumers face many confusing products. The FDA treats whitening products as cosmetics, so they do not need premarket approval, and the ADA seal offers guidance; many toothpastes and one OTC bleaching product carry it. OTC products may cause temporary sensitivity or gum inflammation if they leak. Custom dentist-made trays cost about $400 and take up to four weeks; in-office bleaching can exceed $1,000, uses higher hydrogen peroxide, and gives faster, more dramatic results but is not insurance-covered. In-office procedures rose 29% in 2015. Dentists advise checking oral health first. Bleaching is temporary, some stains are permanent, and the ADA says there is no evidence natural remedies work.

The Tug Ocean Prince, push-towing the oil-laden Barge New London, struck a charted rock outside the navigable channel in the Hudson River, damaging the barge and causing an oil spill. Red Star, owner/charterer of the tug, sought exoneration or limitation; Pittston claimed for barge and cargo damage; the United States sought pollution cleanup costs and brought a separate action. The district court denied exoneration, granted limitation to the tug’s value, dismissed claims against the United States, and limited Red Star’s cleanup liability to $100 per gross ton. On appeal, the Second Circuit held the district court clearly erred in allowing limitation. Red Star had a non-delegable duty to provide a competent master and crew and a seaworthy vessel. It knew pilot Reimer was unfamiliar with the Hudson River, failed to appoint a captain or inform the other pilot, and failed to require a lookout under icy nighttime conditions; custom did not excuse this. The casualty resulted from negligence and unseaworthiness within Red Star’s privity and knowledge, and the failure to post a lookout contributed to the collision. The court affirmed dismissal of claims against the United States. It also held Red Star’s omissions amounted to willful misconduct under the pollution statute, so the $100-per-ton cleanup limitation did not apply. The court vacated the limitation orders, directed judgment for Pittston and the United States for their damages, affirmed in other respects, and remanded.

The Single/Double offense is contained in almost every NBA playbook and is designed to free up an outstanding shooter by running them off double baseline and down screens. Its initial attack goes down the middle, attacking both sides simultaneously and making defensive help nearly impossible. The shooting guard cuts to the basket and can pop out off a single or double screen; the small forward goes opposite. The offense includes basic actions, reads and counters, variations, continuities, game strategy, a case for defense, and required offensive fundamentals. It covers double and single screen options, breaking double screens, down screen execution, post ups, and offensive rebounding. Counters are given for defenders who chase, trail, cheat over, switch, show and recover, or overplay the passing lane. Continuities include motion, side screen, and drive and kick. Teaching stresses precise execution, coordination, drills, scouting, adjustments, and knowing how to defend the offense.

Cannabidiol (CBD), a cannabis derivative, is indicated for FDA approval limited to treating seizures caused by Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and Dravet syndrome in patients aged 2 and older. The product Epidiolex, by GW Pharmaceuticals, is a pharmaceutical-grade syrup-like oral medicine made under good manufacturing practices, purified to 99 percent, and derived from marijuana without THC. Unlike many unsubstantiated CBD products, studies provide substantial evidence of effectiveness for these seizures and risks appear acceptable. Parents of children with Dravet syndrome testified about severe seizures. Doctors are also interested in trying CBD for autism, anxiety, inflammatory, and autoimmune disorders; it differs from medical marijuana because it lacks THC.

Ion traps are used in atomic and quantum physics. Trapped-ion qubits have long coherence times and high gate fidelities, but their entanglement gate operation times are limited by vibrational modes and the ions’ charge-to-mass ratio. Rydberg-excitation dipole-entangled gates reach 700 ns. Free electrons, produced by exceeding the ionization threshold, respond faster to electric fields because of their smaller mass, potentially enabling faster gates in Paul traps, but the field remains in its infancy. Proposed electron state preparation/readout involves coupling to superconducting resonators or transmon qubits and requires temperatures below 1 K, conflicting with scalability. Magnetic-field spin manipulation and readout require low temperatures and high currents, and no technical solution exists for combining individual spin manipulation with collective-state control for multiple electrons. Laser cooling is not naturally applicable to electron-only devices. The paper proposes simultaneously trapping laser-cooled ions and electrons in the same space using a two-frequency Paul trap, with a planar ring design, to provide laser-accessible transitions for manipulating motional and spin states of quasi-free electrons. It describes a Ca2+-electron system, categories of electronic states, photoionization and optical couplings, trapping potentials, and a planar trap design addressing symmetric fields, electron heating, and manufacturing. Applications include quantum computing, photon counting, radio-frequency-to-optical conversion, and a Ca2+-Ca2+-electron Schrödinger-cat state.

The President addresses Congress about the grave crisis in U.S. relations with Spain caused by more than three years of warfare in Cuba. The Cuban question affects the Union, U.S. policy, trade, commerce, citizens, neutrality enforcement, and domestic unrest. The present revolution began in February 1895 and followed earlier insurrections; it devastated Cuba, paralyzed commerce, and caused hunger and destitution. Spain’s devastation and reconcentration policy in Pinar del Rio was extended, herding agricultural populations into towns and causing high mortality.

The President’s predecessor sought mediation in April 1896, but Spain refused. Later Spain promised home rule and more humane methods and released American prisoners. U.S. relief efforts sent money and supplies, saving thousands; Spain revoked General Weyler’s orders and appropriated $600,000 for relief. The President sought an armistice until October 1 and immediate revocation of reconcentration. Spain replied that peace preparation would be confided to the insular parliament and that it would accept a suspension of hostilities if the insurgents asked.

He does not favor recognizing Cuban independence now, citing historical precedents and conditions. He lists grounds for intervention: humanity, protection and indemnity for U.S. citizens, injury to commerce and property, and menace to U.S. peace and expense. He asks Congress to authorize the President to use military and naval forces to end hostilities and secure a stable government in Cuba, and to continue food relief with an appropriation. He notes Spain’s Queen Regent directed General Blanco to proclaim a suspension of hostilities; if it succeeds, aspirations will be realized; if it fails, it will be another justification for contemplated action.
