The study addresses goals-of-care (GOC) discussions in serious illness, which are guideline-recommended but infrequently and inconsistently documented in the electronic health record (EHR). Using Natural Language Processing, it aimed to automatically retrieve GOC discussions from clinical notes anywhere in the EHR in a general hospital population. The task was framed as binary classification of utterances. Data included 776 inpatient notes—400 Advance Care Planning (ACP) notes and 376 general notes—from patients with advanced serious illness admitted to five University of Pennsylvania Health System hospitals between April 1, 2017, and December 31, 2019. Two annotators labeled utterances, with palliative care specialist adjudication; agreement was moderate. The authors trained an ensemble of five classifiers: regular expressions, logistic regression, BERT-base, BioClinical BERT, and RoBERTa, using passive learning, active learning, and all-examples settings. The best classifier, a weighted-average ensemble trained with active learning, achieved F1 scores of 0.557 for utterance classification and 0.629 for note classification. It correctly identified 13 of 18 notes with GOC discussions (72%) while incorrectly flagging 13 notes. Active learning improved performance and reduced annotation to 3,200 additional utterances, or 30% of the unlabeled set. Classifiers trained only on ACP notes underperformed on general notes. Despite moderate performance, the authors judged the classifier suitable for deployment, with future work planned on MIMIC III.

The lecture discusses HQET matching, running, and power corrections. It covers wave-function renormalization for heavy fields labeled by velocity v, calculating Zh in MS-bar and Feynman gauge, and notes MS-bar versus on-shell renormalization should give the same matching. It treats operator renormalization for heavy-to-light and heavy-to-heavy currents, where the latter depends on w = v·v′ and has a nontrivial anomalous dimension. It describes renormalization group evolution, matching, and a dimensional-regularization method using UV and IR regulators that makes HQET scaleless integrals vanish and simplifies matching. It then constructs 1/MQ power corrections by integrating out the B field, obtaining kinetic and magnetic operators, and discusses symmetries, especially reparameterization invariance, which constrains the kinetic Wilson coefficient to 1 and connects leading and subleading operators.

The second half of the course moves from block coding schemes for the additive white Gaussian noise channel toward convolutional codes and codes on graphs. Shannon showed random codes can reach capacity; linear codes can encode with polynomial complexity, but maximum-likelihood decoding has exponential complexity, while algebraic decoding has polynomial complexity but cannot reach capacity. Convolutional codes, invented by Peter Elias from sliding parity-check codes, add finite-state dynamical structure to linear structure and are suitable for lower-complexity decoding, including the Viterbi algorithm.

The canonical example is a rate 1/2 constraint length 2 convolutional encoder with input stream u_k and memory elements. Outputs are y1_k = u_k + u_{k-2} and y2_k = u_k + u_{k-1} + u_{k-2} mod 2. The system is a linear time-invariant filter over F2 and a finite-state system with four states. A convolutional code is defined as the set of output sequences y(D) = u(D)g(D) as u(D) runs through Laurent sequences. Laurent sequences are semi-infinite binary sequences with a definite starting time; D transforms are generating functions. This set is time-invariant and forms a field; multiplication is convolution, inverses exist by long division, inverses of polynomial sequences are periodic, and rational sequences are eventually periodic. Bi-infinite sequences are not used because they would not give unique inverses.

For finite-state realizable encoders, g(D) is rational and causal. The encoder can be realized with ν memory elements, where ν is the maximum degree, giving 2^ν states. Encoders are equivalent if they generate the same code; for rate 1/n codes, g(D) and g'(D) are equivalent if they differ by a rational causal Laurent multiple. A canonical encoder is obtained by multiplying by the denominator and dividing out common factors, giving a least-degree polynomial encoder. For the example rate 1/2 constraint length 2 code, the free distance is 5. Linearity means minimum distance equals minimum nonzero weight, and finite nonzero code words have weight at least 5, as shown by argument and by the four-state transition diagram. Next topics include trellis diagrams, catastrophicity, and the Viterbi algorithm.

In Ward v. Yorba, plaintiff sued to reform a land sale contract, enforce it as reformed, and recover damages. Both parties claimed the land through a common source; plaintiff was in possession, defendant claimed under an attachment for $1,300, and the property was worth $9,000. After defendant’s counsel advised that plaintiff’s title was superior, defendant agreed to pay $4,750 for plaintiff’s interest. The written agreement mistakenly required plaintiff to convey good and perfect title, though the actual agreement was to convey only his interest. Defendant paid $100 but failed to pay the remaining $4,650. The court reformed the contract and awarded $4,650 plus interest. The appellate court affirmed, finding sufficient evidence of mistake, no relief for defendant’s alleged mistake because he knew the facts, and sufficient consideration for the contract.

Options trading in Apple allows traders to speculate on Apple’s share price. Options are contracts giving the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an underlying asset at a predetermined price on or before a certain date. Apple offers call and put options. The SEV-TIO extension lets guests bind to and use trusted devices in their guest private address space. SNP guests discover support via TEE-IO PCIe capabilities, and a device binds on the first SNP TIO Guest Request. TIO-unenlightened guests require VMPL0 firmware for setup; otherwise the SNP guest OS fetches device info, validates the interface report, and configures MMIO and IOMMU. The SNP TIO Guest Request NAE event resembles SNP Guest Request and Extended Guest Request, with non-optional unencrypted data including Guest PCI ID, MMIO range, and TDISP status. Data pages optionally provide data and return measurements, certificates, and a TDISP attestation report; the hypervisor returns required pages and validates supplied pages, returning the required count in RBX and setting SW_EXITINFO2 if insufficient. For TDI_INFO_REQ, a 32-byte nonce may trigger TDI_DEV_MEASUREMENTS. Returned data use a GUID/offset/length table, with missing data length set to 0. How the hypervisor obtains the data is out of scope.

Secure AVIC manages guest-owned APIC state for SEV-SNP guests with a private backing page per vCPU. The backing page must remain in the NPT while the vCPU runs. REGISTER_BACKING_PAGE and UNREGISTER_BACKING_PAGE actions use APIC ID. Support is implied by Secure AVIC in SEV_FEATURES, with no feature bit required. Termination Request NAE event lets a guest request termination; the hypervisor is expected to comply, and an HLT loop or SHUTDOWN is recommended after VMGEXIT. SW_EXITINFO1 contains the reason code set and reason, with set 0x0 code 0x01 indicating an unsupported SEV-ES/GHCB protocol range. SW_EXITINFO2 contains termination information or an unsupported feature mask. Unsupported NAEs not in the negotiated protocol use an “Unsupported Event” VMGEXIT.

SEV-ES guest identification requires CPUID properties: ECX[31], EAX[1], EBX[5:0] encryption bit position, and EBX[11:6] physical address space reduction. SMP AP booting faces register measurement and encryption constraints; the first AP reset uses initial measured registers, while subsequent resets use AP Reset Hold or MSR protocol, with the hypervisor completing on SIPI and the AP transitioning to real mode and setting Initial Processor State registers. UEFI-to-OS transfer uses an AP jump table: a 4K encrypted, page-aligned, single table set via SET NAE, retrieved via GET NAE, with its GPA in the Secrets Page. vCPU hotplug is unsupported under these constraints. SNP AP Creation NAE uses SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0013 to let a guest create or update AP VMSA via RMPADJUST, with forms for INIT or immediate runnable state, allowing hotplug.

For NMI injection, the hypervisor intercepts #DB but not IRET and uses the “NMI Complete” message. Debug virtualization is supported if DebugVirtualization is set; otherwise DR7 is intercepted and values are cached. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported. The #HV doorbell page supports host notifications under Restricted Injection: it has PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields, must be a host-owned shared page, and guest accesses must use C=0. PendingEvent includes NoFurtherSignal, virtual #MC, NMI, and an interrupt vector. The host emulates APIC behavior and writes vectors; the guest atomically exchanges PendingEvent, handles EOI via NoEoiRequired or X2APIC EOI MSR, and validates vectors. Doorbell configuration uses VMGEXIT 0x8000_0014 with functions for requesting the preferred address, SET, and QUERY.

Bollore told the European Commission he will get sole control of Vivendi after its April 25 shareholders meeting; his 20.65 percent stake gives him 29 percent voting rights.

New Student Association State Quad senators believe residents lack enough asbestos information despite notices in housing documents and dorm signage. Senator Cassandra Jones found confusion and concern in Eastman Tower. Residential Life has posted warnings for about 20 years about low crystallite asbestos and asks tenants not to disturb ceilings; asbestos is harmful only through long-term exposure, which can occur if ceilings are disturbed, though Residential Life says ceilings have not been recently disturbed. Some students mistake dried paint shavings for asbestos. Officials discussed posting an asbestos FAQ. Residential Life denied claims that RAs were told not to discuss asbestos; RAs said more dialogue would be better.

Mick Schumacher has admitted he is not ready for F1. The 18-year-old, stepping out of Formula 4 without a title, is in his first European F3 year to learn and be at the front in the rookie ranking. He said he must prove himself and improve, with no F1 plan, while finding interest from Mercedes and Ferrari flattering and getting used to media attention.

In cross appeals from a March 15, 2005 Family Court order, the parties disputed custody and visitation regarding their two daughters. A July 2003 agreement gave the father sole custody and the mother visitation subject to the children’s wishes, with the father required to encourage contact. The mother petitioned after the father moved to Florida without informing her and obstructed communication. Family Court found multiple intentional violations by the father but insufficient basis to change physical custody. In the later proceeding, the father did not testify or appear, and the hearing produced limited evidence about his household or the daughters’ lives in Florida. Family Court denied the mother custody of the younger daughter, continued visitation subject to the children’s wishes, and granted phone, e-mail, and correspondence access. The appellate court did not disturb the custody determination, but held that visitation between the mother and the younger daughter should not have been left to the child’s wishes. It found the father’s conduct constituted a change in circumstances, his interference raised fitness questions, his failure to testify warranted an adverse inference, and the record was not fully developed. The court remitted for immediate consideration of court-ordered visitation based on an updated in camera hearing if necessary. The father’s appeal regarding suspension of child support was rejected for compelling, uncontroverted record support.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q covers the quarterly period ended December 26, 2020 and includes unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and notes. For the three months ended December 26, 2020, net sales were $111,439 million, net income was $28,755 million, and diluted earnings per share were $1.68. Total net sales increased 21% compared with the same quarter in 2020, with growth in all Products and Services categories and all geographic reportable segments. The Company repurchased $24.0 billion of common stock and paid $3.6 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during the quarter. The filing also discusses segment information, debt, derivative instruments, income taxes, legal proceedings, and management’s discussion and analysis.

After Charlottesville, educators consider how to confront bigotry and racism. Derek Weimer, who taught James Alex Fields Jr., says Fields was intelligent and quiet but deeply interested in Adolf Hitler and white supremacy; Weimer tried to steer him away, thought he had succeeded, and felt he failed as a teacher. Facing History and Ourselves has trained teachers for 40 years to teach moral decisions in historical moments; Roger Brooks calls this a teachable moment. Resources listed include identity charts, diverse books, social justice book lists, lesson plans, a UVA syllabus, Facing History, AFT Share My Lesson, #CharlottesvilleCurriculum, and the Critical Media Project.

Denise Ricco, whose son was diagnosed with autism in fourth grade, wonders whether earlier therapy would have helped and wants to give future parents a head start. She, her husband and son were tested in SPARK, a year-old study seeking genetic markers of autism by testing families of 50,000 people with autism. Organizers call it the largest such study and say it accepts any family structure; testing can be done at home by cheek swab through the Internet, with a $50 gift card per family. As of early April, 25,328 individuals with ASD and families were participating. Rush handles the Chicago-area end of the three-year study and offers in-person testing. Researchers hope to learn more about how autism runs in families, study treatments for genetic deletions, and share data; prevention is not the aim.

Strix Group Plc held a Q2 2025 earnings call following its interim results for the period ending June 30. CEO Mark Bartlett described the half year as one of mixed fortunes with much activity, noting that Billi maintained double-digit growth, supported by new products and further geographic expansion.

The passage describes a 2018 Global Geiger-Mueller Counters Industry market research report covering 2018–2025, including industry trends, market dynamics, competitive analysis, segmentation, end-use applications, industry chain, China market coverage, company profiles, raw material and downstream demand analysis, investor opportunities, and forecasts. The passage describes the Passing Game offense as a team-oriented, rule-and-principle-based system rather than one relying on set patterns. It uses off-ball screens and movement so all players are involved, can incorporate pattern or set offenses, and can be run from various alignments against zones or person-to-person defenses. It requires unselfish attitude, patience, ball control, and purposeful movement such as creating a lead, cutting, setting screens, or establishing rebounding position. Strengths include all five players being involved, good ball and player movement, continuous motion, freedom and creativity, effectiveness against all defenses, difficulty to scout, and tempo control. Weaknesses include selfish or exceptional players breaking continuity, offensive rebounding problems, poor reading and countering of defenses, impatience, and dislike of playing without the ball. Required fundamentals include shooting, passing, screening, rebounding, sharp accurate passes, creating leads, 15–18 foot spacing, triple threat position, shot discipline, moving without the ball, off-ball screening, limiting dribbles except for strong moves or passing angles, inside post play, and offensive rebounding. Basic rules cover pass and move, leads, spacing, screens, cuts, triple threat, post ups, and rebound. Variations include 3-person Hi/Lo, 4-person, and 5-person passing/motion games, with entries, screens, back cuts, drive-and-drop/kick actions, and zone adjustments. The passage also notes coach commitment and benefits such as exposing weak defenders, causing physical and mental fatigue, and being stable due to patience and teamwork.

The plaintiff appealed an order denying his motion to set aside a jury verdict for the defendant on liability as against the weight of the evidence and for a new trial, and appealed the judgment dismissing the complaint. The appellate court dismissed the appeal from the order, affirmed the judgment, and awarded costs to the defendant.

This systematic review followed PRISMA and examined digital leadership in education using 39 articles, addressing its definitions, effects, and influencing factors. Only 11 articles defined digital leadership; definitions varied across technology leadership, e-leadership, and digital leadership and often omitted leadership elements or educational, organizational, and environmental contexts. The study suggests a TOE-driven model of digital leadership as a dynamic, adaptive practice integrating technology and shaping organizational culture. Effects were reported at student, teacher, and school levels, mainly on academic performance, technology integration, teacher development, job engagement, school management, digital transformation, and digital culture. Influencing factors were internal, including individual characteristics, professional experience, and digital literacy, and external, including infrastructure, school culture, technical supervision, policies, COVID-19, and training. Research gaps include limited definitions and influencing-factor studies and neglected student behaviors, lifelong learning, digital security, followership, and multicultural teams.

The passage recommends using existing channels to test Soviet intentions and flexibility before seeking improved bilateral relations, maintaining firm positions because no basis exists for major reciprocal deals. It warns that false expectations of progress could lead to pressure for concessions. It disagrees with specific initiatives on Afghanistan, Namibia/Angola, restoring the Joint Commercial Commission, a broad dialogue process, and summitry; it suggests private trade, working through frontline African states on Cuban presence in Angola, and using arms control as a litmus test. The appended memo says Clark agrees on some topics but questions significantly increased U.S.-Soviet dialogues.

Fitch Ratings assigned an expected rating of 'BB(EXP)' to Telenet International Finance S.a.r.L.'s Term Loan AH and Telenet Financing USD LLC's Term Loan AI, both subsidiaries of Telenet BVBA. In college football, targeting is a foul for forcible contact beyond a legal tackle, block, or play, including helmet-to-helmet hits and contact against defenseless players, who are considered defenseless when in question. NCAA penalties include 15 yards and disqualification; first-half fouls mean ejection for the rest of the game, while second-half fouls mean suspension for the first half of the next game, with rules for final games. The NFL calls similar conduct unnecessary roughness against defenseless players and does not automatically disqualify. Targeting was adopted in 2008; 2013 added disqualification, replay could overturn ejections, and 2019 required video review and added repeat-offender punishment. Examples include Michael Taaffe’s unreviewed hit in the 2024-25 Peach Bowl and Shaun Wade’s controversial 2019 Fiesta Bowl targeting call.

Keith Chegwin died at 60 following a long illness. His family said he died peacefully at home shortly after midnight on 11 December after a long-term battle with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, with his wife, daughter and son by his side. They thanked Severn Hospice and asked for privacy. The passage also says IPF scars the lungs, reduces breathing efficiency, is progressive, affects more men, and about 6,000 people in the UK are diagnosed yearly. Possible causes include acid reflux, viruses, and environmental dusts; symptoms include breathlessness, persistent cough, tiredness and clubbing.

Will Ma’s final class begins with an in-depth combinatorial analysis of a deep-stack no-limit cash-game hand: blinds $1/$2, $200 stacks, cutoff opens, button calls with 8-7 suited; flop 10-8-6, turn Q, river A. The second half covers general poker topics: the Moneymaker effect, overconfidence, gambling self-control, poker’s fast evolution, non-results-oriented thinking, variance, and recommended online resources and books. Ma answers questions about the MIT Poker Club, downswings, edges in small online games, casino strategy, avoiding overconfidence, and online poker legality in Massachusetts. He notes Bill Chen will give Friday’s final class and prizes will be awarded.

Facebook shares fell 6.8% Monday, on pace for their largest one-day percentage decline since March 2014 and biggest price drop since its 2012 IPO, after U.S. and U.K. regulators criticized Facebook for allowing Cambridge Analytica to access user data without express permission and retain it despite saying it had destroyed the records. The decline wiped away almost $40 billion in market value. Analysts said the episode posed public-relations and regulatory risks, though views were divided on the impact; some noted Facebook had upgraded privacy and app review, while others expected possible business changes or enhanced scrutiny. Broader tech stocks and major indexes also fell.

The speaker says readiness depends on game development and coach decisions; the team played well despite tough calls and will maintain its game. They expected a fast, strong forechecking hockey team. The article studies coarsening of phase-separating DNA nanostar droplets in a 3D active self-stirring fluid composed of extensile microtubule bundles, depletant, and molecular motors, compared with passive droplets. Active flows continuously advect droplets; after the DNA-rich volume fraction stabilizes, growth occurs mainly by Smoluchowski collision-driven coalescence rather than Ostwald ripening. Active droplets show ballistic then diffusive-like motion, with effective diffusivity independent of droplet size and set by active flow speed and velocity autocorrelation length. Active and passive coarsening have similar mean-radius exponents (βR ≈ 0.33), but active coarsening is accelerated, not self-similar, with an evolving relative size distribution, and has a different number exponent (γN ≈ -1.65 vs -0.89). Hydrodynamic, active-particle, anomalous-diffusion, and probabilistic simulations show that coarsening exponents and loss of self-similarity are governed by droplet motility and a collision-kernel exponent k=3-(m+2)/α. Positive k favors collisions between large droplets, produces a non-linear βR–γN relationship, and breaks self-similarity. The framework is proposed to unify active, self-propelled, and anomalously diffusing passive droplets and to apply to biological condensates and other volume-conserving coarsening, while limitations concern system size, droplet size relative to active length scale, and Ostwald ripening.

The narrator founded a company at 16, invented herbal ecstasy, earned over $350 million in under a year, and became a teenage millionaire. In 2010, while planning nootropic supplement Excelerol, he noticed Amazon sold supplements. He listed Excelerol, requested 100 subscriber reviews, received 65 mostly positive reviews, and sold 50 units at nearly $100 each—$5,000—in one night without advertising or SEO. Amazon brought new customers but raised concerns about losing subscription customers. It proved a double-edged sword: sales accelerated, but Amazon became buyer-centric, treated customers as its own, and could restrict or suspend sellers; suspension insurance emerged. After five years, he leads a team consulting Fortune 500s and startups on Amazon.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture. It covers SECDED ECC protection for HBM2 memory, L2 cache, L1 caches, and register files; a 40 MB L2 cache with partitions, slices, residency controls, and Compute Data Compression; and third-generation Tensor Cores with strong-scaling features such as data sharing, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, and larger shared memory. It details Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), which partitions an A100 into up to seven GPU Instances using GPU slices, L2 slice groups, memory slices, and Compute Instances for isolation, QoS, fault containment, migration, and MPS support. It also covers third-generation NVLink, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, error and fault detection, isolation, and containment. Additional features include NVJPG decode, an Optical Flow Accelerator, atomics improvements, and NVDEC. CUDA advances include task graphs, async copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency control, and Cooperative Groups. The DGX A100 system with eight A100 GPUs, up to 5 PFLOPS, MIG support for up to 56 accelerators, and an optimized software stack is described. A sparse neural network primer discusses fine-grained and coarse-grained sparsity and A100’s fine-grained structured sparsity.

President Trump posted that “Big Homebuilders” were “sitting on” 2 million empty lots and compared them to OPEC, saying he wanted to help restore the American Dream. Bryan Caplan disagreed, arguing the housing shortage is caused by zoning rules and local approvals, not builder greed, and that builders often wait for permission. Trump urged Fannie and Freddie to “get Big Homebuilders going,” but Caplan doubted they could pressure local governments and said zoning changes are needed, especially in heavily regulated metros.

Rare diseases affect about 300 million people globally, but fewer than 50% of affected individuals have a definitive genetic diagnosis. This study analyzed whole-blood RNA-seq from 390 UDN/GREGoR cohort samples using FRASER and FRASER2 to detect transcriptome-wide splicing outliers. It identified excess significant intron retention outliers in minor intron-containing genes in five individuals. Four had rare biallelic RNU4ATAC variants consistent with RNU4atac-opathy; one had rare compound heterozygous RNU6ATAC variants, supporting RNU6ATAC as a candidate disease gene. The authors conclude that transcriptome-wide outlier splicing patterns can aid unbiased diagnosis and gene discovery in rare disease, though additional cases and functional studies are needed to establish RNU6ATAC as disease-associated. Batch effects and sample size influenced outlier detection.

A sophomore studying abroad in Buenos Aires recounts initial uncertainty about how he would be treated due to issues African Americans face in the U.S., but says he experienced hospitality, including help from police and strangers when lost, and made Argentine friends. He was asked about his background and treated with appreciation, did not feel singled out by race, noted few people of African descent, and bonded with others. He says the experience changed his outlook and encourages African American students to go abroad.

Emma Stone signed a $10 million Louis Vuitton deal to be its face for two years. Ryan Gosling reportedly declined an approach. She stars in Battle of the Sexes and used weightlifting and protein shakes to bulk up, eventually enjoying feeling strong.

Vijay Mallya appeared before Westminster Magistrates’ Court for an extradition case, denied all allegations, and claimed he had enough evidence to prove his case. The passage argues that U.S. public higher education funding is deeply inequitable and rooted in historical discrimination. It cites Mississippi, where Ole Miss receives twice the state funding per student as Jackson State, and Connecticut, where UConn’s per-student advantage over SCSU nearly doubled by 2022. These gaps persist because most states use “base plus” allocations rather than formulas based on institutional and student need. The passage distinguishes equity—distribution based on varying need—from adequacy—funding sufficient for institutions to achieve their missions—and argues equity must come before adequacy. It notes K–12 funding systems are further ahead in directing extra money to higher-need students and accounting for outside revenue. It says free college and outcomes-based funding do not solve inequitable resourcing. It recommends funding based on institutional and student need and adjusting for outside revenue, with education and student supports funded separately from research, health care, and agriculture.

The passage argues that mainstream climate education—emphasizing scientific understanding, causes, effects, green energy, emissions reduction, and awareness—omits the interconnected historical arc of colonialism, erasures of Black and Indigenous knowledge systems and cosmologies, and historical injustices requiring reparative projects. It proposes reorienting climate education toward pluriversal thinking and decolonial educational ecologies. In Comparative and International Education, climate change is commonly framed through education for sustainable development and UN Sustainable Development Goals 4, 7, and 13. The authors critique this approach as developing/modernizing and resilience-oriented, and they describe climate coloniality: former colonies and the Global South bear climate impacts despite low emissions, while solutions such as lithium mining perpetuate extraction and dispossession. The passage employs contrapuntal reading inspired by Said to analyze dominant and marginalized voices and colonial legacies. It discusses coloniality, climate apartheid, and decolonial ecology drawing on Ferdinand, and it critiques Anthropocene and technological solutionism. Decolonial educational ecologies incorporate decolonial, anti-colonial, feminist, anti-racist, and anti-capitalist critiques; use critical inquiry; examine geopolitics of knowledge production; and seek distributive justice, reparations, and restitution. The passage links this to critical climate education and concludes that decolonial educational ecologies emphasize context/local adaptation, human well-being, more-than-human relations, and alternative futures beyond universal Western modernity.

The passage argues that the human brain does not contain copies of external stimuli, words, pictures, grammatical rules, or memories, and that the mind should not be understood through the information-processing (IP) metaphor comparing it to a computer. It states that computers literally encode, store, retrieve, move, copy, and transform symbolic data using rules, programs, algorithms, and physical memories. Humans, it says, are not born with or ever develop information, data, rules, software, knowledge, lexicons, representations, algorithms, programs, models, memories, images, processors, subroutines, encoders, decoders, symbols, or buffers. Newborns possess senses, reflexes, and learning mechanisms, not such computational elements.

The passage describes historical metaphors for intelligence—spiritual, hydraulic, mechanical, electrical, and communication-based—and says the computer metaphor became dominant after the 1940s, especially in cognitive science. It claims the IP metaphor rests on a faulty syllogism: because computers are intelligent and are information processors, not all intelligent entities must be information processors.

Using a classroom exercise in which a student draws a dollar bill from memory and then with the bill present, the passage says visualizing something absent is less accurate than seeing it present; it denies that a representation of the dollar bill is stored in the brain. It says memory tasks involve multiple brain areas, that specific memories are not stored in individual neurons, and that learning changes the brain in orderly ways without storing or retrieving songs, poems, or images. It also says each person’s brain changes uniquely from experiences, so the same experience produces different changes in different brains, and a snapshot of all neurons would be meaningless without the brain’s life history and social context.

The passage discusses researchers who reject or question the IP metaphor, gives a baseball-catching example as an alternative account without computations or representations, and notes that mainstream cognitive science still relies on the metaphor. It criticizes predictions that minds can be downloaded to computers and become immortal, and it mentions the European Union’s Human Brain Project as a failed example of neuroscience based on faulty ideas. It concludes that humans are organisms, not computers, and calls for abandoning the IP metaphor.

Mike Francesa, expected to return to WFAN as an afternoon host early next month from 3-6:30 p.m. weekdays, approached Entercom management and accepted a significant pay cut from his roughly $3 million salary, according to sources. Revolution Lighting Technologies announced it will release its first-quarter 2017 financial results before market open on May 2, 2017, and host a conference call and live audio webcast at 11 a.m. ET that day, with replay access available until May 16. The company designs, manufactures, markets, and sells LED lighting solutions for industrial, commercial, and government markets in the United States, Canada, and internationally, and trades on NASDAQ under RVLT.

Solution-processed semiconductors are candidates for inexpensive optoelectronic devices, but laser diodes are challenging. Organic semiconductors face low carrier mobility and losses; inorganic materials and perovskites have advanced, yet electrically pumped lasing remains difficult due to heat, carrier imbalance, ion migration, and electrode corrosion. The passage reports an electrically driven polariton laser based on a solution-grown CsPbBr3 perovskite microplate integrated in an optical microcavity with single-walled carbon nanotube electrodes. A two-stage cooling protocol to 8 K forms a p-i-n rectifying diode, enabling charge injection. Polariton lasing is demonstrated with a threshold of 60 µA, corresponding to about 2.8 kA cm−2, under continuous electrical injection. This introduces a strategy for solution-processed electrically pumped semiconductor lasers and applications of polariton lasers.

The passage describes devices, systems, and methods for real-time determination of material strength during tissue penetration. A system includes an instrument with a working tool, a sensor generating real-time torque signals, a controller processing the signals into torque, energy, power, or combinations, and a display. The controller can determine regional material strength from energy. The instrument may include rotational and axial drive motors, a guide harp with rods, real-time depth control and measurement, and axial force sensors for the guide harp and working tool. Sensors can measure torque in the x, y, and z axes simultaneously. Methods include penetrating tissue, sensing torque, communicating signals to a controller, processing and displaying torque/energy/power, determining regional material strength, controlling depth, and preventing inadvertent plunge. Processed signals may be displayed as accumulated energy or power and communicated wirelessly to an external device. The passage also describes an instrument with first and second axial force sensors and a third torque sensor, and methods for determining regional material strength and preventing plunge using power changes.

The passage examines whether papers that open knowledge gaps in scientific concept networks are more generative. It defines knowledge gaps as unconnected regions or holes in evolving concept networks. Using Microsoft Academic Graph, it analyzes 34,363,623 journal and conference papers from 1900–2020. Concepts are represented by level-3 fields, and edges connect concepts first co-occurring in a paper. Persistent homology detects gaps. Papers are classified as gap openers, non-gap openers with novel pairs, and non-gap openers without novel pairs. Gap openers are 0.84% of articles, twice the random model, with disciplinary and temporal variation. They link newer, less popular concepts, show higher novelty, cite fewer prior works, and use more creation/innovation verbs. Non-gap openers with novel pairs are over 25%, about half the random case; non-gap openers without novel pairs are over 70%. Regression analyses find gap openers more likely to be top cited and disruptive, with suggestive but non-significant Nobel association. They receive fewer short-term citations but more long-term citations and higher Sleeping Beauty Index; non-gap openers with novel pairs show smaller delayed effects. The transition from negative to positive citation coefficients occurs at 8 years for both. Gap openers emerge from smaller, younger, fresher, and more geographically localized teams. The discussion concludes topological significance, not novelty alone, determines generative capacity, and notes delayed recognition implications for evaluation and funding.

The passage discusses LLMs for synthesizing research data, exploring social theories, and AI governance. The passage describes container and distributed-system patterns. The ambassador pattern places a proxy container alongside an application so the application connects to localhost; the ambassador routes to shards, brokers services, or splits requests. Examples include sharded Redis/memcache with Kubernetes StatefulSets, Services, ConfigMaps, and twemproxy; service brokering for portable MySQL; and request splitting/experiments with nginx using IP hashing and weights. The adapter pattern modifies an application container’s interface to conform to common monitoring, logging, or health-check interfaces, with examples using Prometheus exporters, Fluentd, and a MySQL health-check adapter. The passage then covers multi-node patterns: microservices; replicated load-balanced stateless services with readiness probes; session-tracked services; caching layers such as Varnish; rate limiting and SSL termination with nginx; sharded services and caches; sharding functions using hashing, modulo, key selection, and consistent hashing; hot sharding; replicated sharded caches; and scatter/gather for parallel request processing, including leaf sharding and overhead/straggler issues. It ends with FaaS/event-driven processing, its benefits and challenges, background processing, memory, cost, and the decorator pattern for request or response transformation.

Erik Demaine’s final lecture proves a cell-probe lower bound for dynamic connectivity: insertions, deletions, and connectivity queries require Ω(log n) time per operation, where this is the maximum of update and query time, even when components are paths and even for amortized and randomized versions; the lecture proves a worst-case log n lower bound. The proof reduces the problem to block operations on permutations, using a √n × √n grid with perfect matchings between columns and a bad bit-reversal access sequence. A balanced binary tree is built over time, and the analysis shows information must be communicated from left-subtree updates to right-subtree queries. An information-theoretic encoding argument, using r∩w, separators, perfect hash functions, and LCA charging, establishes the lower bound. It notes matching upper bounds such as link/cut trees.

The study reports thalamic DBS in essential tremor, multiple sclerosis, and Parkinson’s disease, noting VIM-DBS is effective for tremor but its mechanism is unclear and current systems are open-loop. It recorded thalamic LFPs from a bipolar pair of a four-contact DBS lead and simultaneous hand accelerometry in 34 patients undergoing lead implantation or pulse generator replacement. There was a moderate correlation between tremor and low-frequency LFP spectral power in alpha and theta bands, a strong correlation between tremor and peak LFP-acceleration coherence, and postural tremor decoded from LFP with an AUC of ~0.7. High-frequency DBS (~130 Hz) reduced low-frequency spectral power, and postural tremor was decoded from LFPs during DBS. Computational modeling found simulated low-frequency LFP power varied with electrode location, spatial distribution of tremor cells, and the proportion of tremor versus non-tremor cells, possibly explaining across-participant differences and the moderate tremor correlation. Methods included IRB approval, informed consent, medication withdrawal, intraoperative recordings, electrode localization, signal analysis, and a thalamus model.

The passage examines high-performance computing (HPC) in manufacturing. HPC is becoming a competitive factor, with demand expected to rise. Four out of five surveyed industry decision makers agree HPC is a game changer for product and process innovation. HPC enables complex calculations, faster high-quality simulations, more iterations, new usage scenarios, and increased innovation and agility.

HPC requires suitable IT infrastructure. 87% of HPC users prefer or plan external HPC infrastructure; 74% operate or plan their own HPC infrastructure in external colocation datacenters; 43% use or plan scientific research institutions; 6% of current HPC users have own on-premises infrastructure, and 28% plan it. Challenges include security for 72%, high energy consumption and sustainability for 58%, high investment and licensing costs, computing power limitations, availability, complexity, and lack of expertise for 42%. Cloud-based HPC and HPCaaS offer scalability, flexibility, cost optimization, modernity, collaboration, and support for new business models; 81% of respondents that already implemented HPC intend to implement HPC-based business models. IDC recommends virtual product and manufacturing development, a holistic data strategy and single source of truth, evaluating HPC operating models, considering scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise and ecosystem partners. The findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and other departmental decision makers from industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

The passage studies popular matchings in three matching markets: house allocation, marriage, and roommates. It defines popular matchings through pairwise plurality elections and introduces the popular dimension as the minimum size of a popular winning set. For the house allocation problem, it proves the popular dimension is exactly 2 in all four cases—unweighted or weighted agents with either strict preferences or ties—and gives a polynomial-time algorithm for a size-2 popular winning set. For the marriage problem, it states that with unweighted agents and strict preferences the popular dimension is 1, while with weights or ties it is at least 2 and at most 3, leaving the exact value open. For the roommates problem, it proves the popular dimension is exactly 2 for unweighted agents with strict preferences and gives a polynomial-time size-2 algorithm; with weights or ties it is at least 2 and at most 3, leaving the exact value open. The passage also relates popular dimension to Condorcet dimension and notes implications for a Condorcet dimension conjecture in these problems.

This paper examines how climate change affects internally displaced K-12 learners in lower- and middle-income countries. Using a literature review and an integrated framework combining the Human Rights-Based Approach to education and Education in Emergencies research, it analyzes educational impacts before and after displacement. Findings indicate climate change restricts educational access and quality through physical barriers, socioeconomic pressures, health and well-being effects, and environmental conditions. Displaced learners face additional financial, administrative, discrimination, resource, distance-learning, and support-system barriers in new destinations. Girls face heightened barriers due to gender inequalities, household responsibilities, economic prioritization of boys, and early marriage risks. The discussion recommends scalable financial support, streamlined enrollment, academic and mental health services, robust data systems, and gender-sensitive policies. It identifies gaps in climate-related Education in Emergencies research, long-term outcome studies, and proactive policy responses. The conclusion calls for comprehensive, long-term, climate-specific educational policies that treat education as a right and part of climate resilience.

An all-optical thermometry approach using fluorescent diamonds containing silicon-vacancy (SiV) centers is described. Temperature is inferred from temperature-dependent SiV photoluminescence and diamond Raman signals. Up to nine features—intensity, peak position, and FWHM of the SiV zero-phonon line and phonon sideband and the Raman signal—were tracked. Experiments used ~1 μm diamonds with ~78 ppm SiV centers, prepared on SiO2 and annealed at 550 °C, with spectra recorded at 25–85 °C in 10 °C increments. Two algorithms were used: multi-feature regression (MFR) and two-stage multi-feature regression (2SMFR), which uses partial least squares, lasso regression, and spline correction. Models were trained on some diamonds and tested on unseen ones, with generalized accuracy and resolution. MFR with 3–4 calibration diamonds and temperature set points achieved 1.7 K accuracy and 1.2 K·Hz−1/2 resolution, about 26% better accuracy than the best single-feature model. 2SMFR with seven diamonds and seven temperature set points achieved 0.7 K accuracy and 0.6 K·Hz−1/2 resolution, about 59% better than MFR and about 70% better than the best single-feature model, and sensitivity of 0.04 K−1, about seven times the best single-feature model. Performance improved with more training data; MFR showed diminishing gains after few points, while 2SMFR required more data. The methods are described as flexible, data-efficient, and instrument-agnostic, with caveats about the linear temperature assumption and extrapolation beyond the training range.

In Mock v. Watson et al., the court held that a widow’s interest in her deceased husband’s real estate is not subject to payment of his debts and may be set apart without reference to them. Her interest attaches upon the concurrence of the husband’s seizin and the wife’s coverture and is not made subject to others’ rights or estate charges like the heirs’ interest. Code sections 2387 and 2391 refer to the estate’s interest, not the wife’s. The lower court’s order was affirmed.

In this transfer tax appeal, Josephine Slosson’s father’s will gave her income from part of a trust fund for life and a power to appoint the fund by will, with a default gift to those entitled to take her property if she died intestate. Slosson’s will directed certain bequests and debts to be paid from the trust fund and the balance to her surviving issue per stirpes. Her children elected to take under their grandfather’s will. The court held that Slosson validly exercised the power and effectively disposed of the trust fund, so the beneficiaries’ interests were subject to a transfer tax. The children could not take under the grandfather’s will because the contingency—failure of their mother to make a valid disposition—never occurred. Because the children did not renounce their legacies under their mother’s will, the effect of renunciation was not before the court. Amounts paid from the trust fund to creditors were taxable, but money advanced by Alice Slosson to pay creditors, since decedent was not indebted to her, was improperly included in Alice Slosson’s taxable bequest. The tax order was modified by deducting $682.04 and otherwise affirmed.

Thai Prime Minister Prayuth Chan-ocha said no trade takes place between Thailand and North Korea and that Thailand has abided by U.N. resolutions. A U.S. envoy is expected in Bangkok to discuss stepping up pressure on North Korea over its weapons programs.

Carol Christ, 73, became chancellor of UC Berkeley, the first woman and oldest chancellor in its history. A Victorian literature scholar and former Smith College president, she previously taught at Berkeley, chaired English, and served as vice chancellor and provost. She takes over as the campus faces sexual assault scandals, budget woes, a fractured community, free speech debates, a student housing shortage, and scrutiny after a state audit found $175 million in undisclosed funds. Christ has made increasing black student enrollment—around 3 percent after Proposition 209—a priority, along with campus sexual assault. She plans a 2017-18 “free speech year,” debates between differing views, housing partnerships with Berkeley and Oakland, and addressing a $110 million deficit by increasing private philanthropy and cutting administration. She also seeks improved Sacramento relations and restoring community. Christ, who will earn nearly $532,000, will not live in the chancellor’s house.

The passage explains the soccer penalty kick taker and penalty kick procedure. A penalty kick is awarded for a direct-free-kick foul by a defender inside their own penalty area; common fouls include tripping and handling. The kick is taken from the penalty mark 12 yards from goal, defended only by the goalkeeper. Law 14 requirements include a stationary ball on the mark, non-moving goalposts/crossbar/net, an identified kicker, the goalkeeper on the goal line facing the kicker, other players at least 10 yards away and outside the penalty area, a referee signal, the ball kicked forward, and the ball in play when kicked and clearly moving. The passage covers coaching responsibilities, routines, experimentation, equipment and setup, choosing kickers and alternates, mental aspects, procedure, setting the ball, run-up, feinting restrictions, plant-foot placement, types of kicks, target locations, follow-up, practice, repetition, visualization, scouting goalkeepers, having at least two kicks, changing kickers, tap penalty kicks, simulating game conditions, and summary tips. It emphasizes consistent routine, accuracy, lower corners, regular practice, and coach responsibility for team positioning, while the kicker must be prepared and score.

Options expiry is when an options contract becomes void and can no longer be used. In the US, the expiration date is the third Saturday of the expiration month, while the last trading day is usually the preceding Friday, or Thursday if Friday is a holiday. Expiration time is 11:59 a.m. EST. Expiration week is the week an options contract expires; large-cap stocks with actively traded options tend to have higher average weekly returns, called OPEX. Quad witching expiration week occurs four times yearly—March, June, September, and December. Backtests found SPY averaged 0.3% during expiry week, an XLV strategy about 0.7% per trade, an SPY overnight strategy 0.46%, and an SPY expiry-day short/day trade 0.18% over 306 trades. Expiry days showed slightly higher volatility than normal days, especially quad days. Developing strategies involves research, backtesting over at least 15 years or different market cycles, and forward-testing.

The UC1825B-SP PWM controller targets high-frequency switched-mode supplies, supports current- or voltage-mode with feed-forward, and offers protection, latched logic, undervoltage lockout, and totem-pole outputs.

Chenai Mathabire, a 35-year-old Zimbabwean nurse and epidemiologist, received an International AIDS Society prize for research showing that a faster tuberculosis test could be implemented at health centers in southeast Africa, helping HIV-positive patients with TB. After choosing nursing, she worked for Doctors Without Borders in Zimbabwe, South Sudan, and elsewhere. Her team studied rapid TB testing in Malawi and Mozambique, finding it produced results in under an hour, required a few hours of staff training, was easy to interpret, and was accepted by patients, unlike standard tests that could take days or months. The findings, published by Doctors Without Borders, led some health centers to adopt rapid TB testing. Mathabire still works for Doctors Without Borders, is considering more HIV/TB research, and moved to Sweden to marry.

The speaker says tonight has been a handful and the opponent played its best game to date, but the team held on and must respond. They discuss the playoffs, not going with Toronto, and better first periods. In Detroit, the speaker calls one phone call destiny-changing, praises a total team effort and five Russian players, thanks Jimmy Devellano and Scotty Bowman, and says the team won four straight and was the best team as the playoffs went on.

The speaker accepts the Democratic nomination and thanks Stevenson, Johnson, Butler, Symington, Humphrey, Rayburn, and Truman. He says the party platform’s pledges, including civil and economic rights, are to be kept. He states that his religious affiliation should not determine votes and that his public policy decisions will be his own. He says victory will not be easy and contrasts the Democrats with Republican opponents, especially Nixon, arguing the nation needs strong, creative Democratic leadership. He describes foreign and domestic changes, including new weapons, Communist influence, population and urban growth, human rights demands, medical advances, and automation. He calls for new leadership and a New Frontier of the 1960s, based on challenges, sacrifice, courage, and national purpose, and asks Americans to help meet the future.

A study of over 33,000 adults found non-exercisers were 44% more likely to suffer depression than those exercising one to two hours weekly. Small exercise could have prevented 12% of depression cases, and one hour weekly may significantly protect against depression. The lead author said exercise could be integrated into mental health plans and public health campaigns.

Republic of Ireland and Florida State soccer player Megan Connolly posted a Twitter video of a scary ride at Myrtle Beach; a teammate laughed, music played, and friends checked in after it went viral.

Google’s Project Fi added three compatible phones: the $199 Moto G6, $740 LG G7 ThinQ, and $899 LG V35 ThinQ. The service, launched in 2015, has few compatible devices and lacks Apple and Samsung phones; an analyst said the lack of iPhones halves its addressable market. Fi is an MVNO using T-Mobile, Sprint, U.S. Cellular, and Wi-Fi; it charges $20 monthly for unlimited calls/texts plus $10 per GB up to 6GB, with no charge for unused data. Google did not answer how a T-Mobile/Sprint merger might affect Fi or how many customers it has.

Liberal leader Andrew Wilkinson criticized Premier John Horgan over rising gas prices, accusing him of a tax grab and urging lower gas taxes. Horgan rejected the tax argument, calling a nine-cent overnight increase a gouging/profit issue and citing supply and refining capacity, adding he raised it with the federal government.

Vernon Leroy Wilson et al. appealed a judgment based on jury findings denying recovery for damages from a May 28, 1955 head-on collision on a three-lane highway. The jury found King was not negligent in the alleged ways, that Wilson drove into the western lane while driving north, that this was negligent and the sole proximate cause of the collision, and that the collision was not unavoidable. Appellants raised six assignments, including failure to submit issues and improper argument. The court found appellants did not object to the charge or timely request special issues, did not furnish opposing counsel a copy of requested issues, and did not object to the complained-of argument at trial. No reversible error was shown, so the judgment was affirmed.

On October 27, 2022, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that it issued a press release regarding its financial results for the fourth fiscal quarter ended September 24, 2022, attached as Exhibit 99.1.

This email compiles May 23, 2001 news reports on Enron’s Dabhol Power Company dispute in India. Reports say Madhav Godbole resigned as chairman of Maharashtra’s Enron renegotiation panel after Sharad Pawar criticized the negotiators’ “negative approach”; Maharashtra’s chief minister refused the resignation and asked Godbole to reconsider, while Pawar said his comments were not on behalf of the state government and that he was misquoted. A renegotiation meeting was called off, though DPC later confirmed it would attend a Godbole panel meeting. The clips also cover termination warnings, lender exposure and stock declines, NPA concerns, Indian power firms’ reluctance to buy DPC, possible damages, Enron’s India business valuation, and its withdrawal from a Qatar gas venture.

The speaker credits Coach Bylsma with bringing confidence when the switch was made, despite a good young core, and says the team reached the playoffs. A five-game road trip, winning the first three, and later trades for Billy and Adams were a turning point and gave a realistic chance to turn the season around. A ring would be a nice memento, though a picture would suffice. Sid’s leadership is mainly on-ice, playing his game and system and contributing defensively even without many points. Jordan is an offensive, responsible two-way forward who helped at both ends. Two skilled leaders can suddenly dominate for minutes and always come out hard. The organization has been remarkable and dominant since winning its first Cup, despite losing significant pieces.

North Tyneside Mayor Norma Redfearn said councils south of the River Tyne could later ask to join the North of Tyne devolution deal. North Tyneside’s cabinet voted unanimously to move ahead. The deal includes an elected mayor, £600m over 30 years, and is set to bring 10,000 jobs. It was announced in November 2017 after a previous seven-council deal was scrapped. Redfearn criticized Durham County Council’s referendum and withdrawal. A new combined authority is planned for summer 2018, with mayoral elections in May 2019. Newcastle leader Nick Forbes rejected “under-powered” claims, citing health, housing, and per-population investment. Northumberland was due to discuss devolution.

Plymouth Studio School is to close because it is only half full—155 students against a capacity of 300—and not financially viable, according to MP Johnny Mercer. The £4.2 million sports-focused free school is expected to cease operating at the end of summer term 2018, subject to government approval, three years after opening. The closure was announced before an imminent Ofsted report expected to criticise the school. The school said a “decision in principle” was made after discussions with the Regional Schools Commissioner’s office and the Department for Education, and the report rated it “inadequate.” Mercer said performance failed to improve significantly, he was deeply disappointed, and he is focused on helping affected students find new places. It would be the 19th studio school to close since the model’s inception.

Assembly Republican Leader Chad Mayes has no regrets about supporting California’s cap-and-trade program, though he wishes he had attended Gov. Jerry Brown’s signing ceremony. His vote drew escalating Republican criticism, including claims that he betrayed party principles and provided political cover to Democrats. Critics called for him to step down, and the state party board was expected to vote on the issue. Mayes faces a possible caucus leadership challenge from Assemblyman Jay Obernolte when lawmakers return Aug. 21. Other Republicans who voted for the legislation also faced backlash. The dispute complicated a state party fundraising agreement and led Assemblywoman Melissa Melendez to be moved out of her office.

The 2017 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons for drawing attention to the catastrophic humanitarian consequences of nuclear weapons and efforts to achieve a treaty-based prohibition. ICAN, a coalition of NGOs in 100 countries, helped drive the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, adopted July 7 with support from 122 nations; the five permanent UN Security Council members did not participate. ICAN said the award was an honor and that nuclear weapons should be rejected; its chief executive called the prize hugely important.

Design details for a push-pull converter using TPS7H500x-SP controllers include a dead time of approximately 25 ns with RPS and RSP of 20.5 kΩ; a leading edge blank time of roughly 50 ns with RLEB of 49.9 kΩ; a 33-nF soft-start capacitor giving ~7.5 ms; a transformer turns ratio of 2.5 and primary inductance of 40 μH; 170-V primary GaN FETs and an 80-V synchronous rectifier; a 0.47-μH output inductor; at least 1.3 mF output capacitance with ~2.3 mF used; RCS of 7.5 Ω; a 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor; Type 2A compensation with RCOMP 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP 15 nF, and CHF 47 pF; and a 102-kΩ slope compensation resistor. It also covers application curves, controller supply recommendations of 4 V to 14 V with a minimum 0.1-µF bypass, layout guidelines, related documentation, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

It featured guest lectures, workshops, a human library, exhibits, and infotainment shows. Exhibits included Hyperloop India, InMoov, KalamSat, ISRO’s Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre displays, and Ugears. The event concluded with a valediction and performances by Suhani Shah and Azeem Banatwalla.

The 2025 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine went to Shimon Sakaguchi, Mary Brunkow and Fred Ramsdell for discovering regulatory T cells, which calm the immune system and prevent it from attacking the body. Failure of these cells can cause autoimmune disorders or damaging inflammation, and they help prevent fetal rejection. Sakaguchi identified T-regs in 1995; Brunkow and Ramsdell found a mutation causing fatal autoimmune disease in mice and revealed mutations in people in 2001. Scientists are exploring harnessing T-regs for cancer and other conditions.

In People v. Arthur Heine, the defendant moved to dismiss a bigamy indictment, arguing his second marriage was void under Domestic Relations Law §11(5) because it was performed by a Justice of the Peace when he was 19. Grand Jury minutes showed his first marriage had not been dissolved and was valid when he married Marie Licciardi at age 19; he admitted both marriages and that he knew he committed bigamy. The court considered whether §11(5) merely prohibited such a solemnization or made the marriage void. Citing conflicting decisions, the court followed Caplan v. Caplan and De Martino v. De Martino and granted the motion to dismiss the indictment.

The federal government suspended a $12.5 million grant, though the university launched an experimental turbine. It has no current plans to revive AFLOAT but will hold private meetings.

Drew Doughty says the team faced the top conference teams and handled adversity, and now must do so again. He is not discouraged, expected a long series, and says the opponent is executing better and playing its system, so adjustments are needed. The team is creating chances; Marty is playing well; they need dirty goals by crashing the net. Distractions involving family, friends, and the Cup must be set aside, with the team first. He says they were frustrated by prior distractions, will be prepared, and discusses attacking an aggressive goalie and getting rebounds. He says they are fine, are motivated by the Cup, and he loves playing with Rob because of communication and accountability.

The Federal Reserve raised short-term interest rates by a quarter point, its third hike since December, moving the key rate to 1%–1.25%. Citing a solid economy, it upgraded growth and unemployment forecasts but lowered its inflation projection to 1.6% for this year. Mortgage rates are not expected to rise immediately. The Fed also plans to begin gradually selling assets later this year, starting at $10 billion a month, and most officials see at least one more hike this year.

The speaker is excited and happy to be in a hostile hometown environment but says the team must treat it like any other road game and keep focus to finish the job. They feel confident at the net, credit the team’s play, expect Edmonton to be ready, and note they are having fun with teammates.

Volkswagen of America asked a Virginia judge to delay excess-emissions trials for at least six months, fearing a lawyer’s documentary comments about monkey diesel-fume tests and Adolf Hitler/the Holocaust would prejudice jurors. The first consumer fraud trial, involving a 2014 diesel Jetta, is set for Feb. 26. Lawyer Michael Melkersen called the motion hogwash. Volkswagen has agreed to spend over $25 billion in the U.S.; about 2,000 owners opted out of a 2016 settlement and most seek additional compensation. Daimler and BMW also suspended or moved staff linked to the monkey tests.

Madison returns to the House a bill setting apart funds for roads, canals, and improving water-course navigation because he cannot reconcile it with the Constitution. He states the power is not among Congress’s enumerated powers, is not within the necessary and proper power, and is not included in the power to regulate commerce among the States. Referring it to the common defense and general welfare clause would undermine enumerated powers and create a general power; state assent cannot confer the power. Though roads and canals are important, he withholds his signature.

NATO’s 2017 annual report shows upward trend lines, Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg said. In 2017, NATO deployed four multinational battle groups to the Baltic republics and Poland, increased forward presence in the Black Sea region, strengthened cyber defenses and resilience against hybrid war, joined the global coalition to defeat ISIS, raised EU cooperation, and welcomed Montenegro as its 29th member. Burden-sharing increased, with three consecutive years of increased defense spending in Europe and Canada, adding $46 billion since the 2014 Wales pledge, including $18 billion on major equipment. NATO deployments rose to over 23,000 troops at the end of 2017 from just under 18,000 in 2014. Stoltenberg cited Russian actions including the Salisbury nerve-agent attack, Georgia, Crimea, support to separatists, election subversion, military buildup, and nuclear-conventional integration. NATO will defend all allies, he said. NATO increased its Resolute Support training mission from 13,000 to around 16,000 and planned a new training mission in Iraq.

The passage argues that scalping is a waste of time because most scalpers lose money. It involves competition with better-equipped traders and institutions, market randomness and noise, slippage, commissions, and other transaction costs. Backtesting scalping strategies is difficult and unlikely to reflect real profitability. Scalping also requires automation and involves stress. The passage states that profitable scalping strategies are rare and that there are better opportunities in longer time frames.

Becton, Dickinson and Company has paid dividends since 1962 and increased them by more than 10% in 12 of the past 13 years since 2004; 2012 rose 9.8%, and since 2004 growth averaged 16.3%. The passage estimates 2017 calendar-year dividends of $2.98, a 10% increase, or a full-year 2017 dividend of $2.92. It cites fiscal 2017 GAAP diluted EPS guidance of $7.90–$8.00 and a falling payout ratio. The CareFusion merger hurt 2015–2016 profits through acquisition, restructuring, and interest costs, while first-quarter 2017 included a $336 million litigation gain. It notes risks from manufacturing issues, higher interest rates, and competing products, and concludes Becton’s dividend is safe and growing, suitable for dividend portfolios.

The study uses DFT calculations to predict three novel o-MAX phases, Mo2A2AlC3 (A = Zr, Nb, Ta), and examines their structural, stability, electronic, mechanical, thermal, and optical properties. The hexagonal P63/mmc compounds are reported to be chemically, dynamically, and mechanically stable; metallic; and characterized by mixed ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding. They are brittle and anisotropic, with Vickers hardness values of 6.025, 6.277, and 6.224 GPa. Mo2Zr2AlC3 shows the highest chemical stability and Debye temperature and relatively high damage tolerance; Mo2Nb2AlC3 shows the highest stiffness, fracture toughness, machinability, and bonding strength; Mo2Ta2AlC3 has the lowest Young’s modulus. Thermal results include minimum thermal conductivities of 0.89, 0.90, and 0.74 W/m·K; TEC values of 11.11, 9.90, and 11.47 ×10−6 K−1; melting temperatures of 2064, 2237, and 2131 K; and Grüneisen parameters of 1.37, 1.44, and 1.37. Optical results indicate metallic behavior and reflectivity above 44% across IR, visible, and mid-UV ranges. The study concludes these phases are potential candidates for thermal barrier coatings and solar heat-shielding layers.

The passage says Celtic are miles ahead, have Champions League millions and may receive more from selling Moussa Dembele, so could spend big and move further away. It says King promised £30million backing but did not deliver, raising expectations and leaving Warburton to pay the price. Warburton’s mistakes include Joey Barton and Joe Garner, while the team’s most consistent players, Clint Hill and Kenny Miller, are 38 and 37. The passage also says Rangers’ cup semi-final win led to Celtic changes under Dermot Desmond, and Celtic have not looked back. It adds Rodgers should strengthen, target Europe, and use Celtic’s chance to move away from Rangers, unlike 2012.

This critical reflection paper addresses how generative AI can be employed in future educational contexts in a humanizing and ethical manner, and how to incorporate it into modern and imagined education systems. It reviews Anders and Foucault on technology, power, and regimes of truth; Freire on humanization and conscientization; Bloom’s and Revised Bloom’s taxonomy for cognitive learning; and Arendt’s hierarchy of labor, work, and action. The authors argue that RBT is useful but insufficient for ethical questions, so they supplement it with Arendt to focus on purpose and action. They propose a framework for assessing AI use in education across online, blended, and in-person settings, centered on student AI use and spanning from consumptive labor to humanizing action, with humanizing, action-oriented use considered ethically more appropriate. The framework includes RBT examples and guiding questions for educators. Applications include community-based political action and Socratic dialogue for individualized research. The paper concludes that AI will remain part of society and education systems, and that ethical guideposts drawing on these philosophers can help educators and learners use AI to foster humanization, agency, and action, while calling for future research, especially in gray areas of AI use.

A method and apparatus handle reduced available processing time in systems using configurable transmission time intervals (TTIs) or short TTIs (sTTIs). A WTRU may determine processing capabilities, send a processing capability (PC) indication to an eNB, receive a PC configuration, determine a maximum timing advance or maximum Rx-Tx time difference based on the PC configuration or capabilities, and limit an applied timing advance or Rx-Tx time difference for a specific TTI length. The WTRU may measure a processing value (PV), determine headroom as the difference between the PV and PC, report the headroom based on a condition, and perform an action. The WTRU may receive a TTI or sTTI configuration, determine a PC based on processing criteria, and report it. For an uplink grant, the WTRU may determine available processing time from the end of DCI to the start of the scheduled transmission and transmit if it meets a threshold; otherwise it may not transmit. For a downlink grant, the WTRU may determine a start time for HARQ-ACK and transmit if the start time is later than an uplink symbol time at least the determined available processing time after the end of the downlink transmission.

India’s truck market is expected to change significantly over the next decade, with trucks becoming faster, more powerful, more efficient and more connected. Population growth and urbanisation are expected to increase demand for haulage. The industry is moving toward Bharat IV and an accelerated Bharat VI rollout, and the Goods and Services Tax is expected to free up long-distance routes, supporting demand for more powerful trucks. Global OEMs could play a greater role, and Make in India/AMP II aims to expand manufacturing, exports, GDP contribution and jobs. The passage states that electric and self-driving trucks remain many decades away from India’s roads.

Examples of the disclosure relate to implementing fundamental computational primitives used by applications such as speech recognition, intelligent industrial control, object detection and recognition, and vision using a matrix multiplication accelerator (MMA). A device includes memory, a processor, and an MMA with a multiplier buffer, multiplicand buffers, result buffers, format components, a row offset component, and a nonlinearity component. The processor includes streaming engines and executes control software for each primitive. A method includes configuring a streaming engine to stream data for the primitive from memory, configuring the MMA to format the data, and executing the primitive. The MMA performs a Load, Store, Execute instruction and supports operations such as =, +=, −=, or none. The disclosure describes implementations of primitives including 2D convolution, small and large matrix matrix multiplication, matrix matrix point wise multiplication, matrix matrix addition, small vector matrix multiplication, small vector summation, affine transformation, FFTs, DCTs, convolution, correlation, matrix assignment, matrix permutation, and matrix transposition. It provides examples of configuring streaming engines and the MMA for these primitives, including batch and large operations, tiling, zero padding, row offsets, and output formatting. Other examples may use a host processor and different processor or buffer dimensions.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated June 3, 2021. Under Item 5.02(b), Jerome Guillen, President, Tesla Heavy Trucking, departed Tesla as of June 3, 2021. Tesla thanked him for his contributions and wished him well. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn on June 7, 2021.

Cowen shares surged 19% after CEFC China agreed to buy about 20% for $100 million and provide $175 million debt financing. CEFC will pay $18 per Class A share, appoint three directors, with the deal expected to close by Q3 2017 subject to approvals.

Apple overtook Samsung in fourth-quarter smartphone sales, selling 77 million iPhones for 17.9% share versus Samsung’s 76.8 million and 17.8%, though Samsung led for the full year. Samsung’s Note7 recall hurt it, but a new flagship and delayed iPhone replacement may help it regain the lead. Huawei, Oppo, and BBK ranked third to fifth.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU is based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture GA100 GPU and built on TSMC 7nm N7 with 54.2 billion transistors and an 826 mm2 die. It adds third-generation Tensor Cores with TF32, IEEE-compliant FP64, BF16, INT8, INT4, binary support, and fine-grained structured sparsity. It has 40 GB HBM2 memory at 1555 GB/sec and a 40 MB L2 cache with residency controls. MIG securely partitions an A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances with isolation and QoS. Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, and it supports PCIe Gen 4 and SR-IOV. This paper examines the use of LLMs as synthetic agents in social science and argues that their outputs are often misinterpreted as draws from human population distributions. It states that LLMs generate text probabilistically through learned patterns and sampling, but are not Bayesian inference engines and do not maintain or update posterior beliefs. The paper addresses statistical limitations and the future of LLM agents, reviewing applications such as LLM-as-respondent surveys, prediction of experimental results, and multi-agent simulations. It discusses non-Bayesian behavior, including violations of the martingale/CID property, introspective hallucination, order dependence, and incoherent predictions. Apparent predictive success is attributed to scale, pattern matching, emergent abilities, and fine-tuning/RLHF, while tuning may improve task performance without statistical correction and may reduce Bayesian coherence. The paper warns against a universal homo silicus and recommends domain-specific agents. Guidelines include treating LLM agents as conditional predictors rather than calibrated beliefs, measuring algorithmic fidelity, subgroup validity, variance, distribution shift, confidence sets, augmentation, individual/task anchoring, avoiding self-conditioning and order effects, stress-testing, and full reproducibility. It concludes that LLMs have promise as near-term predictors and for otherwise difficult research, but their limitations as black boxes and non-principled Bayesian reasoners require specific models for specific social questions.
