The excerpt covers TLV322x open-drain output, ESD protection, TLV321x power-on reset, comparator operation, external hysteresis, low-side current sensing, layout guidance, and support/legal information. The open-drain output is sinking-only and can be pulled up to an external voltage from 0 V to 5.5 V independent of V+, allowing logical OR’ing and level translation. A pull-up current of 100 µA to 1 mA is recommended; lower pull-up resistance can improve rise time but increases VOL and power dissipation, while large pull-ups >1 MΩ create an exponential rising edge. Direct output shorts to a voltage source can cause thermal runaway and device destruction, so a series current-limiting resistor is recommended. Unused open-drain outputs may float or be tied to V−. Inputs and outputs have ESD protection to V+ and V−; input voltages are limited to 0.2 V beyond the rails, and current should be limited to 10 mA or less for low-impedance sources. TLV321x POR operates up to 32 µs after VPOR of 1.65 V is crossed, holding output low for both open-drain and push-pull outputs. Comparator operation compares VIN to VREF, with output state depending on which is greater; chatter can occur near offset, propagation delay varies with transition and overdrive, and smaller overdrive <100 mV lengthens delay. External hysteresis using positive feedback adds to 1.8 mV internal hysteresis and is described for inverting and non-inverting configurations. A low-side current sensing application uses an amplifier and high-speed comparator, with alert high when amplifier output exceeds 1.1 V. Layout guidance includes 0.1 µF low-ESR bypass capacitors, supply options, minimizing output-input coupling, series resistors, and controlled impedance traces. The document also includes support resources, trademarks, ESD caution, revision history, mechanical/packaging/orderable information, and legal notices.

In Phase 1 and Phase 2/3, injection site reactions and systemic events within 7 days after vaccination were recorded in e-diaries. These reactions/events after BNT162b1 or BNT162b2 were well tolerated and went away after a short time; most were mild or moderate. Injection site pain was the most common injection site reaction, and tiredness and headache were the most common systemic events. Results for the first 360 Phase 2 participants were similar to those seen in total Phase 2/3 participants. Reactions/events in booster and BNT162b2SA groups were similar to those in the larger Phase 2/3 group.

Medical problems within 1 month after Dose 2 or boosters were mostly mild or moderate. In Phase 1, all tested BNT162b1 and BNT162b2 doses (10, 20, and 30 µg) were well tolerated except BNT162b1 at 100 µg, which was stopped after Dose 1 because of injection site reactions or systemic events. BNT162b2 at 30 µg was selected for Phase 2/3. No Phase 1 participants left because of medical problems, and no single medical problem occurred in more than 2 participants in any dose group. In Phase 2/3, few BNT162b2 or placebo recipients left the blinded part because of medical problems; most medical problems were mild or moderate, and most in the BNT162b2 group involved injection site reactions or systemic events. Serious medical problems were few; no single serious medical problem occurred in at least 1% of participants in any group. Researchers did not believe many serious problems were related to the study vaccine, while some were considered possibly related. No participant died during Phase 1. In Phase 2/3, deaths occurred among participants who received BNT162b2 at the start, placebo at the start then BNT162b2, and placebo at the start before any BNT162b2; causes differed, and researchers do not believe BNT162b2 caused the deaths. In Phase 3, no participant died among those who had not gotten BNT162b2 before receiving at least 1 dose of BNT162b2SA.

The court of appeals reviewed TEC’s appeal from a judgment awarding Erdy, Wolford, and Jones $5,225 each against TEC and others for breach of contract for educational services. Plaintiffs contracted with PIO, attended ELC after PIO sold its assets, graduated, and later ELC sold assets to TEC. Plaintiffs sued before the ELC-TEC sale; default judgment was entered against PIO and ELC, and TEC’s liability was decided against TEC. TEC argued it was not liable as a successor or as assuming liability. The appellate court held successor corporations generally are not liable absent express or implied assumption, de facto merger, continuation, or fraud. Plaintiffs did not claim merger or fraud. The incorporated asset purchase agreement exempted the buyer from pre-purchase liabilities except specified items not including student contracts, so TEC did not expressly assume liability. No implied assumption arose merely from TEC’s awareness of pending litigation, and no authority required bona fide purchaser status. TEC was not a mere continuation because no common identity of stockholders, directors, and stock was shown, and no evidence showed TEC was not a separate entity. The contract action required plaintiffs to prove their case; the trial court improperly imposed liability on a motion to dismiss. Reversed and remanded.

The Chande Momentum Oscillator (CMO) is a momentum-based technical indicator introduced by Tushar Chande in 1994, similar to the RSI and stochastic indicator. It measures momentum using higher and lower closes over a chosen period, oscillates between +100 and -100, and signals overbought above +50 and oversold below -50. Positive values indicate strength and negative values weakness, with trend direction considered. Divergences and a moving average signal line can also be used. The CMO cannot identify the main trend and should be combined with trend indicators. Best settings and timeframes depend on backtesting. A 9-day CMO backtest on the SPY ETF with a 5-day maximum holding period produced high risk-adjusted returns and lower drawdown than buy-and-hold, while longer holding periods reduced returns. The CMO performs poorly in volatile, non-trending markets, has limitations and false signals, and can be used in sideways markets for mean-reversion or in momentum strategies to spot pullback endings.

Research has long noted bacteria in the intestines, but microbes were once considered freeloaders; this view has changed. The microbiota includes diverse microbes living in and on humans, estimated at about 39 trillion bacteria alongside 30 trillion human cells, and is essential to digestion, metabolism, immune responses, and inflammation. Disruption of gut microbiota may contribute to childhood asthma, obesity, colitis, and colon cancer. The microbiota shows daily, or circadian, rhythmicity. Studies using fecal samples found the gut microbiome differs from morning to evening. In mice, microbiota metabolites circulate in blood and alter liver gene expression for metabolic enzymes; antibiotics and changed feeding times altered liver physiology, and acetaminophen toxicity varied by time of day, being less toxic at dawn and more toxic at dusk. The passage says microbiota regulates liver detoxification over the day, with implications for drug timing and disease treatment or prevention. Technological advances enabled these studies. Microbial communities may not be reducible to single species, as members can depend on others. Findings may be relevant to humans, including those taking long antibiotics or shift workers eating at the wrong time, potentially increasing obesity and metabolic syndrome risk.

The passage explains that the Money Flow Index (MFI) is a momentum indicator combining price and volume to measure money flow into and out of a security over a specified period. It oscillates between 0 and 100, shows overbought and oversold conditions, and can predict potential price reversals. The MFI generates overbought signals above 80, oversold signals at 20 or below, and bullish or bearish divergence signals. It is described as similar to a volume-weighted Relative Strength Index, unlike Chaikin Money Flow, which uses price data alone. Traders use MFI for reversals, with a default 14-day lookback that can be adjusted; higher periods give fewer, possibly more reliable signals, while lower periods give more false signals. The article outlines a strategy using overbought/oversold MFI conditions with bullish or bearish engulfing patterns and reports backtests: on PEP, 581 trades, 71% win rate, 1.8 profit factor, and 10.4% annual return; on SPY, 10.6% CAGR; combined PEP/SPY, 15% CAGR; gold performed poorly. It concludes MFI can be a timing tool and should be backtested.

This research examined 273 full-text studies on modern physics education in Turkey from 2000–2023. Most were articles, in Turkish, from Tübitak Ulakbim, and concentrated between 2010 and 2019. Common topics included the atom, photoelectric effect, theory of relativity, nuclear energy, Compton effect, and Heisenberg uncertainty principle. Quantitative designs, purposive sampling, and high school or undergraduate samples were common, with sample sizes mostly 31–100 and intervention durations varying from 0 to 8 weeks. Data collection mainly used interviews, tests, questionnaires, and scales; frequency, percentage, t-tests, and content analysis were common analyses. Validity and reliability methods varied, with insufficient information reported. Results showed positive and negative developments in modern physics education, but discussions were not sufficiently supported by literature. Recommendations included using different analytical methods, increasing sample sizes, and enriching methods and intervention examples.

Altermagnetism is described as a magnetic phase distinct from ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism; it breaks time-reversal symmetry but preserves its combination with crystallographic symmetries, compensating the net magnetic dipole moment. Its non-symmorphic symmetries cause spin-degenerate bands to split in most of the Brillouin zone without spin-orbit coupling, leaving degeneracies on nodal lines and planes, with d-wave, g-wave, etc. patterns. The passage uses group theory and DFT to calculate higher-order atomic multipoles in real space by projecting spin density onto tesseral harmonics in MnF2, CrSb, and KMnF3. In MnF2, in-phase collinear octupole dxymz and 32-pole gxyz2mz are found; in CrSb, the lowest in-phase collinear multipole is a 32-pole gyz(y2−3x2)mz. Noncollinear spin density components show symmetry-allowed multipoles that vanish without SOC; under SOC, noncollinear octupoles and 32-poles become nonzero linearly, while collinear multipoles change quadratically. In KMnF3, fluorine octahedral rotations induce altermagnetism from antiferromagnetism, with the in-phase 32-pole gxy(x2−y2)mz linear in rotation angle. The passage links these multipoles to tensor observables including piezomagnetism and second-order magnetoelectric effects, and concludes that noncollinear spin density, higher-order multipoles, and SOC are important for altermagnets and macroscopic response.

The passage defines lipid profile, cholesterol, HDL, LDL, triglycerides, and related terms, then reviews HIV/AIDS, cardiovascular disease, dyslipidaemia, atherosclerosis, laboratory diagnosis, and treatment. This application relates to screen display methods and electronic devices. An electronic device displays at least two application interfaces, including a first interface in full screen mode and a second interface as a floating window in the first interface. In response to a first operation on the first interface, the electronic device automatically displays the second interface in a minimized state in the first interface, where the minimized second interface is a floating ball, an icon of the second application, a contact avatar, or a video pop-up window. If the operation is on a first edit box, a focus obtaining event triggers minimization; a focus loss event restores the second interface to a floating window. The minimized interface may be placed away from the cursor location. Operations on the floating second interface may display it in full screen mode and minimize the first interface. Multiple floating windows may be minimized. In another method, two interfaces are displayed side by side without overlap; an operation on the first displays it in full screen mode, minimizes the second, and displays the minimized second interface in the first. A focus loss event or an operation on the minimized second interface can restore side-by-side display. Corresponding apparatuses, electronic devices, computer storage media, and computer program products are also described.

This open-blinded, cross-sectional study evaluated the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) in patients with urinary tract infections (UTIs) and its association with kidney damage. Eighty UTI patients aged 20–65 with suspected proteinuria were recruited; after exclusions for low creatinine and absent proteinuria, 46 patients were analyzed. Based on KDIGO guidelines, participants were classified as Stage I (n=12), Stage II (n=16), and Stage III (n=18). Urinary creatinine excretion was significantly reduced across all stages compared with the reference interval. Urinary microprotein was significantly elevated in Stage III. The P/C ratio increased across stages and was highest in Stage III. The study concluded that proteinuria was significantly associated with UTIs, that urinary creatinine was reduced, and that the P/C ratio was a reliable diagnostic marker for UTI-associated renal impairment.

Potential returns depend on the option, strike price, underlying price at expiration, and price direction. The passage advises understanding risks and rewards, using quantified analysis and backtesting, monitoring trades, and practicing risk management such as stop losses and taking profits. Fees and tax implications vary, and liquidity depends on the specific option. Common mistakes include overtrading and trading without understanding returns and risks. It states profits cannot be protected and recommends relying on quantified backtests and following a plan; if unable to use backtesting and quantified analysis, it advises keeping away from options trading.

The writer returns to the House a bill appropriating for the repair, preservation, and completion of certain public works begun under law, stating objections briefly and promising fuller discussion. The message argues that federal power over internal improvements has long been disputed and remains unsettled. The phrase “internal improvements” is not in the Constitution and lacks exact meaning. If Congress could construct railroads and canals, it could also construct turnpikes, bridges, levees, irrigation canals, and other improvements. The Federal Government is described as having only delegated powers; the preamble and general welfare clause do not grant power. No specific grant authorizes internal improvement appropriations. Enumerated powers such as post-roads, war, navy, armies, commerce, and public property can justify only improvements necessary to those powers, not a general system. The clause on exclusive legislation over federal sites does not confer independent authority. Early practice supported lighthouses, beacons, buoys, and piers; later river and harbor appropriations raised the same issue. The writer says Congress may provide some aids to navigation under long usage, but cannot extend this to general river and harbor improvements. The message discusses navigable waters under federal jurisdiction, Jackson’s rule confining appropriations to places below ports of entry, legislative discretion, and executive responsibility. It recommends cession of soil and jurisdiction for permanent harbor works and separate bills for each appropriation, and suggests confining federal appropriations to works necessary to undoubted powers, leaving others to individual enterprise or the States, or to state tonnage duties with Congress’s consent.

The present disclosure relates to autonomous vehicle systems and methods that use a machine-learned yield model. The model receives feature data descriptive of objects perceived by the autonomous vehicle and/or surrounding environment and outputs yield decisions relative to the objects, such as yield or do not yield, proceed through a selected gap or stop, or enter or not enter an intersection to prevent gridlock. Features can include object state, location relative to travel ways, the vehicle, or a route; required deceleration or acceleration; jerk limits; traffic signal transition timing and last transition; stop line, cross traffic line, and exit point locations; and gap data for additional vehicles based on predicted trajectories. A yield controller can input features into the model and receive decisions. Motion planning can generate a motion plan and control vehicle motion according to the decisions, including via cost functions, an optimization planner, and gap penalties. The model can include decision tree-based models or neural networks and can be trained using supervised techniques with log data and simulated yield behaviors, labeled or scored. The systems are described as improving autonomous driving performance, scalability, adaptability, memory usage, and speed.

Studies, including the CLEERE Study of 4,979 children over 20 years, found that more time outdoors had a protective effect against needing myopic refractive correction. Near-work, computer use, and television were not to blame. Having two nearsighted parents raised risk to about 60% with low outdoor time; about 14 hours outdoors weekly lowered it to about 20%, comparable to children with no nearsighted parents. Time outdoors had little to no effect on prescription changes in already nearsighted children. Theories include exercise, vitamin D, and brighter light stimulating retinal dopamine to slow abnormal eye growth, with evidence indicating light exposure may matter. Sunscreen and sunglasses are advised to avoid ultraviolet problems.

This paper investigates how startups develop Internet-of-Things systems in early stages through a multiple-case exploratory study of eight startups, using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis with the SEMAT Essence framework. It reports that startups often lack all needed competence and use external consultants, component or service providers, and manufacturers. It identifies three MVP types—looks-like, functional works-like, and quality works-like—with development generally starting with looks-like MVPs and later shifting toward functionality and quality. Common ways of working include in-house design, outsourced implementation and manufacturing, rapid prototyping, reuse-oriented development, and iterative or Agile development. Hardware complexity, dependencies, and speed-quality considerations affect early-stage development. The study aims to support methodological adjustments for Internet-of-Things startup development.

The lecture covers link-cut trees, a data structure for maintaining a forest of rooted unordered trees under operations such as make-tree, link, cut, find-root, and path aggregation in logarithmic amortized time. It represents trees using preferred-path decomposition into auxiliary splay trees keyed by depth, connected by path-parent pointers, and reduces most operations to an access helper. Analysis uses heavy-light decomposition to bound preferred-child changes, first yielding a log-squared bound and then, using the splay access lemma, a log n amortized bound. A worst-case version using dynamic heavy-light decomposition and weight-balanced trees is also mentioned.

The CCI (Commodity Channel Index) is a momentum oscillator that measures a security’s current price relative to an average price over a given period and is used to identify overbought/oversold conditions and possible cyclical reversals. It oscillates above and below zero; readings above +100 are generally considered overbought and below -100 oversold, though levels vary by asset. It can show divergences, and its formula uses typical price, moving average, mean deviation, and a constant. Invented by Donald R. Lambert in 1980 for commodities, it is now used on stocks and ETFs. Advantages include spotting overbought/oversold conditions with quantifiable results; disadvantages include being lagging, not a timing tool, and best suited to stocks and bonds. The best setup uses daily bars and short lookback periods, such as 5–9. A S&P 500/SPY backtest using a 9-day lookback and -90 buy threshold produced a profit factor of about 1.8, average gain of 0.55%, and max drawdown of 23%. RSI, ROC, Stochastics, and MACD are similar indicators, and the passage states CCI is good but better indicators exist.

The paper introduces VN-HGCN, a heterogeneous graph convolutional network that uses virtual nodes to learn node embeddings and capture long-range information within 4 layers without predefined meta-paths. Parameter sensitivity analysis indicates robustness across hidden-layer dimension, number of layers, and number of type-level virtual nodes, with 4 layers helping alleviate over-smoothing. Future work includes extending the model to various tasks and large-scale datasets.

GLUCOSE is a distributional offline reinforcement learning model developed to recommend personalized hourly regular insulin doses on the first day after cardiac surgery. Postoperative hyperglycemia is common and associated with infections, acute kidney injury, arrhythmias, longer length of stay, and mortality; the Society of Thoracic Surgeons recommends glucose below 180 mg/dL, but achieving control is challenging. GLUCOSE was trained on MIMIC-IV and externally validated on eICU-CRD, including 6,148 development and 649 validation patients. It was selected from 200 independent models and evaluated with off-policy estimation. Estimated performance returns were 0.0 [-0.07, 0.06] internally and -0.63 [-0.74, -0.52] externally, versus clinician returns of -1.29 and -1.02. Time in range was highest when clinician insulin doses matched GLUCOSE recommendations. SHAP showed current glucose, recent glucose, weight, and mechanical ventilation as important features. In human evaluations, GLUCOSE had lower mean absolute error than treating clinicians against endocrinologist references, and blinded expert ratings of safety, effectiveness, and acceptability were comparable or improved versus human policies. In excluded external-validation subsets with ambiguous medication data, recommendation distributions were comparable and differences were not clinically significant. Limitations include retrospective design, need for prospective trials, only first postoperative day, no dietary data, and exclusions due to missing medication documentation in eICU-CRD. The authors conclude GLUCOSE dynamically optimizes glucose management and showed clinical robustness and safety, with future randomized trials recommended.

The passage introduces SimulRAG, a simulator-based RAG framework for long-form scientific question answering. It addresses hallucination and challenges in applying existing RAG approaches to scientific simulators, including the discrepancy between textual and numerical spaces and the lack of fine-grained control in updating long-form answers. SimulRAG includes a generalized simulator retrieval interface to transform between textual and numerical modalities and a claim-level generation method that decomposes answers into atomic claims for verification and updating. It uses uncertainty estimation scores and simulator boundary assessment (UE+SBA) to selectively verify uncertain and verifiable claims. The authors construct a long-form scientific QA benchmark covering climate modeling and epidemiology, with ground truth verified by simulations and human annotators. Experiments with GPT-4o and Claude-3.5 show SimulRAG outperforms RAG baselines by 30.4% in informativeness and 16.3% in factuality. UE+SBA consistently outperforms baselines across metrics, models, benchmarks, and budgets, and SBA filters non-verifiable claims. A limitation is the assumption that all questions relate to available simulators.

The lecture discusses taint tracking and TaintDroid, a system for information-flow analysis on Android phones. The problem is that apps can exfiltrate sensitive data such as contacts, phone number, email, location, and IMEI. Traditional Android permissions are insufficient because they address device access rather than specific data flows. Banning apps that both read sensitive data and access the network would break legitimate apps and would not stop side channels, app collusion, or tricking other apps into leaking data. Malware may use location or IMEI for ads, steal credentials, or turn phones into bots.

TaintDroid tracks sensitive information from sources such as GPS, accelerometer, contacts, and IMEI, and treats the network as the sink. It uses a 32-bit bitvector for up to 32 taint sources. Taint propagates from right-hand side to left-hand side in Dalvik instructions: move operations copy taint, and binary operations take the union of operand taints. Arrays, IPC messages, and files receive a single taint tag representing the union of their components, which conservatively overestimates taint. Native methods require manual analysis. Taint flags are stored near variables for cache efficiency. Evaluation found apps exfiltrated data without disclosing it in EULAs. Reported overhead is about 3% to 5% memory and 3% to 29% CPU.

TaintDroid does not handle implicit flows through branches, though PC tainting can help. Low-level x86 or ARM taint tracking can increase coverage but is expensive, complex, and can cause false positives or taint explosion. Simple network scanning is insufficient. Label systems allow programmer-defined labels and static checking. TightLip uses doppelganger processes with scrubbed sensitive files and compares system calls to detect leaks in legacy programs, requiring per-file scrubbers.

This study compared REM sleep microstructure in patients with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), RBD associated with Parkinson’s disease (PD+RBD), and controls. iRBD showed increased phasic REM sleep proportion. PD+RBD showed lower STW density than controls and shorter STW duration than controls and iRBD. Both patient groups had altered STW spectral characteristics with a shift toward higher frequencies. NREM/REM sleep transition duration increased from controls to iRBD to PD+RBD. RSWA was higher in iRBD than PD+RBD and controls, and higher in PD+RBD than controls. PD+RBD had lower REM sleep duration and proportion and longer REM sleep latency than controls and iRBD. Arousal index during REM sleep was higher in iRBD than controls and PD+RBD. The predominant transition sequence was atonia-first in controls and STW-first in iRBD and PD+RBD. The study concluded that REM sleep disturbances in RBD extend beyond muscle tone anomalies and include broader microstructural changes.

The lecture models the mechanical behavior of honeycombs. It derives in-plane elastic moduli and Poisson’s ratios, plateau stresses for elastic buckling, plastic yielding, and brittle crushing, and tensile behavior, noting that moduli are the same in tension and compression, with no elastic buckling in tension and similar plastic plateau stresses. It derives fracture toughness for brittle honeycombs and notes its dependence on cell size. It also analyzes triangular honeycombs as pin-jointed trusses, whose modulus scales as t/l rather than t/l cubed, making them stiffer and similar to lattice materials. The lecture then covers out-of-plane properties: Young’s modulus, Poisson’s ratios, shear moduli, compressive strengths for elastic buckling, plastic buckling/yielding, and brittle fracture and crushing. It mentions honeycomb uses in sandwich panels and energy absorption, and states that wood and cork will be discussed next.

Cheryl Tickles appealed a Superior Court judgment affirming the Industrial Accident Board’s denial of workers’ compensation benefits against PNC Bank. In Brennen v. Livingston Circuit Judge, Willis and Goucher began a chancery suit in Livingston County against the Brennens, who resided in Washtenaw County and were served there. This lecture introduces an advanced class on the evolution of proofs in computer science from the mid-1980s onward, not primarily cryptography. It covers course logistics such as weekly meetings, scribe notes, a problem set, recommended readings, and a guest lecture. Technically, it connects NP to proof systems, defines interactive proofs with a polynomial-time randomized verifier and an all-powerful prover, and explains completeness, soundness, and amplification by repetition. It gives a randomized matrix multiplication verification example and presents the sum-check protocol for proving that a sum of a multivariate polynomial over \(H^m\) equals β. It analyzes the protocol’s m rounds, communication, verifier/prover runtimes, completeness 1, and soundness at most \(md/|F|\), noting extension fields can enlarge \(F\). It previews IP=PSPACE, PCP, MIP, doubly efficient proofs, GKR, Fiat-Shamir, SNARGs, and low-degree extensions.

SUDEP is the non-traumatic, non-drowning death of a person with epilepsy, the leading killer of healthy young epilepsy patients, and the second-leading neurological cause of total years of potential life lost after stroke. Risk is highest in patients whose seizures are not medication-controlled, though benign epilepsy patients are also at risk. The strongest risk factor is poor control of generalized tonic-clonic seizures (GTCS). Nocturnal GTCS and prone position are major risk factors; ~70% of SUDEP occurs after nocturnal GTCS, and up to 87.6% of patients are found prone after nocturnal SUDEP, with prone vs non-prone relative risk over 60-fold. SUDEP can be prevented by repositioning, and timing is critical: terminal asystole and apnea occur as soon as 25 seconds postictally and in virtually everyone by 180 seconds. The study aimed to develop a nighttime seizure management system centered on an autonomous body repositioning mattress after GTCS. The Korus mattress uses an 8x4 array of inflatable cells expanding to 14 inches, sheet pressure sensors with 1,152 nodes and 256 pressure levels, networking with PoE boards, and a Random Forest Classifier for four body positions. Eighteen normative controls were enrolled; 10 underwent formal testing. Cells achieved 14-inch inflation in 7 seconds with 1000 lb/cell capacity; prone recovery succeeded 100% in 10 subjects, average 21.75 ± 5.85 seconds. Prone detection accuracy was 96.8%; overall position accuracy was 92.4%, with no supine/prone misidentification. Long-term sleep recording showed correct position 97.3% of the time and false body position change rate 2.3 events/hour, with no incorrect prone detections. The passage states Korus has first-in-class potential to monitor and autonomously intervene to prevent SUDEP, though further tasks remain, and expected SUDEP risk reduction may exceed 50% if goals are realized.

The PGA848 output-stage difference amplifier uses a 6.67kΩ feedback resistor and provides DA_IN– and DA_IN+ pins for external capacitors in parallel with internal resistors to implement noise filtering/shaping and customized attenuating gains. Internal resistor accuracy is 0.01% or better, yielding CMRR of 80dB or better; mismatched leakage currents can degrade CMRR. Internal resistors have ±15% absolute variation. The pins must not be treated as outputs or used to source or sink current. The device has a single functional mode and operates when input-stage supply is greater than ±4.5V (9V) and output-stage supply is greater than ±2.25V (4.5V).

The PGA848 is a monolithic, high-voltage, high-bandwidth, precision programmable gain instrumentation amplifier with single-ended output, combining a current-feedback input stage, internally matched gain resistor network, and four-resistor differential amplifier output stage. It has eight binary gains from 0.5V/V to 100V/V via A0, A1, and A2, and is designed for applications such as factory automation and control, analog input modules, data acquisition, test and measurement, and semiconductor test. Its linear operating input range extends within 3V (maximum) of either supply. A typical application drives the ADS8860 16-bit, 1MSPS SAR ADC with independent supplies, ±15V input stage and 5.3V output stage, REF6250 reference, and OPA192 buffer. Three filters are used; CFB = 75pF with the 6.67kΩ feedback resistors gives a nominal 318kHz cutoff, 277kHz on the high tolerance side, with –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz. Power supply recommendations specify nominal ±15V operation, and supply voltages higher than 40V (±20V) permanently damage the device. Layout guidelines address symmetry, bypass capacitors, leakage, parasitic capacitance, thermal junctions, and trace routing. The passage also covers PSpice for TI, TINA-TI, documentation support, support resources, trademarks, ESD caution, glossary, revision history, mechanical, packaging, orderable information, and legal notices.

In 2013, the European Space Agency deployed the Gaia space observatory, which has cataloged over a billion astronomical objects to help create a precise 3D map of the Milky Way. Using Gaia’s initial data and the RAdial Velocity Experiment, a University of Toronto team led by Jason Hunt calculated that the Sun orbits the Milky Way at 240 km/s and estimated the distance between the Sun and the galactic center at 7.6 to 8.2 kiloparsecs, or about 24,788 to 26,745 light years, narrowing earlier estimates of 7.2 to 8.8 kiloparsecs. The study was published in November 2016, and further Gaia data releases are expected to refine these calculations.

Lawyers for Venezuelan TPS holders asked the Supreme Court to leave in place a federal judge’s order temporarily barring the Trump administration from ending their protected status. The TPS program, created in 1990, allows DHS to designate citizens of countries unable to return because of natural disaster, armed conflict, or other extraordinary temporary conditions. Mayorkas designated Venezuela in 2021, redesignated it in 2023, and extended it through October 2026; Noem later ended the 2023 designation and 2025 extension. Challengers argued the termination was unlawful and racially motivated. Judge Chen temporarily blocked it March 31 and later ruled on Sept. 5 that Noem acted unlawfully. After the government sought Supreme Court intervention, the challengers argued the Court’s earlier stay did not foreclose further litigation to a final judgment.

The passage discusses inclusive education for children with disabilities as an international education agenda, citing Sustainable Development Goal 4, the 1994 Salamanca Declaration, and the 2006 CRPD. It defines inclusive education as quality education meeting every child’s educational needs, with some international documents emphasizing education in regular schools in children’s areas of residence. It reviews debates on regular versus special schools: regular schools may help acquire social and communication skills and future social participation, while special schools may provide specialized skills such as Braille, sign language, and mobility training, role models, and safer environments. It also notes one-track, dual-track, and multiple-track education systems, and that UN 2019 reported 44% of member states educated students with and without disabilities in the same classrooms without indicating whether educational needs were considered.

In Myanmar, the government ratified CRPD in 2011, enacted the Law on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2015, and held an inclusive education seminar in 2019. The study examines actual practice of inclusive education for children with disabilities in Myanmar, specifically visual impairment. It describes special schools under the Department of Social Welfare, limited statistics on education for children with disabilities, and low enrollment rates. The qualitative case study was conducted in Yangon in February 2019 using interviews, focus group discussions, observations, and document reviews with visually impaired students, parents, teachers, principals, and officials. It selected Special School A, Special School B, and connected regular Schools C and D. Students received primary education at special schools and, from lower secondary education, attended regular schools; they were registered at regular schools and took primary final exams there. Regular schools used peer support.

Findings describe a “limited inclusive education in phases,” close to a dual-track system. Informants valued special schools for Braille, life skills, supplementary study, computer skills, and mental security. They valued regular schools for social and communication skills and for helping students without disabilities understand disabilities and empathize. Limitations included insufficient communication between special and regular school teachers, regular teachers’ dependency on special school teachers, and isolation between students with and without disabilities. Only one of 12 visually impaired students reported a good friend without disability. Bullying, teasing, age differences, and limited interaction outside class were noted. Many parents, especially in rural areas, lacked information about special schools; some were refused by regular schools and gave up schooling.

The discussion states the system has pros and cons. It uses existing special and regular school resources, but faces challenges in teacher communication, dependency, and student isolation. It recommends training and policies for mutual exchange and programs promoting inclusion, diversity, and camaraderie. It argues wider needs beyond educational needs must be considered. The author does not deny one-track inclusive education if all needs are fulfilled, but notes many countries face difficulties and that each country, especially low-income countries, should understand and effectively use its resources to fit its context. The Ministry of Education and DSW need to cooperate carefully and creatively to develop their model.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system. The passage covers synchronization of multiple devices using SMPL_SYNC, internal/external voltage reference options, 2-lane and 4-lane SDR/DDR data interfaces, data output randomizer, simple and moving averaging, digital test patterns, reset and power-down, initialization sequence, speed-boost mode, SPI register access and daisy-chain configuration, register descriptions, application information for ATE, power supply and layout recommendations, and support/packaging information.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for neuromuscular stimulation that decode neural activity to identify a desired movement and deliver electrical stimulation to a target to produce it. Methods include measuring neural activity, removing artifacts, extracting features such as signal amplitude or wavelet scale, using decoders including discrete multiclass and movement effort decoders, and employing a body state observer, sensors, feedback history, and a user activation profile. Stimulation may be high-definition, dynamically updated, and multiplexed or interleaved for compound movements. Targets may include body or prosthetic limbs, wheelchairs, computer cursors, exoskeletons, remote control devices, or robotic arms. Training uses cues, graphical feedback, and machine learning. Examples describe hand and arm position sensing, cortical control of rhythmic and discrete thumb movements using a CPG oscillator and NMES, with reported accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity results.
Time off was good for focusing on the game. No specific plans yet; they may watch video later and are focused on tomorrow night against a great shot-blocking team.

This list of papers covers the continuation and spread of the war and efforts toward peace, including 1917 exchanges among the Allied governments, Central Powers, the United States, Mexico, and Greece. It also covers neutral rights affected by German and Allied submarine operations, armed merchant ships, submarine incidents, the severance of relations with Germany, the Zimmermann telegram, and the declaration of a state of war with Germany on April 6. Further sections address neutral seamen, captured American seamen, and Latin-American relations, including responses to U.S. actions, severances or declarations involving Panama, Cuba, Brazil, Bolivia, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Haiti, ship sinkings, and proposals for conferences of American states.

Microsoft Corporation entered into an Underwriting Agreement on August 1, 2016, for the issuance and sale of Notes due 2019, 2021, 2023, 2026, 2036, 2046, and 2056, with specified principal amounts and interest rates. The Notes will be issued under a base indenture and an Eleventh Supplemental Indenture, bear interest payable semi-annually, and be senior unsecured obligations. The filing also lists related exhibits, including the Underwriting Agreement, supplemental indenture, global notes, and legal opinions.

This study uses WHO-compliant verbal autopsy surveys linked to the Consumer Pyramids Household Survey to estimate SARS-CoV-2-attributable and all-cause mortality in India from 2018–2021. It notes that India reported about 44 million confirmed cases and 530,000 SARS-CoV-2 deaths, while contested excess death estimates through mid-2021 ranged from 4 to 6 million; official reports and CRS/SRS data have cause-attribution limitations. The VA sample contained 20,453 deaths after excluding pre-2018 deaths, reflecting a 72.8% response rate. Analyses adjusted for VA non-response, delayed CPHS death reporting, and sampling. SARS-CoV-2 deaths spiked during the lockdown and after the first and second waves. During the pandemic, SARS-CoV-2 accounted for 17.93% of all deaths and 33.15% of excess deaths; the all-cause annual death rate was 81.19% higher in 2020–2021 than in 2018–2019. Cardiovascular disease accounted for 23.15% of excess deaths, while respiratory deaths fell. SARS-CoV-2 death rates rose with age, were highest above age 80 but produced most deaths at ages 61–80, were higher among urban residents although total deaths were greater in rural areas, and were not significantly associated with income. Limitations include possible U07/U08 misclassification, imperfect statistical corrections, and an unvalidated SARS-CoV-2 VA modification. The study also explores ex post verbal autopsies as a method for measuring pandemic burden in lower-income countries.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture GPUs include second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, GDDR6X memory, RTX IO, and display/video features. The passage reports Wolfenstein: Youngblood frame time improving from 51 ms with shaders alone to 20 ms with RT Cores and 12 ms with Tensor Cores/DLSS, while the RTX 3080 renders at 6.7 ms (150 FPS). Second-generation RT Cores accelerate ray-traced motion blur, including via an Interpolate Triangle Position unit; third-generation Tensor Cores add sparsity and TF32/BF16 support for AI and DLSS. GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling for up to 936 GB/sec. RTX IO works with DirectStorage for GPU-based decompression. The passage also covers A40 and RTX A6000 GPUs, NVDEC/NVENC video codecs including AV1 decode, RTX 3090/3070 specifications, and EDR memory error detection.

The 3-4 defense uses 3 down linemen, 4 linebackers, and 4 defensive backs, with outside linebackers creating matchups and a mirror base alignment. It employs bigger two-gap defensive linemen, hybrid outside linebackers, four linebackers often called Sam, Mike, Will, and Jack, and a secondary with two corners and two safeties. Its main strength is bringing pressure from many places, including blitzing both outside linebackers for a five-man rush; two safeties allow multiple coverages and pre- to post-snap disguise. Weaknesses include spread offenses forcing outside linebackers into coverage and creating a five-man box, making it vulnerable to the run; trips formations can cause confusion. Offenses attack by spreading it out and running against a light box, leading to the 3-3 stack. Common blitzes include Weakside Edge and Crossfire; common coverages include Cover 4 and Cover 2 Man. The defense has been used by Bill Parcells and Bill Belichick, whose coaching tree includes Nick Saban and Kirby Smart. Since 2005, 9 college national championships and 7 Super Bowls have been won from this coaching tree.

The lecture begins with quiz results, grading, and review before moving to full factorial design of experiments, contrasts, regression, and ANOVA for assessing main and interaction effects. It discusses model adequacy, higher-order terms, and lack of fit using center points and replicates, illustrated with a break forming example. It then introduces blocks, confounding, nuisance factors, and previews fractional factorial designs.

The Neofoot study was a prospective diagnostic accuracy study conducted in three primary care clinics in Madang Province, Papua New Guinea, as a sub-study of the WANTAIM trial. It aimed to determine the accuracy of newborn foot length measurement for identifying low birth weight (LBW) or preterm birth (PTB) babies in health facilities and community settings, and to compare measurements taken by trained volunteers with those of a researcher. The study enrolled 342 babies; the researcher measured foot length for all 342, and a volunteer measured for 123. LBW was defined as birth weight <2.50 kg, and PTB as birth before 37 completed weeks. Foot length was measured within 72 hours of birth using a plastic ruler. Overall, 21.1% of babies were LBW and 7.3% were PTB. Mean foot length was 7.8 cm. The optimal foot length cut-off for classifying both LBW and PTB was <7.7 cm. For LBW, sensitivity was 84.7%, specificity 69.6%, positive predictive value 42.7%, and negative predictive value 94.5%. For PTB, sensitivity was 88.0%, specificity 61.8%, positive predictive value 15.4%, and negative predictive value 98.5%. The area under the curve was 87.0% for LBW and 85.8% for PTB. Between researcher and volunteer measurements, the mean difference was 0.07 cm, with 95% limits of agreement from -0.55 cm to +0.70 cm; 9/123 pairs were outside these limits. No adverse events were recorded. The study concluded that newborn foot length was a simple and feasible method for identifying LBW and PTB babies and could help improve neonatal health outcomes, while noting limitations including measurement within 72 hours of birth, lack of blinding, and conduct in one coastal province.

Iran’s parliament gave initial approval to a bill to boost spending on its missile program and Revolutionary Guards in retaliation for new U.S. sanctions. The bill would allocate over $260 million each to the ballistic missile program and Quds Force, and requires a strategy against U.S. actions. It needs a second vote and clerical approval.

It covers PMU, clock oscillators/clocks, DMA, event manager, memory organization, flash, SRAM, GPIO, IOMUX, ADC, temperature sensor, VREF, COMP, DAC, security, TRNG, AESADV, Keystore, CRC-P, MATHACL, UART, I2C, SPI, CAN-FD, LFSS, RTC_B, IWDT_B, WWDT, and TIMx. It also includes device analog connections, I/O diagrams, SWD, BSL, factory constants, typical application/layout guidance, device nomenclature, documentation/support, revision history, and mechanical/packaging/orderable information.

New clock gating shuts entire clock trees quickly to save dynamic power; Blackwell gates the entire memory clock tree. Separate voltage rails independently control GPU cores and memory, reducing idle leakage.

A Berliner Testament allows spouses to mutually appoint each other as sole heirs and generally their children as final heirs, providing the survivor financial security since children inherit only after both parents die. However, it is strongly binding and cannot be unilaterally altered unless provisions allow it. It may not account for later changes such as separation or falling out with children. Clauses can ease this binding effect, and inheritance tax allowances should be considered. Experienced succession lawyers can advise.

Delta executives expect premium revenue from first class and other higher-priced cabins to overtake coach cabin sales next year, at least for a quarter or two. Last quarter, Delta’s premium cabin ticket revenue rose 9% to nearly $5.8 billion, while main-cabin ticket revenue fell 4% to just over $6 billion. Delta and other airlines have become more reliant on upmarket seats.

This study compared spatiotemporal forecasting models for fatal opioid-related overdoses at census-tract annual resolution in Cook County, Illinois, and Massachusetts. It used Cook County Medical Examiner records and Massachusetts death certificate data, mapped to census tracts, with covariates including prior overdose counts, location, time, and Social Vulnerability Index features. Models included simple baselines, statistical approaches, and neural networks, evaluated with RMSE, MAE, and a new intervention-focused Best Possible Reach (%BPR) metric. Results showed model rankings varied by metric. In Massachusetts, BST had higher %BPR than GP despite both being noted for top MAE/RMSE performance; in Cook County, Gradient Boosted Trees with SVI had better MAE/RMSE but worse %BPR than a GLM model. Simple historical average baselines performed competitively. The study recommends including tuned historical averages and intervention-aware %BPR, reports that %BPR changed rankings and could identify 15 more annual fatal overdoses in Illinois and 18 in Massachusetts, provides open-source software and Cook County data, and notes limitations including only two locations, K=100, BPR not directly prioritizing rate of change, and limited covariates. It concludes that %BPR and simple baselines should be considered in future overdose forecasting and intervention planning.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is a momentum indicator scaled from 0 to 100, introduced by J. Welles Wilder in 1978, used to assess overbought or oversold conditions. A CFD is a contract based on the difference between an underlying asset’s current value and its value when the contract is established, allowing speculation without ownership. In CFD trading, RSI can help identify potential reversals and support mean-reversion strategies. RSI thresholds vary by asset class, timeframe, and market trend; for day trading, shorter time frames and more extreme levels such as 15 for oversold and 85 for overbought may be used. The passage discusses RSI momentum strategies and combining RSI with other indicators. It emphasizes backtesting, time frame choice, threshold adjustment, cautious use of combined time frames, RSI divergences, and risk management, including commissions, slippage, taxes, and stop-loss orders. It concludes that RSI is flexible but should be combined with other indicators and backtested before implementation.

People have long tried to hack the body and mind, but now science understands why old techniques like caffeine and nicotine work. Recent efforts include Tim Tully’s attempt to develop a “memorization pill,” funded by Ken Dart, involving people with enhanced memory and genome sequencing; genetically engineering fruit flies with photographic memories via CREB activators; a controversial project to find intelligence-related genes for genetic enhancement; and deep brain stimulation devices that monitor brain activation and respond by zapping abnormal states such as panic, depression, or psychosis. Dystopian scenarios are conceivable.

Under republican institutions and peace, the country saw growth in agriculture, commerce, manufacturing, arts, revenue, debt reduction, and public works. The Supreme Court granted review for its 2025-26 term in Hunter’s case, involving a Texas man who pleaded guilty to aiding and abetting wire fraud and waived his right to appeal. Hunter challenges a mandatory medication condition imposed at sentencing; the 5th Circuit dismissed his appeal based on the waiver. Arguments are likely early next year, with a decision by summer.

The court affirmed a judgment for real estate brokers in their action against principals for a commission. It held that a principal could not defeat the broker’s right to commission by refusing to be bound by or sign a contract with a purchaser produced by the broker. It found no prejudicial variance where plaintiffs alleged a contract between defendants and the purchaser but one defendant had signed a codefendant’s name without authority. It also held that defects not affecting substantial rights should be disregarded, that requested instructions on immaterial issues were properly refused, and that overruling a motion to strike was harmless because the allegations presented no material issue.

Yankees rookie Cam Schlittler pitched eight scoreless innings, struck out 12, allowed five hits and no walks against Boston in Game 3 of the AL Wild Card series; scout Matt Hyde praised the historic performance.

Montecito Union School District in Santa Barbara County settled a sexual abuse lawsuit for $7.5 million with two brothers, now 65 and 68, who claimed former superintendent and principal Stanford Kerr molested them in the 1970s. The brothers sought $35 million combined. A third plaintiff settled earlier for $1 million. The district admitted no liability. The settlement equals about 40% of the 350-student district’s 2025-26 budget; the superintendent said it would affect the budget and be managed through a hiring freeze, staff reductions through natural attrition, and redirecting capital repair funds, while avoiding layoffs. The district had no insurance for the alleged abuse period. The settlement followed a legislative stalemate over restoring a statute of limitations; AB 218 had removed such limits for child sexual abuse claims against public agencies. The California School Boards Association gave the district a $50,000 legal-cost grant. A final hearing is scheduled for Nov. 19.

This study compares a Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) approach with an explainable machine learning (ML) approach using a CNN and SHAP for detecting outliers in plantar pressure data. Data were collected across centers from left and right feet under static and dynamic conditions, preprocessed into 64×64 normalized images, expert-annotated into valid and four outlier categories, and augmented with synthetic outliers to 2,798 samples. SPM used affine registration and nonparametric cluster-based permutation testing; ML used a CNN with foot-side embedding, SHAP explanations, and nested stratified cross-validation. The ML approach outperformed SPM on held-out tests (MCC 0.96±0.01 vs. 0.78±0.02; F1 0.99±0.00 vs. 0.93±0.01). In an exploratory human-centered semantic differential survey with 16 experts, both approaches were generally rated positively as clear, correct, useful, relevant, understandable, trustworthy, and relatively complete; no statistically significant differences were found, though SPM was descriptively simpler and ML with SHAP was most often preferred. The study concludes both approaches are promising for detecting technical errors and procedural inconsistencies in plantar pressure data, with ML showing higher accuracy and both explanations perceived favorably.

The passage questions traditional percentage-based definitions of bear, bull, correction, dip and crash markets, saying they lack a rational basis or hard data and are not useful for managing risk or deploying capital. It cites the 2015 correction, when the S&P 500 fell 15.2 per cent and the Russell 2000 lost 27.2 per cent, and the 2011 decline, when the S&P 500 fell 21.58 per cent and the Russell 2000 fell 30.7 per cent, to argue such labels do not meaningfully help investors. The author proposes defining secular bull and bear markets using market gains or losses, long-term economic trends and investor psychology, especially valuations. A secular bull market is described as a 10-to-20-year period of broad economic shifts, rising revenues and earnings, lower volatility, and increasing willingness to pay more for earnings. A secular bear market reflects the opposite, with higher volatility, cyclical rallies and retreats, and declining willingness to pay for earnings. The passage says earnings multiple expansion or contraction often drives returns more than profits, citing the 1982-2000 bull market, and says bear markets begin when this psychology shifts.

A White House official told STAT the administration would begin preparing tariffs on companies that do not build in the U.S. or reach a drug pricing agreement, with no new timeline. Drug executives are receiving near-daily calls from White House and HHS and Commerce officials as the administration seeks deals ahead of the 2026 midterms; it asked Eli Lilly, Pfizer, and AstraZeneca for specific actions. Defending the High Post Split Offense involves a high post split followed by down screens. Defenders must guard the high post with and without the ball, defend initial guard splits, counter down screens, and defend the low post. On a pass to the high post, defenders sag in front of the high post; guards sag one stride in front, wings help, and X5 drops between the high post and basket to prevent handoffs and drives, then jams the high post toward the weak-hand corner pushpoint. Against down screens, NBA teams usually show and recover rather than switch to avoid a big posting a smaller defender; X3 and X4 show to force shooters wide, X1 and X2 chase out, and X4/X5 recover to three-quarter pass denial while X2/X3 deny shooters. Matching up after a pass to the wing uses basic principles: pressure the ball, defend the post by fronting, trapping, or playing straight up, and pack weakside. The SOS disruption defense pressures the ballhandler early to a sideline checkpoint, switches on splits and down screens, and traps passes to the wing or low post. It includes high post feed disruption, split defense with switching and smothering, contact switches on down screens, a double-team wing trap, pass-out rotations, and a post trap; basic SOS rules apply if screening begins.

Deutsche Bank is looking to sell its 8.8% stake in Dubai-based Abraaj, an embattled private equity firm in a dispute with investors over alleged misuse of money in a $1 billion healthcare fund. The potential sale has become more urgent amid Deutsche Bank’s restructuring and job cuts. Abraaj denies wrongdoing and is considering selling some or all of its investment business unit. It faces an investigation by four investors, including the Gates Foundation and the World Bank’s IFC, and has cut jobs, suspended new investments, and seen CFO and COO resignations.

The passage discusses the metaverse in education, noting that science fiction anticipated technologies and that the metaverse appeared in Second Life, Roblox, Pokemon Go, and Fortnite and now attracts investment from companies such as Facebook and Microsoft. It defines the metaverse as a bi-located virtual universe using avatars and classifies types as augmented reality, lifelogging, mirror world, and virtual reality. Educational advantages include collaboration, firsthand scenarios, object inspection, simulations, personalized learning, and risk-free practice in fields such as engineering and medicine. Limitations include difficulty monitoring students, greater mental effort in augmented reality, no significant learning difference from virtual reality, and needs for reliable platforms, connectivity, devices, and teacher training. The metaverse is not a straightforward replacement for conventional learning.

The study aims to determine teachers’ knowledge, views on advantages and disadvantages, suitable educational domains, timing, and obstacles to integrating the metaverse. It surveyed 333 teachers in Türkiye. Teachers’ metaverse knowledge averaged 5.25/9; 78.1% had experienced a metaverse environment, though experiences were limited and often involved virtual reality or three-dimensional virtual worlds. Teachers’ attitude toward educational metaverse use was 6.23, advantageous use 6.19, concerns 5.38, willingness to use it 6.37, suitability of lessons 6.05, and willingness to participate in training 8.08. Advantages included attracting interest, applying knowledge, learning by doing, experiencing new technologies, and eliminating educational boundaries. Concerns included technical problems, psychological problems such as addiction, inequality of opportunity, data security, and teacher readiness. Information technology, physics, biology, chemistry, and mathematics were seen as most suitable. Teachers considered the education system, colleagues, parents, and schools largely unprepared, while students were relatively more ready. Many projected widespread effective use within 3–5 years. The discussion and conclusion state that the metaverse has transformative potential but requires infrastructure, training, health consideration, and research and investment, and that it will not simply replace conventional learning.

The passage describes attacking a Box & One defense with a “Flash/Back Door” offense. Flashing a baseline post player into the middle creates matchup problems. If no shot is available, High/Low post action and wing backdoor action are used. It covers post flash/back cuts, high/low feeds, continuity into Single/Double Screens, and variations using base screens or a point backdoor. Implementation requires execution, coordination, screens, post ups, communication, timing, and experience. Strategies include scouting, recognizing defensive reads and counters, making adjustments after substitutions or timeouts, using various alignments and entries, and attacking weaker defenders. The Box & One defense uses four players in a box zone and one chaser denying the ball.

The Supreme Court will hear on August 17 the bail plea of 2008 Malegaon blast accused Prasad Purohit and a plea challenging co-accused Pragya Singh Thakur’s bail. The Bombay High Court granted Thakur bail but rejected Purohit’s; the NIA cleared Thakur but cited serious charges against Purohit.

LUKB Disease Trajectory (LUKB DT) is a web tool built on R Shiny and integrated into the LUKB UK Biobank data preparation platform. It identifies disease trajectories from electronic medical records requiring participant IDs, diagnoses, and diagnosis dates. The workflow includes disease filtering with Cox regression, disease pair detection with binomial tests, directionality testing, and validation with conditional logistic regression; validated pairs are concatenated into trajectories. In a UK Biobank ICD-10 case study, COVID-19 was associated with 90 diseases; 8,010 disease pairs were formed, and 527 were confirmed. The trajectories mainly involved SARS-CoV-2 infection-related diseases and other medical care. The full calculation took 55 minutes using 8 cores. Limitations include reliance on processed medical records and trajectories that may not reflect real patient trajectories; the authors recommend comprehensive data and using the trajectories primarily for investigating risk factors or mechanisms rather than patient clustering. LUKB DT is presented as an efficient resource for disease trajectory analysis.

Children with language vulnerabilities, such as developmental language disorder, autism, or migration-related challenges, require tailored support. Speech-language therapists collaborate with caregivers and educators, but generating consistent, diverse morphological examples in real time is demanding. Language interventions span implicit and explicit approaches, and game-based learning like Alias is used in therapy. Robot-Assisted Language Learning has been explored, but earlier static, teleoperated, or rule-based systems lack adaptability and speech recognition. The authors developed TalBot, combining ChatGPT with a Furhat conversational robot, tested with 13 preschool children with language vulnerabilities and 7 educators. TalBot leads Alias, manages turn-taking, provides feedback and clues, and uses facial expressions; it can handle mispronunciations and voice recognition errors. The authors plan to expand TalBot to morphological learning by generating linguistic material, providing a linguistic model, and acting as a role model for educators, with future lab, field, and feasibility studies. They note ethical, data protection, regulatory, practical, and cost considerations, and aim for a robust LLM-based RALL application for teaching morphological structures across languages.

David Ellison, whose Paramount Skydance owns CBS News, expressed respect for CBS News while saying it needs to build trust. He dismissed the notion of a plot to make CBS News a Trumpworld media arm. After acquiring The Free Press, he installed Bari Weiss as CBS News editor in chief, raising questions about its direction. A Grand Erie official said the goal is one district association with equitable rules and game counts, but nothing is finalized, and travel and timelines remain part of the discussion.

Young people are considering college options and filling out forms declaring future plans, though at 17 they are not expected to know and plans can change. Change is constant, and technological advancements will bring major changes over coming decades, with examples including petrol and diesel engines, electric cars, electrical engineering, and fax machines. Workers sell their work as a commodity and should make it as valuable as possible, as illustrated by a surgeon versus a burger seller. The passage advises assuming companies seek maximum output for minimum reward and cautions that no job is amazing and fun every day; life outside work matters.

Type 2A compensation was used with a 10-kHz target crossover; power-stage transconductance was 16.2 A/V. Output capacitance was 7 × 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors to meet 2.3 mF; each ESR was about 6 mΩ and equivalent ESR was 0.86 mΩ. RCOMP, CCOMP, and CHF were 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF, with compensation often tuned during testing. Slope compensation via RSC is set to the output inductor’s falling slope and depends on transformer turns ratio, current-sense turns ratio, output inductor, and current-sense resistor; 102 kΩ connects RSC to AVSS. The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require proper bypassing, with at least 0.1 µF from VIN to AVSS and close ceramic capacitors. Layout guidelines cover routing feedback away from magnetics/noisy traces, minimizing switch-node copper and high di/dt/dv/dt loops, separating AVSS from power ground at one point, short/wide high-current traces, placing bypass and compensation components close, filtering CS_ILIM, routing SYNC away from sensitive pins, and using multiple vias for CFP backside metallization to AVSS. Revision F released TPS7H5002/3/4 QMLP options and added SN0022HFT; Revision E released TPS7H5001-SP QMLP and related updates.

The Scottish government and Cosla agreed to abolish local authority burial and cremation fees for children under 18 in Scotland. The government will provide £500,000 to cover the cost. Most councils currently do not charge for under-16s. The change aligns Scotland with England and was welcomed by the Church of Scotland and officials.

NVIDIA Corporation reported that on March 30, 2019, Stephen C. Neal was appointed to its Board of Directors. He received 1,419 restricted stock units vesting approximately semi-annually over three years commencing March 30, 2019, 139 pro-rated annual restricted stock units vesting in full on May 15, 2019, and a $10,890 pro-rated annual cash retainer payable March 30, 2019. NVIDIA entered into an indemnity agreement with him.

Cover 2 is a zone coverage in a 4-3 with five underneath players and two deep safeties. The safeties divide the field in half and cover over the top. It covers short routes while protecting against deep throws with two safeties. It allows defenders to read routes and the quarterback, unlike man coverage. Strengths include balanced coverage, short routes, screens, hard corners, and run support. Weaknesses include multiple deep routes, 4 verticals, trips formations, and run vulnerabilities due to only one linebacker in the box against 2x2, or no weak-side overhang against trips. Rules assign corners to flats, safeties to deep halves, and linebackers to hook/curl or middle hole. Variations include Cover 2 “Switch” and Cover 2 from a 1 High shell.

After negative feedback, especially from Hindus, Emirates Airlines confirmed it will continue its Hindu meal option, having earlier announced its discontinuation. It said Hindu passengers could also choose vegetarian and non-vegetarian regionally-inspired meals.

This paper conducts a co-occurrence analysis of articles published in ISEDJ from 2003–2024 to identify topics over time and look toward the future of IS education. Using author-supplied keywords from 1,076 articles, it groups years into eras and creates term maps with VOSviewer based on frequency and link strength. The eras are characterized as 2003–2007 IS education; 2008–2012 pedagogy and student issues; 2013–2017 cybersecurity, big data, and analytics; 2018–2022 COVID impact on IS education; and 2023–2024 artificial intelligence. The full 2003–2024 network shows pedagogy and curriculum as continuous central areas. Limitations include reliance on author-supplied keywords and possible inflation from special issues; future research may include titles and abstracts and allow data to establish eras organically, especially with continued AI growth.

US non-farm payrolls rose 200,000 in January, exceeding expectations, while average hourly earnings rose 0.3 per cent month-over-month and 2.9 per cent year-on-year, the fastest since 2009. Unemployment held at 4.1 per cent. The data strengthened the case for a March rate rise, and Treasury yields rose.

The speaker says no significant changes were made, citing playoff experience and locker-room confidence, and expects learning from the last game. Ryan Carter cites poor execution, nerves, careless puck play and turnovers that gave momentum, plus costly mistakes. He stresses staying positive, watching video, playing their game and improving forecheck, and notes big hits can create momentum.

FERC issued an order approving an extension of NYISO's Automated Mitigation Procedures (AMP or Circuit Breaker) through April 30, 2002, rather than until October 31, 2002 as NYISO sought; Enron had opposed the request. FERC directs NYISO to file a comprehensive mitigation proposal by March 1, 2002, effective May 1, 2002, addressing concerns with the AMP and how NYISO's mitigation measures work together. FERC acknowledges two AMP problems NYISO committed to fix: limiting mitigation to specific zones and hours that fail the impact test, and exempting bids under 50 MW unless there is a demonstrated market power concern. FERC also directs NYISO to work with market participants to examine whether the AMP is a barrier to entry for new generation and whether new generation should be exempted; examine exemption or accommodation for other energy-limited resources, including those constrained by environmental rules; explain how the AMP works with other mitigation measures, including in-city mitigation; and consider must-run mitigation consistent with ISO-NE and PJM. FERC expects one mitigation plan for the Northeast as part of the RTO process and urges NYISO to collaborate with PJM and ISO-NE. The order also includes procedural background, comments and protests, and discussion of the AMP's operation and requested extension.

He confirmed captain Wes Morgan would miss the Madrid match with a back injury.

In practice over 25 years, Rittenberg emphasizes continuing education and advanced dentistry, and received AACD recognition; Dr. Brittany Jones joins the team.

He says a replacement has a golden opportunity to sponsor his No. 48 Hendrick Motorsports team until his career ends. The 5-day low overnight trading strategy trades the S&P 500 when it opens at a 5-day low but closes higher than its open, entering at the close and exiting at the next day’s open. Overnight S&P 500 trading averages a 0.04% return from close to open. From 2005 forward, the strategy produced an average profit of 15.93% and 0.26% per trade.

This application is a continuation of U.S. application Ser. No. 17/185,393, which is a continuation of PCT/CN2020/111638, claiming priority to Chinese Patent Application No. 201910854877.X. It relates to computer and communication technologies and provides an image processing method and apparatus, an electronic device, and a computer-readable storage medium. The method obtains a to-be-processed video including m frames, places a target three-dimensional model on a target plane of a first frame with feature points of a model surface on the target plane, determines three-dimensional coordinates in a world coordinate system and pixel coordinates on the first frame, determines a camera pose of the first frame relative to the world coordinate system, determines camera poses of the second through m-th frames relative to the world coordinate system based on the target plane, the three-dimensional coordinates, and the first-frame pixel coordinates, and replaces the target three-dimensional model with a target model placed in the world coordinate system to generate a target video including the target model according to each frame’s camera pose. The passage also describes using a neural network to obtain planes and a selection instruction to determine the target plane, using a cube as the target three-dimensional model, tracking the target plane with a homography matrix, calculating poses with a camera intrinsic parameter and a PnP algorithm, projecting and synthesizing the target model onto frames, and corresponding apparatus modules, storage medium, and electronic device. It further discusses CV, ML, and blockchain technologies and states advantages including reduced calculation, fast speed, convenient operation, high accuracy, applicability to more videos, and improved efficiency and effect of placing the target model in video.

New York’s Excelsior Scholarship offers free tuition at SUNY or CUNY colleges to eligible state high school graduates from families with incomes below certain limits, covering only annual tuition, not fees, room and board, or books. Private colleges are responding to affordability concerns and competition from the program with initiatives, scholarships, and guarantees aimed at New York students. Some private colleges report varying impacts and concerns about enrollment and finances, while some administrators prefer increasing the state Tuition Assistance Program. The program has added a new dynamic to public versus private college choices.

Text messaging has become a popular form of communication, and alternative messaging apps are emerging. Music Messenger lets users send songs; WhatsApp offers free text messaging on any smartphone with video, photos, sound clips, and emoticons; Facebook Messenger provides media sharing, HD video chats, sound bites, group chat, no advertising, and customizable graphics.
