The Federal Reserve proposed easing the Volcker Rule, which bars banks’ risky trading bets for their own profit with depositors’ money. The changes would match the strictest applications of the rule to banks that do the most trading, which Fed officials say would resolve some uncertainty for banks. This comes amid other efforts to loosen financial regulations. The Volcker Rule is a key plank of Dodd-Frank; Congress recently rolled back that law, and Consumer Financial Protection Bureau acting director Mick Mulvaney has curbed the agency’s powers.

Lotte Chemical Corp plans to list Lotte Chemical Titan Holding on Bursa Malaysia in Q3 2017, offering up to 740.48 million shares plus over-allotment. Sources say it could raise $1–$1.5 billion. Proceeds would fund petrochemical projects; the IPO was previously shelved amid South Korean fraud investigations.

The offside trap is a soccer defensive maneuver in which all defensive backs move upfield in unison just before an attacking pass, placing a leading striker offside. If the striker receives the ball and gains an advantage, the violation is expected to be called under Law 11, resulting in an indirect free kick for the defending team. Introduced in the 1900s and adopted by many teams mid-century, the trap has become riskier due to offside law changes and more short, quick inter-passing attacks. Its success depends on coordinated movement; one defender failing to step up can leave attackers onside, and an attacker may avoid interfering with play. Coaches must consider player maturity, risk versus benefit, goalkeeper mentality, opponent tactics, and formation, with a flat-back-four more conducive than a stopper-sweeper alignment. One designated defender usually calls the trap with a unique verbal or non-verbal signal. Execution requires a quick three- to five-yard sprint in unison when attackers make forward runs and the passer looks down. Teams should practice repeatedly, avoid overuse, and may use the trap in normal play or free kicks.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture introduces blockchain basics and cryptography through Bitcoin. It identifies key design features including cryptographic hash functions, timestamped append-only logs, block headers and Merkle trees, asymmetric cryptography and digital signatures, Bitcoin addresses, nodes, miners/consensus, nonces, peer-to-peer networking, native currency, and transaction inputs/outputs. Hash functions map any-size input to a fixed size, are deterministic and efficient, and aim for preimage resistance, collision resistance, avalanche effect, and puzzle friendliness. Digital signatures use public/private key pairs; a signature is created from a message and private key and verified with a public key. Bitcoin addresses are derived by hashing public keys twice and using base58. Block headers contain version, previous block hash, Merkle root, timestamp, difficulty target, and nonce. Bitcoin uses a timestamped append-only log, proof of work/mining, a finite native currency, and a transaction ledger. The lecture also discusses the double-spend problem and notes that consensus and transactions will be covered next.

In December 2006, SunPower CEO Tom Werner considered questions about solar industry growth, the duration of SunPower’s advantage, competition with larger companies such as Sharp and Q-Cells and niche technology firms, and turning current advantage into an enduring edge. The passage links renewed interest in solar power to energy independence and environmental benefits, citing fossil-fuel emissions, rising CO2 levels, IPCC data, the Kyoto Protocol, and carbon trading. PV systems convert solar energy to electric current; efficiency is measured by conversion efficiency. First commercial cells from Bell Labs had efficiencies below 4%, while 2006 PV efficiencies ranged from 10%–20%. Cells form modules, arrays, and inverter-connected systems. Solar power was two to three times the retail cost of electricity, but the market grew 41% annually from 2003 to 2006 and was expected to grow 40% annually through 2011. Japan led PV shipments; Europe was second; China surpassed the United States in 2006 as third-largest producer. The value chain included silicon, ingots/wafers, cells, modules, and installation. Silicon shortages raised prices. Solar electricity averaged 25–50¢/kWh versus 4–6¢/kWh for conventional sources. More than 1,000 pro-solar policies existed, including California’s Million Solar Roofs and renewable portfolio standards; government support was estimated at $1.7 billion in 2005 and over $3 billion in 2006. SunPower was founded in 1987 by Richard Swanson, initially pursued concentrator technology, later made cells for Honda and NASA, partnered with Cypress in 2001, began commercial production in 2004, and went public in 2005. It integrated into modules, wafers, silicon supply, and acquired PowerLight. SunPower produced the highest-efficiency commercial solar cells in 2006 using back-contact design; its process cost more and required more steps. Its competitors included Sharp, Q-Cells, REC, First Solar, SunTech, and Citizenre. The passage concludes that Werner faced a challenging road and key strategy choices.

The Sunday North Korean missile launch near Sinpo failed almost immediately. The Pentagon did not identify the missile; the White House called it medium-range. Weapons expert John Schilling said the failure suggested a new or not well-developed system, possibly one shown at a Pyongyang parade. Anonymous US officials told Fox News it was a new Scud, KN-17, a single-stage liquid-fueled missile that could target ships. Susan Thornton said it appeared to be a medium-range ballistic missile using prohibited technology. Schilling said hacking claims were overblown. Pentagon chief Jim Mattis ordered a review of America's nuclear deterrent.

This lecture provides an overview of equity and equity valuation. Equity is ownership in a corporation and a claim on cash flows through dividends and capital gains. Common stock is a residual claimant after bondholders and features limited liability, voting rights, and access to public markets; short sales help inform market prices. Equities trade in primary and secondary markets, and technology has increased secondary-market trading volume. The lecture presents the dividend discount model, valuing a stock as expected future dividends discounted at risk-adjusted rates that vary over time and with risk. Simplified cases include constant dividends (D/r) and growing dividends (D/(r−g)), implying stock prices rise with expected dividends or growth and fall with higher discount rates. Rearranging gives the discount rate as dividend yield plus growth. The general model is difficult because future dividends and discount rates are uncertain, and steady-state formulas may not fit companies with no dividends or earnings. Dividend policy changes are infrequent because cuts are viewed negatively, though special or suspended dividends occur.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC-based DAQ device with integrated AFE, PGA, ADC driver, and precision reference. Analog inputs have resistive impedance ≥1MΩ; external source impedance on AIN_P should be matched on AIN_M to cancel offset error. Internal OVP protects inputs up to ±20V when AVDD = 5V and up to ±15V when AVDD is floating, using input resistors and antiparallel diodes. The PGA converts single-ended or differential signals and adjusts common mode; a second-order antialiasing LPF typically has a –3dB cutoff of 500kHz. Reference options include internal 4.096V or external 4.096V, selected by INTREF_DIS. Output is straight-binary for bipolar and unipolar ranges. Alarm features include programmable input alarms and fixed AVDD alarms at 4.7V and 5.3V. The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI, dual SDO-x, daisy-chain, and source-synchronous protocols. Device states are RESET, ACQ, and CONV. Nine configuration registers control operation. Application information describes an industrial analog input module using the ADS8681W with a MUX36D08, plus power-supply decoupling, NAP/PD modes, and PCB layout recommendations.

This systematic review will examine prospective and retrospective observational cohort studies of Rapid Response Team (RRT) implementation or redesign. It aims to describe implementation methods, reasons for change, time frames, and outcome measures used to assess success. Data will be extracted on study and team characteristics, implementation methods, and system outcomes. Searches will cover Medline, CINAHL, Embase, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, reference lists, conference abstracts, and expert contact. Analysis will be primarily narrative with simple statistics on implementation methods. The review requires no ethical approval and will be disseminated through scientific meetings and a peer-reviewed journal. Limitations include heterogeneity of eligible studies and a possible lack of studies on implementation/change management.

Asia-Pacific equities gained in April on increased risk appetite tied to French election results, easing North Korea concerns, and strong Asian Q1 earnings; Indian stocks led, China lagged. Samsung, CITIC Securities, and TSMC reported higher profits.

Enron replaced Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon, and Fastow took a leave of absence. The change followed an informal SEC inquiry into partnerships Fastow ran, concerns over conflict-of-interest and related-party transactions, a $35 million loss, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. Enron’s stock fell $3.38 to $16.41, analysts issued downgrades or sell recommendations, and shareholder lawsuits were filed. CEO Kenneth Lay said replacing Fastow was necessary to restore investor confidence.

Air cargo containerization is an intermodal process used by civil airlines and military forces to transport goods quickly by air. Market growth is driven by rising demand for rapid global transportation and lightweight containers capable of carrying varied IATA-set loads and rough handling. It is hindered by the global economic slowdown and increased aviation fuel costs, which restrict cargo aircraft flying hours. Opportunities include growing commercial airlines and defense transport demand. The market is segmented by container type, end user, aircraft type, and geography, with listed major vendors.

The passage examines education in China, stating that the former one-child policy often made children the family focus and spoiled them, while parents emphasized study and grades over character and moral development. It argues education should liberate individual interests and desires instead of prioritizing knowledge and discipline. It reports many children cannot do laundry, cook, or housework, and some have emotional, behavioral, interpersonal, and adaptive problems; examination-oriented education is called a tragedy. Proposed improvements include learning to give with love, equal higher education resources, guiding students to unique interests, getting closer to nature, and valuing moral behavior education over scientific knowledge. It cites Yao Jiaxin’s case and discussions of Chinese parenting, praises traditional Chinese moral education’s unity of moral education and self-cultivation, knowing and practicing, and man-nature unity, and says it has referential value. Further recommendations include manual labor or sports for health, parent-child activities to build trust and reduce the generation gap, religious education for values and right standards, and more attention to women’s status in family education. It concludes that family education is a heated topic and stresses morality, humanity, parental guidance, and learning from ancestors’ moral education.

A comprehensive geoarchaeological study of Egypt’s Karnak Temple analyzed 61 sediment cores and tens of thousands of ceramic fragments to trace the site’s landscape over 3,000 years. It found that before about 2520 BCE the area was regularly flooded and unsuitable for permanent occupation, with earliest occupation likely during the Old Kingdom, corroborated by ceramics. Nile channels formed an island of high ground that supported early construction, and later channel changes shaped the temple’s development. Researchers suggest the site’s placement may have mirrored an ancient Egyptian creation myth.

The TPS7H500x-SP family consists of radiation-hardness-assured current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, used with external gate drivers. Output voltage is set by a VOUT-to-VSENSE resistor divider to a 0.613-V reference, with high-tolerance resistors recommended. Soft start uses the SS pin and a capacitor; the SS pin serves as the error-amplifier reference until it rises above VREF, and synchronous rectifier outputs become active after SS reaches 1 V. Switching frequency modes are internal oscillator, external synchronization, and primary-secondary. Internal mode uses RT and provides a SYNC output at twice the switching frequency; external mode leaves RT floating and applies a 200-kHz to 4-MHz clock; primary-secondary mode uses a primary RT and a secondary in external synchronization mode, with secondary clock inversion and 90° or 270° phase shift. Primary outputs OUTA/OUTB and SR outputs SRA/SRB vary by device, have roughly 150-mA peak capability, and are recommended to drive external gate drivers. Dead times and leading-edge blank times are programmable via PS, SP, and LEB pins, except TPS7H5003-SP has fixed values; pulse skipping addresses minimum-on-time issues. Duty cycle is programmed through DCL. CS_ILIM supports peak current mode control, current limiting, and hiccup mode via CHICC. Other features include FAULT pin external protection, RSC slope compensation, Type 2A/2B frequency compensation, and thermal shutdown at 175°C with restart below 160°C. The document also provides a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull GaN converter design example with component selections, power-supply recommendations, layout guidelines, application curves, documentation, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

The article tests trend-following and momentum strategies on Bitcoin using BTC-USD data from 2015 to April 2021, excluding commissions, slippage, and taxes. It states Bitcoin’s volatility suits trend following, though drawdowns are substantial. A short average under 20 days worked best; a five-day exponential average had a 145% CAGR. A two-simple-moving-average strategy using 100 and 250 days made three trades, had a 65% max drawdown in 2018, and achieved 115% CAGR versus 94% buy and hold. A momentum strategy buying when the close is higher than 25 days ago and selling when lower beat buy and hold and minimized drawdown despite a low win ratio. Code for all three strategies is available in Amibroker and Tradestation. The article concludes all three worked reasonably well and may continue if Bitcoin remains volatile. FAQs state trend-following with simple moving averages has shown effectiveness, volatility benefits trend followers, and Bitcoin drawdowns resemble Nasdaq’s 82% but recovered faster, with no guarantee.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K regarding its 2022 Annual Shareholders Meeting held December 13, 2022. 7,456,502,484 shares of common stock were entitled to vote, and 6,407,164,715 were voted. Shareholders elected twelve director nominees, approved on an advisory basis the compensation of named executive officers, and ratified Deloitte & Touche LLP as independent auditor for fiscal year 2023. Shareholders did not approve shareholder proposals concerning a cost/benefit analysis of diversity and inclusion, hiring persons with arrest or incarceration records, retirement fund investment in companies contributing to climate change, government use of Microsoft technology, development of products for the military, and tax transparency. The inspector of election certified vote tabulations. The report was signed December 16, 2022, by Keith R. Dolliver.

The Minnesota Timberwolves (40-30), sixth in the Western Conference, host the NBA-best Houston Rockets (55-14) on Sunday on the second night of a back-to-back for both teams. Minnesota is 4-4 since Jimmy Butler’s Feb. 24 knee surgery, while Karl-Anthony Towns is averaging 25.5 points over his last six games. Engineers at UC San Diego developed ultrasound-powered nanorobots, made of gold nanowires coated with hybrid platelet/red blood cell membranes, that swim through blood to remove harmful bacteria and toxins. Platelets bind pathogens like MRSA, while red blood cells absorb and neutralize bacterial toxins. Ultrasound enables swimming without chemical fuel. In tests, MRSA-contaminated blood samples had three times less bacteria and toxins after five minutes than untreated samples. The proof-of-concept work was published in Science Robotics. Future work includes live animal tests and biodegradable materials.

It said the outlook is encouraging due to a Yum! Brands partnership and smaller-city expansion, with raised 2019 revenue and EPS estimates, though valuation is elevated. Shares fell 1.6%.

The Nobel Prize is globally recognized but spotlights only narrow slices of science and few scientists. Many fields, including ecology, oceanography, weather and climate, and geology, mostly do not qualify. Because only three people can share a prize, many contributors remain unrecognized. Winners tend to be white men from wealthy regions such as the United States and Western Europe; few women have won physiology or medicine, chemistry, or physics, and only one Black person has won a science prize. Causes include unequal access to research environments and long delays from nomination to award. Winning scientists often head their own labs, as with Victor Ambros and Rosalind Lee. The Nobel Foundation is unlikely to change the prizes because of Alfred Nobel’s will. Still, supporters say the prize shows science can change lives and sparks public curiosity about science.

The document relates to artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep convolutional neural networks, including systems and methods for training and using CNNs and atrous convolutional neural networks (ACNNs) for genomic splice site classification and aberrant splicing detection. It describes neural network components such as convolution layers, non-linear layers, dilated/atrous convolutions, sub-sampling/pooling layers, residual blocks, skip/highway connections, densely connected architectures, dimensionality-altering convolutions, batch normalization, 1D convolution, and global average pooling. It also describes training via forward and backward passes, backpropagation, gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent, and Adam, and discusses deep learning in genomics for sequence-based problems including motif discovery, pathogenic variant identification, and gene expression inference.

The disclosed implementations train an ACNN or CNN on donor splice site, acceptor splice site, and non-splicing site training examples. Inputs are target nucleotide sequences flanked by context nucleotides, and outputs include triplet scores for each nucleotide as donor splice site, acceptor splice site, or non-splicing site. ACNN implementations include groups of residual blocks with parameters such as convolution filters, convolution window size, and atrous convolution rate; the atrous rate progresses non-exponentially and window size varies between groups. Named implementations include SpliceNet80, SpliceNet400, SpliceNet2000, and SpliceNet10000.

For aberrant splicing detection, reference and variant sequences are processed through the ACNN or CNN to produce splice site scores. Differences in scores are compared position-wise or row-wise; if a difference exceeds a predetermined threshold, the variant is classified as causing aberrant splicing and pathogenic, and if below the threshold, as not causing aberrant splicing and benign. Thresholds can be selected using benign common variants and pathogenic rare variants. The ACNN can identify variants that cause autism spectrum disorder or developmental delay disorder. Priority applications and incorporated references are also listed.

With recent offensive innovation, teams seek more points; skill players are paid more, while kickers are often undrafted and minimally paid. A kicker’s main job is extra points and field goals: extra points follow touchdowns and are worth 1, field goals are worth 3 from about 25–60 yards in the NFL, with expectations around 80% on field goals and 90% on extra points. Kickoffs are also important for touchbacks and directional kicks, and situational kicks include onside kicks just past ten yards to create recovery chances. In the NFL, punters and kickers are usually separate, but kickers may sub for injured punters. They are called kickers because they strictly kick; placekicker refers to kicks set by a holder or tee. Skills include accuracy, lower-body power/strength, consistent technique, and flexibility; typical build is slim, 5’10–6’2 and 180–210 pounds. Notable kickers include Justin Tucker, Morten Andersen, and Adam Vinatieri, with the records described. Kickers affect fourth-down decisions, are crucial in tight games, and unreliable kicking stresses offenses and defenses; missed field goals waste opportunities and affect field position, while kickoffs and onside recoveries matter to special teams.

VentureWire, dated Thursday, May 31, 2001, reports in its top stories that Insight Capital Partners closed its fourth fund with more than $740 million, Whitney & Co. will spin off its Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London offices, Rho Ventures closed Fund IV with $435 million, and Quake Technologies raised $30 million in a second round. The issue also lists new financings for companies including Arexis, SpeedGreetings, Tools for Health, Remedyne, Fractus, OmniSonics Medical, Xtime, Neurotech, Atherotech, Spirian Technologies, and E Ink. It reports PaperExchange shut down European operations; new deals involving Softbank/Scientia Health Group, Eqvitec/IT Provider, and Incyte/Iconix; new products from Cervalis and Alacra; and M&A transactions including Bertelsmann/MyPlay, TMP Worldwide/FlipDog.com, and Metavante/CyberBills. It also notes board appointments and executive changes, MMC Capital closed Technology Fund II at $250 million, and Royal Bank Capital Partners added two to its Energy Fund team.

North Carolina regulators are discussing whether and how to test backyard gardens near the Chemours plant near Fayetteville for GenX and related chemicals, a state official said. The talks follow a Dutch study that found such chemicals in about 40 per cent of food samples near a Chemours factory; it concluded garden crops were safe but advised nearby residents to limit consumption. North Carolina discussions have not concluded, with home gardens the initial focus. Fish tests near both plants are expected within months. GenX’s human effects are unknown, and there are no federal health standards.

High-κ materials require both a high dielectric constant and a wide band gap, but existing materials such as SiO₂, perovskites, and HfO₂ face trade-offs in capacitance, leakage, processing, or integration. The study develops a machine-learning model that predicts the ionic dielectric constant by separately predicting Born effective charge tensors with an E(3)-EGNN and phonon properties with a pretrained machine-learning potential, then combining them analytically. Trained on 928 oxides, the joint model achieved higher accuracy than a direct prediction model. Using this framework, the authors screened 8,717 oxides and identified 38 previously unknown high-κ oxides; 36 contain transition metals with empty d orbitals, and most have oxygen octahedral networks. Experimental synthesis was reported for 10 of the 38 oxides, and five had reported experimental dielectric constants consistent with predictions. The authors suggest extending the approach to non-oxides and finite-temperature effects.

The higher highs and higher lows pattern signals an uptrend, but backtests of SPY, GLD, and TLT using two consecutive daily bars with higher highs and higher lows, entering at the close and exiting after 1–10 bars, showed weak short-term gains. Longer holding periods improved results in SPY. Gold had poor returns, and TLT had negative short-term returns. The pattern did not work as a short strategy, and three or four consecutive days did not help. It is a short-term reversal pattern but not powerful enough alone as a trading signal.

The speaker has not closely looked at the other team’s injured player and is focused on his own team. He says the group is focused, relaxed, and enjoying the moment, with elimination-game experience, and held a simple practice after a six-hour flight to loosen up. He discusses honoring Marc, who is not on the trip, as part of the team, and praises a player’s leadership, impact, and pregame approach. The team has discussed altering its game and correcting what it did not do well enough before tomorrow’s game.

"Dancing with the Stars" Episode 3 is themed "TikTok night," with live updates. After Week 2’s double elimination, Corey Feldman and Baron Davis were sent home, leaving 12 celebrity contestants; Jordan Chiles remains the only athlete. Judges Derek Hough, Carrie Ann Inaba, and Bruno Tonioli score couples up to 30 points, converted into a Judges’ Score Percentage. Audience votes are converted into a Public Vote Percentage and combined equally with the judges’ percentage. Voting occurs during the live ET/CT broadcast via ABC, Disney+, or text, with up to 10 votes per couple per method.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture GA100, is an 8th-generation data center GPU for AI, HPC, and data analytics. It is fabricated on TSMC 7nm N7 and includes 54.2 billion transistors, 108 SMs, 40 GB HBM2 memory at 1555 GB/sec, and 40 MB L2 cache. Its third-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary data types, with fine-grained structured sparsity doubling throughput; A100 delivers speedups over V100 for TF32, FP16/FP32 mixed precision, FP64, and INT8. A100 adds Multi-Instance GPU partitioning into up to seven GPU Instances with fault isolation and QoS, third-generation NVLink with 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, and support for NVIDIA Magnum IO and Mellanox interconnect solutions. CUDA 11 advances include asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, task graph acceleration, L2 cache residency controls, and cooperative groups. The A100 also adds NVJPG decode, an optical flow accelerator, atomics improvements, and five NVDEC units. DGX A100 is a system with eight A100 GPUs, up to 5 PFLOPS, NVSwitch, and Mellanox ConnectX-6 HDR InfiniBand; with MIG it can provide up to 56 isolated accelerators.

Medora Brown, communications manager at Sanergy, was developing a social media plan for the Kenyan sanitation company. Sanergy, founded by MIT MBA students, provides Fresh Life toilets in Nairobi slums through franchising and converts human waste into Evergrow fertilizer and insect-based animal feed under Farm Star. Brown had to allocate limited funds and content resources, measure ROI, and engage different audiences—slum dwellers, farmers, and global investors/donors. Kenya’s technology and social media use was growing, with Facebook dominant, Twitter and LinkedIn present, and farmers increasingly using Facebook and WhatsApp; slum dwellers had limited access and used Facebook mainly for practical purposes. Sanergy’s brands—Fresh Life, Farm Star, and corporate—had separate Facebook pages; Farm Star used Facebook, WhatsApp, and SMS for leads, while Fresh Life relied on personal contact and had little social media investment. Corporate used blogs, email, and speaking engagements for fundraising, with some doubts about social media’s role. Brown needed to determine platform strategy, content flow, and metrics to support each brand’s business goals.

University of Edinburgh researchers identified 287 independent genetic signals linked to male pattern baldness in a genome-wide study of DNA from more than 52,000 mostly middle-aged men. Forty signals were on the X chromosome, which men inherit from their mothers. The researchers said a formula can predict risk somewhat, but individual prediction remains far off and it is too soon to say whether a blood test could forecast hair loss.

Mercy University’s School of Education has received federal, state, and local grants that support educator preparation and program innovation. The article highlights several grants.

The GRAD-PRO grant is a five-year, $2.8 million U.S. Department of Education PPOHA award received in 2023. It aims to expand graduate and professional opportunities for Hispanic and other underrepresented students, improve academic attainment, support academic and career alignment, expand faculty mentoring, and bolster retention, persistence, and degree attainment through resources including scholarships. It focuses on health sciences, education, faculty mentoring, and business. It co-hosted “Voices from the Field: Mental Well-Being in Schools” with BranchED in 2024.

The BranchED grant, awarded in 2023, is a three-year grant from BranchED to strengthen teacher preparation programs at Minority Serving Institutions. Mercy’s School of Education works on district partnerships, curriculum reviews, data-informed instruction, and collaboration with the Public Schools of the Tarrytowns. It receives biweekly coaching, professional learning, resources, and support. In Year 1, Mercy exceeded the required 80% outcomes with 100% success and was the first institution to complete the Transformation Center process with that distinction. It co-hosted a spring 2024 symposium and the mental health event. Its final year focuses on sustaining collaborative practices.

MISTI, sponsored by the National Science Foundation through the Robert Noyce Teacher Scholarship Program since 2013, prepares science and math teachers for high-need middle and high schools. Eligible fourth-year undergraduates or first-year master’s students with math or science majors can become MISTI Scholars. They begin observations, coursework, and monthly pedagogical seminars on racism and social justice. In the second year, they complete student teaching, earn a master’s in Adolescence Education and state certification, and receive support for exams and job searches. Support continues during early teaching years. Research shows intensive mentoring, the cohort model, and long-term support help Scholars persist in high-need schools.

The STEM Master Teaching Fellowship, funded by the Robert Noyce Teacher Scholarship Program from 2019–2024, supported 14 PK–12 math, science, and computer science teachers from four high-needs districts. Fellows completed 9 graduate credits in STEM pedagogy and leadership projects. Faculty formed a professional learning community. Fellows led STEM programs, community gardens, and professional development; the project produced articles and presentations.

The CR-ITI/ESOL program received $687,500 from NYSED for 2023–2028. It prepares ESOL teachers to address shortages in New York City, leads to an Advanced Certificate in ESOL/TESOL, and includes clinical practice, mentor teachers, supervisors, professional development, observations, feedback, and first-year support.

The conclusion states these grants have advanced the School of Education’s growth, supporting program improvement, professional learning, career readiness, mentoring, and collaboration.

U.S. mortgage application activity fell for a second week, down 0.8 percent to 403.6 in the week ended March 24, MBA data showed. Average 30-year fixed conforming mortgage rates dropped to 4.33 percent from 4.46 percent, the biggest drop since early January. Refinance applications fell 2.9 percent and their share declined to 44.0 percent, while purchase applications rose 1.2 percent. The adjustable-rate mortgage share contracted to 8.5 percent. FHA 30-year rates also fell.

The speaker credits the players in front for playing well and solid defense discouraging opponents. Winning is important, but they must move forward and not get caught up in future reflections. Tight games and a late save kept him focused, and he credits the team for shutouts. He is confident and expects a tough challenge in Anaheim, where those guys will try to forget the trip to New Jersey and apply pressure.

A CORAF report describes results from SRI-WAAPP, the largest System of Rice Intensification project ever undertaken, involving more than 50,000 rice farmers, 1,000 sites, and 13 West African countries. SRI reduces inputs, including agrochemicals, while increasing yields. An independent evaluation in five countries found yield increases of 54 percent for irrigated, 65 percent for rainfed lowland, and 153 percent for rainfed upland systems, plus a 41 percent average increase in farmers’ incomes. Project assessment found increases of 56 percent and 86 percent for irrigated and rainfed lowland systems. In 2015-2016, SRI produced over 20,000 additional tons of milled rice at project sites, valued at about US$10 million; complete adoption in 2017 would have eliminated rice imports. Authors advocate scaling up SRI through local adaptation. Labor concerns, especially for women, led to adoption of labor-saving weeding.

Marcel Strigberger describes decluttering his house by discarding McGill law schoolbooks he bought over 50 years ago and no longer needed after retirement. He reviewed each book, recalling legal concepts and cases such as fee simple, fee tail, and memorable decisions, then threw most away. He later found a used hardcover of one book listed on Amazon for over $1,000 Canadian and briefly reflected on his haste. He kept one five-inch-thick book as a reading stand for standing at his desk.
Minister Mailis Reps signed a directive to create state-run upper secondary schools in Viimsi and Rapla, and opened hiring for their leading positions; construction is in its second phase.

After five days investigating Las Vegas gunman Stephen Paddock, authorities said they still had no clear motive. They pursued about 1,000 leads, reviewed casino video, did not believe Paddock had an accomplice, and planned FBI billboards seeking public help. Investigators examined whether he was with a prostitute, his cruises, a cryptic note with numbers, his politics, finances, possible radicalization, and social behavior. Paddock, a 64-year-old gambler, killed 58 and wounded hundreds at a country music festival from his hotel suite before killing himself. He planned meticulously, stockpiled 23 guns, set up cameras, booked rooms overlooking other festivals, and bought tracer rounds. His girlfriend said she noticed no changes in his mental state and was unaware of his plans.

The passage presents a systematic literature review on robotic coding education in science education. It discusses technology’s role in education, the emergence of robotic coding as part of STEM, definitions of coding and robotics, and reported educational benefits. The study aims to synthesize empirical evidence and suggest future research on robotic coding in science education. It reviews studies published between 2015 and 2022 in WOS and Scopus using inclusion/exclusion criteria and PRISMA, ultimately including 15 peer-reviewed empirical articles. Results are grouped into cognitive skills—21st-century skills and computational thinking—applications in robotic coding teaching, including integration into disciplines and tools such as Arduino and tablets, and affective variables such as interest, motivation, and opinion. Suggestions concern integration of robotic coding, use at different learning levels, teaching robotic coding, different programs, large-scale studies, varied data collection tools, further research, and gender. Recommendations call for more studies on additional 21st-century skills, other STEM areas, other coding tools, affective and psychomotor characteristics, curriculum development, teacher in-service training, and note the study’s limitation to 15 WOS and Scopus articles from 2015–2022.

Plaintiff Smarts moved under Rule 54(b) to revise the court’s prior opinion denying partial summary judgment against Avesta and Zager, citing newly discovered evidence. The court held the motion timely and procedurally proper. The new evidence showed Avesta invited Klener to invest in stock before an anticipated IPO, his investment later increased in value, and he was friendly with Avesta executives, though Klener denied any quid pro quo. Smarts argued this bias made Klener’s declaration insufficient as corroboration for Delphi prior art. The court held bias does not make corroborating testimony inadequate as a matter of law; credibility and weight are for the jury. The passage of time was not new evidence and was less substantial than in Woodland Trust. Because the new evidence did not eliminate genuine issues of material fact, the motion was denied.

The court denied in part and granted in part the motion to dismiss the appeals by the New York City Department of Finance and the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance from the order confirming 1515 Broadway’s reorganization plan. The court held that the City’s challenge to the reorganization of the general partner as a limited partnership was moot under the standards in AOV, Revere Copper, and Texaco, but that the possible future foreclosure of the Building was not moot because the transaction had not yet occurred. The State’s Gains Tax issue was also not moot because it could not have been considered by the bankruptcy court and the application of In re 995 Fifth Avenue remained unresolved. The appeals were limited as described.

The author recounts Weaver's 1947 claim that Russian is coded English. Although Google Translate is useful, machine translation lacks understanding, focusing on decoding; the author asks if understanding is necessary and turns to experiments.

The passage reports that weekend protests in Charlottesville, Virginia, and elsewhere highlighted how people with WiFi can participate from home. The Twitter account @YesYoureRacist, which grew to 271,000 followers over the weekend, worked to identify participants in a Saturday night Charlottesville protest. It identified several marchers, including Cole White, who was fired from Top Dog in Berkeley, California; Peter Cvjetanovic, who was photographed with a torch; and James Allsup, a Washington State University student. The account was also credited with finding a photo of the man who drove into a crowd of protesters. The passage notes Top Dog’s statement and Cvjetanovic’s comments.

The passage discusses software engineering, requirements engineering, and classification of requirements. Requirements are the services provided by software and the constraints under which it operates, and they are classified as functional and non-functional. Functional requirements define what software must do, while non-functional requirements describe business standards, business environment, user experience, and characteristics such as usability, speed, and reliability. The passage reviews classification methods including K-NN, Naïve Bayes, decision tree, and Support Vector Machine. Related work covers domain non-functional requirements, prioritization, effort estimation, NFR interplay, and NFR knowledge reuse. The proposed methodology identifies potential NFRs, uses clustering of semantically similar words from functional requirements, and applies decision tree classification. The implementation classifies null and non-null functions from an IVR dataset using an NFR matrix with a decision tree classifier. Results compare the proposed and existing methods in accuracy and execution time. The conclusion states that null functions reduce project efficiency, and the proposed model, tested in Python, shows high accuracy and less execution time than the existing technique.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces a hybrid rendering model combining real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI, and simulation. Turing GPUs include dedicated RT Cores in each SM to accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, plus Tensor Cores for deep learning. RT Cores work with NVIDIA RTX, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and the soon-to-come Vulkan ray tracing API, and use denoising to reduce rays per pixel. NGX provides AI-based features such as DLSS, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez; DLSS uses DNNs trained on 64x supersampled images and includes DLSS 2X. Turing also adds Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders, Variable Rate Shading with Content Adaptive, Motion Adaptive, and Foveated Rendering, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. It supports VR advancements including USB Type-C/VirtualLink, MVR, foveated rendering, and VRWorks Audio accelerated by RT Cores. The TU104, TU106, and Tesla T4 GPUs implement Turing features with varying GPC, SM, CUDA Core, Tensor Core, and RT Core counts; TU104 supports second-generation NVLink, while TU106 lacks NVLink or SLI support. RTX-OPS is a workload-based metric using Tensor, CUDA, RT, and INT32 operations. The passage also explains ray tracing mechanics, BVH acceleration, denoising, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections. In summary, hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH, and RT Cores enable real-time ray tracing on Turing.

At a Liaquatabad school ceremony, PML-N leader Dr Rana Tariq Khan called students valuable national assets, announced water pump, furniture, continued support, and urged civil society to help government-school students. An education officer cited Punjab's free education, facilities, and Rs1,000 stipends.

Smoky River FCSS seeks parents with babies who will be 2–4 months old in October for the 2017–2018 Roots of Empathy program. Created by Mary Gordon in 1996, the Canadian program uses baby classroom visits to help children reflect on feelings and improve social behavior. Contact Crystal at 780-837-2220.

The passage reports a study on sex differences in sleep phenotypes and cardiovascular disease-related outcomes. It notes higher insomnia prevalence in women and higher obstructive sleep apnea prevalence and some cardiovascular disease incidence in men. It describes challenges in sex-specific Mendelian randomization due to smaller sex-stratified sample sizes, especially in the female Million Veteran Program population, and weak instrumental variables. The authors performed sex-specific sleep-phenotype GWASs in MVP, developed a semi-empirical Bayesian approach with an adaptive posterior mean estimator to improve sex-specific variant-exposure effect estimates by borrowing information across sex groups, and integrated shrinkage estimates into two-sample MR analyses. Simulations compared raw, fixed-effects meta, adaptive posterior mean, and adaptive weight estimates. Shrinkage estimates improved causal effect estimation for the smaller female sample, were less sensitive to sex differences than fixed-effects meta when effects differed, and did not lose efficiency in larger samples. MR-RAPS performed no worse than other methods, especially with weak instruments. In real analyses using MVP sleep GWAS and All of Us CVD outcomes, the method identified sex-specific associations, including insomnia with chronic kidney disease and long sleep with hypertension in females, short sleep with coronary artery disease in males, and additional obstructive sleep apnea associations. Sex differences were found for obstructive sleep apnea on chronic kidney disease and long sleep on several CVD outcomes. Limitations included reliance on MVP sleep GWAS for instrumental variable selection, sensitivity to instrumental variable selection, use of raw estimates for sex-difference tests, and restriction to European ancestry.

Last week included earnings, economic data, fiscal policy moves, and political drama. GDP came in at 3% versus 2.5% expected, though tariff policies distorted the data. Nonfarm payrolls added 73,000 jobs versus 100,000 expected, with sharp downward revisions to the prior two months. The FOMC had two dissenting votes, and Powell signaled patience and data dependency. President Trump fired the BLS commissioner, announced nuclear submarine deployments and new tariff deals, and Fed Governor Adriana Kugler resigned. Earnings were described as the primary market message, with 82% of S&P 500 companies reporting EPS above estimates and 79% above revenue estimates. Markets began bullish but ended in technical deterioration, with a bearish engulfing pattern, risk-off tone, negative internals, and most sectors down. The interest rate market pointed to expectations of Fed cuts.

A University of Copenhagen study found excessive social media use can harm emotional well-being, with passive “lurking” linked to envy and worsened mood. A 2015 study found teens using social media over two hours daily had higher mental illness risk, though such platforms can also provide mental health services. Researchers suggest limiting use or quitting Facebook.

The passage discusses interference in physics, particularly nuclear resonance scattering and Mössbauer interferometry, and introduces a dynamically controllable x-ray interferometer for Mössbauer science. Traditional crystal x-ray interferometers require Angstrom-level alignment, while multi-target Mössbauer setups avoid spatially separated paths but face challenges in selective coupling, phase variation, and radiative coupling. The new setup uses two α-iron targets enriched in 57Fe inside a high-purity polarimetry setup and operates in a dark-fringe mode: only two co-propagating polarization pathways contribute, radiative couplings cancel, and the empty interferometer transmission ideally vanishes. Relative displacement of the targets tunes the phase between pathways. Experiments using event-based detection measured effects of sudden target displacements up to about 7.5 µs (~50 nuclear lifetimes). Applications include nanosecond control of transmitted x-ray intensity and measurement of relative target displacements on x-ray wavelength and nanosecond time scales via mechanical waves over more than 10 µs. The results section explains the polarization-based dark-fringe operation, shows cancellation of multi-scattering pathways, and describes piezoelectric phase control.

The speaker returns to Congress less than three weeks after the inaugural to present plans for extended prosperity and continued peace, calling for governing rather than bickering. He proposes a budget with four features: attention to urgent priorities, investment in the future, an attack on the deficit, and no new taxes. He says economic growth will provide over $80 billion in new revenues without tax increases, allowing modest spending increases, key investments, and an almost 40 percent deficit cut in one year while meeting Gramm-Rudman-Hollings targets. He asks for two-year budgets, a line-item veto, required votes on rescissions, and a balanced-budget amendment.

He lists principles including growth, lower tax rates, greater freedom and choice, private-sector provision where possible, opposition to discrimination, and support for family and faith. Proposals include increased National Science Foundation funding, a permanent research and development tax credit, a competitiveness task force chaired by Vice President Quayle, increased NASA funding and a manned space station, a capital gains tax cut, urban enterprise zones, and education initiatives such as merit schools, teacher awards, National Science Scholars, magnet schools, and alternative certification. He asks Congress to help him be the “Education President.”

On drugs, he requests almost $1 billion more to escalate the war, with Bill Bennett as drug czar, expanded treatment, border protection, tougher prosecution, and the death penalty for worst kingpins. He seeks $1.6 billion for AIDS education and research. On the environment, he proposes a new Clean Air Act with acid-rain reductions, clean-coal funding with Canada, conservation fund acquisitions, ocean protections, postponement of three offshore lease sales, and tougher toxic-waste enforcement. He supports Medicaid increases, a child care tax credit, a doubled adoption deduction, fully funded Social Security, homeless aid, and a Puerto Rico referendum. He urges savings-system reform within 45 days and cleanup of nuclear weapons plants.

He supports a one-year military budget freeze, a national security review, and Pentagon procurement reform. Abroad, he cites change in the Soviet Union, assures Gorbachev of readiness to move forward after review, supports the Strategic Defense Initiative, a chemical-weapons ban, nuclear nonproliferation, self-determination in Central America including Nicaragua, stronger alliances, and trips to Europe and the Pacific. He calls on business, military, farmers, parents, children, and disabled Americans to serve and participate. He closes with Churchill’s words: “Give us the tools, and we will do the job.”

The passage discusses benchmark reliability in language models, noting that benchmark auditing has received less attention than algorithmic advances. Recent work identifies issues such as redundancy and uneven data distributions that can skew results. To investigate reliability distributionally, the authors introduce HARMONY, an entropy-based metric that partitions a benchmark into semantic clusters/subdomains, gathers per-cluster model performances, and measures how uniformly performance is distributed across subdomains. High HARMONY suggests aggregate metrics capture broad competence; low HARMONY obscures strengths and weaknesses. The authors analyze 19 MCQA benchmarks across five model families in the HARMONY mean-variance plane and recommend reporting HARMONY alongside accuracy.

This lecture discusses renormalization group equations for operators and Wilson coefficients in an effective field theory derived from the Standard Model. It treats the weak Hamiltonian for b → c ubar d, four-fermion operators, bare and renormalized forms, the 1,2 and plus-minus bases, and anomalous dimension equations. Since the Hamiltonian is mu-independent, operator anomalous dimensions determine coefficient anomalous dimensions. The equations are solved by changing variables from mu to alpha using the beta function, with boundary conditions at a scale mu_w of order M_w. The solution sums leading logarithms and is applied to B → D pi by evolving coefficients to a scale mu_b of order M_b. The lecture also covers higher-order renormalization group improved perturbation theory, next-to-leading log matching between full and effective theories, scheme dependence, and subtleties involving gamma5 and evanescent operators.

Patient advocacy groups have asked the U.K. antitrust regulator to investigate several large drugmakers and their U.K. lobbying organization over suspected coordinated efforts to drive up medicine prices. The complaint follows a dispute over mandatory NHS rebates, which rose from 10% to 23%, prompting AstraZeneca, Merck, and Eli Lilly to halt or scrap expansion plans worth a combined $2.6 billion.

The Office of the Historian released an ebook edition of *Foreign Relations of the United States, 1919, Volume I: The Paris Peace Conference, 1919*. The ebook reproduces the printed volume, recommends citing document numbers, and notes updates. Its preface states that publishing official American records of the 1919 Paris settlement is timely to help avoid past pitfalls, although no government has yet given a substantially complete public record and unofficial literature exists.

Computing evolved from purpose-built machines to general-purpose programmable machines, time-sharing, and networked client-server architectures. In the early 2000s, the internet and large datacenters led to distributed systems made of multiple applications or replicas on different machines communicating together. Properly structured distributed systems can be more reliable and support scalable organizational models, but are more complex to design, build, and debug and require higher engineering skills. Demand for reliable distributed systems continues to grow, along with tools, patterns, and practices. Containers, container images, and container orchestrators have become popular foundations for reliable distributed systems and reusable components.

At Lansdowne High School, students in Brandon Nicklas’s televideo production class produce five-minute morning announcements from the school’s TV studio, streamed to classrooms and school-issued laptops. Nicklas says the work gives students hands-on video production experience and an outlet to express themselves. Television studio use in county schools is rising: about 100 of 161 schools have studios, about half digital. Costs range from about $400 for live streaming to $15,000-$18,000 for a full digital studio, with no central funding. Broadcast production facilitator compensation was added to union-negotiated extra-duty activities. Experts say media technology builds teamwork, communication, public speaking, creativity, and critical thinking. Hillcrest Elementary debuted a studio, and Arbutus Middle’s principal obtained equipment.

Researchers at Penn Medicine found that psilocybin affected specific brain circuits and may lead to new pain and mental health management options. In mice with chronic nerve injury and inflammatory pain, a single dose reduced pain and pain-induced anxiety and depression-like behaviors for almost two weeks. Psilocybin activated serotonin receptors 5-HT2A and 5-HT1A like a dimmer switch; injection into the anterior cingulate cortex produced similar relief, while spinal cord injection did not. The study suggests potential for non-opioid, non-addictive therapies, but more research is needed on dosing, long-term effects, and safety or feasibility in surgery and anesthesia.

Eighth annual Regional Theatrical Youth Camp runs June 19–30, 2017, ending in a public ticketed production. Level I serves ages 5–8; Level II serves ages 9–18 and includes a role in “Bye, Bye Birdie, Jr.” A second show is July 2. Cindy Brown directs, assisted by Kenny Brown; Oliver Companies sponsors.

The passage reports a study using DIA-based urinary proteomics in HAE. It identified different urinary proteomic profiles among type 1 HAE, type 2 HAE, and healthy controls, with enriched pathways including complement and coagulation cascades, cell adhesion molecules, immune response, proteolysis, and bradykinin catabolic process. A urinary biomarker panel of C1-INH, KNG1, and EGF is described as a promising noninvasive diagnostic tool for HAE. Validation used PRM-based targeted proteomics in an independent cohort. The discovery phase included 20 adult HAE patients and 29 healthy controls; the validation phase included 24 type 1 HAE patients and 18 healthy controls.

The passage describes a magnetically levitated rotor consisting of a hard ferromagnetic rare-earth sphere levitated in a cylindrically symmetric type I superconducting trap. Its motion is detected by a dc SQUID flux sensor via a superconducting pick-up coil and actuated by driving coils. The setup is in a cryogenic vacuum chamber at T = 4.2 K, with helium gas pressure varied. Levitation relies on Meissner repulsion, modeled as dipole-dipole interaction between the sphere’s magnetic moment and an image dipole; translational degrees of freedom x, y, z are trapped, while rotational motion includes polar librational β and azimuthal librational α modes due to residual horizontal field. Synchronous feedback driving is used to initiate and control spinning.

Spin-down measurements under gas damping fit exponential decay Ω = Ω0e−γt, with γ = Γ/I. Gas damping gives Γ ∝ P and γ = (10/π)(P/ρ v̄ R). Damping rate versus gauge pressure Pg is roughly linear; low-pressure fit gives A = (8.2 ± 0.1) (s·mbar)−1 and B = −1.5 × 10−4 s−1, with residual pressure Pg res = 1.8 × 10−5 mbar. The measured γ/P = (11.6 ± 0.2) (s·mbar)−1 agrees with theoretical prediction (12 ± 0.2) (s·mbar)−1. The lowest spin-down damping is γ = 4.75 × 10−7 s−1, corresponding to effective pressure P = 4 × 10−8 mbar, showing pressure sensing from 10−3 to 10−8 mbar. Quality factor Q = πf/γ = 1.33 × 1013 is reported.

A maximum spinning frequency of 2.3 MHz is achieved for R ≈ 30 µm, corresponding to tangential speed 466 m/s and tangential acceleration 0.65 × 1010 m/s2. SQUID electronics distort above ∼2 MHz, while material disintegration may limit frequency to around 5.5 MHz for R = 30 µm. A low-frequency secondary peak is interpreted as precession of the spinning axis around the vertical axis, with fl = fx2/fs and fx ≈ 240 Hz; discrepancy is attributed to a frozen field.

The rotor is described as the fastest magnetically levitated rotor demonstrated, requiring no active feedback stabilization and using synchronous driving with lower heating. It operates as a cryogenic pressure sensor at 4.2 K. Possible applications include gyroscopes, gravimeters, magic angle spinning, material characterization, precision torque measurements, ultrasensitive magnetometry with thermal-noise-limited resolution 1 × 10−16 T/√Hz, probing ultralight dark matter, mechanical tests of spontaneous collapse models, gravitational measurements, and tests of quantum effects. The conclusion states demonstration of ultrafast, ultralow-dissipation magnetic microrotors at cryogenic temperature with frequencies above 2.3 MHz and damping below 10−6 Hz, plus wide-range cryogenic pressure sensing.

Researchers at Columbia created a chip that turns a single laser into a frequency comb, producing dozens of high-power light channels. Using a locking mechanism to clean noisy laser light, they achieved lab-grade precision on a small silicon device. The chip could improve data center efficiency and support sensing, quantum tech, and LiDAR. It may replace racks of individual lasers with one compact device and enable multiple parallel data streams through the same fiber. The work began when researchers noticed a frequency comb while testing high-power chips for LiDAR.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers have three switching-frequency modes—internal oscillator, external synchronization, and primary-secondary—configured through the RT and SYNC pins. Internal oscillator mode uses an RT resistor for 100 kHz to 2 MHz, and SYNC outputs a clock at twice the switching frequency. External synchronization requires RT floating and a SYNC clock at twice the desired switching frequency, 200 kHz to 4 MHz, with 40%–60% duty cycle recommended at 50%, and the clock is internally inverted. Primary-secondary mode uses a populated RT on the primary and floating RT on the secondary with shared SYNC; the secondary inverts the clock, causing 90° or 270° phase shift. The devices provide OUTA/OUTB and SRA/SRB outputs with roughly 150-mA peak current, recommend external gate drive, and use DCL for duty-cycle limits; OUTB/SRB are active only with DCL = AVSS on specified devices. Other features include programmable dead time and leading-edge blank time via PS, SP, and LEB, pulse skipping, CS_ILIM current sensing and hiccup mode, FAULT external protection, RSC slope compensation, Type 2A/2B frequency compensation, and thermal shutdown. The series is for radiation-hardness-assured space-grade DC-DC converters using fixed-frequency peak current mode control, supporting topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. A design example uses the TPS7H5001-SP in a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull GaN converter and provides component and design values. Power supply and layout guidance include a 4-V to 14-V input, 0.1-µF minimum bypass, and layout practices for noise and grounding. The passage also contains revision history and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

The passage examines the MACD indicator and its use in trading strategies. MACD stands for moving average convergence/divergence and consists of two moving averages. The fast MACD line is the 12-day EMA minus the 26-day EMA; the slow signal line is the 9-day EMA of the fast line; the histogram is the fast line minus the signal line. Default settings are 12, 26, and 9. A basic S&P 500 crossover strategy produced a 4.19% CAGR, 0.44% average gain per trade, 1.65 profit factor, and 30% maximum drawdown, and is described as untradeable. Optimization indicated best parameters near default. Adding criteria such as a negative slow line or a 200-day trend filter changed results. A MACD histogram strategy produced a 4.79% CAGR, 0.95% average gain, 4.22 profit factor, and 16% drawdown; combining it with a two-day RSI produced a 6.36% CAGR, 0.76% average gain, 2.45 profit factor, and 16% drawdown. Crypto tests had moderate success. MACD is a lagging indicator; the histogram is described as reliable in backtests, with money expected about 70% of the time in stock mean-reversion tests. MACD is better at momentum and divergencies, while RSI is better at overbought/oversold levels. Best settings depend on asset and time frame. The passage also lists benefits, steps, mistakes, advanced techniques, and a glossary.

The passage reports a retrospective radiogenomic analysis of pediatric low-grade glioma (pLGG) using Children’s Brain Tumor Network data. It analyzed 545 patients, including 494 with multi-omic data and 201 with multiparametric MRI; imaging cohorts were split into discovery (160) and replication (41). RNA-sequencing clustering of 494 pLGGs identified three immunological clusters based on immune cell infiltration-related gene expression: cluster 1 intermediate (n = 189), cluster 2 high (n = 164), and cluster 3 lowest (n = 141). Cluster 2 had the worst overall prognosis and highest tumor inflammation signature; clusters differed in tumor mutational burden and molecular subtype associations. A radioimmunomic signature using conventional MRI and age distinguished cluster 2 from clusters 1 and 3, with AUC 0.77/0.74 and balanced accuracy 76.8%/86.0% in discovery/replication; adding ADC features improved AUC to 0.83/0.79 and balanced accuracy to 81.5%/84.4%. A clinicoradiomic Cox model predicted progression-free survival with Harrell’s concordance indexes of 0.71 and 0.77, Uno’s indexes of 0.72 and 0.80, and integrated Brier scores of 0.24 and 0.16. Key clinical predictors included tumor resection extent, chemotherapy, age at diagnosis, and tumor location; in patients without total/near-total resection, the clinicoradiomic model outperformed a clinical-only model. Predicted risk scores were associated with treatment resistance and immunological clusters, and biological interpretability linked risk to germline SYNE1 variants and transcriptomic pathways. Limitations included limited imaging/genomic data, rarity of pediatric brain tumors, possible non-objective progression determination, and unavailable additional data layers.

Mesocap and Tradelink brought an admiralty action against Torm Lines to recover for damage to Mesocap cargo shipped in 1996 from Savannah to Calabar, Nigeria, by way of Cotonou, Benin. This paper formulates safety evaluation of frontier AI models as a sequential decision-making problem using a modified survival bandit, where an agent seeks to avoid exceeding a safety threshold during evaluation to obtain post-evaluation reward. Experiments show detection performance varies with the safety threshold and post-evaluation horizon. The paper suggests reducing the agent’s awareness of test stringency or post-evaluation freedom may improve detectability, and notes limitations including more sophisticated sandbagging and the need for further characterization of the test.

This study investigated the assessment and management of childhood pneumonia in primary care in Malawi. Semi-structured interviews were conducted in 10 health facilities in Northern Malawi with staff, policy makers, and caregivers; data were analysed using thematic analysis and SEIPS 101 tools. Forty-three interviews were conducted, and a process map was created. Caregivers identified barriers including insufficient education on managing sick children, distance to healthcare, decisions about seeking care, choice between health facilities and traditional healers, transport difficulties, and cost. Staff identified barriers including workload, lack of resources such as medications and batteries, uncertainty regarding severity markers, and the need to give all antibiotics. The health passport system and effective teamwork and community were highlighted as facilitators. Staff expressed indecisiveness about severity and antibiotic decisions and wished for better tools, including a pneumonia mobile app and a rapid diagnostic-like test to differentiate bacterial, viral, and fungal pneumonia. The discussion highlighted challenges in identifying severe illness and children not requiring antibiotics, concerns about antimicrobial resistance, and limitations of current WHO severity criteria. Study limitations included recruiting caregivers at health facilities and possible influence of researchers’ presence. The study concluded that managing childhood pneumonia in primary care in Malawi faces barriers related to resources, staff and caregiver education, heavy workload, and accurate identification of severe illness and antibiotic need.

Turing is NVIDIA’s new GPU architecture, implementing a Hybrid Rendering model that combines real-time ray tracing, rasterization, AI, and simulation. It uses end-to-end memory optimizations, GDDR6, signal and power integrity simulations, reduced crosstalk, larger L2 caches, higher L2 bandwidth, and lossless compression, delivering about 50% higher effective bandwidth over Pascal GP102. Its display engine supports higher resolutions, refresh rates, HDR, DisplayPort 1.4a, DSC 1.2, two 8K 60 Hz displays, USB-C, VirtualLink, NVENC HEVC 8K 30 fps encoding, and NVDEC decoding. VirtualLink provides power, display, and data over a single USB-C connector. NVLink replaces MIO and PCIe for SLI on TU102 and TU104, supporting two-way SLI. Turing includes RT Cores for real-time ray tracing, RTX software, hybrid rendering, denoising, and BVH acceleration. NGX uses Tensor Cores and DNNs for DLSS, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Mesh Shading adds Task and Mesh Shaders. Variable Rate Shading controls shading rate per 16x16 region. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling. Multi-View Rendering supports multiple views per pass. Turing supports DX12 Tier 3 bindless CBV/UAV and Tier 2 resource heaps. VR features include VirtualLink, MVR, VRS foveated rendering, and RT Core-accelerated VRWorks Audio. The passage also details TU104, TU106, and Tesla T4 specifications, RTX-OPS, and ray tracing fundamentals including BVH, denoising, ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections.

Plague is carried by rodents and their fleas and transmitted to humans mainly through fleabites. Officials advised precautions such as avoiding rodent burrows, keeping dogs leashed, not handling sick or dead animals, defleaing pets, using insect repellent, and reporting sudden rodent die-offs. The passage describes the secretive Grin blockchain and Blockstream mathematician Andrew Poelstra’s work on Mimblewimble, a privacy innovation derived from Confidential Transactions. Mimblewimble cancels spent transaction outputs, preserves authentication through blinding keys, and removes arbitrary scripts, reducing functionality to transfers while enabling verification through signatures and compressed history. Grin maintainers accepted Poelstra’s proposed design to allow soft forking of digital assets, including a Bitcoin peg; Grin would initially have Grin and a test currency, with Bitcoin later indistinguishable to outside observers. Poelstra estimated 18 months before the wider ecosystem could use it. The passage also covers “scriptless scripts,” which use signature differences for Lightning-like channels and atomic swaps without extra space or linking transactions, and Poelstra’s plans to publish work on linking transactions across chains using different elliptic curves, such as Bitcoin and Monero. It ends with his comparison of a Mimblewimble sidechain to Bitcoin: smaller for future verifiers, same real-time size as Bitcoin plus Confidential Transactions, but spent outputs and inputs delete quickly.

Gamma-ray astrophysics began around the 1950s to study high-energy astrophysical processes using cosmic gamma rays, which are not deflected by magnetic fields. Because gamma rays are absorbed by the atmosphere, direct surface measurement is impossible; satellite telescopes have small effective areas and are limited above hundreds of GeV. Ground-based imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes measure Cherenkov light from atmospheric showers, achieving effective areas of order 10^4 m^2. Current major IACT systems are MAGIC, H.E.S.S., and VERITAS. The future Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) aims to improve energy and spatial resolution, cover the full night sky, and extend the energy range from 20 GeV to 300 TeV using Large-, Medium-, and Small-Sized Telescopes in Northern and Southern arrays. Prototypes exist, including LST-1. CTAO will be the first ground-based gamma-ray observatory open to external proposals, with 40% of its first ten years devoted to Key Science Projects, including dark matter and fundamental physics.

Dark matter searches focus on WIMPs, using annihilation or decay signatures in massive targets. Simulated CTAO observations of the Galactic Center, Large Magellanic Cloud, Perseus Galaxy Cluster, and dwarf spheroidal galaxies indicate improved limits on the velocity-averaged annihilation cross section for TeV-scale WIMPs. Gamma-ray spectral features are also used. For axion-like particles, CTAO simulations of NGC 1275 estimate constraints on ALP parameters, though current published limits are not very competitive. Other studies concern extragalactic background light, intergalactic magnetic fields, and Lorentz invariance violation. CTAO is expected to enable extended surveys, strong dark matter constraints, and studies of photon propagation over cosmological distances via active galactic nuclei.

This scoping review aimed to identify candidate genes related to brain injury after prenatal Zika virus infection. Searches were conducted across multiple databases using specified inclusion and exclusion criteria. Thirteen articles were included, describing candidate genes potentially contributing to congenital Zika syndrome. The review identified 23 genes with possible roles in modulating susceptibility to virally induced brain injury, including six maternal and 17 fetal/neonatal genes, sometimes associated with injury and sometimes with protection. Candidate genes were related to neurodevelopment, immune and inflammatory responses, and cellular stress/autophagy. The authors note limitations such as small cohorts and difficulty identifying genetic risks specific to congenital Zika syndrome, and they recommend larger replication or genome-wide studies and functional analyses of candidate genes.

The court reversed an order removing Iturea Atwood Hicks as administratrix of Benjamin E. Atwood’s estate and appointing H. B. Sanders as administrator. The estate was community property worth $390 and less than $1,500, and the widow had no children. Sanders petitioned at the request of the decedent’s sister and niece, alleging the widow failed to publish notice to creditors within two months. The court held that under Code of Civil Procedure sections 1511 and 1469, the widow was entitled to have the whole estate set apart to her, no notice to creditors was necessary, and persons without interest could not petition to revoke her letters.

A Finnish study of 5,800 public sector employees who retired between 2000 and 2011 found sleep difficulties decreased after retirement. Nonrestorative sleep and early morning awakening fell significantly, especially among those with poor health and stressful work lives. Sleep problems dropped from 30% before retirement to 26% after; the likelihood of sleep problems fell 11%, early waking 24%, and nonrestorative sleep 53%, while falling or maintaining sleep changed little. Sleep duration increased about 20 minutes, or 45 minutes for those with sleep difficulties or heavy alcohol use before retirement. An outside researcher said the transition to retirement may allow some consequences of poor working conditions to reverse.

Deep ripping can reduce soil compaction but does not guarantee improved water penetration and may worsen topsoil water repellence, especially when dry. This lecture discusses how climate risk affects real estate markets and valuation. It starts with the four-quadrant model and asks whether climate risk affects rental cash flows or cap rates and risk/financing. Empirical work cited compares properties with similar exposure but different saliency of risk; findings include roughly 3% lower prices for high flood and sea-level-rise exposure with no change in rents, suggesting adjustment through cap rates and updated beliefs. It also discusses New York before and after Sandy, including about 9% lower prices for undamaged properties compared with pre-Sandy levels, with properties with major or minor damage stabilizing.

The lecture emphasizes discount rates for resiliency investments, citing Boston Seaport projections of damages up to $8 billion and protection costs around $1 billion; the chosen discount rate changes NPV conclusions. It then discusses climate beliefs using Yale Climate Opinion Map data, variation by politics and economic priorities, and research on disclosure requirements and social-media/NLP sentiment. Finally, it explains difference-in-differences, its parallel-trend assumption, and an application finding an 8% persistent price penalty for flood-zone properties after Hurricane Sandy, while noting that findings across studies and markets can be inconsistent.

Digital leaders emphasize data culture as central, using a learning mindset, transparent data access, clear progress metrics, and alignment. Culture aligns beliefs, values, and daily actions; at digital leaders, employee behavior reflects company values and leadership beliefs. Digital laggards recognize data-driven culture’s importance but face entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient top-down focus. Changing mindsets and behaviors is the hardest transformation part. Technologically mature firms differ in data culture. Organizations fit four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—and can build on strengths and target actions.

A novel high-impedance microstrip transmission line resonator was proposed for multichannel coil arrays at 10.5T MRI, combining microstrip high-frequency capability with high-impedance decoupling. Two 8 cm × 8 cm resonators were made with 3 mm copper tape, ~2 mm Teflon substrate, and tuning/matching capacitors. The coil has two resonant modes; the high-frequency mode was used for 10.5T proton imaging. It was tuned to 447 MHz and matched to 50 ohm. At a 10 mm gap, the high-frequency mode showed -21 dB decoupling between two channels, while the 116 MHz low-frequency mode showed ~-7.6 dB coupling. At a 2 mm gap, the low-frequency mode had unacceptable decoupling and a split peak, while the high-frequency mode remained decoupled. Simulation showed well-defined B1 distribution and B1+ up to 2 µT/√W. The technique was concluded to provide simple, robust high-frequency transceiver arrays for ultrahigh-field MR.

The study discusses four content selection dimensions for human rights education (HRE) at the early childhood education and care (ECEC) level: children’s ages, progression, human rights knowledge anchored in social studies, and children’s own interests. Using the Norwegian ECEC context, it analyses 73 Idebroen posts about observing UN Day through theoretical content analysis. The posts show three main approaches: human rights, diversity, and fundraising, separately or combined. The study finds age adaptations, such as arts and crafts, but little explicit discussion of progression and limited attention to specific human rights articles or legal anchoring. It also finds more focus on values than specific rights, frequent use of NGO/IGO materials and fundraising, and varying inclusion of children’s own interests. The paper identifies opportunities and challenges for using the four dimensions to inform UN Day observance and HRE content selection, including concerns about educational appropriateness, precision, legal anchoring, pluralism of perspectives, and the need for further research and didactic support.

A presidential message notes President Harding’s death and praises his kindness, humanity, greatness, and character, urging those associated with him to continue the wise principles of government he represented. It recommends Justice Department reforms, prison reform, prohibition enforcement, protection of Negro rights and anti-lynching legislation, civil service extension, public buildings, regulatory laws for oil pollution, aviation, radio, load lines, navigation, the Federal Trade Commission, and Alaskan fisheries.
