The lecture discusses Fiat-Shamir in the random oracle model, explaining that a cheating prover can exploit oracle queries and repeated attempts to break soundness if the protocol has non-negligible soundness or if negligible soundness comes from many rounds. It states a theorem that Fiat-Shamir is sound in the random oracle model when the public-coin protocol has negligible soundness and constant rounds, sketches a proof for three rounds and extends it to c rounds, and notes Kilian-Micali has constant rounds. It says the random oracle model is only a sanity check and not a standard-model proof, since contrived hash functions can make protocols insecure. Finally, it discusses that parallel repetition of a specific Hamiltonian-cycle zero-knowledge protocol is not zero knowledge, proved by showing Fiat-Shamir soundness under an LWE-related assumption, and argues that Fiat-Shamir soundness implies not zero knowledge.

This white paper examines AI in higher education. It discusses AI’s role in reshaping knowledge, enhancing student engagement, optimizing administration, and democratizing access through intelligent tutoring systems, predictive analytics, and adaptive learning. It explores institutional responses, effects on pedagogy, research, and administration, and opportunities to improve outcomes, bridge gaps, and prepare students for an AI-driven workforce. Current AI use is growing globally; research increased from 2020 to 2023, with North America, Europe, and East Asia leading and China leading publications, while some regions lag due to infrastructure and policy. The passage reports 86% of students use AI academically and nearly 25% daily. Applications include Carnegie Learning’s Cognitive Tutor, University of Michigan predictive analytics, DreamBox Learning, and Smart Sparrow. Challenges include faculty resistance, ethical concerns, algorithmic bias, data privacy, infrastructural limits, and the digital divide. Institutional responses include faculty training, curricular innovation, policy initiatives, and AI literacy programs, though only 20% of surveyed universities meet student expectations. Impacts include personalized learning, research acceleration, administrative efficiency, ethical concerns, and academic integrity issues. Opportunities include engagement, workforce preparation, collaborative research, translation, emotional recognition, and VR. Risks include academic dishonesty, automation fears, privacy, bias, digital divide, and dependency. AI tools discussed include ChatGPT, Bard, and Gemini, with uses across disciplines, peer-to-peer learning, lifelong learning, disabilities, and career counseling. Recommendations emphasize policy frameworks, faculty training, ethical governance, infrastructure investment, collaboration, and human-AI complementarity. Future trends include emotional recognition, VR/AR, and translation tools, with China and the U.S. as examples.

The speaker said the team stuck to its game plan, stayed composed after being down a goal, kept taking shots, and scored when the puck got through Belfour. They called Dr. McMullen’s need to sell the team unfortunate, said players focus on hockey, and noted facing the same player twice can feel a little weird.

The State of North Dakota appealed a district court order suppressing evidence in Denise Hahne’s DUI case. Hahne was stopped at a temporary sobriety checkpoint after she failed to stop. The district court suppressed the evidence, finding there was no safe or legal way for Hahne to avoid the checkpoint. The Supreme Court held that law enforcement checkpoints need not, as a matter of law, provide motorists with a way to avoid them; avoidability is one factor in assessing constitutional reasonableness. The Court reversed the suppression order and remanded for a determination of whether the checkpoint was constitutionally reasonable.

New Jersey ranked 25th in the Commonwealth Fund’s 2018 healthcare scorecard, down two places, and can improve preventative care, elderly readmissions, and treatment costs; it lags Northeastern neighbors but scores well on access and some child/insurance metrics.
The OECD warns that trade restrictions and high oil prices threaten global growth, confidence, jobs, and incomes. It cut its 2018 growth forecast to 3.8 percent, with 3.9 percent expected next year.

In this tax refund action, the court found that Brister’s 1985 and 1986 returns, which claimed withholding by Solar Roofing, Inc. that was never paid, were false and filed with intent to evade tax. The government proved this by clear and convincing evidence, so the IRS’s 1993 adjustment reversing the withholding credits and applying Brister’s 1989–1992 refunds against the resulting liabilities was not barred by the three-year limitations period. The court entered judgment for the defendant.

The 13/48 trading strategy is a technical analysis method using the 13-period EMA crossing above the 48-period EMA as a bullish signal and below as a bearish signal. It is momentum-based, works in trending markets, and can be risky in sideways or choppy markets because crossovers may be unreliable. Backtests show it is not an easy way to riches, is lagging, and prone to whipsaws, returning 5.1% annually versus 7.2% for buy and hold, with slightly better risk-adjusted return at 7.8%.

The passage addresses distance education and equality/inequality of opportunity in education. It defines distance education as teacher-learner interaction in physically distant environments through mass-communication tools, with synchronous and asynchronous forms, and discusses its advantages and drawbacks. It describes equality of opportunity in education as equal, nondiscriminatory conditions and opportunities, and notes digital gaps in technology access. The study used a qualitative case study, semi-structured interviews, criterion sampling, and content analysis with 21 faculty members and 26 students. Faculty reported distance education supported equality through learning at personal pace and easy access to information, but created inequality through technology access problems, internet connection problems, disregarding learner competencies, unsuitable learning environments, and increased differences among students. Students reported contributions through freedom from time limitations, free education, and access to various sources, while citing financial capabilities and internet problems as causes of inequality. Suggestions included determining learner characteristics, access to technology, improving digital literacy skills, resolving internet infrastructure problems, official budgeting for technology access, and teachers providing consultancy services to students.

The passage presents a lecture on entangled photons. It defines an entangled state as one that cannot be written as a product of two wave functions, while distinguishing true entanglement from an entangled mode involving vacuum or from systems that cannot be physically separated and separately addressed, such as helium’s electrons. Photons are presented as suitable because they can be separated and manipulated; polarization-entangled photons and Bell states are discussed. The lecture describes entanglement purification: from many identical weakly entangled copies, a controlled-NOT operation and measurement can probabilistically produce a Bell state, with success probability related to the initial entanglement. It defines entanglement for pure states as the von Neumann entropy of the reduced density matrix after tracing out one subsystem, noting Bell states have entropy one. Entanglement is described as a resource and as fragile against decoherence. The lecture then discusses difficulties in entangling atoms, a proposed mercury-molecule photodissociation method, and a probabilistic “poor man’s entangler” using photons emitted by atoms. This method uses a beam splitter and Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, plus circular polarizers; detector clicks can indicate polarization states such as H V or V H and can probabilistically entangle atoms.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated August 3, 2017, disclosing that beginning July 1, 2017 it early adopted new accounting standards for revenue recognition and leases. For revenue recognition, Microsoft used the full retrospective method; adoption materially affected consolidated income statements and balance sheets but had no impact on consolidated cash flows. The most significant impact concerned software license revenue, including Windows 10 and certain multi-year commercial software subscriptions, while hardware, cloud offerings such as Office 365 and LinkedIn, and professional services remained substantially unchanged. For leases, Microsoft used a modified retrospective approach; adoption materially affected consolidated balance sheets but not income statements and had no cash flow impact. It recognizes right-of-use assets and lease liabilities for operating leases, while capital lease accounting remains substantially unchanged. Exhibit 99.1 provides restated financial information for fiscal years 2017 and 2016, and a conference call was scheduled for August 3, 2017.

In mid-May 2007, Victor Reinoso had 12 hours to recommend to Mayor Adrian Fenty who should lead Washington, DC Public Schools. Fenty was to take control of DCPS after April 2007 legislation. DCPS had 150 schools, 55,000 students, about 4,000 teachers, and was considered one of the nation’s worst urban systems; it ranked third in per-student spending but first in administrative budget share and last in teachers and instruction. Patronage and high leadership turnover were noted. Reinoso, deputy mayor for education and a former school board member, had concluded the school board was not a path to serious reform and supported mayoral control. During the transition, he built a team, commissioned Parthenon Group data showing DCPS ranked last in reading and math among reviewed systems, declining enrollment, and long-standing pain points. The DC Public Education Reform Act of 2007, drafted largely without outside input, passed after hearings and placed DCPS under the mayor with a chancellor appointed by the mayor and confirmed by the council. In March Reinoso began a chancellor search, seeking an entrepreneurial leader who would rethink public education, did not accept low expectations, and had courage to implement change. Candidates included Rudy Crew, Michelle Rhee, and possibly current superintendent Clifford Janey. A plagiarism incident in early May distracted the process. With his recommendation due, Reinoso needed to choose a leader who would rock the boat but not capsize it.

This work develops quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) methods for estimating expectations of quantities of interest from nonlinear PDE models of tumor growth. It considers a semi-linear parabolic reaction-diffusion PDE with uncertain diffusion and proliferation coefficients modeled as random fields, using finite-dimensional truncation to address high-dimensional integrals and aiming to improve on standard Monte Carlo convergence. The paper establishes well-posedness for the parametric PDE, proves rigorous QMC error estimates for uniform random fields, and confirms them numerically; it also presents numerical results for log-normal random fields on an unstructured domain. A key intermediate result is a parametric regularity bound on solution derivatives, requiring a novel proof for the non-monotone nonlinear term \(u(1-u)\) based on the solution remaining in \([0,1]\) when the initial condition does. The authors state this is the first QMC analysis for a nonlinear PDE apart from eigenvalue problems and do not analyze spatio-temporal discretization error.

This 11/25/01 Commissioner.COM E-Reports email to Paul Lucci includes promotional offers, NFL player news and status updates, and a fantasy matchup breakdown listing Luccis Losers versus Team Chick with both lineups at 0.0 points.

Mesh is an Air Raid play used across offenses because it can produce downfield completions and uses underneath routes against man and zone. It is a short-to-intermediate concept that creates natural picks/confusion, helps receivers stay on the move vs man, and find voids vs zone. It works against man and base cover 2, 3, and 4, but can struggle against zone blitz or simulated pressure. Route coaching points are given for TE, FB, TB, X, and Z against man and zone. The QB progression is flare, shallow drag, deep drag, FB arrow, with the Z corner as a pre-snap option; the progression stays the same against all defensive looks. Variations include mesh rail, with the RB on a rail route and Z on a sit route, and a sit route that answers zone. Bruce Eien also explains mesh as a variation of smash in his single wing offense.

Culp, Inc. held its fiscal 2017 fourth-quarter earnings call. Q4 net sales were $77.4 million, roughly unchanged; pretax income was $7.0 million, including about $250,000 of plant relocation expenses, down 2.3%; net income was $6.2 million, or $0.49 per diluted share. Full-year net sales were $309.5 million, down 1.1%; pretax income was a record $29.7 million; net income was $22.3 million, or $1.78 per diluted share; adjusted EBITDA was $40.1 million, up 7%; return on capital was 32%. Mattress fabrics full-year sales were a record $190.8 million, up 2.4%, with operating income of $29.4 million, up 11%. Upholstery fabrics full-year sales were $118.7 million, down 6%, with operating income of $11.1 million. Cash and investments were $54.2 million, up 29%; cash flow from operations was $33 million and free cash flow was $18 million. The board approved a special dividend of $0.21 per share. The company discussed production consolidations, a Haiti joint venture, hospitality acquisition opportunities, and first-quarter fiscal 2018 guidance of pretax income of $7.8 million to $8.4 million, including about $300,000 in relocation expenses.

Chris Lattner, credited with creating Apple’s Swift, announced on Twitter he is joining Google to work on Google Brain, its artificial intelligence project. He had left Apple for Tesla, led its troubled Autopilot program, and departed after about six months amid conflict with Elon Musk. Google is betting on AI for its cloud division against Amazon Web Services.

This document standardizes the GHCB memory area for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guest-hypervisor communication. The GHCB is a 4 KB decrypted page mapped by the guest, and its format mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area. It defines GHCB protocol versions, hypervisor feature advertisement via a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap, GHCB MSR protocol actions, GHCB GPA registration, and negotiation examples. It lists required Non-Automatic Exits and associated GHCB fields, including MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV Doorbell Page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC backing page, Termination Request, and Unsupported NAE handling. Revisions add support for features such as APIC ID list, multi-VMPL, page state change for SEV-ES, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, VLEK GUID, and 64-bit guest request sequence numbers. The document also addresses guest identification of SEV-ES, SMP booting, NMI handling, debug register support, and states that SMM and nested virtualization are not supported. It further specifies SNP Restricted Injection, #HV doorbell data fields, interrupt shadows, doorbell configuration, and expected host/guest behavior.

The speaker says Scotty will decide when he has had enough of coaching and how much time to devote to hockey and family. The speaker expects him back next year and cites his unmatched passion and energy.

Channel 4 chief executive Alex Mahon called the broadcaster’s 28.6% gender pay gap unacceptable and said she is determined to improve it. She aims for a 50:50 split among its 100 top jobs by 2023. The gap is above the 17.4% national average though 59% of staff are women; she attributed it to a 66% female lower half and only 34 women in the top 100 highest-paid positions. ITN’s gap is 19.6%, and the BBC’s is 10.7%; ITV and Channel 5 have not published details.

The passage describes high-pressure flow control devices such as plug valves and fluid ends used in oil and gas operations. Previously attempted solutions mounted seals to mating components, allowing corrosive and/or abrasive fluid to erode the valve body bore or fluid end body. Embodiments of the technology instead form endless grooves or recesses in the body and mount seals there to seal against components such as inserts, retaining nuts, discharge plugs, suction plugs, valve seats, and stuffing box sleeves. This transfers erosion wear from the body to the less complex and less expensive mating component. The passage also describes related fluid end assemblies with housings, internal chambers, intersecting conduits, plungers, seals, stuffing boxes, and methods of manufacturing.

CTPNet is proposed for multivariate long-term time series forecasting, addressing dependencies across inter-channel, intra-subsequence, and inter-subsequence levels. It consists of Channel-wise Representation Learning, DownSample, an Encoder, Trend-wise Representation Learning, Periodic-wise Representation Learning, a Decoder, and De-Downsample. CRL uses temporal query-based Multi-Head Attention for inter-channel dependencies; TRL uses an efficient attention Transformer for intra-subsequence dependencies; PRL models inter-subsequence dependencies. Residual connections and linear encoding are used. The passage also defines time series forecasting and downsampling preliminaries. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets are reported to demonstrate new state-of-the-art performance and the framework’s robustness and generality.
A 34-year-old Mission man was arrested after a pickup caused collisions at a Maple Ridge strip mall, injuring a woman and son; investigation included impaired driving, hit and run, dangerous driving.

On February 26, 2020, Microsoft Corporation issued a press release updating its revenue guidance for its More Personal Computing segment for the quarter ending March 30, 2020. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 to the Form 8-K.

The speaker says they were disappointed not to score right away after being brought in to score, but believed they were playing well elsewhere despite not appearing on score sheets. They stayed positive, kept working, and thought scoring would come in time. They add that winning matters most, and they would be happiest if the team won even if they did not score again.

The passage examines artificial intelligence, especially generative AI and LLMs, in higher education assessment. It states AI capabilities are rapidly advancing and can create content, provide feedback, and simulate human-like interactions. Concerns include academic integrity, plagiarism, over-reliance, and reduced critical thinking, while opportunities include personalized learning, feedback, and more authentic, diverse assessment. Traditional assessments such as MCQs and essays are challenged by AI, and AI detection tools face accuracy, fairness, and reliability issues. Strategies include avoiding AI, designing AI-resistant tasks, or integrating AI. A UK postgraduate immunology module replaced a traditional essay with an AI-integrated coursework: students received training, used ChatGPT 3.5 to generate a draft outline, peer-evaluated outlines, then completed the final essay without further AI assistance. Surveyed students reported varied AI use and confidence, saw uses in planning, drafting, and summarizing, and identified limitations such as inaccuracy and superficiality, but found the outline useful. The paper concludes AI should be integrated holistically with training, guidance, and AI literacy, while maintaining academic integrity and not replacing educators.

The Supreme Court of Louisiana affirmed Ray Jones, Jr.’s conviction and sentence for first degree murder of his two-and-one-half-month-old son. Jones argued the trial judge improperly admitted inculpatory statements made in the hospital and at the police station, but the court found the hospital statements voluntary and not custodial interrogation, and the police-station statement not interrogation under Miranda or harmless beyond a reasonable doubt. Jones also argued the trial judge improperly restricted cross-examination of Dr. Bienvenue; the court found no abuse of discretion. The conviction and sentence were affirmed.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver said the All-Star Game will remain at the Clippers' Intuit Dome in Los Angeles despite the league's investigation into whether the team circumvented salary cap rules involving Kawhi Leonard and a $28 million endorsement contract with Aspiration. Silver said All-Star planning is operating independently of the investigation. The game is expected to be televised by NBC on Feb. 15 with a new U.S. vs. international format.

Scotland’s Abusive Behaviour and Sexual Harm Act will make disclosing or threatening to disclose intimate photos or videos a criminal offence from April 1, carrying a maximum five-year prison sentence. It covers private images of nudity, underwear, or sexual acts and addresses easier online sharing, the Justice Secretary said.

The description relates to active ground terrain mapping for controlling a mobile agricultural machine. A pose detection sensor generates position and orientation signals along a route, and a point cloud is identified with points estimated to correspond to the ground surface. Elevation values are generated for each point, and in some examples a best-fit plane provides predictive elevation values ahead of the machine. Weight values or confidence may be based on distance from the pose detector, and control signals are generated to control a controllable subsystem, such as a header or boom height actuator, based on the elevation values.

This study examines micro-credentials in higher education, particularly in Mauritius. It defines micro-credentials as certifications of knowledge and skills acquired through specific learning experiences. Literature notes growing interest, employer support, and concerns about reliability, standards, credit mapping, and limited understanding among senior leaders. The study used semi-structured interviews with 10 education leaders from public and private institutions and four industry leaders. Findings show respondents were familiar with micro-credentials but definitions varied; badges were less familiar, and views on their relationship to micro-credentials differed. Most favored a hybrid model integrating micro-credentials with existing credit systems, though implementation was uncertain. Respondents saw value for skills validation, employability, industry responsiveness, lifelong learning, and future higher education, but also raised concerns about recognition, quality, assessment, enrollment, and disruption. They recommended phased implementation, competency-based assessment, reliable standards, mapping to university credits, and integration into the National Qualifications Framework. The conclusion states micro-credentials were not fully understood but broadly considered important, and a unified national framework is recommended so they can contribute to recognized university credits and employer acceptance.

Matthew Shashy, 29, of Montgomery, was sentenced to four years’ probation for discharging a firearm outside Maxwell Air Force Base. After an August 2017 trial, a federal jury found him guilty of impeding, intimidating, and interfering with Air Force personnel. Testimony described his anti-government graffiti and a January 3, 2017 shooting near the Day Street entrance. He later surrendered after barricading himself. The Montgomery Police Department and FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force investigated; Todd A. Brown prosecuted.

Combining 16 weeks of omalizumab with oral immunotherapy (OIT) improved OIT efficacy in children allergic to multiple foods. After 36 weeks, over 80% of children given omalizumab plus OIT could safely eat two-gram portions of at least two allergenic foods, versus one third given placebo plus OIT. The Phase 2 NIAID-funded trial enrolled 48 participants aged 4–15. Omalizumab blocks IgE. Those receiving omalizumab had fewer OIT adverse events during weeks 8–16. Larger studies are needed.

Brookfield recently held an investor day on Brookfield Infrastructure Partners (BIP). BIP is the most successful listed partnership managed by Brookfield Asset Management, with 20% annualized returns since 2008 and Adjusted AFFO rising from $352M in 2012 to $926M. It has a 4% distribution yield and 5.84% AFFO yield, retains 1.84% to grow, and seeks additional funds by selling units. BIP aims to increase distributions 6–9% annually; the author considers this aggressive given low inflation. Past same-store EBITDA growth averaged 5% on a constant-currency basis. BIP historically yielded more, including 5.4% two years ago; lower yield benefits current unitholders if new units are invested above the current AFFO rate, but this depends on unit price. The author concludes future returns may be less strong, though BIP remains attractive with a safe, likely-growing 4% yield and potential ~10% total return.

An archaeological excavation at City Hall in search of a rifle belonging to Willie Halpin from the Easter Rising found no rifle. The search removed debris and recovered other artefacts, including roof fragments, one with a bullet hole, glass milk bottles from the 1930s, a teapot lid, and pottery. Archaeologist Franc Myles said the rifle was likely thrown into the gap but may have been discovered and removed soon after the Rising. The project was pushed by the Halpin family and councillor Nial Ring, who said it was still worth looking.

The passage explains that credit bureaus began with an 1874 blue book, treat regular people as the product and businesses as customers, have grown into massive corporations collecting financial data without opt-in or easy opt-out, and have faced fifty years of regulatory struggle.

A $5.25-million gift was announced at Victoria Hospital for LHSC’s translational ovarian cancer research team. John Knight left the amount from his estate as a tribute to his wife, Mary, who died of ovarian cancer in 2008. The money will help hire researchers, buy equipment and enable worldwide collaborations. A hospital lobby was named the Mary and John Knight atrium.

ETF Channel compared ETF holdings’ trading prices to average analyst 12-month targets. For VOT, the implied target is $145.80 versus a recent $132.83, or 9.77% upside. Underlying holdings ST, GPN, and MKL showed notable upside of 11.37%, 10.34%, and 10.26%, respectively. Whether analysts are justified requires further research.

Tanzania’s government launched the Tanzania Business Clinic (TBC) to speed up improvements to the business climate, following the Cabinet’s adoption of a blueprint for amending laws and regulations. TBC will use business experts and public officials to identify short- and long-term solutions and teach best practices, with headquarters in Dar es Salaam and branches in Sido offices. Implementation is set for 2018/19, after Tanzania ranked 137th in Doing Business 2018.

Several former Facebook executives have expressed second thoughts about products they built. Chamath Palihapitiya feels guilt, saying Facebook's dopamine-driven feedback loops are destroying society globally. Sean Parker echoed concerns about social media's effects. Antonio Garcia-Martinez said Facebook lies about its influence. Palihapitiya believes Facebook does positive good but will focus on structural changes.

Julia Banks, Liberal member for Chisholm, faces questions about dual Greek Australian citizenship. In her multicultural Melbourne eastern suburbs electorate, voters were largely unaware of the controversy; some said they would consider candidates on merit or vote Liberal again, while one Labor voter welcomed damage to the Turnbull government. Monash politics lecturer Zareh Ghazarian said a byelection in the classic marginal seat would likely favour Labor. A senior Labor strategist expressed confidence but expected a tight race. Banks won Chisholm in 2016 after Labor held it for almost 20 years.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says GPT-5 was misunderstood and he changed his attitude to AGI; users/critics cited livestream glitches, an unfriendly model, and unmet expectations.

The passage catalogs on-field non-verbal soccer communications, primarily hand signals, used for set pieces, corner kicks, throw-ins, passing, directing runs, defensive positioning, wall setup, goalkeeper directions, substitution requests, and coach/team-agreed signals. It also notes that coaches and players may need a full set of non-verbal communications when crowd noise prevents oral communication, and invites suggestions for the living document.

The passage describes SD card bus interface modes, initialization, and operations. UHS-I is used in SD mode, not SPI, and adopts 1.8V signaling for SDR50, DDR50, and SDR104 while the host supplies 3.3V and converts signaling. After power cycle, the card starts in 3.3V signaling; CMD0 selects SD or SPI mode, and once 1.8V signaling is entered, the card cannot switch to SPI or 3.3V without a power cycle. ACMD41 checks 1.8V support, CMD11 invokes voltage switching, and successful switching enters UHS-I with default SDR12. UHS-I supports only 4-bit mode except CMD42; CMD6 selects driver strength, bus speed mode, and current/power limit; CMD19 tuning is supported in 1.8V signaling for UHS50 and UHS104 under specified conditions. UHS-II supports legacy SD Bus and UHS-II interfaces; the host detects STB.L on D1 within 200us to start UHS-II initialization, otherwise initializes in SD Bus interface mode. UHS-II initialization includes PHY, device, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN initialization, with CMD0 restarting SD-TRAN initialization. UHS-II modes include FD156, HD312, FD312, and FD624; UHS-III supports Range A to Range D and FD624. The passage also defines card identification and data transfer modes: CMD0 reset, CMD8 voltage verification, ACMD41 initialization with HCS/CCS/S18R/S18A, CMD2 for CID, CMD3 for RCA, CMD7 selection, CMD12 stop, read/write operations, erase, DISCARD, and FULE sequences with error handling. Write protection includes mechanical switch, internal write protection, and password protection via CMD42 with PWD/FEP registers, lock/unlock, Force Erase, FEP Force Erase, and COP functions. ACMD commands are interpreted after CMD55, and CMD6 switches functions in Mode 0 query or Mode 1 set for access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit.

President Ulysses S. Grant proclaimed that illegal military expeditions were being organized in the United States against Canada. He warned citizens and others not to aid or join them, saying participants forfeit government protection, and ordered U.S. officers to prevent such acts and arrest those involved.

An 11-year-old boy was attacked by a relative's dog on June 20, suffered threatening injuries, and had major facial skin-graft surgery to recreate his lips; more surgery and possible tattooing are planned.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Blackwell GPU architecture and related features. It introduces the AI Management Processor (AMP), a fully programmable GPU context scheduler implemented with a dedicated RISC-V processor at the front of the GPU pipeline that offloads GPU context scheduling from the system CPU, provides lower-latency scheduling, and aligns with Microsoft HAGS. Blackwell adds 4:2:2 H.264/HEVC hardware encode/decode, ninth-generation NVENC with AV1/HEVC quality improvements and AV1 UHQ, sixth-generation NVDEC, and DisplayPort 2.1b up to 80 Gbps. Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating, separate voltage rails, accelerated frequency switching, and low-latency sleep, with up to 50% power savings in an SLM inference example. DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation up to three additional frames per rendered frame, a faster/lower-VRAM frame generation model, enhanced Flip Metering, and transformer models for SR, RR, and DLAA. Neural shaders are enabled via Cooperative Vectors API and include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. The document also lists Blackwell GPUs GB202, GB203, and GB205 and GeForce RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070 specifications.

The May 22, 2001 VentureWire newsletter reports top stories: Kodiak Venture Partners closed Fund II with $290M; Mercury Interactive acquired Freshwater Software for $147M in cash; Celetron International raised a $48M first round; and TVM announced a first close on its life science fund. It also lists new funding rounds for many companies, bad news including staff cuts at AgWeb and Ironmax and Rx.com ceasing prescription operations, new products and name changes, M&A transactions, new directors and executives, VC fund and personnel news, and corrections.

This study reports a Phase 2/3 observer-blind, randomized, controlled evaluation of SII-NVX-CoV2373 in Indian children and adolescents aged 2–17 years. Participants received two doses of vaccine or placebo on days 1 and 22. The vaccine was found safe and well tolerated; no AESI or causally related SAE was reported, and most solicited AEs were mild and resolved. SII-NVX-CoV2373 demonstrated non-inferior anti-S IgG and neutralizing antibody responses compared with Indian adults, with higher titers in pediatric groups and higher titers in children aged 2–11 than in adolescents aged 12–17. Seroconversion after the second dose exceeded 98%, with antibody responses also observed against Delta, Omicron BA.1, and Omicron BA.5; titers declined by day 180 but remained above baseline. The authors conclude SII-NVX-CoV2373 may be used in pediatric COVID-19 vaccination.

Mud Bay, a 45-store Pacific Northwest pet chain, introduced an ESOP in 2015 and pursued a “Good Jobs Vision” to create good jobs and a strong customer experience. At Mudstock in May 2018, co-CEO Marisa Wulff discussed financials: strong sales and customer affection, but net profit margins fell from 2.18% in 2014 to 1.99% in 2017. COO Tracy Yamane proposed closing stores an hour earlier to improve employee schedules and save labor; Marisa supported it, while co-CEO Lars opposed it. The case describes the pet store industry, Mud Bay’s history, its 2014 operations, customer experience, and employee experience. In 2014, the executive team developed a Good Jobs Vision with five strategies: invest in staff; offer less at everyday low prices; standardize processes and empower staff through continuous improvement; improve efficiency through cross-training and slack; and partner with animal welfare organizations. From 2014 to 2017, Mud Bay raised wages, increased medical insurance eligibility, launched an ESOP and EAP, changed training, reduced SKUs, lowered prices, created category teams, standardized some processes, and partnered with animal organizations. Sales grew 70% and same-store sales averaged above 9%, turnover fell from 48% to 31%, and employees owned 4.8% of the company. Profit margins declined, and some initiatives lagged. In 2018, the planning team reviewed an analysis of store sales by half hour to decide whether to close stores at 8:00 pm Monday through Saturday.

The passage discusses distance education definitions and Moore’s Theory of Transactional Distance, then reports a qualitative study on education students’ and lecturers’ experiences of Physical Education teacher training in distance mode at North-West University. Participants were 17 third-year B.Ed. Life Orientation FET distance students and four lecturers teaching Physical Education modules. Data were collected through open-ended student questionnaires and semi-structured lecturer interviews and analyzed inductively. Five themes emerged: interaction between students and lecturers; competence, passion and enthusiasm to teach Physical Education; obstacles in distance learning; experiences of practical training; and the influence of program content on perceptions of Physical Education. Lecturers were described as available and responsive via email/WhatsApp, though lack of physical contact was negative. Lecturers reported passion for Physical Education, and students reported increased competence and confidence. Obstacles included limited background knowledge, technological illiteracy and limited internet access, and assignment administration deficiencies. Videos were viewed positively for practical skills, but delayed feedback was negative; some students were aware of practical difficulties when enrolling. Many found course content interesting, and some changed their views of Physical Education’s value. Recommendations included additional lecturer-student face-to-face contact, technological training, improved video/media use, increased interaction functions in learning management systems, and sufficient management and administration systems.

Rieva Lesonsky explains that document management affects every business, and poor document management costs time, money, customers, storage space, and printer supplies, and can expose sensitive documents. A Xerox survey found 40% of business processes are still document driven; better document management’s biggest benefit is improved workflow, with growth and productivity as primary reasons for improvement. The first step is tracking printing costs; 97% of surveyed businesses know their print costs, and 81% plan to implement better document management. Xerox ConnectKey technology supports scanning to cloud services, email, DocuShare, and Office tools; CapturePoint imports scans into apps; Mobile Link supports scanning, faxing, and cloud storage. PIN printing, color restrictions, and toner notifications can help.

A passport states that the person named is a U.S. citizen, and by law it may be issued only to citizens. The Secretary of State and diplomatic/consular officers may issue passports under presidential rules; issuance is general for law-abiding applicants but not obligatory, and rejection does not itself deny citizenship. Applicants must establish citizenship, U.S. domicile, and intent to return to reside and perform citizenship duties; expatriates cannot receive passports. Expatriation is defined as quitting one’s country, abandoning allegiance, and becoming permanently resident/citizen elsewhere. Residence abroad for health, education, amusement, business, or an indefinite period with bona fide intent to return is not expatriation, but permanent withdrawal, foreign political domicile, and avowed nonreturn may create a presumption of expatriation. No legislative definition exists; each case depends on circumstances. Permanent foreign domicile bars a passport even without established expatriation. Adult settlement abroad carries new national character, with a presumption of remaining abroad. Factors such as severed ties, foreign marriage/home/business adversely influence issuance; continued family/property ties, health, financial exigencies, or representation of American enterprises may favor it. Special rules apply in semi-barbarous or extraterritorial countries, including Turkey.

A city court reserved for tomorrow its order on Shashi Tharoor’s anticipatory bail plea in the case relating to his wife Sunanda Pushkar’s death. Tharoor, summoned as an accused for July 7, moved the plea after the chargesheet named him as the only accused under IPC sections 498A and 306; he has not been arrested. Delhi Police opposed the plea, citing possible flight and witness influence, while his counsel disputed this.

Matt Barbet launched the Home Roads podcast, available on iTunes and Acast from June 8. It features him cycling and talking with professional cyclists and other figures about their sport, past, and personal lives. Initial episodes include Alex Dowsett, Sarah Storey, Nicolas Roche, and David Millar, with more recorded featuring Ben Saunders, Simon Warren, Simon Mottram, and Philippa York.

The passage describes the 200-day moving average as a technical indicator averaging an asset’s price over 200 trading days to smooth short-term fluctuations and identify trends; price above it indicates an uptrend, below indicates a downtrend. Its advantages are simplicity, trend-riding, and defense, mainly by keeping investors out of bear markets, as illustrated by the S&P 500 in 2007–09 and oil in 2020. Without recessions or falling prices, it is unlikely to beat buy-and-hold because of whipsaws. Backtests show the 200-day SMA on the S&P 500 since 1960 roughly tracked the index with lower drawdowns, while from March 2009 it underperformed buy-and-hold. Jeremy Siegel’s 1% band version on the DJIA from 1886–2006 improved absolute and risk-adjusted returns before costs; after costs, risk-adjusted returns remained higher but absolute return fell short. The passage also notes many false signals, a low win ratio, and Paul Tudor Jones’s use of the rule as defense.

NVIDIA A100 improves on V100 with a 5-site HBM2 subsystem delivering 1555 GB/sec, over 1.7x V100 bandwidth, and 2.3x L2 cache read bandwidth. It has a 40 MB L2 cache (~7x V100) with cache management controls to minimize writebacks and redundant DRAM traffic; Compute Data Compression saves up to 4x DRAM read/write bandwidth and up to 4x L2 read, improving DRAM bandwidth, L2 bandwidth, and L2 capacity. A100 supports Compute Capability 8.0.

MIG partitions an A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated SMs, L2 cache, memory controllers, and DRAM paths for QoS and fault isolation. GPU Instances are built from GPU slices; Compute Instances configure compute resources and support simultaneous contexts and Volta-style MPS. MIG supports multi-tenant and other use cases and vGPU migration.

Third-generation NVLink has 50 Gbit/sec per signal pair, twelve links, and 600 GB/sec total per A100 vs. 300 GB/sec for V100. A100 supports PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, and enhanced error/fault detection, isolation, and containment. Additional features include NVJPG JPEG decode, Optical Flow Accelerator, improved FP16/FP32 atomics, and five NVDEC units.

CUDA 11 supports Third-Generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, and L2 cache residency controls. Task Graphs reduce launch overhead; async copy moves data global-to-shared; asynchronous barriers improve synchronization; L2 residency control sets aside L2 in 1/16th increments (2.5 MB) and is disabled in MIG; Cooperative Groups add collectives and reductions. DGX A100 is a purpose-built AI system delivering 5 PFLOPS and up to 56 isolated accelerators via MIG. The appendix covers sparse neural networks, pruning, fine-grained and coarse-grained sparsity, and A100’s fine-grained structured 2:4 sparsity.

The lecture discusses hinged dissections, noting there is no general software and suggesting projects to animate them and implement slender adorned chains. It references Greg Frederickson’s hinged-dissection examples and books, including twist and surface hinging. The passage outlines hinged dissections for polyominoes, polyhexes, polyiamonds, and polyabolos via induction using dual graphs, spanning trees, leaf removal, and cyclic hinged constructions; slender triangles can enable continuous motions. It also discusses DNA origami and chain-folding/reconfigurable robots, including MIT Center for Bits and Atoms examples. For rectangle-to-rectangle conversion, it describes an old dissection credited to Montucla and Frederickson’s diagrams. It sketches a pseudopolynomial bound for grid polygons using gadgets, hinge-moving, and pseudocuts. In 3D, equal volume is insufficient; Hilbert’s third problem asks whether equal-volume tetrahedra can be dissected. Dehn’s invariant is necessary, Sidler showed volume plus Dehn invariant is sufficient, 4D has an analogous result, 5D and higher are open, and deciding matching Dehn invariants is decidable but good algorithms remain open.

Researchers found New Caledonian crows and kea parrots, after exploring blocks and ropes of different colors, weights, and patterns, were better at selecting correct tools for tasks. The birds appeared to learn object properties incidentally through exploration, without reinforcement, but showed no evidence of changing interactions after learning objects could be tools. The team suggests testing other species may clarify play, exploration, and tool use.

The passage specifies GHCB protocol requirements for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guest-hypervisor communication. NAE events are exit events that are not AE events; for an SEV-ES guest, hardware throws #VC with an error code equal to the VMEXIT code, and the guest inspects the error code, copies required state to the GHCB, and invokes VMGEXIT to generate an AE event. The guest resumes after VMRUN at the instruction following VMGEXIT. The hypervisor must handle VMGEXIT for listed NAE events, and the guest must handle #VC for all listed NAE events. GHCB fields must have corresponding VALID_BITMAP bits set, with minimum requirements for SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2. The passage covers supported NAE events including IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV Doorbell Page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, Run VMPL, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, Termination Request, and Unsupported Non-Automatic Exits. It also describes error reporting through SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2, page state change error handling, SNP guest request data pages, AP boot and AP jump table handling, guest identification of SEV-ES support, NMI handling, debug register virtualization, and #HV doorbell page interrupt and EOI behavior. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP.

Joan Jordan, 45, an Irish software engineer, was diagnosed with MS in 2010 after becoming paralysed down one side. She faced repeated job rejections and stopped working. She now works 15 hours a week with Eupati, has relapse-remitting MS, and wrote “huManS Multiple Sclerosis”. To mark World MS Day, she is speaking at Trinity College as MS Ireland launches a report on MS research.

The application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 16/192,068 by Morgan et al., titled “ADDRESS OBFUSCATION FOR MEMORY,” filed Nov. 15, 2018. The passage relates to memory devices and address obfuscation. It describes wear-leveling, malicious attacks, and reverse-engineering of data movement patterns. Address obfuscation maps logical addresses for data to physical addresses within memory arrays in an unpredictable manner, and mapping functions may vary across devices, dice, arrays, or over time. Mapping functions may be selectable or customizable and may use per-bit logic operations such as inversion, pass-through, XOR, XNOR, or address swap. A memory device may receive an access command including a logical address, determine a physical address based on the logical address and a selected mapping function, and access stored data. Mapping function selection may be based on a random number, unique identifier, schedule, trigger event, or security key. The passage also describes selection components, mapping components, mapping subcomponents, wear-leveling, tables, system diagrams, block diagrams, and flow diagrams.

This passage is a SanDisk Sansa Fuze user manual covering safety and cleaning instructions, hearing safety, disposal, product overview and features, controls, battery charging, connecting to a computer, firmware updates, formatting, transferring and playing music, photos, and videos, FM radio, voice recording, deleting content, settings, troubleshooting, service, warranty, and software license terms.
Jebel Misma camel engravings reveal early humans in once-verdant Nefud 12,000 years ago.

The passage argues that K-12 education’s emphasis on “skills,” critical thinking, mindset, and metacognition devalues actual knowledge. It contends skills cannot substitute for knowledge, citing examples like cricket terms and string theory, and that broad background knowledge is necessary for strong reading and complex thought. It identifies reasons for knowledge’s devaluation, including equating knowledge with memorization and the belief that the internet makes learning unnecessary. It cites grade inflation, reduced graduation testing, and NAEP trends as evidence of a retreat from knowledge, while noting high-quality instructional materials as a counter-push threatened by AI misuse. It concludes knowledge is essential and children enjoy absorbing it if provided.

Using data from the 2021 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey, this study examined socio-demographic factors associated with insecticide-treated net (ITN) ownership and use among children under 5 years and pregnant women in Nigeria. The survey covered 13,727 households and 14,476 women aged 15–49. Descriptive analysis, chi-square tests, and odds ratios were used. Results showed that 56% of households owned at least one ITN, while 25% owned enough if one ITN were shared by two people. ITN ownership was significantly associated with residence, geopolitical zone, and household wealth quintile. Among children under 5, 41.4% slept under an ITN; use was significantly associated with age, residence, geopolitical zone, and wealth quintile, but not sex. About half of pregnant women used an ITN, with significant associations at the bivariate level for geopolitical zone and wealth quintile, and at the multivariate level for geopolitical zone, education, and wealth quintile. The passage concludes that progress has been made but ITN use remains below the 80% NMSP target, with regional and socioeconomic disparities requiring monitoring, expanded distribution, access to healthcare, and health education.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended May 1, 2022 reports revenue of $8.288 billion, net income of $1.618 billion, and diluted net income per share of $0.64, compared with revenue of $5.661 billion, net income of $1.912 billion, and diluted net income per share of $0.76 for the quarter ended May 2, 2021. Operating expenses included a $1.353 billion acquisition termination cost related to the terminated Arm Share Purchase Agreement. Graphics segment revenue was $4.616 billion and Compute & Networking revenue was $3.672 billion. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $20.338 billion. The company repurchased $2.00 billion of stock and paid $100 million in dividends; the board later increased and extended the repurchase program up to $15 billion through December 2023. The filing also discusses segment results, supply and demand risks, cryptocurrency mining impacts, COVID-19 and Ukraine effects, legal proceedings, an SEC settlement with a $5.5 million civil penalty, and effective disclosure controls.

Mario Batali is taking a leave of absence from his businesses after Eater reported misconduct accusations by a female chef and three women who worked for him; he apologized, said the behavior matched his past actions, and was removed from “The Chew.”

HMD Global’s promise to share Nokia 8 kernel modifications with the open-source community remains unfulfilled after 136 days. Withholding Android kernel modifications violates GPLv2 and has drawn criticism, though the Nokia 8 bootloader will not be unlocked for security reasons.

Researchers report that some seafloor fossils from Newfoundland, about 560 million years old and once considered pseudofossils or decomposed organic matter, may be spongelike animals. The 39 analyzed fossils show pores and fingerlike tubes, suggesting a filter feeder up to almost 53 centimeters long. Named after punk rocker John Lydon due to its spiky appearance, the creature resembles a sponge and may be an ancestor of some modern sponges.

Scientists at The University of Queensland found that Black, Western Green, and Jameson’s mamba venoms launch a dual neurological attack: first causing flaccid paralysis through postsynaptic neurotoxicity, then causing spastic paralysis through presynaptic toxicity after antivenom treatment. This explains why some patients improve and then develop painful spasms. The finding complicates treatment because venom function varies by geographic location, particularly in Black Mambas from Kenya and South Africa. Researchers say specialized antivenoms could improve efficacy. Mamba bites account for 30,000 deaths annually in sub-Saharan Africa.

This systematic review examines AI applications in higher education assessment, grading, and feedback. It uses the TPACK framework and reviews peer-reviewed literature from 2010–2023, searching databases including PubMed, Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, ERIC, and Scopus. Twenty studies met inclusion criteria. The review reports that AI can automate and standardize assessments, handle large volumes, reduce grading workload, and provide efficiency, consistency, and rapid feedback; automated grading systems showed comparable accuracy to human graders in STEM/objective assessments. AI can also provide personalized, real-time feedback, adaptive learning pathways, and progress tracking, supporting engagement and self-regulated learning. Challenges include data privacy, algorithmic transparency, bias, potential reinforcement of inequalities, and limited validity/reliability for subjective constructs such as critical thinking, creativity, and qualitative responses. It also notes concerns about educator and student adoption, infrastructure, training, and ethical governance. The review discusses applications globally, in Africa, and in Zambia, where adoption is nascent. It concludes that AI has transformative potential but requires ethical use, rigorous algorithm design, diverse training data, transparent policies, pedagogical alignment, professional development, and collaboration among stakeholders.
The speaker interpreted cheering as support for their effort before Detroit. They are not a defensive coach, know the players, and react to their tendencies once the puck reaches them.

Ray Lewis, Brian Urlacher and Randy Moss were first-ballot Hall of Famers; Terrell Owens and Brian Dawkins were voted in, along with Bobby Beathard, Jerry Kramer and Robert Brazile.

In April 2010, Transocean’s Deepwater Horizon rig, leased by BP to work the Macondo well in the Gulf of Mexico, exploded. Of 126 aboard, 17 were injured and 11 killed. The rig burned for 36 hours and sank on April 22. The well was capped on July 15, after nearly five million barrels spilled, making it the largest marine oil spill in U.S. waters at the time. BP had publicly emphasized safety, but before the disaster it had faced the Texas City refinery explosion and Prudhoe Bay oil spill. The Baker Report found cost cuts and weak process-safety messages at BP, and BP’s asset federation model gave site managers autonomy with little incentive to share risk-management practices. The Macondo well was 52 miles south of Venice, Louisiana, nearly 5,000 feet below sea level, with high natural gas levels. BP held rights to the prospect, was principal developer and operator with a 65% financial share, and leased the Deepwater Horizon from Transocean. The rig had numerous maintenance issues, alarms had been disabled, and the project was over budget. In closing the well, key decisions involved using long string casing instead of a liner/tieback, using fewer centralizers despite Halliburton/OptiCem warnings of severe gas flow potential, and not running a cement bond log despite having Schlumberger workers available. The passage also cites partial mud circulation and failure to deploy a lockdown sleeve. Investigations and a congressional letter questioned whether BP chose risky procedures to reduce costs and save time. The disaster caused environmental and economic damage, a deepwater drilling moratorium, and BP’s establishment of a $20 billion Gulf Coast Claims Facility. Investigations were ongoing, and the passage states the decisions came down on the side of cost-reduction and expediency over caution.

During Best Buy's Techtober sales event, WIRED found an Acer Swift 16 AI discounted $450 to $800. It has 16 GB RAM, 1 TB storage, a 16-inch 2,880 x 1,800 120-Hz OLED screen, an Intel Core Ultra 7 256V CPU, and 13 hours of YouTube playback. It is 0.79 inches thick. A Lenovo Yoga Slim 7i Aura Edition at $900 offers similar specs, a 15.3-inch screen, and a 0.55-inch chassis. Techtober runs through October 12.

This lecture covers limited attention. It reviews preferences and then focuses on attention, beliefs, and learning. Evidence includes change blindness, dichotic listening, and factors such as physical environment, distractions, worries, sleep, and poverty that may affect attention. High-stakes examples include stock market reactions to EntreMed cancer news and confusion between two companies named Zoom. The Chetty et al. paper studies inattention to taxes: sales taxes are less salient than other price changes, and making sales taxes salient in grocery stores reduced demand by 8.8%, implying consumers react to sales-tax price changes only about a quarter as much as to other price changes. Non-experimental beer data show almost no reaction to sales taxes relative to excise taxes. The lecture then discusses the paper “learning by noticing,” using seaweed farming in Indonesia. Farmers neglected pod size even though they knew other dimensions. Experimental variation alone had insignificant effects, but summarized information changed farming behavior, suggesting systematic learning failures and potentially large welfare losses from inattention.

Documents concern Korea: the Department disapproved Mr. Allen’s request that the U.S. consul-general at Shanghai seek surrender of Kim Ok-kiun’s murderer, since U.S. jurisdiction extended only to U.S. citizens. Mr. Sill reported a growing rebellion, a government defeat near Chon-ju, rebel capture of Chon-ju, and requested a ship at Chemulpo to protect Americans; British, French, Chinese, and Japanese vessels had been sent there. Mr. Denby confirmed China was sending 1,500 troops, to be increased to 2,225, plus warships to Chemulpo at Korea’s request, with assurances of withdrawal after hostilities and willingness for Japan to send gunboats.

An email dated Jan. 19, 2001 from Ann Schmidt to Enron recipients, titled “Enron Mentions,” lists news articles and includes their texts. The articles cover California’s power crisis: PG&E and Southern California Edison face more than $11.5 billion in power-related debt, defaults, and possible bankruptcy; Governor Davis declared a state of emergency; the legislature approved $400 million to buy power; regulators blocked service cuts; and Energy Secretary Richardson ordered power and natural-gas suppliers to sell into California. Articles also discuss rating downgrades, investor reassessment of utilities, natural gas and gasoline supply concerns, and Bush adviser Ken Lay’s opposition to Western wholesale power price caps. Other items announce EOTT Energy Partners’ quarterly cash distribution; expansion of the Dow Jones bandwidth price table and Aquila Broadband as a market maker; Pennsylvania PUC criticism of GPU Energy for comparing its situation to California; and a ten-year Enron Energy Services–Owens-Illinois energy management agreement covering 53 facilities in 20 states with projected energy purchases over $2 billion.

The speaker, on his induction into the Presidency, states that the only thing to fear is fear itself and calls for frank, bold leadership. He describes material hardships: shrinking values, higher taxes, reduced incomes, frozen exchange, industrial decline, lost farm markets and savings, unemployment, and little return for work. He says distress is not due to lack of substance; those controlling exchange have failed, and public opinion rejects unscrupulous money changers. He calls for restoring social values above monetary profit and valuing work and achievement. The primary task is to put people to work through government recruiting and needed projects, redistribution of population, aid to agriculture, preventing foreclosures, reducing government costs, unifying relief, and planning transportation, communications, and utilities. He urges supervision of banking, credit, and investments and an adequate, sound currency. He will ask Congress and states for action; international trade is secondary to a sound national economy. He advocates a good-neighbor world policy, interdependence, discipline, and possible temporary departure from the normal balance of powers, including broad executive power if Congress fails. He affirms faith in democracy and asks God’s blessing.

The passage compiles @ThingsExpo blog posts and articles from Jan. 1–2, 2017. It reports Onalytica rankings naming @ThingsExpo a Top 5 Most Influential Internet of Things Brand and M2M Brand, and later the Number One M2M Brand, with @GonzalezCarmen ranked Number One Influencer. Other entries discuss IoT-connected devices, WebRTC identity management, IoT data platforms, data monetization, blockchain, Microsoft, Scrum, Adobe digital marketing, and @ThingsExpo New York 2017.

The MACD and RSI strategy uses both momentum indicators to analyze and trade markets. MACD is a moving average-based momentum oscillator primarily used to analyze trends, calculated from 12- and 26-period EMAs with a 9-period signal line. RSI is a momentum oscillator ranging from 0 to 100, traditionally used to identify overbought above 70 and oversold below 30 conditions. The two can be combined in different ways, such as using MACD for trend direction and RSI for price swings or confirmations. Example rules include buying when MACD rises above its signal line and RSI rises after being oversold, and selling on the opposite signal. The passage says traders should make rules and backtest. It describes a backtested strategy using MACD, RSI, and a third mean reversion filter, buying when all three conditions are met and selling when the filter reverses. It says the strategy worked best for semis, with 235 trades on SMH, average gain per trade of 0.88% including commissions and slippage, and a 73% win rate. The passage notes opinions differ on whether the combination is useful or redundant, and which indicator is more accurate depends on backtesting, parameters, markets, and scenarios.

President Donald Trump has made major policy reversals, most recently when a U.S. Treasury report did not name China a currency manipulator despite his promises. One analyst hopes Trump will reverse his January withdrawal from the Trans-Pacific Partnership, noting the treaty text remains valid until February 2018 and other members might offer concessions.

The flexbone is a run-heavy offensive system evolved from the wishbone, known for option plays and misdirection. It moves two A-backs closer to the line to present a pass threat. It requires a decisive running quarterback who can hit play-action passes; a strong, athletic B-back; quick A-backs who can block, run, catch, and align at receiver; blocking wide receivers; and athletic, aggressive offensive linemen skilled at cut and combo blocks and rules. Its strengths include uniqueness, preparation difficulty for defenses, ball control, time of possession, multiple run threats, assignment confusion, physical wear on opponents, and exploiting poor tackling. Weaknesses include limited high-volume passing, difficulty coming back or running a two-minute drill, extensive practice time, and struggles in bad weather due to timing and ball security. Common formations include double slot, trips, and receivers over. Common runs include triple option, midline option, and rocket toss. Common passes include play-action wheel, toss boot, and 4 verts. The service academies Navy, Army, and Air Force have run flexbone triple option; Paul Johnson ran it at Georgia Southern, Navy, and Georgia Tech; Harding won Division 2 in 2023; it remains common at the high school level, especially smaller schools.

Mississippi State (8-0), in its first road game, faces Cincinnati (7-2) Tuesday at 6 p.m. on ESPN2 at BB&T Arena in Newport, Kentucky. Cincinnati lost to Florida and is No. 25 in the AP poll.
