In Germany, the Protestant church is marking 500 years since Martin Luther brought about the Reformation. As churchgoers dwindle, clergy are using new media to reach people. In Magdeburg, a Twitter service encourages congregants to tweet about the liturgy and share prayers online, with a screen displaying a hashtagged feed. Pastor Ralf Peter Reimann says social media can help retain and gain followers. The passage compares Luther’s use of pamphlets to Twitter today. Some users share prayers or encouragement, while others find the service too hectic; one elderly attendee prefers a traditional service with hymns.

NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture introduces third-generation Tensor Cores and features for AI and HPC. For deep learning training, TF32 Tensor Cores are used by default with no script adjustment, delivering up to 8x FP32 throughput on A100 and up to 10x on V100; FP16 or BF16 mixed precision is recommended for maximum training speed, up to 2x TF32 and up to 16x FP32 on A100 and up to 20x on V100. For HPC, A100 accelerates IEEE-compliant FP64 computations with up to 2.5x V100 FP64 performance and 19.5 TFLOPS peak FP64 throughput. Mixed-precision Tensor Cores support iterative refinement, and cuSOLVER TCAIRS supports TF32, FP16, BF16, and FP64 Tensor Cores; TF32 is described as fastest and most robust compared with other Tensor Core modes. A100 adds Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity using 2:4 patterns, doubling Tensor Core compute throughput and reducing data footprint, with a recipe of dense training, pruning, and fine-tuning. Other features include combined 192 KB L1/shared memory per SM, simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, 40 GB HBM2 with 1555 GB/s bandwidth and SECDED ECC, 40 MB L2 cache, L2 residency controls, compute data compression, asynchronous copy and barriers, and CUDA task graphs. MIG can partition each A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances with isolated memory paths, L2, memory controllers, and DRAM for QoS and fault isolation. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/s total bandwidth, and PCIe Gen 4 and SR-IOV are supported. Additional features include NVJPG decode, an optical flow accelerator, improved atomics, and five NVDEC units. CUDA 11 adds support for Tensor Cores, sparsity, MIG, L2 controls, async copy, barriers, and cooperative groups. DGX A100 uses eight A100 GPUs, delivers up to 5 PFLOPS, and MIG can provide up to 56 discrete accelerators. Appendix B discusses pruning, fine-grained and coarse-grained sparsity, and fine-grained structured sparsity.

The Larry Swedroe Portfolio is a diversified, evidence-based portfolio allocating 30% to stocks and 70% to bonds, designed for long-term growth while minimizing risk. It typically includes domestic and international stocks, small-cap value, emerging markets, and bonds, implemented through low-cost index funds or ETFs and rebalanced periodically. Swedroe favors value and small-cap value investing through bottom-up analysis of companies with strong fundamentals. The strategy avoids market timing and active management and targets long-term investors. A backtest since 2012 showed a 3.71% annual return, while the portfolio presumably had a 6.28% compound annual return over 30 years, with lower returns than stocks due to its large bond allocation.

Warren Buffett’s 2011 letter favored buying Berkshire stock below intrinsic value. Berkshire announced repurchases up to 110% of book value in 2011, buying only $67 million. The limit rose to 120% in 2012, allowing about $1.3 billion of repurchases; none occurred from 2013–2016, though the threshold was nearly reached in early 2013, 2014, and 2016. The author argues the steady 120% limit is increasingly conservative because book value lags intrinsic value, and notes Buffett reiterated it in 2016. Disclosure: the author is long BRK.B.

European stocks were set for their biggest weekly loss since Nov 2016, with the STOXX 600 down around 1.7-1.8% for the week amid rising bond yields and a stronger euro. Banking results weighed, as Deutsche Bank reported a bigger-than-expected 2017 net loss, while Caixabank and Sabadell results were seen as disappointing. Germany’s DAX fell more than 5% in eight sessions and turned negative year-to-date. Investors watched U.S. payrolls data and tech earnings, and Bank of America Merrill Lynch’s Bull & Bear indicator hit a “Sell” signal.

Danny Langston appealed a summary judgment favoring Personal Service Insurance Company and George Johnson, Jr. Langston was injured in Florida while a passenger in a vehicle operated by Fred Johnson and owned by George Johnson, Jr., the principal on an Ohio surety bond issued by Personal Service. The appellate court reversed, holding that under Florida tort law George Johnson, Jr. could be personally liable as owner. Applying Ohio law to the bond, the court found Personal Service could be liable for a final judgment against the principal for damages resulting from ownership, maintenance, or use of a motor vehicle. Kerr was distinguishable because the accident there occurred in Ohio; Thornton addressed only bond limits. The cause was remanded.

The paper focuses on arts education and the competencies of pre-service primary teachers in an Australian university teacher education programme. It uses education policy sociology theory, drawing on Ball’s three contexts of policy-making—influence, policy text production, and policy practice—and critical discourse analysis to examine how the university addressed gaps in primary pre-service teachers’ arts education competencies through an Arts Specialism. The literature reviewed indicates limited curriculum time and inadequate arts training despite policy recognition of arts education. The Arts Specialism, introduced in 2019, follows a compulsory foundation arts course and consists of four courses covering dance, drama, media arts, music, and visual arts. It was developed with university educators, leaders, policymakers, organisations, community members, and professional arts education bodies. Course content includes Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander arts, digital technologies, experiential learning, and school-based projects. Findings report positive PST feedback and 600 total hours across four courses, while noting challenges including time constraints, resource allocation, staffing, assessment coordination, and COVID-19 disruptions. The paper concludes that the Arts Specialism offers a model for bridging policy and practice in primary arts teacher education, though challenges remain, and identifies opportunities for expansion and further research.

Tales have long circulated about children raised by animals, though many are apocryphal or hoaxes. Some accounts persist. In 1644 Sir Kenelm Digby mentioned Jean de Liège, who lived in the woods about sixteen years, reportedly had sharpened senses, was hair-covered, and could not speak but later learned. His hair growth is unlikely and may reflect hypertrichosis. Nicholas Tulp in 1672 described an Irish sheep-boy brought to Amsterdam who behaved like a sheep, bleated, and ate grass and hay. A U.S. legend tells of a Wolf Girl near Devil’s River in the early nineteenth century who was captured, escaped, vanished for seven years, was seen with pups, and never seen again. The passage asks whether such “humanimals” still exist.

A free five-week self-management course for people with chronic pain will start in Montrose in May, delivered by Pain Association Scotland for Angus Health and Social Care Partnership. It includes an introductory session and four weekly two-and-a-half-hour sessions on topics such as understanding pain, stress, pacing, flare-ups, relaxation and medication. It aims to improve coping and quality of life. It is open to Angus residents aged 18 or over; contact details are provided for information and booking.

The passage specifies that to inject an NMI, the hypervisor must not intercept IRET but must intercept #DB, and must use the guest’s “NMI Complete” message to determine when another NMI can be injected; the guest must send this only when it can safely handle another NMI. It gives an example where the NMI handler sets a per-CPU variable and TF before IRET, and a #VC handler checks the #DB intercept error code and variable, clears it, and issues “NMI Complete” via VMGEXIT. Debug-register virtualization for SEV-ES requires the DebugVirtualization bit and hardware saving/restoring debug state, with all debug-register intercepts cleared; otherwise DR7 reads and writes must be intercepted, with writes cached and reads returned from cache. SMM is not supported in this version, and nested virtualization is not supported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP.

For SNP isolation, guests are expected to run with RestrictInjection, limiting the host to a #HV doorbell. The shared doorbell page defines PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired, with PendingEvent indicating non-maskable events, an interrupt vector, and NoFurtherSignal; NoEoiRequired supports EOI assist. The page is host-owned, guest accesses use C=0, and configuration uses VMGEXIT requests such as SET and QUERY. Interrupt-shadow handling requires guests to execute HLT with interrupts disabled and re-examine interrupt state on resume. The host emulates APIC interrupt presentation, acknowledgement, in-service, and EOI semantics through the doorbell fields, while guests must atomically exchange pending events, validate vectors, handle non-maskable events, and perform EOI explicitly or by clearing NoEoiRequired. Non-cooperative host or guest behavior can cause denial of service or lost #HV notification but not host integrity.

Buying an iPhone involves tradeoffs against Android features, but the passage says security is a key reason Apple users accept them. For iOS 10.3.1, it describes data encryption via password, PIN, and thumbprint; prompts for two-factor authentication; automatic data erasure after ten failed logins; and secure iCloud backups. It says iOS devices are not immune to malware but include built-in anti-malware, updates, and an exclusive app store, unlike Android devices that rely on third-party antivirus. Find My Phone uses iCloud to locate, lock, or erase a stolen device. Apps must get user permission for data access, and Apple is said to restrict permissions better than Android. The passage cites 375 publicly disclosed iOS vulnerabilities in 2015 versus 130 for Android and notes iOS devices receive patches while Android is fragmented. It attributes Android security difficulty to multiple hardware and software versions, while Apple retains exclusivity.

The NAHB/Wells Fargo builder sentiment index slipped to 68 in April from 71 in March, below analysts’ expected 70, with current sales, buyer traffic, and six-month sales outlook also lower. Despite this, new U.S. home sales have been robust and are expected to keep climbing, supported by low mortgage rates and a solid job market.

The passage covers last shot situations in basketball, noting that a single shot can determine winning, losing, and playoff hopes. It explains why and when to hold for the last shot, timing, strategy, and guidelines. Holding for the last shot of a period can combine with the first possessions of the next period to create a 4- to 6-point swing, or a 12-point fluctuation, with more if fouled. It provides timing rules, including holding with less than 30 seconds remaining when leading or trailing by less than eight points, and specific actions at 10, 8, 3-5, and 0-2 seconds. It emphasizes preparation, poise, confidence, getting the ball to the best player, reading defense, offensive rebounding, simple execution, practice with the game clock, and physical conditioning. Fundamentals include skip, baseball, semi-hook, half-court, tipping, and intentionally missing free throws. Strategies include saving timeouts, using them wisely, counter breaks, shooting in line with the basket, bench countdowns, timer reminders, practicing both sides, passing, and a designated inbounds passer. Guidelines address endline, sideline, baseline, opponent field goals, free throws, jump balls, and maximum dribbles.

Sixty-six years after the Battle of Kapyong, Canadian veteran John Bishop doubts Canada could again play a pivotal role amid new Korean Peninsula tensions, citing U.S. President Donald Trump. Former ambassador Marius Grinius says Canada’s “controlled engagement” policy cut diplomatic ties and lost influence. He notes Canada’s Asian trade, cultural ties, and UN Korea command legacy, but says its security commitments have been inconsistent. North Korea conducted nuclear and missile tests, defying UN resolutions, as U.S. Vice-President Mike Pence visited the DMZ and said strategic patience is over; North Korea warned of possible thermonuclear war. Veteran Doug Finney says North Korean suffering and risks to South Koreans require Canadian action. Tina Park says Canada has responsibility-to-protect obligations.

October’s sky features a supermoon and two meteor showers. The full moon on October 6 is a supermoon, appearing about 30% brighter and up to 14% larger, due to perigee; International Observe the Moon Night is October 4. The Draconids, from comet 21P Giacobini-Zinner, peak around October 8 near Draco and can produce up to 10 meteors per hour. The Orionids, from Halley’s Comet debris, peak October 21, produce about 20 meteors per hour, and run September 26–November 22.

The lecture begins with a homework typo correction and notes upcoming linear algebra topics, including eigenvalue decomposition and singular value decomposition. It discusses permutation matrices for reordering rows or columns as preconditioning to reduce numerical error or fill-in. A Plinko example models diffusion with a sparse matrix that spreads probability 50/50 to neighboring cells. Eigenvectors are defined as special vectors transformed only by stretching, and eigenvalues are the stretch factors. The lecture explains finding eigenvalues through the characteristic polynomial and the singularity of A−λI, and discusses algebraic versus geometric multiplicity with examples including diagonal, triangular, zero, and chemical-reaction rate matrices. When a complete set of eigenvectors exists, a matrix can be diagonalized as A=WΛW−1, enabling easier solution of linear systems and decoupled ODEs. Symmetric matrices with normalized eigenvectors have orthogonal eigenvectors, while incomplete eigenvector sets require other transformations such as Jordan normal form or Schur decomposition.

The passage describes SD Memory Card data transfer, write and erase operations, security features, commands, and timing. For block write, CRC bits are added to each data block, and the card performs a 1- or 4-bit CRC check before writing to prevent erroneously transferred data. Write commands may be rejected for BLOCK_LEN_ERROR or ADDRESS_ERROR; CRC failure causes the transferred data to be discarded, not written, and indicated on the DAT line. Multiple block write is preferred over continuous single write for speed, and pre-erasing via ACMD23 can make a following multiple block write faster. Erase uses ERASE_WR_BLK_START, ERASE_WR_BLK_END, and ERASE commands; DISCARD and FULE are similar operations supported for SDHC and SDXC cards but not through SPI. Write protection includes a mechanical switch, optional card internal write protection, and password protection. Card lock/unlock uses CMD42 with PWD/PWD_LEN and optional FEP/FEP_LEN for Card Ownership Protection. Locked cards accept basic commands, ACMD41, CMD16, and lock-card commands. APP_CMD (CMD55) precedes application-specific commands, with defined response and reserved-command rules. CMD6 switch function supports access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit groups, using mode 0 to check functions and mode 1 to set functions. High-Speed mode uses a 50 MHz clock for 25 MB/sec interface speed. CMD8 checks interface condition in Idle state. SDHC and SDXC use block addressing with fixed 512-byte block length and disable partial and misalign access, while SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16-set block length. The passage also specifies host clock control, CRC7 for commands and responses, CRC16 for data, read/write/erase timeout conditions, command types, 48-bit command format, and card command classes.

The passage recounts Taylor Swift’s record-breaking career, including becoming the youngest artist to write and perform a No. 1 Hot Country Songs hit with “Our Song,” the youngest CMA entertainer of the year in 2009, and the youngest album of the year Grammy winner for “Fearless” in 2010. It notes she became the first woman to win album of the year twice and three times, then the first and only person to win it four times. Other cited records include the most American Music Awards, most No. 1 hits on Billboard’s US Digital Song Sales chart, most Grammy song of the year nominations, most weeks at No. 1 on Top Country Albums, longest No. 1 song with “All Too Well (10 Minute Version),” most VMA video of the year wins, and all top 10 Hot 100 entries in one week. It also lists Spotify single-day streaming records for albums, songs, and artist, the $2 billion Eras Tour, and Swift’s $1.6 billion net worth as the richest female musician.

The exponential moving average (EMA), also called the exponentially weighted moving average, is a moving average indicator that gives greater weight to recent data and follows price more closely than the simple moving average. It is a lagging indicator, not predictive, and smooths price data. Its formula is EMA = (K x (C – P)) + P, where C is current price, P is previous EMA, and K = 2/(n + 1). Backtests on SPY tested four EMA strategies. Short-term mean-reversion worked best with a short EMA: buying when close crosses below and selling when it crosses above; the 5-day EMA had 7.41% CAGR and 30.54% max drawdown. Long-term trend-following worked best with a long EMA: buying when close crosses above and selling when below; the 200-day EMA returned 7.84%, with max drawdown 26% versus buy-and-hold 56%. Strategies 3 and 4 entered as before but exited after N days; the best was buying when close crossed below the 50-day EMA and selling after 200 days, producing 10.17% per trade. The passage concludes EMA strategies work best with either low or high numbers of days, and EMA use includes crossover, trend direction, and support/resistance, though it can lag and give false signals; best settings require backtesting.

This paper reports a systematic literature review of selected leading Information Systems journals for papers published from 2000 to 2017. Searches on titles, abstracts, and keywords used digital business strategy, digital transformation, and business digitalization. Following Bandara’s guidelines, the review defined sources, time frame, search terms, and search fields. The first stage found 292 articles; assessing titles, abstracts, and keywords reduced this to 54, and examining article bodies led to a final set of 28. These were analyzed for demographic information and coded using Wolfswinkel’s guidelines through open, axial, and selective coding to identify dimensions, attributes, and core dimensions. Publication activity increased from 2009 and considerably in 2016. Research focused on automotive, banking, telecommunications, healthcare, oil and gas, and manufacturing, mostly in the US and Europe, with less in Asia, the Middle East, Latin America, and Africa. The review identified twelve digital transformation dimensions, six digital business strategy dimensions, and ten organizational capability dimensions. It found overlapping dimensions and proposed a conceptual framework showing inter-relationships among organizational capabilities, digital transformation, and digital business strategy.

YouTube said April the giraffe's livestream is its second-most-watched live channel in company history, behind Riot Games' League of Legends eSports channel. Starting Feb. 10, it drew over 232 million live views, peaking when she gave birth Saturday.

The editors have access to State Department retired records, including central, lot, Executive Secretariat, and overseas post files; central files for 1981–1989 will eventually transfer to the National Archives and be accessible after declassification and processing. Research also uses restricted documents at the Reagan Library and other agencies. Printed material is declassified, though some comes from still-classified documents, and Reagan Library processing may leave items unavailable at publication. RAC scanning covered many but not all records, causing some attachment ambiguity noted as “Not found attached.” Documents are presented chronologically by Washington time, with editorial conventions preserving original text and noting corrections, omissions, and withheld documents.

The paper addresses multi-period resource allocation with stochastic demands, maximizing expected revenue under a total resource constraint. It formulates a static problem that determines all allocations at the start; this is a convex program solved by bisection on the dual variable using marginal CDFs/quantile functions. The static solution is open-loop and ignores temporal correlations and sequentially revealed demand information. To address this, the paper proposes a sequential adaptive shrinking-horizon policy, similar to MPC, which re-solves at each time after conditioning future demand distributions on observed demands; it is a heuristic without global optimality guarantee. For independent demands, the sequential solution reduces to the static solution. Simulations use synthetic jointly log-normal demands and compare static, sequential, roll-forward, and oracle allocations. In non-independent cases, the sequential allocation achieves higher revenue than static and roll-forward, is closer to the oracle bound, and tends to have smaller revenue variance. The paper concludes the method applies under any demand model requiring conditional quantile functions, and future work includes closed-loop model learning.

The passage examines the cultural elements of digital transformation, noting that cultural changes are often harder to introduce than technological ones. It reports research linking tech intensity to business performance, with digital leaders outperforming laggards on revenue and enterprise value CAGR. Leaders and laggards differ in data culture: leaders adopt growth mindsets toward risk and continuous learning, use data to create shared context and transparency, empower teams to examine data and measure performance, and align the organization through common targets while allowing autonomy. Leaders encourage experimentation, long-term development, controlled data sharing, measurement, and coordinated goals; they emphasize data culture as central. Laggards tend to prioritize short-term efforts, discourage risk, provide narrow transactional training, control or hoard data, favor business judgment or a “culture of genius,” set aspirational goals not grounded in data, and fail to connect goals with strategy. Even leaders face tensions in balancing risk, long-term learning, and data use. The passage also describes four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—and says organizations can build on strengths to reach a strong data culture.

The article examines the impacts of anti-CRT bans on Native content instruction in teacher education at predominantly white institutions in Utah and Idaho and in K-12 contexts in Arizona. Using Tribal Critical Race Theory, colonial unknowing, and ethnographic stories, interviews, and observations, it analyzes how anti-CRT campaigns in Idaho, Utah, and Arizona restrict teaching about race and Native histories. The passage states that most public-school teachers are white, teachers often lack knowledge of Native peoples and nations, and Native content is limited in teacher education. It reports that bans and related policies contribute to continued silencing of Native perspectives, invisibilization of Native peoples, and refusal to learn culturally sustaining pedagogies. The authors conclude that teacher education is a foundational space in struggles for critical, socially just democracy and that Native history, nationhood, and tribal sovereignty should be taught in public education.

Lyla Carreyn, 5, returned home after receiving a kidney from her 4K teacher, Beth Battista. Hospitalized since February 21, she had post-surgery complications including an infection. She now wears footie pajamas and drinks water freely, but still needs over 15 daily medications and thrice-weekly labs, with possible re-admission.

On September 4, 2020, Tesla, Inc. completed the sale of $5.0 billion (before commissions) of its common stock through its previously disclosed “at-the-market” offering program. Final settlement of the shares sold is expected by September 9, 2020.

This paper characterizes spatiotemporal heterogeneity in self-reported mask-wearing in the U.S. from September 2020 to May 2021 using the COVID-19 Trends and Impact Survey. Responses were dichotomized and aggregated to county-month. Bayesian binomial regression models with population density as a fixed effect estimated masking proportions; raking and resampling adjusted for county age, sex, and education distributions. To address non-response and social desirability bias, the authors compared CTIS vaccination responses with ground-truth vaccination data, estimated county-level survey bias, and incorporated it as an offset in masking models. They also analyzed community-reported masking. Results show masking was spatially heterogeneous, varied within states, and was positively associated with population density; urban counties generally had higher masking than rural counties. Masking peaked in January 2021 and fell to its lowest in May 2021, coinciding with vaccination increases, declining infections and worry, and changes in CDC guidance and mask mandates. Bias-corrected self-reported masking was well approximated by community-reported masking, with differences from −6% to 5%, especially in April–May 2021. The authors note limitations including incomplete bias correction, exclusion of under-18s, possible Facebook-user differences, and the assumption that masking and vaccination self-reports are equally biased. They conclude masking varied greatly across the U.S., suggesting one-size-fits-all approaches may be ineffective and local behavioral data are needed.

The author agrees with Alan Greenspan that stock market and bond market bubbles exist. He discusses a ratio chart of the 10-year yield versus the S&P 500, noting a precise correlation. The ratio bottomed near the 2008/2009 lows, rose until mid-2016, and its trend line was support until the U.S. election, then resistance, with a 2017 rejection. The ratio is falling as stocks fall and yields rise; it needs yields to drop and stocks to rise, or yields to stop rising. If yields rise and stocks fall, a multi-year head-and-shoulders pattern could form, suggesting the post-2016 rally was a blow-off top. Two bear patterns are present. No immediate collapse is called, but bulls need yields to drop soon; short-term hope exists near critical support.

This MIT lecture moves from optimal control tools to walking robots, stating that walking’s fundamental challenge is control, not actuators or power density. It explains that walking involves limit cycles and impacts/hybrid dynamics. Using the Van der Pol oscillator, it describes stable limit cycles and Poincaré sections/maps, which convert continuous-time limit-cycle stability into discrete-time fixed-point stability; local stability requires eigenvalues less than 1. It reviews Muybridge’s locomotion photography, McMahon’s ballistic walker, and McGeer’s passive dynamic walkers. It then models the rimless wheel with pin-joint stance, instantaneous support transfer, and inelastic impulsive collisions, showing stable rolling limit cycles from energy conversion versus collision losses and an analytical return map. It extends this to compass gait and kneed walkers and announces next topics: applying methods to hybrid dynamics and walking control, with a midterm on Thursday.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated May 9, 2017, regarding results for the quarter ended April 30, 2017. The filing includes Exhibit 99.1, a press release titled “NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for First Quarter Fiscal 2018,” and Exhibit 99.2, CFO Commentary by Colette M. Kress. In his second inaugural, the speaker says an extended address is less necessary than at first because public declarations have covered the war; progress of arms is known, and he ventures no prediction. Four years earlier, an impending civil war was dreaded; insurgents sought to dissolve the Union by negotiation, both sides deprecated war, but war came. One-eighth of the population were colored slaves localized in the South, constituting an interest all knew was somehow the war’s cause. Neither side expected the war’s magnitude or duration. Both read the same Bible and prayed to the same God; prayers were not fully answered. He hopes the war will pass, submits to God’s will, and urges malice toward none, charity for all, care for veterans, widows, orphans, and a just lasting peace.

Gold lacks inherent utility, cash flows, and requires storage/insurance, though it has historically served as an inflation hedge; the article says stocks may be a better hedge. The article tests trend following in gold using monthly prices from 1971 onward, defining trends with a 12-month (250-day) simple moving average: go long when price is above the average, stay in cash when below. Backtest results beat buy and hold, with 100,000 growing to 10 million versus 4 million; 26 trades, long as of May 2021, excluding slippage and commissions. Best results were around the 12-month average, corresponding to a 200–250-day moving average. The system reportedly avoids big drawdowns. For buying/selling gold, options mentioned are ETF (GLD) or futures; tests used spot price. Trend following in commodities may work due to large moves, but no guarantees.

The study investigated the Disc Potentiation Test (DPT) for identifying KPC and MBL carbapenemases in gram-negative isolates. A total of 147 Imipenem-resistant gram-negative bacterial isolates were collected from Evercare Hospital, Dhaka, from January to June 2020. All isolates showed 100% resistance to Imipenem; resistance was highest in the >60 age group, and the ICU had the highest prevalence, with Acinetobacter baumannii most prominent. DPT identified KPC in 39/147 (26.53%) and MBL in 66/147 (44.89%) isolates; 36 (24.49%) exhibited both KPC and MBL, 3 (2.04%) had KPC only, 30 (20.40%) had MBL only, and 78 (53.06%) showed no enzyme. Acinetobacter baumannii had the highest detection of both enzymes, and tracheal aspirates had the highest number of samples with both KPC and MBL. The study emphasizes monitoring and control measures for multidrug-resistant organisms in healthcare settings.

This passage provides technical documentation for MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers, covering electrical characteristics; detailed descriptions of the CPU, operating modes, PMU, clock module, DMA, events, memory, GPIO, IOMUX, ADC, temperature sensor, VREF, comparator, DAC, security, TRNG, AESADV, Keystore, CRC, MATHACL, UART, I2C, SPI, CAN-FD, LFSS, RTC, watchdog timers, timers, analog connections, debug, BSL, and factory constants; application and layout guidance; documentation support; revision history; and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

The speaker discusses power-play control, confidence with the puck, Sami’s development, and careful management of defensemen’s minutes and bench usage. He says Sean gained confidence, returned as a veteran and leader, and helped the locker room. In overtime, the Brind’amour/Francis line had normal ice time, Vasicek’s line got extra time, and the fourth period concerned him. He addresses low-maintenance players, Eric Cole not being treated as a rookie, Bates’s consistency, and the need to generate offense without changing the line’s approach. He is cautious about major playoff changes. He notes difficult minutes for defensemen, Detroit’s strong outlet and five-man defensive play, and problems moving through the neutral zone and forechecking. He says the team needs to reset, examine options, and return to a grinding approach after scoring and frustration issues.

In Kenneth Kaylor’s appeal from a dissolution judgment, the appellate court reversed the financial award because rehabilitative alimony, child support, house expenses, car, insurance, and medical expenses exceeded his ability to pay. Appellant’s net income was about $2,000 monthly, with about $600 remaining after ordered payments. The court remanded for an award consistent with appellee’s needs and appellant’s ability to pay, affirming all other aspects.

The passage describes AGESA native assembler procedures for initializing and removing a pre-memory, stackless register-passing stack region, including core allocation, global address mapping, MTRR handling, mode checks, UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF creation, and AGESA status codes. It also covers AmdCreateStruct for allocating and pre-initializing parameter structures, plus service calls for DIMM data eye results, APIC address/core presence, and pre-memory execution cache size. Dependencies, stack requirements, register destruction, and x86-64 specifics are noted.

This study examines the scope, importance, and role of curriculum literacy in education and the factors hindering its development. Using thematic content analysis, it analyzes Scopus articles written in English and Turkish with the keyword “curriculum literacy,” excluding non-peer-reviewed and indirect studies, leaving 29 studies. Findings describe curriculum literacy as involving understanding curriculum structure, evaluating content, and analyzing applicability, and link it to effective use of materials, teacher development, student success, equity, and digital technology use. Bibliometric analysis shows keyword shifts over time and increasing studies, especially in 2020–2025. Most studies are in social sciences; Australia and the United States have 8 studies each, and Turkey has 6. Results indicate a positive but weak relationship between digital technology use and curriculum literacy. The study discusses digitalization, artificial intelligence, interdisciplinary integration, equity, and teacher support, concluding that curriculum literacy is critical for education quality and should be expanded through training, policies, and broader disciplines.

The paper examines the current state and potential of digitalization in Vietnamese higher education and offers recommendations. Government policy has driven the digital transformation agenda. Before COVID-19, digitalization was slow and varied among higher education institutions, but the pandemic accelerated it. The paper describes Vietnam’s higher education system, including its levels, governance by MOET and other agencies, and public and private universities. Key policies include the National Digital Transformation Program to 2025, vision to 2030, and the 2022–2025 project on IT application and digital transformation in education. These set targets for online learning, digital materials, data warehouses, and technology-based management. Before COVID-19, challenges included underfunding, limited infrastructure and digital skills, fragmented governance, and limited e-learning. After COVID-19, institutions developed learning management systems, blended learning, online administration, national databases, digital materials, and MOOCs, while MOET allowed greater online teaching and testing. Recommendations include policy dissemination, government investment and partnerships, leader training, lecturer and student digital-skill support, and paperless student services.

AMD shares rose 23.71% Monday after OpenAI agreed to deploy up to 6 gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPUs over multiple years, starting with 1 gigawatt in 2026. AMD issued OpenAI a warrant for up to 160 million shares tied to deployment and share-price milestones; full exercise could give OpenAI about 10% ownership. The companies said the deal is worth billions. It positions AMD as a core OpenAI partner and could reduce OpenAI’s reliance on a single vendor. Nvidia shares fell 1%. OpenAI has committed roughly $1 trillion in new buildout spending in two weeks. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at records.

Baseline and demographic characteristics were comparable between the Primary SOC and Additional Educational Program groups; subjects had median age 74, 59.9% were male, and mean CHADS2 and CHADS2-VASc scores were 2.1 and 3.6.

Nasdaq 100 E-mini futures are electronically traded, cash-settled stock index futures based on the Nasdaq 100 index, which comprises the largest 100 non-financial companies on Nasdaq and is primarily technology stocks. The contract debuted June 21, 1999; it is one-fifth the size of the full Nasdaq futures, trades on CME Globex, expires quarterly in March, June, September, and December, and is valued as the index times $20. Trading runs from Sunday 6:00 p.m. to Friday 5:00 p.m. ET with a daily break. Strategies involve fundamental and technical analysis, risk management, and position sizing; the article backtests a volatility strategy. Seasonality notes better performance in spring and fall. As of December 6, 2022, the price was 11615.75; the all-time high was 16,676.50 in November 2021, and the all-time low was 797.50 on October 3, 2002. Risks include leverage and large price movements. CFDs may be offered by brokers.

Tube UK supported the 2017 Manchester Day celebrations, delivering ten audio systems to five carnival floats and five music/compere stages in the city centre. Commissioned by Manchester City Council and produced by Walk the Plank, the project was managed in one day by a nine-person Tube team led by Melvyn Coote with six vans. Setup began at 7 a.m., all systems ran by midday, the parade ran 1–3 p.m., and stages operated 1–6 p.m., followed by immediate de-rig.

The speaker calls winning the Cup with Alex a special moment, noting their similar paths and a conversation when down against Columbus in which they said they would win tomorrow and win a cup together. He was happy for Alex and the group, especially Ovi and Backie, for enduring criticism and coming back in every series. He says the team has gained confidence, played simple hockey, and must carry one game into the next. California authorities charged 29-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht with starting a fire that became Los Angeles’ most destructive and destroyed much of Pacific Palisades. Officials said he lit a fire on Jan. 1 that was extinguished but smoldered and reignited Jan. 7 in high winds. Arrested in Florida, he faces charges including malicious destruction by means of fire; his public defender did not respond. Officials said he fled and later returned to watch, made 911 calls, and lied to investigators. A complaint says the Jan. 1 fire was intentionally lit, other causes were excluded, and a barbecue-style lighter was found in his car. The Jan. 7 blaze killed 12 and destroyed over 6,000 homes and buildings. The cause of a second blaze is undetermined. An outside review found response weaknesses and delayed evacuation warnings.

Pets at Home in Burton has teamed up with the National Autistic Society for the UK’s first week-long event. The St Peters Retail Park store will hold an autism hour on October 8, an hour before opening, by dimming lights, turning down music and till bells, and sharing autism information with employees. The event will also be held in Uttoxeter.

A bear trap is a bullish trading pattern in an uptrend where a bearish candle breaks a significant low, tricking sellers into believing a reversal is occurring; a bullish candle then takes them out and the prior trend continues. It exploits FOMO. Spotting is difficult because traps can resemble downtrend continuation. Signs include a sudden sharp reversal after prolonged upward movement, a break of support or a moving average, divergence between price and RSI or MACD, and positive earnings or acquisition news. In an AAPL example, price broke a lower trendline, retail traders shorted, stops were triggered, and the market resumed its uptrend; MACD divergence could have helped avoid the short. Bear traps can hurt retail traders who sell at a loss. Market manipulators may create sell orders to push prices down, trigger stop-losses, then buy lower. Retail traders can reduce risk by not basing decisions solely on price, considering fundamentals, market conditions and risks, avoiding crowd-following, staying disciplined, and backtesting. The passage also gives FAQ answers, notes no one-size-fits-all indicator, mentions mean reversion and stocks/bonds tailwinds, and describes a strategy that buys breakdowns and sells strength, with QQQ and QLD backtest statistics.

Samsung’s Chromebook Pro, due in April, is designed to run Android apps from Google Play and embodies Google’s push to merge desktop and mobile computing. It and the Chromebook Plus, shipping next week, are 2-in-1s with digital pens. Reviews of pre-production Pro models range from lukewarm to effusive. Reviewers said the new Chromebooks could threaten Microsoft devices and Windows, and Chromebook sales outpaced Macs in early 2016. The Plus starts at $449.99 with a Quad HD display and ARM processor; the Pro starts at $549 with Intel Core m3. Both have 4GB RAM, 32GB storage, eight-hour battery, two USB-C ports, and 4K streaming support. Google also announced improved ChromeVox assistive technology.

Orca submitted a T cell therapy for FDA approval. Other biotech news includes Damian Garde’s return to STAT, nationwide-licensed doctors fueling telehealth, TCGX closing a $1.3 billion fund, Skye’s obesity drug failing in a mid-stage study, and FDA approval of a second generic mifepristone.

NVIDIA Turing GPUs use lossless memory compression to reduce memory bandwidth demands, and Turing improves Pascal’s compression algorithms for about 50% higher effective bandwidth over Pascal in TU102-based RTX 2080 Ti versus GP102-based 1080 Ti. Turing adds a new display engine supporting DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, DSC 1.2, native HDR processing, and BT.2100 tone mapping; enhanced NVENC supports HEVC 8K30 encode with bitrate savings, and NVDEC supports HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing supports USB-C and VirtualLink for single-connector VR, and TU102/TU104 use NVLink instead of MIO/PCIe for SLI GPU-to-GPU transfers, with two-way SLI only. The passage describes use of the UC1825B-SP controller with standard power topologies and gives layout guidance. It recommends low-EMI inductors with ferrite-type closed cores; routing feedback traces away from inductors and noisy power traces, directly and thickly, preferably on the opposite PCB side with a ground plane. Input/output capacitors, feed-forward capacitors, and compensation components should be close to the IC, preferably surface mount. Power traces should be short, direct, and thick, with a minimum of 15 mils per ampere; inductor, output capacitors, and output diode should be close together. Grounds should connect to a ground plane, preferably on both PCB sides, and multilayer boards can separate power and signal planes. Vias should be used per current, and switching current loops should curl in the same direction. Output drivers require a ground plane with dedicated power ground for high di/dt currents; VCC should bypass to power ground and VREF to signal ground, using low ESR/ESL ceramic 1-mF capacitors. The passage also includes documentation updates, support resources, trademarks, ESD caution, glossary, mechanical/packaging/orderable information, and TI disclaimers.

The lecture states the binomial theorem and uses it to prove three special limits: for positive \(p\), \(1/n^p \to 0\); \(p^{1/n} \to 1\); and \(n^{1/n} \to 1\). It defines limsup and liminf for a bounded sequence \(x_n\) as the limits of the supremum and infimum of the tails \(\{x_k: k \ge n\}\). It proves these limits exist because the tail supremum sequence is monotone decreasing and bounded, and the tail infimum sequence is monotone increasing and bounded, with liminf \(\le\) limsup. Examples show \((-1)^n\) has limsup \(1\) and liminf \(-1\), while \(1/n\) has both \(0\). The lecture proves that every bounded sequence has subsequences converging to its limsup and liminf, implying the Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem that every bounded sequence has a convergent subsequence. It also proves that a bounded sequence converges if and only if its limsup equals its liminf, and then all equal the sequence limit.

This retrospective single-center study compared acute ischemic stroke patients treated with alteplase (January 2022–February 2023; 144 included) or tenecteplase (March–November 2023; 120 included). Eligible patients were ≥18 years, diagnosed with ischemic stroke, treated within 4.5 hours of symptom onset, and had no hemorrhage or extensive infarction on CT/MRI. Dosages were alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg) and tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg). Baseline characteristics were largely comparable, though hyperlipidemia and atrial fibrillation differed. The tenecteplase group had significantly lower OTT, DNT, and DPT and higher rates of DNT ≤45 minutes and DPT ≤120 minutes; tenecteplase independently predicted meeting target DNT and DPT. It also had greater 24-hour NIHSS improvement and shorter hospital stays, with no significant differences in sICH or any ICH. Tenecteplase independently predicted 24-hour NIHSS improvement; baseline NIHSS predicted sICH and any ICH, and atrial fibrillation predicted any ICH. The study concludes tenecteplase showed higher early clinical improvement, safety comparable to alteplase, and enhanced target DNT/DPT achievement, though limitations include single-center, nonrandomized design, early outcomes, and mostly mild-to-moderate stroke. Larger multicenter studies are needed.

The passage describes an enhanced DiffCSP framework using guided diffusion to generate crystal structures conditioned on target superconducting critical temperature (Tc). To address limited labeled superconductivity data, the model is pretrained on more than two million crystal structures from the Alexandria Database and fine-tuned for Tc conditioning on a smaller high-quality superconductor set. Classifier-free guidance is used to generate 200,000 candidate structures, followed by a multistage screening workflow using machine-learning models and DFT to assess metallicity, thermodynamic and dynamic stability, and Tc. Of 34,027 unique novel generated structures, 773 are reported with DFT-calculated Tc > 5 K and Ehull < 200 meV/atom. The pipeline reports a 2.3% per-structure hit rate, compared with an element-substitution baseline and a recent generative search. The candidates skew toward ternary compositions. The authors synthesize 18 selected candidates by arc melting; 9 show superconductivity above 4.2 K, with measured Tc generally lower than predicted, and X-ray diffraction indicates the predicted structures generally did not form, instead yielding disordered BCC solid solutions or multiphase mixtures. The discussion notes limitations from sparse reference data and incomplete convex hulls and calls for improved synthesizability prediction and experimental feedback. Validation shows guidance shifts Tc distributions toward targets within the training domain, but an out-of-distribution target of 110 K did not produce high-Tc structures.

The study used bibliometric analysis to determine the place of publications on “special education and mathematics” and “special education and mathematics education” in the literature and to present a panoramic perspective. Findings show a first significant increase in publications in 2017, decreases in 2018 and 2019, and a high increase in 2020. No studies appeared between 1981–1986 and 1988–1990. There were 887 keywords, 120 sources, 1,093 authors, 54 single-authored documents, 3.11 co-authors per document, and 17,813 references. Most publications appeared in special education journals, especially Journal of Special Education and Remedial and Special Education. Bouck Ec was the most influential author, and Xin Yp and Root Jr contributed significantly. Popular keywords included students, mathematics, and children. The study concludes that stronger collaborations and research including teachers, families, technology, and innovative approaches are needed. The lecture introduces the spacetime of a compact, spherically symmetric body with a vacuum exterior, using a static metric in Schwarzschild coordinates and an areal radius. Treating the interior as a perfect fluid, it sets up curvature tensors and Einstein equations. For the vacuum exterior, setting Ricci=0 yields the Schwarzschild metric, with the integration constant fixed by the Newtonian limit. Birkhoff’s theorem states that the exterior vacuum of any spherically symmetric body is described by the Schwarzschild metric, even with spherically symmetric time variation, so no gravitational waves are produced. For the interior, a mass function m(r) is defined; its integral over density gives gravitational mass, generally less than baryonic mass, with the difference interpreted as gravitational binding energy. Combining Einstein equations and local stress-energy conservation yields the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff relativistic hydrostatic equilibrium equation and coupled equations for stellar interiors.

The lecture begins with administrative announcements: a correction for problem 2B is posted, Thanksgiving is noted, the instructor will be away, Jain Jin will present on BARGs/batch arguments, and the final class will wrap up the semester. The lecture reviews Fiat-Shamir, Kilian-Micali, random-oracle soundness, and a zero-knowledge Hamiltonicity protocol with only half soundness, considered under parallel repetition. The main goal is to show the parallel-repeated protocol is sound under Fiat-Shamir in the standard model for a particular commitment. The commitment is implemented using public-key encryption, a trusted common reference string/public key, and openings via randomness. It introduces FHE and circular-secure FHE, and the Canetti-Lombardi-Wichs 2019 result. The proof idea uses a hash key containing an FHE encryption of a circuit g; in analysis, g is replaced by g* that decrypts beta and XORs 1 so it never equals the bad beta. Soundness follows if the cheating prover cannot distinguish encryptions, relying on semantic security and circular security. Motivation includes obtaining NIZK from lattices, applying the technique generally, and eventually SNARGs and BARGs. Q&A addresses zero-knowledge tension, CRS public-key generation, malicious keys, opening/randomness, trapdoor as secret key, and circuit size T.

Research context: monoclonal antibodies and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) are important anti-COVID-19 strategies. SA58 Nasal Spray is a broad-spectrum anti-COVID-19 mAb developed by Sinovac Life Sciences Ltd. that neutralizes ACE2-utilizing sarbecoviruses, including circulating Omicron variants. A PubMed search on Nov 21, 2022 identified three published mAb PEP trials: AZD7442, bamlanivimab, and REGEN-COV. Bamlanivimab and REGEN-COV showed efficacy and safety and were licensed for PEP in the U.S., but their emergency use authorization was discontinued due to Omicron escape; until the end of December 2022, no drug was available for PEP against COVID-19. In this randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial in Beijing during an Omicron BF.7 outbreak, healthy adults within 72 hours of contact with SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals received SA58 or placebo. SA58 reduced laboratory-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 by 80.82% (95%CI 52.41%-92.27%) and SARS-CoV-2 infection by 61.83% (95%CI 37.50%-76.69%). All sequenced variants were Omicron BF.7. No severe COVID-19 or death occurred. Adverse events were all Grade 1; no SAEs or AESIs were reported. Common adverse events included nasal mucosal dryness, runny nose, fever, nasal congestion, headache, cough, and throat dryness, with no significant difference between groups. Limitations included a healthy worker population, low sample size, early study termination, isolation practices, and short monitoring. The study concluded that SA58 showed satisfactory efficacy and safety in healthy adults with early exposure and should be further evaluated in high-risk populations.

This audit reviewed 74 tuberculosis-related mortality files at Kitwe Teaching Hospital from June 2018 to June 2019. Most deaths occurred among males (67.6%), patients with a mean age of 39.2 ± 11.6 years, HIV-positive patients (81.1%), and patients from high-density residential areas (83.8%). Common symptoms included cough, fever, diarrhea, headache, and shortness of breath. Laboratory findings included anemia and multi-organ involvement such as hypoalbuminemia, renal dysfunction, and deranged liver enzymes. Radiological descriptions included cavities, consolidation, miliary patterns, and opacities. The study concludes that TB inpatient presentations included male gender, age younger than 50 years, HIV positivity, high-density residence, and unstable hemodynamics, and recommends a prospective follow-up study to determine mortality predictors.

Night trading means holding positions overnight from the close to the next open, not after-hours trading. Since 1993, all S&P 500 gains have come from owning the index from close to open; gold shows the same tendency. AT-752 is an orally available guanosine nucleotide prodrug inhibitor of DENV polymerase with pan-serotype antiviral activity. This first-in-human Phase 1 study evaluated safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of oral single ascending doses (250–1500 mg) and multiple ascending doses (1000 mg QD, 750 mg BID, 750 mg TID) in healthy subjects. AT-752 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events or discontinuations due to adverse events; treatment-emergent adverse events were mild or moderate and resolved. In SAD cohorts, no PK ethnic sensitivity or food effect on total exposure was observed. In MAD cohorts, 750 mg TID rapidly increased AT-273 levels above the target EC90 and maintained them. Two studies published September 16 and 17 report that two oral GLP-1 drugs, oral semaglutide at 25 milligrams and orforglipron, helped people with obesity lose weight. On March 11, 2011, a 9.0-magnitude earthquake and tsunami struck Japan, causing nuclear meltdowns, over 25,000 casualties, extensive damage, and major disruption to the Japanese auto industry. Toyota, Honda, and Nissan were affected. Nissan had six facilities damaged and about 50 critical suppliers impaired. Nissan’s emergency plan prioritized human life, disaster prevention, recovery and business continuity, and community support, with a Global Disaster Headquarters and simulations. After the disaster, Nissan convened its headquarters quickly, created a Recovery Committee, shared information through regional staff in Japan, allocated constrained parts by margin, slowed production at bottlenecks, used in-transit inventory to find alternatives, secured air freight, and empowered field decisions. Nissan later planned to increase localized Americas production from about 70% to 90% by 2015, reduce Japan-sourced components in North America by 50% by fiscal 2013, and improve business continuity planning beyond Tier 1 suppliers.

Thermoelectric materials directly convert heat and electricity, and their cooling efficiency depends on the figure of merit ZT. Bi2Te3-based compounds are the best thermoelectrics near room temperature, but n-type Bi2Te3−xSex (BTS) lags p-type due to stronger anisotropy and intrinsic defects. This work reports that annealing Se-alloyed n-type BTS synthesized by melting-hot pressing decouples carrier and phonon transport. Annealing at 723 K tunes carrier density and mobility through cation vacancy formation from Te(Se) volatilization, increasing power factor, while atomic-scale defects strengthen phonon scattering and reduce lattice thermal conductivity. The Bi2Te2.6Se0.4 sample annealed for 100 h achieved a peak ZT of 1.06 at 373 K and an average ZT of 0.99 over 300–423 K, offering a practical route for n-type BTS thermoelectric cooling.

Moderation analyses found attachment anxiety and avoidance main effects; mentalization moderated some attachment-personality pathology relationships. Correct other-mentalizing weakened the link between anxious attachment and interpersonal functioning, while hypermentalizing strengthened it. This paper characterizes the thermal performance of the Mod-Cam testbed and its 280 GHz instrument module for FYST/Prime-Cam. The 100 mK detector stage was servo-controlled and showed an RMS temperature fluctuation of \(3.2 \times 10^{-5}\) K. Thermal responsivities were measured for aluminum and titanium-nitride KIDs. Using prior optical responsivity values, the equivalent optical power fluctuations at a 5 pW load were calculated as 0.20 fW for Al and 0.11 fW for TiN, corresponding to fractional contributions of 0.0040% and 0.0023%. The paper concludes that thermally induced noise is negligible and validates the cryogenic and thermal-control design.

The lecture defines the pointer machine model: nodes with a constant number of fields that may hold pointers or data, operations for creating nodes and reading or setting fields, and a root node. It distinguishes persistence from retroactivity, covering persistence. Persistence aims to remember all versions; operations are relative to a specified version, and updates create new versions. Partial persistence allows updating only the latest version, making versions linearly ordered. Full persistence allows updating any version, making versions a tree. Confluent persistence allows combining two versions, making versions a DAG. Functional data structures never modify nodes, only create new ones.

For partial and full persistence, the lecture presents transformations of pointer machine data structures with constant in-degree and out-degree. Partial persistence uses back pointers and mods, node copying, and amortized analysis. Full persistence uses versions as tree nodes, linearizes them with an order-maintenance data structure, maintains back pointers for all versions, and splits nodes. The Driscoll, Sarnak, Sleator, and Tarjan 1989 paper is cited. Deamortization gives constant worst-case slowdown for partial persistence; full persistence deamortization is an open problem. Confluent persistence is harder; Fiat and Kaplan in 2003 define effective depth and achieve overhead related to log number of updates plus effective depth, with a lower bound. A 2011/2012 SOTO result gives logarithmic overhead in a disjoint case. Functional examples include balanced BSTs via path copying, deques with constant-time concatenation, and tries; several open problems remain.

The Missouri Supreme Court will hear two cases on whether the Missouri Human Rights Act prohibits discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, though those terms are not in the act; lower courts are split. The passage discusses incorporating generative AI into computational screening workflows, noting challenges such as nonsensical candidates, wasted computational resources, and model decay. It also describes active learning reducing model decay, supporting multi-objective prioritization using stability, synthesizability, and HMOF-Tanimoto similarity, and balancing exploration and exploitation through upper confidence bound acquisition.

A research group led by Dr. Shinichi Furuya of the NeuroPiano Institute and Sony Computer Science Laboratories reported that pianists can alter piano timbre through touch. Using a high-precision sensor system that measured all 88 keys at 1,000 fps and 0.01 mm resolution, they analyzed 20 internationally renowned pianists and conducted psychophysical experiments with 40 listeners. Listeners distinguished intended timbres regardless of musical experience, with pianists showing greater sensitivity; volume and tempo were controlled. Data analysis identified movement features such as acceleration during escapement and hand synchronization deviation, and experiments confirmed a causal relationship between key movement and timbre. The findings were published in PNAS and may support music education, neuroscience, rehabilitation, skill transfer, and human interface design.

This manuscript describes a KaviKrishna-led participatory action research (PAR)/community-based participatory research (CBPR) and Indigenous Knowledge System (IKS)-based approach to tuberculosis (TB) control and research in rural Kamrup, Assam, India. It notes TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), remains a global health threat, and is complicated by dormant MTB, MDR-TB, diverse strains, and limitations of centrally controlled TB programs. KaviKrishna uses the Indigenous Kamarupa Information Network (IKIN), temple complexes, telemedicine, student volunteers, and community participation for TB screening, diagnosis, treatment, follow-up, and monitoring, along with national and international collaborations. The methods described include ethics approval and consent; sputum, bone marrow, and blood collection; sputum processing, MTB culture, and DNA extraction; drug susceptibility testing; PCR for mycobacterial cross-reactivity and MDR; MSC/HSC sorting; in vitro and mouse-model studies of dormancy/reactivation; MIRU-VNTR, spoligotyping, and whole-genome sequencing; MIC assays; MDK/MPN assays for VBNC MTB; and live/dead assays. The passage reports that dormant MTB can reside in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, that MTB recovered from MSCs in relapsed sputum-negative cases had rpoB and rpoC mutations, and that stem cell niches may be involved in MDR evolution. It also reports WGS data deposition and suggests CBPR/IKS-based methods may serve as a model for novel TB control strategies.

In this MIT OpenCourseWare lecture, Gary Gensler discusses digital ID. The class considers definitions of identity, including philosophical views and identity as attributes, claims, credentials, and attestations. It covers identity and access management, authentication and authorization, users, service providers, identity providers, and certificate authorities. Gensler explains public-key cryptography, digital signatures, and certificate authorities as central to internet security. The lecture lists identity-management pain points such as privacy and security, identity theft, forged credentials, updating personal information, and data breaches. It discusses whether blockchain can help with verification costs, fraud, traceability, censorship, and privacy, while noting challenges of storing personal identifiable information on a blockchain, immutability, deletion rights, and lost keys. State projects include Estonia’s e-identity, which uses X-Road and not blockchain, and India’s Aadhaar, a 12-digit ID and biometric system that is not blockchain-based and has had benefits and problems. It also covers self-sovereign identity, related projects and standards efforts, and MIT blockchain diplomas. Earlier, the class discusses blockchain for supply chain traceability and transparency.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email while off work for Rosh Hashanah after conservative commentator Natalie Winters published alleged past blog posts attributed to him that criticized President Trump. The Miami Herald reported he was the latest of dozens of federal prosecutors fired by Trump’s Justice Department who were believed to be at odds with the president or his agenda. The passage also says three other Southern District of Florida prosecutors who worked with former special counsel Jack Smith were fired.

Stock indexes fell Friday, giving up some weekly gains. After 90 minutes, the S&P/TSX composite index was down 81.78 points at 15,694.52; the Canadian dollar was 79.70 cents US, up from Thursday’s 79.69-cent average. The TSX will close Monday for Thanksgiving, while U.S. markets stay open. High street bank branches are declining as branchless banks accessed via smartphone apps rise. A Which? survey found more than half of under-40s would open a mobile-only account, but willingness drops sharply among those aged 40 and over. Atom Bank’s competitive savings accounts attracted savers, but its app crashed, highlighting drawbacks of no in-branch customer service. Experts would write 10,000–15,000-word pamphlets, with secretly printed and indexed appendices of documents and statistics, under one director with assistants. Colonel House tells Secretary Lansing that Lansing’s memorandum is admirable and will help in planning an organization.

Keaton Jones, a Tennessee middle schooler, went viral after his mother posted a video of him describing bullying. Celebrities, including LeBron James and Mark Ruffalo, expressed support and opposition to bullying.

Defendants were charged with possession of burglar’s tools, attempted petit larceny, and resisting arrest. Testimony alleged they attempted to take a bicycle by partially severing its chain with a bolt cutter but abandoned the attempt after a third person spoke to them. Defense counsel requested a jury charge that renunciation was a defense to both possession of burglar’s tools and attempted petit larceny. The court charged renunciation only as to attempted petit larceny. The jury convicted defendants of possession of burglar’s tools and acquitted them of attempted petit larceny and resisting arrest. Defendants moved to set aside the verdict, arguing the court erred in refusing the renunciation charge. The court denied the motion, finding Penal Law §40.10 did not authorize renunciation as a defense to possession of burglar’s tools.

Insecticides India plans to invest around Rs 200 crore over three years to expand existing plants in Gujarat and Rajasthan and set up two synthesis facilities and one export-oriented unit. It expects 10-15 percent revenue growth this fiscal, aided by normal monsoon and 7-8 new product launches, funded through internal accruals, debt and equity.

The device features a multiSPI digital interface supporting many data transfer protocols; data output modes are controlled by the host or device, with system- or source-synchronous timing. The interface includes input/output shift registers, configuration registers, and a protocol unit, and the host perceives the device as a 32-bit input-output shift register. Connection topologies include single-device all multiSPI options, single-device standard SPI, and multiple-device daisy-chain. In daisy-chain, CONVST/CS and SCLK are shared, SDI and SDO-0 are chained, configuration registers are programmed identically, SDO_CTL_REG bits 7-0 are set to 00h, and optimal frames use 32×N SCLK edges; throughput decreases with device count. Device states are RESET, ACQ, and CONV, controlled by CONVST/CS and RST. RESET can be application or power-on reset; ACQ acquires the analog input; CONV uses an internal clock and ignores CONVST/CS transitions during tconv. Programming uses nine configuration registers and data write/read operations. A data transfer frame begins on the CONVST/CS falling edge and ends on the rising edge; SCLK counter values determine optimal, short, or long frames. Commands include byte and half-word read/write, clear, and set operations, with HWORD LSB address ignored. Output data can contain fixed patterns, register data, or conversion results with optional flags. Protocols include legacy SPI-compatible single/dual SDO-x and source-synchronous modes. The register maps list device ID, reset/power control, SDI/SDO control, data output control, range select, and alarm registers. Application information discusses a 16-bit SAR DAQ, an industrial analog input module with MUX36D08, alarm thresholds/hysteresis, AVDD/DVDD decoupling, NAP and power-down modes, layout guidance, and support/legal information.

The Supreme Court said the CBI-led investigation into the larger conspiracy behind Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination did not appear to have made much headway, and that the MDMA probe could be endless. The court arrayed the Centre as a party in convict A G Perarivalan’s plea seeking suspension of sentence until the CBI concluded its probe into the bomb-making conspiracy, fixing the matter for January 24. Perarivalan, whose death sentence was commuted to life, has spent 26 years in prison.

OSCAR is introduced as the first one-shot multi-label causal autoregressive discovery method. It uses two Transformers as density estimators to extract, for each label, a compact interpretable subgraph and the label’s Markov Boundary, with quantified causal indicators between events and labels. The method aims to handle high-dimensional event sequences without label-cardinality-dependent complexity. Under assumptions including temporal precedence, bounded lagged effects, causal sufficiency, and perfect Transformer modeling, conditional mutual information can identify each label’s Markov Boundary. On a real-world vehicular dataset with about 29,100 diagnostic trouble codes and 474 error-pattern labels, local structure learning algorithms did not output Markov Boundaries within a 3-day timeout; OSCAR ran in 11.7 minutes on 50,000 samples and achieved 55.26% precision, 31.37% recall, and 40.02% F1.

South Carolina Congressman Trey Gowdy has a self-deprecating humor, especially about his hair, and shares a bond with Sen. Tim Scott; they co-wrote “Unified: How Our Unlikely Friendship Gives Us Hope for a Divided Country,” out April 3. Gowdy’s 2016 campaign ad joked about his haircuts. During the Benghazi hearings, he attacked the investigation as a prosecutor; critics said his task was to paint Hillary Clinton as failing to protect citizens and hiding facts. He became a hero to some and villain to others, but grew disillusioned. On Jan. 31, 2018, he announced he would not seek re-election. Afterward, he supported Robert Mueller’s Russia investigation, countered GOP claims about the Nunes memo and Russia, and warned Trump against firing Mueller.

Despite disappointment over the loss, the speaker says the team worked hard, remains positive and optimistic, and believes it can compete and win. The team made mistakes by giving up two two-goal leads in the third period and losing; it must learn, stick to its game plan and systems, and respond in the next must-win game. Returning home and supportive fans are seen as a boost, with all focus on the next game.

The passage discusses iterative methods for large sparse matrices where direct elimination is too expensive. It describes choosing a preconditioner P close to A but simpler, with examples including Jacobi (the diagonal), Gauss-Seidel (lower triangular including diagonal), SOR, and incomplete LU. The iteration error is governed by the iteration matrix m = I − P⁻¹A; convergence requires all eigenvalues of m to be less than 1 in magnitude, and speed is controlled by the spectral radius. For a one-dimensional example matrix, Jacobi’s method gives slow convergence because the largest eigenvalue is near 1 and low-frequency components decay slowly. Weighted Jacobi reduces high-frequency components, and Gauss-Seidel squares the Jacobi eigenvalues but still requires on the order of n² iterations. The passage notes that multigrid is intended to address the remaining slow low-frequency convergence.

The speaker says he will congratulate the winner and wants to see the Stanley Cup up close. He is disappointed after losing four straight but proud of his team’s progress and plans to rebound. He says the opponent beat them in many areas, was more hardened by earlier challenges, and capitalized on mistakes. Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 28, 2020, reporting that it issued a press release regarding its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 28, 2019. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing lists registered securities and is signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President, Chief Financial Officer.

This qualitative phenomenological study examined 45 teacher candidates’ views on a special education course delivered through distance education at a private university in the 2022–2023 academic year, using a researcher-created semi-structured interview form. Most participants reported satisfaction with taking the course via distance education, but noted internet connection problems and stated that distance education was not as effective as face-to-face education. They emphasized the importance of attendance even in distance courses. A majority recommended distance education, citing effectiveness, home comfort, individualized learning, technology familiarity, and economic convenience; some did not recommend it due to learning difficulties and systemic problems. Participants highlighted technical/material deficiencies and recommended improving the system, internet infrastructure, technical support, free internet access, and digital materials. The study concluded that distance education was inefficient in applied courses and that quality may increase if deficiencies are addressed. Limitations included 45 participants, qualitative method, and only the special education course; future quantitative, larger-sample, or different-course studies were suggested.

The passage states that major equity indices are reaching new all-time highs while bearish warnings increase. It says the author will counter these warnings using Ray Dalio’s framework for diagnosing market bubbles. It argues bearish theses sound more compelling, exciting, and action-oriented, but historical data shows patient, “boring” strategies that do little or nothing yield superior results; excitement is called the worst enemy of return. An April 16, 2001 email from Ann Schmidt lists Enron-related media mentions. The included articles report that Sierra Pacific Resources suspended its quarterly dividend due to Western U.S. energy-crisis costs and still hopes to complete its purchase of Enron’s Portland General Electric; UK seabed leases for offshore wind projects were issued to companies including Enron units; Internet rumors are changing how companies handle layoff announcements, with reports on Razorfish, EMC and Enron’s denial of broadband-unit layoffs; and solar and renewable energy are discussed alongside Enron’s Zond purchase. Business Week items say Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay told a Toronto audience the administration went too far on global warming and that President Bush was expected to choose Enron executive Thomas White for the Army. Indian coverage discusses the Godbole committee report, MSEB’s financial crisis over Enron’s Dabhol project, a planned April 25 Maharashtra bandh, and commentary blaming the government rather than Enron for the Enron affair.
