A Chicago Tribune article describes DivX movie-copying and notes Blockbuster-Enron broadband talks broke off.

NVIDIA Turing introduces a new display engine with native HDR processing and tone mapping using ITU-R BT.2100 to avoid color shift on HDR displays. It adds NVENC support for H.265/HEVC 8K at 30 fps, bitrate savings for HEVC and H.264, improved encoding quality over Pascal and fast x264 software encoding, and NVDEC support for HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink for single-cable VR, and uses NVLink for SLI GPU-to-GPU transfers in TU102/TU104, with two-way SLI supported. It introduces RT Cores and RTX technology for real-time ray tracing, using hybrid rendering combining ray tracing and rasterization; RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection, while denoising reduces required rays. NGX uses Tensor Cores for AI features including DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Mesh Shading adds Task and Mesh shaders. Variable Rate Shading controls shading rate per 16x16 region, with content adaptive, motion adaptive, and foveated rendering uses. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling. Multi-View Rendering supports multiple views per pass. Resource management supports bindless CBV/UAV and resource heaps. Turing variants include TU104, Tesla T4, and TU106, with specified core, memory, NVLink, and product details. RTX-OPS is a workload-based metric derating Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 usage. The appendix explains ray tracing, BVH, denoising, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections.

A Reversal Day is a day when a stock or market index changes direction, either upward or downward, after an extended uptrend or downtrend, often with high volume. A Bullish Reversal Day, or Selling Climax, occurs after an extended downtrend, may make a lower low than the previous day, but closes bullish above the previous day’s high. A Bearish Reversal Day, or blowoff, occurs after a prolonged rally, may make a higher high, but closes bearish below the previous day’s low. Causes include changes in market sentiment, economic conditions, company-specific news, and technical analysis. Reversal Days can be spotted through changes in direction, heavy trading volume, and technical indicators such as moving averages, RSI, and Bollinger Bands. Support/resistance levels, divergences, and market trends/cycles are also discussed. Stocks, forex, commodities, and bonds are described as prone to reversals. Two reversal day strategies are backtested in gold, and the article states the backtests indicate the Reversal Day idea has merit.

Cocoa futures are financial derivatives representing contracts to buy or sell a specified quantity of cocoa on a future date at a pre-agreed price, traded on ICE and CME Globex (NYMEX). One contract unit is 10 metric tons; prices are quoted in US dollars per metric ton, with a minimum fluctuation of $1.00 per metric ton ($10.00 per contract). Contracts expire in March, May, July, September, and December, and are financially settled on CME but physically delivered on ICE. Symbols are CC on ICE and CJ on CME. The passage also lists seasonality favoring summer, risks from leverage and liquidity, an ETF (NIB), a block minimum of 100 contracts, and reported all-time high and low prices.

HSAs are savings accounts that can be invested and grow tax-free; withdrawals are tax-free for certain medical expenses and are currently available only to people with high-deductible health plans. Participation is low: about 20 million of 176 million insured people in 2015. Barriers include not having money upfront and psychological difficulty saving. Behavioral economists say people dislike losing money, and framing incentives or using opt-out enrollment may encourage saving, though government costs may arise. HSA users use less health care, but health improvement is unclear; drug costs fell while emergency room visits rose, especially for lower-income families. Estimating health costs is difficult. HSAs may help only those with enough cash beyond daily expenses.

MLPs fell over the year’s last four days, though equal-weight MLPs were slightly higher; both outperformed the S&P 500. Oil and natural gas rose and ended the year with large gains. The AMZE total return was 22.5%, over 400 basis points above the traditional Alerian MLP index. The disparity reflected smaller MLP rallies and Enterprise Products Partners’ unusual underperformance, its first since 2009 not beating the index. In 2016, MLPs rose 18.3%, beating the S&P 500 for the first time since 2011; December returned 4.4%. Global Partners led the sector for a second week, while SXCP was the top-performing MLP still paying distributions and FGP the biggest loser. GPs and midstream corporations underperformed MLPs for a second week. There was little MLP news; PAGP filed to sell up to $500 million in common units, and SHLX announced Gulf of Mexico pipeline acquisitions at a 7.7x EBITDA multiple.

This cross-sectional study investigated burnout, associated factors, and coping strategies among prison officers at Nsawam Medium Security Prison, Ghana. Of 266 recruited, 243 questionnaires were analyzed. Most participants were male, single, junior-ranked, and had less than five years of service. Burnout prevalence was 9%; 42.0% had high emotional exhaustion, 68.7% had low personal accomplishment, and depersonalization was low, moderate, or high in 35.4%, 32.1%, and 32.5%, respectively. Perceived causes included irregular shifts, heavy workload, and lack of training and development opportunities. Emotional exhaustion was associated with shift allocation and depersonalization with rank. Sex and education were significantly associated with burnout: female officers had higher burnout, and diploma/certificate holders had lower odds than postgraduates. Main coping strategies were talking to colleagues, looking forward to off duty, talking to family, keeping thoughts to oneself, and alcohol use. The study concluded that irregular shifts, heavy workload, and training and development need attention; officers had high emotional exhaustion and depersonalization and low personal accomplishment, with night-shift and junior officers particularly affected, and adopted positive coping mechanisms.

The passage discusses the S&P 500 Information Technology sector, which has the highest weighting in the S&P 500, over a quarter of the index’s market cap, and strong growth over the last decade. Major ETFs are VGT and XLK. Top five stocks listed are AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AVGO, and ADBE. The article presents two technology/XLK mean-reversion trading strategies. The SD Card Association releases its SD Simplified Specification/Addendum, a subset of its complete specification, non-confidentially with disclaimers. Implementation may require a license; it is AS-IS without warranties, liability, license, or disclosure obligation.

The M8 prototype has downgraded headlights, standard brakes, and different wheels. Ottawa police warn that a woman allegedly faked car trouble on Innes Road to lure a Good Samaritan to her car, where she and two men robbed him. The victim was injured and hospitalized. Vertigo, an iOS app, announced Wednesday it now integrates with Spotify and Apple Music, allowing users with either premium subscription to share music. Glen Campbell is battling final-stage Alzheimer's, his family told People. They say music comforts him and he sometimes sings along. His daughter Ashley said his release Adios, recorded in 2012 and released June 9, shows his continued love for music despite Alzheimer's.

This study extended a framework for clinical implementation of optical genome mapping (OGM) with a procedure for analysis and reporting of OGM data using VIA software in hematologic malignancies, focused on myeloid neoplasms. Ten retrospective cases (nine AML, one MDS) were analyzed 5–6 times each by independent technologist-director teams. OGM detected all variants reported by standard of care, and in five of six positive cases it revealed additional OGM-only variants. Classification and reporting varied for non-Tier 1A variants. Average technologist review times were 25.2 minutes for negative cases, 28.5 minutes for simple cases, and 47.3 minutes for complex cases; VIA often yielded about a 50% time reduction compared with Bionano Access 1.7 alone. The authors conclude that OGM analysis using Bionano Access and VIA offers a streamlined, efficient approach to interpret and report cytogenomic variants in hematological disorders and may help standardize analysis and clinical interpretation.

Brazilian stocks gained Thursday, led by Vale after solid first-quarter production figures. Vale’s iron ore output fell 6.7% quarterly but rose 11.2% year-on-year to a period record, and its shares rose as much as 4.9%. Usiminas also rose after reversing a first-quarter loss. The Rio Blanco 4-H senior team concluded its 2018 livestock judging season at the 73rd annual Colorado 4-H June conference at Colorado State University. U.S. President Donald Trump warned Iran not to restart its nuclear program and criticized the 2015 nuclear accord during a meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron, who hoped to persuade Trump to keep the United States in the deal. Trump said he and Macron could reach an agreement soon. Iran said it might ramp up its nuclear program or quit a nuclear treaty if Trump scraps the deal. The holder holds the ball for the kicker on extra points and field goals. On kicks, the holder catches the snap, then quickly and steadily places the ball in the kicker’s exact preferred spot, with the laces turned away from the kicker. Any bobble, hesitancy, or errant placement can cause disaster. The holder needs soft hands, consistency and quickness in placement, and the ability to rotate the football, operating with stillness and urgency. Many NFL teams use their punter as holder; high school and college teams may also use backup quarterbacks, receivers, or others. In rare fake field goals, the holder may throw, flip the ball to the kicker, or run. No holding stats or consensus best holders exist. The position is overlooked but important to scoring opportunities.

The Daily Examiner is moving from a metered digital subscription to a premium model; increasing numbers of stories will be subscriber-only, marked PLUS, while public-safety and some local stories remain accessible. The change aims to fund local journalism. Existing subscribers are unaffected and get unlimited access to the website, app, newsletter, breaking-news alerts and other News Corp sites. Thailand recorded 390 road deaths during the seven-day Songkran period, an 11% drop from the previous year after a junta campaign. Drink-driving caused 28% of accidents, and authorities seized 5,600 motorbikes and 1,800 cars. Junta chief Prayut Chan-O-Cha said he was not satisfied because people still died. The EU is preparing a draft policy to push multilateral development banks to align financing with the Paris Agreement, shift lending from fossil fuels toward low-carbon projects, and improve transparency, local-currency financing, and private-sector participation. Germany and France are leading the initiative for upcoming World Bank and IMF meetings, but the U.S. opposes it, arguing it could distract from economic growth and poverty alleviation. MDBs channelled $137 billion into climate projects in 2024, which EU leaders call insufficient; adoption could reshape development finance, though consensus may be difficult.

The Supreme Court of Canada ruled 7-0 that records detailing abuse of former residential school students can eventually be destroyed, upholding a lower court decision that sensitive material collected for independent assessments should be destroyed after 15 years. The court said settlement negotiators intended the assessment process to be confidential and private, and claimants and alleged perpetrators relied on confidentiality assurances.

Eric Thames hit a two-run homer in the fifth inning that accounted for the only runs as the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Minnesota Twins 2-0. Junior Guerra pitched five shutout innings, allowing two hits, walking three and striking out eight. Josh Hader pitched three hitless relief innings, and Corey Knebel earned his ninth save. On each Inauguration Day, people renew dedication to the United States. Washington’s task was to create and weld together a Nation; Lincoln’s task was to preserve it from internal disruption; the present task is to save the Nation and its institutions from external disruption. Opening statements began in the trial of former CIA case officer Kevin Mallory, 60, of Leesburg. Prosecutors say Mallory gave a Chinese spy information about human assets and other top-secret material for $25,000. Defense lawyers say he was a loyal American stringing the Chinese along to expose their intelligence operation. Olean’s Common Council unanimously authorized Mayor Bill Aiello to apply for a $10 million state Downtown Revitalization Initiative grant, part of $100 million for 10 projects statewide. If awarded, it would be among the city’s largest grants. The application was due the next day. The proposed area runs from Olean General Hospital to the Allegheny River and Franchot Park to about Seventh Street. Proposed ideas include redeveloping the former Manufacturers Hanover building, business incubator funding, downtown theater expansion, Lincoln Park pedestrian access, and a park near Olean General. Officials said additional Buffalo Billion assistance may be possible. JCC’s John Sayegh praised the effort and discussed Cutco Theater upgrades.

This IDC White Paper states that industrial enterprises face geopolitical uncertainties, rising energy prices, raw material shortages, supply chain disruptions, skilled labor shortfalls, and sustainability demands, while digitalization is changing manufacturing value creation. It examines industrial simulation, modeling, data analysis, and HPC infrastructures, based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers from discrete and process manufacturing enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Simulation and modeling digitally map real processes; enterprises link them to innovation, faster product development and time to market, cost reduction, decision-making, and quality improvement. Deployment spans product development, production and process planning, and quality management, but data silos and lack of a holistic data strategy require a single source of truth. HPC is presented as a game changer for complex calculations, enabling higher quality and intensity of use, new usage scenarios, innovation, and agility. Challenges include security, investment and licensing costs, energy consumption and sustainability, technical requirements, availability, and lack of expertise. HPC can be run via external/cloud, colocation, scientific partners, or on-premises infrastructure; HPCaaS offers flexibility, cost optimization, scalability, resilience, collaboration, and new business models. The paper concludes that simulation, modeling, data analytics, and HPC are key to industrial digital transformation and recommends virtual development, holistic data strategy, suitable HPC operating models, scalable/secure/energy-efficient solutions, and external expertise.

Uber launched a nationwide panic button enabling riders to dial 911 from its home screen. In most cities it shows the rider’s real-time location; in pilot cities it automatically sends location and vehicle details to dispatchers.

This AMD Geode™ CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 Specification Update lists numerous issues, their implications, and resolutions, covering interrupt/clock gating, ATAC/ACC PRD prefetch, UDMA CRC corruption, SSMI/DMA, ACPI/PMC registers, KEL, PCI, UART/USB clock gating, S3 wake, RTC CMOS, LPC DMA, SMBus, GPIO, GLPCI retry, and Sleep_X behavior. Resolutions include disabling clock gating, using DWORD alignment, blocking UDMA host terminations, SMI traps, normal UDMA procedure, PWRBTN# wake, read-modify-write, and programming delay counters below PM_SED.

The speaker says the opponent is defensively sound and limits chances. The speaker was unhappy with no generated chances, early jitters, a letdown after the first goal, and a two-goal lead, though the game was even except for about ten minutes. The power play struggled, and they gave the game away, wanting a better result.

In spring 1953, the free world weighs the chance for a just peace. The passage recalls 1945’s hope after victory, when Western Allies and Russia met as comrades and peoples sought to guard against domination by an aggressive power. That common purpose perished, and nations divided. The United States and other free nations chose principles: no people is inherently an enemy; security requires cooperation; nations may choose their own government and economy; dictation is indefensible; lasting peace cannot rest on armaments. The Soviet Union chose a different vision based on force, huge armies, subversion, and rule of neighbors, seeking power superiority. The result was fear, armaments, and division. The free nations remain armed, strong, and united, but ready to welcome genuine peaceful purpose. The worst feared is atomic war; otherwise, the best is perpetual fear and burdensome arms spending that steals from human needs. After Stalin’s death, a new Soviet leadership has an opportunity. The passage calls for deeds, not rhetoric: an honorable Korean armistice and peace in Asia; respect for free choice, including Eastern Europe; European unity with a free and united Germany; disarmament with limits, atomic controls, safeguards, and UN inspection; and use of savings for world aid and reconstruction. It asks what the Soviet Union is ready to do.

This study examines the effect of digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth on sustainable supply chain performance through brand image and supply chain image, focusing on Indonesian ICT companies. Data were collected from ICT employees using 568 questionnaires, with 315 valid responses, and analyzed using SEM and PLS. The results supported all seven hypotheses: digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth positively affect brand image, brand image positively affects supply chain image, supply chain image positively affects sustainable supply chain performance, and mediation effects were confirmed. The model explained 82.3% of the variance in sustainable supply chain performance.

This application is a divisional of U.S. Non-Provisional patent application Ser. No. 15/200,149 filed Jul. 1, 2016, and was made with NASA support under Contract No. NNC14CA32C. The disclosure relates to hybrid gas turbine electric engines and a method/apparatus for operating a hybrid gas turbine electric propulsion system during descent. The engine includes a core with first and second compressors and turbines, first and second shafts, a primary flowpath, a motor connected to the first shaft, and a controller. It has takeoff, top of climb, and additional modes, and can be undersized relative to thrust requirements in takeoff or top of climb. In descent, compressor bleed air pressure can be replaced by an electric compressor, and stored energy can power systems. The fan can windmill to drive the first shaft, and the motor can generate or use electricity. The controller can prevent the core from operating or maintain a minimum temperature. A method includes producing thrust at maximum temperature in a first mode and no core thrust in descent by limiting air/fuel or maintaining minimum temperature, windmilling the fan to generate electricity, powering aircraft systems, and storing electricity.

Apple Inc. filed Form 8-K dated February 1, 2021. On February 8, 2021, Apple consummated the issuance and sale of $2.5B 0.700% Notes due 2026, $2.5B 1.200% Notes due 2028, $2.75B 1.650% Notes due 2031, $1.5B 2.375% Notes due 2041, $3.0B 2.650% Notes due 2051, and $1.75B 2.800% Notes due 2061. The Notes were issued under an underwriting agreement dated February 1, 2021, an indenture dated November 5, 2018, and an officer’s certificate dated February 8, 2021. Interest is payable semi-annually on February 8 and August 8, beginning August 8, 2021. The Notes are Apple’s senior unsecured obligations and rank equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. Exhibits were filed.

Cloud providers offer a broad range of technologies and methods because they serve customers with different demands and scenarios, and solutions and innovation are continuously developed. 52% of respondents consider fast, flexible access to cutting-edge analysis and simulation methods and state-of-the-art hardware a core aspect of HPCaaS for innovation. Higher calculation speed can be a competitive factor, while new data processing methods offer better insights and new digital products, services, and business models; this is core for industry digital transformation. Cloud-based HPC datacenters are said to help drive energy efficiency and contribute to sustainability targets at the host manufacturing company. Bridgestone explored cloud HPC for agility and cost effectiveness to overcome peak capacity limits, hardware freshness, and financial challenges of on-premises HPC, taking a step-by-step approach. 81% of respondents already using HPC intend to implement it. IDC views IT-based simulations, modeling, and data analytics as key enablers amid disruptive changes; virtual process steps streamline product development and manufacturing and create usage scenarios. HPC is becoming a prerequisite for modern simulations and modeling, and public cloud and HPCaaS unlock potential. Competitiveness depends on creating and integrating data as a single source of truth across the product life cycle. Recommendations include virtual product and manufacturing development, a holistic data strategy, evaluating HPC operating models, considering scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise. Findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers at industrial enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended October 30, 2022, with unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements. Third-quarter revenue was $5.931 billion, net income was $680 million, and diluted EPS was $0.27; nine-month revenue was $20.923 billion, net income was $2.954 billion, and diluted EPS was $1.17. Q3 revenue fell 17% year over year; Data Center revenue rose 31%, Gaming fell 51%, Professional Visualization fell 65%, Automotive rose 86%, and OEM and Other fell 69%. Gross margin was 53.6%, affected by a $702 million inventory charge. NVIDIA recorded a $1.35 billion acquisition termination cost in Q1 FY2023 related to terminating the Arm share purchase agreement. As of October 30, 2022, cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $13.143 billion; total assets were $40.488 billion; total liabilities were $19.139 billion; shareholders’ equity was $21.349 billion. In Q3 and the first nine months, NVIDIA repurchased $3.65 billion and $8.99 billion of shares and paid $100 million and $300 million in dividends, respectively. The filing also discusses U.S. export license requirements affecting A100/H100 products to China and Russia, litigation, debt, and segment information.

A federal judge ruled that the 1991 Nirvana album cover showing a naked baby underwater is not child pornography and dismissed Spencer Elden’s 2021 lawsuit. Judge Fernando Olguin found no statutory factors except nudity supported the claim, calling the image analogous to a family photo of a nude child bathing.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation in the 2014 murder of Dan Markel, her former son-in-law and FSU law professor. Before sentencing, she said she was innocent, cited a lack of evidence, and said she would have stopped the plan. The judge warned he could consider her lack of remorse. Prosecutors alleged she plotted with her son Charlie, who enlisted a girlfriend and hit men; the alleged motive was the family’s desire to move Markel’s ex-wife Wendi to South Florida. Wendi was not charged; Donna’s husband Harvey supported her account.

Myrna LaPlante, whose aunt Emily Osmond went missing in 2006, supports the National Inquiry’s head and says she would withdraw her family’s story if the inquiry is reset. The Assembly of First Nations voted to call for chief commissioner Marion Buller’s resignation; LaPlante says families were not consulted and supports extending the inquiry deadline. Some Saskatchewan families support Buller’s resignation, citing hearing changes, poor communication, and feeling unsupported.

Interest rates are rising, with the average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage just below 5%, and the passage lists techniques to improve mortgage borrowing power. These include paying off debt to lower the debt-to-income ratio; getting a co-signer, who shares responsibility and liability; changing loan programs; putting more money down, though usually less effective than paying off debt; and changing jobs before applying within the same or a similar field. Lenders compare proposed mortgage payments plus recurring expenses to monthly pre-tax income, and exceeding 50% can be a challenge.

The passage describes Singapore as a small, densely populated, multiethnic Southeast Asian country where education and training are important for economic development. It outlines special education’s development in two periods, pre- and post-2004. Before 2004, students with disabilities were primarily served outside mainstream education by voluntary welfare organizations/social service agencies through special schools, while mainstream education emphasized integration. The year 2004 is described as a watershed after Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong called for better integration of students with disabilities and envisioned an inclusive society. Later developments included Enabling Masterplans, signing the UNCRPD in 2012 and ratifying it in 2013, rising numbers of students with disabilities in mainstream schools, and viewing special schools as part of one national education system. Teacher preparation expanded through programs such as Special Needs Officers later renamed SENOs, the Diploma in Special Education, the Certificate in Special Needs Support, a 2020 professional development roadmap, and compulsory pre-service coursework. Special school teacher preparation evolved from CISE to DISE, ADISE, master’s, and doctoral options. Issues include special schools being run by social service agencies rather than MOE, lower salaries, limited special education options for higher support needs, and less comprehensive special educator preparation. The conclusion states that Singapore’s education system is shifting toward holistic development and inclusion, with special education expected to expand in partnership with mainstream education.

An email dated July 31, 2001, titled “IEP News 7/31” compiles news items on energy. Articles report criticism of California Gov. Gray Davis’ long-term power contracts as costly and creating stranded costs; an SEC preliminary inquiry into whether Davis energy consultants used inside information to trade power company stocks; disclosure that Davis spokesman Steve Maviglio bought Calpine stock; and a settlement in which consultants Chris Lehane and Mark Fabiani agreed to forgo payment and leave the administration. Other items cover San Francisco ballot measures to create public utility districts; a FERC order reducing California’s expected power refunds to under $4 billion; Texas beginning a deregulated electricity pilot program; and a hearing on Baltimore Gas and Electric’s proposed split from Constellation Energy Group. The email also lists article headlines, dates, and publication details.

Sony released an A7Riii firmware update to fix the “Set File Name” function and improve overall camera stability. Mac users with macOS High Sierra may be unable to install it because macOS 10.13 is not supported; the issue appears to be a Mac OS problem. Earlier Mac OS versions or Windows may work.

The lecture discusses PDEs, including homework 7 on a drug-patch diffusion problem to be solved with COMSOL and a finite volume code. It covers sharp gradients, mesh refinement, convergence, finite volume balances, boundary conditions, ghost volumes, sparse matrices, solver choices, the CFL number, time-dependent PDEs, and adaptive meshing. It then introduces probability, measurement noise and physical fluctuations, event and joint probabilities, Bayes’ theorem, probability densities, and cumulative probability distributions.

On Feb. 14, The New York Times reported U.S. agencies intercepted 2016 calls between Russian intelligence officials and Trump campaign members, including Paul Manafort; anonymous officials said they found no evidence the campaign worked with Russia on hacking or election influence. Sen. Rob Portman was among at least six Republican senators awaiting Andrew Puzder’s confirmation hearing over taxes for a housekeeper not authorized to work in the U.S. The FBI interviewed Michael Flynn after Trump’s inauguration; Flynn was ousted Monday, with Sean Spicer citing an erosion of trust. Linda McMahon and David Shulkin were sworn in to lead the SBA and VA. Chuck Schumer called for an independent investigation and Jeff Sessions’ recusal regarding Flynn.

A 1968 study found doctors diagnosing ulcers from x-rays disagreed with each other and contradicted themselves on duplicate images. Researchers created an algorithm from doctors’ stated methods that outperformed the best doctor. The passage notes unanswered questions about the algorithm and asks whether experts will still be needed as AI and big data generate rules.

Which? research suggests lenders were slow to pass higher interest rates to savers but quickly raised mortgage costs. After the November base rate rise, Which? found 48% of variable instant access savings accounts and ISAs had no rate change in five weeks, 21% passed on the full 0.25%, and 30% less. Of 95 providers, 10% applied the full rise to all such accounts and ISAs. For SVR mortgages, 53% of providers increased existing borrowers’ rates by end-2017; fixed-rate market averages rose October-December. UK Finance said rates depend on various factors, most mortgage borrowers are fixed, and switching is easier.
The United Way of Northwest Illinois will launch the Imagination Library in Carroll County on March 28, 2018, providing books to children ages 0–5.

The lecture reviews D-branes after open-string quantization. Open strings on D-branes have massless gauge and scalar fields; scalar fluctuations make D-branes dynamical. The D-brane mass is defined as the vacuum energy of open strings living on it, computed by summing Euclidean surfaces with boundaries weighted by the Euler number, so the disk scales as \(g_s^{-1}\) and the annulus/cylinder as \(g_s^0\). At weak coupling, brane tension scales as \(1/g_s\), with dimensional dependence on \(\alpha'\).

The interaction between two separated D-branes can be viewed as tree-level closed-string/graviton exchange, represented by a cylinder with one boundary on each brane, or equivalently as a one-loop open-string diagram. This channel duality relates closed-string and open-string perspectives.

For multiple coincident D-branes, open strings connecting different branes give fields with two indices; string joining yields matrix products. Phase symmetry and index reshuffling lead to \(U(n)\) symmetry, which becomes a spacetime/worldvolume gauge symmetry, producing Yang-Mills theory. Separating branes gives stretched strings mass, breaking \(U(2)\) to \(U(1)\times U(1)\) via a Higgs mechanism. The low-energy action can be summed to the Dirac-Born-Infeld form, describing gauge fields and relativistic motion of D-branes.

Rare wave-like clouds appeared over Bristol on Monday. Twitter users shared photos; a Met Office meteorologist said they resemble Asperitas, a new International Cloud Atlas feature. Their formation is mysterious, possibly linked to post-thunderstorm conditions or wind changes; they were seen in Monmouthshire, Thornbury and Filton.

The passage describes features and information for the MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 devices, including LFSS, VREF, COMP, security, CRC, UART, I2C, SPI, IWDT, WWDT, RTC_B, TIMx, device analog connections, I/O diagrams, serial wire debug, DEBUGSS, factory constants, typical application and layout guidance, development tools and documentation support, device nomenclature, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

The Hickory Tussock Moth caterpillar, found in Belleville and surrounding areas, is white, fluffy, and has black markings and hairs connected to a poison gland that excrete venom when touched. Found July to September, it can cause rashes, burning, swelling, pain, headache, nausea, or allergic reactions. Officials advise washing the affected area, using calamine or cortisone, seeking medical attention for severe reactions, and looking but not touching.

The passage is an FAQ about options trading in META. It explains that options are contracts to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price, including call and put options. It also covers account opening, a $100 minimum deposit, minimum trade size of one contract, order placement, margin requirements, leverage up to 1:100, broker fees, risk management and analytics tools, educational resources, risks, and strategies such as calls, puts, covered and naked calls and puts, straddles, strangles, and spreads.

The FAQ describes a classical mean reversion strategy for the S&P 500/SPY using IBS and RSI signals, with backtested equity curves since January 2000 under compounding, no taxes, performance stats, and an inverted-parameter version.

This note traces the history of “unskilled” work in the United States from the 19th to the 21st centuries, examining how work was categorized by skill and whether classification reflected the nature of the work, who did it, low barriers to entry, or other factors. It describes Alba Edwards’s early occupational classification and 1938 social-economic groups, in which “unskilled” included farm labor, factory and construction labor, other laborers, and servant classes. In 1930, about 14 million workers were in “unskilled” occupations, and African Americans were disproportionately represented. By the 21st century, “low-skill” and “unskilled” remained common terms, with skill defined by education/experience or job content, while low-paid in-person service jobs grew amid job polarization. The note covers farm labor, factory labor, servant and service occupations, and other labor, including slavery, sharecropping, convict leasing, immigration, domestic service, porters, retail, fast food, care work, gig work, warehousing, and digital labor. It then discusses efforts by government, labor advocates, and employers to improve pay and conditions, including the FLSA, NLRA, minimum wage, unions, strikes, and employer initiatives. During Covid-19, many essential workers held “unskilled” jobs. Future-of-work discussions emphasized job quality for lower-wage workers, and the note asks how to think about work, workers, and pay for jobs historically called “unskilled” if such work is essential.

The Nuclear Medicine market report covers key participants including GE Healthcare, Bracco Imaging, Mallinckrodt, Lantheus Medical Imaging, and Bayer, plus competitive, product, regional, segment, price, cost, gross, and consumption data. It states the market grew at an average annual rate of 6.27% from $3,500 million in 2013 to $4,200 million in 2016 and is expected to reach $5,890 million by 2021.

Atossa Genetics shares fell 12.06% in the most recent session. Analysts project a 52-week price target of $2 based on 1 opinion, with both high and low targets at $2 and a latest close of $0.7. Its ABR is 1, with 1 Outperform recommendation and no Buy, Hold, Underperform, or Sell ratings; its industry ABR rank is 162 of 265. ATR-14 is 0.09, weekly volatility is 37.88%, monthly volatility is 16.66%, and RSI is 73.41. Market capitalization is $17.25 million, outstanding shares are 24.52 million, and previous volume was 29.13 million versus a 3.7 million average.

Eric Hirsch will step down as CEO of EdReports next year, leaving at the end of the school year while the board searches for a successor. Hirsch founded EdReports in 2014 and led its independent, Consumer Reports-style reviews of instructional materials. After initial publisher pushback, it has conducted more than 1,100 reviews and is considered a leading authority by many states and districts. The organization recently revised its scoring process and expanded to review pre-K materials, while facing criticism over its response to reading reforms and emphasis on certain standards; alternatives have also launched. One expert said a new leader should understand AI and curriculum. Hirsch noted research showing that adopting a strong curriculum alone is not enough and that districts often lack piloting or effectiveness measures.

The passage discusses the Gann Fan, a technical analysis tool created by W.D. Gann. It consists of about nine diagonal lines drawn from a significant swing high or low, with the main Gann angle at 45 degrees, known as the 1:1 line, and other time-to-price ratios. The Gann fan trading strategy uses these lines as potential support and resistance to analyze price movements and identify breakouts or reversals. It can be used with other tools and in forex trading, and it requires risk management. The passage states the Gann fan is not always accurate, differs from the Fibonacci fan, and that a meaningful backtest of the strategy was not possible because of subjectivity and lack of strict rules.

Cover 1 is a man-to-man defense covering every receiver, with a free safety playing deep, often called “man-free.” A linebacker or strong safety can become a low-hole player, and edge defenders may align with inside or outside shade. It can take away the run, blitz, and dare offenses to throw vertically. Offenses can attack Cover 1 outside, away from the deep safety, using pick plays, double moves, and routes that get playmakers moving, such as deep crossing, wheel, and out routes, to create separation and YAC. The passage lists examples from Ohio State, Oklahoma, Georgia, and others, including bubble-go, slot fade, double moves, Jerry Rice motion sprint to flat, and scissors/snag-wheel combinations.

Christine Milligan was surprised to be asked whether she wanted to revoke her daughter Cassidey Ouellete’s organ donation after Ouellete was pronounced brain dead following a car accident. Ouellete had signed her organ donation card at 16, and Milligan supported her decision. Ontario’s Trillium Gift of Life Network says families can prevent donation if a loved one expressed regret; such overrides are uncommon, occurring in about 10 per cent of cases in 2016, down from 21 per cent in 2015. Trillium encourages people to share their wishes. Milligan says more is needed: her brother, former MPP Robert Milligan, introduced a 2012 private member’s bill to let only donors revoke registration and to establish presumed consent with opt-out. Gavsie is skeptical, citing a 2015 Ipsos poll and no evidence presumed consent increases donors. Milligan wants the bill reintroduced as Cassidey’s bill.

S&P Global Platts will launch new low-sulphur marine gasoil and diesel oil prices from June 1, 2017 at several bunkering ports in Asia. It cited rising sales and expected tighter global sulphur limits. The assessments will reflect fuels with maximum 0.1% sulphur and be published alongside existing prices.

The passage includes advertising and partner disclosures stating that Motley Fool Money receives compensation from companies, which may affect where offers appear but not product ratings. It describes credit-card offers, including a Wells Fargo Active Cash Card with unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 cash rewards bonus after $500 in purchases in the first 3 months, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, a $0 annual fee, and cell phone protection. It also describes a Capital One Quicksilver card with unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% cash back on Capital One Travel bookings, welcome bonuses, 0% intro APR for 15 months, and a $0 annual fee, and another card offer with 2% on every purchase, a $200 cash back bonus after $1,500 in purchases in the first 6 months, and a balance-transfer-only 0% intro APR for 18 months. The passage recommends a good/excellent credit score of 670–850 and advises choosing a card whose features fit the user.

The passage describes South American misunderstanding that the Monroe Doctrine implied U.S. superiority or protectorate rights. Secretary Root sought to dispel this; at the Rio conference he said the U.S. wanted peace, no territory beyond its own, no sovereignty except over itself, equal respect for all American republics, and no privileges not conceded to them. He urged common prosperity, Hague representation, rejection of colonization, and an all-American public opinion. His words were acclaimed, approved by the speaker, and echoed by Drago, who said U.S. policy opposed European oppression and control without asserting superiority. Buenos Aires displayed U.S. names, Brazil named a building “Palacio Monroe,” and the speaker thanked host governments. The passage ends with reference to a 1905 message on forced debt collection and possible occupation.

The speaker describes a player as great, positionally sound, hard to get around, and consistently making the right play. He praises the city, his family’s enjoyment, the neighborhood, friends, and the team’s family atmosphere, and says winning has attracted fans and season-ticket interest. He discusses promoting hockey in southern markets, children playing, enjoying living in the cities and coaching kids, and hoping to finish his career in Carolina after saying the team had depth and up-and-coming stars and could challenge.

Steve Mitchell, a fifth-generation farmer at Boglily Farm, embraces digital and social media to promote The Buffalo Farm, including a Facebook plea when calf Bert escaped. The farm won the 2016 Scotland Food & Drink Excellence Award in the Meat category and gained credibility with bigger customers. The 2018 awards are seeking entries.

Witnesses said a white van mounted the curb south of Finch and struck pedestrians along the sidewalk on Yonge St., with people hit, bodies on the ground and blood visible. Yang said he and his wife saw at least 10 people hit; other witnesses described the van zigzagging and hitting people. Police said the van and driver were in custody but did not know the motive or cause. Sunnybrook hospital received 10 patients: two were pronounced dead, five were critical and three were serious. North York General Hospital received four patients. Three injured were Seneca College English Language Institute students. Police created a witness hotline and web portal. The investigation was expected to take days and shut down a busy stretch of Toronto. The TTC initially shut down subway service between Finch and Sheppard stations. The city set up emergency social services at Mitchell Field Community Centre. Public Safety Minister Ralph Goodale said no information suggested the public was at risk or a connection to national security.

Edmonton officials call the city’s road-salting pilot a success, but chemical engineer Arthur Potts told council it is too early. He said Edmonton saved $4.2 million in operating costs, while private vehicle owners will face ten times that in damage; liquid calcium chloride is more invasive than traditional salt, causing rust and concrete damage. The city reduced sand use by 68 per cent. Environmental impacts are unknown, preliminary snow-dump data suggest comparable salt content, and collision statistics are unavailable. Committee was to debate and vote.

A recent experiment tested Waldo, an AI tool that reviewed over 430,000 past Reddit posts about cannabis. It flagged more than 28,000 as potentially describing unexpected or harmful side effects; researchers checked 250 flagged posts and verified 86 percent represented problematic experiences. Waldo was trained on 10,000 posts, outperformed ChatGPT but not human reviewers. Researchers suggest such scanning could help public health workers, though its usefulness for other substances is unknown and future use would require ethical privacy protections.

Global migration has reached historic levels, with an estimated 244 million people living outside their home countries and approximately 60 million migrants displaced by wars. The U.S. withdrew from U.N. discussions on a global migration compact, saying the process was inconsistent with U.S. law and policy and could undermine U.S. sovereignty and border enforcement. The U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops expressed disappointment and urged reconsideration, citing Catholic teaching that nations may regulate migration but also have obligations to protect migrants’ rights. Pope Francis supported the U.N. conference in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico, calling for migrants and refugees to be welcomed, protected, promoted and integrated. The negotiations were an intermediate step toward the 2018 Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration, based on the 2016 New York Declaration. Some groups applauded the U.S. withdrawal on sovereignty grounds, while U.N. officials and analysts said international cooperation is necessary and that states would implement the framework consistent with their sovereignty. Commentators discussed balancing national sovereignty with the universal common good.

A quartet from King Edward VI Grammar School in Louth won second place in the national schools University Challenge. After beating St Ivo and Nottingham High School, they reached the finals at the University of Lincoln, losing to Southend High School for Boys 315–280. Their headmaster praised their performance.

Indian Railways adopted a policy: “if no bill, your food is free,” displayed on trains to protect passengers from overcharging. Railway Minister Piyush Goyal made the decision so passengers insist on bills. By March 31, all trains serving food on payment basis should implement it. IRCTC is publicising the message and deploying inspectors to ensure fair prices and bills. Overcharging is the biggest train-food complaint, with over 7,000 complaints from April to October; two caterers’ contracts were terminated and caterers fined 5,000 times.

The government shutdown is worsening America’s air traffic controller shortage: controllers are expected to work without pay, staffing is down 50% in some areas, and sick calls are delaying flights. The shortage predates the shutdown due to costly, lengthy training; high washout rates; pandemic-paused training; retirements; a mandatory retirement age of 56; and an FAA hiring limit of age 31. Controllers earn an average of $144,580 annually, and the profession is projected to grow 3% from 2023 to 2033, with 2,200 openings per year.

Hascall Steel Company is a US steel service center offering diverse inventory and steel processing. It provides cost-effective solutions, partners with steel producers and suppliers, and carries products including cold reduced, blanked, slit, and flat-rolled steel coils. It selects and processes inventory to specifications and tests quality. With over 45 years, it offers competitive rates and in-demand products and services.

Mixed-precision Tensor Cores are used in HPC through iterative refinement methods. The TCAIRS solver in cuSOLVER automates mixed precision; a fusion reaction study showed 3.5x speedup on V100 with FP16 Tensor Cores, and the same technology tripled Summit’s HPL-AI performance. CUDA 11.0 cuSOLVER adds A100 TF32 support. In 37 SuiteSparse tests, TF32 delivered the fastest and most robust results, lowest iterations, and a 2.0X geomean speedup over FP64, versus 1.9X for FP16 and 1.8X for BF16; large complex 40K matrices reached up to 4X with TF32. Applications extend to sparse problems and other numerical methods.

A100 introduces Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity with a 2:4 pattern, compressing weights, reducing data footprint and bandwidth, and doubling Tensor Core math throughput by skipping zeros. A dense-training, pruning, and fine-tuning recipe yields virtually no inferencing accuracy loss. Sparse MMA skips zero entries for a 2x speedup.

The architecture combines L1 data cache and shared memory to 192 KB/SM versus 128 KB/SM on V100; separate FP32 and INT32 cores allow simultaneous execution at full throughput. It includes 40 GB HBM2 with 1555 GB/s bandwidth, ECC, a 40 MB L2 cache that is 6.7x larger than V100’s, two L2 partitions, 2.3x L2 bandwidth, L2 residency controls, and Compute Data Compression. Tensor Core improvements include 108 SMs, data sharing across 32 threads, fewer instructions and register accesses, async copy, asynchronous barriers, and higher L2/DRAM bandwidth.

MIG can partition each A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances with isolated memory paths, QoS, and fault isolation; GPU Instances contain GPU slices and Compute Instances, and support MPS, migration, and multi-tenant/single-tenant use cases. Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth, and PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 and supports SR-IOV. Error/fault detection, isolation, and containment are included. Additional features include NVJPG decode, Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomics, and NVDEC.

CUDA 11 supports task graphs, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency control, and Cooperative Groups. DGX A100 delivers up to 5 PFLOPS with eight A100 GPUs, NVLink/NVSwitch, MIG up to 56 accelerators, and an NGC-based software stack. Appendix B discusses pruning, fine-grained versus coarse-grained sparsity, and 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity with reported accuracy.

The document provides SanDisk’s 1-year limited warranty for original end users, excluding third-party software/content and damage from misuse, improper installation, unauthorized repair, modification, or accident. This paper describes a Training of Trainers (TOT) intervention in Palghar District, western Maharashtra, focused on maternal and newborn health. The intervention scaled up a Pune pilot project with support from UK technical experts and involved two phases: preparing for scale-up and developing local master trainers. A six-step approach included pre-TOT screening, TOT with pre- and post-assessments, staggered induction, continuous support from Pune core trainers, virtual quality assessment by UK experts, and virtual refresher training. Eight Pune core trainers helped develop 32 Palghar master trainers—25 medical doctors and seven general nurse midwives—who trained 505 health providers over 18 months. Post-training assessment scores for clinical knowledge and skills were significantly higher than pre-training scores. Palghar master trainers reported increased clinical competency, confidence as trainers, and career recognition and motivation. The discussion notes the importance of trainer selection, adult-learner-centric pedagogy, longer time frames, hybrid training platforms, and an enabling ecosystem, and calls for further evaluation of long-term effects and costing.

The passage introduces T-Tamer, a general theoretical framework for bi-objective trade-offs in cascaded inference. It formulates routing and termination as costly exploration over a DAG, where nodes represent sub-models and edges encode precedence, cost, and Markov dependencies. The framework uses a weighted sum of two proxy losses controlled by λ and distinguishes no-recall from with-recall strategies. For no-recall, it proves an information-theoretic impossibility: no constant-factor approximation to the offline optimum is achievable, even for two nodes and bounded distributions. For with-recall, it develops a dynamic indexing strategy for the directed-line setting that achieves online optimality and can be computed via dynamic programming. This is extended to directed trees and the transitive closure of a directed line, remaining theoretically optimal and polynomial-time. Experiments evaluate recall-based dynamic indexing on synthetic data and real-world CV/NLP early-exit workloads, reporting accuracy–latency trade-offs. T-Tamer is presented as a model-agnostic, plug-in, provably efficient framework for cascaded inference.

Evidence for dark matter has grown since Coma cluster velocity dispersions and spiral galaxy rotation curve discrepancies. Particle and astroparticle experiments search for dark matter particles, with WIMPs as leading candidates and alternatives including axion-like particles, primordial black holes, warm dark matter, self-interacting dark matter, and modified gravity. Coordination efforts include LHC BSM/DM/LLP working groups, PBC FPC, EuCAPT, iDMEu, DMDC, EOSC, OSCARS, and ESCAPE. The ESCAPE Dark Matter Test Science Project (TSP) uses EOSC/ESCAPE tools to store, distribute, and provide FAIR software and data for dark matter research, focusing on ATLAS, DarkSide, KM3NeT, Fermi LAT, and CTA. It develops workflows for summary plots, direct detection exclusion curves, gamma-ray and neutrino analyses, and common VRE tools such as Baler, Aladin Lite, Gammapy, and Jupyter tutorials. The review also covers astrophysical constraints from gravitational lensing and dwarf spheroidal galaxies, and tools including pyHalo, GAMBIT, AxionLimits, and the Dark Matter Limit Plotter. The TSP has focused on particle and astroparticle experiments and now seeks to incorporate astronomical dark matter searches. The review encourages astronomers to use ESCAPE services to combine complementary constraints from astronomy and particle physics.

The passage introduces the empirical stochastic inverse problem (eSIP), in which unknown physical parameters in Λ are inferred from observations of a quantity of interest \(Q(\lambda)\) using a process model. It adopts a statistical Bayesian approach where the inferential target is a distribution of parameters, defining the eSIP and the abstract stochastic inverse problem (SIP). Using disintegration of measures, the paper states main results: a unique posterior solution under general conditions with an explicit nonparametric density formula, almost-everywhere continuity of the posterior density, maximum entropy for the uniform prior solution, and an importance-sampling numerical estimator that is asymptotically unbiased and strongly consistent. AMD’s ASP verifies AMD signatures on AMD-owned boot firmware and, for SFS updates, verifies AMD’s signature before applying each package, acting as AMD’s root of trust for detection. AMD’s policy is that the system designer (OEM/ODM) owns the firmware root of trust for update; unless AMD PSB is enabled, the system designer is also responsible for detection of its own firmware. Early OEM/ODM x86 code has full ROM access and must enable restrictions such as AMD ROM Armor before untrusted code runs. SFS allows runtime updates and lets OEM/ODM co-sign packages; during early boot OEM/ODM may present a public key, after which ASP requires updates signed by AMD and countersigned by OEM/ODM. Customers maintain co-signing keys, and AMD does not countersign customer keys. SFS updates are non-persistent, re-applied after reboot, applied sequentially, and may patch registers, firmware images, or portions. BIOS enables SFS via APCB tokens, both off by default. Customers provide RSA keys during early boot/SMM setup before BOOT_DONE and cannot update them later. Co-signing uses 2048- or 4096-bit RSA and RSA-PSS. SFS verifies versions, dependencies, and signatures; SEV updates auto-commit and prevent rollback, requiring reboot to revert, while SNP requires HV-FIXED pages via RMPUPDATE. Attestation data/evidence is requested via interfaces, and some attestation schemes prevent certain updates. Commands require aligned TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER and a deployment agent; ASP verifies signatures, loads/runs the patch, updates patch level, and returns status.

The article examines HF-band RFID/NFC wireless communication, in which a reader transfers data and power to a passive transponder. It states NFC increases battery drain in mobile devices and aims to reduce this consumption through power-management algorithms. It presents three investigations of magnetic field strength scaling for power-aware RFID systems: during card detection, during communication, and with multiple transponders. It describes the PTF-Determinator method for field strength scaling during card detection, including electrical characteristics, parameter gathering, physical relation factor approximation, integration into the RFID communication flow, and a PTF library. Related work covers acquisition of the physical relation factor, transponder power requirements, multiple transponders, and system-based power management. A case study reads digital business cards and includes a maximum transmission distance restriction. Simulation and measurement compare operation with and without the PTF-Determinator. Simulation shows up to 80% transmission energy savings at close distance; measurement shows about 26% savings when x<=xmax and about 75% when x>xmax. A state-of-the-art NFC smartphone measurement shows reading increases power consumption up to 107%, and the proposed method could reduce battery drain by up to 13%, or 39% with power cutoff. Future work includes improving approximation and verifying communication and multiple-transponder scaling.

They aim to spread awareness of New Zealand’s mental health crisis and youth suicide statistics, encourage young people to talk about mental health and seek help, and reduce shame and stigma. They cite other Kiwis who have spoken up and express hope that the 2010s will be defined by open discussion of mental health. The passage also lists helplines for mental health support.

The paper reports results of a study of a multitopic mobile app for chronic disease self-management that included a module providing individually tailored sleep psychoeducation to older adults with chronic health conditions and low health literacy. Participants were aged 40 or older, had at least one ongoing chronic health condition under treatment, had less than a college graduate education, and scored below a health literacy cutoff. Assessments occurred at baseline, post-intervention, and three months later. The sleep module included the Insomnia Severity Index, tailored content, feedback on depression and stress, sleep stages, the two-process theory, chronic health conditions and sleep, sleep hygiene, sleep logs, and sleep restriction.

Of 286 individuals who completed baseline assessments and the sleep module, 195 had ISI scores of 8 or greater and were the focus of the report. Most identified as BIPOC, and 61% reported annual incomes below $10,000. Analyses showed SES, health literacy, and total health conditions were significantly associated with sleep quality over time. The intervention effect on PSQI was statistically significant, with a small to medium effect size (d = 0.40), and a model-corrected PSQI decline of 0.85 points. The authors conclude that a brief intervention offering personalized sleep information at appropriate reading levels may help improve sleep, though limitations included reliance on a single self-report sleep measure, other intervention modules, and a primarily low-income and minoritized sample.

The speaker praises a player’s puck handling, skating, physical play, composure, and playmaking, and says he has proven to be a competitive goalie Detroit can count on. He calls Pittsburgh a loud, difficult road building and says the team must be patient, disciplined, protect the puck, manage the ice, and avoid giving quality chances. He discusses the challenge of repeating, the addition of Hossa and his determination, pressure on elite players, and playing in Pittsburgh against an old team. He emphasizes team play, sacrifice, will, and determination over personal stats, and says momentum occurs during games. He also praises a two-way player, along with Pavel, as a best defensive and offensive player who can play any situation, check Crosby, and lead.

The lecture discusses pleat folding, especially the hyperbolic paraboloid made from concentric square creases and diagonals with alternating mountains and valleys, which self-folds into a saddle. A circular version requires a center hole. It explains paper’s elastic and plastic behavior, simulations of pleated models, origami skeletons, hyperhedra, curve-crease sculptures, glassblowing experiments, and the model’s Bauhaus history. It then proves that the concentric-square pattern cannot be properly folded into 3D without added creases; triangulating with diagonals enables construction by intersecting three spheres. Interval arithmetic is used to verify triangulated models up to certain ring counts and angles. The negative result relies on straight creases remaining straight and polygonal boundaries staying flat, so interior faces remain rigid. It also mentions open pillow/tea-bag problems and efforts to recreate David Huffman’s curved-crease origami.

After hours of strong storms, new showers are entering the Houston area. A Severe Thunderstorm Warning is in effect until 9 a.m. for counties north of Houston, with threats including damaging winds, quarter-size hail, heavy rain, and isolated tornadoes.

Adoree’ Jackson said the Titans had not practiced their final offensive play. Mike Mularkey said the team had practiced the play before, but not in the lead-up to Sunday. Cameron Wolfe reported Jackson said they just told him his route. The Titans ran a pass to rookie cornerback Jackson, who had zero career receptions, in a crucial situation. The passage questions using him there given Tennessee’s other pass-catchers and hopes Jackson and the coaching staff get on the same page.

Max Correa, an Appalachian State freshman biochemistry major with no familial ties to Kansas and who has never visited the state, announced his candidacy for Kansas governor. Kansas and Vermont have no age requirement for governor; Correa said he launched his campaign after finding no regulations regarding human candidates. His campaign appeals to younger generations and draws on Jewish concepts, including tikkun olam and kibbutz, with a plan for communal settlements to help reduce college costs. If elected, he would leave App State, move to Topeka, and enroll part-time at the University of Kansas. He plans to address the opioid crisis by offering state-owned properties to pharmaceutical companies to lower Narcan production costs. Political science professor William Hicks influenced his run and supports young people in politics.

Algoma Public Health turns 50 and partners with Healthy Kids Community Challenge Sault Ste. Marie for Get Active Algoma, encouraging community activity away from screen time. Participants join via GooseChase, complete missions, earn points for contest entry. The contest runs March 19–May 31, 2018, with a $600 bike voucher and other prizes.

The passage is an FAQ about Micro E-mini futures. It states CME Group launched them in 2019 to make futures accessible to retail traders with low capital. They are 1/10th the size of E-mini futures, trade on CME Globex, and are mostly financially settled. Initially for S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq 100, and Russell 2000, they later covered assets such as bitcoin, copper, crude oil, Treasury yield, and FX futures. They have lower margin requirements; for example, Micro E-mini S&P 500 represents $5 times the index, while E-mini S&P 500 represents $50 times the index.

A Micro E-mini futures strategy is a method for trading these contracts, often with technical and fundamental analysis, position sizing, and risk management. A backtest example uses E-mini Nasdaq 100 because Micro history is shorter; the strategy enters at the close and exits after 24 hours, with rules not revealed. Seasonality and price factors depend on the underlying asset. Trading hours for Micro E-mini S&P 500 are Sunday–Friday, 6:00 p.m.–5:00 p.m. ET, with a one-hour break; CME ClearPort has a different schedule.

Contract specifications vary by asset. For Micro E-mini S&P 500: quarterly contracts listed for five consecutive quarters; one unit is the index value multiplied by $5; quotation is USD and cents per index point; minimum fluctuation is 0.25 index points ($1.25) for outright trading and 0.05 index points ($0.25) for calendar spread; settlement is financial; trading terminates at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month. Settlement procedure is cash based on special opening quotes. The biggest risk is adverse price movement, especially with leverage. CFDs may track Micro E-mini futures and can be traded indefinitely, unlike futures with fixed expiration. Other details, such as all-time highs/lows, prices, symbols, ETFs, and trading charts, depend on the asset involved or are referenced to external charts.

Stochastic Texture Filtering introduces randomness into texture sampling to reduce aliasing and moiré when traditional filtering is impractical, and can provide higher-order filtering at the cost of a single point sample, running fast on Blackwell GPUs. Neural Radiance Cache uses a neural shader to cache and approximate radiance, taking path-traced rays after one bounce and inferring final lighting for real-time global illumination and dynamic lighting; it trains tiny neural networks on live game data. RTX Skin brings film-rendering subsurface scattering to real-time path tracing for translucent materials. RTX Neural Faces uses a real-time generative AI model to infer natural-looking faces from rasterized faces plus 3D pose data, trained on offline images and TensorRT optimized. Blackwell GPUs include GB202, GB203, and GB205. GB202 has 92.2 billion transistors and is used by RTX 5090. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors and is used by RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti. GB205 has 31 billion transistors and is used by RTX 5070. The document also includes spec comparisons and legal/trademark notices.

Napheesa Collier criticized WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert in her exit interview, accusing her of negligent governance and saying the league has not sufficiently addressed officiating, player compensation, and the overall product. Collier alleged Engelbert privately told her Caitlin Clark and other young standouts should be grateful and “on their knees,” and that only losers complain about refs. Engelbert said she respects Collier but is disheartened by how their conversations were characterized, and remains focused on the players and league’s future. The dispute comes amid collective bargaining negotiations and scrutiny of Collier’s roles with the players union and Unrivaled.

Daniel Jones, a 31-year-old British expatriate, was given a one-year suspended prison sentence in Cambodia after being convicted of using “pornographic” photos to promote a Siem Reap pool party. He had been arrested with 10 foreigners in January. The court found him in breach of decency laws; his lawyer said he would see if Jones wanted to appeal.

Van Buren communicated to the House of Representatives further correspondence between the Secretary of State and the British minister concerning Alexander McLeod. Fox acknowledged Forsyth’s letter stating the President would not comply with the demand to liberate McLeod, imprisoned at Lockport, New York, on charges of murder and arson related to the destruction of the Caroline. Fox expressed regret, said he would await orders, and protested language about the Caroline. Forsyth replied that evidence of the outrage had been presented to the British Government with a demand for redress and that further discussion was neither useful nor proper.

A 50-year-old grandmother, Kay Frazier, who married American prisoner Gary Frazier and visited him in Nebraska, died after a blood clot in an artery caused a brain blockage. During risky surgery, her artery ruptured; she died two days later. The clot was believed natural, and the coroner has not yet returned a verdict.

The author decluttered his house by discarding McGill University law schoolbooks bought over 50 years earlier, after reviewing them and recalling cases from contract, property, and tort law. He recycled the books, noted a used hardcover listed for over $1,000, and kept one thick volume to use as a reading stand.

Opponents were aggressive in front of him, fighting on him on purpose, falling on him, and pushing his teammates onto him while he was down, which he calls dangerous. He does not want teammates to hit Eddie from behind or do slicings, but says they should be more aggressive in front of Eddie. He expects similar play, wants teammates to clear space, and says referees should call penalties. He likes to play the puck behind the net and in corners, especially at home, and notes different ice and bounce conditions in Dallas versus Buffalo. He feels good and his groin is okay.

The speaker assumes the duties of President of the United States, relying on the support of countrymen and the guidance of Almighty God. He cites business depression, idleness of willing labor, losses to enterprises, and industrial disturbances requiring speedy relief. He calls for revision of the financial system, government supervision of currency, an enduring monetary basis, and possible commission study of coinage, banking, and currency laws. He supports international bimetallism and keeping silver at par with gold while preserving the Government’s credit, currency integrity, and obligations. He urges economy, reduced expenditures, adequate revenue, no deficit or increased debt, tariff taxation protecting American interests and labor, and reciprocity. He notes the depression’s severity on workers and small farmers and says reviving manufacturing would relieve both. He calls for law and order, courts rather than mobs, enforcement against trusts, improved naturalization and immigration laws, education, civil service reform, and restoration of the American merchant marine. He advocates peace, non-interference, and arbitration, urging ratification of a treaty with Great Britain. He will convene Congress in extraordinary session on March 15, 1897. He concludes by congratulating the country on fraternal spirit and pledging to preserve the Constitution.

The teams match up closely with similar styles, and an emotional game is expected. The team recognizes its errors and lack of intensity, seeks correction and better effort, and capitalized on a fortunate break. It only began creating chances in the last seven minutes by winning battles and getting pucks to the net, aiming to stay poised and continue that play.

An international team confirmed large quantum systems obey quantum mechanics using Bell’s test across 73 qubits, proving genuine quantum correlations that cannot be explained classically. By minimizing energy, they measured energies far below classical limits, with a 48-standard-deviation difference. They also certified genuine multipartite Bell correlations up to 24 qubits. The study shows quantum computers are becoming more authentically quantum and could improve secure communication, cryptography, and quantum algorithms.

Advanced attacking runs in soccer require offensive players to make conscious decisions to create opportunities ahead of play. They include individual, planned, and supporting runs. Individual runs include blind-side, drawing defenders out, inverted, overlap/underlap, third attacker/third-man, late, and deep-lying runs. Planned runs include designed set plays, runs to receive specific passes, and fast breaks. Supporting runs include back-pass options, square-pass options, and swinging the ball. Other considerations include offside, timing, and unpredictability. Coaching tips state that an effective attacking run requires a completed pass; only one run receives a pass at a time, but all players should complete their runs, and players should scout defenders’ strengths, weaknesses, and tendencies.

This study examines factors medical students consider when deciding whether to report mistreatment. Although mistreatment is prevalent and associated with psychological effects, burnout, decreased empathy, and career regret, reporting remains low. The authors conducted peer-to-peer, semi-structured interviews with 21 current medical students at one institution who had experienced mistreatment. Participants described 34 incidents; 12 were reported and 22 were not. Inductive analysis identified four factor groups influencing reporting: personal, situational, structural, and climate. Personal factors included fear of repercussions, sense of justice, and lack of motivation. Situational factors included mistreatment type and severity, ambiguous definitions, confidant opinions, bystander inaction, and perceptions of the perpetrator. Structural factors included belief that no action would be taken, logistical barriers, and lack of communication about outcomes. Climate factors included a hierarchical culture, expected abuse, powerlessness, and doubt that reporting could change the culture. The discussion states that the hierarchy of medicine can perpetuate mistreatment and prevent reporting, and that few factors motivated reporting. Recommendations include improving reporting systems, transparency, anonymous retaliation reporting, swift responses, bystander training, and top-down culture change. Limitations include a single institution, self-selected volunteers, higher reporting incidence than the general population, and incidents mostly in clinical settings. Future research should examine mistreatment climate and witnesses. The conclusion states that multiple factors affect reporting, with sense of justice and negative bystander effects unique to this study, and that targeting institutional culture may improve reporting and learning environments.

A new paper argues that the Eldgjá eruption, estimated from spring 939 to autumn 940 CE and the largest known lava flood eruption of the Common Era, may have encouraged Iceland’s Christianisation. Researchers cite the 10th-century Völuspá, which describes eruptive and meteorological effects and the pagan gods’ end, suggesting it drew on first-hand experiences and intentionally stimulated conversion. The eruption’s ash lowered temperatures and hindered agriculture. The paper concludes the eruption acted as a catalyst for cultural change, with official conversion in 999/1000 CE; later traditions, including Kristni saga, also associated conversion with volcanic events, likely Eldgjá.

Honor launched the Honor 9i in India on October 5, marking its third anniversary. It is described as the world’s first smartphone with a FullView display and four cameras. It is a rebranded Huawei Maimang 6/Nova 2i, featuring a 5.99-inch FullView IPS LCD, metal body, dual 13MP+2MP front and 16MP+2MP rear cameras, Kirin 659, 4GB RAM, 64GB storage, and a 3,340mAh battery. It costs Rs. 17,999 and may become a top mid-range smartphone.

The passage argues that remaining coal lands should not be alienated. Coal lands indicated by the Geological Survey have been temporarily withdrawn from settlement; legislation should withdraw them from sale or entry except in special cases, leaving ownership with the United States. The government should not work them but allow private individuals to do so under a royalty system, with control to prevent excessive consumer prices and to supervise common carrier rates and conduct. This is analogous to forest land withdrawal, treating coal as public property for public benefit. Congress has advanced national control over interstate corporations through the railway rate bill, pure food bill, and beef-packing inspection; further measures may wait, though labeling dates and charging inspection costs to packers may eventually be advisable. The interstate commerce law did not ruin railroads or accomplish nothing: earnings and dividends rose, and many voluntary freight and fare reductions occurred. The passage calls for enlarged Interstate Commerce Commission powers and more complete national control over interstate corporations, including preventing excessive overcapitalization and requiring disclosure of stockholders, properties, and business through subsidiaries or affiliates, to stop inordinate profits and abuses. It says this is not socialism or a destruction of individual initiative, but a way to avert agitation for government ownership and remedy abuses, while unregulated competition can itself destroy competition and individual character.

This email announces a weekly jobs bulletin for Haas alumni, provides instructions for submitting job openings with location, title, company, degree, and contact information, and lists brief and expanded postings from employers including Kaiser Permanente, University of Michigan, United Nations Foundation, Micron Technology, Informatica, PG&E, Blue Shield of California, ePocrates, an unnamed online comparison shopping service, iVenturi, Extensity, Fremont Group, and Research Dog. It also includes alumni notes information, an online survey, a Big Game BBQ event notice, subscription instructions, and a disclaimer that listed companies and search firms have not been researched by the Haas School.

Delta reported record revenue and beat earnings forecasts, driven by premium and corporate travel. CEO Ed Bastian projected full-year adjusted EPS around $6, at the upper end of guidance. For the quarter ended Sept. 30, adjusted revenue was $15.2 billion and adjusted EPS $1.71. Premium seat revenue rose 9% to nearly $5.8 billion, corporate travel rose 8%, and main cabin sales fell 4% to about $6 billion. Delta now expects premium seat sales to overtake main cabin in 2026, earlier than previously expected. It cited strategic route cuts and premium focus. Shares rose as much as 6%, and analysts viewed the results as a bellwether.

An Energy Central Daily News email dated January 24, 2002, addressed to Paul D. Thomas at Enron, contains electric power and gas industry headlines and articles. Top electric power stories include congressional subpoenas for Arthur Andersen witnesses, Florida Power rate cuts, Long Island’s competitive power market, and revised NRC standards for a nuclear waste site. Gas stories include Enron India fields, possible Las Vegas natural gas rate declines, and Providence gas contract talks. It also covers Enron investigations, restructuring, California ISO load forecasts, rates, projects, financial results, and international energy news.

This article presents research from D’harawal Country in south-west Sydney, where Indigenous community members were asked what education grounded in Indigenous knowledges could look and feel like. It states that schooling in so-called Australia causes ongoing systemic harm to many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students, while Indigenous peoples have practised education successfully for tens of thousands of years. Author Michelle Bishop, a Gamilaroi woman, applies Indigenous, decolonising, and relational theories and methodologies to re-present a vision of Indigenous education sovereignty through story.
