The passage presents MOTO, a multi-objective three-layer optimization framework for systematic local-landscape mapping around a given minimum. Its components are a multi-objective explorer that proposes diverse feasible initial guesses; a bilayer minimum-mode kernel using HVP-based direction optimization and outer minimum-mode-force ascent to locate index-1 saddles; and deterministic two-sided minimum-mode descent to certify connectivity. MOTO is benchmarked on atomistic spin systems and a Cartesian Ni(111) heptamer. The passage reports scaling to 10^6 spins while computing the two lowest curvature modes with less than 1 GB incremental memory and 0.5 s wall time, and says the HVP kernel reduces incremental peak memory and gives a ×10 speedup versus an explicit-Hessian approach on identical hardware. It reports transition-state networks in an artificial Bloch-type spin model, a DFT-parameterized Pd/Fe/Ir(111) model, and a Ni(111) heptamer, including meron–antimeron-mediated skyrmion duplication, chiral-droplet formation, boundary-defect-induced topological-charge change, and up to 32 pathways between a biskyrmion (Q=2) and bi-antiskyrmion (Q=−2). It also notes limitations involving mask and multi-objective target selection, kernel hyperparameters, and near-degenerate curvature.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended April 30, 2017. The filing includes unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and management’s discussion and analysis. For the first quarter of fiscal year 2018, revenue was $1,937 million, gross profit was $1,150 million, income from operations was $554 million, net income was $507 million, and diluted net income per share was $0.79. The passage discusses the debate over Google’s firing of James Damore for a memo criticizing diversity initiatives and claiming biological sex differences explain women’s underrepresentation in tech, including claims about interests, neuroticism, and status drive. It says evidence challenges fixed sex differences: alleged cognitive differences are not clear-cut, brains are a mosaic of male and female characteristics, and the brain is plastic and changed by experience. It describes stereotype threat and self-critical views as affecting performance and brain activity, and says empowerment training can alter brain activity. It concludes that Damore’s assumptions of fixed, unchangeable differences are wrong and that diversity training aimed at changing the environment may be appropriate.

Lamar Jackson suffered a hamstring injury in the third quarter of Baltimore's Week 4 loss to Kansas City and did not return after being listed as questionable. The injury's severity is undetermined; reports indicate he could miss 2-3 weeks or be considered week-to-week, likely miss Week 5 against Houston, and have his Week 6 availability in doubt. As a government shutdown and lapse in Medicare’s Covid-era hospital-at-home waivers loom, home hospital programs are halting admissions. UMass Memorial stopped admitting patients Saturday; it cares for about 20 patients daily, and losing the beds strains overcrowded facilities. CMS said Medicare-funded hospital-at-home patients must be discharged or returned to a medical center by midnight Tuesday absent congressional action. Hackensack Meridian stopped admissions and discharged its census; ChristianaCare stopped Medicare admissions but continues other insurers; Mass General Brigham reduced its census from 60 to 40. There are estimated 1,000 such beds nationwide, concentrated in capacity-constrained areas. Experts call hospital-at-home a partial remedy for crowding. The waiver, tied to a stopgap funding bill, expires Sept. 30; a bipartisan five-year extension is under consideration. Leaders cite uncertainty and disruption.

This study examines EFL pre-service teachers’ and teacher educators’ perceptions of ICT and CALL integration in tertiary EFL initial teacher education in Vietnam. It uses Hong’s (2010) model of CALL technology integration, which includes CALL teacher education, individual factors, and contextual factors. A convergent mixed-methods design was used at a teacher education institution in southern Vietnam with 67 final-year EFL pre-service teachers and 3 EFL teacher educators. Data came from a survey, a focus group interview, and individual interviews; quantitative data were analyzed with SPSS, and qualitative data with NVivo and inductive thematic analysis.

Findings show that most pre-service teachers perceived a high presence of opportunity to learn CALL-related knowledge (M=3.05), including digital media technology competences and ICT pedagogies (M=3.33). High opportunities included searching for teaching materials, downloading resources, using word-processing software, creating lessons with downloaded texts/pictures/graphics, and using data projectors. Lower opportunities included blended learning modules, standard software/media players, coordinating project work with digital media, using classroom digital equipment/mobile/tablet for language learning, organizing computer files, setting/supervising online work, selecting/using online exercises, and troubleshooting classroom digital equipment (M=2.28). Pre-service teachers mainly used ICT for resource discovery (94.0%), archiving lessons and information exchange (91.0% each), and developing pedagogical materials (79.1%), and less for communication with colleagues, personal planning, and organization. Educators reported using ICT weekly, with some using it in every lesson.

Factors affecting ICT integration included individual educator obstacles (skills, knowledge, confidence, and fear of change), provision of infrastructure (unstable internet, unreliable equipment, slow technical support), EFL pre-service teacher-related obstacles (attitudes, interest, readiness, disengagement), and CALL technology integration policies (no official requirements or guidelines; encouragement only). The conclusion states that opportunity to learn CALL-related knowledge and policies on technology pedagogies contribute to ICT/CALL integration, and these components are interdependent. Limitations include a small number of participants, a single southern Vietnamese institution, no examination of educators’ evaluation of ICT integration, and no exploration of how program curriculum affects practice.

In Flinn’s Estate, the court addressed when intact value should be fixed for trust stocks and how undistributed earnings should be allocated between life tenants and remaindermen. The court held that intact value is generally fixed as of the testator’s death, and that the will did not postpone the trusts or require a later date; otherwise income would accumulate illegally under the Act of 1853. For stock held by Booth & Flinn Company and later received by the executors as a dividend, the court held the company was a separate entity and fixed intact value at the book value when received. The court also accepted the lower court’s per diem averaging of Gulf Oil’s yearly earnings. The decree was modified and affirmed.

The passage argues that global citizenship education has developed a diverse literature focused on global challenges, responsibility, participation, and issues such as environment, human rights, and development. However, it says this literature offers insufficient guidance on why violent international conflict occurs, how citizens may relate to it, and the conditions for peaceful cooperation, especially given tensions with China and the war in Ukraine. It proposes supplementing global citizenship education with theories of international politics—realism, regionalism, and institutionalism—to understand anarchy, security, power, regional integration, institutions, conflict, and cooperation. It also discusses global public goods, state foreign policy objectives and tools, and citizen engagement. The passage concludes that global citizenship education should expand its agenda to include military and economic security, foreign policy, cooperation conditions, and didactical implications such as institutional arenas, history, and propaganda, while retaining its values and ambitions.

The speaker says the team does not need more motivation and may have been overmotivated the previous night, taking penalties, so it needs to calm down and return to its proper play. They credit their season-long penalty killing and coach Mike Ramsey’s adjustments, stressing patience and not overcommitting against quick-moving opponents. They also credit the defense’s strong low play and outlet passes, note the opposing power play’s talented players, and say the key to tomorrow’s penalty killing is staying out of the box.

The passage compiles telegrams and documents from November 1918 about the signing of the armistice. President Wilson announces that the armistice was signed and that America’s war aims were accomplished, calling for assistance in establishing just democracy. Edward House sends praise to Wilson. Secretary Lansing sends congratulations to British and French officials, while French, Japanese, and Greek representatives express congratulations, thanks, and admiration for America’s contribution. Wilson also tells Lloyd George he admires the temper and purpose of his address.

The study explored using music software as a contemporary strategy in a general music education course at a Caribbean university for pre-service early childhood and primary teachers. The existing course used traditional methods and limited technology, mainly Canvas. The study used mixed methods and a phenomenological approach with 24 participants. Data came from a questionnaire and an assignment using Sibelius to compose eight bars of music in specified time signatures and note values. Results showed most participants rated the course “very good”; software ratings were mostly “fair”; most said software enhanced understanding; half were comfortable using it; motivation responses were mostly neutral; 67% supported continued technology use; and 75% wanted training. The assignment was completed to 90% accuracy, with four non-submissions. Recommendations included continued selective software use, training, technology in practicum, and technology-based assessments. The conclusion stated music software was relatively easy to integrate and positively impacted student outcomes.
Order dismissing habeas corpus and remanding relator affirmed; Manning dissents.

Using NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope, an international team led by Northwestern University identified the progenitor of supernova SN2025pht in mid-infrared light for the first time. Combined with Hubble archival observations, the data showed the blast came from a massive red supergiant in spiral galaxy NGC 1637, about 40 million light-years away, wrapped in dense dust. The star was brilliant and intensely red, radiating roughly 100,000 times more light than the Sun, but dust made it over 100 times dimmer in visible light. Its dust was unusually carbon-rich, suggesting convection brought carbon to the surface. The findings support the idea that many massive red supergiants do explode but are hidden by dust, explaining why they are rarely seen as supernova progenitors. JWST’s infrared vision allowed this first confirmed detection. The team is searching for similar stars, and NASA’s upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope may help.

The author says readers prefer accurate reports over deadlines and he will aim to send most by 1pm. For a company where he holds a short position, CEO Oozi Cats resigned after an independent review found a US fraud indictment was knowingly withheld from advisers. Share price was 145p, market cap £188.2m.

ECG signals provide information about heart processes and are used to investigate normal and pathological heart conditions. Deviations from the normal ECG pattern are empirically interpreted as ECG abnormalities. The mechanisms behind ST elevation, ST depression, and atypical T-wave morphologies remain unclear, and the QT interval is influenced by heart rate and corrected using formulae such as Bazett’s or Fridericia’s, though QTc has issues.

This study presents the “Simplified Egg and Changing Yolk Model” to explain ventricular repolarisation and T-wave formation. The model represents heart muscle as an egg shape with Wilson’s Central Terminal at its centre. Repolarisation expands from the WCT outward, and a lead detects a one-dimensional signal along its vector. Signals produce positive or negative deflections, with net deflection calculated as LDT = ST – SA. Initially balanced signals yield an isoelectric ST segment; when the signal reaches the asymmetrical “T-zone,” a net deflection generates the T-wave. Damage or non-electrical regions can cause ST depression or ST elevation depending on their location relative to the WCT and lead. The model can reproduce higher, flattened, inverted, and biphasic T-waves.

The model suggests repolarisation starts with the Q-wave and continues through the T-wave, treating the ST interval and T-wave as a unified process. It challenges conventional interpretation of ST depression/elevation and supports the QTp interval (Q-wave start to T-wave peak) as more reliable than QTc, especially for arrhythmia risk and medication effects. The model applies to ventricular repolarisation, while principles apply to other leads with orientation considered. Future work includes U-wave origin, atrial repolarisation, and coronary artery distribution. The conclusion states the model enhances understanding of T-wave morphologies and could improve ECG interpretation, diagnosis, risk stratification, and patient management.

The disclosure describes computer-implemented methods and interactive game systems for creating a virtual game environment from a real-world scene by scanning physical objects with a capturing device to obtain a digital three-dimensional representation, converting that representation into a virtual toy construction model made of virtual toy construction elements, and defining game-controlling elements using information on physical properties. It also describes selecting and arranging physical objects, conversion rules, recognizing known physical objects, creating or modifying the virtual environment in response to recognized objects, and cyclic gameplay involving physical and virtual playable characters. Further embodiments relate to voxelization of mesh representations, mapping surface points to voxels, assigning voxel attributes or palette colors, and apparatus, data processing systems, and computer program products for performing the methods.

This article uses Hodgson and Spours’s four-level lifelong learning ecology to explore the experiences of leaders of education-related undergraduate provision in further education colleges in England. It discusses the macro, exo, meso and micro layers, including widening participation, foundation degrees, top-up degrees, and partnerships between further education institutions and higher education institutions. Drawing on a BESA-funded project with an online questionnaire of 70 programme leaders and follow-up interviews, the article focuses on further education-based leaders and compares them with higher education-based leaders where relevant. Findings describe programme leaders’ routes into the role, qualifications, small staff teams, line-management responsibilities, and poorly defined roles. It identifies three strands of responsibility: administrative and organisational demands, learner support, and pastoral care. The article concludes that further education programme leaders act as a “keystone species” within local learning ecologies but face competing demands, tensions with further education regulations, and limits on scholarly engagement, suggesting a need for better “sightlines” beyond their institutional contexts.

UAE announced the Mars 2117 Project to build an inhabitable human settlement on Mars by 2117, unveiled by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum at the World Government Summit. It will partner with international institutions, focus on faster travel, and begin with Emirati scientists before expanding internationally. The UAE plans a Mars Probe landing in 2021. Gbenga Ogundele, also known as Benson Ogundele, was sentenced to 234 months in federal prison, and his wife, Moji Popoola, also known as Mojisola Oluwakemi Tin Popoola, was sentenced to 18 months for conspiracies to commit wire fraud and money laundering in an internet dating scam. Ogundele was also convicted of aggravated identity theft. Ogundele was ordered to forfeit $2,195,103.36; Popoola was ordered to forfeit about $165,000 and pay $34,100 in restitution. Co-conspirator Victor Oyewumi Oloyede was sentenced to 234 months, while Olusegun Charles Ogunseye, Olufemi Wilfred Williams, and Adeyinka Olubunmi Awolaja Jr. each pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering. The passage describes a compound represented by Chemical Formula 1 and an organic light emitting device including a first electrode, a second electrode facing the first electrode, and one or more organic material layers between them, where one or more organic material layers include the compound. A woman with MS says Delta employees tied her to a regular wheelchair with someone else’s blanket because no strapped chair was available; her son reported bruises. Delta expressed regret and offered 20,000 SkyMiles, but the family wants policy changes.

Waghorn returns to the Stadium of Light with Ipswich Town on Saturday, looking to spoil Ball’s afternoon. Waghorn left Sunderland in 2010 and has scored for several other clubs. GPS technology has led more truck drivers to use a steep, winding section of Arkansas 43 through Ponca in Newton County, causing brake failures and crashes. Truck traffic in Ponca has increased from about six unusual trucks a year to at least six a day, and seven trucks wrecked on a 2-mile stretch north of Ponca over 2½ years. Drivers said GPS or Google Maps showed a straight route and did not reveal the steep hill. Residents and officials say pedestrians are at risk. The Highway Department plans warning signs near Arkansas 103 reading “Crooked and steep next 3 miles. Drive with care,” though a practical detour is considered difficult.

No external funding was received; study costs are limited to investigators’ salaries paid by the orthopedic department. The protocol has privacy identifier p-2023-14990 and was not yet uploaded to OSF. This non-peer-reviewed medRxiv preprint was posted January 4, 2024. The study concerns total hip arthroplasty (THA), periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), and revision approaches: DAIR, one-stage exchange, and two-stage exchange. It aims to describe trends in revision types for PJI after primary THA and the risk of a second revision. Methods: a descriptive, register-based cohort protocol using Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register data from all public and private orthopedic departments in Denmark from 1995 to 2022. Eligible participants are adults ≥18 undergoing primary THA; exclusions are hemiarthroplasty or simultaneous bilateral arthroplasty. Follow-up starts at primary THA and continues until death or first revision, up to 28 years, with at least 90 days. Outcomes include yearly revision numbers overall and for PJI by surgical approach and time since primary surgery, plus risk of second revision after each approach. Analysis uses R and Cox proportional hazards adjusted for calendar time, age, and sex. Results will follow STROBE, including patient flow and Kaplan-Meier plots. Strengths include multiple revision methods and a long data period; limitations include private-clinic completeness and surgeon-reported PJI. Findings are from Denmark and may differ elsewhere.

A floor cleaner is described including a base pivotally coupled to a body, a supply tank, a recovery tank, and a vacuum source. The supply tank stores cleaning fluid, and a distribution nozzle dispenses the cleaning fluid onto a surface. The vacuum source includes a motor and fan and draws cleaning fluid through a suction inlet into the recovery tank. The base includes wheels, a brushroll, a handle with a grip and actuator, and a battery. The passage describes center-of-gravity arrangements relative to a handle axis, a steering axis, the battery, supply tank, recovery tank, and vacuum source. The battery is in a battery chamber with a battery door.

The recovery tank includes a tank body with a lower end wall, a sidewall extending to an open upper end, and an inlet duct extending upwardly from the lower end wall. A cover is removably coupled to the open upper end and includes a lid seal, a baffle, a suction air outlet, a cage, a filter aperture, and a filter. The baffle has arcuate redirecting surfaces and inhibits fluid from traveling into the suction air outlet. The cage has side and bottom apertures, a lip, and optionally a screen. The filter includes a frame, filter media, a tab, and angled sidewalls.

The recovery tank further includes a shutoff float and a strainer. The shutoff float has a float body, a closure, and an extension, with the float body having an aperture that receives the inlet duct. The float moves along the inlet duct, and the closure closes the suction air outlet when fluid exceeds a desired level. The strainer is movable from a lowermost position to a removed position and includes a perforated body, an aperture, and a handle. The inlet duct extends through the aperture, and the strainer engages an outer surface of the inlet duct. The baffle is positioned to inhibit splashing against a portion of the handle. The tank body includes a strainer lip that spaces the perforated body from the lower end wall.

The body includes a recovery tank recess with an inlet and an outlet, and the recovery tank includes a latch received in a latch recess. Projections and corresponding recesses hold the cover relative to the tank recess. The body is pivotable about a first axis between upright and inclined positions and about a second axis to steer the base. A link or yoke connects the body and base, includes stops limiting pivoting movement, and has an opening through which a suction conduit passes. The yoke may be hollow with chambers for a conduit and wires.

The brushroll has an outer cleaning medium including a hydrophobic textile material, optionally a tufted fabric of hydrophobic fibers, and may include hydrophobic coatings. Bristles may be hydrophilic and fixed relative to the base. The brushroll cover is removable and includes first and second actuators sliding in opposite directions to unlatch latches, a spring biasing the actuators, and cam surfaces for reattachment. The distribution nozzle is attached to the brushroll cover and connects via fluid couplings with seals. Lights coupled to a PCB are directed toward the front side to illuminate the spray pattern, and indicator lights may respond to actuator, pump, flow sensor, or vacuum source operation.

The base includes a first squeegee contacting the surface and a second squeegee contacting the brushroll. The first squeegee pushes fluid toward the suction inlet, and the second squeegee wipes fluid and debris from the brushroll toward a suction conduit. The first squeegee may be removably coupled with bristles on a brush bar. The second squeegee is located above the first squeegee and attached to the brushroll cover. Rollers extend from the lower end, and a secondary distribution nozzle may be positioned under the cover. A brushroll cover embodiment has a raised front edge exposing the brushroll. The brushroll may include first and second sets of fibers with different colors, diameters, lengths, and a helical pattern, and may include a sleeve between the spindle and fiber backing.

Before a July 2, 2018 FIBA World Cup qualifier in Bocaue, Bulacan, Australia dominated Gilas Pilipinas. Leam Richardson dismissed the tunnel incident after Wigan Athletic’s match against Fleetwood as minor and not comparable to the Manchester United-Manchester City spat. This study used Q methodology to examine teachers’ opinions on culturally responsive education in the Turkish Education System. Data were collected from 21 public-school teachers in Denizli, Mardin, Erzurum, and Şanlıurfa using 30 Q statements and a forced-distribution Q sort, analyzed with Ken-Q Analysis. Findings yielded three factors—Unification, Student Support, and Teacher Support. Factor 1 participants most agreed that inequalities exist between different cultures and that local culture is promoted in visual media, while disagreeing that local-culture values and beliefs are disseminated. Factor 2 participants most agreed that equality of different cultures is emphasized in education, while disagreeing that local-culture characteristics are examined in the curriculum and that different cultures are a threat. Factor 3 participants most agreed that cultural diversity is important in visual media and that inequalities exist, while disagreeing that teachers are encouraged to use different-culture examples in the curriculum and that elective courses allow experiencing different cultures. Consensus included increasing students’ cultural competence skills, presenting general-culture life practices, and focusing on academic and social development of local-culture students; disagreement included measures against discrimination, seeing different cultures as a threat, and class as a reflection of society. Participants declined to explain their extreme statements. The study concludes that the Turkish Education System views diversity as richness but is not fully culturally responsive, with deficiencies especially in student and teacher support, and recommends workshops, professional development, and greater inclusiveness. Limitations include participant hesitation and the participants’ location in the south-eastern region.

This application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 17/224,999, filed Apr. 7, 2021, which is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 15/159,074, filed May 19, 2016, now U.S. Pat. No. 10,983,626, and claims benefit of U.S. provisional patent application No. 62/171,634, filed Jun. 5, 2015. The passage explains Gary Antonacci’s dual momentum strategy, which uses absolute and relative momentum to select assets. It aims to buy assets with positive absolute and relative momentum and, where possible, short assets with negative absolute and relative momentum. It covers momentum formulas, types of momentum, implementation with ETFs, sector rotation, examples such as S&P 500 vs. gold and crude oil vs. natural gas futures, and backtest/performance results, including the Global Equities Momentum model and related caveats.

The Break, a longtime restaurant and billiards hall in Birmingham’s Five Points South, will be demolished for high-rise apartments. Some welcome the change amid declining crowds, while others want affordable housing instead of expensive rents. No closure date is set; management was unavailable.
Neiman Gracie dislikes Dillon Danis’ trash talk; after Danis declined a Bellator 180 fight, Gracie will face Dave Marfone on June 24 and says 0-0 Danis must fight first.

Researchers found hotter temperatures lead to worse exam grades. Using scores of over 10 million secondary students over 13 years, they found each half-degree rise in average annual temperature equaled a 1% drop in average exam scores; air conditioning can buffer this. In the UK, June exams coincide with temperatures at which negative effects begin. Changing the academic year is complicated by aligned schedules and rigorous simultaneous marking, though grade boundaries based on average scores may prevent long-term disadvantage.

The advance-decline indicator, also called the advance/decline index or AD line, is a market breadth indicator that plots the cumulative difference between advancing and declining stocks, usually daily. It reflects market sentiment, confirms index trends, and may predict reversals when it diverges from the index. Advance/decline issues list advancing and declining stocks, while advance/decline volume compares advancing and declining volume. The NYSE A/D line applies this to NYSE stocks. A backtest using the S&P 500 ETF SPY had 229 trades, an average gain of 0.6%, and a profit factor of 1.55; it was not particularly successful, and many strategy versions failed to produce a good trading strategy.

Dive operators disagree over tourism impact after ex-HMAS Tobruk landed on her side. Glenn Bowman says income could fall 50 per cent because the starboard side is inaccessible to most divers. Ed Gibson says open divers can still see propellers and rudders, tourism will thrive, and tours will adjust; both call the dive spectacular. Keith Pitt's office could not comment after the 2016 handover. Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service says inspections are underway and a report is coming.

A compilation of July 10–11, 2001 news items and transcripts focuses largely on California’s failed federal settlement talks over electricity refunds. California sought $8.9 billion from wholesale power suppliers; after 15 days, Judge Curtis L. Wagner Jr. ended talks and indicated refunds would be closer to $1 billion or less, with possible offsets for amounts suppliers said they were owed. Wagner planned to recommend applying FERC’s price-control order retroactively to October 2, while California sought refunds from May 2000. Gov. Gray Davis and state officials said they would pursue the remainder in court; generators disputed California’s analysis. Other Western states also sought refunds. Related reports covered Calpine’s purchase of natural gas reserves, Edison International’s improved finances but uncertain utility future, warnings that the Western grid was overloaded and needed investment, House GOP efforts on limited energy bills, a Texas brochure contrasting Texas and California electricity markets, an interview with Shaw Group’s CEO, a New York Times article on Peruvian shepherds in California, and Edison’s financial transactions.

Generative AI and LLMs bring transformative changes but also legal and ethical challenges, including misinformation, deepfakes, and bias. Regulation must balance innovation with risk mitigation. Governments and companies have introduced laws and responsible AI principles, but gaps remain between industry and government and across countries, causing inconsistent regulations and compliance costs. At the micro-level, LLM risks may emerge only in real use, such as jailbreaking prompts. The passage calls for human-centered, safe, secure, and trustworthy AI, with partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers; forward-looking rules; and governance combining top-down and bottom-up approaches involving regulators, developers, users, and communities through transparent issue reporting and timely regulatory updates.

The passage profiles wealthy or celebrity women who launched businesses. Millie Mackintosh, a Quality Street heiress and Made In Chelsea star, launched an eponymous fashion range in 2014; it made a £182,833 first-year loss, and liquidators were later brought in for debts of £548,000. Ella Mills, the wealthy “Deliciously Ella” blogger, set up The Mae Deli in 2015; its first year lost £723,811, and two London delis were announced closed, while her separate Deliciously Ella business made £545,497 profit. Petra and Tamara Ecclestone started fashion and haircare businesses: Stark was put on hold and later wound up with debt, while Tamara Ecclestone Brands made growing losses and was restructured and renamed. Salem announced Tuesday its drinking water is contaminated; residents drove to Woodburn for bottled water. Salem and Oregon OEM do not plan coordinated distribution points. Grocery stores report bottled water shortages; Costco and Roth’s expect shipments but don’t know timing. An algae bloom in Detroit Lake is producing low levels of cyanotoxins. The paper studies learning LTLf formulas from traces: given disjoint positive and negative trace sets, find a minimal-size LTLf formula satisfied by all positive traces and none of the negative traces. It surveys LTLf learning motivations in software engineering, programming languages, formal methods, cyber-physical systems and robotics, and AI. It describes the VFB algorithm, based on combinatorial search, fast evaluation via characteristic tables, and observational equivalence. The key idea is to treat Boolean operators differently from temporal operators and use Boolean Set Cover to combine enumerated LTLf formulas with ∧ and ∨. The paper defines Boolean Set Cover, gives a polynomial criterion for solution existence, introduces domination, divide-and-conquer, and a beam-search algorithm. It implements the tool Bolt and consolidates a benchmark suite of over 15,000 LTLf learning tasks. Experiments compare Bolt with Scarlet and a GPU algorithm: Bolt solves more tasks and returns smaller formulas on average than Scarlet, is competitive with the GPU algorithm, and an ablation shows Boolean Set Cover helps solve more hard tasks. The paper argues Boolean Set Cover is fundamental and may have applications beyond LTLf learning.

This article explains American football offensive positions. The offense’s goal is to advance the ball and reach the end zone, or kick a field goal if within range. It describes the quarterback as the offense’s leader, who touches the ball every play, analyzes the defense, throws or hands off, and may call an audible. The running back carries the ball, catches passes, blocks, and protects the ball. The tight end is versatile, combining receiver and lineman duties; tight ends can be attached or sniffer/H-back. The offensive line has five players: two tackles, two guards, and a center. They block on running and passing plays; left tackles protect the quarterback’s blind side, guards double-team and pull, and the center touches the ball every play and directs the line. Wide receivers catch passes, run routes, create space, and block; types include split end/X, flanker/Z, and slot receivers.

The passage advises ending a job interview by leaving promptly, avoiding lingering or desperate self-promotion, conveying confidence, shaking hands, and saying it was nice to meet you. It says not to ask when they will get back to you or make a decision, since they often do not know and may lie.

New research by Adam Anderson, published in Psychological Science, finds people interpret emotions through eye expressions, a process that began as a universal reaction to environmental stimuli and evolved to communicate emotions. Participants associated narrowed eyes with discrimination-related emotions such as disgust and suspicion, and open eyes with sensitivity-related emotions such as fear and awe. The work builds on Anderson’s 2013 research and supports Darwin’s theories that expressions originated for sensory function rather than social communication. Using models of six expressions, participants accurately discerned six basic emotions from eyes alone. Eye openness was most closely related to reading mental states; eyes offered more robust emotional indications than other facial areas. Anderson says eyes evolved for sight but are now essential for interpersonal insight.

Fund shortages and teachers’ involvement in SSLC evaluation and election work led Karnataka’s primary and secondary education department to drop this year’s summer camps for government school students; an official said a cancellation announcement will be made soon. The camps began in 2017-18 and were held last year at 7,049 schools.

A study commissioned by Vegreville, Alta., says moving the federal immigration case processing centre to Edmonton by the end of 2018 would cause population loss, lower property values and higher unemployment. The town and the workers’ union oppose the closure.

Brendon Naidoo, boyfriend of DJ Zinhle, was granted R50,000 bail at Alexandra Magistrate Court. He faces multiple fraud counts in a foreign-exchange trading scheme, must report to Sandton Police twice weekly, and is due back in court May 5.

This study isolated Enterobacteriaceae from untreated wastewater in Western Uttar Pradesh, India, during 2020–2021. Of 150 isolates, 62% were E. coli, 24% K. pneumoniae, 8% other Enterobacteriaceae, and 6% mixed/unidentified. Overall, 111 (74%) isolates were resistant to one or more antibiotics, and 88 were ESBL producers. MDR was found in E. coli (57.14%), K. pneumoniae (28.57%), and Pantoea agglomerans (5.71%). Zone 1 had the highest MDR percentage; Zone 3 had the most MDR E. coli. Colistin resistance was observed in Zones 1 and 2 and in Pantoea spp. The passage links AMR in wastewater to COVID-19 antibiotic use and inadequate wastewater treatment in India, recommending periodic surveys and molecular characterization of resistance genes.

The Court of Appeals affirmed Anthony Davis’s and Eric Simmons’s convictions for Class A felony conspiracy to deal in cocaine in excess of three grams and affirmed Davis’s enhanced sentence. It found sufficient evidence supported the convictions based on the specific facts and alleged overt acts despite no individual transaction exceeding three grams, held the verdicts were not so inconsistent as to require reversal, and concluded the trial court did not err in enhancing Davis’s sentence.

Construction of Fort Buford began in 1866 near Williston at the Missouri and Yellowstone Rivers. It was a military post until 1881, when Sitting Bull surrendered there. Soldiers provided food by gardening, fishing, or hunting; a lack of fruits and vegetables caused scurvy, and there were no trained cooks. Steamboat supplies ended when the Missouri froze. Problems included boredom and alcohol. A 1876 report described insanity and the post library. Fort Buford was abandoned; a museum opened in its old headquarters in 1963.

Flippy, a burger-flipping robot developed by Miso Robotics, has begun work as a grill cook at Caliburger’s Pasadena restaurant after months of practice. It can grill 150 burgers per hour and uses sensors, cameras, AI, and detachable tools, but still requires a human coworker for some tasks. Caliburger has exclusive rights for six months; the robot costs about $60,000 and is currently in one restaurant, with expansion plans after a trial. Miso and Caliburger describe it as part of a human-robot kitchen, though fast food is vulnerable to automation.

John Essey’s suburban Pittsburgh home uses Internet-of-things devices to control lights, thermostat, locks and detect leaks. Critics fear such devices may be insecure and used by companies to spy for profit. Gierad Laput and Carnegie Mellon researchers created a single wall-plugged 2-inch sensor that monitors room vibrations, sounds, light and more, identifying activities like a blender running or a light being on, with domestic and commercial uses. Security expert Bruce Schneier says surveillance is the Internet’s business model and device makers don’t prioritize security; he cites concerns over Roomba mapping and warns of a world-sized robot.

The device supports reset isolation for the PCIE module, allowing the PCIE Subsystem to be reset without resetting the rest of the device. When acting as a Root Complex, software can reset it through the PRCM after putting it in IDLE and ensuring no ongoing PCIE transactions; after reset, bus enumeration should treat all Endpoints as newly connected. When acting as an Endpoint, an in-band reset generates an interrupt; software should put the subsystem in IDLE and assert the PCIE local reset through PRCM. Device-level resets except Test Reset also reset PCIE, so a Hot Reset to downstream devices and bus re-enumeration are required upon reset exit. EMAC Switch reset isolation lets the device undergo resets except POR without disrupting the switch or routed traffic when ISO_CONTROL is set; isolated switch/PLL, some control module registers, and some pin multiplexing are unaffected, while the switch is always reset when not isolated. RSTOUT_WD_OUT reflects reset status, is asserted on Watchdog Reset, and is 3-stated during POR/RESET; BTMODE[11] affects its assertion. Emulation and Trace Logic is reset only by three reset types, and EMU[4:2] multiplexing is reset by all system reset types except Test Reset. Power domains have dedicated Warm and Cold Resets with defined conditions. At reset, I/O pins enter Hi-Z with exceptions for emulation pins, EMAC Switch pins, RSTOUT_WD_OUT, and DDR pins; PINCNTL registers reset, IPU/IPD resistors are enabled, and the Boot ROM modifies PINCNTLx registers. Reset timing, clocking sources, PLLs, SYSCLKs, module clocks, interrupt mapping, and peripheral timing/data are also specified for DCAN, EDMA, AET/trace/JTAG, EMAC/MDIO, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, HDMI, HDVPSS, video DAC, I2C, ISS, and DDR2/DDR3 memory controllers.

The study examines how science education contributes to citizenship education in Turkey by analyzing the science curriculum and interviewing eight science teachers. Thematic analysis identified themes including scientific literacy, technology, society, environment, values, skills, and problems. Findings indicate that both the curriculum and teachers connect science and citizenship mainly through scientific literacy, society, and environmental issues, while the technology link is weaker. Teachers viewed scientific literacy and environmental awareness as important for active citizenship and cited values and skills such as responsibility, critical thinking, inquiry, and problem-solving. However, they reported that practical citizenship goals are hindered by infrastructural deficiencies, an exam-focused education system, curriculum and student readiness issues, and challenges involving refugee students. The study concludes that science education can support citizenship competencies and calls for greater curricular emphasis on citizenship skills, socio-scientific topics, environmental education, teacher training, and alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals.

Demetrious Johnson seeks an 11th title defense against Ray Borg, while Tony Ferguson fights Kevin Lee for the interim lightweight title, with the winner possibly facing Conor McGregor.

AI literacy is a topical issue in digital literacy research. AI enables personalized educational experiences, customized materials, feedback, and may increase children’s engagement and motivation. Early AI literacy is increasingly considered part of digital competencies, and educational robots are used in preschool education. Examples include iRobiQ, NAO, Keepon, KASPAR, AIBO, Iromec, Paro, Probo, PaPeRO, EngKey, RUBI-6, and iCAt. These robots can support inclusive education, emotional and social development, behavioral therapy, pro-social skills, STE(A)M, and language learning.

The study aimed to determine future preschool and primary school teachers’ perceptions of robots and their pedagogical implications. It used a mixed-method approach. The initial sample was 143 students; after identifying 22 misconceptions, the final sample included 121 students—75 future preschool teachers and 46 future primary school teachers. Participants drew robots, described environments and roles, and explained their choices. A DAAT-Checklist was created for coding, and two evaluators had high agreement (Pearson correlation 0.99).

Results showed most respondents had accurate robot conceptions. Misconceptions were classified as incorrect humanoid appearance, electrical appliances, virtual reality, and avatar; electrical appliances were most common (68.18%). Robot appearances were animal (47.1%), typical (24.8%), mechanical object (24%), and humanoid (4.1%). Most drawings showed neutral emotion (76), followed by positive (44) and negative (1). Functions were educational (64), assistive (38), game (6), communicative (2), and other (11). Of those with accurate conceptions, 98 had real-life experience, 21 media experience, and 2 none; 61 encountered robots at the Faculty of Education. Reasons for depiction involved cognitive (41), affective (28), behavioral (20), and 32 unestimable domains. The conclusion states most future teachers had accurate understandings, recommends more frequent and purposeful use of educational robots, curriculum development, and attention to safety, privacy, accessibility, and teacher competencies.

The Packers agreed to a deal with veteran tackle Byron Bell, adding competition to an offensive line with questions at right tackle. Bell previously played for Carolina, Tennessee and Dallas. Bryan Bulaga, recovering from a torn ACL, is part of the team’s plans; Jason Spriggs and Kyle Murphy are other options. Bell could start the season opener against Chicago.

Out of bounds situations are a major part of the game, and teams must prepare to inbound from the baseline, sideline, and full court while knowing the rules. The primary objective is to inbound successfully and then get a high-percentage shot to the best players; plays should be simple and practiced. Inbounding requires vision, communication, execution, timing, cuts, screens, passes, and reads against defenses, plus defensive balance and safety outlets. Automatic reads include cutting to the basket, a give-and-go, or a lob depending on the defender. The passage also lists rules about the five-second count, inbounder movement, timeouts, over-and-back, direct out-of-bounds passes, baseline running after made baskets, and technical fouls for reaching over the vertical plane, and recommends scouting opponents and testing players’ rule knowledge.

The passage discusses how 4IR, artificial intelligence, and machine learning are influencing education toward Education 4.0, requiring changes in curricula, pedagogy, and assessment. It notes a shift from rote learning to personalized teaching and from memory-based to skill-based assessment. The National Education Policy 2020 recommends games and gamification as innovative pedagogical approaches. Digital games in teaching-learning can increase motivation, provide immersive and multimodal learning, and support competency-based approaches. Digital game-based learning can use existing commercial games or customized games designed for learning outcomes and assessment. Digital games and stealth assessment use gameplay data, AI/ML algorithms, evidence-centered design, and feedback to assess cognitive and non-cognitive skills. Challenges include limited teacher use, the need for multidisciplinary development, cognitive load, difficulty calibration, concerns about brain effects, and the need for more research on validity and reliability.

The passage discusses experimental studies of neutrino oscillations. Neutrino sources include supernova explosions, Big Bang relics, cosmic ray showers, the sun, accelerators, and nuclear reactors. Experiments consider length, energy, and sensitivity to mass ranges. Solar neutrino experiments found fewer electron neutrinos than expected; SNO measured total neutrinos consistent with theory, indicating flavor change. Atmospheric experiments found muon neutrinos disappear. Accelerator experiments use near and far detectors to study appearance/disappearance. Reactor experiments study anti-electron neutrino disappearance via inverse beta decay.

The Medina City School District has a 5.2-mill permanent substitute levy on the May 8 ballot to replace a 5.9-mill operating levy expiring in December. Kids First Medina held a rally; supporters said it is not a new tax and a bond issue will drop off Dec. 31, slightly decreasing taxes. The levy would maintain programs and add French and all-day kindergarten, with City Council members voicing support.

Students wore semi-formal attire, and tickets cost $20 through Communiversity. The Office of Communiversity organized the event, which included two dance floors—one with a DJ playing current hits and one with a live jazz combo—plus cartoon drawing, a photo area with a professional photographer, outdoor seating overlooking the pool and city views, and a piano room. An Ernakulam court convicted Muhammed Ameerul Islam, a migrant labourer from Assam, for the rape and murder of a 30-year-old Dalit law student in Kerala. He was found guilty under IPC sections 302, 376 and 376(A), but not under section 201 or SC/ST Act provisions. The judge will pronounce punishment tomorrow. The crime occurred in Perumbavoor on April 28, 2016; he was arrested in Kancheepuram after 50 days. About 100 witnesses were examined.

The passage discusses the emergence of AI policy as a field, citing the EU AI Act, US executive orders, and increased mentions of AI in the Federal Register. It argues AI policy discussions are largely absent from CS curricula, leaving critical competencies underdeveloped. It synthesizes US and EU policy: US efforts are heterogeneous and lack comprehensive federal legislation, with executive orders oscillating between safety/trustworthy AI and economic/national security AI dominance; the EU AI Act defines AI systems, organizes them by risk, prohibits unacceptable risks, and imposes transparency requirements on general-purpose models. Three themes are identified: rapidly changing AI landscape, technical compliance with non-technical specifications, and cross-border implications. The paper proposes a framework for integrating AI policy discussions into CS courses through socio-political, translational, and technical perspectives and scope, power, and agency dimensions, embodied in guiding questions. It concludes the framework is flexible and context-agnostic, and suggests future work on curricular activities and requirements engineering.

When a penalty kick is awarded during normal play, it is a restart, and the ball is live once kicked. Attacking teammates other than the kicker and goalkeeper must be at least 10 yards from the penalty mark, behind the penalty mark, inside the field, and outside the penalty area. They must wait until the ball is touched and moves forward before entering the penalty area or arc. They must follow up saves, blocks, or rebounds and defend if the goalkeeper secures the ball. Sanctions apply if the kicker or a teammate offends.

An Italian man, Luca Traini, opened fire on African migrants in Macerata, injuring six in what police called a racially motivated attack. He also fired at Democratic Party offices. After being captured, onlookers said he made a fascist salute. The attack followed the arrest of a Nigerian migrant over the death of an Italian teenager. Traini had stood as a Northern League candidate. League leader Matteo Salvini distanced himself but blamed mass immigration, while Matteo Renzi and Prime Minister Paolo Gentiloni called for calm and action against violence. Tensions had risen after Pamela Mastropietro’s dismembered body was found and Innocent Oseghale was arrested.

Rutgers historian Mark Bray, author of a 2017 book about antifa, is trying to move to Spain after a far-right online campaign led to death threats and the posting of his home address. The threats followed Trump’s executive order seeking to designate antifa as a domestic terrorist organization and included a message saying, “I’ll kill you in front of your students.” A TPUSA Rutgers chapter petition and a Fox News story preceded further threats. Bray and his family were not allowed to board a United Airlines flight after their reservations disappeared, then were rebooked to Spain. Rutgers says it is gathering information; Bray reported the threats to police and plans to stay in Spain through the academic year.

The passage describes the ADS868xW data acquisition device. It covers an analog front-end with a programmable gain amplifier that converts single-ended or differential inputs and adjusts common-mode level for the SAR ADC; gain is set by RANGE_SEL[3:0]. A second-order anti-aliasing low-pass filter follows the PGA, typically with 500-kHz cutoff. An integrated ADC driver and selectable internal or external 4.096-V reference are provided. The device supports input and AVDD alarms, multiSPI communication with multiple SPI/source-synchronous protocols and daisy-chain topologies, RESET/ACQ/CONV states, data transfer frames, and configuration registers. It also includes application, power-supply decoupling, power-saving, and layout recommendations.

The passage presents a unified multiscale framework linking atomic solid-melt interface energetics to GaN and III-nitride epitaxy growth kinetics. MD simulations with MLIP show ordered liquid Ga layers and localized charge redistribution at Ga-polar and N-polar GaN(s)-Ga(l) interfaces. Metadynamics calculations give free-energy landscapes for N adatom adsorption and lateral and step-edge migration, revealing a “Ga lubrication” mechanism in which interfacial liquid Ga lowers N migration barriers compared with a clean surface. These barriers are used in KMC simulations, which indicate that GaN growth under typical MBE conditions is diffusion-controlled and layer-by-layer, while high N flux can produce rough joint-island growth. A diffusion-controlled growth model based on a modified Fick’s first law and chemical potential gradients predicts steady-state N flux and facet-dependent growth rates without fitted parameters. MBE-grown partially nitridated Ga/GaN particles are characterized by HAADF-STEM/HRTEM, and measured facet/orientation trends in GaN radii and growth rates are compared with model predictions. The predicted rates, about 0.01–0.04 nm/s, and facet trends generally agree with experiment. The work concludes that for systems with low key-element solubility, such as N in liquid Ga, the solid-melt interfacial free-energy profile for adatom adsorption and migration governs crystal growth kinetics and rate; the framework is transferable but has limitations including impurities, MLIP transferability, model assumptions, and facet-averaged experimental statistics.

The second defender provides individual support after the first defender is set. The support/cover defender positions behind and inside relative to the first defender, goalside and far enough back to react if the first is beaten; the inside position forces the dribbler outside. They maintain distance without overrunning, use the same stance as the first defender, announce their arrival, and adjust as the attacker and first defender move. When ready, they may tell the first defender to tackle. Communication is critical: support/help means coverage; jockey/delay/control/contain tells the first to manage and buy time; challenge/take/tackle signals support has arrived and an attempt may be made. If the first defender is beaten, the support defender likely takes over, possibly via a defensive switch; the second defender makes calls because they can see the field.

This study compared air-conduction (AC) and bone-conduction (BC) auditory steady-state response (ASSR) and auditory brainstem response (ABR) thresholds in infants aged 0–6 months with normal hearing (NH) or conductive hearing loss (CHL) confirmed by ABR. Sixty-four infants participated, and 50 completed testing. Thresholds were assessed at 500 and 2000 Hz, with CHL observed only at 500 Hz. AC ABR and AC ASSR thresholds were higher in the CHL group than in the NH group; BC ABR and BC ASSR thresholds did not differ significantly between groups. ABR and ASSR thresholds were poorly correlated, and ASSR thresholds showed greater variability. Air-bone gaps were larger in CHL than NH for both ABR and ASSR, but ASSR showed more overlap between NH and CHL groups. Minimum normal intensities were higher for ASSR than ABR. Screening measures had high sensitivity but poor specificity, while ABG and AC ASSR thresholds showed tradeoffs between sensitivity and specificity. The study concluded that ABR remains the gold standard and should continue to be used in EHDI programs, while ASSR requires more research for detecting mild low-frequency CHL.

Turing GPUs include dedicated ray tracing acceleration hardware and an advanced acceleration structure. Ray tracing and rasterization operate simultaneously and cooperatively in a Hybrid Rendering model. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, offloading the SM. Real-time ray tracing uses fewer rays per pixel with Turing RT Core acceleration and denoising. Turing ray tracing works with NVIDIA RTX, RTX libraries, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and the soon-to-come Vulkan ray tracing API. It can also accelerate physics, collision detection, particle simulations, audio simulation, AI visibility queries, and in-engine path tracing.

NVIDIA NGX is a deep learning-based technology stack using Tensor Cores. Its features include DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Mesh Shading introduces Task and Mesh Shaders. Variable Rate Shading controls shading rate per 16x16 pixel region and supports Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples shading from screen-space pixels. Multi-View Rendering allows multiple views in a single pass. Turing also supports bindless resource views and resource heaps. TU104, TU106, and Tesla T4 are discussed. RTX-OPS provides a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering. Ray tracing casts rays from the camera; BVH reduces intersection tests. Ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections are covered.

The Executive submits report extracts on Texas’s political, military, and civil condition. No Executive steps have been taken to acknowledge Texas independence. Congress previously resolved that independence ought to be acknowledged when satisfactory information showed Texas had a civil government capable of performing the duties and obligations of an independent power. The Executive continues its prior position. Acknowledging a new state is delicate, especially when it has forcibly separated from Mexico and Mexico still claims dominion; premature recognition could be regarded as a cause of war or unfriendly. U.S. policy avoids interference in foreign internal disputes and recognizes the prevailing party based on fact. On expediency, the President concurs that recognition is for Congress, without deciding the strict constitutional right. U.S. precedents with Spanish American states and Mexico waited until independence was secure. Although Mexico’s authority was expelled, its army defeated, and its leader captured, Mexico still appears to have greater force and threatens invasion, so Texas independence is suspended. Modeling nanoscale light-matter interactions is important for quantum technologies, but classical Maxwell solvers cannot capture nonclassical features, while quantum master-equation models often cannot account for propagation and interference in realistic devices and become computationally prohibitive. The passage introduces an SDE approach, without wave-function unraveling, phase-space representations, or operator-valued noise, and derives SDEs from master equations using drift and diffusion matrices. Conventional treatments use symmetric, positive semidefinite diffusion, but the work allows complex, non-symmetric diffusion to include asymmetric noise correlations. It considers a driven two-level system, validates the approach using the Mollow spectrum, and aims to bridge quantum emitter dynamics with classical fields and Maxwell solvers.

This study evaluates machine learning potentials (MLPs) for material surface properties by comparing training from scratch (TS), zero-shot pretrained universal interatomic potentials (ZS), fine-tuning (FT), and multi-head fine-tuning (MHFT). It benchmarks several pretrained UIP models on diatomic potential energy curves and selects MACE as the foundation model. Using surface datasets for gold, RuO2, and BiVO4, it finds that FT consistently outperforms TS and achieves comparable accuracy with fewer training data, while ZS gives reasonable predictions. Diatomic potential analyses show TS can produce unphysical short- and long-range behavior, whereas FT is more physically reasonable. In BiVO4, FT has the lowest force prediction error and fewer outliers than TS, although ZS has few outliers. Case 4 shows that FT exclusively on gold surface data can worsen predictions for other unary metal surfaces, while MHFT using gold surface data and MPTrj bulk data improves out-of-domain surface-energy accuracy over ZS and FT, but requires much more training time and slightly degrades accuracy on the fine-tuned gold surface. The study discusses catastrophic forgetting, alignment of computational conditions and energy references, and practical guidelines. Methodology uses ACEsuit/MACE with specified hyperparameters and VASP DFT calculations.

Human rights education and training (HRE) is part of lifelong learning and is often offered as a university elective or law school module, although human rights principles appear across higher education disciplines. Existing HRE models predate contemporary threats and cannot fully address climate change, humanitarian and refugee crises, digital misinformation, economic inequality, artificial intelligence, or decolonisation efforts. UN efforts and the “Learning About, Through and For” model have mainstreamed HRE, but teaching remains concentrated on international human rights law and offers limited engagement with politically sensitive, complex, or triggering historical cases. This risks retraumatising learners with lived or intergenerational trauma, especially given high rates of adverse childhood experiences among university students.

The article uses a structured literature review to examine trauma-informed human rights education (TIHRE). It defines trauma-informed practice in higher education as principles and pedagogies that promote healing and liberating learning for learners with complex trauma, and states that in HRE it can mitigate adverse responses and secondary or vicarious trauma for teachers and learners. It discusses trauma-informed practice in legal education and practice, learner groups at heightened risk, manifestations of trauma, and the SAMHSA six-part framework: safety, trustworthiness and transparency, peer support, collaboration, empowerment and choice, and recognition of cultural, historical and gender issues.

The article recommends that educators clarify and cultivate a rights-respecting teaching persona and values; embed trauma-sensitive principles in content design and lesson planning through student co-creation, project-based learning, a skills-rich curriculum, and reflective practice; and adopt dialogic teaching. It states that TIHRE should integrate the UN tripartite framework of education about, through, and for human rights, empower learners, avoid retraumatisation, secondary trauma, trauma porn, and romanticised trauma narratives, and use warnings, wellbeing check-ins, flexibility, and reflective resilience exercises. Dialogic learning should engage students with each other, practitioners, and survivors. The conclusion recommends examining teaching persona and values, embedding trauma-informed principles in content design, and encouraging dialogue with peers, practitioners, and survivors to empower learners and teachers as catalysts for hope, healing, and reconciliation, with wellbeing, agency, and dignity at the centre.

Using over 138,000 earnings press releases from 2005–2023, the study evaluates NLP methods, including LDA and BERT-family models, to predict earnings announcement date stock returns. It finds that soft information in press releases is about as informative as earnings surprises; FinBERT provides the most effective extraction, while LDA-based representations enhance interpretability. A rolling-window approach avoids look-ahead bias. Stock prices fully incorporate this soft information by market open, so trading strategies based on publicly released press release signals do not earn excess returns, supporting market efficiency; if the information is available in advance, traders can identify high-return stocks with better-than-random accuracy. Combining earnings surprises and soft information improves identification of top- and bottom-performing stocks.

The video has over 300,000 views, and police are asking people in British Columbia to view it. The victim remains shaken.

RSI as a mean reversion indicator does not work on Bitcoin or other tested cryptos, as buying low RSI readings and selling high readings produced weak results. However, RSI as a momentum indicator appears to work well on Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Doge, with one Bitcoin RSI(5) strategy outperforming buy-and-hold with lower drawdowns. The conclusion is that RSI seems to work on crypto and Bitcoin when used as a momentum indicator, not for mean reversion.

The manuscript aims to illustrate the value and potential of critical approaches to quantitative research and to guide the emergence of critical quantitative scholarship in education. It advances epistemological and methodological considerations to help scholars discern the use and value of critical approaches. Its primary audience is scholars who use quantitative methods and/or critical perspectives in education research, including undergraduate and graduate students, faculty, researchers, institutional research, evaluation, and assessment staff, and methods instructors. It also aims to help students and educators evaluate scholarship applying critical theories to quantitative methods and to encourage researchers to apply critical theories to their own quantitative studies.

The manuscript states that quantitative research is not objective and that quantitative researchers have implicit biases, assumptions, and perspectives. It says methodological self-reflection is essential, though quantitative researchers are rarely asked to situate their positionalities. The authors provide their own positionalities. Jay describes being a white cisgender queer researcher, identifying as a quantitative queer, studying queer and trans collegians with quantitative methods, interrogating survey design and the invisibility of queer and trans students, and seeking to dismantle white cisheteropatriarchal dominance. Jimmy describes being Vietnamese-Chinese American, critiquing the aggregation of Asian Americans in statistics, noting the model minority myth and masked inequalities, and emphasizing critical reflection in institutional research, assessment, and analytics to minimize harm and advance equity.

Quantitative criticalism is described as combining methods and epistemologies. Quantitative research is historically rooted in post-positivism and minimizing bias, while quantitative criticalists examine phenomena rooted in positionality and subjectivity, advocate social justice, and dismantle systems of oppression. Critical quantitative scholars challenge existing policies, theories, and measures and reexamine traditional questions for marginalized populations. The manuscript states that numbers are not neutral, analyses must account for systemic oppression, and descriptive statistics can unearth counterstories. It says researchers must engage in justice-driven scholarship throughout the research process, from research questions to data collection, analysis, and implications. It also emphasizes community, solidarity, transformational change, community partnership, data sovereignty, and transparency in authorship.

The manuscript names tensions in quantitative criticalism. These include white supremacist and cisheteropatriarchal notions embedded in statistics, citing Galton and Pearson and eugenics. It also discusses an unclear threshold of criticality, difficulty discerning authors’ intentions, and views that incremental change can be a tool of white supremacy. Methodological tensions include measuring social identities, essentialist and harmful demographic variables, limited statistical sophistication for intersectional and multiply minoritized respondents, underteaching of nonparametric analyses, individual-level frames that blame minoritized communities, and generalizability that centers white students and assumes homogeneity among BIPOC communities. The manuscript says tensions can be generative.

The manuscript reviews examples organized by critical race theory, queer theory, and intersectionality. It discusses Sablan’s QuantCrit and community cultural wealth study; Garvey’s study of sexual identity classifications using queer theory; Szymanski and Lewis’s study of African American women coping with gendered racism using intersectionality; and Wilson and Urick’s study using intersectionality, community cultural wealth, cultural reproduction theory, and latent class analysis. It examines benefits, limitations, and tensions in each, noting that criticality requires embedding theory throughout a study, that categorization can conflict with fluid identities, and that no consensus exists on integrating intersectionality into quantitative research.

The implications address scholars and methods educators, encourage incorporating methods and epistemology into curricula, and state that claiming expertise in quantitative criticalism is antithetical to critical thought. The authors offer musings on intentions, a threshold or continuum of criticality, and an intentional interplay between research, policy, and advocacy. They close with three questions about intentions for using quantitative criticalism, whether quantitative methods can be used for justice and liberation, and one’s threshold of criticality. The closing states that the goal is to advance social justice and equity, reclaim the power and influence of quantitative methods through critical frames, build a robust coalition, and center criticality in methods use and instruction. It says quantitative methods devoid of philosophical or epistemological groundings cause harm and are limited in generalizability and nuance, and that critical and conscious reflection must be at the forefront.

Poker is a family of card games, with no-limit Texas hold’em being its most widespread variant. It originated in the United States in the early nineteenth century, has tens of millions of players worldwide, and online platforms accelerated its spread since the early 2000s. Poker is a game of incomplete information with private cards and flexible bet sizes, producing an immense game tree. It has served as a testbed for game theory and artificial intelligence. Most progress has concerned two-player cash games, while tournament play differs because player counts and stack sizes change, maximizing chip expected value is no longer optimal, and hands cannot be considered independent and identically distributed. Spin & Go is a hyper-turbo three-player mini-tournament illustrating varying player counts and stack sizes.

Before regret minimization, computer poker used knowledge-based rules, heuristic evaluation, and equilibrium-driven abstractions. CFR was introduced in 2007. In 2015, Cepheus computed a near-perfect Nash equilibrium for heads-up limit hold’em. In 2017, DeepStack and Libratus achieved results in no-limit. In 2019, Pluribus defeated professionals in six-player no-limit Texas hold’em. LLM direct prompting for poker is limited; fine-tuning has been effective, and PokerGPT used low-stakes spectator data. SpinGPT uses Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Its data comprise 320,000 decisions from 8,800 Spin & Go games played professionally on PartyPoker.fr between 2018 and 2020 at €50, €100, and €250 buy-ins. Hand histories were anonymized, parsed, and transformed into structured text prompts. SFT used LLaMA-Factory with LoRA rank 8 and alpha 16, four epochs, and 10 hours on an NVIDIA A100. Offline RL used ORPO on 270,000 synthetic InstaGTO hands plus 50,000 human hands, adding 10 GPU-hours with QLoRA.

Evaluation used a Professional test set of 32,000 decisions and a Solver test set of 30,000 decisions. Metrics were exact accuracy, tolerant accuracy, macro F1, MAE, and MAPE. SpinGPT-SFT on Professional achieved 80% exact, 84% tolerant, 86% macro F1, 0.61 BB MAE, and 19% MAPE. Final SpinGPT on Professional achieved 79% exact, 83% tolerant, 84% macro F1, 0.30 BB MAE, and 12% MAPE. On Solver, SpinGPT achieved 72% exact, 78% tolerant, 77% macro F1, 0.93 BB MAE, and 35% MAPE. Illegal moves were 1.4%. Against Slumbot, after a heuristic all-in patch, SpinGPT-SFT won 13.4 ± 12.9 BB/100 over 30,000 hands. Final SpinGPT beat SpinGPT-SFT by 13.2 ± 7.24 BB/100 over 10,000 duplicate hands at 25 BB. Limitations include no final evaluation against Slumbot, LLM numerical errors and hallucinations, and estimated compute of 5.2 kgCO2e. Future work includes stronger models, higher-quality hands, RAG, chain-of-thought prompting, adaptivity, explainability, and coupling the LLM with a solver.

The passage lists 17 habits to avoid for weight loss or health. These include drinking water from plastic bottles; quitting sweets completely; being a perfectionist; emotional eating; consuming store-bought protein bars and energy drinks; eating sweets whenever desired; hanging out with the wrong people; measuring success only on weighing scales; taking meal-replacement supplements; removing carbs entirely; eating only fat-free or skimmed products; not getting enough sleep; eating too little while working out more; doing the same exercise routine for weeks; drinking calories; being too strict too soon; and copying someone else’s weight-loss routine. It recommends replacing plastic bottles with stainless steel; eating sweet fruits instead of artificial sweets; forgiving oneself; exercising instead of emotional eating; using coconut water or nuts as substitutes; eating sweets only before a workout; avoiding people who derail goals; sticking to a weight-loss routine as a success measure; eating real food; cutting refined carbs and using whole grains; including healthy fats; getting at least 7 hours of sleep; changing exercise routines weekly; eating proper meals; tapering meals; and tailoring a routine to one’s own body type, metabolism, and health status.

The MACD histogram is the difference between the MACD line and signal line; bars above zero indicate bullish momentum and below zero bearish momentum, with height showing momentum strength. The crossover strategy buys when the histogram crosses above zero and sells when it crosses below. The MACD-histogram trading strategy is a mean-reversion system: entry is on the close, long exit is the first day the close is higher than before, and vice versa for shorts. It generated 6,669 trades across 77 ETFs, with long positions better than short. A QLD backtest from 2007 had 85 trades, 2.2% average gain, 10.4% annual returns, 19% max drawdown, and was invested only 5% of the time.

NVENC adds H.265 8K 30 fps encoding and bitrate savings; NVDEC supports HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing supports USB-C and VirtualLink for single-cable VR. Onesmo Rupil, 23, started drugs about seven years ago. He was discontinued from the University of Dodoma in 2013, where he studied commerce and accounting, due to poor performance linked to substance abuse. His father cannot pay for his return. He recovered and manages Philimisana Foundation Sober House, home to about 30 young people in rehabilitation; most use marijuana because cocaine and heroin are expensive. The passage cites a UN report that marijuana was the world’s most widely produced, trafficked and consumed drug in 2010, with 119–224 million adult users. Dr Kassian Nyandindi says 2014 research found 550,000 people affected by drug abuse, about 25,000 addicts countrywide, and 3,500 receiving treatment; HIV infection among drug users is 20–50%. He says marijuana’s THC damages the corpus callosum and can cause mental disorders. Onesmo says he lacked principles and conscious contact with God. He used heroin, stole Udom students’ laptops, was arrested in 2015, detained six months at Isanga Prison, and recovered at Dar es Salaam rehabilitation centres in 2015.

Clinical practice guidelines face implementation challenges, especially in intensive care. This study developed and evaluated an automated system combining FHIR for computer-interpretable guideline representation and the OMOP CDM for patient data to monitor guideline adherence in intensive care. Six recommendations, mainly COVID-19-related, were selected and encoded. The system was implemented in five university hospitals and tested on 82,015 ICU episodes from January 2020 to May 2023. In validation at three hospitals, system accuracy was 97.0% versus 86.6% for human reviewers; system sensitivity was 81.4%, specificity 99.5%, precision 96.6%, and F1 88.3%. Human review of 18,115 patient days took 150 hours, while the system processed >2000 patient days per second. Most mismatches were rater errors; system errors mostly involved unstructured free-text data not transferred into OMOP. Automated adherence varied by recommendation and hospital, mostly 10–60%, except one negative recommendation. Factors included new COVID-19 recommendations, incomplete documentation, and imprecise guideline specifications. The study concludes the system is feasible, effective, scalable, and reliable for monitoring guideline adherence, though validation was retrospective and limited to a few recommendations.

A Journal of Climate paper by Nic Lewis and Judith Curry concludes that high future warming estimates from most computer climate simulations are inconsistent with observed warming since 1850, implying future warming will be 30–45% lower than suggested by the simulations. It derives median ECS of 1.66°C and TCR of 1.33°C using globally complete temperature data, compared with 3.1°C and 1.9°C for 31 CMIP5 models. The paper finds previous criticisms of its methodology unfounded and possible biases minor when using globally complete temperature data.

This statistical analysis plan describes planned summaries of plasma glucose concentration by treatment group and time point, including change from pre-dose and pharmacodynamic metrics, with mean and individual glucose concentration-versus-time figures. Safety analyses will use the safety set and cover extent of exposure, insulin administration before hypoglycemia induction, the hypoglycemia induction procedure, trial medication administration, post-treatment rescue glucose infusion, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory parameters, vital signs, ECG, and immunogenicity. Adverse-event summaries will focus on treatment-emergent AEs and include overview and frequency tables by MedDRA terms, with causal relationship and severity assessments. The plan also describes changes from protocol-specified analyses and appendices for data presentation, programming specifications, SAS programming QC requirements, and lists of tables, figures, and listings.
