Arizona has been the epicenter of school choice in the United States, with open enrollment for district schools for 30 years, charter schools for more than 25 years, a private school tax credit program, and in 2011 the first state direct parent-appropriations through targeted Empowerment Scholarship Account (ESA) vouchers. Arizona later became the first state to expand its ESA voucher program to be universal, an action that has been controversial since voters rejected a capped expansion in 2018 and legislators made it universal in 2022. Arizona provides more than $1 billion annually in subsidies to private education, including private schools and variations on homeschooling, from the state’s general fund directly or indirectly through tax credits. Because Arizona has provided no accountability and little transparency for participating private entities receiving public subsidies, the Grand Canyon Institute aims to improve accountability and transparency. The paper provides a composite of past GCI research, a new zip code analysis of users, and an estimated portion not using ESA vouchers for private schooling. GCI estimates that a growing share of universal participants come from charter or district schools, but still nearly three-quarters of those enrolled did not or would not have attended charter or district schools; about 90% of new universal entrants in FY2025 did attend a district or charter school. Zip code analysis shows ESA vouchers primarily enroll children residing in higher income zip codes, though the degree of difference has been declining. GCI also presents evidence that a significant number of users are not using the program for private school tuition; no more than 40% of students in the total ESA program were using allocations for private school tuition in FY2023, and by the end of FY2024 an estimated $360 million had accumulated in accounts. The Arizona Joint Legislative Budget Committee estimates the gross cost of the ESA program to be $872 million in FY2025, and in FY2024 the Arizona Department of Revenue reported the cost of the student tuition organization tax credit program as $238 million. Contrary to those who believe ESA vouchers save money, GCI’s analysis indicates universal voucher programs are a net cost to the state’s general fund because the primary users never enrolled in public district or charter schools, costing at least $330 million in FY2024 and $350 million in FY2025. The ESA voucher program was initially established and expanded for targeted categories of students, with enrollment modest except for disabilities, which was the main driver before universal vouchers. With universal ESA vouchers requiring no prior public school enrollment, program growth grew quickly but has tapered since then. Voucher amounts are equal to 90% of what a child would receive if attending a charter school; actual awards can exceed $30,000, though most are less than $8,000 paid quarterly. In FY2023, GCI estimated $304 million was spent overall, $173 million went to private schools, 51% of that to religious schools and 44% to schools serving special needs students, accounting for less than 40% of estimated student enrollment. An estimated $111 million was added to rollover accounts, which amounted to $175 million in 60,000 ESA accounts; GCI estimated account balances at the end of FY2024 had climbed to $360 million. Research found primary users of ESA vouchers were from wealthier zip codes; among universal applicants, 45% came from the wealthiest quarter of students, 32% from families with median income less than $60,000, and 80% were not in public school. GCI estimates that in FY2025 almost all new enrollment in the universal program came from charter and district schools, though overall almost three-quarters of current universal ESA voucher students never attended district or charter schools. The state general fund has modest savings when students transfer from charter to ESA universal vouchers, but has a net cost when a student transfers from district to an ESA universal voucher or would not have attended either; GCI estimated the net cost as at least $332 million in FY2024 and $346,289,274 in FY2025, or $349,520,388 with administrative share.

NVIDIA’s passage describes the RTX Blackwell Neural Rendering Architecture and related technologies. Blackwell RT Cores add cluster engines, compression, and up to 2x the ray-triangle intersection rate. Other features include Linear Swept Spheres, SER 2.0, and the AI Management Processor. Video/display additions include 4:2:2 encode/decode, ninth-generation NVENC, improved NVDEC, and DisplayPort 2.1b. Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating, accelerated frequency switching, and low latency sleep. DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation and Transformer models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA. Neural shaders, Cooperative Vectors API, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces are described. This study aimed to determine pre-service teachers’ opinions on the Physical Education and Sports Curriculum (5-8) regarding achievements, content, learning-teaching processes, and measurement/evaluation. It used a scanning model, quantitative methods, and a researcher-developed questionnaire. The sample included 25 students from each of Recreation, Physical Education and Sports Teaching, Sports Management, and Coaching Education departments at Bayburt University Faculty of Sports Sciences. Data were analyzed with frequency and percentage values.

Results showed generally positive views on program achievements; many agreed outcomes were suitable for student levels, structured under correct learning areas, and understandable, while 37 were undecided about scientific errors. For content, many were undecided about scientific errors, age appropriateness, and compatibility with other country programs; 80% agreed or strongly agreed content was meaningfully ordered. In learning-teaching processes, 56% said processes were enriched with activities and 61% said concrete materials were used; 60 disagreed or strongly disagreed that different methods and techniques were used. For assessment/evaluation, 34 were undecided about different teaching methods/techniques, and 43 agreed different forms were used. The discussion noted generally positive evaluations of objectives, insufficient participant information about content, and recommended more studies, informative seminars/congresses, and program review courses in teacher training.

The passage addresses the challenge of developing scalable, efficient systems for complex, dynamic problems, noting manual service composition and a perceived complexity wall. This lecture discusses effective field theory with fine tuning in the context of two-nucleon EFT. It covers non-relativistic elastic scattering, the effective range expansion, and a local contact-interaction theory. It explains that the kinetic term must include both ∂t and ∇²/2M, unlike HQET, and that the large S-wave scattering length requires treating C0 as relevant and keeping it to all orders. The lecture presents off-shell momentum subtraction and power divergence subtraction schemes, renormalization group equations, fixed points, enhancement of higher operators, conformal and spin-isospin SU(4) symmetries, a deuteron bound state, and applications to deuteron physics.

The D.C. Circuit reviewed the NRC’s transfer of regulatory authority over nuclear materials to New Jersey under the Atomic Energy Act. Shieldalloy challenged the transfer as arbitrary and capricious and argued New Jersey’s program was incompatible with federal requirements, particularly criterion 25 concerning pending licenses and the possible exclusion of the Newfield site from the transfer. The court held that the NRC’s explanations on criterion 25 and retention of jurisdiction were insufficient and lacked a rational connection to the facts, so the transfer was arbitrary and capricious. The court granted Shieldalloy’s petition, vacated the transfer, and remanded, without addressing Shieldalloy’s other compatibility claims.

The document describes AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine as an optional extension to System Encryption, SEV, and SNP for page migration, defined as copying page content and updating virtual-to-physical mappings. TMPM support is checked via ENGINE_READY in PM_Status and requires IOMMU enablement. It can migrate pages between system physical addresses while maintaining the same guest physical address, including pages targeted by concurrent DMA and SNP-protected guest pages that HV/OS cannot otherwise access.

Commands include PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, and PM_NOOP. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO supports concurrent DMA and Hypervisor-owned pages in SNP systems and requires IOMMU host PTE information. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages; source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, destination pages must be Pre-Migration, and after migration source pages return to Pre-Migration while destination pages take the original source state. Multi-page commands can move up to 128 pages using a Page Migration List with per-page status; PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking entries, PM_SUCCESS means all migrated, and other returns indicate none migrated. PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE may be retried.

Performance guidance recommends larger batches, keeping the ring buffer ahead of the engine, and using NOP or interrupt-on-complete instead of per-command interrupts. Restrictions state TMPM hardware moves only 4K-aligned to 4K-aligned pages, with host page table entries 8-byte aligned, and certain IOMMU, vIOMMU, ring buffer, and argument pages cannot be migrated. TMPM firmware reload requires paused operations, teardown of the ring buffer, and a BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol; reload errors and version checks apply. EPYC family is distinguished via PM_GET_CAPABILITIES FW_VER_Major, with Family 19h represented by 71 decimal.

The TMPM interface uses a separate page migration ring buffer with mailbox registers, initialization, shutdown, pause/resume, and six interrupt sources. SPA encoding supports SMEE/SME-MK encryption. Error handling reports command/list errors, ring buffer errors, hardware errors via status and/or MCA, and notes that a command can process up to 128 pages in one batch.

This paper experimentally studies whether large language models can autoformalize physical systems into differential game logic, preserving continuous dynamics and discrete transitions. It proposes 20 benchmarks from undergraduate kinematics and a pipeline using Propose and Revise LLM queries, KeYmaera X parser feedback, and semantic checking via symbolic execution and minimum variable writes. With few-shot prompting, OpenAI o3 achieves 70% top-5 success; main failures are checker limitations for complex problems. GPT 4o, GPT 4.1, and o3 improve successively, with few-shot prompting helping all models. Six problems are unsolvable by any model, grouped as optimization problems, non-polynomial continuous dynamics, and complicated dynamics. The paper concludes that results are encouraging and suggests future work on runtime autoformalization from vision and sensor data.

As Britain recovers from snow, this piece comes from Creeting St Peter, Suffolk. It says ministers spent the weekend queuing up to sabotage Theresa May’s EU deal, citing Simon Coveney on commitments that must be upheld irrespective of any future EU-UK agreement. It previews House of Lords business focused on Liberal Democrat contributions, notes Paul Walter on a young activists’ award and Samaritans, and mentions a “goodbye”-themed musical interlude, inviting comments and submissions.

Depression and anxiety are prevalent mental health conditions, and digital phenotyping offers quantitative longitudinal observation. Speech content and linguistic features can provide information about mental state. LLMs show capabilities in clinical reasoning and related areas, but objective digital biomarkers in psychiatry remain scarce. To address research gaps, the authors collected over 15,000 minutes of speech recordings from 1,160 outpatients with 25 diagnoses at SMHC, primarily depression and anxiety, in unstructured real-world settings. They designed a clinical-indicator corpus from EMRs and assessment scales, used a pretrained LLM to identify symptoms and rate scale components, fine-tuned it with psychiatrist annotations, extracted linguistic and acoustic features, and built an ensemble machine-learning pipeline that predicted diagnostic groups and symptoms with moderately high accuracies.

Theo Walcott scored in the 51st minute as Everton beat Newcastle 1-0 at Goodison Park. It was Walcott’s third goal for Everton since January. Everton next plays Huddersfield, while Newcastle hosts West Bromwich Albion.

Cover 0 is an all-out pressure defense that blitzes every player not assigned to an offensive skill player in man-to-man coverage. It aims to create quick pressure and force split-second quarterback decisions, but leaves every coverage player isolated and is high-risk/high-reward. Offenses can attack it with immediate, quick-hitting man beaters, slants, shallow crossing routes, and pick plays, especially with perimeter personnel advantages. The passage lists examples: Double Slants, Full-Slide Fade-Out/RB Seam Gadget, Trips Bunch Jerk Route, Slant-Rub, and Jerry Rice Motion Slant-Flat.

Former Aberdeen manager Steve “Pele” Paterson believes Pittodrie should host the funeral of Neale “Tattie” Cooper, a 54-year-old member of the 1983 European Cup Winners’ Cup team. Cooper died in hospital Monday after falling down stairs in Bucksburn, Aberdeen. Tributes came from Alex McLeish, Willie Miller, Stewart Milne, and thousands of fans; club sources said they will adhere to the family’s wishes.

FlowMotion’s Kickstarter campaign sought $30,000, was funded in one hour, and raised over $600,000 from more than 2,700 backers. FlowMotion ONE is a wearable and handheld smartphone stabilizer with a 3inONE design: it works with existing camera mounts, a joystick handle, or an extension pole. Sensors and high-precision motors eliminate shaking and vibrations for cinema-quality smartphone footage. Founded in 2015 by four outdoor enthusiasts, FlowMotion now has 10 people, offices in Palo Alto and Trondheim, and awards; its mission is to help people tell better stories.

Using Demographic and Health Survey data from Benin (2017–2018) and Cameroon (2018), this study assessed awareness of cervical cancer and cervical screening among women aged 15–49. A total of 21,322 women were surveyed about cervical cancer awareness, and 7,010 were additionally asked about screening awareness. Awareness of cervical cancer was 9.5% in Benin and 46.1% in Cameroon. Among women aware of cervical cancer, awareness of cervical screening was 51.4% in Benin and 59.7% in Cameroon. In both countries, cervical cancer awareness was significantly associated with older age, higher education, and frequent internet use; in Cameroon it was also associated with greater wealth. Cervical screening awareness was highest among women aged 25–34 in Benin and 45+ in Cameroon and among women with higher education in both countries; age, education, radio listening, and internet use were significantly associated with screening awareness. The study reports generally low awareness and calls for strengthened awareness programmes, stakeholder engagement, public enlightenment, media use, and targeting younger women, and notes the need to address wealth-related inequality in Cameroon. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, a small sub-sample, self-reported data, and residual confounding.

COVID-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2, a single-stranded RNA virus transmitted mainly by respiratory droplets but also shed in feces at high concentrations. SARS-CoV-2 RNA can be detected in sewage, making wastewater monitoring a critical surveillance tool. Wastewater processing typically concentrates viruses from 50–250 mL samples using methods such as membrane filtration, PEG precipitation, skim milk, ultracentrifugation, and ultrafiltration, often requiring a centrifuge. Nanotrap particles can capture and concentrate analytes, preserve viruses and nucleic acids, and capture multiple pathogens; they have been used to detect SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory viruses in wastewater. Sampling methods include grab, composite, and passive sampling, with Moore swabs used as passive samplers. The study evaluated parameters affecting SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection and compared automated versus manual Nanotrap methods, and Nanotrap versus membrane filtration and skim milk methods, without compromising sensitivity.

An Oklahoma veterinarian removed 21 pacifiers from a dog named Dovey after a couple with a baby noticed missing pacifiers and the dog’s symptoms. An x-ray suggested 7 to 9, but surgery found 21. Dovey is doing well and going home.

An email dated Dec. 12, 2000 from Ann Schmidt to Enron recipients lists “Enron Mentions.” The included articles report that utility stocks rose 36% year to date but may stall amid a tech rebound; Enron’s Indian unit said four local lenders agreed to cut Dabhol Power loan rates; three firms decided to sell natural gas instead of using it for products; Activate described its 2000 digital media growth; articles criticized Enron’s Maharashtra power project and said the Dabhol agreement could be nullified; Green Mountain applied to be a Texas retail electric provider; The New Power Company was certified as a Georgia retail natural gas marketer; and internet energy trading was dominated by EnronOnline and ICE, while Dynegydirect traded over $1.5 billion in November.

Kratom is an herbal substance from Mitragyna speciosa leaves, consumed as tea or dried powder; mitragynine and 7-hydroxymitragynine cause stimulant-like effects at low doses and opioid-like sedation at higher doses. It is used for pain, anxiety, depression, and opioid withdrawal. Although a DEA drug of concern, it is unscheduled federally; Wisconsin is one of six states where possession is illegal statewide. Using Wisconsin Poison Center/NPDS data from January 1, 2010–September 1, 2022, the study examined 59 kratom exposure calls. Most exposed persons were male; mean age was 35.3 years; three exposures were unintentional ingestions in infants under 2. Calls increased from 2011 to a peak of 15 in 2020, concentrated in southeastern Wisconsin, with Marinette County highest. About half were kratom-only; common co-substances were alcohol and benzodiazepines. Common symptoms included agitation, tachycardia, confusion, and CNS depression. Among 50 known outcomes, 19 were moderate or major; 7 required critical care and 1 death occurred. The authors note increasing calls, polysubstance exposure, surveillance and regulation limitations, and recommend awareness, data collection, education, and safe storage.

Randomized, open-label trial of 1,112 NVAF subjects on apixaban for 48 weeks. Subjects were randomized 1:1 to standard care information or Additional Education Program; at 24 weeks, the program group was re-randomized to continue or revert. Adherence was electronically monitored; investigator-withheld periods were excluded, and >30-day discontinuation was permanent.

Ben Baby’s mailbag addresses whether Florida is a must-win for Kevin Sumlin if Texas A&M is blown out by Alabama (not exactly, but it would reduce his margin for error for an 8-4 season), whether A&M will wear throwback uniforms (none announced) and its field tribute to Gene Stallings and the 1967 team, fall weddings, Aggie DJ music requests, UNT-UTSA attendance ideas involving Steve Austin, “Go Mean Green,” Arsene Wenger, and a favorite burrito place.

The passage presents market headlines and commentary: Asia stocks were muted after mixed Chinese PMIs, and the S&P 500 closed higher ahead of upcoming jobs data. The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July and 7.8% YTD, then slipped 1.6% on August’s first day. Volatility and credit spreads saw a seasonal upturn; investors skewed portfolios toward tech; U.S. electricity demand reached a new all-time high. Short-term technicals looked tenuous, while medium/long-term trend indicators remained healthy. Gold topped $3,800/oz amid U.S. shutdown risks and rate cut bets.

An alleged Swiss spy arrested in Germany raised speculation he acted for Swiss authorities. An OAG watchdog rejected allegations of OAG involvement or failure to redact files. The 54-year-old former policeman/security consultant has been under Swiss investigation since 2015 over stolen banking data. German prosecutors reportedly obtained interrogation records. The case caused German outrage. It remains unclear whether he had an FIS mandate. The Swiss government confirmed FIS helped with a stolen banking data case, ending investigations in May 2014.

The passage contains remarks from Dustin Brown and Anze Kopitar about their team’s long-standing core, trust, and closeness. Brown says the group’s time together helps in tough situations, that leads give breathing room, that big-city TV markets magnify hockey, and that the team focuses on the next playoff game and resets after each round. He discusses the team’s playoff style, a Stanley Cup mentality, Justin Williams as a focused big-game player, and the current core’s continuity and lack of cliques compared with earlier roster turnover. Kopitar says it is not time to reflect, mentions a slow start but the team’s character in winning, praises Drew Doughty’s development and leadership, and comments on Gaborik fitting in.

Memphis police say 2-year-old Laylah Washington died after being shot in the head Sunday while riding in a car with her mother and brothers. No arrests have been made; police are looking for a black Chevrolet Impala.

HMP Northward holds over 220 men despite a 212 maximum, so prison authorities will transfer some low-risk inmates to the Immigration Detention Centre at Fairbanks to ease overcrowding. The IDC is also at capacity. Prison Director Steven Barrett said selected, risk-assessed inmates would be moved to a cordoned-off section, clearing about 22 places as a short-term option. Officials said safety and statutory obligations would not be compromised. The IDC also houses migrants, and nine asylum-seeking detainees began a hunger strike.

The passage describes communication processing methods and communications apparatuses in wireless communications, particularly for a duplication mode in which PDCP data on a radio bearer is transmitted on a first RLC entity corresponding to a first path and duplicately transmitted on a second RLC entity corresponding to a second path. It covers determining, triggering, and sending a data volume report for one path, including receiving an indication of the path from a radio access network or selecting the path by priority or data volume, and sending the report in a cell or cell group. It also covers receiving a first indication message indicating whether to activate a duplication mode of a radio bearer, activating or deactivating the duplication mode, various message structures with fields indicating control, activation, radio bearer, and path information, and data volume reporting when the duplication mode is activated or deactivated. It further describes handling duplicated data, retransmission and radio link failure, configuration information, and corresponding communications apparatuses, computer storage medium, and processor/memory implementations.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2020 includes unaudited interim consolidated financial statements and notes. For the three months ended September 30, 2020, revenue was $37.154 billion, operating income was $15.876 billion, net income was $13.893 billion, and diluted EPS was $1.82, compared with revenue of $33.055 billion, operating income of $12.686 billion, net income of $10.678 billion, and diluted EPS of $1.38 in the prior-year period. Segment revenue was $12.319 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $12.986 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $11.849 billion for More Personal Computing. Commercial cloud revenue was $15.2 billion, up 31%. The report states COVID-19 continued to affect operations and results, with cloud usage and demand benefiting, Surface and Gaming benefiting, Search negatively impacted by reduced customer advertising spend, and continued weakness in transactional licensing. A change in accounting estimate for server and network equipment increased operating income by $927 million and net income by $763 million, or $0.10 per share, for the quarter, and is estimated to increase fiscal year 2021 annual operating income by $2.7 billion. Microsoft entered an agreement to acquire ZeniMax Media for $7.5 billion in cash. The Board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.56 per share. As of September 30, 2020, total assets were $301.001 billion, total liabilities were $177.609 billion, and total stockholders’ equity was $123.392 billion.

Environment Canada issued a special weather statement for Edmonton and areas south and east to the Saskatchewan border Wednesday afternoon, warning funnel clouds may form from weak rotation. The rotation is usually not dangerous near ground but could intensify into a weak landspout tornado. A meteorologist said touchdown is unlikely but possible, potentially causing damage. Funnel clouds should be treated seriously.

Britain’s FTSE 100 fell 0.2 percent on Friday, set for a fourth straight loss and its worst week since Aug 2017, weighed by BT and AstraZeneca results. BT fell over 5 percent to a five-year low, while AstraZeneca dropped 1.7 percent. Miners and oil stocks rose, and mid-cap Capita gained more than 5 percent after a Morgan Stanley upgrade.

The passage describes a data intake and query system for collecting, indexing, and searching machine-generated event data, including components such as forwarders, indexers, search heads, and data stores. It discusses events, timestamps, late-binding schema, field extraction, parsing, indexing, inverted indexes, cloud-based and external data searches via ERP processes, and user interfaces for searching, reporting, and monitoring. It also notes continuation claims to related U.S. patent applications.

The court denied Jennings’s motions to strike the amended answer and for default judgment, and to strike Exhibits C–H to Dorrance’s affidavit, finding no bad faith and that the exhibits were authenticated records of regularly conducted activity. The court granted defendants’ summary judgment on Jennings’s remaining claims. Jennings, a UNC women’s soccer player from 1996 until her May 1998 dismissal, alleged sexual comments and personal inquiries by Coach Dorrance and Assistant Coach Palladino. The court held the conduct was not severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive enough for Title IX or § 1983 sexual harassment, did not violate privacy rights, did not support supervisory liability because no underlying constitutional violation occurred, and did not meet North Carolina’s requirements for common law invasion of privacy. The court also denied defendants’ motion to submit evidence under seal.

Treasury minister Mel Stride said Britain's fish fingers would be "safe in the hands" of the Government during Brexit talks, after Labour MP Mel Onn sought assurances for the fish trade and processing industry in Great Grimsby and its 5,000 jobs.

Education 4.0 introduced Information Technology to education, especially challenging language education in Indonesia because it usually depends on face-to-face interaction and immersive experiences, but it also created opportunities. Alternatives included online learning platforms, mobile learning, asynchronous learning, blended learning, TV and radio broadcasts, new assessment methods, parental involvement, and flexible policies; online platforms and mobile learning stood out for accessibility and effectiveness. Research cited shows IT can improve language education, and the study used qualitative descriptive analysis, literature review, observation, comparative analysis, and framework development. Data included 1010 related articles, with 15.1% strongly relevant from Scopus. Results discuss challenges and benefits, technological innovation, management strategies, and student attitudes. Challenges include teacher technological proficiency, student engagement, resource availability, assessment and feedback, digital divide, self-regulation, loss of social interaction, equity issues, cultural differences, and community support. Technologies include ASR, AR, VR, IoT, AI, LMS, gamification, 3D printing, blockchain, cloud computing, robotics, big data, and task/game-based learning. ASR improves pronunciation and vocabulary through feedback; task/game-based learning increases engagement. Management strategies include digital platforms, teacher professional development, language support tools, global collaborations, virtual exchange, cloud infrastructure, mobile learning, data-driven decisions, and inclusive IT policies. Students generally have positive attitudes toward IT, similar to STEM, though resistance and unequal access remain. The conclusion states IT can greatly enhance language education with careful consideration of teaching methods, management strategies, and student needs. The authors declare no conflict of interest and no external funding.

The Agreement is the entire understanding; unenforceable parts do not affect the rest. California/U.S. law governs, the U.N. CISG does not apply, Santa Clara County courts have exclusive jurisdiction, exports must comply with U.S. regulations, and waivers/amendments must be written and signed.

A federal judge in Illinois dismissed a lawsuit alleging the College Board and 40 selective private colleges conspired to fix prices and inflate tuition. The judge found no plausible allegation of an agreement or collusion, though the suit claimed using noncustodial parents’ financial information raised tuition by about $6,200 on average.

At a human trafficking training in Oshakati, Prosecutor-General Martha Imalwa said human trafficking is the third-largest international syndicate after drugs and arms, earning $32 billion yearly, with 20–30 million enslaved and 600,000–800,000 trafficked across borders annually, 80 percent female. She said Namibia is affected, citing a missing Namibian boy found in South Africa and Angolan children. The UN-assisted training aims to help officials detect, investigate, prosecute, and assist victims. Police Inspector-General Sebastian Ndeitunga reported 25 trafficking cases from 2010–2017.

SA58 Nasal Spray is a broad-spectrum anti-COVID-19 monoclonal antibody developed by Sinovac Life Sciences. In a randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial in Beijing among healthy adult workers within 72 hours of contact with SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals, 1,222 participants entered the full analysis set. During case monitoring, SA58 reduced laboratory-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 by 80.82% (95%CI 52.41%-92.27%) and SARS-CoV-2 infection by 61.83% (95%CI 37.50%-76.69%). All sequenced RT-PCR-positive samples were Omicron BF·7. No severe COVID-19 or death occurred. Adverse events were all Grade 1 and generally similar between groups. Study limitations included early termination before target sample size, a young healthy worker population, short follow-up, and possible impact of isolation practices; further evaluation in high-risk populations and a full-powered sample was advised.

A medical system assists a rescuer with intubation or advanced airway procedures, including rapid sequence intubation. It includes airflow and physiological sensors and a patient monitoring device with a processor and user interface. The processor receives data indicating airflow, determines airflow presence, initiates a timer, receives physiological information, determines whether an endotracheal tube is properly placed or remains properly placed, and presents the determination. It may use ETCO2, transthoracic impedance, acoustic information, or deviations from initial or dynamic baselines. The system may also detect steps of an airway intubation procedure from intubation parameters and adjust feedback, and may include a defibrillator, visual/touchscreen feedback, and portable computing devices.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed SB 53, requiring major AI companies to publicly disclose how they plan to mitigate catastrophic risks from advanced AI models. The law creates safety-incident reporting mechanisms, extends whistleblower protections, and initiates CalCompute, a government consortium for a public computing cluster. Authored by State Sen. Scott Wiener, it follows a failed similar law and focuses on transparency rather than liability, unlike the vetoed SB 1047. Reactions were divided: Anthropic praised it, OpenAI called it a path toward federal harmonization, and Meta supported balanced regulation; critics said it could burden startups and create a state-by-state patchwork. It requires incident reports to California’s Office of Emergency Services and includes civil penalties enforceable by the attorney general, though experts called the penalties relatively weak. Because 32 of the world’s top 50 AI companies are based in California, the law may set oversight standards.

Kevin Love, recovering from a concussion suffered against Boston, is with Cleveland on the eve of his fourth straight NBA Finals. He has dealt with anxiety and panic attacks, and after being questioned by teammates for leaving a Jan. 20 game and missing practice, he wrote a Player’s Tribune essay about his struggles. He received thousands of emails and said the response created a community. Since arriving in 2014, Love has faced criticism and trade rumors. He said basketball is his escape and he does not want sympathy. Coach Tyronn Lue told him to relax and be himself. Love had an uneven postseason, and his status for the Finals opener is in doubt. He said his time in Cleveland has been worth it.

Tropical Storm Nate is expected to move across the northwestern Caribbean Sea, reach the eastern Yucatan peninsula early evening, enter the southern Gulf of Mexico tonight, and approach the northern Gulf coast Saturday evening, strengthening into a hurricane Saturday night into Sunday. It was moving northwest at 14 mph with maximum sustained winds of 45 mph. The forecast cone stretched from the Florida Panhandle to central Louisiana, with Pensacola inside; the National Weather Service said Pensacola would likely be on Nate’s eastern side, where higher wind gusts, storm surge, and tornado formation occur. Escambia and Santa Rosa counties could see heavy rain from Saturday through at least Sunday, possible flash flooding and tornadoes, tropical storm force winds Sunday morning, and rainfall of 3 to 5 inches. A tropical storm watch was issued for much of the Northwest Florida Gulf coast. Eglin Air Force Base was at Hurricane Condition 4, and Gov. Rick Scott declared a state of emergency in Escambia, Santa Rosa, and 27 other counties. Closures and postponements included UWF, Sacred Heart’s Medical Mission at Home, BaseFEST, Gulf Islands National Seashore, Pensacola State College events, Pensacola Day, and Dane-Toberfest. Officials urged residents to prepare and follow local media. Nate formed quickly over warm waters and was blamed for at least 17 deaths in Central America.

The passage describes an odd summer box office with both positive and negative stories and roughly as many good as bad movies. Wonder Woman’s success masked a deficiency in other big-scale movies. Three comic book superhero films—Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2, Wonder Woman, and Spider-Man: Homecoming—dominated and got top-tier business, while most other genres had at best one successful film. Examples include Despicable Me 3, Girls Trip, Annabelle: Creation, Dunkirk, Baby Driver, 47 Meters Down, and The Big Sick, plus Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales as one non-superhero biggie. Many other films disappointed or bombed, including Captain Underpants, Cars 3, The Emoji Movie, King Arthur, Valerian, The Mummy, Transformers: The Last Knight, and War for the Planet of the Apes. Live-action comedy had a hit only with Girls Trip after earlier flops. The passage argues the summer was essentially superhero movies succeeding with one successful offering per other category, which is not good for diverse multiplex content, and notes arguments that superhero films crowded out other large-scale films.

Researchers at the University of California, Irvine and other institutions are rolling out a satellite-based drought severity index using NASA GRACE data. It adds terrestrial water storage (groundwater) to drought assessments, supplementing precipitation-based tools. The data set covers 2002 to 2014 and will be extended with the current mission and the GRACE follow-on mission scheduled for early 2018. Based solely on satellite gravity observations, it provides globally consistent drought monitoring, even where ground readings are difficult, and tracks groundwater storage changes affecting soil moisture recharge and drought recovery. Evaluations in the continental U.S. showed significant agreement with other indices.

On May 25, Tony Iommi announced his sponsored BIMM Birmingham Scholarship at a BIMM Music Institute Q&A, where prospective students were invited and he discussed his career and the drive needed to survive the business.

The message from Ann Schmidt, dated May 24, 2001, subject “Enron Mentions,” compiles news articles. A Houston Chronicle opinion criticizes California Attorney General Bill Lockyer’s remarks about Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay and argues Enron should challenge him. A Los Angeles Times article says Senator James Jeffords’ expected party switch could affect drug, HMO, defense, credit card, tobacco, energy, housing-lender and telecom sectors, and may benefit power traders through uncertainty. Brazil asks for 20 percent power cuts beginning June 1; Enron plans about 800 MW of new generation. California PUC President Loretta Lynch cites evidence generators manipulated prices; generators dispute this. Other items cover Bill Simon Jr.’s energy investments and Hanover Compressor/Enron ties; India’s appointment of A.V. Gokak to the Dabhol dispute panel, Godbole’s resignation and withdrawal, and federal willingness to consider proposals; Poland’s gas market changes; Endesa’s sale of Electra de Viesgo, with Enron invited to bid; Pawar-Godbole political dispute; and Dynegy seeking acquisitions.

Ryan, a six-year-old, stars in Ryan ToysReview, which Forbes ranked among the world’s Top 10 highest-paid YouTube stars and reportedly earned $11 million in 2017. Started in 2015, it has over 10 million subscribers and over eight billion views in a 12-month Forbes tracking period. His family says it will continue only while he enjoys it.

The passage explains the long-short equity strategy: taking long positions in stocks expected to appreciate and short positions in stocks expected to decline. It is a hedging strategy intended to minimize risk and maximize profits from rising and falling stock prices. Hedge funds use it, often with a long bias such as 130/30. The passage gives an example with Merck and Thor, discusses portfolio construction, and notes the strategy may be unsuitable for retail investors. It mentions Ed Thorp in relation to long-short strategies and quantitative investing, and presents a Coca-Cola/Pepsi backtest using strict trading rules that performed well but had flat or negative periods. It says long-short strategies often require many pairs, leverage, and research, and that hedge funds use them to enhance returns and manage risks.

An AI-assisted inverse-design workflow targets diammonium organic spacers for Dion-Jacobson 2D hybrid perovskites with tailored energy level alignment. It uses an invertible 12-digit fingerprint representation, molecular morphing to expand 21 reported spacers into millions of hypothetical candidates, high-throughput DFT calculations, machine-learning regression for HOMO/LUMO prediction, SHAP analysis for structure-property insights, and synthesis feasibility screening via PubChem availability and a topological formability score. For generations G0–G6, the workflow identified and DFT-validated 8 type IIa and 44 type IIb candidates but no type Ib candidates, largely due to synthetic accessibility. Using inverse design with constrained fingerprints, it identified 2 type Ib candidates in G7–G8, 12 type IIa candidates in G3–G9, and 42 type IIb candidates in G2–G6. Type Ib required highly conjugated acene-based spacers, type IIa involved extended conjugation, and type IIb involved pyridine-type nitrogen substitution. The passage also notes limitations, including encoding complex motifs, heuristic synthesis/stability judgments, and lack of experimental validation.

A PGA848 drives an ADS8860 single-ended input SAR ADC with ±15 V input-stage and 5.3 V output-stage supplies, a REF6250 5 V ADC reference, and an OPA192-buffered 2.5 V midscale REF. The circuit uses three filters and provides a nominal 318 kHz f–3dB bandwidth, 277 kHz with high-side resistor tolerance, and –0.1 dB flatness to 41 kHz. Additional sections cover power supply limits, layout guidelines, simulation software, documentation and support resources, trademarks, ESD precautions, revision history, mechanical/packaging/orderable information, and legal notices.

A New York Times survey of federal judges found many expressed concern about the Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions in cases related to President Trump since his second term. Of 65 judges, 12 said the Court used the docket appropriately and 12 said lower courts had sufficient guidance; 42 said it harmed public perception. Some anonymously criticized the orders as “mystical,” “overly blunt,” “demoralizing,” and a “slap in the face”; one Trump appointee said they “flush out anti-democratic rulings.” The Times said at least seven of about 20 emergency orders lacked reasoning, nearly all benefited Trump, and acknowledged respondents may not represent the judiciary. The Volokh Conspiracy critiqued the survey.

Quarter Circle Games announced The Peterson Case, a Unity-made first-person horror game set near the 1947 Roswell UFO incident, coming to PS4, Xbox One, and PC. Players control Detective Franklin Reinhardt exploring a deserted house of missing residents while pursued by an unearthly presence. No release date announced.

Teck Resources was upgraded by Zacks Investment Research from “hold” to “buy,” with a $25.00 price objective and a potential upside of 8.84%. Other analyst reports included upgrades, reiterated ratings, and target price changes. The stock had an average “Buy” rating and a consensus price target of $31.18, with one sell, two hold, twenty-two buy, and one strong buy rating. TECK opened at $22.97, with a 52-week low of $14.56 and high of $26.60, and had a market capitalization of $13.27 billion, a PE ratio of 7.90, and a beta of 1.20. It reported quarterly EPS of $0.73 on revenue of $2.82 billion, and analysts expect $3.52 EPS for the current year. Institutional investors and hedge funds own 46.80% of its stock.

DEA agents destroyed Diane Monson’s medical marijuana plants despite California’s Compassionate Use Act. Monson and Angel Raich, who used medical cannabis for serious conditions, sued, arguing Congress lacked authority under the interstate commerce clause to regulate their local, noncommercial, state-legal activities. The Supreme Court ruled 6-3 for the government, reasoning Congress could regulate in-state medical cannabis to preserve its ban on the interstate cannabis market. O’Connor and Thomas dissented, arguing the decision removed meaningful Commerce Clause limits; Thomas said Congress had not shown a need to regulate local growers or users. After the loss, Raich lost again on constitutional and medical-necessity claims. The passage says federalism was called a casualty of the war on drugs, state-level marijuana legalization later expanded, and Thomas continued to criticize the federal marijuana ban and defend original Commerce Clause limits.

After three Trump accusers appeared on Megyn Kelly Today, CNN’s Brian Karem asked Sarah Huckabee Sanders whether she had ever been sexually harassed and had empathy for accusers. Sanders declined to discuss her personal experience, expressed empathy, and said she relays information for the president.

Motley Fool Money says it receives compensation from companies whose offers appear, which may affect placement but not product ratings. The article promotes credit card offers. It highlights the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card as a no-annual-fee card with unlimited 2% cash rewards on purchases, a $200 cash rewards bonus after spending $500 in the first 3 months, 0% intro APR for 12 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, then 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99% variable APR, and cell phone protection up to $600 with a $25 deductible. It also lists the Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card with unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% cash back on hotels, vacation rentals, and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel, a limited-time $300 welcome bonus, $0 annual fee, no foreign transaction fees, and 0% intro APR on purchases and balance transfers for 15 months. Another listed offer earns 2% on every purchase, a $200 cash back bonus after spending $1,500 in 6 months, and 0% intro APR on balance transfers for 18 months, with balance transfer fees and no purchase intro APR.

The passage describes features of the MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 devices. It details a temperature sensor with a linear voltage output connected to an ADC channel, a factory single-point calibration value, and ADC/VREF configuration. VREF provides 1.4-V and 2.5-V internal references, external reference support, and requires decoupling capacitors on VREF+/- pins. COMP compares two input voltages and supports blanking sources, low-power wakeup, advanced timer fault handling, and input selection; DAC_OUT and COMP0/1_IN3+ connect via PA15. The DAC is 12-bit buffered with 8-bit or 12-bit resolution, self-calibration, data formats, sample time generator, FIFO/DMA, and hardware trigger. Security features include an AES-128/256 accelerator, firewalls, secure storage for up to four AES keys, and CRC-16/CRC-32. TRNG generates 32-bit random numbers every 128 TRNG clock cycles. AESADV performs 128-bit and 256-bit AES encryption/decryption in listed modes. Keystore securely manages AES keys, CRC-P supports CRC16-CCITT and CRC32-ISO3309, and MATHACL provides accelerated 32-bit math functions. UART, I2C, SPI, and CAN-FD features are listed. LFSS contains RTC_B and IWDT_B. RTC_B provides time/calendar, alarms, wakeup intervals, calibration, temperature compensation, and timestamp options. IWDT_B monitors code execution with an LFOSC clock and selectable periods; WWDT supervises code execution with selectable periods and interval timer mode. TIMx includes general-purpose and advanced timers with counters, prescalers, shadow registers, QEI/Hall support, synchronization, triggers, and advanced PWM/fault features. Device analog connections note DAC_OUT/PA15, IOMUX manages digital IO functions, and SWD and BSL interfaces support debug/programming. Factory constants provide read-only device and trim data. The applications section recommends decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup, SYSOSC FCL resistor, VCORE capacitor, and ODIO pullups. Documentation support and revision history are also included.

The University of Minnesota Morris is on land that was once an Indian boarding school. One former boys dormitory remains and now houses the multi-ethnic resource center. In April, 20 to 30 Native American students held a talking circle with MPR News, discussing higher education, trauma, and relatives who attended boarding schools. The application is a continuation of specified U.S. patent applications and generally relates to computer graphics and 3D reconstruction. It describes “passthrough” for head-mounted devices, where external camera images are used to render a user’s physical surroundings. Since camera and eye viewpoints differ and captured images lack depth, the system computes depth measurements, generates a 3D model or mesh of the environment, and re-renders passthrough images from the user’s eye viewpoints. Depth may be computed using stereo triangulation or, for resource-limited devices, using a video encoder and motion vectors. The disclosure addresses incorrect occlusion in mixed-reality scenes by generating instance segmentation masks for objects, computing representative depth values from the 3D model for each instance, and assigning farther depth values to padded borders around the masks. A rendering system uses these values to determine occlusion between passthrough and virtual objects.

This study examines factors that attract and retain rural special education teachers, addressing chronic shortages and annual attrition rates of 30% to 50%, with 40% to 100% turnover over five years. A 32-question adapted survey was completed by 93 special education teachers from three rural remote Midwest U.S. special education cooperatives. Data were analyzed descriptively and with correlations and t-tests, while open-ended responses yielded four themes: provision of support, financial incentives, job-related factors, and rural initiatives. For retention, participants most often cited support (70%), financial incentives (53%), job-related factors (44%), and rural initiatives (2%). For attraction, they most often cited financial incentives (96%), support (31%), job-related factors (15%), and rural initiatives (9%). Sub-themes included administrative, collegial, and community support; increased salary, loan forgiveness, health insurance, housing, and sign-on bonuses; reduced paperwork and caseload, professional development, resources, and work-life balance; and Grow Your Own programs and rural career fairs. Support was negatively related to years of experience but positively related to plans to remain; satisfaction was related to remaining in the profession. Those planning to leave cited job-related factors, lack of support, and limited rural incentives. Limitations included self-reported survey data, a small rural Midwest sample with limited diversity, and mainly descriptive analysis. The study concludes that a combination of support, financial incentives, job-related improvements, and rural initiatives may help recruitment and retention, and calls for further research and intentional policies.

Soccer defending stance: after getting goal side, a defender’s 1 v. 1 stance starts with one foot forward (lead) and one back (trail), usually dominant leg back. Feet are about 18 inches apart on a 30-degree angle, about 12 inches wide, toes slightly outward; the defender is balanced on the balls of both feet, knees slightly bent, arms out with elbows bent. This helps quick reaction, minimal response time, slowing or directing the opponent, avoiding being beaten, and preparing to tackle. By field location, right side uses left lead, left side uses right lead, and center is optional, helping block inside movement and force the opponent toward the sideline. Practice covers right, center, and left stances, adjusting to opponent movement and using sneak peeks or field markings to maintain goal side.

The Iso play is a downhill running scheme in which a fullback lead-blocks a linebacker, with base blocks and double teams at the point of attack; it is designed to overpower a defense and get the ball vertical quickly, and is named because the lead blocker is isolated one-on-one with the linebacker. Its strengths include getting the ball downhill fast, consistent yardage with a bruising tailback and an offensive line that can sustain one-on-one blocks, and simplicity that makes it easy to teach. Its main weakness is dependence on personnel: it generally needs large, powerful offensive linemen and a rugged fullback, while smaller, weaker lines have less success. The passage also details assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts and variations such as Shotgun Iso and Weakside Iso.

This study reviews leadership models in education—administrative/managerial, instructional, transformational, distributed, transactional, ethical, contingent, and participative—analyzing their strengths, weaknesses, and contributions to school functioning. It states that educational management has changed since the 1980s and that no consensus exists on the most appropriate model, as none alone fully responds to changing social and educational conditions. Administrative/managerial leadership emphasizes hierarchy and rules but can be inflexible. Instructional leadership focuses on teaching, learning, mission, educational management, academic climate, and supportive environments, but may be top-down and overlook other school aspects. Transformational leadership emphasizes vision, inspiration, innovation, support, and change but risks authoritarian relationships. Distributed leadership shares leadership across the organization, supporting democracy and participation, though implementation can be challenging. Transactional leadership uses rewards and exchanges. Ethical leadership emphasizes moral values and ethical decisions. Contingent leadership adapts to circumstances. Participative leadership involves members in decision-making, with benefits and challenges. The study concludes no single style is sufficient and suggests a synthetic, flexible, multi-dimensional approach combining strengths of different models to address contemporary educational challenges.

The lecture completes orthonormal expansions from finite to infinite dimensions, stating that projections onto orthonormal vectors converge and that the residual is orthogonal to each vector. Recent interest in rutile RuO2 as an altermagnetic candidate follows reports of a sublattice moment, above-ambient Néel temperature, and predicted band splitting, but debate persists about whether RuO2 intrinsically hosts altermagnetism. This work investigates exchange bias in incoherent RuO2/Fe/Ru heterostructures using SQUID magnetometry, polarized neutron reflectometry and diffraction, atom probe tomography, HRTEM, and EELS. Neutron diffraction shows no signatures of antiferromagnetic ordering in RuO2 thin films. Polarized neutron reflectometry reveals uncompensated, in-plane-canted moments at the RuO2/Fe interface whose canting is sensitive to field history. APT, HRTEM/FFT, and EELS indicate the RuO2/Fe interface contains mainly iron oxide with detectable magnetite (Fe3O4) and a Fe gradient into RuO2. Exchange bias is absent in RuO2/Ni heterostructures, while a Fe/Ru bilayer without RuO2 shows EB attributed to oxidation through the Ru layer. The authors conclude that EB in RuO2/Fe-based ferromagnetic heterostructures does not arise from intrinsic AFM or altermagnetic ordering in sputtered RuO2, but from a magnetically active interfacial reaction layer stabilized by Fe oxidation. They state this does not refute possible altermagnetism in the rutile structure, but cautions that AM or AFM effects should be isolated from interfacial layers.

The paper explores how a Bayesian approach might be applied to relevance-theoretic pragmatics, focusing on the communication of implicit meaning through conversational implicatures. Using a Peter and Mary coffee example, it distinguishes explicatures from implicatures and reviews relevance theory: verbal communication as ostension and intention attribution; manifestness; relevance as positive cognitive effects relative to processing effort; the communicative principle of relevance; and a comprehension heuristic that accesses interpretive hypotheses in order of accessibility until relevance expectations are met. It discusses strong and weak implicatures, parallel adjustment of explicit content, implicit import, and context, and relevance expectations. It argues that RSA-style literal listener/speaker layers are not useful for implicature comprehension. It then develops a probabilistic model in ProbLog: encyclopaedic knowledge as a probabilistic graph, linking words to concepts, modeling explicature/implicature adjustment as a Bayesian network, and evaluating interpretive hypotheses using KL divergence and Herbrand base size. It presents interpretive hypotheses Int1–Int5 and an optimization model that eliminates hypotheses not satisfying relevance expectations, prefers a smaller Herbrand base when KL measures are equal, and accepts the highest KL measure. The conclusion describes the model as an as-if-optimization model for implicature comprehension, focused on audience comprehension with manually constructed hypotheses, and notes future work on speaker perspective, metacognition, higher-level explicatures, and metarepresentational uses.

This study combined 102 medical imaging datasets into a hyper-scale multimodal dataset of 4.5 million images to train ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and VGG16 CNNs to classify images by CT, MRI, PET, and X-ray modality. Data were split by dataset into train, validation, and test sets to prevent leakage; 3D scans were treated as 2D slices, resized to 224×224, and rescaled between 0 and 1. The passage presents educational pacifism, motivated by mass formal schooling systems’ ubiquity, harm, and generally unnoticed or accepted harm. It states that schooling is assumed good, so systemic harm from hierarchical and authoritarian systems is rarely critiqued, and educational ends are often used to justify means. Following Feinberg and Mill, harm is defined as adversely affecting important interests. It provides a taxonomy of schooling harm: personal harm, including student-on-student bullying, physical or psychological harm, threats, name-calling, theft, gossip, teasing, humiliation, exclusion, and verbal harm; and systemic harm, which is more common, wide-ranging, and harmful but normalized. Systemic harm is divided into structural, objective, and symbolic. Structural harm involves patterned relationships and practices, authoritarianism, control, conformity, factory-like schooling, imbalanced power, and maintenance of social control. Objective harm involves hierarchical structures, inequality, and the capitalist economic order, preparing students for subordination, scarcity, and the workplace. Symbolic harm involves power differentials, normalized subordination, curricula and pedagogy transmitting ideologies, testing, ranking, certification, surveillance, rewards and punishments, hierarchy, and obedience. Coercive practices, positive and negative, also harm students’ confidence, motivation, engagement, and critical and creative thinking.

Educational pacifism holds that educational practices are just only if they do not harm innocents; mass formal schooling fails this condition because it extensively harms students, who are generally innocent in the relevant sense, and thereby treats them as means, violating the Kantian formula of humanity. The passage says educational harm does not prevent great harm and that alternatives exist, including Montessori and peace education. It claims the harm is systemic, pervasive, serious, and morally unjust, while not arguing that schooling is inherently harmful, should be entirely jettisoned, or harms all students all the time.

The passage then argues that Montessori’s views broadly align with educational pacifism. Montessori saw education as the means to positive, systemic peace and as work to defend the child from systemic harm. She criticized mass formal schooling for suppressing children’s natural drive to learn, coercing through rewards and punishments, fostering competition, obedience, and subordination, and preparing students for capitalist and bureaucratic life. She emphasized freedom, harmonious activity, respect, noninterference, and a prepared environment supporting peaceful individuals and society. Contemporary Montessori education should share educational pacifism because it provides a moral analysis of schooling harm, Montessori advanced arguments leading toward educational pacifist principles, and her views on educational harm should matter to Montessorians. Both reject paternalism and support structure with freedom. The passage notes concerns about weak implementation, testing, timetabling, coercion, and racial and economic segregation in some Montessori settings, and suggests Montessori educators could form a vanguard against harm. It concludes that mass formal schooling harms many students, while Montessori education can and should provide a nonharmful alternative, though nonharmful education is difficult under external pressures.

This MIT OpenCourseWare lecture introduces Underactuated Robotics. The instructor states the course assumes comfort with differential equations, linear algebra, and MATLAB, and that course notes will be posted online. The lecture motivates underactuated robotics using examples including ASIMO, passive dynamic walkers, aircraft and birds, and a dead fish behind a rock. It defines second-order mechanical systems, fully actuated systems as those where the control-input matrix has full rank equal to the dimension of q, and underactuated systems as those where that rank is less than the dimension of q, meaning the control input cannot accelerate the system in every direction. The definition can depend on state. Fully actuated systems allow feedback linearization, illustrated with a two-link robotic arm. Removing a motor from the arm creates an underactuated Acrobot. The lecture states walking robots, jumping robots, flying machines, and manipulation before force closure are underactuated. Upcoming topics include the simple pendulum, cart-pole, Acrobot, compass gait walking, impacts, limit cycles, higher-dimensional systems, uncertainty, stochasticity, unknown models, optimal control, numerical optimal control, dynamic programming, policy search, reinforcement learning, motion planning, and machine learning. The course website will provide problem sets, lecture notes, and an interactive PDF annotation system.
