He lists uses by regular citizens, researchers, companies, law enforcement, and criminals. He explains onion routing through relays, layered encryption, circuits, symmetric keys, create and extend cells, and relaying TCP stream contents rather than IP packets. He discusses node discovery through multiple trusted directory authorities and signed consensus, abuse and IP-based blocking, hidden services, attacks and defenses, censorship resistance via bridges and pluggable transports, related systems, and future work on hidden services, cryptography, path selection, scaling, and traffic-analysis defenses.

Seven months after Trump administration cuts to the U.S. Department of Education and eight months after cuts to contracts and grants, education researchers report cautious optimism. The department plans to reinstate 20 research contracts, a lawsuit gives a short reprieve to 10 federally funded labs, and it is seeking public input on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences. It has hired an adviser to reform IES and posted high-level NAEP assessment jobs. AERA’s Chavous calls the developments cautiously encouraging but warns severe staff shortages threaten data quality and research progress. Researchers cite limited NCES resources, an executive order requiring a costly admissions-data survey, reduced NAEP reporting, and uncertainty. Some are hopeful about reinvention rather than the death of federal education research, while others remain concerned about long-term impacts and requested anonymity due to funding fears.

This passage discusses saving penalty kicks in soccer. It says saves are difficult, with the chance generally less than 15%, while about 80% of penalty kicks are scored and around 5% are missed. It outlines Law 14 procedures: a penalty kick is usually awarded for a direct-free-kick offense inside the defender’s own penalty area; the ball is placed on the penalty mark; players must be positioned properly; and specific rules apply to the goalkeeper, including consequences for violations. It advises coaches to support and train goalkeepers and to state that they are not expected to save well-placed kicks. It describes psychological qualities, mental preparation techniques such as visualization, positive self-talk, pre-shot routine, controlled breathing, and staying present, and physical preparation. It lists research and cues goalkeepers can study, including ball placement, approach angle, run-up, plant foot, hips, chin direction, body lean, dominant leg, and kneecap position. For the actual kick, it recommends composure, positioning, not diving early, reading cues, reacting, diving technique, and handling outcomes after the kick. It also covers post-kick responses, avoiding mobbing the keeper, substitution rules, rattling the kicker, referee attention to leaving the goal-line early, and studies on standing slightly off-center.

Cement and realty shares traded firm in an otherwise weak market after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced incentives to boost rural and urban housing post-demonetization, with selected BSE-listed stocks up 2%–5%. The S&P BSE Sensex was down 0.39%, or 104 points, at 26,523, and a table listed company price changes.

The speaker discusses a hockey team’s confidence after scoring goals, including a crucial first power-play goal from a deflected shot and Donovan’s second goal. The speaker talks about captaincy, noting young captains around the league and saying Jarome is probably the best player, that becoming great involves being captain and leader, and that a young player should not face too much pressure and is a leader even without the C. Oleg Saprykin is called the unsung hero for blocking a shot that turned into a goal, and the team has traditions involving a silly green hard hat. St. Louis is described as a crafty, skilled forward who creates with space, so the team tries to limit his time and space and finish checks. Kipper is praised for consistency and bouncing back after a rough Colorado game; beating Colorado after the All-Star break made the team feel it could beat elite teams. The speaker stresses focusing when tired and helping teammates. Against the opponent’s forecheck, the team should use the middle, go high off the glass, skate the puck out, and be disciplined rather than only rimming boards. Darryl made players accountable, prevented long slumps, motivated differently, built mental toughness, and believed in the playoffs. Quiet leaders, young players, and late acquisitions helped, and the team believes in itself.

Metagenomic binning clusters fragmented DNA sequences by genome, relying on representations that preserve genomic similarity. Traditional k-mer profiles and embeddings, including large language/genome foundation models, can be computationally heavy, and deterministic embeddings cannot handle sequences shared across genomes or distinct sequences with similar k-mer profiles. The passage proposes probabilistic embeddings that map fragments to distributions, using a contrastive-learning formulation with non-Euclidean distances, closed-form expected pairwise likelihood, and theoretical analysis of covariance. It introduces UNCERTAINGEN, described as the first probabilistic DNA sequence embedding framework for metagenomic binning extending k-mer-based approaches, with theoretical guarantees and empirical improvements over deterministic k-mer and LLM-based embeddings. Related work covers DNA sequence embedding models and probabilistic contrastive embeddings. The proposed model learns an embedding where distance reflects cluster membership, building on lightweight k-mer neural embeddings trained with positive pairs from sequence halves and negative pairs.

Jeff Davis Parish opened schools last Friday and begins the first full week. Summer preparations included streamlining, campus work, bus driver training, orientations, and academic plans. The parish ranks fourth in the state for graduation rate at 92.5%, up three points from last year.

This scoping review examined barriers and facilitators to belonging in graduate health professions education to inform occupational therapy education. Using Arksey and O’Malley’s approach and PRISMA-ScR, searches identified 202 studies; 9 articles met inclusion criteria across occupational therapy, physical therapy, and medicine. Qualitative content analysis revealed three themes that contributed both barriers and facilitators: environment, relationships, and personal factors. Environment included physical space and institutional culture/climate. Relationships included faculty-to-student and peer-to-peer relationships. Personal factors included students’ perceptions of belonging, academic ability, identity, and how identities are received. The review concludes that belonging is important for student success and for diversifying the profession, and it identifies implications for occupational therapy education, including inclusive spaces, teaching, policies, socialization, mentorship, bias education, and further research.

The Supreme Court declined to hear several cases from its Oct. 10 conference and added no cases to its 2025-26 oral argument calendar. It rejected Alex Jones’s appeal of a Connecticut defamation and emotional distress judgment brought by Sandy Hook families. It also rejected Colorado parents’ appeal claiming a school district violated their rights by excluding them from discussions of their children’s gender identity; Justice Alito, joined by Justices Thomas and Gorsuch, concurred in the denial but expressed concern about the constitutional question. The Court denied review, without comment, in a case against Grindr over Section 230 immunity. It declined a death penalty case involving alleged juror misconduct, with Justice Sotomayor, joined by Justices Kagan and Jackson, dissenting. It rejected California property owners’ jury-trial challenge to fines, with Gorsuch writing on the denial. The justices called for the solicitor general’s views in two cases and denied a challenge to New York’s repealed COVID-19 vaccine mandate.

The study proposed a world model framework for autonomous endovascular interventions, specifically mechanical thrombectomy, using reinforcement learning. It trained SAC and TD-MPC2 agents on multiple navigation tasks across ten patient-specific vasculatures in simulation. Single-task SAC training achieved 100% success in phases A1 and A2R and moderate to high success in A2L, A3L, and A3R. In multi-task world model training, TD-MPC2 achieved a mean success rate of 65% versus 37% for SAC (p < 0.001), with significant success-rate increases in A2R, A3L, and A3R, and higher path ratios. TD-MPC2 also showed increased procedure times across all tasks. The study concluded that TD-MPC2 demonstrated superior generalization compared to SAC but remained suboptimal for clinical deployment, requiring future work on planning, generalization, datasets, and translation.

Allison Mack was released on $5 million bail to await trial on sex trafficking and conspiracy charges for recruiting women into a program within Keith Raniere’s Nxivm organization. She will live with her parents under house arrest, and plea negotiations are underway. Raniere is held without bail on sex trafficking charges. Prosecutors allege a secret society where women were branded, restricted and blackmailed. Mack pleaded not guilty; Raniere denied abusing, coercing or harming anyone.

In this bankruptcy adversary proceeding, the court granted summary judgment to Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and Dynamic Management Company, LLC against SCS General Contractors, Inc. SCS opposed but filed no cross motions. The court found no material facts in dispute and granted both motions.

Barnhill’s Buffets filed chapter 11; Wells held a large secured claim and received DIP liens. SCS performed construction work on three Mississippi properties and claimed unpaid balances and equitable liens. As to Wells, the court held that SCS’s equitable lien on the leaseholds terminated when the debtor filed bankruptcy and became a hypothetical bona fide purchaser. SCS was also not a party or third-party beneficiary to the leases. As to the fee interests, Mississippi law required written landlord consent for a lien, which was absent, so no equitable or statutory lien attached. Escrowed funds were to be released to Wells, and SCS retained an unsecured claim.

As to Dynamic, SCS alleged alter ego liability, but the court found the Barber affidavit unrebutted and SCS’s opposing affidavit insufficient. The court granted Dynamic summary judgment, denied SCS’s continuance request, and granted Spirit’s unopposed motion to dismiss.

Los Angeles County settled for nearly $12 million with the family of Milton Olin Jr., a cyclist killed by an on-duty sheriff’s deputy. Lawyers say the deputy texted and typed before the crash and want a district attorney review.

The report offers a comprehensive analysis of the global household sewing machines industry from 2013 to 2023. It provides worldwide and regional market size data for 2013–2017 and forecasts for 2018–2023, along with main manufacturers/suppliers, market status and trends by types and applications, cost and profit status, marketing status, and growth drivers and challenges. It segments the market by region (North America, Europe, China, Japan, Rest APAC, Latin America), type (mechanical and electronic sewing machines), application (home and light commercial), and manufacturers including Brother, Singer, Janome, and others.

The passage attributes human revulsion to eating insects mostly to bugs’ constant presence and weird, alien movement, despite similarities to shrimp or lobster. It cites a UN estimate that two billion people eat bugs, with at least 1,900 edible, nutritious, sustainable species containing healthy fats, protein, fiber, vitamins, and minerals. U.S. reluctance is linked to abundant food and fears about digesting exoskeletons. Primate research found genes for digesting insect chitin, and cooking eases digestion. Cooked insects are appearing on U.S. menus; the Seattle Mariners sold many roasted grasshoppers.

The passage says IES plays a vital role in understanding public education and should be strengthened. A coalition sent the U.S. Secretary of Education recommendations in three areas: prioritizing research on pressing state and local needs; maximizing impact through coordination, scale, and infrastructure; and helping states and districts operationalize knowledge through communication and support. Proposed steps include learning agendas, faster research tracks, decentralized review, rapid-cycle tools like School PULSE, modernizations such as EDPass, restarting RELs and CCs, using AI, social media, professional networks, and coaching to reach teachers, requiring practitioner-facing resources, and recognizing effective research use. The goal is an efficient, effective, accountable federal education research and development system.

LG unveiled its G7 ThinQ smartphone in SA. The G7 is an attractive, competitive device with Gorilla Glass 5, slim bezels, AI camera modes, a Google Assistant/Lens button, Snapdragon 845, 4GB RAM, 64GB expandable storage, dual rear and 8MP front cameras. It arrives in early June from about R13,999, comparable to Sony Xperia XZ2 and Huawei P20.

A stolen handcycle belonging to disabled Navy veteran Gerard Ah-Fook was replaced by Randy Sooter after Sooter saw Tucson News Now’s story. Police are still searching for the person who stole Ah-Fook’s original bike.

The passage outlines a diplomatic offensive and suggested peace terms. It proposes recognizing Bulgaria’s national claims and Serbia’s independence and sea access, and making a strong move toward Italy. Toward Austria-Hungary, it suggests referencing subject nationalities, assuring no dismemberment, and mentioning debts to Germany. Toward Germany, it calls for assurances on democratization, exclusion, partnership, and non-dictation of government form. It addresses Russia, France, and western Allies, then suggests peace terms: Belgium and Northern France must be evacuated and restored; Luxemburg should be ignored; the wrong of 1871 in Alsace-Lorraine must be undone.

The passage discusses how distraction harms productivity, revenue, and opportunities, and presents strategies from The Oracles to improve focus. Suggestions include acting with urgency and avoiding regret; working in a secret location with focusing rituals, deep-breathing, visualization, and 45-minute work blocks; accepting only “heck-yes” opportunities; removing unnecessary activities and prioritizing one task; finding something to obsess about; using a five-step strategy involving stress, a morning routine, 90-minute work blocks, recharging rituals, and optimized sleep; avoiding chasing two rabbits by scheduling areas of focus; and creating an organization-wide “fierce focus” culture with clear purpose and measurable goals.

The disclosure relates to AI-assisted activity training. In embodiments, a system/method/computer program product presents activity categories as multimedia content; receives a voice-based input in a source language including an activity training plan selecting at least one activity and associated activity attributes; processes the input using an NLP model configured in a single intermediate language to extract the selection and attributes; initiates multimedia content with guidance steps performed by a virtual assistant; detects and captures, via distributed cameras, video of the user’s performance; processes the video in real time using an AI model to extract user performance parameters; generates feedback based on a differential between those parameters and target parameters; and renders the feedback contemporaneously in aural, visual, or haptic form. The disclosure also describes a smart mirror or display device, sensors, GUIs, gymnasium embodiments, social sharing, circuit creation, activity augmentation, initial pose determination, feedback prioritization, and multimedia editing.

Devro shares rose nearly a quarter since January; interim results suggest further capital gains and dividends. First-half sales rose 11pc to over £125m, with profits, cash and returns expected to improve as its new plant ramps up.

This VentureWire issue reports that Trinity Ventures closed a $540 million fund, Sun Microsystems will invest an additional $100 million in wireless companies, Bigwords.com ceased operations, and Concrete laid off about 15% of its staff. It also lists numerous private-company financings, M&A deals, board and executive appointments, and venture capital fund and personnel news.

Strength training can build muscle mass, strength, and endurance and help fitness and independence, but incorrect techniques and inadequate warm-up/cool-down can cause injuries. The passage describes rotator cuff injuries from repetitive overhead motions; hamstring strains or tears from sudden powerful movements; herniated discs from sudden extreme or repetitive poor movement during weightlifting; tendonitis from repetitive motions or sudden impact; and tennis or golfer’s elbow from repetitive wrist and arm movements. Prevention includes good posture, stretching, warming up and cooling down, gradual intensity increases, avoiding inappropriate weights, rest, hydration, good diet, ice/compression/elevation, asking for help, and consulting doctors or fitness professionals. Warm-up raises heart rate and blood flow; cooling down regulates blood flow. Pain should not be ignored.

The University of North Texas will hold fall 2017 commencement ceremonies Dec. 15–16 at the UNT Coliseum and Murchison Performing Arts Center. More than 3,400 students are expected to receive degrees; 2,731 undergraduate, 615 master’s and 72 doctoral students applied for graduation, and some summer graduates may attend. Ceremonies include bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral sessions, with live streams available. A special New Orleans ceremony will be held Dec. 15 at the Hilton New Orleans Riverside for graduates attending the New Orleans Bowl; RSVP is required. A reception follows.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2017 states it was incorporated in Washington in 1994 and reincorporated in Delaware in 1996; its common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under “AMZN.” It organizes operations into North America, International, and Amazon Web Services and serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators. It acquired Whole Foods Market on August 28, 2017, and included its financial results from that date. The filing discusses competition, expansion, international operations, fulfillment and data centers, seasonality, intellectual property, employees (approximately 566,000 as of December 31, 2017), properties, legal proceedings, stock prices, selected financial data, liquidity, and tax matters. Selected consolidated financial data show 2017 net sales of $177,866 million, operating income of $4,106 million, net income of $3,033 million, and net cash provided by operating activities of $18,434 million. Total assets were $131,310 million at December 31, 2017.

The speaker said it was difficult because they led by a goal multiple times in the third period and let it slip through soft plays and stick-checking; Detroit capitalized on mistakes. They did not address the team, will bounce back at home, and said Olie not at fault on goals.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting that on March 16, 2021 it issued a revised press release announcing the expiration of its exchange offers for certain outstanding debt securities; the revised amount of 3.041% Notes due 2062 to be issued is $1,934,966,000 rather than $1,934,476,000. On March 17, 2021, in connection with settlement of the Exchange Offers, Microsoft issued $6,250,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 2.921% Notes due 2052 and $1,934,966,000 aggregate principal amount of 3.041% Notes due 2062. The New Notes were issued under a base indenture and a fourteenth supplemental indenture, with semiannual interest and stated maturity dates.

The Supreme Court appointed senior counsel Amarendra Sharan as amicus curiae to examine material produced by petitioner Pankaj Kumud Chandra Phadnis seeking further inquiry into a larger conspiracy behind Mahatma Gandhi’s assassination. The bench said prima facie the material was insufficient for fresh inquiry. Phadnis challenges a Bombay High Court order rejecting his plea and alleges British Secret Service Force 136 involvement.

This lecture introduces graph limits. It motivates them by analogy with completing rational numbers to real numbers, and with minimizing 4-cycle density among graphs of edge density p, where the answer is approached by a sequence of quasirandom graphs rather than a single graph. The main object is a graphon: a symmetric measurable function from the unit square to [0,1]. More general-valued functions may be called kernels. Graphs can be turned into graphons via adjacency matrices viewed as pixelated images; examples include half graphs, quasirandom graphs converging to a constant graphon, and checkerboards showing that rearrangement of rows and columns matters. The lecture defines graph homomorphism densities for graphs and graphons, notes their relation to subgraph densities, and defines convergence of graph sequences by convergence of homomorphism/subgraph densities for every graph H. It discusses distance notions, rejecting ordinary edit distance and introducing cut norm and cut distance using measure-preserving transformations. It states three main theorems: equivalence of density convergence and Cauchy convergence in cut distance; existence of a limit graphon for every convergent sequence; and compactness of the graphon space, related to Szemeredi’s Regularity Lemma and quasirandomness.

An Oct. 16, 2000 email from Steven J. Kean to Maureen McVicker forwards Ann M. Schmidt’s “Enron Mentions,” containing several news articles.

The Wall Street Journal article reports that Lance Stroud, Renard D. Euell, and Ronald Peek won bids for Strategic Petroleum Reserve oil but needed letters of credit. Stroud’s mother died as he sought financing; Euell negotiated with Enron, which said no deal was reached; Peek transferred his interest in three million barrels to Hess Energy Trading Co., and Amerada Hess said an arrangement resulted in “a lot of money” for Peek. DOE said it would accept new bids for seven million forfeited barrels.

The Washington Post article reports Artesia Technologies raised $26 million in a second funding round led by Warburg Pincus Ventures, with investors including Enron Broadband Services, Vignette, Razorfish, EA Systems, and Protege. Artesia is a Rockville-based digital asset manager; funds would support international expansion, sales, and marketing.

Houston Chronicle articles discuss a Nov. 7 referendum on a downtown Houston basketball arena. The arena would be financed through the Harris County-Houston Sports Authority, hotel and car rental taxes, bonds, and a loan; Rockets owner Leslie Alexander and players would benefit. Supporters cite downtown development and economic benefits; opponents call it corporate welfare and question public costs. One editorial urges voters to approve the arena. A Chronicle study of seven recently built NBA arenas found four used less tax money than Houston’s plan, one slightly more, and two considerably more. The articles also mention Enron Field, the football stadium, and Ken Lay as co-chairman of the pro-arena campaign.

Angel, a five-year-old from a Pakistani slum who came to Australia 18 months ago, has rare CLOVES syndrome, causing misshapen, swollen feet and constant pain. She is preparing for a free double amputation in Melbourne by Professor Tony Pennington, arranged after Moira Kelly found her in Pakistan. Initially malnourished and unable to have surgery, Angel is aware she will lose both feet and lower legs but is excited; her mother says Pakistani doctors could not treat her, and her dream is to wear shoes.

The passage documents AGESA software integration requirements, procedures, and host environment interfaces. It covers stack dependencies, the call-out router and single interface portal for binary image builds, UEFI BIOS phases (SEC, PEI, DXE, RT), build tools and libraries, configuration options, PEIM and DXE modules, PPIs/HOBs, build control files, environment variables, and porting steps. It describes stack handling via macros such as AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK and very early reset enablement, plus service procedures for creating/releasing structures, obtaining data eye results, APIC address, execution cache size, PCI address, core identification, memory FRU identification, MMIO merging, and reading event logs. It also details entry procedures AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitLate, AmdInitRtb, and AmdInitResume, along with their parameters, dependencies, and status codes, and required call-outs AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, and system reset.

Tesla Motors, Inc. reported that its 2016 Annual Meeting was held May 31, 2016. Stockholders elected Brad W. Buss and Ira Ehrenpreis as Class III directors, approved ratifying PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal year ending December 31, 2016, and did not approve a stockholder proposal regarding supermajority stockholder voting provisions. The report was signed June 3, 2016.

The Centre, through CBEC, has taken power to verify transitional GST credits, saying only the tax authority can do so. Taxpayers have claimed Rs 1.6 lakh crore, denting CGST cash payments. CBEC says central CGST officers have jurisdiction regardless of taxpayer allotment. A preliminary enquiry found only 5-7% claims invalid. The CBEC also directs that the CGST Act be amended to exclude earlier cess credits, a move experts say could cause state-Centre litigation.

Attorney General Patrick Morrisey renewed a contract with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The program lets West Virginia investigators check stores for recalled products and proper recall notices. More than 40 compliance checks have occurred since 2015, with 25 more expected.

The CCAT Collaboration is constructing FYST, a six-meter off-axis crossed-Dragone telescope at 5600 m on Cerro Chajnantor, with observations scheduled to begin in 2026. It is assembling and testing Mod-Cam and Prime-Cam. Mod-Cam is a cryogenic receiver with a side-car dilution refrigerator, used as an in-lab testbed for a 280 GHz module with over 10,000 KID detectors across three arrays. Prime-Cam, the primary science instrument, has space for seven modules and is undergoing cryogenic validation; additional 350 GHz and 850 GHz cameras and EoR-Spec are under construction. This work presents an overview of the stripline installed in Mod-Cam, characterizes copper RRR and thermal conductivity, and estimates thermal loading for Mod-Cam and Prime-Cam. The measured RRR is about 120, and measured thermal conductivity agrees with OFHC copper literature values. Prime-Cam’s redesigned stripline is estimated to lower 4 K loading despite three times more stripline. Warm crosstalk measurements isolate elevated crosstalk to the SMP-SMA transition PCBs rather than the stripline; redesigned PCBs with impedance-matched vias are simulated to improve crosstalk by about 20 dB. Mod-Cam stripline has proven robust for readout of thousands of KIDs and validates stripline as a scalable readout solution.

The passage presents options strategies for participating in a potential AMD upward move without immediately buying shares. It says AMD has traded from about $9.30 to $15.13, is around $10, has support at the low range and $10, and may have a positive catalyst in its Q1 2018 earnings around 4/25/2018. It describes buying a May 4 $10 call for about $0.60 ($60 per contract versus $1,000 for 100 shares); a call spread buying the $10 call and selling the $12 call for a $0.50 net cost; and selling a cash-covered $10 put for about $0.56, alone or combined with the call spread for a net $0.06 credit. Risks include defined losses, capped profits at $12, and assignment below $10. The author believes AMD earnings will be positive, citing improved products, demand, market-share opportunity, and a 181,917,276-share short position as of 3/29/2018 that could squeeze. Disclosure: long AMD, INTC, NVDA.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 2, 2015. It published a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1 and furnished the information under Items 2.02 and 7.01, stating it is not deemed filed except as expressly referenced. The filing was signed by General Counsel Todd A. Maron.

Police said Jason A. Clifford, 37, a felon armed with a slungshot, forced his way into a southeast Portland apartment. He was taken into custody and booked on burglary, weapon, menacing, coercion and theft charges. A slungshot was found. Two other people with outstanding warrants were arrested but not believed involved.

This WIRED article reviews white-noise and sound machines for sleep. It explains that white noise is a mix of all frequencies humans can hear, while pink and brown noise are lower in the spectrum and may help sleep; many machines offer multiple colors and nature sounds. It discusses tested models including LectroFan, Snooz, Hatch 3/Rest, Babelio, Yogasleep Dohm, Momcozy, ErgoPouch, Amazon, and smart-speaker options, noting features such as timers, volume, portability, night-lights, app controls, subscriptions, and sound quality. For children, it advises keeping machines farther than 200 centimeters (6.5 feet) from where a baby sleeps and limiting sound. It notes some machines run continuously while others auto-shut off, and that a fan can provide consistent noise but a sound machine offers more variety. It also states WIRED selects products independently, may receive compensation from purchases, and donates tested products.

The passage describes the Inverted Hammer candlestick pattern as a single-candle bullish reversal formation occurring at the bottom of a downtrend or downward price swing. It has a small real body near the lower end, little or no lower shadow, and a long upper shadow. Its body color is less important than its position; a green or white body is considered more bullish, while a red or black body is less bullish, though any Inverted Hammer can still indicate a potential bullish reversal. It forms when price opens lower, rallies during the day, and closes near its opening price. The passage says it shows buyers gaining momentum against sellers and may signal an upward reversal, but it should be confirmed with other tools such as trendlines, support levels, moving averages, momentum oscillators, volume, and risk management. It can be used in swing trading and mean reversion strategies, often around support or oversold conditions. It is not the same as a Shooting Star. Backtests cited on the S&P 500/SPY include 132 trades since 1993, a 53–65% win ratio for 1–10 day exits, a 70% win rate, a rank of 39th among 75 candlestick patterns, an average gain of 0.36% per trade, and occurrence as the 11th most frequent pattern. The passage also states 58% of Inverted Hammers occur when the market is overbought versus 42% when oversold, that it is regarded as bearish when overbought and more bullish in a downturn, but the authors regard it as a bearish pattern. Disadvantages include subjectivity, lack of clarity, false signals, and unsuitability for every timeframe.

President Donald Trump will direct his top trade adviser to determine whether to investigate Chinese trade practices that force U.S. firms in China to turn over intellectual property, officials said. The move could lead to tariffs on Chinese goods. Officials said the possible trade probe and diplomacy over North Korea are “totally unrelated.” Trump will direct U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer to determine if an investigation is warranted into Chinese laws, policies, practices or actions that may harm American intellectual property, innovation and technology. Officials said forced technology transfer and IP theft harm the U.S. economy and workers; an investigation could take up to a year.

Violet Brown, a former Jamaican sugarcane farmer, celebrated her 117th birthday and is believed to be the world's oldest living person after Emma Morano's death. The Gerontology Research Group says Brown, born March 10, 1900, is the oldest person with sufficient documentation, though Guinness World Records has not confirmed a new title holder. Brown credits hard work and Christian faith, lives with her son in Duanvale, and Jamaica's prime minister congratulated her.

UC Davis researchers reviewed 50,921 California firearm deaths from 2000 to 2015 and found gun deaths fell. Firearm homicides declined from 4.19 per 100,000 in 2000 to 3.13 in 2014, then rose slightly in 2015, largely due to reduced gang violence and drops in black and Hispanic male homicide rates; white and Asian male rates held steady. Federal research funding was restricted, while California and Kaiser Permanente funded studies.

The passage contrasts digital laggards and leaders in data culture. Laggards set aspirational goals insufficiently grounded in data, leading employees to avoid measurement, adopt best-effort approaches, focus on qualitative process, and stifle innovation. Laggards also fail to connect goals with strategy, causing misalignment. Digital leaders set structured goals and metrics while allowing process flexibility, use transparent data-driven objectives to align teams vertically and horizontally, and require buy-in through top-down and bottom-up processes, though they can struggle with excessive analysis. Leaders emphasize data culture, aligning beliefs, values, and actions; laggards recognize its importance but entrenched habits, lack of skills, and insufficient top-down focus hinder alignment. Changing mindsets and behaviors is difficult, but laggards are not doomed. Organizations fit four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant—and can target actions to reach a strong data culture.

In 2017, the NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU introduced Tensor Cores for deep learning matrix computations. In 2018, the NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU with Turing Tensor Cores and TensorRT brought speedups to data center inferencing, and Turing Tensor Cores enabled AI capabilities in GeForce gaming PCs and Quadro workstations. On MLPerf, Volta GPUs won training categories, Turing GPUs won data center and edge inferencing categories, and Jetson AGX Xavier delivered the best inferencing performance among commercially available SoC devices. The CUDA development platform, CUDA Toolkit, CUDA-X libraries, NGC containers, and Kubernetes on NVIDIA GPUs support GPU-accelerated applications.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU is NVIDIA’s 8th-generation data center GPU, based on the Ampere architecture GA100 GPU. It builds on Tesla V100 and targets HPC, AI, and data analytics workloads. It includes Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), which can partition an A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances with fault isolation and QoS, allowing CSPs to improve utilization and deliver up to 7x more GPU Instances at no additional cost. A100 adds third-generation Tensor Cores supporting TF32, BF16, FP64, FP16/FP32, INT8, INT4, and binary, plus sparsity to double throughput. It delivers 40 GB HBM2 memory, 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, 192 KB combined L1/shared memory per SM, compute data compression, third-generation NVLink with twelve links and 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, task graph acceleration, L2 cache residency controls, improved error and fault detection, NVJPG decode, optical flow accelerator, atomics improvements, and five NVDECs.

The passage also describes CUDA 11 advances for Ampere, including Tensor Core, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, L2 residency controls, async copy, and cooperative groups. It presents DGX A100, an AI system with eight A100 GPUs, up to 5 PFLOPS, third-generation NVLink, NVSwitch, Mellanox ConnectX-6 HDR InfiniBand, and an optimized software stack from NGC. An appendix provides a sparse neural network primer covering pruning, fine-grained, coarse-grained, and fine-grained structured sparsity.

The passage discusses PSA as the most deployed PCa biomarker, but notes it is prostate-specific, not PCa-specific, and can produce false positives in up to 47% of cases, sometimes leading to unnecessary invasive treatment. mpMRI with PSA improves diagnosis, but clinically significant PCa can remain undetected in up to 30% of cases, and biopsies are invasive with risks including sepsis and acute urinary retention. It reviews interest in liquid biopsy biomarkers, including AR-FL, AR-V7, and YAP1, and limitations of RT-qPCR and ddPCR for point-of-care use because of thermal cycling. RT-LAMP/RT-pHLAMP is described as an isothermal alternative. The work reports optimization of RNA extraction and detection of YAP1 nucleic acid and AR-FL and AR-V7 mRNA from PCa patient plasma using benchtop RT-pHLAMP and an ISFET-based Lab-on-Chip device. Benchtop and Lab-on-Chip results were reported as concordant, with Lab-on-Chip detection occurring within minutes and slightly slower TTPs than benchtop. YAP1 nucleic acid presence correlated with more advanced cancer staging and higher initial PSA, while AR-FL mRNA amplification and AR-V7 mRNA were observed in high-risk or metastatic patients. The authors state this is the first ISFET-based Lab-on-Chip capable of detecting endogenous nucleic acids from cancer patient blood and the first handheld biosensor for circulating mRNA for PCa prognosis, while noting needs for larger cohorts and point-of-care-compatible extraction.

European shares rallied after geopolitical tensions had caused their worst weekly losses this year. The STOXX 600 rose 0.7%, euro zone stocks 0.9%, and banks led gains. RWE, Danone, Fiat Chrysler, and Standard Life Aberdeen rose; Ladbrokes Coral fell.

The passage describes Michael Ducey, president and CEO of Compass Minerals International, considering how investors would react to its December 2003 IPO and where he should focus next. It outlines salt’s history and uses, primarily highway deicing and inputs for chemicals, food processing, water treatment, and agriculture. It explains three main dry salt production processes—rock mining, mechanical evaporation, and solar evaporation—plus brine, with differing costs and purity. U.S. salt production grew over the 20th century, demand varied with deicing, and the industry became more concentrated. Highway deicing salt is sold through contracts and bids, while general-purpose salt is sold through sales forces or brokers. Salt use raised environmental concerns, including freshwater salinization, though road salt was not then regulated in the U.S. Compass Minerals completed its IPO on December 12, 2003; its subsidiary North American Salt was the third-largest U.S. salt producer, with general trade salt over 50% of revenue and highway deicing about 40%. Ducey emphasized safety, workforce, and execution, and considered regulatory threats, salt’s large market, and new uses for salt mines.

Mark Schroeder told Steven Kean, copying Richard Shapiro and Elizabeth Linnell, that the EU summary is okay for a quick overview but has errors: Spain’s pool is not mandatory and generation owners may bypass it; Denmark has more than two generators because municipalities own generation; and the Netherlands’ transitional anti-competitive arrangements are not mentioned. He also noted Poland’s omission from Central and Eastern Europe, calling it the most progressive former Communist country. Steven Kean forwarded a note from Suzanne Nimocks saying an attached country-by-country restructuring update might be helpful. The memorandum, from Carol B. White and Pru Sheppard, dated December 6, 2000, is a periodic update on international electric power sector privatization and restructuring from June to November 2000. It says governments lacking funds are opening generation markets to foreign investors even where privatization is not planned, state-owned utilities are unbundling, and competition is being introduced at wholesale and retail levels. Some international players scaled back investments and shifted to less risky markets; European competition was spurred by the EU Directive; Asian economies are recovering and restructuring plans are moving forward; and Latin American privatizations restarted more slowly after currency devaluations. The update covers Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and the Middle East/Africa, with maps and timelines in exhibits, and provides country-by-country summaries for countries across those regions. It notes regional transmission link schemes and hydro/drought issues, asks for comments, criticisms, suggestions, updates, and mailing-list changes, and lists sources and contacts.

The President’s sixth and last State of the Union address discussed challenges, opportunities, and commitments. He said many national problems have existed across administrations, while national strengths include the economy, democracy, exploration symbolized by Apollo 8, common sense, and love of justice. He cited achievements including Medicare, voting rights, federal school assistance, Head Start, college programs, land conservation, job training for five million Americans, 3.3 percent unemployment, and more than 8.5 million new jobs. He urged continued support for model cities, 500,000 homes, an urban development bank, Social Security increases, maternal and child care, catastrophic illness protection, antipoverty efforts, $3.5 billion for job training, Fair Housing enforcement, a five-year Voting Rights extension, $300 million for Safe Streets, firearms licensing, postal reorganization, revised congressional salaries, and a random draft. He reported projected surpluses for fiscal 1969 and 1970 and anticipated extending the surtax with President-elect Nixon’s support. On foreign policy, he discussed Vietnam and Paris talks, the Middle East, arms control and the nonproliferation treaty, Soviet missile talks, aid to developing nations, European unity, trade, and the international monetary system. He closed with personal thanks and support for Nixon.

A study by Rand, Harvard, and UCLA found many U.S. workers face demanding, unhealthy workplaces: one in five report hostile or threatening environments, and some report unwanted sexual attention or verbal abuse. It also found most jobs meaningful and over half supportive bosses.

The passage studies optimal pricing for a monopolist selling a single expiring item to strategic buyers who arrive stochastically. In markets such as event tickets, the item becomes worthless at expiration, making the seller time-sensitive while buyers are modeled as not time-sensitive and may strategically delay purchases for lower prices. The seller commits to a continuous non-increasing pricing schedule over a finite horizon in a Stackelberg game; buyers arrive by a Poisson process, have private uniform valuations and arrival times, observe the schedule, and choose target purchase times, with the earliest target purchasing at the scheduled price. The paper develops Value-Based Threshold strategies and necessary and sufficient conditions to prove existence and uniqueness of buyer equilibrium with continuous valuations, addressing a limitation in prior work. It derives near-optimal closed-form pricing schedules for thin markets (constant price) and thick markets (linear discounting/quasi-auction), validates near-optimality numerically, and shows optimal schedules shift with seller time sensitivity. It reviews related dynamic pricing and mechanism design literature and notes that its model assigns time-dependent disutility only to the seller. The paper is organized into model setup, equilibrium framework, pricing applications and numerical analysis, and conclusion.

The passage explains the toss play, in which a quarterback tosses the ball to a running back attempting to reach the edge of the defense. It says the play is simple, easy to teach and install, and efficient at getting the ball to the perimeter, but it requires a fast tailback and athletic offensive line and is vulnerable to edge pressure. It then details blocking rules from the I Formation against 3-4 and 4-3 defenses, including assignments for each position, and describes Flexbone Toss and Single Back Toss G Pull variations.

The speaker thinks the opposing team is playing the neutral zone differently, with forwards coming back hard and consistently squashing them. They will try something different, review the power play, and hope to tie the series.

Dolliver, Assistant Secretary.

Diane David appealed the trial court’s dissolution judgment, arguing that the court erred in awarding Joseph the marital residence, failing to follow the parties’ desire for equal property division, and not considering tax consequences of liquidating retirement funds. The appellate court found no error on the issues briefed and denied the tax-consequences point as raised for the first time on appeal. However, it vacated and remanded for reconsideration because the trial court made a mathematical error in calculating Diane’s assets.

Tesla, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2016 states that Tesla designs, develops, manufactures, and sells fully electric vehicles and energy storage systems and, through its acquisition of SolarCity Corporation, sells solar energy systems. Its vehicles include Model S and Model X, and it intends to begin volume production and deliveries of Model 3 in the second half of 2017. Its energy storage products include Powerwall 2 and Powerpack 2, with production and deliveries of second-generation products beginning in the fourth quarter of 2016, and it sells solar through SolarLease, SolarPPA, and Solar Loan. Manufacturing occurs at facilities in Fremont and Lathrop, California; Tilburg, Netherlands; Gigafactory 1 near Reno, Nevada; and solar factories in Fremont, California and Buffalo, New York. The filing also discusses risks including production delays, Model 3 execution, supplier and battery-cell constraints, Gigafactory expansion, product defects, competition, and product liability.

His team practiced against New Jersey's power plays, improved each round, and now allows fewer power plays. He calls the playoffs a battle of attrition, says the coach keeps focus on the next game, and stresses denying net access and more traffic in front of the goalie. He says the series comeback boosted confidence, the team believes in itself, and jokes about stealing the puck and picking up game two.

The Red Cross Society of Ghana is appealing to the government and public for ambulances, saying it has personnel and could run an efficient ambulance service; its Chinese-donated ambulance has engine problems and is being repaired. World Bank funded first-aid posts on accident-prone highways. Ghana’s 29 million people have 55 functioning ambulances out of 155, and the Vice President said government had begun processes to provide 275 ambulances.

Vladimir Putin’s fourth presidential election win positions him to further entrench his power, pursue an expansive foreign policy and continue his showdown with the West. A less noticed goal is developing a post-Soviet ideology, amid an identity crisis in which Russia has become hostage to his persona. Oregon public schools have among the lowest graduation rates and instructional days in the country. About one in four students does not graduate in four years. Oregon averages about 165 instructional days versus 180 nationally, though Oregon sets instructional time by hours. State school board member Kim Sordyl says there is a correlation between graduation rates and instruction time and wants more instructional days. Education advocates cite factors including class sizes, start times, absenteeism, poverty, and budget deficits. State Rep. Diego Hernandez says the legislature has not studied the correlation and that adding days is not the answer without adequate supports. A parent moved to Washington for smaller classes and a longer school year, while a high school principal emphasizes instructional time and attendance.

The passage examines whether copper is a leading indicator for stocks. It notes copper is widely used and its demand may reflect economic activity: rising prices may signal growth, while falling prices may indicate slowdown. It tests a copper-vs-stocks strategy that buys SPY for the following week if copper’s last four-week return is positive, otherwise holds cash, backtesting SPY since 2000. Results were decent, with positive CAGR, manageable drawdowns, and smaller drawdowns than Buy & Hold, but the strategy did little from 2008 to 2016. Copper’s past four-week returns were not strongly correlated with SPY’s next four-week returns, especially 2011–2016. It concludes there is no concrete evidence copper is a reliable leading indicator for stocks; performance may be luck or randomness, though copper may help predict business cycles.

The passage reports serious medical problems after BNT162b1, BNT162b2, BNT162b2SA, or placebo. In Phase 1, 2 participants had serious problems: 1/24 (4%) in the BNT162b2 20-µg group had inflamed appendix, and 1/24 (4%) in the 30-µg group had inflamed nerves; researchers did not believe these were vaccine-related. In Phase 2/3, few participants had serious problems, and no single serious problem occurred in at least 1% of participants in any group. Totals included 4/324 (1%) after two 30-µg BNT162b2SA doses and 65/22,470 (<1%) after a 30-µg BNT162b2 booster. For an additional 30-µg BNT162b2 booster, 1 participant had a serious problem between Dose 4 or 5 and 1 month after, which researchers did not believe was related.

Coach Quenneville said his team lost pace and momentum after a perfect start, stopped doing what made it successful, stood around, and played into the opponent’s hands. He praised a player who kept the team in, stood tall, and found the puck, and noted a line’s offensive-zone time and scoring threat. He called Johnny’s season solid and well-earned. He cited high-end conditioning, playoff endurance, line rotation, assessing the opponent over six periods, Finals momentum, home ice, emotional wins, locker-room experience, Boston’s shutdown of Pittsburgh, rest, and game-determined minutes. He said the team must be better and not satisfied.

The President submitted to Congress correspondence concerning trespassers, chiefly from British Provinces, cutting and destroying timber in disputed territory on the Aroostook claimed by Maine. Maine sent its land agent with a force; the agent and two citizens were seized and taken to Frederickton. New Brunswick’s lieutenant-governor sought recall of Maine’s armed party and mentioned British troops, while Maine refused and resolved to support its agent. British officials assumed an agreement gave Great Britain exclusive possession and jurisdiction pending settlement; the Secretary of State denied such an agreement. The President favored amicable settlement, opposed military aid to Maine unless New Brunswick militarily occupied the territory, expected release of prisoners and disbanding of militia, might propose temporary mutual jurisdiction or arbitration, and laid the matter before Congress because its session was ending.

Since 1950, the S&P 500 set 1,526 all-time highs, averaging just under 21 per year, or about 8.3% of trading days; it traded below its high 91.7% of the time and had a 7.67% CAGR without dividends. The longest streak was 12 consecutive years (1989–2000); the market has made highs for ten consecutive years, but 2023 threatens this. All-time highs generally suggest booming business, earnings, momentum, sentiment, and FOMO, though not in high-inflation countries, and the market tends to perform well the following year. The strategy buys when the S&P 500 is less than 5% from its high and sells when more than 5% below. Backtest: 3.20% CAGR, 43.2% time in market, 7.40% risk-adjusted return, 33.75% maximum drawdown. The key is cash when more than 5% below the high; adding 3% annual cash return made a substantial difference.

The passage presents three free mean reversion trading strategies using XLP, FXI, and a 5-day low in the S&P 500, with minor adjustments and performance on different ETFs, plus historical backtesting. It defines mean reversion as prices gravitating over and under a moving average, with abnormal rises tending to revert down and vice versa. Mean reversion is described as the opposite of trend following and as working best in stocks and less well in markets such as commodities. The passage states mean reversion strategies perform best during bear markets, partly due to increased volatility and explosive bear-market rallies, and that long trades worked better than short trades in the author’s experience.

The Federal Government plans to release N750 billion this week to MDAs for 2017 Budget capital projects, bringing this year’s capital releases to N1.2 trillion after N450 billion earlier. Witting cited Finland’s failed summer 1940 effort with Sweden for common defense, attributing failure to Swedish timidity and later Soviet objection, which he called shortsighted because an agreement could have allowed Finland and Sweden to remain neutral. He linked Russian buildup in Finland and the August crisis to Finland’s September acceptance of the Finnish-German transit agreement as relief. Later he said Germans knew of Russian preparations against Germany and Finland. Witting described Finnish dependence on German supplies and geographical limits on Finnish free will. A Swedish colleague and Westman also saw no possibility for such an understanding, Westman fearing German displeasure.

Patanjali launched the Kimbho messaging app, described as a real-time messaging app and pitched as a challenge to WhatsApp. It launched Wednesday, but users could no longer find it on Google Play Store; it remained on iOS App Store and accessible to those who downloaded it. A study in Nature Astronomy by scientists from Caltech, Oxford, and Leicester found hydrogen sulfide in Uranus’s atmosphere, which smells like rotten eggs. The gas was detected via the Gemini North telescope. Scientists say the discovery sheds light on how and when Uranus formed.

The speaker was excited for Manny’s return and contributions on and off the ice, stressed staying even-keeled after a big win and focusing on Boston, and recalled first NHL game, win, and shutout there while being ready when Hank had the puck.

This study examined associations between unintended pregnancy and children’s psychosocial problems over time and indirect effects via maternal mental health and bonding. Data came from the ABCD birth cohort: 7,784 participants, with measurements antepartum and at preschool age, early adolescence, and middle adolescence. Pregnancy intentions were measured as mistiming, unwantedness, and unhappiness; children’s internalizing and externalizing problems were measured with the SDQ. Structural equation modelling controlled for co-occurring risks. At preschool age, pregnancy mistiming predicted more internalizing and externalizing problems, and unwanted pregnancy predicted more internalizing problems; unhappiness did not predict either. In early and middle adolescence, no unintended pregnancy dimension was significantly associated with internalizing or externalizing problems after controlling for co-occurring risks. Maternal bonding problems mediated associations between unintended pregnancy dimensions and preschool internalizing and externalizing problems. Maternal psychosocial distress mediated only the association between mistiming and preschool problems. Some direct associations remained. The authors concluded that maternal mental health and bonding may be important for reducing children’s psychosocial problems rather than unintended pregnancy per se. The authors declared no competing interest.

The speaker says he came to discuss the country’s future, arguing that national success is tested by pursuing citizens’ happiness. The passage describes backtesting a simple trading strategy in Python using pandas, yfinance, and matplotlib. It downloads SPY historical data, calculates simple and exponential moving averages, generates a regime signal of 1 when the close is above both averages and 0 otherwise, calculates returns when the regime equals 1, and plots results. The strategy’s accumulated returns are 804.82%, while buy-and-hold returns are 1505.31%, so the strategy underperforms. It concludes that backtesting a trading strategy can be done easily in Python.

SET_CUST_SFS_SIGNATURE requires the customer to provide an RSA public key for SFS package verification during early boot before BOOT_DONE, and the signature cannot be updated after this stage. Customers define OemCoSignKey using RSA_TOKEN_FORMAT and co-sign AMD update packages with an RSA key pair (2048- or 4096-bit) using RSA-PSS. SFS update packages check patch/firmware versions, can patch registers, firmware images, or drivers, and must validate before applying. SFS commands require specific memory alignment, a customer-provided deployment agent, and ASP verification of customer and AMD signatures before loading/running patches and returning status. Packages are non-persistent across reboots, versioned, and aligned to AGESA releases.

Dane Gudauskas discussed a recent XXL Cloudbreak swell in Fiji, where he paddled into a house-sized left and later felt sore from the adrenaline-heavy experience. He described stormy, challenging conditions with serious wind, many boats watching, and uncertainty over paddling versus towing. After seeing Shaun Lopez tow in, he paddled out, rode a significant wave, wiped out, and broke his board. He compared the wave to his 2016 Cloudbreak ride as having much more energy and power. He rode Patrick’s 8’6″ Channel Islands board, then switched to an 8’10″ backup, but felt undergunned and would have preferred over 9 feet. He called it his most intense surf experience and credited water safety crews, saying he might longboard at San O as a comedown.

Mr. Heard wrote to Mr. Gresham that after April 20 nothing disturbed Seoul’s quiet and no more was heard of the Tong Hâk.
