In a later dispatch, Heard reported rumors that thousands of Tong Hâk were gathering at Po-eun, drilling and threatening Seoul, with flags hostile to Japanese and foreigners. A government officer was refused and asked for troops; 800 European-drilled men with Gatling guns were sent to Suwen. Heard doubted real active hostility, thought urban looting a remote possibility, and said the Tong Hâk seemed quiet and peaceful but had attracted discontented people, possibly under a political party.

Biocon India Group was founded in 1978 by Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw as a joint venture with Biocon Ireland to bulk manufacture enzymes. It later expanded into pharmaceuticals and launched Syngene, a contract research organization, while following an “earn as you learn” philosophy and a culture of openness, trust, and collaboration. By early 2003 it had 800 employees and US$75 million in annual revenues. The Indian pharmaceutical industry grew under policies such as the 1970 India Patent Act and Drug Price Control Order, with outsourcing demand, low-cost English-speaking scientists, genetic diversity, and government biotech support. In 2000 Biocon launched Clinigene to offer clinical trial services and fill a value-chain gap. Concerns included market positioning, organizational culture, publicity, ethics, distraction, and the risk that Clinigene could outgrow its parent. Mazumdar-Shaw had to decide whether Clinigene was a springboard, pitfall, or detour and how Biocon India Group should expand.

The Friday seasonality strategy in crude oil involves buying on Thursday to anticipate a Friday price rise, but it works better if Thursday is a down day, specifically if USO falls at least 0.75 times the 25-day average high-minus-low. Buying on any Thursday’s close may not be good. From April 2006 to the present, it had a P/L of 56.96%, with 98 trades, 60 winners, and an average profit per trade of 0.58%. Thursday is the optimal day, and other days appear random.
#HV doorbell page defines PendingEvent (bytes 0–1) and NoEoiRequired (byte 2); bytes 3–63 reserved. Shared with host, host-owned backing; guest accesses use C=0.

The ADS868xW family consists of single-channel, high-speed data acquisition devices with a SAR ADC and power-optimized AFE. They support true bipolar differential and single-ended inputs up to ±12.288V on a single 5V analog supply and include a multiSPI interface. Features include ≥1MΩ input impedance, a PGA with nine software-programmable unipolar and bipolar ranges, a second-order low-pass antialiasing filter, an ADC driver, input overvoltage protection up to ±20V, and a 4.096V internal reference with fast-settling buffer. The document describes programmable input ranges, internal/external reference options, ADC transfer function, input and AVDD alarms, multiSPI protocols and daisy-chain topology, RESET/ACQ/CONV states, data transfer frames, input commands, output data words, and nine configuration registers. It also covers an industrial analog input module application, NAP and power-down modes, power supply decoupling, and PCB layout recommendations.

Police reported Dylan Kennedy, 19, was ticketed for speeding and marijuana possession and charged with drug paraphernalia; Caton Preston, 18, was charged with minor alcohol possession and third-degree forgery; 75 pounds of unused prescription drugs were collected and taken to Wheelabrator; three children received trespass warrants; a Topstone Road mailbox was smashed; total calls were 204.

The message reports prosperous foreign and domestic affairs, rapid national growth, expanded settlement, and friendly relations abroad though some differences remain unsettled. It discusses commercial conventions and negotiations with France, Great Britain, Russia, Sweden, and other powers; indemnity claims; boundary commissions under the Treaty of Ghent; and efforts to suppress the slave trade, including a London convention and a suspended new convention pending Congress’s views. Relations with Spain, Portugal, Brazil, and new South American states are reviewed, along with commerce and recognition. Revenue is adequate, loans and debt payments are detailed, and the public debt may be discharged within 10 years. The Army, Navy, fortifications, and naval squadrons are maintained to protect commerce and suppress piracy. Congress is asked to consider enlarging engineer corps and supporting surveys for roads and canals. Indian relations include some hostilities, peace measures, and civilization schools. Lafayette’s visit is noted, with a recommendation for a provision for him. The message also addresses peace and wars abroad, judiciary organization, Pacific interests, and improvements to Washington, and recommends preserving the Union and constitutional limits.

Mali’s gold exports are falling, and new discoveries are not enough to offset declining legacy mines. The Sadiola mine needs $380 million to stay open another 10 years and access 3.4 million ounces in reserves, but negotiations over extending its life have stalled in the government, with the reason unclear. Sadiola is a joint venture between IAMGOLD (41%), AngloGold Ashanti (41%), and Mali’s government (18%). Its soft rock/oxide production is depleting, but hard rock/sulphides beneath could support expansion. Sadiola opened in 1997 and helped Mali become Africa’s third top gold producer. Other key mines include Morila, scheduled to close in 2019, and Yatela, which has reached the end of its productive life. Mali’s industrial gold production was 46.5 tonnes in 2015 and 46.9 tonnes in 2016; exports fell from 70 tonnes to 67 tonnes. State mining revenues rose 1 percent last year due to gold prices. Production is expected to fall to 45 tonnes this year, with no new mines until 2018 if all goes well. Gold represents about 25-30 percent of government revenues. Sadiola employs around 1,000 people, 93 percent Malian nationals; expansion could protect and expand jobs. The 2018 election and the Invest in Mali Forum 2017 are noted as relevant to the investment climate. IAMGOLD’s CEO said Sadiola has been a success and the company remains committed to Mali, while IAMGOLD did not comment on deadlock rumors.

NVIDIA RTX IO improves game frame rates and loading, reduces pop-in and stutter, streams high-quality textures, and uses lossless compression to reduce download/install sizes; it plugs into Microsoft DirectStorage, provides GPU-based lossless decompression, and can deliver 100X throughput with 20X lower CPU utilization. The NVIDIA A40, based on GA10x Ampere, is a data center GPU for visual computing with 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, and Ampere GPUs add second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, GDDR6X support, 4K120/8K60 display support, HDMI 2.1, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 decode, and seventh-generation NVENC. The RTX A6000 includes 48GB GDDR6 and NVLink scalability to 96GB, while GA10x GDDR6X memory includes Error Detection and Replay (EDR) to detect and replay data transmission errors during overclocking.

The disclosure relates to systems and methods for providing ground support to vertical takeoff aerial vehicles. Ground stations may include a protective casing, at least one charging mechanism, and an extendable landing pad configured to transition between a closed configuration contained within the casing and an open configuration suitable for landing an aerial vehicle. The ground station may also include a base platform, elevator mechanism, centering mechanism, charging terminals, various power supplies, top-closing flaps, a locking mechanism, a casing transparent to satellite navigation signals, homing aids, a windbreaker, and modules for added functionality. Methods include extending aerial vehicle range by deploying ground stations, and providing a landing pad by raising a base platform, extending a landing pad, allowing the aerial vehicle to land and be centered, retracting it into the protective casing, and charging it.

The study examines near-infrared spectral properties of water ice, epsomite, and halite relevant to Europa. It develops the CRONOS facility with a nitrogen-purged glove box to prepare and measure discrete grain mixtures at cryogenic temperatures. Samples include pure water ice, epsomite, and halite in four grain size bins, plus 50%/50% volume mixtures of water ice grain sizes and water ice with epsomite or halite. Spectra were modeled using Hapke theory with optical constants for crystalline water ice and epsomite; halite was not modeled because optical constants were unavailable. Results show water ice absorption features at 1.25, 1.5, 1.65, and 2.0 µm; reflectance decreases and features saturate with increasing grain size. A ~2.38 µm artifact is attributed to gold standard contamination. Cryogenic epsomite has more absorption features than ambient epsomite; halite shows a 1.95 µm adsorbed water feature. Water ice dominates mixed spectra, and fine grains have disproportionate influence; halite-water ice mixtures are nearly indistinguishable from pure water ice. Hapke models match water ice within about 10%, with linear and intimate mixtures performing similarly, but epsomite fits are poorer and resemble ambient rather than cryogenic epsomite. The passage notes possible errors in published cryogenic epsomite optical constants or desiccation to hexahydrite. It concludes that quantitative spectral mixture analyses using optical constants are needed for abundance and grain size determinations, especially for Europa Clipper MISE and JUICE MAJIS, and that future work will derive corrected epsomite optical constants.

The Sri Lankan rupee weakened for a third session to 158.60/75 per dollar as importer demand outpaced remittances. Dealers cited Fed rate rises, the U.S.-China trade war, and higher oil prices. The rupee hit a record low on June 20 and is down 3.4% this year. Moody’s warned a strong dollar raises emerging-market credit risks. A Chinese port payment eased pressure.

An Uzbek court convicted Zokir Aliyev, a 46-year-old Uzbek-born U.S. citizen, of links to militant Islam and calling for the government's overthrow, fining him $67 for almost 20-year-old offences. Detained June 16, he was freed after six days and tried. Aliyev denied involvement with the Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan; the U.S. embassy declined comment.

The message to the Senate responds to a resolution seeking information about an alleged recent forcible resistance to execution of U.S. laws in Boston. It transmits Patrick Riley’s affidavit; private and unofficial communications concur in the main facts, but no satisfactory official information has been received and some implicated persons deny the account. It calls the violation unexpected and says it appeared to result from sudden violence and some negligence, not from general Boston sentiment. It reviews laws and resolutions on jails for federal prisoners, Massachusetts’s 1843 act withdrawing state jails and penalizing officers for acting under the 1793 fugitive-slave act, and the marshal’s authority to hire a temporary jail. It says no official information shows the marshal provided such a place and that directions will be given if needed. It transmits a proclamation, War and Navy instructions, and State Department telegraphic dispatches. It discusses constitutional and statutory authority over the militia, Army, and Navy; suggests modifying provisions on prior proclamations and militia control and questions summoning organized militia as posse comitatus; and assures that laws will be faithfully executed and forcible opposition suppressed. A separate April 25, 1851 proclamation warns against participating in a military expedition to invade Cuba, a colony of Spain at peace with the United States, citing U.S. law prohibiting such expeditions and threatening penalties and loss of government protection.

Options trading in NVDA is presented as an attractive strategy for potentially large profits from small investments, with long options risking only the premium. It can use calls, puts, writing calls/puts, straddles, strangles, spreads, and collars, and risk-reward depends on the chosen strategy. Prices are influenced by underlying stock price, time to expiration, implied volatility, market sentiment, dividends, market conditions, and liquidity, and should be priced with a model such as Black-Scholes. Key metrics, risk management, hedging, margin, and tax considerations are discussed. Risks include adverse stock movement, time decay, volatility, and liquidity. Margin requirements vary by option type and are generally lower for buying than writing; taxes are generally capital gains and depend on the situation.

Taruni Kumar’s article examines women in India’s 2018-19 Budget. Unlike 2017 and 2016, there is no separate women’s section or allocation. Some economists say the Budget recognizes women mainly in existing social roles and does not address barriers to work or change development patterns. Others see positives, especially the National Health Protection Scheme covering 10 crore vulnerable families with Rs 5 lakh annual insurance per family; Dr Devaki Jain and Dr Ratna Sudarshan praise its potential health access. Dr Reetika Khera criticizes it if similar to RSBY, citing out-of-pocket costs and the need for preventive healthcare. Dr Jayati Ghosh says most promises lack budgetary allocations, citing a 2.7% health allocation increase, a declining health share, cuts to the National Health Mission, and little increase for ICDS. The Budget allocates Rs 3,794 crore to MSMEs and cuts corporate tax for firms up to Rs 250 crore, which Dr Jain says may help small industries employing women. It also discusses sanitation, reduced maternity entitlements, and Ujjwala expansion despite concerns that women may not afford cylinders. The article concludes reactions are mixed and much is continuation.

The speaker has been in Quebec for seven or eight months and feels at home; family members, described as lifelong biggest fans, will attend a game a couple hours away. They credit hard work, preparation, and toughness, with some luck, and say the team can play its style at home or on the road. They expect a tough, exciting atmosphere and will take it one game and one shift at a time, emphasizing the first ten minutes.

The passage explains USB complexity. USB-C and USB-A are connector shapes; USB-C is smaller, reversible, and more common, while USB-A has fixed 5-volt power delivery. USB versions differ in data transfer and power, and a chain runs at its slowest link. USB4, since 2022, supports 20–40 Gbps; USB4 Version 2, certified in 2022, may reach 120 Gbps but is not widely adopted. USB 3 branding is confusing, so speed ratings are recommended; USB-A tops out at 20 Gbps. USB-PD powers or charges devices, with USB-PD 3.1 supporting up to 240 watts. DisplayPort Alternate Mode sends audio and video over USB-C; USB 3.2 uses DisplayPort 1.4, while USB4 requires DisplayPort 2.0. Thunderbolt is an Intel/Apple USB-C standard with stricter certification. Thunderbolt 4 is built on USB4 and supports up to 40 Gbps, 100 watts, DisplayPort 2.0, two 4K displays at 60 Hz, and up to two-meter cables. Thunderbolt 5 supports 80 Gbps bidirectional, up to 120 Gbps with Bandwidth Boost, three 4K displays at 144 Hz, and 240 watts via USB-PD 3.1. Cables must match device speeds and wattage; using the included cable or checking listed speeds can help.

Lincoln argues that a policy intended to end slavery agitation has instead increased it, and that the government cannot permanently remain half slave and half free; it will become all one or all the other. He examines the Nebraska doctrine and the Dred Scott decision as a legal combination that could extend slavery, noting Dred Scott’s points on citizenship, territorial exclusion of slavery, and slavery in free states. He argues that the sequence of events suggests a common plan, even if preconcert cannot be absolutely known, and that the Nebraska bill and Dred Scott decision created openings for further court decisions. Lincoln says a decision making slavery lawful in all states is probably coming unless the power of the present political dynasty is met and overthrown, which he identifies as the work before those who would prevent it. He argues that Senator Douglas is not with them and cannot be relied on because he does not care whether slavery is voted down or up, so the cause must be entrusted to its own friends. He concludes that Republicans, who mustered over 1,300,000 two years earlier, shall not fail if they stand firm.

Henry J. Adams III pleaded guilty to armed bank robbery after acting as a lookout and recruiting a driver. The district court denied his request for a minor-participant offense-level reduction and imposed an above-guidelines sentence of 140 months’ imprisonment. The Tenth Circuit held that Adams was not entitled to the minor-participant reduction because he helped plan the robbery, acted as the lookout, planned to assist in the escape, and expected compensation. It also held that the district court did not abuse its discretion in imposing the above-guidelines sentence, concluding that the sentence was an upward variance based on the § 3553(a) factors, particularly Adams’s extensive criminal history, recidivism, the seriousness of the offense, deterrence, respect for the law, and public protection. The court rejected Adams’s disparity argument comparing his sentence to Nixon’s and affirmed.

Chelsea and Real Madrid are reportedly trying to beat Tottenham to Ajax defender Davinson Sanchez, valued at £40m. Tottenham are expected to hold talks Monday and initially propose £28m, while Chelsea and Real Madrid may make counter bids. Sanchez wants to leave to play in the Premier League and Champions League, despite Ajax's efforts to keep him.

The stick concept is a quick-game passing concept designed for the quarterback to make quick decisions and get the ball out quickly. It is adaptable, has many variations, and is especially useful with a talented tight end, who is the primary throw and can adjust his route. The passage says it does well against man, Cover 3, and Cover 4, but not Cover 2, where the CB can undercut the arrow and the hole shot requires a strong arm and anticipation. Coaching points are given for the TE, TB, slot, X, and Z against man and zone. The QB identifies the flat defender and progresses from arrow to stick based on his movement; slant/arrow is an option against weak-side blitz or a favorable matchup. Variations include 2x2 condensed formation and Trips Flex Sticko.

The address reviews domestic and foreign challenges and asks Congress to act on several goals. Domestically, it proposes making income-tax reductions permanent and effective immediately, ending double taxation of dividends, limiting spending growth, and offering younger workers retirement accounts within Social Security. It seeks affordable health care, Medicare prescription-drug coverage and reform, and medical liability reform. It promotes energy independence and environmental measures, including clean technology, Clear Skies legislation, a Healthy Forests Initiative, and research on hydrogen-powered automobiles. It urges passage of the Faith-Based Initiative and Citizen Service Act, mentoring and drug-treatment programs, protection of infants and a ban on partial-birth abortion, and a law against human cloning. Abroad, it describes assistance to Afghanistan, Middle East peace efforts, a $15 billion AIDS relief plan for Africa and the Caribbean, progress against terrorism, homeland-security measures, and Project BioShield. It identifies outlaw regimes with weapons of mass destruction as a grave threat, cites Iraq’s failure to disarm and alleged weapons programs and terrorist links, supports Iranian and North Korean freedom, and says the United States will lead a coalition to disarm Iraq if necessary.
Walgreens, CVS, and Rite Aid shares fell after reports Amazon might sell drugs online. Amazon held pharmacy benefit manager talks and may decide before Thanksgiving.

The study examines the value loads conveyed by words in 2nd, 3rd, and 4th grade primary school Turkish textbooks offered by MoNE. Reading texts were processed, and words were classified by three applied linguistics experts as positive, negative, or neutral. The database contained 3,637 unique words. Results showed 172 (4.72%) positive, 159 (4.37%) negative, and 3,306 (91.43%) neutral value transfers. By grade, findings included 64 positive, 60 negative, and 1,104 neutral words in 2nd grade; 78 positive, 69 negative, and 1,382 neutral words in 3rd grade; and 119 positive, 109 negative, and 2,199 neutral words in 4th grade. The study concludes there is no observable relationship between grade levels and the values transferred by words and suggests corpus-based methods for preparing textbooks.

This lecture introduces a course on combinatorial theory, graph theory, and additive combinatorics. It explains Schur’s approach to Fermat’s Last Theorem via congruences mod p and how Schur showed this approach fails. It states Schur’s theorem, gives its finitary equivalent, and discusses the equivalence. The lecture proves Ramsey’s theorem for monochromatic triangles and uses it to prove Schur’s theorem by coloring edges of a complete graph according to differences of integers. It then surveys additive combinatorics, including Van der Waerden’s theorem, the Erdős–Turán conjecture, Roth’s theorem, Szemerédi’s theorem, ergodic theory, higher-order Fourier analysis, hypergraph regularity, the structure-versus-randomness dichotomy, multidimensional Szemerédi, polynomial Szemerédi, and the Green–Tao theorem. It also mentions finitary Roth, Mantel’s theorem, a graph problem where every edge lies in exactly one triangle, related bounds, open questions, and course logistics.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email while observing Rosh Hashanah after conservatives published alleged past blog posts criticizing President Trump. Natalie Winters cited comments calling Trump “mentally unfit” and “an institutional terrorist.” The Miami Herald reported Rosenzweig was among dozens of federal prosecutors fired by Trump’s Justice Department who were believed to be at odds with the president or his agenda.

A weekly trading strategy focuses on weekly price action, including positional trading, using the weekly chart for a broader market view in trend following, weekly rotation, or weekly swing trading. Most weekly chart traders are long-term position traders; range trading is common, while weekly trend-following trades can last years. Weekly highs and lows can act as support/resistance on lower timeframes such as H4 and can be traded with breakout or reversal strategies for swing or day trading. The weekly chart itself is likely best for weekly trading, often combined with lower timeframes. Whether weekly or daily charts are better depends on trading style and strategy, so backtesting is needed. Weekly stock swing trading is possible and not subject to the $25,000 pattern day trading rule. A backtested weekly sector rotation strategy is also discussed.

George Morello appealed the district court’s summary judgment in favor of AMCO Insurance Company on claims for breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, intentional infliction of emotional distress, unfair business practices, and Unruh Act violations, and the denial of reconsideration. The Ninth Circuit affirmed. The record did not raise a genuine issue that AMCO breached the implied covenant in handling Morello’s claim. There was no substantial evidence of an unreasonable investigation, AMCO reasonably relied on Dr. Soong’s expert opinion, and no evidence showed bad faith. Because the bad faith claim failed, the related claims also failed. The district court did not abuse its discretion in denying reconsideration; there was no clear error or intervening change in controlling law.

NVIDIA Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended May 2, 2021 reports revenue of $5,661 million, net income of $1,912 million, and diluted net income per share of $3.03. It describes two operating segments, Graphics and Compute & Networking; revenue by market platform was Gaming $2,760 million, Data Center $2,048 million, Professional Visualization $372 million, Automotive $154 million, and OEM and Other $327 million. The filing covers the pending $40 billion acquisition of Arm Limited, subject to regulatory approvals, and the completed April 27, 2020 acquisition of Mellanox for $7.13 billion. It notes a declared four-for-one stock split conditioned on stockholder approval, cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $12.67 billion, $99 million in dividends paid, authorized share repurchases up to $7.24 billion, COVID-19 and supply constraints, debt, leases, stock-based compensation, income taxes, legal proceedings, and segment and geographic data.

The passage describes TMPM page migration commands. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO processes 1–128 migration entries, moves pages in SNP and non-SNP systems, may target DMA-active pages, and updates IOMMU host PTEs. It describes requirements for non-SNP ATS devices, CPU access prevention, SNP Hypervisor states, and 2M-to-4K smashing. Firmware performs validity/state checks, RMP enforcement, TLB invalidations and syncs, hPTE marking, page copying, and hPTE updates.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST moves SNP guest pages, does not support DMA to migrating pages, requires CPU access prevention, source pages in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state, destination pages in Pre-Migration state, and RMP_ENFORCE=1. It performs checks, RMP exclusive access, page-size/state validation, CPU TLB invalidation and sync, copying, and RMP updates.

Errors include command format/content, migration list entry, ring buffer, and hardware errors, reported via command status, migration list entries, PM_STATUS, or MCA. A command can process up to 128 pages; hardware errors may make pages unrecoverable and may cause system failure.

GST requires e-way bills for transporting goods over Rs 50,000, with exemptions. The GST Council approved 153 exempt items, including LPG, kerosene, jewellery, currency, live animals, fruits and vegetables, fresh milk, postal baggage and used personal effects. Non-motorised transport and some customs movements are exempt. Permits, expected after NIC software is ready by October, must detail goods, mode, origin, destination, supplier, recipient and transporter. No conveyance details are needed for intra-state transport under 10 km.

School systems across the country are increasingly equipping buses with technology such as live cameras, GPS tracking, navigation, student check-in/out systems, parent apps, routing and maintenance software, and dispatch monitoring. Districts and vendors say these tools can improve student and driver safety, efficiency, driver recruitment, parent communication, and reliability, and can reduce parent calls. Examples include Kansas City Public Schools’ contract with Zum and Bentonville Schools’ use of Transportant. Costs include upfront and subscription fees. Privacy advocates raise concerns about data collection, storage, retention, and security, while districts and vendors say data are stored securely, not sold, and routinely deleted. Some districts use separate products and store video on their own servers. Limited regulation and affordability affect adoption.

The Infiniti Q Inspiration concept, revealed early this year, will inspire an electrified vehicle platform and up to five new models over five years. They will be built in China at an unconfirmed location and probably as global models. The concept is a four-door coupe, though not all five will share that body style.

SOS pressure defense requires commitment, drill, practice, and coach-driven enthusiasm and positive feedback to build player acceptance; game success reinforces it. On-ball actions are Set, On, and Smother: Set forces the ballhandler to dribble rather than shoot or pass; On guides the dribbler to a sideline or baseline checkpoint; Smother crowds the ballhandler to pressure a shot or pass. Off-ball actions are Snuggle, Off, and Strike: Snuggle denies a pass when the defender is one pass away; Off denies a cut to the basket; Strike is weakside help, including cutting off the three-second area, backside coverage, taking charges, blocking lay-ins, and boxing out/rebounding. Close out moves from Strike to Set after a crosscourt pass.

Fiat Chrysler reportedly rejected an offer from an unidentified Chinese automaker after deciding the financial terms were insufficient. FCA has previously pursued mergers or acquisitions with GM and Volkswagen, while CEO Sergio Marchionne has expressed reluctance to sell the company and favored partnerships in other markets. Chinese automakers may be interested due to Chinese government pressure to expand abroad and their long-standing efforts to enter the U.S. market.

Xiaomi is preparing for its biggest 2018 launch, expected to include Mi 8, Mi 8 SE, Mi Note 5, and Mi Band 3. A report says Xiaomi will not launch Mi A2 in India; a spokesperson said no phone by that name exists but more Android One phones will come. Xiaomi is also preparing to launch Redmi S2/Y2. Last year's Mi A1 was its first stock Android phone in India, originally Mi 5X in China.

In Givens v. Missouri-Kansas-Texas R. Co. of Texas, a brakeman sued the railroad under the Federal Boiler Inspection Act and the Federal Employers’ Liability Act after a passenger train broke down in zero weather when driving wheel tires slipped and one came off. He was ordered to flag the rear and suffered frostbite. The jury awarded $12,000 damages but found the locomotive safe and the accident unavoidable, and the district court entered judgment for the railroad. The Fifth Circuit reversed, holding that the slipping tires and breakdown while the locomotive was in use established a violation of the Boiler Inspection Act as a matter of law, and that the plaintiff was entitled to recover if that violation was the sole or a contributory proximate cause, as the jury found. The court instructed entry of judgment for the plaintiff for $12,000.

North American markets ended a volatile week with sharp losses. The Dow fell 666 points, or 2.5%, to 25,520.96; the S&P 500 lost 2.1%, and Nasdaq dropped 2%, with both benchmarks seeing their worst weekly losses since early 2016. U.S. stocks deepened losses after jobs data showed strong wage growth, while rising bond yields and weak earnings from Exxon Mobil, Chevron, Alphabet and Apple weighed. Canada’s S&P/TSX fell 255 points, or 1.6%, to 15,606.03, its worst week since January 2016, pressured by falling oil, gold and marijuana stocks.

This study analyzes 3,395 syllabi from top 100 NIRF-ranked Indian engineering institutions to examine AI ethics in computing education. Of these, 75 courses (about 2.21%) included AI ethics content across 22 universities, including 15 public and 7 private institutions. Coverage was mostly one session (60%), while 20% had two sessions, 13% one week, and 7% a complete course. Most courses were undergraduate (92%); 76% had no prerequisites. Common topics included privacy, legal aspects, and data governance (42%); accountability and policies (32%); ethical frameworks and moral reasoning (24%); human-AI interaction and agency (24%); algorithmic bias and fairness (18%); AI safety and robustness (16%); generative AI concerns (11%); and social impact and justice (8%). Over 90% of syllabi lacked dedicated AI ethics materials, using standard AI/ML textbooks instead. No courses documented assessments explicitly dedicated to AI ethics. Learning outcomes included privacy risk evaluation, fairness, explainability, ethical dilemmas, regulatory frameworks, moral reasoning, policy, and global governance. The study concludes AI ethics is minimally and inconsistently integrated, with gaps in generative AI, sustainability, justice, and labor ethics. It notes limited public curriculum access and calls for better resources, assessments, transparency, and faculty development.

Sugar and copper drew outsiders to towns like Mazabuka, Zambia, followed by a sex industry and AIDS. Mobile men without spouses and high traffic made transport routes especially affected. Zambia was among the worst-hit countries; at the 2003 peak, 70,000 people died yearly, hospitals and mortuaries were overwhelmed, and many children were orphaned. Zambia is now managing the aftermath through a military-style campaign by DAPP that conducts door-to-door testing, provides drugs and condoms, and uses former sex workers and chiefs to reduce stigma. UN estimates 250 new infections daily remain, but infections have dropped 27% since 2010 and AIDS-related deaths 11%; DAPP has reached over 1.5 million Zambians.

The FBI arrested 23-year-old Jerry Drake Varnell of Sayre, Oklahoma, Saturday for attempting to detonate what he believed was an explosives-laden van outside an Oklahoma bank; he faces a federal charge.

Heart attacks and strokes in the UK have decreased by 30% over the past two decades but remain a major health hazard. Effective medicines to lower cholesterol and blood pressure, plus lifestyle changes such as keeping weight in the healthy range, can reduce LDL and boost HDL. Statins are effective at lowering cholesterol; many side-effect scare stories have been attributed to the nocebo effect, and a study found blinded groups had equal side effects. Other lipid-lowering medicines include Repatha, Praluent, and Leqvio; Leqvio reduced LDL by around 50% with a single six-monthly injection. Quitting smoking, exercise, omega-3 sources, soluble fibre, plant chemicals that block cholesterol absorption, fortified foods, soya, and reduced-sodium salt substitutes are described as heart-healthy measures. The passage also references the TLC diet and health resources.

A federal judge ordered the Trump administration to reverse layoff notices for nearly all remaining Voice of America employees, finding it violated his April order. The ruling criticized officials including Kari Lake, who moved to lay off 532 full-time journalists and support staff as VOA’s broadcasting fell from around the clock to about an hour daily since Trump ordered its closure.

This guide answers common questions about American football. It credits Walter Camp as most responsible for the earliest version of the sport and says he introduced consistent rules, 11-man teams, the line of scrimmage, the quarterback position, and the current scoring format, helping spread the game. It states the origin of the name “football” is unclear and that American football is not an Olympic sport, though flag football may appear in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. It notes 11 players per team on the field, 12 in the Canadian Football League; a 60-minute game of four 15-minute quarters, and a 48-minute high school game. It lists Tom Brady, Jerry Rice, Jim Brown, and Lawrence Taylor among the best players. It describes a field as 100 yards between goal lines, with 10-yard end zones and a 160-foot width. Scoring includes touchdowns (6 points), extra points (1), two-point conversions (2), field goals (3), and safeties (2). It outlines rules and penalties including offsides, encroachment, false start, pass interference, holding, defensive holding, personal foul, roughing the passer, and illegal formation. It defines a catch, turnovers such as interceptions, fumbles, and turnovers on downs, plus the line of scrimmage, neutral zone, special teams, audibles, downs, and the red zone.

“Doubt” premieres Wednesday, Feb. 15, 10–11 PM ET/PT on CBS after “Code Black.” The legal drama stars Katherine Heigl as attorney Sadie Ellis, who falls for client Billy Brennan, a pediatric surgeon accused of murdering his girlfriend 24 years earlier. The cast includes Laverne Cox as transgender lawyer Cameron Wirth, Dulé Hill, and Elliot Gould. The review calls it a soapy, quirky, competent series with a likable cast that addresses real issues but follows a familiar formula.

Police seized a white Holden Commodore over the weekend and are forensically examining it for links to Aaron Marks’s Ballina murder. Investigators seek the passengers, the driver is assisting, and forensics will check for fingerprints, DNA, blood, and related items.

Callum Knott, 21, admitted taking his aunt’s car without consent and driving without a licence or insurance after taking it in Ollerton on November 20 out of boredom and abandoning it when the battery died. Mansfield Magistrates Court gave him a 12-month community order, 80 hours’ unpaid work, a four-month driving ban, £85 costs, and an £85 victim surcharge.

Cover 2 is popular because it works, especially against limited QBs by taking away quick throws and forcing tight downfield throws. It is a 5-under, 2-deep coverage with cornerbacks as flat defenders. Offenses attack it by high-lowing the corners, using 3-receiver surfaces to high-low the middle linebacker carrying the #3 receiver vertical, using vertical concepts, and attacking the open middle of a split-field coverage. Common concepts include smash, fade-out, dig/seam, 4 verticals, and corner/post combinations. Example plays are drawn from Ohio State, Oregon, Michigan, Ole Miss, and TCU.
The East Demerara Football Association held its AGM on Sunday, with six of seven clubs present and Victoria Scorpions absent. Alfred King was returned as president, and a new executive was selected.

Curaleaf Holdings and the cannabis sector rallied last August on news that the Trump administration would consider rescheduling cannabis; the rally fizzled in September but was reignited by Trump’s recent Truth Social post about CBD benefits for elders. Curaleaf reported in-line Q2 2025 results in August and expanded internationally into Turkey. The author maintains a Hold rating on CURLF due to sector uncertainty.

Tesla, Inc. filed Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2020. As of July 20, 2020, 186,361,726 shares of common stock were outstanding. For Q2 2020, total revenues were $6,036 million, net income was $129 million, and net income attributable to common stockholders was $104 million, compared with total revenues of $6,350 million and net loss of $389 million in Q2 2019. Andrew Dawes, CEO of Intels Nigeria Limited, says Intels is partnering with the Federal Government to boost port investment. Dawes, formerly Managing Director of AP Moller Terminal, has 20 years’ experience in terminal operations and logistics. After NPA Managing Director Hadiza Usman visited Intels’ Onne office, he outlined investment plans. Responding to monopoly allegations, he said Intels invests billions of dollars in infrastructure for the NPA as a public-private partner in concessioned terminals and pays more than other private jetties. He could not provide specific 2016 investment figures. Challenges include low oil and gas prices and cargo down 70 per cent, but Intels invests long term. The Phase 4B project can receive a full FPSO alongside and has 4km of key length. Investment pace may slow during recession; the Federal Government controls port allocation. Future plans include closer oil and gas partnership and the Badagry deep seaport with APM Terminals, described as Africa’s largest port with the largest draft. Intels was established 30 years ago to provide integrated logistics and one-stop-shop oil service centres in Nigeria and West Africa.

The passage presents a methodology for studying a digital business ecosystem (DBE), described as a closed or semi-closed system of SMEs interacting in cyberspace through buyer–seller relationships. It asks, under closed and static assumptions, which companies are likely to prosper and survive and which are likely to be suppressed. Because interactions are asymmetric, Markov random fields are considered inappropriate; inspired by biological neural systems, the authors model company interactions with nonlinear coupled differential equations for a fitness variable. The model includes decay, self-excitation, excitatory signals from matching WANT/SELL products weighted by trust, inhibitory signals from similar products sold by other companies, external input, and background input. A simulated DBE of 100 companies and 20 products is constructed using statistical properties from a real DBE, with SELL, WANT, TRUST, and MISTRUST lists; trust is quantified using the Weber-Fechner law. The equations are solved iteratively, with weak companies removed and new ones introduced. Experiments report surviving companies over iterations and monopoly creation under certain parameters. The conclusion discusses limitations and improvements, including the need to associate model parameters with measurable real-DBE quantities.

The passage describes the MOSAIC study, an observational case-control study of 2,513 subjects with and without lung cancer across 77 US clinical sites. Of these, 2,094 were clinically eligible; 1,225 were used for training and 398 for validation. Blood samples were analyzed using untargeted proteomics, RNA-seq, metabolomics, and targeted immunoassays. A machine learning-based classifier was developed. The baseline clinical classifier had an AUC of 0.78; an untargeted proteomics classifier had an all-stage AUC of 0.91; the final multi-omics classifier had an all-stage AUC of 0.96 and a stage I AUC of 0.93. In the validation set, at a threshold set for 87.5% training sensitivity, specificity was 89% and sensitivity was 89% for all stages; stage-specific sensitivity was 80% for stage I, 88% for stage II, and 99% for stage III-IV. The validated model comprised 682 features, including 149 proteins, 346 genes, and 77 metabolic pathways, with no single omics type dominating. Of these features, 412 were significantly associated with cancer stage. Limitations include the need for prospective validation in the intended high-risk screening population. The authors conclude that the multi-omics approach showed high performance for early detection of all- and early-stage lung cancer and may be extensible to additional applications.

The Camarilla pivot point, introduced in 1989 by Nick Scott, extends the classical/floor trader pivot point and provides day traders with key intraday support and resistance levels. It shows four support and four resistance levels, nine total, and uses the previous day’s closing prices. The Camarilla pivot trading strategy is used for day trading, with methods depending on market conditions and various strategies for long and short positions. Fibonacci pivots instead use Fibonacci studies, projections, extensions, and retracements. Day traders use pivot points to define support/resistance or identify potential trend changes. A backtest of ordinary pivot points, based on similar principles, did not reveal super profits, and readers are encouraged to backtest their own ideas.

Long-standing criticisms of academic publishing—research fraud, paper mills, few qualified peer reviewers, and high journal subscription and open-access costs—are helping fuel the Trump administration’s attacks on U.S. science. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and NIH Director Jayanta Bhattacharya have criticized publishing, citing bias, misinformation, access, reproducibility, and “publish or perish.” Scientists interviewed said some grievances are real but doubted proposed reforms and warned the administration was exploiting them. Kennedy criticized top medical journals and moved to bar government-funded scientists from publishing in some; former journal editors said pharmaceutical funding is a problem but his cuts would worsen it. Proposed solutions include a government journal, capping article-processing charges, and public-access changes, but experts questioned whether these would reform publishing or incentives; they said scientists and academic institutions must lead evaluation changes.

The speaker says a line has provided quality minutes, playoffs raise defense and offensive separation, and three players are being rewarded. He discusses puck possession, the team’s comfortable system, close finals games, fortunate bounces, and winning on Sammy Pahlsson’s shot. He also mentions opponent adjustments, regular-season parity due to the salary cap, an injury with pins in a hand requiring doctors’ clearance, optional skates and playoff routines, minor comments about Getzlaf, a big-bodied trade-deadline defenseman’s contributions, limited fourth-line minutes for Carter and Motzko, and team growth after Edmonton, including Chris Pronger’s acquisition and group familiarity.

Lookout researchers reported that over 1,000 Google Play apps contain SonicSpy spyware, which can record audio, take photos, make calls, send texts, retrieve call logs, contacts and Wi-Fi data, and respond to 73 remote commands. Soniac, a messaging app, offered Telegram functionality while stealing data and hiding itself. The account behind Soniac had posted two other now-inactive SonicSpy samples. Lookout noted concerns for enterprises and possible fines from regulatory violations.

The Supreme Court cleared the way for the Trump administration to strip hundreds of thousands of Venezuelan nationals of protected status under federal immigration law. It paused a federal judge in San Francisco’s ruling that barred Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem from terminating that status. The Temporary Protected Status program allows the DHS secretary to designate a country’s citizens as eligible to remain and work in the U.S. when they cannot return due to natural disaster, armed conflict, or other extraordinary temporary conditions. Alejandro Mayorkas designated Venezuela in 2021, redesignated it in 2023, and announced an extension through October 2026. In February, Noem terminated the 2023 designation and the 2025 extension. A challenge followed; Judge Edward Chen temporarily prohibited Noem from ending the status in March, and later ruled on Sept. 5 that Noem acted unlawfully. After the 9th Circuit declined to block Chen’s ruling, Solicitor General D. John Sauer asked the Supreme Court to intervene. On Friday, the justices put Chen’s ruling on hold. Justices Sotomayor, Kagan, and Jackson indicated they would have denied the request; Jackson dissented, calling the order a misuse of the emergency docket.

At the 2018 ICC Under-19 World Cup final, Manjot Kalra appeared nervous in a post-match interview after his unbeaten century, saying the conditions were flat and the team environment great. The passage says winning the U19 title is only a first step, citing limited senior India players from the 2008 and 2012 teams, and Rahul Dravid said the memory should be cherished but not define the players.

Embodiments provide a method, system, and non-transitory computer readable storage medium for dynamic graphics rendering based on saccade detection. A computer simulated scene is rendered for display to a user; an onset of a saccade that causes saccadic masking in the user’s eye movement is detected; and computing resources used for rendering frames are reduced during at least a portion of the saccade duration. Reduction may include skipping or repeating frames, reducing rendering detail or resolution, or adjusting a variable frame rate. Saccade duration may be predicted using an eye movement model and sensor data, and the model may be calibrated. The technique may save power, free resources for other calculations, and be used with foveated rendering and HMD, VR, or AR devices.

The passage provides a step-by-step guide to building an RSI-based TradingView strategy in Pine Script. It describes adding RSI, using DOT on an m5 timeframe with a 14-period RSI and 65/35 overbought/oversold levels, entering long when RSI exits oversold, short when it exits overbought, and exiting at RSI 50. This research studied the basic needs for excellent vocational education management and developed strategies for excellence for institutions under the Office of the Vocational Education Commission. Using R&D methodology, the study had two phases: Phase 1 investigated fundamental data and needs, and Phase 2 developed a strategic framework. Phase 1 surveyed 206 respondents from institutions nationwide using a questionnaire with reliability coefficients of 0.987 for current conditions and 0.983 for expected conditions. Results showed current conditions were at a high level and desired conditions at the highest level; the overall modified priority needs index was 0.179, with Curriculum Development highest (0.198), followed by Cooperation Networks, Personnel, Teaching Management, Graduate Quality, and Management. The developed strategies included vision, mission, objectives, six strategies, and indicators. The six strategies were enhancing professional management effectiveness; developing competency-based curricula to international standards; elevating teaching and learning quality; developing teacher and staff expertise; building a comprehensive vocational education workforce network; and improving graduate quality to high-performance personnel. Experts rated the strategies’ suitability and feasibility at the highest level. Recommendations concerned applying the findings, especially competency-based curricula, and future research on curriculum development models and digital content/professional competency.

American Mint exclusively offers the Band of Brothers Men’s Ring in whole sizes 8–14 for $129.90 for a limited time, available online or toll-free, arriving in a custom jeweler’s box; the 24k gold-layered ring honors brave men and women who fought and sacrificed for liberty and independence.

David Dickinson, a freelance science writer, US Air Force veteran, and amateur astronomer, comments on the August 21 total solar eclipse crossing the US from Oregon to South Carolina in about 90 minutes, with up to two minutes 40 seconds of totality along a 70-mile-wide path. Officials warn of traffic jams, wifi outages, and shortages of alcohol and porta-potties. A small community of eclipse chasers, or umbraphiles, have planned for decades; Dickinson says totality is described as singularly indescribable and primal. He has seen partial and annular eclipses but not totality, and plans to view his first total eclipse at Pisgah Astronomical Research Institute in North Carolina for 107 seconds. Weather may interfere, and some chasers choose Wyoming or Idaho. He warns that partial phases require proper eye protection, such as ISO 12312-2 solar glasses, solar filters, or pinhole projectors. He notes the sun-moon size-distance coincidence, the moon’s recession by 1.5 inches per year, the eventual end of total eclipses in about 600 million years, and another US eclipse on April 8, 2024, over his hometown.
Cancer mitochondria reprogram fibroblasts, fueling growth and altering gene activity.

QQQ mean reversion strategy: exit when the close is higher than yesterday’s high or close. Since January 2000, starting with $100,000 and compounding without taxes, it had a high profit factor, lower drawdown than buy-and-hold, and a 12.34% CAGR versus buy-and-hold’s 9% including reinvested dividends. It worked historically, but future success is uncertain.

The passage reports a study evaluating the maturity of AI in healthcare publications. Prior PubMed searches found limited relevant studies assessing maturity. The study used an in-house collection of PubMed AI in healthcare publications from 2019–2021, classified into 34 medical specialties. After exclusions, final cohorts were 1,647, 3,232, and 2,182 papers. Senior-author country was identified using location-tagger, a BERT model classified maturity from abstracts, and mature articles were manually annotated for model, data, and disease type.

Mature publications numbered 103 in 2019, 253 in 2020, and 83 in 2021, or 6.01%, 7.7%, and 1.81%, respectively; overall, 5% (385/7062) were mature. Radiology had the most mature models, followed by Pathology in 2019, Ophthalmology in 2020, and Gastroenterology in 2021. Mature publications were concentrated in the United States and China, with developing nations less represented. Image data and deep learning models predominated; tabular data declined and text data increased. COVID-19-related mature publications were 4% in 2020 and 1.6% in 2021. The study suggests opportunities to leverage heterogeneous datasets and models across healthcare to increase mature AI publications and guide future research and resource use.

The passage describes the London breakout (daybreak) strategy as a day-trading strategy that trades the upward or downward breakout of the range formed before the London session, usually within the first three hours of that session. Upside breakouts lead to long positions and downside breakouts to short positions. The London range can be defined by the Asian session’s high-low or open-close range. A custom London breakout indicator may provide entry, stop-loss, and take-profit levels and may signal once daily at 3:00 am EST/8:00 am London based on the previous Tokyo range. A EUR/USD backtest found the strategy lost money on breakouts above the high; buying breakouts below the low was better but still poor, with average gains near zero, requiring more parameters or risk management. The passage also gives session times and expresses skepticism about forex strategy performance.

This work investigates bulk MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)ₙ crystals grown by the Inverted Vertical Bridgman Method from Bi, Te, and MnTe. It studies Mn segregation, self-organization of MnBi₂Te₄ septuple layers (SLs) within Bi₂Te₃ quintuple layers (QLs), and effects of stacking sequence and Mn content on structural and magnetic properties. Characterization used TEM/EDX, SEM/EDX, X-band magnetic resonance, and SQUID magnetometry. Four samples from different ingot positions showed distinct layer sequences and average Mn concentrations: Sample A, pure MnBi₂Te₄ and MnBi₂Te₄/Bi₂Te₃ inclusions, 13.5 at.%, with AFM transitions at 26 K and 13.5 K; Sample B, dominant MnBi₂Te₄/Bi₂Te₃, 7.2 at.%, TN = 13.5 K; Sample C, grouped MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)ₙ with n = 7 ± 2, 1.14 at.%, TC = 11 K; Sample D, MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)₄₋₅ with disorder, 1.9 at.%, TC = 9 K. Mn in SLs decreased from about 14 at.% in A/B to 4.9 ± 0.8 at.% in D. Magnetic resonance showed increasing anisotropy near transitions; FM samples C and D had anisotropy fields of about 460 mT and 370 mT. Growth is described in four stages: turbulent flow, rapid MnTe precipitation, stationary flow, and cessation of material flow. Diffusion-driven competition between MnBi₂Te₄ edges gives an inverse relationship between SL spacing and MnTe supersaturation. The conclusions correlate closely spaced, compositionally complete SLs with antiferromagnetic order and larger SL separations or Mn-deficient SLs with ferromagnetic signatures, emphasizing control of melt composition and flow dynamics for tuning structure, magnetism, and topological behavior.

The passage introduces antiferromagnetic domain walls and their dynamics under spin-orbit torque. It presents discrete and continuum models with antiferromagnetic exchange, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, perpendicular anisotropy, damping, and spin torque, and discusses precessional dynamics, propagating domain walls, oscillatory motion for mixed spin polarization, and the magnetic moment of antiferromagnetic textures. Numerical simulations of the spin lattice are used, and the paper’s organization and parameter definitions are also described.

California’s Department of Fish and Wildlife approved Newhall Ranch developers’ plans to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and protect the endangered unarmored three spine stickleback, certifying a final additional environmental analysis and re-approving the project. After a 2015 California Supreme Court directive, Newhall Land/FivePoint revised its greenhouse mitigation plan; the California Air Resources Board concluded it would not result in net additional greenhouse gas emissions. Revised bridge and bank construction methods avoid water contact, eliminating two stickleback-protection measures. The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors is expected to consider final re-approval in July.

Young African entrepreneurs are using new technologies to transform agriculture, improve food security and create jobs, as showcased at the MasterCard Foundation’s Young Africa Works Summit 2017 in Kigali. Jean Bosco Nzeyimana’s Habona Ltd employs 25 young people who collect and separate waste, produce fuel briquettes and organic fertiliser, and reduce greenhouse gases; it produces 50 tonnes of fuel monthly and plans a bigger plant. Pilirani Khoza’s Bunda Female Students Organisation sponsors women science students who train rural women farmers, reaching 360 farmers with methods such as bottle irrigation. Brian Bosire’s UjuziKilimo uses a handheld soil sensor and mobile advice; one farmer earns $300 monthly from vegetable farming, and the company aims to reach 200,000 Kenyan farmers. Richard Munang says agriculture is key to reducing African poverty, employing nearly two-thirds of the population, with women producing up to 80 percent of food.

Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) comprises MEN1, MEN2, and MEN4, all autosomal dominant and typically inherited, though sporadic cases occur. MEN1 involves MEN1 mutations and parathyroid, gastro-entero-pancreatic neuroendocrine, and pituitary tumors; MEN2 involves RET mutations with MEN2A, MEN2B, and FMTC; MEN4 involves CDKN1B mutations and resembles MEN1. This study systematically classified RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B variants from IndiGen, ClinVar, and Mastermind using ACMG/AMP guidelines. It created MAPVar, a compendium of 3,280 ACMG-classified MEN-linked variants, accessible online. From IndiGen pathogenic variants, it estimated that 1 in nearly 341 individuals in India is a likely carrier of MEN-linked pathogenic RET mutations. Variants were compared across 18 global population datasets. MAPVar contains 1,094 pathogenic/likely pathogenic, 1,591 benign/likely benign, and 595 VUS variants. Validation against the GUaRDIAN endocrine cohort found hits in 7 patient cases and 5 unique variants. A multiplex primer panel covering all coding regions of RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B was designed, with 38 amplicons in 2 pools, 65 kb across 33 exons; sequencing 72 patients solved 3 cases. The authors conclude MEN remains understudied in India, RET-linked MEN is highly prevalent, CDKN1B needs more study, and the panel/database aim to aid genetic testing and interpretation.

Bar Harbor Bankshares reported 2016 net income of $14.9 million, including $2.7 million in Lake Sunapee acquisition and core conversion charges. Assets rose $175.3 million to $1.8 billion; loans increased $139 million, or 14 percent; fourth-quarter diluted EPS was 42 cents.

In an argument session, the Supreme Court considered whether the U.S. Postal Service and federal government can be sued over an intentional failure to deliver mail. Lebene Konan, a Texas landlady, sued after alleged intentional nondelivery, saying she filed more than 50 administrative complaints and alleged racial harassment. The government argued a postal exception to sovereign immunity bars the suit; the 5th Circuit allowed some claims, holding intentional nondelivery is not loss, miscarriage, or negligent transmission. Justices debated the terms; some were skeptical of the government’s broad reading of loss, while others feared a wave of lawsuits. A decision is expected by early July.

At the Silverbluff Audubon Center in Aiken County, staff favor the Eagles because a bald eagle pair has nested there since 1994. They note the eagles had not appeared and mention Patriots as national-symbol fans.

Attached is the Rebuttal Testimony of R. Thomas Beach on behalf of the Indicated Electric Generators in CPUC Investigation 99-07-003, supporting the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement and responding to SCGC/TURN’s Post-Interim Settlement Agreement (PISA), which it says fails to unbundle intrastate transmission. Beach argues SCGC/TURN exaggerate differences between the PG&E and SoCalGas systems and that SoCalGas’ backbone system can be unbundled similarly to the PG&E Gas Accord. He says Gas Accord city-gate benefits have been substantial for electric generators, without requiring customers to hold capacity or pay demand charges. He contends SCGC/TURN’s cost/benefit analysis ignores benefits and overstates costs and demand-charge impacts. The Comprehensive Settlement, he says, provides city-gate competition, reduces EG rates and risks, and offers options such as interruptible service, capacity trading, city-gate purchases, and protections against capacity concentration. He recommends adopting the Comprehensive Settlement, including unbundling intrastate transmission, rather than the SCGC/TURN PISA.

Higher education institutions have increasingly prioritized global competencies, with many U.S. colleges incorporating global citizenship into mission statements, but only about one percent of U.S. higher education students participate in study abroad. Non-travel options such as globally oriented coursework, virtual exchanges, and collaborative assignments offer accessible, cost-effective intercultural learning for students facing financial, personal, or visa constraints, while immersive travel offers transformative benefits difficult to replicate virtually. Financial cost and administrative/logistical complexity remain persistent barriers. The article aims to address the absence of robust, replicable frameworks by offering a structured methodology for sustainable education abroad business models, drawing on over two decades of experience and advising universities across six continents. It emphasizes aligning curricular goals with operational realities, mobilizing diverse revenue streams, and cultivating institutional support, and concludes with a typology of business models.

Developing a business model should follow clear curricular, operational, and financial objectives; these three drivers are interdependent. Curricular logistics should primarily shape program design, with considerations including learning outcomes; elective versus required participation; number of credits; when credits are earned; assessment and reflection; strategic alignment; competitive landscape; locational efficacy; modalities of engagement; and programmatic duration. Operational logistics depend on resources and include roles and timing for programmatic design, on-the-ground operations, and ongoing support; risk management; program leadership; travel timing; travel organization; flights; lodging; coordination with partners; local transport; communication; meals; entertainment; emergency preparation; student preparation; student wellbeing; and problem support. Financial logistics aim to keep expenditures at or below income. Expenses include faculty, operational support, external parties, project costs, and coordination expenses. Income includes student tuition and fees, with fees generally going directly to programs; internal and external funding and internal budget distribution are also considered.

The article presents a typology of twelve business models for programs with travel abroad, based on a review of articles from Frontiers: The Interdisciplinary Journal of Study Abroad and Journal of Studies in International Education and 14 informal interviews with faculty, staff, and students. Models include external party-led programs; faculty-led programs with student-payment-driven, revenue-driven, corporate donation-driven, or grant-driven models; and student-led programs often based in student clubs, not for credit, and funded by charitable donations and student activity fees. External party programs use their own employees for logistics and charge student fees. Faculty-led programs may use faculty, staff, or external parties for logistics. Student-led programs may acquire corporate sponsorships and charitable donations. The conclusion states that faculty should address curricular, operational, and financial questions, assess model suitability, and that models can be adapted and combined. Principles include leveraging community engagement revenue or corporate sponsors, using dedicated staff support, and delegating some planning to students.

This qualitative case study examines the effects of advanced technologies on digital transformation in open and distance education, focusing on management. It aims to evaluate technologies used by higher education institutions offering distance education, changes in managerial contexts, future predictions, and a road map. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with four academics at Anadolu University experienced in open and distance education and management, then analyzed using content analysis with Nvivo. The study focuses on technologies such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, augmented/virtual reality, metaverse, brain-computer interfaces, and brain chips. Participants stated advanced technologies will affect future educational environments and require organizations to adapt and reorganize processes. In education, affected dimensions include technology, educational processes, services, and content; in management, they include management, employment, economy, and socio-cultural change. Findings include predictions that AI may take managerial roles; blockchain may support centralized management and recognition of prior learning; AR/VR and metaverse may be used for practice, internships, and virtual selves; brain-computer interfaces and brain chips may support adaptive learning and transfer of learning content. Management may see hierarchy reduction, horizontal/network structures, AI-supported planning, supervision, and evaluation, and changed employment with knowledge workers, automation anxiety, new business areas, and reduced white-collar jobs. Economy may face investment costs, hidden unemployment, increased profit/exports, and new costs. Socio-cultural effects may include increased laziness, lifestyle change, psychological/sociological problems, virtual addiction, decreased communication, and meta-culture. The study recommends developing/testing AI assistants and managers, blockchain certification/recognition, adaptive synthetic content, metaverse teaching systems and virtual selves, and research on brain-computer interfaces and brain chips, as well as larger-scale studies.

The Embassy in the Soviet Union reports that Andropov’s foreign policy shows no significant experimentation or departure from Brezhnev, including a hard line on Afghanistan, Poland, and Southern Africa, and possibly accelerated overtures to China; relations with the U.S. remain a priority. It argues that U.S. policy should return to the first principle of security and lessen the danger of nuclear war, correcting 1970s mistakes by emphasizing both defense and arms control. Arms control should now be a high priority because it is the only available catalyst for improving the overall relationship and is seen by publics as the weakest part of U.S. policy. INF is more urgent than START, and the zero-zero position is reaching the end of its usefulness. The Soviets seek to prevent U.S. deployment without affecting theirs by manipulating Geneva negotiations and propaganda toward European, especially German, opinion. Their position, though a sham, is becoming attractive as layers are peeled off. The application claims priority as a continuation of U.S. application Ser. No. 16/737,601, which is a continuation of U.S. application Ser. No. 15/684,196, now issued as U.S. patent application Ser. No. 10,549,097, and claims benefit of U.S. Provisional Application Ser. No. 62/379,098. It relates generally to medical devices, and more particularly to systems, devices, and methods for delivering neural modulation. Described examples include a system with electrodes on at least one lead, a neural modulation generator, and a programming system configured to determine electrode fractionalizations based on a target multipole, where the target multipole has at least three target poles that directionally and progressively stack fractionalizations to provide a linear electric field over a volume of neural tissue. Examples describe target multipoles with a center, first and second target anodes and cathodes, in-line poles, directional electrodes, flanking electrodes, additional anodes/cathodes, user controls for angle, focus, and spread, user-drawn regions or pain areas, gradient control, automatic movement of the target multipole, and search heuristics to optimize electric field, number of poles, orientation, focus, and spread. Methods include programming a modulation parameter set, determining electrode fractionalizations based on such a target multipole, and delivering energy to provide the linear electric field. The detailed description discusses spinal cord modulation, dorsal column and dorsal horn tissue, sub-perception and supra-perception modulation, activation functions, electrode-tissue coupling calibration, target multipole comparisons with bipoles, field shaping, and modeling/optimization to determine fractionalization.

The passage addresses risk analysis in e-commerce interactions within digital business ecosystems, focusing on a trusting agent and a probable trusted agent. It defines risk as a combination of the probability of failure and possible consequences of failure, and states that the trusting agent should analyze possible risk before interacting. The paper proposes determining the probability of failure using the concepts of FailureLevel and a failure scale. It divides time into pre-interaction and post-interaction start time phases, with the total time space divided into non-overlapping time slots. In the pre-interaction phase, FailureLevel (PFL) can be determined from past interaction history or recommendations, considering recommendation trustworthiness, time, and criteria. In the post-interaction phase, Future FailureLevel (FFL) is predicted from prior FailureLevels using Gaussian distribution and by determining the probability of each failure level on the failure scale. An example compares probable trusted agents B and D. The paper concludes by proposing this methodology and demonstrating it, with determining consequences of failure left as future work.

This study analyzed high-throughput transcriptomic profiles from multiple AD cohorts and brain regions to examine shared transcriptomic signatures and epilepsy-causing genes in AD. Comparing a synaptic plasticity dysfunction (SPD) AD profile with sporadic AD and controls, it found 16 epilepsy-associated genes dysregulated across three cohorts, with 15 consistently downregulated and CERS1 upregulated; nine were mainly synaptic genes. Epilepsy-related pathways, including glutamatergic, dopaminergic, and GABAergic synapses and channel activity, were enriched in the SPD profile. Dysregulation of epilepsy-causing genes was concordant in early and late AD but more pronounced later. The authors conclude that epilepsy-causing genes are disrupted in AD, particularly in later stages, indicating a potential role in AD progression and a two-way epilepsy-AD relationship, though the order of onset remains unclear.

In the Estate of Elizabeth C. Dillingham, the Tax Court considered whether noncharitable gifts by check were complete for federal gift and estate tax purposes upon delivery. Decedent delivered six $3,000 checks on December 24, 1980; the donees presented them and they were paid January 28, 1981. Decedent also delivered six additional $3,000 checks on January 28, 1981, which were paid that day. If delivery completed gifts in 1980, annual exclusions would apply and estate tax limitations would apply; if gifts were complete in 1981, they would not qualify for the annual exclusion and estate tax limitations would apply differently. Petitioner argued payment related back to delivery; respondent argued it did not. The court held payment did not relate back because petitioner failed to prove unconditional delivery of the checks. Under Oklahoma law, a donor’s check does not assign funds, the donor could stop payment, and the donees were not holders in due course. Therefore, decedent parted with dominion and control upon payment in 1981, when the gifts were complete.

NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture introduces fine-grained structured sparsity, which constrains allowed sparsity patterns for efficient hardware operand alignment. NVIDIA’s 2:4 structured sparsity prunes trained weights, fine-tunes non-zero weights, compresses weights for 2x reduction in data footprint and bandwidth, and Sparse Tensor Core operations double math throughput by skipping zeros. NVIDIA states this recipe causes virtually no loss in inferencing accuracy across dozens of networks in vision, object detection, segmentation, natural language modeling, and translation. DLSS uses Tensor Cores to extract multidimensional scene features and combine details from multiple frames, producing an image comparable to native resolution with higher performance. On Ampere, DLSS uses third-generation Tensor Cores and a 9x Super Resolution scaling factor, enabling 8K gaming at 60 fps on ray-traced games; the GeForce RTX 3090 can deliver 60 fps at 8K/8K with DLSS.

GA10x uses GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron, with PAM4 signaling, MTA encoding, new training/equalization, and package/PCB design. GDDR6X supports up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth, over 52% more than TU102, and is the first consumer GPU graphics memory over 900 GB/sec. EDR detects and replays GDDR6X transmission errors using CRC; during overclocking, retried transactions reduce useful bandwidth and cause performance to plateau.

NVIDIA RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and decompression, accelerating I/O up to 100x compared to hard drives and traditional APIs. With Microsoft DirectStorage, it offloads CPU work to RTX GPUs, reduces I/O overhead, supports lossless decompression, improves frame rates and load times, reduces pop-in/stutter, and can reduce download/install sizes. It also benefits professional rendering and VR workloads. The A40, based on GA10x, is a data center GPU for visual computing, with up to 2X FP32, 2X ray tracing, and up to 5X (10X with sparsity) AI throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000, PCIe Gen4, 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, vGPU, Quadro Sync, and EGX compatibility. The A6000 includes a GA102 GPU, 48GB GDDR6, and supports large datasets and NVLink scaling. GA10x supports 4K120 and 8K60 displays, DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a, HDMI 2.1, and HDCP 2.3. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds AV1 hardware decode and supports MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, and VP9; seventh-generation NVENC offers high-quality encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. The GeForce RTX 3090 and 3070 are also described.

This study evaluated PTPN2rs72872125, VDRrs7975232, VDRrs731236, VDRrs11568820, and FCGR2Ars1801274, along with plasma cytokines, in 103 CCM patients; 42 patients were followed for 4 years. Higher frequencies of PTPN2rs72872125 CT and VDRrs7975232 CC were observed in asymptomatic patients. PTPN2rs72872125 CT was associated with higher IL-10 and lower IL-18 and IFN-γ, while VDRrs7975232 C allele carriers had lower IL-27 and IL-23. A weighted diagnostic biomarker using PTPN2rs72872125 CC and GM-CSF distinguished symptomatic from asymptomatic patients. FCGR2Ars1801274 GG predicted symptomatic events during follow-up with high accuracy. In silico analysis predicted an H131R substitution for FCGR2Ars1801274. VDRrs731236 AA was associated with later symptoms, and VDRrs11568820 CC with earlier symptoms. The study reports possible genetic biomarkers for CCM behavior and proposes immune-mediated mechanisms.

Gas bubbles in shallow muddy aquatic sediments, primarily methane generated by microbial decomposition of organic matter, threaten environment safety, climate sustainability, and sediment mechanical stability. CH4 bubbles nucleate under supersaturated conditions, grow beyond pore scale, expel pore water, and deform sediment; larger bubbles are isolated, non-spherical, disc-shaped cavities. The growth and rise of CH4 bubbles in fine-grained aquatic muds are governed by coupled mechanical and biogeochemical processes. Experimental studies indicate that Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics (LEFM) accurately describes bubble growth beyond pore scale in consolidated muds. The model treats large sediment-displacing CH4 bubbles as Mode I gas-filled cracks. The methodology uses a coupled mechanical-reaction-transport model integrating dissolved CH4 diffusion and LEFM sediment response. A sediment cell with a symmetry plane and penny-shaped seed is modeled until a mature inverted tear-drop bubble forms. Solute transport, solid mechanics with a Kelvin-Voigt model, elasticity, fracturing, Henry’s Law, ideal gas pressure, stress intensity factors, and strain energy density criterion are included. The model is implemented in COMSOL Multiphysics using FEM, with meshing and simulation conditions based on Eckernförde Bay data. Validation against analytical solutions for mature elliptic bubbles shows good agreement across varying fracture toughness. Limitations include applicability to individual bubbles and the need for upscaling to effective properties of gassy aquatic muds for remote sensing, acoustic applications, sediment destabilization, geohazard assessment, and CH4 flux estimates.

This passage discusses diagnosing student learning problems and designing teaching activities. It defines diagnosis as teachers observing students’ performances during teaching activities designed for their cognitive processes and identifying possible reasons for missing learning effectiveness. It reviews collaborative inquiry, in which teachers observe and document student performance, hold post-lesson discussions, and adjust teaching plans; it also introduces panoramic cameras to collect evidence of student learning. The study implemented a teacher education course, “Professional Teaching Practicum,” from September 2022 to January 2023 with 22 TESs in five groups. The course had a five-week preparation stage and a 12-week collaborative inquiry cycle, with four repeated three-week cycles in which members alternated as teaching educators and observers. Observers recorded student learning performances and used panoramic cameras; teams then reviewed footage and records, discussed student problems, and instructors adjusted lesson plans. Data included an Observation Record Form and a questionnaire on perceived instructional design capabilities. Results showed observation report scores improved across four cycles, from about 0.47 to above 1.88 out of 2. Perceived capabilities improved significantly in lesson preparation, linking student learning with teaching practice during observation, and adjusting lesson plans after discussion (p < 0.05). The study concludes the program was feasible and improved TESs’ diagnostic abilities and perceived instructional design capabilities, while noting difficulty in ascertaining the effectiveness of proposed instructional strategies due to limited teaching experience.
