The CAT offense is a simple, successful offense against traps, double teams, and full- or half-court zone presses. It uses a 2-1-2 spread and sharp passing, with a skilled triple-threat player in the middle. Rules include baseline back cuts when the ball goes middle, post rolls when it goes to a corner, an optional post interchange, passing to the opposite corner when trapped or double-teamed, and sparing dribble penetration with drive-and-kick. If double teams stop, hold the ball or flow into penetrating spread offenses.

Tight ends remain a big part of football and arguably create the biggest matchup problem for defenses. They split time running short-to-medium routes and blocking, often lining up next to offensive linemen and helping in the run and pass game. The name comes from old football: wide receivers were “ends,” and those who stayed tighter on the line became “tight ends.” They are also called TE or H-back. The position requires strong hands, athleticism, speed, run/pass blocking, route running, and physicality, with a general body type of 6’3–6’8 and 240–270 pounds. Tony Gonzalez, Rob Gronkowski, Antonio Gates, and Shannon Sharpe are cited among the best ever. Because tight ends can line up in different places, run routes, and block, they diversify an offense and give coordinators a reliable weapon.

Guangdong Province is facing China’s largest recorded chikungunya outbreak, with more than 4,000 confirmed cases since late July. Shunde District in Foshan has over 3,600 cases, with additional infections in Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, and Macao. The disease spreads through Aedes mosquito bites and does not pass directly between people. Authorities are encouraging residents to eliminate standing water. Variance components linear mixed models quantify genetic contributions to phenotypes and their sharing. The simplest univariate model assumes two variance components but is likely misspecified for gene/isoform expression because cis-SNPs exert stronger effects than trans-SNPs; the simplest multivariate model is likely inadequate for isoform-level expression because genetic correlation can differ among SNP sets. General multivariate ML/REML estimation with more than two phenotypes and more than two variance components remains challenging, and existing methods are limited. The authors implemented a minorization-maximization algorithm in Julia for such models. In PsychENCODE isoforms, partitioning cis- and trans-SNPs showed cis variants sparse but large, trans variants individually small but collectively large, substantial shared cis-SNP influences, and more isoform-level than gene-level genetic signals; some isoform-specific signals were associated with psychiatric disorders such as autism spectrum disorder.

The passage introduces Solvent Data-Driven Embeddings (SoDaDE), a new data-driven fingerprint for solvents. It trains a transformer on the Spange solvent property dataset, augmenting data via shuffled property-value sequences and using mask, causal, and attention masks. It assesses property prediction and the Catechol Benchmark for solvent selection. SoDaDE achieved lower average MSE than averaged values, RF, and GP on predicting properties of five test solvents. On the Catechol Benchmark, SoDaDE outperformed ACS PCA, DRFPs, fragprints, Spange with GP imputation, RXNFP, and ChemBERTa, with MSE 0.0029 without tuning and 0.0026 with tuning on full data, and 0.0044 on single solvent. Performance was stronger on full data than single solvent, suggesting good representation for solvent mixtures. Non-finetuned and fine-tuned models were similar. The authors conclude SoDaDE is an effective solvent fingerprint from a small dataset and invite replication.

This lecture introduces causality and stability for discrete-time systems. For linear shift-invariant systems, stability is equivalent to absolute summability of the unit sample response, and causality requires the unit sample response to be zero for n < 0. It then introduces systems described by linear constant coefficient difference equations, noting that these equations require boundary or initial conditions to specify a system uniquely. For a first-order example, a causal condition yields h[n] = a^n u[n], stable if |a| < 1, while a different noncausal boundary condition yields another solution. Finally, it introduces the frequency response as an alternative representation to convolution: complex exponentials are eigenfunctions, H(e^jω) is the sum of h[k]e^−jωk, sinusoidal amplitude and phase are determined by its magnitude and angle, and the frequency response is periodic with period 2π.

The lecture begins a new topic on radiation or self-emission from plasmas as a diagnostic. Plasmas are usually hot and can emit radiation from radiofrequency through X-rays and gamma rays; hotter objects emit higher-energy photons. Radiation can cool plasma and also provide information through spectrum, location, and temporal variation. Radiation transport is complicated and potentially non-local, and a diffusive assumption is often used. The radiation transport equation gives the change in spectral radiance \(I\) along a path \(s\) as \(j - \alpha I\), where \(j\) is emissivity and \(\alpha\) is opacity, both frequency- and position-dependent. It treats frequencies independently and neglects processes such as fluorescence. Optical depth \(\tau\) is the integral of opacity along the path. The equation is rewritten as \(dI/d\tau = j/\alpha - I\) and solved as \(I(s_2)=I(s_1)e^{-(\tau_2-\tau_1)} + \int_{s_1}^{s_2} j(s)e^{-(\tau_2-\tau_s)}ds\). In a homogeneous plasma, the limits are optically thin and optically thick; the optically thick case corresponds to a blackbody and leads to Kirchhoff’s law relating emissivity and opacity. Optically thick and cutoff are not the same: cutoff involves reflection and evanescent decay, while optically thick involves absorption with an oscillating attenuated wave. For radiation from charges, stationary charges do not radiate; constant-velocity charges move fields but do not produce propagating radiation; accelerated charges radiate. The proper electric field has near-field and far-field terms, and only the far field gives propagating radiation. Applying this to plasma requires solving the particle equation of motion and integrating over the distribution function; the lecture will give results and later calculate emissivity for free and bound electrons.

MMFP-Tableau is a bioinformatics platform developed at CHOP’s Mitochondrial Medicine Frontier Program to extract, unify, clean, and integrate siloed clinical, genomic, and clinical research data, including EPIC/Clarity EMR, REDCap, and Excel sources. Using Alteryx and Tableau, it provides secure, role-based Web dashboards for approved clinicians and researchers to query and visualize patient- and cohort-level data in real time. It supports precision medicine for heterogeneous rare disorders such as primary mitochondrial disease through use cases including cohort characterization, clinical trial eligibility, genotype-phenotype mapping, medication trends, and risk factor delineation. The platform integrates data from over 2,000 individuals and includes data quality review, HPO coding, automated extraction, and provenance. Limitations include inaccessible non-discretized EMR data, imaging/PACS, scanned PDFs, external-institution data, and server performance issues. It is designed to be scalable and transferable to other diseases and cohorts.

The passage explains the head and shoulders chart pattern, formed by three consecutive price rallies and two intervening pullbacks, with the second rally highest. In an uptrend it is a bearish reversal signal, completed when price breaks below the neckline. The inverse head and shoulders is a bullish reversal pattern with three swing lows and two swing highs. The passage gives examples, target-estimation methods, and notes that quantifying and backtesting the strategy is difficult. It cites Thomas Bulkowski’s research, which found the head and shoulders pattern reliable, with a 93% success rate in a sample of 431 and an average 23% price drop; inverse formations reportedly gave 20–30% returns within 73 days. It also mentions a 1995 Federal Reserve article supporting the strategy but advises caution because Bulkowski used after-the-fact analysis.

The passage presents a first attempt to identify promotional language, or “hype,” in scientific texts, focusing on biomedical research. It defines hype as hyperbolic and/or subjective language authors use to glamorize, promote, embellish, or exaggerate aspects of their research. The authors create formal annotation guidelines and annotate 550 sentences from NIH grant application abstracts containing novelty adjectives, yielding 537 sentences after disagreements are resolved, with 392 labeled Hype and 145 Not Hype. They frame automatic hype detection as text classification and test traditional classifiers, pretrained language models, and large language models. Finetuned BERT outperforms all methods, including the human baseline, while GPT-4O-MINI performs on par with the human baseline. The work notes limitations including subjectivity, a small dataset, coverage of only one adjective group, and a focus on biomedical English texts.

A friend’s conversation with his 28-year-old son about the son’s new job ended with the son angry and defensive when the father offered guidance. The author, a career coach, says giving career advice to grown children is tricky because they are adults who should make their own career decisions, yet the modern workplace is challenging. Ruth Nemzoff offers three guiding principles: know yourself, know your grown child, and know the environment. She also suggests setting a positive tone by asking whether the child wants to vent or receive advice, opening with curiosity, acknowledging what you don’t know, and sharing your own career mistakes. To avoid overstepping, help the child focus on the next best step, suggest talking with a wise third party or therapist for serious issues, and don’t expect the child to follow advice or resent it if ignored.

In January 2008 Nike launched the Air Jordan XX3, a high-performance shoe designed with recycled sneakers and reduced solvent use, as part of Nike’s Considered sustainable design strategy. Nike Inc., with FY08 revenues of $18.6 billion, sourced footwear from about 50 factories and materials from nearly 700 factories in 52 countries; its supply chain had significant energy, greenhouse gas, waste, toxic material, and water risks. In the 1990s, Nike faced criticism over overseas contract factory labor practices. It later consolidated corporate responsibility under a VP and began addressing labor issues strategically. Environmental programs included replacing SF6 in Nike Air, developing water-based cements, sustainability training and metrics, and a 2005 Considered shoe line.

In December 2004 Hannah Jones became VP of Corporate Responsibility, reporting to Mark Parker. Jones developed a CR strategy emphasizing value creation, collaboration, and ROI2. Under Parker, Jones focused on product design as an intervention point. In late 2005 Parker, Jones, and John Hoke formed the Considered Group to diffuse Considered design into product creation units. Nike product creation used triads of marketer, designer, and developer; Considered aimed to integrate environmental choices into that process.

After 18 months, the Considered Group introduced the Considered Index in September 2007. The Index scored materials, solvents, and waste, plus change-agent innovation points, and awarded Bronze, Silver, or Gold ratings. Nike committed that 100% of footwear in Spring 2011 would meet a minimum Considered standard. Core Performance, Nike’s largest category by volume, made Considered part of its strategy and task force; its Spring 2009 line was largely Silver, and the Dual D Hoop was scheduled for Gold in Summer 2009.

Implementation faced challenges: performance and aesthetic risks from EPMs, design complexity, time constraints, profit-margin pressure, uneven supply-chain partner capabilities, and consumer skepticism about green performance products. Some employees worried about Index manipulation, but response was generally favorable, with little expressed opposition. Impact measurement was limited because the first official Considered season would reach shelves in Spring 2009. Competitors such as Timberland, Adidas, and Brooks also pursued greener products. Jones planned to expand Considered to apparel and collaborate with supply-chain partners, while Nike debated how to market sustainability alongside performance.

This study used DFT and molecular dynamics to investigate chlorothalonil (CLT) adsorption on (8,0), (10,0), and (12,0) CNTs and BNNTs. Adsorption was moderate and physical, increasing with nanotube radius due to stronger π-π stacking. MD showed stable adsorption in water with the aromatic ring parallel to the surface. Both nanotubes could remove CLT, but BNNTs were more suitable for detection because of shorter recovery times and larger band gap/electrical conductivity changes; CNTs showed negligible electronic and work-function changes. BNNT work-function response decreased with larger radius. The interaction remained physisorption even as adsorption energy increased.

Pneumonia and tuberculosis pose global health challenges, especially in low-resource settings. Pneumonia is predominantly caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae and contributes to 14% of deaths in children under five; TB caused 1.25 million deaths in 2022. Misdiagnosis is critical, with 22.3% of pneumonia cases misdiagnosed as pulmonary TB. AI, ML, and DL algorithms, including CNNs, are used for medical imaging. The passage reviews studies on TB and pneumonia detection from chest X-rays using UNet, DenseNet, Xception, VGG16, ViT, ensembles, QCNN, knowledge distillation, and hybrid features, reporting high accuracies. It identifies limitations including imbalanced or overlapping datasets, limited generalizability, computational cost, binary classification, and lack of handling non-X-ray/unknown cases. The study proposes a pretrained CNN-based multi-class system classifying CXRs as normal, pneumonia, tuberculosis, or non-X-ray. The ethics statement notes anonymized, publicly available data, no additional approval, adherence to the Declaration of Helsinki, and no funding. The proposed approach compiles a diverse dataset from multiple publicly available sources.

Backtests are scarce, but academic research says it worked well, though the effect has diminished over recent decades.

The passage states that the ISM Manufacturing Index, or PMI, introduced by the ISM in 1948, assesses the US manufacturing sector. The paper reviews integrating NLP and LLMs into psychometrics, especially embeddings of questionnaire items for personality and value inventories. It identifies a key limitation in prior embedding approaches: they rarely reproduce negative correlations between items, which are important for psychometric structure. The authors introduce SQuID (Survey and Questionnaire Item Embeddings Differentials), which subtracts the average questionnaire embedding from each item embedding to strengthen negative-correlation signals without fine-tuning. Using the PVQ-RR values questionnaire, they test several models, with Linq-Embed-Mistral performing best. SQuID-treated embeddings show internal consistency, dimension-dimension correlations, and MDS configurations comparable to human rater judgments. The authors argue semantic embeddings can usefully complement human rater judgments, offering a cheap, flexible, scalable approach, while noting limitations such as unresolved measurement-validity questions, possible training-data memorization, and ethical concerns about replacing crowdwork and creating LLM-based norms.

The Shayona team participated in SMM4H’23 in Task-1 and Task-4, both binary classification problems using social media data. Task-1 distinguished self-reported COVID-19 diagnoses (“1”) from non-diagnostic mentions (“0”). Task-4 used r/socialanxiety data to identify positive/probable social anxiety disorder diagnoses (“1”) from negative/unclear cases (“0”). Task-1 data included 7,600 training, 400 validation, and 10,000 test tweets; Task-4 data included 6,090 training, 680 validation, and 1,347 test tweets. Preprocessing filtered non-alphabet characters, tags, emojis, URLs, stopwords, and punctuation. The authors used a Hugging Face BERT model, digitalepidemiologylab/covid-twitter-bert-v2, and LightGBM. For Task-1, RoBERTa achieved 0.83 validation F1; fine-tuned BERT 0.89; BERT+LightGBM 0.93 validation and 0.94 test F1, with test precision, recall, and F1 of 0.949, 0.938, and 0.943. The same hybrid model for Task-4 achieved test precision, recall, and F1 of 0.756, 0.871, and 0.809. LightGBM showed best results. Limitations included time/computation constraints, possible layer/dimension changes, and Task-4’s lower score because the BERT model was pretrained on COVID-19 Twitter data rather than Task-4-specific data. The conclusion states the hybrid BERT and LightGBM model performed well in Task-1.

A100 combines L1 data cache and shared memory at 192 KB/SM versus 128 KB/SM in V100, includes separate FP32 and INT32 cores, and supports HBM2 with 40 GB, five active stacks, 1555 GB/s bandwidth, SECDED ECC, and a 40 MB L2 cache that is 6.7x larger than V100’s with 2.3x L2 bandwidth. Appendix B discusses sparse neural network pruning, fine-grained and coarse-grained sparsity, and fine-grained structured sparsity.

The device includes an internal 4.096V reference selected by setting INTREF_DIS to 0; REFIO becomes an output, requires at least a 4.7µF decoupling capacitor to REFGND, and must not drive external ac or dc loads unless followed by an acceptable op amp buffer. External reference mode is selected by setting INTREF_DIS to 1, applies 4.096V at REFIO as an input, uses an internal buffer, and requires at least 10µF plus 1µF at REFCAP; buffer drift is typically 0.5ppm/°C and maximum 2ppm/°C.

The multiSPI interface uses a 32-bit input-output shift register. Data transfer frames start on CONVST/CS falling edge and end on rising edge; 32 SCLK cycles is optimal, fewer is short, more is long. It has nine configuration registers and supports write/read, HWORD, SET, and CLEAR commands, appended output flags, and programmable data output. Low-power modes include NAP and power-down. The Rate of Change (ROC), also referred to as PROC or momentum, is a momentum-based technical indicator that compares a security’s current price to its price “n” periods ago. It is plotted as an oscillator above or below a zero line. Positive ROC indicates upward momentum; negative ROC indicates downward momentum. Its formula is (Current Price – Price “n” periods ago) / Price “n” periods ago. Centerline crossovers may indicate trend changes but are prone to whipsaw. ROC has overbought/oversold levels adjusted to market conditions and can remain extreme for prolonged periods. Divergence may signal potential reversals but is not reliable. The “n” period depends on trading style; smaller values are more volatile and produce more signals, while larger values produce fewer signals. ROC was developed by Tom Demark. Traders use centerline crossovers, overbought/oversold signals, and divergences in strategies. Backtests on the S&P 500 (SPY) found an oversold mean-reversion strategy decent with best 4- and 6-day settings but with sharp setbacks; breakout and zero-line crossing strategies were poor; divergences were not backtested. ROC differs from RSI: RSI uses upward and downward price change, while ROC measures one direction and directly measures price momentum. It can be combined with other indicators, such as trend-following indicators. Limitations include ineffectiveness in volatile markets and whipsaw/false signals. ROC performs well in trending markets when traded with the trend and can be used for short-term trading. It does not directly determine stop-losses or position size but can be part of a backtested trading system. The best markets are any with the right trend and volatility, since ROC is based on price alone and can be used in markets with real-time price data.

The passage is a specification update for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3. It lists numerous issues, each with a description, implications, and resolution. Topics include illegal LBAR values at 10000h or higher; PIC interrupt failure with automatic clock gating; prefetch and PRD alignment errors; UDMA CRC corruption; SSMI/DMA and SSMI synchronization problems; GLIU, UART, and USB clock-gating failures; ACPI and PMC register access restrictions and corruption; KEL status reporting errors; PCI timing and read failures; unsupported PIC polling; PIO/UDMA/CD-ROM operation failures; wake event and RTC CMOS limitations; LPC DMA and abort issues; SMBus and GPIO errors; and sleep-state signal deassertion. Resolutions advise avoiding unsupported settings, disabling clock gating, using proper access sizes or alignment, or applying software workarounds. The document ends with AMD copyright and legal disclaimer.

The lecture covers running dynamics using the SLIP model, a spring-loaded inverted pendulum with stance coordinates and flight coordinates. It seeks a 1-D iterated map by using the apex as the surface of section, since x does not affect stability, y determines x dot at apex, and touchdown angle is fixed. Assumptions include a massless leg and toe, an ideal lossless spring, perfectly elastic collisions, and instantaneous leg positioning to the desired theta and rest length, making the system conservative. The lecture describes apex-to-touchdown, stance, and takeoff-to-apex transitions; stance dynamics lack a closed-form solution but can be linearized under small-angle and small-displacement assumptions, producing a return map with stable and unstable fixed points. It also discusses a toe-mass model with spring control, comparative biomechanics across animals, tendon springs, cockroach perturbation experiments and preflex, Raibert hoppers, and SLIP walkers.

The passage reports repeated cross-sectional surveys of pregnant women attending first antenatal care visits in Chadiza, Chipata, Chongwe, and Lusaka districts, Zambia, from September 2021 to September 2022; Chadiza surveillance ended in July 2022. Among 9,221 enrolled women, 8,304 valid SARS-CoV-2 antibody results were analyzed, and 63.8% were seropositive. Seroprevalence was highest in Lusaka and lowest in Chadiza. In Lusaka, Chipata, and Chongwe, seroprevalence rose to near 100% by August or September 2022, while in Chadiza it peaked at 77.2% in April 2022 and declined to 56.6% by July 2022. Most antibody responses were infection-induced; COVID-19 vaccination was associated with higher odds of seropositivity, and infection plus vaccination produced the strongest response. Ratios of seroprevalence to cumulative incidence ranged from 29:1 to 92:1. The study notes limitations including nonrepresentative sampling, antibody waning, and test performance.

This study evaluated the clinical relevance of circulating tumor cell (CTC) genomic variation in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Using whole-exome sequencing of CTC pools from 29 mCRC patients and paired PBMCs as controls, the authors described CTC mutational landscapes and computed 15 diversity metrics. Downstream analyses were restricted to 28 MSS cases after one MSI patient was identified. CTC pools showed high genomic variation among patients. In univariate analyses, patient age, high binary mutant allele tumor heterogeneity (bMATH), high binary proportion of aberrant genome (bPAG), and non-silent BCL9L mutations were associated with shorter overall survival. Multivariate analysis confirmed high bMATH and mutated BCL9L as significant prognostic factors. Low-bMATH patients had longer median survival than high-bMATH patients, and BCL9L-mutated patients had shorter median survival than non-mutated patients. MATH scores from a custom 55-gene panel correlated with WES-derived MATH scores, and high bMATH from this panel was associated with worse overall survival, whereas commercial panels did not show a significant association. The authors conclude that CTC genomic diversity is associated with overall survival in mCRC and may be a prognostic tool, while noting that the small cohort limits generalizability.

BerkeleyGW is presented as achieving exascale quantum many-body materials simulations with performance portability across AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPU architectures, excellent strong scaling, and high fraction of peak for core kernels. It enables predictive quantum materials modeling with double-precision throughput above 1.0 ExaFLOP/s. The passage describes GW and GWPT methods for quasiparticle excitations and electron-phonon coupling, with innovations including GWPT, fast full-frequency GW using a static subspace approximation, mixed stochastic-deterministic pseudobands, OpenACC/OpenMP portability, and optimized HIP/SYCL/CUDA GPP kernels for diagonal and off-diagonal self-energy. Performance was measured on Frontier, Aurora, and Perlmutter using applications including Si divacancy up to 2,742 atoms, LiH defect up to 17,574 atoms, and twisted BN moiré. Results include 1.069 ExaFLOP/s on Frontier, 59.45% of theoretical peak, and 707.52 PFLOP/s on Aurora, 48.79% of attainable peak, with scaling to nearly full machines.

ASP checks DRAM address protection from x86 access, verifies customer and AMD signatures, loads/runs an executable patch, updates patch level information, and returns status. The ASP interface provides base firmware and patch levels. Commands use two 4096-byte pages. GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO is an SFS subcommand whose output buffer is initialized to C7h and contains API version, current SFS and system patch levels, and supported firmware version info. SFS update packages are binary objects aligned to AGESA releases with specified naming and must match the firmware/system patch combination. Updates run parallel with x86/DMA traffic, aiming for minimal impact; some SEV or SEV/ES VMs must stop and restart for an SEV firmware update, while SEV/SNP VMs can continue.

The passage introduces ABXLAB (ABx = Agent Behavior eXperiments), an open-source man-in-the-middle framework that intercepts and modifies real-world web content in real time to create controlled behavioral testbeds. It derives from AgentLab and WebArena and uses a binary forced-choice product-selection setup in OneStopMarket. The study tests 17 state-of-the-art LLM agents across over 80,000 experiments, manipulating product pairs, ratings, prices, presentation order, and nudges: authority, social proof, scarcity, negative framing, and incentives. Conditions include original pairs, matched ratings, and matched ratings and prices. Additional experiments use user profiles and a human baseline of 30 participants. Results report systematic agent biases exceeding human susceptibility. Ratings increased selection by 30–80pp in most models; price effects were strong and intensified when ratings were matched; order effects were heterogeneous and sometimes near-deterministic; nudges shifted choices by 10–60pp, with Wirecutter authority, Buy 1 Get 1 Free, and best-seller cues among the largest. Negative framing nudges were effective. User profiles acted like categorical switches that dominated decisions and suppressed competing attributes. Human baseline effects were modest. The passage states limitations: binary forced choices, controlled textual nudges, one domain, and contemporary models limit ecological breadth. It concludes that rigorous study of agent behavior is needed and releases ABXLAB as a foundation.

It had been the largest and lowest-cost producer for nearly a decade. By FY2011, revenues were $2.7 billion, but revenue growth slowed from 66% in FY2009 to 24% in FY2010 and 8% in FY2011, and the company reported a $39 million net operating loss, its first year-end net operating loss in seven years. The passage attributes slower growth to broader PV industry trends: Chinese government-subsidized manufacturers flooding the market with low-price crystalline-silicon panels, weakening demand, shrinking European solar subsidies, reduced bank financing for solar projects, and falling silicon prices that helped silicon-based competitors but not First Solar. It also describes PV supply chains, market segments, global incentives, Chinese entry, U.S. and Chinese competition, bankruptcies, and First Solar’s history, manufacturing, vertical integration, financial strategy, and acquisitions of downstream solar installers. It closes with deJong’s questions about whether First Solar’s competitive edge had eroded permanently, how to respond to Chinese manufacturers, how to maintain its cost advantage, and whether its systems acquisitions were a strategic benefit or a distraction.

The lecture demonstrates sampling, aliasing, and properties of discrete-time linear systems using a programmable digital filter. The system includes a sampler/continuous-to-discrete converter, a digital filter, a discrete-to-continuous converter, and a smoothing low-pass filter. With the digital filter set as an identity system, the lecture examines time waveforms and spectra for sampling and aliasing. A sinusoidal example shows that if the input frequency is too high relative to the sampling frequency, aliasing occurs; a nonideal low-pass filter can also produce beating. The lecture then inserts a digital low-pass filter with a symmetric impulse response, linear phase, stopband ripple, and cutoff frequency pi over 5, or one tenth of 2 pi. It derives an equivalent continuous-time frequency response by rescaling the digital frequency by the sampling period, so the cutoff is tied to the sampling frequency. Demonstrations show aliasing, filter frequency response, periodicity, changes in cutoff when sampling frequency changes, and low-pass filtering of live audio at different sampling rates.

Michelle Munson and Sarah Narendorf study mental health narratives among marginalized young adults. Research shows illness narratives help improve health management; mental health narratives may involve fear, shame, and stigma. Marginalized youth are defined by the Institute of Medicine as facing social exclusion and added challenges including poverty, safety-net care, disabilities, and young parenthood. How young adults understand their symptoms and help sources influences treatment engagement and self-care. Munson and Narendorf argue patients and practitioners should uncover these narratives together and train providers to consider them, potentially transforming mental health care. The transition to adulthood can be devastating or hopeful, and how the mental health system engages and communicates with young adults matters. A team approach between professional and young adult is best. Their studies use in-depth interviews and qualitative methods; current NIMH research, “Just Do You,” takes place in Brooklyn and the Bronx. They call for replication and technology-based interventions with the Jed Foundation. Many marginalized young adults do not get help due to lack of access, poverty, competing demands, and feeling unheard or disrespected; providers need cultural humility and to listen to their narratives.

Sixteen-year-old Murad Rahimov, who has loved space since age three in Uzbekistan, toured NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center with his mother. The private tour came after listener Aaron Schnittman heard an NPR story about the Rahimov family’s naturalization and connected Murad with his brother Jeremy, an astrophysicist at Goddard. Jeremy showed them the clean room, spacecraft testing chambers, and laser lab, and discussed black holes, Einstein, and time travel. Murad, a U.S. citizen and high school junior, dreams of becoming an astronaut and working for NASA, aims for Cal Tech, and hopes to lead a Mars mission. He plans to watch the total solar eclipse in Kansas City.

Anita Anand, presenter of BBC Radio 4’s Any Answers since 2012, was told to stand down less than 24 hours before presenting an edition because it was due to discuss the BBC pay dispute. Julian Worricker presented instead, and she is thought to return next week. Critics accused the BBC of implying women journalists could not be impartial. The BBC cited impartiality rules for presenters who have publicly commented on a subject; Jenni Murray had similarly opted out of a BBC pay discussion.

The NRA told members YETI had cut ties with it. YETI responded that it had notified the NRA Foundation and others it was eliminating outdated discounting programs and offering an alternative customization program broadly available. YETI said the NRA-ILA’s statement contradicted these facts. Some NRA supporters planned a boycott, and some destroyed YETI products under #YetiCoolerChallenge. YETI said it supports the Second Amendment.

This study benchmarks 15 summary-level data-based Mendelian randomization (MR) methods using real-world GWAS datasets. It evaluates type I error control under population stratification, pleiotropy, and family-level confounding; accuracy of causal effect estimates using six same-trait exposure-outcome pairs with true effect one; and replicability/power using LDL-C and CAD across six LDL-C GWAS datasets and varied IV thresholds. MR-APSS, Egger, and Weighted-mode generally controlled type I errors across confounding scenarios, while CAUSE often produced deflated p-values. Many other methods showed inflated type I errors, especially under population stratification, and performance varied with IV threshold. MR-APSS produced accurate estimates closer to the true value with confidence intervals covering it. CAUSE and MR-APSS showed high replicability in LDL-C–CAD analyses, though CAUSE p-values were deflated. Looser IV thresholds generally increased type I error inflation and bias. The authors recommend negative controls, multiple IV selection standards, and multiple independent data sources. Limitations include coexisting confounders, indirect power assessment, use of same-trait pairs for accuracy, and focus on summary-level MR.

The passage lists foods rich in folate/vitamin B9, including asparagus, broccoli, citrus fruits, legumes, avocado, lady’s finger, nuts and seeds, cauliflower, beetroot, carrots, and corn. It provides folate amounts or percentages for several foods, such as asparagus, broccoli, oranges, avocado, lady’s finger, cauliflower, beetroot, carrots, and corn, and notes preparation or other nutrient details.

Zita Kovács began winemaking seven years ago, faced early prejudice as a woman, and now designs labels and names wines. Zsófi Laposa says winemaking was male-centred and physical, but technology and greater openness brought more women, who add gentleness and uniqueness. Krisztina Csetvei founded Csetvei Winery in Mór in 2011, combines winemaking with raising daughter Panna, and will present Panna Rose at VinCE Budapest. Andi Gere co-manages Gere Attila winery, where femininity has refined wines and women balance men’s heavy wines with elegance.

The present disclosure provides articles exhibiting structural color through optical elements, optionally combined with a textured surface, primer layer, protective layer, or polymeric layer, without requiring inks or pigments. The optical element can include at least one optical layer, such as a single or multilayer reflector or multilayer filter, and can be disposed on components of footwear, apparel, or sporting equipment. Structural color can be single-hue, multihued, iridescent, or limited iridescence and can be characterized using CIE 1976, CIELCH, or PANTONE standards. Methods include disposing the optical element onto a surface of an article or component.

New deals announced Monday suggest mergers and acquisitions among junior mining companies, especially gold, could be heating up after slow months. Hecla Mining proposed a US$462-million cash-and-share acquisition of Klondex Mines, and Alio Gold proposed a $128-million cash acquisition of Rye Patch Gold. Canada’s metals and mining sector had six mergers in 2018 versus 19 at the same time in 2017. Hecla would acquire three Nevada gold mines producing about 150,000 ounces annually, raising its output to about 370,000 ounces of gold plus 10 million ounces of silver. Alio offered $1.57 per share, and Anaconda Mining proposed 14 cents per share for Maritime Resources. Leagold’s CEO expects more junior consolidation.

The speaker says Detroit is the strongest team faced, with firepower and arguably the best goaltender in the world. Players must recognize the first ten minutes’ calls, play tough and clean, and avoid penalties, especially after the whistle and against Detroit’s power play. The speaker has old-school views on embellishment and marginal calls. Detroit’s line is big, strong, skates well, and is coordinated, with Kris Draper as an underrated catalyst. A meeting focused on sticking to the game and setting aside family, ticket requests, and distractions before tomorrow night’s game. The speaker is excited to play in front of home fans in the finals and expects tailgating. Last night’s penalties limited flow; the line must rebound and generate offense. Faceoffs are important against a puck-possession team, and centers must win draws. Detroit has crafty faceoff men, including Yzerman, Fedorov, and Draper. An opposing player is called the league’s best defenseman, smart positionally and hard to hit. The speaker thinks their arena is louder than Detroit’s. Line changes require alertness, and the speaker jokes his beard is growing out of control.

MSPM0C1105/6 are cost-optimized, ultra-low-power 32-bit MCUs in the MSPM0 family, based on Arm Cortex-M0+ and operating up to 32MHz, from -40°C to 125°C and 1.62V to 3.6V. They provide up to 64KB flash, 8KB SRAM, an on-chip oscillator, DMA, CRC-16, analog peripherals such as a 12-bit ADC, comparator with DAC, temperature sensor, timers, and UART/SPI/I2C communication peripherals. They are supported by hardware and software ecosystem resources, including LaunchPad, a free SDK, MSP Academy, and TI E2E forums.
Pusa, 63, a Congress member and former Nagaland minister, was buried in Viswema after his funeral. He leaves his wife, two sons and a daughter.

India’s state-run banks posted a combined loss of 853.7 billion rupees in the fiscal year ended March, the highest in their history, as provisions for bad loans surged after stricter central bank rules. For the March quarter alone, losses totaled 626.81 billion rupees, with all but two of 21 majority state-owned banks losing money. Gross non-performing loans rose about 15 percent to 8.96 trillion rupees. New Delhi has a 2.11 trillion-rupee recapitalization plan.

A Zillow analysis found that U.S. homes with air conditioning sold for 2.5 percent more than homes without it, a premium of nearly $5,500. The premium was highest in San Antonio at 5.8 percent, followed by Cincinnati at 5.7 percent; Detroit, Indianapolis and Las Vegas had 5 percent premiums. Air conditioning was listed as a required feature by 62 percent of buyers, compared with 48 percent for private outdoor space. Nationwide, 66.1 percent of homes sold in the past year had air conditioning, including 99.1 percent in Las Vegas and 97.9 percent in Phoenix. Rentals with central air conditioning rented for 2.8 percent more, or about $40 per month.

Options trading in IWM involves buying and selling call and put options. Call options give the right to buy shares at an agreed-upon price before expiration, while put options give the right to sell. Options can offer leverage, hedging, and speculation, but they carry risks, including loss of the entire investment and potentially unlimited risk from short calls. Available order types include market, limit, stop, and trailing stop orders. Strategies include buying calls or puts, selling covered calls, and buying protective puts. Requirements include eligibility, sufficient funds, a broker margin account, and awareness of risks and regulations; margin trading is allowed but risky. Investors should research, use technical indicators, set stop-losses, diversify, limit allocation, and backtest strategies. Fees, minimum balances, and taxes depend on the broker and holding period. The passage advises beginners not to trade options and to backtest before committing funds.

Gov. Kay Ivey announced the voluntary Alabama Sentry Program to train school administrators. In schools without a resource officer, participating administrators may keep a firearm in a secured safe to respond to an active shooter. Participants need training and approval from the local superintendent, school board, and county sheriff, and must provide an approved weapon, ammunition, and bullet-proof vest. Ivey said it provides security until more school resource officers are added, a SAFE Council recommendation.

This disclosure describes systems and methods for blockchain transaction risk management and automated tracing of digital asset flows using artificial intelligence and machine learning. Blockchain transaction data and intelligence labels are received, transaction flows are selected, labels are applied to addresses, and trace parameters are used with an artificial intelligence graph search algorithm to determine auto-traced paths. Reports may include suspicious blockchain addresses and may trigger alerts or transaction suspension. The disclosure also describes risk classification, risk scoring regression, rules-based risk policy, security controls, address clustering, and AutoML model training and prediction pipelines for identifying risky or illicit blockchain activity.

The Bank of England warned that AI-related stock valuations may be unsustainable and resemble dot-com bubble excess, with concentrated gains among Nvidia, Microsoft, and Meta potentially amplifying systemic risks. It cited power, semiconductor, and data infrastructure bottlenecks as possible constraints and said a loss of confidence could cause cross-border market volatility. While the UK financial system remains broadly stable, the BoE urged investor caution, warning that a correction could be swift and severe.

Plum School District officials began 2018-19 budget discussions Tuesday, hoping to avoid a third straight tax increase. The district starts the year more than $4 million in debt; its $66 million budget included a 0.866-mill tax hike. The workshop also covers recruiting Chinese tuition students, elementary construction, consolidation, redistricting, and beginning the Regency Park Elementary closure process, plus a special personnel meeting.

A survey of 100 financial services professionals by Infosys Finacle found over 80% of global bankers expect commercial blockchain adoption by 2020; over half of financial institutions are investing or planning to invest this year. Average investment is expected to be about $1 million, and private blockchains were preferred by 69%.

A pump and dump scheme involves a promoter acquiring a position, often in a penny stock, and spreading false or misleading information to artificially raise the share price before selling shares to latecomers, causing the price to drop. The passage says these strategies are bad because they are scams, mostly illegal, and immoral; they benefit few promoters and early investors while latecomers face losses. They are most likely in the OTC/penny stock market and unregulated crypto market, and less likely on major regulated exchanges. FOMO can drive participation. A study found such investing is fairly common and average returns are negative, while Wikipedia says pump and dump schemes account for 15% of spam emails. Investors are advised to avoid them and think long-term.

The disclosure relates to wireless communications and provides methods, apparatuses, and a system for transmitting paging information. A first communication node calculates a time domain position of a paging occasion (PO) of a second communication node and transmits paging information within the PO; the paging information includes paging downlink control information and/or a paging message. The PO includes a group of paging resources for paging transmissions on one or more preset beams or ports and may correspond to a synchronous signal burst set or preset sweeping resources. A second communication node calculates the PO and receives the paging information within it. The disclosure also provides transmitting or configuring quasi-co-location relationship information between a paging-related signal and other sweeping signals or channels, and transmitting or receiving paging information according to that relationship. PO determination parameters may include a DRX cycle, paging transmission interval, number of paging transmissions, device ID, and/or PO offset. Corresponding apparatuses, system, computer-readable storage medium, base station, terminal device, and computer program product are also provided.

The article examines Orbital ATK after Argus Research upgraded the stock from hold to buy with a $120 price target. Orbital ATK reported fiscal Q2 2017 sales of $1.12 billion, slightly above estimates and up 3% year over year. Adjusted earnings were $1.56 per share, beating expectations by $0.13, but GAAP profits fell 3% to $1.51 per share. Operating margin fell 140 basis points to 12.2%, and free cash flow was negative $55.8 million versus positive $107.2 million a year earlier. Management remained optimistic, citing strong bookings and backlog, and raised full-year sales and earnings guidance while leaving free cash flow guidance at $250 million to $300 million. Argus cited milestones, increased defense spending, and valuation. The author said the stock has risen 44% and is too expensive, noting 22 times trailing earnings, 17 times the top 2017 earnings projection, and an EV/FCF ratio above 40, or 25 using $300 million in free cash flow.

In 2009, Shepard Fairey was arrested outside the ICA before his exhibition opening; 130,000 people attended the show. The passage describes the ICA’s transformation under Director Jill Medvedow, who arrived in 1998 when it had little money, few members, no permanent collection, about 25,000 annual visitors, and operated from an old police station. Contemporary art had historically struggled in Boston. Medvedow formed a business planning group, sought audience growth, expanded education, considered collecting, and pursued a waterfront location. In 1999 the ICA won Parcel J on Fan Pier. It hired Paul Bessire, launched a capital campaign, added board members, and selected Diller + Scofidio as architect in 2001. It broke ground in 2004, faced approvals, the Pritzker sale, and construction delays, and opened its new $51 million building on December 10, 2006. It raised over $75 million, surpassed its campaign goal, drew over 280,000 visitors in its first year, and had combined attendance over 450,000 in 2008 and 2009.
The Eighth Circuit docketed and dismissed the appeal on appellee's motion and appellant's consent.

The study proposes “whole human pedagogy,” a decolonial framework for education abroad centered on four tenets: embodiment, emotions, belonging, and becoming. It is informed by hooks, Thompson, and decolonial theory, and draws on literature about education abroad and experiential learning, decolonial theory, and alternative pedagogies. The qualitative study used purposive and snowball sampling to recruit education abroad practitioners at U.S.-based organizations serving undergraduates. Seventeen participants completed 60–90-minute semi-structured virtual interviews in Fall 2023; data were transcribed and inductively coded in NVivo. Findings showed participants viewed students as whole human beings and expressed enthusiasm for research on whole human teaching and learning. Embodiment involved physical, sensory, place-based, and experiential learning; emotions included culture shock, reflection, and discomfort; belonging centered relationships, reciprocity, and learning communities; becoming emphasized transformation, self-knowing, and self-sufficiency. The discussion states the data offer preliminary confirmation that whole human pedagogy is a compelling framework for education abroad praxis, centering collaboration, presence, mutuality, creativity, and wellbeing while destabilizing dominant Euro-U.S. epistemological values. Its significance includes a novel holistic education approach tailored to education abroad, practical use in program development and professional development, and a framework for future research.

Sean “Diddy” Combs was sentenced Friday to four years and two months in prison and fined half a million dollars for transporting people across state lines for sexual encounters under the Mann Act. Having served a year, he would be released in about three years. He was acquitted of sex trafficking and racketeering. The trial included testimony that he beat, threatened, sexually assaulted and blackmailed women. The judge said Combs had the power and resources to continue and was not caught. Combs apologized, asked for leniency, and six of his seven children addressed the judge.

At its fall hardware event, Amazon announced new devices and features. Alexa+ is available in four new Echo devices and Ring cameras. New Echo devices include Echo Dot Max, Echo Studio, and Show models, with new AZ3/AZ3 Pro chips, Omnisense, and Alexa+ support. This passage describes single-node container patterns—sidecar, ambassador, and adapter—and multi-node distributed patterns. The sidecar pattern adds a second container to augment an application container without modifying it; examples include adding HTTPS termination to a legacy service using nginx, synchronizing configuration from an API, providing topz resource introspection, and building a simple Git-based PaaS. Sidecars should be parameterized, have stable APIs, and be documented. The ambassador pattern brokers interactions between an application and external services; examples include client-side sharding proxies for sharded Redis and memcache, service brokering for portability, and request splitting for experiments. The adapter pattern modifies an application’s interface to conform to a common interface; examples include Prometheus monitoring adapters, fluentd log normalization, and MySQL health-check adapters. The passage then introduces multi-node microservices patterns: replicated stateless services with load balancers, readiness probes, session tracking, caching layers, rate limiting, and SSL termination; sharded services and caches with sharding functions, consistent hashing, replicated shards, and hot sharding; and scatter/gather for parallel request processing.

Mr. Stevens’s March 8, 1892, communication reported revolutionary plans checked only by a U.S. naval vessel, hostility to the “half English” heir educated in England, and growing inclination toward U.S. annexation. His dispatches continued similarly. Dissatisfaction with the queen’s subjection to Wilson and revolutionary schemes persisted. After a cabinet was voted out, deadlock followed; a no-confidence vote came October 17. Stevens thought the Queen must yield or the monarchy would be overthrown. In November he urged annexation or a customs union, an ocean cable, Pearl Harbor ceded to the United States, and an implied American protectorate. Navy reports corroborated events until January 28, when telegraphic news reported a peaceful revolution and the Queen’s dethronement. The report described U.S. policy from 1820 to 1893 as friendship and protection, distrust of foreign intervention, and occasional contemplation of annexation, notably under President Pierce. It noted continuation in the February 15, 1893, report sending a treaty signed February 14, 1893.

Seven months after the Trump administration cut the U.S. Department of Education and eight months after cuts to research and grants, education researchers expressed cautious optimism. The department said it planned to reinstate 20 of more than 100 key research contracts, sought public input on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences, and began hiring for high-level NAEP assessment jobs. Amber Northern was brought in to reform IES, and the 10 regional education labs are expected to restart work under the remaining federal contract. Researchers called the developments cautiously encouraging, citing plans to update surveys and release existing data, but warned of severe staff shortages, threats to data quality and research progress, and NCES staff reduced from about 100 to three. Reporting functions and some district-level NAEP reporting have been cut, and an executive order requires a massive retroactive admissions data collection. Researchers remained uncertain, with some saying IES might be reinvented rather than eliminated, while DOGE caused great damage.

Theratechnologies Inc. announced an agreement with underwriters led by RBC Capital Markets to sell US$50 million aggregate principal amount of convertible unsecured senior notes due June 30, 2023, at US$1,000 per note, plus an over-allotment option for up to US$7.5 million. The notes bear 5.75% annual interest and are convertible into common shares at US$14.85, with specified redemption terms. Proceeds are intended for EMD Serono termination payments, Trogarzo™ approval and commercialization in Europe and other jurisdictions, and general corporate purposes. This Hubble image shows NGC 5949, a dwarf barred spiral galaxy about 44 million light-years away. Though relatively massive for a dwarf, it has few stars; its proximity enabled William Herschel's 1801 discovery and studies, while dwarf galaxies pose dark matter and missing satellites problems.

The Ultimate Oscillator is a momentum indicator developed by Larry Williams in 1976 and popularized in 1985. It measures price momentum across three timeframes—7, 14, and 28—and combines them in a weighted average, with the shortest timeframe weighted most and the longest least. It ranges from 0 to 100, with below 30 considered oversold and above 70 overbought. Its calculation involves buying pressure, true range, averages for the three periods, and a 4:2:1 weighting. Trading signals are generated on divergence between price and the indicator; buy signals require bullish divergence from oversold territory and the oscillator rising above the divergence high, with opposite conditions for sells. The passage states that backtests and optimization show the indicator performing well over many settings and representing a consistent, stable mean reversion indicator, though default settings performed poorly.

India’s Supreme Court dismissed Varun Thakur’s plea to cancel interim bail for the Pinto family in his son Pradyuman’s murder. The High Court had granted anticipatory bail, restricted travel, and ordered cooperation; Pradyuman’s family alleged complicity.

American truck drivers may be displaced by automation, with 3.5 million professionals and growing investment in driverless vehicles. Automation also threatens other jobs, and the World Economic Forum says the Fourth Industrial Revolution will eliminate over five million jobs in five years. The passage explores human augmentation as a response, citing the Bodyhacking Conference. Proposed augmentations include neural laces to boost brain input-output and compete with AI, and exosuits to combine human intelligence with robotic strength. For skills, Tom Davenport and Julia Kirby advise workers to stand out through creativity or machine knowledge, though physical laborers face a harder transition. Davenport distinguishes narrow AI from artificial general intelligence, saying “all bets are off” if AGI arises.

President Trump denied a New York Times article saying he watches four to eight hours of television daily; The Times stood by its reporting, sourced from 60 interviews, after Trump criticized media outlets for “fake news.”

A fast-moving lava flow from Kilauea crossed Highway 132, destroyed electric utility equipment, and cut power. Hawaii County Civil Defense confirmed 71 homes destroyed, with the number expected to rise, plus other structures. Kapoho-area residents were told to evacuate; one trapped person was rescued. Since May 3, 24 fissures have opened, over 400 utility poles and two geothermal plant wells were covered, and thousands have been displaced.

Meb Faber’s Tactical Asset Allocation strategy is an active trend-following strategy using market timing and allocating across stocks, bonds, REITs, and commodities, divided into U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and world commodities. It can use five diversified index ETFs, with 20% allocated to each position and cash when no signal. Backtests over 16 years reportedly produced a -13.24% drawdown, lower than passive portfolios’ 40%–50% drawdowns.

Richard Berg appealed an amended judgment increasing his child support. The trial court found his net income had increased 34.5% since the original decree and raised support to the guidelines level, while denying continued support for the oldest daughter and accepting respondent’s withdrawal of her motion for continued support for the mentally retarded son. The Minnesota Court of Appeals held the amount was within the trial court’s discretion but found the findings inadequate under Moylan v. Moylan, which requires specific findings to justify a child support increase. The matter was remanded for further factual inquiry consistent with Moylan.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2017, contains unaudited consolidated financial statements and notes, management’s discussion and analysis, market risk disclosures, controls and procedures, and other information including legal proceedings and risk factors. For Q3 2017, net sales were $43.744 billion and net income was $256 million; for the nine months ended September 30, 2017, net sales were $117.413 billion and net income was $1.176 billion. The filing describes acquisitions including Souq and Whole Foods Market, long-term debt issuances and assumed notes, segment results for North America, International, and AWS, and commitments, tax matters, and legal proceedings.

BidaskClub upgraded Rapid7 from “hold” to “buy.” Other analysts issued buy, sell, and positive ratings, with price targets of $20.00, $23.00, and $25.00. The stock’s average rating is “Buy,” with a consensus price target of $20.19. Rapid7 opened at $18.47 and had a market cap of $796.26 million. It reported quarterly earnings per share of ($0.26) and revenue of $47.44 million, up 27.3% year-over-year. Insiders sold 93,770 shares worth $1,601,139 over 90 days; insiders owned 56.90% and institutional investors 71.01%.

The Canadian dollar was little changed at C$1.2857, or 77.78 U.S. cents, as investors awaited a Federal Reserve rate decision and a Thursday speech by Bank of Canada Governor Stephen Poloz. The currency fell 1.3 percent last week after the central bank left its benchmark rate at 1 percent, while bond prices were slightly higher and speculators trimmed bullish bets.

A senior Revolutionary Guards commander said the Guards were ready to prevent regional oil exports if the U.S. banned Iranian oil sales, after President Rouhani threatened to disrupt neighboring countries’ oil shipments.

The UAF Senate approved Rs3.28 billion non-development accounts for 2015-16. Its VC reported 48 new degree programs, enrollment over 25,000, financial assistance over Rs700 million, and a research portfolio over Rs2.5 billion. He said Pakistan spends 0.1% of GDP on agricultural research, urged government investment, and cited malnutrition and 40% post-harvest losses, recommending modern techniques.

Richard Mosse’s Heat Maps addresses the refugee crisis, which the passage describes as increasingly politicized around national borders rather than human rights, with 65.3 million people displaced worldwide by war or persecution, according to UNHCR. The project uses a military-grade thermal telephoto camera attached to a robotic arm to scan landscapes and interiors across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East. The images turn human flesh grey and eye sockets black, stripping identities. Mosse says the camera reveals how the West and governments regard refugees and creates a sense of complicity; he aims to use sinister surveillance technology against its intended purpose. The large-scale works are constructed from grids of smaller frames and include glitches. Access was difficult over three years, though Mosse was admitted to Berlin’s Tempelhof Airport, where Ai Weiwei was refused. The work is ambivalent and meant to force viewers to decide what it is.

India demanded that the UN secretariat disclose information on crimes and misconduct by UN personnel and immunity invoked against prosecution. India’s legal adviser criticized the UN for not vigorously following up serious wrongdoing allegations or waiving immunity. He requested data on registered cases, refused waivers, host-country prosecution requests, and consultations with countries that sent personnel, excluding diplomats. The UN has published peacekeeping sexual misconduct data since 2015 but not a full roster. He said accountability remains elusive due legal complexities, immunity, and national capability or willingness, and the UN cannot prosecute.

President Donald Trump said the U.S. would impose a new 100% tariff on imports from China “over and above any Tariff that they are currently paying,” starting Nov. 1, and export controls on “any and all critical software” on the same date. He said the move was retaliation for China’s new export controls on rare earth minerals. Around 70% of the global supply of rare earths comes from China, and the minerals are essential for high-tech industries. Trump earlier suggested canceling a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at an upcoming summit in South Korea.

The passage explains the double bottom chart pattern: two swing lows near the same level with a swing high between them. It appears in a downtrend, creates support and a neckline resistance, and is considered complete when price breaks above the neckline. It is viewed as a bullish reversal pattern. Aggressive traders may act at the second low; conservative traders wait for a volume-backed close above the neckline. Profit targets are estimated by projecting pattern size from the neckline, with stop-loss options discussed. Coding/backtesting is difficult, though code is offered. Bulkowski’s manual study of 500 stocks over five years found 68% reached target and was better than the double top, but the passage regards it as only an indication.

Emperor penguins are classified as near-threatened; conservationists fear declining numbers due to rising temperatures, and a 2014 study projected a 19 percent population drop by 2100. A new low-cost system uses time-lapse photography and weather data, displayed online, to monitor colonies. It suggested penguins huddle when warmer, possibly indicating less body fat and trouble finding fish, though the cause is debated.

Mark Palmer forwarded to Enron colleagues an email containing a class action complaint filed in San Diego Superior Court by Pamela R. Gordon against Reliant Energy, Southern Company, NRG Energy, Dynegy, AES, Williams Energy, Duke Energy North America, and Does 1-100. The complaint alleges defendants manipulated California’s wholesale electricity market beginning May 22, 2000 by using confidential real-time data, withholding capacity, underbidding forward markets, exporting or parking power, and scheduling outages or transmission flows, causing unjust and unreasonable prices and billions in overcharges. It asserts violations of California antitrust and unfair competition laws, the Consumers Legal Remedies Act, and unconscionability, and seeks class certification, treble damages, restitution, disgorgement, injunctive relief, fees, and interest. Palmer states a reporter said their suit will look the same.

The court imposed six fines of $1,000 each on Pomeroy, totaling $6,000, and six fines of $18,000 each on The New York Central and Hudson River Railroad Company, totaling $108,000. The speaker criticized the unsatisfactory state of criminal law, largely caused by setting aside judgments on technicalities unrelated to the merits, and proposed a law barring reversal or new trial for certain errors unless they caused a miscarriage of justice. On injunctions, the speaker said abolishing them in labor cases is doubtful and wrong, while mob violence should be dealt with summarily. Injunctive power is necessary but subject to grave abuse; it should be used carefully, not to forbid lawful labor efforts or merely aid corporations. Improper preliminary injunctions in labor disputes can do irreparable wrong and threaten the process’s existence. Judges may need to disregard public sentiment when it is wrong.

UDMA write CRC corruption after device termination stems from host_pio_term residue from a prior UDMA read with host termination. After device termination in a UDMA write, ATAC sends correct first CRC but continues the last CRC for the next, causing errors. UDMA writes generally cannot be used; resolution is UDMA I/O blocking with ATAC Error MSR bit 8.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed the district court’s dismissal of Innofood and Sea Breeze’s antitrust and related claims against Mitsubishi and ESSA. It held the action was barred by the act of state doctrine because it challenged Mexico’s official sovereign decision, through government-controlled ESSA, to distribute and export Mexico’s sea salt exclusively through Mitsubishi, and the relief sought would require invalidating that decision. The court found no applicable commercial exception and concluded the Sabbatino factors favored applying the doctrine. It also held Sea Breeze’s appeal was not dismissed despite the temporary suspension of its corporate status.

Interferometric second-harmonic generation (SHG) polarimetry is reported as a method to resolve antiparallel domains and their boundaries in CVD-grown hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), which conventional methods cannot easily assess over large areas. SHG intensity varies by up to three orders of magnitude among hBN films from different CVD methods, while Raman E2g linewidths and intensities vary less. Polarized SHG imaging maps crystallographic orientation, and dual-polarization measurements reveal domain distributions and orientational spreads in samples grown on Ni, Cu, and Fe-Ni catalysts. Interferometric SHG with a local oscillator detects 180° phase shifts, confirming antiparallel domains even in apparently unidirectional films. A mixed-domain model shows that destructive interference among antiparallel domains accounts for the large SHG reduction and scales with domain size. Correlations among SHG intensity, Raman intensity, Raman linewidth, and orientational disorder establish metrics for hBN crystallinity. The methodology is described as applicable to TMDs and other non-centrosymmetric 2D crystals for scalable structural imaging and quality assessment.

This study performed untargeted metabolomic analysis of hepatic and peripheral vein blood from patients undergoing TIPS to identify metabolite changes associated with post-TIPS hepatic encephalopathy. The largest peripheral metabolome changes occurred between post-TIPS and before discharge, with bile acids as major contributors. Greater pre- to post-TIPS hepatic vein metabolome dissimilarity was associated with higher HE grades, suggesting less intrahepatic shunting. More severe HE was associated with greater decreases from baseline in bile acids and glycerophosphocholines, and three conjugated hydroxylated bile acids were inversely correlated with HE grade. Bilirubin and glycerophosphocholine transformations were also implicated. The authors note limitations including limited metabolite coverage and the need for larger validation.

The passage describes container and distributed-system patterns. It shows adapter containers for monitoring and logging: Prometheus collects metrics through a metrics API, an open source Prometheus exporter adapts Redis, Fluentd adapters normalize logs and add slow-query and Storm logging, and adapter containers can add rich health checks to MySQL without modifying its image. It then discusses microservices as components communicating over APIs, contrasted with monoliths, with benefits in reliability, agility, team decoupling, and independent scaling, and downsides in debugging and system design. Replicated load-balanced stateless services use identical servers behind a load balancer, readiness probes, horizontal scaling, session-tracked services, consistent hashing, caching layers such as Varnish, rate limiting, and nginx SSL termination. Sharded services divide requests among shards for stateful or large data, using sharding functions, key selection, consistent hashing, replicated sharded caches, and hot sharding, with examples involving memcache, twemproxy, and nginx. Scatter/gather sends requests to all replicas and combines partial results, useful for parallel computation; leaf sharding handles data too large for one machine, while overhead and stragglers limit benefits, and shards can be replicated for reliability and scale. Finally, FaaS and event-driven processing are described, including benefits like simplified deployment and automatic scaling, challenges in decoupling, monitoring, background processing, in-memory data, and cost, and patterns for decorators, events such as two-factor authentication, and event-based pipelines such as new-user signup.

The passage reports apixaban therapy results in atrial fibrillation across SOC and educational program groups. Opening range breakout (ORB) strategies are popular, partly due to Tony Crabel’s 1990 book. An ORB occurs when price breaks away from a trader-defined opening range, such as the high and low of the first five-minute bar. Backtests of S&P 500 futures and other contracts (NQ, GC, SI, CL) found simple ORB strategies did not work well: the best average gain was 0.04% per trade, and flipped strategies were worse. Filters, such as daily-bar filters, may improve results; one filtered strategy had 198 trades, 0.27% average gain, 65% win ratio, and profit factor 2, but it was not revealed. Reasons for reduced effectiveness include false breakouts, overnight gains, computer-driven arbitrage, and daily highs/lows often occurring in the morning and close. The article concludes ORB strategies are less relevant now for major futures/ETFs, recommends daily filters, and warns against overfitting.

Overbought means the stock market has risen over a defined period, which may indicate weaker short-term returns; long-term returns tend to gravitate toward average returns. Mean-reversion, or regression to the mean, suggests strong deviations from a trend are likely to reverse. Overbought can be defined using indicators like RSI, such as a 2-day RSI above 95. A backtest showed lower returns in the first five days after an overbought condition than the long-term average, then returns moved toward average. Overbought is bearish in trading and can signal an impending correction or reversal. The media can amplify overbought conditions through positive articles and FOMO, or panic during downturns.

The passage covers adapter and multi-node distributed system patterns. It shows Fluentd as an adapter to normalize logs from Redis SLOWLOG and Apache Storm via plugins, and adapter containers for richer database health checks, arguing such modularity enables reuse. It introduces microservices, contrasting them with monoliths: benefits include small teams, formal APIs, independent releases and scaling; downsides include harder debugging and design, motivating distributed patterns.

It then describes replicated load-balanced stateless services: identical replicas behind a load balancer, readiness probes, session-tracked services using IP, cookies, or consistent hashing, and application-layer additions. A caching layer such as Varnish can be deployed as a sidecar or separate tier; it supports rate limiting and denial-of-service defense, while nginx can add SSL termination. Kubernetes examples deploy a dictionary server, Varnish cache, and nginx.

Sharded services route requests to shards that each serve a subset, often for stateful or large data. Sharded caches improve memory utilization but make failures and upgrades more impactful; replicated sharded caches add resilience and hot sharding. Sharding functions normally use hash modulo, require determinism and uniformity, and need appropriate keys; consistent hashing minimizes remapping when shard count changes. Examples include memcache with ambassador or twemproxy and an nginx consistent HTTP sharding proxy. Sharded replicated serving can be used beyond caches.

Scatter/gather farms requests to all leaves and combines partial results at a root, useful for parallelizable work such as distributed document search. Leaf sharding handles data larger than one machine, but overhead and stragglers limit parallel speedup; replicating shards improves reliability and scale.

For functions and event-driven processing, FaaS simplifies deployment, scaling, and stateless modularity, but complicates operations and debugging and is poor for long background processing, memory-heavy services, and high sustained request-based costs. Patterns include decorator transformations, event handlers such as two-factor authentication, and event pipelines such as new-user signup. Finally, the passage discusses distributed ownership and master election, noting singleton services are simple and can be reasonably available under orchestration but have downtime during failures and upgrades.

The lecture discusses collective/coherent Thomson scattering, which occurs when the scattering wavelength is greater than the Debye length and samples collective plasma motion. It reviews ion acoustic waves and electron plasma waves, notes that plasma contains fluctuations in all directions, and explains that scattering transfers energy and momentum to a mode and grows it. The expected spectrum has low-frequency ion acoustic peaks and higher-frequency electron plasma wave peaks, broadened by thermal effects and detector angular range. The derivation first relates scattered power to density fluctuations, then models density fluctuations using a test-particle treatment and the Klimontovich distribution to obtain a spectral density function involving electron and ion distribution functions and susceptibilities. Peaks arise where permittivity equals zero, corresponding to normal modes. For Maxwellian distributions, the susceptibility involves the Debye length and a tabulated function; warm-plasma treatment requires the Landau contour.

The passage concerns Massachusetts General Hospital’s Pre-Admission Testing Area (PATA), which had struggled with inefficiencies and long patient wait times for over two years. A letter forwarded from the president’s office described a nearly four-hour clinic visit with only about 1½ hours of face time.
