Its average appointment was two-and-a-half hours, and limited capacity meant it saw about 65% of outpatients, with healthier patients receiving work-ups in the OR, sometimes delaying surgery. A PATA Task Force formed in 2008 considered internal changes, while an MBA intern’s time study and a June 2009 meeting discussed options such as extending hours, adding resources, reducing volume, or improving with existing resources.

This 4-year naturalistic follow-up of the ePOD-methylphenidate RCT assessed long-term effects of stimulant treatment on resting cerebral blood flow (CBF) and CBF-response to an acute methylphenidate challenge in stimulant treatment-naive adolescents and adults with ADHD. The study found no evidence that stimulant medication use was associated with change over time in resting relative CBF or CBF-response in either age group or any region of interest. However, stimulant use extent was associated with resting rCBF and rCBF-response in an age-dependent manner: adults taking more stimulant medication or with longer exposure showed lower thalamic resting rCBF, while adolescents taking more stimulant medication or with longer exposure showed lower medial prefrontal cortex rCBF-response. These associations were already present before stimulant treatment and were unrelated to ADHD symptom severity. Initial RCT treatment allocation had no long-lasting effects. Whole-brain CBF-response was associated with noradrenaline transporter distribution, but not dopamine receptor/transporter distributions. The authors conclude there was no evidence for long-lasting effects of stimulant treatment on dopamine system development, but identify an age-dependent association between mPFC dopamine function and extent of stimulant treatment.
The team is excited, healthy except for Dwayne, and confident, rested, and energetic. It will keep the same approach, execute its game plan, and play well to get the desired result.

This cross-sectional study recruited 7,264 teachers from 11 schools in Zhengzhou, China, to examine personal health literacy, school health literacy environment, and health outcomes. It found that 56.9% of teachers had inadequate or problematic personal health literacy, and 31.0% perceived a supportive school health literacy environment. Both lower personal health literacy and less supportive school health literacy environment were associated with higher odds of poor health status, at least one health-compromising behaviour, at least one health service use, and healthcare cost of RMB 1000 or more. Health literacy levels varied by sociodemographic characteristics. The study concluded that promoting health literacy at individual and organizational levels may improve teachers’ health outcomes, while noting limitations of convenience sampling, self-report measures, cross-sectional design, and limited consideration of other environments.

Linguistics expert Martin O’Leary researched etymology and showed that seemingly unrelated words—such as flamingo, phlegm, blue, architect, dachshund, science, and sh*t—share Proto-Indo-European roots. Proto-Indo-European, the mother tongue of Indo-European languages thought to have originated north of the Caspian Sea and last spoken between roughly 4,500 and 2,500 BC, has no surviving texts, making reconstruction difficult. O’Leary’s Twitter charts of these cognates drew thousands of retweets and comments.

Analog input is captured on an internal capacitor array in hold mode; the source must charge a typical 25pF sampling capacitor, input current depends on conversion rate, and no further input current flows after full charge. The ADS7828 can use an internal 2.5V reference or an external reference. A +5V supply requires an external +5V reference for full 0V to +VDD dynamic range, while a +2.7V supply with the internal +2.5V reference provides full dynamic range. Lower reference voltage reduces LSB size, increasing apparent offset, gain, and internal noise; 2.5V reference noise is typically 0.32LSB peak-to-peak, while a 50mV external reference gives 16LSBs. Internal noise is Gaussian and can be reduced by averaging.

The ADS7828 supports I2C standard, fast, and high-speed modes as a slave. The master controls SCL, bus access, and START/STOP; SDA and SCL are open-drain. Data must remain stable while the clock is HIGH, and START/STOP are SDA transitions while SCL is HIGH. Each byte has a ninth acknowledge bit. The address byte begins with 10010, followed by A1/A0 device select bits and the R/W bit; up to four devices can share a bus. Conversion data is read after initiating a conversion, returned as 12-bit words in two bytes, Byte 0 first. HS mode stretches SCL low until conversion completes; repeated START maintains HS mode.

The internal reference defaults off; PD1 controls it, settling time is required for 12-bit accuracy after turning it on, and external reference requires PD1=0 and a settled reference. Layout should use clean, bypassed power with 0.1µF close to the device, possibly 1µF–10µF, and clean analog ground away from microcontroller/DSP grounding. The SAR architecture is sensitive to transients, and external reference noise or ripple can appear in digital results. The passage also provides package, tape/reel, RoHS/MSL, and legal warranty/disclaimer information.

Webster Elementary dedicated two recycled-material buddy benches in honor of former music teacher Robert Pickell, who died in July after falling through his roof. Interfacial mobility is described as a coarse-grained parameter controlling microstructural evolution and material behavior. The passage discusses challenges in connecting atomistic and microstructural scales, especially for solute-interface interactions and solute drag. Mobility reflects atomic sub-processes and is extracted from molecular dynamics using capillary fluctuation or linear response methods, both assuming Markovian, memory-free motion. However, interfaces can exhibit memory effects, transient sub-diffusion, and non-Markovian behavior, complicating mobility extraction. Generalized approaches from biochemistry can correct for memory. The authors adapt such techniques using a simplified kinetic Monte Carlo model of interface migration with interacting solute, demonstrate inconsistency with the capillary fluctuation method, propose mean boundary motion extraction, and apply a time convolutionless propagator approach. They introduce a discrete two-dimensional lattice model with tunable boundary stiffness, solute binding, and diffusion kinetics, using a DGSOS Hamiltonian in the absence of solute.

Online retailer listings indicate Intel’s rumored Core i7-8086K, marking the 8086’s 40th anniversary, may have a 5GHz maximum clock speed, six cores, 12 threads, and 12MB L3 cache, matching the Core i7-8700K but faster and overclockable. It may be cherry-picked and cost around $480.

Using the Netherlands as a case study, the study develops an agent-based, demographically and geographically stratified model of the first COVID-19 wave (February 27–June 1, 2020), using demography, mobility, mixing, hospitalization, and seroprevalence data. It calibrates national hospital admissions and assesses national non-pharmaceutical interventions and potential subnational, municipality-level interventions. Mobility reductions contributed most to epidemic control; behavioral changes had considerable impact; school closure had little impact. Subnational interventions based on local infection thresholds showed a trade-off: higher thresholds produced more hospital admissions but fewer municipalities under intervention, while lower thresholds approached national outcomes with more intervention-free municipalities. The authors conclude subnational implementation could reduce societal burden if infection levels can be monitored, while noting limitations such as omitted household granularity and mobility-data constraints.

SWIM’s 2013 annual conference, themed “Dare to Fail: Taking Risks When it Matters Most,” was scheduled for February 8 after 11 months of planning. Baking powder and baking soda are not interchangeable; they differ chemically though both help dough rise. Substitutions require different amounts. Baking powder lasts 3–12 months; baking soda has no expiration date if sealed and cool. Both can be tested by bubbling.

Minutes from the September 16-17 Fed meeting showed officials were strongly inclined to cut rates, with near unanimity on a quarter-point reduction to 4%-4.25%. The passage introduces LLM-proposed Open Taxonomy (LOT), an inductive method for identifying human-readable reasoning features that distinguish large reasoning models (LRMs) from their outputs. LOT uses an LLM to compare reasoning traces from two LRMs, propose distinguishing features, annotate these features in other traces as vectors, train a logistic classifier to predict the source model, and iteratively add features when classification fails. Applied to 12 open-source LRMs across five datasets, LOT reportedly achieves 80–100% accuracy when models differ substantially and outperforms few-shot prompting, VML, and a human-defined reasoning taxonomy. Its taxonomies give natural-language explanations, such as smaller models more often showing circular reasoning and a code-specialized model sometimes using Python functions for math. The passage reports systematic reasoning differences by parameter scale, base-model family, and task specialization. A Qwen3 case study links reasoning differences to GPQA-Diamond performance gaps; aligning smaller Qwen3 models’ reasoning style to the largest Qwen3 improves accuracy by 3.3–5.7%. Limitations include lack of causal links between LRM meta-attributes and reasoning patterns, taxonomy variability, and underexplored annotator effects.

The lecture discusses policy with behavioral agents, focusing on paternalism and internalities, where consumers do not fully account for effects on their future selves. It contrasts neoclassical reasons for government intervention—externalities, equity, monopoly, public goods, information, macroeconomic policy, competition policy, and redistribution—with behavioral justifications. It defines hard paternalism as forcing choices or changing prices significantly, and soft, libertarian, and asymmetric paternalism as influencing behavior while preserving or nearly preserving choice and minimizing harm to optimizing people. It presents arguments against paternalism, including government mistakes, information problems, heterogeneity, corruption, regulatory capture, freedom of choice, and implementation costs, and arguments for it, including people’s mistakes, costly choices, and opt-out soft policies. It discusses popular and unpopular paternalistic policies, nudges such as defaults, reminders, court-appearance texts, and energy reports, and evidence that some nudges work while others do not and that some people dislike being nudged. The Save More Tomorrow plan is described as voluntary, opt-out, and using present bias, loss aversion, and defaults. Market solutions are discussed as limited because firms may target naive consumers and exploit self-control problems, while sludges can harm people. The lecture concludes that soft paternalism can improve welfare, nudges can backfire, some people dislike nudging, markets do not solve everything, and reducing sludges can help.

New research co-authored by a University of Calgary professor found that dinosaur egg incubation took nearly three months for 194-gram Protoceratops embryos and six months for over 4-kg Hypacrosaurus embryos. Researchers studied fossilized embryos from Mongolia and Alberta and counted daily growth lines in teeth. These periods were longer than birds’ 11–85 days and closer to primitive reptiles, suggesting birds evolved faster incubation after branching off. Longer incubation exposed dinosaurs to prolonged risks and may have made it harder to reproduce quickly; birds’ shorter incubation may have helped them survive extinction. The study examined two species and expects further embryo research.

Andrew Anton Sabo appealed his conviction after pleading guilty to possessing cocaine with intent to deliver as a second or subsequent offense and two counts of being a felon in possession of a firearm. The passage relates generally to overlay network routing over the publicly-routed Internet and describes CDNs, overlay networks, WANs, MPLS, VPN concentrators, and the use of Internet links as an optimized WAN. It discloses enhanced overlay network-based transport of traffic, such as IPsec traffic, to and from customer branch office locations using Internet-based overlay routing infrastructure. It describes selecting an ingress edge region of an overlay network having an authoritative DNS. The method includes receiving and mapping a service hostname to an IKEv2 destination of an outer IPsec tunnel associated with a first overlay network edge, with the service hostname received at the authoritative DNS from a DNS resolver associated with a customer router. An IKEv2 session is established from the first overlay network edge to the customer router. Upon tunnel establishment, a secondary lookup is performed by the first overlay network edge to the authoritative DNS to determine whether the first edge is an appropriate ingress region. Based on the response, an IKEv2 redirect is issued from the first edge to a second overlay network edge, and a new tunnel is established from the second edge to the customer router. An additional lookup may be performed by the second edge to determine whether it remains an appropriate ingress region; based on the response, responses to liveness probes over the new tunnel may be dropped, triggering the customer router to initiate another service hostname lookup.

The lecture treats exact solutions of inviscid Burgers’ equation and related nonlinear PDEs. For a delta-function initial condition, the solution is expected to be a fan followed by a shock. Using conservation of total mass, the shock position is found as the square root of 2t; the shock speed and entropy condition are checked. An exact minimization formula for the solution is introduced and said to give the same result. The lecture then discusses Burgers’ equation with viscosity, which can be transformed into the heat equation by introducing an integral variable and a nonlinear change of variables. Solving the heat equation and letting viscosity go to zero leads to a limiting integral analyzed by focusing on where the exponent is minimized. The lecture also describes the Korteweg-de Vries (KDV) equation, traveling-wave solutions, numerical discovery of solitons, conservation laws, and the search for completely integrable nonlinear equations such as nonlinear Schrödinger. It mentions Navier-Stokes as not on that list and the Clay prize question about solutions for all time, plus a numerical experiment on a possible blow-up. Upcoming topics include finite differences, the level set method, financial mathematics, and large linear systems.

PMC WORD and BYTE register writes can corrupt local or cross PMC registers because shadow-register updates occur at 32-bit granularity and inactive byte lanes retain previous data. ACPI registers PM1_STS, PM1_EN, PM1_CNT, and PM2_CNT allow WORD/BYTE accesses; non-ACPI CS5535 registers are DWORD-only. An SMI I/O trap can be set up for ACPI-defined registers.

NeuroAdapter is an end-to-end brain-decoding framework that conditions a latent diffusion model directly on fMRI data via parcel-wise embeddings and cross-attention, avoiding intermediate image/text embedding spaces. It is evaluated on NSD, NSD-Imagery, and Deeprecon, showing competitive performance on high-level semantic metrics. The paper also proposes IBBI, a bi-directional interpretability framework that uses cross-attention dynamics across diffusion steps to analyze brain parcel contributions and ROI attention maps in reconstructed images. Ablation studies examine factors including token dropout, parcel-wise mapping, brain encoder-based image selection, and causal perturbations. The authors note stochastic generation variability and possible saturation of image-quality benchmarks, suggesting interpretability offers a complementary perspective.

In this original proceeding, the Bond petitioners sought reversal of the Denver District Court’s denial of a protective order in their personal injury action against YMCA. They sought to prohibit discovery of notes and records kept by their mental health therapists. The Supreme Court held the discovery order was reviewable because disclosure could cause damage not curable on appeal. Although the physician-patient and psychologist-patient privilege applied, the petitioners waived it by placing their mental condition in issue and seeking damages for mental suffering and psychiatric care. However, the Court concluded the respondent court abused its discretion by denying the protective order without balancing the petitioners’ confidentiality interests against YMCA’s need for evidence. Given Dr. Vary’s affidavit describing potential harm to therapy, the Court made the rule absolute and remanded for reconsideration under the correct balancing standard and possible C.R.C.P. 26(c) protections.

The Put-Call ratio is a popular sentiment indicator. Extreme readings, often signaling panic or climax, are used as contrarian signals to fade the market; a high put reading might signal panic and an imminent market bottom. It divides put and call volume or open interest for an instrument or asset class daily. There are different types, such as index and stock Put-Call ratios. High readings generally signal fear, while low readings signal complacency; no universal rules define a good or bad ratio. The ratio can be calculated by dividing traded put options by traded call options, but volume and open interest differ. Backtests reveal better sentiment indicators, such as the VIX, and the passage says its own backtest performance is not impressive. The authors have never used the Put-Call ratio and consider it inferior to similar sentiment indicators. It is available on trading and investing websites, apps, and official exchanges, but free download sources are not easy to find.

Ramu Damodaran writes about water and UN efforts ahead of World Water Day. He cites an early UN General Assembly resolution on headquarters subsoil water rights as a metaphor for “we the peoples” claims and the unseen. AI encoding and decoding apparatuses and methods are provided. An AI encoding apparatus determines whether to perform AI down-scaling of an original image; if so, it obtains a first image through a down-scaling DNN, encodes the first image, and transmits image data and AI data indicating whether AI down-scaling was performed. This lecture reviews the similarity between the large-N expansion of gauge theory and string scattering. Identifying \(g_{\text{string}}\) with \(1/N\) makes the genus expansion of Feynman diagrams match string worldsheet topology; Feynman diagrams of genus \(h\) can be viewed as triangulations of genus-\(h\) surfaces. If each diagram’s weight can be matched to a string action, large-N gauge theory can be described as a string theory, with glueball or single-trace states as string states. This is difficult because the target string theory/action is unknown, Feynman diagrams are discrete, and geometric behavior is expected only at strong coupling. Simple matrix integrals and matrix quantum mechanics provide explicit examples. Adding fundamental quarks gives diagrams classified by surfaces with boundaries and open strings; symmetric or antisymmetric matrices give unorientable surfaces. A naive 3+1 Minkowski string dual to QCD does not work because string theory is consistent only in 26 or 10 dimensions and contains gravity or a massless spin-2 particle, which QCD lacks. Holographic-principle and consistency hints suggest a five-dimensional string theory, and for a large-N conformal field theory in \(D\) dimensions the dual string lives in \(AdS_{D+1}\), with \(1/N\) related to \(g_{\text{string}}\). The lecture also recounts history and begins string theory formalism: the Nambu-Goto action, Polyakov action equivalence, and quantization as 2D gravity coupled to \(D\) scalar fields.

The disclosure describes display systems and methods for driving light sources in a near-eye display. A maximum luminance location of the display may be determined based on a user's eye field of view, including by eye tracking, and light sources may be driven according to their locations relative to that maximum luminance location. For the same input display value, a light source closer to the maximum luminance location may be driven at a higher luminance level than one farther away. Different display zones may use different relationships between input display values and luminance levels.

The passage covers PGA848 linear input range, a typical SAR ADC application, power supply recommendations, layout guidelines, and support/documentation information. The linear operating input voltage range extends within 3 V (maximum) of either supply, with common-mode rejection maintained throughout this range at all temperatures; the linear input common-mode range depends on input common-mode voltage, input differential voltage, gain, and reference input voltage, with valid ranges shown in Figures 8-4 through 8-1. In the typical application, a PGA848 drives a 16-bit, 1-MSPS ADS8860 SAR ADC and accepts single-ended or differential input signals; ±15 V supplies power the input stage, and a unipolar 5.3 V supply powers the output stage and ADC, with REF6250 and OPA192 establishing the ADC midscale reference. Filters at the PGA input, across feedback resistors, and at ADC inputs address EMI/RFI, bandwidth/noise, charge kickback, settling, and distortion. Design requirements list VS± = ±15 V, VLVDD = 5.3 V, VLVSS = GND, and ADC REFIN = 5 V. Power supply recommendations specify nominal performance with ±15 V input and output stages and mid-supply VICM and VREF; output supplies are clamped within input-stage levels, and voltages higher than 40 V (±20 V) permanently damage the device. Layout guidance includes symmetrical and matched input paths, local low-ESR bypass capacitors, separation or perpendicular crossing of noisy traces, minimizing leakage and parasitic capacitance, reducing thermal junctions, and keeping distance from thermal sources. The passage also lists simulation tools, related documentation, notification and support resources, trademarks, ESD handling recommendations, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

This cross-sectional analysis evaluated BCHE-K carrier status by APOE4 allelic status in 45 patients aged 50–74 years with CSF biomarker-confirmed mild AD from trial NCT03186989. In APOE4 carriers (N = 33), mean age-at-diagnosis of AD in BCHE-K carriers (n = 11) was 6.4 years earlier than in BCHE-K noncarriers (n = 22; P < .001, ANOVA), and mean age-at-baseline was also over 6 years earlier. No similar influence of BCHE-K was observed in APOE4 noncarriers (N = 12). APOE4 carriers with versus without BCHE-K had slightly higher amyloid and tau accumulations. A predominant amyloid, limited tau pathophysiology, and limbic-amnestic phenotype was exemplified by APOE4 homozygotes with BCHE-K. Multiple regression analyses associated amyloid accumulation with APOE4 carrier status, larger total brain ventricle volume, less synaptic injury, and less tau; tau pathophysiology was associated with more neuroaxonal damage, more synaptic injury, and higher glial activation. The conclusion states that in mild AD patients aged less than 75 years, the mean age-at-diagnosis in APOE4 carriers was reduced by over 6 years in BCHE-K carriers versus noncarriers, and functional activation of glia may explain much of the effects of APOE4 and BCHE-K on the phenotype of early AD. Limitations include small cross-sectional size, possible unrepresentativeness of trial participants, and findings not to be extrapolated to mild AD patients aged over 75 years.

This lecture focuses on finite impulse response (FIR) systems and structures that exploit FIR properties. It reviews direct, transposed, and cascade forms, and notes that a parallel form is not generally applicable because FIR systems have no poles. For linear phase FIR systems, whose impulse response satisfies h(n)=h(N−1−n), a structure can use half the multiplies of the direct form while still requiring the same delays. A frequency sampling structure is derived from the DFT coefficients H(k), implemented as a cascade of 1−z^−N with a parallel bank of first-order poles whose coefficients are frequency samples; the poles cancel zeros in 1−z^−N. Its advantages include possible reductions in multiplies and delays when many frequency samples are zero and shared components for filter banks, while drawbacks arise from pole-zero cancellation and finite register length effects. The lecture compares structures by delays, multiplications, modularity, and finite register length effects. It discusses coefficient quantization and pole sensitivity, concluding that direct form is most sensitive, while cascade and parallel forms using lower-order sections are less sensitive. Second-order sections and coupled form give different realizable pole locations under quantization.

Ultralight backpacking is defined as a base weight of 10 pounds or less, with super ultralight at 5 pounds or less and lightweight at 15 pounds or less. The movement is credited to a 1994 Mark Jenkins article, and early gear was often DIY. The most important way to reduce weight is to bring less and to assess whether items are needed for warmth, comfort, food, or safety. The heaviest items are the backpack, sleep system, and shelter; the author suggests starting with shelter and sleep and experimenting with tarps, cowboy camping, and quilts. Ultralight backpacking is described as a philosophy and approach, not just a weight limit, and experimentation helps people learn what they do not need.

The passage reports a US vital-statistics analysis from January 1, 2014, to December 31, 2020, examining excess mortality from cancer and other chronic conditions during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using underlying-cause and multiple-cause death records, it modeled six cancer types and diabetes, Alzheimer’s disease, ischemic heart disease, and kidney disease nationally and in New York, California, and Texas. It found at most modest cancer mortality elevation: 12,000 national multiple-cause excess cancer deaths, a 2% increase over baseline, with the largest relative increase in hematological cancers at 5%; no multiple-cause excess was seen for pancreatic or lung cancer. Diabetes and Alzheimer’s showed substantial excess mortality synchronous with COVID-19 waves. A demographic model under the null hypothesis that the conditions were not themselves COVID-19 mortality risk factors projected patterns consistent with observations, supporting demography and competing cancer mortality risk as explanations. Coding changes affected underlying- versus multiple-cause cancer deaths. The study concludes it rules out the immune incompetence rescue hypothesis and notes limitations including model uncertainty and reliance on mortality outcomes.

To investigate the 2022 US RSV surge, researchers sequenced RSV genomes from symptomatic patients at Massachusetts General Hospital and outpatient practices. Of 105 residual upper respiratory specimens, 54 near-complete and 23 partial genomes were produced. The surge involved multiple RSV-A (91%) and RSV-B (9%) lineages; all near-complete genomes were GA2.3.5 or GB5.0.5a. RSV-A genomes belonged to at least 10 lineages with tMRCA between 2014 and 2017; RSV-B had a tMRCA estimate of 2019. Washington RSV-A genomes belonged to 6 lineages, 4 shared with Massachusetts. Genetic divergence was consistent with estimated clock rates, unlike accelerated evolution in certain SARS-CoV-2 variants. The authors conclude the surge consisted of numerous pre-existing lineages, many shared across distant areas, inconsistent with a single highly transmissible lineage, and call for investigation of non-viral factors including COVID-19-related immunity changes.

Environmental education and sustainable development are presented as interconnected responses to global warming, natural disasters, resource overuse, pollution, and environmental degradation. Global cooperation began with the 1972 UN Conference on the Human Environment in Stockholm; the 1992 Earth Summit adopted Agenda 21, and a 1975 UNEP/UNESCO workshop in Belgrade addressed environmental education. Environmental education is defined as an interdisciplinary process fostering environmental awareness, values, responsible behavior, knowledge, skills, attitudes, and participation. Its term was first mentioned in the 1947 book “Communitas”; Thomas Pritchard proposed the idea in 1948, and it was first used in 1965 at Keele University, leading to the Council for Environmental Education. The Belgrade Charter sets six objectives—awareness, knowledge, attitude, skill, participation, and evaluation ability—and guiding principles including lifelong, interdisciplinary, participatory, global/regional, current/future, developmental-impact, and value/problem-solving approaches. Environmental education components and objectives include awareness, knowledge, attitude, skills, participation, and evaluation. The environment is defined as physical and biological elements surrounding humans, classified as natural or man-made, with biotic/abiotic and physical/social subcategories. Environmental knowledge groups include natural resources, social environment, environmental technology, and waste/pollution. Environmental properties include unique characteristics, interdependence, dependence, integration, chain reactions, varied resilience/vulnerability, and temporal changes. Formal and non-formal environmental education, including learning outside the classroom, is described as beneficial, including for students with special needs. Sustainable development is defined as meeting present needs without compromising future generations, with principles of balance, improvement, meeting present needs without harming future potential, and local/community efforts. The 17 SDGs and 169 targets address economic growth, public health, social equality, and environmental protection. Guidelines for sustainable environmental development include reducing energy consumption, minimizing waste, conserving natural resources and environmental quality, and utilizing clean technologies. Environmental management uses tools such as ISO 14000 and technological, economic, social, and legal measures. Examples include the Collaborative Learning Project for Community Development, the Royal Initiative Huai Sai project, and Thailand/UNEP natural capital accounting and National Ecosystem Assessment projects. The conclusion states environmental education processes foster behavioral changes, awareness, and skills for sustainable environmental development.

The passage discusses interdisciplinary music education, describing its integration with other disciplines and its benefits. It states that music is related to mathematical structures, language development, motor skills, emotional intelligence, and multiple intelligences. Interdisciplinary music education combines music teaching and learning with methods, knowledge, and perspectives from other disciplines and is said to support innovative and critical thinking. The passage addresses cognitive development, mathematics-music connections, language development, STEAM, emotional and social skills, and academic studies on programming, language skills, STEAM, autism, and mathematics. It lists application areas in preschool, middle/high school, and university. The study aims to examine the music department from the perspective of a social studies teacher studying in the music department at a Fine Arts Faculty, using a qualitative literature review and a single-participant case study with a semi-structured interview. Findings from participant P1 concern inadequate basic music education, the need for a preparatory class, separate curricula, creative drama, media literacy, material design, presentation work, and courses addressing history, geography, Turkish, and mathematics. Discussion and conclusions state that interdisciplinary basic music education supports academic success, cognitive development, cultural awareness, social skills, creativity, and higher-order skills, and is considered a necessity. Suggestions include practical music theory, active methods such as Kodály, Suzuki, and Orff, repertoire for bağlama and piano, micro-teaching, workshops, drama, learning and developmental psychology, preparatory classes, learning-style tests, guitar and ukulele instruction, and integrating interdisciplinary music education into curricula and policies.

This descriptive study assessed Faculty of Industrial Education students’ readiness, expertise, and needs in educational multimedia. It reviewed literature, interviewed teachers, and surveyed 124 students about multimedia tools and learning topics. The study concluded that targeted learning tools matched to students’ needs and expertise are beneficial, while noting the small sample size and recommending future research with larger, more diverse groups.

The passage describes the Trump administration’s cuts and policy changes affecting K-12 multilingual learners, including canceled professional development, closed newcomer centers, and suspended hiring of English learner teachers. New research from Yale’s Budget Lab and the Brookings Institution found no evidence of a “discernible disruption” to U.S. jobs since ChatGPT launched in November 2022. Most shifts in the occupational mix were already underway in 2021, and higher-AI-exposure industries’ changes largely predate widespread AI use. SOS low post disruptions emphasize fronting the post as the primary way to disrupt strong post-ups. Low Helpside I defender double-teams on post lobs and Base Go traps. The options are Post Front, Base Go, Go Top, Wing Go, Hold, and Yo-Yo. Post Front minimizes inside post passes and offensive touches/shots; X5 fronts O5 with one arm high in the passing lane and one low on the opponent’s leg, sitting on the thigh and pushing O5 into the three-second area. Base Go is the primary low post double-team, used when the post is moved off the low block, on a coach’s call in the deep low post, with a 3/4 high side pass denial, or when the defender is late fronting; X2 pressures the passer and forces baseline, while the low Helpside I defender locks up the post. Go Top is a secondary high post trap for fronting problems, weak ball pressure, weakside clearouts, or when the post tends to turn middle. Go Wing is a secondary wing post trap for similar situations or when the wing is a poor outside shooter. Hold disrupts open three-point shots by having X5 play 3/4 pass denial and the other four deny kick-out passes. Yo-Yo is used when the wing passer is not an outside threat; X2 may sag off and double-team while others deny kick-outs, then close out on pass out. The passage also details right-side and left-side rotations, final matchups, skip-pass coverage, and that rotations occur as the ball leaves the passer’s hands.

The gold overnight trading strategy buys gold futures, GLD, or gold miners ETFs (GDX/GDXJ) at the market close and sells at the next open to capture overnight price differentials caused by global market conditions. Backtests show GDX averaged a 0.12% overnight gain, while buying at the open and selling at the close averaged a 0.09% loss. GLD close-to-open returns were 8.4% annually versus 8.2% buy-and-hold, with a 0.04% average gain; open-to-close gains were practically zero. The strategy is described as high-risk and volatile, and commodities are considered difficult to trade. An incubating long overnight strategy had 741 trades and a 0.17% average gain, or 0.11% since 2012. A short strategy had 205 trades and a 0.7% average gain. Risk management and psychology require discipline, patience, and emotional control.

In 1881, Blaine stated that Hawaii could not grant privileges exclusively given the United States by the 1875 treaty without violating it; if another power used undue influence, the United States would support Hawaii’s treaty obligations. He also said Hawaii, as key to the American Pacific, required benevolent neutrality, failing which the United States would seek an American solution. In 1883 Frelinghuysen declined to join Hawaii’s protest against British and French territorial extension in Polynesia. Strokes are time-sensitive, so immediate action is important. The American Stroke Association uses FAST: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, and Time to call 911. If any symptom appears, even briefly, call 911 and note when symptoms began. A similar mnemonic, S.T.R., asks a suspected stroke victim to smile, talk, and raise both arms.

Sara Zaske said her daughter Sophia rarely wanted a cell phone until the family moved from Berlin to California’s San Francisco Bay Area. In Berlin, few third-graders had phones, mostly flip phones without internet; after moving, Sophia entered fourth grade as the only student in her class without a smartphone and asked for a phone. The passage cites international data: about 51% of German children ages 6 to 13 have a mobile phone; about 46% of European children 9 to 16 own a smartphone; in the US, about 45% of children 10 to 12 own a smartphone with a service plan, and 42% of children 8 and younger have tablets. Robin Chase, co-founder of Zipcar, discovered in October 2000 that September revenue was half her estimate and the company could not break even with those numbers. This application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 16/721,644 and claims benefit of U.S. Provisional Patent Application No. 62/886,852, with identified priority applications incorporated by reference. The passage describes information management systems for protecting data through backup, archive, snapshot, replication, deduplication, and lifecycle operations. Enterprises may use network or cloud computing systems for primary and/or backup services, including virtual machines. Backups may be full, incremental, or differential; incremental and differential backups reduce resources by backing up only changed blocks. Some cloud or network architectures, such as OpenStack, do not natively support changed-block tracking or expose APIs for obtaining changed blocks in a format used by an information management system. The disclosure enables differential and incremental backups in such architectures by generating virtual machine disk images at different times, comparing them to identify changed blocks, generating a map of changed-block locations, loading a copy of the virtual machine disk at a virtual server agent, extracting the changed blocks using the map, and backing them up. The passage also details information management system components, including storage managers, data agents, media agents, policies, and distributed architectures.

This study performed genomic sequencing and characterization of SARS-CoV-2 genomes from Rio Grande do Sul (RS), Brazil, and aimed to identify selection traits in E, M, and N proteins. Twelve respiratory samples from Esteio, RS, collected April 9–June 29, 2021, were sequenced; coverage ranged from 84.92% to 99.76%. Ten samples belonged to P.1 and two to P.1.17, both in the Gamma clade. Sixty-eight nucleotide substitutions were found, including 36 non-synonymous; common mutations included NSP13:E341D, S:D614G, S:V1176F, NSP12:P323L, S:K417T, S:T1027I, ORF8:E92K, N:P80R, 5’UTR:C241T, NSP3:K977Q, and S:H655Y. Some mutations were first described in RS, D1208A was first found in Brazil, and NSP12:I136V was not described on GISAID. Analysis of 4,706 RS sequences from GISAID showed lineage changes over time, with B.1.1.33 predominant in 2020; Zeta, B.1.1.28, and P.7 later; P.1 and derivatives prevalent in 2021; Delta from June/August 2021; and Omicron from December 2021. Common RS mutations included NSP12:P323L, C241T, NSP3:F106F, and S:D614G. Phylogenomic analysis placed the 12 genomes in the Gamma clade; global analysis related some to genomes from Brazil, Chile, Mexico, USA, and Canada. Molecular evolution tests found no positively selected sites in E, two positively selected sites in M by FUBAR, and fourteen in N by FUBAR and/or FEL, plus negatively selected sites. DynaMut2 predicted stability effects for positively selected M and N mutations.

This study protocol presents a three-arm randomized controlled trial examining the effectiveness of a digital mindfulness psychoeducation programme (Digital-MindCAN) on psychological symptoms among cancer survivors. The programme links cancer-related matters with mindfulness principles and practice and is delivered real-time via videotelephony software. Eligible participants are adults aged 21–65 with stage 0–III cancer who completed curative treatments two weeks to two years earlier. A convenience sample of 150 will be recruited from a tertiary hospital in Singapore and randomly assigned to Digital-MindCAN plus standard care, Palouse Mindfulness plus standard care, or a wait-list control group. Primary outcomes are objective and subjective stress; secondary outcomes are psychological well-being, perceived relaxation, mindfulness, resilience, depression, and anxiety. Data will be collected using self-administered questionnaires, physiological measures, and focus group interviews after the eighth session. Quantitative data will be analyzed with descriptive statistics, ANCOVA, and repeated measures ANOVA; qualitative data with realist evaluation. The study aims to test the intervention and inform clinical practice.

This study examined preschool teachers’ views on sensory education and their classroom practices using a phenomenological qualitative design. The study group consisted of 20 preschool teachers selected through maximum diversity sampling. Data were collected using a 12-question semi-structured interview form and analyzed by content analysis. Three main themes emerged: the importance of sensory education, its relationship with the preschool education program, and difficulties and limitations. Teachers viewed sensory education as important in early childhood and stated it supports all developmental areas. They reported using visual, auditory, game, music-rhythm, experiment, art, touch, kneading, drama, and balance activities in daily routines, and evaluating sensory activities through observation, development forms, question-answer, family cooperation, or no evaluation. Most participants stated sensory education is included in the preschool program but not sufficiently or clearly. They reported insufficient materials, unfavorable physical conditions, and inadequate self-efficacy in coping with sensory integration problems; almost all wanted training. Recommendations include in-service training, occupational therapist support, sensory materials for classrooms and schools, more sensory education in undergraduate education, and sample activities prepared by occupational therapists and teachers.

Stanford researchers developed biofilm lithography, using genetically engineered E. coli that secrete a sticky protein when exposed to a specific wavelength of blue light, to pattern bacterial communities into designs at 25-micrometer resolution. It could help study biofilm growth and interactions and lead to biomaterials, synthetic microbial communities, microfluidic chips, or biofilm-based circuits. The researchers observed unexpectedly sharp patterns, suggesting bacteria weakly bind and continuously jump on and off surfaces. This study examines higher education projects (HEPs) relocated or created abroad by Russian academics after the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine and subsequent repression in Russian higher education. Using interviews with HEP leaders and discourse analysis of public materials from four projects with varying institutionalisation, it asks how relocated HEPs conceptualise themselves in relation to their homeland, how “exiled consciousness” affects their strategies, and what roles they play beyond academic knowledge production. Findings describe HEPs as safe havens supporting scholars and students; as spaces preserving and partially reconceptualising academic heritage, teaching practices, and Russian-language academic work; and as hope-making praxis focused on feasible action despite hopes of return. They maintain connections to Russia by teaching prohibited topics, attracting Russian students, and collaborating across borders. The conclusion calls for further research on continuity, biases, international influence, everyday practice, and the broader landscape.

A Markov state transition model was developed to assess whether a RATIONS-style nutritional intervention would be cost-effective for reducing TB incidence and mortality among HIV-negative household contacts of persons with TB (PWTB) in India. The RATIONS study provided a food basket costing $13 per month for 6 months to household contacts and reported a 40% reduction in TB incidence over two years; PWTB receiving nutritional support had an approximately 35% mortality reduction compared with a previous National TB Elimination Program cohort. The model compared usual care with nutritional supplementation, using an assumed incidence rate ratio of 0.61 for two years and a mortality risk ratio of 0.65. Per 100,000 household contacts, the RATIONS intervention reduced lifetime TB incidence, TB mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) compared with usual care. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was $229 per DALY averted from a healthcare perspective and $184 per DALY averted from a societal perspective, both below India’s willingness-to-pay threshold of $550 per DALY averted. Sensitivity analyses showed the intervention remained cost-effective across a range of supplementation costs and effect sizes, with probabilistic sensitivity analysis favoring it in over 99% of simulations at a willingness-to-pay of $550. The analysis concluded that a RATIONS-style intervention would be cost-effective in populations with a high dual burden of TB and undernutrition in India and could reduce TB incidence and mortality among household contacts of PWTB.

The lecture addresses dynamic optimality: whether one binary search tree can be at least as good as all others. It defines the BST model, assumes successful searches and no insertions or deletions, and notes log n worst-case cost. It reviews properties including sequential access, dynamic finger, entropy, working set, and unified, and discusses splay trees, which achieve several properties but are not known to be dynamically optimal. It then presents a geometric view: access sequences are plotted as points, and valid BST executions are arborally satisfied point sets, where every rectangle spanned by two nonaligned points contains another point. Cost corresponds to touched nodes, making dynamic optimality a minimum satisfied superset problem. Treaps prove the equivalence, and a greedy algorithm that adds points to satisfy rectangles is described as an offline optimal candidate and can be made online using split trees.

A newborn girl from a Followers of Christ Church family died in Oregon City from complications of prematurity; a medical examiner said immediate care could have saved her. Her twin survived. No charges have been filed; deputies are investigating.

The lecture discusses a finite-temperature CFT on a sphere and its gravity description. Unlike flat space, where temperature is the only scale and physics is the same at all temperatures, on a sphere the dimensionless product rT controls low- and high-temperature behavior. Thermal AdS is allowed on the sphere. A black hole solution also exists; its inverse temperature versus horizon radius has a maximum, giving a minimum temperature and, above it, two black holes: a small one with negative specific heat and a big one with positive specific heat. The three possible gravity phases are thermal AdS, small black hole, and big black hole. Saddle-point approximation selects the lowest free energy. The small black hole never dominates; thermal AdS dominates below a critical temperature Tc, and the big black hole dominates above Tc, giving a first-order Hawking-Page transition at Tc, where their free energies are equal. A toy model of N squared harmonic oscillators with an SU(N) singlet constraint illustrates the field-theory interpretation: low-energy states have O(1) degeneracy, while energy of order N squared gives entropy of order N squared, which can dominate at sufficiently high temperature.

Faviola Dadis said at a Los Angeles news conference that Steven Seagal sexually assaulted her in 2002, when she was 17, during a supposed Beverly Hills hotel casting session; she alleged he grabbed her nipples and genitals, and she left. Meizu’s Pro 7 and Pro 7 Plus received a 600 Yuan price cut in China, with new pricing starting at 1,999 Yuan and going live on December 12. They feature Super AMOLED displays, Helio processors, dual 12MP rear cameras, a 16MP front camera, Flyme OS 6 on Android Nougat, and 3,000/3,500mAh batteries with mCharge 3.0/4.0.

Rushin Shah, former head of Natural Language Understanding on Apple’s Siri team, left Apple after five years to join Facebook’s Menlo Park headquarters. He announced the move on LinkedIn and will work on natural language and dialogue understanding at Facebook. Shah helped launch Siri features including voice recognition and classification for casual conversation. His departure comes as Siri faces increased competition, while Apple has refocused Siri development and announced a Siri-based smart speaker. No replacement is known.

The podcast episode discusses the relationship between cost and complexity in investment plans, noting that lower fees can come from simple changes but that higher costs may sometimes be accepted for simplicity and convenience. Guest John Robertson discusses his revised book *The Value of Simple*, indexing options, robo-advisors, the AutoInvest.ca comparison tool, which receives affiliate commissions, and an online course. At Discover 2017, HPE introduced the HPE Edgeline Services Platform and two related apps, the Edgeline Data Aggregation App and Edgeline Address Translation App, to help customers manage expanding IoT inventories and combine IT with OT. The platform runs IoT applications and services outside traditional data centers or the cloud, near equipment. The Data Aggregation App combines data from OT devices such as PLCs and SCADA systems; the Address Translation App delivers network address translations to subset networks and uses software-defined configuration for remote management. An analyst said HPE offers a full solution from a single vendor amid competition.

ESA inaugurated the New Norcia 3, a 35-meter deep space antenna at its New Norcia site in Western Australia, the fourth for its Estrack network and second at the site. It uses cryogenically cooled components near -263°C and a 20kW radio-frequency amplifier, and is scheduled to enter service in 2026. It will support missions including Juice, Solar Orbiter, BepiColombo, Mars Express, Hera, and upcoming Plato, Envision, Ariel, Ramses, and Vigil, and can support NASA, JAXA, ISRO, and commercial missions. Construction began in 2021 and cost an estimated EUR 62.3 million, with EUR 3 million from the Australian Space Agency. European industry led construction with Australian company involvement. The New Norcia station, opened in 2003 and locally operated by CSIRO, provides strategic deep-space coverage and also hosts a 4.5-meter antenna for Vega-C and Ariane 6 telemetry and a Biomass calibration transponder.

Researchers led by UCL and Imperial College London showed that polymyxin antibiotics break down Gram-negative bacteria by triggering active cells to overproduce and shed their outer armor, leaving gaps that let the drug enter and kill them. The process occurred only in active cells; dormant bacteria were not killed because armor production was switched off. Adding sugar woke dormant cells and allowed polymyxin B to kill them after a delay. The findings may help explain recurrent infections and suggest combining polymyxins with treatments that wake dormant bacteria.

The passage describes SD card initialization and identification after bus activation, including ACMD41, HCS, CMD8, CCS, the busy bit, CMD2/CID, CMD3/RCA, UHS-I voltage switching, CMD11, and CMD19 tuning. It covers data transfer mode commands, read/write block operations, CMD12 stop, programming states, erase/DISCARD/FULE, write protection, password lock/unlock, COP, FEP, and CMD42 sequences. It also describes CMD55/ACMD handling, CMD6 switch function groups and modes, power limits, busy status, high-speed mode, command system expansion, CMD8, and capacity-type differences between SDSC and SDHC/SDXC.

In Cordle v. General Hugh Mercer Corp., three at-will cleaning maids at a Holiday Inn signed agreements to take polygraph tests when required, later refused, and were terminated on October 12, 1982. They sued for wrongful termination. The circuit court found the termination violated substantial public policy and certified questions. The West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals affirmed, holding that public policy is a question of law; that at-will employees are not distinguished for this purpose; and that requiring or requesting an employee to submit to a polygraph or similar test as a condition of employment is contrary to West Virginia public policy grounded in individual privacy, though not absolute and subject to statutory exceptions. Dissenting opinions argued that no established public policy prohibited such discharge at the time, that the later statute W.Va. Code 21-5-5b did not apply, and that retroactive application was unfair.

The speaker says the Stanley Cup is now a three-game series against Tampa Bay Lightning, which both teams would have taken earlier. They need killer instinct and better scoring chances; both goalies played great, but the other team had the upper hand. They will work hard for breaks next game.

He said past frustrations could have led to coups, commended the military, and warned politicians not to take that patience for granted. She and Darren Jones did not dismiss breaking manifesto tax caps. The lecture announces schedule changes: no Monday class, Monday’s class moved to Tuesday, no Wednesday class but a Wednesday-night quiz, and normal Friday; TAs may hold a Wednesday review and normal Monday office hours, with homework possibly posted early and PSAT returned. The topic is ordinary differential equations initial value problems (ODE-IVPs), where differentials are with respect to one variable and all initial conditions are given at a single t. Higher-order ODEs can be converted to first-order form, and Matlab expects f(t,y). The output is typically time points and corresponding y-values for plots, ideally close to the true solution. Forward Euler is presented, along with its relation to the rectangle rule and its order-delta-t error. Methods using an average g, such as trapezoid and midpoint, improve error order. For f(y), midpoint/trapezoid need unknown future values, so Runge-Kutta methods approximate them; RK2 uses Forward Euler for the midpoint, and RK4/5 compares fourth- and fifth-order extensions to estimate error and choose step size. Error propagation, numerical stability, and the amplification factor involving identity plus delta t times dg/dy are discussed. If the norm exceeds one, errors may grow. Unstable ODEs have positive Jacobian eigenvalues, while intrinsically stable ODEs have negative eigenvalues. A well-behaved ODE such as dy/dt = -2y can become unstable with Forward Euler at too-large delta t, producing oscillations or blow-up. The textbook discusses evaluating g methods for stability, and homework requires writing an ODE solver and comparing update formulas.

The passage discusses representing and validating digital business processes in extended enterprises. It presents an MDA-driven business process model with static domain, workflow, and value components. It examines rule-based business modeling using controlled English and SBVR, formal grounding, closed-world and open-world assumptions, hybrid reasoning, and modal evaluation of business rules. It reviews workflow languages, including BPMN, temporal logic, consistency checking, and declarative representation. It describes graphical and logic-based value models for estimating and monitoring profitability. It outlines relations among value, process, and business-rule models, including static, semi-dynamic, and dynamic consistency, and a posteriori monitoring. It concludes with open issues such as critical-area detection and representing pragmatics.

The passage discusses education as a human right and notes that African nations face access and quality challenges due to poverty, lack of infrastructure, and conflict. It examines digital storytelling (DST) in African higher education and teacher training. DST uses digital media to create personal narratives and stories. The study is a qualitative document analysis of 15 scientific articles selected through databases and a PRISMA-based process. The reviewed studies report that DST can increase student engagement, motivation, self-expression, collaboration, reflection, higher-order thinking, digital and media literacy, creativity, problem-solving, oral performance, and community building. It is used in contexts including pre-service teacher training, geography and map reading, language learning, postgraduate research, cultural preservation, and social activism. DST is described as promoting empowerment, cultural enrichment, and transformative learning while preserving oral traditions and giving voice to marginalized groups. Challenges include limited resources, insufficient digital equipment, inconsistent electricity, lack of technological proficiency, time constraints, and rigid curricula. The passage concludes that DST is adaptable across academic settings and is a transformative educational tool, though narrative content should be emphasized over technology in assessment.

On Tuesday, a Ford Galaxy waited 40 minutes on double yellow lines outside Jeremy Corbyn’s north London home before a six-mile journey to Westminster. This lecture introduces an AMO physics course. It defines AMO physics by what AMO researchers do or by its building blocks: atoms, molecules, photons, and electromagnetic fields. Historically it studied gas-phase atoms and molecules and collisions; it has moved toward few-body physics, entanglement, quantum information, many-body physics, quantum gases, and overlap with condensed matter. AMO physics is described as low-energy quantum physics, with paradigms including the hydrogen atom, two-level system, and harmonic oscillator. The lecture traces development from observation to control of nature: internal states, optical pumping, motion, laser cooling, Bose-Einstein condensation, and single quantum systems. It notes technology advances including lasers, solid-state/diode lasers, short and high-intensity pulses, frequency combs, and high-finesse cavities. Course 8.422 can be taken out of sequence with 8.421; prerequisites include 8.05 and 8.06, especially perturbation theory. Topics include QED, light-atom interactions, dissipation and density-matrix/master-equation formulations, mechanical forces of light, trapping and cooling, single photons, quantum information building blocks, and many-body physics of quantum gases. Excluded topics include physics above 10 electron volts, high-energy collisions, advanced atomic structure, and high-intensity/short-pulse lasers. Requirements include 10 problem sets, no midterm or final, and a term paper due on the last day. The teaching team includes a secretary and five TAs. The lecture uses atoms in optical lattices as an appetizer, discussing periodic potentials, spontaneous emission and Sisyphus cooling, deep and shallow lattices, atomic clocks, Mott insulators, atom interferometry, and many-body spectroscopy.

CPFL Energia launched Envo to tap Brazil’s growing solar-powered homes market, offering equipment, installation and assistance to connect systems to the grid and sell excess energy. Solar grid connections rose from 7,500 at end-2016 to 10,000 by April. Santander Brasil will finance Envo clients. CPFL declined to disclose investment.

The passage is a guide to numerous TV shows and docuseries available on HBO Max, describing new, returning, and final seasons across genres such as crime dramas, true-crime docuseries, comedies, fantasy, sci-fi, superhero spinoffs, period pieces, adaptations, and reality/competition programming. Old Faithful is Yellowstone’s most famous landmark, but relatively little was known about its subsurface geology and fluid pathways. University of Utah scientists mapped near-surface geology around Old Faithful using portable seismographs and new seismic analysis techniques. The study revealed a heated water reservoir feeding the geyser’s vent and how ground shaking behaves between eruptions. The Park Service asked the scientists to survey the area. In 2015, the team deployed 133 small seismometers in the Old Faithful and Geyser Hill areas for two weeks. Sensors recorded intense seismic tremors about 60 minutes long, separated by about 30 minutes of quiet, with eruptions occurring at the end of shaking. The reservoir fills with hot water, and imploding pressurized bubbles cause tremors. Researchers identified a reservoir west of Old Faithful, estimated at about 200 meters in diameter and able to hold approximately 300,000 cubic meters of water, while each eruption releases around 30 cubic meters. Further surveys were planned.

The Secretary suggested keeping open minds and few formal commitments at a general conference, since formal positions are harder to change, and urged a flexible rather than crystallized approach; the Dumbarton Oaks proposals were made informal because they might require modifications. Discussion covered objections to the name “United Nations” and Chapter I’s enumeration of principles. A footnote states the term “United Nations” came into being on December 31, 1941, when Roosevelt suggested it to Churchill for the January 1, 1942 joint declaration. Stettinius’s diary describes arranging trips to Yalta and Mexico City, urging that six Latin American associated nations be told they might be excluded from initial participation unless they declared war and qualified as United Nations, preparing policy memoranda for the President for the Big-Three meeting, seeking to start machinery for a United Nations Conference, and addressing Security Council voting procedure: Britain would accept a compromise formula, and Roosevelt reportedly moved toward the Russian unanimity view but felt the Russians would yield on seventeen votes.

In this habeas corpus appeal, Ronald L. Johnson challenged the admission of a confession at his 1964 Massachusetts trial for first degree murder, armed robbery, and related offenses, which occurred before Escobedo and Miranda. The court applied Procunier v. Atchley and affirmed that the confession was voluntary. Johnson had objected before trial that police physically coerced him; the trial court rejected that claim. After Escobedo, he sought a new trial because he lacked counsel; the trial court denied it, finding he had not requested or been denied counsel, and the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court affirmed. On appeal, Johnson argued the trial court failed to consider the totality of circumstances, that Lego v. Twomey applied retroactively, and that his confession was involuntary as a matter of law. The court found it unnecessary to decide the first two issues because its independent review under the totality standard showed the confession voluntary even under Lego. Considering his injuries, limited education and intelligence, lack of sleep, police presence, lineups, and lack of warnings, along with his prior police experience and conduct, the court concluded his will was not overborne and affirmed.

Eighteen initial winners, including 13 based in the U.S., received French President Macron’s “Make Our Planet Great Again” climate grants. Two winners told AP they welcomed moving their research to France. Camille Parmesan cited eroding U.S. climate science, funding problems and psychological strain; Benjamin Sanderson cited difficulty getting U.S. funding and France’s prioritization of climate research. Macron congratulated winners before a Paris climate summit.

The study describes the Healthy Davis Together/Healthy Yolo Together (HDT/HYT) program, launched in September 2020 and expanded to Yolo County in July 2021, which provided free saliva-based asymptomatic COVID-19 testing and related interventions. The analysis summarized 770,165 tests among 89,924 Yolo County residents, including 53,869 Davis residents, reaching approximately 41.1% of Yolo County and 78.4% of Davis residents. Tests were grouped into Pre-Delta, Delta, Omicron, and Post-Omicron periods. Omicron had the highest average daily tests and positive cases, and frequent testing was most prominent during Omicron; participation dropped after Omicron. Women, individuals aged 19–34, and White participants were consistently the most frequent testers. Highest positivity rates were observed among American Indian/Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander, Latino, and 20–44 age groups. The authors state that the data do not allow conclusions about reasons for observed differences.

In 2017, Worcester paid over $11 million in overtime; police, fire and public works combined received over $7 million. Police overtime was $4,399,365, with John Towns receiving the most at $59,577. Police details totaled $9,326,718; George Kelly earned $100,384 in details, more than his $75,508 regular pay. Officials said overtime was not due to understaffing, citing special projects, protests, training, grants, and emergencies. City Manager Edward Augustus Jr. was highest paid; 223 employees earned over $100,000 in regular pay.

In Indiana, 278 people have died from the flu this season, and flu season can last until mid-April. Many illnesses spread through contact, with flu viruses living on surfaces about a day and norovirus for days or weeks. An IU Health handwashing experiment found 15 bacteria types on hands with no large difference before and after washing, indicating harder, longer washing was needed. A cell phone test found 10 bacteria types consistent with normal mouth, throat, and skin flora, with no “bad bacteria.” Proper handwashing is described as the easiest way to prevent disease spread.

The passage discusses a study on walking as a bodily and sensory act involving interaction with place and the physical environment, shaped by people and objects, and assigned different meanings in art. It notes that walking can shape identity mutually and, in artistic expression, serve as a medium for understanding mind, body, and place. In education, walking can encourage questioning relationships with place and support sensory, relational, and social investigations in place-based critical art education. The study used an art-based methodology and an interpretive, phenomenological perspective over 10 weeks in 2023 in an undergraduate fine arts teaching program in western Türkiye, with seven prospective teachers, conducted online after the 2023 earthquake. Participants integrated walking routes into daily routines, created visual diaries, texts, and photographs, examined artworks including Francis Alÿs’ *The Collector*, conducted aesthetic inquiry, and created their own works. Data included visual diaries, class recordings, course texts, and interviews, analyzed through axial coding and thematic analysis, with triangulation and participant validation. Findings were organized around “from conceptual perception to sensory experience,” the “artistic inquiry of walking,” and “place in art-based practices.” Participants initially described walking as ordinary or simple, then expanded its meanings, developed sensory awareness, drew on personal experiences, noticed people, animals, places, sounds, and social issues, and produced videos, performances, collages, and digital works. They reported positive evaluations of walking as a teaching tool and connections among art, life, and education, while noting difficulties in visualizing feelings, choosing subjects, satisfaction, public performance, and materials. The study concludes that a daily life experience can become an aesthetic experience through art-based practices focused on walking, and that such studies can benefit prospective teacher training and expand participants’ sense of place and relationships with place.

India’s Supreme Court on Monday ordered that parties can no longer seek votes in the name of religion, caste, creed, community, and language. The author says it is unclear how the court reached the order and that he has not seen the judgment or the dissent of three judges on the seven-judge bench. He calls the order problematic: it assumes identity-based politics is wholly bad, overlooks Indian social hierarchies and democracy’s role in challenging them, and ignores that discrimination led to identity mobilisation, with voting helping marginalised communities and the Constitution addressing historic discrimination through reserved seats. He notes communal appeals, riots, polarisation, and impunity, but says the solution is rule of law and democracy’s self-correcting mechanisms, not judicial fiat. He also cites a shift toward issues and delivery, says the order is un-implementable nationwide, and argues the judiciary should let electoral democracy evolve.

They reviewed video and will review more at the hotel; they know what to do. They are working on getting shots through, reducing windups and blocked shots, and getting the puck to the net. The #MeToo reckoning changed Canadian politics through rapid resignations after allegations: Jamie Baillie, Patrick Brown, and Kent Hehr. None was proven in court. Backlash compared the movement to McCarthyism and raised due-process concerns. The passage asks when accused political figures should resign and argues parties should hold leaders to a higher standard, including avoiding apparent gross impropriety. It distinguishes sexual coercion from clumsy advances and says party responses reveal how women are valued. It addresses belief of accusers and presumption of innocence, saying fairness now includes presuming alleged victims are truth-telling. Timing skepticism is valid, but women are now believed. #MeToo must be fair while changing a status quo that silenced women.

Previously, governments and foundations led development financing through loans and grants. Kim and Gates argued large capital pools could profit by investing in hospitals in Pakistan and Nigeria. Abraaj, the largest private equity firm focused on developing economies, manages $13.6 billion. Its $1 billion health care fund drew $545 million to buy hospitals in Nigeria, Pakistan, and India. Investors found over $200 million in uninvested cash and requested bank statements. Naqvi cited regulatory delays and a need for cash, then returned more than $100 million in December. Investors sought an independent auditor; Abraaj hired KPMG, and investors including Proparco and CDC Group requested forensic proof the money was not used for Abraaj operations. The World Bank’s corruption unit investigated and closed without finding evidence of wrongdoing. The fund invested about half its $1 billion; its $145 million CARE hospital investment saw earnings fall from $14 million to $8 million before taxes. Naqvi founded Abraaj in 2002 and is trying to start a $6 billion fund in 30 developing countries.

Indiana is the latest state to try outcomes-based contracting, hiring private tutoring companies to improve middle school reading, with pay largely based on student improvement. State education secretary Katie Jenner said the state will only pay if a partner helps deliver outcomes, though contract structure, guaranteed pay and incentives remain undecided. Other states and the Center for Outcomes-Based Contracting provide examples. The center recommends at least 40 percent of a contract depend on clearly defined student gains, but results are mixed and research is limited. In 2025, about half of member contract learning goals were achieved, with vendors earning about 68 percent of possible bonuses. Texas, Florida and Denver examples had varied results. Stanford researchers reported promising findings but noted financial risks for vendors and implementation complexity. Indiana’s effort will focus on struggling students, and Jenner is seeking donations and grants.
